english_text:
Jacob Meets Esau
1Later that day Jacob met Esau coming with his 400 men. So Jacob told his children to walk with their mothers. 2The two servant women, Zilpah and Bilhah, together with their children went first, followed by Leah and her children, then by Rachel and Joseph. 3Jacob himself walked in front of them all, bowing to the ground seven times as he came near his brother.
4But Esau ran toward Jacob and hugged and kissed him. Then the two brothers started crying.
5When Esau noticed the women and children he asked, “Whose children are these?”
Jacob answered, “These are the children the Lord has been kind enough to give to me, your servant.”
6Then the two servant women and their children came and bowed down to Esau. 7Next, Leah and her children came and bowed down; finally, Joseph and Rachel also came and bowed down.
8Esau asked Jacob, “Why did you send those herds I met along the road?”
“Master,” Jacob answered, “I sent them so you would be friendly to me.”
9“But, brother, I already have plenty,” Esau replied. “Keep them for yourself.”
10“No!” Jacob said. “Please accept them as a sign of your friendship for me. When you welcomed me and I saw your face, it was like seeing the face of God. 11Please accept these as gifts I brought to you. God has been good to me, and I have everything I need.” Jacob kept insisting until Esau agreed.
12“Let's get ready to travel,” Esau said. “I'll go along with you.”
13But Jacob answered, “Master, you know traveling is hard on children, and I have to look after the sheep and goats that are nursing their young. If my animals travel too much in one day, they will all die. 14Why don't you go on ahead and let me travel along slowly with the children, the herds, and the flocks. We can meet again in the country of Edom.”
15Esau replied, “Let me leave some of my men with you.”
“You don't have to do that,” Jacob answered. “I am happy, simply knowing that you are friendly to me.”
16So Esau left for Edom. 17But Jacob went to Succoth, where he built a house for himself and set up shelters for his animals. That's why the place is called Succoth.
Jacob Arrives at Shechem
18After leaving northern Syria, Jacob arrived safely at Shechem in Canaan and set up camp outside the city. 19 The land where he camped was owned by the descendants of Hamor, the father of Shechem. So Jacob paid them 100 pieces of silver for the property, 20then he set up his tents and built an altar there to honor the God of Israel.

1Jekob yaa zak zuk a nya Iisɔ ale wa cheena ale wa nuruba kobsinaansiwa. Ate wa yaa lab bisaŋa a te Leya ale Arekel ale dɔkliema bayewa. 2Wa jam basi ate dɔkliema ale ba bisaŋa a dɛ ka niŋ, ate Leya ale wa bisaŋa a pai a saŋ, ate Arekel ale Josefi a wari ŋaaŋ. 3Wadek yaa ga dɛ niŋ a koori tɛŋ naŋtuok nɔi buyopɔi ase wa ale moata wa suoku la.
4Alege Iisɔ a chali kama a ga tu wa suik a yaa gbaari wa ale pai nisa vi wa ŋinni zuk a yaa puusi wa. Ate ba kum. 5Iisɔ yaa zuk nya nipooma ale bisaŋa. Wa yaa bek ayen, <<Baai ale bo ale fu la a nyini ka bɛ?>> Jekob yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Ba ka fi tomteerɔwa bisa ate Naawen a pai te wa.>>
6Ate dɔkliema ale ba bisaŋa ale moata la, ba yaa koori tɛŋ. 7Ate Leya ale wa bisaŋa a jam koori tɛŋ. Ate Josefi ale Arekel a wari ŋaaŋ ate ba mɛ a koori tɛŋ.
8Iisɔ yaa bek ayen, <<Alege duŋsaŋa de meena ate ni choa cheena la kiri ale boa?>> Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<M nyɔnɔ, mi a yaali kama ayen fi ŋman te mu.>>
9Alege Iisɔ yaa weeni wa ayen, <<M suowa tanla fi ŋantaŋa, mi mɛ dek a ta ŋanta kama nna yegayega.
10Jekob yaa weeni ayen, <<Mi kan siagi, ase fi dan sum a ta ŋmanteka ale mu, be tuesi m tiirimu a nyini m jigi. M le nya fi nimbidiaka la a nye ase ka Wen nimbidiak ate m nya la, fi ŋmanteka nyiŋ ate yɔgyɔgla de fi a tuesi mi la. 11Mi a saalim fu kama ayen fi tuesi tiirimu de ate m ta jam ayen m te fu la, diila Wen a nala ka nna yegayega a te mi ate m ta jaab meena ate mi a silim la.>> Jekob ale kasim jam va wa la, Iisɔ yaa tuesi.
12Ate Iisɔ yaa weeni ayen, <<Basi ate ti lɔ suik po ate m bani fu ate ti cheŋ.>>
13Alege Jekob a weeni wa ayen, <<M nyɔnɔ, fi seba kama ayen bisaŋa a pɔsima kama, ate m magsi mi a nya pa bisaŋa ale niiŋa ale a ŋoosi la zuk. Fi daa yiak ŋa nwuli nwuli dai yeŋ ate duŋsaŋa meena ale kpi. 14Dila nyiŋ be dɛ niŋ a cheŋ m nyɔnɔ, ate mi fi tomteerɔwa a vi duŋsaŋa ŋaaŋ maga maga ale bisaŋa ate ti jam paari fu Seir tɛŋka, m dek nyɔnɔ.
15Iisɔ yaa weeni ayen, <<Te m basi m nidoama gela ate ba bo ale fu.>> Jekob yaa bek wa ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi a namsi fi dega? M nyɔnɔ, fidek tin basi ate nya fi ŋmanteka.>>
16Ate di danni Iisɔ a ŋman lɔ suik po a cheŋ Seir. 17Alege Iisɔ a jam cheŋ ka Sukkot, wa yaa sɛ yeri dula a te wadek ale nye goom jigi a te wa duŋsaŋa. Dila ale soa ate ba a wi jigini ayen Sukkot.
18Jekob ale nyini Paddan Araam la, wa ga paari Sikiim tɛŋka ale bo Keenan po la ka nalimnyiini, ate wa yaa kali tɛŋ kpieŋka po jigi. 19Jekob a jam da tɛŋka ka kpana kook a nyini, Sikiim biika Ayaamo bisaŋa jigi, tɛŋ kala zuk ate wa jam ti wa viuku. 20Dula ate wa jam nye kuŋkuŋ a wi ku ayen El Eloye Izirali.

Dinah Is Raped
1Dinah, the daughter of Jacob and Leah, went to visit some of the women who lived nearby. 2She was seen by Hamor's son Shechem, the leader of the Hivites, and he grabbed her and raped her. 3But Shechem was attracted to Dinah, so he told her how much he loved her. 4Shechem even asked his father to arrange for him to marry her.
5Meanwhile, Jacob heard what had happened. But his sons were out in the fields with the cattle, so he did not do anything at the time. 6Hamor arrived at Jacob's home 7just as Jacob's sons were coming in from work. When they learned that their sister had been raped, they became furiously angry, because nothing is more disgraceful than rape, and it must not be tolerated.
8Hamor said to Jacob and his sons:
My son Shechem really loves Dinah. Please let him marry her. 9Why don't you start letting your families marry into our families and ours marry into yours? 10You can share this land with us. Move freely about until you find the property you want; then buy it and settle down here.
11Shechem added, “Do this favor for me, and I'll give whatever you want. 12Ask anything, no matter how expensive. I'll do anything, just let me marry Dinah.”
13Jacob's sons wanted to get even with Shechem and his father because of what had happened to their sister. 14So they tricked them by saying:
You're not circumcised! It would be a disgrace for us to let you marry Dinah now. 15But we will let you marry her, if you and the other men in your tribe agree to be circumcised. 16Then your families can marry into ours, and ours can marry into yours, and we can live together like one nation. 17But if you don't agree to be circumcised, we'll take Dinah and leave this place.
18Hamor and Shechem liked what was said. 19Shechem was the most respected person in his family, and he was so in love with Dinah that he hurried off to get everything done. 20The two men met with the other leaders of their city and told them:
21These people really are friendly. Why not let them move freely about until they find the property they want? There's enough land here for them and for us. Then our families can marry into theirs, and theirs can marry into ours.
22We have to do only one thing before they will agree to stay here and become one nation with us. Our men will have to be circumcised just like theirs. 23Just think! We'll get their property, as well as their flocks and herds. All we have to do is to agree, and they will live here with us.
24Every grown man followed this advice and got circumcised.
Dinah's Brothers Take Revenge
25Three days later the men who had been circumcised were still weak from pain. So Simeon and Levi, two of Dinah's brothers, attacked with their swords and killed every man in the town, 26including Hamor and Shechem. Then they took Dinah and left. 27Jacob's other sons came and took everything they wanted. All this was done because of the horrible thing that had happened to their sister. 28They took sheep, goats, donkeys, and everything else that was in the town or the countryside. 29After taking everything of value from the houses, they dragged away the wives and children of their victims.
30Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “Look what you've done! Now I'm in real trouble with the Canaanites and Perizzites who live around here. There aren't many of us, and if they attack, they'll kill everyone in my household.”
31They answered, “Was it right to let our own sister be treated that way?”
translation_text:
1Yɔgyɔgla Daina, lie waai ate Leya a jam biak a te Jekob la, yaa jam nyini peelim a cheŋ tɛŋka nipooma jigi ayen wa puusi ba. 2Ayaamo biika Sikiim Yivi denɔwa, waai ale soa kauk kula a nya la, ale ga nya wa la, wa yaa yik wa, a fɛ goa ale wa. 3Wa suinum yaa jam doa Jekob liewa Daina zuk, ate wa ta yaalika ale nipokbinni, ate wa biisi bi masik a te wa. 4Ate Sikiim a yaa weeni wa kowa Ayaamo ayen, <<Yaali nipokbinni nna a te mu ate wa chim m pok.>>
5Jekob ale ga wom ayen ba taŋ wa liewa la, ale wa bisaŋa a jam ta ka duŋsa a bo vaasaŋa po, ate wa yaa jam sina ate ba ga jam yeri.
6Ate Ayaamo ale ka Sikiim ko la, yaa cheŋ ayen wa biisi ale Jekob. 7Yɔgyɔgla Jekob bisaŋa ale ga nyini vaasaŋa po a jam la, ba yaa wom dii ale nye la. Ate ku yaa jam cha ba ate ba sue yaa jaa puuri, dii nyiŋla Sikiim a nye ka chivie wari Izirali po, wa ale goa ale Jekob liewa la, wa dii ale kan magsi ayen di nye.
8Alege Ayaamo a jam weeni ba kama ayen, <<M biika Sikiim suinum ale doa fi liewa zuk. Mi a saalim fu ayen fi pai wa a te wa ate wa chim wa pok. 9Ni te ate ti a faari chaab lieba. Ni pai ni liema a te ti, abe tama mɛ a pai ti liema a te ni. 10Ni baga a kali ale ti kama. Tɛŋka ale la a lak doa te ni. Ni kali ka po, ni a nye geruŋ ka po, abe ni ta ŋanta ka po.
11Ate Sikiim yaa weeni Daina kowa ale wa tuama ayen, <<Ni ŋman te mu, ate ni ale a yaali jaabuuri meena la, m le te ni. 12Ni weeni dii ale magsi m tuni nipowa nyiŋla ale tiirim buui ale magsi m te la. Dii meena ate ni a weeni la ku dan poom zuak a soa dii ya, m le tuni ni. Nama dek a tin pai nipokbinni ate wa chim m pok.>>
13Ba le taŋ ba toawa Daina la nyiŋ, Jekob bisaŋa a jam tulisi Ayaamo ale ka Sikiim ko la ale ka pimpaasima ase ba le a biisi ale wa. 14Ba jam weeni wa kama ayen, <<Tama kan nye wa dila choa. Tama a kan pai ti toa a te nuru waai ate ba an gebi wa yoari ya. Ku le chim ka chivie a te ti. 15Tama le pai ti ale a siak wa dii zuk la a dueni ni niŋ. Di be ka wa yeŋ dekki. Ase ni dan siak ayen ni gebi ni nidoama meena yoaŋa ate ni nye ase tama la. 16Dila tɔgni, ti le pai ti liema a te, abe ti tuesi nama mɛ liema a tara. Ate ti le kali ale ni, ate ti chim nuru yeŋsa ale chaab. 17Alege ni dan kan siak ayen ni gebi ni yoaŋa, ti le ta ti toawa a cheŋ.>>
18Ba le jam weeni diila a jam nala kama a te Ayaamo ale wa biika Sikiim. 19Duorɔwa, waai le ta zula a gaam ba meena wa ko yenni po la, an poom jam beni ale ba ale weeni wa diila. Dii nyiŋla wa jam ta suipeentik ale Jekob liewa kama. 20Ate Ayaamo ale wa biika a jam cheŋ tɛŋka nansuiŋku ayen ba biisi a sak tɛŋka nidoama. 21Ba yaa weeni ayen, <<Nuruma de ka ti doaba, ni te ti te ba suik ate ba kali ti tɛŋka po a gerim. Tɛŋka doa kama nna yegayega a baga a paari ba. Ti baga a faari ba lieba kama ate ba mɛ a baga a faari tama mɛ lieba. 22Alege nuruma ale siak a kali ale ti ase ka tama a nin nye ba le a weeni dii ayen, ti nidoama a gebi ba yoaŋa ase ba ale gebi diila. 23Ba le a wuuk ŋan baai la ale ba paaruŋku ale ba duŋsaŋa meena, a kan chim daa tama ŋanta? Dila nyiŋ ni te ti siak te ba, ate ba kali ale ti.>>
24Nidoama meena ale nyini nansuiŋku la a siak Ayaamo ale wa biika Sikiim ale weeni diila ate nidoama meena ale jam bo tɛŋka po la a jam gebi ba yoaŋa kama.
25Ba le gebi ba yoaŋa ate ku paari daa ŋata, ate ba niraŋa a dom la, ate Jekob bisa baye, ba jam ka Simeyon ale Livai, ale ka Daina toaba la, yaa jam pai gebik woŋsa, a ga yik tɛŋ kaai ale kan seba kpaliŋ nɔi po la nidoama a ko nidoama meena. 26Ba jam maa ko Ayaamo ale wa biika Sikiim alege yaa ta Daina a nyini Sikiim yenni po a cheŋ. 27Jekob bisaŋa yaa jam kpiema zuk a kɔlim ba ŋantaŋa, ale juijui ate ba taŋ ba toawa la. 28Ba jam choa ba piisa ale ba niiga ale ba bonsa ale ba ŋanta ale bo diina po ale peelim la kama. 29Ba jam kɔlim ba paaruŋku ale ba nipooba ale ba bisa meena ale ba yieŋa po ŋanta meena a jam ta cheŋ kama.
30Ate Jekob yaa weeni Simeyon ale Livai ayen, <<Ni ta daanika a jam te mu diila ni nye kama ate m chim ja nyuŋtik ate Keenan demma ale Perizzi demma ale nuru baai ale bo tɛŋka de la. Tama a fiisa kama, ate ba dan gum chaab ayen ba nye kpaliŋ ale mi ale m yenni demma, ba a kaasi ti kama.>>
31Alege ba tulisi wa ayen, <<Ti be basi ate wa nye ti toawa ase waai ale pai wadek a te nidoaba a tuesi ŋanta la ya?>>

english_text:
Jacob Returns to Bethel
1 God told Jacob, “Return to Bethel, where I appeared to you when you were running from your brother Esau. Make your home there and build an altar for me.”
2Jacob said to his family and to everyone else who was traveling with him:
Get rid of your foreign gods! Then make yourselves acceptable to worship God and put on clean clothes. 3Afterwards, we'll go to Bethel. I will build an altar there for God, who answered my prayers when I was in trouble and who has always been at my side.
4So everyone gave Jacob their idols and their earrings, and he buried them under the oak tree near Shechem.
5While Jacob and his family were traveling through Canaan, God terrified the people in the towns so much that no one dared bother them. 6Finally, they reached Bethel, also known as Luz. 7Jacob built an altar there and called it “God of Bethel,” because that was the place where God had appeared to him when he was running from Esau. 8While they were there, Rebekah's personal servant Deborah died. They buried her under an oak tree and called it “Weeping Oak.”
God Blesses Jacob at Bethel
9-11 After Jacob came back to the land of Canaan, God appeared to him again. This time he gave Jacob a new name and blessed him by saying:
I am God All-Powerful, and from now on your name will be Israel instead of Jacob. You will have many children. Your descendants will become nations, and some of the men in your family will even be kings. 12I will give you the land that I promised Abraham and Isaac, and it will belong to your family forever.
13After God had gone, 14 Jacob set up a large rock, so that he would remember what had happened there. Then he poured wine and olive oil on the rock to show that it was dedicated to God, 15and he named the place Bethel.
Benjamin Is Born
16Jacob and his family had left Bethel and were still a long way from Ephrath, when the time came for Rachel's baby to be born. 17She was having a rough time, but the woman who was helping her said, “Don't worry! It's a boy.” 18Rachel was at the point of death, and right before dying, she said, “I'll name him Benoni.” But Jacob called him Benjamin.
19Rachel was buried beside the road to Ephrath, which is also called Bethlehem. 20Jacob set up a tombstone over her grave, and it is still there. 21Jacob, also known as Israel, traveled to the south of Eder Tower, where he set up camp.
22 During their time there, Jacob's oldest son Reuben slept with Bilhah, who was one of Jacob's other wives. And Jacob found out about it.
Jacob's Twelve Sons
23-26Jacob had twelve sons while living in northern Syria. His first-born Reuben was the son of Leah, who later gave birth to Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun. Leah's servant Zilpah had two sons: Gad and Asher.
Jacob and his wife Rachel had Joseph and Benjamin. Rachel's servant woman Bilhah had two more sons: Dan and Naphtali.
Isaac Dies
27 Jacob went to his father Isaac at Hebron, also called Mamre or Kiriath-Arba, where Isaac's father Abraham had lived as a foreigner. 28-29Isaac died at the ripe old age of 180, then his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.
translation_text:
1Ate Wen yaa weeni Jekob ayen, <<Yiti cheŋ ga kali Betel, abe fi sɛ kuŋkuŋ dula a te Wen dii ale jam fi jigi diipo ate fi jam chali a nyini fi suoku Iisɔ jigi la.>>
2Ate Jekob yaa weeni wa yenni demma ale baai meena ale bo ale wa la ayen, <<Ni yuk ni wen chaŋsaŋa ale bo ale ni la a basi, abe ni so nidek, abe ni tagri ni gattaŋa. 3Abe ni jam ate ti cheŋ jueli Betel, ate m sɛ kuŋkuŋku a te Wen dii ale tulisi mu diipo ate m bo daanika po la ale kasim a cheŋ ale mu juijui meena ate mi a cheŋ la.>> 4Ate ba yaa pai ba wen chaŋsaŋa meena a te Jekob ale ba tukpanaŋa ale bo ba tueŋa po la, ate Jekob yaa pai ŋa a gu Sikiim tiimu tɛŋ. 5Ate ba yaa lɔ suik po ate Wen yɔgsum a jam tɛŋ sii ale moata la, ate waai an jam a vi ba.
6Jekob ale nuru baai meena ale maa bo ale wa la yaa jam Luz tɛŋka. Betel ale la a bo Keenan tɛŋka po. 7Ate wa sɛ kuŋkuŋ dula, ate wa te jigini yuei ayen El Betel, diila ka dula ate Wen a jam yeeri wadek a sak wa diipo ate wa jam chali a nyini wa suoku jigi la.
8Yɔgyɔgla Debora ale ka Aribeka tomteerɔ la, yaa jam kpi ate ba gu wa Betel tiib tɛŋ ate ba a wi jigini yuei ayen Allon Bakut.
9Jekob ale nyini Paddan Araam la, Wen a ŋman jam wa jigi a yaa niak wa. 10Wen yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Fi yuei ale Jekob, alege ba a kan ŋman wi fu ayen Jekob. Fi yuenni ale Izirali.>> Ate wa te wa yuenni ayen Izirali.
11Ate Wen yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Mi le Wen Dii Ale A Niak La. Be biak a piisi. Fi ka tɛŋ kpieŋ ale tɛŋsa ate nuruba a sueri si po, ate nalima ale nyini fi nyiŋ po a nyini. 12Tɛŋka ate m jam pai te Abrayam ale Aizik la, m le pai a te fi mɛ, ate m le pai te fi ŋaaŋbisa baai ale za ba nyini fi ŋaaŋnyiŋ a jam la.>> 13Ate Wen a cheŋ jueli a nyini juijui ate wa biisi ale wa la.
14Ate juijui ate Wen a biisi ale Jekob la wa yaa feri buntain ase zaŋi la a zaani, ate wa yaa kpiiri nyiam tiirim di zuk. Wa jam kpiiri kpaam mɛ di zuk. 15Jekob a wi juijui ate Wen a biisi ale wa la ayen Betel.
16Ate ba cheŋ nyini Betel. Ba ale jam yalima maga a nyini Efrat la, Arekel yaa jam boro a yaa yen wa biak ate ku jam tua te wa. 17Ate ku ale jam tua wa biamu po la, waai ale jam boro yik wa la yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Kan chali yɔgsummoa, fi ale nya ka nidoabili.>> 18Wa le vuusi kpeglim la, wa yaa te biika yuei ayen Ben Oni, alege yaa kpi. Alege wa kowa a te wa yuei ayen Benjamin.
19Ate Arekel a kpi ate ba gu wa ase ba ale jam bo Efrat ale ka Betiliyem suik po la. 20Ate Jekob a feri buntain ase zaŋi la wa boosuku zuk, a jam paari jinla tanni a za kama a teeri Arekel boosuku wari.
21Izirali a ŋman cheŋ wa niŋ nyiŋ a gaam Migdal Eder a ga ti wa viuku. 22Izirali ale jam bo tɛŋ kala po la, Aruben yaa cheŋ a ga bobi Bilya ale ka wa kowa pok la a goa ale wa, ate Izirali a jam wom. Jekob a jam ta ka nidoabilisa pi ale baye. 23Leya nidoabilisaŋa ale nna. Aruben jam le Jekob bikpagni, ate baai ale paasaŋ la ale nna. Simeyon ale Livai ale Juda ale Isaka ale Zebulun. 24Arekel nidoabilisaŋa ale nna. Josefi ale Benjamin. 25Arekel dɔkliewa Bilya nidoabilisaŋa ale nna. Dan ale Nafitali. 26Leya dɔkliewa Zilpa nidoabilisaŋa ale nna. Gad ale Asɛ. Ba ale jam biak nidoabili sii Paddan Araam tɛŋka a te Jekob la ale la.
27Jekob yaa jam yiti wa kowa Aizik jigi a ga bo Mamre tɛŋka po, a moata Kiriat Arba, Yebron ale la, juijui ate Abrayam ale Aizik a jam kali la. 28Aizik a jam kali ka bena kook ale pinaanuŋ. 29Ate wa yaa vuusi wa vuusumu a kpeglim alege yaa kpi, ate wa maa ga gum wa nuru baai ale kpi la po, wa jam kpaŋ kama ate wa benaŋa mɛ a piisi. Ate wa nidoabilisaŋa Iisɔ ale Jekob a gu wa.

english_text:
Esau's Family
1Esau, also known as Edom, had many descendants. 2 He married three Canaanite women: The first was Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite; the second was Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah and the granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite; 3 the third was Basemath, who was Ishmael's daughter and Nebaioth's sister.
4-5Esau and his three wives had five sons while in Canaan. Adah's son was Eliphaz; Basemath's son was Reuel; Oholibamah's three sons were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
6Esau took his children and wives, his relatives and servants, his animals and possessions he had acquired while in Canaan, and moved far from Jacob. 7He did this because the land was too crowded and could not support him and his brother with their flocks and herds. 8That's why Esau made his home in the hill country of Seir.
9-14Esau lived in the hill country of Seir and was the ancestor of the Edomites. Esau had three wives: Adah, Basemath, and Oholibamah. Here is a list of his descendants: Esau and Adah had a son named Eliphaz, whose sons were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz. Timna was the other wife of Esau's son Eliphaz, and she had a son named Amalek.
Esau and Basemath had a son named Reuel, whose sons were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
Esau and Oholibamah had three sons: Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
Chiefs and Leaders in Edom
15Esau and Adah's oldest son was Eliphaz, and the clans that descended from him were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz, 16Korah, Gatam, and Amalek. These and Esau's other descendants lived in the land of Edom.
17The clans that descended from Esau and Basemath's son Reuel were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
18The clans that descended from Esau and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. 19All of these clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom.
20Seir was from the Horite tribe that had lived in Edom before the time of Esau. The clans that had descended from him were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, 21Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.
22Lotan's sons were Hori and Heman; his sister was Timna.
23Shobal's sons were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
24Zibeon's sons were Aiah and Anah—the same Anah who found an oasis in the desert while taking the donkeys of his father out to pasture.
25Anah's children were Dishon and Oholibamah.
26Dishon's sons were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
27Ezer's sons were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
28Dishan's sons were Uz and Aran.
29The clans of the Horites were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, 30Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan, and they lived in the land of Seir.
31-39Before there were kings in Israel, the following kings ruled Edom one after another:
Bela son of Beor from Dinhabah;
Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah;
Husham from the land of Teman;
Hadad son of Bedad from Avith (Bedad had defeated the Midianites in Moab);
Samlah from Masrekah;
Shaul from the city of Rehoboth on the Euphrates River;
Baalhanan son of Achbor;
Hadar from the city of Pau (his wife Mehetabel was the daughter of Matred and the granddaughter of Mezahab).
40The clans that descended from Esau took their names from their families and the places where they lived. They are Timna, Alvah, Jetheth, 41Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon, 42Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar, 43Magdiel, and Iram. These clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom, the father of the Edomites. They took their names from the places where they settled.
translation_text:
1Iisɔ buuni ale nna, Edom ale la. 2Iisɔ jam faari wa pooma nyini ka Keenan nipooma po. Ba jam le Ada, Elon Yit denɔwa lie ale Oyolibama Anaya liewa wa jam ka Zibeon Yivi denɔwa ŋaaŋ. 3Wanyi mɛ jam le Basemat, Ismael lie ale chim Nebaiot toa.
4Ada yaa jam biak Elifaz a te Iisɔ, ate Basemat a yaa jam biak Areuel 5ate Oyolibama a biak Jeus ale Jalam ale Koora. Iisɔ nidoabilisaŋa a jam le nna ate wa biak Keenan tɛŋka po.
6Iisɔ yaa pai wa pooma ale wa nidoabilisaŋa ale wa liema ale duŋ yoŋsa meena ale wa kɔlima meena ate wa paari Keenan la, a yaa torisi cheŋ jigi yoŋ ale ge wa suoku Jekob. 7Ba ŋantaŋa ate ba paari la a jam zuak ka yega ale ba ale bo ale chaab. Tɛŋ kaai ate ba jam boro la an jam baga a maari ba nɔi bayewa, ba wuuni ŋantaŋa nyiŋ. 8Dila nyiŋ Iisɔ, Edom ale la a jam kali moata Seir ale bo guutaŋa la.
9Iisɔ buuni ale nna. Wa jam ka Edom demma koa ale jam kali moata Seir guuku la.
10Iisɔ nidoabilisaŋa yue ale nna. Elifaz Iisɔ powa Ada nidoabili ale Areuel Iisɔ powa Basemat nidoabili.
11Elifaz nidoabilisaŋa ale nna. Teman ale Omar ale Zefo ale Gatam ale Kenaz. 12Iisɔ nidoabinni Elifaz mɛ jam ta ka nɔŋ pokbili wa yuei le Timna ate wa biak Amalek te wa. Bade jam ka Iisɔ powa Ada ŋaaŋsa.
13Areuel nidoabilisaŋa jam ale nna. Nayat ale Zera ale Sammaya ale Mizza. Bade jam ka Iisɔ powa Basemat ŋaaŋsa.
14Iisɔ powa Oyolibama Anaya liewa a chim Zibeon ŋaaŋ la, ale jam biak nidoabili sii a te Iisɔ la ale nna. Jeus ale Jalam ale Koora.
15Nalima ŋaai ale jam bo Iisɔ buuni po la ale nna. Iisɔ bikpagni Elifaz nidoabilisaŋa. Teman ale Omar ale Zefo ale Kenaz ale 16Koora ale Gatam ale Amalek. Nalima ŋaai ale nyini Elifaz po a bo Edom la ale la. Ba jam ka Ada ŋaaŋsa.
17Iisɔ nidoabinni Areuel nidoabilisaŋa ale nna. Nayat ale Zera ale Sammaya ale Mizza jam ka nalima a nyini Areuel po a bo Edom la. Ba jam ka Iisɔ powa Basemat ŋaaŋsa.
18Iisɔ powa Oyolibama nidoabilisaŋa ale nna. Jeus ale Jalam ale Koora jam ka nalima a nyini Iisɔ powa Oyolibama waai ale ka Anaya lie la. 19Iisɔ nidoabilisaŋa jam ale la. Ba nalimaŋa mɛ ale la.
20Yori denɔwa Seir nidoabilisaŋa jam le nna. Ba jam bo ka tɛŋka po. Ba le Lotan ale Sobal ale Zibeon ale Anaya ale 21Dison ale Ezer ale Disan. Seir bisaŋa dɛ ale jam nyini Edom la jam ka Yori demma nalima.
22Lotan nidoabilisaŋa jam le nna. Yori ale Yeman. Timna jam ka Lotan toa.
23Sobal nidoabilisaŋa jam le nna. Alvan ale Manahat ale Ebal ale Sefo ale Onam.
24Zibeon nidoabilisaŋa jam le nna. Aiaya ale Anaya. Anaya wa dɛ ale jam nya buli tuilisaŋa gɔnni po wa le jam a nya wa kowa Zibeon bonsaŋa zuk ate si a dɛ la.
25Anaya bisaŋa jam le nna. Dison ale Oyolibama Anaya liewa.
26Dison nidoabilisaŋa jam le nna. Yemdan ale Esban ale Itran ale Cheran.
27Ezer nidoabilisaŋa jam le nna. Bilyan ale Zaavan ale Akan.
28Disan nidoabilisaŋa jam le nna. Uz ale Aran.
29Yori demma nalimaŋa jam le nna. Lotan ale Sobal ale Zibeon ale Anaya ale 30Dison ale Ezer ale Disan. Yori demma nalimaŋa jam ale la a va chaab ale ba poori dii Seir tɛŋka po la.
31Nalimaŋa de ale jam dɛ naam Edom alege ate Izirali naab a dɛ la ale nna. 32Biio biika Bela ale jam chim Edom naab. Wa tɛŋka ba jam te ka yuei ka Dinyaba. 33Bela ale kpi la, Jobab waai ale ka Zera ko a nyini Bozra la ale dɛ naam. 34Jobab ale kpi la, Yusam ale nyini Teman demma tɛŋka la ale dɛ naam.
35Yusam ale kpi la, Bedad nidoabinni Yadad ate wa jam nak dɛ Midian tɛŋka ale bo Moab po la ale dɛ naamu. Wa tɛŋka ba jam te ka yuei ayen ka Avit. 36Yadad ale kpi la, Samla ale nyini Masreka la ale dɛ naamu. 37Samla ale kpi la, Sɛyaul ale nyini Areyobot ate ka bo Benni nɔi la ale dɛ naamu.
38Sɛyaul ale kpi la, Baal Yanan, Achbor nidoabinni ale dɛ naamu. 39Baal Yanan, Achbor nidoabinni ale kpi la, Yadar ale dɛ naamu. Wa tɛŋka ba jam te ka yuei ayen ka Pau. Wa powa yuei jam le Meyetabel. Wa jam ka Matred lie. Matred mɛ jam ka Mezayab lie.
40Nalima ŋaai ale jam nyini Iisɔ buuni po ale ba yue a va chaab ale ba diina ale ba tɛŋsa ale nna. Timna ale Alva ale Jetet ale 41Oyolibama ale Elaya ale Pinon ale 42Kenaz ale Teman ale Mibzar ale 43Magdiel ale Iram. Edom nalimaŋa ale la a va chaab ale ba ale kali dii tɛŋ kaai ate ba jam boro la. Wade jam ka Iisɔ Edom demma kowa.

english_text:
Joseph and His Brothers
1Jacob lived in the land of Canaan, where his father Isaac had lived, 2and this is the story of his family.
When Jacob's son Joseph was 17 years old, he took care of the sheep with his brothers, the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah. But he was always telling his father all sorts of bad things about his brothers.
3Jacob loved Joseph more than he did any of his other sons, because Joseph was born when Jacob was very old. Jacob had even given Joseph a fancy coat 4which showed that Joseph was his favorite son, and so Joseph's brothers hated him and would not be friendly to him.
5One day, Joseph told his brothers what he had dreamed, and they hated him even more. 6Joseph said, “Let me tell you about my dream. 7We were out in the field, tying up bundles of wheat. Suddenly my bundle stood up, and your bundles gathered around and bowed down to it.”
8His brothers asked, “Do you really think you are going to be king and rule over us?” Now they hated Joseph more than ever because of what he had said about his dream.
9Joseph later had another dream, and he told his brothers, “Listen to what else I dreamed. The sun, the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me.”
10When he told his father about this dream, his father became angry and said, “What's that supposed to mean? Are your mother and I and your brothers all going to come and bow down to you?” 11 Joseph's brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept wondering about the dream.
Joseph Is Sold and Taken to Egypt
12One day when Joseph's brothers had taken the sheep to a pasture near Shechem, 13his father Jacob said to him, “I want you to go to your brothers. They are with the sheep near Shechem.”
“Yes, sir,” Joseph answered.
14His father said, “Go and find out how your brothers and the sheep are doing. Then come back and let me know.” So he sent him from Hebron Valley.
Joseph was near Shechem 15and wandering through the fields, when a man asked, “What are you looking for?”
16Joseph answered, “I'm looking for my brothers who are watching the sheep. Can you tell me where they are?”
17“They're not here anymore,” the man replied. “I overheard them say they were going to Dothan.”
Joseph left and found his brothers in Dothan. 18But before he got there, they saw him coming and made plans to kill him. 19They said to one another, “Look, here comes the hero of those dreams! 20Let's kill him and throw him into a pit and say that some wild animal ate him. Then we'll see what happens to those dreams.”
21Reuben heard this and tried to protect Joseph from them. “Let's not kill him,” he said. 22“Don't murder him or even harm him. Just throw him into a well out here in the desert.” Reuben planned to rescue Joseph later and take him back to his father.
23When Joseph came to his brothers, they pulled off his fancy coat 24and threw him into a dry well.
25As Joseph's brothers sat down to eat, they looked up and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were loaded with all kinds of spices that they were taking to Egypt. 26So Judah said, “What will we gain if we kill our brother and hide his body? 27Let's sell him to the Ishmaelites and not harm him. After all, he is our brother.” And the others agreed.
28 When the Midianite merchants came by, Joseph's brothers took him out of the well, and for 20 pieces of silver they sold him to the Ishmaelites who took him to Egypt.
29When Reuben returned to the well and did not find Joseph there, he tore his clothes in sorrow. 30Then he went back to his brothers and said, “The boy is gone! What am I going to do?”
31Joseph's brothers killed a goat and dipped Joseph's fancy coat in its blood. 32After this, they took the coat to their father and said, “We found this! Look at it carefully and see if it belongs to your son.”
33Jacob knew it was Joseph's coat and said, “It's my son's coat! Joseph has been torn to pieces and eaten by some wild animal.”
34Jacob mourned for Joseph a long time, and to show his sorrow he tore his clothes and wore sackcloth. 35All of Jacob's children came to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. “No,” he said, “I will go to my grave, mourning for my son.” So Jacob kept on grieving.
36Meanwhile, the Midianites had sold Joseph in Egypt to a man named Potiphar, who was the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_text:
1Jekob jam bo ka tɛŋ kaai ate wa kowa jam boro la, Keenan tɛŋka.
2Jekob wie ale nna. Josefi waai ale jam ka nidoa paalik a ta bena pi ale ŋayopɔi la, a jaa nya ka piisa ale wa suataŋa. Wa suataŋa, Bilya nidoabilisaŋa ale Zilpa nidoabilisaŋa, wa kowa pooma. Wa jam weeni wa kowa biem buui wa nya ale ba nye la.
3Izirali jam yaali Josefi a gaam wa nidoabili sinsila kama dii nyiŋla wa jam biak wa ka wa kpaŋsa po. Wa yaa nye garuk kuui ale nala a te wa. 4Wa suataŋa ale nya ayen wa yaali wa a gaam ba kama la ba yaa kisi wa a kan biisi wamaŋa a te wa.
5Josefi yaa goa daasim. Wa le weeni sak wa suataŋa la ba yaa ŋmasi kisi wa yega. 6Wa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni wom gɔdaasimaŋa de ate mi a gɔdaasim la. 7Ti boro a bobi kpari ŋanta laŋka po ate mi kpari ŋantaŋa deri yiti zaani, alege ate nama bobaŋa a zaani gilim mi koori tɛŋ di niŋ.>> 8Wa suataŋa yaa weeni ayen, <<Fi a yaali ayen fi a dɛ naam tama zuk kama? Fi le sum a nya tama zuwa? Ate ba yaa ŋmasi kisi wa yega wa gɔdaasimaŋa nyiŋ ale wa le weeni diila nyiŋ. 9Josefi yaa ŋman gɔdaasim a weeni wa suataŋa. Wa weeni ayen, <<Ni wom mi ŋmana, mi gɔdaasim kama. Yɔgyɔgla de wenbinni ale chiika ale chiŋmarisa pi ale kanyi ale koori a zuli mi.>> 10Wa le weeni wa kowa ale wa suataŋa la, wa kowa yaa toariŋ wa ale weeni ayen, <<Ka boan gɔdaasima? Fi mawa ale mi ale fi suataŋa ale sum jam koori tɛŋ fi niŋŋa?>> 11Ate wa suataŋa a jaa dɛ nyuri ale wa alege wa kowa a ta ku wa popola po. 12Josefi suataŋa yaa ta ba kowa piisaŋa a cheŋ ayen ŋa dɛ a moata Sikiim. 13Izirali yaa weeni Josefi ayen, <<Ase fi le poom seba la, fi suataŋa a ta piisaŋa a moata ka Sikiim ate ŋa a dɛ. Jam, mi a yaali ayen m tom fu kama ba jigi.>> 14Wa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Cheŋ ga nya ase wari meena a cheŋ nalimnyiini ale fi suataŋa ale piisaŋa abe fi jam weeni mu.>> Ate wa yaa tom wa ate wa zaani Yebron Viaka a cheŋ. Josefi ale ga paari Sikiim la, 15nuru yaa nya wa bo laŋsaŋa po a nyiem a gilim a yaa bek wa ayen, <<Fi a gisi ka boa?>> 16Wa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Mi a gisi ka m suataŋa. Fi baga a dak ba le ta ba piisaŋa a bo juijui ate ŋa a dɛ la?>> 17Nuruwa yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Ba nyini dela a cheŋ kama, mi wom ba weeni ayen, ti cheŋ Dotan.>> Dila Josefi yaa saŋ wa suataŋa ŋaaŋ a ga nya ba Dotan. 18Alege ba zaani niŋ a nya wa. Alege ate wa paari ba la, ba deri zɔk kama ayen ba ko wa. 19Ba weeni chaab ayen, <<Gɔdaasima nyɔnɔwa ale la cheena.>> 20Ba weeni ayen, <<Ni jam ate ti ko wa a pai nyo viliŋa de dinyi po abe ti weeni ayen gɔi duŋ ale yik wa. Ate ti yaa nya wa gɔdaasimaŋa ale ŋa nye diila.>> 21Aruben ale wom nna la, wa yaa pii nyiŋ ayen wa vari wa ba nisima po a basi. Wa weeni ayen, <<Ni kan te ti ko wa.>> 22Wa ŋman weeni ayen, <<Ni kan tiri ziimoa. Ni yuk wa basi vinni de po gɔnni po dela. Ni kan pai nisa a tiri wa a ko wa.>> Aruben a weeni nna la ayen ka wa vari wa ba jigi a ta wa a ga te wa kowa. 23Josefi ale jam wa suataŋa jigi la, ba yaa yeeri wa garuk naliŋka ate wa jo la. 24Ba yaa pai wa basi vinni po. Vinni a jam ka vili koruk, nyiam jam ka di po. 25Ba le kali a dɛ ba ŋandiinta la, ba yaa nya Ismael dem a bo ba toroko po a nyini Gilead a cheena. Ba laalaakomima a ji ka ŋan baai nyum ale masa la, ale ŋan baai ate ba dan pai sa jaab wa kan kaasi la ale tiib sim, a cheŋ Ejipiti. 26Juda yaa weeni wa suataŋa ayen, <<Ka boan nyuenta ate ti le nya ase ti nin ko ti yua baaŋka alege lik wa ziimu? 27Ni jam, ni te ti pai wa da te Ismael demma abe ti kan pai nisa ko wa, wa ka ti suok, tidek nyiŋ lam ale ziim. Wa suataŋa a yaa siak. 28Midian geruŋdɔma ale jam paari la, wa suataŋa yaa dari Josefi yeeri vinni po a pai wa da kpana ligbie pisiye a te Ismael demma ate ba ta wa cheŋ. 29Aruben ale ŋman cheŋ vinni a nya ale Josefi karo la, wa yaa dari wa gattaŋa cheeri. 30Wa yaa ŋman cheŋ wa suataŋa jigi a weeni ba ayen, <<Biika karo. Mi m cheem va ka bɛ?>> 31Ba yaa pai Josefi garukku, a tɔgri buuk a pai garukku a lusi ziimu po. 32Ba yaa ta Josefi garuk naliŋka a cheŋ wa kowa jigi a weeni wa ayen, <<Tama ale nya diila ale nna. Kpesi nya ase ka fi biika garukku ale la ya.>> 33Wa yaa miŋ ku a weeni ayen, <<Ka m biika garukku ale la. Gɔi duŋ ale yik m biika. Ka sum dari Josefi a passi ka zɔna zɔna.>> 34Jekob yaa dari wa gattaŋa cheeri a pai garuk zagsik a jo a kum wa biika da boari. 35Wa nidoabilisaŋa ale wa liema a jam ayen ba yik wa ate wa sui yɔk, alege wa zɛri. Wa weeni ayen, <<Aaya, mi a kum kama ayen m ga siŋ vɔrup a cheŋ m biika jigi.>> Dila wa kowa a yaa kum wa biika. 36Alege dila meena, Midian demma a pai Josefi a da ka Ejipiti a te Potifar, Faaro niŋdeerɔma wanyi, limisidɔma kpagni.

english_text:
Judah and Tamar
1About that time Judah left his brothers in the hill country and went to live near his friend Hirah in the town of Adullam. 2While there he met the daughter of Shua, a Canaanite man. Judah married her, 3and they had three sons. He named the first one Er; 4she named the next one Onan. 5The third one was born when Judah was in Chezib, and she named him Shelah.
6Later, Judah chose Tamar as a wife for Er, his oldest son. 7But Er was very evil, and the Lord took his life. 8So Judah told Onan, “It's your duty to marry Tamar and have a child for your brother.”
9Onan knew the child would not be his, and when he had sex with Tamar, he made sure that she would not get pregnant. 10The Lord wasn't pleased with Onan and took his life too.
11Judah did not want the same thing to happen to his son Shelah, and he told Tamar, “Go home to your father and live there as a widow until my son Shelah is grown.” So Tamar went to live with her father.
12Some years later Judah's wife died, and he mourned for her. He then went with his friend Hirah to the town of Timnah, where his sheep were being sheared. 13Tamar found out that her father-in-law Judah was going to Timnah to shear his sheep. 14She also realized that Shelah was now a grown man, but she had not been allowed to marry him. So she decided to dress in something other than her widow's clothes and to cover her face with a veil. After this, she sat outside the town of Enaim on the road to Timnah.
15When Judah came along, he did not recognize her because of the veil. He thought she was a prostitute 16and asked her to sleep with him. She asked, “What will you give me if I do?”
17“One of my young goats,” he answered.
“What will you give me to keep until you send the goat?” she asked.
18“What do you want?” he asked in return.
“The ring on that cord around your neck,” was her reply. “I also want the special walking stick you have with you.” He gave them to her, they slept together, and she became pregnant.
19After returning home, Tamar took off the veil and dressed in her widow's clothes again.
20Judah asked his friend Hirah take a goat to the woman, so he could get back the ring and walking stick, but she wasn't there. 21Hirah asked the people of Enaim, “Where is the prostitute who sat along the road outside your town?”
“There's never been one here,” they answered.
22Hirah went back and told Judah, “I couldn't find the woman, and the people of Enaim said no prostitute had ever been there.”
23“If you couldn't find her, we'll just let her keep the things I gave her,” Judah answered. “And we'd better forget about the goat, or else we'll look like fools.”
24About three months later someone told Judah, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has behaved like a prostitute, and now she's pregnant!”
“Drag her out of town and burn her to death!” Judah shouted.
25As Tamar was being dragged off, she sent someone to tell her father-in-law, “The man who gave me this ring, this cord, and this walking stick is the one who got me pregnant.”
26“Those are mine!” Judah admitted. “She's a better person than I am, because I broke my promise to let her marry my son Shelah.” After this, Judah never slept with her again.
27-28Tamar later gave birth to twins. But before either of them was born, one of them stuck a hand out of her womb. The woman who was helping tied a red thread around the baby's hand and explained, “This one came out first.”
29At once his hand went back in, and the other child was born first. The woman then said, “What an opening you've made for yourself!” So they named the baby Perez. 30When the brother with the red thread was born, they named him Zerah.
translation_text:
1Va ŋala po, Juda yaa basi wa suataŋa ale cheŋ a ga bo le nuru ate wa nyini Adullam tɛŋka. Wa yuei jam le Yira. 2Dula Juda yaa tu Keenan denɔ lie. Keenan denɔwa yuei jam le Sɛyua. Wa yaa faari wa. Wa yaa goa ale wa, 3ate wa yik lɔgi a biak nidoabili ate ba te wa yuei ayen Ɛri. 4Wa ŋman yik lɔgi a biak nidoabili ate ba te wa yuei ayen Onan. 5Wa ŋman biak nidoabili wa choa ate ba te wa yuei ayen Sɛla. Ba jam biak wa ka Kezib tɛŋka.
6Juda jam yaali ka nipok a te Ɛri waai ate wa liŋ biak la. Nipowa yuei jam le Tamara. 7Alege Juda bikpagni Ɛri le jam nye diila a bie kama Naawen nimbie po, dila nyiŋ Naawen yaa ko wa.
8Juda weeni Onan ayen, <<Goa ale fi suoku powa a tom dii ale magsi la ase fi suok pok la a biak a te fi suoku.>> 9Alege Onan seba ayen bisaŋa a kan chim wa bisa, dila wa nyiem yaa le boro a goa le wa suoku powa la wa yaa sam basi tɛŋ ate wa kan biak a te wa suoku. 10Wa le jam nye diila a bie kama Naawen nimbie po, dila wa yaa ko wa mɛ.
11Juda yaa weeni wa sampowa Tamara ayen, <<Bo fi kowa yenni ase pukɔgi la ate m biika Sɛla pak.>> Diila wa poli kama ayen, <<wa mɛ ale kpi ase wa suataŋa la.>> Dila Tamara yaa cheŋ ga bo wa kowa yenni.
12Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ku le jam beni la, Juda powa Sɛyua liewa yaa kpi. Juda suinni ale ga yɔk la wa yaa cheŋ Timnaya nuru baai ale jaa che wa piisaŋa kɔbtaŋa la jigi. Wa doawa Adullam denɔwa Yira jam va wa cheŋ kama.
13Ba le weeni Tamara ayen, <<Fi ŋiak nidoawa a bo ka suik a cheŋ Timnaya ayen wa che wa piisaŋa kɔbtaŋa la, 14wa yaa yeeri wa pukɔgi gattaŋa, ale lik wadek ale garuk nyaara nyaara ayen ba kan miŋ wa. Wa yaa kali nansuiŋku ale a cheŋ Enaim la, juijui ale bo Timnaya suiku po. Diila wa nya kama ayen Sɛla a chim kama yɔgla, ba an pai wa te wa ase wa pok la.
15Juda ale nya wa la wa pai wa chim ka nidoa yaalik, diila wa lik wa nimbidiaka kama. 16Wa an miŋ ayen ka wa sampowa ale la, wa yaa cheŋ wa jigi suiku nɔi a weeni ayen, <<Jam yɔgyɔgla a goa ale mu.>> Wa yaa bek wa ayen, <<Fi le te mu ka boa abe fi goa ale mu?>>
17Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<M le te fu buuk a nyini m duŋsaŋa po.>> Nipowa yaa ŋman bek wa ayen, <<Fi le te mu jaab ase pumpuulima la ate fi ga tom te?>> 18Wa yaa weeni ayen, <<M te fu boan jaab pumpuulima? Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Fi nifelinni ale di miika ale fi nisa po doani.>> Wa yaa pai te wa ale goa ale wa ate wa yik lɔgi. 19Nipowa ale basi wa la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, wa yaa yeeri wa garukku ale jo wa pukɔgi garukku ŋmana.
20Juda a jam tom ka wa doawa Adullam denɔwa ale buuk ayen wa tuesi wa tachekka ate wa pai te wa la, alege wa doawa an jam nya wa. 21Wa jam bek ka nuru baai ale bo dula la ayen, <<Bɔgluk taabuka a bo ka be waai ale bo Enaim suiku nakpiaka la.>> Ba yaa tulisi ayen, <<Bɔgluk taabuk a ka dela.>>
22Wa yaa ŋman cheŋ Juda jigi a weeni ayen, <<Mi an nya wa. Nuruma ale bo dula la ayen, <Bɔgluk taabuk a ka dela.>>> 23Ate Juda ayen, <<Basi ate wa tanla jabuui ate wa ta la kan daa di, ba le nye ti a la kama. Dila meena ŋaaŋnyiŋ m tom ka bu paaluk a te wa, alege fi an nya wa.>>
24Chiisa sita ŋaaŋnyiŋ ba jam weeni Juda ayen, <<Fi sampowa Tamara ka taabuk, wa be nya ku tutuna kama, wa ta ka puuk.>> Ate Juda ayen, <<Ni ta wa a nyini a ju wa ko.>>
25Ase ba le ta wa a nyini la, wa yaa tom tomtomiŋ a weeni wa ŋaandɔwa ayen, <<Mi ta ka puuk ale nuru waai ale soa ŋantaŋa de la. Nya ase fi a nin baga a miŋ ase ka wana nifelinni ale miik ale wa tachek ale nna.>>
26Juda yaa miŋ ŋantaŋa ale weeni ayen, <<Wa welema a gaam mi kama, ase m le kan pai wa a te m biika Sɛla la.>> Wa kan ŋman a goa ale wa.
27Ase ku le paari wa biamu la, nidoabilisa yibsa ale jam bo ponni po. 28Wa le boro a biak la, wanyi yaa yeeri nisa, ate nipok waai ale nya ate nipooba a biak la a yaa pai garuk miik mɔnuŋ a bobi wa nisa ale weeni ayen, <<Wade ale dɛ niŋ a nyini.>> 29Alege wa le ŋman ta wa nisaŋa a jo la, wa suoku yaa nyini ate wa weeni ayen, <<Fi ale biisi dii ate ku nyini la ale nna.>> Ate ba te wa yuei ayen Perezi. 30Ate wa suoku waai ale ta garuk miik mɔniŋka wa nisa po la a yaa nyini ate ba te wa yuei ayen Zera.

english_text:
Joseph and Potiphar's Wife
1The Ishmaelites took Joseph to Egypt and sold him to Potiphar, the king's official in charge of the palace guard. 2-3 So Joseph lived in the home of Potiphar, his Egyptian owner.
Soon Potiphar realized that the Lord was helping Joseph to be successful in whatever he did. 4Potiphar liked Joseph and made him his personal assistant, putting him in charge of his house and all of his property. 5Because of Joseph, the Lord began to bless Potiphar's family and fields. 6Potiphar left everything up to Joseph, and with Joseph there, the only decision he had to make was what he wanted to eat.
Joseph was well-built and handsome, 7 and Potiphar's wife soon noticed him. She asked him to make love to her, 8but he refused and said, “My master isn't worried about anything in his house, because he has placed me in charge of everything he owns. 9No one in my master's house is more important than I am. The only thing he hasn't given me is you, and that's because you are his wife. I won't sin against God by doing such a terrible thing as this.” 10She kept begging Joseph day after day, but he refused to do what she wanted or even to go near her.
11One day, Joseph went to Potiphar's house to do his work, and none of the other servants were there. 12Potiphar's wife grabbed hold of his coat and said, “Make love to me!” Joseph ran out of the house, leaving his coat there in her hands.
13When this happened, 14she called in her servants and said, “Look! This Hebrew has come just to make fools of us. He tried to rape me, but I screamed for help. 15And when he heard me scream, he ran out of the house, leaving his coat with me.”
16Potiphar's wife kept Joseph's coat until her husband came home. 17Then she said, “That Hebrew slave of yours tried to rape me! 18But when I screamed for help, he left his coat and ran out of the house.”
19Potiphar became very angry 20and threw Joseph in the same prison where the king's prisoners were kept.
While Joseph was in prison, 21 the Lord helped him and was good to him. He even made the jailer like Joseph so much that 22he put him in charge of the other prisoners and of everything that was done in the jail. 23The jailer did not worry about anything, because the Lord was with Joseph and made him successful in all that he did.
translation_text:
1Yɔgyɔgla ba jam ta Josefi a cheŋ ka Ejipiti. Potifar Ejipiti denɔ waai ale jam ka Faaro nyaarɔma kpagi la a da wa a ta nyini Ismael demma waai ale ta wa a cheŋ dula la jigi.
2Naawen a jam bo ale Josefi ate wa jigsi, a bo wa Ejipiti kpagni yenni po. 3Wa kpagni ale nya ayen Naawen a bo ale wa la, ate Naawen a te wa niaka wie meena po la, 4Josefi yaa nya ŋmanteka wa nina po ate wa a nya wa yenni zuk. Potifar yaa basi ate wa a nya wa yenni meena zuk ale pai jaab meena ate wa ta la a nyo wa nisa po. 5A nyini diipo ate wa basi ate wa a nya yenni meena ale jabuui meena ate wa soa la, Naawen yaa niak Ejipiti denɔwa yenni meena Josefi nyiŋ. Naawen niauŋku a jam bo jaab meena nyiŋ ate Potifar a soa la kama, yenni po ale laŋsaŋa po meena.
6Dila wa yaa pai jaab meena ate wa soa la nyo Josefi nisa po, wa an jam a te wari a daani wa ka wa ŋandiintaŋa ate wa a dɛ la. Yɔgyɔgla Josefi nyiŋka a jam boka jigi yeŋ ale nala, 7ku ale ga nye maga la wa kpagni powa nina yaa jam dua Josefi zuk ate wa weeni ayen <<Jam goa ale mu!>>
8Alege wa jam zɛri ale weeni ayen, <<Mi ale toalim a bo dela la, m kpagni niŋ a ka wari po a bo yenni po. Wa le soa jaabuuri meena la wa pai a nyo ka m nisa po ate m soa a nya. 9Waai a ka yenni de po a zuak a gaam mi. M kpagni an pai jaab a suk mi ka fi nyiini, dii nyiŋla fi ka wa pok. Mi tin nye ka sɛ a nye biemu de choa a tom kaasi Wen ya?>> 10Wa poom kasim jam a biisi ale Josefi kama daa meena, wa jam a zɛri kama ayen wa kan duak tiak po ale wa yaase wa bo wa jigi ya.
11Dai yeŋ ate wa jɔ yenni po ayen wa tom wa tuimaŋa ate yenni yɔmma waai a jam karo. 12Wa yaa yik wa garukku a tara ale weeni wa ayen, <<Jam duak ale mu!>> Alege wa jam liisi wa garukku a basi wa nisa po ale yiti chali nyini yenni po.
13Wa le nya ayen wa basi wa garukku wa nisa po alege a chali nyini yenni po la, 14wa yaa wi wa yenni yɔmma ayen, <<Ni nya ba ta Yiburu denɔwa de a jam kama ayen wa lɛ ti. Wa jam ka dela ayen wa goa ale mu alege ate mi a kaari. 15Wa le wom ayen m kaari a yaali maarika la, wa yaa basi wa garukku m tɛŋ ale yiti chali nyini yenni po.>>
16Wa yaa jam pai garukku a dueni ka wa tɛŋ ate wa kpagni a ga jam yeri. 17Ate wa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Yiburu yɔmawa ate fi ta jam a te ti la a jam kama ayen wa lɛ ti. 18Alege mi ale ga kaari ayen ba maari mu la, wa yaa basi wa garukku a dueni m tɛŋ ale yiti chali nyini yenni de po.>>
19Wa kpagni ale ga wom wari dii ate wa powa a weeni wa ayen, <<Fi yɔmawa ale nye mu diila ale nna la,>> suipuurum yaa jam dɛ wa. 20Josefi kpagni yaa jam yik wa a lik juijui ate naawa a lik wa nuruma la.
Alege Josefi ale jam bo likka dɔkku po la, 21Naawen a jam bo ale wa kama. Ate wa sak nyemagsika ale te wa ŋmanteka waai ale a nya ligrɔma zuk la jigi. 22Ate waai ale a nya ligrɔma zuk la yaa basi ate Josefi a nya dii meena ale a nye dula la zuk. 23Ligrɔma nyaarɔwa ale pai jaab meena a nyo Josefi nisa po la wari a kan jam a daani wa, dii nyiŋla Naawen a jam bo ale Josefi kama, ate wa a nya niaka dii meena ate wa nye la po.

english_text:
Joseph Tells the Meaning of the Prisoners' Dreams
1-3While Joseph was in prison, both the king's personal servant and his chief cook made the king angry. So he had them thrown into the same prison with Joseph. 4They spent a long time in prison, and the official in charge of the palace guard, made Joseph their servant.
5One night each of the two men had a dream, but their dreams had different meanings. 6The next morning, when Joseph went to see the men, he could tell they were upset, 7and he asked, “Why are you so worried today?”
8“We each had a dream last night,” they answered, “and there is no one to tell us what they mean.”
Joseph replied, “Doesn't God know the meaning of dreams? Now tell me what you dreamed.”
9The king's personal servant told Joseph, “In my dream I saw a vine 10with three branches. As soon as it budded, it blossomed, and its grapes became ripe. 11I held the king's cup and squeezed the grapes into it, then I gave the cup to the king.”
12Joseph said:
This is the meaning of your dream. The three branches stand for three days, 13and in three days the king will pardon you. He will make you his personal servant again, and you will serve him his wine, just as you used to do. 14But when these good things happen, please don't forget to tell the king about me, so I can get out of this place. 15I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and here in Egypt I haven't done anything to deserve being thrown in jail.
16When the chief cook saw that Joseph had given a good meaning to the dream, he told Joseph, “I also had a dream. In it I was carrying three breadbaskets stacked on top of my head. 17The top basket was full of all kinds of baked things for the king, but birds were eating them.”
18Joseph said:
This is the meaning of your dream. The three baskets are three days, 19 and in three days the king will cut off your head. He will hang your body on a pole, and birds will come and peck at it.
20Three days later, while the king was celebrating his birthday with a dinner for his officials, he sent for his personal servant and the chief cook. 21He put the personal servant back in his old job 22and had the cook put to death.
Everything happened just as Joseph had said it would, 23but the king's personal servant completely forgot about Joseph.
translation_text:
1Ku ale beni maga la, waai ale a te Ejipiti naawa daam la ale baai ale te wa boroborok la kpagni a jam nye ate naawa sui a kaasi. 2Faaro sui a jam kaasi ale wa kpaŋŋa bayewa kama, daam teerɔ kpagni ale boroborok seerɔ kpagni, 3ate wa yaa pai ba a nyo ligrɔma kpagni nisima po, juijui dek ate ba jam lik Josefi la.
4Ligrɔma kpagni a jam pai ba a nyo ka Josefi nisa po ate wa a nya ba zuk. Ba ale jam bo likka dɔkku po ate ku beni magadek la, 5bayema meena a jam gɔdaasim kama, Ejipiti naawa daam teerɔma kpagni ale boroborok seerɔma kpagni, baai ate ba jam lik ba la a jam gɔdaasim kama yok yeŋ, ate gɔdaasima meena a ta ŋa kiri.
6Vari ale veenti ate Josefi a jam ba jigi la, wa yaa jam nya ale ba sue a kaasi. 7Dila wa jam bek Faaro kpaŋŋa baai ale jam bo likka dɔkku wa kpagni yenni po ale wa la ayen, <<Ka boa ate ni nimbidaasa a kaasi jinla?>>
8Ba yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ti meena a gɔdaasim kama alege nuru karo a weeni ŋa kiriya.>> Josefi yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Gɔdaasima kie miŋka daa Wen ale soa? Ni weeni mu ni gɔdaasimaŋa.>>
9Ate daam teerɔ kpagni yaa weeni Josefi wa gɔdaasimaŋa. Wa weeni wa ayen, <<M gɔdaasimaŋa po m nya ka tiib m niŋ, 10ate tiimu zuk naŋsa sita a boro. Naŋsaŋa ale pusi la si deri chim a yɔn yɔna a muni. 11Faaro beerika a jam bo ka m nisa po, mi yaa pai yɔnaŋa ŋmiak a nyo Faaro beerika po a te wa.>>
12Josefi yaa weeni wa ayen. <<Di kiri ale, naŋsa sitawa ka daa ŋata. 13Daa ŋata po Faaro ale zak fi zuk a zaani a ŋman pai fu a zaani fi naŋkulaŋa po, ate fi ale pai Faaro beerika a nyo wa nisa po ase fi ale jam a nye diila, ase diipo ate fi jam chim daam teerɔ la. 14Alege ku dan cheŋ nalimnyiini ale fu, teeri ate fi sak nyemagsika ale mu. Weeni m wari a te Faaro ate wa yeeri mu a ta nyini likka dɔkku de po a nyini. 15Diila ba fɛ mi kama a ta nyini Yiburu demma tɛŋka a nyini, ate dela mɛ mi an nye wari ya a magsi ba a nyo mu likka dɔk po.>>
16Boroborok seerɔma kpagni ale jam nya ayen Josefi a tulisi magsi la, wa yaa weeni Josefi ayen, <<Mi mɛ gɔdaasim kama ayen, mi jika kpanjɔkta tita ale boroborok. 17Ŋmani kpanjɔkku po ba jam sɛka ŋandiinta tɔgatɔga a nyo ku po a te Faaro, alege nuinsaŋa a jaa dɛ ti kama kpanjɔkku ate m ji la po.>>
18Josefi yaa weeni ayen, <<Kude kiri ale nna, kpanjɔkta titawa ka daa ŋata. 19Daa ŋata po, Faaro ale gebi fi zukku a pai fi nyiŋka a saŋ tiib nyiŋ. Ate nuinsaŋa ale dɛ ka.>>
20Yɔgyɔgla de daa ŋatawa a jam ka Faaro biam dai, ate wa yaa jam nye tigi a te wa kpaŋŋa meena. Wa jam zak daam teerɔ kpagni ale boroborok seerɔma kpagni zuima a zaani wa kpaŋŋa niŋ. 21Wa ŋman jam pai daam teerɔ kpagni kpaŋtaŋa a te wa, ate wa ŋman pilim pai daam beerika a nyo Faaro nisima po, 22alege wa jam pai boroborok seerɔ kpagni a yik ka tiib nyiŋ, ase Josefi ale weeni gɔdaasimaŋa kiri diila.
23Alege daam teerɔ kpagni an jam teeri Josefi wari ya, wa jam baŋ wa wari kama.

english_text:
Joseph Interprets the King's Dreams
1Two years later the king of Egypt dreamed he was standing beside the Nile River. 2Suddenly, seven fat, healthy cows came up from the river and started eating grass along the bank. 3Then seven ugly, skinny cows came up out of the river and 4ate the fat, healthy cows. When this happened, the king woke up.
5The king went back to sleep and had another dream. This time seven full heads of grain were growing on a single stalk. 6Later, seven other heads of grain appeared, but they were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert. 7The thin heads of grain swallowed the seven full heads. Again the king woke up, and it had only been a dream.
8 The next morning the king was upset. So he called in his magicians and wise men and told them what he had dreamed. None of them could tell him what the dreams meant.
9The king's personal servant said:
Now I remember what I was supposed to do. 10When you were angry with me and your chief cook, you threw us both in jail in the house of the captain of the guard. 11One night we both had dreams, and each dream had a different meaning. 12A young Hebrew, who was a servant of the captain of the guard, was there with us at the time. When we told him our dreams, he explained what each of them meant, 13and everything happened just as he said it would. I got my job back, and the cook was put to death.
14The king sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of jail. He shaved, changed his clothes, and went to the king.
15The king said to him, “I had a dream, yet no one can explain what it means. I am told that you can interpret dreams.”
16“Your Majesty,” Joseph answered, “I can't do it myself, but God can give a good meaning to your dreams.”
17The king told Joseph:
I dreamed I was standing on the bank of the Nile River. 18I saw seven fat, healthy cows come up out of the river, and they began feeding on the grass. 19Next, seven skinny, bony cows came up out of the river. I have never seen such terrible looking cows anywhere in Egypt. 20The skinny cows ate the fat ones. 21But you couldn't tell it, because these skinny cows were just as skinny as they were before. At once, I woke up.
22I also dreamed that I saw seven heads of grain growing on one stalk. The heads were full and ripe. 23Then seven other heads of grain came up. They were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert. 24These heads of grain swallowed the full ones. I told my dreams to the magicians, but none of them could tell me the meaning of the dreams.
25Joseph replied:
Your Majesty, both of your dreams mean the same thing, and in them God has shown what he is going to do. 26The seven good cows stand for seven years, and so do the seven good heads of grain. 27The seven skinny, ugly cows that came up later also stand for seven years, as do the seven bad heads of grain that were scorched by the desert wind. The dreams mean there will be seven years when there won't be enough grain.
28It is just as I said—God has shown what he intends to do. 29For seven years Egypt will have more than enough grain, 30but that will be followed by seven years when there won't be enough. The good years of plenty will be forgotten, and everywhere in Egypt people will be starving. 31The famine will be so bad that no one will remember that once there had been plenty. 32God has given you two dreams to let you know that he has definitely decided to do this and that he will do it soon.
33Your Majesty, you should find someone who is wise and will know what to do, so that you can put him in charge of all Egypt. 34Then appoint some other officials to collect one fifth of every crop harvested in Egypt during the seven years when there is plenty. 35Give them the power to collect the grain during those good years and to store it in your cities. 36It can be stored until it is needed during the seven years when there won't be enough grain in Egypt. This will keep the country from being destroyed because of the lack of food.
Joseph Is Made Governor over Egypt
37The king and his officials liked this plan. 38So the king said to them, “Who could possibly handle this better than Joseph? After all, the Spirit of God is with him.”
39The king told Joseph, “God is the one who has shown you these things. No one else is as wise as you are or knows as much as you do. 40 I'm putting you in charge of my palace, and everybody will have to obey you. No one will be over you except me. 41You are now governor of all Egypt!”
42 Then the king took off his royal ring and put it on Joseph's finger. He gave him fine clothes to wear and placed a gold chain around his neck. 43He also let him ride in the chariot next to his own, and people shouted, “Make way for Joseph!” So Joseph was governor of Egypt.
44The king told Joseph, “Although I'm king, no one in Egypt is to do anything without your permission.” 45He gave Joseph the Egyptian name Zaphenath Paneah. And he let him marry Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, a priest in the city of Heliopolis. Joseph traveled all over Egypt.
46Joseph was 30 when the king made him governor, and he went everywhere for the king. 47For seven years there were big harvests of grain. 48Joseph collected and stored up the extra grain in the cities of Egypt near the fields where it was harvested. 49In fact, there was so much grain that they stopped keeping record, because it was like counting the grains of sand along the beach.
50Joseph and his wife had two sons before the famine began. 51Their first son was named Manasseh, which means, “God has let me forget all my troubles and my family back home.” 52His second son was named Ephraim, which means “God has made me a success in the land where I suffered.”
53Egypt's seven years of plenty came to an end, 54 and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was not enough food in other countries, but all over Egypt there was plenty. 55 When the famine finally struck Egypt, the people asked the king for food, but he said, “Go to Joseph and do what he tells you to do.”
56The famine became bad everywhere in Egypt, so Joseph opened the storehouses and sold the grain to the Egyptians. 57People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was so severe in their countries.
translation_text:
1Bena ŋaye ale taam la, Faaro yaa gɔdaasim. Wa jam za ka Nile benni nɔi, 2ate niiga ŋayopɔi yaa nyini benni po a nyaksi ale biigi, ate ŋa yaa bo wuuku po a dɛ. 3Ŋala ŋaaŋnyiŋ niiga ŋayopɔi a buk a lɔrima a nyini Nile benni po a jueli za naa ŋaai ale za beni nɔi la gauŋ. 4Ate naa ŋaai ale buk a lɔrima la, a nɛ niiga ŋayopɔi ŋaai ale a nyaksi ale biigi la. Ate Faaro yaa yiti wa gɔdaasimaŋa po.
5Wa jam a lo ka goom po a gɔdaasim a nye buye. Wa gɔdaasimaŋa po wa yaa nya chɔlomben a pɛ chɔlombena ŋayopɔi ate ŋa nyiŋsa a pagra ale nala. 6Ŋan maŋsaŋa ale nye nueri la, ŋan jetisa ŋayopɔi a pusi nyini a nye ase viok tuilik ale wobri ŋa la. 7Chɔlomben ŋaai ale jeta la a yaa nɛ chɔlomben ŋaai ale a nyaksi ale biigi la, ate Faaro yaa yiti wa gɔdaasimaŋa po.
8Ku saluiku wa popola yaa ta wa a daani, ate wa tom wi sampoporisaŋa ale yam nyama meena Ejipiti tɛŋka po. Faaro yaa weeni ba wa gɔdaasimaŋa alege waai a karo a weeni ŋa kiri a sak wa.
9Ate daam teerɔ kpagni yaa weeni Faaro ayen, <<Jinla m teeri m kaasuŋku. 10Faaro sui yaa jam puuri ale wa tomteerɔma, ate wa yaa jam yik mi a lik ale boroborok seerɔma kpagni limisidɔma kpagni yenni po. 11Ti meena a jam gɔdaasim kama yok yeŋ po, ate gɔdaasimaŋa meena a ta ŋa kiri. 12Ate Yiburu bi paalik a yaa jam bo dula ale ti, limisidɔma kpagni tomteerɔ. Ti weeni wa ti gɔdaasimaŋa ate wa weeni ŋa kiri a sak ti. 13Ate wie a sum tulim nye a magsi chaab ale wa ale weeni ti diila. Mi ŋman pilim nya m kpaŋtaŋa kama, ate nuru nwala ba pai wa a yik tiib nyiŋ.>>
14Ate Faaro yaa tom wi Josefi, ate ba ta wa nyini likka dɔkku po a nyini nwuli. Ba ale poni wa zukku ale tagri wa kɔlimaŋa la, wa yaa jam Faaro niŋ.
15Faaro yaa weeni Josefi ayen, <<M gɔdaasim kama ate waai an baga a weeni mu ŋa kiri ya. Alege mi wom kama ale ba weeni ayen, fi dan wom fi baga a weeni ŋa kiri kama.>>
16Josefi yaa tulisi Faaro ayen, <<Mi an baga a nye, alege Wen ale te Faaro weeni ŋaai ate wa a yaali la.>>
17Ate Faaro yaa weeni Josefi ayen, <<M gɔdaasimaŋa po m jam za ka Nile benni nɔi, 18Ate niiga ŋayopɔi a nyini benni po a jueli a biigi ale a nyaksi a bo wuutaŋa po a dɛ. 19Ŋala ŋaaŋnyiŋ, niiga gela ŋayopɔi ate ŋa jeta ale lɔrima ale buk. Mi an diem nya naa buloatila Ejipiti tɛŋka meena po. 20Naa ŋaai ale bugi a lɔrima la a yaa nɛ niiga ŋayopɔiwa ale biigi a nyini benni po a jueli la. 21Alege ŋa le poom a nɛ ŋa a nueri la, waai an baga a weeni ayen ŋa nɛ jaaboa. Ŋa lɔrima ase ka ŋa le poom ka diila. Ate mi yaa yiti.
22<<M gɔdaasimaŋa po mi ŋman nya ka chɔlombena ŋayopɔi a sueri ale nala a bo kinka yeŋ nyiŋ a chim. 23Ŋala ŋaaŋnyiŋ chɔlombena ŋayopɔi yaa pusi ŋala nyiŋ a kɔ a jeta ate kori vioku a fuk ŋa a kaasi. 24Chɔlomben ŋaai ale jeta la a yaa nɛ chɔlombena ŋayopɔi ŋaai ale nala la. Mi weeni nya kude a sak sampoporisaŋa alege ba waai an baga a tɔk ku kiri a sak mu.>>
25Ate Josefi yaa weeni Faaro ayen, <<Gɔdaasimaŋa meena ka bunyi. Wen a pai sak Faaro wa le za wa nye diila kama. 26Naa naliŋsa ŋayopɔiwa kiri ale bena ŋayopɔi, chɔlombena ŋayopɔiwa kiri ale bena ŋayopɔi. Gɔdaasimaŋa meena ka bunyi. 27Niiga ŋayopɔi ŋaai ale bugi a lɔrima la ale jam ŋaaŋ nyiŋla ka bena ŋayopɔi, ku ka dila mɛ ale chɔlombena ŋayopɔi ŋaai ate kori vioku a fuk ŋa a kaasi la. Ku a magsi ka chaab ale bena ŋayopɔi kɔm.
28<<Ku ka dii dek ate m weeni sak Faaro la. Wen a sak wa le boro a yaali wa nye diila kama. 29Bena ŋayopɔi ŋandiinta yegayega ale jam Ejipiti tɛŋka po, 30alege bena ŋayopɔi kɔm ale pai saŋ. Ate ba le baŋ ŋandiinta yegayega wari Ejipiti tɛŋka po, ate kɔm ale bo tɛŋka po. 31Ate ba kan teeri ŋandiinta yegayega wari tɛŋka po, dii nyiŋla kɔmmu ale paasaŋ la ale pagra yegayega. 32Kude a za ku sum a nye kama dii nyiŋla Wen a te fu wanni de ka gɔdaasima buye po.
33<<Basi ate naawa a nya nuru waai ale ta yam ale a miŋ wie ate wa a nya Ejipiti tɛŋka zuk. 34Basi ate Faaro lueri kpaga tɛŋka po ate ba lab ŋandiinta yegayega ku naŋtuok nɔi bunu Ejipiti po a pai bunyi a dueni. 35Ba tuesi ŋandiintaŋa meena ben maŋsaŋa de po ale cheen la, naawa pagrim nyiŋ ba tigsi kpari ŋantaŋa a dueni tɛŋ kpieŋka po a nya ŋa zuk. 36Ŋandiintaŋa de ni tali ŋa a zaani tɛŋka po ate ni jam pai de bena ŋayopɔiwa po ate kɔm a cheen Ejipiti po la, ate kɔm kan kaasi tɛŋka.>>
37Popolaŋa a jam nala kama a te Faaro ale wa kpaŋŋa meena. 38Ate Faaro yaa bek ba ayen, <<Ti baga a nya waai ase nuruwa dela, waai ate Wen Chiika a bo wa po la?>>
39Ate Faaro yaa weeni Josefi ayen, <<Ase Wen ale basi ate fi seba kude meena la, waai a karo a miŋ wie ale ta yam ase fi la. 40Fi ale fi a nya m nayenni zuk, ate fi ale a weeni diila m nuruma meena a siak a te fu. Ka m naamu zukpaglika zuk nyiini ate m le gaam fu.
41Dila Faaro yaa weeni Josefi ayen, <<M pai Ejipiti tɛŋka meena a nyo fi nisa po.>> 42Faaro yaa yeeri wa nifelinni wa nandummu nyiŋ a su Josefi nandummu nyiŋ. Wa yaa pai koaliŋ naliŋsa a jo wa ale pai ligmɔniŋ chɔrinni a su wa ŋinni. 43Wa basi ate wa dɔ wusum ale toroko ase waai ale pai a saŋ wa ŋaaŋ la, ate nuruba a de wa niŋ a nuem ayen, <<Ni te suik.>> Wa basi ate wa a nya Ejipiti tɛŋka meena zuk.
44Faaro yaa weeni Josefi ayen, <<Mi ka Faaro alege fi a dan kan weeni wari ya, nuru karo a zak wa nisa yaase wa naŋ Ejipiti tɛŋka po.>> 45Faaro yaa te Josefi yuei ayen Zafenat Panea a ŋman pai nipok a te wa, wa yuei ale Asenat. Wa jam ka Potifera On kaabteerɔwa lie. Josefi yaa jam nyiem Ejipiti tɛŋka meena po.
46Josefi a jam ta ka bena pisita ale piilim a tom a te Faaro Ejipiti naawa la. Ate Josefi a yaa basi Faaro ale cheŋ gilim Ejipiti tɛŋka. 47Bena ŋayopɔiwa po tɛŋka a jam sueri ale ŋandiinta nna yegayega. 48Josefi yaa jam tuesi ŋandiintaŋa yegayega meena ale jam nye bena ŋayopɔiwa Ejipiti tɛŋka po la a ta ga dueni tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa po. Ate tɛŋ meena ate ba bori ŋanta la, wa pai ŋa a dueni ka ka dek po. 49Josefi yaa dueni kpari ŋanta nna yegayega ase beli tintain busuŋ la. Ŋa jam piisi ka nna yegayega ate wa ŋman zɛ ŋa nɔi ya.
50Alege ate kɔmmu benaŋa a jam la, Potifera ale ka On kaabteerɔ la, wa liewa Asenat a jam biak ka nidoabilisa baye a te Josefi. 51Josefi yaa jam te bikpagni yue ayen Manasa ale weeni ayen, <<Diila Wen a nye kama ate m baŋ m daanika meena ale m kowa yenni demma meena wari.>> 52Nidoabi dii ale pai a saŋ la wa te wa yue ayen Ɛfraim ale weeni ayen, <<Diila ka Wen ale basi ate m biak nidoabilisa tɛŋ kaai po ate m nam la.>>
53Benna ŋayopɔiwa ate ŋandiinta yegayega a jam boro la yaa kpeglim, 54ate bena ŋayopɔiwa kɔmmu yaa piilim, ase Josefi ale weeni diila. Kɔm ale jam bo tɛŋ sinsila, alege Ejipiti tɛŋka po meena ŋandiinta jam boro kama. 55Ase Ejipiti demma meena ale jam miŋ ayen kɔm a boro la, nuruma yaa jam kaari te Faaro ayen ti a yaali ka ŋandiinta. Ate Faaro yaa weeni Ejipiti demma meena ayen, <<Ni cheŋ Josefi jigi a nye dii meena ate wa a weeni ni la.>>
56Ase kɔmmu ale tagli tɛŋka meena la, Josefi yaa lak ŋandiintaŋa yeeŋa a pai da te Ejipiti demma, dii nyiŋla kɔmmu a jam pagra kama Ejipiti tɛŋka meena po. 57Ate tɛŋsaŋa meena yaa jan jam Ejipiti ayen ba da ŋandiinta Josefi jigi, dii nyiŋla kɔmmu a jam pagra kama tɛŋzuk de meena.

english_text:
Joseph's Brothers Go to Egypt To Buy Grain
1When Jacob found out there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you just sitting here, staring at one another? 2 I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down and buy some, so we won't starve to death.”
3Ten of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy grain. 4But Jacob did not send Joseph's younger brother Benjamin with them; he was afraid that something might happen to him. 5So Jacob's sons joined others from Canaan who were going to Egypt because of the terrible famine.
6Since Joseph was governor of Egypt and in charge of selling grain, his brothers came to him and bowed with their faces to the ground. 7-8They did not recognize Joseph, but at once he knew who they were, though he pretended not to know. Instead, he spoke harshly and asked, “Where do you come from?”
“From the land of Canaan,” they answered. “We've come here to buy grain.”
9 Joseph remembered what he had dreamed about them and said, “You're spies! You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
10“No sir,” they replied. “We're your servants, and we have only come to buy grain. 11We're honest men, and we come from the same family—we're not spies.”
12“That isn't so!” Joseph insisted. “You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
13But they explained, “Sir, we come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and one of our brothers is dead.”
14Joseph replied:
It's like I said. You're spies, 15and I'm going to find out the truth. I swear by the life of the king that you won't leave this place until your youngest brother comes here. 16Choose one of you to go after your brother, while the rest of you stay here in jail. That will show whether you are telling the truth. But if you are lying, I swear by the life of the king that you are spies!
17Joseph kept them all under guard for three days, 18before saying to them:
Since I respect God, I'll give you a chance to save your lives. 19If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in jail, and the rest of you can take the grain back to your starving families. 20But you must bring your youngest brother to me. Then I'll know that you are telling the truth, and you won't be put to death.
Joseph's brothers agreed 21and said to one another, “We're being punished because of Joseph. We saw the trouble he was in, but we refused to help him when he begged us. That's why these terrible things are happening.”
22 Reuben spoke up, “Didn't I tell you not to harm the boy? But you wouldn't listen, and now we have to pay the price for killing him.”
23They did not know that Joseph could understand them, since he was speaking through an interpreter. 24Joseph turned away from them and cried, but soon he turned back and spoke to them again. Then he had Simeon tied up and taken away while they watched.
Joseph's Brothers Return to Canaan
25Joseph gave orders for his brothers' grain sacks to be filled with grain and for their money to be put in their sacks. He also gave orders for them to be given food for their journey home. After this was done, 26they each loaded the grain on their donkeys and left.
27When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get some grain for his donkey, and at once he saw his moneybag. 28“Here's my money!” he told his brothers. “Right here in my sack.”
They were trembling with fear as they stared at one another and asked themselves, “What has God done to us?”
29When they returned to the land of Canaan, they told their father Jacob everything that had happened to them:
30The governor of Egypt was rude and treated us like spies. 31But we told him, “We're honest men, not spies. 32We come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and the other is dead.”
33Then the governor of Egypt told us, “I'll find out if you really are honest. Leave one of your brothers here with me, while you take the grain to your starving families. 34But bring your youngest brother to me, so I can be certain that you are honest men and not spies. After that, I'll let your other brother go free, and you can stay here and trade.”
35When the brothers started emptying their sacks of grain, they found their moneybags in them. They were frightened, and so was their father Jacob, 36who said, “You have already taken my sons Joseph and Simeon from me. And now you want to take away Benjamin! Everything is against me.”
37Reuben spoke up, “Father, if I don't bring Benjamin back, you can kill both of my sons. Trust me with him, and I'll bring him back.”
38But Jacob said, “I won't let my son Benjamin go down to Egypt with the rest of you. His brother is already dead, and he is the only son I have left. I am an old man, and if anything happens to him on the way, I'll die from sorrow, and all of you will be to blame.”
translation_text:
1Ase Jekob ale ga wom ayen ŋandiinta a bo Ejipiti la, wa yaa weeni wa nidoabilisaŋa ayen, <<Ka boa ate ni zak a nya chaaba?>> 2Wa yaa weeni gum du ayen, <<Mi wom kama ayen ŋandiinta a bo Ejipiti. Ni siŋ dula a ga da ŋandiinta a ta jam, ate ti kan kpi abe ti vuuk.>>
3Josefi suata pi yaa cheŋ ayen ba da ŋandiinta Ejipiti. 4Alege Jekob ale jam tom mbala la, Josefi suoku Benjamin an jam maa gum du, dii nyiŋla wa jam a yɔgsa kama ayen wari ale nye wa. 5Dila la Izirali nidoabilisaŋa a jam gum ka baai ale cheŋ ayen ba da ŋandiinta la po, diila kɔmmu a jam bo Keenan tɛŋka po mɛ kama.
6Yɔgyɔgla de Josefi ale jam chim tɛŋka kpagi, waai ale jam da ŋandiintaŋa a te nuruba la, ase Josefi suataŋa ale ga paari la ba yaa koori tɛŋ wa niŋ. 7Josefi ale deri ga nya wa suataŋa la wa yaa miŋ ba? Alege wa yaa potim seba ale nye wadek ase nichaanɔ la a biisi ba a kaasi. Wa jam bek ba kama ayen, <<Nama nyini ka be?>> Ate ba tulisi ayen, <<Ti nyini ka Keenan tɛŋka ayen ti da ŋandiinta.>>
8Josefi a jam miŋ wa suataŋa kama alege ba an jam miŋ wa. 9Ate wa yaa teeri wa le jam gɔdaasim ba wie diila a yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni ka kpesi nyaarɔba. Ni jam ni nya ka ti tɛŋka wobsim jigi.>>
10Ate ba yaa tulisi ayen, <<Aaya, m nyɔnɔ. Fi tomteerɔma a jam ba da ka ŋandiinta. 11Ti meena ka nuru yeŋ bisa. Fi tomteerɔma ka nuru maŋsa ba daa kpesi nyaarɔba.>>
12Wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Aaya, ni jam ni nya ka ti tɛŋka wobsim jigi.
13Alege ba tulisi ayen, <<Fi tomteerɔma a jam ka suata pi ale baye, nuru yeŋ bisa waai ale bo Keenan tɛŋka po la. Baaŋka a bo ale ka ti kowa, ate wanyi a karo.>>
14Josefi yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ase mi ale weeni ni diila, ni ka kpesi nyaarɔba. 15M le m nye ni diila ale nna. Faaro ale vua la, ni kan basi dela jigini nin ka nama ale ta ni yoa baaŋka a nin jam dela. 16Ni tom ni po wanyi ate wa ga ta ni suoku a jam. Ni meena ale jo ka likka dɔkku po ate ti kpesi a nya ni wieŋa ase ni a biisi wensie ya. Ni dan kaa biisi wensie, ase Faaro ale diem vua la ni ka kpesi nyaarɔba.>> 17Ate wa yaa lik ba meena daa ŋata.
18Daa ŋatawa danni, Josefi yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni nye nnala ate ni boro, ale mi a chali Wen kama. 19Ni dan ka wensie nuruba, ni basi ate ni suataŋa wanyi a bo likka dɔkku po dela, alege ate ni meena cheŋ a ga ta ŋandiinta a ga te ni yenni demma meena ale a viiri la. 20Alege ku a fɛ ni ta ni yoa baaŋka a jam te mi, ate ni ale a weeni diila a chim wensie ate ni kan kpi.>> Ba yaa cheŋ a ga nye kude.
21Ba yaa weeni chaab ayen, <<Chekki ba a namsi ti ka ti suoku nyiŋ. Ti nya ku ale jam a daani wa dii ate wa a saalim ti wa nyuvunni nyiŋla kama, alege ti an wom ya dila ale soa ate namsika de a jam ti jigi.>>
22Ate Aruben yaa tulisi ayen, <<Mi an weeni ni ayen ni kan tom a kaasi nidoabilika? Alege ni an jam a wom ya. Yɔgyɔgla de ku a fɛ ate ti tuni wa ziimu nyiŋ.>> 23Ba an jam a miŋ ayen Josefi a miŋ ba ale a weeni diila kiri ya. Wa le jam basi ate waai tulisi a te wa la nyiŋ.
24Wa yaa viriŋ nakpiak alege ba a piilim a kum, ale ŋman a biisi ale ba. Wa yaa basi ate ba yik Simeyon a ta nyini a bobi wa ba nimbie po.
25Josefi yaa weeni ayen ba nye ŋandiinta a nyo ba boorisaŋa po, abe ba pai waai meena ligra a nyo wa boorik po, abe ba te ba ŋanta a magsi ba chelim. Ba le jam nye dila a te ba la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, 26ba yaa jam pai ba ŋandiintaŋa a vi ba bonsaŋa zuk a cheŋ.
27Ba le zaani juijui yokku la, ba po wanyi yaa foli wa boorik ayen wa nye ŋandiinta a te wa bonika, wa yaa jam nya wa kpanaŋa wa boorika po. 28Wa yaa weeni wa suataŋa ayen, <<Ba pilim pai m kpanaŋa a te mu kama, ŋa ale nna m boorika po.>> Ba kpaziita yaa nak, ate ba cheem nya chaab ate ba nyiŋsa a gɔk, ate ba weeni ayen, <<Ka boa ale nna ate Wen nye ti?>>
29Ba le jam ba kowa Jekob jigi Keenan tɛŋka po la, ba yaa weeni wa dii meena ale jam nye ba la. Ba weeni ayen, 30<<Nuru waai ale a nya tɛŋka zuk la a jam biisi ti a kaasi kama, a nye ti ase ka baai ale jam ayen ba kpesi nya tɛŋka la. 31Alege ate ti weeni wa ayen, <Ti ka nuru maŋsa ti daa kpesi nyaarɔba. 32Ti ka suata pi ale baye a chim nuru yeŋ bisa, wanyi a karo ate baaŋka ale kowa a bo Keenan.>
33<<Ate nuru waai ale soa tɛŋka a nya la yaa weeni ti ayen, <Kude ale basi ate m miŋ ase ni ka wensie nuruba ya. Ni basi ni suataŋa wanyi dela ale mu abe ni ta ŋandiinta a ga te ni yeri dem baai ale a viiri la. 34Alege ni ta ni yoa baaŋka a jam te mu ate m le seba ayen ni daa kpesi nyaarɔba, alege ni ka wensie nuruba. Ate mi yaa le ŋman pai ni suoku a te ni, ate ni le baga a gerim tɛŋka po.>>>
35Ase ba ale jam boro a kpiiri ba ŋantaŋa boorisaŋa po la, waai meena a jam nya wa kpana fook wa boorik po kama. Ba ale ba kowa ale jam nya ligra foataŋa la, ate ba nyiŋsa yaa jaa gɔk. 36Ba kowa Jekob yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni basi kama ate mi an paari m bisaŋa. Josefi a karo ate Simeyon mɛ a ŋman karo, ate yɔgyɔgla de ni a yaa ayen ni pai Benjamin. Jaab meena a ta chaab ale mu kama.>>
37Ate Aruben yaa weeni wa kowa ayen, <<Fi baga a ko m bisa bayewa kama ase m nin kan ta wa a jam a te fu. Pai wa a nyo mi nisa po ate m le pilim ta wa jam te fu.>>
38Alege Jekob a weeni ayen, <<M biika a kan va fu a siŋ dula wa suoku a kpi kama wa la nyiini ale tali. Ase wari a dan nye wa suiku po, fi ale gu mi zu peelukku nyɔnɔ ale niniga.

english_text:
Joseph's Brothers Return to Egypt with Benjamin
1The famine in Canaan got worse, 2until finally, Jacob's family had eaten all the grain they had bought in Egypt. So Jacob said to his sons, “Go back and buy some more grain.”
3-5Judah replied, “The governor strictly warned us that we would not be allowed to see him unless we brought our youngest brother with us. If you let us take Benjamin along, we will go and buy grain. But we won't go without him!”
6Jacob asked, “Why did you cause me so much trouble by telling the governor you had another brother?”
7They answered, “He asked a lot of questions about us and our family. He wanted to know if you were still alive and if we had any more brothers. All we could do was answer his questions. How could we know he would tell us to bring along our brother?”
8Then Judah said to his father, “Let Benjamin go with me, and we will leave at once, so that none of us will starve to death. 9I promise to bring him back safely, and if I don't, you can blame me as long as I live. 10If we had not wasted all this time, we could already have been there and back twice.”
11Their father said:
If Benjamin must go with you, take the governor a gift of some of the best things from our own country, such as perfume, honey, spices, pistachio nuts, and almonds. 12Also take along twice the amount of money for the grain, because there must have been some mistake when the money was put back in your sacks. 13Take Benjamin with you and leave at once.
14When you go in to see the governor, I pray that God All-Powerful will be good to you and that the governor will let your other brother and Benjamin come back home with you. But if I must lose my children, I suppose I must.
15The brothers took the gifts, twice the amount of money, and Benjamin. Then they hurried off to Egypt. When they stood in front of Joseph, 16he saw Benjamin and told the servant in charge of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and cook it, so they can eat with me at noon.”
17The servant did as he was told and took the brothers to Joseph's house. 18But on the way they got worried and started thinking, “We are being taken there because of the money that was put back in our sacks last time. He will arrest us, make us his slaves, and take our donkeys.”
19So when they arrived at Joseph's house, they said to the servant in charge, 20“Sir, we came to Egypt once before to buy grain. 21But when we stopped for the night, we each found in our grain sacks the exact amount we had paid.
