1Naawen yaa weeni Moosis ayen, <<Basi dela jigini, fi ale nuruma ate fi ta ba nyini Ejipiti po a nyini la, abe ni cheŋ tɛŋ kaai ate mi a puulim a te Abrayam ale Aizik ale Jekob ayen, <M le pai ka a te ni ŋaaŋbisaŋa la.> 2Mi ale tom Wen maarɔ ate wade ni niŋ a yiak Keenan ale Amori ale Yit ale Perizzi ale Yivi ale Jebus demma a basi te ni. 3Ni cheŋ tɛŋ kaai ate biisim ale siita a sueri ka po la. Alege mi Naawen a kan va ni a cheŋ, dii nyiŋla ni ka tukpari nyam. Dai dii dai m le ko ni suiku po.>>
4Ase nuruma ale jam wom daanika wieŋa de la, ba yaa piilim a kum ba wanyi mɛ la an jam su nifelima ale baŋsa. 5Dii nyiŋla Naawen a weeni Moosis kama ayen, <<Weeni Izirali demma ayen, <Ni ka tukpari nyam. Mi a dan poom va ni a cheŋ magdega, m te ko ni kama. Yɔgyɔgla de ni yeeri ni nifelimaŋa ale baŋsaŋa ate m poli m le a yaali ayen nye ni diila.> >> 6Dila Izirali demma yaa yeeri ba nifelimaŋa ale baŋsaŋa Yoreb Guuku zuk.
7Moosis nyiem ta viuku a nyini ba boka jigini kama a ga nakpiak a ga ti ate ku yalima, a wi ku ayen, <<tuka viuk.>> Waai a dan ta wari a yaa wa miŋ di a nyini Naawen jigi, wa a basi ba boka jigini kama ale a cheŋ tuka viuku po. 8Diipo meena Moosis a dan cheŋ jo viuku po, nuruma meena nyiem jam yiti za kama ba viitaŋa nansuiŋtaŋa noa a nya Moosis ate wa ga jo viuku po. 9Ase Moosis ale ga jo viuku po la chiŋmanni ale jam bo ku nansuiŋku nɔi alege ate Naawen a biisi ale Moosis. 10Diipo meena ate nuruma a nya ale chiŋmanni ale di za viuku nansuiŋku nɔi, ba meena nyiem yiti zaani kama a puusi, waai meena a jam boka wa viuk nɔi. 11Naawen a jam a biisi ale Moosis ase ka nuru ale a biisi ale wa doa diila. Ate Moosis nyiem yaa ŋman pilim cheŋ nuruma ale bo juijui la. Alege wa maarɔ paalika Nun nidoabinni Josua an jam basi viuku.
12Moosis yaa weeni Naawen ayen, <<Fi kasim a weeni mi kama ayen, <Dɛ nuruma de niŋ,> alege fi an basi ate m seba waai ate fi tom ayen wa cheŋ ale mi la. Fi weeni ayen, <Mi seba fi yue kama ale ta ŋmanteka ale fu.> 13Fi sui a dan peenti ale mu, sak mu fi suitaŋa ate dila ale basi ate m seba fu abe m diem gum du a nya ŋmanteka a nyini fi jigi. Teeri ayen tɛŋka de demma ka fi nuruba.>> 14Ate Naawen a tulisi ayen, <<Mi ale cheŋ ale fu, abe m basi ate fi vuusi.>>
15Ate Moosis a weeni wa ayen, <<Fi a dan kan va ti a cheŋ, kan basi ate ti nyini dela. 16Nuru yoŋ ale nye ka sɛ a seba ayen fi sui a yɔk ale mi ale fi nuruma ase fi nin kan va ti cheŋ yaa? Ka boa ale ku a sak ayen mi ale fi nuruma ka ti tɔga ale nuru mbala meena tɛŋzuk de?>>
17Ate Naawen a weeni Moosis ayen, <<Mi ale nye wanni de dek ate fi a bek la, dii nyiŋla mi sui a yɔk ale fu kama ate m seba fi yuei.>>
18Moosis ayen, <<Yɔgyɔgla de be sak mu fi zulaŋa.>>
19Ate Naawen ayen, <<Mi ale nye ate m wamaŋsaŋa meena a va fi niŋ a taam, abe m mooli m yuenni, Naawen fi niŋ. Mi ale ta jiirim ale waai ate m le ta jiirim la, abe waai niniga ale jo mu la m le nya wa niniŋŋa zuk.>> 20Wa weeni ayen, <<Alege, fi a kan nya m nimbidiaka, nuru a kan nya mi ale a boro.>>
21Naawen ayen, <<Jigi ale boro a moata mi juijui ate fi ale zaani piuŋ zuk. 22Ase mi zulaŋa a daa taam, m le pai fu a nyo piuŋ muulik po a lik fu ale m nisaŋa ate m ga taam nueri. 23Mi yaa le yeeri m nisaŋa ate fi nya m ŋaaŋka, alege mi nimbidiaka ku a fɛ ate fi kan nya.>>

english_text:
The Second Set of Commandments
(Deuteronomy 10.1-5)
1One day the Lord said to Moses, “Cut two flat stones like the first ones I made, and I will write on them the same commandments that were on the two you broke. 2Be ready tomorrow morning to come up Mount Sinai and meet me at the top. 3No one is to come with you or to be on the mountain at all. Don't even let the sheep and cattle graze at the foot of the mountain.” 4So Moses cut two flat stones like the first ones, and early the next morning he carried them to the top of Mount Sinai, just as the Lord had commanded.
5The Lord God came down in a cloud and stood beside Moses there on the mountain. God spoke his holy name, “the Lord.” 6 Then he passed in front of Moses and called out, “I am the Lord God. I am merciful and very patient with my people. I show great love, and I can be trusted. 7I keep my promises to my people forever, but I also punish anyone who sins. When people sin, I punish them and their children, and also their grandchildren and great-grandchildren.”
8Moses quickly bowed down to the ground and worshiped the Lord. 9He prayed, “Lord, if you really are pleased with me, I pray that you will go with us. It is true that these people are sinful and rebellious, but forgive our sin and let us be your people.”
A Promise and Its Demands
(Exodus 23.14-19; Deuteronomy 7.1-5; 16.1-17)
10The Lord said:
I promise to perform miracles for you that have never been seen anywhere on earth. Neighboring nations will stand in fear and know that I was the one who did these marvelous things. 11I will force out the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, but you must do what I command you today. 12Don't make treaties with any of those people. If you do, it will be like falling into a trap. 13 Instead, you must destroy their altars and tear down the sacred poles they use in the worship of the goddess Asherah. 14I demand your complete loyalty—you must not worship any other god! 15Don't make treaties with the people there, or you will soon find yourselves worshiping their gods and taking part in their sacrificial meals. 16Your men will even marry their women and be influenced to worship their gods.
17 Don't make metal images of gods.
18 Don't fail to observe the Festival of Thin Bread in the month of Abib. Obey me and eat bread without yeast for seven days during Abib, because that is the month you left Egypt.
19 The first-born males of your families and of your flocks and herds belong to me.
20 You can save the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must save every first-born son.
Bring an offering every time you come to worship.
21 Work for six days and rest on the seventh day, even during the seasons for plowing and harvesting. 22 Celebrate the Harvest Festival each spring when you start harvesting your wheat, and celebrate the Festival of Shelters each autumn when you pick your fruit.
23Your men must come to worship me three times a year, because I am the Lord God of Israel. 24As you advance, I will force the nations out of your land and enlarge your borders. Then no one will try to take your property when you come to worship me these three times each year.
25 When you sacrifice an animal on the altar, don't offer bread made with yeast. And don't save any part of the Passover meal for the next day.
26 I am the Lord your God, and you must bring the first part of your harvest to the place of worship.
Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
27The Lord told Moses to put these laws in writing, as part of his agreement with Israel. 28Moses stayed on the mountain with the Lord for 40 days and nights, without eating or drinking. And he wrote down the Ten Commandments, the most important part of God's agreement with his people.
Moses Comes Down from Mount Sinai
29 Moses came down from Mount Sinai, carrying the Ten Commandments. His face was shining brightly because the Lord had been speaking to him. But Moses did not know at first that his face was shining. 30When Aaron and the others looked at Moses, they saw this, and they were afraid to go near him. 31Moses called out for Aaron and the leaders to come to him, and he spoke with them. 32Then the rest of the people of Israel gathered around Moses, and he gave them the laws that the Lord had given him on Mount Sinai.
33The face of Moses kept shining, and after he had spoken with the people, he covered his face with a veil. 34Moses would always remove the veil when he went into the sacred tent to speak with the Lord. And when he came out, he would tell the people everything the Lord had told him to say. 35They could see that his face was still shining. So after he had spoken with them, he would put the veil back on and leave it on until the next time he went to speak with the Lord.
translation_text:
1Naawen yaa weeni Moosis ayen, <<Peesi tintain paglaksa siye ase ŋaai ate fi liŋ ta la, ate m le ŋmarisi wie ŋaai ate m daam ŋmarisi ate fi mobi ŋa la. 2Gomsi saluik a jueli jam Sinai Guuku zuk. Ta fidek a jam mi jigi guuku zuk. 3Waai a kan va fu a jam yaase m nya waai guuku zuk kauk kuui ya. Ni duŋsaŋa a poom kan dɛ guuku zuwa.>>
4Moosis yaa peesi tintain paglaksa siye ase nŋala la, a jueli Sinai Guuku zuk saluik yokyokwa, ase Naawen ale jam weeni wa diila. Ate wa yaa ta tintain paglaksa siyewa wa nisa po. 5Ate Naawen yaa siŋ jam chiŋmanni po a za ale wa a mooli wa yuenni ayen Naawen. 6Wa yaa va Moosis niŋ a taam ale a mooli ayen, <<Naawen, Naawen, jiirim ale yaalika Wen. Waai sui ale kan kpabi a puuri, wa ŋmanteka ale wa wensieŋa mɛ a zuak a tom nalimnyiini ale 7diem ta ŋmanteka ale tusa, a vɔŋ a te gaasa ale tukpari ale biem nyam. Alege wa kan basi baai ale kaasi la tue darika. Wa le dari bisa ale ba mɛ ale biak baai la tue ba koma biemu nyiŋ a ta ga paari ŋaaŋbisa buta ale bunaansiwa po.>>
8Moosis yaa jam koori tɛŋ a puusi ale weeni ayen, 9<<Nyɔnɔ, ase m dan ta ŋmantiik fi nina po basi ate Nyɔnɔwa a va ti a cheŋ. Nuruma de ka tukpari nyam, vɔŋ ti gaasaŋa ale ti biemu a te ti, abe fi ta ti ase fi nitalim la.>>
10Ate Naawen ayen, <<Mi a nyeka nɔiyeŋ ale fu. Fi nuruma meena niŋ mi ale nye ka wakinkagla ŋaai ale kan nye tɛŋ kaai po tɛŋzuk de a nya la. Nuru baai po ate fi bo la ale nya tuin dii ate mi, Naawen ale nye a te fu la. 11Ni nye tuewomma a te dii ate mi a weeni ni jinla de la. Mi ale yiak Amori ale Keenan ale Yit ale Perizzi ale Yivi ale Jebus demma a basi a te ni. 12Ni be kpesi nidek ate ni kan nye nɔiyeŋ ale baai ale bo tɛŋ kaai po ate ni a cheŋ ka po la, ni dan nye dila ba le chim baruk a bo ni po. 13Ni kpiti ba kuŋkuŋtaŋa a ŋɔriŋ ba tintain weleŋsaŋa a che ba Asera dawoŋtaŋa a lɔnsi. 14Ni kan puusi wen yona ale Naawen, waai yuei ale ka a Anyuri la, ka nyuri dɛka Wen.
15<<Ni kpesi nidek ate ni kan nye nɔiyeŋ ale baai ale bo tɛŋka po la, diila ba dan pai badek a te ba wenaŋa ase taabuksa la, a kaab ŋa, ba le wi ni ate ni dɛ ba kaabka ŋandiintaŋa. 16Ase nama a dan lueri ba liema gela ase pooba la a te ni nidoabilisaŋa ate ba lie bala a pai badek a te ba wenaŋa ase taabuksa la, ba le sak ni nidoabilisaŋa ka dila degadega.
17<<Ni kan nyaliŋ ŋanta a mɛ bɔgta a te ni dega.
18<<Ni a ŋɔbi Boroborok Kuui Ate Dabinta Ka Ku Po La Tigini. Daa ŋayopɔi ni a dɛ boroborok kuui ale kan ta dabinta la ase mi ale weeni ni diila. Ni nye kude diipo ate mi a dak Abib chiika po la ale ka chiik kala ate ni basi Ejipiti tɛŋka.
19<<Ba le dɛ niŋ a biak baai meena la ka mi ale soa a gum chaab ale duŋsaŋa ale dɛ niŋ a biak ŋandoa tiila, ŋa dan poom chim niiga yaase piisa. 20Pai pabiik a da tuesi boniŋ ale liŋ biak kaai la, alege fi dan kan da tuesi ka, wɛ ka ŋinni. Ni da tuesi biik kaai meena ate ba liŋ biak ni bisaŋa po la. Ni waai a kan jam mi jigi ale nisim koruta.
21<<Daa ŋayuebi ni pai a tom tuima, alege daa ŋayopɔiwa danni ni vuusi. Ku dan poom ka kpari wen yaase cheka wen ku a fɛ ate ni vuusi.
22<<Ni dɛ Bakoa Tigini ale ŋandiin tii ale dɛ niŋ ka a bɛ la ale Tigsi Tajoka Tigini benni kpeglimka po. 23Buta meena benni po ni nidoama a magsi ba jam Nyɔnɔwa waai ale ka Naawen niŋ, dii ale ka Izirali Wenni la. 24Mi ale yiak tɛŋsa a basi te ni abe m basi ate ni tɛŋka a lagri, ate waai a kan vari ni tɛŋka ase nama a nin jueli buta meena benni po Naawen ni Wenni niŋ.
25<<Fi kan pai zi buui ate fi pai nye kaabka la a gum chaab ale jabuui ate dabinta a boro la a te mi, abe fi kan basi ate Gaambasika Tigini kaabka ŋantaŋa a tali paari saluiwa.
26<<Ta ŋandiin tii ale dɛ niŋ a bɛ fi kaduksaŋa po la a jam Naawen fi Wenni yenni po. Be kan dik bu poali ku ma biisim po.>>
27Ate Naawen a weeni Moosis ayen, <<Ŋmarisi wieŋa de, a ta va wieŋa de zuk mi nyeka nɔiyeŋ ale fi ale Izirali demma.>> 28Moosis a jam boka dula ale Naawen a paari daa pisinaansi ale yokta pisinaansi wa an dɛ ŋandiinta wa abe nyu nyiamoa. Wa yaa jam ŋmarisi tintain paglaksaŋa zuk nɔiyeŋka wieŋa, Wie Piika.
29Ase Moosis ale nyini Sinai Guuku zuk a siŋ ale tintain paglaksa siyewa wa nisaŋa po la, wa jam zɛ ayen wa nimbidiaka a jam a nyaksi wa ale jam biisi ale Naawen la nyiŋŋa. 30Ase Aaron ale Izirali demma meena ale jam nya ale Moosis nimbidiaka a nyaksi la, ba yaa yɔgsa ale ba le ba cheŋ a moata wa. 31Alege Moosis yaa wi ba, ate Aaron ale Izirali naakuuni niŋdeerɔma meena a jam wa jigi ate wa biisi ale ba. 32Dila ŋaaŋnyiŋ Izirali demma meena yaa jam moata wa, ate wa yaa te ba wieŋa meena ate Naawen a jam te wa Sinai Guuku zuk la.
33Ase Moosis ale ga biisi ale ba a nueri la, wa yaa pai garuk a lik wa nimbidiaka. 34Alege diipo ate wa jo Naawen niŋ ayen wa biisi ale wa la, wa nyiem a lagri garukku kama ate ku paari diipo ate wa nyini peelim la. Ase wa le nyini peelim a weeni Izirali demma wa ale weeni diila, 35ba jam nya ale wa nimbidiaka a nyaksi kama. Ate Moosis a ŋman pai garukku a lik wa nimbidiaka ate ku paari diipo ate wa a jo wa biisi ale Naawen la.

english_text:
Laws for the Sabbath
1Moses called together the people of Israel and told them that the Lord had said:
2 You have six days in which to do your work. But the seventh day must be dedicated to me, your Lord, as a day of rest. Whoever works on the Sabbath will be put to death. 3Don't even build a cooking fire at home on the Sabbath.
Offerings for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 25.1-9; 35.10-19)
4Moses told the people of Israel that the Lord had said:
5I will welcome an offering from anyone who wants to give something. You may bring gold, silver, or bronze; 6blue, purple, or red wool; fine linen; goat hair; 7tanned ram skin or fine leather; acacia wood; 8olive oil for the lamp; sweet-smelling spices for the oil of dedication and for the incense; or 9onyx stones or other gems for the sacred vest and breastpiece.
10If you have any skills, you should use them to help make what I have commanded: 11the sacred tent with its covering and hooks, its framework and crossbars, and its post and stands; 12the sacred chest with its carrying poles, its place of mercy, and the curtain in front of it; 13the table with its carrying poles and all that goes on it, including the sacred bread; 14the lamp with its equipment and oil; 15the incense altar with its carrying poles and sweet-smelling incense; the ordination oil; the curtain for the entrance to the sacred tent; 16the altar for sacrifices with its bronze grating, its carrying poles, and its equipment; the large bronze bowl with its stand; 17the curtains with the posts and stands that go around the courtyard and the curtain at the entrance; 18the pegs and ropes for the tent and the courtyard; 19and the finely woven priestly clothes for Aaron and his sons.
Gifts for the Lord
20Moses finished speaking, and everyone left. 21Then those who wanted to bring gifts to the Lord, brought them to be used for the sacred tent, the worship services, and the priestly clothes. 22Men and women came willingly and gave all kinds of gold jewelry such as pins, earrings, rings, and necklaces. 23Everyone brought their blue, purple, and red wool, their fine linen, and their cloth made of goat hair, as well as their ram skins dyed red and their fine leather. 24Anyone who had silver or bronze or acacia wood brought it as a gift to the Lord.
25The women who were good at weaving cloth brought the blue, purple, and red wool and the fine linen they had made. 26And the women who knew how to make cloth from goat hair were glad to do so.
27The leaders brought different kinds of jewels to be sewn on the special clothes and the breastpiece for the high priest. 28They also brought sweet-smelling spices to be mixed with the incense and olive oil that were for the lamps and for ordaining the priests. 29Moses had told the people what the Lord wanted them to do, and many of them decided to bring their gifts.
Bezalel and Oholiab
(Exodus 31.1-11)
30Moses said to the people of Israel:
The Lord has chosen Bezalel of the Judah tribe. 31-33Not only has the Lord filled him with his Spirit, but he has given him wisdom and made him a skilled craftsman who can create objects of art with gold, silver, bronze, precious stones, and wood. 34The Lord is urging him and Oholiab from the tribe of Dan to teach others. 35And he has given them all kinds of artistic skills, including the ability to design and embroider with blue, purple, and red wool and to weave fine linen.
translation_text:
1Ate Moosis a jam tigsi Izirali naakuuni meena a weeni ba ayen, <<Wieŋa de ate Naawen ayen ni nye. 2Daa ŋayuebi tuima a tom, alege daa ŋayopɔiwa danni a chim dai dii ale ta tuilum, Vuusum dai a te Naawen. Nuru waai a dan tom tuini ku a fɛ ate ba ko wa. 3Ni kan cheem bolim ni boka jiŋŋa Vuusumu danni.>>
4Moosis yaa weeni Izirali naakuuni meena ayen, <<Dii ate Naawen a weeni la ale nna. 5A nyini ŋan baai ate ni ta la po, ni te Naawen. A nyini waai meena suinum po wa abe te Naawen tiiritaŋa de, ligmɔniŋ ale kpana ale kutuk mɔnuŋ ale 6garuk miik sobluk ale garuk miik ŋmiŋmiruk ale garuk miik mɔnuŋ ale gattiak peelik kaai diak ale pagra ate ba nye ale buuk kɔbta la. 7Ale padiak gbana ŋaai ate ba tak ale muni ŋa la ale gbaŋ maŋsa ale siik daata 8ale kpaam a magsi bolimu ale tinaŋsa a magsi naam bobika kpaamu ale ŋanti baai nyum ale masa la. 9Ale tintain ŋaai ale gamisi ale tintain yona ŋaai ale a nyaksi a pai ŋa a maŋ garuk genni ale kuui ale a lik suinummu la nyiŋ.
10<<Baai meena ale seba tuima a bo ni po la a jam nye dii meena ate Naawen a weeni la. 11Viuku ale ku ŋan pilintaŋa ale ŋanyiŋta ale zaŋŋa ale chibsa ale kpana gola. 12Dakanni ale di daataŋa ale biem duisi basika nanlikka ale garuk panni ale a lik di la. 13Jazaanimu ale ku daataŋa ale ku ŋantaŋa meena ale Wen niŋ boroboroku. 14Zeuŋ jazaanimu ale a magsi bolim tɔtika la ale ku ŋantaŋa ale zeuŋku ale kpaam a magsi bolim. 15Kuŋkuŋku ate ba a ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la du ale ku daataŋa ale naam bobika kpaamu ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa la ale garuk panni ale a yik viuku nansuiŋku tuoku nyiŋla. 16Ale kuŋkuŋku ate ba nye juka tiirim du la ale ku kutuk mɔnuŋ ŋoari ale ku daataŋa ale ku jaab meena ate ba ta a tom la ale kutuk mɔnuŋ chin kpienni ale di le a zaani jabuui zuk la. 17Ale dabiaka garuk panni ale daataŋa ale kpana gola ale garuk pali a magsi dabiaka nansuiŋku. 18Ale viuku kpaasaŋa a magsi viuku ale dabiaka ale miisaŋa 19Ale garuk tii ate ba yɔk a magsi ayen ba jo a tom jigi dii ale ta tuilum la, tuilum gattaŋa a magsi Aaron waai ale ka kaabteerɔ la ale garuk tii ale magsi wa nidoabilisaŋa ase ba nin jam a tom ase kaabteerɔba la.>>
20Izirali naakuuni meena yaa ŋmani ale basi Moosis, 21ate waai meena ale a yaali la ale baai ate ku tiri ba suiniima la a yaa jam ta tiirim a jam te Naawen a magsi Tuka Viuku tuimaŋa ale ku tuimaŋa meena tomka ale tuilum gattaŋa. 22Baai meena ale jam a yaali la, nidoaba ale nipooba meena a jam ta ka ligmɔniŋ buuri meena a jam. Ba le jam maa ta ŋan ti baai a jam la ale nna, ŋan baai ate ba a kpi gatta nyiŋ ale tukpana ale nifelima ale baŋsa, ase zak sakka tiirim la a te Naawen. 23Waai meena ale jam ta garuk miik sobluk yaase garuk miik ŋmiŋmiruk yaase garuk miik mɔnuŋ yaase gattiak peelik yaase buuk kɔbta yaase padiak gbana ate ba muni si la yaase gbaŋ maŋsa, ba jam ta ŋa a jam kama. 24Baai ale jam ta kpana yaase kutuk mɔnuŋ a jam la, ba jam pai te ka Naawen ase tiirim la, ate waai mɛ ale jam ta siik daata a magsi tuini la a pai ti a te. 25Nipok meena nisa ale ta tuima la yaa ta wa nisa ale yɔk jabuui la a jam kama. Ŋan bala ale garuk miik sobluk ale garuk miik ŋmiŋmiruk ale garuk miik mɔnuŋ ale gattiak naliŋ. 26Ate nipooma meena baai ale jam a yaali la a seba tuima la a yaa yɔk buuk kɔbta. 27Niŋdeerɔma yaa ta tintain ŋaai ale gamisi ale ŋanta ba chaab jam ayen ba maŋ garuk genni ale suinum jaligimmu nyiŋ. 28Ba jam maa ta ka ŋan baai nyum ale masa ale kpaam a magsi bolim toatika ale naam bobika kpaam ale nyum masik ŋanta juka. 29Izirali nipooma ale nidoama meena baai ale jam a yaali la a yaa ta yaalika tiirita a te Naawen a magsi tuini meena ate Naawen a jam ta va Moosis zuk a weeni ba ayen ba nye la.
30Moosis a jam weeni Izirali demma ayen, <<Nya de, Naawen lueri ka Bezalel Uri biika ate Yur a chim wa ko kpieŋ a nyini Juda dɔkku la 31ale sueri wa ale Wen Chiika ale tuima sebika ale wie miŋka yam a bo nisa tuima meena po la. 32Ate wa baga a pai ligmɔniŋ ale kpana ale kutuk mɔnuŋ a ŋmirisi ŋa a magsi tuima meena po 33wa baga a gebi tintana, wa ale baga a tom daata tuima ale nisa tuima meena. 34Wa jam te ka ba nɔi bayema, wa ale Oyoliab Ayisamak nidoabinni ale nyini Dan dɔkku la ka nyiŋ pagra ayen wa sak nuruba ba chaab. 35Wa jam sueri ba ale ka sebika ayen ba baga a nye nisa tuima meena, a ŋmirisi ŋanta abe ba baali ŋanta ale garuk miik sobluk ale garuk miik ŋmiŋmirita ale garuk miik mɔnuŋ ale garuk pali naliŋ la ale yɔgdɔba, ba meena jam ka baai ale ŋmasi seba nisa ale ŋmirisika tuima nna yegayega.

english_text:
1The Lord has given to Bezalel, Oholiab, and others the skills needed for building a place of worship, and they will follow the Lord's instructions.
2Then Moses brought together these workers who were eager to work, 3and he gave them the gifts that the people of Israel had donated for building the place of worship. In fact, so much was being given each morning, 4that finally everyone stopped working 5and said, “Moses, there is already more than we need for what the Lord has assigned us to do.” 6So Moses sent word for the people to stop giving, and they did. 7But there was already more than enough to do what needed to be done.
The Curtains and Coverings for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 26.1-14)
8-9The skilled workers got together to make the sacred tent and its linen curtains that were woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. Each of the ten panels was twelve meters long and two meters wide, 10and they were sewn together to make two curtains with five panels each. 11-13Then 50 loops of blue cloth were put along one of the wider sides of each curtain, and the two curtains were fastened together at the loops with 50 gold hooks.
14-15As the material for protecting the tent, goat hair was used to weave eleven sections 13 meters by 2 meters each. 16These eleven sections were joined to make two panels, one with five and the other with six sections. 17Fifty loops were put along one of the wider sides of each panel, 18and the two panels were fastened at the loops with 50 bronze hooks. 19Two other coverings were made—one with fine leather and the other with ram skins dyed red.
The Framework for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 26.15-30)
20Acacia wood was used to build the framework for the walls of the sacred tent. 21Each frame was 4 meters high and 66 centimeters wide 22-26with two wooden pegs near the bottom. Then two silver stands were placed under each frame with sockets for the pegs, so they could be joined together. Twenty of these frames were used along the south side and 20 more along the north. 27Six frames were used for the back wall along the west side 28-29with two more at the southwest and northwest corners. These corner frames were joined from top to bottom. 30Altogether, along the back wall there were eight frames with two silver stands under each of them.
31-33Five crossbars were made for each of the wooden frames, with the center crossbar running the full length of the wall. 34The frames and crossbars were covered with gold, and gold rings were attached to the frames to run the crossbars through.
The Inside Curtain for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 26.31-37)
35They made the inside curtain of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. 36They also made four acacia wood posts and covered them with gold. Then gold rings were fastened to the posts, which were set on silver stands.
37For the entrance to the tent, they used a curtain of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with fancy needlework. 38They made five posts, covered them completely with gold, and set each of them on a gold-covered bronze stand. Finally, they attached hooks for the curtain.
translation_text:
1<<Bezalel ale Oyoliab ale nuru waai meena ate Naawen a te wa nisa tuima ale bag nyeka ate wa seba wa le wa tom dii a ta va Wen yenni sɛka la, a magsi ba tom tuini ase ka Naawen ale weeni diila.>>
2Ate Moosis yaa wi Bezalel ale Oyoliab ale waai meena ale seba nisa tuima ate Naawen a te wa bag nyeka ale waai ale a yaali wa jam tom tuini la. 3Ba yaa tuesi tiiritaŋa meena ate Izirali demma a ta jam magsi Naawen yenni tuini la a ta nyini Moosis jigi. Nuruma a jam diem cheesi ka yaalika tiirita saluik meena a ta jam. 4Dila nyiŋla nuru baai ale seba tuima la, baai ale jam a tom Naawen yenni tuini meena la yaa basi ba tuini 5ale weeni Moosis ayen, <<Nuruma a ta jam a gaam tuini ate Naawen a weeni ayen ba nye la kama.>>
6Ate Moosis yaa tom weeni tigsuŋku meena ayen, <<Nidoa yaase nipok a kan ŋman nye wari ase cheesika la a magsi Naawen yenni.>> Ate dila a nye ate nuruma an ŋman ta jaab a jam ya, 7dii nyiŋla ba le poom ta ŋanti baai la a piisi gaam tuini meena tomka kama.
8Baai meena ale seba nisa tuima a bo nuru baai ale tom viuku tuimaŋa ale garuk palaŋa, ale gattiak peelik kaai diak ale pagra la ale garuk miik sobluk ale garuk miik ŋmiŋmiruk ale garuk miik mɔnuŋ ale yɔk ŋanta ase ŋanvuta la a nyo garukku nyiŋ. 9Garuk palaŋa meena a jam soa ase ka chaab la ate ŋa magsika woglimmu a paari anamagib pisinu ale buyuebi ate ŋa labsimu a paari anamagib naaniŋ. 10Wa jam pai ka garuk pala ŋanu a baali a maŋ chaab ale nye nŋala ŋanuwa mɛ dila. 11Wa jam pai garuk pali sobluk a nye ŋanyiŋta garuk panni kpeglimka, dila degadega ate wa jam nye ndila mɛ. 12Wa jam nyeka ŋanyiŋta pisinu garuk yeŋ nyiŋ ale ŋman nye ŋanyiŋta pisinu a basi ndila kpeglimka ate ŋanyiŋtaŋa a tuk chaab. 13Wa jam nyeka ligmɔniŋ ŋanta pisinu a kpi garuk pala buyewa a maŋ chaab ate viuku a chim bunyi.
14Wa jam pai ka buuk kɔbta a nye garuk pala pi ale dinyi a lik viuku. 15Garuk pala pi ale dinyiwa meena a jam a soa ase ka chaab la. Ŋa magsika woglimmu a jam paari ka anamagib pisiyuebi, ate ŋa labsimu a paari naaniŋ. 16Wa jam pai ka garuk pala ŋanu a maŋ chaab ale pai nŋala ŋayuebiwa mɛ a maŋ chaab. 17Wa jam nyeka ŋanyiŋta pisinu a kpi garuk palaŋa kpeglimka ale nye ndila kpeglimka mɛ dila. 18Wa jam nyeka kutuk mɔnuŋ ŋanyiŋta pisinu a tuiri kpi garuk palaŋa kpeglimka a maŋ chaab. 19Wa jam pai ka padiak gbana a mun si a lik viuku ale pai gbaŋ maŋsa a lik ŋmani.
20Wa jam pai ka siik zaŋŋa ŋaai ale teenti la a magsi viuku. 21Zaŋŋi dinyi meena woglimmu a jam paari ka anamagib pisiye ate labsimu a paari anamagib buta 22ale kpaasa ŋaye meena a feri ŋa ate ŋa kan tu chaaba. Wa jam nye viuku zaŋŋa meena ka wayeŋ. 23Wa jam nyeka zaŋŋa pisiye a zaani viuku yeseoku geŋsa 24ale nye kpana gola pisinaansi a chɔgsi ŋa, kpaasa ŋaye meena a magsi zaŋi yeŋ, dinyi a bo goluk yeŋ po. 25Kauk kunkula viuku wiilukku geŋsaŋa wa jam zaani ka zaŋŋa pisiye 26ale kpana gola pisinaansi ate gola ŋaye meena a magsi zaŋi yeŋ. 27Wa jam nye ka zaŋŋa ŋayuebi a zaani viuku yeniŋ geŋsa, 28ale yaali zaŋŋa ŋaye a zaani viuku kpeglimka gugotta tiyewa po. 29Gugotta tiyewa de po, zaŋŋa a jam ka ŋaye a nyini tɛŋ a jueli a paari ŋmani a jo voan yeŋ po. Zaŋŋa buyewa mɛ a jam ka dila. 30Ŋa meena jam ka zaŋŋa naaniŋ ale kpana gola pi ale ŋayuebi ate zaŋi yeŋ a soa gola ŋaye.
31Wa ŋman jam yaali ka siik chibsa. Sinu meena a magsi viuku kauk kunyi zaŋŋa, 32sinu mɛ a bo kauk kunkula, sinu mɛ a vi zaŋŋa ale bo viuku yeniŋka kpeglimka la. 33Wa jam basi ate suŋsuŋka chimmu a vi zaŋŋa zuk a nyini ka kpeglimka a ga paari kpegli kinkala. 34Wa jam pai ka ligmɔniŋ a taari zaŋŋa zuk ale nye ligmɔniŋ baŋsa a su zaŋŋa ate si yik chibsaŋa a ta. Ba ŋman jam pai ka ligmɔniŋ a taari chibsaŋa zuk.
35Ba jam yɔk garuk panni ale ka garuk miik sobluk ale garuk miik ŋmiŋmiruk ale garuk miik mɔnuŋ ale gattiak naliŋ. Ate nuru a yɔk ŋanta ase ŋanvuta la a kali garuk panni nyiŋ. 36Ba jam nye ka siik daata tinaansi a magsi garuk panni ale pai ligmɔniŋ a taari ti. Ba jam nye ka ligmɔniŋ ŋanyiŋta a magsi ti ale nye kpana gola ŋanaansi. 37Nansuiŋku ale a jo viuku po la, wa jam yɔk ka garuk pali ale garuk miik sobluk ale garuk miik ŋmiŋmiruk ale garuk miik mɔnuŋ ale gattiak peelik ate ka diak a pagra la, ate nuru a yɔk garuk panni nyiŋ. 38Ba jam maa nye ka daata tinu ale ŋanyiŋta. Ba jam taari daataŋa ale ŋan bobintaŋa ale ka ligmɔniŋ ale nye gola ŋanuwa ale kutuk mɔnuŋ.

english_text:
The Sacred Chest
(Exodus 25.10-22)
1Bezalel built a chest of acacia wood 110 centimeters long, 66 centimeters wide, and 66 centimeters high. 2He covered it inside and out with pure gold and put a gold edging around the top. 3He made four gold rings and attached one of them to each of the four legs of the chest. 4Then he made two poles of acacia wood, covered them with gold, 5and put them through the rings, so the chest could be carried by the poles.
6The entire lid of the chest, which was made of pure gold, was the place of mercy. 7-9On each of the two ends of the chest he made a winged creature of hammered gold. They faced each other, and their wings covered the place of mercy.
The Table for the Sacred Bread
(Exodus 25.23-30)
10Bezalel built a table of acacia wood 88 centimeters long, 44 centimeters wide, and 66 centimeters high. 11-12He covered it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it with a border 75 millimeters thick. 13He made four gold rings and attached one to each of the legs 14near the edging. The poles for carrying the table were placed through these rings 15and were made of acacia wood covered with gold. 16Everything that was to be set on the table was made of pure gold—the bowls, plates, jars, and cups for wine offerings.
The Lampstand
(Exodus 25.31-40)
17Bezalel made a lampstand of pure gold. The whole lampstand, including its decorative flowers, was made from a single piece of hammered gold, 18with three branches on each of its two sides. 19There were three decorative almond blossoms on each branch 20and four on the stem. 21There was also a blossom where each pair of branches came out from the stem. 22The lampstand, including its branches and decorative flowers, was made from a single piece of hammered pure gold. 23-24The lamp and its equipment, including the tongs and trays, were made of about 35 kilograms of pure gold.
The Altar for Burning Incense
(Exodus 30.1-5)
25For burning incense, Bezalel made an altar of acacia wood. It was 45 centimeters square and 90 centimeters high with each of its four corners sticking up like the horn of a bull. 26He covered it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it. 27Then below the edging on opposite sides he attached two gold rings through which he put the poles for carrying the altar. 28These poles were also made of acacia wood and covered with gold.
The Oil for Dedication and the Incense
(Exodus 30.22-38)
29 Bezalel mixed the sacred oil for dedication and the pure spices for the sweet-smelling incense.
translation_text:
1Bezalel a jam pai ka siik daata a nye nɔiyeŋka dakanni ate di magsika woglimmu a paari anamagib bunu ate labsimu a chim anamagib buta ate ku juelika a paari anamagib buta. 2Wa jam pai ka cheri ligmɔniŋ a taari di ponni po ale di ŋaaŋka meena ale pai ligmɔniŋ a gebiri a gilim di noawaaŋa. 3Wa jam nyeka ligmɔniŋ baŋsa sinaansi a maŋ di gugotta tinaansiwa, baŋsa siye meena a bo ganaŋa. 4Ate wa jam yaali siik daata a pai ligmɔniŋ a taari ti zuk. 5Wa jam pai daataŋa a su baŋsaŋa ale bo dakanni ganaŋa la a magsi yik jika.
6Wa jam nye ka biem duisi basika nanlikka ale cheri ligmɔniŋ. Ka woglimmu a paari anamagib bunu ate labsimu a paari anamagib buta. 7Wa jam pai ka ligmɔniŋ a kuri mɛ ŋanta ase ŋanvuta baye la nanlikka noawaaŋa. 8Wa jam nye ka javuk kunyi a basi noawanni dinyi ale nye wanyi mɛ noawari ndila nyiŋ. Noawaaŋa ŋayewa, wa jam pai ka ligmɔniŋ sandari a nye ba ale nanlikka. 9Ŋanvutaŋa a jam ta ka kinkaŋŋa ate ŋa lagri a ti wen a lik nanlikka. Ŋanvutaŋa a jam za a tuk ka chaab a nya nanlikka geŋsa.
10Wa jam pai ka siik daata a nye jazaanimu. Ku woglimmu a chim anamagib bunaansi ate labsimu a chim anamagib buye ate ku juelika a chim anamagib buta. 11Wa jam pai ka cheri ligmɔniŋ a taari ku ale pai ligmɔniŋka a gebiri gilim ku. 12Wa jam nye ka jagigiluk ate ku labsa ase nitali la a gilim ku a pai ligmɔniŋ a gebiri ku a gilim noawaaŋa. 13Wa jam nye ka ligmɔniŋ baŋsa sinaansi a magsi jazaanimu gugotta tinaansiwa juijui ate naŋsaŋa sinaansiwa jam boro la. 14Baŋsaŋa a jam moata ka noawaaŋa a yik daataŋa ate ba pai a ji jazaanimu la a tara. 15Wa jam pai ka siik daata a nye ti a pai ligmɔniŋ a taari ti, ate ba ta a yik jazaanimu. 16Wa jam pai ka cheri ligmɔniŋ a nye jazaanimu ŋantaŋa, ku taasi tanlaŋsaŋa ale chinaŋa a magsi ŋan baai nyum ale masa la, ale ku taasaŋa ale ku leŋsaŋa ate ba ta a kpiiri daam tiiritaŋa la.
17Wa jam pai cheri ligmɔniŋ a kuri nye zeuŋ jazaanimu kinni ale nyiŋka ale ŋan baai ale nye ase puuta beerisa la ale naŋsaŋa ate ba meena a bo jigi yeŋ. 18Zeuŋku naŋsaŋa a jam chim ka siyuebi, sita a bo kaukku kunyi, sita mɛ a bo kauk kunkula. 19Wa jam nye ka beerisa sita ale jam a niesi almond puuta a bo naŋ kanyi zuk, sita a bo naŋ kinkala zuk, wa jam nyeka dila dek a basi naŋsa siyuebiwa zuk meena ale tom zeuŋ jazaanimu nyiŋla. 20Wa jam nye zeuŋ jazaanimu zuk ka beerisa sinaansi ale a niesi almond puuta la. 21Puuk fiik kunyi ale jam bo naŋsa siyewa ale dɛ niŋ a teeri nyini zeuŋ jazaanimu nyiŋla, ate buyewa po, puuk fiik a bo naŋsa siyewa nyiŋ, ate butawa po, puuk fiik a bo naŋsa sitawa nyiŋ, si meena a jam ka naŋsa siyuebi. 22Puuk fiisaŋa ale naŋsaŋa meena a jam boka jigi yeŋ ale zeuŋ jazaanimu, ka cheri ligmɔniŋ ate ba jam kuri a nye ŋantaŋa de.
23Wa jam pai ka cheri ligmɔniŋ a nye zeuŋta tiyopɔi ale boom ŋangebinta ale taasi tanlaŋ kpiemaŋa. 24Ka cheri ligmɔniŋ dobrim ase boorik yeŋ la ate ba jam pai nye zeuŋ jazaanimu ale ku ŋantaŋa meena.
25Wa jam pai ka siik daata a nye kuŋkuŋ a magsi ŋan baai nyum ale masa la juka. Ku jam ka kuŋkuŋ ŋmɔgluk, ku magsika woglimmu a jam paari ka anamagib buye ate ku labsimu a paari anamagib buye, ku juelika a paari anamagib bunaansi, ku ale ku nyiilaŋa a jam boka jigi yeŋ. 26Wa jam pai ka cheri ligmɔniŋ a taari ku ŋmanni ale ku ganaŋa ale nyiilaŋa ale pai ligmɔniŋ a gebiri gilim ku. 27Wa jam nye ka ligmɔniŋ baŋsa siye a basi ba le gebiri juijui ale ligmɔniŋka la kinni po ate siye a bo gauŋ kunyi meena a yik dawoŋtaŋa ate ba yik a ji la. 28Wa jam nye ka siik dawoŋta a pai ligmɔniŋ a taari ti.
29Ba jam maa nyeka naam bobika tuilum kpaam ale cheri ŋan baai nyum ale masa la. Ka waai ale seba ŋantaŋa de nyeka la ale nye dila.

english_text:
The Altar for Offering Sacrifices
(Exodus 27.1-8)
1Bezalel built an altar of acacia wood for offering sacrifices. It was 2.25 meters square and 1.34 meters high 2with each of its four corners sticking up like the horn of a bull, and it was completely covered with bronze. 3The equipment for the altar was also made of bronze—the pans for the hot ashes, the shovels, the bowls, the meat forks, and the fire pans. 4About halfway up the altar he built a ledge around it and covered the bottom half of the altar with a decorative bronze grating. 5Then he attached a bronze ring beneath the ledge at the four corners to put the poles through. 6He covered two acacia wood poles with bronze and 7put them through the rings for carrying the altar, which was shaped like an open box.
The Large Bronze Bowl
(Exodus 30.18-21)
8 Bezalel made a large bowl and a stand out of bronze from the mirrors of the women who helped at the entrance to the sacred tent.
The Courtyard around the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 27.9-19)
9-17Around the sacred tent Bezalel built a courtyard 44 meters long on the south and north and 22 meters wide on the east and west. He used 20 bronze posts on bronze stands for the south and north and 10 for the west. Then he hung a curtain of fine linen on the posts along each of these three sides by using silver hooks and rods. He placed three bronze posts on each side of the entrance at the east and hung a curtain 6.67 meters wide on each set of posts.
18-19For the entrance to the courtyard, Bezalel made a curtain nine meters long, which he hung on four bronze posts that were set on bronze stands. This curtain was 2.25 meters high, the same height as the one for the rest of the courtyard, and was made of fine linen embroidered and woven with blue, purple, and red wool. He hung the curtain on the four posts, using silver hooks and rods. 20The pegs for the tent and for the curtain around the tent were made of bronze.
The Sacred Tent
21-23Bezalel had worked closely with Oholiab, who was an expert at designing and engraving, and at embroidering blue, purple, and red wool. The two of them completed the work that the Lord had commanded to be done.
Moses put Aaron's son Ithamar in charge of the Levites who kept record of the metals used for the sacred tent. 24According to the official weights, the amount of gold given was a ton, 25 and the silver that was collected when the people were counted came to 3.4 tons. 26 Everyone who was counted paid the required amount, and there was a total of 603,550 men who were 20 years old or older.
27Thirty-four kilograms of the silver were used to make each of the 100 stands for the sacred tent and the curtain. 28The remaining 30 kilograms of silver were used for the hooks and rods and for covering the tops of the posts.
29Two thousand four hundred and twenty-five kilograms of bronze were given. 30And it was used to make the stands for the entrance to the tent, the altar and its grating, the equipment for the altar, 31the stands for the posts that surrounded the courtyard, including those at the entrance to the courtyard, and the pegs for the tent and the courtyard.
translation_text:
1Wa jam pai ka siik daata a nye juka kuŋkuŋ ate ku juelika magsika a chim anamagib buyuebi, ku jam ka kuŋkuŋ ŋmɔgluk ate ku woglimmu magsika a chim anamagib pi, ate ku labsimu magsika mɛ a chim anamagib pi. 2Wa jam nyeka nyiila a basi gugotta tinaansiwa meena po, ate nyiilaŋa ale kuŋkuŋku a chim bunyi, wa jam pai ka kutuk mɔnuŋ a taari kuŋkuŋku. 3Wa jam pai ka kutuk mɔnuŋ a nye ku ŋantaŋa de, ku samɔnsaŋa ale saabulutaŋa ale chin ŋaai ate wa ta a misi la ale duisuk nyinaŋa ate ba ta a yeeri lam la ale bolim chinaŋa. 4Wa jam pai ka kutuk mɔnuŋ a nye jaab ase ŋoari a magsi kuŋkuŋku, kutuk mɔnuŋ ŋanta ale jam bo yeliŋka tɛŋ, kuŋkuŋku suŋsuŋsa po. 5Wa jam nyeka baŋsa ate si yik daataŋa ale bo gugotta tinaansiwa po juijui ate kutuk mɔnuŋ voanaŋa a boro la. 6Wa jam nye ka siik dawoŋta yaa pai kutuk mɔnuŋ a taari ti. 7Wa jam pai dawoŋtaŋa a su ka baŋsaŋa po ate si bo kuŋkuŋku gana a magsi yik jika. Wa jam pai ka tapaga a nye ku ate ku lak.
8Nipok baai ale jam bo Tuka Viuku nansuiŋku nɔi a tom la, nyaasuŋta ate ba jam pai nye ku kutuk mɔnuŋ chin kpienni ale ku kutuk mɔnuŋ jazaanimu.
9Ate wa jam nye dabiaka ale ka garuk palaŋa. Yeseoku geŋka woglimmu magsika a jam ka anamagib kobsiye ale gattiak peelik kaai diak ale pagra 10ale zaŋŋa pisiye ale kutuk mɔnuŋ gola pisiye ale kpana ŋanyiŋta a su yik zaŋŋa nyiŋ. 11Wiilukku geŋsaŋa wa jam nye ka garuk pala ate woglimmu magsika a chim anamagib kobsiye ale ta zaŋŋa pisiye ale kutuk mɔnuŋ gola pisiye ale kpana ŋanyiŋta.
12Yeniŋka geŋsa wa jam nye ka garuk pala ate labsimu magsika a chim anamagib kook, a ta garuk pala ale zaŋŋa pi ale kutuk mɔnuŋ gola pi ale kpana ŋanyiŋta a su yik zaŋŋa nyiŋ. 13Kori geŋka wa jam nye dabiaka labsimu magsika ate ku chim ka anamagib kook. 14Garuk palaŋa magsika woglimmu jam ka anamagib pisita a bo nansuiŋku kauk yeŋ ale zaŋŋa ŋata ale kutuk mɔnuŋ gola ŋata 15ate garuk pala magsika woglimmu ale paari anamagib pisita la mɛ a jam bo kauk kunkula ale a jo dabiaka la po ale zaŋŋa ŋata ale kutuk mɔnuŋ gola ŋata. 16Garuk palaŋa meena ale jam gilim dabiaka la diak a jam pagra kama. 17Golaŋa ale zaŋŋa jam ka kutuk mɔnuŋ. Ŋanyiŋtaŋa ale ŋan bobintaŋa ale bo zaŋŋa nyiŋla jam ka kpana, ate ba pai kpana a taari ŋa zuk. Zaŋŋa meena ale jam bo dabiaka po la, jam ta ka kpana ŋan bobinta.
18Garuk panni ale jam bo dabiaka nansuiŋku la, jam ka garuk miik sobluk ale garuk miik ŋmiŋmiruk ale garuk miik mɔnuŋ ale gattiak naliŋ ate waai ale seba nisa tuima la a yɔk. Di magsika woglimmu jam paarika anamagib pisinaansi, ase dabiaka garuk palaŋa la, ŋala juelika magsika jam ka anamagib pi 19ale zaŋŋa ŋanaansi ale kutuk mɔnuŋ gola ŋanaansi. Ŋa ŋanyiŋtaŋa ale ŋan bobintaŋa jam ka kpana ate ba pai kpanaŋa a taari ŋa zuk. 20Viuku kpaasaŋa meena ale dabiaka gilagilawa jam ka kutuk mɔnuŋ ate ba pai nye.
21Ŋantaŋa de ate ba jam pai nye tuka viuku, Pumpuulima Viuku, wie ŋaai ate Moosis a jam weeni ate Itamar Aaron biika, kaabteerɔwa a basi ate Livaima a ŋmarisi la. 22Bezalel Uri biika ate Yur a chim wa ko kpieŋ a nyini Juda dɔkku la a jam nye dii meena ate Naawen a jam weeni Moosis la kama. 23Waai ale jam gum wa po la ale Oyoliab Ayisamak biika ale nyini Dan dɔkku a peesi ale a ŋmirisi ŋanta ale garuk miik sobluk ale garuk miik ŋmiŋmiruk ale garuk miik mɔnuŋ ale gattiak naliŋ. 24Ligmɔniŋka meena ale nyini zak sakka tiirimu po a magsi Wen yenni tuini meena la jam ka boorisa pisiye ale neok dobrim ale ligbie dobrim kobsa pisiyopɔi ale pisita, magsi chaab ale Wen yenni ale ka diila.
25Kpanaŋa ate ba jam nya nyini baai ale bo naakuuŋa po ate ba jam chiini ba la ka boorisa kook dobrim ale ligbie tusidi ale kobsiyopɔi ale pisiyopɔi ale ŋanu (1,775) dobrim a magsi chaab ale Naawen yenni magsika ale ka diila. 26Nuru yeŋ a te ka ligbie geli dobrim a magsi chaab ale Naawen yenni ale ka diila, a nyini waai meena ale gaam taam gum baai ate ba chiini la po, ate ba bena a paari pisiye yaase ŋa gaam dila la. Ate ba meena nɔi a chim tusa kobsiyuebi ale ŋata ale kobsinu ale pisinu la (603,550). 27Kpana dobrim ase boorisa kook la ate ba jam pai nye kpana gola a magsi Wen dɔkku ale garuk panni, kpana gola kook ale nyini boorisa kook dobrim po, bunyi a magsi goluk kunyi. 28Ba jam pai ligbie tusidi ale kobsiyopɔi ale pisiyopɔi ale ŋanu (1,775) dobrim ayen ba nye ŋanyiŋta ale zaŋŋa ale taari ŋa ŋmanni.
29Kutuk mɔnuŋku ale nyini zak sakka tiirimu po la jam ka boorisa pisiyopɔi dobrim ale ligbie tusa ŋaye ale kobsinaansi (2,400) dobrim. 30Ba jam pai ŋa a nye ka kutuk mɔnuŋ gola tuka viuku nansuiŋku ale kutuk mɔnuŋ kuŋkuŋku ale ku kutuk mɔnuŋ ŋantaŋa meena, 31golaŋa ale bo dabiaka gilagilawa la ale ŋaai ale bo ku nansuiŋku la ale viuku kpaasaŋa ŋaai ale bo ku nansuiŋku la ale viuku kpaasaŋa meena ale ŋaai ale bo dabiaka gilagilawa la.

english_text:
Making the Priestly Clothes
(Exodus 28.1-14)
1Beautiful priestly clothes were made of blue, purple, and red wool for Aaron to wear when he performed his duties in the holy place. This was done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
2-3The entire priestly vest was made of fine linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool. Thin sheets of gold were hammered out and cut into threads that were skillfully woven into the vest. 4-5It had two shoulder straps to support it and a sash that fastened around the waist. 6Onyx stones were placed in gold settings, and each one was engraved with the name of one of Israel's sons. 7Then these were attached to the shoulder straps of the vest, so the Lord would never forget his people. Everything was done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Breastpiece
(Exodus 28.15-30)
8The breastpiece was made with the same materials and designs as the priestly vest. 9It was 22 centimeters square and folded double 10with four rows of three precious stones: A carnelian, a chrysolite, and an emerald were in the first row; 11a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond were in the second row; 12a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst were in the third row; 13and a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper were in the fourth row. They were mounted in a delicate gold setting, 14and on each of them was engraved the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
15-18Two gold rings were attached to the upper front corners of the breastpiece and fastened with two braided gold chains to gold settings on the shoulder straps. 19Two other gold rings were attached to the lower inside corners next to the vest, 20and two more near the bottom of the shoulder straps right above the sash. 21To keep the breastpiece in place, a blue cord was used to tie the two lower rings on the breastpiece to those on the vest. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Clothes for the Priests
(Exodus 28.31-43)
22The priestly robe was made of blue wool 23with an opening in the center for the head. The material around the collar was bound so as to keep it from wearing out. 24-26Along the hem of the robe were woven pomegranates of blue, purple, and red wool with a bell of pure gold between each of them. This robe was to be worn by Aaron when he performed his duties.
27-29Everything that Aaron and his sons wore was made of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, including their robes and turbans, their fancy caps and underwear, and even their sashes that were embroidered with needlework.
30The words “Dedicated to the Lord” were engraved on a narrow strip of pure gold, 31which was fastened to Aaron's turban. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Work Is Completed
(Exodus 35.10-19)
32So the people of Israel finished making everything the Lord had told Moses to make. 33Then they brought it all to Moses: the sacred tent and its equipment, including the hooks, the framework and crossbars, and its posts and stands; 34the covering of tanned ram skins and fine leather; the inside curtain; 35the sacred chest with its carrying poles and the place of mercy; 36the table with all that goes on it, including the sacred bread; 37the lampstand of pure gold, together with its equipment and oil; 38the gold-covered incense altar; the ordination oil and the sweet-smelling incense; the curtain for the entrance to the tent; 39the bronze altar for sacrifices with its bronze grating, its carrying poles, and its equipment; the large bronze bowl with its stand; 40the curtain with its posts and cords, and its pegs and stands that go around the courtyard; everything needed for the sacred tent; 41and the finely woven priestly clothes for Aaron and his sons.
42-43When Moses saw that the people had done everything exactly as the Lord had commanded, he gave them his blessing.
translation_text:
1Ka garuk miik sobluk ale garuk miik ŋmiŋmiruk ale garuk miik mɔnuŋ ate ba pai yɔk garuk woŋ a magsi jigi dii ale ta tuilum la po tomka. Ba jam maa nyeka tuilum gatta a te Aaron, ase Naawen ale jam weeni Moosis diila.
2Ligmɔniŋ ate ba jam pai nye garuk geli ale garuk miik sobluk ale garuk miik ŋmiŋmiruk ale garuk miik mɔnuŋ ale gattiak peelik kaai diak ale pagra la. 3Ba jam pai ka ligmɔniŋ a kuri a nye garuk miik a yaa pai ka a yɔk ale garuk miik sobluk ale garuk miik ŋmiŋmiruk ale garuk miik mɔnuŋ ale gattiak peelik kaai diak ale pagra la, waai ale seba nisa tuima la ale nye dila. 4Ba jam nyeka ŋmankpala ŋaye a te garuk genni ate ŋa maŋ di gugottaŋa tiyewa nyiŋ ate dila ale basi ate di yik wa a magsi. 5Ku chiak gbainni ate ba yɔk di nalimnyiini a magsi ku la a nye ase ka garuk ŋmankpali pasaŋa dek la, a bo garuk ŋmankpali pasaŋa nyiŋ, ba jam yɔk di ale ka ligmɔniŋ ale garuk miik sobluk ale garuk miik ŋmiŋmiruk ale garuk miik mɔnuŋ ale gattiak naliŋ, ase Naawen ale jam weeni Moosis diila.
6Ba jam pai ka tintain ŋaai ale gamisi a maŋ du a ŋmarisi Izirali nidoabilisaŋa yue ŋa nyiŋ. 7Wa yaa jam pai ŋa a maŋ garuk genni nyiŋ ase tintain ŋaai ale ŋa chim teerika a te Izirali nidoabilisaŋa meena, ase Naawen ale jam weeni Moosis diila.
8Wa jam nye ka jabuui ale a lik suinum la, ka waai ale seba yɔkka la ale jam pai ligmɔniŋ ale garuk miik sobluk ale garuk miik ŋmiŋmiruk ale garuk miik mɔnuŋ ale gattiak peelik kaai diak ale pagra la a nye suinum jaligimmu ase garuk genni dek la. 9Suinum jaligimmu jam ka nna ŋmɔgluk ŋmɔglukwa ate ku magsika woglimmu a paari anamagib buye ate ku labsimu a chim anamagib buye a kpamsi buye. 10Ba jam pai ka tintana a dueni vuuta tinaansi ku nyiŋ. Vuuk kuui ale dɛ niŋka la tanaŋa jam ka tintain munta ale tintain ŋaai ale a nye ase dubuulim la ale tintain paata. 11Kuui ale paasaŋ la, ka tintain ŋmiŋmirita ale tintain sobta ale tintain ŋaai ale a nye ase gunungoona la. 12Vuuta titawa po jam ka tintain bibituk ale tintain paasa ale tintain ŋaai ale a nye ase busumbooŋ. 13Vuuk kuui ale saari tinaansiwa la po, jam ka tintain salima ale tintain ŋaai ale gamisi ale tintain mɔnta. Ba jam pai ka ligmɔniŋ a nye a pai ŋa a su. 14Ŋa jam ka tintana pi ale ŋaye, dinyi meena zuk jam ka Izirali nidoabilisaŋa wanyi wanyi meena yuei ale jam ŋmarisi du, dinyi meena zuk ba jam ŋmarisi ka Izirali buuni wanyi wanyi yuei a dueni du.
15Suinum jaligimmu ba jam pai ka cheri ligmɔniŋ a nye chɔrima ase miik la. 16Ba jam nye ka ligmɔniŋ miisa siye ale ligmɔniŋ baŋsa siye a tuiri maŋ suinum jaligimmu ŋmankpalaŋa. 17Ba jam pai ka ligmɔniŋ chɔrima ŋayewa a tuiri baŋsaŋa ale bo suinummu jaligimmu gugottaŋa po la. 18Ba jam basi ate chɔrimaŋa ŋayewa kpeglimka ale a su vie ŋayewa po la, a maŋ chaab garuk genni ŋmankpalaŋa niŋka. 19Ba jam nye ka ligmɔniŋ baŋsa siye a maŋ nsila siyema ale bo suinum jaligimmu gugottaŋa po a moata garuk genni la. 20Ba jam ŋman nye ka ligmɔniŋ baŋsa siye a pai si a maŋ suinummu jaligimmu tɛŋka garuk genni niŋka, a moata vuurisa siyewa ale tu chaab a bo garuk genni chiak gbainni ŋmai la. 21Ba jam bobi suinum jaligimmu baŋsaŋa a maŋ ka garuk genni baŋsaŋa ale miik sobluk, a tom chaab ale chiak gbainni, ayen suinum jaligimmu a kan cheŋ nyini peelim abe ku ge garuk genni, ase Naawen ale jam weeni Moosis diila.
22Ba nye garuk genni garuk woŋku ale ka garuk pali sobluk. 23Wa jam nyeka voan garuk woŋku suŋsuŋka ate viok a jo ale yɔk ku ŋinni ate ku kan cheeri. 24Ba jam pai ka garuk miik sobluk ale garuk miik ŋmiŋmiruk ale garuk miik mɔnuŋ ale gattiak kaai diak ale pagra a yɔk ŋangilima ase yɔna la a gilim garuk woŋku ate ba yɔk la. 25Ba jam pai ka cheri ligmɔniŋ lɔŋŋa ale ŋan baai ale a nye ase yɔn gigiluta la, a baali yik garukku tɛŋka noawaaŋa. Lɔŋŋa ale jam bo yɔnaŋa suŋsuŋ. 26Lɔŋŋa ale ŋantaŋa ale a nye ase yɔn gigiluta ate ba yɔk a gilim garukku la ba le jo ku a tom kama, ase Naawen ale jam weeni Moosis diila.
27Aaron ale wa nidoabilisaŋa ka baai ale seba ŋanta yɔkka la ale jam pai gattiak kaai diak ale pagra la a yɔk garuk woŋ peelita. 28Ba pai gattiak kaai diak ale pagra la a nye zutɔk ale ka noaŋa garuk panni ale tɛŋ gattaŋa. 29Ba jam pai ka gattiak kaai diak ale pagra la ale garuk miik sobluk ale garuk miik ŋmiŋmiruk ale garuk miik mɔnuŋ, a nye garuk pali dii ale a bobi chiaka la. Waai ale seba yɔkka la ale nye dila, ase Naawen ale jam weeni Moosis diila.
30Ba jam pai ka cheri ligmɔniŋ a nye jatanlaŋ, tuilum zutɔk ate ba ŋmarisi ka zuk ayen, <<Ta tuilum a te Naawen.>> 31Ate ba yaa pai miik sobluk a bobi jatanlaŋka a maŋ zutɔkka, ase Naawen ale jam weeni Moosis diila.
32Ba jam tom viuku ale Tuka Viuku tuimaŋa meena a nueri. Izirali demma a jam nye wari meena kama ase dii dek ate Naawen a jam weeni Moosis la. 33Ba jam ta viuku a jam te Moosis. Viuku ale ku jaab meena ŋanyiŋtaŋa ale zaŋŋa ale chibsaŋa ale golaŋa 34ale padiak gbana ate ba mun si la ale gbaŋ maŋsa ale garuk pali dii ale a lik ŋmani la. 35Nɔiyeŋka dakanni ale di dawoŋta ale biem duisi basika nanlikka 36ale jazaanimu ale ku ŋantaŋa meena ale boroboroku ate ba ta a jam Naawen niŋ la. 37Cheri ligmɔniŋ jazaanimu ale zeuŋtaŋa ale ku ŋantaŋa meena ale kpaamu a magsi bolimu tɔtika la 38ale ligmɔniŋ kuŋkuŋku ale naam bobika kpaamu ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa la a magsi juka ale garuk panni ale a lik viuku nansuiŋku nɔi la, 39ale kutuk mɔnuŋ kuŋkuŋku ale kutuk mɔnuŋ kuui ale yik yeliŋka la ale ku dawoŋtaŋa ale ku ŋan baai meena ate ba ta a tom ku tuimaŋa la ale chin kpienni ale di jazaanimu 40ale garuk palaŋa ale a lik dabiaka po la ale zaŋŋa ale kutuk mɔnuŋ golaŋa ale garuk panni ale a lik dabiaka nansuiŋku la. Dabiaka miisaŋa ale kpaasaŋa ale ŋan baai meena ate ba ta a tom tuima viuku ale Tuka Viuku po la. 41Ale garuk tii ate ba yɔk a magsi ayen ba jo a tom jigi dii ale ta tuilum la, tuilum gattaŋa a magsi Aaron waai ale ka kaabteerɔ la ale garuk tii ale magsi wa nidoabilisaŋa ase ba nin jam a tom ase kaabteerɔba la.
42Izirali demma a jam tom tuini meena ka dii dek ate Naawen a jam weeni Moosis la. 43Moosis yaa jam kpesi nya tuini ate ba tom la, ku jam ka dii dek ate Naawen a jam weeni la. Dila nyiŋ Moosis a yaa niak ba.

english_text:
The Lord's Tent Is Set Up
1The Lord said to Moses:
2Set up my tent on the first day of the year 3and put the chest with the Ten Commandments behind the inside curtain. 4Bring in the table and set on it those things that are made for it. Also bring in the lampstand and attach the lamps to it. 5Then place the gold altar of incense in front of the sacred chest and hang a curtain at the entrance to the tent. 6Set the altar for burning sacrifices in front of the entrance to my tent. 7Put the large bronze bowl between the tent and the altar and fill the bowl with water. 8Surround the tent and the altar with the wall of curtains and hang the curtain that was made for the entrance.
9Use the sacred olive oil to dedicate to me the tent and everything in it. 10Do the same thing with the altar for offering sacrifices and its equipment 11and with the bowl and its stand. 12Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent and tell them to wash themselves. 13Dress Aaron in the priestly clothes, then use the sacred olive oil to ordain him and dedicate him to me as my priest. 14Put the priestly robes on Aaron's sons 15and ordain them in the same way, so they and their descendants will always be my priests.
16Moses followed the Lord's instructions. 17And on the first day of the first month of the second year, the sacred tent was set up. 18The posts, stands, and framework were put in place, 19then the two layers of coverings were hung over them. 20The stones with the Ten Commandments written on them were stored in the sacred chest, the place of mercy was put on top of it, and the carrying poles were attached. 21The chest was brought into the tent and set behind the curtain in the most holy place. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
22The table for the sacred bread was put along the north wall of the holy place, 23after which the bread was set on the table. 24The lampstand was put along the south wall, 25then the lamps were attached to it there in the presence of the Lord. 26The gold incense altar was set up in front of the curtain, 27and sweet-smelling incense was burned on it. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
28The curtain was hung at the entrance to the sacred tent. 29Then the altar for offering sacrifices was put in front of the tent, and animal sacrifices and gifts of grain were offered there. 30The large bronze bowl was placed between the altar and the entrance to the tent. It was filled with water, 31then Moses and Aaron, together with Aaron's sons, washed their hands and feet. 32In fact, they washed each time before entering the tent or offering sacrifices at the altar. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
33Finally, Moses had the curtains hung around the courtyard and at the entrance.
The Glory of the Lord
34 Suddenly the sacred tent was covered by a thick cloud and filled with the glory of the Lord. 35And so, Moses could not enter the tent. 36Whenever the cloud moved from the tent, the people would break camp and follow; 37then they would set up camp and stay there, until it moved again. 38No matter where the people traveled, the Lord was with them. Each day his cloud was over the tent, and each night a fire could be seen in the cloud.
translation_text:
1Ate Naawen a jam weeni Moosis ayen, 2<<Ti viuku a zaani, Tuka Viuku chiik kaai ale dɛ niŋka la piilimka danni. 3Pai nɔiyeŋka dakanni a zaani du a pai garuk pali a yik a kasi dakanni. 4Ta jazaanimu a jo a pai jaab meena ale magsi ku bo ku zuk la a zaan du. Yaa ta zeuŋ jazaanimu a jo a zaani a magsi. 5Pai ligmɔniŋ kuŋkuŋku ate ba a ju nyum masik du la a zaani nɔiyeŋka dakanni niŋ a pai garuk panni a yik viuku nansuiŋku nɔi.
6<<Pai kuŋkuŋku ate ba nye juka tiirimu du la a zaani viuku nansuiŋku niŋka, Tuka Viuku. 7Pai chin kpienni a zaani Tuka Viuku ale kuŋkuŋku suŋsuŋ a ŋari nyiam a nyoro. 8Nye dabiaka a gilim ku, a pai garuk panni a yik dabiaka nansuiŋku nɔi.
9<<Pai naam bobika kpaamu a nyo viuku ale ku ŋantaŋa meena nyiŋ. Nye ate ku ŋantaŋa meena a gaari a ta tuilum. 10Yaa pai bobika kpaamu a nyo kuŋkuŋku ate ba a nye juka tiiritaŋa du la ale ku ŋantaŋa meena nyiŋ a gaari kuŋkuŋku ate ku ŋmasi ta tuilum. 11Pai bobika kpaamu a nyo chin kpienni nyiŋ ale di jazaanimu nyiŋ ate ba ta tuilum.
12<<Ta Aaron ale wa nidoabilisaŋa a jam tuka viuku nansuiŋku nɔi a so ba ale nyiam. 13Pai tuilum gattaŋa a jo Aaron, pai naam bobika kpaamu a nyo wa zuk a gaari wa ate wa tom a te mi ase kaabteerɔ la. 14Ta wa nidoabilisaŋa a jam a pai garuk tii ate ba yɔk la a jo ba. 15Pai naam bobika kpaam a kpiiri ba zuimaŋa zuk ase fi ale jam bobi ba kowa diila ate ba mɛ a tom a te mi ase kaabteerɔba la. Kpaammu ate fi kpiiri ba zuk ase kaabteerɔba la, ale kasim bo ba jigi ka dila a ta ga paari ŋaaŋ bi sii meena ale cheen la.>> 16Moosis a jam nye wari meena ase ka dii dek ate Naawen a jam weeni wa la.
17Dila nyiŋ viuku ba jam ti ku ka chiik kaai ale dɛ niŋka la piilimka dai bena ŋayewa po. 18Moosis ale jam ti viuku la, wa jam nyeka kpana gola a zaani zaŋŋa a pai chibsaŋa a vi du. 19Ate wa yaa pili viuku ase Naawen ale jam weeni wa diila.
20Wa yaa pai tintain paglaksa ate wieŋa a boro la a nyo dakanni po ale pai dawoŋtaŋa a su dakanni nyiŋ a pai biem duisi basika nanlikka a lik du. 21Wa yaa ta nɔiyeŋka dakanni a jam viuku po a pai garuk panni ate ba ta a yik a kasi dakanni ate wanni a boro la ase Naawen ale jam weeni Moosis diila.
22Moosis yaa pai jazaanimu a zaani tuka viuku po ku wiilukku geŋsa garuk panni peelim 23a pai boroboroku a vi ku zuk Naawen niŋ, ase Naawen ale jam weeni wa diila.
24Wa jam pai zeuŋ jazaanimu a zaani ka Tuka Viuku po jazaanimu nakpiak viuku yeseoku geŋsa 25a gomsi zeuŋtaŋa a magsi Naawen niŋ, ase Naawen ale jam weeni wa diila.
26Moosis a jam pai ligmɔniŋ kuŋkuŋku a zaani ka Tuka Viuku po garuk panni niŋ 27ale ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la ku zuk, ase Naawen ale jam weeni wa diila. 28Ate wa yaa pai garuk panni a yik viuku nansuiŋku nɔi.
29Wa jam pai kuŋkuŋku ate ba a nye juka tiirimu du la a zaani moata ka viuku nansuiŋku tuka viuku ale la, a yaa nye juka ale ŋandiinta tiirita ku zuk, ase Naawen ale jam weeni wa diila.
30Wa jam pai chin kpienni a zaan ka Tuka Viuku ale kuŋkuŋku suŋsuŋ a nyo nyiam du a magsi sugrika, 31ate Moosis ale Aaron ale wa nidoabilisaŋa a pai bu a sugri ba nisaŋa ale ba naŋsaŋa. 32Ba nyiem sugri kama diipo ate ba a jo Tuka Viuku po yaase ba torisi a kpaŋ kuŋkuŋku la, ase Naawen ale jam weeni Moosis diila.
33Moosis yaa pai ŋantaŋa a ti dabiaka a gilim viuku ale kuŋkuŋku meena a yaa pai garuk panni a yik dabiaka nɔi. Moosis yaa nueri tuimaŋa.
34Ate chiŋmari a jam lik Tuka Viuku ate Naawen zulaŋa a sueri viuku. 35Moosis an jam baga a jo Tuka Viuku po, dii nyiŋla chiŋmanni a jam bo ka ku zuk ate Naawen zulaŋa a sueri viuku.
36Izirali demma nyeerimu meena po, diipo meena ate chiŋmanni a dan ga zagri ale basi viuku ba nyiem yaa basi dula ale cheŋ. 37Alege chiŋmanni a dan kan zagri ya, ba mɛ a kan cheŋ, ate ku paari dai dii dai ate di a zagri la. 38Naawen chiŋmanni a jam bo viuku zuk ka dila danni po, ate bolim a bo chiŋmanni po yokku, kude jam a nye kama Izirali demma nimbie po ba nyeerimu po meena.

english_text:
1-3The Lord spoke to Moses from the sacred tent and gave him instructions for the community of Israel to follow when they offered sacrifices.
Sacrifices To Please the Lord
The Lord said:
Sacrifices to please me must be completely burned on the bronze altar.
Bulls or rams or goats are the animals to be used for these sacrifices. If the animal is a bull, it must not have anything wrong with it. Lead it to the entrance of the sacred tent, and I will let you know if it is acceptable to me. 4Lay your hand on its head, and I will accept the animal as a sacrifice for taking away your sins.
5After the bull is killed in my presence, some priests from Aaron's family will offer its blood to me by splattering it against the four sides of the altar.
6Skin the bull and cut it up, 7while the priests pile wood on the altar fire to make it start blazing. 8-9Wash the bull's insides and hind legs, so the priests can lay them on the altar with the head, the fat, and the rest of the animal. A priest will then send all of it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
10If you sacrifice a ram or a goat, it must not have anything wrong with it. 11Lead the animal to the north side of the altar, where it is to be killed in my presence. Then some of the priests will splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
12-13Cut up the animal and wash its insides and hind legs. A priest will put these parts on the altar with the head, the fat, and the rest of the animal. Then he will send all of it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
14If you offer a bird for this kind of sacrifice, it must be a dove or a pigeon. 15A priest will take the bird to the bronze altar, where he will wring its neck and put its head on the fire. Then he will drain out its blood on one side of the altar, 16remove the bird's craw with what is in it, and throw them on the ash heap at the east side of the altar. 17Finally, he will take the bird by its wings, tear it partially open, and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_text:
1Naawen yaa bo Tuka Viuku po a wi Moosis a biisi ale wa. Wa yaa weeni wa ayen, 2<<Weeni Izirali demma ayen, ni waai a dan ta tiirim a cheen ni te Naawen, ni yeeri duŋ niiŋa po yaase piisaŋa ale buaŋa po.
3<<Juka tiirimu a dan ka naab buui ate ni a ju bu meena la tiirim ni yeeri lalik koluk kuui ale kan ta jomi ya. Wa ta jam te tuka jigini nansuiŋku ate Naawen a siak tuesi wa. 4Wa pai nisa a vi juka tiirim duŋ kaai ate ba le ju meena la zukku ate Naawen a siak a nye biem duisi basika a te wa. 5Wa yaa tɔgri lalik koluku Naawen niŋ ate Aaron nidoabilisaŋa, kaabteerɔma a tuk ziimu a boori basi kutuk kuŋkuŋku zuk kabtaŋa meena Tuka Viuku nansuiŋku. 6Wa yaa puli juka tiirim duŋka a boani ka. 7Kaabteerɔwa Aaron nidoabilisaŋa ale pai bolim a vi juka kutukku kuŋkuŋku zuk a yaa pai daata a vi du. 8Aaron nidoabilisaŋa kaabteerɔma ale pai lantaŋa ale zukku ale kpapalaŋa a vi daataŋa zuk. 9Wa yaa sugri duŋka ponni po ŋantaŋa meena ale naŋsaŋa. Kaabteerɔwa a yaa ju ba meena kuŋkuŋku zuk. Ka meena juka tiirim buui ale a ju ale bolim la. Nyummu abe masa kama a te Naawen.
10<<Tiirimu a dan ka tiirim buui ate ni le ju bu meena la wa lueri piisaŋa po, yaase booŋa po, jaduok kuui ale kan ta jomi la. 11Wa tɔgri duŋka juka kutukku kuŋkuŋku wiiluk geŋka Naawen niŋ, ate Aaron nidoabilisaŋa kaabteerɔma a pai ziimu boori basi juka kuŋkuŋku kabtaŋa meena. 12Wa boani duŋka a gebi zukku ale kpapalaŋa tɔgatɔga ate kaabteerɔwa a gomsi bu vi daataŋa zuk tii ale a dɛ kuŋkuŋku zuk la. 13Wa sugri duŋka ponni po ŋantaŋa ale naŋsaŋa ale nyiam. Ate kaabteerɔma yaa pai ba meena a ju juka kuŋkuŋku zuk. Bu ka meena juka tiirim, ba te ale ka bolim, buui nyum ale masa a te Naawen la.
14<<Tiirimu a dan ka kiŋkaŋŋa ŋanta ate wa yaa ayen wa ju bu meena te Naawen, wa pai nangbaŋ yaase kawuruk. 15Kaabteerɔwa yaa ta nangbaŋka yaase kawuruku jam juka kuŋkuŋku zuk, a ŋmeeni zukku a gebi a ju juka kuŋkuŋku zuk. Wa basi ate ka ziimu a nyini a nyo juka kuŋkuŋku zuk. 16Abe wa yaa yeeri fɔnni meena a pai yuk basi juka kuŋkuŋku kori geŋka, ate tintuemu doa la. 17Wa yaa mobi ka a lagri kiŋkaŋŋa. Wa kan lagri meena. Kaabteerɔwa le juka kuŋkuŋku zuk. Bu ka meena juka tiirim, ba te ale ka bolim, buui nyum ale masa a te Naawen.

english_text:
Sacrifices To Give Thanks to the Lord
The Lord said:
1When you offer sacrifices to give thanks to me, you must use only your finest flour. Put it in a dish, sprinkle olive oil and incense on the flour, 2and take it to the priests from Aaron's family. One of them will scoop up the incense together with a handful of the flour and oil. Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, the priest will lay this part on the bronze altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. 3The rest of this sacrifice is for the priests; it is very holy because it was offered to me.
4If you bake bread in an oven for this sacrifice, use only your finest flour, but without any yeast. You may make the flour into a loaf mixed with olive oil, or you may make it into thin wafers and brush them with oil.
5If you cook bread in a shallow pan for this sacrifice, use only your finest flour. Mix it with olive oil, but do not use any yeast. 6Then break the bread into small pieces and sprinkle them with oil. 7If you cook your bread in a pan with a lid on it, you must also use the finest flour mixed with oil.
8You may prepare sacrifices to give thanks in any of these three ways. Bring your sacrifice to a priest, and he will take it to the bronze altar. 9Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, the priest will lay part of it on the altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. 10The rest of this sacrifice is for the priests; it is very holy because it was offered to me.
11Yeast and honey must never be burned on the altar, so don't ever mix either of these in a grain sacrifice. 12You may offer either of them separately, when you present the first part of your harvest to me, but they must never be burned on the altar.
13Salt is offered when you make an agreement with me, so sprinkle salt on these sacrifices.
14Freshly cut grain, either roasted or coarsely ground, must be used when you offer the first part of your grain harvest. 15You must mix in some olive oil and put incense on top, because this is a grain sacrifice. 16A priest will sprinkle all of the incense and some of the grain and oil on the altar and send them up in smoke to show that the whole offering belongs to me.
translation_text:
1<<Nuru waai a dan ta ŋandiinta tiirim a jam wa te Naawen, wa ta zom buui ale nala a jam. Wa kpiiri kpaam a nyoro abe wa pai ŋan baai ate ba dan ju ba, ba nyummu masa la a nyoro. 2A yaa ta cheŋ Aaron nidoabilisaŋa kaabteerɔma jigi. Ate bala wanyi ale nye zom naliŋka ale kpaam ale ŋan baai nyummu ale masa la meena nisa nɔi a ju ase teerika juka la kuŋkuŋku zuk. Ka meena juka tiirim buui nyum ale masa a te Naawen. 3Ŋandiin tii ale a tali la ka Aaron ale wa bisaŋa nyiini ale a dɛ. Bu ka tiirim buui ale ŋmasi ta tuilum tiiritaŋa meena po a te Naawen.
4<<Fi dan ta ŋandiinta tii ale se la tiirim a jam ayen fi te Naawen, zommu a magsi bu nala kama. Nye maasa ŋaai ale kan ta dabinta abe kpaam a dam du yaase boroborok kuui ale kan ta dabinta abe kpaam sa ku. 5Fi dan a labri tiirim ŋandiinta taasi tanlaŋ po zom naliŋ, buui ale kan ta dabinta ate kpaam a gum du. 6Gariŋ abe fi kpiiri kpaam a nyo du. Ka tiirim ŋandiinta. 7Ase fi tiirim ŋandiintaŋa a daa ti dik kutuk binbili po, be nye ale zom naliŋ ale kpaam. 8Ta fi ŋandiinta tiirimu ate fi pai ŋantaŋa de a dik la a jam Naawen niŋ. Pai te kaabteerɔwa ate wa ta cheŋ juka kuŋkuŋku ate ba a ju ŋantaŋa la jigini. 9Kaabteerɔwa yaa le nye zommu a ju jaamu zuk ale bolim a te mu ate ku sak ayen Nyɔnɔwa ale soa. Ku ka tiirim buui nyum ale masa a te Naawen. 10Ŋandiin tii ale a tali la ka Aaron ale wa bisaŋa nyiini ale a dɛ. Bu ka tiirim buui ale ŋmasi ta tuilum tiiritaŋa meena po a te Naawen.
11<<Ŋandiin tii meena ate ni ta cheena ayen ni te Naawen la, ni kan nyo dabinta du, dii nyiŋla ku kan magsi ayen ni nyo dabinta ale siita du a ju ale bolim a te Naawen. 12Ni baga ta ba jam a te Naawen ase kpari ŋandiin tii ate ni liŋ a te wa la, alege ni kan pai ju kuŋkuŋku zuk ase nyum masik ŋanta la. 13Ni pai yesa a nyo ni ŋandiinta tiirimu po, dii nyiŋla yesa a sak kama ayen Naawen ale nye nɔiyeŋ ale ni a beni. Ni kan basi yesaŋa diila ni a nye ka nɔiyeŋ ale Wen. Dila la ni pai yesa a nyo tiirimu po.
14<<Ni le dɛ niŋ a pai kpari ŋan baai a te Naawen, ni sɛ ba yaa gariŋ. 15Ni pai kpaam ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa la a nyo du. Ka ŋandiinta tiirim. 16Kaabteerɔwa yaa nye ŋan baai ale gariŋ la gela ale kpaamu gela ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa la meena a ju ale bolim a te Naawen. Ku a sak kama ayen mi ale soa.

english_text:
Sacrifices To Ask the Lord's Blessing
The Lord said:
1When you offer sacrifices to ask my blessing, you may offer either a bull or a cow, but there must be nothing wrong with the animal. 2Lead it to the entrance of the sacred tent, lay your hand on its head, and have it killed there. A priest from Aaron's family will splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
3Offer all of the fat on the animal's insides, 4as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. 5Some of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me, together with the sacrifice that is offered to please me.
6Instead of a bull or a cow, you may offer any sheep or goat that has nothing wrong with it. 7If you offer a sheep, you must present it to me at the entrance to the sacred tent. 8Lay your hand on its head and have it killed there. A priest will then splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
9Offer the fat on the tail, the tailbone, and the insides, 10as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. 11One of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke as a food offering for me.
12If you offer a goat, you must also present it to me 13at the entrance to the sacred tent. Lay your hand on its head and have it killed there. A priest will then splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
14Offer all of the fat on the animal's insides, 15as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. 16One of the priests will put these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke as a food offering with a smell that pleases me.
All fat belongs to me. 17So you and your descendants must never eat any fat or any blood, not even in the privacy of your own homes. This law will never change.
