A nye biem duisi basika a te Livaima. 13Basi ate Livaima a zaani Aaron ale wa nidoabilisaŋa niŋ a pai ba ase zak sakka tiirim la a te Naawen. 14Suiku de po fi ale gaari Livaima ka ba tɔga a ta nyini Izirali dem mbala po ate ba chim mi nuruba.
15<<Ase fi le nye ate Livaima a nye cheri, ale pai ba a te ase zak sakka tiirim la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, ba a magsi ba jam a tom ba tuimaŋa ka Tuka Viuku po. 16Bala ale Izirali demma baai ale ba pai badek meena a te mi la. Mi a pai ba ase ka m dek nuruba la ate ba tagri za ba le dɛ niŋ a biak baai la naŋkula po, Izirali nipooma ale dɛ niŋ a biak nidoabili sii la. 17Jaduok meena ate ba dɛ niŋ biak Izirali po la, ka nurubiik yaase duŋ ka mi ale soa. Ase m daam le ko ba le dɛ niŋka a biak baai Ejipiti po la, mi jam gaari ba a te ka m dek. 18Mi abe pai Livaima ate ba tagri za ka Izirali demma ale dɛ niŋ a biak nidoabili sii la meena naŋkula po. 19Izirali demma meena po, mi pai Livaima ase ka tiirim la a te Aaron ale wa nidoabilisaŋa ayen ba a tom Tuka Viuku po a te Izirali demma abe ba nye biem duisi basika ate nyiŋtuila a kan yik Izirali demma ase ba nin cheŋ moata Wen yenni.>>
20Moosis ale Aaron ale Izirali naakuuni meena a jam nye ale Livaima ka dii dek ate Naawen a jam weeni Moosis la. 21Livaima a jam nye badek ka cheri ale sugri ba gattaŋa. Aaron a jam pai ba ase ka zak sakka tiirim la a te Naawen ale nye biem duisi basika a te ba ayen ba nala. 22Kula ŋaaŋnyiŋ, Livaima a yaa jam ba tom ba tuimaŋa Tuka Viuku po, ka Aaron ale wa nidoabilisaŋa ale jam a nya ba zuk ate ba a tom. Ba jam a nye ale Livaima ase ka Naawen ale jam weeni Moosis diila.
23Naawen a jam weeni Moosis ayen, 24<<Kude a cheŋ ka Livaima jigi. Nidoama ale paari bena pisiye ale ŋanu yaase ba gaam di la, a jam maa tom tuimaŋa Tuka Viuku po, 25alege baai a dan paari bena pisinu, ku a fɛ kama ate ba basi ba le a tom veruveruk la abe ba kuli a ga vuusi, ba kan ŋman tom tuini. 26Ba diem baga a maari ba suataŋa kama ate ba a tom ba tuimaŋa Tuka Viuku po, alege badek ku a fɛ ate ba kan ŋman tom tuini. Kude ale magsi ni nye ate Livaima a seba ba tuimaŋa ale ka diila>>.

english_text:
Regulations for Celebrating Passover
1 During the first month of Israel's second year in the Sinai Desert, the Lord had told Moses 2to say to the people, “Celebrate Passover 3in the evening of the fourteenth day of this month and do it by following all the regulations.” 4-5Moses told the people what the Lord had said, and they celebrated Passover there in the desert in the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month.
6Some people in Israel's camp had touched a dead body and had become unfit to worship the Lord, and they could not celebrate Passover. But they asked Moses and Aaron, 7“Even though we have touched a dead body, why can't we celebrate Passover and offer sacrifices to the Lord at the same time as everyone else?”
8Moses said, “Wait here while I go into the sacred tent and find out what the Lord says about this.”
9The Lord then told Moses 10to say to the community of Israel:
If any of you or your descendants touch a dead body and become unfit to worship me, or if you are away on a long journey, you may still celebrate Passover. 11But it must be done in the second month, in the evening of the fourteenth day. Eat the Passover lamb with thin bread and bitter herbs, 12 and don't leave any of it until morning or break any of the animal's bones. Be sure to follow these regulations.
13But if any of you are fit to worship me, and yet refuse to celebrate Passover when you are not away on a journey, you will no longer belong to my people. You will be punished because you did not offer sacrifices to me at the proper time.
14Anyone, including foreigners who live among you, can celebrate Passover, if they follow all the regulations.
The Cloud over the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 40.34-38)
15-16As soon as the sacred tent was set up, a thick cloud appeared and covered it. The cloud was there each day, and during the night, a fire could be seen in it. 17-19The Lord used this cloud to tell the Israelites when to move their camp and where to set it up again. As long as the cloud covered the tent, the Israelites did not break camp. But when the cloud moved, they followed it, and wherever it stopped, they camped and stayed there, 20-22whether it was only one night, a few days, a month, or even a year. As long as the cloud remained over the tent, the Israelites stayed where they were. But when the cloud moved, so did the Israelites. 23They obeyed the Lord's commands and went wherever he directed Moses.
translation_text:
1Naawen a jam biisi ale Moosis Sinai Gɔi Kosikka po chiik kaai ale dɛ niŋka la bena ŋayewa po ate ba jam basi Ejipiti tɛŋka la ŋaaŋnyiŋ. Wa jam weeni ayen, 2<<Basi ate Izirali demma a dɛ Gaambasika Tigini diipo ale magsi la. 3Ni de di diipo ale magsi la junɔi chiika de daa pi ale ŋanaansiwa danni a ta va di ŋmarisika ale di buusaŋa ale ka diila.>>
4Dila nyiŋ Moosis yaa jam weeni Izirali demma ayen ba dɛ Gaambasika Tigini, 5ate ba nye dila Sinai Gɔi Kosikka po junɔi chiik kaai ale piilim la, ka daa pi ale ŋanaansiwa danni. Izirali demma a jam nye ka dii meena ate Naawen a jam weeni Moosis la.
6Alege ba gela an jam bag a dɛ Gaambasika Tigini dai dila danni, dii nyiŋla ba jam taŋ ka badek ale kpio. Ba yaa jam Moosis ale Aaron jigi dai dila danni 7a weeni Moosis ayen, <<Tama a taŋ kama dii nyiŋla ti tiri ka kpio, alege ka boa ale a kasi tama ate ti an baga a te Naawen ti tiirimu ale Izirali dem mbala diipo ale magsi la?>>
8Moosis yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<Ni limisi ate m bek Naawen a wom wa le ta dii wa weeni ni la.>>
9Ate Naawen a jam weeni Moosis ayen, 10<<Weeni Izirali demma ayen, <Ase ni wanyi yaase ni ŋaaŋbisa a dan daŋ badek ba le tiri kpio la nyiŋ, yaase ba bo nyeerim po, ba diem baga dɛ Naawen Gaambasika Tigini kama. 11Ba magsi ba dɛ tigini ka daa pi ale ŋanaansiwa danni chiisa siyewa po junɔi. Ba a magsi ba ŋɔbi pabiika a gum chaab ale ŋandiin tii ate ba an nyo dabinta du la ale tinaŋ tuasa. 12Ku a fɛ ate ba kan tali lammu ate vari veenti bu yaase ba ŋɔbi ka kobaŋa. Ase ba daa dɛ Gaambasika Tigini, ku a fɛ ate ba va ŋmarisika meena. 13Alege nuru waai a dan nala, ale an bo nyeerim po, a zɛri an dɛ Gaambasika Tigini, kula nyɔnɔwa ku a fɛ ate ba yiak wa, wa nuruma po a basi dii nyiŋla wa an te Naawen tiirim diipo ale magsi la. Nuru wala ale nya wa biemu tutuna.
14<< <Nichaanɔ a dan bo ni po a yaali wa dɛ Naawen Gaambasika Tigini, ku a fɛ ate wa mɛ a nye dila a ta va di ŋmarisika ale di buusaŋa ale ka diila. Ku a fɛ ate ni ta ŋmarisi yena a te nicham ale tɛŋ bisaŋa.> >>
15Dai dii danni ate viuku, viuku kuui ate Naawen wanni a boro ate ba jam ti ku la, chiŋmari ale jam lik ku. A nyini junɔi a ta ga paari saluik, chiŋmanni a jam bo viuku zuk ase ka bolim la. 16Ku le jam ka dii a tom du a cheŋ la ale la. Chiŋmanni a jam lik ku kama, tɛŋka a dan sobiri di a nya ase ka bolim la. 17Diipo meena ate chiŋmanni a zagri ale a ge viuku la, Izirali demma a basi dula kama. Diipo ate chiŋmanni a zaani la, Izirali demma mɛ a kali ka dula. 18Naawen a nyiem le biisi ate Izirali demma a cheŋ, wa dan ŋman weeni ayen ba zaani ba nyiem a bo ka dula. Chiŋmanni ale bo viuku zuk a beni diila, ba a bo ka dula. 19Ase chiŋmanni a dan bo viuku zuk ate ku beni, Izirali demma a nyiem siak a te Naawen wanni kama a kan cheŋŋi. 20Dai dii dai chiŋmanni a bo viuku zuk ka daa maga, ate Naawen a dan biisi, ba wari bo dula jigini, ate wa dan ŋman biisi ayen ba cheŋ, ba yaa basi dula ale cheŋ. 21Dai dii dai chiŋmanni a boro a nyini ka junɔi a ga paari saluik, ase di dan ga zagri saluiku ba a basi dula kama. Ku dan poom ka kantueŋ yaase yok, chiŋmanni a dan ga zagri ba a cheŋ kama. 22Chiŋmanni a dan bo viuku zuk a paari daa ŋaye yaase chiik yaase ben, Izirali demma a bo ka dula ba kan cheŋ, alege di dan zagri, ba a cheŋ kama. 23Naawen a dan biisi, ba nyiem tigsi a bo ka jigi yeŋ, ate wa nyiem ŋman biisi ate ba basi dula ale cheŋ. Ba jam a wom Naawen wanni kama, a ta va wa wanni ate wa jam biisi a ta va Moosis zuk la.

english_text:
The Silver Trumpets
1The Lord told Moses:
2Have someone make two trumpets out of hammered silver. These will be used to call the people together and to give the signal for moving your camp. 3If both trumpets are blown, everyone is to meet with you at the entrance to the sacred tent. 4But if just one is blown, only the twelve tribal leaders need to come together.
5-6Give a signal on a trumpet when it is time to break camp. The first blast will be the signal for the tribes camped on the east side, and the second blast will be the signal for those on the south. 7But when you want everyone to come together, sound a different signal on the trumpet. 8The priests of Aaron's family will be the ones to blow the trumpets, and this law will never change.
9Whenever you go into battle against an enemy attacking your land, give a warning signal on the trumpets. Then I, the Lord, will hear it and rescue you. 10During the celebration of the New Moon Festival and other religious festivals, sound the trumpets while you offer sacrifices. This will be a reminder that I am the Lord your God.
The Israelites Begin Their Journey
11On the twentieth day of the second month of that same year, the cloud over the sacred tent moved on. 12So the Israelites broke camp and left the Sinai Desert. And some time later, the cloud stopped in the Paran Desert. 13This was the first time the Lord had told Moses to command the people of Israel to move on.
14Judah and the tribes that camped alongside it marched out first, carrying their banner. Nahshon son of Amminadab was the leader of the Judah tribe, 15Nethanel son of Zuar was the leader of the Issachar tribe, 16and Eliab son of Helon was the leader of the Zebulun tribe.
17The sacred tent had been taken down, and the Gershonites and the Merarites carried it, marching behind the Judah camp.
18Reuben and the tribes that camped alongside it marched out second, carrying their banner. Elizur son of Shedeur was the leader of the Reuben tribe, 19Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was the leader of the Simeon tribe, 20and Eliasaph son of Deuel was the leader of the Gad tribe.
21Next were the Kohathites, carrying the objects for the sacred tent, which was to be set up before they arrived at the new camp.
22Ephraim and the tribes that camped alongside it marched next, carrying their banner. Elishama son of Ammihud was the leader of the Ephraim tribe, 23Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was the leader of the Manasseh tribe, 24and Abidan son of Gideoni was the leader of the Benjamin tribe.
25Dan and the tribes that camped alongside it were to protect the Israelites against an attack from behind, and so they marched last, carrying their banner. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was the leader of the tribe of Dan, 26Pagiel son of Ochran was the leader of the Asher tribe, 27and Ahira son of Enan was the leader of the Naphtali tribe.
28This was the order in which the Israelites marched each time they moved their camp.
29Hobab the Midianite, the father-in-law of Moses, was there. And Moses said to him, “We're leaving for the place the Lord has promised us. He has said that all will go well for us. So come along, and we will make sure that all goes well for you.”
30“No, I won't go,” Hobab answered. “I'm returning home to be with my own people.”
31“Please go with us!” Moses said. “You can be our guide because you know the places to camp in the desert. 32Besides that, if you go, we will give you a share of the good things the Lord gives us.”
33The people of Israel began their journey from Mount Sinai. They traveled three days, and the Levites who carried the sacred chest led the way, so the Lord could show them where to camp. 34And the cloud always stayed with them.
35 Each day as the Israelites began their journey, Moses would pray, “Our Lord, defeat your enemies and make them run!” 36And when they stopped to set up camp, he would pray, “Our Lord, stay close to Israel's thousands and thousands of people.”
translation_text:
1Naawen a yaa weeni Moosis ayen, 2<<Kuri kpana a nye damunsa siye a ta peeri a wi naakuuni ate ba a jam jigi yeŋ. 3Ase siyewa a dan peeri, naakuuni meena ale tigsi fi niŋ Tuka Viuku nansuiŋku nɔi. 4Ase kanyi dekki a dan kum, niŋdeerɔma ale yezuimaŋa nyam a yaa le tigsi fi niŋ. 5Ase damuniŋka a dan kumu, diin ŋaai ale bo kori geŋsa la a yaa le nyini a cheŋ. 6Damuniŋka a dan kum saari buye, baai ale bo yeseoku geŋsa la mɛ ale nyini. Damuniŋka kumsaŋa ale ku sak ayen ku magsika ba nyini a cheŋ. 7Ate fi tigsi tigsuŋku la, peeri damunsaŋa, alege si kumsaŋa a chim ku tɔga ale nyinika kumsaŋa.
8<<Kaabteerɔwa Aaron nidoabilisaŋa ale magsi ba peeri damunsaŋa. Kude ale chim ka ŋmarisi kaai ale ka beni a te fi ale fi gaŋsaŋa. 9Ase nama a dan cheŋ ni nye kpaliŋ nidek tɛŋka po ale ni dachiak waai ale a namsi ni la, ni peeri ni damunsaŋa. Naawen ni Wenni ale teeri ni wari a vari ni ni dachaasaŋa nisa po a basi. 10Ate diipo ate ni mariŋ nidek a dɛ Chiik Paalika tigini la, ni yaa peeri damunsaŋa a basi ni juka ale ni suiyɔgni tiiritaŋa zuk ate ku la chim teerika a te ni, ni Wen niŋ. Mi ale Naawen ni Wenni.>>
11Daa pisiyewa danni chiisa siyewa, bena ŋayewa po, chiŋmanni a yaa basi viuku ate Naawen Wanni a boro la. 12Ate Izirali demma a yaa basi Sinai Gɔnni a taam dɛ, a ga dɛ ate ku ga paari diipo ate chiŋmanni a ga bo Paran Gɔnni zuk la. 13Ba yaa jam piilim nyini a cheŋ ase Naawen ale jam weeni Moosis la.
14Juda nidoabilisaŋa tiktiwa a va chaab ale ba tugurik tommu yueŋa ale dɛ niŋ a nyini, ate Amminadab nidoabinni Naason, a nya tommu zuk. 15Zuar nidoabinni Netanel ale jam chim Isaka dɔkku niŋdeerɔ, 16alege ate Yelon nidoabinni Eliab a chim Zebulun dɔkku niŋdeerɔ. 17Ate Livaima yaa kpiti viuku, ate Gerson ale Merari kabini a ji nyini a cheŋ.
18Aruben dɔkku ale jam pai a saŋ ale ba tiktiwa a ta va ba ale ka diila. Ka Sedeur nidoabinni Elizur ale jam dɛ ba niŋ. 19Zurisaddai nidoabinni Selumiel ale jam dɛ Simeyon dɔkku niŋ, 20alege ate Deuel nidoabinni Eliasaf a chim Gad dɔkku niŋdeerɔ. 21Koyat kabini a yaa nyini a ji ŋan weleŋsaŋa. Viuku a jam magsi ka ku ti alege jigi ate ba paari du.
22Ɛfraim dɔkku ale jam pai saŋ ale ba tiktiwa a ta va ba ale ka diila. Ka Ammiyud nidoabinni Elisama ale jam dɛ ba niŋ. 23Pedazur nidoabinni Gamaliil ale jam dɛ Manasa dɔkku niŋ, 24alege ate Abidan nidoabinni Abidan a jam dɛ Benjamin dɔkku niŋ.
25Kpeglimka po ase baai ale jam potim a nya labika zuk la, ka Dan dɔkku ale jam wari ŋaaŋ a nyini ale ba tikti wa a ta va ba mɛ ale ka diila. Ammisaddai nidoabinni Ayiezer ale jam dɛ ba mɛ niŋ. 26Okran nidoabinni Pagiel ale jam a nya Asɛ dɔkku zuk, 27alege ate Enan nidoabinni Ayira a nya Nafitali dɔkku zuk. 28Izirali demma ale jam labi dii a cheŋ la ale la.
29Moosis yaa weeni Areuel nidoabinni Yobab, Midian denɔwa, wa ŋachobwa ayen, <<Ti a yaali ti nyini cheŋ ka juijui ate Naawen a weeni ayen, <M le pai dula a te ni la.> Cheŋ ale ti, tama ale nye fu a magsi, Naawen a puulim ka wamaŋsa ale Izirali demma.>>
30Alege ate wa tulisi ayen, <<Aaya, m kan cheŋŋi. Mi a yaa m ŋman kuli ka m dek tɛŋka ale m nuruma jigi.>>
31Alege Moosis a weeni ayen, <<Jenje kan basi ti. Fi seba kauk kuui ale magsi ti tigsi gɔnni de po la kama, fi a baga a chim tama nina kama. 32Fi a dan cheŋ ale ti, tama ale chari ale fu jamaŋ kaai ate Naawen a te tama la.>>
33Ate ba yaa basi Naawen guuku ale nyini cheŋ daa ŋata meena. Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni ale jam dɛ ba niŋ daa ŋatawa meena po a gisi jigi a te ba ayen ba vuusi. 34Naawen chiŋmanni a nyiem le dɛ ba niŋ danni meena po ase ba nin nyini ba cheŋ.
35Diipo meena nɔiyeŋka dakanni a dan ga nyini, Moosis nyiem jam weeni kama ayen, <<M Naawen, yiti zaani, ate fi dachaasaŋa a waaŋ chaab. Fi dachaasaŋa a chali bɛ fi niŋ.>>
36Ase di dan jam zaani, wa nyiem weeni kama ayen, <<Ŋman jam m Naawen Izirali demma baai ale kan ta chiina la jigi.>>

english_text:
The Israelites Complain
1One day the Israelites started complaining about their troubles. The Lord heard them and became so angry that he destroyed the outer edges of their camp with fire.
2When the people begged Moses to help, he prayed, and the fire went out. 3They named the place “Burning,” because in his anger the Lord had set their camp on fire.
The People Grumble about Being Hungry
4One day some foreigners among the Israelites became greedy for food, and even the Israelites themselves began moaning, “We don't have any meat! 5In Egypt we could eat all the fish we wanted, and there were cucumbers, melons, all kinds of onions, and garlic. 6But we're starving out here, and the only food we have is this manna.”
7 The manna was like small whitish seeds 8-9 and tasted like something baked with sweet olive oil. It appeared at night with the dew. In the morning the people would collect the manna, grind or crush it into flour, then boil it and make it into thin wafers.
10The Israelites stood around their tents complaining. Moses heard them and was upset that they had made the Lord angry. 11He prayed:
I am your servant, Lord, so why are you doing this to me? What have I done to deserve this? You've made me responsible for all these people, 12but they're not my children. You told me to nurse them along and to carry them to the land you promised their ancestors. 13They keep whining for meat, but where can I get meat for them? 14This job is too much for me. How can I take care of all these people by myself? 15If this is the way you're going to treat me, just kill me now and end my miserable life!
Seventy Leaders Are Chosen To Help Moses
16The Lord said to Moses:
Choose 70 of Israel's respected leaders and go with them to the sacred tent. 17While I am talking with you there, I will give them some of your authority, so they can share responsibility for my people. You will no longer have to care for them by yourself.
18As for the Israelites, I have heard them complaining about not having meat and about being better off in Egypt. So tell them to make themselves acceptable to me, because tomorrow they will have meat. 19-20In fact, they will have meat day after day for a whole month—not just a few days, or even 10 or 20. They turned against me and wanted to go back to Egypt. Now they will eat meat until they get sick of it.
21Moses replied, “At least 600,000 grown men are here with me. How can you say there will be enough meat to feed them and their families for a whole month? 22Even if we butchered all our sheep and cattle, or caught every fish in the sea, we wouldn't have enough to feed them.”
23The Lord answered, “I can do anything! Watch and you'll see my words come true.”
24Moses told the people what the Lord had said. Then he chose 70 respected leaders and went with them to the sacred tent. While the leaders stood in a circle around the tent, Moses went inside, 25and the Lord spoke with him. Then the Lord took some authority from Moses and gave it to the 70 leaders. And when the Lord's Spirit took control of them, they started shouting like prophets. But they did it only this one time.
26Eldad and Medad were two leaders who had not gone to the tent. But when the Spirit took control of them, they began shouting like prophets right there in camp. 27A boy ran to Moses and told him about Eldad and Medad.
28Joshua was there helping Moses, as he had done since he was young. And he said to Moses, “Sir, you must stop them!”
29But Moses replied, “Are you concerned what this might do to me? I wish the Lord would give his Spirit to all his people so everyone could be a prophet.” 30Then Moses and the 70 leaders went back to camp.
The Lord Sends Quails
31Some time later the Lord sent a strong wind that blew quails in from the sea until Israel's camp was completely surrounded with birds, piled up about a meter high for many kilometers in every direction. 32The people picked up quails for two days—each person filled at least ten large baskets. Then they spread them out to dry. 33But before the meat could be eaten, the Lord became angry and sent a deadly disease through the camp.
34After they had buried the people who had been so greedy for meat, they called the place “Graves for the Greedy.”
35Israel then broke camp and traveled to Hazeroth.
translation_text:
1Nuruma a yaa jam fɔbili a ta va wapagra ŋaai ate ba bo ŋa po la Naawen tue po, ase wa le ga wom ba la, wa sui yaa puuri. Ate bolim a nyini Naawen jigi a dɛ ba alege a kaasi ba boka jigini nakpiaka gela. 2Ase nuruma ale jam kum te Moosis la, wa yaa puusi a te Naawen ate bolimu a kpi. 3Ba jam a wi dula jigini ayen ka Tabera, dii nyiŋla bolimu ale nyini Naawen jigi a dɛ ba.
4Nicham baai ale jam va ba a nyini Ejipiti la, kɔrisa a yaa jam bo ŋandiin yonta jigi, ate Izirali demma a ŋman piilim kum a weeni ayen, <<Ase ti dan poom taka lam a ŋɔbi, 5tama a teeri jumaŋa ate ti jam bo Ejipiti a ŋɔbi ale kan tuni ŋa nyiŋla kama, ti jam maari a dɛ yɔna tɔgatɔga mɛ ale alabasa ale galik kama. 6Alege yɔgyɔgla de ti jɔk koarisila kama. Tama an ŋman nya jaaboa ka Nyɔnɔwa ŋandiintaŋa nyiini.>>
7Naawen ŋandiintaŋa a jam a nye ase ka ŋan bie fiisa la alege a mak. 8Nuruma a yaa cheŋ gilim a pisi ŋa, a num ŋa niri po yaase ba gariŋ tuik po. Ba jam dik ŋa ka samɔniŋ po yaase ba nye maasa. Ŋa jam a ŋɔbi ka nna ase kpaam ale bo ŋa po la. 9Ase maglim a dan ga lo ba boka jigini yok, Naawen ŋandiintaŋa mɛ nyiem lo kama.
10Moosis a yaa wom ale dɔkdem meena nuruba a bo ba viuk nɔi a kum. Ate Naawen sui yaa ŋmasi puuri nna yegayega, ate ku daani Moosis. 11Ate wa bek Naawen ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi a ta daanika dɛ a jam fi yɔmawa jigi ya? Ka boa ate mi nye a kaasi fi, ate fi pai nuruma de daanika a seeri mi? 12Ka mi puuka po ate nuruma de meena a nyini? Ka mi ale biak ba? Ka boa ate fi weeni ayen mi ta ba m nigoruk po ase buluek ma ale ta wa biluak diila, a cheŋ tɛŋ kaai po ate fi puulim ale ba kokpieŋsaŋa la? 13Ka bɛ ate mi ale nya lam a te nuruma de meena? Ba kasim a kum a te mu kama ayen, <Te ti lam ate ti ŋɔbi. 14Mi a kan baga a ta nuruma de meena m dega, wanni a ŋmasi pagra a gaam mu kama. 15Fi a daa fi nye mi kan nnala, be ko mu yɔgyɔgla de ase ku nin yɔk fi sui. Kan basi ate mi kpi mi dek kummoa.>>
16Naawen a yaa weeni Moosis ayen, <<Ta Izirali demma nisɔm pisiyopɔi baai ate fi seba ayen ba ka niŋdeerɔba ale kpaga nuruma po la a jam te mu. Basi ate ba jam Tuka Viuku po a zaani ale fu. 17M le siŋ jam biisi ale fu dula jigini, mi ale pai Chiik kaai ale bo fi po la, a nyo ba po. Ba le maari fu ate fi baga a nya nuruma zuk, dii le ku basi ate ku kan chim fi nyiini wari ya.
18<<Weeni nuruma ayen, <Ni gomsi nidek a magsi chum, ale ni a ni ŋɔbi ka lam, Naawen a wom ni kama diipo ate ni kum ayen, ase tama a dan poom ta ka lam a ŋɔbi, ti jam zunchoŋ kama diipo ate ti jam bo Ejipiti po la. Yɔgyɔgla de Naawen ale te ni lam ate ni ŋɔbi. 19Ni kan ŋɔbi ti ka dai yeŋ yaase daa ŋaye yaase daa ŋanu yaase daa pi yaase daa pisiye nyiini, 20alege ni le ŋɔbi a paari ka chiik pumi ate ti va ni nyueŋa nyini dii nyiŋla ni zɛri Naawen dii ale bo ale ni la kama a kum wa niŋ a weeni ayen, ka boa ate tama a basi Ejipiti tɛŋka?> >>
21Alege Moosis a weeni ayen, <<Dela mi bo ka nidoaba tusa kobsiyuebi (600,000) po a cheŋ naŋta, ate fi weeni ayen, <Mi ale te ba lam ate ba ŋɔbi chiika meena.> 22Ba le nya yega ase ba nin poom tɔgri duŋsa a te ba? Ba le chagi ase ba nin yik jumaŋa meena nyakpiemu po a te ba?>>
23Naawen a yaa tulisi Moosis ayen, <<Naawen nisaŋa a ŋmasi gela kama? Fi yaa le nya ase m le weeni diila ale nye wensie a te fu ya.>>
24Moosis yaa nyini peelim a weeni nuruma dii ate Naawen a weeni la. Wa yaa ta ba niŋdeerɔba pisiyopɔi a jam jigi yeŋ a gilim Viuku. 25Ate Naawen a yaa siŋ jam chiŋmanni po a biisi ale wa ale pai Chiik kaai ale bo wa po la a nyo niŋdeerɔba pisiyopɔiwa po. Ase Chiika ale jo ba po la, ba yaa biisi Naawen wie, ba an ŋman biisi dila diipo diipo.
26Alege nuruba baye, ba yue jam le Eldad ale Medad ale jam tali bo ba boka jigini. Ba jam chiini ba a gum nisɔmma po kama alege ba an jam nyini cheŋ Viuku po. Alege Chiika a diem jam bo ba po kama ate ba biisi Naawen wie. 27Nuru paalik a yaa chali cheŋ Moosis jigi a ga weeni ayen, <<Eldad ale Medad a biisi ka Wen wie ba boka jigini.>>
28Nun nidoabinni Josua waai ale jam a maari Moosis wa paalimu po la, a yaa biisi ayen, <<Moosis m nyɔnɔwa, kasi ba!>>
29Alege Moosis yaa tulisi ayen, <<Fi a dɛka nyuri mi nyiŋŋa? Mi a yaali ayen Naawen nuruma meena ate ka biisiteerɔba ate Naawen a pai wa Chiika a nyo ba po.>> 30Ate Moosis ale Izirali nisɔmma a yaa ŋman cheŋ ba boka jigini.
31Viok a yaa nyini Naawen jigi a ta yeŋsa nyini nyakpiemu geŋsa a jam te ba. Ku ta jam gilim ba boka jigini meena kama ate si vi chaab a jueli paari duna a yalima ase danni po meena chelim la. 32Dai dila meena ale yok kula ale dai dii ale paasaŋ la meena, nuruma a jam nyini a tigsi ka yeŋsa. Waai an jam tigsi boorisa ate si an paari pi. Ba jam kati si a waaŋ gilim ba boka jigini meena kama. 33Alege lammu ale diem jam bo ba nyinaŋa po la, alege jigi ate ba nɛ bu la, Naawen sui yaa puuri ale nuruma, ate wa yaa basi ate nyiŋtuila a yik ba. 34Dila nyiŋla ba yaa te dula yuei ayen Kibrot Yattaava dii nyiŋla, dula jigini ate ba gu nuru baai ale dɛ ŋandiin yonta la.
35A nyini Kibrot Yattaava nuruma a jam cheŋ ka Yazerot a ga bo dula jigini.

english_text:
Miriam and Aaron Are Jealous of Moses
1-3 Although Moses was the most humble person in all the world, Miriam and Aaron started complaining, “Moses had no right to marry that woman from Ethiopia! Who does he think he is? The Lord has spoken to us, not just to him.”
The Lord heard their complaint 4and told Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to come to the entrance of the sacred tent. 5There the Lord appeared in a cloud and told Aaron and Miriam to come closer. 6Then after commanding them to listen carefully, he said:
“I, the Lord, speak to prophets
in visions and dreams.
7 But my servant Moses
is the leader of my people.
8He sees me face to face,
and everything I say to him
is perfectly clear.
You have no right to criticize
my servant Moses.”
9The Lord became angry with Aaron and Miriam. And after the Lord left 10and the cloud disappeared from over the sacred tent, Miriam's skin turned white with leprosy. When Aaron saw what had happened to her, 11he said to Moses, “Sir, please don't punish us for doing such a foolish thing. 12Don't let Miriam's flesh rot away like a child born dead!”
13Moses prayed, “Lord God, please heal her.”
14 But the Lord replied, “Miriam would be disgraced for seven days if her father had punished her by spitting in her face. So make her stay outside the camp for seven days, before coming back.”
15The people of Israel did not move their camp until Miriam returned seven days later. 16Then they left Hazeroth and set up camp in the Paran Desert.
translation_text:
1Miriam ale Aaron a yaa piilim a biisi Moosis a kaasi Kus tɛŋka liewa ate wa jam faari la nyiŋ. 2Ba bek ayen, <<Naawen a biisi ale ka Moosis nyiini? Wa kan biisi a ta va tama mɛ zuwa?>> Ate Naawen a wom kude.
3Moosis a jam ka nuru waai ale a yik wadek la, wa jam ŋmasi yik wadek a gaam waai meena kama tɛŋzuk de.
4Ate Naawen yaa deri weeni Moosis ale Aaron ale Miriam ayen, <<Ni nyini jam Tuka Viuku po ni nɔi ni tama meena.>> Ate ba nɔi ba tama a yaa nyini. 5Ate Naawen a yaa siŋ jam ba jigi ase chiŋmari la. Wa jam za ka Viuku nansuiŋku nɔi a wi Aaron ale Miriam. Ase ba nɔi bayema ale jam niŋ la. 6Wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni wom mi wieŋa. Ase Naawen biisiteerɔ a dan bo ni po, m te pai m dek sak wa kama, m le biisi ale wa gɔdaasima po. 7Alege kude a daa wensie a ta va mi tomteerɔwa Moosis jigi ya, wa ta siaka ale m yenni meena kama. 8Mi a biisi le wa ka wa nina po nalimnyiini, daa sunsuelima, wa a nya mi ase ka mi ale ka diila. Ka boa ate nama a kan chali yɔgsum ale biisi m tomteerɔwa Moosis a kaasi?>>
9Ate Naawen sui yaa puuri ale ba ate wa basi ba.
10Ase chiŋmanni ale basi Viuku la, Miriam yaa deri za a peenti nna tektek. Aaron a yaa viriŋ tuk wa a nya ale wa nyiŋka a kaasi, 11ate wa weeni Moosis ayen, <<Jenje m nyɔnɔ, kan pai tuni ti, tama le nye betta nyeka a tom biem buui la nyiŋŋa. 12Kan fi basi ate wa nye ase biluak kpiuk ale nyini wa ma popo a nyini ate wa nyiŋka kabta a ka diila.>>
13Dila nyiŋla Moosis yaa kaari a te Naawen ayen, <<Wen yaa, tebi wa.>>
14Ate Naawen a yaa tulisi Moosis ayen, <<Ase wa kowa a dan chesi tuntueta a nyo wa ninaŋa po, wa ti le bo chivie po a paari daa ŋayopɔi. Basi ate wa jam ni boka jigini.>> 15Dila nyiŋ Miriam yaa jam boka peelim a paari daa ŋayopɔi, nuruma an jam ga jigi ya ate ku paari diipo ate ba ta wa ŋman jam la.
16Kula ŋaaŋnyiŋ, nuruma a basi Yazerot kama ale cheŋ ga bo Paran Gɔnni po.

1Naawen a yaa weeni Moosis ayen, 2<<Tom nuruba ate ba ga kpesi nya Keenan tɛŋka, kaai ate mi ale pai te Izirali demma la. A nyini ba ŋiaka dɔkku po tom ku niŋdeerɔma wanyi meena.>>
3Ase Naawen ale weeni la, Moosis yaa tom ba ate ba nyini Paran Gɔnni. Ba meena a jam ka Izirali niŋdeerɔba.
4Ba yueŋa ale nna. A nyini Aruben dɔkku po, ba tom ka Zakkur nidoabili Sammua. 5A nyini Simeyon dɔkku, ba jam tom ka Yori nidoabili Safat. 6A nyini Juda dɔkku, ba jam tom ka Jefunne nidoabili Kaleb. 7A nyini Isaka dɔkku, ba jam tom ka Josefi nidoabili Igal. 8A nyini Ɛfraim dɔkku, ba jam tom ka Nun nidoabili Yoseya. 9A nyini Benjamin dɔkku, ba jam tom ka Arafu nidoabili Palti. 10A nyini Zebulun dɔkku, ba jam tom ka Sodi nidoabili Gaddiel. 11A nyini Josefi dɔkku Manasa, ba jam tom ka Susi nidoabili Gaddi. 12A nyini Dan dɔkku, ba jam tom ka Gemalli nidoabili Ammiel. 13A nyini Asɛ dɔkku, ba jam tom ka Maakil nidoabili Setur. 14A nyini Nafitali dɔkku, ba jam tom ka Vofsi nidoabili Nabi. 15A nyini Gad dɔkku, ba jam tom ka Maki nidoabili Geuel. 16Nuruma de yueŋa ale nna, ate Moosis a jam tom ayen ba ga kpesi nya tɛŋka la. Moosis ale jam tagri Nun nidoabili Yoseya yuenni ale te wa yue ayen Josua.
17Ase Moosis ale tom ba ayen ba ga kpesi nya Keenan tɛŋka la, wa weeni ayen, <<Ni va Negev tɛŋka po ale tɛŋ kaai ate guuta a bo ka po la. 18Ni nya ase tɛŋka a nye ase ka se la, nuru baai ale bo ka po la a ta pagrim yaase ba wobsa kama, ba piisi yaase ba an piisi ya. 19Ba bo ka tɛŋ boan choa po? Ka nala yaase ka lɔrima? Tɛŋ sin chaab po ate ba boro? Ba an se parik a gilim si yaase ba se parik a gilim si? 20Ka tantaŋa ka sɛ? Poosuk a bo ka po yaase poosuk a ka? Tiisa a bo ka po yaase tiisa ka? Ni nye dii ate ni ale baga a ta tɛŋka tiisaŋa yɔnaŋa gela a jam la.>> Ku jam ka diipo ale magsi yɔn fi gilima ŋaai ale dɛ niŋ a muni la.
21Ba yaa jam cheŋ a ga kpesi nya tɛŋka a nyini Zin Gɔnni po a ta ga paari Areyob a tuk Lebo Yamat tɛŋsaŋa nyiŋ. 22Ba yaa va Negev tɛŋka po a jam paari Yebron tɛŋka, kauk kuui ate Anak ŋaaŋbisaŋa Ayiman ale Sesai ale Talmai a boro la. Ba le jam se Yebron la ku paari ka bena ŋayopɔi alege ate ba se Zoan ale bo Ejipiti po la. 23Ase ba le jam paari Eskol Viaka la, ba yaa jam che tiib naŋ ale yɔn fi gilima sagi. Nuruba baye ale jam pai yɔn fi gilima a yik diok nyiŋ a ji ate di bo ba suŋsuŋ ale yɔn kpieŋ gilima ale kiŋkama. 24Ba jaa wi dula ayen ka Eskol Viak dii nyiŋla, Izirali demma ale jam gbesi yɔn fi gilima sagni dula la nyiŋ. 25Ba ale kpesi a nya tɛŋka a nueri daa pisinaansiwa ŋaaŋ nyiŋla, ba yaa ŋman jam.
26Ba yaa ŋman jam Moosis ale Aaron ale Izirali naakuuni ale jam bo Kades, Paran Gɔnni po la jigi. Dula jigini ate ba yaa jam weeni dii ate ba nya la sak Moosis ale Aaron Izirali tigsuŋku meena ale pai tɛŋka yɔnaŋa a sak ba. 27Ba yaa jam weeni Moosis wieŋa de ayen, <<Ti cheŋ tɛŋ kaai ate fi a tom ti la kama, siita ale biisim ale sueri ka po ka yɔnaŋa abe le nna. 28Alege nuru baai ale bo ka po la a pagra kama, ate ba se parik a gilim ka ale ŋmasi zuak mɛ. Ti nya Anak ŋaaŋbisaŋa mɛ ale ba bo dula. 29Amalek demma a bo ka Negev tɛŋka. Yit demma ale Jebus demma ale Amori demma a bo ka guuku zuk tɛŋka, alege ate Keenan demma a jam moata ka nyakpiemu ale sali Jodan Benni la.>>
30Kaleb a yaa basi ate nuruma a nye chorototo Moosis niŋ ale weeni ayen, <<Ti cheŋ a ga tuesi tɛŋka, tama ale baga a nye dila kama.>>
31Alege nuru baai ale va wa cheŋ la a weeni ayen, <<Tama an baga a nye kpaliŋ ale nuru bala. Ba pagra a gaam tama ale ka diila kama.>> 32Ate ba yaa basi ate wanni de a waaŋ paari Izirali demma meena ba le nya dii tɛŋka po la. Ba weeni ayen, <<Tɛŋ kaai ate tama cheŋ ga kpesi nya la, a nɛ baai ale bo ka po la kama. Nuru baai meena ate tama a nya la ka ganduata. 33Ti nya Anak ŋaaŋbisaŋa Nefilim demma mɛ a boka dula. Tama a nye ase ka nanchoŋta la tama dek nina po, ti ka dila a te ba.>>

english_text:
The Israelites Rebel against Moses
1After the Israelites heard the report from the twelve men who had explored Canaan, the people cried all night 2and complained to Moses and Aaron, “We wish we had died in Egypt or somewhere out here in the desert! 3Is the Lord leading us into Canaan, just to have us killed and our women and children captured? We'd be better off in Egypt.” 4Then they said to one another, “Let's choose our own leader and go back.”
5Moses and Aaron bowed down to pray in front of the crowd. 6Joshua and Caleb tore their clothes in sorrow 7and said:
We saw the land ourselves, and it's very good. 8If we obey the Lord, he will surely give us that land rich with milk and honey. 9 So don't rebel. We have no reason to be afraid of the people who live there. The Lord is on our side, and they won't stand a chance against us!
10The crowd threatened to stone Moses and Aaron to death. But just then, the Lord appeared in a cloud at the sacred tent.
Moses Prays for the People
11The Lord said to Moses, “I have done great things for these people, and they still reject me by refusing to believe in my power. 12So they will no longer be my people. I will destroy them, but I will make you the ancestor of a nation even stronger than theirs.”
13-16 Moses replied:
With your mighty power you rescued your people from Egypt, so please don't destroy us here in the desert. If you do, the Egyptians will hear about it and tell the people of Canaan. Those Canaanites already know that we are your people, and that we see you face to face. And they have heard how you lead us with a thick cloud during the day and flaming fire at night. But if you kill us, they will claim it was because you weren't powerful enough to lead us into Canaan as you promised.
17Show us your great power, Lord. You promised 18 that you love to show mercy and kindness. And you said that you are very patient, but that you will punish everyone guilty of doing wrong—not only them but their children and grandchildren as well.
19You are merciful, and you treat people better than they deserve. So please forgive these people, just as you have forgiven them ever since they left Egypt.
20Then the Lord said to Moses:
In answer to your prayer, I do forgive them. 21 But as surely as I live and my power has no limit, 22-23I swear that not one of these Israelites will enter the land I promised to give their ancestors. These people have seen my power in Egypt and in the desert, but they will never see Canaan. They have disobeyed and tested me too many times.
24 But my servant Caleb isn't like the others. So because he has faith in me, I will allow him to cross into Canaan, and his descendants will settle there.
25Now listen, Moses! The Amalekites and the Canaanites live in the valleys of Canaan. And tomorrow, you'll need to turn around and head back into the desert toward the Red Sea.
The Israelites Are Punished for Complaining
26The Lord told Moses and Aaron 27-28to give this message to the people of Israel:
You sinful people have complained against me too many times! Now I swear by my own life that I will give you exactly what you wanted. 29 You will die right here in the desert, and your dead bodies will cover the ground. You have insulted me, and none of you men who are over 20 years old 30will enter the land that I solemnly promised to give you as your own—only Caleb and Joshua will go in.
31You were worried that your own children would be captured. But I, the Lord, will let them enter the land you have rejected. 32You will die here in the desert! 33 Your children will wander around in this desert 40 years, suffering because of your sins, until all of you are dead. 34I will punish you severely every day for the next 40 years—one year for each day that the land was explored. 35You sinful people who ganged up against me will die here in the desert.
36Ten of the men sent to explore the land had brought back bad news and had made the people complain against the Lord. 37So he sent a deadly disease that killed those men, 38but he let Joshua and Caleb live.
The Israelites Fail To Enter Canaan
(Deuteronomy 1.41-45)
39The people of Israel were very sad after Moses gave them the Lord's message. 40So they got up early the next morning and got ready to head toward the hill country of Canaan. They said, “We were wrong to complain about the Lord. Let's go into the land that he promised us.”
41But Moses replied, “You're disobeying the Lord! Your plan won't work, 42-43so don't even try it. The Lord refuses to help you, because you turned your backs on him. The Amalekites and the Canaanites are your enemies, and they will attack and defeat you.”
44But the Israelites ignored Moses and marched toward the hill country, even though the sacred chest and Moses did not go with them. 45The Amalekites and the Canaanites came down from the hill country, defeated the Israelites, and chased them as far as the town of Hormah.
translation_text:
1Yok kula naakuuni nuruma meena a yaa kaari nna bɔgbɔg. 2Izirali demma meena a yaa fɔbili te Moosis ale Aaron, ate tigsuŋku a weeni ba ayen, <<Ti dan poom kpi Ejipiti tɛŋka yaase gɔnni po a zunchoŋŋa. 3Ka boa ate Naawen a ta ti jam tɛŋka de po ayen ba tɔgri ti? Ti pooma ale ti bisaŋa ale chim ka ŋan koaliŋta. Ku kan zunchoŋŋa ase ti ale ŋman cheŋ Ejipiti tɛŋka?>> 4Ate ba yaa weeni chaab ayen, <<Ti lueri niŋdeerɔ a ŋman cheŋ Ejipiti.>>
5Ate Moosis ale Aaron yaa lo pai nina a vuk tɛŋ Izirali tigsuŋku meena niŋ dula jigini. 6Nun nidoabinni Josua ale Jefunne nidoabinni Kaleb baai ale jam bo nuru baai ale ga kpesi nya tɛŋka la, a yaa jam dari ba gattaŋa a cheeri 7ale weeni Izirali tigsuŋka meena ayen, <<Tɛŋka ate ti jam va ka po a taam a kpesi nya la a nala kama a gaam taam. 8Naawen sui a dan yɔk ale ti, wa le de ti niŋ a ta ti jo tɛŋ kala po, kaai ate biisim ale siita sueri ka po la, abe wa pai ka a te ti. 9Ka nama tin kan nye tukpari ale Naawen ya. Abe ni kan chali tɛŋka nuruma yɔgsummoa, dii nyiŋla ti le zak ba a nɛ. Waai a kan nya ba zuwa, alege Naawen a bo ale ti kama. Ni kan chali ba yɔgsum.>>
10Alege tigsuŋku meena a jam a biisi ayen ba yuk ba ale tana. Ate Naawen zulaŋa a yaa jam Tuka Viuku zuk Izirali demma meena jigi. 11Naawen a jam weeni Moosis ayen, <<Nuruma de ale zɛri mi zula te ka a paari ka dimpo? Ka dimpo ate ba ale kasim a zɛri a kan ta siaka ale mi, wakinkagla ŋaai meena ate mi a nye ba suŋsuŋ la? 12Mi ale nak ba dueni tɛŋ ale nyiŋtuila a kaasi ba, alege m le basi ate nama a chim tɛŋ kpieŋ a ta pagrim a gaam ba ale ka diila.>>
13Moosis yaa weeni Naawen ayen, <<Ejipiti demma ale wom dila wari ayen, fi pagrimu nyiŋ, fi ta nuruma de a nyini ba po. 14Ate ba le weeni nuruma ale bo tɛŋka de po la ku wari. Ba poom ŋaam wom kama ayen, Naawen yaa, fi bo ale nuruma de kama, Naawen yaa, ba nya fu kama ale nimbie, fi chiŋmanni ale jam bo ba zuk la diipo ate fi a jam de ba niŋ a cheŋ ase chiŋmari la danni po ale de ba niŋ ase chiŋmari ale bolim la yokku po. 15Fi dan ko nuruma de meena bunyi, tɛŋ sii ale ba wom fi wanni de la ale weeni ayen, 16<Naawen an baga a ta nuruma de a jam tɛŋ kaai ate wa puulim a pɛ ale ba la po. Wa ko ba kama gɔnni po.>
17<<Naawen abe sak wa pagrimu, ase fi le weeni dii dek la. 18<Naawen sui a kan kpabi a puuri, wa ta ŋmanteka nna yegayega a vɔŋ tukpari nyam biem a te ba. Alege wa kan basi baai ale nye kaasi la namsika, wa a namsi bimbaansa ba koma biemu nyiŋ, a nyini gaŋsa butawa a ta ga paari bunaansiwa po.> 19A ta va fi ŋmante kpieŋka nyiŋ, vɔŋ nuruma de biemu a te ba ase fi le jam vɔŋ te ba diipo ate ba basi Ejipiti tɛŋka a ta jam paari jinla la.>>
20Ate Naawen a tulisi ayen, <<Mi vɔŋ te ba kama ase fi ale bek diila. 21Alege ase mi ale vua la nyiŋ, ase Naawen zulaŋa ale sum a sueri tɛŋ zuk de meena la, 22nuruma de wanyi baai ale jam nya m zulaŋa ale wakinkaglaŋa ate mi nye Ejipiti ale gɔnni po la, alege baai ale zɛri mi ale nye mi nya a paari naŋtuok nɔi pi la, 23ba wanyi mɛ la a kan nya tɛŋ kaai ate m puulim ale ba kokpieŋsaŋa la. Ba wanyi mɛ la waai ale nye mi a kaasi la kan nya ka. 24Alege mi tomteerɔwa Kaleb a ta ka chiik katɔga ale va mi ale wa suinum meena, m le ta wa jam tɛŋ kaai ate wa a yaali wa jo la po, ate wa ŋaaŋbisaŋa ale soa ka. 25Ase Amalek ale Keenan demma ale bo vaasaŋa po la nyiŋ, chum ni viriŋ ŋaaŋ a duŋ gɔnni nyiŋ a va suik kuui ale a cheŋ Nyakpiem Mɔnuŋku jigini la.>>
26Naawen yaa jam weeni Moosis ale Aaron ayen, 27<<Gaasa nyama de ale ŋuuni a te mi a paari ka dimpo? Mi wom Izirali naakuuni de funfɔblaŋa ale ŋuunika kama. 28Dila weeni ba ayen, <Ka mi Naawen ale a weeni ayen, ase mi ale vua la, mi le nye wie ŋaai dek ate m wom ale ni a weeni ayen, 29Gɔnni de ni ale kpi, nama baai ale paari bena pisiye yaase ba gaam di ate ba jam chiini ba, ate ba ŋuuni a te mi la. 30Ni wanyi mɛ la a kan jo tɛŋ kaai ate m pɛ ayen m te ni ase ni yeri la po, ka Jefunne nidoabili Kaleb ale Nun nidoabili Josua nyiini ale ba jo ka po. 31Dan ka ni bisaŋa ate ni weeni ayen ba ale koaliŋ ba la, m le ta ba a jam ate ba dɛ masim tɛŋ kaai ate ni zɛri la po. 32Alege nama, ni ale kpi a wari gɔnni de po. 33Ni bisaŋa ale chim naapeerisa dela a paari bena pisinaansi, a nam nama ale kan ta wensie la nyiŋ, ate ku paari diipo ate ni po waai ale wari ŋaaŋ a kpi gɔnni po la. 34Bena pisinaansi, bein yeŋ a magsi daa pisinaansiwa ate ni ga kpesi nya tɛŋka la, ni ale nam ni biemu nyiŋ ate ni seba ku ale ka dii ase nama a nin ta chaab ale mi.> 35Mi Naawen ale biisi, m be le sum nye wieŋa de a te gaasa naakuuni de meena, baai ale jam jigi yeŋ a ta chaab ale mi la. Ba le nya ba kpeglimka jigi gɔnni de po. Dela jigini ba le kpi.>>
36Dila nuru baai ate Moosis a jam tom ayen ba ga kpesi nya tɛŋka la, baai ale ŋman jam nye ate naakuuni meena a ŋuuni a te wa, ase ba le jam velim tɛŋka wie diila. 37Nuruma de baai ale jam velim tɛŋka wie la, nyiŋtuila ale jam ko ba Naawen niŋ. 38Nuru baai ale jam ga kpesi nya tɛŋka la, ka Nun nidoabinni Josua ale Jefunne nidoabinni Kaleb nyiini ale tali vua.
39Ase Moosis ale jam weeni kude a te Izirali demma meena la, ba yaa kum nna tuotuowa. 40Dai dii ale pa saŋ la saluik yokyokwa ba yaa cheŋ a duŋ gu kpioŋku tɛŋka nyiŋ ayen, <<Ti nye ka biem ti ale jueli juijui ate Naawen a puulim la.>>
41Alege Moosis ayen, <<Ka boa ate nama a zɛri Naawen wanni? Kude a kan nye niagi. 42Ni kan jueli, dii nyiŋla Naawen an bo ale ni. Ni dachaasaŋa ale nak a yik ni. 43Amalek demma ale Keenan demma ale tu chaab ale ni dula. Ni ale basi Naawen vaka la nyiŋ, wa kan bo ale ni ate ba le ko ni.>>
44Ba le a poli ayen ba nya badek a chak kama la ba cheŋ a duŋ guuk kpioŋku tɛŋka nyiŋ, Moosis yaase Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni an jam va ba. 45Ate Amalek demma ale Keenan demma baai ale jam bo tɛŋ kaai ate guuku a bo ka po la a siŋ jam nye kpaliŋ ale ba a nak ba a ta ga va suiku ale cheŋ Yorma tɛŋka la.

english_text:
Laws about Sacrifices
1The Lord told Moses 2to give the Israelites the following laws about offering sacrifices:
3Bulls or rams or goats are the animals that you may burn on the altar as sacrifices to please me. You may also offer sacrifices voluntarily or because you made a promise, or because they are part of your regular religious ceremonies. The smell of the smoke from these sacrifices is pleasing to me.
4-5If you sacrifice a young ram or goat, you must also offer a kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of olive oil as a grain sacrifice. A liter of wine must also be poured on the altar.
6-7And if the animal is a full-grown ram, you must offer two kilograms of flour mixed with one and a half liters of olive oil. One and a half liters of wine must also be poured on the altar. The smell of this smoke is pleasing to me.
8If a bull is offered as a sacrifice to please me or to ask my blessing, 9you must offer three kilograms of flour mixed with two liters of olive oil. 10Two liters of wine must also be poured on the altar. The smell of this smoke is pleasing to me.
11-13If you are a native Israelite, you must obey these rules each time you offer a bull, a ram, or a goat as a sacrifice. 14And the foreigners who live among you must also follow these rules. 15-16 This law will never change. I am the Lord, and I consider all people the same, whether they are Israelites or foreigners living among you.
17-19When you eat food in the land that I am giving you, remember to set aside some of it as an offering to me. 20From the first batch of bread dough that you make after each new grain harvest, make a loaf of bread and offer it to me, just as you offer grain. 21All your descendants must follow this law and offer part of the first batch of bread dough.
22-23The Lord also told Moses to tell the people what must be done if they ever disobey his laws:
24If all of you disobey one of my laws without knowing it, you must offer a bull as a sacrifice to please me, together with a grain sacrifice, a wine offering, and a goat as a sacrifice for sin. 25Then the priest will pray and ask me to forgive you. And since you did not mean to do wrong, and you offered sacrifices, 26the sin of everyone—both Israelites and foreigners among you—will be forgiven.
27 But if one of you does wrong without knowing it, you must sacrifice a year-old female goat as a sacrifice for sin. 28The priest will then ask me to forgive you, and your sin will be forgiven.
29The law will be the same for anyone who does wrong without meaning to, whether an Israelite or a foreigner living among you.
30-31But if one of you does wrong on purpose, whether Israelite or foreigner, you have sinned against me by disobeying my laws. You will no longer belong to my people.
A Man Put to Death for Gathering Firewood on the Sabbath
32Once, while the Israelites were traveling through the desert, a man was caught gathering firewood on the Sabbath. 33He was taken to Moses, Aaron, and the rest of the community. 34But no one knew what to do with him, so he was not allowed to leave.
35Then the Lord said to Moses, “Tell the people to take that man outside the camp and stone him to death!” 36So he was killed, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Tassels on the People's Clothes
37The Lord told Moses 38 to say to the people of Israel, “Sew tassels onto the bottom edge of your clothes and tie a blue string to each tassel. 39-40These will remind you that you must obey my laws and teachings. And when you do, you will be dedicated to me and won't follow your own sinful desires. 41I am the Lord your God who led you out of Egypt.”

Mi ale Naawen ni Wenni.> >>

english_text:
Korah, Dathan, and Abiram Lead a Rebellion
1-2 Korah son of Izhar was a Levite from the Kohathite clan. One day he called together Dathan, Abiram, and On from the Reuben tribe, and the four of them decided to rebel against Moses. So they asked 250 respected Israelite leaders for their support, and together they went to Moses 3and Aaron and said, “Why do you think you're so much better than everyone else? We're part of the Lord's holy people, and he's with all of us. What makes you think you're the only ones in charge?”
4When Moses heard this, he knelt down to pray. 5Then he said to Korah and his followers:
Tomorrow morning the Lord will show us the person he has chosen to be his priest, and that man will faithfully serve him.
6-7Korah, here is what you and your followers must do: Get some fire pans, fill them with coals and incense, and place them near the sacred tent. And the man the Lord chooses will be his priest. Korah, this time you Levites have gone too far!
8-9You know that the God of Israel has chosen you Levites from all Israel to serve him by being in charge of the sacred tent and by helping the community to worship in the proper way. What more do you want? 10The Lord has given you a special responsibility, and now, Korah, you think you should also be his priest. 11You and your followers have rebelled against the Lord, not against Aaron.
12Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, but they sent back this message: “We won't come! 13It's bad enough that you took us from our rich farmland in Egypt to let us die here in the desert. Now you also want to boss us around! 14You keep promising us rich farmlands with fertile fields and vineyards—but where are they? Stop trying to trick these people. No, we won't come to see you.”
15Moses was very angry and said to the Lord, “Don't listen to these men! I haven't done anything wrong to them. I haven't taken as much as a donkey.”
16Then he said to Korah, “Tomorrow you and your followers must go with Aaron to the Lord's sacred tent. 17Each of you take along your fire pan with incense in it and offer the incense to the Lord.”
18The next day the men placed incense and coals in their fire pans and stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the sacred tent. 19Meanwhile, Korah had convinced the rest of the Israelites to rebel against their two leaders.
When that happened, the Lord appeared in all his glory 20and said to Moses and Aaron, 21“Get away from the rest of the Israelites so I can kill them at once!”
22But the two men bowed down and prayed, “Our God, you gave these people life. Why would you punish everyone here when only one man has sinned?”
23The Lord answered Moses, 24“Tell the people to stay away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.”
25Moses walked over to Dathan and Abiram, and the other leaders of Israel followed. 26Then Moses warned the people, “Get away from the tents of these sinful men! Don't touch anything that belongs to them or you'll be wiped out.” 27So everyone moved away from those tents, except Korah, Dathan, Abiram, and their families.
28Moses said to the crowd, “The Lord has chosen me and told me to do these things—it wasn't my idea. And here's how you will know: 29If these men die a natural death, it means the Lord hasn't chosen me. 30But suppose the Lord does something that has never been done before. For example, what if a huge crack appears in the ground, and these men and their families fall into it and are buried alive, together with everything they own? Then you will know they have turned their backs on the Lord!”
31As soon as Moses said this, the ground under the men opened up 32-33and swallowed them alive, together with their families and everything they owned. Then the ground closed back up, and they were gone.
34The rest of the Israelites heard their screams, so they ran off, shouting, “We don't want that to happen to us!”
35Suddenly the Lord sent a fire that burned up the 250 men who had offered incense to him.
36Then the Lord said to Moses, 37“Tell Aaron's son Eleazar to take the fire pans from the smoldering fire and scatter the coals. The pans are now sacred, 38because they were used for offering incense to me. Have them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar. Those men died because of their sin, and now their fire pans will become a warning for the rest of the community.”
39Eleazar collected the pans and had them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar, 40just as the Lord had told Moses. The pans were a warning to the Israelites that only Aaron's descendants would be allowed to offer incense to the Lord. Anyone else who tried to would be punished like Korah and his followers.
The Israelites Rebel and Are Punished
41The next day the people of Israel again complained against Moses and Aaron, “The two of you killed some of the Lord's people!”
42As the people crowded around them, Moses and Aaron turned toward the sacred tent, and the Lord appeared in his glory in the cloud covering the tent. 43So Moses and Aaron walked to the front of the tent, 44 where the Lord said to them, 45“Stand back! I am going to wipe out these Israelites once and for all.”
They immediately bowed down and prayed. 46Then Moses told Aaron, “Grab your fire pan and fill it with hot coals from the altar. Put incense in it, then quickly take it to where the people are and offer it to the Lord, so they can be forgiven. The Lord is very angry, and people have already started dying!”
47-48Aaron did exactly what he had been told. He ran over to the crowd of people and stood between the dead bodies and the people who were still alive. He placed the incense on the pan, then offered it to the Lord and asked him to forgive the people's sin. The disease immediately stopped spreading, and no one else died from it. 49But 14,700 Israelites were dead, not counting those who had died with Korah and his followers.
50Aaron walked back and stood with Moses at the sacred tent.

1Livai nidoabili jam le Koyat, Koyat nidoabili jam le Izyar, Izyar nidoabili jam le Koora, ale Aruben dɔkku dem gela, Eliab nidoabilisaŋa Datan ale Abiram, ale Pelet nidoabinni On a jam ka zula, 2a yaa yiti ta chaab ale Moosis. Izirali nuruba kobsiye ale pisinu baai ale ka naakuuni niŋdeerɔba ate ba seba a paari la ale jam maa boro, baai ate ba lueri ayen ba dɛ ba niŋ la. 3Ba yaa jam ase tigsuŋ la a yaa zɛri Moosis ale Aaron nɔi ale weeni ba ayen, <<Nama nye cheŋ ka niŋ, naakuuni meena a welema kama waai meena ate Naawen a bo le ba. Ka boa ate nama a zak nidek ŋmai gaam Naawen tigsuŋku?>>
4Ase Moosis ale ga wom di dɛ la, wa yaa lo pai nina a vuk tɛŋ. 5Wa yaa weeni Koora ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔma meena ayen, <<Saluik Naawen ale sak waai ate wa soa la ale waai ale welema la, abe wa basi ate nuru wala a jam moata wa. Nuru waai ate wa lueri la wa le basi ate wa moata wa. 6Fi Koora ale fi ŋaaŋviirɔma meena ku a magsi ni nye ka nna, pai ŋan baai ate ba pai a ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la, 7ate chum fi pai bolim ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa la a nyo ba po a te Naawen. Nuru waai ate Naawen a lueri la ale chim waai ale welema la. Nama Livaima a nye cheŋ ka niŋ.>>
8Moosis a ŋman weeni Koora ayen, <<Yɔgyɔgla de ni wom nama Livaima. 9Ku an diem magsi a te nama, ase Izirali Wenni ale gaari nama a ta nyini Izirali naakuuni meena po a ta ni jam moata wadek ayen ni tom Naawen tuimaŋa wa viuku po, abe ni zaani naakuuni niŋ a sak ba ya? 10Wa ta ni ale ni Livai mbala meena a jam moata ka wadek, alege yɔgyɔgla de nama a yaali ni tuesi kaabka kpaŋtaŋa kama. 11Ku kan va Naawen yaalika ase fi ale fi ŋaaŋviirɔma meena ale jam jigi yeŋ la. Ka wana ale Aaron ate nama a ŋma wa?>>
12Moosis yaa tigsi Eliab nidoabilisaŋa, Datan ale Abiram alege ba weeni ayen, <<Ti kan jamu. 13Fi an ta ti a nyini tɛŋ kaai ate biisim ale siita a bo ka po la ayen fi ko ti kama gɔnni po la? Ate yɔgyɔgla de fi a yaali ayen fi chim naab tama zuwa? 14Fi an ta ti jam tɛŋ kaai ate biisim ale siita a bo ka po la yaase fi te ti tata yaase kaduksa. Fi ale baga yeeri nuruma de nina? Aaya, ti kan jamu.>>
15Moosis sui yaa ŋmasi puuri ate wa weeni Naawen ayen, <<Fi kan tuesi ba tiirimu. Mi an tuesi boniŋ ba jigi ya, yaa m nye ba kaasi ya.>>
16Moosis yaa weeni Koora ayen, <<Fi ale fi ŋaaŋviirɔma meena ale jam Naawen niŋ chum, fi ale ba ale Aaron. 17Nuru yeŋ a pai jabuui ate ba ta a ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la a nyoro. Ŋantaŋa ate ba le pai ju bolimu la a paari ka kobsiye ale pisinu ate ba pai te Naawen. Nama ale Aaron mɛ a te.>> 18Dila nyiŋla nuru meena yaa pai wa jaamu ate wa ju bolim wa po la a nyo bolim ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa la du a yaa za ale Moosis ale Aaron Tuka Viuku nansuiŋku nɔi. 19Ase Koora ale jam tigsi wa ŋaaŋviirɔma meena ayen ba kan siak te ba Tuka Viuku nansuiŋku nɔi la. Naawen zulaŋa a yaa jam tigsuŋku meena jigi. 20Naawen yaa weeni Moosis ale Aaron ayen, 21<<Ni gaari nidek a nyini tigsuŋku po ate mi ale basi ate ba kpi a kpeglim.>>
22Alege Moosis ale Aaron yaa lo pai nina a vuk tɛŋ a yaa kaari ayen, <<Wen yaa, nurubisa meena chiisa Wen, fi sui ale puuri ale tigsuŋku meena ale nuru yeŋ biem nyiŋŋa?>>
23Naawen yaa biisi te Moosis ayen, 24<<Weeni tigsuŋku ayen ba cheŋ nakpiak ba kan moata Koora ale Datan ale Abiram viitaŋa.>>
25Moosis yaa yiti cheŋ Datan ale Abiram jigi. Izirali nisɔmma a jam va wa cheŋ kama. 26Wa yaa kaam tigsuŋku ayen, <<Ni forisi ga ŋaaŋ abe le ge nuru baataŋa de viitaŋa. Ni kan tiri jabuui meena ate ba soa la, ni kan tiri ba ŋantaŋa, kan daa di wa ale ko ni ba wabaataŋa nyiŋ.>> 27Dila nyiŋ ba yaa forisi cheŋ ale basi Koora ale Datan ale Abiram viitaŋa. Datan ale Abiram a yaa nyini peelim a za ale ba pooma ale ba bisaŋa ale ŋan fiisaŋa ba viitaŋa nansuiŋtaŋa nɔi.
28Ate Moosis yaa weeni ayen, <<Kude ale ku basi ate ni seba ayen ka Naawen ale tom mu ayen m nye wieŋa de meena ku daa mi dek popola. 29Ase nuruma de a dan kpi waai meena ale a kpi diila, dan ka di Naawen an tom mi. 30Alege ase Naawen a dan ta wapaali jam ate tɛŋka a lagri a nɛ ba ale jabuui meena ate ba soa la, ate ba siŋ vɔrumu po vuta dila ale basi ate ni seba ayen Nuruma de an nye Naawen magsi ya.>>
31Wa le biisi wieŋa de meena a ga nueri la tɛŋka kauk kuui ate ba za la a yaa na lagri 32a nɛ ba ale ba yeeŋa demma ale Koora nuruma meena ale ba ŋantaŋa meena. 33Ba jam siŋ vɔrumu po ka vuta ale ŋantaŋa meena. Tɛŋka a jam lik ba a basi du kama ate ba kpi cheŋ alege naakuuni. 34Ba le kaari la Izirali demma meena ale za gilim ba la a yaa chali ga nakpiak ale na nna yegayega ayen, <<Tɛŋka a yaa ka nɛ tama kama.>>
35Ate bolim yaa jam nyini Naawen jigi a dɛ nuruba kobsiye ale pisinu baai ale jam boro a nye ŋan baai nyum ale masa tiirim la a ko.
36Naawen yaa weeni Moosis ayen, 37<<Weeni Aaron nidoabinni Eleaza, kaabteerɔwa ate wa yeeri ŋan baai ate ba ta a ju bolim wa po la a ta nyini bolimu po a nyini a kati bolim kaalaŋa a waaŋ, ŋantaŋa ate ba a ju bolim ba po la a ta tuilum kama. 38Nuru baai ale tom kaasi la ŋan baai ate baa ju bolim ba po la, ni jaŋsi ba a mati a pai ba pati lik juka kuŋkuŋku zuk diila ba jam pai ba ta ka Naawen niŋ ate ba ta tuilum. Basi ate ba chim daana a te Izirali demma.>>
39Kaabteerɔwa Eleaza a yaa tuesi kutuk mɔnuŋ ŋan baai ate ba cheem bolim ba po, ate baai ate bolimu a dɛ ba ko la a ta jam la, wa jam basi ate ba jaŋsi ba a mati kama a vi juka kuŋkuŋku zuk, 40ase Naawen ale sak wa a ta va Moosis zuk la. Kude yaa ku a teeri ka Izirali demma ayen waai an magsi ya, ka Aaron dɔkku po nyiini ale magsi ba ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la Naawen niŋ, kan daa di wa le kpi ase Koora ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔma la.
41Dai dii ale pai saŋ la Izirali naakuuni meena yaa jaa ŋma Moosis ale Aaron ayen, <<Ni ko Naawen nuruma.>>
42Alege ase tigsuŋku ale tigsi chaab a ŋma Moosis ale Aaron ale tulim a tuk Tuka Viuku nyiŋla, ku an beni ya, chiŋmari yaa lik dula jigini ate Naawen zulaŋa a yaa jam dula. 43Moosis ale Aaron a yaa cheŋ Tuka Viuku nɔi, 44ate Naawen yaa weeni Moosis ayen, 45<<Nyini tigsuŋku po a ga nakpiak ate m basi ate ba kpeglim bunyi.>> Ate ba yaa jam lo pai nina a vuk tɛŋ.
46Moosis yaa weeni Aaron ayen, <<Pa fi jabuui ate fi ta a ju bolim la a nyo ŋan baai nyum ale masa la du, a moak bolim juka kuŋkuŋku zuk a nyoro a nye nwuli a ga tigsuŋku jigi a nye biem duisi basika a te ba. Suipuurum ale nyini Naawen jigi a jam, nyiŋtuilaŋa a piilim kama.>> 47Aaron yaa nye dii ate Moosis a weeni wa la, a yaa chali jo tigsuŋku suŋsuŋ. Nyiŋtuilaŋa a poom ŋaam piilim kama alege Aaron a pai ŋan baai nyum ale masa la a te a nye biem duisi basika a te ba. 48Wa jam za ka ŋanvutaŋa ale kpiema suŋsuŋ ate nyiŋtuilaŋa a basi. 49Alege nuruba tusa pi ale ŋanaansi ale kobsiyopɔi (14,700) ale jam kpi nyiŋtuilaŋa nyiŋ a gum baai ale jam kpi Koora nyiŋla. 50Aaron yaa ŋman cheŋ Moosis jigi Tuka Viuku nansuiŋku nɔi dii nyiŋla nyiŋtuilaŋa a jam basi kama.

english_text:
Aaron's Walking Stick Blooms and Produces Almonds
1The Lord told Moses:
2-3Call together the twelve tribes of Israel and tell the leader of each tribe to write his name on the walking stick he carries as a symbol of his authority. Make sure Aaron's name is written on the one from the Levi tribe, then collect all the sticks.
4Place these sticks in the tent right in front of the sacred chest where I appear to you. 5I will then choose a man to be my priest, and his stick will sprout. After that happens, I won't have to listen to any more complaints about you.
6Moses told the people what the Lord had commanded, and they gave him the walking sticks from the twelve tribal leaders, including Aaron's from the Levi tribe. 7Moses took them and placed them in the Lord's sacred tent.
8 The next day when Moses went into the tent, flowers and almonds were already growing on Aaron's stick. 9Moses brought the twelve sticks out of the tent and showed them to the people. Each of the leaders found his own and took it.
10But the Lord told Moses, “Put Aaron's stick back! Let it stay near the sacred chest as a warning to anyone who might think of rebelling. If these people don't stop their grumbling about me, I will wipe them out.” 11Moses did what he was told.
12The Israelites cried out to Moses, “We're done for 13and doomed if we even go near the sacred tent!”
translation_text:
1Naawen yaa biisi te Moosis ayen, 2<<Biisi a te Izirali demma abe fi yaali tacheksa pi ale siye a ta nyini ba jigi, kanyi a ta nyini ba ŋiak dɔk meena niŋdeerɔ jigi. Ŋmarisi nuru meena yuei a dueni wa tachek nyiŋ. 3Livaima tachekka nyiŋ ŋmarisi Aaron yuei a dueni du, ku a fɛ ate tachek yeŋ a magsi ŋiak dɔk meena niŋdeerɔ. 4Pa si a zaani Tuka Viuku po nɔiyeŋka dakanni niŋ kauk kuui ate mi a tu ni la. 5Tachekka ate nuru waai soa ate mi lueri la ale pusi vaata ate mi dek ale basi ate Izirali demma ale a ŋma fi diila a kpeglim?>>
6Moosis yaa biisi te Izirali demma ate ba niŋdeerɔma a te wa tacheksa pi ale siye, kanyi a magsi ŋiak dɔk meena niŋdeerɔ, Aaron tachekka a jam maa bo si po kama. 7Moosis yaa pai tacheksaŋa a zaani Naawen niŋ nɔiyeŋka Dakanni Viuku po.
8Dai dii ale pai a saŋ la Moosis yaa jo nɔiyeŋka Dakanni Viuku po a yaa nya ale Aaron tachekka kaai ale za Livaima naŋkula po la a pusi vaata a yɔni yɔna. 9Moosis yaa ta tacheksaŋa meena a nyini Naawen niŋ a jam te Izirali demma meena. Ba le nya si la, nuru meena yaa pai wadek tachek.
10Naawen yaa weeni Moosis ayen, <<Ta Aaron tachekka a ŋman cheŋ ga dueni Nɔiyeŋka dakanni niŋ ate ka bo dula ase daana la a te tukpari nyama. Kude ale basi ate ba le a ŋma mi diila a kpeglim, ate dila ale basi ate ba kan kpi?>> 11Moosis yaa nye dii dek ate Naawen a weeni wa la.
12Izirali demma yaa weeni Moosis ayen, <<Ti le kpi tama bɛ kama, tama meena a bɛ kama. 13Waai ale cheŋ a moata Naawen viuku la ale kpi. Tama meena za ti kpi kama?>>

english_text:
The Duties of the Priests and Levites
1The Lord said to Aaron:
You, your sons, and the other Levites of the Kohath clan, are responsible for what happens at the sacred tent. And you and your sons will be responsible for what the priests do. 2The Levites are your relatives and are here to help you in your service at the tent. 3You must see that they perform their duties. But if they go near any of the sacred objects or the altar, all of you will die. 4No one else is allowed to take care of the sacred tent or do anything connected with it. 5Follow these instructions, so I won't become angry and punish the Israelites ever again.
6I alone chose the Levites from all the other tribes to belong to me, and I have given them to you as your helpers. 7But only you and your sons can serve as priests at the altar and in the most holy place. Your work as priests is a gift from me, and anyone else who tries to do that work must be put to death.
The Priests' Share of Offerings Given to the Lord
(Deuteronomy 18.1-8)
8-9The Lord said to Aaron:
I have put you in charge of the sacred gifts and sacrifices that the Israelites bring to me. And from now on, you, your sons, and your descendants will receive part of the sacrifices for sin, as well as part of the grain sacrifices, and the sacrifices to make things right. Your share of these sacrifices will be the parts not burned on the altar. 10Since these things are sacred, they must be eaten near the sacred tent, but only men are allowed to eat them.
11You will also receive part of the special gifts and offerings that the Israelites bring to me. Any member of your family who is clean and acceptable for worship can eat these things. 12For example, when the Israelites bring me the first batches of oil, wine, and grain, you can have the best parts of those gifts. 13And the first part of the crops from their fields and vineyards also belongs to you. The people will offer this to me, then anyone in your family who is clean may have some of it.
14 Everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me will now belong to you.
15The first-born son in every Israelite family, as well as the first-born males of their flocks and herds, belong to me. But every first-born son and first-born donkey must be bought back from me. 16The price for a first-born son who is at least one month old will be five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards. 17However, all first-born cattle, sheep, and goats belong to me and cannot be bought back. Splatter their blood on the altar and send their fat up in smoke, so I can smell it and be pleased. 18You are allowed to eat the meat of those animals, just as you can eat the choice ribs and the right hind leg of the special sacrifices.
19From now on, the sacred offerings that the Israelites give to me will belong to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is my promise to you and your descendants, and it will never change.
20You will not receive any land in Israel as your own. I am the Lord, and I will give you whatever you need.
What the Levites Receive
The Lord said to Aaron:
21 Ten percent of the Israelites' crops and one out of every ten of their newborn animals belong to me. But I am giving all this to the Levites as their pay for the work they do at the sacred tent. 22-23They are the only ones allowed to work at the tent, and they must not let anyone else come near it. Those who do come near must be put to death, and the Levites will also be punished. This law will never change.
Since the Levites won't be given any land in Israel as their own, 24they will be given the crops and newborn animals that the Israelites offer to me.
What the Levites Must Give
25The Lord told Moses 26to say to the Levites:
When you receive from the people of Israel ten percent of their crops and newborn animals, you must offer a tenth of that to me. 27Just as the Israelites give me part of their grain and wine, you must set aside part of what you receive 28as an offering to me. That amount must then be given to Aaron, 29so the best of what you receive will be mine.
30After you have dedicated the best parts to me, you can eat the rest, just as the Israelites eat part of their grain and wine after offering them to me. 31Your share may be eaten anywhere by anyone in your family, because it is your pay for working at the sacred tent. 32You won't be punished for eating it, as long as you have already offered the best parts to me.
The gifts and sacrifices brought by the people must remain sacred, and if you eat any part of them before they are offered to me, you will be put to death.
