14Ate ni tulisi mu ayen, <<Dii ate mi a yaali ayen ni nye la a nala kama.>>
15Dila nyiŋla ate mi yaa a pai ni buuraŋa po niŋdeerɔma, baai ale ta yam ale zula la, a yaa basi ate ba ta pagrim ni zuk ase baai ale a nya nuruba tusa ale kobsa ale pisinuba ale piisa ase kpaga la. 16Ate m yaa weeni ni boteerɔma dila po ayen: Ba wom ba suataŋa kaasuŋku abe ba bo buusa nalimnyiini, ase wanni bo, ka badek kobirinni po yaase ka ba ale nichamma. 17Kan lugi a bo mini waai ya; wom nyini bisa ale ŋankpagsa meena jigi. Kan chali nuru yɔgsum, ale buusa boka, ka Wen ale soa. Ta wa dii ale pagra a te fu la a jam, m le wom di. 18A nyini dila po m jam weeni fu dii meena ale magsi ayen fi nye la kama.
19Ase Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la ale weeni ti la, ti yaa nyini Yoreb a yaa jam tuaga Amori tɛŋka ate ka bo guutaŋa zuk la a ga va gɔi kpienni ale bie la ate ni nya la a ga paari Kades Barnea. 20Ate mi yaa weeni ni, <<Ni paari Amori tɛŋka ale bo guuku zuk la kama, kaai ate Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la a te ti la. 21Nya Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a te ni tɛŋka kama. Cheŋ a ga tuesi ka ase Naawen dii ale ka ti kokpieŋsaŋa Wen la ale weeni diila. Ni kan chali yɔgsummoa. Ni be kan jɔk nyiŋbiiri.>>
22Nama meena a jam mi jigi kama ayen, <<Ti tom nuruba ate ba dɛ niŋ a ga nya tɛŋka a te ti abe ba ŋman jam weeni ti ti ale ti va suik kuui ale tɛŋ sii ate tama ale paari la.>>
23Popola ŋala a nala kama a te mu, ate mi a lueri ni po nuruba pi ale baye, nuru yeŋ a ta nyini ni kobisaŋa po. 24Ba yaa basi dula alege cheŋ tɛŋ kaai ale bo guutaŋa zuk la, a yaa jam Eskol Viaka a nya ka po. 25Ba yaa jam ta tɛŋka tiisaŋa yona gela a ŋman jam weeni ti ayen, <<Tɛŋ kaai ate Naawen ti Wenni a te ti la a nala kama.>>
26Alege ni kan yaali ayen ni cheŋ; ni zɛri Naawen ni Wenni ale weeni ni diila kama. 27Ni bo ni viitaŋa po a ŋuuni kama ayen, <<Naawen a kisi ti kama, dila nyiŋla wa ta ti a nyini Ejipiti a pai te Amori demma ayen ba kaasi ti. 28Ka bɛ ate tama ale cheŋ? Ti suataŋa a nye ate ka ti sue a kaasi. Ba weeni ayen, <Nuruma a pagra kama ale wɔŋa a gaam tama ale ka diila; Tɛŋsaŋa a zuak kama ale pari wɔŋsa ate si paari chiŋmaaŋa. Ti poom maa nya Anak bisaŋa kama dula jigini.> >>
29Ate mi a weeni ayen, <<Ni kan chali ba yɔgsummoa. 30Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la, ale bo ni niŋ la ale kpaliŋ a te ni ase wa ale jam nye dii a te ni Ejipiti ate waai meena a nya la, diipo ate ni jam bo gɔnni po la. 31Dula ni jam nya Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale ta ni dii ase ko ale ta wa bisa diila kama a ta jam paari dela.>>
32Kude meena a te mi a nye la nama a diem ka siaka ale Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la. 33Wa ale dɛ ni niŋ yokku ase bolim la, ale ŋman chim chiŋmari danni po, a sak ni ale magsi ni va suik kuui la.
34Ase Naawen ale wom dii ate ni weeni la, wa sui yaa jam puuri ate wa pɛ ayen, 35<<Buuni de po nuru yeŋ mɛ la a kan nya tɛŋ naliŋka kaai ate m pɛ ayen m te ba koma la, 36ka Kaleb Jefunne biika nyiini. Wa ale nya ka ate mi ale pai tɛŋ kaai ate wa pai wa naŋ ka a tabi du la a te wa ale wa ŋaaŋbisaŋa, dii nyiŋla wa va Naawen kama ale wa suinum meena.>>
37Nama nyiŋ Naawen sui a puuri ale mi mɛ kama ale weeni ayen, <<Fi mɛ a kan jo ka po. 38Alege fi maarɔwa, Nun nidoabinni Josua, ale jo ka po. Bi te wa nyiŋbiiri, dii nyiŋ, la wala ale wa dɛ ba niŋ ate ba jo tɛŋka po. 39Ale bi fiisaŋa baai ate fi a weeni ayen ba ale cheŋ yontidi po la, ni bi sii baai ale kan diem seba nalim ale biem la, bala ale jo tɛŋka po. Mi ale m te ba ate ba ale soa ka. 40Alege fi, cheŋ gɔnni po, va suik kuui ale a cheŋ Nyakpiem Mɔnuŋku la.>>
41Ate ni yaa tulisi ayen, <<Tama a tom kaasi Naawen kama. Ti ale cheŋ a ga kpaliŋ, ase Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la ale weeni ti diila.>> Dila nyiŋla waai meena pai wa kpaliŋ kɔlima a cheŋ tɛŋ kaai ale bo guutaŋa zuk la, a poli ayen guutaŋa zuk jueli kpaliŋka ka moali. 42Alege Naawen a weeni mi, ayen, <<Weeni ba, <Ni kan cheŋ a ga kpalimu, dii nyiŋla m kan yaali ayen, m bo ale ni. Ni dachaasaŋa ale nya pagrim ni zuk.> >>
43Dila nyiŋ m weeni kama, alege nama, an wom ya. Ni zɛri Naawen ale weeni diila kama ale nye tukpari a cheŋ tɛŋ kaai ale bo guuku zuk la. 44Ate Amori demma baai ale bo guutaŋa zuima la a yaa jam a tu chaab ale ni; Ba jam a vi ni kama ase sewuruk la ale nak ni a ta nyini Seir a ta ga paari Yorma. 45Ate ni ŋman jam a kum a te Naawen, alege wa a wom ni kumsaŋa ale nye ase wa kan wom la. 46Ate ni yaa jam bo Kades paari da boari, ni kasim jam bo ka dula.

english_text:
1 We spent many years wandering around outside the hill country of Seir, 2until the Lord said:
Moses, 3Israel has wandered in these hills long enough. Turn and go north. 4 And give the people these orders: “Be very careful, because you will soon go through the land that belongs to your relatives, the descendants of Esau. They are afraid of you, 5but don't start a war with them. I have given them the hill country of Seir, so I won't give any of it to you, not even enough to set a foot on. 6And as you go through their land, you will have to buy food and water from them.”
7The Lord has helped us and taken care of us during the past 40 years that we have been in this huge desert. We've had everything we needed, and the Lord has blessed us and made us successful in whatever we have done.
8We went past the territory that belonged to our relatives, the descendants of Esau. We followed Arabah Road that starts in the south at Elath and Ezion-Geber, then we turned onto the desert road that leads to Moab.
9 The Lord told me, “Don't try to start a war with Moab. Leave them alone, because I gave the land of Ar to them, and I will not let you have any of it.”
Tribes That Lived near Canaan
10Before the Lord gave the Moabites their land, a large and powerful tribe lived there. They were the Emim, and they were as tall as the Anakim. 11The Moabites called them Emim, though others sometimes used the name Rephaim for both the Anakim and the Emim.
12The Horites used to live in Seir, but the Edomites took over that region. They killed many of the Horites and forced the rest of them to leave, just as Israel did to the people in the land that the Lord gave them.
Israel Crossed the Zered Gorge
Moses said to Israel:
13When we came to the Zered Gorge along the southern border of Moab, the Lord told us to cross the gorge into Moab, and we did. 14 This was 38 years after we left Kadesh-Barnea, and by that time all the men who had been in the army at Kadesh-Barnea had died, just as the Lord had said they would. 15-16The Lord kept getting rid of them until finally none of them were left.
17Then the Lord told me, 18“Moses, now go past the town of Ar and cross Moab's northern border 19 into Ammon. But don't start a war with the Ammonites. I gave them their land, and I won't give any of it to Israel.”
More Nations That Lived near Canaan
20Before the Ammonites conquered the land that the Lord had given them, some of the Rephaim used to live there, although the Ammonites called them Zamzummim. 21The Zamzummim were a large and powerful tribe and were as tall as the Anakim. But the Lord helped the Ammonites, and they killed many of the Zamzummim and forced the rest to leave. Then the Ammonites settled there. 22The Lord helped them as he had helped the Edomites, who killed many of the Horites in Seir and forced the rest to leave before settling there themselves.
23A group called the Avvim used to live in villages as far south as Gaza, but the Philistines killed them and settled on their land.
Israel Crossed the Arnon Gorge
Moses said:
24After we went through Ammon, the Lord told us:
Israel, pack up your possessions, take down your tents, and cross the Arnon River gorge. The territory of the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon lies on the other side of the river, but I now give you his land. So attack and take it! 25Today I will start making all other nations afraid of you. They will tremble with fear when anyone mentions you, and they will be terrified when you show up.
The Defeat of King Sihon of Heshbon
(Numbers 21.21-30)
Moses said to Israel:
26After we had crossed the Arnon and had set up camp in the Kedemoth Desert, I sent messengers to King Sihon of Heshbon, telling him that his nation and ours could be at peace. I said:
27Please let Israel go across your country. We will walk straight through, without turning off the road. 28-29You can even sell us food and water, and we will pay with silver. We need to reach the Jordan River and cross it, because the Lord our God is giving us the land on the west side. The Edomites and Moabites have already let us cross their land. Please let us cross your land as well.
30-31But Sihon refused to let us go across his country, because the Lord made him stubborn and eager to fight us. The Lord told me, “I am going to help you defeat Sihon and take his land, so attack him!”
32We met Sihon and his army in battle at Jahaz, 33and the Lord our God helped us defeat them. We killed Sihon, his sons, and everyone else in his army. 34Then we captured and destroyed every town in Sihon's kingdom, killing everyone, 35but keeping the livestock and everything else of value. 36The Lord helped us capture every town from the Arnon River gorge north to the boundary of Gilead, including the town of Aroer on the edge of the gorge and the town in the middle of the gorge.
37However, we stayed away from all the Ammonite towns, both in the hill country and near the Jabbok River, just as the Lord had commanded.
translation_text:
1Ate ti yaa ŋmani ŋaaŋ a va gɔnni suiku ale a cheŋ Nyakpiem Mɔnuŋku la, a va Naawen ale dak mu la. Ti kasim cheŋ gilim tɛŋ kaai le bo guutaŋa zuk ti ba a wi ayen Seir la kama.
2Ate Naawen yaa weeni mi ayen, 3<<Ni cheŋ gilim tɛŋ kaai ale bo guutaŋa zuk la ate ku beni ka yega, yɔgyɔgla de ni ŋman va wiiluk geŋ. 4Te nuruma wieŋa de, <Ni boro a yaali ni va ka ni suataŋa Iisɔ ŋaaŋbisaŋa ale bo Seir la tɛŋ banni. Ba le chali yɔgsum ale ni, alege ni kpesi nidek. 5Ni kan daani ba ale kpaliŋ ŋa, mi a kan pai ba tɛŋka kanyi mɛ la a te ni, ni poom kan pai ni naŋ a tabi du. Mi pai guuku zuk tɛŋka Seir a te ka Iisɔ ayen wa tanla. 6Ku magsi kama ayen ni tuni ba kpana a magsi ŋandiintaŋa ate ni dɛ la ale nyiamu ate ni nyu la.> >>
7Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a niak ni kama ni nisima tuima meena po. Wa nya ni chelimu zuk kama gɔi kpienni po. Bena pisinaansi wa de Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a kasim bo ale ni kama ate ni an jam a yaali jaaboa.
8Ti yaa jam gaam ti suataŋa Iisɔ buuni, baai ale bo Seir tɛŋka la a taamu. Tama viriŋ kama a va Araba suiku, kuui ale nyini Elat ale Ezion Geber a ga va Moab gɔnni po la.
9Ate Naawen a yaa weeni a sak mi ayen, <<Kan fi daani Moab demma yaase fi nye ate ba nye kpaliŋŋa, ale mi a kan yaali ayen m te ni ba tɛŋka kauk wa. M te Lɔti buuni ka Ar tɛŋka ayen ba tanla.>>
10Emi demma a jam bo ka dula, ba jam ka nuru baai ale pagra ale piisi mɛ ale wɔŋa ase Anak demma la. 11Ase ba ale jam a nye ase Anak demma la, ba jam pai ba chim ka Arefa demma po, alege Moab demma a jam a wi ba ayen ka Emi dem. 12Yori demma ale jam bo Seir tɛŋka, alege Iisɔ buuni a jam yiak ba kama ate ba basi dula. Ba jam kaasi Yori demma kama alege kali dula ase Izirali demma ale nye dii tɛŋ kaai po ate Naawen a pai te ba la.
13Ate Naawen a yaa weeni ayen, <<Yɔgyɔgla de ni yiti ga lo Zered Viaka jueli.>> Ate ti yaa lo viak a jueli.
14Bena pisita ale naaniŋ ale taam la, a zaani diipo ate ti basi Kades Barnea a jam paari diipo ate ti lo Zered Viaka jueli la, dila po gaŋ sii meena ale jam ka tugurik tɔŋdɔba la a kpi kama ase Naawen ale pɛ ayen wa le nye diila. 15Naawen a jam ta ka chaab ale ba ate wa ga yeeri ba meena ba suŋsuŋ.
16Ase tugurik tɔŋdɔma de ale jam kpi la, 17Naawen a yaa weeni mi ayen, 18<<Jinla ku magsi kama ayen ni ga va Moab ale bo Ar po la a taam. 19Ase ni dan paari Ammon demma tɛŋka, ni ka m daani ba yaase ni daani ba ale kpaliŋ ŋa, ale mi a kan yaali ayen m pai Ammon tɛŋka jaab a te ni. Mi pai ka a te ka Lɔti ŋaaŋbisaŋa.>>
20Ba jam a wi dula jigini ayen ka Arefa demma tɛŋ, ba la ale jam bo dula, alege Ammon demma a jam a wi ba ayen ka Zamzum dem. 21Ba jam ka nuru baai ale pagra ale piisi mɛ ale wɔŋa ase Anak demma la. Naawen a jam ko ba kama ate Ammon demma, baai ale jam yiak ba a bo ba boka jigini. 22Wa a nye ka dila dek mɛ ate Iisɔ ŋaaŋbisaŋa baai ale bo Seir tɛŋka po la ase wa ale jam kaasi Yor demma ba nimbie po diila. Ba jam yiak ba kama alege bo ba tɛŋka po a ta jam paari jinla. 23Alege Avvi demma baai ale bo tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa po a ga paari Gaza tɛŋka la, Kaftor demma a jam nyini ka Kaftor a kaasi ba alege bo ba boka jigini.
24Naawen a yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Ni cheŋ a ga lo Arnon benni a jueli. Nya de m pai Siyon Amori denɔwa Yesbon Naawa ale, wa tɛŋka meena a nyo ka ni nisima po. Ni nye ate ni jo ka po a nye kpaliŋ ale wa. 25Jinla danni m le basi ate tɛŋsa meena ale bo tɛŋzuk a chali ni yɔgsum. Ba ale wom le wie ate ba nyiŋsaŋa a gɔk ate ba ale yɔgsa ale ni.>>
26A nyini Kedemot gɔnni po m jam tom ka nuruba Yesbon Naawa Siyon jigi ale suiyɔgni ayen, 27<<Basi ate ti va ni tɛŋka po a taam. Ti ale ga zaani ka suik kpioŋku po. Ti kan viriŋ juga yaase gala. 28Ni pai ŋandiinta a da a te ti ate ti dɛ abe ni pai nyiam mɛ a te ti ate ti nyu abe ti tuni ni kpana. Ka ni tin basi ate ti cheŋ naŋta a taam. 29Ase Iisɔ ŋaaŋbisaŋa baai ale bo Seir la ale Moab demma baai ale bo Ar, ale jam nye dii a te ti suik ayen ti ga lo Jodan a jueli a cheŋ tɛŋ kaai ate Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la a yaali ayen wa pai a te ti la.>> 30Alege Siyon Yesbon Naawa a zɛri an basi ate tama a taam ya. Dii nyiŋla la Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la basi kama ate wa ta tukpari ale suinum pagrik ayen wa pai wa a nyo ni nisima po, ase wa ale nye dii yɔgyɔgla de la.
31Naawen a yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Nya, mi a yaali ayen m pai Siyon ale wa tɛŋka a nyo ka ni nisa po. Yɔgyɔgla de m nak a tuesi ka a tara.>>
32Ase Siyon ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena ale jam nyini ayen ba nye kpaliŋka Jayaz la, 33Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la a pai wa nyo ka ti nisima po ate ti nak lɔnsi wa ale wa bisaŋa ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena tɛŋ. 34A nyini dila po ti tuesi ba tɛŋsaŋa kama ale ko nidoama ale nipooma ale ba bisaŋa meena. Ti an jam tali javuk wa. 35Alege ba duŋsaŋa ale ba ŋanmaŋsaŋa ti jam pai kama ba tɛŋka po a tara. 36A nyini Aroer ale bo Arnon benni la ale tɛŋ kaai ale bo benni jigini la a ta ga paari Gilead, tɛŋ yeŋ mɛ la a jam karo a pagra. Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la a pai ba meena a te ti kama. 37Alege a magsi chaab ale Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la sinsaŋŋa, ni an gaam a taam Ammon demma tɛŋka, yaase tɛŋ kaai ale bo Jabbok benni la yaase tɛŋ sii ale bo guutaŋa zuima la.

english_text:
The Defeat of King Og of Bashan
(Numbers 21.31-35)
Moses said to Israel:
1When we turned onto the road that leads to Bashan, King Og of Bashan led out his whole army to fight us at Edrei. 2But the Lord told me, “Moses, don't be afraid of King Og. I am going to help you defeat him and his army and take over his land. Destroy him and his people, just as you did with the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon.”
3-6The Lord our God helped us destroy Og and his army and conquer his entire kingdom of Bashan, including the Argob region. His kingdom had lots of villages and 60 towns with high walls and gates that locked with bars. We completely destroyed them all, killing everyone, 7but keeping the livestock and everything else of value.
8Sihon and Og had ruled Amorite kingdoms east of the Jordan River. Their land stretched from the Arnon River gorge in the south to Mount Hermon in the north, and we captured it all. 9Mount Hermon is called Mount Sirion by the people of Sidon, and it is called Mount Senir by the Amorites. 10We captured all the towns in the highlands, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, two of the towns that Og had ruled.
Og's Coffin
11King Og was the last of the Rephaim, and his coffin is in the town of Rabbah in Ammon. It is made of hard black rock and is four meters long and almost two meters wide.
The Land East of the Jordan River Is Divided
(Numbers 32.1-42)
Moses said to Israel:
12-17I gave some of the land and towns we captured to the tribes of Reuben and Gad. Their share started at the Arnon River gorge in the south, took in the town of Aroer on the edge of the gorge, and went far enough north to include the southern half of the Gilead region. The northern part of their land went as far east as the upper Jabbok River gorge, which formed their border with the Ammonites. I also gave them the eastern side of the Jordan River valley, from Lake Galilee south to the Dead Sea below the slopes of Mount Pisgah.
I gave the northern half of Gilead and all of the Bashan region to half the tribe of Manasseh. Bashan had belonged to King Og, and the Argob region in Bashan used to be called the Land of the Rephaim. Jair from the Manasseh tribe conquered the Argob region as far west as the kingdoms of Geshur and Maacah. The Israelites even started calling Bashan by the name “Villages of Jair,” and that is still its name. I gave the northern half of Gilead to the Machir clan.
18-19 At that time I told the men of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh:
The Lord our God told me to give you this land with its towns, and that's what I have done. Now your wives and children can stay here with your large flocks of sheep and goats and your large herds of cattle. But all of you men that can serve in our army must cross the Jordan River and help the other tribes, because they are your relatives. 20The Lord will let them defeat the enemy nations on the west side of the Jordan and take their land. Afterwards, you can come back here to the land I gave you.
21-22Then I told Joshua, “You saw how the Lord our God helped us destroy King Sihon and King Og. So don't be afraid! Wherever you go, the Lord will fight on your side and help you destroy your enemies.”
God Refused To Let Moses Enter Canaan
Moses said to Israel:
23 At that time I prayed and begged, 24“Our Lord, it seems that you have just begun to show me your great power. No other god in the sky or on earth is able to do the mighty things that you do. 25The land west of the Jordan is such good land. Please let me cross the Jordan and see the hills and the Lebanon Mountains.”
26But the Lord was angry with me because of you people, and he refused to listen. “That's enough!” he said. “I don't want to hear any more. 27Climb to the top of Mount Pisgah and look north, south, east, and west. Take a good look, but you are not going to cross the Jordan River. 28Joshua will lead Israel across the Jordan to take the land, so help him be strong and brave and tell him what he must do.”
29After this we stayed in the valley at Beth-Peor.
translation_text:
1Ti ŋman a viriŋ a jueli va Basan suiku ate Basan naawa Og ale wa tugurik tommu meena a yaa nyini a tu chaab ale ti ayen ti nye kpaliŋ Edrei. 2Ate Naawen a weeni mi ayen, <<Kan chali wa yɔgsummoa ale mi a pai wa ale wa tugurik tommu meena ale wa tɛŋka a nyo fi nisa po kama. Nye wa ase fi ale nye Siyon Amori demma naawa diila waai ale jam a nya Yesbon la.>>
3Ate Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la a pai Basan Naawa Og ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena a nyo ti nisima po. Ate ti ko ba meena nuru vuk mɛ la an tali ya. 4Dila po wa, ti jam tuesi wa tɛŋsaŋa meena kama. Tɛŋsa pisiyuebi wa po kanyi mɛ la karo ate tama an tuesi ya a ta nyini ba jigi ya. Argob tɛŋka meena ale Og tɛŋ kpieŋka ale bo Basan la. 5Tɛŋsaŋa de meena ba jam se si parisaŋa ate si pagra kama ale wɔŋa ale nye nansuiŋta ale da biga alege tɛŋsa gela a jam piisi kama ate parisa an gilim si. 6Ti jam kaasi ba kama ase ti ale jam nye Yesbon Naawa Siyon diila ale kaasi tɛŋ meena nidoaba, nipooba ale bisa diila. 7Alege ba duŋsa meena ale ba ŋanmaŋsaŋa ale bo ba tɛŋsaŋa po la tama a jam pai ba kama a tara.
8A zaani dila po ti yaa tuesi Jodan kori geŋsaŋa ale Arnon Buboalika geŋsaŋa a ta ga paari Yermon Guuku nalima ŋaye wa dɛ jigi. 9Saidon demma a jam a wi Yermon Guuku ayen ka Sirion alege ate Amori demma a wi ku ayen Senir. 10Ti yaa jam tuesi tɛŋsaŋa meena a ta ga paari Gilead ale Basan a ta va dula ga paari Saleka ale Edrei tɛŋsaŋa ale tɛŋ kpieŋka Basan ate Og a bo du la. 11Ka Og Basan Naawa ale jam tali Arefa buuni po. Wa gaduokku a jam ka kutuk ale jam woŋŋa ase naŋtuok nɔi pi ale buta la alege ku labsimu mɛ a nye ase naŋtuok nɔi buyuebi la. Ku diem bo ka Arabba Ammon demma tɛŋka.
12Tɛŋka ate ti jam tuesi dila po la, m pai ka Aroer wiiluk geŋka kauk ale maŋ Arnon benni la, ale Gilead tɛŋka ale bo guutaŋa zuk la geli ale ka tɛŋsaŋa a te Aruben ale Gad ŋaaŋbisaŋa. 13Gilead tɛŋka meena ale Basan, Og ale jam bo juijui la meena, mi a jam pai a te ka Manasa dɔkku geli. Ale Argob ate ka bo Basan po la ate ba jam a wi ka ayen Arefa demma tɛŋ la. 14Jair Manasa ŋaaŋbiik ale la, wa ale jam soa Argob tɛŋka meena a ta ga va Gesur ale Maaka demma tɛŋsaŋa, Ba ale jam a wi wa diila tɛŋka mɛ yuei a jam ale la. Dila ale soa ate ba diem a wi ka ayen Yavvot Jair la.
15Ate mi yaa pai Gilead a te Makir. 16Alege Aruben ale Gad ŋaaŋbisaŋa m pai ka Gilead ale Arnon Benni geŋsaŋa ate ba gum chaab ale Jabbok Benaŋka geŋsa kauk kuui ale moata Ammon demma la. 17Ka yeniŋ geŋsaŋa Jodan ale bo Araba la, a ta ga Kinneret ga va nyakpiemu ale bo Araba, Yesa Nyakpiem ale la, a churinti a siŋ Pisga.
18M weeni ni kama dila po ayen, <<Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a pai tɛŋka de a te ni kama ayen ni tanla. Alege ni nuru pagrisaŋa baai ale gomsi magsi kpaliŋka la a gaam taam ni suataŋa Izirali demma jigi. 19Alege, nipooma ale ni bisaŋa ale ni duŋsaŋa, m seba kama ni duŋsaŋa a piisi kama, ale wari ka tɛŋ sii ate m te ni la po, 20ate ku ga paari diipo ate Naawen ale te ni suataŋa vuusum ase wa ale te nama mɛ diila, ase Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale weeni ayen wa ale te ba Jodan Benni kunkɔŋni din dila la. Ate kula ŋaaŋnyiŋ ni wanyi wanyi ale ŋman cheŋ kauk kuui ate m te ni la.>>
21Dila po mi weeni Josua kama ayen, <<Fi nya kama ale fidek nina dii meena ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a nye nalimaŋa ŋayewa la. Naawen ale nye tɛŋ sii meena ate ni a cheŋ la ka dila dekdega. 22Kan chali ba yɔgsummoa. Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la dek ale kpaliŋ a te fu.>>
23A zaani dila po m saalim Naawen kama ayen, 24<<Nyɔnɔwa waai ale ka Naawen la, fi piilim boro a sak fi tomteerɔwa fi zuaka ale fi pagrimu ale ka diila kama. A nyini wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋzuk de wen a karo a tom wakpiema ŋaai ate fi a tom la? 25Basi ate m cheŋ a ga nya tɛŋ maŋka ale gaam Jodan a taam la, kaai ale bo guuta zuk la ale Lebanon tɛŋka.>>
26Alege nama nyiŋ Naawen sui a jam puuri ale mu kama ate wa an wom m puusaŋa. <<Ku magsi ya.>> Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna, <<Kan ŋman biisi wanni de wie ale mu. 27Jueli Pisga guuku zuk a nya yeniŋ geŋ ale yeseoku geŋ ale wiiluk geŋ ale kori geŋsaŋa. Nya tɛŋka ale fidek nimbie dii nyiŋla fi a kan yaali fi gaam Jodan benni a taamu. 28Alege sak Josua abe fi maari a te wa nyiŋbiiri ate wa ale dɛ nuruma dɛ niŋ a ta ba gaam a taam a tuesi tɛŋ kaai ate fi a nya la.>> 29Ate tama a yaa jam bo viaka po a moata Bet Peor.

english_text:
Israel Must Obey God
Moses said:
1Israel, listen to these laws and teachings! If you obey them, you will live, and you will go in and take the land that the Lord is giving you. He is the God your ancestors worshiped, 2 and now he is your God. I am telling you everything he has commanded, so don't add anything or take anything away.
3 You saw how he killed everyone who worshiped the god Baal Peor. 4But all of you that were faithful to the Lord your God are still alive today.
5-8 No other nation has laws that are as fair as the ones the Lord my God told me to give you. If you faithfully obey them when you enter the land, you will show other nations how wise you are. In fact, everyone that hears about your laws will say, “That great nation certainly is wise!” And what makes us greater than other nations? We have a God who is close to us and answers our prayers.
9You must be very careful not to forget the things you have seen God do for you. Keep reminding yourselves, and tell your children and grandchildren as well. 10Do you remember the day you stood in the Lord's presence at Mount Sinai? The Lord said, “Moses, bring the people of Israel here. I want to speak to them so they will obey me as long as they live, and so they will teach their children to obey me too.”
11 Mount Sinai was surrounded by deep dark clouds, and fire went up to the sky. You came to the foot of the mountain, 12and the Lord spoke to you from the fire. You could hear him and understand what he was saying, but you couldn't see him. 13 The Lord said he was making an agreement with you, and he told you that your part of the agreement is to obey the Ten Commandments. Then the Lord wrote these Commandments on two flat stones.
14 That's when the Lord commanded me to give you the laws and teachings you must obey in the land that you will conquer west of the Jordan River.
Don't Worship Idols
Moses said to Israel:
15When God spoke to you from the fire, he was invisible. So be careful 16 not to commit the sin of worshiping idols. Don't make idols to be worshiped, whether they are shaped like men, women, 17 animals, birds, 18reptiles, or fish. 19And when you see the sun or moon or stars, don't be tempted to bow down and worship them. The Lord put them there for all the other nations to worship. 20 But you are the Lord's people, because he rescued you from Egypt, that fiery furnace.
21 The Lord was angry with me because of what you said, and he told me that he would not let me cross the Jordan River into the good land that he is giving you. 22So I must stay here and die on this side of the Jordan, but you will cross the river and take the land.
23Always remember the agreement that the Lord your God made with you, and don't make an idol in any shape or form. 24 The Lord will be angry if you worship other gods, and he can be like a fire destroying everything in its path.
25-26Soon you will cross the Jordan River and settle down in the land. Then in the years to come, you will have children, and they will give you grandchildren. After many years, you might lose your sense of right and wrong and make idols, even though the Lord your God hates them. So I am giving you fair warning today, and I call the earth and the sky as witnesses. If you ever make idols, the Lord will be angry, and you won't have long to live, because the Lord will let you be wiped out. 27 Only a few of you will survive, and the Lord will force you to leave the land and will scatter you among the nations. 28There you will have to worship gods made of wood and stone, and these are nothing but idols that can't see or hear or eat or smell.
29-30 In all of your troubles, you may finally decide that you want to worship only the Lord. And if you turn back to him and obey him completely, he will again be your God. 31The Lord your God will have mercy—he won't destroy you or desert you. The Lord will remember his promise, and he will keep the agreement he made with your ancestors.
32-34When the Lord your God brought you out of Egypt, you saw how he fought for you and showed his great power by performing terrifying miracles. You became his people, and at Mount Sinai you heard him talking to you out of fiery flames. And yet you are still alive! Has anything like this ever happened since the time God created humans? No matter where you go or who you ask, you will get the same answer. No one has ever heard of another god even trying to do such things as the Lord your God has done for you.
35-36 The Lord wants you to know he is the only true God, and he wants you to obey him. That's why he let you see his mighty miracles and his fierce fire on earth, and why you heard his voice from that fire and from the sky.
37The Lord loved your ancestors and decided that you would be his people. So the Lord used his great power to bring you out of Egypt. 38Now you face other nations more powerful than you are, but the Lord has already started forcing them out of their land and giving it to you.
39So remember that the Lord is the only true God, whether in the sky above or on the earth below. 40Today I am explaining his laws and teachings. And if you always obey them, you and your descendants will live long and be successful in the land the Lord is giving you.
Safe Towns
41-43 Moses said, “People of Israel, you must set aside the following three towns east of the Jordan River as Safe Towns: Bezer in the desert highlands belonging to the Reuben tribe; Ramoth in Gilead, belonging to the Gad tribe; and Golan in Bashan, belonging to the Manasseh tribe. If you kill a neighbor without meaning to, and if you had not been angry with that person, you can run to one of these towns and find safety.”
The Second Speech: Moses Tells What the Lord Demands
Israel at Beth-Peor
44-46The Israelites had come from Egypt and were camped east of the Jordan River near Beth-Peor, when Moses gave these laws and teachings. The land around their camp had once belonged to King Sihon of Heshbon. But Moses and the Israelites defeated him 47and King Og of Bashan, and took their lands. These two Amorite kings had ruled the territory east of the Jordan River 48from the town of Aroer on the edge of the Arnon River gorge, north to Mount Hermon. 49Their land included the eastern side of the Jordan River valley, as far south as the Dead Sea below the slopes of Mount Pisgah.
translation_text:
1Ni wom de, Izirali demma, sinsaŋŋa ate m boro a yaali ayen m sak ni la ale wie ŋaai ate ni a va la. Ni va ŋa ate ni vua ate ni jo tɛŋka po a tuesi ka, kaai ate Naawen dii ale ka ni kokpieŋsaŋa Wen la ale te ni la. 2Ni kan yaali wari a gum dii ate mi a weeni la po abe ni kan yeeri wari dii ate mi a weeni ni la po mɛ a basi alege ni tanla Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la sinsaŋŋa ate mi a te ni la.
3Ni nya kama ale nidek nina dii ate Naawen a nye Baal Peor la kama. Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a jam ko waai meena ale va Peor bɔglukku Baal la, 4Alege nama baai meena ale chiib va Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a diem vua kama jinla.
5Nya de m jam a sak ni wie ale sinsaga ase Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale weeni mu diila, ayen tɛŋ kaai po ate nama a jo ni tuesi la ni va ŋa. 6Ni kpesi a va ŋa nalimnyiini, ale ka dila ale ku sak ni yam ale miŋ chakka tɛŋsaŋa de jigi, waai meena ale wa wom wieŋa de meena la a yaa le weeni ayen, <<Wensie tɛŋ kpieŋka de ka yam ale miŋ chakka nuruba nyiini.>> 7Ka tɛŋ boa ale zuak a ta ka wena ate ŋa moata ba ase Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la ale moata ti diipo meena ate tama a puusi a te wa? 8Ka tɛŋ kana ale zuak a ta ŋmarisika ale buusa ase sinsaŋŋa de meena ate mi a pai a te ni jinla nna la?
9Ni kpesi yik nidek, a moata chaab ate ni kan baŋ dii ate ni nya ale ni ninaŋa la yaase ni basi ate ŋa sati a nyini ni suiniimaŋa po a nyini ase ni le diem vua la. Ni pai ŋa a sak ni bisaŋa ale ni ŋaaŋsaŋa mɛ. 10Ni teeri dai dii danni ate ni jam zaani Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la niŋ Yoreb guuku zuk la diipo ate wa weeni mi ayen, <<Tigsi nuruma m niŋ ate ba wom m wieŋa ate ba zamsi ate ba va mi diipo meena ate ba vua a bo tɛŋka po la, abe ba pai ŋa a sak ba bisaŋa.>> 11Ni jam torisi moata kama ale za guuku zuk alege ate ku jam a nyaksi ase bolim la a jueli wenŋmazuk ale chiŋma sobta ate ku jam nye legi, 12Ate Naawen a yaa jam biisi bolimu po ale ni. Ni wom ka wieŋa nuemka alege ni an jam nya jaaboa ku jam ka lueluk nyiini. 13Wa yaa weeni ni wa nɔiyeŋka, Wie Piika ŋaai ate wa weeni ni ayen ni va ŋa abe ni ŋmarisiŋa a dueni tintain paglaksa siye zuk. 14Ate Naawen a yaa weeni mi dipo ayen m sak ni wa wieŋa ale sinsaŋŋa ate ni va ŋa tɛŋ kaai ate ni a yaali ni gaam Jodan benni a taam soaka la.
15Ni an jam nya wari ya da dii danni ate Naawen a biisi ale ni bolimu po Yoreb guuku zuk la. Dila nyiŋla ni be kpesi nidek nalimnyiini, 16dii ale ku nye ate ni kan taŋ nidek ale bɔgta, yaali ŋan mɛɛnta, baai ale a nye ase nidoa yaase nipok la. 17Yaase duŋ tɛŋka po yaase nuim ale a yiri wenzuk la, 18yaase ŋanta baai ale a cheŋ tɛŋka zuk la yaase ŋan baai ale bo nyaataŋa po la. 19Ase ni dan zak nya chiŋmaaŋa po a nya wenbinni ale chiika ale chiŋmarisaŋa ale wenŋmazuk ŋantaŋa meena ni kan koori tɛŋ a zuli ŋan baai ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a pai te tɛŋ meena tɛŋzuk de la. 20Alege nama, Naawen a jam yeeri ni kama a ta ni nyini Ejipiti bolimu po a nyini ayen ni chim nuru baai ale ba soa wa ŋantaŋa la ase ni yaa le ka dii yɔgyɔgla de la.
21Naawen sui ale jam puuri ale mu nama nyiŋ, ate wa yaa pɛ ayen m kan gaam Jodan benni a jo wenŋmazuk kuui ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a yaali wa te ni ate ni ta la. 22M le kpi kama tɛŋka de po; m kan gaam Jodan benni a taamu, alege nama boro a yaali ni gaam kama abe le tuesi tɛŋ naliŋka. 23Ni be kpesi nidek ate ni kan baŋ Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale nye nɔiyeŋ kaai ale ni la; ni kan nye bɔgta a te ni dega a ta va dii ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a kisi la. 24Ale Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a nye ase ka bolim buui ale dɛ la, wa ka Naawen dii ale a dɛ nyuri.
25Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ni yaa dan ta bisa ale ŋaaŋsa a bo tɛŋka po ate ku beni ate ni yaa taŋ nidek a basi a yaa se bɔgta, a nye biem Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la nimbie po a nye ate wa sui a puuri, 26mi ale wi ka wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋ ate ba chim m seerɔba a ta va ni jigi ate daaŋa de po ate nama ale kpi nwuli tɛŋ kaai po ate nama a yaali ni gaam Jodan benni a taam a ta la. Ni kan bo dula a beni ni ale kpi kama. 27Naawen ale kati ni a waaŋ kama nuruma po, ka ni maga ale ni vuuk a bo tɛŋ sii ate Naawen a ta ni a cheŋ la. 28Dula jigini ni yaa ale kaab bɔgluk tii ate nuruba a pai nisa a nye ale daata ale tintana la, tii ale kaa nya yaase ti a wom yaase ti a dɛ yaase ti a wom nyum la. 29Alege a nyini dula ni gisi Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la, ni ale nya wa ase ni ale a gisi wa ale ni suinum ale ni chiik meena. 30Ase ni dan bo watuasa po ate wieŋa de meena a nye ni ku kan beni ale ni ale tulim Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la jigi a wom wa. 31Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ka jiirim Wen. Wa kan zɛri ni yaase wa kaasi ni yaa wa baŋ nɔiyeŋka ate wa nye ale ni kokpieŋsaŋa kaai la.
32Yɔgyɔgla de ni bek da ŋaai ale taam alege ate nama daaŋa a paari la wie. A nyini diipo ate Wen a nye nuru tɛŋka zuk la, ni bek jigi meena ase wa kpienni de choa a nye yaase wanni de choa ba wom di? 33Nuru yonta a wom Wen lueluk ale ku a biisi bolim po ale boro ase nama ale wom diila? 34Bɔgluk kuui a diem baga a tuesi tɛŋ a tara a ta va nyenyaka yaase wakperikaliisa yaase wakinkagla yaase zuaka ale nyeka ase wie ŋaai meena ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a nye ni nimbie po a te ni diipo ate ni jam bo Ejipiti po la?
35Ni jam nya wieŋa de kama ate ku basi ate ni seba ayen Naawen ka Wen; kan daa wala waai a ŋman karo. 36A nyini wenŋmazuk wa basi ate ni wom wa lueluku ayen wa namsi ni. Tɛŋzuk de sak ni wa bolim kpiemu ale ka diila kama, ate ni wom wa wieŋa bolimu po. 37Wa ale jam a yaali ni kokpieŋsaŋa ale lueri ba ŋaaŋbisaŋa la nyiŋ ate wa yaa ta ni a nyini Ejipiti po nyini ale wa pagrim kpiemu, 38ale yiak tɛŋ sii ale pagra a gaam ni la ate si nyini ale ta ni a jam ba tɛŋsaŋa po ayen ni tanla se ku ale ka dii jinla de la.
39Ni be seba, abe le basi ate ku bo ni suiniima po jinla danni ayen, Naawen ka Wen wenŋmazuk po ale tɛŋzuk de mɛ. Waai a ŋman karo. 40Ni be ta wa wieŋa ale wa sinsaŋŋa, ŋaai ate mi a te ni jinla de la, ate ku ale cheŋ nalimnyiini ale nama ale ni bisaŋa ate ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ate ni ale goa tɛŋ kaai ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a pai a te ni la po a beni.
41Ate Moosis a yaa lueri tɛŋsa sita Jodan benni kori geŋsa. 42Kauk kuui ate waai a dan ko nuru abe wa chali a cheŋ ase wa dan kan ta waai ale wa a potim seba ale ko wa. Wa baga a chali a cheŋ tɛŋsaŋa de kanyi kama a vari wa nyuvunni a basi. 43Tɛŋ sila abe le nna: Bezer, Aruben dɔkku ale soa dula, Aramat ate ka bo Gilead la ate Gad demma soa la ale Golan ale bo Basan po la Manasa dɔkku mɛ ale soa dula.
44Sinsaŋŋa ale nna ate Moosis a weeni Izirali demma la. 45Sinsaŋŋa de ate Moosis a jam te ba diipo ate ba nyini Ejipiti po a nyini la 46ale diipo ate ba jam bo Bet Peor viaka po Jodan kori geŋka la, tɛŋ kaai ate ba a wi ayen Amori la, ate Siyon a jam chim ka naab la waai ale jam a nya Yesbon ate Moosis ale Izirali demma nak yik ba diipo ate ba jam nyini Ejipiti po a nyini la. 47Ba jam tuesi wa tɛŋka kama ale Basan Naawa Og tɛŋka, nalima ŋayewa ale jam bo Amori tɛŋsaŋa ale bo Jodan benni kori geŋsa la. 48Tɛŋka de a jam zaani ka Aroer a ga nye ban ale Arnon Buboalika a ta ga va Sirion guuku (Yermon ale la), 49a ga pai Araba ale bo Jodan benni kori geŋsa la meena a gum du a ta ga paari nyakpiemu ale bo Araba la a ta jueli tuak Pisga.

english_text:
The Ten Commandments
(Exodus 20.1-17)
1Moses called together the people of Israel and said:
Today I am telling you the laws and teachings that you must follow, so listen carefully. 2The Lord our God made an agreement with our nation at Mount Sinai. 3That agreement wasn't only with our ancestors but with us, who are here today. 4The Lord himself spoke to you out of the fire, 5but you were afraid of the fire and refused to go up the mountain. So I spoke with the Lord for you, then I told you that he had said:
6I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
7Do not worship any god except me.
8 Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth. 9 Don't bow down and worship idols. I am the Lord your God, and I demand all your love. If you reject me and worship idols, I will punish your families for three or four generations. 10But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
11 Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
12 Show respect for the Sabbath Day—it belongs to me. 13 You have six days when you can do your work, 14but the seventh day of the week belongs to me, your God. No one is to work on that day—not you, your children, your oxen or donkeys or any other animal, not even those foreigners who live in your towns. And don't make your slaves do any work. 15This special day of rest will remind you that I reached out my mighty arm and rescued you from slavery in Egypt.
16 Respect your father and mother, and you will live a long and successful life in the land I am giving you.
17 Do not murder.
18 Be faithful in marriage.
19 Do not steal.
20 Do not tell lies about others.
21 Do not desire to possess anything that belongs to another person—not a house, a wife, a husband, a slave, an ox, a donkey, or anything else.
22 When we were gathered at the mountain, the Lord spoke to us in a loud voice from the dark fiery cloud. The Lord gave us these commands, and only these. Then he wrote them on two flat stones and gave them to me.
The People Were Afraid
(Exodus 20.18-21)
Moses said to Israel:
23When fire blazed from the mountain, and you heard the voice coming from the darkness, your tribal leaders came to me 24and said:
Today the Lord our God has shown us how powerful and glorious he is. He spoke to us from the fire, and we learned that people can live, even though God speaks to them. 25But we don't want to take a chance on being killed by that terrible fire, and if we keep on hearing the Lord's voice, we will die. 26Has anyone else ever heard the only true God speaking from fire, as we have? And even if they have, would they live to tell about it? 27Moses, go up close and listen to the Lord. Then come back and tell us, and we will do everything he says.
28The Lord heard you and said:
Moses, I heard what the people said to you, and I approve. 29I wish they would always worship me with fear and trembling and be this willing to obey me! Then they and their children would always enjoy a successful life.
30Now, tell them to return to their tents, 31but you come back here to me. After I tell you my laws and teachings, you will repeat them to the people, so they can obey these laws in the land I am giving them.
Moses said:
32Israel, you must carefully obey the Lord's commands. 33Follow them, because they make a path that will lead to a long successful life in the land the Lord your God is giving you.

1Moosis a tigsi Izirali demma meena a weeni ba ayen. Izirali demma, ni wom sinsaŋŋa ale wieŋa ate mi a weeni jinla de la. Ni zamsi ŋa abe ni seba a chak ayen ni va ŋa kama. 2Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la a jam nye ka nɔiyeŋ ale ti Yoreb guuku. 3Ku be daa ti koma ate Naawen a jam nye nɔiyeŋka ale ba alege ka tama, baai meena ale vua a bo dela jinla de la. 4Naawen a jam biisi bolimu po ale ni ka nidek nimbie po guuku zuk. 5Diipo ate mi a jam zaani Naawen ale nama suŋsuŋ a pai wa wanni a te ni la dii nyiŋla ni jam yɔgsa kama ale bolimu ate ni an jueli guuku zuwa. Ate wa yaa weeni ayen. 6<<Mi ale Naawen dii ale ka fi Wen la, waai ale ta fu nyini Ejipiti a nyini yɔntidi tɛŋka po a nyini la. 7<<Kan ta wen yona a gum mi po. 8<<Kan nye bɔgluk ate ku a neesi jaab wenŋmazuk yaase tɛŋzuk yaase nyiam po a te fi dega. 9<<Kan koori tɛŋ a zuli ba yaase fi puusi ba, diila mi Naawen dii ale ka fi Wen la, ka nyuri Wen, a namsi bimbaansa ba koba biem nyiŋ a ta ga paari ba gaŋ sii ale a saari buta ale bunaansi la baai ale kisi mi la. 10Alege a sak ŋmanteka ale gaŋ sii ale saari tusidi a yaali mi ale ŋman ta m wieŋa la. 11<<Kan wi Naawen dii ale ka fi Wen la yuenni kinla, diila Naawen a kan basi waai ale a wi Wa yuenni kinla la. 12Kpesi Vuusum Danni abe fi basi ate di ta tuilum, ase Naawen dii ale ka fi Wen la ale weeni diila. 13Daa ŋayuebi fi pai tom fi tuimaŋa meena, 14alege daa ŋayopɔiwa danni ka Vuusum dai a te Naawen dii ale ka fi Wen la. Dai dila danni kan tom tuin yoŋŋoa. Fi dek kan tom yaase fi nidoabili yaase fi lie yaase tomteerɔ yaase dɔklie yaase fi lalik yaase boniŋ yaase fi duŋsaŋa kaai yaase nichaanɔ ale bo ale fi la. Dila ale ku basi ate fi tomteerɔwa ale dɔkliewa a vuusi ase fi la. 15Fi abe a teeri ayen fi jam ka yɔma a bo Ejipiti po ate Naawen dii ale ka fi Wen la a ta fi nyini ale wa nisima pagrim. Dila nyiŋla Naawen dii ale ka fi Wen la a weeni kama ayen fi a kpesi Vuusum Danni. 16<<A zuli fi ko ale fi ma ase Naawen dii ale ka fi Wen la ale weeni fi diila, ate fi goa a benni ate wari meena ale nye nalimnyiini a te fu tɛŋ kaai ate Naawen dii ale ka fi Wen la a te fu la. 17Kan ko nuru. 18Kan nye kaboŋŋa. 19Kan zu. 20Kan chim venta seerɔ a velim te fi vaanchoa. 21Kan ta kɔrisa ale fi vaanchoa powa, be kan ta kɔrisa ale fi vaanchoa yeri ya, yaase wa tɛŋŋa yaase wa tomteerɔ yaase wa dɔklie yaase wa lalik yaase wa boniŋa yaase jaabuuri meena ate fi vaanchoa a ta la.
22Sinsaŋŋa de ate Naawen weeni ale lueluk kpioŋ a nyini bolimu po ate tigsuŋku meena ale jam bo guuku zuk la a nyini chiŋmaaŋa ale legini po ale an ŋman gum wari du. Ate wa yaa ŋmarisi ŋa a dueni tintain paglaksa siye zuk a te mu.
23Ase nama ale ga wom lueluku legini po la, alege ate guuku zuk a dɛ ale bolim la, ni buuni po niŋdeerɔma meena a jam jam ka mi jigi. 24Ate ni yaa weeni ayen, <<Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la a sak ti wa zulaŋa ale wa pagrimu kama ate tama me a wom wa lueluk bolimu po. Jinla ti nya kama ayen nuru a baga a boro kama ase Wen a nin poom a biisi ale wa. 25Alege yɔgyɔgla de, ka boa ale soa ate tama a kpi? Bolim kpiemu dɛ ale dɛ ti, ate ti kpi ase tama ale a wom Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la lueluku ŋmana. 26Ka nuru wana ale diem wom Wen dii ale vua la lueluk ale ku a biisi bolim po ase tama la ale vua? 27Forisi moata ate fi wom dii meena ate Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la a weeni la. Ate fi a yaa le weeni ti dii ate Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la a weeni fu la. Tama ale wom abe ti va ŋa.>>
28Naawen a wom kama diipo ate nama a biisi ale mu la ate Naawen a yaa weeni mu ayen, <<M wom dii ate nuruma de a weeni fu la kama. Dii meena ate ba weeni la a nala kama. 29Mi dek a yaali kama ayen ba le chali mu yɔgsum ale ba suiniima meena abe ba ta m sinsaŋŋa diipo meena ate ku ale cheŋ nalimnyiini a te ba ale ba bisaŋa taam wuu!
30<<Cheŋ a ga weeni ba ate ba pilim a ŋman cheŋ ba viitaŋa po. 31Alege fi bo dela ale mi ate mi ale te fu wieŋa ale sinsaŋŋa meena ate fi ale sak ba ate ba ale va ŋa tɛŋ kaai po ate mi ale te ba la.>>
32Dila nyiŋla ni kpesi nidek ate ni nye dii ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a weeni ni la; ni kan viriŋ gala yaase juga. 33Cheŋ kauk kuui meena ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a weeni ni la, dii ale ku nye ate ni boro ale niaka ate nama a goa tɛŋ kaai ate nama ni tuesi la po a beni.

english_text:
The Most Important Commandment
Moses said to Israel:
1The Lord told me to give you these laws and teachings, so you can obey them in the land he is giving you. Soon you will cross the Jordan River and take that land. 2And if you and your descendants want to live a long time, you must always worship the Lord and obey his laws. 3Pay attention, Israel! Our ancestors worshiped the Lord, and he promised to give us this land that is rich with milk and honey. Be careful to obey him, and you will become a successful and powerful nation.
4 Listen, Israel! The Lord our God is the only true God! 5 So love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and strength. 6 Memorize his laws 7and tell them to your children over and over again. Talk about them all the time, whether you're at home or walking along the road or going to bed at night, or getting up in the morning. 8Write down copies and tie them to your wrists and foreheads to help you obey them. 9Write these laws on the door frames of your homes and on your town gates.
Worship Only the Lord
Moses said to Israel:
10 The Lord promised your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that he would give you this land. Now he will take you there and give you large towns, with good buildings that you didn't build, 11and houses full of good things that you didn't put there. The Lord will give you wells that you didn't have to dig, and vineyards and olive orchards that you didn't have to plant. But when you have eaten so much that you can't eat any more, 12don't forget it was the Lord who set you free from slavery and brought you out of Egypt. 13 Worship and obey the Lord your God with fear and trembling, and promise that you will be loyal to him.
14Don't have anything to do with gods that are worshiped by the nations around you. 15If you worship other gods, the Lord will be furious and wipe you off the face of the earth. The Lord your God is with you, 16 so don't try to make him prove that he can help you, as you did at Massah. 17Always obey the laws that the Lord has given you 18-19and live in a way that pleases him. Then you will be able to go in and take this good land from your enemies, just as he promised your ancestors.
20Someday your children will ask, “Why did the Lord give us these laws and teachings?”
21Then you will answer:
We were slaves of the king of Egypt, but the Lord used his great power and set us free. 22We saw him perform miracles and make horrible things happen to the king, his officials, and everyone else. 23The Lord rescued us from Egypt, so he could bring us into this land, as he had promised our ancestors. 24-25That's why the Lord our God demands that we obey his laws and worship him with fear and trembling. And if we do, he will protect us and help us be successful.
translation_text:
1Sinsaŋŋa ale wieŋa de ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a weeni ayen mi a sak ni ate ni kpesi a va ŋa tɛŋ kaai po ate ni za ni gaam Jodan benni a taam ka po la; 2dila ale ku basi ate nama ale ni bisaŋa ale ni ŋaaŋsaŋa a chali Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la yɔgsum diipo meena ate ni vua ale ta wa ŋmarisika ale wa wieŋa meena ate mi a te ni la ate ni goa tɛŋka zuk a beni. 3Ni wom de Izirali demma, abe ni kpesi nidek ate ni wom dii ale ku nye ate wari meena a cheŋ nalimnyiini ate ni piisi tɛŋ kaai po ate biisim ale siita a boro la, ase Naawen ni kokpieŋsaŋa Wenni ale jam puulim ale ni la.
4Ni wom de Izirali demma: Naawen ka ti Wen. Naawen ka dinyi. 5Yaali Naawen dii ale ka fi Wen la ale fi suinum meena ale fi chiik meena ale fi pagrim meena. 6Sinsaŋŋa de ate mi a te ni jinla de la a magsi ŋa bo ka ni suiniimaŋa po. 7Ni pai ŋa a te ni bisaŋa. Ni a biisi ŋa wie ase ni ale bo yeri yaase nama a nin bo suitaŋa po a cheŋ yaase ni doa yaase ni yiti. 8Ni bobi ŋa ni nisimaŋa nyiŋ ase daana la abe ni pai ŋa a mag ni deeŋa nyiŋ. 9Ni ŋmarisiŋa a dueni ni tuataŋa nyiŋ ale ni nansuiŋtaŋa nyiŋ.
10Ase Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale ta ni a jam tɛŋka po la wa pɛ kama ale ni kokpieŋsaŋa Abrayam ale Aizik ale Jekob ayen wa te ni tɛŋ kaai ale zuak ate daa nama ale se ya, 11Yie ŋaai ate ŋanmaŋsa meena a sueri ŋa ale daa nama ale pai ba a nyoro, vili ŋaai ate mama an tu ŋa, tali tii ate nama an bori jaab ti po ate nama a yaa dan dɛ a chak, 12Ni be kpesi nidek ate ni kan baŋ Naawen, waai ale ta ni a nyini Ejipiti yontini tɛŋka po a nyini la wari ya.
13Chali Naawen dii ale ka fi Wen la nyiini, puusi te wala nyiini abe fi nye ni pɛka wa yuenni nyiŋ. 14Kan va wen yona, nuru baai ale bo ale ni la wenaŋa, 15ale Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la, waai ale bo ale ni la, ka nyuri dɛka Wen ate ni dan va wen yona wa sui ale puuri ale ni ate wa le kaasi ni tɛŋka de po. 16Be kan nye Naawen ni Wenni a nya ase ni ale jam a nye dii Massaya la. 17Ni be seba ate ni ta sinsaŋŋa abe ni a teeri wie ŋaai ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a te ni la. 18Ni nye dii ale magsi ale nala mɛ la ate Naawen a basi ate wari meena cheŋ nalimnyiini a te ni ate ni cheŋ a ga tuesi tɛŋ maŋ kaai ate Naawen a puulim ale pɛ ale ni kokpieŋsaŋa la, 19ale yiak ni dachaasaŋa meena, ase Naawen ale weeni ni la?>>
20Chum diipo fi biik a dan bek fu ayen, wieŋa de ale sinsaŋŋa de ate Naawen ti Wenni a te ni la kiri ale boa?>> 21Weeni wa ayen, <<Tama a jam ka yɔm a te Faaro Ejipiti tɛŋka po, alege Naawen a yeeri ti Ejipiti po a ta nyini ale wa pagrimu. 22Naawen a tom ka wakinkagla ale wakperikaliisa, sii ale zuak a ta va Ejipiti ale Faaro ale wa yenni meena tama nimbie po. 23Alege wa ta ti a nyini dula kama a jam ayen wa te ti tɛŋ kaai ate wa puulim ale pɛ ale ti kokpieŋsaŋa la. 24Naawen a weeni ti kama ayen ti va abe ti a zuli sinsaŋŋa de meena abe ti a chali Naawen ti Wenni yɔgsum, dii ale ku basi ate ti nya niaka abe wa te ti vua ase ku ale ka dii jinla de la. 25Ase ti dan kpesi tidek a va Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la sinsaŋŋa de meena ase wa ale weeni diila, kula ale chim ti wayɔrisima.>>

english_text:
Force the Other Nations Out of the Land
(Exodus 34.11-16)
Moses said:
1 People of Israel, the Lord your God will help you take the land of the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. These seven nations have more people and are stronger than Israel, but when you attack them, 2the Lord will force them out of the land. Then you must destroy them without mercy. Don't make any peace treaties with them, 3and don't let your sons and daughters marry any of them. 4If you do, those people will lead your descendants to worship other gods and to turn their backs on the Lord. That will make him very angry, and he will quickly destroy Israel.
5 So when you conquer these nations, tear down the altars where they worship their gods. Break up their sacred stones, cut down the poles that they use in worshiping the goddess Asherah, and throw their idols in the fire.
The Lord's Chosen People
Moses said:
6 Israel, you are the chosen people of the Lord your God. There are many nations on this earth, but he chose only Israel to be his very own. 7You were the weakest of all nations, 8but the Lord chose you because he loves you and because he had made a promise to your ancestors. Then with his mighty arm, he rescued you from the king of Egypt, who had made you his slaves.
9 You know that the Lord your God is the only true God. So love him and obey his commands, and he will faithfully keep his agreement with you and your descendants for a thousand generations. 10But if you turn against the Lord, he will quickly destroy you. 11So be sure to obey his laws and teachings I am giving you today.
The Lord Will Bless You if You Obey
(Deuteronomy 28.1-14; Leviticus 26.3-13)
Moses said to Israel:
12 If you completely obey these laws, the Lord your God will be loyal and keep the agreement he made with you, just as he promised our ancestors. 13The Lord will love you and bless you by giving you many children and plenty of food, wine, and olive oil. Your herds of cattle will have many calves, and your flocks of sheep will have many lambs. 14God will bless you more than any other nation—your families will grow and your livestock increase. 15You will no longer suffer with the same horrible diseases that you sometimes had in Egypt. You will be healthy, but the Lord will make your enemies suffer from those diseases.
Destroy the Nations and Their Gods
Moses said to Israel:
16When the Lord helps you defeat your enemies, you must destroy them without pity! And don't get trapped into worshiping their gods.
17You may be thinking, “How can we destroy these nations? They are more powerful than we are.” 18But stop worrying! Just remember what the Lord your God did to Egypt and its king. 19You saw how the Lord used his tremendous power to work great miracles and bring you out of Egypt. And he will again work miracles for you when you face these enemies you fear so much. 20Some of them may try to survive by hiding from you, but the Lord will make them panic, and soon they will be dead. 21So don't be frightened when you meet them in battle. The Lord your God is great and fearsome, and he will fight at your side.
22As you attack these nations, the Lord will force them out little by little. He won't let you get rid of them all at once—if he did, there wouldn't be enough people living in the land to keep down the number of wild animals. 23-24But when you attack your enemies, the Lord will make them panic, and you will easily destroy them. You will defeat their kings one after another until they are gone, and no one will remember they ever lived.
25After you conquer a nation, burn their idols. Don't get trapped into wanting the silver or gold on an idol. Even the metal on an idol is disgusting to the Lord, 26so destroy it. If you bring it home with you, both you and your house will be destroyed. Stay away from those disgusting idols!
translation_text:
1Ase Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a dan ta ni a jam tɛŋ kaai po ate ni a jo ni soa la, ale yiak tɛŋ sii ale piisi la ate si nyini. Tɛŋ sila abe le Yit demma ale Girgas demma ale Amori demma ale Keenan demma ale Perizzi demma ale Yivi demma ale Jebus demma, tɛŋsaŋa de siyopɔiwa a zuak kama ale pagra a gaam ni. 2Ase Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a yaa dan pai ba a nyo ni nisima po ate ni nya pagrim ba zuk ku a magsi kama ayen ni ko ba. Ni kan nye nɔiyeŋ ale ba yaase ni ta jiirim ale ba. 3Ni kan faari ba liema. Ni kan pai ni liema a yalisi ba bisaŋa yaase ni faari ba liema a te ni bisaŋa, 4ale ba ale basi ate ni bisaŋa a basi mi vaka be ba a kaab bɔgluk yonta, ate Naawen sui a puuri ale ni ate wa ko ni nwuli. 5Dii ale magsi ni nye bala ale nna: Ni kaasi ba kuŋkuŋtaŋa abe ni ŋɔriŋ ba bɔgluk tintanaŋa, abe ni kaasi Asera nipok bɔglukku abe ni ju ba bɔgtaŋa ale bolim. 6Ale nama ka nuru weleŋsa a te Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la. Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a lueri ni kama a ta nyini nuruba meena po tɛŋka zuk de ayen wa soa ni ase tuilum nuruba la.
7Naawen an sak wa yaalika ale lueri ni ayen ka ni piisi a gaam nuruba ba chaab nyiŋŋa. Ka ni ale sum fiisa nuruma meena po la. 8Alege ku abe le ka diila ale nna, ate wa yaa ta wa ale nye pɛka ale ni kokpieŋsaŋa a ta ni a jam la wadek pagrim ale da tuesi ni yɔntini tɛŋka Ejipiti ale ka Naawa Faaro pagrimu po a nyini la. 9Yɔgyɔgla de, ni be seba ayen Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ka Wen; Wa ka Naawen dii ale ta wensie, ale ta wa nɔiyeŋka ale wa ŋmanteka a ta paari buura tusa baai ale a yaali wa la. 10Alege baai ale kisi wa la wa ale tuni ba ale kaasuŋ ba nina po. Wa kan beni abe wa tuni baai ale kisi wa la ba nina po. 11Dila nyiŋla, ni kpesi nidek a va wieŋa ale sinsaŋŋa ate mi a te ni jinla de la.
12Ase ni dan kpesi nidek a va buusaŋa de nalimnyiini ayen Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale ta wa nɔiyeŋka ale wa ŋmanteka ate wa nye ale ni la kama ase wa ale pɛ ale ni kokpieŋsaŋa diila. 13Wa ale yaali ni abe wa niak ni abe wa basi ate ni piisi mɛ. Wa ale niak ni ale bisa abe wa niak ni kpari ŋantaŋa ale ni da paalika ale ni kpaamu. Wa le ŋman niak ni ale niiga ale piisa. Wa le te ni niaka de meena kama wa ale puulim dii ale ni kokpieŋsaŋa tɛŋka po ayen wa te ni la. 14Nama ale nya niaka a gaam nuru yonta; nama nidoama yaase ni nipooma waai mɛ la a kan chim kiriga yaase ni duŋsaŋa a kan biak bisa. 15Naawen ale yeeri ni a ta nyini tueta meena po a nyini. Wa kan basi ate nyiŋtuila ŋaai ate ni seba ŋa nɔi po Ejipiti tɛŋka po la a yik ni. Alege wa ale basi ate ŋa yik ka baai ale kisi ni la. 16Ni ko nuru baai meena ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a pai te ni la. Ni kan sak jiirim ale ba yaase ni maari a kaab ba bɔgtaŋa ale dila ale chim ka baruk a te ni.
17Da dii dai ni ale weeni nidek ayen, <<Tɛŋsaŋa de demma a pagra a gaam tama ale ka diila kama. Tama a yaali ti nye ka sɛ a yiak ba?>> 18Alege ni kan chali ba yɔgsummoa; ni teeri nalimnyiini dii ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a nye Faaro ale Ejipiti demma meena la. 19Ni jam nya kama ale dek nina nyenya kpieŋ kaai ale wakperikaliik sii ale wakinkagla ŋaai ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a tom ale pagrim a ta ni a nyini Ejipiti po a nyini la. Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale nye nuru baai meena ate nama a chali ba yɔgsum la ka dila dekdega.
20Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale tom see ate ŋa cheŋ ba po ate baai le ba vuugi a chali suk la a ga kpi meena. 21Ni kan chali ba yɔgsummoa, ale Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la waai ale bo ale ni la ka Wen dii ale zuak. 22Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale yiak tɛŋsaŋa de meena maga maga a basi te ni. Ni kan baga a deri yiak ba meena dila bunyi. Ni dan nye dila gɔi duŋsaŋa ale piisi a gilim ni. 23Alege Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale pai ba a nyo ni nisima po abe wa basi ate butimka a jam ba po a pai ba nyo ni nisima po ate ni kaasi ba meena. 24Wa le pai ba nalimaŋa a nyo ni nisima po ate ba yueŋa a kan ŋman bo tɛŋzuk de. Waai a kan baga a zaani ale ni; ni ale kaasi ba. 25Ba bɔgtaŋa a magsi ka ni ju ti ale bolim. Ni kan pai kpanaŋa ale ligmɔniŋka ale bo bɔgtaŋa zuk la. Ni be kan pai ba a ta ni dega, ku le chim baruk a te ni, ale ku ta ka daanika a te Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la. 26Ni be kan ta bɔgtaŋa de kuui a jam ni yeeŋa, ni dan nye dila kika sii ale cheen ba jigi la ale jam nama mɛ jigi. Ku a magsi ka ni a kisi abe le zɛri ba bɔgtaŋa. Ni yeeri ba a ju.

english_text:
The Lord Takes Care of You
Moses said:
1Israel, do you want to go into the land the Lord promised your ancestors? Do you want to capture it, live there, and become a powerful nation? Then be sure to obey every command I am giving you.
2Don't forget how the Lord your God has led you through the desert for the past 40 years. He wanted to find out if you were truly willing to obey him and depend on him, 3 so he made you go hungry. Then he gave you manna, a kind of food that you and your ancestors had never even heard about. The Lord was teaching you that people need more than food to live—they need every word that the Lord has spoken.
4Over the past 40 years, your clothing hasn't worn out, and your feet haven't swollen. 5 So keep in mind that the Lord has been correcting you, just as parents correct their children. 6Obey the commands the Lord your God has given you and worship him with fear and trembling.
7The Lord your God is bringing you into a good land with streams that flow from springs in the valleys and hills. 8-9You can dig for copper in those hills, and the stones are made of iron ore. And you won't go hungry. Wheat and barley fields are everywhere, and so are vineyards and orchards full of fig, pomegranate, and olive trees, and there is plenty of honey.
Don't Forget the Lord
Moses said to Israel:
10After you eat and are full, give praise to the Lord your God for the good land he gave you. 11 Make sure that you never forget the Lord or disobey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today. If you always obey them, 12you will have plenty to eat, and you will build good houses to live in. 13You will get more and more cattle, sheep, silver, gold, and other possessions.
14But when all this happens, don't be proud! Don't forget that you were once slaves in Egypt and that it was the Lord who set you free. 15Remember how he led you in that huge and frightening desert where poisonous snakes and scorpions live. There was no water, but the Lord split open a rock, and water poured out so you could drink. 16He also gave you manna, a kind of food your ancestors had never even heard about. The Lord was testing you to make you trust him, so that later on he could be good to you.
17When you become successful, don't say, “I'm rich, and I've earned it all myself.” 18Instead, remember that the Lord your God gives you the strength to make a living. That's how he keeps the promise he made to your ancestors.
19-20But I'm warning you—if you forget the Lord your God and worship other gods, the Lord will destroy you, just as he destroyed the nations you fought.
translation_text:
1Ni be va wa dii ate mi a pai a te ni jinla de la, dii ale ku basi ate ni vua abe ni piisi a jo tɛŋ kaai po ate Naawen a pɛ ale ni kokpieŋsaŋa ayen wa ale pai ka a te ni ate ni soa la. 2Ni a teeri Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale nye dii a te ni diipo ate ni jam bo gɔnni po a paari bena pisinaansiwa la ayen ni yik nidek ale nye ni mɛ ayen wa nya ase ni suiniimaŋa ka sɛ, abe ni le ta wa wieŋa yaase ni kan ta ŋa. 3Wa jam te ni yik nidek a basi ate kɔm a yik ni ale ŋman te ni ŋandiin tii ate ba a wi ayen, wenzuk ŋandiinta la ate ni dɛ, ŋandiin tii ate ni poom zɛ ni kokpieŋsaŋa mɛ a jam zɛ la, ate kula a sak ayen nurubiik an boro ka ŋandiinta nyiini nyiŋŋa alege ka wa dii meena ale nyini Naawen nɔi po a nyini la. 4Ni kɔlimaŋa ate ni jam jo la an jam cheeri ya ni naŋsaŋa mɛ an jam fuusi ya diipo ate ni jam bo gɔnni po a paari bena pisinaansiwa la. 5Ni be a seba ni suiniimaŋa po ayen ase nuru ale a dari wa biik tuiri diila, Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la mɛ ale dari nama mɛ tue ka dila.
6Ni a teeri Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la wieŋa, abe ni a va wa suitaŋa abe ni a zuli wa. 7Nama Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a ta ni cheena ka tɛŋ naliŋ kaai ale ta buboalisa ale bela ate nyiam a bo ŋa po, ale ta vila vaasaŋa po ale guutaŋa zuima; 8ale ta ŋandiinta tɔgatɔga, ale ti sii ale a yɔni yɔna ale kinkaŋsa ale ti sii yɔna ale a te kpaam la, siita mɛ a maa boro kama, 9ka tɛŋ kaai ate ŋandiinta a ka kɔm ka po ni kan yaali jaaboa; ka ka tɛŋ kaai ate pinaŋa a chim kuta ate ni baga a tu a yeeri kutuk mɔnta guutaŋa zuk.
10Ate ni yaa dan dɛ chak, ni pak Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la wa ale pai tɛŋ naliŋka a te ni la nyiŋ. 11Ni be kpesi nidek nalimnyiini ate ni kan baŋ Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la wari ya yaase wa wieŋa ale wa buusaŋa ale wa ŋmarisika ate mi a te ni jinla de la. 12Ase ni be a dan dɛ chak ale sɛ yie maŋsa a bo ŋa po, 13yaase ni niiŋa ale ni piisaŋa ale ni kpanaŋa ale ni ligmɔniŋka ale ni ŋanta mbala meena a dan piisi a gum du, 14ni be a seba ate ni kan ta kanjanta abe ni baŋ Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la wie, waai ale vari ni a ta nyini Ejipiti po a nyini tɛŋ kaai ate ni jam boro ase yɔm la. 15Wa ta ni a nyini gɔi kpienni po kauk kuui ate waapiisa ale nuenta a boro la a nyini, kauk kuui ate nyanyuila a boro alege tɛŋka mɛ a ko. Wa jam basi ate nyiam a nyini piuŋ pagrik po a nyini ate nama a nyu. 16Wa te ni <wenzuk ŋandiinta> gɔnni po ate ni dɛ baai ate ni kokpieŋsaŋa a poom zɛ ba la ale nye ni nya ayen ni yik nidek ate kpeglimka abe wari meena a cheŋ nalimnyiini a te ni. 17Da dii dai ni ale weeni nidek kama ayen, <<Mi pagrimu ale m nisima tuima nyiŋ ale soa ate mi a nya ŋanta. 18Alege ni a teeri Naawen ni Wenni, ale ka wa la ale ni pagrim ate ni ta ŋanta, ni be ta wa nɔiyeŋka kaai ate wa pɛ ale ni kokpieŋsaŋa la ase ku ale ka dii jinla de la.
19Ase ni dan baŋ Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la wie ale va bɔgluk yonta a koori tɛŋ a zuli ti, mi a weeni ni kama jinla de m za m kaasi ni kama. 20Ase tɛŋ sii ate Naawen a kaasi ate ni nya la, wa le kaasi nama mɛ ka dila ase nama a nin kan a zuli Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la.

english_text:
Why the Lord Will Help Israel
Moses said:
1Israel, listen to me! You will soon cross the Jordan River and go into the land to force out the nations that live there. They are more powerful than you are, and the walls around their cities reach to the sky. 2Some of these nations are descendants of the Anakim. You know how tall and strong they are, and you've heard that no one can defeat them in battle. 3But the Lord your God has promised to go ahead of you, like a raging fire burning everything in its path. So when you attack your enemies, it will be easy for you to destroy them and take their land.
4-6After the Lord helps you wipe out these nations and conquer their land, don't think he did it because you are such good people. You aren't good—you are stubborn! No, the Lord is going to help you, because the nations that live there are evil, and because he wants to keep the promise he made to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
When Israel Made an Idol
(Exodus 32)
Moses said to Israel:
7Don't ever forget how you kept rebelling and making the Lord angry the whole time you were in the desert. You rebelled from the day you left Egypt until the day you arrived here.
8At Mount Sinai you made the Lord so angry that he was going to destroy you. 9-11 It happened during those 40 days and nights that I was on the mountain, without anything to eat or drink. He had told me to come up there so he could give me the agreement he made with us. And this agreement was actually the same Ten Commandments he had announced to you when he spoke from the fire on the mountain. The Lord had written them on two flat stones with his own hand. But after giving me the two stones, 12he said:
Moses, hurry down the mountain to those people you led out of Egypt. They have already disobeyed me and committed the terrible sin of making an idol.
13I've been watching the Israelites, and I've seen how stubborn and rebellious they are. 14So don't try to stop me! I am going to wipe them out, and no one on earth will remember they ever lived. Then I will let your descendants become an even bigger and more powerful nation than Israel.
Moses said:
15Fire was raging on the mountaintop as I went back down, carrying the two stones with the commandments on them. 16I saw how quickly you had sinned and disobeyed the Lord your God. There you were, worshiping the metal idol you had made in the shape of a calf. 17So I threw down the two stones and smashed them before your very eyes.
18-20I bowed down at the place of worship and prayed to the Lord, without eating or drinking for 40 days and nights. You had committed a terrible sin by making that idol, and the Lord hated what you had done. He was angry enough to destroy all of you and Aaron as well. So I prayed for you and Aaron as I had done before, and this time the Lord answered my prayers.
21It was a sin for you to make that idol, so I threw it into the fire to melt it down. Then I took the lump of gold, ground it into powder, and threw the powder into the stream flowing down the mountain.
22 You also made the Lord angry when you were staying at Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth-Hattaavah. 23 Then at Kadesh-Barnea the Lord said, “I am giving you the land, so go ahead and take it!” But since you didn't trust the Lord, you rebelled and disobeyed his command. 24In fact, you've rebelled against the Lord for as long as he has known you.
25After you had made the idol in the shape of a calf, the Lord said he was going to destroy you. So I lay face down in front of the Lord for 40 days and nights 26and prayed:
Our Lord, please don't wipe out your people. You used your great power to rescue them from Egypt and to make them your very own. 27Israel's ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob obeyed you faithfully. Think about them, and not about Israel's stubbornness, evil, and sin. 28If you destroy your people, the Egyptians will say, “The Lord promised to give Israel land, but he wasn't powerful enough to keep his promise. In fact, he hated them so much that he took them into the desert and killed them.” 29But you, our Lord, chose the people of Israel to be your own, and with your mighty power you rescued them from Egypt.
translation_text:
1Ni wom, Izirali demma. Ni moata ayen ni lo Jodan benni a jueli kama a ga tuesi tɛŋ sii ale zuak ale pagra a gaam ni ate tɛŋsaŋa parisaŋa a wɔŋa a tiri chiŋmaaŋa la. 2Nuruma a pagra kama ale wɔŋa mɛ. Anak buuni ale la: nama a seba ba nɔi po kama ale ŋman wom ba ale weeni ayen, <<Ka wana ale baga a zaani ale Anak demma?>> 3Alege ni be a seba a chak ayen jinla Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale waai ale wa dɛ niŋ a lo jueli ase bolim la a dɛ ba. Wa ale kaasi ba a ta ba a siŋ tɛŋ nama niŋ. Ate nama ale yiak ba ate ba nyini abe wa kaasi ba nwuli ase Naawen ale puulim dii ale ni la.
4Ase Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a dan ga yiak ba a nueri te ni, ni be kan weeni nidek ayen, <<Naawen a ta mi a jam dela ayen m tuesi tɛŋka de ka mi weleŋsa nyiŋŋa.>> Aaya, ka tɛŋ sila biemu nyiŋ ate Naawen a yaa yiak ba a basi te ni. 5Ku daa ni wayɔrisima yaase nama ale ka baai la nyiŋŋa ate ni a cheŋ ayen ni tuesi ba tɛŋka, alege ka tɛŋsaŋa de biemu nyiŋ ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a yiak ba a te ni ayen wa nye wa ale pɛ dii ale ni kokpieŋsaŋa Abrayam ale Aizik ale Jekob la. 6Ni be a ŋman miŋ chak ayen daa yen ka ni weleŋsa nyiŋŋa ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a yaali ayen wa pai tɛŋ naliŋ ka de a te ni nama mɛ ka tuikpari nyam.
7Ni a teeri nya kude abe ni kan baŋ nama ale jam nye dii ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la sui a puuri ale ni gɔnni po la. A zaani dai dii danni ate nama a basi Ejipiti a jam paari dela la, ni jam a zɛri Naawen nɔi kama. 8Yoreb guuku zuk, ni nye ate Naawen sui a yiti ate wa suinni a puuri nna yegayega ate wa a yaali ayen wa kaasi ni. 9Mi ale jam cheen guuku zuk ayen m tuesi tintain paglaksaŋa, sii ate Naawen a nye nɔiyeŋka ale ni la. Mi jam bo guuku zuk a paari ka daa pisinaansi ale yɔkta pisinaansi; mi an dɛ ŋandiinta yaase m nyu nyiamoa. 10Ate Naawen a yaa pai wadek nandub a ŋmarisi tintain paglaksa siye zuk a te mu. Ŋa zuk ka sinsak ŋaai meena ate Naawen a jam biisi ale ni a ta nyini bolimu po guuku zuk dai dila danni a te tigsuŋku la.
11Daa pisinaansi ale yɔkta pisinaansiwa kpeglim ka danni, Naawen a yaa jam pai tintain paglaksa siyewa a te mi, nɔiyeŋka tintain paglaksaŋa ale la. 12Naawen a yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Nye nwuli a siŋ tɛŋ dii nyiŋla fi nuruma baai ate fi ta ba a nyini Ejipiti po a nyini la a tom kaasi kama. Ba zɛri ka nna nwuli mi ale weeni ba ayen ba nye abe ba va m sinsaŋŋa la kama ale nye bɔgluk a te badek.>>
13Ate Naawen a yaa weeni mi ayen, <<M nya nuruma de kama, ba sum ka tuikpari nuruba. 14Dan ka mi nyiini, basi ate m ko ba abe m duisi, ba yueŋa tɛŋzuk a basi. Abe m basi ate fi chim tɛŋ kaai ale pagra piisi a gaam ba ale ka diila.
15Mi yaa viriŋ a nyini guuku zuk a siŋ tɛŋ alege guuku a kasim a dɛ ale bolim, alege ate nɔiyeŋka tintain paglaksa siyewa a bo m nisimaŋa po. 16Ase mi ale jam nya la, mi nya kama ale ni tom ka biem a kaasi Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la; ni mɛ ka bɔgluk a te nidek ate ku a nye ase naabiik la. Ni basi Naawen ale weeni ayen ni va diila kama nwuli. 17Mi yaa pai tintain paglaksaŋa siyewa ale bo m nisaŋa po la a yuk a basi ate si mobi yisayisa nama nimbie po.
18Mi yaa ŋman pilim lo tɛŋ Naawen niŋ daa pisinaansi ale yɔgta pisinaansi; mi an dɛ ŋandiinta m be an nyu nyiam mɛ nama ale nye biem buui la nyiŋ, nye kaai ale bie Naawen jigi ale kasim basi ate wa sui a puuri. 19M jam yɔgsa kama ale Naawen suipuurumu, dii nyiŋla wa suinni a jam a puuri ka nna yegayega ate wa a yaali ayen wa kaasi ni. Alege Naawen a ŋman wom mi puusaŋa. 20Ate Naawen sui a yaa jam a puuri ale Aaron ate wa a yaali ayen wa ko wa alege dila po mi jam puusi a te wa mɛ kama. 21M ŋman pai ni biemu jaamu, naabi kaai ate ni mɛ la a ju kama bolimu po a num ka nna lɔklɔk ase nyuŋ la a yuk nyuŋku a basi buboali kaai ale chali va guuku chiak a taam la po.
22Ni ŋman jam nye ate Naawen sui a puuri kama diipo ate ni jam bo Tabera ale Massaya ale Kibrot Yattaava la.
23Ase Naawen ale jam ta ni a nyini Kades Barnea a nyini la, Wa weeni ayen, <<Ni cheŋ a ga tuesi tɛŋ kaai ate mi a pai te ni la.>> Alege ate ni zɛri Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale weeni diila. Ni ka siaka ale wa ni be an wom wa nɔi mɛ. 24Nama a kasim a nye ka tukpari ale Naawen a zaani dii ate mi a seba ni la.
25Mi jam lo tɛŋ a puusi a te Naawen kama a paari daa pisinaansi ale yɔkta pisinaansi dii nyiŋla Naawen weeni kama ayen wa le kaasi ni. 26Mi puusi a te Naawen kama ayen, <<Nyɔnɔwa waai ale ka Naawen la kan kaasi fi nuruma, fidek nuru baai ate fi a da tuesi ale yeeri ba ale fidek pagrimu a ta nyini Ejipiti po a nyini la. 27Teeri fi tomteerɔma Abrayam ale Aizik ale Jekob. Kan nya nuruma tukpanni nyeka ale ba gaasaŋa ale ba biemu. 28Kan daa di tɛŋ sii ate fi a yeeri ti a ta nyini ba po a nyini la ale weeni ayen, <Naawen ale kan baga a ta ba a paari tɛŋ kaai ate wa puulim ayen wa te ba la ate wa kisi ba la nyiŋ ate wa ta ba a nyini peelim ayen wa ko ba gɔnni po.> 29Alege ba ka fi nuruba, fi ale soa ba ate fi ta ba nyini ale fidek nisimaŋa pagrimu.>>

english_text:
The Second Set of Commandments
(Exodus 34.1-10)
Moses said to the people:
1The Lord told me to chisel out two flat stones, just like the ones he had given me earlier. He also commanded me to make a wooden chest, then come up the mountain and meet with him. 2He told me that he would write on the new stones the same words he had written on the ones I broke, and that I could put these stones in this sacred chest.
3So I made a chest out of acacia wood, and I chiseled two flat stones like the ones I broke. Then I carried the stones up the mountain, 4where the Lord wrote the Ten Commandments on them, just as he had done the first time. The commandments were exactly what he had announced from the fire, when you were gathered at the mountain.
After the Lord returned the stones to me, 5I took them down the mountainside and put them in the chest, just as he had commanded. And they are still there.
Aaron Died
(Numbers 20.22-29)
Moses said to Israel:
6 Later we set up camp at the wells belonging to the descendants of Jaakan. Then we moved on and camped at Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried, and his son Eleazar became the priest. 7Next, we camped at Gudgodah and then at Jotbathah, where there are flowing streams.
The Levites Were Appointed To Carry the Chest
Moses said to Israel:
8 After I put the two stones in the sacred chest, the Lord chose the tribe of Levi, not only to carry the chest, but also to serve as his priests at the place of worship and to bless the other tribes in his name. And they still do these things. 9The Lord promised that he would always provide for the tribe of Levi, and that's why he won't give them any land, when he divides it among the other tribes.
The Lord Answered the Prayers of Moses
(Exodus 34.9,10,27-29)
Moses said to Israel:
10 When I had taken the second set of stones up the mountain, I spent 40 days and nights there, just as I had done before. Once again, the Lord answered my prayer and did not destroy you. 11Instead, he told me, “Moses, get ready to lead the people into the land that I promised their ancestors.”
What the Lord Wants
Moses said:
12People of Israel, what does the Lord your God want from you? The Lord wants you to respect and follow him, to love and serve him with all your heart and soul, 13and to obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today. Do this, and all will go well for you.
14Everything belongs to the Lord your God, not only the earth and everything on it, but also the sky and the highest heavens. 15Yet the Lord loved your ancestors and wanted them to belong to him. So he chose them and their descendants rather than any other nation, and today you are still his people.
16Remember your agreement with the Lord and stop being so stubborn. 17 The Lord your God is more powerful than all other gods and lords, and his tremendous power is to be feared. His decisions are always fair, and you cannot bribe him to change his mind. 18 The Lord defends the rights of orphans and widows. He cares for foreigners and gives them food and clothing. 19And you should also care for them, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
20Respect the Lord your God, be faithful, and serve only him, making promises in his name. 21Offer your praises to him, because you have seen him work such terrifying miracles for you.
22 When your ancestors went to live in Egypt, there were only 70 of them. But the Lord has blessed you, and now there are more of you than there are stars in the sky.
translation_text:
1Dila po Naawen a yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Peesi tintain paglaksa siye ase ŋaai ate fi liŋ ta la a jueli jam guuku zuk mi jigi. Mi ta tapaga dakari a jam. 2M le ŋmarisi tintain paglaksaŋa zuk wie ŋaai ate mi a liŋ ŋmarisi ate fi a mobi ŋa la ate fi a yaa pai ŋa a nyo dakanni po.
3Ate mi yaa pai siik daata a nye dakari ale peesi tintain paglaksaŋa siyewa ate ŋa a nye ase ŋaai ate mi a poom liŋ jam ta la, a yaa ta ŋa noa ŋayewa m nisimaŋa po a jueli guuku zuk. 4Naawen a yaa jam ŋmarisi tintain paglaksaŋa de siyewa zuk dii ate wa liŋ jam ŋmarisi la. Sinsaga piika ate wa jam pai te ni guuku zuk la a ta nyini bolimu po la, da dii danni ate ni meena a jam tigsi chaab ate Naawen a pai ŋa a te mu la. 5Mi yaa jam nyini guuku zuk a siŋ tɛŋ a pai tintain paglaksaŋa a nyo dakanni ate m nye la po, ase Naawen ale weeni mu diila, ŋa diem bo ka dula nna.
6Izirali demma a yaa jam basi viliŋa ate Jaakan demma a jam soa ate ŋa bo Mosera la. Dula jigini ate Aaron kpi ate ba gu wa, alege ate wa biika Eleaza a yaa jam chim kaabteerɔ. 7A nyini dula ba yaa jam cheŋ Gudgoda ale Jotbata tɛŋsaŋa kauk kuui ate nyiam a boro la. 8Dila po Naawen a lueri ka Livaima dɔkku po ayen ba ji Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni, a zaani wa niŋ a tom abe ba mooli niaka wa yuenni nyiŋ ase ba le diem a nye dii jinla de la. 9Dila ale soa ate Livaima a ka badek tɛŋ ba suataŋa ale bo kauk kuui la. Naawen ale ba ŋantaŋa ase Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ale weeni ba diila.
10Mi bo guuku zuk a paari ka daa pisinaansi ale yɔkta pisinaansi, ase mi ale liŋ jam nye diila ate Naawen a jam wom dila po ŋmana. Ku jam daa wa yaalika ayen wa kaasi ni. 11Naawen a weeni mi ayen m cheŋ, <<A ga dɛ nuruma niŋ, dii ale ku basi ate ba jo tɛŋ kaai po ate m puulim ale ba kokpieŋsaŋa ayen m le te ba la.
12Yɔgyɔgla de, Izirali demma, ka boa ate Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a yaali nama jigi ya? Ka nama a chali Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la yɔgsum ale a va wa suitaŋa meena ale a yaali wa abe le a va wa ale ni suiniima meena ale ni chiisa meena, 13abe ni a kpesi a zuli Naawen wieŋa ale wa ŋmarisika ate mi a te ni jinla de la dii ale nala a te ni la.
14Ka Naawen dii ale ka nama Naawen la ale soa wenŋmazukku ale tɛŋzuk de meena ale jaabuuri meena ale bo ka po la. 15Alege Naawen a diem sak wa yaalika ale ni kokpieŋsaŋa ale lueri ni ate ni buuni po ale gaam tɛŋsa meena ase ku ale ka dii jinla de la. 16Ni nye ni suiniimaŋa cheri abe ni basi tukpari tuima. 17Ale Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la ka wena meena Wen ale nyama meena Nyɔnɔ, Wen kpien dii ale zuak ate ba a chali wa mɛ. Waai ale ka a lugi wa be kan tuesi nuru jaaboa ale nye wari a te wa. 18Wa ale a maari baai ale kan ta koba la ale pukɔga ale a yaali nicham ale a te ba ŋandiinta ale kɔlima. 19Nama mɛ magsi kama ayen ni a yaali nichamma dii nyiŋla nama dek a jam ka nicham Ejipiti tɛŋka po. 20Ni a chali Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la abe ni a va wa. Ni kpesi a yik wa nalimnyiini abe ni a puulim wa yuenni nyiŋ. 21Ni a pak wa, wa ka ni Wen. Ni nya kama ale dek nina wakperikaliik sii ale wakinkagla ŋaai ate wa nye la. 22Ni kokpieŋsaŋa baai ale jam jo Ejipiti po la ba meena jam ka pisiyopɔi, alege Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la a basi kama ate ni piisi ase chiŋmarisaŋa ale bo wenŋmazukku po la.

english_text:
If You Are Loyal to the Lord, He Will Bless You
Moses said to Israel:
