Samson snapped the bowstrings, as though they were pieces of scorched string. The Philistines had not found out why Samson was so strong.
10“You lied and made me look like a fool,” Delilah said. “Now tell me. How can I really tie you up?”
11Samson answered, “Use some new ropes. If I'm tied up with ropes that have never been used, I'll be just as weak as anyone else.”
12Delilah got new ropes, and again some Philistines hid in the room. Then she tied up Samson's arms and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!”
Samson snapped the ropes as if they were threads.
13“You're still lying and making a fool of me,” Delilah said. “Tell me how I can tie you up!”
“My hair is in seven braids,” Samson replied. “If you weave my braids into the threads on a loom and nail the loom to a wall, then I will be as weak as anyone else.”
14While Samson was asleep, Delilah wove his braids into the threads on a loom and nailed the loom to a wall. Then she shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!”
Samson woke up and pulled the loom free from its posts in the ground and from the nails in the wall. Then he pulled his hair free from the woven cloth.
15“Samson,” Delilah said, “you claim to love me, but you don't mean it! You've made me look like a fool three times now, and you still haven't told me why you are so strong.” 16Delilah started nagging and pestering him day after day, until he couldn't stand it any longer.
17Finally, Samson told her the truth. “I have belonged to God ever since I was born, so my hair has never been cut. If it were ever cut off, my strength would leave me, and I would be as weak as anyone else.”
18Delilah realized that he was telling the truth. So she sent someone to tell the Philistine rulers, “Come to my house one more time. Samson has finally told me the truth.”
The Philistine rulers went to Delilah's house, and they brought along the silver they had promised her. 19Delilah had lulled Samson to sleep with his head resting in her lap. She signaled to one of the Philistine men as she began cutting off Samson's seven braids. And by the time she was finished, Samson's strength was gone. Delilah tied him up 20and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!”
Samson woke up and thought, “I'll break loose and escape, just as I always do.” He did not realize that the Lord had stopped helping him.
21The Philistines grabbed Samson and poked out his eyes. They took him to the prison in Gaza and chained him up. Then they put him to work, turning a millstone to grind grain. 22But they didn't cut his hair any more, so it started growing back.
23The Philistine rulers threw a big party and sacrificed a lot of animals to their god Dagon. The rulers said:
Samson was our enemy,
but our god Dagon
helped us capture him!
24-25Everyone there was having a good time, and they shouted, “Bring out Samson—he's still good for a few more laughs!”
The rulers had Samson brought from the prison, and when the people saw him, this is how they praised their god:
Samson ruined our crops
and killed our people.
He was our enemy,
but our god helped us
capture him.
They made fun of Samson for a while, then they told him to stand near the columns that supported the roof. 26A young man was leading Samson by the hand, and Samson said to him, “I need to lean against something. Take me over to the columns that hold up the roof.”
27The Philistine rulers were celebrating in a temple packed with people and with 3,000 more on the flat roof. They had all been watching Samson and making fun of him.
28Samson prayed, “Please remember me, Lord God. The Philistines poked out my eyes, but make me strong one last time, so I can take revenge for at least one of my eyes!”
29Samson was standing between the two middle columns that held up the roof. He felt around and found one column with his right hand, and the other with his left hand. 30Then he shouted, “Let me die with the Philistines!” He pushed against the columns as hard as he could, and the temple collapsed with the Philistine rulers and everyone else still inside. Samson killed more Philistines when he died than he had killed during his entire life.
31His brothers and the rest of his family went to Gaza and took his body back home. They buried him in his father's tomb, which was located between Zorah and Eshtaol.
Samson was a leader of Israel for 20 years.
translation_text:
1Dai yeŋ ate Samson yaa cheŋ Gaza, dula jigini wa yaa nya nidoa yaalik. Wa yaa jo a daliŋ yok ku la meena. 2Gaza demma yaa wom ayen, <<Samson a bo dela, ate ba yaa gilim jigini a doa yokku meena a limisi wa. Ba an jam cheŋ jigiya yokku meena ale weeni ayen, <<Saluik yokyokwa ti le ko wa.>>
3Alege Samson a jam doa ka dula a paari yok suŋsuŋ. Wa yaa ga yik tɛŋka nansuiŋku tuataŋa ale zaŋŋa ŋayewa a gum chaab a ŋɔriŋ ba meena. Wa jam zak ba ji ka ŋmankpala a ta jueli guuku ale tuk Yebron la zuk.
4Daa magadek ale taam la, wa yaa jam de nɔŋta ale nipok Sorek Viaka, wa yuei ale Delila. 5Filistia niŋdeerɔma yaa cheŋ wa jigi ayen, <<Nya de fi dan baga a paasi wa ate wa weeni wa ale nye dii a pagra la, ale ti le ti nye dii a nya pagrim wa zuk a bobi wa la. Tama wanyi meena ale te fu kpana ligbie tusidi ale kook (1,100).>>
6Ate Delila yaa weeni Samson ayen, <<Weeni mu fi ale nye dii a pagra dila la, ale ba le ba nye dii a nya pagrim fi zuk a bobi fu la.>> 7Samson yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Ase waai a dan bobi mi ale gie ŋaai ale yɔgsa la ŋayopɔi, m ni wobsa ase ka waai meena la.>>
8Baai ale a nya Filistia tɛŋka zuk la yaa ta gie yɔgsa ŋayopɔi a jam te wa ate wa pai ŋa a bobi wa. 9Nidoaba ale jam suk dɔk po. Delila yaa wi wa ayen Samson Filistia demma a cheen ba yik fu. Ate wa nye ate gieŋa a deri na gebi ase miik ale moata bolim ŋiak diila. Ba an jam baga a miŋ wa pagrimu kiri ya.
10Delila yaa weeni Samson ayen, <<Fi paasi mu, fi velim kama ale mi, jam de weeni mu ba le ba nye dii a bobi fu la.
11Ate wa weeni ayen, <<Ase waai a dan pai miisa sii ale paala la a bobi mu sii ate ba an pai bobi ŋanta a nya la, m le wobsa ase ka waai meena la.>>
12Delila yaa pa miik paalisa a bobi wa, ale basi ate nuruma diem suk bo dɔkku po, wa yaa wi ayen, <<Samson Filistia demma a cheen ba yik fu. Ate wa ŋman gebi miisaŋa nna ase garuk miisa la.
13Delila a ŋman pilim weeni Samson ayen, <<Ale a najin fi diem a velim ale mu kama, weeni mu ba le ba nye dii a bobi fu la.>> Wa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Ase fi dan poori zuisaŋa m zukku po buyopɔi a panni ale garuk miisa maŋ chaab ase garuk la a pai zuk pein a kpi maŋ, m le wobsa ase ka waai meena la.>> Ase wa ale doa goa la, Delila yaa yik wa zuisaŋa a poori buyopɔi a panni si maŋ chaab, 14a yaa pai zuk pein a kpi. Wa ŋman wi wa ayen, <<Samson Filistia demma a cheen ba yik fu,>> ate wa yiti wa goomu po a dari ŋan baai ate Delila a pa bobi wa zuisaŋa la a gebi.
15Ate wa weeni wa ayen, <<Fi le nye ka sɛ a weeni ayen, mi a yaali fu, fi ale kan seba mi a chak la nyiŋŋa? Ku nɔi buta ale nna ate fi paasi mu an weeni mu fi pagrimu kiri ya.>> 16Wa kasim ta wa ka dila daa meena ate wa ga jiak.
17Dila wa yaa weeni wa wari meena ayen, <<Aaya, poniŋ a diem su mi zukku po nya ya, dii nyiŋla mi ka Naziri, waai ale gaari wadek a te Wen a nyini diipo ate ba biak mu la. Ba dan che m zukku m pagrimu ale nyini ate m le wobsa ase waai meena la.>>
18Ase Delila ale nya ale wa weeni wa wari meena la, wa yaa tom weeni Filistia niŋdeerɔma ayen, <<Ni ŋman jam bunyi dekki, wa weeni mu wari meena kama, ate Filistia niŋdeerɔma a yaa pilim ŋman ale kpana ligbie. 19Ase nipowa ale ta wa, wa naŋsa zuk ate wa a goa la, wa yaa wi nidoa ayen wa che wa zuisa buyopɔiwa, a piilim baliŋ wa, ate wa pagrimu a basi wa.
20Wa yaa wi ayen, <<Samson, Filistia demma a cheen ba yik fu.>> Wa yaa lak nina ale a poli ayen wa le yiti kama ase wa le poom liŋ a nye diila a kpaanti vari wadek a basi. Alege wa zɛ ayen Naawen a basi wa kama.
21Filistia demma yaa yik wa, a pusi wa ninaŋa ale ta wa a cheŋ Gaza. Ba jam pai ka kutuk mɔnuŋ chɔrima a bobi wa ate wa a num ŋanta likka dɔk po. 22Alege wa zuisaŋa yaa ŋman pilim a nyini ba le che si la ŋaaŋnyiŋ.
23Filistia demma yaa tigsi chaab ayen ba kaab a te ba wenni Dagon ale nye tigi ayen, <<Ti wenni a pa Samson ti dachiaka a nyo ti nisa po.
24Ase nuruma ale ga nya wa la, ba yaa pak ba wenni ayen, <<Ti wenni a pa ti dachiaka a nyo ti nisa po, waai ale basi ate tɛŋka a doa koruk ale tɔgri ti a piisi la.>>
25Ase ba sueŋa ale peenti la, ba yaa na ayen, <<Ni ta Samson jam ate wa a daliŋ ti. Ba yaa wi Samson ate wa nyini likka dɔkku po a nyini a daliŋ ba. Ase ba le pa wa zaani zaŋŋa suŋsuŋ la, 26Samson yaa weeni waai ale a dari wa la ayen, <<Basi ate m zaani juijui ate m baga a yik zaŋŋa ale chɔgsi yenni a ta la, ate m sali ŋa. 27Dɔkku nidoaba ale nipooba ale jam sueri ku, Filistia tɛŋka niŋdeerɔma meena a jam boro kama, baai mɛ ale jam bo gboŋku zuk la jam ka nidoaba ale nipooba tusa ŋata (3,000) ale jam a nya Samson ale a nye diila. 28Samson yaa puusi te Naawen ayen, <<M Nyɔnɔwa waai ale ka Naawen yaa, teeri m wie. Wen, mi a saalim ŋman te mu pagrim maga dega ate m tuni Filistia demma m nina ŋayewa nyiŋ. 29Samson yaa forisi paari suŋsuŋ zaŋŋa ŋayewa ale ta dɔkku a za la. Wa jam pai ka juga a ji dinyi alege pa wa gala mɛ a ji ndila, 30Samson jam weeni kama ayen, <<Basi ate mi kpi ale Filistia demma,>> ale tusi ale wa pagrim meena ate dɔkku ale lo baai ale a nya Filistia demma zuk la ale nurubiika meena ale jam bo ku po la zuk. Dila danni wa jam ko nuruba a piisi gaam wa le jam vua a ko baai la kama.
31Ate wa suataŋa ale wa kowa dɔkdemma meena yaa cheŋ ba pa wa. Ba jam ta wa jam gu ka Zoraya ale Estaol suŋsuŋ, Manoa wa kowa boosuku po. Wa jam de Izirali demma niŋ ka bena pisiye.

english_text:
Micah Makes Idols and Hires a Priest
1Micah belonged to the Ephraim tribe and lived in the hill country. 2One day he told his mother, “Do you remember those 1,100 pieces of silver that were stolen from you? I was there when you put a curse on whoever stole them. Well, I'm the one who did it.”
His mother answered, “I pray that the Lord will bless you, my son.”
3-4Micah returned the silver to his mother, and she said, “I give this silver to the Lord, so my son can use it to make an idol.” Turning to her son, she said, “Micah, now the silver belongs to you.”
But Micah handed it back to his mother. She took 200 pieces of the silver and gave them to a silver worker, who made them into an idol. They kept the idol in Micah's house. 5He had a shrine for worshiping God there at his home, and he had made some idols and a sacred priestly vest. Micah chose one of his own sons to be the priest for his shrine.
6 This was before kings ruled Israel, so all the Israelites did whatever they thought was right.
7-8One day a young Levite came to Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim. He had been staying with one of the clans of Judah in Bethlehem, but he had left Bethlehem to find a new place to live where he could be a priest.
9“Where are you from?” Micah asked.
“I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,” the man answered, “and I'm on my way to find a new place to live.”
10Micah said, “Why don't you stay here with me? You can be my priest and tell me what God wants me to do. Every year I'll give you ten pieces of silver and one complete set of clothes, and I'll provide all your food.”
The young man went for a walk, 11-12then he agreed to stay with Micah and be his priest. He lived in Micah's house, and Micah treated him like one of his own sons. 13Micah said, “I have a Levite as my own priest. Now I know that the Lord will be kind to me.”
translation_text:
1Yɔgyɔgla de nuru, wa yuei a jam le Maika a nyini Ɛfraim tɛŋka ate guuta a bo ka po la, 2a yaa weeni wa mawa ayen, <<Kpana ligbie tusidi ale kook (1,100) ate ba tuesi fi jigi ate dila a basi ate fi ka kikaasa la, ŋa boka mi jigi, ka mi ale pai ŋa.>> Ate wa mawa yaa weeni ayen, <<Naawen a niak fu m nidoabili yaa.>> 3Ase wa le ŋman pilim pai kpana ligbie tusidi ale kook (1,100) a te wa mawa la, wa weeni ayen, <<Mi pa kpanaŋa de a te Naawen m nidoabinni nyiŋ ate wa nye jameem ale bɔgluk. Mi ale pilim pa ku a te fu.>>
4Wa le ta ligraŋa a ŋman ga te wa mawa la, wa yaa gaari kpana ligbie kobsiye a te choabiik ate wa kuri ŋa a nye jameem ale bɔgluk. Ate ba pa ti a zaani Maika yenni po. 5Maika wade a jam ta ka tangbain a nye garuk geli ale bɔgta a bobi wa nidoabilisaŋa wanyi ase kaabteerɔ la. 6Da ŋala po Izirali demma a jam ka naaba. Waai meena a jam a nye ka wa ale a yaali diila.
7Livai bi paalik ale jam nyini Betiliyem ale bo Juda po la, waai ale jam bo Juda yezukku po la, 8yaa basi tɛŋ kpieŋka ale a gisi jigi ayen wa boro. Wa le bo suiku po a cheŋ la, wa yaa paari Maika yenni ale bo Ɛfraim tɛŋka ate guutaŋa a bo ka po la.
9Maika yaa bek wa ayen, <<Fi nyini ka be? Ate wa mɛ a tulisi ayen, <<Mi ka Livai a nyini Betiliyem ale bo Juda po la, mi a gisi ka jigi ayen m boro.>>
10Maika yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Boro ale mi a chim m ko ale m kaabteerɔ, ate mi a te fi kpana ligbie pi bein meena, fi gatta ale ŋandiinta mi ale nya dila zuk. 11Ate Livaiwa yaa siak a boro ale wa. Nidoa paalika de a jam boro kama ase nuruwa dek nidoabili la. 12Maika a sum jam basi ate Livaiwa de a chim ka wa kaabteerɔ ale bo wa yenni po. 13Ate Maika a weeni ayen, <<Mi seba ayen Naawen a nala kama a te mi, Livaiwa ale chim m kaabteerɔ la nyiŋ.>>

english_text:
1These things happened before kings ruled Israel.
The Tribe of Dan Takes Micah's Priest and Idols
About this time, the tribe of Dan was looking for a place to live. The other tribes had land, but the people of Dan did not really have any to call their own. 2The tribe chose five warriors to represent their clans and told them, “Go and find some land where we can live.”
The warriors left the area of Zorah and Eshtaol and went into the hill country of Ephraim. One night they stayed at Micah's house, 3because they heard the young Levite talking, and they knew from his accent that he was from the south. They asked him, “What are you doing here? Who brought you here?”
4The Levite replied, “Micah hired me as his priest.” Then he told them how well Micah had treated him.
5“Please talk to God for us,” the men said. “Ask God if we will be successful in what we are trying to do.”
6“Don't worry,” answered the priest. “The Lord is pleased with what you are doing.”
7The five men left and went to the town of Laish, whose people were from Sidon, but Sidon was too far away to protect them. Even though their town had no walls, the people thought they were safe from attack. So they had not asked anyone else for protection, which meant that the tribe of Dan could easily take over Laish.
8The five men went back to Zorah and Eshtaol, where their relatives asked, “Did you find any land?”
9-10“Let's go!” the five men said. “We saw some very good land with enough room for all of us, and it has everything we will ever need. What are you waiting for? Let's attack and take it. You'll find that the people think they're safe, but God is giving the land to us.”
11Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan strapped on their weapons and left Zorah and Eshtaol with their families. 12One night they camped near Kiriath-Jearim in the territory of Judah, and that's why the place just west of Kiriath-Jearim is still known as Dan's Camp. 13Then they went into the hill country of Ephraim.
When they came close to Micah's house, 14the five men who had been spies asked the other warriors, “Did you know that someone in this village has several idols and a sacred priestly vest? What do you think we should do about it?”
15-18The 600 warriors left the road and went to the house on Micah's property where the young Levite priest lived. They stood at the gate and greeted the priest. Meanwhile, the five men who had been there before went into Micah's house and took the sacred priestly vest and the idols.
“Hey!” the priest shouted. “What do you think you're doing?”
19“Quiet!” the men said. “Keep your mouth shut and listen. Why don't you come with us and be our priest, so you can tell us what God wants us to do? You could stay here and be a priest for one man's family, but wouldn't you rather be the priest for a clan or even a whole tribe of Israel?”
20The priest really liked that idea. So he took the vest and the idols and joined the others 21from the tribe of Dan. Then they turned and left, after putting their children, their cattle, and the rest of their other possessions in front.
22They had traveled for some time before Micah asked his neighbors to help him get his things back. He and his men caught up with the people of Dan 23and shouted for them to stop.
They turned to face him and asked, “What's wrong? Why did you bring all these men?”
24Micah answered, “You know what's wrong. You stole the gods I made, and you took my priest. I don't have anything left.”
25“We don't want to hear any more about it,” the people of Dan said. “And if you make us angry, you'll only get yourself and your family killed.” 26After saying this, they turned and left.
Micah realized there was no way he could win a fight with them, and so he went back home.
The Tribe of Dan Captures Laish
27-28The tribe of Dan took Micah's priest and the things Micah had made, and headed for Laish, which was located in a valley controlled by the town of Beth-Rehob. Laish was defenseless, because it had no walls and was too far from Sidon for the Sidonians to help defend it. The leaders of Laish had not even asked nearby towns to help them in case of an attack.
The warriors from Dan made a surprise attack on Laish, killing everyone and burning it down. Then they rebuilt the town and settled there themselves. 29But they named it Dan, after one of Israel's sons, who was the ancestor of their tribe.
30-31Even though the place of worship was in Shiloh, the people of Dan set up the idol Micah had made. They worshiped the idol, and the Levite was their priest. His name was Jonathan, and he was a descendant of Gershom the son of Moses. His descendants served as priests for the tribe of Dan, until the people of Israel were taken away as prisoners by their enemies.
translation_text:
1Da ŋala po Izirali a jam ka naaba. Da ŋala powa mɛ Dan dɔkku buuni a jam diem a gisi ka badek jigi ayen ba kali, dii nyiŋla ba an diem jam nya charuk Izirali buuni po. 2Dila Dan demma a yaa jam tom kpaliŋ nyeerisa banu a nyini Zoraya ale Estaol ayen ba kpesi nya tɛŋka. Nuruma de a jam za ka ba yezuimaŋa meena naŋkula po. Ba jam weeni ba ayen, <<Ni cheŋ ga kpesi nya tɛŋka.>> Nidoama yaa jam jo Ɛfraim tɛŋka ate guuta a bo ka po la a jam paari Maika yenni, dula ate ba jam goa. 3Ase ba le jam moata Maika yenni la, ba yaa miŋ Livai nidoa paalika lueluku, dila ba yaa mobi jo dula a bek wa ayen, <<Ka wana ale ta fi a jam dela? Ka boa ate fi a nye dela? Boan nyiŋ ate fi bo dela?
4Wa yaa weeni ba Maika ale nye dii a te wa la, wa weeni ayen, <<Wa pa mu kama a tuni mu ate mi chim wa kaabteerɔ.>>
5Ate ba weeni wa ayen, <<Ti a saalim kpesi bek Wen a nya ase ti chelimu ale cheŋ nalimnyiini ya.>>
6Kaabteerɔwa yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<Ni cheŋ ale suiyɔgni. Naawen a seba ni chelimu nɔi po kama.>>
7Dila nidoaba banuwa yaa basi dula ale jam Lais, dula ate ba yaa nya ale nuruma a boro ka fasiyaa, ase Saidon demma la, ba boro ale ka suiyɔgni ale boro boka dek. Ase ba tɛŋka ale kan jam a silim la, ba jam jigsi kama. Ba ŋman yalima kama ale Saidon demma, ale ka wari ale waai ya.
8Ase ba le ŋman jam Zoraya ale Estaol tɛŋsaŋa la, ba suataŋa yaa bek ba ayen, <<Nama nya wie ka sɛ?>>
9Ate ba tulisi ayen, <<Ni jam ate ti nye kpaliŋ ale ba, tama ale nya la tɛŋka a ŋmasi nala kama. Ni kan yaa ni nye wari ya? Ni kan beni ale ka ga tuesi ka. 10Ni dam paari dula, ni le nya nuru baai ate ni zɛ ba wari la ale tɛŋ kaai ale lagri ate Wen a pa nyo ni nisima po, tɛŋ kaai ale kaa silim jaab la.>>
11Ate nidoaba kobsiyuebi a nyini Dan yezukku a gomsi magsi kpaliŋ, a nyini Zoraya ale Estaol. 12A nyini dula, ba yaa jam kala moata ka Kiriat Jearim ale bo Juda po la. Kude nyiŋ ale soa ate jigi dii ale bo Kiriat Jearim yeniŋ geŋsa la yuei a te ayen Mayane Dan a jam paari jinla de la. 13A nyini dula ba jam cheŋ ka Ɛfraim tɛŋka ate guutaŋa a bo ka po la a jam Maika yenni.
14Nidoaba banuwa baai ale ga kpesi nya Lais tɛŋka la yaa weeni ba suataŋa ayen, <<Nama a seba ayen yeeŋa de dinyi a ta ka garuk geli, wena gela, a peesi ŋanta ase jameem la ale kutuk bɔgluwa? Yɔgyɔgla de ni seba ni le ni nye diila kama.>> 15Dila ba yaa viriŋ cheŋ Livaiwa nidoa paalika yenni ale bo Maika jigini la a puusi wa. 16Nidoaba kobsiyuebiwa ale nyini Dan demma po, a gomsi magsi kpaliŋka la, a yaa jam zaani nansuiŋku nɔi. 17Nidoaba banuwa baai ale ga kpesi nya tɛŋka la yaa jo a pai jameemmu ale garuk genni ale wena gela ale kutuk bɔgluk alege ate kaabteerɔwa ale nidoaba kobsiyuebiwa ale gomsi a magsi kpaliŋ la a jam za nansuiŋku nɔi.
18Ase nidoama de ale jam jo Maika yenni po a pai jameemmu ale garuk genni ale wena gela ale kutuk bɔglukku la, kaabteerɔwa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ka boa ale la ate ni a nye?>>
19Ba yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Nye diki, kan weeni wari ya. Va ti a jam, chim ti ko ale ti kaabteerɔ. Fi a dan tom a te Izirali buuni ale yezuk ase kaabteerɔ la a zunchoŋ fi le tom a te nuru yeŋ dɔkdemma kama la?>> 20Kaabteerɔwa sui yaa jam peenti. Ate wa yaa pa garuk genni ale wena gela, ŋan mɛɛntaŋa a va nuruma a cheŋ. 21Ba yaa piilim ba chelimu ŋmana, ate ba bi fiisaŋa ale ba duŋsaŋa ale ba ŋantaŋa meena a jam de ba niŋ.
22Ase ba le cheŋ ate ku yalima magadek ale Maika yenni la, nidoama baai ale jam kala moata Maika yenni la, ba jam wi ba ka jigi yeŋ ate ba cheŋ paari Dan demma. 23Ase ba le na a vi ba la, Dan demma yaa viriŋ weeni Maika ayen, <<Ka fi wanni ale boa ate fi nidoama ayen ba nye kpaliŋ ale ti?>>
24Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Fi pa wenaŋa ate mi nye la, ale m kaabteerɔwa a ta cheŋ. Ka boa ate mi a ŋman tara? Fi ale nye ka sɛ a bek ayen di nya mu ka be?>>
25Ate Dan demma a yaa tulisi ayen, <<Kan nak nanpaga ale ti, fi dan nye dila nidoa baai sue ale kaa daliŋ puurika la ale nye kpaliŋ ale fu ate fi ale fi dɔkdemma ale jɔk ni nyuvooŋa.>> 26Dila Dan demma yaa cheŋ, ase Maika ale nya ale ba ŋmasi pagra gaam wa la, wa yaa ŋman kuli yeri.
27Ba yaa jam pai Maika ale nye ŋan baai la ale wa kaabteerɔwa a cheŋ Lais a ga tu chaab ale suiyɔgni nuru baai ate ba zɛ ba nɔi po la. Ba jam nye ka kpaliŋ ale ba ale ju ba tɛŋka. 28Waai a jam karo a vari ba a basi dii nyiŋla ba jam yalima kama ale Saidon demma ale kan jam a nye ale nuruba ba chaaba. Tɛŋ kpieŋka a jam bo ka viak po moata Bet Areyob. Dan demma a ŋman jam se tɛŋ kpieŋka kama a bo ka po. 29Ba jam te ka yuei ayen ka Dan, ka ba kokpieŋka yuei ate ba pai te ka, waai ale ka Izirali nidoabili la. Tɛŋ kpieŋka yuei kpakka jam le Lais. 30Dula jigini Dan demma a jam se ka bɔgta a te badek, ate Gersom nidoabinni Jonatan, Manasa ŋaaŋbiika ale wa nidoabilisaŋa a jam ka kaabteerɔba ate Dan dɔkku buuni a ta ga paari diipo ate ba chim yɔm tɛŋka po la. 31Ba diem jam a kaab bɔgluk tii ate Maika a jam se la kama diipo meena ate Wen yenni a diem jam bo Siilo po la.

english_text:
A Woman Is Murdered
1Before kings ruled Israel, a Levite was living deep in the hill country of the Ephraim tribe. He married a woman from Bethlehem in Judah, 2but she was unfaithful and went back to live with her family in Bethlehem.
Four months later 3her husband decided to try and talk her into coming back. So he went to Bethlehem, taking along a servant and two donkeys. He talked with his wife, and she invited him into her family's home. Her father was glad to see him 4and did not want him to leave. So the man stayed three days, eating and drinking with his father-in-law.
5When everyone got up on the fourth day, the Levite started getting ready to go home. But his father-in-law said, “Don't leave until you have a bite to eat. You'll need strength for your journey.”
6The two men sat down together and ate a big meal. “Come on,” the man's father-in-law said. “Stay tonight and have a good time.”
7The Levite tried to leave, but his father-in-law insisted, and he spent one more night there. 8The fifth day, the man got up early to leave, but his wife's father said, “You need to keep up your strength! Why don't you leave right after lunch?” So the two of them started eating.
9Finally, the Levite got up from the meal, so he and his wife and servant could leave. “Look,” his father-in-law said, “it's already late afternoon, and if you leave now, you won't get very far before dark. Stay with us one more night and enjoy yourself. Then you can get up early tomorrow morning and start home.”
10But the Levite decided not to spend the night there again. He had the saddles put on his two donkeys, then he and his wife and servant traveled as far as Jebus, which is now called Jerusalem. 11It was beginning to get dark, and the man's servant said, “Let's stop and spend the night in this town where the Jebusites live.”
12“No,” the Levite answered. “They aren't Israelites, and I refuse to spend the night there. We'll stop for the night at Gibeah, 13or maybe we can even reach Ramah before dark.”
14They walked on and reached Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin just after sunset. 15They left the road and went into Gibeah. But the Levite couldn't find a house where anyone would let them spend the night, and they sat down in the open area just inside the town gates.
16Soon an old man came in through the gates on his way home from working in the fields. Most of the people who lived in Gibeah belonged to the tribe of Benjamin, but this man was originally from the hill country of Ephraim. 17He noticed that the Levite was just in town to spend the night. “Where are you going?” the old man asked. “Where did you come from?”
18“We've come from Bethlehem in Judah,” the Levite answered. “We went there on a visit. Now we're going to the place where the Lord is worshiped, and later we will return to our home in the hill country of Ephraim. But no one here will let us spend the night in their home. 19We brought food for our donkeys and bread and wine for ourselves, so we don't need anything except a place to sleep.”
20The old man said, “You are welcome to spend the night in my home and to be my guest, but don't stay out here!”
21The old man brought them into his house and fed their donkeys. Then he and his guests washed their feet and began eating and drinking. 22 They were having a good time, when some worthless men of that town surrounded the house and started banging on the door and shouting, “A man came to your house tonight. Send him out, so we can have sex with him!”
23The old man went outside and said, “My friends, please don't commit such a horrible crime against a man who is a guest in my house. 24Let me send out my daughter instead. She's a virgin. And I'll even send out the man's wife. You can rape them or do whatever else you want, but please don't do such a horrible thing to this man.”
25The men refused to listen, so the Levite grabbed his wife and shoved her outside. The men raped her and abused her all night long. Finally, they let her go just before sunrise, 26and it was almost daybreak when she went back to the house where her husband was staying. She collapsed at the door and lay there until sunrise.
27About that time, her husband woke up and got ready to leave. He opened the door and went outside, where he found his wife lying at the door with her hands on the doorstep. 28“Get up!” he said. “It's time to leave.”
But his wife didn't move.
He lifted her body onto his donkey and left. 29 When he got home, he took a butcher knife and cut her body into twelve pieces. Then he told some messengers, “Take one piece to each tribe of Israel 30and ask everyone if anything like this has ever happened since Israel left Egypt. Tell them to think about it, talk it over, and tell us what should be done.”
Everyone who saw a piece of the body said, “This is horrible! Nothing like this has ever happened since the day Israel left Egypt.”
translation_text:
1Da ŋala po Izirali a jam ka naaba. Yɔgyɔgla de ka Livai waai ale jam bo niŋniŋ Ɛfraim tɛŋka ate guuta a bo ka po la, ale jam ta nipok a nyini Betiliyem ale bo Juda po la a jam ayen wa boro ale wa. 2Alege wa jam ka wensie ale wa. Nipowa a jam basi wa kama ale nyini ga bo wa kowa yenni ale Betiliyem ale bo Juda po la. Wa le jam bo dula paari chiisa sinaansi ŋaaŋnyiŋ la, 3wa chorɔwa a jam saŋ wa ŋaaŋ kama ayen wa ta wa a kuli. Nidoawa a jam ta ka wa tomteerɔ ale bonsa siye a cheŋ. Nipowa yaa ta wa a jo wa kowa yenni po. Ase wa ŋachobwa ale nya wa la, wa sui yaa peenti nna yegayega ate wa tuesi wa nalimnyiini. 4Wa ŋachobwa, nipowa kowa yaa weeni wa ayen wa goa, dila wa yaa jam bo dula a paari daa ŋata a dɛ ale a nyu a goa paari daa ŋata.
5Daa ŋanaansiwa danni wa yaa zue yiti gomsi ayen wa kuli, alege nipowa kowa a weeni wa chicham biika ayen, <<Wa limisi ate ba yaa nyiam ate wa nyu abe wa kuli.>> 6Dila ba nɔi bayema a yaa kali ba dɛ abe ba nyu ale chaab. Dila ŋaaŋnyiŋ nipowa kowa a ŋman weeni wa ayen, <<Jianje goa dela yokku a dɛ masim.>> 7Nuruwa ale yiti wa kuli la, wa ŋachobwa a diem va wa kama ayen wa goa, ate wa ŋman goa yok kula. 8Saluik daa ŋanuwa danni, ase nuruwa ale yiti wa cheŋ la, nipowa kowa ayen yɔgli fidek. <<A limisi ate ku paari kantueŋ.>> Dila ba nɔi bayema a ŋman dɛ ale chaab.
9Ase nidoawa ale wa powa ale wa tomteerɔwa ale yiti ba kuli la, wa ŋachobwa nipowa kowa yaa weeni ayen, <<Yɔgyɔgla de nya ku boro a paari ka junɔi. Goa dela yokku de ale vanni a moata ka veentika, ni goa dela a dɛ masim ale chaab. Chum saluik yokyokwa abe ni yaa yiti a lo suik po a kuli.>> 10Alege ba le kaa yaali ba ŋman goa yok ku choa la, nidoama a yaa nyini a duŋ Jebus nyiŋ, Jerusalem ale la, ale wa bonduensa siyewa ale wa powa.
11Ase ba le ga moata Jebus ale vanni a moata veenti ka la, tomteerɔwa yaa weeni wa kpagni ayen <<Jam basi ate ti goa Jebus demma de tɛŋka po.>>
12Ate wa kpagni a tulisi ayen, <<Aaya, ti kan jo tɛŋ chaŋ po nuru baai ale kan daa Izirali dem la tɛŋ po. Ti le cheŋ ka Gibea tɛŋka.>> 13Wa ŋman weeni a gum du ayen ni jam ate ti paari Gibea yaase Arama a goa tɛŋsaŋa de kanyi po.>> 14Dila ba yaa jam a cheŋ, wenbinni a jam boro a siŋ kama ase ba le moata Gibea ale bo Benjamin po la. 15Ba yaa jam goa dula yok kula. Ba jam ga kala ka tɛŋ kpieŋka peelimmu po, alege waai an jam ta ba a kuli wa yeri ayen ba goa.
16Junɔi dila nisɔmma ale nyini Ɛfraim tɛŋka ate guuta a bo ka po la, waai ale jam bo Gibea po la. Nuru baai ale jam bo dula la ka Benjamin dem, a nyini talim tuima jigi a jam. 17Wa le nya nyeendɔma ale ba kala tɛŋ kpieŋka peelimmu po la, nisɔmawa yaa bek ba ayen, <<Nama a cheŋ ka bɛ? Ni abe nyini ka bɛ?>>
18Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ti nyini ka Betiliyem ale bo Juda po la a cheŋ tɛŋ kpaŋ ale bo Ɛfraim ate guuta a bo ka po la juijui ate mi a boro la. Mi jam bo ka Betiliyem ale bo Juda po la, yɔgyɔgla de mi cheŋ ka Naawen yenni. Waai an jam ta mi a kuli wa yeri ya. 19Ti nɔi tiyema a ta ŋandiinta a magsi ti bonsaŋa dɛka kama. Tama a ta ŋandiinta ale daam a magsi tidek, fi tomteerɔwa mi ale fi nipokbili tomteerɔwa nidoabili paalika ale va ti la. Ti kan yaali jaaboa.>>
20<<Mi a nye fi tia fi le jam m yenni la,>> ate nisɔmawa a yaa weeni ayen, <<Basi ate mi a te ni jaabuui meena ate fi a yaali la kan goa peelimmu po.>> 21Dila wa yaa ta wa a jo wa yenni po a te wa bonsaŋa ŋandiinta. Ba le sugri ba naŋsaŋa a nueri la, ba yaa dɛ ŋandiinta ale nyu.
22Ase ba le boro a dɛ la, gaasa nuruma de gela ale bo tɛŋ kpieŋka po la, a yaa jam gilim yenni. A nak tuoku ale a na nisɔmawa waai ale soa yenni la ayen, <<Ta nuruwa a nyini peelim waai ale jam fi yenni la ate ti goa ale wa.>>
23Yenni nyɔnɔwa yaa nyini peelim a weeni ba ayen, <<Aaya, m doaba. Ni kan ta gaasa dila. Ase nuruwa de ale ka mi nichaanɔ la, ni kan nye chivie wanni de. 24Nya, m lie ale nna wa zɛ nidoa ale nichaanɔwa pok ale nna. Mi ale pa ba a te ni yɔgyɔgla de, ate ni nye ba dii meena ate ni a yaali la. Alege nuruwa de ni kan nye chivieŋa de.>>
25Alege nidoama an jam wom wa. Nuruwa yaa ta wa powa, a nyini te ba ate ba fɛ goa ale wa yokku meena, ale basi wa saluik yokyok ate wa kuli. 26Vari ale veenti la nipowa yaa ŋman kuli yeri juijui ate wa kpagni a boro la, a lo doa nansuiŋku nɔi ate wenbinni pusi paari wa dula.
27Ase wa kpagni ale yiti saluiku a lak yenni tuoku a nyini wa cheŋ la, dula ale wa powa a doa, a lo doa yenni tuoku nɔi, ate wa nisaŋa a vi gaam joka jigini. 28Ate wa weeni wa ayen, <<Yiti ŋmai ate ti cheŋ,>> alege wa an tulisi ya. Ate nuruwa a yaa pa wa a kali wa bonika zuk a duŋ yeri.
29Wa le jam paari yeri la, wa yaa pa gebik a gebi wa powa bunabuna a paari pi ale buye a ta cheŋ gilim Izirali kabtaŋa meena. 30Waai meena ale jam nya dila la a weeni kama ayen, <<Ba an nya wanni de choa yaase wanni de choa a nye ya a nyini diipo ate Izirali demma a nyini Ejipiti po a nyini la. Ni poli di zuk, ni kpesi nya di, a weeni ti le ti nye diila.>>

english_text:
Israel Gets Ready for War
1-3The Israelites called a meeting of the nation. And since they were God's people, the meeting was held at the place of worship in Mizpah. Men who could serve as soldiers came from everywhere in Israel—from Dan in the north, Beersheba in the south, and Gilead east of the Jordan River. Four hundred thousand of them came to Mizpah, and they each felt the same about what those men from the tribe of Benjamin had done.
News about the meeting at Mizpah reached the tribe of Benjamin.
As soon as the leaders of the tribes of Israel took their places, the Israelites said, “How could such a horrible thing happen?”
4The husband of the murdered woman answered:
My wife and I went into the town of Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night. 5Later that night, the men of Gibeah surrounded the house. They wanted to kill me, but instead they raped and killed my wife. 6It was a terrible thing for Israelites to do! So I cut up her body and sent the pieces everywhere in Israel.
7You are the people of Israel, and you must decide today what to do about the men of Gibeah.
8The whole army was in agreement, and they said, “None of us will go home. 9-10We'll send one tenth of the men from each tribe to get food for the army. And we'll ask God who should attack Gibeah, because those men deserve to be punished for committing such a horrible crime in Israel.”
11Everyone agreed that Gibeah had to be punished.
12The tribes of Israel sent messengers to every town and village in Benjamin. And wherever the messengers went, they said, “How could those worthless men in Gibeah do such a disgusting thing? 13We can't allow such a terrible crime to go unpunished in Israel! Hand the men over to us, and we will put them to death.”
But the people of Benjamin refused to listen to the other Israelites. 14Men from towns all over Benjamin's territory went to Gibeah and got ready to fight Israel. 15The Benjamin tribe had 26,000 soldiers, not counting the 700 who were Gibeah's best warriors. 16In this army there were 700 left-handed experts who could sling a rock at a target the size of a hair and hit it every time.
17The other Israelite tribes organized their army and found they had 400,000 experienced soldiers. 18So they went to the place of worship at Bethel and asked God, “Which tribe should be the first to attack the people of Benjamin?”
“Judah,” the Lord answered.
19The next morning the Israelite army moved its camp to a place near Gibeah. 20Then they left their camp and got into position to attack the army of Benjamin.
The War Between Israel and Benjamin
21Benjamin's soldiers came out of Gibeah and attacked, and when the day was over, 22,000 Israelite soldiers lay dead on the ground.
22-24The people of Israel went to the place of worship and cried until sunset. Then they asked the Lord, “Should we attack the people of Benjamin again, even though they are our relatives?”
“Yes,” the Lord replied, “attack them again!”
The Israelite soldiers encouraged each other to be brave and to fight hard. Then the next day they went back to Gibeah and took up the same positions as they had before.
25That same day, Benjamin's soldiers came out of Gibeah and attacked, leaving another 18,000 Israelite soldiers dead on the battlefield.
26-28The people of Israel went to the place of worship at Bethel, where the sacred chest was being kept. They sat on the ground, crying and not eating for the rest of the day. Then about sunset, they offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing. Phinehas the priest then prayed, “Our Lord, the people of Benjamin are our relatives. Should we stop fighting or attack them again?”
“Attack!” the Lord answered. “Tomorrow I will let you defeat them.”
29The Israelites surrounded Gibeah, but stayed where they could not be seen. 30Then the next day, they took the same positions as twice before, 31-41but this time they had a different plan. They said, “When the men of Benjamin attack, we will run off and let them chase us away from the town and into the country roads.”
The soldiers of Benjamin attacked the Israelite army and started pushing it back from the town. They killed about 30 Israelites in the fields and along the road between Gibeah and Bethel. The men of Benjamin were thinking, “We're mowing them down like we did before.”
The Israelites were running away, but they headed for Baal-Tamar, where they regrouped. They had set an ambush, and they were sure it would work. Ten thousand of Israel's best soldiers had been hiding west of Gibeah, and as soon as the men of Benjamin chased the Israelites into the countryside, these 10,000 soldiers made a surprise attack on the town gates. They dashed in and captured Gibeah, killing everyone there. Then they set the town on fire, because the smoke would be the signal for the other Israelite soldiers to turn and attack the soldiers of Benjamin.
The fighting had been so heavy around the soldiers of Benjamin, that they did not know the trouble they were in. But then they looked back and saw clouds of smoke rising from the town. They looked in front and saw the soldiers of Israel turning to attack. This terrified them, because they realized that something horrible was happening. And it was horrible—over 25,000 soldiers of Benjamin died that day, and those who were left alive knew that the Lord had given Israel the victory.
42The men of Benjamin headed down the road toward the desert, trying to escape from the Israelites. But the Israelites stayed right behind them, keeping up their attack. Men even came out of the nearby towns to help kill the men of Benjamin, 43who were having to fight on all sides. The Israelite soldiers never let up their attack. They chased and killed the warriors of Benjamin as far as a place directly east of Gibeah, 44until 18,000 of these warriors lay dead.
45Some other warriors of Benjamin turned and ran down the road toward Rimmon Rock in the desert. The Israelites killed 5,000 of them on the road, then chased the rest until they had killed 2,000 more. 46Twenty-five thousand soldiers of Benjamin died that day, all of them experienced warriors. 47Only 600 of them finally made it into the desert to Rimmon Rock, where they stayed for four months.
48The Israelites turned back and went to every town in Benjamin's territory, killing all the people and animals, and setting the towns on fire.
translation_text:
1Ate Izirali demma meena a nyini Dan dɔkku buuni a ta ga paari Beerseba ale Gilead tɛŋka a yaa nyini ase nuru yeŋ la a tigsi chaab Naawen niŋ Mizpa tɛŋka po. 2Ate Izirali buuni meena niŋdeerɔma ale Wen tigsuŋku yaa za ale tugurik tɔŋdɔba tusa kobsinaansi (400,000) a gomsi ale gebisa. 3Benjamin demma a yaa wom ayen Izirali demma a cheŋ Mizpa. Izirali demma yaa weeni ayen, <<Weeni ti wabiokku de ale nye dii a nye la.
4Dila Livai waai powa ate ba jam ko la yaa weeni ayen, <<Mi ale m powa, a jam ka Gibea ale bo Benjamin po la ayen ti goa. 5Yɔkku po ate Gibea demma a saŋ m ŋaaŋ a jam gilim yenni a yaa ba ko mu. Ba fɛ goa ale m powa kama ate wa kpi. 6Mi yaa jam pai m powa a gebi wa bunabuna a ta boanni dinyi meena a cheŋ Izirali tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa a te, dii nyiŋla ba nye wakaasuŋku de ale chivieŋa de ka Izirali tɛŋka po. 7Yɔgyɔgla de nama Izirali demma meena a biisa ni le ta diila.
8Nuruma meena yaa jam yiti ase nuru yeŋ la ayen, <<Ti waai a kan kuli yeri ya. Aaya, ti wanyi mɛ la a kan kuli wa yeri ya. 9Alege yɔgyɔgla de ti le ti nye Gibea demma diila ale nna. Ti le tu chaab ale ba ase ti ni nak gbaŋka ate ka weeni ti diila. 10Ti le ta ka nuruba pi a nyini nuruba kook po Izirali buuni meena po, a ta nuruba kook a nyini nuruba tusidi po, abe ti ta nuruba tusidi a nyini tusa pi (10,000) meena po, a yaa ŋanta a te tugurik tɔŋdɔma. Ase tugurik tɔŋdɔma a dan ga paari Gibea ale bo Benjamin tɛŋka po la, dila ale basi ate ba nya jabuui nyiŋ ate chivieŋa de nye Izirali tɛŋka po la.>> 11Dila Izirali demma meena yaa tigsi chaab ale nɔiyeŋ ase nuru yeŋ la, a nye kpaliŋ ale tɛŋ kpieŋka.
12Izirali buuni yaa tom nuruba ate ba cheŋ Benjamin dɔkku buuni meena jigi ayen, <<Alege wabiokku de ale nye ni po la? 13Yɔgyɔgla de ni pai Gibea gaasa nuruma de a nyo ti nisima po, ate ti ko ba a yeeri biemu de Izirali po.>> Alege Benjamin an jam wom ba Izirali dem mbala. 14A nyini ba tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa po, ba yaa gum chaab a jam Gibea tɛŋka po ayen ba nye kpaliŋ ale Izirali demma. 15Benjamin dɔkku buuni yaa deri lueri tugurik tɔŋdɔba tusa pisiye ale ŋayuebi (26,000) ale gebisa ba tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa po a gum chaab ale nuruba kobsiyopɔi waai ate ba lueri a ta nyini Gibea tɛŋka po la. 16Tugurik tɔŋdɔma de meena po, ka galisa kobsiyopɔi ale jam bo ba po, ba wanyi meena a kan nak visiŋ tain a jɔgi.
17Benjamin watɔga, Izirali nyiini a jam ta ka nuruba tusa kobsinaansi (400,000) ale gebisa, ba meena tugurik tɔŋdisa.
18Izirali demma yaa cheŋ Betel ayen ba wom a nyini Wen jigi. Ba yaa bek ayen, <<Ka ti ban dek ale ti dɛ niŋ a ga nye kpaliŋ ale Benjamin demma?>> Ate Naawen weeni ayen, <<Juda dɔkku buuni a dɛ niŋ.>>
19Saluik kuui ale pai saŋ la Izirali demma yaa ga kali moata Gibea tɛŋka. 20Izirali demma yaa cheŋ ba nye kpaliŋ ale Benjamin demma, ba jam za ka kpaliŋ zaana jigi ayen ba nye kpaliŋ ale ba, Gibea tɛŋka po. 21Benjamin demma yaa nyini Gibea tɛŋka po a nyini a ko Izirali demma tusa pisiye ale ŋaye (22,000) kpaliŋka po dai dila danni. 22Alege Izirali demma yaa jam te chaab nyiŋbiiri a ŋman pilim zaani kpaliŋ zaana jigi, ba le poom liŋ za kab tii la. 23Izirali a jam cheŋ ka Naawen niŋ a puusi a kum a ta ga paari junɔi, a bek Naawen. Ba weeni ayen, <<Ti ŋman ga nye kpaliŋ ale Benjamin demma ti suataŋa?>> Ate Naawen yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ni ga nye kpaliŋ ale ba.>>
24Ate Izirali demma yaa torisi kpaŋ Benjamin demma daa ŋayewa danni. 25Dai dila danni ase Benjamin demma ale nyini Gibea po a nyini ayen, ba zɛri badek nyiŋ a kan siak a te ba la, ba ŋman ko Izirali demma tusa pi ale naaniŋ (18,000), ba meena a gomsi badek ale ka gebisa.
26Ate Izirali demma, nuruma meena yaa jam cheŋ Betel a kala Naawen niŋ a kum. Ba jam bobi ka nɔi a puusi ate ku paari junɔi a nye juka kaabka tiirita ale suiyɔgni tiirita a te Naawen. 27Izirali demma a ŋman pilim bek Naawen. Da ŋala po Wen nɔiyeŋka dakanni a jam bo ka dula, 28ale Eleaza nidoabinni Fineyas, Aaron ŋaaŋka a jam ka kaabteerɔwa. Ba jam bek kama ayen, <<Ti ŋman pilim ga nye kpaliŋ ale Benjamin demma ti suataŋa yaa ti kan cheŋ?>> Ate Naawen ayen, <<Ni cheŋ ale chum mi ale pa ba a nyo ni nisima po.>>
29Ate Izirali demma yaa ga suk doa gilim Gibea tɛŋka. 30Ba yaa cheŋ ba nye kpaliŋ ale Benjamin demma daa ŋatawa danni, ba jam za ka kpaliŋ zaana jigi ayen ba nye kpaliŋ ale Gibea ase ba le poom liŋ jam za juijui la. 31Benjamin demma yaa nyini ba tu chaab ale ba dari ba a ta nyini tɛŋ kpieŋka po a nyini. Ba piilim a te Izirali demma tueta ase ba ni liŋ jam nye ba diila, ate nuruba pisita a kpi peelimmu niŋ ale suitaŋa ale a cheŋ Betel ale Gibea la po.
32Ase Benjamin demma ale a weeni ayen, <<Ti a nya pagrim ba zuk ase ku le poom liŋ jam ka diila>> Izirali demma mɛ ayen, <<Ni basi ate ti chali a ta ba a nyini ba tɛŋka po a nyini suitaŋa po.>>
33Izirali demma meena yaa basi ba ale bo juijui la ale ga za Baal Tamara, ate Izirali demma ale suk doa la yaa yiti a nyini Gibea yeniŋ geŋsa. 34Izirali tugurik tɔŋdɔma tusa piwa (10,000) yaa tu Gibea demma suik. Kpaliŋka a jam pagra kama ate Benjamin demma a jam zɛ kaasuŋ ale moata ba dii ya. 35Naawen a jam nya pagrim Benjamin demma zuk a te Izirali demma, dai dila danni Izirali demma a jam ko Benjamin demma ka tusa pisiye ale ŋanu ale kook (25,100). Ba meena jam ka tugurik tɔŋdɔba. 36Ate Benjamin demma a yaa nya ayen ba nak ba kama. Yɔgyɔgla de Izirali demma a jam yiti chali ale basi Benjamin demma dii nyiŋla, ba sebchakka meena a jam bo ka ba ale suk doa moata Gibea la zuk. 37Nuru baai ale jam suk doa la yaa deri yiti nna nwuli a jo Gibea tɛŋka, a waaŋ ka meena po, a ko tɛŋka nuruma meena ale gebik.
38Izirali demma a weeni baai ale suk doa la kama ayen ba ju tɛŋka ale bolim ate ba dan nya nyuisa ase chiŋmari la a nyini tɛŋka po, 39Izirali demma baai ale kan suk doa la yaa le chali jam kpaliŋka po. Benjamin demma a jam pilim te Izirali demma ka tueta a paari ase nuruba pisita la, ale weeni ayen, <<Ti a nya pagrim ba zuk ase ka ti le poom liŋ nya pagrim ba zuk diila.>> 40Alege nyuisaŋa ale yiti tɛŋ kpieŋka po la, Benjamin demma a viriŋ nya ale tɛŋka meena a chɔgsi bolim ate nyuisa a jo chiŋmaaŋa po. 41Izirali demma a yaa viriŋ jueli ba zuk, Benjamin demma nyiŋsa yaa jam a gɔk nna pampam, dii nyiŋla ba jam seba kama ayen kaasuŋ ale jam ba zuk. 42Ba yaa yiti chali alege Izirali demma a duŋ gɔnni po, alege ba an jam baga chali beya. Izirali dem baai ale jam nyini tɛŋka po nyini la yaa kasi ba a che che ba a lɔnsi dula. 43Ba jam gilim Benjamin demma a basi ka suŋsuŋ a vi yik ba nna moali moali ya Gibea tɛŋka kori geŋsa. 44Benjamin demma tusa pi ale naaniŋ (18,000) ale jam kpi, ba meena a jam ka tugurik tɔŋdɔba dek. 45Ase ba le viriŋ a duŋ gɔnni po Arimmon Piuŋku nyiŋla, Izirali demma a ko ba po ka tusa ŋanu (5,000) suiku po. Ba jam a saŋ ba ŋaaŋ ka dila a ga paari Gidom a ŋman ko nuruba tusa ŋaye (2,000).
46Dai dila danni Benjamin demma tusa pisiye ale ŋanu (25,000) ale kpi, ba meena a jam ka tugurik tɔŋdɔba dek. 47Alege nuruba kobsiyuebi ale chali jo gɔnni po Arimmon piuŋku geŋsa a bo dula a paari chiisa sinaansi. 48Izirali demma a yaa ŋman cheŋ Benjamin demma jigi a ko ba meena, a gum chaab ale ba duŋsaŋa ale jaab meena ate ba nya la. Tɛŋ kpien sii meena ate ba a nya la, ba ju si ale ka bolim.

english_text:
Wives for the Men of Benjamin
1When the Israelites had met at Mizpah before the war with Benjamin, they had made this sacred promise: “None of us will ever let our daughters marry any man from Benjamin.”
2After the war with Benjamin, the Israelites went to the place of worship at Bethel and sat there until sunset. They cried loudly and bitterly 3and prayed, “Our Lord, you are the God of Israel. Why did you let this happen? Now one of our tribes is almost gone.”
4Early the next morning, the Israelites built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing. 5Then they asked each other, “Did any of the tribes of Israel fail to come to the place of worship? We made a sacred promise that anyone who didn't come to the meeting at Mizpah would be put to death.”
6The Israelites were sad about what had happened to the Benjamin tribe, and they said, “One of our tribes was almost wiped out. 7Only a few men of Benjamin weren't killed in the war. We need to get wives for them, so the tribe won't completely disappear. But how can we do that, after promising in the Lord's name that we wouldn't let them marry any of our daughters?”
8-9Again the Israelites asked, “Did any of the tribes stay away from the meeting at Mizpah?”
After asking around, they discovered that no one had come from Jabesh in Gilead. 10-11So they sent 12,000 warriors with these orders: “Attack Jabesh in Gilead and kill everyone, except the women who have never been married.”
12The warriors attacked Jabesh in Gilead, and returned to their camp at Shiloh in Canaan with 400 young women.
13The Israelites met and sent messengers to the men of Benjamin at Rimmon Rock, telling them that the Israelites were willing to make peace with them. 14So the men of Benjamin came back from Rimmon Rock, and the Israelites let them marry the young women from Jabesh. But there weren't enough women.
15The Israelites were very sad, because the Lord had almost wiped out one of their tribes. 16Then their leaders said:
All the women of the Benjamin tribe were killed. How can we get wives for the men of Benjamin who are left? 17If they don't have children, one of the Israelite tribes will die out. 18But we can't let the men of Benjamin marry any of our daughters. We made a sacred promise not to do that, and if we break our promise, we will be under our own curse.
19Then someone suggested, “What about the Lord's Festival that takes place each year in Shiloh? It's held north of Bethel, south of Lebonah, and just east of the road that goes from Bethel to Shechem.”
20The leaders told the men of Benjamin who still did not have wives:
Go to Shiloh and hide in the vineyards near the festival. 21Wait there for the young women of Shiloh to come out and perform their dances. Then rush out and grab one of the young women, then take her home as your wife. 22If the fathers or brothers of these women complain about this, we'll say, “Be kind enough to let those men keep your daughter. After all, we couldn't get enough wives for all the men of Benjamin in the battle at Jabesh. And because you didn't give them permission to marry your daughters, you won't be under the curse we earlier agreed on.”
23The men of Benjamin went to Shiloh and hid in the vineyards. The young women soon started dancing, and each man grabbed one of them and carried her off. Then the men of Benjamin went back to their own land and rebuilt their towns and started living in them again.
24Afterwards, the rest of the Israelites returned to their homes and families.
Israel Was Not Ruled by a King
25 In those days Israel wasn't ruled by a king, and everyone did what they thought was right.
translation_text:
1Izirali demma a jam pɛ kama Mizpa tɛŋka po ayen, <<Ti wanyi mɛ la a kan pa ti lie a yalisi Benjamin buuni po.>>
2Nuruma yaa cheŋ Betel, dula jigini ba jam kali Wen niŋ a paari ka junɔi a kaari ate ku a jueli nna tuotuowa. 3Ba jam kaari ayen, <<Naawen yaa, Izirali Wenni, ka boa ate wanni de a nye Izirali demma? Ka boa ate Izirali buuni dinyi a be jinla de?>>
4Vari ale veenti la saluik yokyok foribi nuruma yaa se kuŋkuŋ a nye juka tiirita ale suiyɔgni tiirita.
5Ate Izirali demma a yaa bek ayen, <<Ka wana ale nyini Izirali buuni meena po a ka tigsuŋku po Naawen niŋŋa?>> Ba jam nye ka pɛka ayen waai a dan kan tigsi Naawen niŋ Mizpa tɛŋka po ba le ko wa.
6Izirali demma sue ale jam kaasi ba suataŋa Benjamin demma nyiŋ. Ba jam a weeni kama ayen, <<Jinla de ba jɔk Izirali buuni dinyi kama.>> 7<<Ti le nye ka sɛ a faari nipooba a te baai ale tali la ase tama ale pɛ ale Naawen ayen ti kan pa ti liema a yalisi ba la?>> 8Ba yaa bek ayen, <<Ka buui dina ale kan tigsi Naawen niŋ Mizpa tɛŋka po?>> Ba yaa nya ale waai an nyini Jabes Gilead a bo tigsuŋku po. 9Ba le jam chiini nuruma la, ba nya kama ale Jabes Gilead wanyi mɛ la a jam karo.
10Dila tigsuŋku yaa tom tugurik tɔŋdɔba tusa pi ale ŋaye (12,000) ayen ba cheŋ Jabes Gilead a ga ko baai ale bo dula la, ba maa ko nipooma ale bisaŋa meena. 11Ba weeni ayen, <<Ni le ni nye diila ale nna: Ni ko nidoa meena ale nipok meena abe ni basi baai ale kan seba nidoa la.>> 12Ba yaa jam nya nuru baai ale jam bo Jabes Gilead po la, nipok paalisa kobsinaansi ale ba diem zɛ nidoa, ate ba ta bala a cheŋ Siilo ale bo Keenan po la.
13Tigsuŋku meena a yaa te Benjamin demma ale jam bo Arimmon piuŋku la suiyɔgni. 14Dila Benjamin demma yaa ŋman jam ba jigi va ŋala po, ate ba te ba nipok bi paalukku ate ba ta nyini Jabes Gilead la, alege ba an jam paari chari ba meena.
15Nuruma sue a jam kaasi kama Benjamin demma nyiŋ, dii nyiŋla Naawen a jam basi ate ka pari a bo Izirali buuni suŋsuŋ. 16Ate tigsuŋku nisɔmma yaa bek badek ayen, <<Ale Benjamin nipooma meena ate ti ko la, ti le nye ka sɛ a nya nipooba a te baai ale tali vua la? 17Ba weeni ayen, <<Benjamin buuni ale vua la, ku a fɛ ate ba ta bisa. Ate Izirali buuni dinyi mɛ la a kan kpeglimu. 18Tama an ŋman baga pa ti lie a yalisi ba, ase tama Izirali demma ale pɛ ayen, <Kikaasa a va waai ale pa wa lie a yalisi Benjamin buuni po la.> 19Alege nya, bein meena Naawen tigini feoku dɛka ale bo Siilo po, Betel wiilukku geŋsa ale suiku ale nyini Betel a cheŋ Sikiim la kori geŋ ale Lebona tɛŋka yeseoku geŋsa.>>
20Dila ba yaa sak Benjamin demma ayen, <<Ni cheŋ a ga suk kaduksaŋa po 21a kpesi a nya. Siilo tɛŋka liema a dan jam maa boro a gɔk, ni nyini kaduksaŋa po a nyini nwuli, ni wanyi meena a yik Siilo lie a ta kuli Benjamin tɛŋka. 22Ba koma yaase ba suataŋa a daa fɔbili a te ti, ti le weeni ba ayen, Ba sak jiirim ale ti a maari ba, dii nyiŋla ti an jam baga a nya nipooba a te ba diipo ate kpaliŋka vaaŋa po, ni zɛ ku nɔi po, daa nama dek ale pa ni liema a yalisi ba.>>
23Benjamin demma ale jam nye diila ale la. Ase nipokbilisaŋa ale jam a gɔk la, nuru meena yaa jam yik nipokbili ate wa chim wa pok. Ba jam ŋman kuli ka ba tɛŋka a ŋman se ka a kala ka po.
24Va ŋala po Izirali demma a yaa basi dula a ŋman kuli ba buuni ale ba yezuimaŋa badek charuku jigini.
25Da ŋala po Izirali jam ka naaba, waai meena a jam a nye ka dii ate wa a poli ayen ku magsi la.

english_text:
Ruth Is Loyal to Naomi
1-2Before Israel was ruled by kings, Elimelech from the clan of Ephrath lived in the town of Bethlehem. His wife was named Naomi, and their two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. But when their crops failed in Israel, they moved to the country of Moab. And while they were there, 3Elimelech died, leaving Naomi with only her two sons.
4Later, Naomi's sons married Moabite women. One was named Orpah and the other Ruth. About ten years later, 5Mahlon and Chilion also died. Now Naomi had no husband or sons.
6-7When Naomi heard that the Lord had given his people a good harvest, she and her two daughters-in-law got ready to leave Moab and go to Judah. As they were on their way there, 8Naomi said to them, “Don't you want to go back home to your own mothers? You were kind to my husband and sons, and you've always been kind to me. I pray that the Lord will be just as kind to you. 9May he give each of you another husband and a home of your own.”
Naomi kissed them. They cried 10and said, “We want to go with you and live among your people.”
11But she replied, “My daughters, why don't you return home? What good will it do you to go with me? Do you think I could have more sons for you to marry? 12You must go back home, because I am too old to marry again. Even if I got married tonight and later had more sons, 13would you wait for them to become old enough to marry? No, my daughters! Life is harder for me than it is for you, because the Lord has turned against me.”
14They cried again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth held on to her. 15Naomi then said to Ruth, “Look, your sister-in-law is going back to her people and to her gods! Why don't you go with her?”
16Ruth answered,
“Please don't tell me
to leave you
and return home!
I will go where you go,
I will live where you live;
your people will be my people,
your God will be my God.
17I will die where you die
and be buried beside you.
May the Lord punish me
if we are ever separated,
even by death!”
18When Naomi saw that Ruth had made up her mind to go with her, she stopped urging her to go back.
19They reached Bethlehem, and the whole town was excited to see them. The women who lived there asked, “Can this really be Naomi?”
20Then she told them, “Don't call me Naomi any longer! Call me Mara, because God has made my life bitter. 21I had everything when I left, but the Lord has brought me back with nothing. How can you still call me Naomi, when God has turned against me and made my life so hard?”
22The barley harvest was just beginning when Naomi and Ruth, her Moabite daughter-in-law, arrived in Bethlehem.
translation_text:
1Diipo ate niŋdeerɔba jam a nya Izirali tɛŋka zuk la, kom kpiem yaa yiti tɛŋka po. Nuru wanyi ale jam nyini Betiliyem ate ka bo Juda po la. Nuruwa de ale wa pok ale wa bisa baye a yaa cheŋ Moab tɛŋka ayen ba goa maga. 2Nuruwa de yuei ale Elimelek, wa powa yuei ale Naomi, wa nidoabinni wanyi yuei ale Malon, nwala yuei ale Kilion. Ba jam nyini ka Efrat buuni po a bo Betiliyem ale bo Juda po la. Ba yaa jam cheŋ ga bo Moab tɛŋka po. 3Naomi chorɔwa Elimelek yaa kpi alege wa le bisa bayewa. 4Wa nidoabilisa bayewa yaa faari Moab tɛŋka nipooba, nipowa wanyi yuei ale Orpa, nwala mɛ yuei ale Arut. Ba ale goa dula a nya bena pi la, 5Naomi nidoabilisaŋa bayewa Malon ale Kilion mɛ a kpi alege wadek wa nyiini. Wa nidoabilisaŋa ka. Wa chorɔwa mɛ ka.
6Naomi yaa wom ayen Naawen a maari wa nuruma ate ba kpa nya ŋandiinta yegayega, ate wa ale wa sampooma yaa gomsi ayen ba kuli. 7Wa ale wa sampooma bayewa yaa basi ba ale bo juijui la, alege lo suik po ayen ba kuli. 8Wa yaa weeni wa sampooma bayewa ayen ba ŋman kuli ba mama jigi. Ni le jam ta jiirim ale mi chorɔwa ale m bisaŋa diila, Naawen ale ta jiirim ale ni. 9Naawen ale maari ni ate ni nya chorɔba a kali nalimnyiini. 10Naomi yaa banti ba. Alege ba deri a kum ale a weeni ayen, <<Ti kan ŋmani, tama va fu a cheŋ ka fi nuruma jigi.>> 11Wa yaa ŋman weeni ayen, <<M lieba ku a fɛ ate ni ŋmani, ka boa ale soa ate ni a yaali ayen ni va mu cheŋ? Nama a poli ayen m le ŋman nya bisa ate ni yali ba? 12Ni ŋman kuli, diila mi kpaŋ kama ale yalika ŋmana. Mi abe dan poom a poli ayen yiila boro, a yali yokku de a biak bisa. 13Ni le limisi ate ba pagi? Kude ale kasi ate ni kan yali? M lieba ni seba kama ayen kude kan baga a nye. Naawen ale basi ate kude a nye mi. Dii meena abe le nye ni la ku a daani mu yegayega.>> 14Ba ŋman deri a kum. Ate Orpa yaa gbaari wa ŋianipowa a banti wa ale ŋman kuli, alege Arut zɛri ale va. 15Naomi yaa weeni Arut ayen, <<Nwala ŋmani a kuli wa nyama jigi kama ale ba wenaŋa jigi. Va wa a kuli.>>
16Arut yaa ŋman weeni ayen, Kan weeni mu ayen m basi fu. Basi ate m va fu. Juijui meena ate fi a cheŋ la, m le va cheŋ, juijui meena mɛ ate fi a boro la, m le maa boro. Fi nuruma ale chim mi mɛ nuruba, fi Wenni ale chim mi mɛ Wen. 17Juijui ate fi a kpi la, mi mɛ a kpi ka dula ate ba a gu mu dula. Naawen a basi ate ninam yegayega a jam m zuk, ase m nin basi ate wayoŋ a poori mu fi jigi alege daa kum ale poori mu fi jigi ya. 18Naomi ale nya ale Arut a tik kama ayen wa va wa la, wa an ŋman weeni wari ya.
19Ba yaa cheŋ ga paari Betiliyem. Ba le paari dula la, tɛŋka demma sui yaa peenti, ate nipooma a weeni ayen, <<Ka Naomi ni nna suma?>> 20Wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni kaa wi mu ayen Naomi, ni a wi mu ayen Mara dii nyiŋla Wen Dii Ale a Niak La a basi kama ate m boka a toa nna katikati. 21Mi ale basi dela la, m ta kama yegayega, alege Naawen an ta mi ŋmani ale jaaboa. Ka boa ale soa ate ni a wi mu ayen Naomi. Naawen dii ale zuak la a bo mini mi kama a basi ate ninam a jam mi jigi.>>
22Naomi ale wa sampowa Arut ale nyini Moab tɛŋka a jam diila ale nna. Ba ale jam Betiliyem la ale ŋanta a nye magsi a yaali ka cheka.

english_text:
Ruth Meets Boaz
1-3 One day, Ruth said to Naomi, “Let me see if I can find someone who will let me pick up the grain left in the fields by the harvest workers.”
Naomi answered, “Go ahead, my daughter.” So immediately Ruth went out to pick up grain in a field. She didn't know it was owned by Boaz, a relative of Naomi's husband Elimelech, as well as a rich and important man.
4When Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and went out to his field, he said to the harvest workers, “The Lord bless you!”
They replied, “And may the Lord bless you!”
5Then Boaz asked the man in charge of the harvest workers, “Who is that young woman?”
6The man answered, “She is the one who came back from Moab with Naomi. 7She asked if she could pick up grain left by the harvest workers, and she has been working all morning without a moment's rest.”
8Boaz went over to Ruth and said, “I think it would be best for you not to pick up grain in anyone else's field. Stay here with the women 9and follow along behind them, as they gather up what the men have cut. I have warned the men not to bother you, and whenever you are thirsty, you can drink from their water jars.”
10Ruth bowed down to the ground and said, “You know I come from another country. Why are you so good to me?”
11Boaz answered, “I've heard how you've helped your mother-in-law ever since your husband died. You even left your own father and mother to come and live in a foreign land among people you don't know. 12I pray that the Lord God of Israel will reward you for what you have done. And now that you have come to him for protection, I pray that he will bless you.”
13Ruth replied, “Sir, it's good of you to speak kindly to me and make me feel so welcome. I'm not even one of your servants.”
14At mealtime Boaz said to Ruth, “Come, eat with us. Have some bread and dip it in the sauce.” At once she sat down with the workers, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. Ruth ate all she wanted and had some left over.
15When Ruth left to start picking up grain, Boaz told his men, “Don't stop her, even if she picks up grain from where it is stacked. 16Be sure to pull out some stalks of grain from the bundles and leave them on the ground for her. And don't speak harshly to her!”
17Ruth worked in the field until evening. Then after she had pounded the grain off the stalks, she had a large basket full of grain. 18She took the grain to town and showed Naomi how much she had picked up. Ruth also gave her the food left over from her lunch.
19Naomi said, “Where did you work today? Whose field was it? God bless the man who treated you so well!” Then Ruth told her that she had worked in the field of a man named Boaz.
20 “The Lord bless Boaz!” Naomi replied. “He has shown that he is still loyal to the living and to the dead. Boaz is a close relative, one of those who is supposed to look after us.”
21Ruth told her, “Boaz even said I could stay in the field with his workers until they had finished harvesting all his grain.”
22Naomi replied, “My daughter, it's good that you can pick up grain alongside the women who work in his field. Who knows what might happen to you in someone else's field!” 23And so, Ruth stayed close to the women, while picking up grain in his field.
Ruth worked in the fields until the barley and wheat were harvested. And all this time she lived with Naomi.
translation_text:
1Nuru ale jam boro, wa yuei ale Boazi. Wa jam ka nuru maŋ. Wa be ka Naomi chorɔwa suok a nyini Elimelek buuni po. 2Arut waai ale nyini Moab la yaa weeni Naomi ayen, <<Basi ate m cheŋ tattaŋa po, waai a dan boro a ŋari wa ŋanta, ate kula nyɔnɔ a ta jiirim ale mu abe m yiisi a vi wa. Naomi a yaa weeni wa ayen, <<M lie fi baga a cheŋ kama.>> 3Wa yaa cheŋ a ga yiisi a vi baai ale a ŋari la ŋaaŋ. Wa ga a miŋ ale wa bo ka Boazi talim po a yiisi. Boazi abe nyini ka Elimelek buuni po.
4Ku an beniya ate Boazi a nyini Betiliyem a jam a yaa te baai ale a ŋari ŋantaŋa la jiam ale weeni ayen, Naawen a bo ale ba, ate ba mɛ tulisi ayen, <<Naawen abe niak fi mɛ,>> 5Boazi a yaa bek waai ale a nya baai ale a ŋari la zuk ayen, <<Ka wana lie ale nna?>> 6Waai ale a nya ba zuk la a yaa weeni ayen wa nyini ka Moab a va Naomi a jam. 7Wa abe weeni kama ayen, wa a saalim m basi ate wa yiisi a vi baai ale a ŋari la ŋaaŋ. Wa abe jo talimu po kama a tom nyini saluiku a jam paari yɔgyɔgla de. Wa kali vuusi ka maga viuku po. 8Boazi a yaa weeni Arut ayen, <<M lie, wom m le a weeni fu diila kan basi dela abe fi cheŋ talim yoŋ po a yiisi ŋanta. Bo dela ale nipokbili sii ale tom a te mi la. 9Kpesi a nya talim buui ate mi nuruma a tom la abe fi va nipokbilisaŋa. M weeni nuruma kama ayen ba kan nye fu wari ya. Nyanyuila a dan ta fu diipo, nuruma a ŋari nyiam a sueri samɔnsaŋa kama, ga ŋari nyu.>> 10Wa yaa domsi kali a nye wa jiam, wa ale ŋmani te wa ale pai wa nichaanɔwa a chim nuru diila. 11Boazi yaa weeni ayen, <<Ba weeni mu fi ale nye dii meena a te fi ŋianipowa a zaani diipo ate fi chorɔwa a kpi la kama. Ale fi ale basi fi mawa ale fi kowa ale fi tɛŋka ale jam ayen fi bo ale nuru baai ate fi zɛ ba la. 12Naawen ale pilim tuni fu fi ale nye diila, Izirali Wenni ate fi ta fidek a jam su wa kiŋkaŋŋa po la, ale tuni fu dii meena ate fi nye la. 13Arut yaa weeni ayen, <<M be kasim a nya fi ŋmanteka kama. Fi basi ate m sui a yɔk kama ale biisi jiirim biik ale mi, fi tomteerɔwa alege mi an poom soa ale nipokbili sii ale tom a te fu la wanyi mɛ.>>
14Boazi a yaa weeni wa ayen, ku dan paari ŋandiinta dɛka po, wa ga pai boroboroku a lusi damiisiŋka po a ŋɔbi. Wa ale kala ale baai ale a ŋari ŋantaŋa la ba yaa sɛ ŋanta te wa, ate wa ŋɔbi chak ale tali. 15Wa ale yiti ayen wa yiisi la, Boazi a yaa weeni wa nuruma ayen, <<Wa dan poom a tigsi bobaŋa ni basi, ni kan nyo wa chivie po. 16Ni goanti yeeri gela ate wa pai, ni kan toariŋ wa.>> 17Arut yaa yiisi talimu po a ga paari junɔi. Wa yaa fɔbi ŋantaŋa a nya ase taasi kpienni nɔi la. 18Wa yaa ta kuli yeri ate wa ŋianipowa a nya ŋantaŋa ale soa diila. Wa ŋman pai ŋandiin tii ate wa dɛ ale tali la a te wa. 19Wa ŋianipowa a yaa bek wa ayen, <<Fi yiisi ka be jinla? Fi tom ka be? Nuru waai ale seba fi nɔi po la ale nya niaka.>> Arut yaa weeni wa ŋiak nipowa waai jigi ate wa a tom la, <<Nuru waai jigi ate mi tom jinla la ale Boazi.>> 20Naomi a yaa weeni wa sampowa ayen, <<Naawen ale niak wa. Wa an basi jiirim sakka ale ŋanvuta ale kpieba.>> Wa yaa ŋman weeni ayen, <<Nuru wala ka tama dek suok. Wa ka ti da tuesirɔma wanyi.>> 21Arut waai ale nyini Moab la a yaa weeni ayen, <<Wa poom weeni mi kama ayen m bo ale wa tuimtomdɔma ate ba ga ŋari wa ŋantaŋa a nueri.>> 22Naomi a yaa weeni wa sampowa Arut ayen, <<Ku nala kama m lie, ate fi cheŋ ale nipokbilisaŋa dii nyiŋla nuru yoŋ talim po ba baga a nye fu biem kama.>> 23Dila nyiŋ Arut yaa kasim bo ale ka nipokbili sii ale a tom a te Boazi la ate ŋantaŋa ŋarika ga nueri. Arut jam kasim boro ale ka wa ŋianipowa.

english_text:
Naomi Makes Plans for Ruth
1One day, Naomi said to Ruth:
It's time I found you a husband, who will give you a home and take care of you.
2You have been picking up grain alongside the women who work for Boaz, and you know he is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be threshing the grain. 3Now take a bath and put on some perfume, then dress in your best clothes. Go where he is working, but don't let him see you until he has finished eating and drinking. 4Watch where he goes to spend the night, then when he is asleep, lift the cover and lie down at his feet. He will tell you what to do.
5Ruth answered, “I'll do whatever you say.” 6She went out to the place where Boaz was working and did what Naomi had told her.
7After Boaz finished eating and drinking and was feeling happy, he went over and fell asleep near the pile of grain. Ruth slipped over quietly. She lifted the cover and lay down near his feet.
8In the middle of the night, Boaz suddenly woke up and was shocked to see a woman lying at his feet. 9“Who are you?” he asked.
“Sir, I am Ruth,” she answered, “and you are the relative who is supposed to take care of me. So spread the edge of your cover over me.”
10Boaz replied:
The Lord bless you! This shows how truly loyal you are to your family. You could have looked for a younger man, either rich or poor, but you didn't. 11Don't worry, I'll do what you have asked. You are respected by everyone in town.
12 It's true that I am one of the relatives who is supposed to take care of you, but there is someone who is an even closer relative. 13Stay here until morning, then I will find out if he is willing to look after you. If he isn't, I promise by the living God to do it myself. Now go back to sleep until morning.
14Ruth lay down again, but she got up before daylight, because Boaz did not want anyone to know she had been there. 15Then he told her to spread out her cape. And he filled it with grain and placed it on her shoulder.
When Ruth got back to town, 16Naomi asked her what had happened, and Ruth told her everything. 17She also said, “Boaz gave me this grain, because he didn't want me to come back without something for you.”
18Naomi replied, “Just be patient and don't worry about what will happen. He won't rest until everything is settled today!”
translation_text:
1Dai yeŋ ate Naomi, Arut ŋianipowa a yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Ku an magsi ayen m yaali dɔk a te fu ate ba a nya fi zuwa? 2Boazi waai ate fi bo wa jigi ale nipokbilisaŋa la, daa tama suowa? Jinla yokku wa za wa fɔbi wa ŋantaŋa a yali kama. 3Fi yaa so fi nyiŋka a sa kpa buui nyum ale masa la abe fi jo garuk tii ate fi mariŋ la. Fi dan nye dila fi yaa cheŋ ŋantaŋa yalika jigini alege kan basi ate wa seba ayen fi bo dula, se ka wa nin dɛ nueri. 4Wa yaa bɛ dan so, kpesi nya juijui ate wa doa la. Fi yaa yik jabuui ale lik wa la a zak abe fi ge wa naŋsaŋa a yaa duak. Fi dan nye dila wa yaa le weeni fi le fi nye diila.>> 5Arut yaa weeni ayen, <<M le nye dii meena ate fi weeni la.>>
6Wa yaa cheŋ ŋantaŋa fɔbika jigini a ga nye dii meena ate wa ŋianipowa a weeni wa ayen wa nye la. 7Boazi ale dɛ nueri ate wa nyiŋka a yɔk la, wa yaa ga duak wa ŋantaŋa ale vi chaab zuk dua la jigini kpeglimka. Arut yaa mak cheŋ a ga lagri alege wa naŋsaŋa a yaa duak. 8Yɔkku suŋsuŋ jaab yaa nye ate Boazi nye nna legi, a ga a labri la ale nipok ale dua wa naŋsa po. 9Boazi yaa bek ayen, <<Ka wana?>> Arut yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ka mi Arut fi tomteerɔwa.>> Arut yaa ŋman weeni ayen pai fi garukku kauk a lik mu fi le ka m da tuesirɔ la nyiŋ. 10Boazi yaa weeni ayen, <<M lie, Naawen ale niak fu. Jiirim buui ate fi sak ale mu la a poom gaam fi ale liŋ sak jiirim buui la kama. Fi an chali a vi bimbaan paaluk ŋaaŋŋa, jigsirɔba yaase ŋanjaksa. 11Yɔgyɔgla de, m lie, kan te fi kpaziim a nak. M le nye dii meena ate fi a yaali la a te fu. Mi tɛŋka nuruma meena a seba ayen fi ka nipok waai nyeka ale nala. 12Ku ka wensie ayen m ka da tuesirɔ, alege da tuesirɔ a boro a moata gaam mi. 13Be goa dela yokku de ate chum saluik wa dan da tuesi fu ku nala. Alege wa dan kan da tuesi fu, Naawen boro mi ale da tuesi fu.>> 14Dila la, wa yaa duak wa naŋsa geŋ, a yaa kpabi yiti diipo ate nuru kan nya a miŋ la, a yaa weeni ayen, <<Kan basi ate ba miŋ ayen nipok a jam ŋantaŋa fɔbika jigini.>> 15Boazi yaa ŋman weeni wa ayen, <<Ta garuk kuui ate fi pai a lik fi zukku la a jam lagri.>> Wa ale lagri la, wa yaa pai jaab magsi barli ku nɔi buyuebi a kpiiri nyoro a ji wa ate wa ta kuli. 16Arut ale ga wa ŋianipowa jigi la, wa yaa bek wa ayen, <<Fi le cheŋ la ku nye ka sɛ, m lie?>> Wa yaa weeni dii meena ate Boazi a nye te wa la, 17ale ŋman weeni wa le magsi barliwa jaamu nɔi buyuebiwa te wa ale weeni ayen, <<Kan kuli fi ŋianipowa jigi ale nikotta>> la. 18Naomi yaa weeni ayen, <<M lie limisi ate fi nya dii meena ale za ku nye la. Nuruwa kan vuusi se ka wanni a nin nye magsi jinla.>>

english_text:
Ruth and Boaz Get Married
1In the meanwhile, Boaz had gone to the meeting place at the town gate and was sitting there when the other close relative came by. So Boaz invited him to come over and sit down, and he did. 2Then Boaz got ten of the town leaders and also asked them to sit down. After they had sat down, 3he said to the man:
Naomi has come back from Moab and is selling the land that belonged to her husband Elimelech. 4I'm telling you about this, since you are his closest relative and have the right to buy the property. If you want it, you can buy it now. These ten men and the others standing here can be witnesses. But if you don't want the property, let me know, because I am next in line.
The man replied, “I'll buy it!”
5“If you do buy it from Naomi,” Boaz told him, “you must also marry Ruth. Then if you have a son by her, the property will stay in the family of Ruth's first husband.”
6The man answered, “If that's the case, I don't want to buy it! That would make problems with the property I already own. You may buy it yourself, because I cannot.”
7 To make a sale legal in those days, one person would take off a sandal and give it to the other. 8So after the man had agreed to let Boaz buy the property, he took off one of his sandals and handed it to Boaz.
9Boaz told the town leaders and everyone else:
All of you are witnesses that today I have bought from Naomi the property that belonged to Elimelech and his two sons, Chilion and Mahlon. 10 You are also witnesses that I have agreed to marry Mahlon's widow Ruth, the Moabite woman. This will keep the property in his family's name, and he will be remembered in this town.
11 The town leaders and the others standing there said:
We are witnesses to this. And we pray that the Lord will give your wife many children, just as he did Leah and Rachel, the wives of Jacob. May you be a rich man in the tribe of Ephrath and an important man in Bethlehem. 12 May the children you have by this young woman make your family as famous as the family of Perez, the son of Tamar and Judah.
13Boaz married Ruth, and the Lord blessed her with a son. 14After his birth, the women said to Naomi:
Praise the Lord! Today he has given you a grandson to take care of you. We pray that the boy will grow up to be famous everywhere in Israel. 15He will make you happy and take care of you in your old age, because he is the son of your daughter-in-law. And she loves you more than seven sons of your own would love you.
16Naomi loved the boy and took good care of him. 17The neighborhood women named him Obed, but they called him “Naomi's Boy.”
When Obed grew up he had a son named Jesse, who later became the father of King David. 18-22Here is a list of the ancestors of David: Jesse, Obed, Boaz, Salmon, Nahshon, Amminadab, Ram, Hezron, and Perez.

Hannah Asks the Lord for a Child
1Elkanah lived in Ramah, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His great-great-grandfather was Zuph, so Elkanah was a member of the Zuph clan of the Ephraim tribe. Elkanah's father was Jeroham, his grandfather was Elihu, and his great-grandfather was Tohu.
2Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Although Peninnah had children, Hannah did not have any.
3Once a year Elkanah traveled from his hometown to Shiloh, where he worshiped the Lord All-Powerful and offered sacrifices. Eli was the Lord's priest there, and his two sons Hophni and Phinehas served with him as priests.
4Whenever Elkanah offered a sacrifice, he gave some of the meat to Peninnah and some to each of her sons and daughters. 5But he gave Hannah even more, because he loved Hannah very much, even though the Lord had kept her from having children of her own.
6Peninnah liked to make Hannah feel miserable about not having any children, 7especially when the family went to the house of the Lord each year.
One day, Elkanah was there offering a sacrifice, when Hannah began crying and refused to eat. 8So Elkanah asked, “Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why do you feel so bad? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?”
9When the sacrifice had been offered, and they had eaten the meal, Hannah got up and went to pray. Eli was sitting in his chair near the door to the place of worship. 10Hannah was heartbroken and was crying as she prayed, 11 “Lord All-Powerful, I am your servant, but I am so miserable! Please let me have a son. I promise to give him to you for as long as he lives, and his hair will never be cut.”
12-13Hannah prayed silently to the Lord for a long time. But her lips were moving, and Eli thought she was drunk. 14“How long are you going to stay drunk?” he asked. “Sober up!”
15-16“Sir, please don't think I'm no good!” Hannah answered. “I'm not drunk, and I haven't been drinking. But I do feel miserable and terribly upset. I've been praying all this time, telling the Lord about my problems.”
17Eli replied, “Go home. Everything will be fine. The God of Israel will answer your prayer.”
18“Sir, thank you for being so kind to me,” Hannah said. Then she left, and after eating something, she felt much better.
Samuel Is Born
19Elkanah and his family got up early the next morning and worshiped the Lord. Then they went back home to Ramah. Later the Lord blessed Elkanah and Hannah 20with a son. She named him Samuel because she had asked the Lord for him.

Then I'll give him to the Lord, and he can stay there at Shiloh for the rest of his life.”
