translation_text:
1Nuru ale jam boro wa yuei ale Elkana. Wa jam nyini ka Arama tɛŋka ate ka bo Zuf, Ɛfraim tɛŋka po, kauk kuui ate guuta a boro la. Wa kowa yuei jam le Jeroyam. Wa kokpieŋka yuei jam le Eliyu. Wa kokpieŋka kowa yuei jam le Toyu. Toyu a jam ka Zuf biik. Elkana ale wa nuruma jam nyini ka Ɛfraim dɔkku po. 2Elkana jam ta ka nipooba baye. Wanyi yuei jam le Yanna, nwala yuei jam le Peninna. Peninna jam ta bisa kama alege Yanna jam ka kirik.
3Bein meena Elkana ale wa dɔkdemma a nyiem basi ba tɛŋka Arama kama alege cheŋ Siilo ayen ba puusi Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La abe ba nye kaabka te wa. Nuru ale jam bo Siilo ate ba a wi wa ayen Eli. Wa jam ka Naawen kaabteerɔ. Eli jam ta ka nidoabilisa baye, Yofni ale Fineyas. Ba mɛ jam ka kaabteerɔba. 4Elkana a dan jam nye kaabka wa nyiem chari wa dɔkdemma lammu kama. Wa le gebi lammu dii a te wa powa Peninna la, wa a gebi ka dila mɛ a te wa bisaŋa ale wa liema. 5Alege Yanna wa nyiem te ka ku nɔi buye dii nyiŋla wa a yaali wa ka nna yegayega, ale Naawen ale diem lik wa bisa biamu la meena. 6Peninna waai ale ka Yanna ŋaanchoa la a nye wa a la a basi ate wa sui a puuri dii nyiŋla Naawen a basi kama ate Yanna a ka bisa. 7Peninna a kasim a nye Yanna ka dila bein meena. Diipo meena ba dan cheŋ Naawen yenni ale bo Siilo la, Peninna a nye Yanna a la kama ate wa kum a zɛri ŋandiinta. 8Kude nyiem dan nye, Elkana yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Yanna, ka boa ale soa ate fi a kum? Ka boa ale soa ate fi a zɛri ŋandiinta dɛka? Ka boa ate fi sui a kaasi? Mi ale yaali fu a soa diila an gaam bisa pi?>>
9Dai yeŋ Elkana ale wa dɔkdemma ale dɛ nueri Siilo po la, Yanna yaa yiti zaani. Eli waai ale ka kaabteerɔ la a jam kali ka zukpaglik zuk Naawen yenni tuoku nɔi peelim. 10Yanna sui ale jam kaasi nna yegayega ate wa puusi a te Naawen ale kasim a kum. 11Wa puusaŋa po wa yaa puulim a weeni ayen, <<Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, nya m niniga, kan baŋi. Fi dan te fi liewa nidoabili, mi a puulim kama ayen m le pai wa te fu wa boka po meena. Dii ale di sak ayen m pai wa te fu la wa kan che wa zuisaŋa.>>
12Yanna ale a puusi a te Naawen la, Eli yaa kpesi a nya wa nɔnni. 13Wa le a puusi la, Eli a poli ayen wa nyu ka daam, diila wa nɔngbanvaataŋa ale a choa alege wa an jam puusi ate ku a jueli. Wa jam a puusi ka wa suinummu po. 14Eli yaa weeni Yanna ayen, <<Ka boa ti fi buk daam a jam dela? Basi fi daamu yibaŋa.>> 15Yanna yaa weeni ayen, <<Daa di m nyɔnɔ. Mi an nyu daamoa. Mi an poom a nyu daamoa. Ka m sui ale kaasi ate mi a puusi dila. Mi a weeni ka Naawen dii ale a daani mu la. 16Mi a weeni wa ka m niniŋŋa ale ka diila. Kan poli ayen m daa nipok maŋŋa.>> 17Eli yaa weeni ayen, <<Fi baga a cheŋ kama ale suiyɔgni. Izirali Wenni ale nye dii ate fi bek wa la te fu.>> 18Yanna yaa weeni ayen, <<Mi a nye fi jiam. Be kasim poli wamaŋsa a te mu.>> Wa le biisi nueri la wa yaa basi Eli ale ga yaali ŋandiinta dɛ. Wa sui a ŋman jam kaasi ya.
19Vari ale veenti la saluik yokyokwa Elkana ale wa dɔkdemma a yaa yiti a puusi Naawen wa yenni po Siilo ale ŋman kuli ba yenni ale bo Arama la. Elkana yaa goa ale Yanna wa powa, ate Naawen a teeri wa wari. 20Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ Yanna yaa yik lɔgi a biak nidoabili a te wa yuei ayen Samuel. Wa mawa weeni wadek ayen dii nyiŋla m bek ka Naawen ate wa te mu.
21Ku ŋman jam paari ka diipo ale magsi Elkana ale wa dɔkdemma a cheŋ Siilo a ga nye ben nuerika kaabka ate Naawen. Elkana mɛ poom jam a yaali kama ayen wa ga tuni wa pumpuulimaŋa a te Naawen. 22Yanna an jam va cheŋ ya. Wa jam weeni wa chorɔwa kama ayen, <<M kan va cheŋ yɔgyɔgla. M le limisi ate biika gaari biisiri abe m yaa ta wa cheŋ Wen yenni ale bo Siilo po la a pai wa te Naawen ate wa kasim bo dula.>>
23Wa chorɔwa Elkana yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Ku bo ka fi jigi. Nye dii ale nala a te fu la. Wari bo yeri ate biika a gaari biisiri. Naawen a maari fu ate fi ta fi pumpuulimaŋa.>> Yanna yaa wari a nya wa biika zuk.
24Biika ale gaari biisiri la, ba yaa ta wa cheŋ Naawen yenni ale bo Siilo la. Ba jam ta ka bena ŋata lalik, ale boorik geli ale zom, ale bunlɔk ale daam a cheŋ ayen ba te Naawen. 25Wa nyama ale ko lalikka a te Naawen la, ba yaa pai Samuel a te Eli Naawen yenni po ale bo Siilo la. 26Yanna yaa bek Eli ayen, <<M koa, fi a teeri mu? Mi ale nipok waai ate fi jam nya ale wa puusi a te Naawen bena maga ale taam la. 27M jam puusi a yaali ka biika de ate Naawen a te mu mi ale bek diila. 28Dila nyiŋ yɔgyɔgla de m pai wa a te ka Naawen. Wa le kasim tom a te ka Naawen wa boka po meena.>> Wa le biisi nueri la, ba yaa puusi Naawen dula jigini.

english_text:
1 Hannah prayed:
You make me strong
and happy, Lord.
You rescued me.
Now I can be glad
and laugh at my enemies.
2No other god is like you.
And with you we are safer
than on a high mountain.
3I can tell those proud people,
“Stop your boasting!
Nothing is hidden from the Lord,
and he judges what we do.”
4Our Lord, you break
the bows of warriors,
but you give strength
to everyone who stumbles.
5People who once
had plenty to eat
must now hire themselves out
for only a piece of bread.
But you give the hungry more
than enough to eat.
A woman did not have a child,
and you gave her seven,
but a woman who had many
was left with none.
6 You take away life,
and you give life.
You send people down
to the world of the dead
and bring them back again.
7Our Lord, you are the one
who makes us rich or poor.
You put some in high positions
and bring disgrace on others.
8You lift the poor and homeless
out of the garbage dump
and give them places of honor
in royal palaces.
You set the world on foundations,
and they belong to you.
9You protect your loyal people,
but everyone who is evil
will die in darkness.
We cannot win a victory
by our own strength.
10Our Lord, those who attack you
will be broken in pieces
when you fight back
with thunder from heaven.
You will judge the whole earth
and give power and strength
to your chosen king.
Samuel Stays with Eli
11Elkanah and Hannah went back home to Ramah, but the boy Samuel stayed to help Eli serve the Lord.
Eli's Sons
12-13Eli's sons were priests, but they were dishonest and refused to obey the Lord. So, while people were boiling the meat from their sacrifices, these priests would send over a servant with a large, three-pronged fork. 14The servant would stick the fork into the cooking pot, and whatever meat came out on the fork was taken back to Eli's two sons. That was how they treated every Israelite who came to offer sacrifices in Shiloh. 15Sometimes, when people were offering sacrifices, the servant would come over, even before the fat had been cut off and sacrificed to the Lord.
Then the servant would tell them, “The priest doesn't want his meat boiled! Give him some raw meat that he can roast!”
16Usually the people answered, “Take what you want. But first, let us sacrifice the fat to the Lord.”
“No,” the servant would reply. “If you don't give it to me now, I'll take it by force.”
17Eli's sons did not show any respect for the sacrifices that the people offered. This was a terrible sin, and it made the Lord very angry.
Hannah Visits Samuel
18The boy Samuel served the Lord and wore a special linen garment 19and the clothes his mother made for him. She brought new clothes every year, when she and her husband came to offer sacrifices at Shiloh.
20Eli always blessed Elkanah and his wife and said, “Samuel was born in answer to your prayers. Now you have given him to the Lord. I pray that the Lord will bless you with more children to take his place.” After Eli had blessed them, Elkanah and Hannah would return home.
21The Lord was kind to Hannah, and she had three more sons and two daughters. But Samuel grew up at the Lord's house in Shiloh.
Eli Warns His Sons
22Eli was now very old, and he heard what his sons were doing to the people of Israel. 23-24“Why are you doing these awful things?” he asked them. “I've been hearing nothing but complaints about you from all of the Lord's people. 25If you harm another person, God can help make things right between the two of you. But if you commit a crime against the Lord, no one can help you!”
But the Lord had already decided to kill them. So he kept them from listening to their father.
A Prophet Speaks to Eli
26 Each day, as Samuel grew older, the Lord was pleased with him, and so were the people.
27One day a prophet came to Eli and gave him this message from the Lord:
When your ancestors were slaves of the king of Egypt, I came and showed them who I am. 28-29 Out of all the tribes of Israel, I chose your family to be my priests. I wanted them to offer sacrifices and burn incense to me and to find out from me what I want my people to do. I commanded everyone to bring their sacrifices here where I live, and I allowed you and your family to keep those that were not offered to me on the altar.
But you honor your sons instead of me! You don't respect the sacrifices and offerings that are brought to me, and you've all grown fat from eating the best parts.
30I am the Lord, the God of Israel. I promised to always let your family serve me as priests, but now I tell you that I cannot do this any longer! I honor anyone who honors me, but I put a curse on anyone who hates me. 31The time will come when I will kill you and everyone else in your family. Not one of you will live to an old age.
32Your family will have a lot of trouble. I will be kind to Israel, but everyone in your family will die young. 33If I let anyone from your family be a priest, his life will be full of sadness and sorrow. But most of the men in your family will die a violent death! 34 To prove to you that I will do these things, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will die on the same day.
35I have chosen someone else to be my priest, someone who will be faithful and obey me. I will always let his family serve as priests and help my chosen king. 36But if anyone is left from your family, he will come to my priest and beg for money or a little bread. He may even say to my priest, “Please let me be a priest, so I will at least have something to eat.”

1Yanna yaa puusi a weeni ayen, <<M sui peenti ale Naawen kama. M pagrimu a nyini ka fi jigi. Mi a la m dachaasaŋa kama dii nyiŋla m sui peenti kama fi le vari mu ba jigi a basi la. 2Naawen, waai karo a welema ase fi la. Fi nyiini ale Wen. Fi a nye ase ka piuŋ la, a lik ti. 3Naawen, basi ate baai ale a kuulim a biisi ale kanjanta la a nye diki. Diila fi Naawen ka Wen dii ale seba wari meena ale a bo nuru meena ale a nye diila buusa. 4A basi ate tugurik tɔŋdɔba tima a wɛ, alege baai ale wobsa la, fi ale a te ba pagrim. 5Baai ale jam ta ŋandiinta yegayega a dɛ la a nyini kama a tom a yaali ŋandiinta. Alege baai ate kɔm jam ta ba la, a yaa dɛ kama a chak. Waai ale jam kaa biak la, yaa biak ka bisa bayopɔi, Alege waai ale jam ta nidoabilisa piisi la ba meena a kpi. 6Naawen ale ta kum a jam, wa abe le a te nyuvuri. Wa le te nuruba a cheŋ kpiluŋ, wa le te ba a yiti. 7Naawen ale basi ate jaŋsa a jam ale basi ate jigsika a jam. Wa le basi ate nuru a chim nuru fiik wa abe le basi ate nuru a chim nuru kpioŋ. 8Naawen ale zak jajak wa niniga po ate wa a yiti. Naawen ale a te ba kpaŋta ale yuei. Wa le a nye tɛŋka nyubaŋa. Wa be nye tɛŋka ka nyubi ŋala zuk. 9Naawen ale a lik wa nuruma baai ale a va wa ale wensie la juijui meena ate ba a cheŋ la, alege ku daa di wabaata nyama jigi ya. Ba le kpi a cheŋ kpiluŋ. Ku daa pagrim ate nuru dek a baga a nye wari ya. 10Baai ale ta chaab ale Naawen la wa le kaasi ba. Wa ale na wenŋmazuk a ta chaab ale ba. Naawen ale bo baai meena ale bo tɛŋzuk la buusa. Wa le lueri naab waai la, wa le te wa pagrim ate wa a nya tɛŋka zuk abe wa te wa yuei.
11Elkana ale wa powa Yanna yaa kuli ba yenni ale bo Arama la. Alege ba biika Samuel yaa wari Siilo ate Eli a sak wa ate wa tom a te Naawen.
12Eli nidoabilisaŋa a jam ka bi baata. Ba jam kan zuli Naawen. 13Kaabteerɔma ale jam a nye nuruma diila ale nna. Ase nuru a dan jam nye kaabka, ba le pai ka samɔniŋ a dik lammu. Kaabteerɔwa yɔmawa nyiem yaa pai duisuk nyina ŋata, 14a su samɔniŋka po. Duisuku ale lu yeeri lam buui a ta jueli la kaabteerɔwa ale soa. Alege ba le jam a nye Izirali demma meena ale a jam Siilo a nye kaabka la ale nna. 15Alege ate ba ju kpaamu la, kaabteerɔwa yɔmawa a nyiem jam waai ale a nye kaabka la jigi kama a weeni ayen, <<Te kaabteerɔwa lam ate wa se. Wa kan yaali lam digmoa.>>
16Waai ale a nye kaabka la a dan weeni ayen, <<Basi ate kpaamu a se nueri ase ku le magsi diila abe fi yaa lueri dii ate fi a yaali la,>> kaabteerɔwa yɔmawa a tulisi kama ayen, <<Te mu kpaamu yɔgyɔgla dan kan daa di m le fɛ yeeri.>>
17Naawen yaa nya ayen Eli bisaŋa biemu a zuak ka yega dii nyiŋla ba kan sak zula ale kaabka ate ba nye a te Naawen la.
18Alege Samuel jam kasim tom a te Naawen kama. Wa jam ka biik a jo garuk geli ate ba pai garuk naluŋ a nye. 19Ben meena wa mawa nyiem baali ka garuk woŋ a te wa. Wa le wa chorɔwa nyiem dan cheŋ ayen ba nye benni kaabka wa yaa deri pai te wa. 20Eli nyiem yaa weeni niauŋ a te Elkana ale wa powa ayen, <<Mi a yaali ayen ka Naawen niak fi ale fi powa ale bisa ate ba tagri waai ate wa bek ale pai wa te Naawen la.>> Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ate ba yaa kuli. 21Ate Naawen sak jiirim ale Yanna ate wa biak nidoabilisa bata ale nipokbilisa baye. Samuel jam kasim tom a te Naawen kama alege a chim.
22Eli jam kpaŋ kama ale kasim a wom biem buui meena ate wa bisaŋa a nye Izirali demma la. A wom ba le a goa ale nipooma baai ale a nya ŋantaŋa ale bo juijui ate Naawen a tu wa nuruma la nansuiŋku nɔi. 23Eli yaa weeni wa nidoabilisaŋa ayen, <<Ka boa ale soa ate ni a nye wieŋa de? Nuruma jam a weeni mu waba tii meena ate ni a nye la kama. 24Ni kaa nye wieŋa de chaaba. Ba a biisi ate ku a cheŋ kama biem buui meena ate ni a nye la. 25Ni seba ayen nuru a dan nye kaasi wa choa, Wen a baga yik ba a niak chaab kama, alege nuru a dan potim nye kaasi Naawen dii karo a maari wa?>> Alege wa nidoabilisaŋa zɛri ba an wom wa kaamka. Dii ate ba zɛri la, Naawen poom poli kama ayen wa basi ate ba kpi ba wabaataŋa nyiŋ.
26Alege Samuel jam kasim a chim kama. Naawen sui a peenti ale wa kama. Izirali demma mɛ sui a peenti ale wa.
27Dila po Wen nuru yaa jam Eli jigi a weeni wa ayen, <<Naawen ale weeni fu diila ale nna. <Fi seba ayen diipo ate fi kokpieŋsaŋa a jam chim Faaro yɔm Ejipiti la, Mi pai m dek kama a sak Aaron ale wa dɔkdemma. 28Mi lueri wa kama ale ayen wa chim Naawen Yenni kaabteerɔba kpagi a tom a te mu. Ku jam ka wa tuini ayen wa nye kaabka kuŋkuŋku zuk abe wa ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa a te mu zula. Wa mɛ jam nya suik kama a jo Naawen Yenni kaabteerɔba kpagi garuk geli, ayen wa a gisi m yaalika. Daa dila nyiini, m jam te wa suik kuŋkuŋku zuk kama la. 29Alege fi ale fi nidoabilisaŋa a kan zuli tiiritaŋa ate mi weeni m nuruma Izirali demma ate ba ta jam a nye kaabka la. Ka boa ale soa ate fi zuli fi nidoabilisaŋa a gaam mi basi ate ba luk a yeeri ŋan baai ale zunchoŋ la a te ba dega?
30<< <Mi Naawen Izirali Wenni ale puulim ayen ni buuni ale kasim a chim ka Naawen Yenni kaabteerɔba kpaga. Alege yɔgyɔgla, Mi Naawen ale a weeni ayen ku ŋman daa di fi ale fi dɔkdemma jigiya. Baai ale a zɛri mi la, mi mɛ ale zɛri ba. Mi a zuli ka baai ale a zuli mi la. 31Ku cheena ate nidoabili paalukku fi buuni po m le ko ba. Ba wanyi mɛ la a kan pagi. 32Izirali demma ate mi a bo ale ba la ale nya niaka alege nama a kan nya jaaboa alege ka daanika yegayega. 33M le tali ni po wanyi ate wa a tom ase Naawen yenni kaabteerɔba kpagi la, alege fi le kum ate ninyaata a sueri fi ninaŋa ate ku a daani fu. Ku le ka diila, fi ŋaaŋsaŋa a kan pagi, ba le kpi ale ba diem paala kama.
34<< <Fi bisa bayewa Yofni ale Fineyas a dan maa chaab kpi dai yeŋ, ku la le sak ayen m le weeni diila ka wensie. 35M le lueri ka waai ale ta wensie m a nya wa ale wa ŋaaŋsaŋa ate ba tom a te naab waai ate m lueri la. 36Kude dan nye fi ŋaaŋsa baai ale kan kpi la ale cheŋ kpagi dila jigi a ga a juisi ŋandiinta ale ligra. Ba le saalim a yaali ayen ba nya suik a tom a dɛ vuuk.> >>

english_text:
The Lord Speaks to Samuel
1-2Samuel served the Lord by helping Eli the priest, who was by that time almost blind. In those days, the Lord hardly ever spoke directly to people, and he did not appear to them in dreams very often. But one night, Eli was asleep in his room, 3and Samuel was sleeping on a mat near the sacred chest in the Lord's house. They had not been asleep very long 4when the Lord called out Samuel's name.
“Here I am!” Samuel answered. 5Then he ran to Eli and said, “Here I am. What do you want?”
“I didn't call you,” Eli answered. “Go back to bed.”
Samuel went back.
6Again the Lord called out Samuel's name. Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am,” he said. “What do you want?”
Eli told him, “Son, I didn't call you. Go back to sleep.”
7The Lord had not spoken to Samuel before, and Samuel did not recognize the voice. 8When the Lord called out his name for the third time, Samuel went to Eli again and said, “Here I am. What do you want?”
Eli finally realized that it was the Lord who was speaking to Samuel. 9So he said, “Go back and lie down! If someone speaks to you again, answer, ‘I'm listening, Lord. What do you want me to do?’ ”
Once again Samuel went back and lay down.
10The Lord then stood beside Samuel and called out as he had done before, “Samuel! Samuel!”
“I'm listening,” Samuel answered. “What do you want me to do?”
11The Lord said:
Samuel, I am going to do something in Israel that will shock everyone who hears about it! 12I will punish Eli and his family, just as I promised. 13He knew that his sons refused to respect me, and he let them get away with it, even though I said I would punish his family forever. 14I warned Eli that sacrifices or offerings could never make things right! His family has done too many disgusting things.
15The next morning, Samuel got up and opened the doors to the Lord's house. He was afraid to tell Eli what the Lord had said. 16But Eli told him, “Samuel, my boy, come here!”
“Yes, sir!” Samuel answered.
17Eli said, “What did God say to you? Tell me everything. I'll ask God to punish you terribly if you don't tell me every word he said!”
18Samuel told Eli everything. Then Eli said, “He is the Lord, and he will do what's right.”
The Lord Helps Samuel
19As Samuel grew up, the Lord helped him and made everything Samuel said come true. 20From the town of Dan in the north to the town of Beersheba in the south, everyone in the country knew that Samuel was truly the Lord's prophet. 21The Lord often appeared to Samuel at Shiloh and told him what to say.
translation_text:
1Samuel ale jam diem ka biik la, wa jam tom a te Naawen kama a va Eli sinsaŋŋa. Da ŋala po Naawen a jam a biisi ale nuruba ka ka dapo dapo. Wa an jam pai wadek kasim a sak nuruba.
2Eli an ŋman jam nya a chagi. Yɔk kunyi wa yaa dua juijui ate wa duak a goa la. 3Samuel yaa duak Naawen yenni po ayen wa goa. Ku an jam diem sobi ya. Zeuŋku bolimu a diem a dɛ kama. Wen nɔiyeŋka dakanni mɛ za ka yenni po. 4Dila po Naawen yaa wi Samuel yuenni. Samuel yaa wom tulisi ayen, <<Mi ale nna.>> 5Wa yaa chali cheŋ Eli jigi ayen, <<Fi le wi mu la mi ale nna.>> Eli yaa weeni ayen, <<Mi an wi fu. Ga duak,>> Samuel yaa ŋman ga duak.
6Naawen yaa ŋman wi ayen, <<Samuel!>> Samuel ŋman cheŋ ga ayen, <<Fi le wi mu la mi ale nna.>> Eli yaa weeni ayen, <<Aaya, m biiga, mi an wi fu. Ga duak goa.>>
7Dila po Samuel diem jam zɛ Naawen ya, diila wa an diem a biisi ale wa nya ya.
8Naawen yaa ŋman wi Samuel nye buta. Ate Samuel yiti ŋman cheŋ Eli jigi, a weeni wa ayen, <<Fi sum wi mu kama, mi ale nna.>> Eli yaa miŋ ayen ka Naawen ale a wi biika. 9Eli yaa sak Samuel ayen, <<Ga duak. Wa dan ŋman wi fu weeni ayen, <Biisi, Naawen, ale fi yɔmawa a wom kama.> >> Samuel yaa ŋman cheŋ wa goomu jigini a duak.
10Naawen yaa jam zaani wa tɛŋ a wi ayen, <<Samuel! Samuel!>> Samuel yaa weeni ayen, <<Biisi, ale fi yɔmawa a wom kama.>>
11Ate Naawen yaa weeni Samuel ayen, <<Wom mi, mi a yaali ayen m nye Izirali demma ka wari ate waai a dan wom abe wa nyiŋ a gɔk. 12Dila m le nye dii ate m weeni la. M le namsi Eli dɔkdemma. M kan ŋman te wa, m le nye dii ate m weeni ayen mi le nye la. 13M kpaam wa kama ayen m le kasim a namsi wa dɔkdemma, dii nyiŋla Eli seba wa bisaŋa wabaataŋa nyeka ka leeta te mu alege wa an toariŋ ba. 14Dila nyiŋ mi pɛ kama ayen waba tii ate ba nye la m kan vɔŋ te ba diipo, diipo. Ba dan poom te mu tiirim diidii ya.>>
15Samuel yaa duak ate vanni veenti. Ate wa yaa lak Naawen yenni tuataŋa. Wa jam a chali ka yɔgsum ale wa le weeni Eli Naawen ale weeni wa diila. 16Alege Eli yaa wi Samuel ayen, <<M biiga.>> Samuel yaa jam ayen, <<Nya mi ale nna.>> 17Eli yaa bek wa ayen, <<Naawen weeni fu ayen ka boa? Kan suk wari ale mu. Fi dan suk wari mi jigi Wen ale nye ale fu. Weeni mu wari meena ate wa weeni fu la.>> 18Samuel jam weeni wari meena kama wa an suk wari ya. Eli yaa weeni ayen, <<Wa ka Naawen, wa bɛ nye dii ale nala la.
19Samuel chimta po Naawen jam a niak wa kama. Wa jam a nye dii meena ate Samuel a weeni nuruma la kama. 20Izirali tɛŋka po, a zaani Dan a ga paari Beerseba a jam miŋ kama ayen Samuel ka biisiteerɔ ate Naawen a tom. 21Naawen a jam kasim pai wadek a sak Samuel kama Siilo tɛŋka po. Dula jigini wa pai wa wanni a sak wa kama ate wa a biisi.

english_text:
1Then Samuel would speak to the whole nation of Israel.
The Philistines Capture the Sacred Chest
One day the Israelites went out to fight the Philistines. They set up camp near Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek. 2The Philistines made a fierce attack. They defeated the Israelites and killed about 4,000 of them.
3The Israelite army returned to their camp, and the leaders said, “Why did the Lord let us lose to the Philistines today? Let's get the sacred chest where the Lord's agreement with Israel is kept. Then the Lord will help us and rescue us from our enemies.”
4 The army sent some soldiers to bring back the sacred chest from Shiloh, because the Lord All-Powerful has his throne on the winged creatures on top of the chest.
As Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, 5brought the chest into camp, the army cheered so loudly that the ground shook. 6The Philistines heard the noise and said, “What are those Hebrews shouting about?”
When the Philistines learned that the sacred chest had been brought into the camp, 7they were scared to death and said:
The gods have come into their camp. Now we're in real trouble! Nothing like this has ever happened to us before. 8We're in big trouble! Who can save us from these powerful gods? They're the same gods who made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians in the desert.
9Philistines, be brave and fight hard! If you don't, those Hebrews will rule us, just as we've been ruling them. Fight and don't be afraid.
10The Philistines did fight. They killed 30,000 Israelite soldiers, and all the rest ran off to their homes. 11Hophni and Phinehas were killed, and the sacred chest was captured.
Eli Dies
12That same day a soldier from the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battlefront to Shiloh. He had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show his sorrow. 13He went into town and told the news about the battle, and everyone started crying.
Eli was afraid that something might happen to the sacred chest. So he was sitting on his chair beside the road, just waiting. 14-15He was 98 years old and blind, but he could hear everyone crying, and he asked, “What's all that noise?”
The soldier hurried over and told Eli, 16“I escaped from the fighting today and ran here.”
“Young man, what happened?” Eli asked.
17“Israel ran away from the Philistines,” the soldier answered. “Many of our people were killed, including your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas. But worst of all, the sacred chest was captured.”
18Eli was still sitting on a chair beside the wall of the town gate. And when the man said that the Philistines had taken the sacred chest, Eli fell backwards. He was a very heavy old man, and the fall broke his neck and killed him. He had been a leader of Israel for 40 years.
19The wife of Phinehas was about to give birth. And soon after she heard that the sacred chest had been captured and that her husband and his father had died, her baby came. The birth was very hard, 20and she was dying. But the women taking care of her said, “Don't be afraid—it's a boy!”
She didn't pay any attention to them. 21-22Instead she kept thinking about losing her husband and her father-in-law. So she said, “My son will be named Ichabod, because the glory of Israel left our country when the sacred chest was captured.”
translation_text:
1Ate Izirali demma meena jam a siak ayen Samuel wieŋa ka wensie. Da ŋala po Filistia demma ya tigsi ba tugurik tɔŋdɔma ayen ba nye kpaliŋ ale Izirali. Izirali demma a tigsi Ebenezer alege ate Filistia demma a tigsi Afek. 2Filistia tugurik tɔŋdɔma a jam siti ba kama ale pagrim a nak dɛ Izirali demma. Filistia tugurik tɔŋdɔma a jam ko Izirali tugurik tɔŋdɔma a paari ka tusa ŋanaansi (4,000). 3Izirali tugurik tɔŋdɔba baai ale tali a ŋman cheŋ ba tigsika jigini la Izirali niŋdeerɔma yaa bek chaab ayen, <<Ka boa ate Naawen a basi ate Filistia demma a nak dɛ ti jinla? Ti ga pai Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni Siilo ate wa va ti cheŋ kpaliŋka ate ti dachaasaŋa a kan ŋman nak dɛ ti.>>
4Ba meena yaa siak a tom nuruma ate ba cheŋ Siilo ayen ba pai Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale gaam jaab meena la nɔiyeŋ dakanni. Dakanni nanlikka zuk maarɔba baye ale ba mɛ a zaani ka zuk. Naawen a jam bo ka maarɔma suŋsuŋ. Ba le ta dakanni a jam Izirali tigsika jigini la, Yofni ale Fineyas a maa va jam.
5Izirali tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale nya dakanni la, ba yaa kaari ate ku jueli ate tɛŋka a choa. 6Filistia demma ale wom kaarika la, ba yaa bek chaab ayen, <<Ka boa ate Izirali tugurik tɔŋdɔma a kaari ba jigini?>> Ba yaa miŋ ayen Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni ale ba ta jam ba jigini. 7Ba yaa jam a chali yɔgsum. Ba yaa weeni ayen, <<Ti bo wari po, ba ta wen a jam ba jigini. Wanni de choa an nye nya ya. 8Ku bie. Ku tua kama ale waai ale vari ti Izirali wen kpiemaŋa de jigi a basi. Wena ŋaai ate ba ta jam ba jigini la ale wena ŋaai ale ko Ejipiti demma gɔnni po la. 9Dila nyiŋ, ni piiri nyiŋ. Ni kpaliŋ ase tugurik tɔŋdɔba tuasa la, dan kan daa di Izirali demma ale nak dɛ ti ate ba a nya ti zuk ase tama ale a nya ba zuk diila. Ni chim nidoaba a nye kpaliŋka.>>
10Filistia tugurik tɔŋdɔma a jam chiib kpaliŋ kama ale ninpagra a nak dɛ Izirali demma. Izirali demma baai ale tali la meena yaa basi kpaliŋka ale chali kuli. Nakdeka jam bie ka nna yegayega ate Izirali tugurik tɔŋdɔba tusa pisita (30,000) a kpi. 11Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni mɛ ba jam tuesi kama ale ko Eli bisa bayewa Yofni ale Fineyas.
12Da dila danni dek nuru a yaa nyini Benjamin buuni po a chali nyini kpaliŋka po a cheŋ Siilo. Wa dari wa gattaŋa kama cheeri ale pai buntuem a basi wa zukku po a sak wa sui ale kaasi la. 13Wa le jam paari la, Eli jam kali ka wa zukpaglika zuk suiku nɔi a limisi wa wom diila wa jam a chali ka yɔgsum wari a nin nye nɔiyeŋka dakanni. Nuruwa ale jo tɛŋka po a weeni dii ale nye la, nuruma meena a yaa kaari. 14Eli yaa wom kaarika a yaa bek ayen, <<Nuemka de kiri ale boa?>> Nuru yaa chali cheŋ Eli jigi. 15Eli jam ka bena pineok ale naaniŋ ate wa ninaŋa an ŋman jam a nya. 16Wa weeni Eli ayen, <<Mi nyini ka kpaliŋka jigini. Mi chali nyini dula ka jinla dek.>> Eli yaa bek ayen, <<Ka boa ale nye yaa, m biiga?>>
17Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Filistia tugurik tɔŋdɔma nak yiak Izirali tugurik tɔŋdɔma kama ate ba chali. Ti tugurik tɔŋdɔma yega ale kpi. Fi bisa bayewa Yofni ale Fineyas a maa kpi kama. Daa dila nyiini, ba tuesi Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni kama.>>
18Eli ale wom dii ale nye nɔiyeŋka dakanni la, wa deri lo ŋaaŋnyiŋ tɛŋka nansuiŋku nɔi. Wa le lo la wa ŋinni yaa wɛ ate wa kpi, diila wa jam kpaŋ kama ale biigi. Wa jam chim Izirali niŋdeerɔ a paari ka bena pisinaansi.
19Eli sampowa, Fineyas powa a jam maa bo ka tɛŋka po. Wa jam ta ka lɔgi a moata biam. Wa le wom dii ale nye nɔiyeŋka dakanni la ale wa chorɔwa ate wa ŋiak nidoawa a kpi la, wa deri a dom. Wa deri biak diila domka jam pagra ka yega. 20Wa jaa kpi kama alege nipok baai ale jam yik ate wa biak la a weeni ayen wa kan te ku daani wa biak ka nidoabili. Alege wa an jam tulisi yaa.
21Wa jam te wa yuei ayen ka Ichabod. Di kiri ale Naawen zulaŋa a basi Izirali kama. Wa jam weeni dila kama dii nyiŋla ba tuesi nɔiyeŋka dakanni kama ate wa chorɔwa ale wa ŋiak nidoawa mɛ a kpi. 22Wa weeni ayen, <<Naawen zulaŋa a basi Izirali kama diila nɔiyeŋka dakanni ba tuesi kama.>>

english_text:
God Causes Trouble for the Philistines
1The Philistines took the sacred chest from near Ebenezer to the town of Ashdod. 2They brought it into the temple of their god Dagon and put it next to the statue of Dagon, which they worshiped.
3When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, they found the statue lying facedown on the floor in front of the sacred chest. They put the statue back where it belonged. 4But early the next morning, it had fallen over again and was lying facedown on the floor in front of the chest. The body of the statue was still in one piece, but its head and both hands had broken off and were lying on the stone floor in the doorway. 5This is why the priests and everyone else step over that part of the doorway when they enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod.
6The Lord caused a lot of trouble for the people of Ashdod and their neighbors. He made sores break out all over their bodies, and everyone was in a panic. 7Finally, they said, “The God of Israel did this. He is the one who caused all this trouble for us and our god Dagon. We've got to get rid of this chest.”
8The people of Ashdod invited all the Philistine rulers to come to Ashdod, and they asked them, “What can we do with the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel?”
“Send it to Gath,” the rulers answered. But after they took it there, 9the Lord made sores break out on everyone in town. The people of Gath were frightened, 10so they sent the sacred chest to Ekron. But before they could take it through the town gates, the people of Ekron started screaming, “They've brought the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel! It will kill us and our families too!”
The Philistines Send Back the Sacred Chest
11The people of Ekron called for another meeting of the Philistine rulers and told them, “Send this chest back where it belongs. Then it won't kill us.”
Everyone was in a panic, because God was causing a lot of people to die, 12and those who had survived were suffering from the sores. They all cried to their gods for help.
translation_text:
1Filistia demma ale tuesi Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni Izirali demma jigi la, ba pai ta nyini Ebenezer a cheŋ ka ba tɛŋka Asdod. 2Ba yaa ta di jo ba wenni Dagon yenni po a yaa pai zaani di gauŋ. 3Asdod demma yaa yiti saluik yokyokwa. Ba le cheŋ wenni yenni la ba yaa nya wenni Dagon lo kama pai nyue vuk tɛŋ nɔiyeŋka, dakanni niŋ. Ba yaa ŋman zak Dagon zaani di zaanaŋa. 4Saluik yokyokwa Asdod demma ŋman yiti a nya wenni Dagon lo kama po nyiŋ a dua nɔiyeŋka dakanni niŋ. Yɔgyɔgla de luetaŋa ku zukku ale di nisimaŋa a wɛ kama a dua tuoku nɔi. Di nyiŋka nyiini ale kan wɛ ya. 5Kude nyiŋ, a nyini dila po a cheŋ baai ale a kaab Dagon la a daa jo wenni yenni po ba kan tabi juijui ate wenni jam lo dua la. Ba nyiem gaam tabi kama taam.
6Naawen jam namsi Asdod demma kama ale baai meena ale bo gilagilawa la. Wa jam basi ate ba nam ka nna yegayega. A basi ate ŋan pagra a moari ba nyiŋsaŋa. 7Asdod demma ale nya dii ale a nye la, ba yaa weeni chaab ayen, <<Ti jɔgi ta nɔiyeŋka dakanni ale ka Izirali demma wen la a ga te ya. Ba wenni a namsi tama ale ti wenni Dagon kama.>> 8Ba yaa tom nuruba ate ba wi Filistia nalima ŋanuwa a bek ba ayen, <<Ti ta Izirali demma Wenni nɔiyeŋka dakanni a ga ka bɛ?>> Ba yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ti ta di cheŋ Gat.>> Ba yaa te di cheŋ Filistia tɛŋka kanyi ate ba wi ayen Gat la.
9Alege ba le te di ga Gat la, Naawen basi ate ninam a paari ba ate ku daani ba nna yegayega. Wa basi ate ba nyiŋsaŋa a moari, bimbaansa ale ŋankpagsa meena. 10Nuruma dula jigini a basi ate di cheŋ Ekron, Filistia tɛŋ mɛ ale la. Alege ba le ta a jo Ekron la, nuruma deri a kaari ayen, <<Ba ta Izirali Wenni nɔiyeŋka dakanni a cheen ka dela ba ko ti ale ti nuruma meena.>> 11Ba yaa wi Filistia nalimaŋa a weeni ayen, <<Ni te di cheŋ Izirali. Ni te di cheŋ di nyama jigi, dan kan daa di di le ko ti meena.>> Dii nyiŋla ku jam a jo ba nyiŋ ka yegayega ate nuruba poom kpi. 12Baai ale kan jam kpi la jam a yuak kama ale ba nyiŋsaŋa ŋanmɔrintaŋa. Nuruma yaa kaari a wi ba wenaŋa.

english_text:
1After the sacred chest had been in Philistia for seven months, 2the Philistines called in their priests and fortunetellers, and asked, “What should we do with this sacred chest? Tell us how to send it back where it belongs!”
3“Don't send it back without a gift,” the priests and fortunetellers answered. “Send along something to Israel's God to make up for taking the chest in the first place. Then you will be healed, and you will find out why the Lord was causing you so much trouble.”
4“What should we send?” the Philistines asked.
The priests and fortunetellers answered:
There are five Philistine rulers, and they all have the same disease that you have. 5So make five gold models of the sores and five gold models of the rats that are wiping out your crops. If you honor the God of Israel with this gift, maybe he will stop causing trouble for you and your gods and your crops. 6Don't be like the Egyptians and their king. They were stubborn, but when Israel's God was finished with them, they had to let Israel go.
7Get a new cart and two cows that have young calves and that have never pulled a cart. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take the calves back to their barn. 8Then put the chest on the cart. Put the gold rats and sores into a bag and put it on the cart next to the chest. Then send it on its way.
9Watch to see if the chest goes on up the road to the Israelite town of Beth-Shemesh. If it goes back to its own country, you will know that it was the Lord who made us suffer so badly. But if the chest doesn't go back to its own country, then the Lord had nothing to do with the disease that hit us—it was simply bad luck.
10The Philistines followed their advice. They hitched up the two cows to the cart, but they kept their calves in a barn. 11Then they put the chest on the cart, along with the bag that had the gold rats and sores in it.
12The cows went straight up the road toward Beth-Shemesh, mooing as they went. The Philistine rulers followed them until they got close to Beth-Shemesh.
13The people of Beth-Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the chest, they were so happy that they stopped working and started celebrating.
14-15The cows left the road and pulled the cart into a field that belonged to Joshua from Beth-Shemesh, and they stopped beside a huge rock. Some men from the tribe of Levi were there. So they took the chest off the cart and placed it on the rock, and then they did the same thing with the bag of gold rats and sores. A few other people chopped up the cart and made a fire. They killed the cows and burned them as sacrifices to the Lord. After that, they offered more sacrifices.
16When the five rulers of the Philistines saw what had happened, they went back to Ekron that same day.
17That is how the Philistines sent gifts to the Lord to make up for taking the sacred chest. They sent five gold sores, one each for their towns of Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron. 18They also sent one gold rat for each walled town and for every village that the five Philistine rulers controlled. The huge stone where the Levites set the chest is still there in Joshua's field as a reminder of what happened.
The Sacred Chest Is Sent to Kiriath-Jearim
19Some of the men of Beth-Shemesh looked inside the sacred chest, and the Lord God killed 70 of them. This made the people of Beth-Shemesh very sad, 20and they started saying, “No other God is like the Lord! Who can go near him and stay alive? We'll have to send the chest away from here. But where can we send it?”
21They sent messengers to tell the people of Kiriath-Jearim, “The Philistines have sent back the sacred chest. Why don't you take it and keep it there with you?”
translation_text:
1Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni ale bo Filistia paari chiisa siyopɔi la, 2nuruma yaa wi kaabteerɔma ale sampoporisaŋa a weeni ba ayen, <<Ti a ti nye nɔiyeŋka dakanni ka sɛ? Ni weeni ti le ti nye dii ate di cheŋ Izirali la.>>
3Ba yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ti daa yaali ayen ti te nɔiyeŋka dakanni a cheŋ Izirali, ti kan te di cheŋ kinla ti gum nyemagsika tiirim du a saalim ba wenni ti le kaasi la. Ni dan nye dila, wa le tebi ni. Ni dan te tiirimu wa le basi ni namsika.>>
4Filistia demma yaa bek ayen, <<Ti tin ti te ka boan tiirim a magsi ti kaasuŋku?>> Ba yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ti pai ligmɔniŋ a nye ŋanta ase ŋanmɔrinta la banu abe ni pai ligmɔniŋ mɛ a nye dawuita tinu a magsi Filistia nalima ŋanuwa. Dii nyiŋla tuemu a yik ka nama ale nalimaŋa. 5Ni pai ŋanmɔrintaŋa ale dawuitaŋa ale a kaasi tɛŋka la, a te Izirali Wenni a saalim wa. Da dii dai wa le basi tama ale ti wenaŋa ale ti tɛŋka namsika. 6Ni nye tama ale a weeni diila abe ni kan basi ate ni tue a kpari ase Ejipiti demma ale ba naawa la. Wen jam namsi ba ka nna yegayega ate ba yaa siak ate Izirali demma a cheŋ.
7<<Ni be yaali toroko paalik a yaa yaali naa ŋaai ale ta naabisa an diem a dari toroko a nya ya. A yaa bobi toroko a maŋ niiŋa ate ŋa ta cheŋ. Ni gaari ŋa bisaŋa a bobi zaani. 8Ni dan nye dila ni yaa pai Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni a zaani toroko zuk. A yaali dakari mɛ a pai ŋanmɔrintaŋa ale dawuitaŋa ate ni nye la a nyoro a te ase nyemagsika tiirim la. Ni kan te nuru a dari. 9Abe ni a nya ŋa, ŋa daŋ ga paari ŋa dek jigini tuak Bet Sɛmes abe ku sak ayen ka Naawen ale ta ninammu a jam ti zuk. Alege ŋa dan kan ta cheŋ du ti yaa le seba ayen ka ninam kama ale jam ti zuk daa Naawen ale ta jam.>>
10Ba yaa siak sinsaŋŋa de a yaa niiga ŋaye ŋaai ale ta naab bisa a bobi toroko a maŋ ŋa, ale bobi naabisaŋa. 11A yaa pai Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni a zaani toroko zuk. A pai dakari di choa a pai ŋanmɔrintaŋa ale dawuitaŋa ate ba nye la a nyoro. 12Ate niiŋa a cheŋ a duŋ Bet Sɛmes nyiŋ. Ŋa le a cheŋ ale a ŋuuni la ŋa an mobi gala yaase juga. Nalimaŋa yaa va ŋa a ga paari Bet Sɛmes banni.
13Dila po Bet Sɛmes demma a jam boro a che ka za viaka po. Ba le zak zuima nya nɔiyeŋka dakanni la, ba sue yaa jam peenti. 14Niiŋa yaa ga wari zaani Josua talim po Bet Sɛmes tɛŋka. Ŋa jam ga za ka piuŋ kpieŋ tɛŋ. Nuruma yaa che toroko wa daataŋa a ko niiŋa mɛ a ju ŋa a te Naawen. 15Livaima yaa yeeri Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni ale ŋanmɔrintaŋa ale dawuitaŋa ate ba nye la, a zaani piuŋ kpioŋku zuk. Da dila danni mɛ dek Bet Sɛmes demma a jam ko ka duŋsa si chaab ale ŋanta ba chaab a te Naawen. 16Filistia nalima ŋanuwa yaa zaani niŋ a nya dii meena ale nye la ate ba yaa ŋman cheŋ Ekron dai dila danni.
17Filistia demma a te ka ŋanmɔrinta banu ate ba nye ale ligmɔniŋ la a magsi ba nyemagsika tiirim. Dinyi meena a magsi ba tɛŋsaŋa Asdod ale Gaza ale Askelon ale Gat ale Ekron. 18Ba jam pai ka ligmɔniŋka mɛ dawuita a magsi chaab ale Filistia tɛŋsaŋa, sii ale sɛ parisa a gilim ale sii ale kan sɛ parisa ate nalima ŋanuwa a nya si zuk la. Piuŋ kpioŋku ate ba pai nɔiyeŋka dakanni a zaani ku zuk Josua talimu po Bet Sɛmes po la a chim ka seerɔ dai dila danni ate dii nye la.
19Alege Naawen a ko ka Bet Sɛmes nuruba pisiyopɔi ba le chuiri nya nɔiyeŋka dakanni po la. Nuruma sui jam kaasi kama wa le ko nuruma soa diila ate ba jam a kum. 20Bet Sɛmes demma yaa bek chaab ayen, <<Ka wana ale baga a zaani Naawen, Wen weleŋka dɛ niŋŋa? Ti a ti ta dakanni ga te ka wana?>>
21Ba yaa tom nuruba ate ba cheŋ Kiriat Jearim a ga weeni ayen, <<Filistia demma a ta Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni a jam ti jigi kama. Ni jam pai ta cheŋ ni jigini.>>

english_text:
1 The people of Kiriath-Jearim got the chest and took it to Abinadab's house, which was on a hill in their town. They chose his son Eleazar to take care of it, 2and it stayed there for 20 years.
During this time everyone in Israel was very sad and begged the Lord for help.
The People of Israel Turn Back to the Lord
3One day, Samuel told all the people of Israel, “If you really want to turn back to the Lord, then prove it. Get rid of your foreign idols, including the ones of the goddess Astarte. Turn to the Lord with all your heart and worship only him. Then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
4The people got rid of their idols of Baal and Astarte and began worshiping only the Lord.
5Then Samuel said, “Tell everyone in Israel to meet together at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.”
6The Israelites met together at Mizpah with Samuel as their leader. They drew water from the well and poured it out as an offering to the Lord. On that same day they went without eating to show their sorrow, and they confessed they had been unfaithful to the Lord.
The Philistines Attack Israel
7When the Philistine rulers found out about the meeting at Mizpah, they sent an army there to attack the people of Israel.
The Israelites were afraid when they heard that the Philistines were coming. 8“Don't stop praying!” they told Samuel. “Ask the Lord our God to rescue us.”
9-10 Samuel begged the Lord to rescue Israel, then he sacrificed a young lamb to the Lord. Samuel had not even finished offering the sacrifice when the Philistines started to attack. But the Lord answered his prayer and made thunder crash all around them. The Philistines panicked and ran away. 11The men of Israel left Mizpah and went after them as far as the hillside below Beth-Car, killing every enemy soldier they caught.
12-13The Philistines were so badly beaten that it was quite a while before they attacked Israel again. After the battle, Samuel set up a monument between Mizpah and the rocky cliffs. He named it “Help Monument” to remind Israel how much the Lord had helped them.
For as long as Samuel lived, the Lord helped Israel fight the Philistines. 14The Israelites were even able to recapture their towns and territory between Ekron and Gath.
Israel was also at peace with the Amorites.
Samuel Is a Leader in Israel
15Samuel was a leader in Israel all his life. 16Every year he would go around to the towns of Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah where he served as judge for the people. 17Then he would go back to his home in Ramah and do the same thing there. He also had an altar built for the Lord at Ramah.
translation_text:
1Kiriat Jearim demma yaa ga pai Naawen nɔiyeŋ dakanni a ta jam Abinadab yenni. Di jam za ka guuk zuk. Ba yaa jam gaari Abinadab nidoabinni Eleaza ayen wa a nya dakanni zuk.
2Nɔiyeŋ dakanni a jam Kiriat Jearim a beni kama a paari bena pisiye. Ate Izirali demma yaa kaari a saalim Naawen ayen wa maari ba.
3Ate Samuel yaa weeni Izirali demma ayen, <<Ni daa yaali ayen ni ŋmani Naawen jigi ale ni suiniima meena ni basi tɛŋ yonsa wena vaka. Abe ni maa basi bɔgluk nipowa ate ba a wi ayen Astarot la. Ni pai nidek a te Naawen abe ni a puusi wa. Ni dan nye dila, wa le vari ni Filistia demma jigi basi.>> 4Izirali demma yaa basi Baal ale Astarot bɔgtaŋa vaka ale va Naawen nyiini.
5Samuel yaa weeni niŋdeerɔma ayen, <<Ni wi Izirali demma meena ate ba tu Mizpa ate m puusi a te ni.>> 6Ba le tu Mizpa la, ba yaa ŋari nyiam a kpiiri a basi ase tiirim la a te Naawen. Da dila danni ba bobi ka nɔi a puusi a weeni ayen, <<Ba tom kaasi Naawen kama.>> Samuel jam le ba niŋdeerɔ Mizpa po.
7Filistia demma yaa wom ayen Izirali demma a tu chaab Mizpa. Nalima ŋanuwa yaa dɛ ba tugurik tɔŋdɔma niŋ ayen ba siti Izirali demma. Izirali demma ale wom ayen Filistia demma a cheen ba jigi la ba yaa chali yɔgsum. 8Ba yaa weeni Samuel ayen, <<Wa kasim puusi a te Naawen ti Wenni ate wa vari ti Filistia tugurik tɔŋdɔma nisa po basi.>> 9Samuel yaali pabiik a nye kaabka ase juka tiirim la a te Naawen. Wa yaa puusi a te Naawen ayen wa vari Izirali basi ate Naawen a tulisi wa.
10Diipo ate Samuel boro a nye kaabka la, ale Filistia demma a poom cheŋ moata kama ayen ba nye kpaliŋ. Naawen yaa basi ate wenni a na nyigsi Filistia demma, ate ba nyiŋsa a gɔk ate ba a chali. 11Izirali tugurik tɔŋdɔma yaa chali Mizpa tɛŋka po a vi Filistia tugurik tɔŋdɔma a ko ba Bet Kar suiku po.
12Samuel yaa pai tintain a ti Mizpa ale Sen suŋsuŋ a yaa te jigini yuei ayen, Ebenezer, <<Naawen a maari ti ate ti nak dɛ.>> 13Ba jam nak dɛ Filistia tugurik tɔŋdɔma kama. Naawen an ŋman jam basi ate ba soa Izirali tɛŋka kauk kuui ya Samuel daaŋa po. 14Izirali tɛŋ sii ale jam bo Ekron ale Gat suŋsuŋ ate Filistia demma jam tuesi soa la, a ŋman jam chim ka Izirali tɛŋsa. Daa dila nyiini Amori demma a jam basi kpaliŋ nyeka ale Izirali kama.
15Samuel kasim a nya Izirali tɛŋka zuk kama ase niŋdeerɔ la wa boka meena po. 16Ben meena wa nyiem nyini ka Arama a gilim va Betel ale Gilgal ale Mizpa a bo Izirali demma buusa jiŋŋa de meena. 17Wa dan nueri wa tuimaŋa wa nyiem ŋman kuli ka wa tɛŋka Arama. Wa jam sɛ ka kaabka kuŋkuŋ dula jigini a te Naawen.

english_text:
The People of Israel Want a King
1-2Samuel had two sons. The older one was Joel, and the younger one was Abijah. When Samuel was getting old, he let them be leaders at Beersheba. 3But they were not like their father. They were dishonest and accepted bribes to give unfair decisions.
4One day the nation's leaders came to Samuel at Ramah 5 and said, “You are an old man. You set a good example for your sons, but they haven't followed it. Now we want a king to be our leader, just like all the other nations. Choose one for us!”
6Samuel was upset to hear the leaders say they wanted a king, so he prayed about it. 7The Lord answered:
Samuel, do everything they want you to do. I am really the one they have rejected as their king. 8Ever since the day I rescued my people from Egypt, they have turned from me to worship idols. Now they are turning away from you. 9Do everything they ask, but warn them and tell them how a king will treat them.
10Samuel told the people who were asking for a king what the Lord had said:
11If you have a king, this is how he will treat you. He will force your sons to join his army. Some of them will ride in his chariots, some will serve in the cavalry, and others will run ahead of his own chariot. 12Some of them will be officers in charge of 1,000 soldiers, and others will be in charge of 50. Still others will have to farm the king's land and harvest his crops, or make weapons and parts for his chariots. 13Your daughters will have to make perfume or do his cooking and baking.
14The king will take your best fields, as well as your vineyards, and olive orchards and give them to his own officials. 15He will also take a tenth of your grain and grapes and give it to his officers and officials.
16The king will take your slaves and your best young men and your donkeys and make them do his work. 17He will also take a tenth of your sheep and goats. You will become the king's slaves, 18and you will finally cry out for the Lord to save you from the king you wanted. But the Lord won't answer your prayers.
19-20The people would not listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We want to be like other nations. We want a king to rule us and lead us in battle.”
21Samuel listened to them and then told the Lord exactly what they had said. 22“Do what they want,” the Lord answered. “Give them a king.”
Samuel told the people to go back to their homes.
translation_text:
1Samuel yaa le jam kpaŋ la wa yaa lueri wa bisa baye ayen ba chim Izirali niŋdeerɔba. 2Wa bikpagni yuei jam le Joel, waai ale pai saŋ la yuei ale Abaija. Ba jam a tom ka Beerseba. 3Alege wa bisaŋa an jam va wa nye maŋka. Ba jam a gebi ka nuruma ŋanta a nya ba ŋantaŋa. Ba jam basi ate ka nuruba a da ba ale ligra ate ba kan bo buusa a magsi. Ba jam ŋmani a te ka baai ale a da bala.
4Izirali nisɔmma yaa jam jigi yeŋ ayen ba nya Samuel Arama tɛŋka. 5Ba yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Yɔgyɔgla de fi kpaŋ kama alege fi bisaŋa a kan va fi nyeka, dila nyiŋ lueri naab ate wa a nya ti zuk ate tama mɛ ta naab ase tɛŋ yonsa la.>>
6Samuel ale wom ayen ba a yaali naab la wa sui an peenti ya. Wa yaa puusi te Naawen ayen wa sak wa. 7Alege Naawen yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Nye nuruma ale a yaali diila. Lueri naab a te ba. Fi a poli ayen ba zɛri ka fi, ka mi ate ba zɛri. 8A zaani diipo ate mi ta ba nyini Ejipiti tɛŋka po nyini la, ba kasim a zɛri mi kama alege a va wena. Dila dek ate ba a nye fi mɛ. 9Wom ba le a weeni diila, alege chiib kpaam ba naawa ale za wa yaali ayen ba nye dii te wa la.>>
10Samuel yaa jam weeni Naawen wieŋa meena a te nuru baai ale jam bek a yaali naab la. 11Wa weeni ba ayen, <<Dii ate naab waai a za wa a nya ni zuk la ale nye la ale nna. Wa le basi ate ni bisaŋa a tom a te wa, abe ba a dam kpaliŋ torokoba ale wusuma abe ba chali dɛ kpaliŋ torokoma niŋ a mooli juijui meena ate wa a cheŋ la. 12Wa le lueri ni gela ate ba a nya tugurik tɔŋdɔba tusidi tusidi zuk ate ba gela a nya tugurik tɔŋdɔba pisinu pisinu zuk. Wa le basi ate ba gela a kpa wa tattaŋa abe ba che wa ŋantaŋa. Wa le basi ate ba gela a nye gbatta ale gebik woŋsa, ale ŋanta a magsi kpaliŋ torokoba. 13Ni liema wa le basi ate ba a nye kpa buui nyum ale masa, abe ba gela a dik a te wa nuruma. Abe ba gela a nye boroborok a te ba. 14Wa le tuesi ni laŋsaŋa po ŋan baai ale zunchoŋ la, ale ni kaduksaŋa yɔn maŋsaŋa a te baai ale tom a te wa la. 15Ni kpanni ŋantaŋa ale ni daamu meena piika po wa le yeeri bunyi bunyi a te wa kpaŋŋa ale wa yɔmma. 16Wa le lueri ni nuruma gela nidoaba ale nipooba ate ba a tom wa yenni. Wa le lueri ni naab maŋsaŋa ale ni bon maŋsaŋa a te wadek. 17Daa dila nyiini piisa ale bua meena piik po wa le lueri kunyi. Di kpeglimka meena ni le chim ni naawa yɔm. 18Kula dan nye ni le kum a wi Naawen ayen wa basi ate ni naawa a ta jiirim ale ni. Alege Naawen a kan wom ni. Samuel ale weeni diila ale la.>>
19Alege nuruma a zɛri ba an wom Samuel. Ayen, <<Aaya, ti a yaali ka naab. 20Ti a yaali ka naab ayen wa a dɛ ti niŋ ate ti a cheŋ kpaliŋsa ate tama mɛ a nye ase tɛŋ yonsa ale ta nalima diila.>>
21Samuel ale wom dii meena ate nuruma weeni la, wa yaa ŋman weeni sak Naawen. 22Ate Naawen yaa tulisi ayen, <<Wom ba le weeni diila abe fi te ba naab.>> Samuel yaa weeni Izirali demma ayen waai meena a kuli.

english_text:
Saul Meets Samuel
1Kish was a wealthy man who belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. His father was Abiel, his grandfather was Zeror, his great-grandfather was Becorath, and his great-great-grandfather was Aphiah. 2Kish had a son named Saul, who was better looking and more than a head taller than anyone else in all Israel.
3Kish owned some donkeys, but they had run off. So he told Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”
4Saul and the servant went through the hill country of Ephraim and the territory of Shalishah, but they could not find the donkeys. Then they went through the territories of Shaalim and Benjamin, but still there was no sign of the donkeys. 5Finally they came to the territory where the clan of Zuph lived. “Let's go back home,” Saul told his servant. “If we don't go back soon, my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us!”
6“Wait!” the servant answered. “There's a man of God who lives in a town near here. He's amazing! Everything he says comes true. Let's talk to him. Maybe he can tell us where to look.”
7Saul said, “How can we talk to the prophet when I don't have anything to give him? We don't even have any bread left in our sacks. What can we give him?”
8“I have a small piece of silver,” the servant answered. “We can give him that, and then he will tell us where to look for the donkeys.”
9-10“Great!” Saul replied. “Let's go to the man who can see visions!” He said this because in those days God would answer questions by giving visions to prophets.
Saul and his servant went to the town where the prophet lived. 11As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to get water, and the two men said to them, “We're looking for the man who can see visions. Is he in town?”
12“Yes, he is,” they replied. “He's in town today because there's going to be a sacrifice and a sacred meal at the place of worship. In fact, he's just ahead of you. Hurry 13and you should find him right inside the town gate. He's on his way out to the place of worship to eat with the invited guests. They can't start eating until he blesses the sacrifice. If you go now, you should find him.”
14They went to the town, and just as they were going through the gate, Samuel was coming out on his way to the place of worship.
15The day before Saul came, the Lord had told Samuel, 16“I've seen how my people are suffering, and I've heard their call for help. About this time tomorrow I'll send you a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who will rescue my people from the Philistines. I want you to pour olive oil on his head to show that he will be their leader.”
17Samuel looked at Saul, and the Lord told Samuel, “This is the man I told you about. He's the one who will rule Israel.”
18Saul went over to Samuel in the gateway and said, “A man who can see visions lives here in town. Could you tell me the way to his house?”
19“I am the one who sees visions!” Samuel answered. “Go on up to the place of worship. You will eat with me today, and in the morning I'll answer your questions. 20Don't worry about your donkeys that ran off three days ago. They've already been found. Everything of value in Israel now belongs to you and your family.”
21“Why are you telling me this?” Saul asked. “I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel, and my clan is the least important in the tribe.”
Saul Eats with Samuel and Stays at His House
22Samuel took Saul and his servant into the dining room at the place of worship. About 30 people were there for the dinner, but Samuel gave Saul and his servant the places of honor. 23-24Then Samuel told the cook, “I gave you the best piece of meat and told you to set it aside. Bring it here now.”
The cook brought the meat over and set it down in front of Saul. “This is for you,” Samuel told him. “Go ahead and eat it. I had this piece saved especially for you, and I invited these guests to eat with you.”
After Saul and Samuel had finished eating, 25they went down from the place of worship and back into town. A bed was set up for Saul on the flat roof of Samuel's house, 26and Saul slept there.
About sunrise the next morning, Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, “Time to get up! I'll help you get started on your way.”
Saul got up. He and Samuel left together 27and had almost reached the edge of town when Samuel stopped and said, “Tell your servant go on. Stay here with me for a few minutes, and I'll tell you what God has told me.”
