Ta Baal biisiteerɔba kobsinaansi ale pisinuwa ale Asera biisiteerɔba kobsinaansiwa a jam, baai ale bo Jezebel yenni a dɛ la.>>
20Dila Ayab yaa tom weeni Izirali meena a tigsi biisiteerɔma Karmel Guuku zuk. 21Elaja yaa cheŋ nuruma niŋ a weeni ba ayen, <<Ku ale beni a paari ka disa po ate nama a basi ni chichamaŋa? Naawen a dan ka Wen ni va wa, alege Baal mɛ abe dan ka Wen, ni be a va wa.>> Alege nuruma an jam weeni wari ya.
22Ate Elaja yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Mi nyiini ale Naawen biisiteerɔ a tali boro, alege Baal a ta ka biisiteerɔba kobsinaansi ale pisinu. 23Ni ta lalisa siye a jam te ti. Basi ate ba lueri kanyi a te badek, basi ate ba boani ka boanaboana a vi daataŋa zuk alege ba kan cheem bolim bu zuwa. Mi ale gomsi lalik m kala a vi daata zuk m kan cheem bolim bu zuwa. 24Ate nama ale wi ni wenni yuei ate mi mɛ ale wi Naawen yuei. Wen dii ale a tulisi ale bolim la wala ale Wen.>> Ate nuruma meena ayen, <<Dii ate fi a weeni la ka wamaŋ.>>
25Elaja yaa weeni Baal biisiteerɔma ayen, <<Ni dɛ niŋ a lueri lalik kanyi a gomsi ka nama ale piisi la nyiŋ. Ni wi ni wenni yuei, alege ni kan cheem bolimoa.>> 26Dila ba yaa yik lalik a te ba ate ba gomsi ka. Ba yaa wi Baal yuei a nyini saluik a ga paari kantueŋ suŋsuŋ ayen, <<Baal, tulisi ti!>> Alege tulisika an jam ya, waai an tulisi ya. Ba jam gɔk kama a gilim kuŋkuŋku ate ba jam sɛ la.
27Ku ale ga paari kantueŋ suŋsuŋ la, Elaja yaa piilim koosi a la ba. Wa weeni ayen, <<Wa sum ka wen, dai dii dai wa bo ka popola po yaase wa nina ale muni yaase wa bo nyeerim po. Dai dii dai wa a goa kama ku a fɛ ate wa yiti.>> 28Dila ba yaa jam a na ate ku jueli ale a gebi badek ale gebisa ale gbatta ase ba ŋiaka wieŋa ale jam ka diila ate ba ziim a kasim a nyini. 29Wenni ale ga gbeli la ba diem jam a porisi kama a ta ga paari diipo ate ba a nye junɔinni kaabka la. Alege tulisa a jam karo, waai an jam tulisi ya, waai an jam wom ba.
30Elaja yaa weeni nuruma meena ayen, <<Ni jam mi jigi ate ba jam wa jigi,>> ate wa gomsi Naawen kuŋkuŋku kuui ale jam ŋɔriŋ la. 31Elaja jam pa ka tintana pi ale ŋaye, dinyi meena a magsi ŋaaŋbiik buuri meena ale nyini Jekob jigi, waai jigi ate Naawen wanni a jam ayen, <<Fi yue ale chim ka Izirali la.>> 32Tintanaŋa wa jam pa sɛ ka kuŋkuŋku Naawen yuenni nyiŋ ale tu goluk a gilim ku ate ku ŋmasi zuak a baga a jo kuruba kpienta tiye ale ŋanbie. 33Wa yaa tigsi daataŋa a boanni lalikka boanaboana a vi daataŋa zuk. Wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni ŋari nyiam a sueri samɔn kpieŋsa sinaansi a kpiiri vi tiirimu ale daataŋa zuk.>>
34Wa weeni ayen, <<Ni ŋman pilim nye,>> ate ba ŋman nye dila. Ate wa ŋman weeni ayen, <<Ni nye a saari buta,>> ate ba kpiiri du a saari buta. 35Nyiamu a jam chali nyini kuŋkuŋku zuk a siŋ sueri golukku kama.
36Diipo ate ba a nye junɔinni kaabka la, biisiteerɔwa Elaja yaa nyini jam niŋ nyiŋ a puusi ayen, <<Naawen yaa, Abrayam ale Aizik ale Izirali Wenni, basi ate jinla ba seba ayen fi ka Wen Izirali tɛŋka po, ate mi a chim fi tomteerɔ a nye ŋade meena fi wanni nyiŋ. 37Tulisi mu Naawen yaa, tulisi mu, ate nuruma de ale seba ayen fi Naawen ka Wen, abe ba seba ayen fi a tagri ba suiniimaŋa kama ŋmana.>>
38Ate bolim a nyini Naawen jigi a lo a dɛ kaabka ale daataŋa ale tintanaŋa ale tantaŋa a maa leeli nyiamu meena ale bo golukku po la.
39Ase nuruma meena ale jam nya kude la, ba yaa lo tɛŋ a kaari ayen, <<Naawen wa ka Wen! Naawen wa ka Wen!>>
40Elaja yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni yik Baal biisiteerɔma. Ni kan basi ate ba wanyi a muriŋ bɛ.>> Ba yaa yik ba ate Elaja a basi ate ba ta ba a jam Kison Viaka po a tɔgri ba dula.
41Elaja yaa weeni Ayab ayen, <<Ga dɛ abe fi nyu ale ka ŋmoruk kpioŋ ale cheena.>> 42Ayab yaa jam cheŋ wa dɛ abe wa nyu alege Elaja a ga jueli Karmel guuku zuk a koori tɛŋ a pa wa ninaŋa a basi wa dunaŋa suŋsuŋ.
43Wa weeni wa tomteerɔwa ayen, <<Cheŋ ga tuk nyakpiemu nyiŋ a nya,>> ate wa cheŋ ga nya, a weeni ayen, <<Wa an nya jaaboa.>> Elaja a weeni wa ayen wa ŋman pilim ga nya. Elaja a jam weeni dila a paari ka buyopɔi.
44Buyopɔiwa po tomteerɔwa yaa weeni ayen, <<Chiŋmari nna nyiin ase nuru nisa la ale nyini nyakpiemu po a jueli.>> Elaja yaa weeni ayen, <<Cheŋ ga weeni Ayab ayen wa nye nwuli a jueli wa torokowa a kuli alege jigi ate ŋmorukku a kasi fu.>>
45Alege wenni a jam ko sobri kama ale chiŋma, ate viok a yiti, ate ŋmoruk kpioŋ a jan jam ate Ayab a dam a cheŋ Jezreel. 46Naawen pagrim yaa jam Elaja jigi a bobi wa garukku ale wa chiak gbanni a magsi ate wa chali dɛ Ayab niŋ a cheŋ Jezreel.

english_text:
Elijah Runs Away from Ahab and Jezebel
1Ahab told his wife Jezebel what Elijah had done and that he had killed the prophets. 2She sent a message to Elijah: “You killed my prophets. Now I'm going to kill you! I pray that the gods will punish me even more severely if I don't do it by this time tomorrow.”
3Elijah was afraid when he got her message, and he ran to the town of Beersheba in Judah. He left his servant there, 4 then walked another whole day into the desert. Finally, he came to a large bush and sat down in its shade. He begged the Lord, “I've had enough. Just let me die! I'm no better off than my ancestors.” 5Then he lay down in the shade and fell asleep.
Suddenly an angel woke him up and said, “Get up and eat.” 6Elijah looked around, and by his head was a jar of water and some baked bread. He sat up, ate and drank, then lay down and went back to sleep.
7Soon the Lord's angel woke him again and said, “Get up and eat, or else you'll get too tired to travel.” 8So Elijah sat up and ate and drank.
The food and water made him strong enough to walk 40 more days. At last, he reached Mount Sinai, the mountain of God, 9and he spent the night there in a cave.
The Lord Appears to Elijah
While Elijah was on Mount Sinai, the Lord asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
10 He answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
11“Go out and stand on the mountain,” the Lord replied. “I want you to be there when I pass by.”
All at once, a strong wind shook the mountain and shattered the rocks. But the Lord was not in the wind. Next, there was an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake. 12Then there was a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire.
Finally, there was a gentle breeze, 13and when Elijah heard it, he covered his face with his coat. He went out and stood at the entrance to the cave.
A voice asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
14Elijah answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
15 The Lord said:
Elijah, you can go back to the desert near Damascus. And when you get there, appoint Hazael to be king of Syria. 16 Then appoint Jehu son of Nimshi to be king of Israel, and Elisha son of Shaphat to take your place as my prophet.
17Hazael will start killing the people who worship Baal. Jehu will kill those who escape from Hazael, and Elisha will kill those who escape from Jehu.
18 But 7,000 Israelites have refused to worship Baal, and they will live.
Elisha Becomes Elijah's Assistant
19Elijah left and found Elisha plowing a field with a pair of oxen. There were eleven other men in front of him, and each one was also plowing with a pair of oxen. Elijah went over and put his own coat on Elisha.
20Elisha stopped plowing and ran after him. “Let me kiss my parents goodbye, then I'll go with you,” he said.
“You can go,” Elijah said. “But remember what I've done for you.”
21Elisha left and took his oxen with him. He killed them and boiled them over a fire he had made with the wood from his plow. He gave the meat to the people who were with him, and they ate it. Then he left with Elijah and became his assistant.
translation_text:
1Ayab yaa jam weeni Jezebel dii meena ate Elaja nye la ale wa ale ko Baal biisiteerɔma meena ale gebik la. 2Jezebel yaa tom a weeni Elaja ayen, <<Wenaŋa abe te ku jo mi nyiŋ chaŋni ase chum nna po de mi a dan kan nye fi nyuvunni ase bade wanyi la.>>
3Elaja yaa jam a chali yɔgsum a yiti chali wa nyuvunni nyiŋ. Ase wa ale jam paari Beerseba ale bo Juda po la, wa yaa basi wa tomteerɔwa dula, 4alege wadek a cheŋ danni po meena a jo sagni po. Wa yaa jam paari tii fiik a kali bu kiri a puusi ayen wa kpi. Wa weeni ayen, <<Mi tom ka nna yegayega Naawen yaa. Tuesi mi nyuvunni. Mi an zunchoŋ mi kokpieŋsaŋa.>> 5Wa yaa duak tiimu tɛŋ a goa. Wen maarɔ yaa jam tiri wa ale weeni ayen, <<Yiti ŋmai a dɛ.>> 6Wa yaa nya gilim dula a moata wa zukku ale ka boroborok ale sɛ doa bolim kaala zuk ale leŋ ale nyiam. Wa yaa dɛ ale nyu ale ŋman pilim duak.
7Naawen maarɔwa yaa jan jam a saari buye a tiri wa ayen, <<Yiti ŋmai a dɛ ale chelimu a ŋmasi zuak kama a te fu.>> 8Wa yaa yiti ŋmai a dɛ ale nyu. Ŋandiintaŋa ale te wa pagrim la, wa yaa cheŋ daa pisinaansi ale yogta pisinaansi a paari Yoreb, Wen guuku. 9Dula wa jam jo ka vɔrup po a goa. Ate Naawen wanni a jam wa jigi ayen, <<Boa ate fi bo dela a nye Elaja?>>
10Ate wa tulisi ayen, <<Mi kɔrisa ale kasim bo Naawen, Wen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La. Izirali demma a zɛri fi nɔiyeŋka kama, a kpiti fi kuŋkuŋtaŋa a basi ale ko fi biisiteerɔma ale gebik. Mi dek mi nyiini ale tali, yɔgyɔgla de ba a gomsi ba ko mi mɛ kama.>>
11Naawen yaa weeni ayen, <<Cheŋ ga zaani guuku zuk Naawen niŋ, ale Naawen a yaali wa jam taam kama.>> Ate viok kpioŋ yaa jam nye ate guuku a lab buye ate pinaŋa a mobi Naawen niŋ alege Naawen a jam ka vioku po. Vioku ŋaaŋnyiŋ tɛŋka ale jam choa alege Naawen a jam ka tɛŋka choaka po. 12Tɛŋka choaka ŋaaŋnyiŋ bolim ale jan jam alege Naawen jam ka bolimu po. Bolimu ŋaaŋnyiŋ, ka waasika. 13Ase Elaja ale wom waasika la, wa yaa dari wa tankaluŋku a lik wa ninaŋa a nyini peelim a za vɔrumu nɔi. Ate lueluku yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Boa ate fi a nye dela Elaja?>>
14Ate wa tulisi ayen, <<Mi kɔrisa ale kasim bo Naawen, Wen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La. Izirali demma a zɛri fi nɔiyeŋka kama, a kpiti fi kuŋkuŋtaŋa a basi ale ko fi biisiteerɔma ale gebik. Mi dek nyiini ale tali, yɔgyɔgla de ba a gomsi ba ko mi mɛ kama.>>
15Naawen a weeni wa ayen, <<Ŋmani a va suik kuui dek ate fi a va jam la a cheŋ Damasikus Sagni po. Ase fi a dan paari dula, bobi Yazael naab ate wa a nya Araam tɛŋka zuk. 16Maa bobi Nimsi nidoabinni Jeyu naab ate wa nya Izirali zuk abe fi bobi Safat nidoabinni Ɛlaisa ale nyini Abel Meyola la ate wa zaani fi nankula po a chim biisiteerɔ. 17Jeyu ale ko waai meena ate Yazael an ko ale gebika la, ate Ɛlaisa ale ko waai meena ate Jeyu an jam ko ale gebika la. 18Mi ta ka nuruba tusa ŋayopɔi (7,000) a bo Izirali baai ale kan koori tɛŋ Baal niŋŋa, ba abe an te ku zula.>>
19Elaja yaa nyini dula a cheŋ ga nya Safat nidoabinni Ɛlaisa. Wa jam ta ka lalik kpaansa pi ale buye a boro a kpa, wadek ale jam yik lalisa pi ale buyewa kunni. Elaja yaa cheŋ wa jigi a yeeri wa tankaluŋku a yi wa. 20Ɛlaisa yaa basi wa lalik kpaansaŋa ale chali va Elaja. Wa weeni ayen, <<Basi ate mi gbaari m kowa ale m mawa a banti ba abe m va fu a cheŋ.>> Elaja yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ŋmani mi nye ka boa a te fu?>>
21Ɛlaisa yaa basi wa ale ŋmani. Wa jam yik wa lalik kpaansaŋa siyewa a tɔgri kama. Wa jam ju niiŋa daataŋa kama a dik lammu a te nuruma ate ba ŋɔbi. Wa yaa jam va Elaja ŋaaŋ a chim wa maarɔ.

english_text:
Syria Attacks Israel
1King Benhadad of Syria called his army together. He was joined by 32 other kings with their horses and chariots, and together they marched to Samaria and attacked. 2Benhadad sent a messenger to tell King Ahab of Israel, 3“Ahab, give me your silver and gold, your wives, and your strongest sons!”
4“Your Majesty,” Ahab replied, “everything I have is yours, including me.”
5Later, Benhadad sent another messenger to say to Ahab, “I already told you to give me your silver and gold, your wives, and your children. 6But tomorrow at this time, I will send my officials into your city to search your palace and the houses of your officials. They will take everything else that you own.”
7Ahab called a meeting with the leaders of Israel and said, “Benhadad is causing real trouble. He told me to give him my wives and children, as well as my silver and gold. And I agreed.”
8“Don't listen to him!” they answered. “You don't have to do what he says.”
9So Ahab sent someone to tell Benhadad, “Your Majesty, I'll give you my silver and gold, and even my wives and children. But I won't let you have anything else.”
When Benhadad got his answer, 10he replied, “I'll completely destroy Samaria! There won't even be enough of it left for my soldiers to carry back in their hands. If I don't do it, I pray that the gods will punish me terribly.”
11Ahab then answered, “Benhadad, don't brag before the fighting even begins. Wait and see if you live through it.”
12Meanwhile, Benhadad and the other kings had been drinking in their tents. But when Ahab's reply came, he ordered his soldiers to prepare to attack Samaria, and they all got ready.
13At that very moment, a prophet ran up to Ahab and said, “You can see that Benhadad's army is very strong. But the Lord has promised to help you defeat them today. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
14“Who will fight the battle?” Ahab asked.
The prophet answered, “The young bodyguards who serve the district officials.”
“But who will lead them into battle?” Ahab asked.
“You will!” the prophet replied.
15So Ahab called together the 232 young soldiers and the 7,000 troops in Israel's army, and he got them ready to fight the Syrians.
Israel Defeats the Syrians
16-17At noon, King Ahab and his Israelite army marched out of Samaria, with the young soldiers in front.
King Benhadad of Syria and the 32 kings with him were drunk when the scouts he had sent out ran up to his tent, shouting, “We just now saw soldiers marching out of Samaria!”
18“Take them alive!” Benhadad ordered. “I don't care if they have come out to fight or to surrender.”
19The young soldiers led Israel's troops into battle, 20and each of them attacked and killed an enemy soldier. The rest of the Syrian army turned and ran, and the Israelites went after them. Benhadad and some others escaped on horses, 21but Ahab and his soldiers followed them and captured their horses and chariots.
Ahab and Israel's army crushed the Syrians.
22Later, the prophet went back and warned Ahab, “Benhadad will attack you again next spring. Build up your troops and make sure you have some good plans.”
Syria Attacks Israel Again
23Meanwhile, Benhadad's officials went to him and explained:
Israel's gods are mountain gods. We fought Israel's army in the hills, and that's why they defeated us. But if we fight them on flat land, there's no way we can lose.
24Here's what you should do. First, get rid of those 32 kings and put army commanders in their places. 25Then get more soldiers, horses, and chariots, so your army will be as strong as it was before. We'll fight Israel's army on flat land and wipe them out.
Benhadad agreed and did what they suggested.
26In the spring, Benhadad got his army together, and they marched to the town of Aphek to attack Israel. 27The Israelites also prepared to fight. They marched out to meet the Syrians, and the two armies camped across from each other. The Syrians covered the whole area, but the Israelites looked like two little flocks of goats.
28The prophet went to Ahab and said, “The Syrians think the Lord is a god of the hills and not of the valleys. So he has promised to help you defeat their powerful army. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
29For seven days the two armies stayed in their camps, facing each other. Then on the seventh day the fighting broke out, and before sunset the Israelites had killed 100,000 Syrian troops. 30The rest of the Syrian army ran back to Aphek, but the town wall fell and crushed 27,000 of them.
Benhadad also escaped to Aphek and hid in the back room of a house. 31His officials said, “Your Majesty, we've heard that Israel's kings keep their agreements. We will wrap sackcloth around our waists, put ropes around our heads, and ask Ahab to let you live.”
32They dressed in sackcloth and put ropes on their heads, then they went to Ahab and said, “Your servant Benhadad asks you to let him live.”
“Is he still alive?” Ahab asked. “Benhadad is like a brother to me.”
33Benhadad's officials were trying to figure out what Ahab was thinking, and when he said “brother,” they quickly replied, “You're right! You and Benhadad are like brothers.”
“Go get him,” Ahab said.
When Benhadad came out, Ahab had him climb up into his chariot.
34Benhadad said, “I'll give back the towns my father took from your father. And you can have shops in Damascus, just as my father had in Samaria.”
Ahab replied, “If you do these things, I'll let you go free.” Then they signed a peace treaty, and Ahab let Benhadad go.
A Prophet Condemns Ahab
35About this time the Lord commanded a prophet to say to a friend, “Hit me!” But the friend refused, 36 and the prophet told him, “You disobeyed the Lord, and as soon as you walk away, a lion will kill you.” The friend left, and suddenly a lion killed him.
37The prophet found someone else and said, “Hit me!” So this man beat him up.
38The prophet left and put a bandage over his face to disguise himself. Then he went and stood beside the road, waiting for Ahab to pass by.
39When Ahab went by, the prophet shouted, “Your Majesty, right in the heat of battle, someone brought a prisoner to me and told me to guard him. He said if the prisoner got away, I would either be killed or forced to pay 3,000 pieces of silver. 40But I got busy doing other things, and the prisoner escaped.”
Ahab answered, “You will be punished just as you have said.”
41The man quickly tore the bandage off his face, and Ahab saw that he was one of the prophets. 42The prophet said, “The Lord told you to kill Benhadad, but you let him go. Now you will die in his place, and your people will die in place of his people.”
43Ahab went back to Samaria, angry and depressed.
translation_text:
1Yɔgyɔgla de Araam tɛŋka naawa Ben Yadad yaa tigsi wa tugurik tommu meena. Nalima pisita ale ŋaye ale jam va wa ale ba wusuma ale torokoba, wa yaa ga siti Samaria a nye kpaliŋ. 2Wa yaa tom nuruba tɛŋ kpieŋka po Ayab Izirali naawa jigi ayen, <<Ben Yadad ale weeni diila ale nna. 3<Fi kpanaŋa ale fi ligmɔniŋka mi ale soa, fi pok maŋsaŋa ale fi bi maŋsaŋa ka mi ale soa.> >> 4Izirali naawa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ase dii dek ate fi a weeni la, m nyɔnɔ naaba. Mi ale jaab meena ate mi a ta la ka fi ale soa.>>
5Nuru baai ate wa jam tom la yaa ŋman jam ayen, <<Ben Yadad ale weeni diila ale nna, <M tom ka nuruba a yaali fi kpanaŋa ale fi ligmɔniŋka ale fi pooma ale fi bisaŋa. 6Alege chum nna po de mi a yaali m tom m kpaŋŋa ate ba gisi fi yenni po ale fi kpaŋŋa yeeŋa po. Ba ale vari jaab meena ale ta dobrim a te fu la a ta cheŋ.> >>
7Izirali naawa yaa tigsi nisɔmma meena tɛŋka po a weeni ba ayen, <<Nya nuruwa de ale yaali kpaliŋka la, ase wa le tom a weeni ayen wa a yaali mi pooma ale m bisaŋa ale kpanaŋa ale m ligmɔniŋka la mi an zɛri ya.>> 8Nisɔmma ale nuruma meena yaa tulisi ayen, <<Kan wom wa yaase fi siak a te wa ale a yaali diila.>>
9Dila wa yaa tulisi Ben Yadad ale tom baai la ayen, <<Weeni mi nyɔnɔwa naawa ayen, <Fi tomteerɔwa ale nye dii meena ate fi dɛ niŋ a weeni la alege fi ale yaali dii ŋmana la mi an baga a nye dila.> >> Ba yaa ta wa le tulisi diila a ga te Ben Yadad. 10Ben Yadad yaa tom tomtomiŋ ka choa Ayab jigi ayen, <<Wenaŋa abe nye ale mu ate ku jo m nyiŋ, ase tanta a nin poom a tali a zuak Samaria po a te mi nidoa meena nisa nɔi.>>
11Izirali naawa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ni weeni wa ayen, <Waai ale jo wa kpaliŋ garuk la a kan kuulim ase waai ale yeeri ku a dueni la.> >> 12Ben Yadad a jam wom tontomiŋka de diipo la ale ka wa ale nalimaŋa chaab ale jam bo ba viita po a nyu, ate wa weeni ba ayen ba gomsi ate ba ga siti ba. Ba yaa gomsi ayen ba siti tɛŋka.
13Biisiteerɔ yaa jam Ayab Izirali naawa jigi a mooli ayen, <<Nnala ate Naawen a weeni ayen, <Nya Ben Yadad tugurik tom boanni. Mi ale pa ba a nyo fi nisima po jinla ate fi ale seba ayen ka Mi ale Naawen.> >> 14Ayab yaa bek ayen, <<Ka wana ale wa nye kude?>> Biisiteerɔwa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Nnala ate Naawen a weeni la ayen, <Ka tɛŋsaŋa kpaŋŋa nuru paalukku ale ba nye.> >> Ate wa ŋman bek ayen, <<Ka wana ale wa piilim kpaliŋka?>> Ate biisiteerɔwa ayen, <<Fi ale piilim.>>
15Ayab yaa wi tɛŋsaŋa kpaŋŋa nuru paalukku kobsiye ale pisita ale baye. Wa yaa tigsi Izirali dem mbala meena a gum chaab a nye tusa ŋayopɔi (7,000). 16Ba yaa basi ba boka jigini kantueŋ suŋsuŋ, dila po Ben Yadad ale nalima pisita ale ŋayewa ale jo chaab la a jam bo ka ba viitaŋa po a boro a buk. 17Tɛŋsaŋa kpaŋŋa nuru paalukku yaa dɛ niŋ a nyini. Ben Yadad yaa tom baai ale ga kpesi nya a jam weeni ayen, <<Nidoaba ale nyini Samaria a cheena.>>
18Ben Yadad yaa weeni ayen, <<Ase ba dan jam ale ka suiyɔgni ni yik ba vuta. Ba abe a dan jam ba nye ka kpaliŋ ni yik ba vuta.>>
19Tɛŋsaŋa kpaŋŋa nuru paalukku yaa gɔk santiri a nyini tɛŋka po a nyini ate tugurik tommu a bo ba ŋaaŋ, 20ba wanyi meena a jam ko ka wa dachiak. Ate dila a basi ate Araam demma a yiti chali ate Izirali demma a vi ba. Alege Araam naawa Ben Yadad a jam dɔ ka wusum a chali bɛ ale wa nuru baai ale ta wusuma la gela. 21Izirali naawa a jam a jueli ba zuk ka nna kparikpari a nak yik baai ale ta wusumaŋa ale torokoma la a ko Araam demma yega.
22Dila ŋaaŋnyiŋ biisiteerɔwa yaa jam Izirali naawa jigi ayen, <<Gomsi fidek a nya dii ale magsi fi nye la, dii nyiŋla wulum wen Araam naawa ale ŋman siti fu.>>
23Dila po dek Araam naawa kpaŋŋa a jam kaam wa kama ayen, <<Izirali demma wenaŋa ka guuta zuima wena dila ale soa ate ba ŋmasi pagra a te ti la. Alege ti dan kpaliŋ ale ba peelimmu ale doa nna jassi la po, ti ale nya pagrim ba zuk. 24Nye nnala, yeeri nalimaŋa meena ba naamu po a pa kpaga yonta a zaani ba nankula po. 25Ku a fɛ ate fi tigsi tugurik tom ase baai ate ni jɔk la, yaali wusuma a tagri ŋaai ate fi jɔk la ale torokoba a tagri baai ate fi jɔk la, ate dila ale basi ate ti baga a kpaliŋ ale ba peelimmu ale doa nna jassi la po, ate ti nak dɛ ba.>> Ben Yadad yaa jam siak te ba nye ba ale weeni diila.
26Wulum wen ale paari la Ben Yadad yaa tigsi Araam demma a cheŋ Afek wa nye kpaliŋ ale Izirali demma. 27Ase Izirali demma mɛ ale jam gomsi magsi kpaliŋ la, ba yaa gɔk santiri a tu ba. Izirali demma a jam kala a tuk ba ase ka bua ale tigsi buye la, alege ate Araam demma a lik tɛŋka meena.
28Wen nuruwa yaa jan jam weeni Izirali naawa ayen, <<Dii ate Naawen a weeni la ale nna, <Araam demma ale a poli ayen Naawen ka guuta zuima wen daa vaasa po wen la nyiŋ, Mi ale pa nuru boanni de a nyo ni nisima po, ate nama ale seba ayen ka Mi ale Naawen.> >>
29Daa ŋayopɔi meena ba jam kala a tuk ka chaab, daa ŋayopɔiwa danni ate kpaliŋka a piilim. Izirali demma a jam ko Araam demma tugurik tɔŋdɔma ka tusa kook (100,000) dai yeŋ. 30Baai ale tali la meena a jam chali cheŋ ka Afek, juijui ate parika a lo je ba a paari tusa pisiye ale ŋayopɔi la (27,000). Ben Yadad a jam chali cheŋ ka tɛŋka dek po a suk niŋ dɔk po.
31Wa kpaŋŋa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Nya, ti wom kama ayen Izirali nalimaŋa a ta ka jiirim. Basi ate ti jo boorisa gatta a pa miisa a bobi ti zuimaŋa. Dai dii dai wa ale basi ate fi vua.>>
32Ba yaa jo boorisa gatta a basi ba chaasa a pa miisa a bobi gilim ba zuima a cheŋ Izirali naawa jigi ayen, <<Fi tomteerɔwa Ben Yadad ayen, <Mi a saalim basi ate m vua.> >> Ate naawa a tulisi ayen, <<Wa diem vua kama? Wa ka mi suok.>>
33Nuruma a yaa nya kude ase ka daana maŋsa la a siak wa ale weeni diila nna mwuli. Ba weeni ayen, <<Mm fi suoku Ben Yadad.>> Naawa a weeni ayen, <<Ni ga ta wa a jam.>> Ase ba ale ga ta Ben Yadad a jam la, Ayab yaa basi ate wa jueli wa torokowa.
34Ben Yadad yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Mi ale pa tɛŋsaŋa ate mi kowa a jam tuesi fi kowa jigi la a ŋman te fu, fi baga a dueni fidek yaba kama Damasikus tɛŋka po ase mi kowa ale jam nye dii Samaria la.>> Ayab weeni ayen, <<Ase fi dan siak kude mi ale basi ate fi cheŋ fasiyaa.>> Wa yaa nye nɔiyeŋ ale wa ale basi wa ate wa cheŋ.
35Naawen wanni nyiŋ biisiteerɔba bisa wanyi a weeni wa vaanchoa ayen, <<Chub mu ale fi kpaliŋ jaamu,>> alege nuruwa a zɛri. 36Biisiteerɔwa ayen, <<Fi ale kan siak a te Naawen la nyiŋ, fi dan ga a basi mi gbeŋli ale ko fu.>> Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ nuruwa ale ga cheŋ la gbeŋli yaa nya wa a ko wa.
37Biisiteerɔwa a jam nya ka nuru wa choa ayen, <<Mi a saalim chub mu.>> Dila nuruma a yaa chub wa a te wa tuem. 38Biisiteerɔwa yaa jam ga za suiku niŋ a limisi naawa. Wa jam pa ka garuk a bobi lik wa ninaŋa ayen waai a kan miŋ wa. 39Ase naawa ale a taam la, biisiteerɔwa yaa wi wa ayen, <<Fi tomteerɔwa a jo ka kpaliŋ nummu po, ate waai a jam mi jigi ale nagyigrɔ ayen a nya nuruwa de a te mu. Wa dan vari cheŋ fi ale kpi a tuni yaase fi tuni kpana boorik. 40Ase fi tomteerɔwa nina ale muni dela ale dula la, nuruwa yaa muriŋ bɛ.>> Izirali naawa yaa weeni ayen, <<Ka fi tutuna ale la, fidek ale mooli.>>
41Biisiteerɔwa yaa kpabi a lagri garukku ate wa pa bobi wa ninaŋa la, ate Izirali naawa a miŋ wa ase biisiteerɔma wanyi la. 42Wa jam weeni naawa ayen, <<Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna, <Fi basi nuru waai ate mi a weeni ayen wa kpi la a cheŋ kama fasiyaa. Dila nyiŋ fi ale kpi a tuni ate fi nuruma a tagri chim wa nuruba.> >> 43Izirali naawa yaa kuli wa naam yenni ale bo Samaria po la ale suipuurum.

english_text:
Jezebel Has Naboth Killed
1Naboth owned a vineyard in Jezreel near King Ahab's palace.
2One day, Ahab said, “Naboth, your vineyard is near my palace. Give it to me so I can turn it into a vegetable garden. I'll give you a better vineyard or pay whatever you want for yours.”
3Naboth answered, “This vineyard has always been in my family. I won't let you have it.”
4So Ahab went home, angry and depressed because of what Naboth had told him. He lay on his bed, just staring at the wall and refusing to eat a thing.
5Jezebel his wife came in and asked, “What's wrong? Why won't you eat?”
6“I asked Naboth to sell me his vineyard or to let me give him a better one,” Ahab replied. “And he told me I couldn't have it.”
7“Aren't you the king of Israel?” Jezebel asked. “Get out of bed and eat something! Don't worry, I'll get Naboth's vineyard for you.”
8-10Jezebel wrote a letter to each of the leaders of the town where Naboth lived. In the letters she said:
Call everyone together and tell them to go without eating today. When they come together, give Naboth a seat at the front. Get two liars to sit facing him and swear that Naboth has cursed God and the king. Then take Naboth outside and stone him to death!
She signed Ahab's name to the letters and sealed them with his seal. Then she sent them to the town leaders.
11After receiving her letters, they did exactly what she had asked. 12They told the people that it was a day to go without eating, and when they all came together, they seated Naboth at the front. 13The two liars came in and sat across from Naboth. Then they accused him of cursing God and the king, so the people dragged Naboth outside and stoned him to death.
14The leaders of Jezreel sent a message back to Jezebel that said, “Naboth is dead.”
15As soon as Jezebel got their message, she told Ahab, “Now you can have the vineyard Naboth refused to sell. He's dead.” 16Ahab got up and went to take over the vineyard.
Elijah Condemns Ahab
17The Lord said to Elijah the prophet, 18“King Ahab of Israel is in Naboth's vineyard right now, taking it over. 19Go tell him that I say, ‘Ahab, you murdered Naboth and took his property. And so, in the very spot where dogs licked up Naboth's blood, they will lick up your blood.’ ”
When Elijah found him, 20Ahab said, “So, my enemy, you found me at last.”
Elijah answered:
Yes, I did! Ahab, you have managed to do everything the Lord hates. 21Now you will be punished. You and every man and boy in your family will die, whether slave or free. 22Your whole family will be wiped out, just like the families of King Jeroboam and King Baasha. You've made the Lord very angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
23 And as for Jezebel, dogs will eat her body there in Jezreel. 24Dogs will also eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
25-29When Ahab heard this, he tore his clothes in sorrow and wore sackcloth day and night. He was depressed and refused to eat.
Some time later, the Lord said, “Elijah, do you see how sorry Ahab is for what he did? I won't punish his family while he is still alive. I'll wait until his son is king.”
No one was more determined than Ahab to disobey the Lord. And Jezebel encouraged him. Worst of all, he had worshiped idols, just as the Amorites had done before the Lord forced them out of the land and gave it to Israel.
translation_text:
1Ku ale jam beni magadek la wari ale jam nye kaduk kaai ate Jezreel denɔwa Nabot a soa la. Kadukka a jam bo ka Jezreel a moata Izirali naawa Ayab yenni ale bo Samaria po la. 2Ayab yaa weeni Nabot ayen, <<Basi kadukka ate mi pa bori jenvaata, ka ale moata mi yenni la nyiŋ. Mi ale tagri a te fu kaduk kaai ale zunchoŋ la yaase fi a daa yaali, mi ale tuni fu jabuui meena ale magsi la.>> 3Alege Nabot a tulisi ayen, <<Naawen a kasi mu ate mi a kan pa mi kowa nitalimu a te fu.>>
4Ayab yaa kuli yeri ale suipuurum dii nyiŋla Jezreel denɔwa Nabot a weeni kama ayen, <<Mi a kan pa m kowa nitalimu a te fu.>> Wa yaa jam doa wa gaduokku zuk nna diki a zɛri ŋandiinta dɛka.
5Wa powa Jezebel yaa jam jo a bek wa ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi sui a yiti? Ka boa ate fi kan dɛ?>> 6Ate wa tulisi ayen, <<Dii nyiŋla mi weeni ka Nabot Jezreel denɔwa ayen, <Pa fi kadukka a da te mu yaase fi daa yaali mi ale tagri a te fu kaduk yoŋ.> Alege ate wa zɛri ayen, <Mi a kan te fu m kadukka.> >>
7Wa powa Jezebel yaa weeni ayen, <<Ka nnala ate fi a nye ase Izirali naab la? Yiti ŋmai a dɛ. Mariŋ fidek. Mi ale te fu Nabot Jezreel denɔwa kadukka.>>
8Jezebel yaa ŋmarisi gbaŋsa Ayab yuenni nyiŋ a pai wa yuenni a ji si zuk, a tom si a te nisɔmma ale kpaŋŋa baai ale bo Nabot tɛŋ kpieŋka po ale wa la. 9Gbaŋsaŋa ate wa ŋmarisi la ayen, <<Te dai ate nuruma meena a bobi nɔi, wi nuruma jigi yeŋ a te Nabot zula dek jigi nuruma po. 10Basi ate wɔkwɔk nyam baye a kali a tuk wa, te a ti ba weeni ayen ba a wom ale Nabot a biisi Wen ale naawa a kaasi. Ba yaa yik Nabot a ta nyini tɛŋ kpieŋka po a nyini a yuk wa ale tintana a ko.>>
11Dila nisɔmma ale kpaŋŋa baai ale bo Nabot tɛŋ kpieŋka po la yaa nye dii ate Jezebel a ŋmarisi gbaŋsaŋa po ayen ba nye la. 12Ba yaa jam nye tigi a pa Nabot a kali kalidek jigi nuruma po. 13Wɔkwɔk nuruma bayewa yaa jam, a kali tuk wa a velim te Nabot nuruma niŋ ayen, <<Nabot a biisi Wen ale naawa a kasi.>> Ba yaa yik wa ate nyini tɛŋ kpieŋka po a nyini a yuk wa ale tintana a ko. 14Ba yaa tom weeni Jezebel ayen, <<Ti yuk Nabot ale ka tintana a ko.>>
15Ase Jezebel ale ga wom ayen ba yuk Nabot ale tintana a ko la, wa yaa weeni Ayab ayen, <<Yiti ŋmai a tuesi Nabot Jezreel denɔwa kadukka ate wa zɛri an pa da te fu la. Wa an ŋman vua, wa kpi kama.>> 16Ase Ayab ale wom ayen Nabot a kpi la, wa yaa yiti cheŋ a ga tuesi Nabot kadukka.
17Naawen wanni yaa jam Tisbi denɔwa Elaja jigi ayen, 18<<Cheŋ ga tu Ayab Izirali naawa waai ale a nya Samaria la jigi. Wa bo ka Nabot kadukka po juijui ate wa cheŋ wa tuesi la. 19Weeni wa ayen, <Dii ate Naawen a weeni la ale nna. Fi an ko daa nuru ale vari wa nitalim la?> Yaa weeni wa ayen, <Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: Juijui ate baasaŋa a leeli Nabot ziimu la, dula dek baasa ale leeli fi mɛ ziimu.> >>
20Ayab yaa weeni Elaja ayen, <<Dila fi nya mi kama m dachiaga!>> Ate wa tulisi ayen, <<Mm, Mi nya fu kama, dii nyiŋla fi ta fidek a nyini kama ayen fi nye biem Naawen nimbie po. 21Naawen weeni ayen, <Mi a yaali m ta ka kaasuŋ a jam fi yenni zuk. Mi ale ko fi ŋaaŋbisaŋa abe m ko fi nidoama meena fi dɔkdemma po baai ale ka yɔm ale baai ale kan daa yɔm la. 22Mi ale nye fi yenni ase ka Nebat nidoabinni Jeroboam ale Ayija nidoabinni Baasia ate mi jam nye diila, dii nyiŋla ni nye ate ka m sui a puuri ale basi ate Izirali demma a nye biem.>
23<<A ta va Jezebel Naawen a weeni wa mɛ ayen, <Baasa ale ŋɔbi Jezebel nyiŋka Jezreel po.> 24Baasa ale ŋɔbi Ayab ale soa baai ate ba kpi tɛŋ kpieŋka po la ate nuinsaŋa ale bo wen ŋmazuk la a dɛ baai ale kpi tɛŋka nakpiak la.>>
25Nuru a jam karo ase Ayab la, waai ale jam ta wadek a nyini ayen wa nye biem Naawen nimbie po la, wa powa Jezebel ale jam basi ate wa nye dila. 26Wa jam nye ka biem nna yegayega a ta va wa ale jam a kaab bɔgta la, dii dek ate Amori demma a jam nye ate Naawen a yiak ba ale pa ba tɛŋka a te Izirali demma la.
27Ase Ayab ale ga wom wieŋa de la, wa yaa cheeri wa gattaŋa ale sui kaasuŋ ale jo boorisa garuk a bobi nɔi. Wa jam a goa ale ka boorisa garuk, a jo ku a gilim nna diki.
28Naawen wanni yaa jan jam Tisbi denɔwa Elaja jigi ayen, 29<<Fi nya Ayab ale yik wadek dii mi niŋ la? Wa ale yik wadek la nyiŋ, mi a kan ŋman ta kaasuŋku de a jam wa vaaŋa po, alege mi ale ta ku a jam wa yenni zuk wa nidoabinni vaaŋa po.>>

english_text:
Micaiah Warns Ahab about Disaster
(2 Chronicles 18.2-27)
1For the next three years there was peace between Israel and Syria. 2During the third year King Jehoshaphat of Judah went to visit King Ahab of Israel.
3Ahab asked his officials, “Why haven't we tried to get Ramoth in Gilead back from the Syrians? It belongs to us.” 4Then he asked Jehoshaphat, “Would you go to Ramoth with me and attack the Syrians?”
“Just tell me what to do,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army and horses are at your command. 5But first, let's ask the Lord.”
6Ahab sent for about 400 prophets and asked, “Should I attack the Syrians at Ramoth?”
“Yes!” the prophets answered. “The Lord will help you defeat them.”
7But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
8“We could ask Micaiah son of Imlah,” Ahab said. “But I hate Micaiah. He always has bad news for me.”
“Don't say that!” Jehoshaphat replied. 9Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.
10All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria. They were listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
11Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was one of the prophets. He had made some horns out of iron and shouted, “Ahab, the Lord says you will attack the Syrians like a bull with iron horns and wipe them out!”
12All the prophets agreed that Ahab should attack the Syrians at Ramoth, and they promised that the Lord would help him defeat them.
13Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
14“I'll say whatever the living Lord tells me to say,” Micaiah replied.
15Then Micaiah went to Ahab, and Ahab asked, “Micaiah, should I attack the Syrians at Ramoth?”
“Yes!” Micaiah answered. “The Lord will help you defeat them.”
16“Micaiah, I've told you over and over to tell me the truth!” Ahab shouted. “What does the Lord really say?”
17 He answered, “In a vision I saw Israelite soldiers walking around in the hills like sheep without a shepherd to guide them. The Lord said, ‘This army has no leader. They should go home and not fight.’ ”
18Ahab turned to Jehoshaphat and said, “I told you he would bring bad news!”
19 Micaiah replied:
Listen to this! I also saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him. 20The Lord asked, “Who can trick Ahab and make him go to Ramoth where he will be killed?”
They talked about it for a while, 21then finally a spirit came forward and said to the Lord, “I can trick Ahab.”
“How?” the Lord asked.
22“I'll make Ahab's prophets lie to him.”
“Good!” the Lord replied. “Now go and do it.”
23This is exactly what has happened, Ahab. The Lord made all your prophets lie to you, and he knows you will soon be destroyed.
24Zedekiah walked up to Micaiah and slapped him on the face. Then he asked, “Do you really think the Lord would speak to you and not to me?”
25Micaiah answered, “You'll find out on the day you have to hide in the back room of some house.”
26Ahab shouted, “Arrest Micaiah! Take him to Prince Joash and Governor Amon of Samaria. 27Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
28Micaiah said, “If you do come back, I was wrong about what the Lord wanted me to say.” Then he told the crowd, “Don't forget what I said!”
Ahab Dies at Ramoth
(2 Chronicles 18.28-34)
29Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead. 30Before they went into battle, Ahab said, “Jehoshaphat, I'll disguise myself, but you wear your royal robe.” Then Ahab disguised himself and went into battle.
31The king of Syria had ordered his 32 chariot commanders to attack only Ahab. 32So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But when Jehoshaphat shouted out to them, 33they realized he wasn't Ahab, and they left him alone.
34However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab where two pieces of his armor joined. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”
35The fighting lasted all day, with Ahab propped up in his chariot so he could see the Syrian troops. He bled so much that the bottom of the chariot was covered with blood, and by evening he was dead.
36As the sun was going down, someone in Israel's army shouted to the others, “Retreat! Go back home!”
37Ahab's body was taken to Samaria and buried there. 38Some workers washed his chariot near a spring in Samaria, and prostitutes washed themselves in his blood. Dogs licked Ahab's blood off the ground, just as the Lord had warned.
39Everything else Ahab did while he was king, including the towns he strengthened and the palace he built and furnished with ivory, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. 40Ahab died, and his son Ahaziah became king.
King Jehoshaphat of Judah
(2 Chronicles 20.31—21.1)
41Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king of Judah in Ahab's fourth year as king of Israel. 42Jehoshaphat was 35 years old when he became king, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 25 years. His mother was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
43-46Jehoshaphat obeyed the Lord, just as his father Asa had done, and during his rule he was at peace with the king of Israel.
He got rid of the rest of the prostitutes from the local shrines, but he did not destroy the shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
Everything else Jehoshaphat did while he was king, including his brave deeds and military victories, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
47The country of Edom had no king at the time, so a lower official ruled the land.
48Jehoshaphat had seagoing ships built to sail to Ophir for gold. But they were wrecked at Ezion-Geber and never sailed. 49Ahaziah son of Ahab offered to let his sailors go with Jehoshaphat's sailors, but Jehoshaphat refused.
50Jehoshaphat died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king.
King Ahaziah of Israel
51Ahaziah son of Ahab became king of Israel in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria.
52Ahaziah disobeyed the Lord, just as his father, his mother, and Jeroboam had done. They all led Israel to sin. 53Ahaziah worshiped Baal and made the Lord God of Israel very angry, just as his father had done.
translation_text:
1Bena ŋata meena Araam ale Izirali an jam kpaliŋ chaaba. 2Bena ŋatawa po Jeyosafat Juda naawa yaa jam cheŋ wa nya Izirali naawa Ayab. 3Izirali naawa a ŋaam weeni wa kpaŋŋa kama ayen, <<Nama a seba ayen Aramot Gilead ka tama ale soa alege ti kan nye wari ayen ti ŋman a tuesi ka a ta nyini Araam naawa jigi ya.>>
4Wa yaa bek Jeyosafat ayen, <<Fi ale va mu a ga nye kpaliŋ ale Aramot Gilead?>> Jeyosafat yaa tulisi Izirali naawa ayen, <<Mi a nye ase ka fi la, mi nuruma ase fi nuruma la, mi wusumaŋa ase fi wusumaŋa la.>> 5Jeyosafat a ŋman weeni Izirali naawa a gum du ayen, <<De niŋ a bek ase ka Naawen yaalika ya.>>
6Dila Izirali naawa yaa jam ta biisiteerɔba a jam jigi yeŋ ase kobsinaansi la a bek ba ayen, <<Mi ga nye kpaliŋ ale Aramot Gilead yaa m kan cheŋ?>> Ba yaa tulisi ayen, <<Cheŋ ale Nyɔnɔwa ale pa ka a nyo naawa nisa po.>>
7Alege Jeyosafat a jam bek ayen, <<Naawen biisiteerɔ a ka dela ate ti ga kpesi wom?>> 8Izirali naawa yaa tulisi Jeyosafat ayen, <<Nuru wanyi a diem boro ate tama a baga a va wa zuk a kpesi a wom a nyini Naawen jigi, alege mi kisi wa kama dii nyiŋla wa an diem porisi wa maŋ a te mi, wa a weeni mi ka kaasuŋ nyiini. Wa ka Imla nidoabinni Mikaiya.>> Jeyosafat yaa tulisi ayen, <<Naawa an magsi wa weeni dila.>>
9Dila Izirali naawa yaa wi wa kpaŋŋa wanyi ayen, <<Ta Imla nidoabinni Mikaiya a jam.>>
10Izirali naawa ale Juda naawa Jeyosafat a jam jo ba naam gatta a kala ba naam zukpagliksaŋa zuk, juijui ate ba a fɔbi ŋanta la Samaria tɛŋka nansuiŋku nɔi ate biisiteerɔma meena a porisi ba niŋ. 11Chenaana nidoabinni Zedekia a jam nye ka kutuk nyiila ale mooli ayen, <<Dii ate Naawen a weeni la ale nna, <Ni ale pa ka nyiilaŋa de a chub Araam demma ate ku paari diipo ate ni ko ba la.> >>
12Biisiteerɔ mbala a jam a porisi ka wayeŋka ayen, <<Nye kpaliŋ ale Aramot Gilead a nya pagrim ba zuk, ale Naawen ale pa ba a nyo naawa nisa po.
13Tomtomdɔ waai ale jam cheŋ wa wi Mikaiya la yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Nya de, biisiteerɔ mbala meena a weeni kama ayen naab Ayab ale nya nak dɛka, basi ate fi ale a weeni diila a va bala ale weeni diila biisi ale ŋmanteka.>>
14Alege Mikaiya a weeni wa ayen, <<Ase Naawen ale vua la, mi ale weeni wa ka dii nyiini ate Naawen a weeni mi la.>>
15Ase wa ale jam paari la, naawa yaa bek Mikaiya ayen, <<Mikaiya, ti cheŋ ga nye kpaliŋ ale Aramot Gilead yaa ti kan cheŋ?>> Wa yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Ni ga nye a nya nakdeka ale Naawen ale pai Aramot Gilead a nyo fi nisa po.>>
16Naawa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Ka bu dina ate mi ale te fi pɛ a kan weeni mu wayoŋ alege ka wensie nyiini Naawen yuenni nyiŋŋa?>>
17Mikaiya yaa tulisi ayen, <<Mi nya ale Izirali meena a waaŋ chaab guutaŋa zuima ase piisa ale kan ta naapeerik diila, ate Naawen ayen, <Nuruma de a ka niŋdeerɔ. Basi ate ba kuli yeri ale suiyɔgni.> >>
18Izirali naawa yaa weeni Jeyosafat ayen, <<Mi an poom weeni fu ayen wa an diem porisi wamaŋ a te mi, ka kaasuŋ nyiini?>>
19Mikaiya a weeni a gum du ayen, <<Dila nyiŋ wom Naawen wanni. Mi nya ale Naawen a kala ka wa naam zukpaglika zuk ate wenŋmazuk tommu a za gilim wa juga ale gala meena. 20Naawen yaa weeni ayen, <Ka wana ale wa paasi Ayab ate wa nye kpaliŋ ale Aramot Gilead tɛŋka ate wa ga kpi dula?> Nuru yeŋ a zok nna ate wa choa ayen nnala. 21Kpeglimka chichirik biok yaa jam niŋ nyiŋ, a zaani Naawen niŋ ayen, <Mi ale paasi wa.>
22<<Naawen a bek ayen, <Fi ale nye ka sɛ a nye dila?> Ate chichirik bioku a tulisi ayen, <Mi ale nyini peelim a ga jo wa biisiteerɔma meena nɔi po.> Naawen ayen, <Fi le nya suik a paasi wa, cheŋ ga nye dila.> >>
23Mikaiya a weeni ayen, <<Naawen a basi ate fi biisiteerɔma a velim te fu kama, Naawen abe weeni kama ayen kaasuŋ a jam fi zuk.>>
24Chenaana nidoabinni Zedekia yaa ga fɔbi Mikaiya ale bek ayen, <<Ka suik kuna po ate Naawen Chiika a nyini mi po a ga biisi ale fi?>>
25Mikaiya yaa tulisi ayen, <<Fi ale nya dila ka dai dii dai ate fi ale chali ga suk niŋ dɔk po la.>>
26Izirali naawa yaa weeni ayen, << Ni yik Mikaiya a ta wa ŋman ga te Amon tɛŋ kpieŋka niŋdeerɔwa ale naawa nidoabinni Joas 27ale weeni ayen, <Dii ate naawa a weeni la ale nna. Ni pa nuruwa de a nyo likka dɔk po abe ni kan te wa jaaboa, ni te wa boroborok ale nyiam nyiini ate ku paari diipo ate mi ale jam ale suiyɔgni la.> >> 28Mikaiya yaa tulisi ayen, <<Fi a dan ŋman nalimnyiini, Naawen an va mi zuk a biisi ya.>> Wa yaa ŋman biisi a gum du ayen, <<Ni a teeri mi wieŋa, nama nuruba meena.>>
29Dila Izirali naawa ale Juda naawa Jeyosafat yaa jueli Aramot Gilead. 30Izirali naawa yaa weeni Jeyosafat ayen, <<Mi ale cheŋ kpaliŋ ka po, mi ale jo ka garuk yoŋta a cheŋ ate waai a kan baga a miŋ mu. Alege fi a jo fi naam gattaŋa.>> Izirali naawa yaa jo garuk yoŋta a cheŋ kpaliŋka po.
31Araam naawa yaa weeni kpaga ŋaai ale a nya torokoma pisita ale ŋayewa zuk la ayen, <<Ni kan nye kpaliŋ ale waai ya, bi fiik yaase jakpak, ka Izirali naawa nyiini.>> 32Ase torokoma kpaŋŋa ale jam nya Jeyosafat la, ba yaa jam a poli ayen, <<Chekki wa ale chim ka Izirali naawa.>> Ba yaa viriŋ ba nye kpaliŋ ale wa, alege Jeyosafat ale kaari la. 33Torokoma kpaŋŋa yaa nya ayen daa Izirali naawa ale la a yaa basi wa vi ka.
34Alege waai yaa yeeri wa tom nna kadi a tɔŋ kali Izirali naawa. Ate naawa a weeni wa toroko damdɔwa ayen, <<Dam a gilim a ta mu a nyini kpaliŋ ka po a nyini ale mi koani kama.>> 35Danni po meena kpaliŋka a jam boro kama, ate naawa a jam bo torokowa po a tuk Araam demma a nya. Wa ziimu a jam sueri torokowa kama a nyini. Junɔi ale paari la wa yaa kpi. 36Ase wenbinni ale a pusi la kaarik ale nyini tugurik jigini ayen, <<Waai meena a kuli wa tɛŋ.>>
37Naawa yaa jam kpi ate ba ta wa a jam Samaria a gu wa dula. 38Ba jam sugri torokowa ka Samaria bulik po ate taabuksa a so di po la, ate baasa a jam leeli wa ziimu ase Naawen wanni ale jam weeni diila.
39Dan ka Ayab wayoŋ ntila, ale dii meena ate wa nye la, naam yenni ate wa jam sɛ a ŋmirisi di ale yauk nyina la ale tɛŋ kpieŋka ate wa sɛ parik a gilim la, ŋala a ŋmarisi a doa Izirali nalima gbaŋsaŋa po kama. 40Ayab a jam kpi kama a gum wa koma po ate wa nidoabinni Ayaziya a zaani wa nankula po a chim naab.
41Asa nidoabinni Jeyosafat a jam chim Juda naab ka bena ŋanaansiwa po ate Izirali naawa Ayab a dɛ naamu la. 42Jeyosafat a jam ta ka bena pisita ale ŋanu ale chim naab, a dɛ naamu Jerusalem po a paari bena pisiye ale ŋanu. Wa mawa yuei jam le Azuba, wa jam ka Silyi lie. 43Jeyosafat jam ka nuru maŋ ase wa kowa Asa la, wa jam a nye ka dii ate Naawen ayen ku nala la. Alege Jeyosafat an jam kaasi pimpitimaŋa a basi ya, ate nuruma a diem jam a nye tiirim kaabka ale a ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la dula. 44Jeyosafat ale Izirali naawa a jam boro ale ka suiyɔgni ale chaab.
45Dan ka Jeyosafat wayoŋ ntila, wie ŋaai ate wa jam nye la ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma wie, ŋala a ŋmarisi doa Izirali nalima gbaŋsaŋa po kama. 46Wa jam kaasi nipok yaali tuima tangbanaŋa nidoama kama, ŋaai ale diem jam boro wa kowa Asa naamu ŋaaŋnyiŋ la. 47Dila powa naab a jam ka Edom tɛŋka, ka nansuiŋ naab.
48Jeyosafat a jam nye ka geruŋ ŋaaruŋta ayen ti a cheŋ Ofir a ta ligmɔniŋ a jam, alege dila an jam baga a nye ya, ti jam kaasi ka Ezion Geber tɛŋka. 49Dila powa Ayab nidoabinni Ayaziya a jam weeni Jeyosafat kama ayen, <<Basi ate mi nuruma a nyeemu ale fi nuruma,>> alege Jeyosafat a zɛri.
50Jeyosafat yaa kpi a gum wa koma po ate ba gu wa a gum ba po, Deevid tɛŋka po, wa ko kpieŋ ale la. Ate wa nidoabinni Jeyoram a jam zaani wa nankula po a chim naab.
51Ayab nidoabinni Ayaziya a jam chim naab Izirali ale bo Samaria po la ka bena pi ale ŋayopɔiwa po ate Juda tɛŋka naawa Jeyosafat a dɛ naamu la. Ayaziya jam nya Izirali zuk ka bena ŋaye. 52Wa jam nye ka biem Naawen nimbie po, dii nyiŋla, wa jam a nye ka wa kowa ale wa mawa nyeelaŋa ale bo Nebat nidoabinni Jeroboam boka, waai ale basi ate Izirali demma a nye biem la. 53Wa jam tom a te ale a kaab ka Baal a nye ate Naawen, Izirali Wenni sui a puuri, ase dii dek ate wa kowa a jam nye la.

english_text:
The Lord Condemns Ahaziah
1-2Soon after King Ahab of Israel died, the country of Moab rebelled against his son King Ahaziah.
One day, Ahaziah fell through the wooden slats around the porch on the flat roof of his palace in Samaria, and he was badly injured. So he sent some messengers to the town of Ekron with orders to ask the god Baalzebub if he would get well.
3About the same time, an angel from the Lord sent Elijah the prophet from Tishbe to say to the king's messengers, “Ahaziah has rejected Israel's own God by sending you to ask Baalzebub about his injury. 4Tell him that because he has done this, he's on his deathbed!” And Elijah did what he was told.
5When the messengers returned to Ahaziah, he asked, “Why are you back so soon?”
6“A man met us along the road with a message for you from the Lord,” they answered. “The Lord wants to know why you sent us to ask Baalzebub about your injury and why you don't believe there's a God in Israel. The man also told us that the Lord says you're going to die.”
7“What did the man look like?” Ahaziah asked.
8 “He was hairy and had a leather belt around his waist,” they answered.
“It must be Elijah!” replied Ahaziah. 9So at once he sent an army officer and 50 soldiers to meet Elijah.
Elijah was sitting on top of a hill at the time. The officer went up to him and said, “Man of God, the king orders you to come down and talk with him.”
10 “If I am a man of God,” Elijah answered, “God will send down fire on you and your 50 soldiers.” Fire immediately came down from heaven and burned up the officer and his men.
11Ahaziah sent another officer and 50 more soldiers to Elijah. The officer said, “Man of God, the king orders you to come see him at once.”
12“If I am a man of God,” Elijah answered, “fire will destroy you and your 50 soldiers.” And God sent down fire from heaven on the officer and his men.
13Ahaziah sent a third army officer and 50 more soldiers. This officer went up to Elijah, then he got down on his knees and begged, “Man of God, please be kind to me and these 50 servants of yours. Let us live! 14Fire has already wiped out the other officers and their soldiers. Please don't let it happen to me.”
15The angel from the Lord said to Elijah, “Go with him and don't be afraid.” So Elijah got up and went with the officer.
16When Elijah arrived, he told Ahaziah, “The Lord wants to know why you sent messengers to Ekron to ask Baalzebub about your injury. Don't you believe there's a God in Israel? Ahaziah, because you did that, the Lord says you will die.”
17Ahaziah died, just as the Lord had said. But since Ahaziah had no sons, Joram his brother then became king. This happened in the second year that Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat was king of Judah. 18Everything else Ahaziah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_text:
1Ayab kummu ŋaaŋnyiŋ, Moab a jam ta ka chaab ale Izirali. 2Yɔgyɔgla de Ayaziya a jam nyini ka gboŋ zuk a va ŋan nyaara po a lo Samaria tɛŋka po a kɔni wadek. Ate wa tom nuruba ayen, <<Ga kpesi nyini Baal Zebub ale ka Ekron wen la, a nya ase m le nya nyiŋyɔgsa a nyini m le kɔni la ya.>>
3Alege Naawen maarɔwa a jam weeni Elaja ale ka Tisbi denɔ la ayen, <<Cheŋ a ga tu Samaria naawa ale tom baai la a bek ba ayen, <Ka Izirali ale kan ta Wen la nyiŋ ale soa ate ni a cheŋ ayen ni ga kpesi nyini Baal Zebub ale ka Ekron wen la jigi ya?> 4Dila nyiŋ Naawen ale a weeni diila ale nna, fi a kan yiti fi gaduokku zuwa. Fi za fi kpi kama.>> Ate Elaja a jam cheŋ.
5Nuruma ale jam cheŋ naawa jigi la, wa yaa bek ba ayen, <<Ka boa ate nama a ŋman jam?>>
6Ba yaa tulisi ayen, <<Nuru ale jam tu tama a weeni ti ayen, <Ni ŋman naab waai ale tom ni la jigi a weeni wa ayen, <<Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna, ayen ka Izirali ale kan ta Wen la nyiŋ ale soa ate fi a tom nuruba ayen ba ga kpesi nyini Baal Zebub ale ka Ekron wen la jigi ya? Dila nyiŋ fi kan yiti fi gaduokku zuwa. Fi za fi kpi kama.>> > >>
7Naawa yaa bek ba ayen, <<Ka boan nuru choa ale la a jam tu a weeni nya kude a sak ni?>> 8Ba yaa tulisi ayen, <<Wa ka nuru waai ale jo garuk ate ku ta kɔbta ale chiak gbain a bobi wa chiaka.>> Naawa yaa weeni ayen, <<Ku ale chim ka Elaja, Tisbi denɔwa.>>
9Ate ba cheŋ Elaja jigi ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔba kpagi ale wa nuruba pisinu. Tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagni yaa cheŋ jueli Elaja jigi ale wa kala guuk zuk, ate wa weeni wa ayen, <<Wen nuroa, naawa ayen siŋ jam.>> 10Elaja yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ase mi a dan ka Wen nuru, bolim abe nyini wenŋmazuk a jam dɛ fu ale fi nuruba pisinuwa.>> Ate bolim a nyini wenŋmazuk lo a dɛ tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagni ale wa nuruba pisinuwa.
11Nya kude naawa a ŋman jam tom ka tugurik tɔŋdɔba kpagi ale wa nuruba pisinu. Tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagni a jam weeni wa kama ayen, <<Wen nuroa, naawa ale a weeni diila ale nna ayen, <Nye nwuli a siŋ jam.> >> 12Elaja yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ase mi dan ka Wen nuru, bolim abe nyini wenŋmazuk a jam dɛ fu ale fi nuruba pisinuwa.>> Ate Wen bolim a jam dɛ wa ale wa nuruba pisinuwa.
13Ate naawa a jam tom tugurik tɔŋdɔ kpagi dii ale a saari buta la ale wa nuruba pisinu. Tugurik tɔŋdɔ kpagni de ale saari buta la a jam cheŋ jueli kama a ga kpi duna Elaja niŋ a saalim ayen, <<Wen nuroa, mi a saalim fu ayen fi nya m nyuvunni ale nuruba pisinuwa nyuvooŋa zuk, fi tomteerɔma. 14Nya, bolim ale nyini wenŋmazuk a jam dɛ tugurik tɔŋdɔ kpaŋŋa bayewa ale ba nuruma. Alege yɔgyɔgla de nya m nyuvunni.>>
15Naawen maarɔwa yaa weeni Elaja ayen, <<Siŋ a cheŋ ale wa. Kan chali yɔgsum ale wa.>> Ate Elaja a yiti ŋmai ate ba va chaab a cheŋ naawa jigi.
16Wa jam weeni naawa kama ayen, <<Nya kude ate Naawen a weeni ayen, <Ka Izirali ale kan ta Wen la nyiŋ ate fi a tom nuruba ayen ba cheŋ Baal Zebub ale ka Ekron wen la jigi a ga kpesi nya ya? Fi ale nye nya kude la nyiŋ fi kan yiti fi gaduokku zuwa. Fi za fi kpi kama.> >> 17Ate wa kpi a vachaab ale Naawen wanni ate Elaja a biisi la. Ayaziya ale kan ta nidoabili la nyiŋ, Jeyoram ale jam tagri wa a chim naab bena ŋayewa po ate Jeyoram ale ka Jeyosafat nidoabili la a chim Juda naab. 18Wie ŋaai ale nye Ayaziya naamu vaaŋa po ale dii ate wa nye la, ŋala a ŋmarisi a doa Izirali nalimaŋa gbaŋka po kama.

english_text:
The Lord Takes Elijah Away
1Not long before the Lord took Elijah up into heaven in a strong wind, Elijah and Elisha were leaving Gilgal. 2Elijah said to Elisha, “The Lord wants me to go to Bethel, but you must stay here.”
Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I will stay with you no matter what!” And he went with Elijah to Bethel.
3A group of prophets who lived there asked Elisha, “Do you know that today the Lord is going to take away your master?”
“Yes, I do,” Elisha answered. “But don't remind me of it.”
4Elijah then said, “Elisha, now the Lord wants me to go to Jericho, but you must stay here.”
Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life, that I will stay with you no matter what!” And he went with Elijah to Jericho.
5A group of prophets who lived there asked Elisha, “Do you know that today the Lord is going to take away your master?”
“Yes, I do,” Elisha answered. “But don't remind me of it.”
6Elijah then said to Elisha, “Now the Lord wants me to go to the Jordan River, but you must stay here.”
Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I will never leave you!” So the two of them walked on together.
7Fifty prophets followed Elijah and Elisha from Jericho, then stood at a distance and watched as the two men walked toward the river. 8When they got there, Elijah took off his coat, then he rolled it up and struck the water with it. At once a path opened up through the river, and the two of them walked across on dry ground.
9 After they had reached the other side, Elijah said, “Elisha, the Lord will soon take me away. What can I do for you before that happens?”
Elisha answered, “Please give me twice as much of your power as you give the other prophets, so I can be the one who takes your place as their leader.”
10“It won't be easy,” Elijah answered. “It can happen only if you see me as I am being taken away.”
11Elijah and Elisha were walking along and talking, when suddenly there appeared between them a flaming chariot pulled by fiery horses. At once, a strong wind took Elijah up into heaven. 12 Elisha saw this and shouted, “Israel's cavalry and chariots have taken my master away!” After Elijah had gone, Elisha tore his clothes in sorrow.
13Elijah's coat had fallen off, so Elisha picked it up and walked back to the Jordan River. 14He struck the water with the coat and wondered, “Will the Lord perform miracles for me as he did for Elijah?” As soon as Elisha did this, a dry path opened up through the water, and he walked across.
15When the prophets from Jericho saw what happened, they said to each other, “Elisha now has Elijah's power.”
They walked over to him, bowed down, 16and said, “There are 50 strong men here with us. Please let them go look for your master. Maybe the Spirit of the Lord carried him off to some mountain or valley.”
“No,” Elisha replied, “they won't find him.”
17They kept begging until he was embarrassed to say no. He finally agreed, and the prophets sent the men out. They looked three days for Elijah but never found him. 18They returned to Jericho, and Elisha said, “I told you that you wouldn't find him.”
Elisha Makes the Water Pure at Jericho
19One day the people of Jericho said, “Elisha, you can see that our city is in a good spot. But the water from our spring is so bad that it even keeps our crops from growing.”
20He replied, “Put some salt in a new bowl and bring it to me.”
They brought him the bowl of salt, 21and he carried it to the spring. He threw the salt into the water and said, “The Lord has made this water pure again. From now on you'll be able to grow crops, and no one will starve.”
22The water has been fine ever since, just as Elisha said.
Some Boys Make Fun of Elisha
23Elisha left and headed toward Bethel. Along the way some boys started making fun of him by shouting, “Go away, baldy! Get out of here!”
24Elisha turned around and stared at the boys. Then he cursed them in the name of the Lord. At once two bears ran out of the woods and ripped to pieces 42 of the boys.
25Elisha went up to Mount Carmel, then returned to Samaria.

1Diipo ate Naawen a jam boro ayen wa pai va pagrik a ta Elaja a jueli wenŋmazuk la, Elaja ale Ɛlaisa a jam nyini ka Gilgal a bo suik po a cheŋ 2Elaja a jam weeni Ɛlaisa ayen, <<Bo dela. Naawen a tom mu ka Betel.>> Alege Ɛlaisa weeni ayen, <<Ase Naawen ale vua la, ate fi mɛ a vua la, m kan basi fu.>> Ate ba jam cheŋ siŋ Betel.
3Wen biisiteerɔma tigsuŋku ale bo Betel po la yaa nyini jam Ɛlaisa jigi a bek wa ayen, <<Fi seba ayen Naawen jinla a za wa pai fi kpagni a ta cheŋ?>> Ɛlaisa yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<Mm, m seba kama alege ni kan biisi ku wari ya.>>
4Ate Elaja a jam weeni wa ayen, <<Ɛlaisa, bo dela ale Naawen a tom mu ka Jeriko.>> Ate wa tulisi wa ayen, <<Ase Naawen ale vua la nyiŋ ate fi mɛ a vua la, m kan basi fu.>> Ate ba jam cheŋ Jeriko.
5Wen biisiteerɔma tigsuŋku ale bo Jeriko la yaa jam cheŋ Ɛlaisa jigi a bek wa ayen, <<Fi seba ayen Naawen a za wa pai fi kpagni jinla a ta nyini fi jigi ya?>> Ate wa tulisi ba ayen, <<Mm, m seba kama alege ni kan biisi ku wari ya.>>
6Ate Elaja a jam weeni wa ayen, <<Bo dela ale ka Naawen ale tom mu ayen m cheŋ Jodan Benni.>> Ate wa tulisi wa ayen, <<Ase Naawen ale vua la nyiŋ ate fi mɛ a vua la, m kan basi fu.>> Ate ba nɔi bayema a jam va chaab a cheŋ.
7Wen biisiteerɔma tigsuŋku pisinu ale jam bo jigi yeŋ a ga za niŋniŋŋa a pai ba nina a tuk juijui ate Elaja ale Ɛlaisa a jam zaani a bo Jodan la. 8Elaja yaa pai wa tankaluŋ a vili a nak nyiamu. Ate nyiamu a lab basi a juga ale a gala ate ba nɔi bayewa a jam a cheŋ tɛŋ kosik zuk a taam.
9Ba ale jam lɔ jueli la, ate Elaja a jam weeni Ɛlaisa ayen, <<Weeni mu, ka boa ate m le nye a te fu abe m ge ate ba pai mu a nyini fi jigi ya?>> Ɛlaisa yaa jam tulisi ayen, <<Basi ate m ta fi chiika ku naŋtuok nɔi buye.>> 10Elaja yaa weeni ayen, <<Fi bek ka ja pagrik alege fi dan nya ale ba pai mu ta a cheŋ a nyini fi jigi, fi ale soa ku. Alege kan daa di fi kan nya ku.>>
11Ase ba ale jam va chaab a biisi a cheŋ la, ate toroko ale bolim ale wusuma ale bolim a jam na nyini ba jigi a poori ba nɔi bayema, ate va pagrik a jam ta Elaja a cheŋ wenŋmazuk. 12Ɛlaisa a jam nya kude kama a kaari ayen, <<M koa! M koa! Torokoma ale Izirali wusum duerɔma!>> Ɛlaisa an ŋman jam nya wa. Ate wa yaa jam yik wadek tankaluŋtaŋa dari cheeri.
13Wa jam pai ka tankaluŋ kuui ale nyini Elaja jigi a lo la a pilim ŋmani cheŋ ga zaani Jodan benni nɔi. 14Ate wa jam pai tankaluŋ kuui ale nyini wa jigi a lo la a nak nyiamu. Wa yaa jam bek ayen, <<Naawen ale Elaja Wenni yɔgyɔgla de a boka bɛ?>> Wa ale jam nak nyiamu la, bu jam lab kama a basi a juga ale a gala ate wa lo jueli.
15Wen biisiteerɔma tigsuŋku ale jam nyini Jeriko a za a nya la yaa weeni ayen, <<Elaja chiika a jam bo Ɛlaisa zuk kama.>> Ate ba cheŋ a ga tu wa ale kpi duna tɛŋ wa niŋ. 16Ba jam weeni wa kama ayen, <<Nya, tama fi tomteerɔma a ta ka nuruba pisinu ate ba paari chaab. Basi ate ti te ba cheŋ a ga gisi fi kpagni. Da dii dai Naawen Chiika a pai wa kama a ta ga basi guuk kuui zuk yaase viak po.>> Ɛlaisa yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<Aaya, ni kan tom ba.>>
17Alege ba jam kasim ta wa kama ate chivie a ga yik wa ate wa an baga a zɛri. Ate wa weeni ayen, <<Ni tom ba.>> Ate ba jam tom nuruba pisinu ate ba pai daa ŋata a gisi alege ba an nya wa. 18Ba ale ŋmani jam Ɛlaisa jigi la waai ale jam bo Jeriko la, wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Mi an weeni ni ayen ni kan cheŋ?>>
19Tɛŋka nuruma yaa weeni Ɛlaisa ayen, <<Nya, ti nyɔnɔ, tɛŋka de a bo ka jigi maŋ, ase fi ale poom a nya la, alege nyiamu a bie kama ate tɛŋka mɛ a ka jaaboa.>> 20Wa jam weeni ayen, <<Ni pai yesa a nyo chin paali po a ta jam a te mu.>> Ate ba jam ta cheŋ a ga te wa.
21Ate wa cheŋ benni a pai yesaŋa a lɔnsi nyiamu po ale weeni ayen, <<Nya kude ate Naawen a weeni ayen, <M tebi nyiamu de kama. Bu a kan ŋman ta kum a jam yaase tɛŋka a kan ta jaaboa.> >> 22Ate nyiamu a kasim nala a jam paari jinla a ta va chaab ale Ɛlaisa ale jam weeni diila.
23A nyini dula Ɛlaisa a jam cheŋ jueli ka Betel. Ase wa ale jam va suiku a cheŋ la, bi paaluk ale jam nyini tɛŋka po a cheŋ wa jigi a weeni wa ayen, <<Fi zuk kpaauŋku nyɔnɔ, cheŋ nwuli, fi zuk kpaauŋku nyɔnɔ, cheŋ nwuli.>> 24Wa jam viriŋ kama a nya a yaa ka basi ba zuk Naawen yuenni nyiŋ. Ate gɔi baasa siye a jam nyini tiisaŋa po a yik bi paalukku pisinaansi ale baye a dari ba ŋasi. 25Ate wa yaa jam cheŋ Karmel guuku zuk, a zaani dula a ŋman cheŋ Samaria.

english_text:
King Joram of Israel
1Joram son of Ahab became king of Israel in Jehoshaphat's eighteenth year as king of Judah. Joram ruled twelve years from Samaria 2and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He tore down the stone image his father had made to honor Baal, and so he wasn't as sinful as his parents. 3But he kept doing the sinful things that Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel to do.
The Country of Moab Rebels against Israel
4For many years the country of Moab had been controlled by Israel and was forced to pay taxes to the kings of Israel. King Mesha of Moab raised sheep, so he paid the king of Israel 100,000 lambs and the wool from 100,000 rams. 5But soon after the death of Ahab, Mesha rebelled against Israel.
6One day, Joram left Samaria and called together Israel's army. 7He sent this message to King Jehoshaphat of Judah, “The king of Moab has rebelled. Will you go with me to attack him?”
“Yes, I will,” Jehoshaphat answered. “I'm on your side, and my soldiers and horses are at your command. 8But which way should we go?”
“We will march through Edom Desert,” Joram replied.
9So Joram, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom led their troops out. But seven days later, there was no drinking water left for them or their animals. 10Joram cried out, “This is terrible! The Lord must have led us out here to be captured by Moab's army.”
11Jehoshaphat said, “Which of the Lord's prophets is with us? We can find out from him what the Lord wants us to do.”
One of Joram's officers answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He was one of Elijah's closest followers.”
12Jehoshaphat replied, “He can give us the Lord's message.”
The three kings went over to Elisha, 13and he asked Joram, “Why did you come to me? Go talk to the prophets of the foreign gods your parents worshiped.”
“No,” Joram answered. “It was the Lord who led us out here, so that Moab's army could capture us.”
14Elisha said to him, “I serve the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as he lives, I swear I wouldn't even look at you if I didn't respect King Jehoshaphat.” 15Then Elisha said, “Send for someone who can play the harp.”
The harpist began playing, and the Lord gave Elisha this message for Joram:
16The Lord says that this dry riverbed will be filled with water. 17You won't feel any wind or see any rain, but there will be plenty of water for you and your animals.
18That simple thing isn't all the Lord is going to do. He will also help you defeat Moab's army. 19You will capture all their walled cities and important towns. You will chop down every good tree and stop up every spring of water, then ruin their fertile fields by covering them with rocks.
20The next morning, while the sacrifice was being offered, water suddenly started flowing from the direction of Edom, and it flooded the land.
21Meanwhile, the people of Moab had heard that the three kings were coming to attack them. They had called together all of their fighting men, from the youngest to the oldest, and these troops were now standing at their border, ready for battle. 22When they got up that morning, the sun was shining across the water, making it look red. The Moabite troops took one look 23and shouted, “Look at that blood! The armies of those kings must have fought and killed each other. Come on, let's go take what's left in their camp.”
24But when they arrived at Israel's camp, the Israelite soldiers came out and attacked them, until they turned and ran away. Israel's army chased them all the way back to Moab, and even there they kept up the attack. 25The Israelites destroyed the Moabite towns. They chopped down the good trees and stopped up the springs of water, then covered the fertile fields with rocks.
Finally, the only city left standing was Kir-Hareseth, but soldiers armed with slings surrounded and attacked it. 26King Mesha of Moab saw that he was about to be defeated. So he took along 700 soldiers with swords and tried to break through the front line where the Edomite troops were positioned. But he failed. 27He then grabbed his oldest son who was to be the next king and sacrificed him as an offering on the city wall. The Israelite troops were so horrified that they left the city and went back home.
translation_text:
1Jeyoram ale ka Ayab nidoabili la, a jam chim ka Izirali naab a bo Samaria po diipo ate Jeyosafat a jam chim naab a bo Juda a paari bena pi ale naaniŋ po la. Joram abe jam kali naamu zuk a paari ka bena pi ale ŋaye. 2Wa jam nye ka biem Naawen niŋ, alege wa an jam nye a paari wa kowa ale wa mawa ale jam nye diila. Baal tintain ferini ate wa kowa a jam nye la, wa jam kpiti ŋa a basi kama. 3Alege wa jam bo ka Nebat nidoabinni Jeroboam wabaataŋa po, ate wa jam te Izirali a nye. Wa an jam pai ŋa a basi ya.
4Yɔgyɔgla de Mesa ale ka Moab naab la a jam wuuk ka piisa, ate wa magsi ayen wa te Izirali naawa pabisa tusa kook (100,000) ale padaasa tusa kook (100,000) kɔbta. 5Alege Ayab ale jam kpi la ŋaaŋnyiŋ Moab naawa a jam ta ka chaab ale Izirali naawa. 6Dila va ŋala po naab Jeyoram a jam gomsi kama a nyini Samaria ale ta Izirali meena a jam jigi yeŋ. 7Wa jam weeni ka wari a te Jeyosafat ale ka Juda naab la ayen, <<Moab naawa a ta ka chaab ale mu, fi ale cheŋ ale mu ate ti kpaliŋ ale Moab? Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<M le cheŋ, mi a nye ase ka fi la, m nuruma ase fi nuruma la, m wusumaŋa ase fi wusumaŋa la.
8Jeyoram yaa bek wa ayen, <<Ti ale va ka suik boan po a siti ba?>> Ate wa tulisi ayen, <<Ti ale va ka Edom gɔnni po.>>
9Dila Izirali naawa ale Juda naawa ale Edom naawa a yaa nyini. Ba ale gɔk santiri a gilim a paari daa ŋayopɔi la, tugurik tɔŋdɔma a ŋman ka nyiam a nyu ba dega yaase ba duŋsaŋa a nyu.
10Izirali naawa yaa na ayen, <<Boa! Naawen a wi tama nalima ŋatawa a ta ti a jam jigi yeŋ ayen wa pai ti a te ka Moab yaa?>> 11Alege Jeyosafat a jam bek ayen, <<Naawen biisiteerɔ a ka dela ayen ti va wa zuk a miŋ ku kiri a nyini Naawen jigi ya?>> Izirali naawa kpagi yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ɛlaisa ale ka Safat nidoabili la a bo dela. Wa jam ka Elaja tomteerɔ.>>
12Jeyosafat yaa jam weeni ayen, <<Naawen wanni a bo ale wa kama.>> Ate Izirali naawa ale Jeyosafat ale Edom naawa a yaa jam cheŋ wa jigi.
13Ɛlaisa yaa jam weeni Izirali naawa ayen, <<Tama ale nye tidek ka sɛ? Cheŋ fi kowa biisiteerɔma ale fi mawa biisiteerɔma jigi.>> Izirali naawa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Aaya, dii nyiŋla ka Naawen ale wi tama nalima ŋatawa ayen wa pai ti a nyo Moab nisa po.>>
14Ɛlaisa yaa jam weeni ayen, <<Ase Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale vua la, waai ate mi tom a te la, ase mi a dan kan ta zula a te Jeyosafat ale ka Juda naab la, m ti kan zak a nya fu yaase m poom miŋ fu. 15Alege ni ta waai ale a nak kpanuŋ la a jam te mu.>> Ase kpanuŋ nagrɔwa ale jam boro a nak la, ate Naawen nisa a yaa jam Ɛlaisa zuk, 16ate wa weeni ayen, <<Naawen ale a weeni diila ale nna, ayen ni tu gola woŋta a sueri viaka po. 17Dii ate Naawen a weeni la ale nna ayen, fi a kan nya viok yaase ŋmoruwa, alege viaka de ale sueri ale nyiam, ate fi ale fi niiga ale fi duŋ yonsaŋa ale nyu nyiam. 18Nya kude ka moali Naawen nina po. Wa ale pai Moab a nyo ni nisa po. 19Ni ale nya pagrim tɛŋ pagrik ale tɛŋ kpieŋ meena zuk. Ni ale che tiib maŋsa meena a lɔnsi tɛŋ, abe ni si bulisa meena, abe ni pai tana a kaasi tɛŋ maŋsaŋa meena.>>
20Vanni ale veenti la, a moata diipo ate ba a nye kaabka la, nyiam ale jam nyini Edom tɛŋka geŋsaŋa a jam sueri tɛŋka!
21Yɔgyɔgla de Moab demma a jam wom kama ayen nalimaŋa a jam kama ayen ba nye kpaliŋ ale ba. Ate nuru meena, bi paalukku ale ŋankpagsa ale baga a yik kpaliŋ kɔlima la, ba jam wi ba kama a ta ba ga zaani tɛŋka banni. 22Ba ale jam yiti saluik yokyokku la, wenbinni a jam a nyaksi nyiamu zuk kama. Moab demma ale jam gaam suiku a za la jigi, ku jam muni ka nna gbaŋgbaŋ ase ziim la. 23Ba yaa weeni ayen, <<Ziim ale la. Da dii dai nalim ŋala a nye ka kpaliŋ a tɔgri chaab. Yɔgyɔgla de ka Moab ale ba kɔlim ba ŋantaŋa.>>
24Alege Moab demma ale jam cheŋ Izirali bo ka jigini la, Izirali demma a yiti kama a kpaliŋ ale ba ate ba chali be. Ate Izirali demma a fɛ jo tɛŋka po a yik Moab demma a tɔgri. 25Ba jam kaasi tɛŋsaŋa kama, ate nuru meena a yuk tana a basi tɛŋ maŋ meena zuk ate tanaŋa a ga lik ka. Ba jam si bulisaŋa meena kama ale che tiib maŋ meena a lɔnsi. Ka Kir Yareset nyiini ale jam tali ate ka tanaŋa a doa si jigini, alege nuruba ale jam ta visiŋsa a gilim ka ale siti ka mɛ.
26Moab naawa ale jam nya ayen kpaliŋka a baga wa la, wa jam pai ka nuru baai ale ta gebik woŋsa la kobsiyopɔi ayen ba nya nakdeka Edom naawa zuk alege ba jam nye kpeeri kama. 27Ate wa pai bi kaai ate wa dɛ niŋ a biak la, waai ate wa dan kan boro wa tagri wa zuk a chim naab la, a nye kaabka tɛŋka parika zuk. Ba sueŋa a jam a puuri ale Izirali ka nna yegayega. Izirali demma yaa jam pai basi ale ŋman cheŋ badek tɛŋka po.

english_text:
Elisha Helps a Poor Widow
1One day the widow of one of the Lord's prophets said to Elisha, “You know that before my husband died, he was a follower of yours and a worshiper of the Lord. But he owed a man some money, and now that man is on his way to take my two sons as his slaves.”
2“Maybe there's something I can do to help,” Elisha said. “What do you have in your house?”
“Sir, I have nothing but a small bottle of olive oil.”
3Elisha told her, “Ask your neighbors for their empty jars. And after you've borrowed as many as you can, 4go home and shut the door behind you and your sons. Then begin filling the jars with oil and set each one aside as you fill it.” 5The woman left.
Later, when she and her sons were back inside their house, the two sons brought her the jars, and she began filling them.
6At last, she said to one of her sons, “Bring me another jar.”
“We don't have any more,” he answered, and the oil stopped flowing from the small bottle.
7After she told Elisha what had happened, he said, “Sell the oil and use part of the money to pay what you owe the man. You and your sons can live on what is left.”
Elisha Brings a Rich Woman's Son Back to Life
8Once, while Elisha was in the town of Shunem, he met a rich woman who invited him to her home for dinner. After that, whenever he was in Shunem, he would have a meal there with her and her husband.
9Some time later the woman said to her husband, “I'm sure the man who comes here so often is a prophet of God. 10Why don't we build him a small room on the flat roof of our house? We can put a bed, a table and chair, and an oil lamp in it. Then whenever he comes, he can stay with us.”
11The next time Elisha was in Shunem, he stopped at their house and went up to his room to rest. 12-13He said to his servant Gehazi, “This woman has been very helpful. Have her come up here to the roof for a moment.” She came, and Elisha told Gehazi to say to her, “You've gone to a lot of trouble for us, and we want to help you. Is there something we can request the king or army commander to do?”
The woman answered, “With my relatives nearby, I have everything I need.”
14“Then what can we do for her?” Elisha asked Gehazi.
Gehazi replied, “I do know that her husband is old, and that she doesn't have a son.”
15“Ask her to come here again,” Elisha told his servant. He called for her, and she came and stood in the doorway of Elisha's room.
16 Elisha said to her, “Next year at this time, you'll be holding your own baby son in your arms.”
“You're a man of God,” the woman replied. “Please don't lie to me.”
17But a few months later, the woman got pregnant. She gave birth to a son, just as Elisha had promised.
18One day while the boy was still young, he was out in the fields with his father, where the workers were harvesting the crops. 19Suddenly he shouted, “My head hurts. It hurts a lot!”
“Carry him back to his mother,” the father said to his servant. 20The servant picked up the boy and carried him to his mother. The boy lay on her lap all morning, and by noon he was dead. 21She carried him upstairs to Elisha's room and laid him across the bed. Then she walked out and shut the door behind her.
22The woman called to her husband, “I need to see the prophet. Let me use one of the donkeys. Send a servant along with me, and let me leave now, so I can get back quickly.”
23“Why do you need to see him today?” her husband asked. “It's not the Sabbath or time for the New Moon Festival.”
“That's all right,” she answered. 24She saddled the donkey and said to her servant, “Let's go. And don't slow down unless I tell you to.” 25She left at once for Mount Carmel to talk with Elisha.
When Elisha saw her coming, he said, “Gehazi, look! It's the woman from Shunem. 26Run and meet her. And ask her if everything is all right with her and her family.”
“Everything is fine,” she answered Gehazi. 27But as soon as she got to the top of the mountain, she went over and grabbed Elisha by the feet.
Gehazi started toward her to push her away, when Elisha said, “Leave her alone! Don't you see how sad she is? But the Lord hasn't told me why.”
28The woman said, “Sir, I begged you not to get my hopes up, and I didn't even ask you for a son.”
29“Gehazi, get ready and go to her house,” Elisha said. “Take along my walking stick, and when you get there, lay it on the boy's face. Don't stop to talk to anyone, even if they try to talk to you.”
30But the boy's mother said to Elisha, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I won't leave without you.” So Elisha got up and went with them.
31Gehazi ran on ahead and laid Elisha's walking stick on the boy's face, but the boy didn't move or make a sound. Gehazi ran back to Elisha and said, “The boy didn't wake up.”
32Elisha arrived at the woman's house and went straight to his room, where he saw the boy's body on his bed. 33He walked in, shut the door, and prayed to the Lord. 34 Then he got on the bed and stretched out over the dead body, with his mouth on the boy's mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hand on his hands. As he lay there, the boy's body became warm. 35Elisha got up and walked back and forth in the room, then he went back and leaned over the boy's body. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
36Elisha called out to Gehazi, “Ask the boy's mother to come here.” Gehazi did, and when she was at the door, Elisha said, “You can take your son.”
37She came in and bowed down at Elisha's feet. Then she picked up her son and left.
Elisha Makes Some Stew Taste Better
38Later, Elisha went back to Gilgal, where there was almost nothing to eat, because the crops had failed.
One day while the prophets who lived there were meeting with Elisha, he said to his servant, “Prepare a big pot of stew for these prophets.”
39One of them went out into the woods to gather some herbs. He found a wild vine and picked as much of its fruit as he could carry, but he didn't know that the fruit was very sour. When he got back, he cut up the fruit and put it in the stew.
40The stew was served, and when the prophets started eating it, they shouted, “Elisha, this stew tastes terrible! We can't eat it.”
41“Bring me some flour,” Elisha said. He sprinkled the flour in the stew and said, “Now serve it to them.” And the stew tasted fine.
Elisha Feeds One Hundred People
42A man from the town of Baal-Shalishah brought Elisha some freshly cut grain and 20 loaves of bread made from the first barley that was harvested. Elisha said, “Give it to the people so they can eat.”
43“There's not enough here for 100 people,” his servant said.
“Just give it to them,” Elisha replied. “The Lord has promised there will be more than enough.”
44So the servant served the bread and grain to the people. They ate and still had some left over, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_text:
1Nuru wanyi ale jam maa bo Wen biisiteerɔma tigsuŋku po la pok yaa jam kum sak Ɛlaisa ayen, <<Fi tomteerɔwa m chorɔwa a kpi kama, fi abe seba kama ayen wa jam a zuli Naawen kama. Alege wa ale ta waai pami la a cheen kama ayen wa pai m nidoabilisa bayewa ase yɔm la.>> 2Ɛlaisa yaa tulisi wa ayen, << M nye se a maari fu? Weeni a sak mu, ka boa ate fi ta bo fi yenni po?>> Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Fi tomteerɔwa a ka jaaboa, ka kpaam nna maga.>>
3Ɛlaisa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Cheŋ fi ale moata baai la a weeni ba ate ba te fu samɔn koruta. Kan tuesi maga. 4Fi yaa jo dɔkku po a lik fidek ale fi nidoabilisaŋa du, boori kpaamu a nyo samɔnsaŋa meena po, ate kanyi meena a dan ga sueri pai zaani nakpiak.>>
5Wa yaa jam cheŋ ga jo dɔkku po lik wa tuoku ale wa nidoabilisaŋa. Ba jam ta samɔnsaŋa kama a ga te wa ate wa kasim jam a kpiiri kpaamu. 6Samɔnsaŋa meena ale jam sueri la, wa yaa weeni wa nidoabinni ayen, <<Ta ka choa a jam te mu.>> Alege wa tulisi wa kama ayen, <<Samɔniŋ an tali ya.>> Ate kpaamu yaa gebiri.
7Wa yaa cheŋ ga weeni sak Wen nuruwa ate wa weeni wa ayen, <<Cheŋ ga pai kpaamu a da tuni fi pamaŋa. Dii ale tali la, fi ale fi nidoabilisaŋa abe pai a dɛ.>>
8Dai yeŋ ate Ɛlaisa a jam cheŋ Sunem. Ate nipok waai ale jigsi la jam bo dula. Nipowa yaa weeni Ɛlaisa ayen wa te ate wa te wa ŋandiinta. Ate diipo meena ate wa a va dula la, wa nyiem zaani dula kama a dɛ. 9Wa yaa weeni sak wa chorɔwa ayen, <<Mi seba kama ayen nuru waai ale kasim a jam ti jigi la ka Wen nuru weleŋ. 10Basi ate ti nye dɔk fiik ti yenni zuk a pai gaduok ale jazaanim ale zukpaglik ale zeuŋ a te wa. Ate wa dan jam ti jigi diipo meena wa bo dula.>>
11Dai yeŋ ate Ɛlaisa a jam, wa yaa cheŋ wa dɔkku po a ga duak dula. 12Wa yaa weeni wa tomteerɔwa Geyazi ayen, <<Wi Sunem denɔwa a te mu. Ate wa ga wi wa ate wa jam zaani wa niŋ. 13Ɛlaisa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Weeni wa ayen, <Fi jo ninammu de po meena a te ka tama. Yɔgyɔgla de ti le nye ka boa a te fu? Ti weeni naawa yaase tugurik tɔŋdɔma ate wa maari fu?> >> Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<M bo ale ka m nuruma.>>
14Ɛlaisa yaa bek ayen, <<Te le nye ka boa a te wa?>> Geyazi yaa weeni ayen, <<Wa ka nidoabili ya. Wa chorɔwa mɛ a kpaŋ kama.>>
