15Ɛlaisa yaa weeni ayen, <<Wi wa.>> Ate wa wi wa, ate wa jam zaani nansuiŋku nɔi. 16Ɛlaisa weeni ayen, <<Bali nna po de, fi ale ta nidoabili fi nisa po.>> Wa yaa zɛri wa ale weeni wa diila ale ayen, <<Aaya, m nyɔnɔ, kan paasi fi tomteerɔwa, Wen nuroa.>>
17Alege nipowa a jam yik lɔgi kama ate ben dii ale paasaŋ la dila po dek wa biak nidoabili ase Ɛlaisa ale jam weeni la.
18Nidoabinni yaa chim, ate dai yeŋ wa yaa cheŋ wa kowa jigi, juijui ate nuruba a boro a pisi ŋan baai ate ba kpa la. 19Wa yaa weeni wa kowa ayen, <<M zuk! M zuk!>> Wa kowa yaa weeni wa tomteerɔma wanyi ayen, <<Pai wa ga te wa mawa.>> 20Tomteerɔwa ale ta wa a ga te wa mawa la nidoabinni yaa kali wa mawa naŋsa zuk a ga paari kantueŋ, ate wa yaa kpi. 21Wa yaa ta wa cheŋ ga dueni Wen nuruwa gaduokku zuk, a yaa kpari tuoku ale cheŋ nyini.
22Wa yaa wi wa chorɔwa ayen, <<Mi a saalim ayen fi te ate fi tomteerɔma wanyi ta boniŋ a jam te mu ate m cheŋ Wen nuruwa jigi nwuli abe m ŋman jam.>> 23Wa yaa bek wa ayen, <<Ka boan wari ate fi a cheŋ wa jigi jinla? Ku daa Chiik Paalik yaase Vuusum Dai ya. Wa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Jaab meena a magsi kama.>>
24Wa yaa gomsi bonika ale weeni wa tomteerɔwa ayen, <<De niŋ. Kan a cheŋ maga maga ka mi nin weeni fu.>> 25Ate wa yaa jam cheŋ paari Karmel Guuku juijui ate Wen nuruwa a boro la. Wa ale jam zaani niŋ a nya wa la, Wen nuruwa yaa weeni wa tomteerɔwa Geyazi ayen, <<Nya, Sunem denɔwa ale nna. 26Chali a ga tu wa abe fi bek wa ayen, <Nalim a bo ni meena jigi ya? Nalim a bo fi chorɔwa jigi ya? Nalim a bo fi nidoabinni jigi ya?> >> Sunem denɔwa yaa weeni ayen, <<Nalim a bo waai meena jigi kama.>>
27Wa ale ga paari Wen nuruwa guuku zuk la, wa yaa yik wa naŋsaŋa a tara Geyazi yaa nyini ayen wa tusi wa a basi, alege Wen nuruwa a weeni wa ayen, <<Basi wa. Wa sui ale kaasi, alege Naawen a pai suk mi kama ale an weeni wari a sak mi.>>
28Wa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<M nyɔnɔ, mi weeni fu ayen mi a yaali nidoabili ya? Mi weeni fu ayen, kan basi ate m ta yiila.>>
29Ɛlaisa yaa weeni Geyazi ayen, <<Yik fi garukku a basi fi chiak gbainni po, abe fi pai m dachekka a nyo fi nisa po a chali. Fi dan zik waai suiku po, kan puusi wa, waai abe dan puusi fu, kan tulisi wa. Pai m dachekka a vi nidoabinni ninaŋa zuk.>>
30Alege biika mawa a weeni ayen, <<Ase Naawen ale vua la, ate fi mɛ a vua la, m kan basi fu.>> Ate wa jam yiti a va wa a cheŋ.
31Geyazi a jam de ka niŋ a ga pai dachekka a vi biika ninaŋa zuk, alege chiok a kan choa yaase wa poom tulisi. Ate Geyazi a pilim ŋmani a ga tu Ɛlaisa suik a weeni sak wa ayen, <<Nidoabinni an yiti ya.>>
32Ɛlaisa ale ga paari yenni la, wa nya ka biika ale kpi doa wa gaduokku zuk. 33Wa yaa cheŋ jo ale kpari tuoku ate ba nɔi bayewa nyiini a boro, ate Ɛlaisa puusi te Naawen. 34Ate wa yaa jueli gaduokku zuk a yaa duak biika zuk, a pai wa nɔnni a tuk wa nɔnni, ale pai wa ninaŋa a tuk wa ninaŋa ale pai wa nisaŋa a yik wa nisaŋa. Ase wa ale jam neenti a basi wa nyiŋla, biika nyiŋka yaa tuila. 35Ɛlaisa yaa viriŋ a cheŋ ŋaaŋnyiŋ ale niŋ nyiŋ dɔkku po ale ŋman jueli gaduokku zuk a neenti a ŋman basi wa nyiŋ. Biika yaa chesim buyopɔi ale lak wa nina.
36Ɛlaisa yaa weeni Geyazi ayen, <<Wi Sunem denɔwa. >> Ate wa ga wi wa. Wa ale jam la, wa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Pai fi biika.>> 37Wa yaa cheŋ jo, a yaa lo wa naŋsa tɛŋ a yaa koori tɛŋ. Wa yaa jam pai wa biika ta cheŋ nyini peelim.
38Ɛlaisa yaa ŋmani cheŋ Gilgal ate kom a jam bo tɛŋ kala po. Wen biisiteerɔma ale jam tigsi a boro a tu wa la, wa yaa weeni wa tomteerɔwa ayen, <<Pai samɔn kpieŋ a dik jenta a te nuruma de.>>
39Ba wanyi yaa cheŋ tattaŋa po ayen wa yaali jenvaata, ate wa yaa nya tiib ale zuak. Wa yaa yaali bu yɔnaŋa a sueri wa garukku po. Wa ale jam paari la, wa yaa gebi ŋa a nyo jenta samɔniŋka po. Waai mɛ a poom zɛ ba ale ka ŋan baai la. 40Ba jam nye jentaŋa kama a te nuruma, alege ba ale jam boro ayen ba dɛ la, ba kaari ayen, <<Wen nuroa, kum ale bo samɔniŋka po.>> Ate ba an jam baga a dɛ ya.
41Ɛlaisa yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni ta zom a jam.>> Wa yaa pai nyo samɔniŋ po ale weeni ayen, <<Ni nye a te nuruma ate ba dɛ.>> Ate jaab a jam ka samɔniŋka po a daani.
42Nuru ale jam nyini Baal Salisaya a ta barli ŋanbie ŋaai ale dɛ niŋ a muni la a nye borobotta pisiye ale ŋandiin paala nna tɔgatɔga a ta jam te Wen nuruwa. Ɛlaisa yaa weeni ayen, <<Pai te nuruma ate ba dɛ.>>
43Wa tomteerɔwa yaa bek ayen, <<Mi ale nye ka sɛ ate nya kude a paari nuruba kookwa?>> Alege Ɛlaisa a tulisi ayen, <<Pai te nuruma ate ba dɛ. Diila Naawen ale a weeni diila ale nna, <Ba ale de abe ba tali ŋa gela a zaani.> >> 44Ate wa nye te ba ate ba dɛ ale tali ŋa gela a zaani, a magsi chaab ale Naawen wanni ale weeni diila.

english_text:
Elisha Heals Naaman
1 Naaman was the commander of the Syrian army. The Lord had helped him and his troops defeat their enemies, so the king of Syria respected Naaman very much. Naaman was a brave soldier, but he had leprosy.
2One day while the Syrian troops were raiding Israel, they captured a girl, and she became a servant of Naaman's wife. 3Some time later the girl said, “If your husband Naaman would go to the prophet in Samaria, he would be cured of his leprosy.”
4When Naaman told the king what the girl had said, 5the king replied, “Go ahead! I will give you a letter to take to the king of Israel.”
Naaman left and took along 30,000 pieces of silver, 6,000 pieces of gold, and 10 new outfits. 6He also carried the letter to the king of Israel. It said, “I am sending my servant Naaman to you. Would you cure him of his leprosy?”
7When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes in fear and shouted, “That Syrian king believes I can cure this man of leprosy! Does he think I'm God with power over life and death? He must be trying to pick a fight with me.”
8As soon as Elisha the prophet heard what had happened, he sent the Israelite king this message: “Why are you so afraid? Send the man to me, so that he will know there is a prophet in Israel.”
9Naaman left with his horses and chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house. 10Elisha sent someone outside to say to him, “Go wash seven times in the Jordan River. Then you'll be completely cured.”
11But Naaman stormed off, grumbling, “Why couldn't he come out and talk to me? I thought for sure he would stand in front of me and pray to the Lord his God, then wave his hand over my skin and cure me. 12What about the Abana River or the Pharpar River? Those rivers in Damascus are just as good as any river in Israel. I could have washed in them and been cured.”
13His servants went over to him and said, “Sir, if the prophet had told you to do something difficult, you would have done it. So why don't you do what he said? Go wash and be cured.”
14Naaman walked down to the Jordan; he waded out into the water and stooped down in it seven times, just as Elisha had told him. At once, he was cured, and his skin became as smooth as a child's.
15Naaman and his officials went back to Elisha. Naaman stood in front of him and announced, “Now I know that the God of Israel is the only God in the whole world. Sir, would you please accept a gift from me?”
16“I am a servant of the living Lord,” Elisha answered, “and I swear that I will not take anything from you.”
Naaman kept begging, but Elisha kept refusing. 17Finally Naaman said, “If you won't accept a gift, then please let me take home as much soil as two mules can pull in a wagon. Sir, from now on I will offer sacrifices only to the Lord. 18But I pray that the Lord will forgive me when I go into the temple of the god Rimmon and bow down there with the king of Syria.”
19“Go on home, and don't worry about that,” Elisha replied. Then Naaman left.
Elisha Places a Curse on Gehazi
After Naaman had gone only a short distance, 20Gehazi said to himself, “Elisha let that Syrian off too easy. He should have taken Naaman's gift. I swear by the living Lord that I will talk to Naaman myself and get something from him.” 21So he hurried after Naaman.
When Naaman saw Gehazi running after him, he got out of his chariot to meet him. Naaman asked, “Is everything all right?”
22“Yes,” Gehazi answered. “But my master has sent me to tell you about two young prophets from the hills of Ephraim. They came asking for help, and now Elisha wants to know if you would give them 3,000 pieces of silver and some new clothes?”
23“Sure,” Naaman replied. “But why don't you take twice that amount of silver?” He convinced Gehazi to take it all, then put the silver in two bags. He handed the bags and the clothes to his two servants, and they carried them for Gehazi.
24When they reached the hill where Gehazi lived, he took the bags from the servants and placed them in his house, then sent the men away. After they had gone, 25Gehazi went in and stood in front of Elisha, who asked, “Gehazi, where have you been?”
“Nowhere, sir,” Gehazi answered.
26Elisha asked, “Don't you know that my spirit was there when Naaman got out of his chariot to talk with you? Gehazi, you have no right to accept money or clothes, olive orchards or vineyards, sheep or cattle, or servants. 27Because of what you've done, Naaman's leprosy will now be on you and your descendants forever!”
Suddenly, Gehazi's skin became white with leprosy, and he left.
translation_text:
1Yɔgyɔgla de Naaman a jam ka Araam naawa tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagi. Wa jam ka nuru kpioŋ wa kpagni nina po ate ba a te wa zula nna yegayega. Wa nyiŋ ate Naawen a pai nakdeka a te Araam. Wa jam ka tugurik tɔŋdɔ, a ta suinum pagrik, alege wa jam ka gami.
2Yɔgyɔgla de nuruba ale jam nyini Araam a cheŋ ga yik nipokbili a nyini Izirali a jam ate wa boro a tom a te Naaman powa. 3Wa weeni wa mawa ayen, <<Ase m kowa a dan baga ga a nya Wen biisiteerɔ waai ale bo Samaria la. Wa ale tebi wa gama tuemu.>>
4Naaman yaa cheŋ wa kpagni jigi a ga weeni wa nipokbinni ale weeni diila. 5Araam naawa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ku nala kama be cheŋ, m le te gbaŋ ate ka cheŋ Izirali naawa jigi.>> Ate Naaman yaa jam pai kpana boorik dobrim pi ale ligmɔniŋ ligbie dobrim tusa ŋayuebi (6,000) ale gatta joka pi a yaa cheŋ. 6Gbaŋka ate wa jam ŋmarisi ayen wa ta ga te naawa la a jam a weeni kama ayen, <<M va ka gbaŋka de zuk a tom m tomteerɔwa Naaman fi jigi ayen, fi tebi wa gama tuemu.>>
7Izirali naawa ale ga karim gbaŋka la, wa yaa dari wa garuk woŋku a cheeri ale sui kaasuŋ weeni ayen, <<Mi ka Wen yaa? Mi baga a ko a ŋman baga ta nyuvuri a jamu? Ka boan nyiŋ ate nuru wade a tom a waai m jigi ayen m tebi wa gama tuemoa? Nya wa ale a nye ayen wa nye tugurik ale mu la.>>
8Wen nuruwa Ɛlaisa ale jam wom ayen Izirali naawa a dari wa garuk woŋku a cheeri ale sui kaasuŋ la, wa yaa tom ayen ba ga weeni wa ayen, <<Ka boan nyiŋ ate fi dari fi garuk woŋku a cheeri? Te ate nuruwa a jam mi jigi ate wa ale seba ayen Wen biisiteerɔ a bo Izirali.>> 9Ate Naaman a jam cheŋ ale wa wusumaŋa ale torokoma a ga zaani Ɛlaisa yenni tuoku nɔi. 10Ɛlaisa yaa tom nuru ayen wa ga weeni wa ayen, <<Cheŋ ga so fidek naŋtuok nɔi buyopɔi Jodan benni po, ate fi nyiŋka ale ŋman nye ka denni ate fi nala.
11Alege Naaman jam basi wa kama ale suipuurum ale weeni ayen, <<Mi poli kama ayen wa le nyini ka peelim a tu mu a zaani a wi Naawen dii ale ka wa Wen la yuenni, abe wa pai wa nisa a vi m niraŋa zuk a tebi m gama tuemu. 12Abana ale Farpar belaŋa an bo daa Damasikus? Belaŋa de an zunchoŋ Izirali belaŋa? Mi ate m poom so m dek ka dula a nala.>> Dila wa viriŋ a cheŋ ale suipuurum.
13Naaman tomteerɔma yaa ga weeni wa ayen, <<M koa, ase Wen biisiteerɔwa a dan weeni fu kama ayen fi nye wari a gaam dila, fi kan nye? Kude yaa be ka boan wari ase wa le weeni fu ayen so fidek ate fi nye cheri.>> 14Wa yaa cheŋ siŋ Jodan benni po a musi du naŋtuok nɔi buyopɔi ase Wen nuruwa ale weeni wa diila, ate wa nyiŋka a ŋman nye ka ale ka diila, a nala nna se nidoabili paalik nyiŋla.
15Ate Naaman ale baai ale va wa la yaa ŋman cheŋ Wen nuruwa jigi. Wa ga zaani ka wa niŋ a weeni wa ayen, <<Yɔgyɔgla de mi yaa seba kama ayen tɛŋka meena ale doa la Wen a ka juijui ya, ka Izirali nyiini. Mi a saalim fu kama yɔgyɔgla de ayen, fi tuesi tiirim a nyini fi tomteerɔwa jigi.>> 16Wen biisiteerɔwa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ase Naawen ale vua la, waai ate mi tom a te la, mi kan siak a tuesi jaaboa.>> Ate Naaman a jam a weeni wa ayen wa tuesi alege wa jam zɛri.
17Naaman yaa weeni ayen, <<Fi be dan kaa siagi, mi a saalim fu ayen basi ate fi tomteerɔwa a vaari tanta ate wusumbonsa siye ale baga a ji la, dii nyiŋla fi tomteerɔwa a kan ŋman nye juka tiirita ale kaabka a te wen yoŋŋoa alege ka Naawen nyiini. 18Alege Naawen abe vɔŋ wari yeŋ a te fi tomteerɔwa. Ase m kpagni a dan jo Arimmon puusika yenni po a koori tɛŋ ale sali m nisa ate mi mɛ a koori tɛŋ. Ase m dan koori tɛŋ a bo Arimmon puusika yenni po, Naawen abe vɔŋ te fi tomteerɔwa nya kude nyiŋ.>>
19Ɛlaisa yaa weeni ayen, <<Cheŋ ale suiyɔgni.>> Naaman ale jam cheŋ niŋ maga dek la, 20Wen nuruwa Ɛlaisa tomteerɔwa Geyazi, yaa weeni wadek ayen, <<M kpagni a nye wadek ka nna moali a te Naaman, Araam denɔwa de, wa ale kan siak tuesi ŋan baai ate wa ta jam la. Ase Naawen ale vua la, m le chali vi wa a tuesi jaab a nyini wa jigi.>>
21Dila Geyazi a nye nwuli a vi Naaman. Naaman ale nya ale wa a vi wa la, wa yaa nyini wa wusummu torokowa zuk a siŋ a tu wa. A bek wa ayen, <<Jaab meena a cheŋ nalimnyiini?>> 22Geyazi yaa tulisi ayen, <<Jaab meena a cheŋ ka nalimnyiini. M kpagni ale tom ayen m weeni fu ayen, Wen biisiteerɔma tigsuŋku nuruba baye ale nyini Ɛfraim tɛŋka guuku zuk a jam m jigi. Mi a saalim fu ayen fi te ba kpana boorik dobrim ale gatta joka buye.>>
23Naaman yaa weeni ayen, <<Ku nala kama pai kpana boorik dobrim buye.>> Wa jam weeni Geyazi ayen wa tuesi ale pai boorisa siye a bobi kpana boorik dobrim buyewa ale gatta joka buyewa a pai te wa tomteerɔma baye ate ba de Geyazi niŋ a ji ate ba cheŋ. 24Ase Geyazi ale ga paari guuku zuk la, wa yaa tuesi ŋantaŋa a nyini tomteerɔma jigi a pai ŋa a dueni yenni po. Wa yaa basi nuruma ate ba cheŋ. 25Wa yaa cheŋ ga zaani wa kpagni Ɛlaisa niŋ. Ɛlaisa yaa bek wa ayen, <<Geyazi, fi cheŋ ka bɛ? Geyazi yaa tulisi ayen, <<Fi tomteerɔwa an cheŋ jigi ya.>>
26Alege Ɛlaisa a jam weeni wa ayen, <<Mi chiika an bo ale fu kama diipo ate nuruwa a nyini wa wusum torokowa zuk a siŋ tɛŋ a tu fi la? Ka nna po de ale magsi ligra tuesika, yaase gatta tuesika ale tiisa ale si yɔna ale laŋsa ale piisa ale duŋsa yaase nidoa tomteerɔba ale nipok tomteerɔba tuesika? 27Naaman gama tuemu ale siŋ fi ale fi ŋaaŋsaŋa nyiŋ taam wuu.>> Ate Geyazi a basi Ɛlaisa ale bo juijui la ate wa chim gami a peenti nna tektek.

english_text:
Elisha Makes an Ax Head Float
1One day the prophets said to Elisha, “The place where we meet with you is too small. 2Why don't we build a new meeting place near the Jordan River? Each of us could get some wood, then we could build it.”
“That's a good idea,” Elisha replied, “get started.”
3“Aren't you going with us?” one of the prophets asked.
“Yes, I'll go,” Elisha answered, 4and he left with them.
They went to the Jordan River and began chopping down trees. 5While one of the prophets was working, his ax head fell off and dropped into the water. “Oh!” he shouted. “Sir, I borrowed this ax.”
6“Where did it fall in?” Elisha asked. The prophet pointed to the place, and Elisha cut a stick and threw it into the water at that spot. The ax head floated to the top of the water.
7“Now get it,” Elisha told him. And the prophet reached in and grabbed it.
Elisha Stops an Invasion of the Syrian Army
8Time after time, when the king of Syria was at war against the Israelites, he met with his officers and announced, “I've decided where we will set up camp.”
9Each time, Elisha would send this warning to the king of Israel: “Don't go near there. That's where the Syrian troops have set up camp.” 10So the king would warn the Israelite troops in that place to be on guard.
11The king of Syria was furious when he found out what was happening. He called in his officers and asked, “Which one of you has been telling the king of Israel our plans?”
12“None of us, Your Majesty,” one of them answered. “It's an Israelite named Elisha. He's a prophet, so he can tell his king everything—even what you say in your own room.”
13“Find out where he is!” the king ordered. “I'll send soldiers to bring him here.”
They learned that Elisha was in the town of Dothan and reported it to the king. 14He ordered his best troops to go there with horses and chariots. They marched out during the night and surrounded the town.
15When Elisha's servant got up the next morning, he saw that Syrian troops had the town surrounded. “Sir, what are we going to do?” he asked.
16“Don't be afraid,” Elisha answered. “There are more troops on our side than on theirs.” 17Then he prayed, “Lord, please help him to see.” And the Lord let the servant see that the hill was covered with fiery horses and flaming chariots all around Elisha.
18As the Syrian army came closer, Elisha prayed, “Lord, make those soldiers blind!” And the Lord blinded them with a bright light.
19Elisha told the enemy troops, “You've taken the wrong road and are in the wrong town. Follow me. I'll lead you to the man you're looking for.” Elisha led them straight to the capital city of Samaria.
20When all the soldiers were inside the city, Elisha prayed, “Lord, now let them see again.” The Lord let them see that they were standing in the middle of Samaria.
21The king of Israel saw them and asked Elisha, “Should I kill them, sir?”
22“No!” Elisha answered. “You didn't capture these troops in battle, so you have no right to kill them. Instead, give them something to eat and drink and let them return to their leader.”
23The king ordered a huge meal to be prepared for Syria's army, and when they finished eating, he let them go.
For a while, the Syrian troops stopped invading Israel's territory.
King Benhadad of Syria Attacks Samaria
24Some time later, King Benhadad of Syria called his entire army together, then they marched to Samaria and attacked. 25They kept up the attack until there was nothing to eat in the city. In fact, a donkey's head cost 80 pieces of silver, and a small bowl of pigeon droppings cost 5 pieces of silver.
26One day as the king of Israel was walking along the top of the city wall, a woman shouted to him, “Please, Your Majesty, help me!”
27“Let the Lord help you!” the king said. “Do you think I have grain or wine to give you?” 28Then he asked, “What's the matter anyway?”
The woman answered, “Another woman and I were so hungry that we agreed to eat our sons. She said if we ate my son one day, we could eat hers the next day. 29 So yesterday we cooked my son and ate him. But today when I went to her house to eat her son, she had hidden him.”
30The king tore off his clothes in sorrow, and since he was on top of the city wall, the people saw that he was wearing sackcloth underneath. 31He said, “I pray that God will punish me terribly, if Elisha's head is still on his shoulders by this time tomorrow.” 32Then he sent a messenger to Elisha.
Elisha was home at the time, and the important leaders of Israel were meeting with him. Even before the king's messenger arrived, Elisha told the leaders, “That murderer is sending someone to cut off my head. When you see him coming, shut the door and don't let him in. I'm sure the king himself will be right behind him.”
33Before Elisha finished talking, the messenger came up and said, “The Lord has made all these terrible things happen to us. Why should I think he will help us now?”
translation_text:
1Wen biisiteerɔma tigsuŋku yaa weeni Ɛlaisa ayen, <<Nya, tama ale fi ale a tu juijui la a fiisa kama a te ti. 2Basi ate ti cheŋ Jodan, juijui ate waai meena ale nya laarik. Ate ti baga sɛ a kali dula.>> Ate wa weeni ayen cheŋ.
3Ate ba wanyi yaa weeni ayen, <<Mi a saalim, fi a kan jam ale fi tomteerɔma?>> Ɛlaisa yaa tulisi ayen, <<M le jam.>> 4Ate wa cheŋ ale ba. Ba jam cheŋ ka Jodan a yaa piilim a che tiisa. 5Ase ba wanyi ale jam boro a che tiib ayen wa lɔnsi la, liaka yaa kpeeri lo nyiamu po. Wa yaa kaari ayen, <<M nyɔnɔ, mi piem liaka kama.>>
6Wen nuruwa yaa bek ayen, <<Ka lo ka bɛ? Wa ale jam dak jigini a sak wa la, Ɛlaisa yaa che diok a yuk ku basi dula ate liaka a jueli doa nyiamu zuk. 7Wa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Ga pai.>> Ate nuruwa yaa laari nisa a pai ka.
8Yɔgyɔgla de, Araam naawa a jam ta ka tugurik ale Izirali. Wa ale biisi ale wa kpaŋŋa a nueri la, wa yaa weeni ayen, <<M bo ka jigini ka de ale de.>>
9Wen nuruwa yaa te nɔi ayen ba ga weeni Izirali naawa ayen, <<Ni seba dula jigini nɔi po, dii nyiŋla Araam demma a siŋ tuak ka dula.>> 10Ate Izirali naawa a jam kpesi juijui ate Wen nuruwa a weeni la a paari. Ɛlaisa jam kasim a kaam naawa kama ate wa seba dula jiŋŋa nɔi po a paari.
11Nya kude a jam daani Araam naawa kama. Wa yaa ta wa kpaŋŋa a jam jigi yeŋ a bek nyini ba jigi ayen, <<Ka ni wana ale bo ti po alege bo ale Izirali naawa?>> 12Wa kpaŋŋa wanyi yaa weeni ayen, <<M nyɔnɔ naaba, daa ti waai ya, alege ka Ɛlaisa, Wen biisiteerɔ waai ale bo Izirali la, wa la ale a weeni Izirali naawa wie ŋaai ate fi a weeni fi goomu dɔkku po la.
13Naawa yaa te suik ayen, <<Ni cheŋ ga gisi nya juijui ate wa boro la, ate m tom nuruba ate ba ga yik wa.>> Ba ŋman jam weeni wa kama ayen, <<Wa bo ka Dotan.>> 14Ate wa yaa tom wusuma ale torokoba ale nuru pagrisa dula. Ba jam cheŋ ka yok a ga gilim tɛŋka.
15Wen nuruwa tomteerɔwa ale jam yiti nwuli varivientini la, tugurik tɔŋdɔba ale jam ta wusuma ale torokoba a gilim tɛŋka. Tomteerɔwa yaa bek ayen, <<M nyɔnɔ, ti ale nye ka sɛ?>> 16Wen biisiteerɔwa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Kan chali yɔgsummoa. Baai ale bo ale tama la a zuak gaam baai ale bo ale ba la kama.>>
17Ate Ɛlaisa yaa puusi ayen, <<Naawen yaa, lak wa nina ate wa nya.>> Ate Naawen yaa lak wa tomteerɔwa nina, ate wa nya guutaŋa zuk ale ka wusuma ale torokoba ale bolim ale bo jigini meena a gilim Ɛlaisa. 18Ase dachaasaŋa ale jam siŋ cheena wa jigi la, Ɛlaisa yaa puusi te Naawen ayen, <<Basi ate nuruma de a yi.>> Ate wa basi ate ba yi, ase Ɛlaisa ale jam bek diila.
19Ɛlaisa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Daa suiku ale nya kude, be daa tɛŋka mɛ ale nna. Ni va mu ate m de ni niŋ a ta ni cheŋ nuru waai ate ni a gisi la jigi.>> Ate wa jam ta ba cheŋ Samaria.
20Ba ale jam jo tɛŋka po a nueri la Ɛlaisa yaa weeni ayen, <<Naawen, lak nuruma nina ate ba nya.>> Ate Naawen yaa lak ba ninaŋa ate ba ga nya la ale ba bo ka Samaria po.
21Izirali naawa ale jam nya ba la, wa yaa bek Ɛlaisa ayen, <<M koa, m ko ba? M ko ba?>> 22Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Kan ko ba, fi ale ko nuru baai ate fi yik ba ale fidek gebik woŋ yaase fidek tommu la? Te ba ŋandiinta ate ba dɛ ale nyiam ate ba nyu ate ba ŋman cheŋ ba kpagni jigi.>> 23Ate wa gomsi ŋandiinta tigi a te ba, ate ba ale dɛ a nyu nueri la, wa yaa basi ate ba ŋman cheŋ ba kpagni jigi. Ate Araam nuruma yaa basi tugurik nyeka ale Izirali tɛŋka.
24Ku ale nye magadek la, Araam naawa, Ben Yadad a jam gomsi ka wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena ate ba gɔk santiri a gilim Samaria. 25Kom bolim yaa jam bo tɛŋka po. Tugurik tɔŋdɔma a jam gilim tɛŋka kama ate ku beni ate boniŋ zuk a jam da a paari kpana ligbie dobrim pinaanuŋ. Ate ŋanbie pagta chimbili nɔi, a da ligbie dobrim bunu.
26Ase Izirali naawa ale jam va siaka zuk a taam la, nipok yaa kaari wi wa ayen, <<Nyɔnɔ, naabaa, maari mu.>> 27Naawa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ase Naawen a dan kan maari fu, mi ale nya maarika ka bɛ a te fu? M le ta nyini ka juijui ate ba a fɔbi ŋan kpaata la? Ku ale nyini ka juijui ate ba nye daam la?>> 28Ate Naawa yaa bek wa ayen, <<Ka boan wari?>> Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Nipok wade ale weeni ayen, <M pai m biik ate ti maa chaab a ko dik ŋɔbi jinla, abe chum ti yik wa mɛ biika a ko dik.> 29Ate ti maa chaab a dik mi biika a ŋɔbi. Vanni ale veenti la mi yaa weeni wa ayen, <Pai fi biika ate ti dik ŋɔbi,> alege wa pai wa kama a suk.>> 30Naawa ale jam wom nipowa wieŋa la, wa yaa cheeri wa garuk woŋku ale sui kaasuŋ. Ase wa ale jam va siaka zuk a taam la, nuruma a jam nya kama ale wa naamu garukku tɛŋ wa jo ka boorisa garuk. 31Wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Wen a nye ale mu ate ku jo m nyiŋ ase ba dan kan gebi Safat nidoabinni Ɛlaisa zukku jinla.>>
32Yɔgyɔgla de, Ɛlaisa a jam kala ka wa yenni, ate nisɔmma a jam kala ale wa. Naawa yaa jam tom nuru ate wa dɛ niŋ, alege ate wa paari la, Ɛlaisa a jam weeni wa nisɔmma kama ayen, <<Nama an nya nuru koorika de ale tom a waai ayen wa jam a gebi m zukku la? Ni nya, ase nuruwa a dan jam, ni lik tuoku a yik tara ate wa kan jo. Daa wa kpagni mɛ naŋkima ale bo wa ŋaaŋ nna?>>
33Ɛlaisa ale jam diem boro a biisi ale ba la, naawa tintomdɔwa yaa jam wa jigi, a weeni ayen, <<Kaasuŋ kude a nyini ka Naawen jigi. Boan nyiŋ ate mi ŋman za a limisi Naawen yaa?>>

english_text:
1Elisha answered, “I have a message for you. The Lord promises that tomorrow here in Samaria, you will be able to buy a large sack of flour or two large sacks of barley for almost nothing.”
2The chief officer there with the king replied, “I don't believe it! Even if the Lord sent a rainstorm, it couldn't produce that much grain by tomorrow.”
“You will see it happen, but you won't eat any of the food,” Elisha warned him.
The Syrian Army Stops Its Attack
3About the same time, four men with leprosy were just outside the gate of Samaria. They said to each other, “Why should we sit here, waiting to die? 4There's nothing to eat in the city, so we would starve if we went inside. But if we stay out here, we will die for sure. Let's sneak over to the Syrian army camp and surrender. They might kill us, but they might not.” 5-8That evening the four men got up and left for the Syrian camp.
As they walked toward the camp, the Lord caused the Syrian troops to hear what sounded like the roar of a huge cavalry. The soldiers said to each other, “Listen! The king of Israel must have hired Hittite and Egyptian troops to attack us. Let's get out of here!” So they ran out of their camp that night, leaving their tents and horses and donkeys.
When the four men with leprosy reached the edge of the Syrian camp, no one was there. They walked into one of the tents, where they ate and drank, before carrying off clothes, as well as silver and gold. They hid all this, then walked into another tent; they took what they wanted and hid it too.
9They said to each other, “This isn't right. Today is a day to celebrate, and we haven't told anyone else what has happened. If we wait until morning, we will be punished. Let's go to the king's palace at once and tell the good news.”
10They went back to Samaria and shouted up to the guards at the gate, “We've just come from the Syrian army camp, and all the soldiers are gone! The tents are empty, and the horses and donkeys are still tied up. We didn't see or hear anybody.”
11The guards reported the news to the king's palace. 12The king got out of bed and said to his officers, “I know what those Syrians are doing. They know we're starving, so they're hiding in the fields, hoping we will go out to look for food. When we do, they can capture us and take over our city.”
13One of his officers replied, “We have a few horses left—why don't we let some men take five of them and go to the Syrian camp and see what's happening? We're going to die anyway like those who have already died.” 14They found two chariots, and the king commanded the men to find out what had happened to the Syrian troops.
15The men rode as far as the Jordan River. All along the way they saw clothes and equipment that the Syrians had thrown away as they escaped. Then they went back to the king and told him what they had seen.
16At once the people went to the Syrian camp and carried off what was left. They took so much that a large sack of flour and two large sacks of barley sold for almost nothing, just as the Lord had promised.
17The king of Israel had put his chief officer in charge of the gate, but he died when the people trampled him as they rushed out of the city. 18Earlier, when the king was at Elisha's house, Elisha had told him that flour or barley would sell for almost nothing. 19But the officer refused to believe that even the Lord could do that. So Elisha warned him that he would see it happen, but would not eat any of the food. 20And that's exactly what happened—the officer was trampled to death.
translation_text:
1Ɛlaisa yaa weeni ayen, <<Wom Naawen wanni. Naawen ale a weeni diila ale nna. Chum nna po de, zom kuruba kpioŋ nɔi ale da ligbie dobrim bunyi ate barli kuruba kpioŋ buye ale da ligbie dobrim bunyi Samaria nansuiŋku nɔi.>>
2Naawa ale a sali kpagi dii nisa la yaa tulisi Wen nuruwa ale weeni ayen, <<Nya, Naawen a dan poom lak wenŋmazuk tuataŋa nya kude ale baga a nye?>> Ɛlaisa yaa weeni ayen, <<Fi nina ale nya alege fi kan maa dɛ.>>
3Yɔgyɔgla de, gama ŋanaansi ale jam bo tɛŋka nansuiŋku. Ba yaa weeni chaab ayen, <<Ka boan nyiŋ ate ti bo dela ayen ti kpi? 4Ase ti dan weeni ayen, <Ti le cheŋ tɛŋka po,> kɔmmu a bo dula kama, ate ti ale kpi. Ti be dan bo dela mɛ, ti le kpi. Dila nyiŋ basi ate ti cheŋ Araam demma ale bo juijui la a ga siak te ba. Ba dan basi ti, ti le boro. Ase ba dan ko ti, di ni la.>>
5Tɛŋka ale a sobri la, ba yaa yiti cheŋ Araam demma boka jigini. Ase ba ale jam paari jigini la, nuru yeŋ mɛ la a jam karo, 6diila Nyɔnɔwa a jam nye kama ate Araam demma a jam a wom torokoba ale wusuma ale tugurik tɔŋdɔba nna yegayega chiok, ate ba yaa weeni chaab ayen, <<Ni nya, Izirali naawa a yaali ka Yit ale Ejipiti nalimaŋa ayen ba kpaliŋ ale ti.>> 7Dila ba yiti chali junɔi dila ale basi ba viitaŋa ale ba wusumaŋa ale ba bonsaŋa. Ba jam basi ba bo ka jigini kama ba nyuvooŋa nyiŋ.
8Nuru baai ale ta gama tuem la ale ga paari jigini a jo viitaŋa kunyi la. Ba jam dɛ ale nyu ale pai kpana ale ligmɔniŋ ale gatta a ta cheŋ ga suk. Ba ŋman jam jo viuk ku choa a pai ŋanta gela a ta ga suk.
9Ba yaa weeni chaab ayen, <<Ti kan nye a magsi. Ka wamaŋsa dai ale jinla ate ti ta tidek ti nyiini ti dan limisi ate vanni a vienti, namsika ale jam ti zuk. Basi ate ti ga weeni sak naab yenni.>>
10Ate ba jam cheŋ a ga wi tɛŋka nansuiŋku nuruma a weeni ba ayen, <<Tama cheŋ ka Araam demma boka jigini, nuru yeŋ mɛ abe karo. Fi poom kan wom chiowa. Ka wusuma ale bonsa ate ba diak a zaani, ate viitaŋa a za ti denni.>> 11Nansuiŋku nuruma yaa nye nuemka wamaŋka de nyiŋ ale ga weeni sak naab yenni.
12Naawa yaa yiti yok a weeni wa kpaŋŋa ayen, <<M le weeni ni Araam demma ale nye ti diila. Ba seba kama ayen, ti a viiri kama. Ate ba yaa basi ba boka jigini alege ga suk tɛŋka nakpiak ale a poli ayen, <Izirali demma ale nyini peelim ate ti yik ba vuta abe ti jo tɛŋka po.> >> 13Wa kpaŋŋa wanyi yaa tulisi ayen, <<Te nuruba a pai wusuma ŋanu ale tali bo tɛŋka po la. Dii ale a daani ba la ale nye ase ka Izirali demma meena ale tali bo dela la, mm, ba ale nye ase ka Izirali demma de meena baai ale bo kaasuŋ po la. Dila basi ate ti tom ba ate ba ga nya dii ale nye la.>>
14Ate ba lueri torokoba baye ale ba wusuma, ate naawa a basi ate ba a vi Araam demma tugurik tɔŋdɔma ŋaaŋ. Wa jam weeni baai ale a dam la ayen, <<Ni cheŋ a ga nya ase ka boa ale nye.>> 15Ba jam va ba naŋsa a ga paari ka Jodan benni, ate ba nya gatta ale lo doa suiku po meena ale Araam demma a yuk ba tuima ŋantaŋa a basi ase ba le a kpabi la. Ate nuruma ŋman ga weeni sak naawa. 16Ate nuruma a cheŋ Araam demma boka jigini a ga kɔlim ba ŋantaŋa. Ate zom kuruba kpioŋ a jam da ligbie dobrim bunyi, ate barli kuruba kpioŋ nɔi buye a jam da ligbie dobrim bunyi, ase Naawen ale jam weeni la.
17Yɔgyɔgla de, naawa a pai ka kpagi waai ate wa a sali wa nisa la ayen wa a nya nansuiŋku zuk, ate nuruma a tabi wa nansuiŋku nɔi ate wa kpi. Ase Wen nuruwa ale poom dɛ niŋ a weeni la, diipo ate naawa a siŋ jam wa yenni la. 18Ku nye kama ase Wen nuruwa ale jam weeni naawa diila ayen, <<Chum nna po de, zom kuruba kpioŋ ale da ligbie dobrim bunyi, ate barli kuruba kpioŋ nɔi buye ale da ligbie dobrim bunyi Samaria nansuiŋku nɔi.>>
19Kpagni a weeni ayen, <<Nya, Naawen a dan poom lak wenŋmazuk tuataŋa nya kude ale baga a nye?>> Wen nuruwa a tulisi ayen, <<Fi nina ale nya alege fi kan maa dɛ.>> 20Ate dila dekdek a sum jam nye wa, diila nuruma a jam tabi wa kama nansuiŋku nɔi ate wa kpi.

english_text:
The Woman from Shunem Is Given Back Her Land
1 Elisha told the woman whose son he had brought back to life, “The Lord has warned that there will be no food here for seven years. Take your family and go live somewhere else for a while.” 2The woman did exactly what Elisha had said and went to live in Philistine territory.
She and her family lived there seven years. 3Then she returned to Israel and immediately begged the king to give back her house and property.
4Meanwhile, the king was asking Gehazi the servant of Elisha about the amazing things Elisha had been doing. 5While Gehazi was telling him that Elisha had brought a dead boy back to life, the woman and her son arrived.
“Here's the boy, Your Majesty,” Gehazi said. “And this is his mother.”
6The king asked the woman to tell her story, and she told him everything that had happened. He then said to one of his officials, “I want you to make sure that this woman gets back everything that belonged to her, including the money her crops have made since the day she left Israel.”
Hazael Kills Benhadad
7Some time later Elisha went to the capital city of Damascus to visit King Benhadad of Syria, who was sick. And when Benhadad was told he was there, 8he said to Hazael, “Go meet with Elisha the man of God and get him to ask the Lord if I will get well. And take along a gift for him.”
9Hazael left with forty camel loads of the best things made in Damascus as a gift for Elisha. He found the prophet and said, “Your servant, King Benhadad, wants to know if he will get well.”
10“Tell him he will,” Elisha said to Hazael. “But the Lord has already told me that Benhadad will definitely die.” 11Elisha stared at him until Hazael was embarrassed, then Elisha began crying.
12“Sir, why are you crying?” Hazael asked.
Elisha answered, “Because I know the terrible things you will do to the people of Israel. You will burn down their walled cities and slaughter their young men. You will even crush the heads of their babies and rip open their pregnant women.”
13 “How could I ever do anything like that?” Hazael replied. “I'm only a servant and don't have that kind of power.”
“Hazael, the Lord has told me that you will be the next king of Syria.”
14Hazael went back to Benhadad and told him, “Elisha said that you will get well.” 15But the very next day, Hazael got a thick blanket; he soaked it in water and held it over Benhadad's face until he died. Hazael then became king.
King Jehoram of Judah
(2 Chronicles 21.2-20)
16Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat became king of Judah in Joram's fifth year as king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was still king of Judah. 17Jehoram was 32 years old when he became king, and he ruled 8 years from Jerusalem.
18Jehoram disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He married Ahab's daughter and was as sinful as Ahab's family and the kings of Israel. 19 But the Lord refused to destroy Judah, because he had promised his servant David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah.
20 While Jehoram was king, the people of Edom rebelled and chose their own king. 21So Jehoram and his cavalry marched to Zair, where the Edomite army surrounded him and his commanders. During the night he attacked the Edomites, but he was defeated, and his troops escaped to their homes. 22Judah was never able to regain control of Edom. Even the town of Libnah rebelled at that time.
23Everything else Jehoram did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 24Jehoram died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Ahaziah then became king.
King Ahaziah of Judah
(2 Chronicles 22.1-6)
25Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah in the twelfth year of Joram's rule in Israel. 26Ahaziah was 22 years old when he became king, and he ruled from Jerusalem for only one year. His mother was Athaliah, a granddaughter of King Omri of Israel. 27Since Ahaziah was related to Ahab's family, he acted just like them and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong.
28Ahaziah went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle, 29so he went to the town of Jezreel to recover. Ahaziah went there to visit him.
translation_text:
1Yɔgyɔgla de Ɛlaisa yaa jam weeni Sunem nipok waai ate wa nak wa nidoabinni a yiti kum po la ayen, <<Ta fi dɔkdemma a cheŋ juijui ate fi a yaali la a ga boro ate ku nye maga, dii nyiŋla Naawen a weeni kama ayen kɔm a jam tɛŋka po a paari bena ŋayopɔi.>> 2Nipowa yaa nye dii ate Wen nuruwa a weeni wa la. Wa ale wa dɔkdemma a jam cheŋ ga bo ka Filistia demma tɛŋka po bena ŋayopɔi.
3Bena ŋayopɔiwa ale jam nueri la, wa ŋman pilim nyini Filistia demma tɛŋka po a jam taam cheŋ naawa jigi a ga saalim a yaali wa yenni ale wa tɛŋka. 4Naawa a jam boro a biisi ale ka Geyazi, waai ale ka Wen nuruwa tomteerɔ la ayen, <<Weeni wakpiema ŋaai meena ate Ɛlaisa a nye la a sak mu.>> 5Diipo ate Geyazi a jam boro a weeni naawa ayen Ɛlaisa a nye ate waai ale kpi la a ŋman jam vum po la, nipok waai nidoabinni ate Ɛlaisa a nak wa a yiti kum po la, yaa jam boro a saalim naawa ayen wa pai wa yenni ale wa tɛŋka a te wa. Geyazi yaa weeni ayen, <<Nipowa ale nna, m nyɔnɔ naabaa, wa nidoabinni mɛ ale nna, waai ate Ɛlaisa a ŋman ta wa a jam vum po la.>> 6Naawa yaa jam bek nipowa ku wari, ate nipowa a weeni wa. Ate naawa yaa lueri kpagi ayen wa nya nipowa wanni zuk ale weeni kpagni ayen, <<Ŋman pilim pai nipowa ale soa ŋan baai meena la a te wa ale wa tɛŋka ale ta nyuenta tii meena a jam la a te wa, a zaani diipo ate wa basi tɛŋka la a jam paari yɔgyɔgla de.>>
7Ɛlaisa a jam cheŋ ka Damasikus, ate Ben Yadad ale ka Araam naab la a jam a yuak. Ba ale jam weeni naawa ayen, <<Wen nuruwa a jam bo dela la,>> 8wa yaa weeni Yazael ayen, <<Pai tiirim a ga nya Wen nuruwa. Va wa nyiŋ a kpesi nya a nyini Naawen jigi. Bek wa ayen, m le nya nyiŋyɔgsa a nyini nyiŋtuilaŋa de po?>>
9Yazael yaa jam cheŋ Ɛlaisa jigi. Wa jam pai ka laalaakomiba pisinaansi ale ji Damasikus kɔlim maŋsa ase tiirim la. Wa jam jo kama a yaa ga zaani wa niŋ, a yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Fi biika Ben Yadad ale ka Araam naab la ale tom mu ayen m bek fu ayen, <M le nya nyiŋyɔgsa a ta nyini nyiŋtuilaŋa de po ya?> >> 10Ɛlaisa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Cheŋ ga weeni wa ayen, <Fi ale nya nyiŋyɔgsa.> Alege Naawen a pai sak mu kama ayen wa za wa kpi kama.>> 11Wa kasim a nya wa kama ate chivie a ga yik Yazael. Ate Wen nuruwa yaa piilim a kum.
12Yazael yaa bek ayen, <<Ka boan nyiŋ ate m nyɔnɔwa a kumu? Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Dii nyiŋla m seba daani kaai ate ni za ni pai nye Izirali demma la kama. Ni ale toati ka bolim a basi ba jigi pagrisaŋa zuk, abe ni pai gebik woŋsa a ko ba nuru baai ale diem paala la, abe ni chiak ba bi fiisaŋa a fɔbi tɛŋ a ko, abe ni yik ba nipok puusaŋa a mobi.>> 13Yazael yaa weeni ayen, <<Fi tomteerɔwa waai ale kan daa jaab la ale nye ka sɛ a nye wapagrika de choa?>> Ɛlaisa yaa tulisi ayen, Naawen a pai sak mi kama ayen fi a za fi chim ka Araam naab.>>
14Ate Yazael yaa basi Ɛlaisa ale ŋman cheŋ wa kpagni jigi. Ben Yadad yaa bek ayen, <<Ɛlaisa a weeni fu ayen ka boa? Yazael yaa tulisi ayen, <<Wa weeni mu kama ayen fi ale nya nyiŋyɔgsa.>> 15Alege vanni ale jam vienti la, wa jam pai ka garuk jibsuk a mooŋ nyiam a pai pati lik naawa ninaŋa, ate wa kpi. Ate Yazael yaa chim naab a tagri wa.
16Joram ale ka Izirali naawa Ayab nidoabili la, wa bena ŋanuwa po diipo ate Jeyosafat a jam ka naab a bo Juda la, Jeyoram ale ka Jeyosafat nidoabili la yaa jam piilim wa naamu dɛka Juda po. 17Wa jam ta ka bena pisita ale ŋaye ale jam chim naab, wa jam dɛ wa naamu a paari ka bena naaniŋ Jerusalem po. 18Wa jam va ka Izirali nalimaŋa suitaŋa ase Ayab yenni ale jam nye diila, dii nyiŋla, wa jam faari ka Ayab lie. Wa jam nye ka biem Naawen nina po. 19Alege kula ŋaaŋnyiŋ meena, wa tomteerɔwa Deevid nyiŋ, Naawen an yaali ayen wa kaasi Juda. Wa puulim kama ayen wa ale basi ate zeuŋ a boro a te Deevid ale wa ŋaaŋsaŋa taam wuu.
20Jeyoram vaaŋa po, Edom a jam ta ka chaab ale Juda alege bobi badek naab. 21Ate Joram jam ta wa wusuma torokoma meena a cheŋ Zair. Edom demma a jam gilim wa kama ale wa wusuma torokoma niŋdeerɔma, alege wa jam yiti ka yok a wɛ va ba po a taam. Alege wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma jam ŋman chali kuli ka ba yeeŋa. 22A jam paari jinla de, Edom a kasim ta ka chaab ale Juda. Ate Libna mɛ a ta chaab ale ba dila dekdega.
23Dii ale nye Joram vaaŋa po ale dii meena ate wa nye la, ŋala a ŋmarisi a doa Juda nalimaŋa gbaŋka po kama. 24Joram a jam kpi kama ate ba gu wa Deevid Tɛŋka po ate wa vuusi ale wa koma. Ate wa nidoabinni Ayaziya a chim naab a tagri wa.
25Joram ale ka Izirali naawa Ayab nidoabili la bena pi ale ŋaye wa po, Ayaziya ale ka Juda naawa Jeyoram nidoabili la, yaa piilim ayen wa dɛ naam. 26Ayaziya a jam ta ka bena pisiye ale ŋaye ale jam chim naab, ate wa jam dɛ naam ka ben yeŋ Jerusalem po. Wa mawa yuei jam le Ataliaya, wa jam ka Izirali naawa Omri ŋaaŋ. 27Wa jam ta ka Ayab yenni nyeelaŋa ale nye biem Naawen nina po, ase Ayab yenni ale jam nye diila, dii nyiŋla wa mawa a jam nyini ka Ayab dɔkdemma po.
28Ayaziya a jam cheŋ ale ka Joram ale ka Ayab nidoabinni la a ga nye kpaliŋ ale Araam naawa Yazael Aramot Gilead po. Araam demma a jam koani Joram kama. 29Ate naab Joram a jam ŋman cheŋ Jezreel ayen wa nya wadek ate Araam demma a koani wa Aramot po la, wa ale jam kpaliŋ ale Araam naawa Yazael la. Ate Juda naawa Jeyoram nidoabinni Ayaziya a jam cheŋ Jezreel ayen wa nya Ayab nidoabinni Joram dii nyiŋla ba koani wa kama.

english_text:
Jehu Becomes King of Israel
1One day, Elisha called for one of the other prophets and said:
Take this bottle of olive oil and get ready to go to the town of Ramoth in Gilead. 2When you get there, find Jehu son of Jehoshaphat and grandson of Nimshi. Take him to a place where the two of you can be alone, 3then pour olive oil on his head to show that he is the new king. Say to him, “The Lord has chosen you to be king of Israel.” Then leave quickly—don't wait around for anything!
4The young prophet left for Ramoth. 5When he arrived, the army officers were meeting together. “Sir, I have a message for you,” he said.
“For which one of us?” Jehu asked.
“You, sir,” the prophet answered. 6 So Jehu got up and went inside. The prophet poured olive oil on Jehu's head and told him:
The Lord God of Israel has this message for you: “I am the Lord, and I have chosen you to be king of my people Israel. 7I want you to wipe out the family of Ahab, so Jezebel will be punished for killing the prophets and my other servants. 8Every man and boy in Ahab's family must die, whether slave or free. 9His whole family must be destroyed, just like the families of Jeroboam son of Nebat and Baasha son of Ahijah. 10 As for Jezebel, her body will be eaten by dogs in the town of Jezreel. There won't be enough left of her to bury.”
Then the young prophet opened the door and ran out.
11Jehu went back to his officers, and one of them asked, “What did that crazy prophet want? Is everything all right?”
“You know him and how he talks,” Jehu answered.
12“No, we don't. What did he say?” they asked.
“He had a message from the Lord,” Jehu replied. “He said that the Lord has chosen me to be the next king of Israel.”
13They quickly grabbed their coats and spread them out on the steps where Jehu was standing. Someone blew a trumpet, and everyone shouted, “Jehu is king!”
Jehu Kills Joram and Ahaziah
14-16King Joram of Israel had been badly wounded in the battle at Ramoth, trying to defend it against King Hazael and the Syrian army. Joram was now recovering in Jezreel, and King Ahaziah of Judah was there, visiting him.
Meanwhile, Jehu was in Ramoth, making plans to kill Joram. He said to his officers, “If you want me to be king, then don't let anyone leave this town. They might go to Jezreel and tell Joram.” Then Jehu got in his chariot and rode to Jezreel.
17When the guard in the watchtower at Jezreel saw Jehu and his men riding up, he shouted to the king, “I see a large group of men coming this way.”
Joram ordered, “Send someone out to ask them if this is a friendly visit.”
18One of the soldiers rode out and said to Jehu, “King Joram wants to know if this is a friendly visit.”
“What's it to you?” Jehu asked. “Just stay behind me with the rest of my troops!”
About the same time the guard in the watchtower said, “Your Majesty, the rider got there, but he isn't coming back.”
19So Joram sent out another rider, who rode up to Jehu and said, “The king wants to know if this is a friendly visit.”
“What's it to you?” Jehu asked. “Just get behind me with the rest of my troops!”
20The guard in the watchtower said, “Your Majesty, the rider got there, but he isn't coming back either. Wait a minute! That one man is a reckless chariot driver—it must be Jehu!”
21Joram commanded, “Get my chariot ready.” Then he and Ahaziah got in their chariots and rode out to meet Jehu. They all met on the land that had belonged to Naboth. 22Joram asked, “Jehu, is this a peaceful visit?”
“How can there be peace?” Jehu asked. “Your mother Jezebel has caused everyone to worship idols and practice witchcraft.”
23“Ahaziah, let's get out of here!” Joram yelled. “It's a trap!” As Joram tried to escape, 24Jehu shot an arrow. It hit Joram between his shoulders, then it went through his heart and came out his chest. He fell over dead in his chariot.
25-26 Jehu commanded his assistant Bidkar, “Get Joram's body and throw it in the field that Naboth once owned. Do you remember when you and I used to ride side by side behind Joram's father Ahab? It was then that the Lord swore to Ahab that he would be punished in the same field where he had killed Naboth and his sons. So throw Joram's body there, just as the Lord said.”
27Ahaziah saw all of this happen and tried to escape to the town of Beth-Haggan, but Jehu caught up with him and shouted, “Kill him too!” So his troops shot Ahaziah with an arrow while he was on the road to Gur near Ibleam. He went as far as Megiddo, where he died. 28Ahaziah's officers put his body in a chariot and took it back to Jerusalem, where they buried him beside his ancestors.
29Ahaziah had become king of Judah in the eleventh year of the rule of Ahab's son Joram.
Jehu Kills Jezebel
30Jehu headed toward Jezreel, and when Jezebel heard he was coming, she put on eye shadow and brushed her hair. Then she stood at the window, waiting for him to arrive. 31As he walked through the city gate, she shouted down to him, “Why did you come here, you murderer? To kill the king? You're no better than Zimri!”
32He looked up toward the window and asked, “Is anyone up there on my side?” A few palace workers stuck their heads out of a window, 33and Jehu shouted, “Throw her out the window!” They threw her down, and her blood splattered on the walls and on the horses that trampled her body.
34Jehu left to get something to eat and drink. Then he told some workers, “Even though she was evil, she was a king's daughter, so make sure she has a proper burial.”
35But when they went out to bury her body, they found only her skull, her hands, and her feet. 36 They reported this to Jehu, and he said, “The Lord told Elijah the prophet that Jezebel's body would be eaten by dogs right here in Jezreel. 37And he warned that her bones would be spread all over the ground like manure, so that no one could tell who it was.”
translation_text:
1Wen biisiteerɔwa Ɛlaisa jam wi ka nuru a ta nyini Wen biisiteerɔma tigsuŋku po a weeni wa ayen, <<Yik fi garukku a su fi chiak gbainni po, pai kpaamu ale bo leŋka de po la a cheŋ Aramot Gilead. 2Ase fi dan ga paari dula, gisi Jeyu ale ka Jeyosafat nidoabinni la, Nimsi nidoabinni. Cheŋ wa jigi, ta wa nyini wa ale kala ale baai la a ta wa a jo niŋ dɔk po. 3Pai leŋka ale kpaamu a kpiiri basi wa zuk abe fi weeni ayen, <Naawen ale a weeni diila ale nna ayen, Mi bobi fu ka naab Izirali zuk.> Abe fi yaa a lak tuoku a chali. Kan beni.>>
4Dila nuruwa ale ka Wen biisiteerɔ la a jam cheŋ Aramot Gilead. 5Wa ale ga paari la wa jam nya ka tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpaŋŋa ale kala jigi yeŋ. Ate wa weeni ayen, <<M ta ka wari ayen m weeni sak fi kpagi yaa.>> Jeyu yaa bek ayen, <<Ti po wana?>> Ate wa tulisi ayen, <<M te fi, kpagi yaa.>>
6Jeyu yaa yiti a jo yenni po. Ate Wen biisiteerɔwa a kpiiri kpaamu a nyo Jeyu zukku po ale weeni ayen, <<Naawen dii ale ka Izirali Wenni ale weeni diila ale nna ayen, <M bobi fu ka naab Izirali Naawen nuruma zuk. 7Fi magsi kama ayen fi kaasi fi kpagni Ayab yenni, ate mi ale namsi Jezebel a tuni wa le ko m tomteerɔma biisiteerɔma la, ale Naawen tomteerɔma meena la nyiŋ. 8Ayab yenni a kan boro. M le ko Ayab nidoa meena ale bo Izirali po la. Wa dan poom chim ka yɔma yaase daa yɔmma. 9M le nye Ayab yenni ase ka Jeroboam ale ka Nebat nidoabinni la yenni ale Baasia ale ka Ayija nidoabinni yenni la. 10Dan ka Jezebel, baasa le ŋɔbi wa Jezreel tɛŋka zuk, ate waai a kan gu wa.> >> Ate wa yaa lak tuoku a chali.
11Jeyu ale jam cheŋ wa kpagi chaama jigi la, ba wanyi yaa bek wa ayen, <<Jaab meena a cheŋ nalimnyiini ya? Nuru yesiŋka de a jam fi jigi ayen wa nye ka boa?>> Jeyu yaa tulisi ayen, <<Fidek seba nuruwa kama ale wa ale a weeni wie ŋaai la. 12Ba yaa weeni ayen, <<Ku daa wensie. Weeni sak ti.>> Jeyu yaa weeni ayen, <<Wa ale weeni mi diila ale nna ayen, nya kude ate Naawen a weeni ayen, m bobi fu ka naab Izirali zuk.>>
13Ba yaa nye nwuli a pai ba gattaasa a pati wa naŋsa po. Ba yaa peeri damuniŋ ale nuem ayen, <<Jeyu ka naab.>>
14Dila Jeyu ate wa kowa a chim Jeyosafat la ate wa kokpieŋka a chim Nimsi la, yaa poli ayen wa nye Naab Joram biem. Joram ale Izirali a poom jam a maari ka Aramot Gilead ate ba a kpaliŋ ale Yazael ale ka Araam naab la, 15alege Joram a ŋmani kama a cheŋ Jezreel ayen wa nya wadek ate Araam demma a jam koani wa kpaliŋka po ate wa jam ta ale Yazael ale ka Araam naab la. Jeyu yaa weeni wa kpaga chaama ayen, <<Ase ni dan sum a yaali ayen mi chim naab, kan te waai a sati nyini tɛŋka po a nyini a cheŋ ga weeni dii ate ti ta la Jezreel po.>> 16Ate Jeyu cheŋ ga jueli wa wusum torokowa zuk a cheŋ Jezreel, dii nyiŋla Joram a jam bo ka dula a ayen wa nya wadek ate Juda naawa Ayaziya a jam bo ka dula ayen wa nya Joram.
17Limisidɔwa ale jam za Jezreel gboŋku zuk ale ga nya Jeyu tugurik tɔŋdɔma a cheena la, wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Mi nya tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale cheena.>> Joram yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni yaali wusum duerɔ ate wa ga a tu ba suik a bek ba ayen, ni cheen ale ka suiyɔgni?>>
18Wusum duerɔwa yaa dɔ wa wusummu a ga tu Jeyu a yaa bek wa ayen, <<Naawa ale a weeni diila ale nna. <Ayen ni cheen ale ka suiyɔgni?> >> Jeyu yaa tulisi ayen, <<Daa fi niŋ ale bo kude po. Va mu.>> Limisidɔwa yaa ga weeni ayen, <<Waai ate fi tom la a paari ba kama, alege wa an diem cheena.>>
19Ate naawa a ŋman tom wusum duerɔ waai ale a saari buye. Wa ale jam a cheŋ ba jigi la, wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Naawa a weeni kama ayen, <Nama jam ale ka suiyɔgni?> >> Jeyu yaa tulisi ayen, <<Daa fi niŋ ale bo kude po. Va mu.>>
20Limisidɔwa yaa ga weeni ayen, <<Wa paari ba kama, alege wa an diem cheena. Damka a nye ase ka Jeyu ale ka Nimsi nidoabinni la. Wa a dam ase ka yesiŋ la.>>
21Joram yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni gomsi m wusuma torokowa a magsi.>> Ba ale jam gomsi nueri la, Izirali naawa Joram ale Juda naawa Ayaziya yaa jam nyini, ate waai meena a jueli wadek wusum toroko zuk ayen ba ga tu Jeyu. Ba jam ga tu wa ka tɛŋ kaai ate Jezreel denɔ Nabot a soa la. 22Joram ale jam ga nya Jeyu la, wa bek wa ayen, <<Jeyu, fi jam ale ka suiyɔgni?>> Jeyu yaa tulisi ayen, <<Suiyɔgni ale nye ka sɛ a boro ase fi mawa Jezebel bɔgtaŋa ale sampoporinni ale diem boro la?>> 23Joram yaa viriŋ ŋaaŋ a yiti chali ale kaari a weeni Ayaziya ayen, <<Ayaziya! Ku bie kama!>>
24Ate Jeyu yaa yeeri wa tommu a tɔŋ Joram maŋkpalaŋa suŋsuŋsa po. Penni yaa feri wa ŋaaŋka a jo wa suinummu po ate wa lo wa wusum torokowa po a kpi. 25Jeyu yaa weeni Bidkar ale ka wa wusum toroko kpagi la ayen, <<Pai wa a yuk basi tɛŋ kaai ate Jezreel denɔwa Nabot soa la. Teeri fi ale mi ale jam maa chaab a dɔ ti wusum torokoma a bo wa kowa ŋaaŋ ate Naawen a jam weeni dii a ta va wa nyiŋla. 26Deemwa mi nya ka Nabot ale wa nidoabilisaŋa ziimu, ka Naawen ale a weeni dila ate mi ale te ate fi sum tuni ku nyiŋ tɛŋka de zuk, ka Naawen ale a weeni dila. Yɔgyɔgla de, be pai wa a yuk basi tɛŋka zuk, a magsi chaab ale Naawen wanni.>>
27Ase Juda naawa Ayaziya ale ga nya dii ale nye la, wa yaa chali jueli va suiku a cheŋ Bet Yaggan. Jeyu yaa jam chali vi wa ale a kaari ayen, <<Ko wa mɛ!>> Ba jam koani wa kama wa wusum torokowa po Gur suiku po a moata Ibleam, alege wa jam chali be a cheŋ Megiddo a kpi dula. 28Wa tomteerɔwa a jam pai ka wusum toroko a pai wa ta cheŋ Jerusalem a gu wa ale wa koma wa vɔrumu po Deevid Tɛŋka po. 29Ku jam ka Ayab nidoabinni Joram bena pi ale dinyiwa po, Ayaziya yaa jam chim naab Juda po.
30Ate Jeyu a jam cheŋ Jezreel. Jezebel ale jam wom la, wa yaa jam pai ŋanta a sa wa ninaŋa ale gomsi wa zuisaŋa ale va tuokparuk a liisi nya. 31Ase Jeyu ale jam va tuoku a jo la, wa yaa bek wa ayen, <<Zimri, fi jam ale ka suiyɔgni, fi waai ale ko fi kpagni la?>>
32Wa va ka tuokparuku a yaa wi ayen, ka wana ale za m tɛŋŋa? Ka wana? Naab yeri kpaga baye yaase bata yaa jam nya wa. 33Jeyu yaa jam weeni ayen, <<Ni yuk wa lɔnsi tɛŋ.>> Dila ba yaa yuk wa lɔnsi tɛŋ ate wa ziimu gela a misi siaka ale wusumaŋa nyiŋsaŋa ase ŋa ale a tabi wa la.
34Jeyu yaa jam cheŋ ga dɛ ale nyu. Wa jam weeni kama ayen, <<A nya kikaasa nipowa zuk abe fi gu wa dii nyiŋla, wa jam ka naab lie.>> 35Alege ba ale jam cheŋ ayen ba gu wa la, ba an nya jaaboa, ka wa zukoluku ale wa naŋtaataŋa ale wa nisaŋa. 36Ba jam ŋmani kama a ga weeni Jeyu, ate wa weeni ayen, <<Nya kude ka Naawen wanni ate wa jam biisi va wa biisiteerɔwa Elaja ale ka Tisbi denɔ la ayen Jezreel tɛŋka zuk ate baasa ale ŋɔbi Jezebel nyiŋka. 37Jezebel nyiŋka ale nye ase ka tampoi la Jezreel tɛŋka po ate waai a kan baga a weeni ayen, <Ka Jezebel ale nna.> >>

english_text:
Jehu Kills All of Ahab's Descendants
1Ahab still had 70 descendants living in Samaria. So Jehu wrote a letter to each of the important leaders and officials of the town, and to those who supported Ahab. In the letters he wrote:
2Your town is strong, and you're protected by chariots and an armed cavalry. And I know that King Ahab's descendants live there with you. So as soon as you read this letter, 3choose the best person for the job and make him the next king. Then be prepared to defend Ahab's family.
4The officials and leaders read the letters and were very frightened. They said to each other, “Jehu has already killed King Joram and King Ahaziah! We have to do what he says.” 5The prime minister, the mayor of the city, as well as the other leaders and Ahab's supporters, sent this answer to Jehu, “We are your servants, Your Majesty, and we will do whatever you tell us. But it's not our place to choose someone to be king. You do what you think is best.”
6Jehu then wrote another letter which said, “If you are on my side and will obey me, then prove it. Bring me the heads of the descendants of Ahab! And be here in Jezreel by this time tomorrow.”
The 70 descendants of King Ahab were living with some of the most important people of the city. 7And when these people read Jehu's second letter, they called together all 70 of Ahab's descendants. They killed them, put their heads in baskets, and sent them to Jezreel.
8When Jehu was told what had happened, he said, “Put the heads in two piles at the city gate, and leave them there until morning.”
9The next morning, Jehu went out and stood where everyone could hear him, and he said, “You people are not guilty of anything. I'm the one who plotted against Joram and had him killed. But who killed all these men? 10Listen to me. Everything the Lord's servant Elijah promised about Ahab's family will come true.”
11 Then Jehu killed the rest of Ahab's relatives living in Jezreel, as well as his highest officials, his priests, and his closest friends. No one in Ahab's family was left alive in Jezreel.
12-13Jehu left for Samaria, and along the way, he met some relatives of King Ahaziah of Judah at a place where shepherds meet. He asked, “Who are you?”
“We are relatives of Ahaziah,” they answered. “We're going to visit his family.”
14“Take them alive!” Jehu said to his officers. So they grabbed them and led them to the well near the shepherds' meeting place, where they killed all 42 of them.
15As Jehu went on, he saw Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him. Jehu greeted him, then said, “Jehonadab, I'm on your side. Are you on mine?”
“Yes, I am.”
“Then give me your hand,” Jehu answered. He helped Jehonadab into his chariot 16and said, “Come with me and see how faithful I am to the Lord.”
They rode together in Jehu's chariot 17to Samaria. Jehu killed everyone there who belonged to Ahab's family, as well as all his officials. Everyone in his family was now dead, just as the Lord had promised Elijah.
Jehu Kills All the Worshipers of Baal
18Jehu called together the people in Samaria and said:
King Ahab sometimes worshiped Baal, but I will be completely faithful to Baal. 19I'm going to offer a huge sacrifice to him. So invite his prophets and priests, and be sure everyone who worships him is there. Anyone who doesn't come will be killed.
But this was a trick—Jehu was really planning to kill the worshipers of Baal. 20He said, “Announce a day of worship for Baal!” After the day had been announced, 21Jehu sent an invitation to everyone in Israel. All the worshipers of Baal came, and the temple was filled from one end to the other. 22Jehu told the official in charge of the sacred robes to make sure that everyone had a robe to wear.
23Jehu and Jehonadab went into the temple, and Jehu said to the crowd, “Look around and make sure that only the worshipers of Baal are here. No one who worships the Lord is allowed in.” 24Then they began to offer sacrifices to Baal.
Earlier, Jehu had ordered 80 soldiers to wait outside the temple. He had warned them, “I will get all these worshipers here, and if any of you let even one of them escape, you will be killed instead!”
25As soon as Jehu finished offering the sacrifice, he told the guards and soldiers, “Come in and kill them! Don't let anyone escape.” They slaughtered everyone in the crowd and threw the bodies outside. Then they went back into the temple 26and carried out the image of Baal. They burned it 27and broke it into pieces, then they completely destroyed Baal's temple. And since that time, it's been nothing but a public toilet.
28That's how Jehu stopped the worship of Baal in Israel. 29 But he did not stop the worship of the gold statues of calves at Dan and Bethel that Jeroboam had made for the people to worship.
30Later the Lord said, “Jehu, you have done right by destroying Ahab's entire family, just as I had planned. So I will make sure that the next four kings of Israel will come from your own family.”
31But Jehu did not completely obey the commands of the Lord God of Israel. Instead, he kept doing the sinful things that Jeroboam had caused the Israelites to do.
Jehu Dies
32In those days the Lord began to reduce the size of Israel's territory. King Hazael of Syria defeated the Israelites and took control 33of the regions of Gilead and Bashan east of the Jordan River and north of the town of Aroer near the Arnon River. This was the land where the tribes of Gad, Reuben, and Manasseh had once lived.
34Everything else Jehu did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. 35Jehu died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Jehoahaz became king. 36Jehu had ruled Israel 28 years from Samaria.
translation_text:
1Dila po Ayab yenni a jam ta ka nidoabilisa pisiyopɔi Samaria po. Dila Jeyu a jam ŋmarisi gbaŋsa a tom te Samaria. A te kpaŋŋa ale bo Jezreel ale niŋdeerɔma ale baai ale a nya Ayab bisaŋa zuk la. Wa jam weeni kama ayen, 2<<Ase gbaŋka de a dan ga paari fu, fi kpaŋŋa nidoabilisaŋa ale toalim bo ale fu la, ate fi ta wusum torokoba ale wusuma ale tɛŋ pagrik ale kpaliŋ kɔlima la, 3lueri fi kpagni nidoabilisaŋa waai ale magsi la ale ta zula la, a pai wa a kali wa kowa naamu zukpaglika zuk. Abe fi yaa kpaliŋ te fi kpagni yenni.
4Alege ba kpaziita ale jam a nak a weeni ayen, <<Ase nalima baye a dan kan bag a zaani ale wa, tama ale nye ka sɛ?>>
5Dila waai ale a nya naab yeri tuimaŋa zuk la ale tɛŋka nyɔnɔwa ale niŋdeerɔma ale baai ale a nya bisaŋa zuk la yaa jam ta wanni a cheŋ ga te Jeyu ayen, <<Tama ka fi tomteerɔba, ate fi ale a weeni dii meena la ale tama ale nye. Tama a kan lueri waai ya ayen wa chim ti naaba. Fidek nye dii ale magsi la.>>
6Ate Jeyu a ŋman ŋmarisi gbaŋ kaai ale a saari buye la ayen, <<Ase fi dan va ka mi ale a wom mi, ta fi kpagni nidoabilisaŋa zuimaŋa a jam m jigi Jezreel po chum nna po de.>> Yɔgyɔgla de nabisa pisiyopɔi ale jam bo niŋdeerɔma jigi ate ba jam ta ba a nya. 7Gbaŋka ale jam paari la, nuruma de a jam yik nabisaŋa kama a tɔgri ba nɔi pisiyopɔiwa meena. Ba jam pai ba zuimaŋa kama a nyo busisa po a ta ga te Jeyu Jezreel po. 8Waai ate ba tom la ale ga paari la, wa jam weeni Jeyu kama ayen, <<Ba ta nabisaŋa zuimaŋa a jam kama.>> Ate Jeyu a weeni ayen, <<Dueni ŋa puula ŋaye tɛŋka nansuiŋku nɔi ate ku paari saluik.>>
9Vanni ale veenti la saluik Jeyu yaa nyini peelim. Wa jam zaani ka nuruma meena niŋ a weeni ayen, <<Ni zɛ wari nɔi po. Ka mi ale magi a nya nuruba ate ba ko m kpagni, alege ka wana ale ko bade meena? 10Seba ayen, Naawen ale weeni dii a ta va Ayab yenni zuk la, dinyi mɛ la a kan yuli bɛ. Naawen a nye dii ate wa puulim a ta va wa tomteerɔwa Elaja zuk la kama.>> 11Dila Jeyu a jam ko waai meena ale jam bo Jezreel a tali bo Ayab yenni la kama ale wa naawa kpaŋŋa meena ale wa doa baai ale moata wa la ale wa kaabteerɔma, wa an jam tali nuru vuuwa.
12Jeyu a jam gomsi kama a duŋ Samaria. Bet Eked po naapeerisaŋa jigini, 13wa jam tu ka Juda naawa Ayaziya nuruba gela a yaa bek ba ayen, <<Nama ka bana?>> Ba yaa weeni ayen, <<Tama ka Ayaziya nuruba, ti be jam kama ayen ti puusi naawa ale wa powa dɔkdemma.>>
14Wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni yik ba vuta.>> Dila ba jam yik ba a ta ga tɔgri Bet Eked vinni, ba jam ka nuruba pisinaansi ale baye. Wa an jam basi nuru.
15Wa ale jam basi dula la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, wa jam ka Arekab nidoabinni Jeyonadab zuk, waai ale bo suik po a cheŋ ayen wa ga tu wa. Jeyu a jam puusi wa kama ale weeni ayen, <<Fi va m nɔi ya, ase m le bo ale fu diila?>> Jeyonadab yaa tulisi ayen, <<M va fi nɔi kama.>> Jeyu yaa weeni ayen, <<Ku abe dan ka dila, yik m nisa.>> Ate wa jam nye dila, ate Jeyu a maari wa ate wa jueli wusum torokowa. 16Jeyu yaa weeni ayen, <<Jam va mu a nya m nyiŋ ale a zeenti dii a te Naawen la.>> Ate wa te wa maa kali wa wusum torokowa zuk.
17Jeyu ale ga jam Samaria la, wa jam ko Ayab dɔkdemma meena ale jam tali la kama, wa jam kaasi ba kama a magsi chaab ale Naawen wanni ate wa jam weeni Elaja la.
18Ate Jeyu a ta nuruma meena a jam jigi yeŋ a yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ayab a tom ka nna maga a te Baal. Jeyu ale tom ka nna yegayega a te wa. 19Yɔgyɔgla de wi Baal biisiteerɔma meena ate ba jam ale baai ale tom a te wa la meena ale wa kaabteerɔma meena. Nya ate waai a kan bɛ, dii nyiŋla mi a yaali m nye ka kaab kpieŋ a te Baal. Waai ale kan baga a jam la, a kan boro.>> Alege Jeyu a jam a paasi kama ayen wa baga a kaasi baai ale tom a te Baal la.
20Jeyu yaa jam weeni ayen, <<Wi ate nuruba tigsi Baal yuenni nyiŋ.>> Dila ba yaa jam mooli. 21Ate wa yaa jam te nɔi Izirali meena po, ate baai meena ale a tom a te Baal la a jam, nuru yeŋ mɛ la an tali ya. Ba jam fakka chaab Baal yenni po ate jigi meena a sueri. 22Ate Jeyu a weeni waai ale a nya gattaŋa dueni ka jigini la ayen, <<Ta gatta a jam te baai meena ale tom a te Baal la.>> Dila wa yaa ta gatta a jam te ba.
23Ate Jeyu ale Arekab nidoabinni Jeyonadab a jam cheŋ Baal yenni po. Jeyu yaa weeni baai ale tom a te Baal la ayen, <<Gisi nya ate Naawen tomteerɔma waai a kan bo dela ale fu. Ka baai ale tom a te Baal la nyiini.>> 24Dila ba cheŋ jo ayen ba nye kaabka ale juka tiirita. Yɔgyɔgla de Jeyu te ka nuruba pinaanuŋ ate ba za peelim ale kaamka de ayen, <<Ase ni wanyi a dan te nuruma de ate m pai a nyo ni nisa po la a dan bɛ, ka ni nyuvooŋa ate ni ale pai a tagri.>>
25Jeyu ale ga nye juka tiirimu a nueri la, wa yaa weeni limisidɔma ale kpaŋŋa ayen, <<Ni jo ko ba, ni kan te ba wanyi mɛ la a chali bɛ.>> Dila ba pai gebik woŋ a che ba lɔnsi tɛŋ. Limisidɔma ale kpaŋŋa a jam yuk ba nyiŋsaŋa a basi ka peelim ale jo Baal kaabka poi po dɔkku. 26Ba jam ta ka ba tintain weleŋka ale bo Baal yenni po la a nyini ju basi. 27Ba jam kaasi Baal tintain ferimaŋa kama ale nak Baal yenni a lɔnsi, ate nuruba a pai ku a chim binta zaanika jigi a jam paari jinla de.
28Dila Jeyu a yaa kaasi Baal puusika yenni Izirali po. 29Alege wa an jam basi Nebat nidoabinni Jeroboam wabaataŋa, dii ate wa nye ate Izirali a puusi naabisa ate ba pai ligmɔniŋ a nye Betel ale Dan po la.
30Naawen a jam weeni Jeyu kama ayen, <<Fi ale nye nalimnyiini a baga a nye dii ale nala mi nina po la nyiŋ ale nye dii meena ale bo m popola po ayen m pai nye Ayab yenni la nyiŋ, fi ŋaaŋbisa ale kali Izirali naam zukpaglika zuk a paari gaŋsa bunaansiwa po.>> 31Alege Jeyu an jam kpesi ta Naawen dii ale ka Izirali Wen la sinsaŋŋa ale wa suinum meena. Wa an jam basi Jeroboam wabaataŋa, tii ate wa te ate Izirali a nye la.
32Va ŋala po Naawen yaa piilim nye ate Izirali ale soa diila a siŋ tɛŋ. Yazael a jam nya pagrim Izirali demma zuk kama ba tɛŋka meena po. 33Jodan koni po ale Gad ale Aruben ale Manasa ale bo Gilead tɛŋka po la, a nyini Aroer a va Arnon Buboalika a ga va Gilead a cheŋ Basan.
34Dan ka Jeyu naamu wayoŋ tintila ale dii meena ate wa jam nye la, ŋala a ŋmarisi dua Izirali nalimaŋa gbaŋka po kama.
35Jeyu a jam kpi kama ase wa koma la, ate ba gu wa Samaria po. Ate wa nidoabinni Jeyoayaz a tagri wa a chim naab. 36Jeyu a dɛ naam Izirali zuk Samaria po a paari ka bena pisiye ale naaniŋ.

english_text:
Queen Athaliah of Judah
(2 Chronicles 22.10-12)
1As soon as Athaliah heard that her son King Ahaziah was dead, she decided to kill any relative who could possibly become king. She would have done that, 2but Jehosheba rescued Joash son of Ahaziah just as he was about to be murdered. Jehosheba, who was Jehoram's daughter and Ahaziah's half sister, hid her nephew Joash and his personal servant in a bedroom in the Lord's temple where he was safe from Athaliah. 3Joash hid in the temple with Jehosheba for six years while Athaliah ruled as queen of Judah.
Jehoiada Makes Joash King of Judah
(2 Chronicles 23.1-21)
4Joash son of Ahaziah had hidden in the Lord's temple six years. Then in the seventh year, Jehoiada the priest sent for the commanders of the king's special bodyguards and the commanders of the palace guards. They met him at the temple, and he asked them to make a promise in the name of the Lord. Then he brought out Joash 5and said to them:
Here's what I want you to do. Three of your guard units will be on duty on the Sabbath. I want one unit to guard the palace. 6Another unit will guard Sur Gate, and the third unit will guard the palace gate and relieve the palace guards.
7The other two guard units are supposed to be off duty on the Sabbath. But I want both of them to stay here at the temple and protect King Joash. 8Make sure they follow him wherever he goes, and tell them to keep their swords ready to kill anyone who tries to get near him.
9The commanders followed Jehoiada's orders. Each one called together his guards—those coming on duty and those going off duty. 10Jehoiada brought out the swords and shields that had belonged to King David and gave them to the commanders. 11Then they gave the weapons to their guards, who took their positions around the temple and the altar to protect Joash on every side.
12Jehoiada brought Joash outside, where he placed the crown on his head and gave him a copy of instructions for ruling the nation. Olive oil was poured on his head to show that he was now king, while the crowd clapped and shouted, “Long live the king!”
13Queen Athaliah heard the crowd and went to the temple. 14 There she saw Joash standing by one of the columns, which was the usual place for the king. The singers and the trumpet players were standing next to him, and the people were celebrating and blowing trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes in anger and shouted, “You betrayed me, you traitors!”
15At once, Jehoiada said to the army commanders, “Kill her! But don't do it anywhere near the Lord's temple. Take her out in front of the troops and kill anyone who is with her!” 16So the commanders dragged her to the gate where horses are led into the palace, and they killed her there.
17Jehoiada the priest asked King Joash and the people to promise that they would be faithful to each other and to the Lord. 18Then the crowd went to the temple built to honor Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and idols and killed Mattan the priest of Baal right in front of the altars.
After Jehoiada had placed guards around the Lord's temple, 19he called together all the commanders, the king's special bodyguards, the palace guards, and the people. They led Joash from the temple, through the Guards' Gate, and into the palace. He took his place on the throne and became king of Judah. 20Everyone celebrated because Athaliah had been killed and Jerusalem was peaceful again. 21Joash was only seven years old when this happened.
translation_text:
1Ataliaya ale ka Ayaziya ma la, ale ga nya ayen wa nidoabinni a kpi kama la, wa cheŋ kama a ga kaasi naab yeri dɔkdemma meena. 2Alege Jeyoseba ale ka Naab Joram lie la ale ŋman chim Ayaziya toa la, a jam zu pai ka Joas ale ka Ayaziya nidoabili la, a ta nyini nabisaŋa po, baai ate ba za ba ko la. Wa jam pai wa ale waai ale a nya wa la a basi ka goom dɔk po, a suk wa a nyini Ataliaya jigi ate ba an jam ko wa. 3Wa jam suk bo ka Naawen yenni po ale waai ale a nya wa la a paari bena ŋayuebi alege ate Ataliaya a nya tɛŋka zuk.
4Bena ŋayopɔiwa po Jeyoiada a jam tom wi ka kpaga ale a de kpaliŋsa niŋ la labka ale paari kook ale Kari demma ale limisidɔba ate ba ta ba a jam wa jigi Naawen yenni po. Wa jam nye ka nɔiyeŋ ale ba a basi ate ba pɛ Naawen yenni po. Ate wa yaa pai naawa nidoabinni sak ba. 5Wa jam weeni ba kama ayen, <<Ni ale za ni nye diila ale nna. Nama beŋsa butawa ale za ni bo tuima po Vuusumu danni la, ni po bunyi a nya naab yenni zuk, 6bunyi mɛ a nya Sur nansuiŋku, bunyi mɛ a bo nansuiŋku limisidɔwa ŋaaŋ, baai ale tagri chaab a nya Naawen yenni la 7ate nama baai ale bo beŋsa buyewa po ate ni nyiem kan cheŋ tuima Vuusumu danni la, ni meena ale nya ka Naawen yenni zuk a te naawa. 8Ni zaani a gilim naawa, nuru meena abe ta wa kpaliŋ kɔlima wa nisa po. Waai a dan jam ni jigi, ku a fɛ ate ni ko wa. Ni za moata naawa juijui meena ate wa a cheŋ la.>>
9Kpaŋŋa ale a nya labka kook zuk la a jam nye ka dii dek ate Jeyoiada kaabteerɔwa a jam weeni la. Waai meena a jam ta ka wa nuruba. Baai ale a cheŋ tuima Vuusumu danni ale baai ale kaa cheŋ tuima Vuusumu danni la, a jan jam Jeyoiada kaabteerɔwa jigi. 10Ate wa pai gbattaŋa ale kpaliŋ ŋanchɔgsintaŋa ate Deevid jam soa ate ŋa bo Naawen yenni po la a te kpaŋŋa. 11Limisidɔma wanyi meena a jam ta ka wa kpaliŋ kɔlima wa nisa po a zaani gilim naawa a moata kuŋkuŋku ale Naawen yenni, a nyini yeseoku geŋsa ta a cheŋ Naawen yenni wiilukku geŋsa.
12Jeyoiada a ta ka naawa nidoabinni nyini peelim a pai naam zutɔk a vuk wa. Wa te wa ka nɔiyeŋka gbaŋka ale weeni ayen wa ka naab. Ba jam bobi wa kama, ate nuruma a jam nak nisa ale nuem ayen, <<Naabaa, ta nyuvu woŋ!>>
13Ataliaya ale jam wom nuemka a nyini limisidɔma ale nuruma jigi la, wa jam cheŋ ka nuruma ale bo Naawen yenni la jigi. 14Wa jam nya ka naawa ale wa za zaŋŋi tɛŋ ase ku le ka ba nyeka la. Kpaŋŋa ale damuniŋ peerisaŋa a za naawa tɛŋ, ate tɛŋka demma meena a dɛ masim ale a peeri ba damunsaŋa. Ate a Ataliaya yaa cheeri wa garuk woŋtaŋa ale weeni ayen, <<Ninmuna wari! Ninmuna wari!>>
15Jeyoiada ale ka kaabteerɔ la yaa weeni kpaŋŋa ale a nya labka kook zuk la ate ba a nya tugurik tommu zuk la ayen, <<Ni ta wa nyini peelim, abe waai ale a va wa la ni te ate gebik woŋ a siŋ wa zuk.>> Diila kaabteerɔwa a weeni kama ayen, <<Ku a fɛ ate ba kan ko wa Naawen yenni po.>> 16Dila ba yaa yik wa ase wa ale paari wusumaŋa ale a jo naab yenni peelimmu po la, dula ate ba jam ko wa.
17Jeyoiada yaa nye nɔiyeŋ ale Naawen ale naawa ale nuruma ayen ba ale chim ka Naawen nuruba. Wa jam nyeka nɔiyeŋ mɛ ale naawa ale nuruma. 18Nuruma meena ale bo tɛŋka zuk la a jam cheŋ ka Baal yenni po a dari di lɔnsi tɛŋ. Ba jam kaasi kuŋkuŋtaŋa ale bɔgtaŋa ka nna yariyari ale kɔ Matan ale ka Baal kaabteerɔ a bo kuŋkuŋtaŋa niŋ la. Ate Jeyoiada ale ka kaabteerɔ la a jam pai limisidɔba ate ba bo Naawen yenni. 19Wa jam maa ta ka kpaga ŋaai ale a nya kobsa zuk la ale Kari demma ale limisidɔma ale nuruma meena ale bo tɛŋka zuk la, ate ba gum chaab a ta naawa a nyini Naawen yenni a cheŋ naab yenni, ba jam va limisidɔma ale bo nansuiŋ kuui la a jo. Naawa yaa jam kali naam zukpaglika zuk, 20ate nuruma meena ale bo tɛŋka po la a jam dɛ masim. Ate tɛŋka a jam yok, dii nyiŋla ba ale pai gebik woŋ a ko Ataliaya naab yenni la nyiŋ.
21Jeyoas a jam ta ka bena ŋayopɔi ale piilim naam dɛka.

english_text:
King Joash of Judah
(2 Chronicles 24.1-16)
1Joash became king of Judah in Jehu's seventh year as king of Israel, and he ruled 40 years from Jerusalem. His mother Zibiah was from the town of Beersheba.
2Jehoiada the priest taught Joash what was right, and so for the rest of his life Joash obeyed the Lord. 3But even Joash did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
4 One day, Joash said to the priests, “Collect all the money that has been given to the Lord's temple, whether from taxes or gifts, 5and use it to repair the temple whenever you see the need.”
6But the priests never started repairing the temple. So in the twenty-third year of his rule, 7Joash called for Jehoiada and the other priests and said, “Why aren't you using the money to repair the temple? Don't take any more money for yourselves. It is only to be used to pay for the repairs.” 8The priests agreed that they would not collect any more money or be in charge of the temple repairs.
9Jehoiada found a wooden box; he cut a hole in the top of it and set it on the right side of the altar where people went into the temple. Whenever someone gave money to the temple, the priests guarding the entrance would put it into this box. 10When the box was full of money, the king's secretary and the chief priest would count the money and put it in bags. 11Then they would give it to the men supervising the repairs to the temple. Some of the money was used to pay the builders, the woodworkers, 12the stonecutters, and the men who built the walls. And some was used to buy wood and stone and to pay any other costs for repairing the temple.
13While the repairs were being made, the money that was given to the temple was not used to make silver bowls, lamp snuffers, small sprinkling bowls, trumpets, or anything gold or silver for the temple. 14It went only to pay for repairs. 15 The men in charge were honest, so no one had to keep track of the money.
16 The fines that had to be paid along with the sacrifices to make things right and the sacrifices for sin did not go to the temple. This money belonged only to the priests.
17About the same time, King Hazael of Syria attacked the town of Gath and captured it. Next, he decided to attack Jerusalem. 18So Joash collected everything he and his ancestors Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah had dedicated to the Lord, as well as the gold in the storage rooms in the temple and palace. He sent it all to Hazael as a gift, and when Hazael received it, he ordered his troops to leave Jerusalem.
19Everything else Joash did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 20-21At the end of his rule, some of his officers rebelled against him. Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer murdered him in a building where the land was filled in on the east side of Jerusalem, near the road to Silla. Joash was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Amaziah became king.
translation_text:
1Jeyu bena ŋayopɔiwa po, ate Jeyoas a chim naab, wa jam dɛ naam Jerusalem po ka bena pisinaansi. Wa mawa yue jam le Zibiya. Wa jam nyini ka Beerseba. 2Jeyoas a jam nyeka dii ale nala Naawen nina po bena ŋaai meena ate Jeyoiada kaabteerɔwa a jam a sak wa la. 3Alege wa an jam yeeri kaabka kunkutimaŋa a basi ya. Nuruba jam kasim cheŋ kama a ga a nye kaabka ale a ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la.
4Jeyoas a jam weeni kaabteerɔma kama ayen, <<Tuesi tuilum ŋantaŋa ligraŋa meena ate ba ta jam Naawen yenni po la ate ni tuesi nuruma chiinika po la, ale ligra ŋaai ate ni tuesi nyini nuruba ale nye ba puulimka la ale ligra ŋaai ate nuruba dek a poli ayen ba ta jam Naawen yenni po la. 5Basi ate kaabteerɔ meena a tuesi ligraŋa a nyini ligtaarɔma po wanyi, ate ba pai a gomsi Naawen yenni kab tii meena ale kaasi la.>>
6Alege Naab Jeyoas bena pisiye ale ŋatawa po, kaabteerɔma an diem jam gomsi Naawen yenni. 7Dila nyiŋ Jeyoas a yaa wi Jeyoiada kaabteerɔwa ale kaabteerɔ mbala a bek ba ayen, <<Ka boan nyiŋ ate ni kan gomsi Naawen yenni kab tii ale kaasi la? Ni kan ŋman tuesi ligra a nyini ni ligtaarɔma jigi ya, alege ni pai ŋa a te a magsi Naawen yenni gomsika.>> 8Kaabteerɔma a jam siak kama ayen ba a kan ŋman tuesi ligri a nyini nuruma jigi ya. Badek abe kan gomsi Naawen yenni.
9Jeyoiada kaabteerɔwa yaa jam pai dakari nanlik a vuri vɔrup. Wa jam pai dueni ka kuŋkuŋku tɛŋ a bo a juga geŋsa ase nuruba ale a jo Naawen yenni la. Kaabteerɔma ale za a nya nansuiŋku la yaa pai ligraŋa meena ate ba pai nyo dakanni po la a ta jam Naawen yenni. 10Ba dan ga nya ayen ligra a zuak a bo dakanni po, naab yenni gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa ale kaabteerɔ kpioŋku nyiem yaa jam a chiini ligraŋa ate ba ta jam Naawen yenni po la a nyo boorisa po. 11Ase ba dan nya ligraŋa nɔi ale ka diila, ba yaa pai ligraŋa a te nidoa baai ate ba lueri ayen ba a nya Naawen yenni tuimaŋa zuk la. Ba jam pai ka ligra ŋala po a tuni baai ale a tom Naawen yenni la ale danagrɔma ale seerɔma. 12Seerɔma ale baai ale a peesi tana la. Ba jam da ka daata ale tintain peesima ayen ba pai a gomsi Naawen yenni ale te dii meena ale magsi Naawen yenni gomsika la.
13Ligraŋa ate ba jam ta jam Naawen yenni po la, ba an jam pai nye daa kpana china yaase zeuŋta boomsa ŋangebinta, yaase misika china, yaase damunsa yaase ŋan baai ate ba pai ligmɔniŋ yaase kpana a nye a basi Naawen yenni po la. 14Ba jam pai ŋa a tuni ka tuimtomdɔma ale pai ŋa a da kɔlima a magsi Naawen yenni gomsika. 15Ba an jam bek baai ate ba te ligraŋa ayen ba pai tuni tuimtomdɔma la ayen ba weeni ba ale pai ŋa a nye diila, dii nyiŋla ba jam tom ale ka wensie. 16Ba an jam pai foolaa ale tom kaasika tiiritaŋa a ta jo Naawen yenni po. Ka kaabteerɔma ale jam soa ŋala.
17Ase nna po de la Yazael Araam naawa a jam cheŋ ga siti Gat a nya nakdeka ba zuk. Ate wa ŋman cheem ayen wa siti Jerusalem. 18Alege Jeyoas Juda naawa a jam pai ka ŋan baai meena ale ta tuilum ate wa koma Jeyosafat ale Jeyoram ale Ayaziya Juda nalimaŋa ale tuilum ŋantaŋa ate wa mɛ dek a jam pai ti a nyo Naawen nisa po la ale ligmɔniŋka meena ale bo Naawen yenni po la ale naab yenni po la, a ta cheŋ ga te Yazael Araam naawa la, ate wa basi tugurika ate wa a yaali ayen wa nye ale Jerusalem la.
19Dan ka Joas naamu wayoŋ tintila ale dii meena ate wa jam nye la, ŋala a ŋmarisi doa Juda nalimaŋa gbaŋka po kama. 20Wa kpaŋŋa a jam nya ka chaab a ko Joas Bet Millo, suik kuui ale va a siŋ Silla la. 21Kpaŋŋa baai ale jam ko wa la jam le Jozabad ale ka Simeat nidoabili la ale Jeyozabad ale ka Somer nidoabili la. Wa jam kpi kama ate ba gu wa ale wa koma Deevid Tɛŋka po. Ate wa nidoabinni Amaziya a tagri wa a chim naab.

english_text:
King Jehoahaz of Israel
1Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king of Israel in the twenty-third year of Joash's rule in Judah. Jehoahaz ruled 17 years from Samaria 2and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He never stopped following the example of Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
