7Wa jam pai ka Asera zaŋni ate wa nye la, a ta ga dueni Naawen yenni po, dii ate Naawen a weeni Deevid ale wa nidoabinni Solomon ayen, <<Yenni de ale Jerusalem po, dii ate m lueri nyini Izirali buuni meena po la, ate m le pai m Yuenni a dueni du taam wuu. 8M kan ŋman nye ate Izirali demma a cheŋ tuiri a nyini tɛŋ kaai ate m pai te ba kokpieŋsaŋa la, ase ba ale kpesi nye dii meena ate m weeni ba la ale ta Sinsaŋŋa meena ate m tomteerɔwa Moosis a pai te ba la.>> 9Alege nuruma an jam wom ya. Manasa a jam ta ba cheŋ be kama, ate ba kasim nye biem a gaam tɛŋ kpieŋ sii ate Naawen a kaasi si Izirali demma niŋ la.
10Naawen a jam weeni kama a va wa tomteerɔma biisiteerɔma zuk ayen, 11<<Juda naawa Manasa a nye ka biem buui ate Naawen a kisa. Wa nye ka biem a gaam Amori demma baai ale de wa niŋ la ale ta Juda a jo biem po ale wa bɔgtaŋa. 12Dila nyiŋla, Naawen dii ale ka Izirali Wenni ale a weeni ayen, M ta ka kaasuŋ a cheena Jerusalem ale Juda zuk ate nuru baai meena ale a wom la kpaziim ale nak. 13M le teeri cheŋ Jerusalem zuk ale m magsika miika ate m jam pai basi Samaria zuk la ale m miŋka miika ate m jam pai tom Ayab yenni la. M le duisi Jerusalem a basi ase ba ale a nari china a tulim a vuk diila. 14M le zɛri nuru baai ale tali la, a pai ba a te ba dachaasaŋa. Ba dachaasaŋa ale nak de ba abe ba kɔlim ba, 15dii nyiŋla ba nye ka biem m nina po ale nye ate m sui a puuri a nyini da dii dai ate ba kokpieŋsaŋa a basi Ejipiti a jam paari jinla de la.>>
16A ŋman gum du Manasa a jam ko ka nuru baai ale kan seba wari nɔi po la nna yegayega, ate ku lik Jerusalem tɛŋka meena, wa abe le nye ate Juda a nye biem buui la an maa gum du, ate ku nye ate ba nye biem Naawen nina po.
17Dii ale nye Manasa naamu vaaŋa po la ale dii meena ate wa nye la ale waba tii ate wa nye la, ŋala a ŋmarisi a doa ka Juda nalimaŋa gbaŋka po. 18Manasa a jam kpi kama a vuusi ale wa koma, ate ba gu wa naab yenni talim fiika po. Uzza ale jam soa bu. Ate wa nidoabinni Amon a chim naab a tagri wa.
19Amon a jam ta ka bena pisiye ale ŋaye alege chim naab. Wa jam nya Jerusalem zuk ka bena ŋaye. Wa mawa yuei jam le Mesullemet. Wa be jam ka Yaruz lie. Wa jam nyini ka Jotba. 20Wa jam nye ka biem Naawen nina po, ase wa kowa Manasa ale jam nye diila. 21Wa jam va ka wa kowa suitaŋa meena. Wa jam kaab ka bɔgta tii ate wa kowa a jam a kaab la ale koori tɛŋ a te ti. 22Wa jam zɛri Naawen dii ale ka wa koma Wenni ale an cheŋ va Naawen suiku.
23Amon kpaŋŋa a jam suk a nya ka chaab a ko naawa wa naab yenni po. 24Ate tɛŋka nuruma yaa ko baai meena ale jam nye susuga popola a va naab Amon la, ate ba bobi wa nidoabinni Josia ate wa chim naab a tagri wa.
25Dii ale nye Amon naamu vaaŋa po la, ale wa ale nye diila, ŋala a ŋmarisi a doa ka Juda nalimaŋa gbaŋka po. 26Ba jam gu wa ka wa boosuku po Uzza kadukka po. Ate wa nidoabinni Josia a chim naab a tagri wa.

english_text:
King Josiah of Judah
(2 Chronicles 34.1,2)
1 Josiah was 8 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled 31 years from Jerusalem. His mother Jedidah was the daughter of Adaiah from Bozkath. 2Josiah always obeyed the Lord, just as his ancestor David had done.
Hilkiah Finds The Book of God's Law
(2 Chronicles 34.8-28)
3After Josiah had been king for 18 years, he told Shaphan, one of his highest officials:
Go to the Lord's temple 4and ask Hilkiah the high priest to collect from the guards all the money that the people have donated. 5Tell Hilkiah to give it to the men supervising the repairs to the temple. They can use some of the money to pay 6the workers, and with the rest of it they can buy wood and stone for the repair work. 7 They are honest, so we won't ask them to keep track of the money.
8While Shaphan was at the temple, Hilkiah handed him a book and said, “Look what I found here in the temple—The Book of God's Law.”
Shaphan read it, 9then went back to Josiah and reported, “Your officials collected the money in the temple and gave it to the men supervising the repairs. 10But there's something else, Your Majesty. The priest Hilkiah gave me this book.” Then Shaphan read it out loud.
11When Josiah heard what was in The Book of God's Law, he tore his clothes in sorrow. 12At once he called together Hilkiah, Shaphan, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Achbor son of Micaiah, and his own servant Asaiah. He said, 13“The Lord must be furious with me and everyone else in Judah, because our ancestors did not obey the laws written in this book. Go find out what the Lord wants us to do.”
14The five men left at once and went to talk with Huldah the prophet. Her husband was Shallum, who was in charge of the king's clothes. Huldah lived in the northern part of Jerusalem, and when they met in her home, 15she said:
You were sent here by King Josiah, and this is what the Lord God of Israel says to him: 16“Josiah, I am the Lord! And I will see to it that this country and everyone living in it will be destroyed. It will happen just as this book says. 17The people of Judah have rejected me. They have offered sacrifices to foreign gods and have worshiped their own idols. I cannot stand it any longer. I am furious.
18“Josiah, listen to what I am going to do. 19I noticed how sad you were when you read that this country and its people would be completely wiped out. You even tore your clothes in sorrow, and I heard you cry. 20So I will let you die in peace, before I destroy this place.”
The men left and took Huldah's answer back to Josiah.
translation_text:
1Josia a jam ta ka bena naaniŋ ale jam chim naab, ate wa nya Jerusalem zuk a paari bena pisita ale dinyi. Wa mawa yuei jam le Jedida, ate wa chim Adaiya lie. Wa jam nyini ka Bozkat. 2Wa jam nye ka dii ale nala Naawen niŋ ale va wa kowa Deevid suitaŋa meena, wa abe an jam viriŋ a gala yaase a juga.
3Naab Josia ale jam de wa naamu a paari bena pi ale naaniŋ la, wa yaa tom gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa Safan ate wa chim Azaliya nidoabili ate wa kokpieŋka a chim Mesullam ayen wa cheŋ Naawen yenni. Wa jam weeni kama ayen, 4<<Cheŋ kaabteerɔ kpioŋku Yilkia jigi a weeni wa ate wa gomsi ligraŋa ate ba ta jam Naawen yenni po, ate nansuiŋku nuruma a tuesi nyini nuruma jigi la. 5Te ate ba pai ŋa a te nidoa baai ate ba lueri ba ayen ba a nya Naawen yenni tuimaŋa zuk la. Ate nidoama de a tuni tuimtomdɔ baai ale a tebi Naawen yenni la. 6Ba le pai danagrɔba ale seerɔba. Abe fi te ate ba da daata ale tana ŋaai ate ba gomsi la ate ba pai a tebi Naawen yenni. 7Alege ba kan namsi badek a chiini ba ale pai ligraŋa a nye diila, dii nyiŋla ba a tom ale ka wensie.>>
8Kaabteerɔ kpioŋku Yilkia yaa weeni gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa Safan ayen, <<M nya Sinsaŋŋa Gbaŋka Naawen yenni po kama.>> Wa yaa pai te Safan ate wa karim ka. 9Ate gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa Safan yaa cheŋ naawa jigi a ga weeni sak wa ayen, <<Fi kpaŋŋa a tuni ligraŋa ale bo Naawen yenni po la kama a pai nyo tuimtomdɔma ale baai ale a nya di zuk a bo Naawen yenni la.>> 10Ate gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa a weeni sak naawa ayen, <<Kaabteerɔ kpioŋku Yilkia a te mi ka gbaŋ.>> Ate Safan a zaani naawa niŋ a kariŋ dii ale bo gbaŋka bo la.
11Naawa ale ga wom Sinsaŋŋa wieŋa ale bo Gbaŋka po la, wa yaa dari wa gattaŋa a cheeri. 12Wa jam weeni ka wieŋa de a te kaabteerɔwa Yilkia ale Safan nidoabinni Ayikam ale Mikaiya nidoabinni Achbor ale gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa Safan ale naawa ŋaaŋviirɔwa Asaiya ayen, 13<<Ni cheŋ a ga bek Naawen nya te mi ale nuruma ale Juda meena a va chaab ale dii ale ŋmarisi gbaŋka de po ate ba nya la. Naawen sui a puuri ale ti ka nna yegayega, dii nyiŋla ti koma an wom wieŋa ale bo gbaŋka de po la. Ba an nye a va chaab ale dii meena ale ŋmarisi a va tama nyiŋla.>>
14Kaabteerɔwa Yilkia ale Ayikam ale Achbor ale Safan ale Asaiya a jam cheŋ ayen ba biisi ale Wen biisiteerɔwa Yulda waai ale ka nipok la, ate wa chim Tikva nidoabinni Sallum pok ate wa ŋaaŋbiika a chim Yaryas, ate wa a nya gatta zuk la. Yulda a jam bo ka Jerusalem po Tɛŋ Kaai Ale Labi Bunaansiwa La, Siyewa po.
15Nipowa jam weeni ba kama ayen, <<Naawen dii ale ka Izirali Wen la ale a weeni diila ale nna, <Ni weeni nuru waai ale tom ni mi jigi la ayen, 16<<Naawen a weeni kama ayen. M le ta kaasuŋ a jam jigini de ale nuruma zuk ta va chaab ale dii meena ale ŋmarisi gbaŋka po ate Juda naawa kariŋ la. 17Ba ale zɛri mi ale ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la a te wen yona ale nye ate m suinni a puuri ale bɔgtaŋa meena ate ba pai ba nisa a nye la, m suinni ale kasim a dɛ ale dela jigini ate di kan yɔgi.>> > 18<<Ni ga weeni Juda naawa, waai ale tom ni ayen ni ga kpesi wom nyini Naawen jigi la ayen, <Dii ate Naawen, Izirali Wenni a weeni a magsi chaab ale wieŋa ate fi wom la ale nna: 19fi suinummu ale siak ate fi zaab fidek Naawen niŋ la nyiŋ, ase fi le wom dii ate m weeni a basi jigini de ale ka nuruma la, ayen ba le nya kikaasa ate ba kan ta kiri ya, ate fi a cheeri fi gattaŋa ale kum mi niŋ la nyiŋ, m wom fu kama, ka Naawen ale a weeni. 20Mi ale basi ate fi kpi paari fi koma ate ba gu fu ale suiyɔgni. Fi nina a kan nya kaasuŋku de meena ate mi a yaali ayen m ta jam dela jigini la.> >> Ba yaa jam ta nipowa ale tulisi diila a ga weeni naawa.

english_text:
Josiah Reads The Book of God's Law
(2 Chronicles 34.29-33)
1King Josiah called together the older leaders of Judah and Jerusalem. 2Then he went to the Lord's temple, together with the people of Judah and Jerusalem, the priests, and the prophets. Finally, when everybody was there, he read aloud The Book of God's Law that had been found in the temple.
3After Josiah had finished reading, he stood by one of the columns. He asked the people to promise in the Lord's name to faithfully obey the Lord and to follow his commands. The people agreed to do everything written in the book.
Josiah Follows the Teachings of God's Law
(2 Chronicles 34.3-7)
4 Josiah told Hilkiah the priest, the assistant priests, and the guards at the temple door to go into the temple and bring out the things used to worship Baal, Asherah, and the stars. Josiah had these things burned in Kidron Valley just outside Jerusalem, and he had the ashes carried away to the town of Bethel.
5Josiah also got rid of the pagan priests at the local shrines in Judah and around Jerusalem. These were the men that the kings of Judah had appointed to offer sacrifices to Baal and to the sun, moon, and stars. 6Josiah had the sacred pole for Asherah brought out of the temple and taken to Kidron Valley, where it was burned. He then had its ashes ground into dust and scattered over the public cemetery there. 7He had the buildings torn down where the male prostitutes lived next to the temple, and where the women wove sacred robes for the idol of Asherah.
8In almost every town in Judah, priests had been offering sacrifices to the Lord at local shrines. Josiah brought these priests to Jerusalem and had their shrines made unfit for worship—every shrine from Geba just north of Jerusalem to Beersheba in the south. He even tore down the shrine at Beersheba that was just to the left of Joshua Gate, which was named after the highest official of the city. 9Those local priests could not serve at the Lord's altar in Jerusalem, but they were allowed to eat sacred bread, just like the priests from Jerusalem.
10 Josiah sent some men to Hinnom Valley just outside Jerusalem with orders to make the altar there unfit for worship. That way, people could no longer use it for sacrificing their children to the god Molech. 11He also got rid of the horses that the kings of Judah used in their ceremonies to worship the sun, and he destroyed the chariots along with them. The horses had been kept near the entrance to the Lord's temple, in a courtyard close to where an official named Nathan-Melech lived.
12 Some of the kings of Judah, especially Manasseh, had built altars in the two courts of the temple and in the room that Ahaz had built on the palace roof. Josiah had these altars torn down and smashed to pieces, and he had the pieces thrown into Kidron Valley, just outside Jerusalem. 13 After that, he closed down the shrines that Solomon had built east of Jerusalem and south of Spoil Hill to honor Astarte the disgusting goddess of Sidon, Chemosh the disgusting god of Moab, and Milcom the disgusting god of Ammon. 14He tore down the stone images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred pole used in the worship of Asherah. Then he had the whole area covered with human bones.
15 But Josiah was not finished yet. At Bethel he destroyed the shrine and the altar that Jeroboam son of Nebat had built and that had caused the Israelites to sin. Josiah had the shrine and the Asherah pole burned and ground into dust. 16 As he looked around, he saw graves on the hillside. He had the bones in them dug up and burned on the altar, so that it could no longer be used. This happened just as God's prophet had said when Jeroboam was standing at the altar, celebrating a festival.
Then Josiah saw the grave of the prophet who had said this would happen 17 and he asked, “Whose grave is that?”
Some people who lived nearby answered, “It belongs to the prophet from Judah who told what would happen to this altar.”
18Josiah replied, “Then leave it alone. Don't dig up his bones.” So they did not disturb his bones or the bones of the old prophet from Israel who had also been buried there.
19Some of the Israelite kings had made the Lord angry by building pagan shrines all over Israel. So Josiah sent troops to destroy these shrines just as he had done to the one in Bethel. 20He killed the priests who served at them and burned their bones on the altars.
After all that, Josiah went back to Jerusalem.
Josiah and the People of Judah Celebrate Passover
(2 Chronicles 35.1-19)
21Josiah told the people of Judah, “Celebrate Passover in honor of the Lord your God, just as it says in The Book of God's Law.”
22This festival had not been celebrated in this way since the time that tribal leaders ruled Israel or the kings ruled Israel and Judah. 23But in Josiah's eighteenth year as king of Judah, everyone came to Jerusalem to celebrate Passover.
The Lord Is Still Angry with the People of Judah
24Josiah got rid of every disgusting person and thing in Judah and Jerusalem—including magicians, fortunetellers, and idols. He did his best to obey every law written in the book that the priest Hilkiah found in the Lord's temple. 25No other king before or after Josiah tried as hard as he did to obey the Law of Moses.
26But the Lord was still furious with the people of Judah because Manasseh had done so many things to make him angry. 27The Lord said, “I will desert the people of Judah, just as I deserted the people of Israel. I will reject Jerusalem, even though I chose it to be mine. And I will abandon this temple built to honor me.”
Josiah Dies in Battle
(2 Chronicles 35.20—36.1)
28Everything else Josiah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 29During Josiah's rule, King Neco of Egypt led his army north to the Euphrates River to help the king of Assyria. Josiah led his troops north to fight Neco, but when they met in battle at Megiddo, Josiah was killed. 30A few of Josiah's servants put his body in a chariot and took it back to Jerusalem, where they buried it in his own tomb. Then the people of Judah found his son Jehoahaz and poured olive oil on his head to show that he was their new king.
King Jehoahaz of Judah
(2 Chronicles 36.2-4)
31Jehoahaz was 23 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem only 3 months. His mother Hamutal was the daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah. 32Jehoahaz disobeyed the Lord, just as some of his ancestors had done.
33King Neco of Egypt had Jehoahaz arrested and put in prison at Riblah near Hamath. Then he forced the people of Judah to pay him 3.4 tons of silver and 34 kilograms of gold as taxes. 34 Neco appointed Josiah's son Eliakim king of Judah, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. He took Jehoahaz as a prisoner to Egypt, where he died.
35Jehoiakim forced the people of Judah to pay higher taxes, so he could give Neco the silver and gold he demanded.
King Jehoiakim of Judah
(2 Chronicles 36.5-8)
36 Jehoiakim was 25 years old when he was appointed king, and he ruled 11 years from Jerusalem. His mother Zebidah was the daughter of Pedaiah from Rumah. 37Jehoiakim disobeyed the Lord by following the example of his ancestors.
translation_text:
1Ate naawa yaa jam wi Juda ale Jerusalem nisɔmma meena a ta jam jigi yeŋ. 2Wa jam cheŋ ka Naawen yenni ale Juda nidoama ale Jerusalem nuruma ale kaabteerɔma ale Wen biisiteerɔma ale nuru fiisa ale nuru kpienta meena jigi. Wa jam kariŋ ka wieŋa meena ale bo nɔiyeŋ gbaŋka po ate ba nya Naawen yenni po la ate ba wom. 3Naawa a jam zaani ka zaŋni tɛŋ a pilim nye nɔiyeŋ Naawen niŋ ayen wa le va Naawen abe wa ta wa wieŋa ale wa kaamka ale wa ŋmarisika ale wa suinum ale wa chiik meena, ate ku sak ayen nɔiyeŋ wieŋa ale ŋmarisi gbaŋka de po la ka wensie. Ate nuruma meena a puulim ayen ba le yik nɔiyeŋka a tara.
4Naawa a jam weeni ka kaabteerɔ kpioŋku Yilkia ale kaabteerɔma ale paasaŋ la ale baai ale a nya nansuiŋku la ayen ba yeeri ŋan baai meena ate ba nye te Baal ale Asera ale chiŋmarisaŋa meena ate ŋa bo Naawen yenni po la. Wa jam ta ŋa nyini Jerusalem po kama a cheŋ Kidron Viaka laŋsaŋa po a ju ŋa dula ale ta buntuemmu a cheŋ Betel. 5Wa jam basi kaabteerɔ baai ale kan seba Naawen ate Juda nalimaŋa a lueri ba ayen ba a ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la kaabka kunkutimaŋa Juda tɛŋsaŋa ale baai ale moata Jerusalem la ale baai ale a ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la a te Baal la ale wenbinni ale chiika ale chiŋmarisaŋa. 6Wa jam pai Asera zaŋni kama Naawen yenni po a nyini Jerusalem po ta cheŋ Kidron Viaka a ju di dula. Wa jam num di kama ate di chim zom ate wa yarinti bu a basi nuruba boosuta zuk. 7Wa jam kaasi diinaŋa ate nidoa taabuksaŋa a bo ŋa po la kama, ate ŋa bo Naawen yenni po la ale juijui ate nipooma a yɔk gatta a te Asera la.
8Josia a jam ta kaabteerɔma meena ate ba nyini Juda tɛŋsaŋa la kama a jam ale taŋ ba kaabka kunkutimaŋa, a zaani Geba a ga paari Beerseba, juijui ate kaabteerɔma a jam ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la. Wa jam wɛ tangbanaŋa ale bo nansuiŋtaŋa la kama, ate ku bo Josua tɛŋka kpagni nansuiŋku va jɔka jigini a gala geŋ la. 9Kaabka kunkutimaŋa kaabteerɔma an jam tom te Naawen kuŋkuŋku Jerusalem po, ba jam ŋɔbi boroborok kuui ate dabinta a ka ku po la kama ale ba kaabteerɔba mbala.
10Wa jam taŋ Tofet ale bo Ben Yinnom Viaka la kama ate waai an pai ku a nye wa nidoabili yaase wa lie kaabka bolim po a te Molek. 11Wa jam yeeri wusumaŋa ate ba mɛ a zaani Naawen yenni va joka jigini ate Juda naawa a pai te wenbinni la. Ŋa jam bo ka dabiak po a moata kpagi ate ba a wi ayen Natan Melek dɔk. Josia yaa jam ju torokoma ate ba pai te wenbinni la.
12Wa jam dari kuŋkuŋtaŋa ate Juda nalimaŋa a jam sɛ gboŋku zuk a moata Ayazi dɔkku ale bo ŋmanni la le kuŋkuŋtaŋa ate Manasa a jam sɛ a Naawen yenni dabaasa siyewa po la. Wa jam yeeri ŋa kama a nyini dula, ale nak ŋa a ŋɔriŋ nna bunabuna a ta ŋa a ga basi Kidron Viaka po. 13Naawa a jam taŋ kaabka kunkutimaŋa ale jam bo Jerusalem kori geŋ a bo Kaasuŋ Guuku yeseok geŋ la. Ŋaai ate Izirali naawa Solomon a jam sɛ a te Astoret nipok wen dii ale bie ate Saidon demma a soa la, a te Chemos wen dii ale bie ate Moab a soa la ale sɛ a te Milkom wen dii ale bie a te Ammon nuruma la. 14Josia a jam ŋɔriŋ tain weleŋsaŋa kama ale che Asera zaŋŋa a lɔnsi ale pai nuruba koba a lik jiŋŋa.
15Betel kuŋkuŋku ale kaabka kunkutuŋku ate Nebat nidoabinni Jeroboam a jam nye la, waai ale choa Izirali a basi biem po la. Kuŋkuŋku ale kaabka kunkutuŋku ate wa jam kaasi la. Wa ju kaabka kunkutuŋku ale jam num ku ase zom la ale ju Asera zaŋni mɛ a basi. 16Ate Josia ale nya gilagilawa la, wa jam nya ka boosita ale bo guuku geŋ, wa jam te ba yeeri kobaŋa kama a nyini ŋa po ale ju ŋa kuŋkuŋku zuk ayen wa taŋ ku, a va chaab ale Naawen wanni ate Wen nuruwa waai ale liŋ a mooli wieŋa de la.
17Naawa yaa bek ayen, <<Ka boan boosuk tain ale la ate mi a nya?>> Tɛŋka nuruma yaa weeni ayen, <<Ku a sak ka Wen nuruwa boosuku waai ale jam nyini Juda a weeni dii a basi Betel kuŋkuŋku nyiŋla, dila dek ale la ate fi nye ku.>>
18Wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Basi ŋa ŋadek ŋa nyiini. Kan te waai a daani wa kobaŋa.>> Ate ba jam basi wa kobaŋa ale Wen biisiteerɔ baai ale nyini Samaria la.
19Ase wa ale jam nye dii Betel la, Josia a jam yeeri ale taŋ tangbana ale kaabka kunkutimaŋa meena ate Izirali nalimaŋa a jam sɛ Samaria tɛŋsaŋa po ate ku ta suipuurum a jam Naawen jigi la kama. 20Josia a jam tɔgri kaabka kunkutimaŋa kaabteerɔma meena kama kuŋkuŋtaŋa zuima ale ju nuruba koba ŋa zuk. A yaa ŋman cheŋ Jerusalem.
21Naawa a jam weeni ka wanni de a te nuruma meena ayen, <<Ni dɛ Gaambasika Tigi a te Naawen dii ale ka ni Wen la, ase ku ale ŋmarisi bo nɔiyeŋ gbaŋka de po la.>> 22A zaani boteerɔma baai ale jam a de Izirali niŋ la, yaase Izirali nalimaŋa ale Juda nalimaŋa, Gaambasika Tigini de choa an nye nya ya. 23Alege Naab Josia bena pi ale naaniŋ po, Gaambasika Tigini a jam dɛ kama a te Naawen Jerusalem po.
24Josia a ŋman jam yeeri chichirik wiirisa ale sampoporinni ale yie po wena ale bɔgta ale kisita ŋan baai meena ale bo Juda ale Jerusalem po la kama. Wa jam nye kude a va ka chaab ale sinsaŋŋa ale ŋmarisi dii gbaŋka po ate kaabteerɔwa Yilkia a jam nya Naawen yenni po la. 25Naab a ka Josia niŋŋa yaase wa ŋaaŋŋa a nye ase wa la, ate wa cheem cheŋ Naawen jigi a nye jaab meena ale wa suinum ale wa chiik meena ale wa pagrim meena a va chaab ale dii meena ate Moosis sinsaŋŋa a weeni la.
26Alege, Naawen an jam basi wa suipuurumu ate wa jam ta ale Juda la, dii nyiŋla Manasa ale jam nye dii meena a puuri wa suinni la nyiŋ. 27Ate Naawen a weeni ayen, <<M le yeeri Juda ate wa nyini m niŋ ase m le yeeri Izirali la, ate m le zɛri Jerusalem, tɛŋ kaai ate m lueri la ale mi yenni de, ate m weeni ayen, <Dela ate m Yuenni ale boro la.> >>
28Dii ale nye Josia naamu vaaŋa po la ale dii meena ate wa nye la, ŋala a ŋmarisi a doa ka Juda nalimaŋa gbaŋka po.
29Ase Josia ale jam chim naab la, ate Ejipiti naawa Faaro Neko a jam cheŋ Yufiretis Benni ayen wa maari Assiria naawa la. Naab Josia yaa jam gɔk santiri a cheŋ ayen wa nye tugurik ale wa, alege Neko a tu chaab ale wa kama, a ko wa Megiddo po. 30Josia tomteerɔma a jam pai wa nyiŋka a nyo ka toroko po a nyini Megiddo a cheŋ Jerusalem a gu wa, wadek vɔrup po. Ate tɛŋka nuruma a pai Josia nidoabinni Jeyoayaz a kpiiri kpaam a nyo wa zuk po ale bobi wa naab a tagri wa kowa.
31Jeyoayaz a jam ta ka bena pisiye ale ŋata ale jam chim naab, ate wa jam nya Jerusalem zuk ka chiisa sita. Wa mawa yuei jam le Yamutal. Wa jam ka Jeremaya lie, a nyini Libna. 32Wa jam nye ka biem Naawen niŋ ase wa koma ale jam nye diila. 33Faaro Neko a jam su wa ka chɔrima a Aribla ale bo Yamat tɛŋka po la ayen wa kan baga a dɛ naam Jerusalem po ale gebi kpana ligbie boorik dobrim kook ale ligmɔniŋ boorik dobrim kanyi a basi Juda zuk. 34Faaro Neko a jam nye ka Josia nidoabinni Eliakim naab a tagri wa kowa Josia ale tagri Eliakim yuenni a ta jam Jeyoiakim. Alege wa jam pai Jeyoayaz a ta cheŋ ka Ejipiti ate wa kpi dula. 35Jeyoiakim a jam tuni Faaro Neko kpanaŋa ale ligmɔniŋka ate wa jam bek la kama. Ate wa baga a nye dila la, wa jam a tuesi ka kpana ale ligmɔniŋ a nyini tɛŋka nuruma jigi a va chaab ale waai meena ale baga dii a te la.
36Jeyoiakim a jam ta ka bena pisiye ale ŋanu alege jam chim naab, ate wa jam chim naab Jerusalem po a paari ka bena pi ale dinyi. Wa mawa yue jam le Zebida, wa be jam ka Pedaiya lie. Wa jam nyini ka Aruma. 37Wa abe jam nye ka biem Naawen nina po ase wa koma ale jam nye diila.

english_text:
1 During Jehoiakim's rule, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia invaded and took control of Judah. Jehoiakim obeyed Nebuchadnezzar for three years, but then he rebelled.
2At that time, the Lord started sending troops to rob and destroy towns in Judah. Some of these troops were from Babylonia, and others were from Syria, Moab, and Ammon. The Lord had sent his servants the prophets to warn Judah about this, 3and now he was making it happen. The country of Judah was going to be wiped out, because Manasseh had sinned 4and caused many innocent people to die. The Lord would not forgive this.
5Everything else Jehoiakim did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 6Jehoiakim died, and his son Jehoiachin became king.
7King Nebuchadnezzar defeated King Neco of Egypt and took control of his land from the Egyptian Gorge all the way north to the Euphrates River. So Neco never invaded Judah again.
King Jehoiachin of Judah Is Taken to Babylon
(2 Chronicles 36.9,10)
8Jehoiachin was 18 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled only 3 months from Jerusalem. His mother Nehushta was the daughter of Elnathan from Jerusalem. 9Jehoiachin disobeyed the Lord, just as his father Jehoiakim had done.
10King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia sent troops to attack Jerusalem soon after Jehoiachin became king. 11During the attack, Nebuchadnezzar himself arrived at the city. 12 Jehoiachin immediately surrendered, together with his mother and his servants, as well as his army officers and officials. Then Nebuchadnezzar had Jehoiachin arrested. These things took place in the eighth year of Nebuchadnezzar's rule in Babylonia.
13The Lord had warned that someday the treasures would be taken from the royal palace and from the temple, including the gold objects that Solomon had made for the temple. And that's exactly what Nebuchadnezzar ordered his soldiers to do. 14He also led away as prisoners the Jerusalem officials, the military leaders, and the skilled workers—10,000 in all. Only the very poorest people were left in Judah.
15 Nebuchadnezzar took Jehoiachin to Babylon, along with his mother, his wives, his officials, and the most important leaders of Judah. 16He also led away 7,000 soldiers and 1,000 skilled workers, all of them trained for battle.
17 Then Nebuchadnezzar appointed Jehoiachin's uncle Mattaniah king of Judah and changed his name to Zedekiah.
King Zedekiah of Judah
(2 Chronicles 36.11-16; Jeremiah 52.1-3)
18 Zedekiah was 21 years old when he was appointed king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 11 years. His mother Hamutal was the daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah. 19Zedekiah disobeyed the Lord, just as Jehoiakim had done. 20 It was Zedekiah who finally rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar.
The people of Judah and Jerusalem had made the Lord so angry that he turned his back on them. That's why these horrible things were happening.
translation_text:
1Jeyoiakim naamu vaaŋa po, ate Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar a jam vari jo tɛŋka, ate Jeyoiakim a chim wa tomteerɔ a paari bena ŋata. Alege wa jam tagri wa popola kama a jam zɛri Nebukadnezzar nɔi. 2Naawen a jam tom ka tugurik tɔŋdɔba ate ba chim Kaldiya dem ale Araam dem ale Ammon dem ate ba ga nye tugurik ale wa. Wa jam tom ba kama ayen ba kaasi Juda, a va chaab ale Naawen wanni ate wa jam weeni va wa tomteerɔma biisiteerɔma la. 3Ŋade a jam sum nye Juda kama a va chaab ale Naawen wanni, ayen wa yeeri ba wa nina po, dii nyiŋla Manasa wabaataŋa ale dii meena ate wa nye la nyiŋ, 4a gum chaab ale nuru baai ale kan seba wari nɔi po ate wa kɔ ba la. Diila wa jam te ka nuru baai ale kan seba wari nɔi po la ziim a sueri Jerusalem, ate Naawen a kan yaali ayen wa vɔŋ te.
5Dii meena ale nye Jeyoiakim naamu vaaŋa po ale dii meena ate wa nye la, ŋala a ŋmarisi a doa ka Juda nalimaŋa gbaŋka po. 6Jeyoiakim a jam kpi kama a vuusi ale wa koma. Ate Jeyoiachin wa nidoabinni a chim naab a tagri wa.
7Ejipiti naawa an jam cheŋ ale wadek tɛŋka ŋmana. Dii nyiŋla Babilon naawa a jam pai wa tɛŋka kama, a nyini Ejipiti Buboalika a ga paari Yufiretis Benni.
8Jeyoiachin a jam ta ka bena pi ale naaniŋ ale jam chim naab, wa abe jam nya Jerusalem zuk ka chiisa sita. Wa mawa yuei jam le Neyusta ate wa chim Elnatan lie. Wa abe jam nyini ka Jerusalem. 9Wa jam nye ka biem Naawen nina po, ase wa kowa ale jam nye diila.
10Va ŋala po Nebukadnezzar kpaŋŋa a jam nya pagrim Jerusalem zuk ka nna yegayega a yaa gilim ka. 11Ate Nebukadnezzar dek a jam tɛŋka po ate wa kpaŋŋa mɛ a gilim ka. 12Juda naawa Jeyoiachin mawa ale baai ale a nya wa zuk la ale wa nuru kpientaŋa ale wa kpaŋŋa meena a jam siak a te wa kama. Babilon naawa le jam kali wa naamu zuk a paari bena naaniŋ la, wa yaa jam yik Jeyoiachin a lik. 13Ase Naawen ale jam weeni la, Nebukadnezzar a jam yeeri Naawen yenni ale naab yenni ŋantaŋa meena kama ale pai ligmɔniŋka ŋantaŋa ate Izirali naawa Solomon a jam nye basi Naawen yenni po la kama. 14Wa jam yik Jerusalem meena kama. Kpaŋŋa meena ale tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale baai ale a yɔk ale a gobi ŋanta la. Ba meena a jam ka tusa pi (10,000). Ka nuru baai ale jaŋ la nyiini ate wa jam basi ba.
15Nebukadnezzar a jam yik ka Jeyoiachin a ta cheŋ Babilon. Wa jam maa ta ka naawa mawa ale wa pooma ale wa kpaŋŋa ale wa niŋdeerɔma ale bo tɛŋka po la a ta nyini Jerusalem a cheŋ Babilon. 16Babilon naawa a jam maa ta ka tugurik tɔŋdɔba tusa ŋayopɔi (7,000), ate ba pagra a magsi tugurik nyeka ale baai ale a yɔk ale a gobi ŋanta la tusidi ta jam Babilon. 17Wa jam nye ate ka Jeyoiachin suoku biika Mattania ate wa chim naab a tagri wa. Wa jam tagri wa yuenni kama a ta cheŋ Zedekia.
18Zedekia a jam ta ka bena pisiye ale dinyi, ale chim naab wa abe jam dɛ naam Jerusalem zuk ka bena pi ale dinyi. Wa mawa yuei jam le Yamutal, wa jam ka Jeremaya lie. Wa jam nyini ka Libna. 19Wa jam nye ka biem Naawen nina po ase Jeyoiakim ale jam nye diila. 20Ka Naawen suinni ale jam puuri ale Jerusalem ale Juda la nyiŋ ale soa ate kude meena a nye ba ate ku nuerika wa yiak ba wa nina po a basi. Dila po Zedekia a jam zɛri Babilon naawa nɔi kama.

english_text:
Jerusalem Is Captured and Destroyed
(2 Chronicles 36.17-21; Jeremiah 52.3-30)
1 In Zedekiah's ninth year as king, on the tenth day of the tenth month, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia led his entire army to attack Jerusalem. The troops set up camp outside the city and built ramps up to the city walls.
2-3After a year and a half, all the food in Jerusalem was gone. Then on the ninth day of the fourth month, 4 the Babylonian troops broke through the city wall. That same night, Zedekiah and his soldiers tried to escape through the gate near the royal garden, even though they knew the enemy had the city surrounded. They headed toward the desert, 5but the Babylonian troops caught up with them near Jericho. They arrested Zedekiah, but his soldiers scattered in every direction.
6Zedekiah was taken to Riblah, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial and found him guilty. 7 Zedekiah's sons were killed right in front of him. His eyes were then poked out, and he was put in chains and dragged off to Babylon.
8About a month later, in Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year as king, Nebuzaradan, who was his official in charge of the guards, arrived in Jerusalem. 9 Nebuzaradan burned down the Lord's temple, the king's palace, and every important building in the city, as well as all the houses. 10Then he ordered the Babylonian soldiers to break down the walls around Jerusalem. 11He led away as prisoners the people left in the city, including those who had become loyal to Nebuchadnezzar. 12Only some of the poorest people were left behind to work the vineyards and the fields.
13 The Babylonian soldiers took the two bronze columns that stood in front of the temple, the ten movable bronze stands, and the large bronze bowl called the Sea. They broke them into pieces so they could take the bronze to Babylonia. 14 They carried off the bronze things used for worship at the temple, including the pans for hot ashes, and the shovels, snuffers, and also the dishes for incense, 15as well as the fire pans and the sprinkling bowls. Nebuzaradan ordered his soldiers to take everything made of gold or silver.
16The pile of bronze from the columns, the stands, and the large bowl that Solomon had made for the temple was too large to be weighed. 17Each column had been eight meters tall with a bronze cap over one meter high. These caps were decorated with bronze designs—some of them like chains and others like pomegranates.
18Next, Nebuzaradan arrested Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah his assistant, and three temple officials. 19Then he arrested one of the army commanders, the king's five personal advisors, and the officer in charge of gathering the troops for battle. He also found 60 more soldiers who were still in Jerusalem. 20Nebuzaradan led them all to Riblah 21near Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar had them killed.
Most of the people of Judah had been carried away as captives from their own country.
Gedaliah Is Made Ruler of the People Left in Judah
(Jeremiah 40.7-9; 41.1-3)
22 King Nebuchadnezzar appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam to rule the few people still living in Judah. 23When the army officers and troops heard that Gedaliah was their ruler, the officers met with him at Mizpah. These men were Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth from Netophah, and Jaazaniah from Maacah.
24Gedaliah said to them, “Everything will be fine, I promise. We don't need to be afraid of the Babylonian rulers, if we live here peacefully and do what Nebuchadnezzar says.”
25 Ishmael was from the royal family. And about two months after Gedaliah began his rule, Ishmael and ten other men went to Mizpah. They killed Gedaliah and his officials, including those from Judah and those from Babylonia. 26 After that, the army officers and all the people in Mizpah, whether important or not, were afraid of what the Babylonians might do. So they left Judah and went to Egypt.
Jehoiachin Is Set Free
(Jeremiah 52.31-34)
27Jehoiachin was a prisoner in Babylon for 37 years. Then Evil-Merodach became king of Babylonia, and in the first year of his rule, on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month, he let Jehoiachin out of prison. 28Evil-Merodach was kind to Jehoiachin and honored him more than any of the other kings held prisoner there. 29Jehoiachin was even allowed to wear regular clothes, and he ate at the king's table every day. 30As long as Jehoiachin lived, he was paid a daily allowance to buy whatever he needed.
translation_text:
1Dila Zedekia naamu bena neokku po, chiisa piika, ka daa piika po, ate Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar yaa jam gɔk santiri a jueli Jerusalem ale wa tugurik tommu meena zuk. Wa jam ga bo ka tɛŋka peelim alege basi ate nuruba a gilim tɛŋka meena. 2Ba jam gilim tɛŋka a ta ka kama ate ku ga paari naab Zedekia naamu bena pi ale dinyiwa. 3Chiisa sinaansiwa ku daa neokku danni, kɔmmu tɛŋka po yaa jam pagra ate ŋandiinta a jam karo ate nuruma a dɛ. 4Ate tɛŋka siaka a jam wɛ lo tɛŋ, ate tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena yaa jam va juijui ale lo la a yiti chali yokku a moata naawa kadukka. Kaldiya demma a jam gilim tɛŋka kama alege ba va ka du la a chali. Ba jam chali a duŋ ka Araba, 5alege Kaldiya tugurik tommu a jam vi naawa kama a chali gaam wa Jeriko peelitaŋa po. Wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena a jam gaari badek kama a nyini wa po a chali waaŋ chaab. 6Ate ba jam yik wa. Ba jam ta wa a cheŋ ka Babilon naawa jigi Aribla, dula jigini ate ba jam weeni ba ale ba nye wa diila. 7Ba jam ko Zedekia nidoabilisaŋa ka wadek nimbie po. Ate ba yaa kpiti wadek ninaŋa a yeeri ale bobi wa ale kutuk mɔnuŋ chɔrima a ta wa a cheŋ Babilon.
8Chiisa sinuwa daa ŋayopɔiwa danni, Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar bena pi ale neokku po ate wa dɛ wa naamu la, waai ale a cheŋ ale wa la, ate wa chim Babilon naawa kpagi la, yaa jam Jerusalem. 9Wa jam toati ka bolim a basi Naawen yenni ale naab yenni ale Jerusalem yieŋa meena. Wa jam ju yeri meena ale ta kiri kama a basi. 10Babilon tugurik tommu meena ate ba bo kpagi dii ale a nya naab yenni nyaarɔma zuk la, nisa po la yaa jam wɛ parisaŋa ale gilim Jerusalem la. 11Nyaarɔma kpagni Nebuzaradan yaa jam pai nuru baai ale jam bo tɛŋka po la ale baai ale tali boro la le baai ale siak a cheŋ Babilon naawa jigi la. 12Alege kpagni a jam basi ka ŋanjaksaŋa gela ŋaaŋ ayen ba a tom kaduksaŋa ale tattaŋa po.
13Kaldiya demma a jam wɛ kutuk mɔnuŋ zaŋŋa kama ale ŋanzaan tii ate fi baga a pai la ale kutuk mɔnuŋ Nyakpiemu ale bo Naawen yenni po la, yaa ji kutuk mɔnuŋku a ta cheŋ Babilon. 14Ba jam maa pai ka samɔnsa ale saabuluta ale boomsa ŋangebinta, ale taasi ŋaai ate ba ta a misi ale china ale kuta mɔnta ŋanta ate ba ta a tom Naawen yenni tuimaŋa la. 15Nyaarɔma kpagni a jam pai ka ŋan baai ate ba pai a ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la ale chin ŋaai ate ba pai a misi la. Ba jam pai ka ligmɔniŋ yaase kpana maŋsa a nye ŋa.
16Kutuk mɔnuŋku ale nyini zaŋŋa ŋayewa po la ale Nyakpiemu ale ŋanzaanitaŋa ate fi baga a pai la, ate Solomon a jam nye basi Naawen yenni po la, a jam zuak gaam magsika kama. 17Zaŋŋi yeŋ meena woglim a jam magsi paari ka anamagib pisita ale buyuebi a jueli ŋmai. Kutuk mɔnuŋku tulika ale jam bo zaŋni zuk la a jam jueli ka anamagib pi la alege ŋmirisi ate kuta yɔn fii gilima a gilim. Zaŋŋi dindila ale di yɔn fii gilimaŋa a jam ka dila.
18Limisidɔma kpagni a jam pai ka kaabteerɔ kpagni Seraiya ale kaabteerɔ pai saŋdɔwa Zefania ale nansuiŋ limisidɔma bata ase ligrɔba la. 19Baai ale diem jam bo tɛŋka po la, wa jam pai ka kpagi dii ale a nya tugurik tɔŋdɔma zuk la ale sagrɔ baai ale bo naab yenni po la banu. Wa jam maa pai ka gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa, wa ale chim kpagi dii ale a pai tɛŋka nuruma a gum tugurik tɔŋdɔma po ale wa nuruma pisiyuebi baai ate wa jam a nya ba tɛŋka po la. 20Kpagni Nebuzaradan a jam pai ba meena kama a ta ba jam Babilon naawa jigi Aribla. 21Aribla po, Yamat tɛŋka po, ate naawa a jam ko ba. Ba abe jam yik Juda demma a nyini ka badek tɛŋka a ta cheŋ.
22Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar a jam lueri ka Ayikam nidoabinni Gedalia ate Ayikam a chim Safan ŋaaŋbiik la ayen wa a nya nuru baai ate wa pai ba a basi Juda la zuk. 23Tugurik tommu kpaŋŋa meena ale ba nidoama ale jam wom ayen Babilon naawa a lueri ka Gedalia ayen wa chim kpagi la, ba yaa jam Mizpa Gedalia jigi. Ba jam ka Ismael nidoabinni Netania ale Karea nidoabinni Joyanan ale Tanhumet Netofat denɔwa nidoabinni Seraiya ale Maaka denɔwa nidoabinni Jaazania ale wa nidoama. 24Gedalia yaa jam nye pɛka ale ba ayen, <<Ni kan yɔgsa ale Babilon demma kpaŋŋa. Ni kali tɛŋka po abe ni tom te Babilon naawa, ate ku cheŋ nalimnyiini a te ni.>>
25Chiisa siyopɔiwa po, Ismael ate wa chim Netania nidoabili la ale chim Elisama ŋaaŋbiik la, waai ale nyini naab yeri la, yaa ta nidoaba pi a jam yik Gedalia a ko. Wa jam maa ko Juda nidoama kama ale Kaldiya dem baai ale jam bo Mizpa ale wa la. 26Nya kude nyiŋ, nuruma meena a nyini nuru fiisa a ga paari nuru kpienta, a jam pai tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpaŋŋa, a jam chali cheŋ ka Ejipiti. Kaldiya demma yɔgsum nyiŋ.
27Juda naawa Jeyoiachin bena pisita ale ŋayopɔiwa ate wa bo Babilon la, ben dii ate Evil Merodak a jam chim Babilon naab la, wa yaa lak Jeyoiachin chiisa pi ale siye daa pisiye ale ŋayopɔiwa danni likka dɔkku po a basi. 28Wa jam biisi ka bisɔŋ a te wa ale te wa zula zukpaglik ate ka gaam nalima nŋala ale bo Babilon po ale wa la. 29Ate Jeyoiachin yaa jam pai wa likka gattaŋa a dueni nakpiak ale kasim jam a dɛ ale naawa wa daa ŋaai ale jam tali la meena po. 30Jeyoiachin ale toalim jam boro la, naawa a jam kasim a tuni wa kama daa meena.

english_text:
The Descendants of Adam
(Genesis 5.1-32; 10.1-32; 11.10-32)
1-4Adam was the father of Seth, and his descendants were Enosh, Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared, Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech, and Noah, who had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
5Japheth was the father of Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras, and they were the ancestors of the kingdoms named after them. 6Gomer was the ancestor of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah. 7Javan was the ancestor of Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
8Ham was the father of Ethiopia, Egypt, Put, and Canaan, and they were the ancestors of the kingdoms named after them. 9Ethiopia was the ancestor of Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah, and Sabteca. Raamah was the ancestor of Sheba and Dedan. 10Ethiopia was also the father of Nimrod, the world's first mighty warrior. 11Egypt was the ancestor of Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim, 12Pathrusim, Casluhim, and Caphtorim, the ancestor of the Philistines. 13Canaan's oldest son was Sidon; his other son was Heth. 14-16Canaan was also the ancestor of the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and Arkites, the Sinites, the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites.
17Shem was the ancestor of Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech; they were the ancestors of the kingdoms named after them. 18Arpachshad was Shelah's father and Eber's grandfather. 19Eber named his first son Peleg, because in his time the earth was divided into tribal regions. Eber's second son was Joktan, 20-23the ancestor of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah, Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah, Ebal, Abimael, Sheba, Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab.
24-27Shem's descendants included Arpachshad, Shelah, Eber, Peleg, Reu, Serug, Nahor, Terah, and Abram, later renamed Abraham.
Abraham's Family
(Genesis 25.1-4,12-16)
28Abraham was the father of Isaac and Ishmael.
29-31Ishmael had twelve sons, who were born in the following order: Nebaioth, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam, Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
32Abraham and his slave woman Keturah had six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. Jokshan was the father of Sheba and Dedan. 33Midian was the father of Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah.
Esau's Family
(Genesis 36.1-14)
34Abraham's son Isaac was the father of Esau and Jacob. 35Esau was the father of Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. 36Eliphaz was the father of Teman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek. 37Reuel was the father of Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
The First Edomites and Their Kings
(Genesis 36.20-43)
38Seir was the father of Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. 39Lotan was the father of Hori and Homam; Lotan's sister was Timna. 40Shobal was the father of Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. Zibeon was the father of Aiah and Anah.
41Anah was the father of Dishon and the grandfather of Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran. 42Ezer was the father of Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. Dishan was the father of Uz and Aran.
43Before kings ruled in Israel, Bela son of Beor ruled the country of Edom from its capital of Dinhabah. 44After Bela's death, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah became king. 45After Jobab's death, Husham from the land of Teman became king. 46After Husham's death, Hadad son of Bedad became king and ruled from Avith. Earlier, Bedad had defeated the Midianites in the territory of Moab. 47After Hadad's death, Samlah from Masrekah became king; 48after Samlah's death, Shaul from the town of Rehoboth on the Euphrates River became king; 49and after Shaul's death, Baal Hanan son of Achbor became king. 50After Baal Hanan's death, Hadad ruled from Pai. His wife was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred and granddaughter of Mezahab.
51The Edomite clans were Timna, Alvah, Jetheth, 52Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon, 53Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar, 54Magdiel, and Iram.
translation_text:
1Adam ale jam biak Sɛti ate Sɛti a biak Enos ate Enos a biak 2Kenan ate Kenan a biak Mayalale ate Mayalale a biak Jared ate Jared a biak Ɛnok ate 3Ɛnok a biak Metusela ate Metusela a biak Lamek ate Lamek a biak Nowa.
4Nowa nidoabilisaŋa jam le Sɛm ale Yɛm ale Jafet. 5Jafet nidoabilisaŋa jam le Gomer ale Megɔg ale Madai ale Javan ale Tubal ale Mesek ale Tiras. 6Gomer nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Askenaz ale Arifat ale Togarma. 7Javan nidoabilisaŋa mɛ a jam le Elisa ale Tarsis ale Kittim ale Arodanim.
8Yɛm nidoabilisaŋa jam ka Kus ale Mizraim ale Put ale Keenan. 9Kus nidoabilisaŋa jam ka Sɛba ale Yavila ale Sabta ale Araamaya ale Sabteka. Araamaya nidoabilisaŋa jam le Siiba ale Dedan. 10Kus jam ka Nimrod ko. Nimrod ale jam piilim yiti a chim pagrɔ a nak kpaliŋsa tɛŋka zuk. 11Mizraim jam ka Lud demma ale Anam demma ale Lehab demma ale Naftu demma ale 12Patrus demma ale Kaftor demma ale Kaslu demma ko. Filistia demma a nyini ka bala po. 13Keenan nidoabili kpagni jam le Saidon. Wa abe jam ka Yit demma ale 14Jebus demma ale Amori demma ale Girgas demma ale 15Yivi demma ale Arki demma ale Sin demma ale 16Arvad demma ale Zemar demma ale Yamat demma ko.
17Sɛm nidoabilisaŋa jam le Iilam ale Assur ale Afakasad ale Lud ale Araam ale Uz ale Yul ale Geter ale Mesek. 18Afakasad a jam ka Sɛla ko ate Sɛla a chim Eber ko. 19Eber jam biak ka nidoabilisa baye. Wa jam te wanyi wa yuei ayen ka Peleg, diila wa daaŋa po tɛŋka jam poori kama. Wa suoku yuei jam le Joktan. 20Joktan a jam biak ka Almodad ale Selef ale Yazarmavet ale Jera ale 21Yadoram ale Uzal ale Dikla ale 22Ebal ale Abimael ale Siiba ale 23Ofir ale Yavila ale Jobab. Bade meena jam ka Joktan nidoabilisa.
24Ba dɔkdemma tomini a jam le Sɛm ale Afakasad ale Sɛla ale 25Eber ale Peleg ale Areu ale 26Serug ale Nayo ale Tɛra ale 27Abram, waai yuei ale jam chim Abrayam ŋaaŋnyiŋ la.
28Abrayam nidoabilisaŋa jam le Aizik ale Ismael.
29Ba ŋaaŋbisaŋa a jam le nna Ismael bikpagni jam le Nebaiot ate wa pa te Kedar ale Adbeel ale Mibsam ale 30Misma ale Duma ale Massa ale Yadad ale Tema ale 31Jetur ale Nafis ale Kedema. Ismael nidoabilisaŋa a jam le la.
32Ketura Abrayam pokbinni ale jam biak bi sii la ale Zimran ale Joksan ale Medan ale Midian ale Isbak ale Suya. Joksan nidoabilisaŋa jam le Siiba ale Dedan. 33Midian nidoabilisaŋa jam le Efa ale Efer ale Yanok ale Abida ale Eldaa. Bade meena jam ka Ketura ŋaaŋbisa.
34Abrayam jam ka Aizik ko ate Aizik nidoabilisa a nye Iisɔ ale Izirali. 35Iisɔ nidoabilisaŋa jam le Elifaz ale Areuel ale Jeus ale Jalam ale Koora. 36Elifaz nidoabilisaŋa jam le Teman ale Omar ale Zefo ale Gatam ale Kenaz ale Timna ale Amalek. 37Areuel nidoabilisaŋa jam le Nayat ale Zera ale Sammaya ale Mizza.
38Seir nidoabilisaŋa jam le Lotan ale Sobal ale Zibeon ale Anaya ale Dison ale Ezer ale Disan. 39Lotan nidoabilisaŋa jam le Yori ale Yomam. Timna jam ka Lotan toa. 40Sobal nidoabilisaŋa jam le Alian ale Manahat ale Ebal ale Sefi ale Onam. Zibeon nidoabilisaŋa jam le Aiaya ale Anaya. 41Anaya nidoabili jam le Dison. Dison nidoabilisa jam le Yamran ale Esban ale Itran ale Cheran. 42Ezer nidoabilisaŋa jam le Bilyan ale Zaavan ale Jakan. Disan mɛ nidoabilisa jam le Uz ale Aran.
43Nalimaŋa de ale jam dɛ naam Edom alege ate Izirali naab a dɛ la ale nna. Bala a jam le Biio nidoabinni Bela waai tɛŋ kpieŋ yuei ale chim Dinyaba la. 44Ase Bela ale jam kpi la, ka Zera nidoabinni Jobab ale nyini Bozra la ale jam zaani wa nankula po a chim naab. 45Jobab ale jam kpi la, Yusam ale nyini Tema demma tɛŋka la ale jam zaani wa nankula po a chim naab. 46Yusam ale kpi la, Bedad nidoabinni Yadad ate wa jam nak dɛ Midian tɛŋka ale bo Moab po la ale dɛ naamu. Wa tɛŋka ba jam te ka yuei ayen ka Avit. 47Yadad ale kpi la, Samla ale nyini Masreka la ale dɛ naamu. 48Samla ale jam kpi la, Sɛyaul ale nyini Areyobot ale bo Benni nɔi la ale jam chim naab. 49Sɛyaul ale jam kpi la, Achbor nidoabinni Baal Yanan ale jam chim naab. 50Baal Yanan ale jam kpi la, Yadad ale jam chim naab. Wa tɛŋ kpieŋka yuei jam le Pai, wa powa yuei jam le Meyetabel a chim Matred lie ate Matred a chim Mezayab lie. 51Yadad mɛ a jam kpi kama. Edom nalimaŋa jam le Timna ale Alva ale Jetet ale 52Oyolibama ale Elaya ale Pinon ale 53Kenaz ale Teman ale Mibzar ale 54Magdiel ale Iram. Bade jam le Edom nalimaŋa.

english_text:
The Descendants of Judah
1-2Jacob was the father of twelve sons: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
3Judah and his Canaanite wife Bathshua had three sons: Er, Onan, and Shelah. But the Lord had Er put to death, because he disobeyed and did what the Lord hated. 4Judah and his daughter-in-law Tamar also had two sons: Perez and Zerah.
5Perez was the father of Hezron and Hamul. 6Zerah was the father of Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Darda. 7 Achan, who was a descendant of Zerah and the son of Carmi, caused trouble for Israel, because he kept for himself things that belonged only to the Lord. 8Ethan's son was Azariah.
The Ancestors of King David
9Hezron was the father of Jerahmeel, Ram, and Caleb. 10Ram was the father of Amminadab and the grandfather of Nahshon, a tribal leader of Judah. 11Nahshon's descendants included Salma, Boaz, 12Obed, and Jesse. 13-15Jesse had seven sons, who were born in the following order: Eliab, Abinadab, Shimea, Nethanel, Raddai, Ozem, and David. 16Jesse also had two daughters: Zeruiah and Abigail. Zeruiah was the mother of Abishai, Joab, and Asahel. 17Abigail's husband was Jether, who was a descendant of Ishmael, and their son was Amasa.
The Descendants of Hezron
18Hezron's son Caleb married Azubah, and their daughter was Jerioth, the mother of Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon. 19After the death of Azubah, Caleb married Ephrath. Their son Hur 20was the father of Uri and the grandfather of Bezalel.
21When Hezron was 60 years old, he married the daughter of Machir, who settled the region of Gilead. Their son Segub 22was the father of Jair, who ruled 23 villages in the region of Gilead. 23Some time later the nations of Geshur and Aram captured 60 towns in that region, including the villages that belonged to Jair, as well as the town of Kenath and the nearby villages. Everyone from the region of Gilead was a descendant of Machir.
24After the death of Hezron, Caleb married Ephrath, his father's wife. Their son was Ashhur, who later settled the town of Tekoa.
The Descendants of Jerahmeel
25Jerahmeel, Hezron's oldest son, was the father of Ram, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah. 26Jerahmeel had a second wife, Atarah, who gave birth to Onam. 27Ram was the father of Maaz, Jamin, and Eker. 28Onam was the father of Shammai and Jada.
Shammai was the father of Nadab and Abishur. 29Abishur married Abihail, and their two sons were Ahban and Molid. 30Nadab was the father of Seled and Appaim. Seled had no children; 31Appaim's son was Ishi, the father of Sheshan and the grandfather of Ahlai.
32Jada was the father of Jether and Jonathan. Jether had no children, 33but Jonathan had two sons: Peleth and Zaza.
34-35Sheshan had no sons, and so he let one of his daughters marry Jarha, his Egyptian slave. Their son was Attai, 36the father of Nathan and the grandfather of Zabad. 37-41Zabad's descendants included Ephlal, Obed, Jehu, Azariah, Helez, Eleasah, Sismai, Shallum, Jekamiah, and Elishama.
The Descendants of Caleb
42Caleb, Jerahmeel's brother, had the following descendants: Mesha, Ziph, Mareshah, Hebron, 43and Hebron's four sons, Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema. 44Shema was the father of Raham and the grandfather of Jorkeam. Rekem was the father of Shammai, 45the grandfather of Maon, and the great-grandfather of Bethzur.
46Ephah was one of Caleb's wives, and their sons were Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran named his son after his brother Gazez. 47Ephah was the daughter of Jahdai, who was also the father of Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, and Shaaph.
48Maacah was another of Caleb's wives, and their sons were Sheber and Tirhanah. 49Later, they had two more sons: Shaaph the father of Madmannah, and Sheva the father of Machbenah and Gibea. Caleb's daughter was Achsah. 50-51All of these were Caleb's descendants.
Hur, the oldest son of Caleb and Ephrath, had three sons: Shobal, Salma, and Hareph, who settled the town of Beth-Gader. 52Shobal, who settled the town of Kiriath-Jearim, was the ancestor of Haroeh, half of the Menuhoth clan, 53and the clans that lived near Kiriath-Jearim; they were the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites. The Zorathites and the Eshtaolites were descendants of the Mishraites.
54Salma settled the town of Bethlehem and was the ancestor of the Netophathites, the people of Atroth-Bethjoab, half of the Manahathite clan, and the Zorites. 55Salma was also the ancestor of the clans in Jabez that kept the court and government records; they were the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Sucathites. These clans were the descendants of Hammath the Kenite, who was also the ancestor of the Rechabites.
translation_text:
1Izirali nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Aruben ale Simeyon ale Livai ale Juda ale Isaka ale Zebulun ale 2Dan ale Josefi ale Benjamin ale Nafitali ale Gad ale Asɛ. 3Juda nidoabilisaŋa jam le Ɛri ale Onan ale Sɛla. Bade batama ka Keenan tɛŋka lie Bat Sɛyua ale jam biak ba a te wa. Juda nidoabili kpagni Ɛri a jam ta ka gaasa Naawen nimbie po ate Naawen a ko wa. 4Tamara Juda sampowa jam biak ka Perezi ale Zera. Juda nidoabilisaŋa meena jam ka banu. 5Perezi nidoabilisaŋa jam le Ayeziron ale Yamul. 6Zera nidoabilisaŋa jam le Zimri ale Etan ale Yeman ale Kalkol ale Darda. Ba meena ka banu. 7Karmi nidoabili ale Achar, waai ale jam ta daanika a jam Izirali zuk ta va kisuk ŋantaŋa ate ba ayen ba kan tiri la. 8Etan nidoabili jam le Azariya. 9Ayeziron nidoabilisaŋa jam le Jerameel ale Aram ale Chelubai.
10Aram jam ka Amminadab ko, Amminadab jam ka Nayson ko Juda nuruma niŋdeerɔ. 11Nayson jam ka Salimon ko, Salimon jam ka Boazi ko, 12Boazi jam ka Obed ko, Obed jam ka Jese ko, 13Jese nidoabili kpagni jam ka Eliab a pasaŋ Abinadab ate wala a pai te Simea. 14Netanel ale saari banaansi. Bunuwa po ka Araddai ate 15Ozem a saari bayuebi. Buyopɔiwa ka Deevid. 16Ba toama jam le Zeruiya ale Abigail. Zeruiya nidoabilisaŋa batawa jam le Abisai ale Joab ale Asayel. 17Abigail jam ka Amasa ma waai ko ale jam ka Jeter Ismael denɔ la.
18Ayeziron nidoabinni Kaleb jam ta ka nidoabilisa ale wa powa Azuba ale wa pok wa choawa Jeriot. Azuba nidoabilisaŋa jam le Jeser ale Sobab ale Ardon. 19Azuba ale jam kpi la, Kaleb a jam faari ka Efrat ate wa mɛ a biak Yur. 20Yur jam ka Uri ko, Uri jam ka Bezalel ko. 21Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ Ayeziron a jam goa ale ka Makir lie Gilead ko ale la, wa ale jam faari wa la ale wa ta ka bena pisiyuebi, ate wa biak Segub. 22Segub jam ka Jair ko, waai ale jam a nya tɛŋsa pisiye ale sita zuk Gilead po. 23Alege Gesur ale Araam a jam nak yik Yavvot Jair ale Kenat ale ka tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa pisiyuebiwa kama. Bade meena jam ka Makir Gilead kowa ŋaaŋbisa.
24Ayeziron ale jam kpi Kaleb Efrata po la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, Abaija Ayeziron powa a jam biak ka Asur Tekoa kowa.
25Ayeziron nidoabili kpagni jam le Jerameel. Jerameel nidoabilisaŋa jam le Aram ale Bunaya ale Oren ale Ozem ale Ayija. Aram jam le Jerameel nidoabili kpagni. 26Jerameel jam ta ka nipok wa choa, wa yuei jam le Ataraya. Wa jam ka Onam ma. 27Jerameel nidoabili kpagni Aram a jam ta ka nidoabilisa, bala abe le Maaz ale Jamin ale Eker. 28Onam nidoabilisaŋa jam le Sammai ale Jada. Sammai mɛ nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Nadab ale Abisur. 29Abisur powa yuei a jam le Abiyail, wala ale jam biak Aban ale Molid. 30Nadab mɛ nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Seled ale Appaim. Seled an jam biak bisa ale kpi ya. 31Appaim nidoabili jam le Isi. Isi a jam ka Sesan ko ate Sesan a jam chim Alai ko. 32Jada Sammai suoku nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Jeter ale Jonatan. Jeter an jam biak bisa ale kpi ya. 33Jonatan nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Pelet ale Zaza. Bade a jam le Jerameel ŋaaŋbisaŋa.
34Sesan an jam biak nidoaba ka lieba nyiini. Wa jam ta ka Ejipiti tɛŋka tomteerɔ, wa yuei jam le Jarha. 35Sesan a jam pa ka wa lie a yalisi wa tomteerɔwa Jarha, ate wa biak Attai. 36Attai jam ka Natan ko, Natan jam ka Zabad ko, 37Zabad jam ka Eflal ko, Eflal jam ka Obed ko, 38Obed jam ka Jeyu ko, Jeyu jam ka Azariya ko, 39Azariya jam ka Yelez ko, Yelez jam ka Eleasaya ko, 40Eleasaya jam ka Sismai ko, Sismai jam ka Sallum ko, 41Sallum jam ka Jekamia ko, Jekamia jam ka Elisama ko.
42Jerameel suoku Kaleb nidoabilisaŋa ale nna: Mesa wa nidoabili kpagni, waai ale jam ka Zif ko la ate wa nidoabili Maresa a jam chim Yebron ko. 43Yebron mɛ nidoabilisaŋa jam le Koora ale Tappua ale Arekem ale Sɛma. 44Sɛma jam ka Arayam ko, Arayam jam ka Jorkeam ko. Arekem jam ka Sammai ko. 45Sammai jam ka Maon ko, Maon jam ka Bet Zur ko. 46Kaleb pokbinni Efa jam ka Yaran ale Moza ale Gazez ma. Yaran jam ka Gazez ko. 47Jadai nidoabilisaŋa jam le Aregem ale Jotam ale Gesan ale Pelet ale Efa ale Saaf. 48Kaleb pokbinni Maaka jam ka Seber ale Tirana ma. 49Wa ale jam maa biak Saaf Madmanna kowa ale Seva Makbena kowa ale Gibeya. Kaleb lie jam le Aksaya. 50Bade a jam le Kaleb ŋaaŋbisaŋa. Kaleb nidoabinni Yur a jam le wa mawa Efrata nidoabi kpagi. Yur Efrata bikpagni nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Sobal Kiriat Jearim ko, 51Salma ka Betiliyem ko ate Yaref a chim Bet Gader kowa. 52Sobal Kiriat Jearim kowa ŋaaŋbisaŋa a jam le Yaroe ale Manahat demma geli ale 53Kiriat Jearim yezuimaŋa. Bala ale Itri demma ale Puti demma ale Sumat demma ale Misra demma. Ŋaaŋbisaŋa de po ale Zorat demma ale Estaol demma a nyini la. 54Salma ŋaaŋbisaŋa a jam le Betiliyem ale Netofat demma ale Atrot Bet Joab ale Manahat demma geli ale Zor demma buuraŋa ale 55gbaŋ ŋmarisidoama yezuimaŋa baai ale bo Jabez la. Bala abe le Tirat demma ale Simeat demma ale Sukat demma. Bade ale Ken demma waai ale nyini Yammat, Arekab kowa yenni la.

english_text:
The Descendants of King David
1-4 King David ruled from Hebron for seven years and six months, and during that time he had six sons, who were born in the following order: Amnon, Daniel, Absalom, Adonijah, Shephatiah, and Ithream. Ahinoam from Jezreel was the mother of Amnon; Abigail from Carmel was the mother of Daniel; Maacah daughter of King Talmai of Geshur was the mother of Absalom; Haggith was the mother of Adonijah; Abital was the mother of Shephatiah; and Eglah was the mother of Ithream.
David then ruled from Jerusalem for 33 years, 5 and during that time, he had 13 more sons. His wife Bathsheba daughter of Ammiel gave birth to Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon. 6-8David's other sons included Ibhar, Elishua, Eliphelet, Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet. 9David's other wives also gave birth to sons. Tamar was his daughter.
The Descendants of King Solomon
10-15Solomon's descendants included the following kings: Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa, Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, Ahaziah, Joash, Amaziah, Azariah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, Manasseh, Amon, and Josiah and his four sons, Johanan, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah, and Jehoahaz. 16Jehoiakim was the father of Jehoiachin and Zedekiah.
17Jehoiachin, who was taken to Babylon as a prisoner, had seven sons: Shealtiel, 18Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah. 19Pedaiah had two sons: Zerubbabel and Shimei. Zerubbabel was the father of Meshullam, Hananiah, and Shelomith their sister. 20He also had five other sons: Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushabhesed. 21Hananiah's descendants were Pelatiah, Jeshaiah, Rephaiah, Arnan, Obadiah, and Shecaniah, 22the father of Shemaiah and the grandfather of Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat. 23Neariah was the father of Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam. 24Elioenai was the father of Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani.
translation_text:
1Deevid nidoabilisaŋa ate wa jam biak Yebron la ale nna. Nidoabi kpagni jam le Amnon, wa mawa jam le Ayinoam ate wa nyini Jezreel la a pa saŋ Daniel wa mawa jam le Abigail a nyini Karmel. 2Buta nyɔnɔwa jam le Absalom, wa mawa jam le Maaka, wa jam ka Talmai Gesur naawa lie. Bunaansiwa po jam ka Adonija, wa mɛ mawa jam le Yaggit. 3Bunuwa po jam ka Sefatia wa mawa jam le Abital. Buyuebiwa po ka Itream, wa mawa jam le Egla. 4Bade bayuebiwa Deevid a jam biak ba ka Yebron tɛŋka po juijui ate wa jam dɛ naamu a paari bena ŋayopɔi ale chiisa siyuebi la. Deevid a jam dɛ naam Jerusalem po a paari ka bena pisita ale ŋata. 5Wa nidoabilisaŋa ale nna ate wa jam biak Jerusalem po la. Sammua ale Sobab ale Natan ale Solomon. Nidoabilisa banaansiwa de ka Deevid ale Bat Sɛyua Ammiel liewa ale jam biak. 6Ba gela jam le Ibyar ale Elisua ale Elifelet ale 7Noga ale Nefeg ale Jafia ale 8Elisama ale Eliada ale Elifelet. Ba meena jam ka neok. 9Bade meena jam ka Deevid bisa, wa pokbinni nidoabilisaŋa a maa karo. Tamara jam ka ba toa.
10Solomon nidoabili jam le Areyoboam, Areyoboam nidoabili jam le Abaija, Abaija nidoabili jam le Asa, Asa nidoabili jam le Jeyosafat. 11Jeyosafat nidoabili a jam le Joram, Joram nidoabili jam le Ayaziya, Ayaziya nidoabili jam le Joas. 12Joas nidoabili jam le Amaziya, Amaziya nidoabili jam le Azariya, Azariya nidoabili jam le Jotam. 13Jotam nidoabili jam le Ayazi, Ayazi nidoabili jam le Azekaya, Azekaya nidoabili jam le Manasa. 14Manasa nidoabili jam le Amon, Amon nidoabili jam le Josia. 15Josia nidoabilisaŋa a jam le nna. Wa nidoabili kpagni a jam le Joyanan a paasaŋ Jeyoiakim batawa po jam ka Zedekia ate Sallum a saari banaansi. 16Jeyoiakim nidoabinni Jekonaya ale jam tagri zaani wa nankula po, kula ŋaaŋnyiŋ wa kowa suoku Josia nidoabinni Zedekia ale tagri a zaani wa nankula po.
17Jekonaya ate ba jam nak yik la nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Sealtiel ale 18Malkiram ale Pedaiya ale Senazzar ale Jekamia ale Yosama ale Nedabia. 19Pedaiya nidoabilisaŋa mɛ a jam le Zerubabel ale Simei. Zerubabel nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Mesullam ale Yanania, ba tua a jam le Selomit. 20Zerubabel mɛ a jam ta ka bi yoŋta banu. Bala abe le Yasuba ale Oyel ale Berekiya ale Yasadia ale Jusab Yesed. 21Yanania ŋaaŋbisaŋa a jam le Pelatia ale Jesaiya. Arefaiya nidoabili jam le Arnan, Arnan nidoabili ale Obadia, Obadia nidoabili ale Sekania, 22Sekania nidoabili a jam le Sɛmaiya. Sɛmaiya nidoabilisa mɛ a jam le Yattus ale Igal ale Baria ale Nearia ale Safat. Ba meena a jam ka nidoabilisa bayuebi. 23Nearia nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Elioenai ale Yizkia ale Azrikam. Ba meena jam ka bata. 24Elioenai nidoabilisaŋa mɛ a jam le Yodavia ale Eliasib ale Pelaiya ale Akkub ale Joyanan ale Delaiya ale Anani. Ba meena jam ka bayopɔi.

english_text:
The Descendants of Judah
1Judah was the father of five sons: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal. 2Shobal was the father of Reaiah, the grandfather of Jahath, and the great-grandfather of Ahumai and Lahad. These men all belonged to the Zorathite clan.
3-4Hur was the oldest son of Caleb and Ephrath. Some of his descendants settled the town of Bethlehem. Hur's other descendants included Etam, Penuel, and Ezer. Etam's sons were Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash, and his daughter was Hazzelelponi. Penuel settled the town of Gedor, and Ezer settled the town of Hushah.
5Ashhur, who settled the town of Tekoa, had two wives: Helah and Naarah. 6Ashhur and Naarah were the parents of Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari. 7Ashhur and Helah were the parents of Zereth, Izhar, and Ethnan.
8Koz, the father of Anub and Zobebah, was also the ancestor of the clans of Aharhel, the son of Harum.
9Jabez was a man who got his name because of the pain he caused his mother during birth. But he was still the most respected son in his family. 10One day he prayed to Israel's God, “Please bless me and give me a lot of land. Be with me so I will be safe from harm.” And God did just what Jabez had asked.
11Chelub was the brother of Shuhah and the father of Mehir. Later, Mehir had a son, Eshton, 12whose three sons were Bethrapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah. It was Tehinnah who settled the town of Nahash. These men and their families lived in the town of Recah.
13Kenaz was the father of Othniel and Seraiah. Othniel had two sons: Hathath and Meonothai, 14who was the father of Ophrah. Seraiah was the father of Joab, who settled a place called “Valley of Crafts” because the people who lived there were experts in making things.
15Caleb son of Jephunneh had three sons: Iru, Elah, and Naam. Elah was the father of Kenaz.
16Jehallelel was the father of Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.
17-18Ezrah was the father of Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. Mered was married to Bithiah the daughter of the king of Egypt. They had a daughter named Miriam and two sons: Shammai and Ishbah. It was Ishbah who settled the town of Eshtemoa. Mered was also married to a woman from the tribe of Judah, and their sons were Jered, Heber, and Jekuthiel. Jered settled the town of Gedor; Heber settled the town of Soco; and Jekuthiel settled the town of Zanoah.
19A man named Hodiah was married to the sister of Naham. Hodiah's descendants included Keilah of the Garmite clan and Eshtemoa of the Maacathite clan.
20Shimon was the father of Amnon, Rinnah, Benhanan, and Tilon.
Ishi was the father of Zoheth and Benzoheth.
21-22Judah also had a son named Shelah, whose descendants included Jokim and the people of the town of Cozeba, as well as Er who settled the town of Lecah and Laadah who settled the town of Mareshah. The people who lived in Beth-Ashbea were also descendants of Shelah, and they were experts in weaving cloth. Shelah was the ancestor of Joash and Saraph, two men who married Moabite women and then settled near Bethlehem—but these family records are very old. 23The members of these clans were the potters who lived in the towns of Netaim and Gederah and worked for the king.
The Descendants of Simeon
24Simeon had five sons: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul. 25The descendants of Shaul included his son Shallum, his grandson Mibsam, and his great-grandson Mishma. 26The descendants of Mishma included his son Hammuel, his grandson Zaccur, and his great-grandson Shimei. 27Shimei had 16 sons and 6 daughters. But his brothers did not have as many children, so the Simeon tribe was smaller than the Judah tribe.
28-31 Before David became king, the people of the Simeon tribe lived in the following towns: Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar-Shual, Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad, Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag, Beth-Marcaboth, Hazarsusim, Bethbiri, and Shaaraim. 32They also lived in the five villages of Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan, 33as well as in the nearby villages as far as the town of Baal. These are the places where Simeon's descendants had settled, according to their own family records.
34-38As their families and clans became larger, the people of Simeon had the following leaders: Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah, Joel, Jehu, Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah, and Ziza. 39When the people needed more pastureland for their flocks and herds, they looked as far as the eastern side of the valley where the town of Gerar is located, 40and they found a lot of good pastureland that was quiet and undisturbed. This had once belonged to the Hamites, 41but when Hezekiah was king of Judah, the descendants of Simeon attacked and forced the Hamites and Meunites off the land, then settled there.
42Some time later, 500 men from the Simeon tribe went into Edom under the command of Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel the sons of Ishi. 43They killed the last of the Amalekites and lived there from then on.
translation_text:
1Juda nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Perezi ale Ayeziron ale Karmi ale Yur ale Sobal. 2Sobal nidoabinni Areaiya a jam ka Jayat ko, Jayat jam ka Ayumai ale Layud ko. Bade jam le Zorat yezuimaŋa. 3Etam nidoabilisaŋa a jam le nna. Jezreel ale Isma ale Idbas. Ba tuawa yuei jam le Yazzeleponi. 4Penuel jam ka Gedor ko, Ezer jam ka Yusa ko. Bade a jam le Yur ŋaaŋbisaŋa, Efrata nidoabili kpagni ale Betiliyem kowa. 5Tekoa kowa Asur a jam ta ka nipooba baye, Yela ale Naaraya. 6Naaraya a jam biak ka Ayuzzam ale Yefer ale Temeni ale Yaayastari a te wa. Naaraya ŋaaŋbisaŋa le la.
7Yela nidoabilisaŋa a jam le nna. Zeret ale Zoyar ale Etnan ale 8Koz waai ale jam biak Anub ale Yazzobeba ale Ayaryel Yarum nidoabinni yezuimaŋa. 9Jabez a jam ta zula a gaam wa suataŋa kama. Ate wa mawa a jam te wa yuei ayen Jabez, di kiri ale, <<Mi biak wa ale ka nyiŋdomma.>> 10Jabez yaa jam puusi a weeni Izirali Wenni ayen, <<Fi a niak mu a basi ate m tɛŋka a lagri a gum du, basi ate fi nisaŋa a bo ale mu, abe fi kasi mu ate wari a kan paari mu ate dila ale basi ate mi nye fasiyaa ale nyiŋdomma.>> Ate Wen a tulisi wa puusaŋa.
11Suyaya suoku Chelub a jam ka Meyir ko, Meyir jam ka Eston ko. 12Eston jam ka Bet Arafa ale Pasea ale Teyinna ko. Teyinna a jam ka nuru baai ale nyini Nayas tɛŋka la ko. Nuruma de a nyini ka Areka.
13Kenaz nidoabilisa a jam le Otniel ale Seraiya. Otniel mɛ nidoabilisa a jam le Yatat ale Meonotai. 14Meonotai a jam ka Ofra ko. Seraiya a jam ka Joab ko, wa mɛ jam ka Ge Yarasim ko. Ba yuei a jam le la dii nyiŋla ba jam ka yɔgrɔba.
15Jefunne nidoabili a jam le Kaleb. Kaleb mɛ nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Iru ale Elaya ale Naam. Elaya nidoabili a jam le Kenaz.
16Jeyallelel nidoabilisa a jam le Zif ale Zifaya ale Tiria ale Asarel.
17Ezraya nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Jeter ale Mered ale Efer ale Jalon. Mered pooma wanyi ate ba jam a wi ayen Bitia la ale jam biak Miriam ale Sammai ale Estemoa kowa Isba. 18Wa Juu powa ale jam biak Gedor kowa Jered ale Soko kowa Ɛba ale Zanoaya kowa Jekutiel. Bitia a jam ka Faaro lie ate Mered a faari. Miriam ale Sammai ale Isba a jam ka Bitia bisa. 19Yodia powa jam ka Nayam ko lie. Yodia powa nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Estemoa ale Keila kowa. Keila a jam nyini ka Garm demma po, ate Estemoa a jam nyini Maaka demma po.
20Sɛyɛmon nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Amnon ale Arinnaya ale Ben Yanan ale Tilon. Isi ŋaaŋbisaŋa jam le Zoyet ale Ben Zoyet.
21Juda nidoabinni Sɛla nidoabilisaŋa jam le nna: Ɛri a jam ka Leka ko, Laada jam ka Maresa ko ale ŋman chim dɔkdem baai buuri ale a nye garuk naliŋsa la po a bo Bet Asbea 22ale Jokim ale nuru baai ale nyini Kozeba ale Joas ale Saraf waai ale jam a nya Moab ale Jasubi Leyem tɛŋsaŋa zuk la. Ba ŋmarisi ŋade ka dipodipo. 23Ba jam ka mɛɛrɔba a bo Netaim ale Gedera tɛŋsaŋa po. Ba jam bo ka dula a tom a te naawa.
24Simeyon ŋaaŋbisaŋa a jam le Nemuel ale Jamin ale Jarib ale Zera ale Sɛyaul. 25Sɛyaul jam ka Sallum ko, Sallum jam le Mibsam ko. Mibsam nidoabili a jam le Misma. 26Misma nidoabili a jam le Yammuel. Yammuel nidoabili a jam le Zakkur. Zakkur mɛ nidoabili a jam le Simei.
27Simei a jam taka nidoabilisa pi ale bayuebi ale lieba bayuebi, alege wa suataŋa a jam ka bisa a soa dii ya, dila nyiŋ ba yezukku an jam piisi ase Juda la. 28Simei nidoabilisaŋa a jam bo ka Beerseba ale Molada ale Yazar Sual ale 29Bilya ale Ezem ale Tolad ale 30Betuel ale Yorma ale Ziklag ale 31Bet Markabot ale Yazar Susim ale Bet Biri ale Saaraim tɛŋsaŋa. Ba jam bo ka tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa de po ate ku paari diipo ate Deevid a chim naab la. 32Tɛŋ kpaŋsa sinuwa ale jam moata tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa de la a jam le Etam ale Ain ale Arimmon ale Token ale Asan. 33Tɛŋ kpaŋsa si chaab ale jam maa boro a yalima a paari Baalat. Dela ale ba jam boro la. Ate ba yaa jam ŋmarisi ba dɔkdemma ŋiak wie a dueni.
34Nidoama de yueŋa ale ŋmarisi la jam ka niŋdeerɔba ba dɔkdemma po. Bala abe le, Mesobab ale Jamlek ale Amaziya nidoabinni Josa ale 35Joel ale Josibia nidoabinni Jeyu, Josibia jam le Seraiya nidoabili, wa mɛ jam ka Asiel nidoabili. 36Ba gela ale nna. Elioenai ale Jaakoba ale Jesohaiya ale Asaiya ale Adiel ale Jesimiel ale Benaya ale 37Ziza ale ka Sifi nidoabili la, Sifi mɛ jam ka Allon nidoabili, Allon jam ka Jedaya nidoabili, Jedaya jam ka Simri nidoabili, Simri jam ka Sɛmaiya nidoabili.
38Nidoama yueŋa ale ŋmarisi ŋmazukku la a jam ka niŋdeerɔba ba yezuimaŋa po. Ba dɔkdemma a jam ŋmasi piisi kama, 39ate ba yaa jam nyini Gedor tɛŋka nakpiak viaka kori geŋsa ayen ba gisi wuyɔgsuk a te ba duŋsaŋa. 40Ba yaa jam nya wuuk maŋ ate ku piisi, tɛŋka a jam ta peelim nna jalɔ a ta suiyɔgni nna chim. Yɛm demma gela ale jam liŋ bo dula.
41Nidoama de baai yueŋa ale ŋmarisi la a jan jam ka Juda naawa Azekaya daaŋa po. Ba jam nye ka kpaliŋ ale Yɛm demma ba boka jigini ale jam maa nye kpaliŋ ale Meuni dem baai ale jam bo dula la a kaasi ba meena ase ti ale nya ku dii jinla danni la. Ba yaa jam kali bala jigini, dii nyiŋla wuyɔgsuk ale jam bo dula a magsi ba duŋsaŋa dɛka. 42Isi nidoabilisaŋa Pelatia ale Nearia ale Arefaiya ale Uzziel yaa jam dɛ Simeyon demma nuruba kobsinu niŋ a ga nye kpaliŋ ale nuru baai ale bo Seir guutaŋa zuk la. 43Ba jam ko Amalek demma baai ale jam chali be la. A nyini dai dila danni a ta jam paari jinla, Simeyon demma a diem bo ka Seir tɛŋka.

english_text:
The Descendants of Reuben
1 Reuben was the oldest son of Jacob, but he lost his rights as the first-born son because he slept with one of his father's wives. The honor of the first-born son was then given to Joseph, 2 even though it was the Judah tribe that became the most powerful and produced a leader.
3Reuben had four sons: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
4-6 The descendants of Joel included Shemaiah, Gog, Shimei, Micah, Reaiah, Baal, and Beerah, a leader of the Reuben tribe. Later, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria took Beerah away as prisoner.
7-8The family records also include Jeiel, who was a clan leader, Zechariah, and Bela son of Azaz and grandson of Shema of the Joel clan. They lived in the territory around the town of Aroer, as far north as Nebo and Baal-Meon, 9and as far east as the desert just west of the Euphrates River. They needed this much land because they owned too many cattle to keep them all in Gilead.
10When Saul was king, the Reuben tribe attacked and defeated the Hagrites, then took over their land east of Gilead.
The Descendants of Gad
11The tribe of Gad lived in the region of Bashan, north of the Reuben tribe. Gad's territory extended all the way to the town of Salecah. 12Some of the clan leaders were Joel, Shapham, Janai, and Shaphat. 13Their relatives included Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber.
14They were all descendants of Abihail, whose family line went back through Huri, Jaroah, Gilead, Michael, Jeshishai, Jahdo, and Buz. 15Ahi, the son of Abdiel and the grandson of Guni, was the leader of their clan.
16The people of Gad lived in the towns in the regions of Bashan and Gilead, as well as in the pastureland of Sharon. 17Their family records were written when Jotham was king of Judah and Jeroboam was king of Israel.
18The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh had 44,760 soldiers trained to fight in battle with shields, swords, bows, and arrows. 19They fought against the Hagrites and the tribes of Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab. 20Whenever these soldiers went to war against their enemies, they prayed to God and trusted him to help. That's why the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh defeated the Hagrites and their allies. 21These Israelite tribes captured 50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep, 2,000 donkeys, and 100,000 people. 22Many of the Hagrites died in battle, because God was fighting this battle against them. The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh lived in that territory until they were taken as prisoners to Assyria.
The Tribe of East Manasseh
23East Manasseh was a large tribe, so its people settled in the northern region of Bashan, as far north as Baal-Hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon. 24Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel were their clan leaders; they were well-known leaders and brave soldiers.
The Tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh Are Defeated
25The people of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh were unfaithful to the God their ancestors had worshiped, and they started worshiping the gods of the nations that God had forced out of Canaan. 26 So God sent King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria to attack these Israelite tribes. The king led them away as prisoners to Assyria, and from then on, he forced them to live in Halah, Habor, Hara, and near the Gozan River.
translation_text:
1Izirali nidoabili kpagni Aruben nidoabilisaŋa ale nna: Wa ale jam chim nidoabili kpagni, alege wa ale taŋ wa kowa powa la nyiŋ, wa biam kpaŋtaŋa yaa cheŋ Izirali nidoabinni Josefi nidoabilisaŋa jigi. Dila nyiŋ wa yuenni a ka dɔkdemma po ase wa ka nidoabi kpagi la. 2Juda a jam le pagrɔwa wa suataŋa po ate niŋdeerɔ a nyini wa buuni po. Josefi yaa jam soa biam kpaŋtaŋa. 3Izirali nidoabili kpagni Aruben nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Yanok ale Pallu ale Ayeziron ale Karmi.
4Joel ŋaaŋbisaŋa a jam le nna: Sɛmaiya a jam ka Joel nidoabili. Gɔg a jam ka Sɛmaiya nidoabili. Simei jam ka Gɔg nidoabili. 5Maika jam ka Simei nidoabili, Areaiya jam ka Maika nidoabili. Baal jam ka Areaiya nidoabili. 6Beeraya jam ka Baal nidoabili. Beeraya a jam ka Aruben dɔkku buuni niŋdeerɔ, waai ate Assiria naawa Tilgat Pilneser a jam nak yik la.
7Ba kobirinni yezuimaŋa ale ŋmarisi doa ba ŋiak wieŋa po la ale nna: Jeiel ale kpagi ale Zakaria 8ale Azaz nidoabinni Bela, Azaz mɛ jam ka Sɛma nidoabili, Sɛma jam ka Joel nidoabili. Ba jam boka Aroer kabini a va dula meena a cheŋ Nebo ale Baal Meon. 9Nuruma a jam bo ka kori geŋsa a yalima a paari sagni ale bo Yufiretis Benaŋka la, dii nyiŋla ba duŋsaŋa a jam piisi kama Gilead tɛŋka po.
10Sɔɔl naamu vaaŋa po ba jam nye ka kpaliŋ ale Yagri demma a nak yik ba. Ba jam tuesi Yagri demma boka jigini kama a kala ka meena po ale bo Gilead kori geŋka la.
11Gad dɔkku ale jam paasaŋ ba a bo Basan a ta ga paari Saleka. 12Joel a jam le kpagi a pasaŋ Safam ale Janai ale Safat Basan po. 13Ba kobirinni a ta va ba dɔkdemma a jam le Maakil ale Mesullam ale Seba ale Jorai ale Jakan ale Zia ale Eber, ba meena jam ka bayopɔi. 14Bade a jam le Abiyail nidoabilisaŋa. Abiyail jam ka Yuri nidoabili. Yuri jam ka Jaroa nidoabili. Jaroa jam ka Gilead nidoabili. Gilead jam ka Maakil nidoabili. Maakil jam ka Jesisai nidoabili. Jesisai jam ka Jado nidoabili, Jado jam ka Buz nidoabili. 15Ayi jam ka Abdiel nidoabili, Abdiel jam ka Guni nidoabili. Ayi a jam le ba dɔkdemma niŋdeerɔ. 16Gad demma a jam boka Gilead tɛŋka ale bo Basan po la ale ka tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa ale wuuk a bo Saaron po a lagri a cheŋ la. 17Ŋade meena a jam bo ka gaŋka wieŋa ale jam ŋmarisi doa diipo ate Juda naawa Jotam ale Izirali naawa Jeroboam a dɛ ba naataŋa la.
18Aruben demma ale Gad demma ale Manasa demma buuni geli a jam ta ka nuruba tusa pisinaansi ale ŋanaansi ale kobsiyopɔi ale pisiyuebi (44,760) a magsi tugurik tuima, baai ale baga a nye kpaliŋ la, a baga a yik kpaliŋ kɔlima ale gebik, baai ale baga a tɔŋ tom ale baai ate ba sak ba a magsi kpaliŋ nyeka la. 19Ba jam nye ka kpaliŋ ale Yagri ale Jetur ale Nafis ale Nodab demma. 20Manasa ale Aruben diinaŋa buuni a jam puusi kama a te Naawen diipo ate kpaliŋka a nye la ayen wa maari ba. Wa yaa maari ba dii nyiŋla ba jam ta ka sebchakka ale wa. Wa yaa jam pai Yagri ale baai meena ale jam gum wa po la a nyo ba nisima po. 21Ba jam vari Yagri demma duŋsaŋa ka laalaakomiba tusa pisinu (50,000) ale piisa tusa kobsiye ale pisinu (250,000) ale bonsa tusa ŋaye (2,000). Ba jam maa ta ka nuru vuta tusa kook (100,000) a cheŋ ase yɔm la ale 22ko nuru boari dii nyiŋla kpaliŋka ka Wen ale soa. Ba jam bo tɛŋka po ka dila a ta ga paari diipo ate Kaldiya demma a jam nak yik ba a ta cheŋ la.
23Manasa dɔkku buuni geli a jam piisi kama. Ba jam bo ka Basan tɛŋka po a nyini dula a cheŋ Baal Yermon ale Senir ale Yermon Guuku.
24Ba yeeŋa nyama a jam le Efer ale Isi ale Eliel ale Azriel ale Jeremaya ale Yodavia ale Jadiel. Ba jam ka baai zuima ale koi kpaliŋ po a ta yuei ale chim niŋdeerɔba ba dɔkdemma po. 25Alege ba jam ka wensie ale ba koma Wenni ale pai badek a te wen yona ŋaai ate Wen a kaasi ba nina po la. 26Izirali Wenni yaa basi ate Assiria naawa Pul chiika a siti ba. Assiria naawa Tilgat Pilneser ale la, waai ale jam ta Aruben dɔkku ale Gad dɔkku ale Manasa dɔkku buuni geli a cheŋ yɔntidi po. Wa jam ta ba a cheŋ ka Yala ale Yabor ale Yara tɛŋsaŋa ale Gozan benaŋka, juijui ate ba boro a jam paari jinla de la.

english_text:
The Descendants of Levi
1Levi was the father of Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
2Kohath was the father of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. 3Amram was the father of Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.
Aaron had four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
4-14Eleazar's descendants included Phinehas, Abishua, Bukki, Uzzi, Zerahiah, Meraioth, Amariah, Ahitub, Zadok, Ahimaaz, Azariah, Johanan, Azariah the priest who served in the temple built by King Solomon, Amariah, Ahitub, Zadok, Shallum, Hilkiah, Azariah, Seraiah, and Jehozadak. 15King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia took Jehozadak to Babylon as prisoner when the Lord let the people of Judah and Jerusalem be dragged from their land.
16 Levi's three sons had sons of their own. 17Gershon was the father of Libni and Shimei. 18Kohath was the father of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. 19Merari was the father of Mahli and Mushi. These descendants of Levi each became leaders of their own clans.
20-21Gershon's descendants included Libni, Jahath, Zimmah, Joah, Iddo, Zerah, and Jeatherai.
22-24Kohath's descendants included Amminadab, Korah, Assir, Elkanah, Ebiasaph, Assir, Tahath, Uriel, Uzziah, and Shaul.
