4David appointed some of the Levites to serve at the sacred chest; they were to play music and sing praises to the Lord God of Israel. 5Asaph was their leader, and Zechariah was his assistant. Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and another man named Jeiel were appointed to play small harps and stringed instruments. Asaph himself played the cymbals, 6and the two priests Benaiah and Jahaziel were to blow trumpets every day in front of the sacred chest.
David's Song of Praise
(Psalms 105.1-15; 96.1-13; 106.1,47,48)
7That same day, David instructed Asaph and his relatives for the first time to sing these praises to the Lord:
8Praise the Lord
and pray in his name!
Tell everyone
what he has done.
9Sing praises to the Lord!
Tell about his miracles.
10Celebrate and worship
his holy name
with all your heart.
11Trust the Lord
and his mighty power.
Worship him always.
12Remember his miracles
and all his wonders
and his fair decisions.
13You belong to the family
of Israel, his servant;
you are his chosen ones,
the descendants of Jacob.
14The Lord is our God,
bringing justice
everywhere on earth.
15We must never forget
his agreement and his promises,
not in thousands of years.
* 16 God made an eternal promise
17to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
18when he said, “I'll give you
the land of Canaan.”
19At the time there were
only a few of us,
and we were homeless.
20We wandered from nation
to nation, from one country
to another.
21 God did not let anyone
mistreat our people.
Instead he protected us
by punishing rulers
22and telling them,
“Don't touch my chosen leaders
or harm my prophets!”
23Everyone on this earth,
sing praises to the Lord.
Day after day announce,
“The Lord has saved us!”
24Tell every nation on earth,
“The Lord is wonderful
and does marvelous things!
25The Lord is great and deserves
our greatest praise!
He is the only God
worthy of our worship.
26Other nations worship idols,
but the Lord created
the heavens.
27Give honor and praise
to the Lord,
whose power and beauty
fill his holy temple.”
28Tell everyone of every nation,
“Praise the glorious power
of the Lord.
29He is wonderful! Praise him
and bring an offering
into his temple.
Worship the Lord,
majestic and holy.
30Everyone on earth, now tremble!”
The world stands firm,
never to be shaken.
31Tell the heavens and the earth
to be glad and celebrate!
And announce to the nations,
“The Lord is King!”
32Command the ocean to roar
with all of its creatures
and the fields to rejoice
with all of their crops.
33Then every tree in the forest
will sing joyful songs
to the Lord.
He is coming to judge
all people on earth.
34 Praise the Lord
because he is good to us,
and his love never fails.
35Say to him, “Save us, Lord God!
Bring us back
from among the nations.
Let us celebrate and shout
in praise of your holy name.
36 Lord God of Israel,
you deserve to be praised
forever and ever.”
After David finished, the people shouted, “Amen! Praise the Lord!”
David Appoints Worship Leaders at Jerusalem and Gibeon
37David chose Asaph and the Levites in his clan to be in charge of the daily worship at the place where the sacred chest was kept. 38Obed-Edom and 68 of his relatives were their assistants, and Hosah and Obed-Edom the son of Jeduthun were the guards.
39David also chose Zadok the priest and his relatives who were priests to serve at the Lord's sacred tent at Gibeon. 40They were to offer sacrifices on the altar every morning and evening, just as the Lord had commanded in the Law he gave Israel. 41 Heman and Jeduthun were their assistants, as well as the other men who had been chosen to praise the Lord for his never-ending love. 42Heman and Jeduthun were also responsible for blowing the trumpets, and for playing the cymbals and other instruments during worship at the tent. The Levites in Jeduthun's clan were the guards at Gibeon.
43 After that, everyone went home, and David went home to his family.
translation_text:
1Ba yaa ta Wen nɔiyeŋka dakanni a jam a pai di a zaani viuku ate Deevid a jam ti magsi di la po, ba jam nye ka juka tiirita ale suiyɔgni tiirita Wen niŋ. 2Deevid ale ga nueri juka tiiritaŋa ale suiyɔgni tiiritaŋa kaabka la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, wa yaa niak nuruma Naawen yuenni nyiŋ. 3Wa yaa jam pai boroborok ale maasa a te Izirali nidoa ale nipok meena.
4Wa jam lueri ka Livaima gela ate ba a tom Naawen dakanni niŋ. Ba ale jam a de nuruma niŋ ate ba a puusi ale a te jiam ale a pak Naawen, Izirali Wenni. 5Asaf a jam le kpagni ate Zakaria pasaŋ a pai vi Jeiel ale Sɛmiramot ale Jeyiel ale Mattitia ale Eliab ale Benaya ale Obed Edom ale Jeiel. Ba ale jam a nak baganisaŋa ale kpantaŋa, Asaf ale jam a nak dalinkinkeŋsaŋa. 6Benaya ale Jayaziel kaabteerɔma ale jam ayen ba a peeri damunsaŋa veruveruk Wen nɔiyeŋka dakanni niŋ.
7Dai dila danni Deevid a jam dɛ niŋ a te Asaf ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ka yiini de ayen ba a te Naawen jiam:
8Te Naawen jiam, a wi wa yuenni basi ate tɛŋsaŋa a seba wa ale nye diila. 9Leni yiila a te wa, lenni pimpauk yiila a te wa, weeni wa wakinkagla nyeelaŋa meena te wa. 10Ta suipeentik wa tuilum yuenni nyiŋ, basi ate baai suiniima ale a gisi Naawen la a ta mariŋka. 11Zak nya Naawen ale wa pagrimu, kasim a gisi wa nimbidiaka diipo meena. 12A teeri wakperikaliisaŋa ate wa nye la wie, wa wakinkaglaŋa ale wa buusaŋa ate wa weeni la. 13Izirali wa tomteerɔwa ŋaaŋbisa, Jekob waai ate wa lueri la nidoabilisaŋa.
14Wa ka Naawen tama Wen, wa buusaŋa a bo tɛŋzuk de meena kama. 15Wa a teeri wa nɔiyeŋka kama taam wuu, wanni ate wa weeni a te gaŋsa tusa la, 16nɔiyeŋka ate wa jam nye ale Abrayam la, pumpuulimaŋa ate wa jam puulim ale Aizik la. 17Wa jam ŋman biisi di wari kama ale Jekob ase sinsaga la, ayen wa weeni Izirali demma ase ka nɔiyeŋ kaai ale ka boro a beni. 18<<Mi ale pai Keenan tɛŋka a te ni ase kauk kuui ale ku chim ni nitalim la.>>
19Ba ale jam kan soa diila, an sum soa diila, ale chim nicham ka po la, 20ba jam bo ka tɛŋsaŋa po a tuinti, a nyini naam po a taam m bu po. 21Wa an jam basi ate nuru a daani ba, ba nyiŋ wa toariŋ nalima. 22Wa weeni ayen, <<Ni kan tiri mi ale lueri baai la, kan nye mi biisiteerɔma wari ya.>>
23Ni lenni yiila a te Naawen, nama tɛŋzuk demma meena, ni mooli wa varibasika wie daa meena. 24Ni weeni wa zulaŋa tɛŋsa meena po, ni weeni wa wakinkaglaŋa ate nuru meena a wom. 25Ale Naawen a ŋmasi zuak ka yega a magsi pimpauk. Wa magsi ba chali wa a gaam wena meena. 26Tɛŋsaŋa meena wenaŋa ka bɔgta, alege ka Naawen ale nye wenŋmazukku. 27Nalim ale naam a bo ka wa niŋ, pagrim ale masim ale bo wa boka jigini. 28Ni pak Naawen tɛŋsa meena tɛŋzuk de ni pak Naawen zulaŋa ale wa pagrimu, 29ni te Naawen zula ŋaai ale magsi wa yuenni la, ni ta tiirim a jam wa niŋ, ni puusi Naawen nalim weleŋsaŋa po. 30Ni te ni nyiŋsa a gɔk wa niŋ tɛŋzuk de meena tɛŋka a feri paari kama, ka kan choa. 31Basi ate wenŋmazukku a dɛ masim, basi ate tɛŋzuk de sui a peenti. Basi ate ba weeni tɛŋsa meena po ayen, <<Naawen a dɛ naam.>> 32Basi ate nyakpiemu a pilim nuem ale ŋan baai meena ale bo bu po la. Basi ate tattaŋa ale jaab meena ale bo ti po la a naŋ. 33Ate tiisaŋa ale bo sagni po la lenni yiila ale masim Naawen niŋ, diila wa cheen wa bo ka tɛŋzuk de buusa.
34Ni te Naawen jiam ale wa ka Naawen maŋ, wa ŋmanteka a boro kama taam wuu. 35Ni kaari a weeni ayen, <<Vari ti a basi, Wen tama varibasidɔ, tigsi ti a vari ti a basi a ta nyini tɛŋsaŋa jigi, ate tama ale te fi tuilum yuenni jiam, ate tama ale ta zula fi pimpaukku po.>> 36Pimpauk a cheŋ Naawen, Izirali Wenni jigi, a kasim a cheŋ taam wuu. Ate nuruma meena jam weeni ayen, <<Ku be nye dila,>> ale <<Pak Naawen.>>
37Deevid yaa jam basi Asaf ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔma Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni niŋ ayen ba tom dula veruveruk a ta va chaab ale dii meena ale magsi ba nye la. 38Wa jam maa basi Obed Edom ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔba pisiyuebi ale naanika kama ayen ba a tom ale ba. Obed Edom ale ka Jedutun nidoabili la, ale Yosa, mɛ jam ka nansuiŋ limisidɔba.
39Deevid yaa basi Zadok kaabteerɔwa ale wa kaabteerɔba ba chaama ayen ba bo Naawen viuku po pimpitini ale bo Gibeon po la. 40Ayen ba a nye juka tiirita a te Naawen kuŋkuŋku zuk ate ba a nye juka tiirimu veruveruk la, saluik ale junɔi a ta va dii meena ale ŋmarisi Naawen Sinsaŋŋa po la, ŋaai ate wa te Izirali demma la. 41A gum ba po jam ka Yeman ale Jedutun ale baai meena ate ba jam lueri a ŋmarisi ba yueŋa ayen ba te Naawen jiam la, <<Diila wa ŋmanteka a boro ka dila taam wuu.>> 42Yeman ale Jedutun tuini jam le damunsaŋa peerika sinyaara nakka ale ŋan nagin yonta a magsi yi weleŋsa. Jedutun nidoabilisaŋa a jam bo ka nansuiŋku.
43Nuruma meena yaa basi dula, waai meena a kuli wadek yeri, ate Deevid a ŋmani kuli yeri ayen wa niak wa dɔkdemma.

english_text:
The Lord's Message to David
(2 Samuel 7.1-17)
1Soon after David moved into his new palace, he said to Nathan the prophet, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest is kept in a tent.”
2Nathan replied, “The Lord is with you—do what you want.”
3That night, the Lord told Nathan 4to go to David and tell him:
David, you are my servant, so listen carefully: You are not the one to build a temple for me. 5I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them. 6I chose special leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
7David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people. 8Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
9I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace. They will no longer have to tremble with fear—evil nations won't bother them, as they did 10when I let judges rule my people, and I will keep your enemies from attacking you.
Now I promise that like you, your descendants will be kings. 11I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried beside your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler, 12and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me. 13 I will be like a father to him, and he will be like a son to me. I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you. 14I will make sure that your son and his descendants will rule my people and my kingdom forever.
15Nathan told David exactly what the Lord had said.
David Gives Thanks to the Lord
(2 Samuel 7.18-29)
16David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. He sat there and prayed:
Lord God, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us, 17and yet you have promised to do even more for my descendants. You are treating me as if I am a very important person. 18I am your servant, and you know my thoughts. What else can I say, except that you have honored me? 19It was your choice to do these wonderful things for me and to make these promises.
20No other god is like you, Lord—you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true. 21And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so that your people could live here. 22You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
23 Lord God, please do what you promised me and my descendants. 24Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord All-Powerful rules Israel and is their God.”
My kingdom will be strong, 25because you are my God, and you have promised that my descendants will be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
26You are the Lord God, and you have made this good promise to me. 27Now please bless my descendants forever, and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already blessed my family, and I know you will bless us forever.
translation_text:
1Deevid ale ga kali wa naab yenni po la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, wa yaa weeni biisiteerɔwa Natan ayen, <<Mi ale nna dela, a bo naab yeri ate ba pai nyunyoŋ daata a sɛ di la po, alege Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni a bo viuk po.>>
2Natan yaa tulisi Deevid ayen, <<Dii ate fi ta fi popolaŋa po la nye di ale Wen a bo ale fu kama.>>
3Yok kula Naawen wanni yaa jam Natan jigi ayen, 4<<Cheŋ ga weeni mi tomteerɔwa Deevid ayen, <Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna. Daa fi ale waai ale wa sɛ yeri a te mi a bo di po la. 5Mi an bo yeri po a nyini dai dii danni ate mi ta Izirali demma a nyini Ejipiti po la a jam paari danni de. Mi jam nyini ka viuk po a jo ku choa po, a nyini boka jigi a jo ka choa jigi. 6Mi jam a cheŋ ale Izirali demma meena kama, mi diem weeni ba niŋdeerɔma wanyi baai ate mi weeni ba ayen ba nya mi nuruma zuk la ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi an pai nyunyoŋ daata a sɛ yeri a te mi?>>
7Yɔgyɔgla de, weeni mi tomteerɔwa Deevid ayen, <Dii ate Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La a weeni la ale nna: Diipo ate fi jam chim naapeerik a kasi duŋsa la ate mi a ta fu a jam ayen fi a nya mi nuruma Izirali demma zuk. 8Mi jam bo ale fu kama juijui meena ate fi a cheŋ la, mi abe jam kaasi fi dachaasaŋa meena kama fi niŋ. Yɔgyɔgla de mi ale basi ate fi yuenni a nye ase ka nuru kpientaŋa ale jam bo tɛŋzuk de la yueŋa la. 9Mi ale yaali jigi a te m nuruma Izirali demma abe m te ba jigi ate dila ale basi ate ba ta badek yeri ate daanika a kan ŋman tu ba. Gaasa nyam a kan ŋman namsi ba, ase ku ale jam nye ba piilimka po diila, 10ale jam nye ba dii, diipo ate mi jam lueri niŋdeerɔba m nuruma Izirali demma zuk la. Mi ale nak yik ni dachaasaŋa meena. <<Mi a weeni fu kama ayen Naawen ale sɛ yeri a te fu. 11Ase fi daaŋa a dan nueri ate fi cheŋ ayen fi bo ale fi koma, mi ale lueri ka fi nidoabili ate wa zaani fi nankula po, fidek nidoabilisaŋa po wanyi, mi ale basi ate wa naamu a zaani nalimnyiini. 12Wa ale waai ale wa sɛ yeri a te mi, mi ale basi ate wa naamu a zaani nalimnyiini taam wuu. 13Mi ale chim wa ko ate wa ale chim mi nidoabili. Mi a kan basi m ŋmanteka ale wa ase m le jam basi ŋmanteka ale Sɔɔl diila. 14Mi ale basi ate wa nya mi yenni ale m naamu zuk taam wuu, wa naam zukpaglika ale zaani nalimnyiini taam wuu.
15Natan a jam weeni Deevid a va chaab ale wieŋa de meena ale pai sakka de meena kama. 16Naab Deevid yaa jam cheŋ ga kali Naawen niŋ ayen, <<Mi ka wana, Naawen dii ale ka Wen la, m dɔkdemma ka bana, ate fi nye nnala meena a te mi? 17Fi nye ka nna ase kude an poom magsi fi nina po la Wen yaa, fi poom biisi fi tomteerɔwa chum po yenni wari kama. Fi a nya mi ase ka nuru waai ale ta yuei a gaam nidoaba ale ta yue la, Naawen dii ale ka Wen la.
18<<Ka boa ate Deevid ale weeni fi a gaam fi ale zuli fi tomteerɔwa la? Diila fi seba fi tomteerɔwa kama, 19Naawen yaa, fi tomteerɔwa nyiŋ ale fi yaali ka nyiŋ, fi nye wakpienni de kama ale seba pumpuulimaŋa de meena.
20Waai a karo ase fi la, Naawen yaa, Wen abe karo alege ka fi, ase tama ale wom ale tidek tue la. 21Ka wana ale a nye ase fi nuruma Izirali la, tɛŋ yeŋ kaai tɛŋzuk de baai Wen ale jam nyini ayen wa da tuesi nuruba a te wadek la, abe wa nye yuei a te wadek, abe wa nye wakpiema ale kpazinagsuk wakinkagla, a yiak tɛŋsa a basi fi nuruma niŋ, baai ate fi da tuesi a ta nyini Ejipiti la? 22Fi nye fi nuruma Izirali ka fidek nuruba a taa cheŋ, Naawen yaa, fi ale chim ba Wen.
23<<Yɔgyɔgla de, Naawen, basi ate pumpuulinni ate fi jam nye a ta va fi tomteerɔwa ale wa yenni la a zaani paari taam wuu. Nye ase fi ale jam puulim diila, 24ate dila ale basi ate di zaani paari ate fi yuenni ale yiti taam wuu. Ate nuruba yaa le weeni ayen, <Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Wen dii ale a nya Izirali zuk la, ka Izirali Wen.> Ate fi tomteerɔwa Deevid yenni ale zaani paari taam wuu.
25<<Fi, mi Wenni, a pai sak fi tomteerɔwa kama ayen fi ale sɛ yeri a te wa. Dila fi tomteerɔwa yaa nya nyiŋbiiri a puusi a te fi. 26Naawen yaa, fi ka Wen. Fi puulim wamaŋsaŋa de a te fi tomteerɔwa kama. 27Yɔgyɔgla de fi sui a peenti kama ate fi niak fi tomteerɔwa yenni, ayen ku le tom du taam wuu fi jigi a cheŋ, fi jigi, Naawen yaa, fi niak di kama, di be le nya niaka taam wuu.>>

english_text:
A List of David's Victories in War
(2 Samuel 8.1-14)
1Later, David attacked and defeated the Philistines. He captured their town of Gath and the nearby villages.
2David also defeated the Moabites, and so they had to accept him as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
3While King Hadadezer of Zobah was trying to gain control of the territory near the Euphrates River, David met him in battle at Hamath and defeated him. 4David captured 1,000 chariots, 7,000 chariot drivers, and 20,000 soldiers. And he crippled all but 100 of the horses.
5When troops from the Syrian kingdom of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David killed 22,000 of them. 6Then David stationed some of his troops in Damascus, and the people there had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
7Hadadezer's officers had carried gold shields, but David took these shields and brought them back to Jerusalem. 8 He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Tibhath and Cun, which had belonged to Hadadezer. Later, Solomon used this bronze to make the large bowl called the Sea, and to make the pillars and other furnishings for the temple.
9-10King Tou of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Tou heard that David had defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Hadoram to congratulate David on his victory. Hadoram also brought him gifts made of gold, silver, and bronze. 11David gave these gifts to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold he had captured from Edom, Moab, Ammon, Philistia, and Amalek.
12 Abishai the son of Zeruiah defeated the Edomite army in Salt Valley and killed 18,000 of their troops. 13Then he stationed troops in Edom, and the people there had to accept David as their ruler.
Everywhere David went, the Lord gave him victory in war.
A List of David's Officials
(2 Samuel 8.15-18)
14David ruled all Israel with fairness and justice.
15Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army.
Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
16Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar were the priests.
Shavsha was the secretary.
17Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard.
David's sons were his highest-ranking officials.
translation_text:
1Ku ale beni magadek la, Deevid yaa nya pagrim Filistia demma zuk a nak yik ba, a tuesi Gat ale ka tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa ale gilim ka la a ta nyini Filistia demma jigi.
2Deevid a jam maa nya pagrim Moab demma mɛ zuk kama ate ba siak te wa a tuni lampoo.
3Deevid a jam kpaliŋ ale Zoba naawa Yadadezer kama, a ga paari Yamat, ase wa le jam a yaali wa naamu a tati paari Yufiretis Benaŋka la. 4Deevid a jam nak yik ka wa torokoba tusidi ale toroko damdɔba tusa ŋayopɔi (7,000) ale tugurik tɔŋdɔba tusa pisiye (20,000). Wa jam gebi wusumaŋa meena nanjiinaŋa kama ka toroko wusuma kook nyiini.
5Ase Araam demma ale bo Damasikus la ale jam ba maari Zoba naawa Yadadezer la, Deevid a jam ko ba ka tusa pisiye ale ŋaye (22,000). 6Wa jam basi ka tugurik tɔŋdɔba beŋsa Araam tɛŋka naamu ale bo Damasikus po la, ate Araam demma a siak te wa a tuni lampoo. Naawen a jam te Deevid ka nak dekka juijui meena ate wa jam cheŋ la.
7Deevid yaa pai ligmɔniŋ kpaliŋ ŋanchɔgsintaŋa ate Yadadezer kpaŋŋa a jam ji la a ta ba a jam Jerusalem po. 8A nyini Tibyat ale Kun, tɛŋ kpieŋ sii ate Yadadezer a soa la, Deevid a jam pai ka kutuk mɔnuŋ nna yegayega, tii ate Solomon a jam pai a nye kutuk mɔnuŋ Nyakpiemu ale zaŋŋa ale kutuk mɔnuŋ ŋantomtaŋa la.
9Ase Yamat naawa Tou ale ga wom ayen Deevid a nya pagrim Zoba naawa Yadadezer tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena zuk la, 10wa yaa tom wa nidoabinni Yadoram naab Deevid jigi ayen wa puusi wa abe wa pak wa ale nak de kpaliŋka Yadadezer waai ale jam ta chaab ale Tou la. Yadoram a jam ta ka ŋanta buuri meena ate ba pai ligmɔniŋ ale kpana ale kutuk mɔnuŋ a nye ba la a jam.
11Naab Deevid a jam pai ŋantaŋa a nyo ka Naawen nisa po ase wa ale jam nye kpanaŋa ale ligmɔniŋka ate ba pai Edom ale Moab ale Amon ale Filistia ale Amalek tɛŋsaŋa po a nye diila.
12Zeruiya nidoabinni Abisai a ko ka Edom dem tusa pi ale naaniŋ (18,000) Yesa Viaka po. 13Wa jam basi ka tugurik tɔŋdɔba beŋsa Edom po ate Edom demma meena a siak te Deevid. Naawen a jam te Deevid ka nak dɛka juijui meena ate wa jam cheŋ la.
14Deevid a jam dɛ naam Izirali meena po, a nye dii ale nala la ale wensie a te wa nuruma meena. 15Zeruiya nidoabinni Joab ale jam a nya tugurik tɔŋdɔma zuk. Ayilud nidoabinni Jeyosafat a jam le gbaŋ ŋmarisidoa. 16Ayitub nidoabinni Zadok ale Abiata nidoabinni Ayimelek jam le kaabteerɔma. Savsa jam le teeridɔwa. 17Jeyoiada nidoabinni Benaya ale jam a nya Keret ale Pelet demma zuk, ate Deevid nidoabilisaŋa a jam chim kpaga a tom ale wa.

english_text:
Israel Fights Ammon and Syria
(2 Samuel 10.1-19)
1Some time later, King Nahash of Ammon died, and his son Hanun became king. 2David said, “Nahash was kind to me, so I will be kind to his son.” He sent some officials to Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died.
But when David's officials arrived at Ammon, 3the Ammonite leaders said to Hanun, “Do you really believe King David is honoring your father by sending these men to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our country, so he can come and destroy it.”
4Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off and their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away. 5They were terribly ashamed.
When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message that told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
6The Ammonites realized they had made David furious. So they paid 34 tons of silver to hire chariot troops from Mesopotamia and from the Syrian kingdoms of Maacah and Zobah. 7Thirty-two thousand troops, as well as the king of Maacah and his army, came and camped near Medeba. The Ammonite troops also left their towns and came to prepare for battle.
8David heard what was happening, and he sent out Joab with his army. 9The Ammonite troops marched to the entrance of the city and prepared for battle, while the Syrian troops took their positions in the open fields.
10Joab saw that the enemy troops were lined up on both sides of him. So he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Syrians. 11Then he put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and told them to fight against the Ammonites. 12Joab told his brother, “If the Syrians are too much for me to handle, come and help me. And if the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you. 13Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the towns of our Lord God. I pray he will do whatever pleases him.”
14Joab and his soldiers attacked the Syrians, and the Syrians ran from them. 15When the Ammonite troops saw that the Syrians had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab then returned to Jerusalem.
16As soon as the Syrians realized they had been defeated, they sent for their troops that were stationed on the other side of the Euphrates River. Shophach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led these troops to Ammon.
17David found out what the Syrians were doing, and he brought Israel's entire army together. They crossed the Jordan River, and he commanded them to take their positions facing the Syrian troops.
Soon after the fighting began, 18the Syrians ran from Israel. David killed 7,000 chariot troops and 40,000 regular soldiers. He also killed Shophach, their commander.
19When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had defeated them, they made peace with David and accepted him as their new ruler. The Syrians never helped the Ammonites again.
translation_text:
1Ku ale beni magadek la, Ammon naawa Nayas yaa kpi ate wa nidoabinni a zaani wa naŋ kula po a chim naab. 2Deevid yaa poli ayen, <<Mi ale sak nyemagsika ale Nayas nidoabinni Yanun, dii nyiŋla wa kowa a jam sak ka jiirim ale mu.>> Dila Deevid yaa tom nuruba ayen ba ga puusi wa, wa kowa ale kpi la nyiŋ. Ase Deevid nuruma ale jan jam Yanun jigi Ammon tɛŋka po ayen ba puusi wa la, 3Ammon kpaŋŋa yaa weeni Yanun ayen, <<Fi a poli Deevid a zuli fi kowa kama a tom nuruba ayen ba puusi fu? Wa nuruma an jam fi jigi tɛŋka po ba kpesi nya ka ti tɛŋka a tuesi ka?>> 4Dila nyiŋ Yanun yaa yik Deevid nuruma a chiiri ba teeŋsaŋa, a cheeri ba gattaŋa suŋsuŋsaŋa po ba butagkolaŋa geŋsa a basi ba suik po.
5Ase nuru ale jam weeni Deevid nuruma wie la, wa yaa tom nuruba ayen ba tu ba, ba jam nyo ba ka chivie po nna yegayega. Naawa jam weeni kama ayen, <<Ni bo Jeriko ate ni teeŋsaŋa a chim ate ni ŋman jam.
6Ase Ammon demma ale ga miŋ ayen ba wanni a nyuŋ ka Deevid nyue la, Yanun ale Ammon demma yaa tom nuruba ale kpana ligbie dobrim tusidi ayen ba yaali wusuma torokoba ale toroko damdɔba ate ba nyini Araam Nayaraim ale Araam Maaka ale Zoba tɛŋsaŋa. 7Ba jam tuni tuesi ka torokoba ale damdɔba tusa pisita ale ŋaye (32,000) a pai Maaka naawa tugurik tɔŋdɔma a gum du, baai ale jam kali moata Medeba la, alege ate Ammon demma a tigsi chaab a nyini ba tɛŋsaŋa po a magsi kpaliŋ.
8Deevid ale ga wom kude la, wa yaa tom Joab ate wa nyini ale tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena. 9Ammon demma a jam nyini kama a zaani magsi kpaliŋ ba tɛŋka nansuiŋku nɔi, alege ate nalim ŋaai ale jam badek la a bo tɛŋka peelimmu po.
10Joab yaa nya ayen kpaliŋ ale bo wa niŋ ale wa ŋaaŋ. Dila wa yaa luk lueri tugurik tɔŋdɔ maŋsaŋa gela ale bo Izirali po la ate ba tu chaab ale Araam demma. 11Wa jam pai mbala meena a nyo ka wa suoku Abisai nisa po, ate ba mɛ a nyini tu chaab ale Ammon demma. 12Joab a jam weeni kama ayen, <<Ase Araam demma a dan ŋmasi pagra a te mi, ni yaa jam vari mu a basi, alege Ammon demma a dan ŋmasi pagra a te ni, mi ale vari ni a basi. 13Ni be pagra abe ni basi ate ti kpaliŋ tuotuowa a te ti nuruma ale ti Wenni tɛŋka. Naawen ale nye dii ale nala la wa nimbie po.>>
14Joab ale tugurik tɔŋdɔma yaa cheŋ ba siti Araam demma ate ba yiti chali. 15Ase Ammon demma ale jam nya ale Araam demma a chali la, ba mɛ yaa yiti chali ale ge wa suoku Abisai a jo tɛŋ kpieŋka po. Dila Joab yaa ŋmani cheŋ Jerusalem.
16Araam demma ale ga nya ale Izirali demma a nak yik ba kama la, ba yaa tom wi Araam dem baai ale gaam Benni a kala la ate ba jam ale Yadadezer tugurik tɔŋdɔma niŋdeerɔwa Sofak.
17Ase Deevid ale ga wom kude la, wa yaa tigsi Izirali meena a lo Jodan Benni a jueli, wa jam ga moata ba kama, a zaani wa kpaliŋ zaaniŋa a tuk ba nyiŋ. Deevid a jam nye dila ayen wa siti ka Araam demma, ba jam siti ba kama. 18Alege Araam demma jam yiti chali ale ge Izirali demma, ate Deevid a ko ba toroko damdɔma tusa ŋayopɔi (7,000) ale ba tugurik tɔŋdɔba tusa pisinaansi (40,000). Wa jam ko tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagni Sofak mɛ kama.
19Ase Yadadezer nuruma ale ga nya ale Izirali demma a nak yik ba la, ba yaa nye nɔiyeŋ ale Deevid a siak te wa. Dila Araam demma an ŋman jam a yaali ba maari Ammon demma diipo diipo.

english_text:
The End of the War with Ammon
(2 Samuel 11.1; 12.26-31)
1 The next spring, the time when kings go to war, Joab marched out in command of the Israelite army and destroyed towns all over the country of Ammon. He attacked the capital city of Rabbah and left it in ruins. But David stayed in Jerusalem.
2Later, David himself went to Rabbah, where he took the crown from the statue of their god Milcom. The crown was made of about 34 kilograms of gold, and there was a valuable jewel on it. David put the jewel on his crown, then carried off everything else of value. 3He forced the people of Rabbah to work with saws, iron picks, and axes. He also did the same thing with the people in all the other Ammonite towns.
David then led Israel's army back to Jerusalem.
The Descendants of the Rephaim
(2 Samuel 21.15-22)
4Some time later, Israel fought a battle against the Philistines at Gezer. During this battle, Sibbecai from Hushah killed Sippai, a descendant of the Rephaim, and the Philistines were defeated.
5 In another battle against the Philistines, Elhanan the son of Jair killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam.
6Another one of the Philistine soldiers who was a descendant of the Rephaim was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot. During a battle at Gath, 7he made fun of Israel, so David's nephew Jonathan killed him.
8David and his soldiers killed these three men from Gath who were descendants of the Rephaim.
translation_text:
1Fanɔi diipo ate nalima a vuusi a kan cheŋ kpaliŋ po la, Joab ale jam dɛ tugurik tɔŋdɔma niŋ. Wa jam kaasi Ammon tɛŋka kama ale cheŋ Arabba a gilim ka, alege Deevid a jam wari bo ka Jerusalem po. Joab a jam siti Arabba kama a nye ate ka doa koruk. 2Deevid a jam lak naam zutɔkka ba naawa zukku po kama. Ka dobrimu jam ka ligmɔniŋ boorik dobrim ate tintain naliŋsa a bo ka nyiŋ, ka jam vuk ka Deevid zukku po. Wa jam kɔlim ka ŋanta nna yegayega a nyini tɛŋka po. 3Ale ta nuru baai ale jam bo dula la a nyini, ate ba a tom yontidi tuima ale gebisa ale kutuk mɔnuŋ pein gaasa ale laasa. Deevid a jam nye kude ale ka Ammon tɛŋsaŋa meena. Deevid ale wa tugurik tommu meena yaa ŋmani cheŋ Jerusalem.
4Ku ale beni magadek la, kpaliŋ ale jam yiti Filistia ale bo Gezer po la. Va ŋala po Yusat denɔwa Sibbekai a jam ko ka Arefa ŋaaŋbisaŋa po wanyi Sippai, ate Filistia demma a jam siak te ba.
5Ba le jam ta kpaliŋ ka choa ale Filistia demma la, Jair nidoabinni Elhanan jam ko ka Gitti denɔwa Goliat suoku Lami, waai ale jam ta gbaluk ate ku yikka jigini a woŋŋa ase yɔgdɔ doari la.
6Kpaliŋ ka choa ale ŋman jam nye Gat po la, nuru ganduok ale nandubsa siyuebi naŋsa ale nisa meena, naŋ yeŋ siyuebi nisa mɛ siyuebi, si meena pisiye ale sinaansi. Wa mɛ jam ka Arafa ŋaaŋbiik. 7Wa le jam nye Izirali a la la, Simeaya nidoabinni Jonatan, Deevid suoku a yaa ko wa.
8Bade jam ka Arafa ŋaaŋbisa Gat tɛŋka po, ba jam bo ka Deevid ale wa nidoama nisa po.

english_text:
David Counts the People
(2 Samuel 24.1-9)
1Satan decided to cause trouble for Israel by making David think it was a good idea to find out how many people there were in Israel and Judah. 2David told Joab and the army commanders, “Count everyone in Israel, from the town of Beersheba in the south all the way north to Dan. Then I will know how many people can serve in my army.”
3Joab answered, “Your Majesty, even if the Lord made your kingdom a hundred times larger, you would still rule everyone in it. Why do you need to know how many soldiers there are? Don't you think that would make the whole nation angry?”
4But David would not change his mind. And so Joab went everywhere in Israel and Judah and counted the people. He returned to Jerusalem 5and told David that the total number of men who could serve in the army was 1,100,000 in Israel and 470,000 in Judah. 6Joab refused to include anyone from the tribes of Levi and Benjamin, because he still disagreed with David's orders.
God Punishes Israel
(2 Samuel 24.10-17)
7David's order to count the people made God angry, and he punished Israel. 8David prayed, “I am your servant. But what I did was stupid and terribly wrong. Please forgive me.”
9The Lord said to Gad, one of David's prophets, 10“Tell David that I will punish him in one of three ways. But he will have to choose which one it will be.”
11Gad went to David and told him:
You must choose how the Lord will punish you: 12Will there be three years when the land won't grow enough food for its people? Or will your enemies constantly defeat you for three months? Or will the Lord send a horrible disease to strike your land for three days? Think about it and decide, because I have to give your answer to God who sent me.
13David was miserable and said, “It's a terrible choice to make! But the Lord is kind, and I'd rather be punished by him than by anyone else.”
14So the Lord sent a horrible disease on Israel, and 70,000 Israelites died. 15Then he sent an angel to destroy the city of Jerusalem. But just as the angel was about to do that, the Lord felt sorry for all the suffering he had caused the people, and he told the angel, “Stop! They have suffered enough.” This happened at the threshing place that belonged to Araunah the Jebusite.
16David saw the Lord's angel in the air, holding a sword over Jerusalem. He and the leaders of Israel, who were all wearing sackcloth, bowed with their faces to the ground, 17and David prayed, “It's my fault! I sinned by ordering the people to be counted. They have done nothing wrong—they are innocent sheep. Lord God, please punish me and my family. Don't let the disease wipe out your people.”
David Buys Araunah's Threshing Place
(2 Samuel 24.18-25)
18The Lord's angel told the prophet Gad to tell David that he must go to Araunah's threshing place and build an altar in honor of the Lord. 19David followed the Lord's instructions.
20Araunah and his four sons were threshing wheat at the time, and when they saw the angel, the four sons ran to hide. 21Just then, David arrived, and when Araunah saw him, he stopped his work and bowed down.
22David said, “Would you sell me your threshing place, so I can build an altar on it to the Lord? Then this disease will stop killing the people. I'm willing to pay whatever you say it's worth.”
23Araunah answered, “Take it, Your Majesty, and do whatever you want with it. I'll even give you the oxen for the sacrifice and the wheat for the grain sacrifice. And you can use the threshing-boards for the fire. It's all yours!”
24But David replied, “No! I want to pay you what they're worth. I can't just take something from you and then offer the Lord a sacrifice that cost me nothing.”
25So David paid Araunah 600 gold coins for his threshing place. 26David built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. David prayed, and the Lord answered him by sending fire down on the altar. 27Then the Lord commanded the angel to put the sword away.
28When David saw that the Lord had answered his prayer, he offered more sacrifices there at the threshing place, 29-30because he was afraid of the angel's sword and did not want to go all the way to Gibeon. That's where the sacred tent that Moses had made in the desert was kept, as well as the altar where sacrifices were offered to the Lord.
translation_text:
1Sitaana yaa jam yiti a ta chaab ale Izirali a choa Deevid ayen wa chiini Izirali demma meena. 2Dila Deevid yaa weeni Joab ale tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpaŋŋa ayen, <<Ni ga chiini Izirali demma a nyini Beerseba a ga paari Dan. Ni ŋman jam weeni mu ate m seba ba nɔi ale ka diila.>>
3Alege Joab a tulisi ayen, <<Naawen a basi ate wa tugurik tommu a piisi ka ku nɔi kook a gum du. Mi nyɔnɔ naabaa, ba meena an bo daa mi nyɔnɔwa nisa po? Ka boa ate mi nyɔnɔwa a yaali wa nye wanni de? Ka boa ate wa a yaali ayen wa ta foolaa nyeka a jam Izirali zuwa?>>
4Naawa wanni a jam pagra gaam Joab kama. Dila Joab yaa jam cheŋ Izirali meena po a yaa ŋman jam Jerusalem po. 5Joab yaa ga weeni tugurik tɔŋdɔma nɔi ale ka diila a sak Deevid. Izirali meena po ka nuruba tusa kobsi pi ale kook (1,100,000) baai ale seba gebik yikka la, a gum nuruba tusa kobsinaansi ale pisiyopɔi (470,000) ale nyini Juda la.
6Alege Joab an jam chiini Livaima ale Benjamin dɔkku a gum du, dii nyiŋla naawa wanni jam ka daanika a te wa. 7Wanni de a jam ka biem mɛ Wen nina po. Dila wa yaa dari ba tue.
8Deevid yaa weeni Wen ayen, <<Mi nye ka biem kpiem mi ni nye kude la nyiŋ. Yɔgyɔgla de, mi a saalim fu, yeeri foolaa nyeelaŋa fi tomteerɔwa jigi. Mi nye ka betta nyeka.>>
9Naawen yaa weeni Gad, Deevid biisiteerɔwa ayen, 10<<Cheŋ ga weeni Deevid ayen, <<Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna. Mi a te fu ka wie ŋata. Lueri ŋa po dinyi ate m nye m le ta dii ale fu la.>>
11Dila Gad yaa cheŋ Deevid jigi a weeni wa ayen, <<Dii ate Naawen a weeni la ale nna: Lueri fi ale a yaali diila. 12Bena ŋata kom ale jam yaase fi dachaasaŋa a vi ni chiisa sita ale ba gebisaŋa yaase daa ŋata Naawen maarɔwa a jam fi tɛŋka po ale gebik a ko ni Izirali meena po.> Yɔgyɔgla de poli dii ate mi ale ga tulisi waai ale tommu la.>>
13Deevid yaa weeni Gad ayen, <<Mi bo ka daani kpieŋ po. Basi ate mi lo Naawen nisa po ale wa jiirimu a zuak ka yega, alege kan basi ate m lo nurubiik nisa po.>>
14Dila Naawen yaa tom nyiŋtuila ate ŋa jam Izirali tɛŋka po, ate nuruba tusa pisiyopɔi (70,000) a jam kpi Izirali po. 15Ate Naawen yaa tom maarɔ ayen wa kaasi Jerusalem. Alege maarɔwa ale boro a nye dila la, Naawen yaa tagri wa popola kaasuŋku nyiŋ, a weeni maarɔwa waai ale jam a ko nuruma la ayen, <<Ku magsi ta fi nisaŋa a ga ŋaaŋ.>> Naawen maarɔwa yaa jam za ka Jebus denɔwa Ornan ŋanta fɔbika jigini.
16Deevid yaa nya ale Naawen maarɔwa a bo wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋzuk de suŋsuŋ, ale wa gebika wa nisa po a dak Jerusalem nyiŋ. Deevid ale nisɔmma yaa jo boorisa gatta, a doa pai nina a vuk tɛŋ.
17Deevid yaa weeni Wen ayen, <<Daa mi ale weeni ayen ba chiini tugurik tɔŋdɔma? Ka mi ale waai ale nye biemu ale nye kaasi la. Nuruma de a va mi ase ka piisa la. Ka boa ate ba nye? Naawen mi Wen yaa, basi ate fi suipuurumu a jam mi ale m dɔkdemma jigi, alege kan basi ate kaasuŋku de a wari fi nuruma zuwa.>>
18Ate Naawen maarɔwa yaa weeni Gad ayen wa weeni Deevid ate wa cheŋ ga sɛ kuŋkuŋ a te Naawen Jebus denɔwa Arauna ŋanta fɔbika jigini. 19Dila Deevid yaa siak jueli a va wanni ate Gad a weeni wa Naawen yuenni nyiŋla.
20Ase Arauna ale boro a fɔbi wiiti la, wa yaa viriŋ nya maarɔwa, wa nidoabilisa banaansiwa yaa jam chali suk. 21Deevid yaa forisi paari, ase Arauna ale ga nya wa la, wa ya basi ŋantaŋa fɔbika jigini ale koori tɛŋ Deevid niŋ ate wa nina a bo tɛŋ.
22Deevid yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Te mu jigi fi ŋanta fɔbika jigini ate m sɛ kuŋkuŋ a te Naawen, ate kaasuŋku nuruma zuk ale kpeglim. Da te mu ku le magsi ku da diila.>>
23Arauna yaa weeni Deevid ayen, <<Tanla, basi ate m nyɔnɔwa naawa nye dii ale a yɔk wa suinni la. Nya, m le te lalisa a magsi juka tiirimu abe m pai talimu nakpiaka daataŋa a te fu, abe wiiti a magsi ŋandiinta tiirimu. Mi ale te ŋantaŋa de meena.>>
24Alege naab Deevid yaa tulisi Arauna ayen, <<Aaya, mi a yaali m tuni jigini ale a da diila kama. Mi a kan pai jabuui ate fi soa la a te Naawen yaase m nye juka tiirim buui ate mi an tuni jaaboa.>>
25Dila Deevid yaa jam tuni Arauna ligmɔniŋ dobrim kobsiyuebi jigini nyiŋ. 26Deevid yaa sɛ kuŋkuŋ a te Naawen dula a kaab juka tiirita ale suiyɔgni tiirita. Wa jam wi ka Naawen, ate Naawen a tulisi wa ate bolim a nyini wenŋmazuk a lo kuŋkuŋku ate juka tiirimu a vi du la zuk.
27Naawen yaa biisi ale wa maarɔwa ate wa pai wa gebika a su ka fooku po. 28Dila powa dek, ase Deevid ale nya ayen Naawen a tulisi wa Arauna Jebus denɔwa ŋanta fɔbika jigini la, wa yaa nye kaabka tiirita dula. 29Naawen viuku kuui ate Moosis a jam nye sagni po la, juka tiirim kuŋkuŋku dipo a jam bo ka pimpitini zuk Gibeon po. 30Alege Deevid an jam baga a jueli dula a kpesi a nyini Wen jigi ya, dii nyiŋla wa jam yɔgsa kama ale Naawen maarɔwa ale jam ta wa gebika la.

english_text:
1David said, “The temple of the Lord God must be built right here at this threshing place. And the altar for offering sacrifices will also be here.”
David Prepares To Build the Temple
2David ordered the foreigners living in Israel to come to Jerusalem. Then he assigned some to cut blocks of stone for building the temple. 3He got a large supply of iron to make into nails and hinges for the doors, and he provided so much bronze that it could not be weighed. 4He also brought an endless supply of cedar logs from the cities of Sidon and Tyre.
5He said, “The temple for the Lord must be great, so that everyone in the world will know about it. But since my son Solomon is young and has no experience, I will make sure that everything is ready for the temple to be built.”
That's why David did all these things before he died.
David Instructs Solomon To Build the Temple
6David sent for his son Solomon and told him to build a temple for the Lord God of Israel. 7 He said:
My son, I wanted to build a temple where the Lord my God would be worshiped. 8But some time ago, he told me, “David, you have killed too many people and have fought too many battles. That's why you are not the one to build my temple. 9But when your son becomes king, I will give him peace throughout his kingdom. His name will be Solomon, because during his rule I will keep Israel safe and peaceful. 10Solomon will build my temple. He will be like a son to me, and I will be like a father to him. In fact, one of his descendants will always rule in Israel.”
11Solomon, my son, I now pray that the Lord your God will be with you and keep his promise to help you build a temple for him. 12May he give you wisdom and knowledge, so that you can rule Israel according to his Law. 13 If you obey the laws and teachings that the Lord gave Moses, you will be successful. Be strong and brave and don't get discouraged or be afraid of anything.
14I have all the supplies you'll need to build the temple: You have more than 3,000 tons of gold and over 34,000 tons of silver. There's also plenty of wood, stone, and more bronze and iron than I could weigh. Ask for anything else you need. 15I have also assigned men who will cut and lay the stone. And there are carpenters and people who are experts in working with 16gold, silver, bronze, and iron. You have plenty of workers to do the job. Now get started, and I pray that the Lord will be with you in your work.
17David then gave orders for the leaders of Israel to help Solomon. 18David said:
The Lord our God has helped me defeat all the people who lived here before us, and he has given you peace from all your enemies. Now this land belongs to the Lord and his people. 19Obey the Lord your God with your heart and soul. Begin work on the temple to honor him, so that the sacred chest and the things used for worship can be kept there.
translation_text:
1Deevid yaa weeni ayen, <<Naawen Wen yenni ale boka dela ale kuŋkuŋku a magsi juka tiirimu mɛ a te Izirali demma.>>
2Dila Deevid yaa tom weeni ate ba tigsi nichamma meena ale bo Izirali po la, a nyini ba po wa jam lueri ka tintain peesirɔba ayen ba peesi tana a magsi Wen yenni sɛka. 3Wa jam te ka kuta a piisi ayen ba gebi peema a magsi nansuiŋku tuataŋa ale ŋan yiginta, ale kutuk mɔnuŋ a piisi gaam magsika. 4Wa jam te ba ka nyunyoŋ daata mɛ ate ba an baga a chiini ti, diila Saidon demma ale Taaya demma a jam ta ti a piisi kama a jam te Deevid.
5Deevid yaa weeni ayen, <<Mi nidoabinni Solomon a paala kama ale diem zɛ wari ya, yenni ate ti za ti sɛ te Naawen la, ale zuak ale nalim abe di ta yuei abe di a nyaksi a te tɛŋ kpieŋsa meena. Dila nyiŋ mi ale gomsi ŋanta a magsi di.>> Dila Deevid yaa jam gomsi nna yegayega alege kpi.
6Wa yaa wi wa nidoabinni Solomon a weeni wa ayen wa sɛ yeri a te Naawen, Izirali Wenni. 7Deevid a weeni Solomon ayen, <<M biiga, mi ta ku kan m suinum po ayen m sɛ yeri Naawen m Wenni Yuenni nyiŋ. 8Alege Naawen wanni de a jam mi jigi ayen, <Fi basi ate ka ziim a nyini nna yegayega ale kpaliŋ boari. Fi a kan sɛ yeri mi Yuenni nyiŋŋa, dii nyiŋla fi basi ate ka ziim a nyini nna yegayega tɛŋzuk de mi nina po. 9Alege fi le nya nidoabili dii ale wa chim nidoa waai ale ta suiyɔgni ale vuusum la, ate mi ale te wa vuusum a nyini wa dachaasaŋa jigi kauk meena. Wa yuei ale chim ka Solomon, ate mi ale te Izirali vuusum abe ba nye diki wa naamu vaaŋa po. 10Ka wala ale waai ale wa sɛ yeri mi Yuenni nyiŋ. Wa le chim ka mi nidoabili ate mi ale chim wa ko. Mi ale basi ate wa naam zukpaglika a bo Izirali po taam wuu.
11<<Yɔgyɔgla de, m biiga, Naawen a bo le fu, abe fi ta nyeboka a sɛ Naawen fi Wen yenni, ase wa ale weeni la fi le nye. 12Naawen a te fu vuutaŋa ale miŋ chakka ase wa nin te suik ayen fi a nya Izirali zuk, ate dila ale basi ate fi ta Naawen fi Wenni sinsaŋŋa. 13Fi yaa le nya nyeboka ase fi a nin kpesi a ta wa ŋmarisika ale buusaŋa ate Naawen a jam te Moosis ate wa weeni Izirali la. Be pagra abe fi toa. Kan chali yɔgsum yaase fi jɔk nyiŋbiiri.
14<<Mi ko ka m dek nna yega a yaali ŋanta a magsi Naawen yenni, ligmɔniŋ boorik dobrim tusa kook (100,000), kpana dobrim tusa kobsa pi (1,000,000), kutuk mɔnuŋ ale kuta a piisi a ka magsika ale daata ale tintana. Fi baga a gum ŋanta du kama. 15Fi ta ka tuimtomdisa nna yegayega: tintain gebdisa ale yeseerisa ale danagrisa ale nidoa baai ale ŋmasi seba tuini meena tomka la. 16Ligmɔniŋ po ale kpana tuima ale kutuk mɔnuŋ tuima ale kutuk meena tuima ba ka chiina. Yɔgyɔgla de piilim tuini, Naawen a bo le fu.>>
17Deevid yaa jam weeni Izirali nisɔmma meena ayen ba maari wa nidoabinni Solomon. 18Wa jam weeni ba ayen, <<Naawen ni Wenni an bo le ni? Wa abe an te ni vuusum a nyini jigi meena? Wa pai tɛŋka demma meena a te mi kama, ate tɛŋka a siak te Naawen ale wa nuruma. 19Yɔgyɔgla de pai fi suinum ale fi chiik a gisi Naawen fi Wenni. Piilim a sɛ Naawen fi Wenni yenni, ate dila ale basi ate fi ta Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni ale ŋan weleŋsaŋa ate Wen a soa la a jam yenni ate fi sɛ Naawen Yuenni nyiŋla po.

english_text:
David Assigns the Levites Their Duties
1 David was old when he chose his son Solomon to be king of Israel. 2Some time later, David called together all of Israel's leaders, priests, and Levites. 3He then counted the Levite men who were at least 30 years old, and the total was 38,000. 4He said, “Twenty-four thousand of the Levites will be in charge of the temple, 6,000 will be temple officials and judges, 54,000 will be guards at the temple, and 4,000 will praise the Lord by playing the musical instruments I have given them.”
6David then divided the Levites into three groups according to the clans of Levi's sons, Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
7Gershon had two sons: Ladan and Shimei. 8Ladan was the father of Jehiel, Zetham, and Joel. 9They were all family leaders among their father's descendants. Shimei was the father of Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran. 10-11Later, Shimei had four more sons, in the following order: Jahath, Ziza, Jeush, and Beriah. But Jeush and Beriah didn't have many children, so their descendants were counted as one family.
12Kohath had four sons: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. 13 Amram was the father of Aaron and Moses. Aaron and his descendants were chosen to be in charge of all the sacred things. They served the Lord by offering sacrifices to him and by blessing the people in his name. 14-15Moses, the man of God, was the father of Gershom and Eliezer, and their descendants were considered Levites. 16Gershom's oldest son was Shebuel. 17Rehabiah, who was Eliezer's only son, had many children. 18The second son born to Kohath was Izhar, and his oldest son was Shelomith. 19Hebron, the third son of Kohath, was the father of Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam. 20Kohath's youngest son, Uzziel, was the father of Micah and Isshiah.
21Merari had two sons: Mahli and Mushi. Mahli was the father of Eleazar and Kish. 22Eleazar had no sons, only daughters, and they married their uncle's sons. 23Mushi the second son of Merari, was the father of Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth.
24These were the clans and families of the tribe of Levi. Those who were 20 years and older were assigned to work at the Lord's temple.
25David said:
The Lord God of Israel has given his people peace, and he will live in Jerusalem forever. 26 And so, the Levites won't need to move the sacred tent and the things used for worship from place to place. 27From now on, all Levites at least 20 years old 28 will serve the Lord by helping Aaron's descendants do their work at the temple, by keeping the courtyards and rooms of the temple clean, and by making sure that everything used in worship stays pure. 29They will also be in charge of the sacred loaves of bread, the flour for the grain sacrifices, the thin wafers, any offerings to be baked, and the flour mixed with olive oil. These Levites will weigh and measure these offerings.
30Every morning and evening, the Levites are to give thanks to the Lord and sing praises to him. 31They must also give thanks and sing praises when sacrifices are offered on each Sabbath, as well as during New Moon Festivals and other religious feasts. There must always be enough Levites on duty at the temple to do everything that needs to be done. 32They were once in charge of taking care of the sacred tent; now they are responsible for the temple and for helping Aaron's descendants.
translation_text:
1Ase Deevid ale jam kpaŋ ate wa benaŋa a piisi la, wa yaa bobi wa nidoabinni Solomon naab Izirali tɛŋka zuk.
2Wa jam maa tigsi niŋdeerɔma meena kama jigi yeŋ Izirali po ale kaabteerɔma ale Livaima. 3Livaima ale paari bena pisita yaase ba gaam di la ba jam chiini ba kama ate nidoama meena nɔi a chim tusa pisita ale naaniŋ (38,000). 4Deevid yaa weeni ayen, <<Chekki nidoaba tusa pisiye ale ŋanaansi (24,000) ale ba a nya Naawen yenni tuini zuk abe tusa ŋayuebi (6,000) a chim kpaga ale buusa boorisa. 5Tusa ŋanaansi (4,000) ale chim nansuiŋ limisidɔba abe tusa ŋanaansi (4,000) a pak Naawen ale yiila ŋannagin tii ate mi yaali magsi dila la.>>
6Deevid yaa labi Livaima beŋsa a ta va Livaima yiilaŋa ale ka diila. Bala ale Gerson ale Koyat ale Merari.
7Baai ale nyini Gerson dɔkku la ale Ladan ale Simei. 8Ladan nidoabilisaŋa a jam le Jeyiel kpagni ale la, ale Zetam ale Joel ba meena jam ka bata. 9Simei nidoabilisaŋa jam le Selomot ale Yaziel ale Yaran. Ba meena jam ka bata. Bade a jam le Ladan dɔkdemma kpaŋŋa. 10Simei nidoabilisaŋa jam le Jayat ale Ziza ale Jeus ale Beriya. Bade jam le Simei nidoabilisaŋa. Ba meena jam ka banaansi. 11Jayat jam le kpagni a pasaŋ Ziza, alege Jeus ale Beriya a jam ka nidoabilisa a piisi ya, dila ba jam a nya ba ase ka dɔkdem yeŋ la ba tuimaŋa wayeŋ.
12Koyat nidoabilisaŋa jam le Amram ale Izyar ale Yebron ale Uzziel. Ba meena jam ka banaansi. 13Amram nidoabilisaŋa jam le Aaron ale Moosis. Aaron a jam gaari ka wa tɔga, wa ale wa ŋaaŋbisaŋa taam wuu, ayen ba a nya ŋan baai ale ŋmasi ta tuilum la zuk, abe ba a nye kaabka Naawen niŋ abe ba a tom wa niŋ abe ba a mooli niauŋ wa niŋ taam wuu. 14Moosis Wen nuruwa nidoabilisaŋa ba jam a chiini ba ase ka Livaima buuni kauk la. 15Moosis nidoabilisaŋa jam le Gersom ale Ɛlieza. 16Gersom ŋaaŋbisaŋa Subael jam le kpagi. 17Ɛlieza ŋaaŋbisaŋa Areyabiya jam le kpagi. Ɛlieza jam ka nidoabilisa ba chaaba, alege Areyabiya nidoabilisaŋa a jam piisi kama. 18Izyar nidoabilisaŋa jam le Selomit wa ale kpagi. 19Yebron nidoabilisaŋa jam le Jeria ate Amariya pasaŋ ate Jayaziel a saari buta ate Jekameam a kpeglim nisa. 20Uzziel nidoabilisaŋa jam le Maika a pasaŋ Issia.
21Merari nidoabilisaŋa jam le Mayali ale Musi. Mayali nidoabilisaŋa jam le Eleaza ale Kis. 22Eleaza a jam ka nidoabilisa ale kpi la, wa jam ta ka lieba nyiini. Ba kowa suoku nidoabilisaŋa ale jam faari ba. 23Musi nidoabilisaŋa jam le Mayali ale Eder ale Jerimot. Ba meena jam ka bata.
24Bade jam le Livai ŋaaŋbisaŋa ale ba dɔkdem, yie nyam ase ba ale jam chiini ba a ŋmarisi ba yueŋa wanyi wanyi la, dila ale tuimtomdisaŋa ale paari bena pisiye yaase ba gaam dila a tom Naawen yenni po la. 25Diila Deevid a jam weeni kama ayen, <<Ase Naawen, Izirali Wenni ale te wa nuruma vuusum ale jam wa bo Jerusalem po taam wuu la, 26Livaima an ŋman magsi ba ji viuku yaase ŋan baai ate ba ta a tom ku tuimaŋa la.>> 27A ta va Deevid ale weeni dii a kpeglim la, Livaima ba jam chiini ba a nyini ka baai ale paari bena pisiye yaase ba gaam di la.
28Livaima tuini jam le ba a maari Aaron ŋaaŋbisaŋa Naawen yenni tuini po, abe ba a nya dabaasaŋa zuk ale ganaŋa diinaŋa, a nye ate ŋanta meena ale ta tuilum ale ŋanta gela ale bo Wen yenni po la. 29Ba le jam a nya boroboroku ale a duak jazaanimu zuk la ale zommu ale a nye ŋandiinta tiirimu la ale boroborok kuui ate dabinta a ka ku po la, sɛka ale damka, ale magsi zuaka meena ale bu le soa diila. 30Ba jam a zaani kama saluik meena mɛ a te jiam ale a pak Naawen. Ba jam a nye ka dila dek mɛ junɔi meena, 31ale diipo meena ate ba a nye juka tiirita Naawen Vuusum Daaŋa ale Chiik Paalik Tiŋŋa ale lueri doa la faataŋa. Ba ale ba a tom Naawen niŋ veruveruk ase ba le magsi ba soa diila ale ba le sak ba diila.
32Dila Livaima yaa jam a tom ba tuini Tuka Viuku po, jigi dii ale ta tuilum la, a tom a te ba suataŋa ale Aaron ŋaaŋbisaŋa ale Naawen yenni tuini.

english_text:
David Assigns the Priests Their Duties
1Aaron's descendants were then divided into work groups. Aaron had four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. 2 But Nadab and Abihu died long before their father, without having any sons. That's why Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
3David divided Aaron's descendants into groups, according to their assigned work. Zadok, one of Eleazar's descendants, and Ahimelech, one of Ithamar's descendants, helped David.
4Eleazar's descendants were divided into 16 groups, and Ithamar's were divided into eight groups, because Eleazar's family included more family leaders. 5However, both families included temple officials and priests, and so to make sure the work was divided fairly, David asked God what to do.
6As each group was assigned their duties, Shemaiah the son of Nethanel the Levite wrote down the name of the family leader in charge of that group. The witnesses were David and his officials, as well as Zadok the priest, Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the family leaders from the clans of the priests and the Levites.
7-18Each group of priests went by the name of its family leader, and they were assigned their duties in the following order: Jehoiarib, Jedaiah, Harim, Seorim, Malchijah, Mijamin, Hakkoz, Abijah, Jeshua, Shecaniah, Eliashib, Jakim, Huppah, Jeshebeab, Bilgah, Immer, Hezir, Happizzez, Pethahiah, Jehezkel, Jachin, Gamul, Delaiah, Maaziah. 19These men were assigned their duties at the temple, just as the Lord God of Israel had commanded their ancestor Aaron.
The Rest of the Levites Are Assigned Their Duties
20Here is a list of the other descendants of Levi:
Amram was the ancestor of Shubael and Jehdeiah.
21Rehabiah was the ancestor of Isshiah, the oldest son in his family.
22Izhar was the father of Shelomoth and the grandfather of Jahath.
23Hebron had four sons, in the following order: Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam.
24Uzziel was the father of Micah and the grandfather of Shamir.
25Isshiah, Micah's brother, was the father of Zechariah.
26Merari was the father of Mahli, Mushi, and Jaaziah.
27Jaaziah had three sons: Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri. 28-29Mahli was the father of Eleazar and Kish. Eleazar had no sons, but Kish was the father of Jerahmeel. 30Mushi had three sons: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth.
These were the descendants of Levi, according to their clans. 31Each one was assigned his duties in the same way that their relatives the priests had been assigned their duties. David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the family leaders of the priests and Levites were the witnesses.
translation_text:
1Aaron nidoabilisaŋa labika ale nna: Aaron nidoabilisaŋa jam le Nadab ale Abiyu ale Eleaza ale Itamar. 2Alege Nadab ale Abiyu a jam kpi kama alege ba kowa, ba jam ka nidoabilisa, dila Eleaza ale Itamar ale jam a tom ase kaabteerɔba la. 3Zadok ale ka Eleaza ŋaaŋbiik la ale Ayimelek ale ka Itamar ŋaaŋbiik la, bala maarika nyiŋ, Deevid a jam labi ba ka beŋsa a magsi ba le ba a tom diila. 4Ba jam nya niŋdeerɔba Eleaza ŋaaŋbisaŋa po a gaam Itamar kama, ba be jam labi ba kama ase ku le magsi ba nye diila. Yie nyam pi ale bayuebi ale jam nyini Eleaza ŋaaŋbisaŋa po ate yie nyam naaniŋ a nyini Itamar ŋaaŋbisaŋa po. 5Ba jam nak ka gbaŋ a labi ba lukka a jam karo, diila ba jam ka kpaga Naawen yenni po a chim Wen kpaga a bo Eleaza ale Itamar ŋaaŋbisaŋa po.
6Netanel nidoabinni Sɛmaiya ŋmarisidoawa ale ka Livai la, ale jam ŋmarisi ba yueŋa naawa ale kpaŋŋa niŋ. Kaabteerɔwa Zadok ale Abiata nidoabinni Ayimelek ale kaabteerɔma ale Livaima yieŋa nyama, nuru yeŋ ale lueri a nyini Eleaza dɔkdemma po, a lueri wanyi a nyini Itamar dɔkdemma po. 7Gbaŋ kaai ale dɛ niŋ la jam lo ka Jeyoiarib zuk kaai ale saari siyewa la a lo Jedaya zuk ate 8butawa po ka jam lo ka Yarim zuk ate bunaansiwa po a lo Seorim zuk ate 9bunuwa po a lo Malkija zuk ate buyuebiwa po a lo Mijamin zuk ate 10buyopɔiwa po a lo Yakkoz zuk ate naanika po a lo Abaija zuk ate 11neokku po a lo Jesua zuk ate piika po a lo Sekania zuk ate 12pi ale bunyiwa po a lo Eliasib zuk ate pi ale buyewa po a lo Jakim zuk ate 13pi ale butawa po a lo Yuppa zuk ate pi ale bunaansiwa po a lo Jesebeab zuk ate 14pi ale bunuwa po a lo Bilga zuk ate pi ale buyuebiwa po a lo Immer zuk ate 15pi ale buyopɔiwa po a lo Yezir zuk ate pi ale naanika po a lo Yappizzez zuk ate 16pi ale neokku po a lo Petayia zuk ate pisiyewa po a lo Jeyezkel zuk ate 17pisiye ale bunyiwa po a lo Jakin zuk ate pisiye ale buyewa po a lo Gamul zuk ate 18pisiye ale butawa po a lo Delaiya zuk ate pisiye ale bunaansiwa po a lo Maazia zuk.
19Ba ale jam weeni ba diila ale nna ase ba ale a jo Naawen yenni po ba tom, a ta va suik tii ate ba kokpieŋka Aaron a jam sak ase Naawen, Izirali Wenni ale jam weeni wa la.
20Dan ka Livai ŋaaŋbisaŋa mbala meena, a nyini Amram nidoabilisaŋa po jam ka Subael, a nyini Subael nidoabilisaŋa po jam ka Jedeiya. 21Dan ka Areyabiya, a nyini wa nidoabilisaŋa po jam ka Issia ale dɛ niŋ. 22A nyini Izyar demma po jam ka Selomot. A nyini Selomot nidoabilisaŋa po jam ka Jayat. 23Yebron nidoabilisaŋa po jam ka Jeria ale jam dɛ niŋ ate Amariya a saari baye, butawa po jam ka Jayaziel, banaansiwa po jam ka Jekameam. 24Uzziel nidoabilisaŋa po jam ka Maika, a nyini Maika nidoabilisaŋa po jam ka Samir. 25Maika suok jam le Issia. A nyini Issia nidoabilisaŋa po jam ka Zakaria. 26Merari nidoabilisaŋa po jam ka Mayali ale Musi. Jaazia nidoabili jam le Beno. 27Merari nidoabili jam le Jaazia. A nyini Jaazia po jam ka Beno ale Soyam ale Zakkur ale Ibri. 28A nyini Mayali po jam ka Eleaza, waai ale kan jam ta nidoabilisa la. 29A nyini Kis po, Kis nidoabinni jam le Jerameel. 30Musi nidoabilisaŋa jam le Mayali ale Eder ale Jerimot. Bade jam le Livaima a ta va ba dɔkdemma ale ka diila.
31Ba mɛ a jam nak ka gbaŋsa ase ba suataŋa Aaron ŋaaŋbisaŋa ale jam nye dii naab Deevid ale Zadok ale Ayimelek ale kaabteerɔma ale Livaima yie nyama niŋ diila. Suok kpagni dɔkdemma ate ba jam a nye ba diila, dila dekdek ate ba jam nye baansaŋa mɛ.

english_text:
David Assigns the Temple Musicians Their Duties
1David and the temple officials chose the descendants of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun to be in charge of music. They were to praise the Lord by playing cymbals, harps and other stringed instruments. Here is a list of the musicians and their duties:
2Asaph's four sons, Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah, were under the direction of their father and played music whenever the king told them to.
3Jeduthun's six sons, Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, were under the direction of their father and played harps and sang praises to the Lord.
4Heman had 14 sons: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamtiezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, Mahazioth. 5Heman was one of the king's prophets, and God honored Heman by giving him 14 sons and 3 daughters. 6His sons were under his direction and played cymbals, harps, and other stringed instruments during times of worship at the temple.
Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman took their orders directly from the king.
7There were 288 of these men, and all of them were skilled musicians. 8David assigned them their duties by asking the Lord what he wanted. Everyone was responsible for something, whether young or old, teacher or student.
9-31The musicians were divided into 24 groups of twelve, and each group went by the name of their family leader. They were assigned their duties in the following order: Joseph, Gedaliah, Zaccur, Zeri, Nethaniah, Bukkiah, Asarelah, Jeshaiah, Mattaniah, Shimei, Uzziel, Hashabiah, Shebuel, Mattithiah, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Joshbekashah, Hanani, Mallothi, Eliathah, Hothir, Giddalti, Mahazioth, and Romamtiezer.

1Deevid ale tugurik tommu kpaŋŋa a jam gaari ka Asaf ale Yeman ale Jedutun nidoabilisaŋa gela a magsi biisiteerɔ tuini, ale kpanta ale bagansa ale dalinkinkeŋsa. Baai ate ba ŋmarisi ayen ba a tom tuini de la ale nna: 2A nyini Asaf nidoabilisaŋa po ba jam lueri ka Zakkur ale Josefi ale Netania ale Asarelaya. Asaf nidoabilisaŋa a jam ka Asaf dek ale jam a nya ate ba a tom, waai ate naawa a jam a nya ate wa a tom la. 3Dan ka Jedutun, a nyini wa nidoabilisaŋa po, ba jam lueri ka Gedalia ale Zeri ale Jesaiya ale Simei ale Yasabia ale Mattitia, ba meena jam ka bayuebi, ate ba kowa Jedutun a nya ate ba a tom, ate wadek a biisi Wen wanni ale a nak kpanuŋ a nye Naawen jiam ale a pak wa. 4Dan ka Yeman, a nyini wa nidoabilisaŋa po, ba jam lueri ka Bukkia ale Mattania ale Uzziel ale Subael ale Jerimot ale Yanania ale Yanani ale Eliata ale Giddalti ale Aromamti Ezer ale Josbekasa ale Malloti ale Yotir ale Mayaziot. 5Bade meena jam ka Yeman naawa biisiteerɔwa nidoabilisa. Ba te ba kama a ta va Wen pumpuulimaŋa ayen ba a pak wa. Wen a jam te Yeman ka nidoabilisa pi ale banaansi ale lieba bata.
6Nidoama de meena a jam ka ba koma ale nya ate ba a lenni yiila Naawen yenni po ale dalinkinkeŋsa ale bagansa ale kpanta a te Wen yenni tuini. Asaf ale Jedutun ale Yeman ka naawa ale jam a nya ba zuk. 7Nuruma de ale baai ale moata ba la ba jam sak ba kama ate ba seba yiila lenka a te Naawen, ba jam ka nuruba kobsiye ale pinaanuŋ ale naaniŋ. 8Nuru paaluk ale ŋankpagsa meena, sagrɔba ale zamsidɔba meena a jam nak ka gbaŋ a nya ba ale magsi ba tom diila.
9Gbaŋ kaai ale dɛ niŋ la, kaai ale magsi Asaf la a lo ka Josefi ale wa nidoabilisaŋa ale wa kobisaŋa zuk. Ba meena pi ale baye. Kaai ale saari buyewa la a jam lo ka Gedalia ale wa kobisaŋa ale wa nidoabilisaŋa zuk. Ba meena pi ale baye. 10Butawa po gbaŋ ka jam lo ka Zakkur ale wa nidoabilisaŋa ale wa kobisaŋa zuk. english_text:
The Temple Guards Are Assigned Their Duties
1The temple guards were also divided into groups according to clans.
Meshelemiah son of Kore was from the Korah clan and was a descendant of Asaph. 2He had seven sons, who were born in the following order: Zechariah, Jediael, Zebadiah, Jathniel, 3Elam, Jehohanan, and Eliehoenai.
4-5 Obed-Edom had been blessed with eight sons: Shemaiah, Jehozabad, Joah, Sachar, Nethanel, Ammiel, Issachar, and Peullethai.
6-7Shemaiah was the father of Othni, Rephael, Obed, Elzabad, Elihu, and Semachiah. They were all respected leaders in their clan. 8There were 62 descendants of Obed-Edom who were strong enough to be guards at the temple.
9Eighteen descendants of Meshelemiah were chosen for this work.
10-11Hosah, from the Merari clan, was the father of Shimri, Hilkiah, Tebaliah, and Zechariah. Hosah had made Shimri the family leader, even though he was not the oldest son. Thirteen men from Hosah's family were chosen to be temple guards.
12The guards were divided into groups, according to their family leaders, and they were assigned duties at the temple, just like the other Levites. 13Each group, no matter how large or small, was assigned a gate to guard, and they let the Lord show them what he wanted done.
14Shelemiah was chosen to guard the East Gate. Zechariah his son was a wise man and was chosen to guard the North Gate. 15Obed-Edom was then chosen to guard the South Gate, and his sons were chosen to guard the storerooms. 16Shuppim and Hosah were chosen to guard the West Gate and the Shallecheth Gate on the upper road.
The guards were assigned the following work schedule: 17Each day six guards were on duty on the east side of the temple, four were on duty on the north side, and four were on duty on the south side. Two guards were stationed at each of the two storerooms, 18four were stationed along the road leading to the west courtyard, and two guards stayed in the court itself.
19These were the guard duties assigned to the men from the clans of Korah and Merari.
Guards Are Assigned to the Treasury
20The Levites who were relatives of the Korahites and the Merarites were in charge of guarding the temple treasury and the gifts that had been dedicated to God.
21Ladan was from the Gershon clan and was the father of Jehieli. Many of his other descendants were family leaders in the clan. 22Jehieli was the father of Zetham and Joel, and they were responsible for guarding the treasury.
23Other guards at the treasury were from the Kohathite clans of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
24Shebuel was a descendant of Gershom the son of Moses. He was the chief official in charge of the temple treasury. 25The descendants of Gershom's brother Eliezer included Rehabiah, Jeshaiah, Joram, Zichri, and Shelomoth.
26Shelomoth and his relatives were in charge of all the gifts that were dedicated to the Lord. These included the gifts that King David had dedicated, as well as those dedicated by the family leaders, army officers, and army commanders. 27And whenever valuable things were captured in battle, these men brought back some of them to make repairs to the temple. 28Shelomoth and his relatives were responsible for any gifts that had been given to the temple, including those from Samuel the prophet, King Saul the son of Kish, Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah.
Other Officers Are Assigned Their Duties
29Chenaniah from the Izhar clan and his sons were government officials and judges. They did not work at the temple.
30Hashabiah from the Hebron clan and 1,700 of his skilled relatives were the officials in charge of all religious and government business in the Israelite territories west of the Jordan River.
31-32Jerijah was the leader of the Hebron clan. David assigned him and 2,700 of his relatives, who were all respected family leaders, to be the officials in charge of all religious and government business in the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. David found out about these men during the fortieth year of his rule, when he had a list made of all the families in the Hebron clan. They were from the town of Jazer in the territory of Gilead.
translation_text:
1Nansuiŋ limisidɔma labika ale nna. A nyini Koora dɔkku buuni ka Kore nidoabinni Meselemia, Asaf nidoabilisaŋa wanyi.
2Meselemia a jam ta ka nidoabilisa, bala ale Zakaria nidoabili kpagni ale la a pasaŋ Jediael ate Zebadia a saari bata, bunaansiwa jam ka Jatniel ate, 3Iilam a saari banu ate Jeyoyanan a saari bayuebi ate Elieyoenai a saari bayopɔi.
4Obed Edom mɛ a jam ta ka nidoabilisa. Bala ale Sɛmaiya nidoabili kpagni ale la a pasaŋ Jeyozabad, butawa po ka Joa, ate Sakar a nye bunaansi ate Netanel a saari bunu. 5Buyuebiwa po jam ka Ammiel, ate buyopɔiwa po a chim Isaka ate Peulletai a saari naaniŋ. Wen a jam niak Obed Edom kama.
6Wa nidoabinni Sɛmaiya mɛ a jam ta ka nidoabilisa, baai ale jam ka niŋdeerɔba ba kowa dɔkdemma po, dii nyiŋla ba jam ka nidoa baai ale zaani ŋmam a nye wie. 7Sɛmaiya nidoabilisaŋa jam le Otni ale Arefael ale Obed ale Elzabad, wa kobisaŋa Eliyu ale Sɛmakiya jam ka baai ale zaani ŋmam a nye wie. 8Bade meena jam ka Obed Edom ŋaaŋbisa, ba ale ba nidoabilisaŋa ale ba kobisaŋa ale baga a nye wie ale ta pagrim a bag tuini a tom. Obed Edom ŋaaŋbisaŋa meena jam ka pisiyuebi ale baye.
9Meselemia jam ta ka nidoabilisa ale kobisa baai ale baga wie a nye la, ba meena jam ka pi ale naaniŋ.
10Yosa Merari denɔwa a jam ta ka nidoabilisa, Simri ale nidoabili kpagni, daa wa ate wa dɛ niŋ a biagi alege wa kowa ale lueri wa kpagi. 11Buyewa ka Yilkia ate Tabalia a saari buta ate Zakaria a saari bunaansi. Yosa nidoabilisaŋa ale wa kobisaŋa meena jam ka pi ale bata.
12Nansuiŋ limisidɔma de labika, ba yieŋa nyama a jam ta ka tuima a tom Naawen yenni po ase ba kobisaŋa ale ka diila. 13Gbaŋsa ate ba jam nak a te nansuiŋ meena, a ta va ba dɔkdemma ale ka diila, paalik ale jakpak meena.
14Gbaŋ kaai ale bo Kori Nansuiŋku la, a jam lo ka Selemia zuk. Ba jam nak ka gbaŋsa a te wa nidoabinni Zakaria, yam sagrɔwa, ate Wiilukku Nansuiŋku geŋsa gbaŋka a lo wa zuk. 15Gbaŋ kaai ale magsi Yeseoku Nansuiŋku la a jam lo ka Obed Edom zuk, ate gbaŋ kaai ale magsi ŋanta duenika jigini la a lo wa nidoabilisaŋa zuk. 16Gbaŋ sii ale magsi Yeniŋ Nansuiŋku ale Salleket Nansuiŋku ale ŋmazuk suiku geŋsa la a jam lo ka Suppim ale Yosa zuima. Limisidɔ ale jam za ganaŋa meena ale limisidɔ. 17Livaiba bayuebi ale jam bo kori geŋka danni po, banaansi a bo wiilukku geŋ kantueŋ ate banaansi a bo yeseoku geŋ kantueŋ ate baye a bo ba le a dueni ŋanta juijui la. 18Dan ka dabiaka ale bo yeniŋka la, banaansi ale bo suiku po ate baye a bo dabiaka dek po.
19Bade jam le nansuiŋ limisidɔma labika baai ale jam ka Koora ale Merari ŋaaŋbisa la.
20Ba Livai chaama ale jam a nya ligra jigini Wen yenni po ale ŋan weleŋsaŋa ligra jigini.
21Ladan ŋaaŋbisaŋa, baai ale ka Gerson dem baai ale jam ka yie nyam a nyini Ladan Gerson denɔwa buuni po la, jam ka Jeyieli. 22Jeyieli nidoabilisaŋa jam le Zetam ale wa suoku Joel, ba ale jam a nya ligraŋa zuk Naawen yenni po.
23A nyini Amram demma po ale Izyar demma po ale Yebron demma po ale Uzziel demma po ale bade: 24Subael jam ka Moosis nidoabinni Gersom ŋaaŋbiik. Wa jam ka kpagi a nya ligraŋa zuk. 25Wa kobisaŋa a nyini Ɛlieza buuni po jam le nna: Areyabiya jam ka wa nidoabili, Jesaiya jam ka wa nidoabili, Joram jam ka wa nidoabili, Zikri jam ka wa nidoabili, Selomit jam ka wa nidoabili. 26Selomit ale wa kobisaŋa ale jam a nya ŋantaŋa ate naab Deevid ale yieŋa nyama baai ale a nya nidoaba tusidi zuk la ale nidoaba kook zuk ale tugurik tommu kpaga m ŋala a jam pa nyo Naawen yenni po la. 27Ŋantaŋa gela ate ba jam ta nyini kpaliŋka po a jam la, ba jam pai ba zaani magsi ka Naawen yenni tebika. 28Jaab meena ate Samuel biisiteerɔwa a jam pai te la ale Kis nidoabinni Sɔɔl a te la, ale Ner nidoabinni Abner a te la, ale Zeruiya nidoabinni Joab a te la ale ŋan baai meena ate ba jam te la ka Selomit ale wa kobisaŋa ale jam a nya ba zuk.
29A nyini Izyar demma po, Kenania ale wa nidoabilisaŋa tuimaŋa a jam ka Naawen yenni po, ba jam ka kpaga ale buusa boorisa a nya Izirali zuk.
30A nyini Yebron demma po ba jam lueri ka Yasabia ale wa kobisaŋa, ba jam ka nidoaba tusidi ale kobsiyopɔi (1,700) a nya Izirali zuk Jodan Benni yeniŋ geŋsa ba ale jam a nya Naawen tuini ale naawa tuini zuk. 31Dan ka Yebron demma, Jeria jam le ba kpagi a ta va ba gaŋka buuni ŋmarisika. Bena pisinaansiwa po ate Deevid a jam de wa naamu a paari la, ba jam gisi ŋmarisika po kama ale nidoa ale baga wie a nye a bo Yebron demma po Jazer ale bo Gilead tɛŋka po la. 32Jeria a jam ta ka tusa ŋaye ale kobsiyopɔi (2,700), baai ale jam baga a nye wie ale ta dɔkdem la, ate naab Deevid a jam pai ba a nyo Aruben dɔkku buuni ale Gad dɔkku buuni ale Manasa dɔkku buuni kaukku dii meena ale ta wari a nye ale Naawen ale naawa wie la.

1Izirali demma yieŋa nyama ale kpak ŋaai ale a nya tusa zuk la, kpak ŋaai ale a nya kobsa zuk la ale ba kpaŋŋa, baai ale tom a te naawa dii meena ale ta wari a nye le tugurik tommu beŋsa sii ale bo tuima chiik, chiik benni meena po la yueŋa ale nna. Beŋ meena jam ta ka nidoaba tusa pisiye ale ŋanaansi (24,000).
2Waai ale jam a nya beŋ kaai ale dɛ niŋka, chiik kaai ale dɛ niŋka la po, jam ka Zabdiel nidoabinni Jasobeam. Ba jam ka nidoaba tusa pisiye ale banaansi (24,000) a bo wa beŋka po. 3Wa jam ka Perezi ŋaaŋbiik ale chim kpagi tugurik tommu kpaŋŋa meena zuk chiik kaai ale dɛ niŋka la po.
4Waai ale jam a nya beŋsa buyewa zuk la jam ka Ayoyi denɔwa Dodai. Miklot a jam le beŋ kala niŋdeerɔ. Ba jam ka nidoaba tusa pisiye ale ŋanaansi (24,000) a bo wa beŋka po.
5Tugurik tom kpaga butawa po chiisa sitawa po, jam ka Jeyoiada kaabteerɔwa nidoabinni Benaya. Wa jam le kpagni ba be jam ka nidoaba tusa pisiye ale banaansi (24,000) a bo wa beŋka po. 6Benaya wade waai ale jam ka pagrɔ Pisitawa po la a jam a nya ka Pisita zuk. Wa nidoabinni Ammizabad ale jam a nya wa beŋka zuk.
7Bunaansiwa po, chiisa sinaansiwa po, jam ka Joab suoku Asayel. Wa nidoabinni Zebadia ale jam tagri wa. Ba jam ka nidoaba tusa pisiye ale banaansi (24,000) a bo wa beŋka po.
8Bunuwa po, chiisa sinuwa po jam ka kpagi dii ate ba wi ayen Samyut la, Izra denɔwa. Ba jam ka nidoaba tusa pisiye ale banaansi (24,000) a bo wa beŋka po.
9Buyuebiwa po, chiisa siyuebiwa po jam ka Ikkes Teko denɔwa nidoabinni Ira. Ba jam ka nidoaba tusa pisiye ale banaansi (24,000) a bo wa beŋka po.
10Buyopɔiwa po, chiisa siyopɔiwa po jam ka Pelon denɔwa Yelez, wa jam ka Ɛfraim ŋaaŋbiik. Ba jam ka nidoaba tusa pisiye ale banaansi (24,000) a bo wa beŋka po.
11Naanika po, chiisa naanika po jam ka Yusat denɔwa Sibbekai, wa jam ka Zera ŋaaŋbiik. Ba jam ka nidoaba tusa pisiye ale banaansi (24,000) a bo wa beŋka po.
12Neokku po, chiisa neokku po jam ka Anatot denɔwa Abiezer, wa jam ka Benjamin ŋaaŋbiik. Ba jam ka nidoaba tusa pisiye ale banaansi (24,000) a bo wa beŋka po.
13Piika po, chiisa piwa po jam ka Netofat denɔwa Mayarai, wa jam ka Zera ŋaaŋbiik. Ba jam ka nidoaba tusa pisiye ale banaansi (24,000) a bo wa beŋka po.
14Pi ale bunyiwa, chiisa pi ale kanyi wa po jam ka Piraton denɔwa Benaya, wa jam ka Ɛfraim ŋaaŋbiik. Ba jam ka nidoaba tusa pisiye ale banaansi (24,000) a bo wa beŋka po.
15Pi ale buyewa po, chiisa pi ale siyewa po jam ka Yeldai Netofat denɔwa a nyini Otniel dɔkdemma po. Ba jam ka nidoaba tusa pisiye ale banaansi (24,000) a bo wa beŋka po.
16Kpaŋŋa ale jam a nya Izirali buuni la ale nna. Aruben dɔkku zuk ka Zikri nidoabinni Ɛlieza ale jam a nya ba. Simeyon dɔkku zuk ka Maaka nidoabinni Sefatia ale jam a nya ba. 17Livaima dɔkku zuk ka Kemuel nidoabinni Yasabia ale jam a nya ba, ate Zadok mɛ a nya Aaron dɔkku zuk. 18Juda dɔkku zuk ka Deevid suoku Eliyu ale jam a nya ba. Isaka dɔkku zuk ka Maakil nidoabinni Omri ale jam a nya ba. 19Zebulun dɔkku zuk ka Obadia nidoabinni Ismaiya ale jam a nya ba. Nafitali dɔkku zuk ka Azriel nidoabinni ale jam a nya ba. 20Ɛfraim dɔkku zuk ka Azaziya nidoabinni Yoseya ale jam a nya ba. Manasa dɔkku genni ka Pedaiya nidoabinni Joel ale jam a nya ba. 21Manasa dɔkku genni ale bo Gilead po la ka Zakaria nidoabinni Iddo ale jam a nya ba. Benjamin dɔkku zuk ka Abner nidoabinni ale jam a nya ba. 22Dan dɔkku zuk ka Jeroyam nidoabinni Azarel ale jam a nya ba. Bade jam le kpaŋŋa a nya Izirali diinaŋa buuni meena zuk.
23Deevid an jam chiini nidoa baai ale paari bena pisiye yaase ba an paari dila la, dii nyiŋla Naawen a puulim kama ayen wa le basi ate Izirali a piisi ase chiŋmarisaŋa ale bo wenŋmazuk la. 24Zeruiya nidoabinni Joab ale piilim wa chiini nidoama la wa an jam chiini nueri ya. Kaasuŋ yaa jan jam Izirali zuk nuruma chiinika nyiŋ, ate ba ale jam chiini ba nɔi diila a jo Deevid nalima wie gbaŋka po.
25Adiel nidoabinni Azmavet ale jam a nya naab yeri ŋanta duenika jigini. Yuzaya nidoabinni Jonatan ale jam a nya tɛŋsaŋa ale tɛŋ kpaŋsa ale gbirim woŋtaŋa ale bo tɛŋ kpieŋka po la zuk.
26Chelub nidoabinni Ezri ale jam a nya baai ale a kpa la zuk.
27Simei Aramat denɔwa ale jam a nya kaduksaŋa zuk. Zabdi Sifmi denɔwa ale jam a nya kaduksaŋa ŋandiintaŋa zuk.
28Geder denɔwa Baal Yanan ale jam a nya kpaam tiisaŋa ale kinkaŋ tiisaŋa ale bo yeniŋ guuku chiak la zuk. Joas mɛ ale jam a nya kpaamu teka zuk.
29Saaron denɔwa Sitrai ale jam a nya duŋsaŋa dɛka zuk Saaron po, ate Adlai nidoabinni Safat a nya naapeerisaŋa ale bo vaasaŋa po la zuk.
30Ismael tɛŋka denɔwa Obil ale jam a nya laalaakomima zuk, ate Meronot denɔwa Jedeiya jam a nya bonsaŋa zuk.
31Yagri denɔwa Jaziz ale jam a nya duŋsaŋa zuk. Bade meena jam ka kpaga a nya Deevid nitalimu zuk.
32Deevid kobiika Jonatan jam ka sagrɔ ale yam nyɔnɔ ale ŋmarisidoa. Yachmoni nidoabinni Jeyiel ale jaa nya naawa nidoabilisaŋa.
33Ayitofel jam le naawa sagrɔ. Arki denɔwa Yusai jam le naawa doa. 34Benaya nidoabinni Jeyoiada ale Abiata ale jam tagri zaani Ayitofel nankula po. Joab mɛ ale jam chim naab yeri tugurik tommu kpagi.

english_text:
David Gives Solomon the Plans for the Temple
1David called a meeting in Jerusalem for all of Israel's leaders, including the tribal leaders, the government officials, the army commanders, the officials in charge of the royal property and livestock, the palace officials, and the brave warriors.
2 After everyone was there, David stood up and said:
Listen to me, my people. I wanted to build a place where the sacred chest would be kept, so we could go there and worship the Lord our God. I have prepared all the supplies for building a temple, 3but the Lord has refused to let me build it, because he said I have killed too many people in battle.
4The Lord God chose Judah to be the leading tribe in Israel. Then from Judah, he chose my father's family, and from that family, he chose me to be the king of Israel, and he promised that my descendants will also rule as kings. 5The Lord has blessed me with many sons, but he chose my son Solomon to be the next king of Israel. 6The Lord said to me, “Your son Solomon will build my temple, and it will honor me. Solomon will be like a son to me, and I will be like a father to him. 7If he continues to obey my laws and commands, his kingdom will never end.”
8My friends, you are the Lord's people. And now, with God as your witness, I want you to promise that you will do your best to obey everything the Lord God has commanded us. Then this land will always belong to you and your descendants.
9Solomon, my son, worship God and obey him with all your heart and mind, just as I have done. He knows all your thoughts and your reasons for doing things, and so if you turn to him, he will hear your prayers. But if you ignore him, he will reject you forever. 10The Lord has chosen you to build a temple for worshiping him. Be confident and do the work you have been assigned.
11After David finished speaking, he gave Solomon the plans for building the main rooms of the temple, including the porch, the storerooms, the rooms upstairs and downstairs, as well as the most holy place. 12He gave Solomon his plans for the courtyards and the open areas around the temple, and for the rooms to store the temple treasures and gifts that had been dedicated to God.
13David also gave Solomon his plans for dividing the priests and the Levites into groups, as well as for the work that needed to be done at the temple and for taking care of the objects used for worship. 14He told Solomon how much gold and silver was to be used in making the sacred objects, 15including the lampstands and lamps, 16the gold table which held the sacred loaves of bread, the tables made of silver, 17the meat forks, the bowls and cups, 18the gold incense altar, and the gold statue of a chariot for the winged creatures which were on the lid of the sacred chest.
19David then said to Solomon:
The Lord showed me how his temple is to be built. 20But you must see that everything is done according to these plans. Be confident, and never be afraid of anything or get discouraged. The Lord my God will help you do everything needed to finish the temple, so it can be used for worshiping him. 21The priests and Levites have been assigned their duties, and all the skilled workers are prepared to do their work. The people and their leaders will do anything you tell them.
translation_text:
1Deevid a jam wi kpaŋŋa meena Izirali po ayen ba tigsi Jerusalem tɛŋka po: Bala ale kpaŋŋa ale a nya diinaŋa buuni zuk la ale kpaŋŋa ale a nya naawa beŋsaŋa zuk la, kpaŋŋa ale a nya tusa zuk la ale kpaŋŋa ale a nya kobsa zuk la ale kpaŋŋa nitalimu meena ale duŋsaŋa meena ate naawa a soa la ale wa nidoabilisaŋa, a gum chaab ale naab yeri kpaŋŋa, nuru kpientaŋa ale tugurik tɔŋdɔ tuasaŋa meena.
2Naab Deevid yaa yiti zaani ale weeni ayen, <<Ni wom mi, m suata ale m nuruba. Mi ta ku m suinum po kama ayen m sɛ yeri ase vuusika jigi la a te Naawen nɔiyeŋka dakanni, naŋsa zukpaglik a te ti Wenni, m be zɔk kama ayen m sɛ di. 3Alege Wen a weeni mi ayen, <<Fi a kan sɛ yeri mi Yuenni nyiŋŋa, dii nyiŋla fi ka tugurik tɔŋdɔ ale basi ate ziim a siŋ.
