13The priests and Levites from the northern tribes of Israel gave their support to King Rehoboam. 14And since Jeroboam and the kings of Israel that followed him would not allow any Levites to serve as priests, most Levites left their towns and pasturelands in Israel and moved to Jerusalem and other towns in Judah. 15 Jeroboam chose his own priests to serve at the local shrines in Israel and at the places of worship where he had set up statues of goat-demons and of calves.
16But some of the people from Israel wanted to worship the Lord God, just as their ancestors had done. So they followed the priests and Levites to Jerusalem, where they could offer sacrifices to the Lord. 17For the next three years, they lived in Judah and were loyal to Rehoboam and his kingdom, just as they had been loyal to David and Solomon.
Rehoboam's Family
18Rehoboam married Mahalath, whose father was Jerimoth son of David, and whose mother was Abihail the daughter of Eliab and granddaughter of Jesse. 19Rehoboam and Mahalath had three sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham. 20Then Rehoboam married Maacah the daughter of Absalom. Their sons were Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
21Rehoboam had 18 wives, but he also married 60 other women, and he was the father of 28 sons and 60 daughters. Rehoboam loved his wife Maacah the most, 22so he chose their oldest son Abijah to be the next king. 23Rehoboam was wise enough to put one of his sons in charge of each fortified city in his kingdom. He gave them all the supplies they needed and found wives for every one of them.
translation_text:
1Ase Areyoboam ale jam paari Jerusalem po la, wa yaa tigsi Juda dɔkku ale Benjamin dɔkku tugurik tɔŋdɔba tusa kook ale pinaanuŋ (180,000) ayen ba nye kpaliŋ ale Izirali abe ba ŋman tuesi naamu a te wa.
2Alege Naawen wanni yaa jam Wen nuruwa Sɛmaiya jigi ayen, 3<<Weeni Juda naawa Solomon nidoabinni Areyoboam ale Izirali demma meena ale bo Juda ale Benjamin po la ayen, 4<Nnala ate Naawen a weeni. Kan jueli a nye kpaliŋ ale ni suataŋa. Ni kuli yeri, ni waai meena, ale kude ka mi ale nye.> >> Dila nyiŋ ba yaa wom Naawen wieŋa a ŋmani an nye kpaliŋ ale Jeroboam.
5Areyoboam jam bo ka Jerusalem po a se tɛŋ fiisa ate parisa a gilim si Juda po. 6Sila ale Betiliyem ale Etam ale Tekoa 7ale Bet Zur ale Soko ale Adullam 8ale Gat ale Maresa ale Zif 9ale Adoraim ale Lachis ale Azeka 10ale Zoraya ale Aijalon ale Yebron. Side ka tɛŋ sii ate parik pagrisa a gilim si Juda ale Benjamin po. 11Wa jam nye kama ate ba pagra kpaliŋ wie po ale basi ate kpaga a nya ba zuk, a te ba ŋandiinta ale kpaam ale daam. 12Wa jam pai ka kpaliŋ ŋanchɔgsinta ale gbatta a basi si meena po, a nye ate si meena a ŋmasi pagra. Dila Juda ale Benjamin ka wa ale jam soa.
13Kaabteerɔma ale Livaima ale nyini ba tɛŋ ninaŋa meena Izirali meena po la yaa jam va wa. 14Livaima a jam zɛri ba wuyɔgsuku jiŋŋa ale ba nitalimu kama ale jam Juda ale Benjamin dii nyiŋla Jeroboam ale wa nidoabilisaŋa a jam zɛri ba kama ase Naawen kaabteerɔba la. 15Wa jam lueri ka wadek kaabteerɔba a magsi pimpitima ale buuku ale naabiika bɔgtaŋa ate wa jam nye la. 16Baai ale nyini Izirali buuni meena po baai ale pai ba suiniima meena a gisi Naawen, Izirali Wenni la, a yaa va Livaima a cheŋ Jerusalem ayen ba nye kaabka a te Naawen, ba koma Wenni. 17Ba jam chɔgsi Juda naamu kama ale maari Solomon nidoabinni Areyoboam bena ŋata, a cheŋ Deevid ale Solomon suitaŋa po vaaŋa de po.
18Areyoboam a jam faari ka Mayalat, wa jam ka Jerimot Deevid nidoabili wanyi lie, wa mawa jam le Abiyail, Deevid suoku Eliab lie. 19Nipowa ale jam biak nidoabili sii a te wa la jam le Jeus ale Sɛmariya ale Zayam. 20Wa ŋman jam faari ka Absalom lie Maaka, waai ale jam biak Abaija ale Attai ale Ziza ale Selomit la. 21Areyoboam a jam a yaali Absalom liewa Maaka a gaam wa pok yontaŋa ale pok dɔkliema kama. Ba meena a gum chaab, wa jam ta ka nipooba pi ale naaniŋ, pok dɔklieba pisiyuebi, nidoabilisa pisiye ale naaniŋ ale lieba pisiyuebi.
22Areyoboam a jam lueri ka Maaka nidoabinni Abaija ayen wa chim nabi kpagi wa suataŋa po a gomsi wa a magsi naab chimka. 23Wa jam nye ale ka yam a waaŋ wa nidoabilisaŋa gela Juda ale Benjamin tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa po ale tɛŋ sii meena ate parisa a gilim la po. Wa jam te ba ka nitalim nna yegayega ale faari nipooba a te ba.

english_text:
King Shishak of Egypt Invades Judah
(1 Kings 14.25-28)
1Soon after Rehoboam had control of his kingdom, he and everyone in Judah stopped obeying the Lord. 2So in the fifth year of Rehoboam's rule, the Lord punished them for their unfaithfulness and allowed King Shishak of Egypt to invade Judah. 3Shishak attacked with his army of 1,200 chariots and 60,000 cavalry troops, as well as countless Egyptian soldiers from Libya, Sukkoth, and Ethiopia. 4He captured every one of the fortified cities in Judah and then marched to Jerusalem.
5Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah had gone to Jerusalem to escape Shishak's invasion. And while they were there, Shemaiah the prophet told them, “The Lord says that because you have disobeyed him, he has now abandoned you. The Lord will not help you against Shishak!”
6Rehoboam and the leaders were sorry for what they had done and admitted, “The Lord is right. We have deserted him.”
7When the Lord heard this, he told Shemaiah:
The people of Judah are truly sorry for their sins, and so I won't let Shishak completely destroy them. But because I am still angry, 8he will conquer and rule them.
Then my people will know what it's like to serve a foreign king instead of serving me.
9 Shishak attacked Jerusalem and took all the valuable things from the temple and from the palace, including Solomon's gold shields.
10Rehoboam had bronze shields made to replace the gold ones, and he ordered the guards at the city gates to keep them safe. 11Whenever Rehoboam went to the Lord's temple, the guards carried the shields. But they always took them back to the guardroom as soon as he had finished worshiping.
12Rehoboam turned back to the Lord, and so the Lord did not let Judah be completely destroyed, and Judah was prosperous again.
Rehoboam's Rule in Judah
(1 Kings 14.21,29-31)
13Rehoboam was 41 years old when he became king, and he ruled 17 years from Jerusalem, the city where the Lord had chosen to be worshiped. His mother Naamah was from Ammon. Rehoboam was a powerful king, 14but he still did wrong and refused to obey the Lord.
15Everything else Rehoboam did while he was king, including a history of his family, is written in the records of the two prophets, Shemaiah and Iddo. During Rehoboam's rule, he and King Jeroboam of Israel were constantly at war. 16When Rehoboam died, he was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Abijah became king.
translation_text:
1Areyoboam ale jam chim naab a nueri a pagra la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, wa ale Izirali demma meena a jam zɛri Naawen sinsaŋŋa kama. 2Dii nyiŋla ba jam ka wensie ale Naawen ya, Ejipiti naawa Sisak a jam nye ka kpaliŋ ale Jerusalem bena ŋanuwa po ate Areyoboam a dɛ naam la. 3Torokoba tusidi ale kobsiye (1,200) ale wusum duerisa tusa pisiyuebi (60,000) ale Libia tommu ale kan ta chiina la, Suki ale Kus demma ale jam va wa nyini Ejipiti a jam la, 4wa jam nak yik tɛŋ sii ate ba se parik pagrisa a gilim si Juda po la kama a jam paari Jerusalem.
5Biisiteerɔwa Sɛmaiya a yaa jam Areyoboam ale Juda niŋdeerɔma baai ale jam tigsi Jerusalem po Sisak yɔgsum chalika nyiŋla jigi, ate wa weeni ba ayen, <<Dii ate Naawen a weeni la ale nna, <Ni zɛri mi kama, dila nyiŋ, mi yɔgyɔgla de a zɛri ni kama a te Sisak.> >>
6Izirali niŋdeerɔma ale naawa yaa yik badek ayen, <<Naawen ka wensie nyɔnɔ.>>
7Ase Naawen ale jam nya ayen ba yik badek la, Naawen wanni de yaa jam Sɛmaiya jigi ayen, <<Ase ba le yik badek la, mi a kan kaasi ba, m le te ba ka varibasika. M suipuurumu a kan va Sisak zuk a jam Jerusalem zuwa. 8Ba ale tom a te wa kama, ate dila ale basi ate ba zamsi ku tɔgatɔgaka ale ka dii ate fi tom a te mi abe fi tom a te tɛŋ yonsa nalima.>>
9Ase Sisak Ejipiti naawa ale jam nye kpaliŋ ale Jerusalem la, wa jam ji Naawen yenni paaruŋku ale naab yeri paaruŋku a ta cheŋ kama. Wa jam pai jaab meena kama a gum chaab ale ligmɔniŋ kpaliŋ ŋanchɔgsinta ate Solomon a jam nye la. 10Dila naab Areyoboam yaa jam nye kutuk mɔnuŋ kpaliŋ ŋanchɔgsinta ate bala a tagri mbala zuk a pa bade a nyo kpaga ŋaai ale a nya baai ale jam bo naab yeri nansuiŋku nɔi a limisi la. 11Diipo meena ate naawa a cheŋ Naawen yenni la, limisidɔma a nyiem a jam pai kpaliŋ ŋanchɔgsinta a yik tara, dila ŋaaŋnyiŋ ba ŋman ta ba a jo limisidɔma dɔkku po.
12Areyoboam ale jam yik wadek la nyiŋ, Naawen suipuurumu yaa basi wa, wa an jam kaasi wa. Chekki wamaŋsa maga a jam bo Juda po kama.
13Naab Areyoboam a jam kali paari kama Jerusalem po a tom du a cheŋ ase naab la. Wa jam ta ka bena pisinaansi ale dinyi ale chim naab, ale dɛ naam bena pi ale ŋayopɔi Jerusalem po, tɛŋ kaai ate Naawen a lueri nyini Izirali buuni meena po ayen wa pai wa Yuenni a basi du la. Wa mawa yuei jam le Naama, wa jam ka Ammon denɔ. 14Areyoboam jam nye ka biem dii nyiŋla wa an jam pai wa suinum a gisi Naawen ya.
15Dan ka Areyoboam naamu wieŋa a nyini piilimka a ta a cheŋ kpeglimka, ŋala a jam ŋmarisi doa ka biisiteerɔwa Sɛmaiya ale biisiteerɔwa Iddo ate ba jam a nye ale gaŋsa wie la gbaŋka po. Kpaliŋ ale kasim jam bo Areyoboam ale Jeroboam suŋsuŋ. 16Areyoboam a jam vuusi ale ka wa koma ate ba gu wa Deevid Tɛŋka po. Ate Abaija wa nidoabinni a zaani wa nankula po a chim naab.

english_text:
King Abijah of Judah
(1 Kings 15.1-8)
1Abijah became king of Judah in Jeroboam's eighteenth year as king of Israel, 2and he ruled from Jerusalem for three years. His mother was Micaiah the daughter of Uriel from Gibeah.
Some time later, Abijah and King Jeroboam of Israel went to war against each other. 3Abijah's army had 400,000 troops, and Jeroboam met him in battle with 800,000 troops.
4Abijah went to the top of Mount Zemaraim in the hills of Ephraim and shouted:
Listen, Jeroboam and all you Israelites! 5The Lord God of Israel has made a solemn promise that every king of Israel will be from David's family. 6But Jeroboam, you were King Solomon's official, and you rebelled. 7Then right after Rehoboam became king, you and your bunch of worthless followers challenged Rehoboam, who was too young to know how to stop you.
8Now you and your powerful army think you can stand up to the kingdom that the Lord has given to David's descendants. The only gods you have are those gold statues of calves that Jeroboam made for you. 9You don't even have descendants of Aaron on your side, because you forced out the Lord's priests and Levites. In their place, you appoint ordinary people to be priests, just as the foreign nations do. In fact, anyone who brings a bull and seven rams to the altar can become a priest of your so-called gods.
10But we have not turned our backs on the Lord God! Aaron's own descendants serve as our priests, and the Levites are their assistants. 11Two times every day they offer sacrifices and burn incense to the Lord. They set out the sacred loaves of bread on a table that has been purified, and they light the lamps in the gold lampstand every day at sunset. We follow the commands of the Lord our God—you have rejected him! 12That's why God is on our side and will lead us into battle when the priests sound the signal on the trumpets. It's no use, Israelites. You might as well give up. There's no way you can defeat the Lord, the God your ancestors worshiped.
13But while Abijah was talking, Jeroboam had sent some of his troops to attack Judah's army from behind, while the rest attacked from the front. 14Judah's army realized they were trapped, and so they prayed to the Lord. The priests blew the signal on the trumpet, 15and the troops let out a battle cry. Then with Abijah leading them into battle, God defeated Jeroboam and Israel's army. 16The Israelites ran away, and God helped Judah's soldiers slaughter 17500,000 enemy troops. 18Judah's army won because they had trusted the Lord God of their ancestors.
19Abijah kept up his attack on Jeroboam's army and captured the Israelite towns of Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephron, as well as the villages around them.
20Jeroboam never regained his power during the rest of Abijah's rule. The Lord punished Jeroboam, and he died, but Abijah became more powerful.
21Abijah had a total of 14 wives, 22 sons, and 16 daughters. 22Everything Abijah said and did while he was king is written in the records of Iddo the prophet.
translation_text:
1Jeroboam ale jam dɛ naam a paari bena pi ale naaniŋ po la, Abaija yaa jam chim Juda naab, 2wa jam nya Jerusalem zuk ka bena ŋata. Wa mawa yuei jam le Mikaiya, Gibea denɔwa Uriel lie. Kpaliŋ ale jam bo Abaija ale Jeroboam suŋsuŋ. 3Abaija yaa jo kpaliŋ po ale kpaliŋ tugurik tɔŋdɔba tusa kobsinaansi (400,000) ate Jeroboam yaa gomsi a tu wa ale tugurik tom tusa kobsinaaniŋ (800,000).
4Abaija a jam za ka Zemaraim Guuku zuk Ɛfraim tɛŋka ate guuta a bo ka po la zuk ayen, <<Jeroboam ale Izirali meena a wom mi. 5Nama zɛ ayen Naawen, Izirali Wenni, a pai Izirali naamu a te ka Deevid ale wa ŋaaŋbisaŋa taam wuu ale yesa nɔiyeŋ la? 6Dila meena Nebat nidoabinni Jeroboam ale jam ka Deevid nidoabinni Solomon kpagi la, yaa zɛri an siak a te wa kpagni. 7Baai ale kan ta zula a ka kiri la gela yaa tigsi gilim wa a zɛri Solomon nidoabinni Areyoboam diipo ate wa diem paala a kan poli wie zuk la ale an pagra a tu chaab ale ba.
8<<Ate yɔgyɔgla fi a yaali ayen fi kan siak a te Naawen naamu, buui ale bo Deevid ŋaaŋbisaŋa nisa po. Chekki ni ka tugurik tom buui ale zuak la ale ta ligmɔniŋ naabisaŋa ate Jeroboam a nye ate si chim ni wena la. 9Alege nama an yiak Naawen kaabteerɔma a basi ya, Aaron nidoabinni ale Livaima, ale lueri nidek kaabteerɔba ase tɛŋsa si chaab nuruba ale nye diila? Waai meena ale jam a nye wadek cheri ale lalik paalik ale padaasa siyopɔi la a baga a chim kaabteerɔ ale ŋan baai ale kan daa wena la kama.
10<<Dan ka tama, Naawen ale ti Wen, tama abe an zɛri wa. Kaabteerɔma baai ale tom a te Naawen la ka Aaron nidoabilisa ate Livaima a maari ba. 11Saluik meena ba a te Naawen ka juka tiirita ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa la. Ba a dueni boroborok ka jazaanimu ale nala la zuk a tɔti zeuŋtaŋa ligmɔniŋ jazaanimu zuk junɔi meena. Ti kpesi a nya Naawen ti Wenni wie ŋaai ale magsi la kama. 12Wen a bo le ti kama, wa ale tama niŋdeerɔ. Wa kaabteerɔma ale ba damunsaŋa ale kum kpaliŋ kaarika a siti ni. Izirali nidoaba, ni kan kpaliŋ ale Naawen, ni koma Wenni, ni kan nya nakdeka.>>
13Jeroboam a jam tom ka tugurik tom ate ba bo ŋaaŋ, ase wa ale bo Juda niŋ la baai ale suk doa la a jam bo ka ŋaaŋ. 14Juda demma yaa viriŋ nya ale ba siti ba kama niŋ ale ŋaaŋ. Ba yaa kaari a te Naawen. Kaabteerɔma yaa peeri ba damunsaŋa 15ate Juda nidoama yaa kaari kpaliŋ kaarik, ase kpaliŋ kaarika ale jueli la, Wen yaa pai Jeroboam ale Izirali demma meena a nyo Abaija ale Juda nisima po. 16Izirali demma a jam yiti chali kama Juda niŋ, ate Wen a pai ba a nyo ba nisa po. 17Abaija ale wa nidoama a jam te ba ka tuem nna yega, ate nuruba tusa kobsinu (500,000) a kpi. 18Izirali nidoama ba jam nya pagrim ba zuk kama dila po, ate Juda demma a chim nakdeerɔba dii nyiŋla ba jam zak a nya ka Naawen ba koma Wenni.
19Abaija a jaa vi Jeroboam ka dila a ga tuesi Betel ale Jesana ale Efron tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa ale si tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa ale gilim si la a nyini wa jigi. 20Jeroboam an ŋman jam nya pagrimoa Abaija vaaŋa po. Naawen a jam nak wa a lɔnsi kama ate wa kpi.
21Abaija a jam boro ale ka nyiŋ pagra. Wa jam faari ka nipooba pi ale banaansi, a ta nidoabilisa pisiye ale baye ale lieba pi ale bayuebi.
22Abaija naamu wayoŋ tintila, dii ate wa jam nye la ale dii ate wa jam weeni la, a ŋmarisi doa biisiteerɔwa Iddo gbaŋka po kama.

english_text:
King Asa of Judah
1Abijah died and was buried in Jerusalem. Then his son Asa became king, and Judah had ten years of peace.
2Asa obeyed the Lord his God and did right. 3He destroyed the local shrines and the altars to foreign gods. He smashed the stone images of gods and cut down the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah. 4Then he told everyone in Judah to worship the Lord God, just as their ancestors had done, and to obey his laws and teachings. 5He destroyed every local shrine and incense altar in Judah.
6The Lord blessed Judah with peace while Asa was king, and so during that time, Asa fortified many of the towns. 7He said to the people, “Let's build walls and defense towers for these towns, and put in gates that can be locked with bars. This land still belongs to us, because we have obeyed the Lord our God. He has given us peace from all our enemies.” The people did everything Asa had suggested.
8Asa had a large army of brave soldiers: 300,000 of them were from the tribe of Judah and were armed with shields and spears; 280,000 were from Benjamin and were armed with shields and bows.
Judah Defeats Ethiopia's Army
9Zerah from Ethiopia led an army of 1,000,000 soldiers and 300 chariots to the town of Mareshah in Judah. 10Asa met him there, and the two armies prepared for battle in Zephathah Valley.
11Asa prayed:
Lord God, only you can help a powerless army defeat a stronger one. So we depend on you to help us. We will fight against this powerful army to honor your name, and we know that you won't be defeated. You are the Lord our God.
12The Lord helped Asa and his army defeat the Ethiopians. The enemy soldiers ran away, 13but Asa and his troops chased them as far as Gerar. It was a total defeat—the Ethiopians could not even fight back!
The soldiers from Judah took everything that had belonged to the Ethiopians. 14The people who lived in the villages around Gerar learned what had happened and were afraid of the Lord. So Judah's army easily defeated them and carried off everything of value that they wanted from these towns. 15They also attacked the camps where the shepherds lived and took a lot of sheep, goats, and camels. Then they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_text:
1Abaija a jam vuusi kama ale wa koma ate ba gu wa Deevid Tɛŋka po. Asa wa nidoabinni ale jam zaani wa nankula po ase naab la, wa daaŋa po tɛŋ kpieŋka a jam ta ka suiyɔgni bena pi.
2Asa a jam nye ka wamaŋsa ale dii ale nala Naawen wa Wenni nina po. 3Wa jam kpiti kuŋkuŋ chaŋsaŋa ale pimpitimaŋa ale ŋɔriŋ tintain ferim weleŋsaŋa ale che Asera zaŋŋa a lɔnsi. 4Wa jam weeni Juda kama ayen ba gisi Naawen, ba koma Wenni abe ba siak wa sinsaŋŋa ale wa wieŋa. 5Wa jam kpiti pimpitimaŋa ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa la kuŋkuŋtaŋa Juda tɛŋsaŋa po meena kama ate naamu a jam ta suiyɔgni wa vaaŋa po. 6Wa jam sɛ ka parik pagrisa a gilim Juda tɛŋsaŋa diila tɛŋka a jam ta ka suiyɔgni. Waai a jam ka kpaliŋ ale wa bein ŋala po, diila Naawen a jam te wa ka vuusum.
7Wa jam weeni Juda ayen, <<Ni basi ate ti sɛ tɛŋsaŋa de, a gilim si ale parisa ale kiaga a su tuata ale taperisa. Tɛŋka ka tama ale diem soa, dii nyiŋla ti gisi Naawen ti Wenni kama, ti gisi wa kama ate wa te ti vuusum jigi meena.>> Dila ba yaa jam sɛ ale jigsi.
8Asa a jam ta ka tugurik tom tusa kobsita (300,000) Juda po, wa gomsi ba ale kpaliŋ ŋanchɔgsin kpienta ale gbatta, ate tusa kobsiye ale pinaanuŋ (280,000) a nyini Benjamin, ate ba mɛ a gomsi ale kpaliŋ ŋanchɔgsin fiisa ale tima. Bade meena jam ka tugurik tɔŋdɔ baai ale toa.
9Kus denɔwa Zera yaa gɔk santiri a tu chaab ale ba ale tugurik tom nna bissi ale torokoba kobsita ate ku yalima a nyini Maresa. 10Asa yaa nyini ayen wa tu wa, ate ba yaa zaani kpaliŋ zaana jigi Zefata Viaka po moata Maresa.
11Asa yaa wi Naawen wa Wenni ayen, <<Naawen yaa, waai a karo ase fi la a maari waai ale kan ta pagrim la a tu chaab ale tanjaŋini. Maari ti, Naawen ti Wen yaa, ale tama zak a nya ka fi, fi yuenni nyiŋ ate tama a baga a tu tugurik tom boanni de. Naawen yaa, fi ka tama Wen, kan basi ate nurubiik a nya pagrim fi zuwa.>>
12Naawen yaa lɔnsi Kus demma tɛŋ Asa ale Juda niŋ ate ba yiti chali, 13ate Asa ale wa tommu a vi ba a ta ga paari Gerar tɛŋka Kus nuru boanni ale jam lo la an ŋman jam yiti ya, ba jam ŋɔriŋ kama Naawen ale wa tugurik nyama niŋ. Juda nidoama a jam ji ka ŋanta nna yega a ta cheŋ. 14Ba jam kaasi tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa meena ale gilim Gerar la kama, diila Naawen yɔgsum ale lo ba zuk. Ba jam kɔlim tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa de meena kama, ŋan maŋsa ale jam bo si po la nyiŋ. 15Ba jam maa siti naapeerisaŋa boka jigini kama a yiak piisa ale bua ale laalaakomiba a ta cheŋ. Ba yaa ŋman cheŋ Jerusalem.

english_text:
Asa Destroys the Idols in Judah
1Some time later, God spoke to Azariah son of Oded. 2At once, Azariah went to Asa and said:
Listen to me, King Asa and you people of Judah and Benjamin. The Lord will be with you and help you, as long as you obey and worship him. But if you disobey him, he will desert you.
3For a long time, the people of Israel did not worship the true God or listen to priests who could teach them about God. They refused to obey God's Law. 4But whenever trouble came, Israel turned back to the Lord their God and worshiped him.
5There was so much confusion in those days that it wasn't safe to go anywhere in Israel. 6Nations were destroying each other, and cities were wiping out other cities, because God was causing trouble and unrest everywhere.
7So you must be brave. Don't give up! God will honor you for obeying him.
8As soon as Asa heard what Azariah the prophet said, he gave orders for all the idols in Judah and Benjamin to be destroyed, including those in the towns he had captured in the territory of Ephraim. He also repaired the Lord's altar that was in front of the temple porch.
9Asa called together the people from Judah and Benjamin, as well as the people from the territories of Ephraim, West Manasseh, and Simeon who were living in Judah. Many of these people were now loyal to Asa, because they had seen that the Lord was with him.
10In the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's rule, they all met in Jerusalem. 11That same day, they took 700 bulls and 7,000 sheep and goats from what they had brought back from Gerar and sacrificed them as offerings to the Lord. 12They made a solemn promise to faithfully worship the Lord God their ancestors had worshiped, 13and to put to death anyone who refused to obey him. 14The crowd solemnly agreed to keep their promise to the Lord, then they celebrated by shouting and blowing trumpets and horns. 15Everyone was happy because they had made this solemn promise, and in return, the Lord blessed them with peace from all their enemies.
16Asa's grandmother Maacah had made a disgusting idol of the goddess Asherah, so he cut it down, crushed it, and burned it in Kidron Valley. Then he removed Maacah from her position as queen mother. 17As long as Asa lived, he was faithful to the Lord, even though he did not destroy the local shrines in Israel. 18He placed in the temple all the silver and gold objects that he and his father had dedicated to God.
19There was peace in Judah until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's rule.
translation_text:
1Wen Chiika yaa jam Oded nidoabinni Azariya po. 2Wa jam nyini wa tu Asa a yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Wom mi, Asa ale Juda ale Benjamin demma, Naawen a bo le ni ase nama a nin bo ale wa. Ni dan gisi wa, ni le nya wa, alege ni dan zɛri wa wa le zɛri ni. 3Ku beni ka nna yega Izirali an jam bo ale wensie Wenni, kaabteerɔ a jam karo a sagi, ba ŋman jam ka sinsaga. 4Alege ba ninammu po, ba jam viriŋ Naawen, Izirali Wenni jigi kama a gisi wa a jam nya wa. 5Va ŋala po ku jam daa moali ate fi nyiem a gilimmu, diila tɛŋsaŋa meena a jam bo ka daani kpieŋ po. 6Tɛŋ kpieŋ kanyi nyiem ale ŋɔriŋ nka ate tɛŋ fiik a ŋɔriŋ ka choa, dii nyiŋla Wen a jam namsi ba ale daanika nna tɔgatɔga. 7Alege dan ka fi, be pagra abe fi kan jɔk yiila, fi le nya tutuna fi tuini nyiŋ.>>
8Ase Asa ale ga wom wieŋa de ale Oded nidoabinni biisiteerɔwa Azariya ale porisi diila, wa yaa jam nya nyiŋbiiri. Wa yaa jam kpiti kisuk bɔgtaŋa meena Juda ale Benjamin tɛŋsaŋa po ale tɛŋ sii ate wa nak yik Ɛfraim tɛŋka ate guuta a bo ka po la. Wa ŋman jam tebi Naawen kuŋkuŋku ale jam bo Naawen yenni po suiku niŋ la kama.
9Wa yaa jam tigsi Juda ale Benjamin demma meena ale Ɛfraim nuruma ale Manasa ale Simeyon baai ale jam kali ba po la, nuru boari ale jam nyini Izirali a jam wa jigi ase ba le jam nya ayen Naawen wa Wenni a jam bo ale wa la.
10Ba jam tigsi ka Jerusalem po chiisa sitawa po bena pi ale ŋanuwa po ate Asa a dɛ naam la po. 11Va ŋala po ka niiga kobsiyopɔi ale piisa ale bua tusa ŋayopɔi (7,000) ate ba jam kaab te Naawen. Ba jam ta ŋa nyini ka kpaliŋka po ate ba kɔlim la a jam. 12Ba jam jo ka nɔiyeŋ po ayen ba gisi Naawen ba koma Wenni ale ba suiniima meena ale ba chiisa meena. 13Baai meena ale ka a gisi Naawen, Izirali Wenni la, ba le kpi kama, wa dan ka nuru kpioŋ yaase nuru fiik yaase nidoa yaase nipok wa le kpi. 14Ba jam nye ka pɛka a te Naawen ale nyiŋ zeentika nuemka ale a na a peeri damunsa. 15Juda meena a jaa naŋ kama pɛka nyiŋ dii nyiŋla ba jam pɛ ale ka ba suiniima meena. Ba jam nya gisi Wen kama nalimnyiini a jam nya wa. Dila Naawen a jam te ba ka vuusum jigi meena.
16Naab Asa a jam yeeri wa ma kpieŋka Maaka wa naamu po kama ase naab pok la, dii nyiŋla wa jam nye ka Asera kisuk zaŋŋi. Asa a jam che zaŋni a lɔnsi kama, a wɛ di a ju di Kidron Viaka po. 17Alege wa an jam kpiti pimpitimaŋa Izirali po a basi ya, Asa suinummu meena a jam bo ka Naawen jigi wa boka po meena. 18Wa jam ta kpanaŋa ale ligmɔniŋka ale ŋantomtaŋa ate wa ale wa kowa a pai te Wen wa yenni po.
19Kpaliŋ a ŋman jam ka ate ku paari bena pisita ale ŋanu ate Asa a dɛ naam la.

english_text:
King Baasha of Israel Invades Judah
(1 Kings 15.16-22)
1In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's rule, King Baasha of Israel invaded Judah and captured the town of Ramah. He started making the town stronger, and he put troops there to stop people from going in and out of Judah.
2When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. Then he sent it to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria: 3“I think we should sign a peace treaty, just as our fathers did. This silver and gold is a present for you. Would you please break your treaty with King Baasha of Israel and force him to leave my country?”
4Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, Abel-Maim, and all the towns in Naphtali where supplies were kept. 5When Baasha heard about it, he stopped his work on the town of Ramah.
6Asa ordered everyone in Judah to carry away the stones and wood Baasha had used to fortify Ramah. Then he fortified the towns of Geba and Mizpah with these same stones and wood.
Hanani the Prophet Condemns Asa
7Soon after that happened, Hanani the prophet went to Asa and said:
You depended on the king of Syria instead of depending on the Lord your God. And so, you will never defeat the Syrian army. 8Remember how powerful the Ethiopian and Libyan army was, with all their chariots and cavalry troops! You trusted the Lord to help you then, and you defeated them. 9The Lord is constantly watching everyone, and he gives strength to those who faithfully obey him. But you have done a foolish thing, and your kingdom will never be at peace again.
10When Asa heard this, he was so angry that he put Hanani in prison. Asa was also cruel to some of his people.
Asa Dies
(1 Kings 15.23,24)
11Everything Asa did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel. 12In the thirty-ninth year of his rule, he got a very bad foot disease, but he relied on doctors and refused to ask the Lord for help. 13He died two years later.
14Earlier, Asa had his own tomb cut out of a rock hill in Jerusalem. So he was buried there, and the tomb was filled with spices and sweet-smelling oils. Then the people built a bonfire in his honor.
translation_text:
1Asa ale jam dɛ naamu a paari bena pisita ale ŋayuebi la, Izirali naawa Baasia yaa jueli siti Juda a sɛ parik a gilim Arama a kasi ayen waai a kan baga a nyini ka po yaase wa jo Juda naawa Asa tɛŋ banni po.
2Asa yaa jam pai kpanaŋa ale ligmɔniŋka Naawen yenni ŋanta dueni ka jigini ale wadek yenni po a ta nyini ga te Araam naawa Ben Yadad, waai ale jaa nya Damasikus zuk la. 3Wa jam weeni kama ayen, <<Basi ate nɔiyeŋ a bo mi ale fi suŋsuŋ ase ku le jam ka dii mi kowa ale fi kowa suŋsuŋ la. Nya, mi a tom ka kpana ale ligmɔniŋ a te fu. Kaasi fi nɔiyeŋka ate fi nye ale Izirali naawa Baasia la ate dila ale basi ate wa ŋmani abe wa basi mi.>>
4Ben Yadad yaa siak dii ate naab Asa a weeni la a tom wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpaga ate ba ga siti Izirali. Ba jam nak yik Ijon ale Dan ale Abel Maim ale Nafitali ŋanta duenika jigini tɛŋsaŋa kama. 5Ase Baasia ale ga wom kude la, wa yaa basi Arama sɛka ale banti tuini. 6Naab Asa yaa ta Juda nidoama meena a jam ate ba ji tanaŋa ale daataŋa ate Baasia a jam tom la a ta nyini Arama a cheŋ. Wa jam pai tanaŋa ale daataŋa a sɛ ka Geba ale Mizpa tɛŋsaŋa.
7Va ŋala po biisiteerɔwa Yanani yaa jam Juda naawa Asa jigi a weeni wa ayen, <<Fi ale pai yiila a basi Araam zuk alege daa Naawen fi Wenni zuk la nyiŋ ate Araam naawa tugurik tommu a bɛ nyini fi nisa po la. 8Kus demma ale Libia demma tugurik tommu an jam zuak a piisi ale torokoba ale wusum duerɔba? Alege fi ale jam pai fi yiila a basi Naawen jigi la, wa jam pai ba a nyo fi nisa po kama. 9Naawen nina a bo tɛŋzuk de meena kama ayen wa te baai suiniima meena ale bo wa jigi la pagrim. Ni tom ka betta tuini, a nyini yɔgyɔgla de a cheŋ ni le kasim bo ka kpaliŋ po.>>
10Asa sui ale jam a puuri ale biisiteerɔwa kude nyiŋ ku jam kasim a kab wa kama ate wa pai wa nyo likka dɔk po. Va ŋala dek po, Asa a jam te ku jo nuruma gela nyiŋ ka nna yegayega.
11Asa naamu wieŋa, a nyini piilimka a ta ga paari kpeglimka, a jam ŋmarisi doa Juda ale Izirali nalima gbaŋka po kama. 12Asa naamu bena pisita ale neokku po nyiŋtuila ale jam yik wa naŋtaataŋa. Nyiŋtuilaŋa a jam ŋmasi pagra kama, wa yuammu po meena wa an jam gisi maarika a nyini Naawen jigi ya, ka tinaŋsa nyam nyiini. 13Asa naamu bena pisinaansi ale dinyiwa po, wa yaa kpi a vuusi ale wa koma. 14Ba jam gu wa ka vɔrumu ate wa jam keri a magsi wadek la Deevid tɛŋka po. Ba jam pai wa a dueni ka kpieba jaab zuk a pai ŋan baai nyum ale masa la ale kpaata nna tɔgatɔga a gum chaab, a cheem bolim kpiem a te wa zula.

english_text:
King Jehoshaphat of Judah
1Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king and strengthened his defenses against Israel. 2He assigned troops to the fortified cities in Judah, as well as to other towns in Judah and to those towns in Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.
3-4When Jehoshaphat's father had first become king of Judah, he was faithful to the Lord and refused to worship the god Baal as the kings of Israel did. Jehoshaphat followed his father's example and obeyed and worshiped the Lord. And so the Lord blessed Jehoshaphat 5and helped him keep firm control of his kingdom. The people of Judah brought gifts to Jehoshaphat, but even after he became very rich and respected, 6he remained completely faithful to the Lord. He destroyed all the local shrines in Judah, including the places where the goddess Asherah was worshiped.
7In the third year of Jehoshaphat's rule, he chose five officials and gave them orders to teach the Lord's Law in every city and town in Judah. They were Benhail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah. 8Their assistants were the following nine Levites: Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-Adonijah. Two priests, Elishama and Jehoram, also went along. 9They carried with them a copy of the Lord's Law wherever they went and taught the people from it.
10The nations around Judah were afraid of the Lord's power, so none of them attacked Jehoshaphat. 11Philistines brought him silver and other gifts to keep peace. Some of the Arab people brought him 7,700 rams and the same number of goats.
12As Jehoshaphat became more powerful, he built fortresses and cities 13where he stored supplies. He also kept in Jerusalem some experienced soldiers 14from the Judah and Benjamin tribes. These soldiers were grouped according to their clans.
Adnah was the commander of the troops from Judah, and he had 300,000 soldiers under his command. 15Jehohanan was second in command, with 280,000 soldiers under him. 16Amasiah son of Zichri, who had volunteered to serve the Lord, was third in command, with 200,000 soldiers under him.
17Eliada was a brave warrior who commanded the troops from Benjamin. He had 200,000 soldiers under his command, all of them armed with bows and shields. 18Jehozabad was second in command, with 180,000 soldiers under him. 19These were the troops who protected the king in Jerusalem, not counting those he had assigned to the fortified cities throughout the country.
translation_text:
1Asa nidoabinni Jeyosafat ale jam zaani wa nankula po ase naab la ale te wadek nyiŋ pagra a tu chaab ale Izirali. 2Wa jam pa ka tugurik tom boari a basi Juda tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa po meena ate ba sɛ parisa a gilim ale basi tɔŋdɔba Juda ale Ɛfraim ate wa kowa Asa a jam nak yik la po.
3Naawen a jam bo ale Jeyosafat kama dii nyiŋla wa paalimu benaŋa po, wa jam a cheŋ ka suik tii ate wa kowa Deevid a jam va la po. Wa an jaa bek Baal wen jigi ya, 4alege wa goanti a gisi ka wa kowa Wenni ale va wa wieŋa, wa kan tomsi Izirali demma nyeelaŋa. 5Naawen a jam basi ate naamu a zaan paari kama wa nisima po, ate Juda demma meena a te Jeyosafat tiirita, ate dila a basi ate wa jigsi a ta zula. 6Wa suinummu a jam bo ka Naawen suitaŋa jigi, a ŋman gum du wa jam kpiti pimpitima kama ale che Asera zaŋŋa Juda po a basi.
7Bena ŋatawa po ate wa de naamu la wa yaa jam tom wa kpaŋŋa Ben Yail ale Obadia ale Zakaria ale Netanel ale Mikaiya ayen ba ga sak Juda tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa po. 8Livaiba gela ale jam va ba. Bala abe le Sɛmaiya ale Netania ale Zebadia ale Asayel ale Sɛmiramot ale Jeyonatan ale Adonija ale Tobijaya ale Tob Adonija ale kaabteerɔma Elisama ale Jeyoram. 9Ba jam sak kama ale gaam Juda a basi, ba jam pai ka Naawen Sinsaŋŋa Gbaŋka, ba jam cheŋ kama a gilim Juda tɛŋsaŋa meena a sak nuruma.
10Naawen yɔgsum yaa yik tɛŋsaŋa meena naataŋa ale gilim Juda la, ate ba an nye kpaliŋ ale Jeyosafat. 11Filistia demma gela yaa ta tiirita a jam Jeyosafat jigi ale kpana ase zula la, ate Arab demma a ta duŋ buulim a jam te wa. Duŋsaŋa a jam ka padaasa tusa ŋayopɔi ale kobsiyopɔi (7,700) ale bua tusa ŋayopɔi ale kobsiyopɔi (7,700).
12Jeyosafat yaa ŋmasi jam pagra a gum du, wa jam sɛ ka yie ale ŋanta duenika jigi Juda po 13ale jam tali ŋanta a zuak basi Juda po. Wa jam maa basi ka nuru baai ale nye kpaliŋ nya la Jerusalem po. 14Ba dɔkdemma po ate ba jam te ba tuimaŋa la ale nna. A nyini Juda dɔkku tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale jam a nya beŋsa tusidi zuk la jam le: Adnaa a jam a nya ka tugurik tɔŋdɔba tusa kobsita (300,000) zuk. 15Jeyoyanan ale jam pasaŋ a nya tugurik tɔŋdɔba tusa kobsiye ale pinaanuŋ (280,000) zuk, 16butawa po jam ka Zikri nidoabinni Amasiya, waai ale pa wadek a te Naawen tuini ale tugurik tɔŋdɔba tusa kobsiye (200,000). 17A nyini Benjamin dɔkku jam ka Eliada tugurik tɔŋdɔ tuak ale nuruba tusa kobsiye (200,000) ale tima ale kpaliŋ ŋanchɔgsinta. 18Jeyozabad mɛ a jam ta ka tugurik tɔŋdɔba tusa kook ale pinaanuŋ (180,000) a gomsi magsi kpaliŋ.
19Bade jam le nidoa baai ale jam tom a te naawa la, baai ate wa jam basi ate ba bo Juda tɛŋka meena po la an jam gum du.

english_text:
Micaiah Warns King Ahab of Israel
(1 Kings 22.1-28)
1Jehoshaphat was now very rich and famous. He signed a treaty with King Ahab of Israel by arranging the marriage of his son and Ahab's daughter.
2One day, Jehoshaphat went to visit Ahab in his capital city of Samaria. Ahab slaughtered sheep and cattle and prepared a big feast to honor Jehoshaphat and the officials with him. Ahab talked about attacking the city of Ramoth in Gilead, 3and finally asked, “Jehoshaphat, would you go with me to attack Ramoth?”
“Yes,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army is at your command. 4But first let's ask the Lord what to do.”
5Ahab sent for 400 prophets and asked, “Should I attack the city of Ramoth?”
“Yes!” the prophets answered. “God will help you capture the city.”
6But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
7“We could ask Micaiah son of Imlah,” Ahab said. “But I hate Micaiah. He always has bad news for me.”
“Don't say that!” Jehoshaphat replied. 8Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.
9All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria, listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
10Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was one of the prophets. He had made some horns out of iron and shouted, “Ahab, the Lord says you will attack the Syrians like a bull with iron horns and wipe them out!”
11All the prophets agreed that Ahab should attack the Syrians at Ramoth and promised that the Lord would help him defeat them.
12Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
13“I'll say whatever the living Lord my God tells me to say,” Micaiah replied.
14Then Micaiah went up to Ahab, who asked, “Micaiah, should we attack Ramoth?”
“Yes!” Micaiah answered. “The Lord will help you capture the city.”
15Ahab shouted, “Micaiah, I've told you over and over to tell me the truth! What does the Lord really say?”
16 Micaiah answered, “In a vision I saw Israelite soldiers wandering around, lost in the hills like sheep without a shepherd. The Lord said, ‘These troops have no leader. They should go home and not fight.’ ”
17Ahab turned to Jehoshaphat and said, “I told you he would bring me bad news!”
18Micaiah replied:
I then saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him. 19The Lord asked, “Who can trick Ahab and make him go to Ramoth where he will be killed?”
They talked about it for a while, 20then finally a spirit came forward and said to the Lord, “I can trick Ahab.”
“How?” the Lord asked.
21“I'll make Ahab's prophets lie to him.”
“Good!” the Lord replied. “Now go and do it. You will be successful.”
22Ahab, this is exactly what has happened. The Lord made all your prophets lie to you, and he knows you will soon be destroyed.
23Zedekiah walked over and slapped Micaiah on the face. Then he asked, “Do you really think the Lord would speak to you and not to me?”
24Micaiah answered, “You'll find out on the day you have to hide in the back room of some house.”
25Ahab shouted, “Arrest Micaiah! Take him to Prince Joash and Governor Amon of Samaria. 26Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
27Micaiah said, “If you do come back, I was wrong about what the Lord wanted me to say.” Then he told the crowd, “Don't forget what I said!”
Ahab Dies at Ramoth
(1 Kings 22.29-35)
28Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead. 29Before they went into battle, Ahab said, “Jehoshaphat, I'll disguise myself, but you wear your royal robe.” Ahab disguised himself and went into battle.
30The king of Syria had ordered his chariot commanders to attack only Ahab. 31So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But Jehoshaphat prayed, and the Lord made the Syrian soldiers stop. 32And when they realized he wasn't Ahab, they left him alone.
33However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab between two pieces of his armor. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”
34The fighting lasted all day, with Ahab propped up in his chariot so he could see the Syrian troops. He stayed there until evening, and by sundown he was dead.
translation_text:
1Yɔgyɔgla de Jeyosafat a jam jigsi kama a ta zula, wa yaa nye nɔiyeŋ ale Ayab a faari wa lie. 2Bena magadek ale taam la wa yaa cheŋ Samaria ayen wa puusi Ayab. Ayab a jam tɔgri ka piisa ale niiga nna yegayega a te wa ale nuruma ale jam va wa la ale weeni wa ayen wa ga nye kpaliŋ ale Aramot Gilead tɛŋka. 3Izirali naawa Ayab yaa bek Juda naawa Jeyosafat ayen, <<Fi ale va mu a ga nye kpaliŋ ale Aramot Gilead?>> Jeyosafat yaa tulisi ayen, <<Mi a nye ase ka fi la, ate m nuruma mɛ a nye ase fi nuruma la, ti le gum fi po kpaliŋka po.>> 4Jeyosafat mɛ yaa weeni Izirali naawa ayen, <<De niŋ a bek Naawen.>>
5Dila Izirali naawa yaa jam ta biisiteerɔba kobsinaansi a jam jigi yeŋ a bek ba ayen, <<Ti ga nye kpaliŋ ale Aramot Gilead yaa ti kan cheŋ?>> Ba yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ni cheŋ ale Wen ale pai ka a nyo naawa nisa po.>>
6Alege Jeyosafat a jam bek ayen, <<Naawen biisiteerɔ a ka dela ate ti ga kpesi wom?>>
7Izirali naawa yaa tulisi Jeyosafat ayen, <<Nuru wanyi a diem boro ate tama a baga a va wa zuk a kpesi a wom a nyini Naawen jigi, alege mi kisi wa kama dii nyiŋla wa an diem porisi wa maŋ a te mi, wa kasim a weeni mi ka kaasuŋ nyiini. Wa ka Imla nidoabinni Mikaiya.>> Jeyosafat yaa tulisi ayen, <<Naawa an magsi wa weeni dila.>>
8Dila Izirali naawa yaa wi wa kpaŋŋa wanyi ayen, <<Ta Imla nidoabinni Mikaiya a jam.>>
9Izirali naawa ale Juda naawa Jeyosafat a jam jo ba naam gatta a kala ba naam zukpagliksaŋa zuk, juijui ate ba a fɔbi ŋanta la Samaria tɛŋka nansuiŋku nɔi ate biisiteerɔma meena a porisi ba niŋ. 10Chenaana nidoabinni Zedekia a jam nye ka kutuk nyiila ale mooli ayen, <<Dii ate Naawen a weeni la ale nna, <Ni ale pa ka nyiilaŋa de a chub Araam demma ate ku paari diipo ate ni ko ba la.> >>
11Biisiteerɔ mbala a jam a porisi ka wayeŋka ayen, <<Nye kpaliŋ ale Aramot Gilead a nya pagrim ba zuk, ale Naawen ale pa ba a nyo naawa nisa po.
12Tomtomdɔ waai ale jam cheŋ wa wi Mikaiya la yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Nya de, biisiteerɔ mbala meena a weeni kama ayen naab Ayab ale nya nak dɛka, basi ate fi ale a weeni diila a va bala ale weeni diila biisi ale ŋmanteka.>> 13Alege Mikaiya a weeni wa ayen, <<Ase Naawen ale vua la, mi ale weeni wa ka dii nyiini ate mi Wenni a weeni la.>>
14Ase wa ale jam paari la, naawa yaa bek Mikaiya ayen, <<Mikaiya, ti cheŋ ga nye kpaliŋ ale Aramot Gilead yaa m kan cheŋ?>> Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ni ga nye a nya nakdeka, ba ale jo ni nisa po.>>
15Naawa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Ka bu dina ate mi ale te fi pɛ a kan weeni mu wayoŋ alege ka wensie nyiini Naawen yuenni nyiŋŋa?>>
16Mikaiya yaa tulisi ayen, <<Mi nya ale Izirali meena a waaŋ chaab guutaŋa zuima ase piisa ale kan ta naapeerik diila, ate Naawen ayen, <Nuruma de a ka niŋdeerɔ. Basi ate ba kuli yeri ale suiyɔgni.> >> 17Izirali naawa yaa weeni Jeyosafat ayen, <<Mi an poom weeni fu ayen wa an diem porisi wamaŋ a te mi, ka kaasuŋ nyiini?>>
18Mikaiya a weeni a gum du ayen, <<Dila nyiŋ wom Naawen wanni. Mi nya ale Naawen a kala ka wa naam zukpaglika zuk ate wenŋmazuk tommu a za gilim wa juga ale gala meena. 19Naawen yaa weeni ayen, <Ka wana ale wa paasi Izirali demma naawa Ayab ate wa nye kpaliŋ ale Aramot Gilead tɛŋka ate wa ga kpi dula?> Nuru yeŋ a zok nna ate wa choa ayen nnala.
20Kpeglimka chichirik biok yaa jam niŋ nyiŋ, a zaani Naawen niŋ ayen, <Mi ale paasi wa.>
21<<Naawen a bek ayen, <Fi ale nye ka sɛ a nye dila?> Ate chichirik bioku a tulisi ayen, <Mi ale nyini peelim a ga jo wa biisiteerɔma meena nɔi po.> Naawen ayen, <Fi le nya suik a paasi wa, cheŋ ga nye dila.> >> 22Mikaiya a weeni ayen, <<Naawen a basi ate fi biisiteerɔma a velim te fu kama, Naawen abe weeni kama ayen kaasuŋ a jam fi zuk.>>
23Chenaana nidoabinni Zedekia yaa ga fɔbi Mikaiya ale bek ayen, <<Ka suik kuna po ate Naawen Chiika a nyini mi po a ga biisi ale fi?>>
24Mikaiya yaa tulisi ayen, <<Fi ale nya dila ka dai dii dai ate fi ale chali ga suk niŋ dɔk po la.>>
25Izirali naawa yaa weeni ayen, << Ni yik Mikaiya a ta wa ŋman ga te Amon tɛŋ kpieŋka niŋdeerɔwa ale naawa nidoabinni Joas 26ale weeni ayen, <Dii ate naawa a weeni la ale nna. Ni pa nuruwa de a nyo likka dɔk po abe ni kan te wa jaaboa, ni te wa boroborok ale nyiam nyiini ate ku paari diipo ate mi ale ŋmani ale suiyɔgni la.> >>
27Mikaiya yaa tulisi ayen, <<Fi a dan ŋman nalimnyiini, Naawen an va mi zuk a biisi ya.>> Wa yaa ŋman biisi a gum du ayen, <<Ni a teeri mi wieŋa, nama nuruba meena.>>
28Dila Izirali naawa ale Juda naawa Jeyosafat yaa jueli Aramot Gilead. 29Izirali naawa yaa weeni Jeyosafat ayen, <<Mi ale tagri m dek a jo kpaliŋka po alege fi a jo fi naam gattaŋa.>> Dila Izirali naawa yaa jam tagri wadek a cheŋ kpaliŋka po.
30Araam naawa a jam weeni wa torokoma kpaŋŋa kama ayen, <<Ni kan kpaliŋ ale waai ya ku nyɔnɔwa dan poom pɔsima yaase wa zuak, ka Izirali naawa nyiini.>> 31Ase torokoma kpaŋŋa ale ga nya Jeyosafat la, ba poli ayen, <<Izirali naawa ale nna.>> Dila ba yaa viriŋ ba kpaliŋ ale wa, ate Jeyosafat yaa kaari ate Naawen a jam maari wa. Wen yaa yiak ba a basi ale ge wa. 32Torokoma kpaŋŋa ale jam nya ayen daa Izirali naawa ale la la, ba yaa jam basi wa vika.
33Alege nuru wanyi yaa yeeri wa tom nna kadi a tɔŋ Izirali naawa kpaliŋ kɔlimaŋa paaŋa po. Naawa yaa weeni toroko damdɔwa ayen, <<Dam a gilim a ta mu a nyini kpaliŋka po, mi nya ka tuem.>> 34Danni po meena kpaliŋka a jam pagra kama, ate Izirali naawa a gomsi wadek a bo wa torokowa po a tu chaab ale Araam demma ate ku paari junɔi, wenni ale ga siŋ la wa yaa kpi.

english_text:
1Jehoshaphat returned safely to his palace in Jerusalem. 2But the prophet Jehu son of Hanani met him and said:
By helping that wicked Ahab, you have made friends with someone who hates the Lord. Now the Lord God is angry with you! 3But not everything about you is bad. You destroyed the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah—that shows you have tried to obey the Lord.
Jehoshaphat Appoints Judges To Settle Cases
4Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, but he often traveled through his kingdom, from Beersheba in the south to the edge of the hill country of Ephraim in the north. He talked with the people and convinced them to turn back to the Lord God and worship him, just as their ancestors had done.
5He assigned judges to each of the fortified cities in Judah 6and told them:
Be careful when you make your decisions in court, because you are judging by the Lord's standards and not by human standards, and he will know what you decide. 7So do your work in honor of him and know that he won't allow you to be unfair to anyone or to take bribes.
8Jehoshaphat also chose some Levites, some priests, and some of the family leaders, and he appointed them to serve as judges in Jerusalem. 9He told them:
Faithfully serve the Lord! 10The people of Judah will bring you legal cases that involve every type of crime, including murder. You must settle these cases and warn the people to stop sinning against the Lord, so that he won't get angry and punish Judah. Remember, if you follow these instructions, you won't be held responsible for anything that happens.
11Amariah the high priest will have the final say in any religious case. And Zebadiah, the leader of the Judah tribe, will have the final say in all other cases. The rest of the Levites will serve as your assistants. Be brave, and I pray that the Lord will help you do right.
translation_text:
1Ase Juda naawa Jeyosafat ale jam ŋmani nalimnyiini Jerusalem po la, 2Yanani nidoabinni biisiteerɔwa Jeyu, yaa jam nyini wa tu wa a yaa weeni naawa ayen, <<Fi ale maari gaasa nyama abe fi a yaali baai ale kisa Naawen la? Kude nyiŋ Naawen suipuurumu ale jam fi zuk. 3Alege wamaŋ ale bo fi po fi che Asera zaŋŋa tɛŋka po a basi kama ale gisi Wen ale fi suinum.>>
4Jeyosafat a jam bo ka Jerusalem po ale jam ŋman pilim va nuruma a nyini Beerseba a ga paari Ɛfraim tɛŋka ate guutaŋa a bo ka po la a tulim ba a te Naawen, ba koma Wenni. 5Wa jam lueri ka boteerɔba tɛŋka po, Juda tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa ate parisa a gilim la po. 6Wa jam weeni ba kama ayen, <<Ni kpesi dii ate ni a nye la nalimnyiini, dii nyiŋla ni an bo a te daa nuru, ka Naawen, waai ale bo ale ni ate ni a bo buusa la. 7Yɔgyɔgla de ni basi ate Naawen yɔgsum a bo ni jigi. Ni kpesi a bo buusaŋa nalimnyiini, Naawen ti Wenni jigi ŋurima ŋurima yaase lukka yaase diak wari a karo.>>
8Jerusalem po mɛ, Jeyosafat a jam lueri ka Livaiba gela ale kaabteerɔba ale Izirali dɔkdemma yieŋa nyam ayen ba a sak Naawen sinsaŋŋa abe ba a nya nanpaga wie zuk. Ba abe jam bo ka Jerusalem po. 9Wa jam te ba ka wieŋa de ayen, <<Ku a fɛ ate ni tom a te ale wensie ale ni suiniima meena abe ni a chali Naawen yɔgsum. 10Wari meena po dii ale nyini nidek tɛŋ demma baai ale bo tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa po ale ni la jam ni jigi la, ku dan poom ka ziim ale nyini yaase wayoŋ a nyini sinsaŋŋa ale wieŋa ale ŋmarisika yaase buusa nama ale ni kaam ba ate ba kan nye biem a kaasi Naawen ya, kan daa di wa suipuurumu ale jam nama ale ni suataŋa zuk. Ni nye kude ate ni kan nye biemmoa.
11<<Kaabteerɔ kpagni Amariya ale wa a nya ni zuk dii meena ale ta wari a nye ale Naawen la, abe Ismael nidoabinni Zebadia, Juda dɔkku buuni niŋdeerɔwa, wala ale wa nya ni zuk dii meena ale ta wari a nye ale naawa la, abe Livaima a tom ase kpaga la ni niŋ. Ni nye ale nyiŋbiiri, Naawen abe bo ale baai ale a tom nalimnyiini la.>>

english_text:
Moab and Ammon Are Defeated
1Some time later, the armies of Moab and Ammon, together with the Meunites, went to war against Jehoshaphat. 2Messengers told Jehoshaphat, “A large army from Edom east of the Dead Sea has invaded our country. They have already reached En-Gedi.”
3Jehoshaphat was afraid, so he asked the Lord what to do. He then told the people of Judah to go without eating to show their sorrow. 4They immediately left for Jerusalem to ask for the Lord's help.
5After everyone from Judah and Jerusalem had come together at the Lord's temple, Jehoshaphat stood in front of the new courtyard 6and prayed:
You, Lord, are the God our ancestors worshiped, and from heaven you rule every nation in the world. You are so powerful that no one can defeat you. 7 Our God, you forced out the nations who lived in this land before your people Israel came here, and you gave it to the descendants of your friend Abraham forever. 8Our ancestors lived in this land and built a temple to honor you. 9They believed that whenever this land is struck by war or disease or famine, your people can pray to you at the temple, and you will hear their prayer and save them.
10 You can see that the armies of Ammon, Moab, and Edom are attacking us! Those are the nations you would not let our ancestors invade on their way from Egypt, so these nations were not destroyed. 11Now they are coming to take back the land you gave us. 12Aren't you going to punish them? We won't stand a chance when this army attacks. We don't know what to do—we are begging for your help.
13While every man, woman, and child of Judah was standing there at the temple, 14the Lord's Spirit suddenly spoke to Jahaziel, a Levite from the Asaph clan. 15 Then Jahaziel said:
Your Majesty and everyone from Judah and Jerusalem, the Lord says that you don't need to be afraid or let this powerful army discourage you. God will fight on your side! 16So here's what you must do. Tomorrow the enemy armies will march through the desert around the town of Jeruel. March down and meet them at the town of Ziz as they come up the valley. 17 You won't even have to fight. Just take your positions and watch the Lord rescue you from your enemy. Don't be afraid. Just do as you're told. And as you march out tomorrow, the Lord will be there with you.
18Jehoshaphat bowed low to the ground and everyone worshiped the Lord. 19Then some Levites from the Kohath and Korah clans stood up and shouted praises to the Lord God of Israel.
20Early the next morning, as everyone got ready to leave for the desert near Tekoa, Jehoshaphat stood up and said, “Listen my friends, if we trust the Lord God and believe what these prophets have told us, the Lord will help us, and we will be successful.” 21Then he explained his plan and appointed men to march in front of the army and praise the Lord for his holy power by singing:
“Praise the Lord!
His love never ends.”
22As soon as they began singing, the Lord confused the enemy camp, 23so that the Ammonite and Moabite troops attacked and completely destroyed those from Edom. Then they turned against each other and fought until the entire camp was wiped out!
24When Judah's army reached the tower that overlooked the desert, they saw that every soldier in the enemy's army was lying dead on the ground. 25So Jehoshaphat and his troops went into the camp to carry away everything of value. They found a large herd of livestock, a lot of equipment, clothes, and other valuable things. It took them three days to carry it all away, and there was still some left over.
26Then on the fourth day, everyone came together in Beracah Valley and sang praises to the Lord. That's why that place was called Praise Valley.
27-28Jehoshaphat led the crowd back to Jerusalem. And as they marched, they played harps and blew trumpets. They were very happy because the Lord had given them victory over their enemies, so when they reached the city, they went straight to the temple.
29When the other nations heard how the Lord had fought against Judah's enemies, they were too afraid 30to invade Judah. The Lord let Jehoshaphat's kingdom be at peace.
Jehoshaphat Dies
(1 Kings 22.41-50)
31Jehoshaphat was 35 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 25 years. His mother was Azubah daughter of Shilhi. 32Jehoshaphat obeyed the Lord, just as his father Asa had done, 33but he did not destroy the local shrines. So the people still worshiped foreign gods, instead of faithfully serving the God their ancestors had worshiped.
34Everything else Jehoshaphat did while he was king is written in the records of Jehu son of Hanani that are included in The History of the Kings of Israel.
35While Jehoshaphat was king, he signed a peace treaty with Ahaziah the wicked king of Israel. 36They agreed to build several seagoing ships at Ezion-Geber. 37But the prophet Eliezer warned Jehoshaphat, “The Lord will destroy these ships because you have supported Ahaziah.” The ships were wrecked and never sailed.
translation_text:
1Kude ŋaaŋnyiŋ Moab demma ale Ammon demma ale Meuni demma gela yaa jan jam ayen ba nye kpaliŋ ale Jeyosafat.
2Nidoaba gela jam weeni Jeyosafat ayen, <<Tugurik tom boari ale nyini Edom tɛŋka a cheena ayen ba nye kpaliŋ ale fu, ba nyini ka nyakpiemu kauk kunkula. Ba poom bo ka Yazazon Tamara.>> En Gedi ale la. 3Yɔgsum yaa yik Jeyosafat ate wa poli wa kpesi a wom Naawen jigi ale weeni ate Juda meena a bobi nɔi. 4Juda nuruma meena yaa jam jigi yeŋ a gisi maarika a nyini Naawen jigi. Ba jam nyini ka jigi meena Juda tɛŋka po a jam a gisi Naawen.
5Jeyosafat yaa jam yiti zaani Juda ale Jerusalem tigsuŋku po Naawen yenni dabiak paalika po, 6ayen, <<Naawen yaa, tama koma Wenni, fi daa Wen ya waai ale bo wenŋmazuk la? Fi ale a nya tɛŋsa meena naataŋa zuk. Pagrim ale zuaka a bo ka fi nisa po, ate waai an baga a zaani ale fi. 7Ti Wen yaa, fi an yiak tɛŋka de demma a basi a te fi nuruma Izirali demma ale pai ka a te Abrayam fi doawa ŋaaŋbisaŋa taam wuu? 8Ba bo ka ka po a sɛ yeri fi Yuenni nyiŋ ayen, 9<Ase kaasuŋ a dan lo ti zuk, ku ka gebik buusa yaase nyiŋtuila yaase kɔm, ti le zaani fi niŋ yenni de ale ta fi Yuenni la po a kaari a te fi ti ninammu po, ate fi le wom ti a vari ti basi.>
10<<Alege yɔgyɔgla de nuruba ale nna a nyini Ammon ale Moab ale Seir Guuku baai tɛŋsa ate fi an basi ate Izirali a fɛ jo si po diipo ate ba nyini Ejipiti a jam la, dila ba yaa viriŋ cheŋ ale basi ba an ko ba. 11Nya dii ate ba ŋman pai a tuni tama ase ba le jam a yiak ti ayen ti basi tɛŋka ate fi te ti ase ti nitalim la. 12Ti Wen yaa, fi a kan bo ba buusa? Tama a ka pagrim a tu chaab ale tom boanni de ale a siti ti la. Tama a zɛ ti le ti nye diila, alege ti ninaŋa a bo ka fi zuk.>>
13Juda nidoama meena ale ba pooma ale bisaŋa ale ŋan fiisaŋa yaa jam za dula Naawen niŋ.
14Naawen Chiika yaa jam Zakaria nidoabinni Jayaziel zuk. Benaya nidoabili ale jam nye Zakaria ate Jeiel nidoabili a chim Benaya ate Mattania nidoabili a chim Jeiel. Mattania jam ka Livai denɔ a chim Asaf ŋaaŋbiik, ase wa le jam yiti zaani tigsuŋku po la.
15Wa weeni ayen, <<Naab Jeyosafat ale baai meena ale bo Juda ale Jerusalem po la a wom de, dii ate Naawen a weeni la ale nna: <Kan chali yɔgsummoa yaase fi jɔk nyiŋbiiri tugurik tom boanni de nyiŋŋa. Ale kpaliŋka daa fi le soa, ka Wen. 16Chum gɔk santiri a siŋ siti ba. Ba le jueli va Ziz Suiku, ate fi le nya ba vooliŋka kpeglimka ale bo Jeruel Gɔnni po la. 17Ku an magsi fi kpaliŋ kpaliŋka de. Ni zaani ni jiŋŋa. Ni zaani giŋgiŋ ate ni nya varibasika ate Naawen ale te ni la, Juda ale Jerusalem demma. Ni kan chali yɔgsummoa, ni be kan jɔk nyiŋbiiri, ni nyini a ga tu ba chum, Naawen ale bo ale ni.> >>
18Jeyosafat yaa koori a pai nina a vuk tɛŋka ate Juda ale Jerusalem nuruma meena a lo tɛŋ a puusi Naawen. 19Livaiba gela yaa nyini Koyat ale Koora diinaŋa yaa jam zaani a seni Naawen, Izirali Wenni ate ku jueli.
20Saluik yokyokwa ba yaa cheŋ Tekoa Gɔnni po. Ase ba le nyini la, Jeyosafat yaa zaani ayen, <<Ni wom mi, Juda ale Jerusalem nuruba! Ni ta siaka ale Naawen ni Wenni ate ni le nya pagrim. Ni ta siaka ale wa biisiteerɔma ate ni nya bo maŋ.>> 21Wa le wom nuruma ale sak wa diila ŋaaŋnyiŋ, Jeyosafat a jam lueri ka nuruba ayen ba lenni yiila a te Naawen abe ba a seni wa zuaka weleŋsaŋa ase ba le jam nyini le wom tugurik tommu kpagni ale weeni ayen, <<Ni te Naawen jiam ale wa ŋmanteka a boro kama taam wuu.>>
22Ase ba le piilim, a lenni ale a pak la, Naawen yaa gu a limisi Ammon ale Moab ale Seir Guuku nidoama baai ale jam fɛ a jo Juda po la a nak yik ba. 23Ammon ale Moab nidoama yaa yiti ta chaab ale nidoa baai ale nyini Seir Guuku la ayen ba kaasi ba chessi. Ba ale jam tɔgri nidoama ale nyini Seir la a ga nueri la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, badek yaa jam a ko chaab.
24Ase Juda nidoama ale jam paari gɔnni po la ba nya ka tugurik tom boanni ale kpi doa tɛŋka. Ba wanyi an chali bɛ ya. 25Dila Jeyosafat ale wa nuruma yaa ga pai ba ŋantaŋa a ta cheŋ, ba jam nya ka kɔlima ale gatta nna yega ale ŋantomta mɛ ate ba dobra a gaam ba pai ta cheŋka. Ŋantaŋa a jam piisi ka nna yega ate ba pai daa ŋata a ji ba. 26Daa ŋanaansiwa danni ba yaa jam tigsi Berakaya Viaka po, yuenni kiri ale niaka, juijui ate ba jam pak Naawen la. Dila ale soa ate ba a wi dula ayen Berakaya Viak jinla danni la.
27Jeyosafat yaa jam de Juda ale Jerusalem demma meena niŋ ate ba ŋmani ale suipeentik a cheŋ Jerusalem. Ka Naawen ale te ba suik ayen ba a naŋ ba dachaasaŋa zuk. 28Ba jam jo Jerusalem po kama a cheŋ Naawen yenni po ale kpanta ale dunduirisa ale damunsa.
29Wen yɔgsum yaa yik tɛŋsaŋa meena naataŋa ase ba ale jam wom dii ate Naawen a nye a kpaliŋ ale Izirali dachaasaŋa la. 30Ate Jeyosafat naamu a jam boro ale suiyɔgni, ka wa Wenni ale jam te wa vuusum jigi meena.
31Dila Jeyosafat yaa jaa nya Juda zuk. Wa jam ta ka bena pisita ale ŋanu ale chim naab Juda ale de naamu Jerusalem po bena pisiye ale ŋanu. Wa mawa yuei jam le Azuba wa jam ka Silyi lie. 32Wa jam a cheŋ ka wa kowa Asa suitaŋa po, wa an basi ti vaka, wa jam a nye ka dii ale nala Naawen nina po la. 33Kaabka pimpitimaŋa an jam kpiti ya, nuruma mɛ an diem jam pai ba suiniima a basi ba koma Wenni jigi ya.
34Jeyosafat naamu wayonaŋa, a nyini piilimka a ga paari kpeglimka, a jam ŋmarisi doa ka Yanani nidoabinni Jeyu wieŋa po, ŋaai ale jam ŋmarisi doa Izirali nalima gbaŋka po la.
35Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ Juda naawa Jeyosafat a jam nye ka nɔiyeŋ ale Izirali naawa Ayaziya waai ale jam nye nna foola gaasa nyiŋla. 36Wa jam siak kama ayen wa le nye geruŋ ŋaaruŋta. Ŋaaruŋtaŋa de ale jam nye Ezion Geber tɛŋka po a nueri la ŋaaŋnyiŋ. 37Dodavayu ale nyini Maresa la nidoabinni Ɛlieza yaa jam porisi basi Jeyosafat nyiŋ ayen, <<Fi ale nye nɔiyeŋ ale Ayaziya la nyiŋ, Naawen ale kaasi dii ate fi nye la.>> Ŋaaruŋtaŋa a jam kaasi kama a kan tom geruŋ tuima.

english_text:
1Jehoshaphat died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king.
King Jehoram of Judah
(2 Kings 8.16-24)
2King Jehoshaphat had seven sons: Jehoram, Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah. 3Jehoshaphat gave each of them silver and gold, as well as other valuable gifts. He also put them in charge of the fortified cities in Judah, but he had chosen his oldest son Jehoram to succeed him as king.
4After Jehoram had taken control of Judah, he had his brothers killed, as well as some of the nation's leaders. 5He was 32 years old when he became king, and he ruled eight years from Jerusalem.
6Jehoram married Ahab's daughter and followed the sinful example of Ahab's family and the other kings of Israel. He disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong, 7 but because the Lord had made a solemn promise to King David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah, he refused to wipe out David's descendants.
8 While Jehoram was king, the people of Edom rebelled and chose their own king. 9Jehoram, his officers, and his cavalry marched to Edom, where the Edomite army surrounded them. He escaped during the night, 10but Judah was never able to regain control of Edom. Even the town of Libnah rebelled at that time.
Those things happened because Jehoram had turned away from the Lord, the God his ancestors had worshiped. 11Jehoram even built local shrines in the hills of Judah and let the people sin against the Lord by worshiping foreign gods.
12One day, Jehoram received a letter from Elijah the prophet that said:
I have a message for you from the Lord God your ancestor David worshiped. He knows that you have not followed the example of Jehoshaphat your father or Asa your grandfather. 13Instead you have acted like those sinful kings of Israel and have encouraged the people of Judah to stop worshiping the Lord, just as Ahab and his descendants did. You even murdered your own brothers, who were better men than you.
14Because you have done these terrible things, the Lord will severely punish the people in your kingdom, including your own family, and he will destroy everything you own. 15You will be struck with a painful stomach disease and suffer until you die.
16The Lord later caused the Philistines and the Arabs who lived near the Ethiopians to become angry with Jehoram. 17They invaded Judah and stole the royal property from the palace, and they led Jehoram's wives and sons away as prisoners. The only one left behind was Ahaziah, his youngest son.
18After this happened, the Lord struck Jehoram with an incurable stomach disease. 19About two years later, Jehoram died in terrible pain. No bonfire was built to honor him, even though the people had done this for his ancestors.
20Jehoram was 32 years old when he became king, and he ruled 8 years from Jerusalem. He died, and no one even felt sad. He was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs.
translation_text:
1Jeyosafat yaa vuusi ale wa koma ate ba jam gu wa a gum ba po Deevid Tɛŋka po. Jeyoram wa nidoabinni ale jam zaani wa naŋkula po ase naab la. 2Jeyosafat nidoabinni Jeyoram suataŋa jam le Azariya ale Jeyiel ale Zakaria ale Azariayu ale Maakil ale Sefatia. Bade meena jam ka Izirali naawa Jeyosafat nidoabilisa. 3Ba kowa a jam te ba ka tiirita yega ale kpana ale ligmɔniŋ ale ŋan baai ale ta dobrim ale tɛŋ sii ate parisa a gilim la Juda po, alege a pai naamu a te Jeyoram dii nyiŋla wala jam le wa nidoabili kpagi.
4Ase Jeyoram ale jam kali wa kowa naamu po a paari la, wa yaa jam tɔgri wa suataŋa meena ale Izirali nabisaŋa gela. 5Jeyoram jam ta ka bena pisita ale ŋaye ale chim naab, a dɛ naamu Jerusalem po bena naaniŋ. 6Wa jam va Izirali nalimaŋa nyeelaŋa ase Ayab yenni ale jam nye diila, wa jam faari ka Ayab lie. Wa jam nye ka biem Naawen nina po. 7Alege nɔiyeŋka ate Naawen a jam nye ale Deevid la nyiŋ, Naawen an jam a yaali wa kaasi Deevid yenni. Wa puulim kama ayen wa pai naamu a te wa ale wa ŋaaŋbisaŋa taam wuu.
8Jeyoram vaaŋa po, Edom an jam siak a te Juda ale bobi badek naab. 9Dila Jeyoram yaa jam cheŋ dula ale wa kpaŋŋa ale wa kpaliŋ torokoma meena, Edom demma a jam gilim wa ale wa torokoma kpaŋŋa a basi ka suŋsuŋ alege wa yiti yok a chali bɛ. 10A ta jam paari jinla Edom a diem ta ka tukpari ale Juda. Dila po dek ate Libna ta tɛŋka mɛ a poori nyini Jeyoram jigi dii nyiŋla Jeyoram a jam zɛri Naawen wa koma Wenni kama. 11Wa jam maa sɛ ka pimpitima Juda guutaŋa zuima a nye ate Jerusalem demma a nye nidoa yaalik tuima ale ta Juda demma a cheŋ bɛ.
12Jeyoram a jam nya ka gbaŋ a nyini biisiteerɔwa Elaja jigi ayen, <<Dii ate Naawen fi kowa Deevid Wenni a weeni la ale, <Fi an va fi kowa Jeyosafat yaase Asa Juda naawa suitaŋa. 13Fi jam nye ka Izirali nalimaŋa nyeelaŋa ale nye ate Juda ale Jerusalem nuruma a nye nidoa yaalik tuima, ase dii dek ate Ayab yenni a jam nye la. Fi jam ko ka fidek suata mɛ, baai ale ka fi kowa yenni dem la, nidoa baai ale jam zunchoŋ fu la. 14Dila nyiŋ Naawen a boro a yaali wa jueli ka fi nuruma ale fi nidoabilisaŋa ale fi pooma ale jabuui meena ate fi soa la zuk. Wa cheena ale ka niguri. 15Fidek ale nya nyiŋtuila ate nyiŋtuilaŋa a nye ate fi nyuetaŋa a nyini.>>
16Naawen yaa jam basi ate Filistia ale Arab demma ale kali moata Kus la sue yaa jam puuri ale Jeyoram. 17Ba jam nye ka kpaliŋ ale Juda a fɛ jo ka po a ji ŋan maŋsaŋa meena ate ba nya naab yenni po la a ta cheŋ a gum chaab ale wa nidoabilisaŋa ale wa pooma. Ba an jam tali nidoabili yeŋ mɛ a te wa ka wa bibaaŋka Jeyoayaz. 18Ŋade meena ŋaaŋnyiŋ, Naawen a jam basi ate ka nyueta nyiŋtuila ŋaai ale kan ta tebika la a yik Jeyoram. 19Ku an beni ya, bena ŋayewa kpeglimka po, wa nyuetaŋa yaa nyini peelim nyiŋtuilaŋa nyiŋ, ate wa kpi ale nyiŋdomma nna yegayega, wa nuruma an jam cheem bolim a te wa zula ase wa koma la.
20Jeyoram jam ta ka bena pisita ale ŋaye ale chim naab la, wa jam de naamu Jerusalem po ka bena naaniŋ. Wa kummu an jam daani waai ya, ate ba gu wa Deevid Tɛŋka po alege daa naawa boosuku po.

english_text:
King Ahaziah of Judah
(2 Kings 8.25-29; 9.21,27,28)
1Earlier, when the Arabs led a raid against Judah, they killed all of Jehoram's sons, except Ahaziah, the youngest one. So the people of Jerusalem crowned him their king. 2He was 22 years old at the time, and he ruled only one year from Jerusalem.
Ahaziah's mother was Athaliah, a granddaughter of King Omri of Israel, 3and she encouraged her son to sin against the Lord. He followed the evil example of King Ahab and his descendants. 4In fact, after his father's death, Ahaziah sinned against the Lord by appointing some of Ahab's relatives to be his advisors.
Their advice led to his downfall. 5He listened to them and went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle, 6and he went to the town of Jezreel to recover. And Ahaziah later went there to visit him. 7It was during that visit that God had Ahaziah put to death.
When Ahaziah arrived at Jezreel, he and Joram went to meet with Jehu grandson of Nimshi. The Lord had already told Jehu to kill every male in Ahab's family, 8and while Jehu was doing that, he saw some of Judah's leaders and Ahaziah's nephews who had come with Ahaziah. Jehu killed them on the spot, 9then gave orders to find Ahaziah. Jehu's officers found him hiding in Samaria. They brought Ahaziah to Jehu, who immediately put him to death. They buried Ahaziah only because they respected Jehoshaphat his grandfather, who had done his best to obey the Lord.
There was no one from Ahaziah's family left to become king of Judah.
Queen Athaliah of Judah
(2 Kings 11.1-3)
10As soon as Athaliah heard that her son King Ahaziah was dead, she decided to kill any relative who could possibly become king. She would have done just that, 11but Jehosheba rescued Joash son of Ahaziah just as the others were about to be murdered. Jehosheba, who was Jehoram's daughter and Ahaziah's half sister, was married to Jehoiada the priest. So she was able to hide her nephew Joash and his personal servant in a bedroom in the Lord's temple where he was safe from Athaliah. 12Joash hid in the temple with them for six years while Athaliah ruled as queen of Judah.
translation_text:
1Jerusalem nuruma jam bobi ka Jeyoram nidoabili baaŋka Ayaziya naab a tagri wa, ase baai ale jam fɛ jo ale Arabia demma la ale jam ko wa bi kpaŋŋa meena la. Dila Jeyoram nidoabinni Ayaziya yaa piilim a nya Juda zuk.
2Ayaziya jam ta ka bena pisinaansi ale ŋaye ale chim naab, wa jam de naamu Jerusalem po ka ben yeŋ. Wa mawa yuei jam le Ataliaya Omri ŋaaŋ lie.
3Wa mɛ a jam a nye ka Ayab yenni nyeelaŋa. Ka wa mawa ale jam te wa nyiŋbiiri ate wa nye a kaasi. 4Wa jam nye ka biem Naawen nimbie po ase Ayab yenni ale jam nye diila, wa kowa kummu ŋaaŋnyiŋ ba jam chim ka wa dachaasa. 5Wa jam wom ka ba nɔi a va Ayab nidoabinni Jeyoram Izirali naawa a ga nye kpaliŋ ale Araam naawa Yazael Aramot Gilead tɛŋka. Araam demma jam nak Joram a koani kama. 6Wa yaa ŋman jam Jezreel ayen wa nya ba le koani wa Arama kpaliŋka po ate wa ga nye ale Araam naawa Yazael la zuk. Jeyoram nidoabinni Azariya Juda naawa yaa jam siŋ Jezreel ayen wa nya Ayab nidoabinni Joram dii nyiŋla wa jam koani kama.
7A ta va Ayaziya ale cheŋ Joram jigi la, Wen a va ka dila zuk a lɔnsi Ayaziya. Ase Ayaziya ale jam la, wa yaa va Joram ayen wa tu Nimsi nidoabinni Jeyu, waai ate Naawen a lueri ayen wa kaasi Ayab yenni la. 8Ase Jeyu ale jam boro a bo buusa Ayab yenni po la, wa yaa nya Juda nabisaŋa ale Ayaziya nidoabilisaŋa kobisaŋa baai ale jam tom a te Ayaziya la ate wa ko ba meena. 9Wa yaa jam jo a gisi Ayaziya, wa nuruma a jam yik wa ale wa suk bo ka Samaria po. Ba jam ta wa jam ka Jeyu jigi a ko wa. Ba jam gu wa kama ale ge weeni ayen, <<Wa jam ka Jeyosafat nidoabili, waai ale jam va Naawen ale wa suinum meena.>> Dila waai a jam ka Ayaziya yenni po a pagra a tuesi naamu.
10Ase Ayaziya mawa Ataliaya ale jam nya ayen wa nidoabinni a kpi la, wa yaa poli ayen wa kaasi Juda nadɔkku meena. 11Alege naab Jeyoram liewa Jeyosabeat yaa pai Ayaziya nidoabinni Joas a ta nyini nabisaŋa po waai ate ba jam a yaali ba ko la ale wa biika a suk wa ale wa nyaarɔwa goom dɔk po. Dii nyiŋla naab Jeyoram liewa Jeyosabeat ale ka kaabteerɔwa Jeyoiada pok la, jam ka Ayaziya toa. Wa jam pai biika a suk kama ate wa an baga a ko wa. 12Biika a diem jam suk bo ale ba kama Wen yenni po bena ŋayuebi ale ge ate Ataliaya a nya tɛŋka zuk.

english_text:
Jehoiada Makes Joash King of Judah
(2 Kings 11.4-21)
1After Ahaziah's son Joash had hidden in the temple for six years, Jehoiada the priest knew that something had to be done. So he made sure he had the support of several army officers. They were Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri. 2These five men went to the towns in Judah and called together the Levites and the clan leaders. They all came to Jerusalem 3 and gathered at the temple, where they agreed to help Joash.
Jehoiada said to them:
Joash will be our next king, because long ago the Lord promised that one of David's descendants would always be king. 4Here is what we will do. Three groups of priests and Levites will be on guard duty on the Sabbath—one group will guard the gates of the temple, 5one will guard the palace, and the other will guard Foundation Gate. The rest of you will stand guard in the temple courtyards. 6Only the priests and Levites who are on duty will be able to enter the temple, because they will be the only ones who have gone through the ceremony to make themselves clean and acceptable. The others must stay outside in the courtyards, just as the Lord has commanded. 7You Levites must protect King Joash. Don't let him out of your sight! And keep your swords ready to kill anyone who comes into the temple.
8The Levites and the people of Judah followed Jehoiada's orders. The guards going off duty were not allowed to go home, and so each commander had all his guards available—those going off duty as well as those coming on duty. 9Jehoiada went into the temple and brought out the swords and shields that had belonged to King David, and he gave them to the commanders. 10They gave the weapons to the guards, and Jehoiada then made sure that the guards took their positions around the temple and the altar to protect the king on every side.
11Jehoiada and his sons brought Joash outside, where they placed the crown on his head and gave him a copy of the instructions for ruling the nation. Olive oil was poured on his head to show that he was now king, and the crowd cheered and shouted, “Long live the king!”
12As soon as Queen Athaliah heard the crowd cheering for Joash, she went to the temple. 13There she saw Joash standing by one of the columns near the entrance, which was the usual place for the king. The commanders and the trumpet players were standing next to him, and the musicians were playing instruments and leading the people as they celebrated and blew trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes in anger and shouted, “You betrayed me, you traitors!”
14At once, Jehoiada said to the army commanders, “Don't kill her near the Lord's temple. Take her out in front of the troops, and be sure to kill all of her followers!” 15She tried to escape, but the commanders caught and killed her near the gate where horses are led into the palace.
16Jehoiada asked King Joash and the people to join with him in being faithful to the Lord. They agreed, 17then rushed to the temple of the god Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and the idols and killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars.
18Jehoiada assigned the priests and Levites their duties at the temple, just as David had done. They were in charge of offering sacrifices to the Lord according to the Law of Moses, and they were responsible for leading the celebrations with singing. 19Jehoiada ordered the guards at the temple gates to keep out anyone who was unclean.
20Finally, Jehoiada called together the army commanders, the most important citizens of Judah, and the government officials. The crowd of people followed them as they led Joash from the temple, through the Upper Gate, and into the palace, where he took his place as king of Judah. 21Everyone celebrated because Athaliah had been killed and Jerusalem was peaceful again.
translation_text:
1Bena ŋayopɔiwa po Jeyoiada yaa sak wa pagrimu. Wa jam nye ka nɔiyeŋ ale kpaga ale a nya beŋsa kobsa zuk la. Bala ale Jeroyam nidoabinni Azariya ale Jeyoyanan nidoabinni Ismael ale Obed nidoabinni Azariya ale Adaiya nidoabinni Maaseiya ale Zikri nidoabinni Elisafat. 2Ba jam cheŋ Juda po meena a tigsi Livaima ale Izirali yeeŋa nyama a nyini tɛŋsaŋa meena po. Ba ale jan jam Jerusalem la, 3Tigsuŋku meena yaa nye nɔiyeŋ ale naawa Joas Wen yenni po. Jeyoiada yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Naawa nidoabinni ale za wa dɛ naamu, ase Naawen ale jam puulim a ta va Deevid ŋaaŋbisaŋa zuk diila.
4<<Yɔgyɔgla de fi le fi nye diila ale nna: nama kaabteerɔma ale Livaima gela ale a cheŋ tuima Vuusum Danni la ale ni a limisi tuataŋa 5abe ni gela a bo naab yeri abe ni gela a bo Nyubini Nansuiŋku abe mbala meena a magsi ba bo ka Naawen yenni dabiaka po. 6Waai an magsi wa jo Naawen yenni dabiaka po, ka kaabteerɔma ale Livaima ale bo tuima la nyiini, bala a baga a jo kama dii nyiŋla ba ta tuilum kama, alege nuru mbala meena a magsi ba a nya ka Naawen ale te ba tuin diila. 7Livaima a magsi ba zaani a gilim ka naawa, nuru meena ale a ta wa ja kpalim wa nisa po. Waai a dan jo Naawen yenni po ku a fɛ ate ba ko wa. Ni bo naawa tɛŋ juijui meena ate wa a cheŋ la.
8Livaima ale Juda demma meena a jam nye ka dii dek ate kaabteerɔwa Jeyoiada a weeni la. Waai meena a jam ta ka wa nuruba baai ale jam bo tuima Vuusum danni la ale baai ale jam kan bo tuima Vuusum danni la, diila kaabteerɔwa Jeyoiada an jam te beŋ kaai suiwa. 9Wa yaa jam te kpaga ale a nya beŋsa kobsa zuk la gbatta ale kpaliŋ ŋanchɔgsin kpienta ale ŋan fiisa ate naab Deevid a jam soa ate ba bo Wen yenni po la. 10Wa jam pai nidoama meena a zaani kama, nuru meena ale wa kpaliŋ jaab wa nisa po, a gilim naawa a moata kuŋkuŋku ale Wen yenni, a nyini yeseoku gensa ta ga paari Wen yenni wiilukku geŋsa.
11Jeyoiada ale wa nidoabilisaŋa a yaa ta naawa nidoabinni a nyini a pai zutɔk mun a vuk wa. Ba jam pai ka nɔiyeŋka gbaŋ a te wa ale mooli ayen wa ka naab. Ba yaa bobi wa naam ale na ayen, <<Goa beni naaba.>>
12Ase Ataliaya ale ga wom nuruma nuemka ale a chali a seni naawa la, wa yaa cheŋ ba jigi Naawen yenni po, 13Ataliaya yaa nya ale ka naawa, ale la a za wa zaŋni tɛŋ nansuiŋku nɔi. Kpaŋŋa ale damun peerisaŋa a jam za ka naawa gauŋ ate nuruma meena tɛŋka po a jam a naŋ ale a peeri damunsa, ate yilendisa ale ŋannaginta a jam a keri yiilaŋa. Ataliaya yaa dari wa gattaŋa a cheeri ale na ayen, <<Yiaka! Yiaka!>>
14Kaabteerɔwa Jeyoiada yaa jam tom kpaŋŋa ale a nya beŋsa kobsa zuk la, baai ale a nya tugurik tommu zuk la a weeni ba ayen, <<Ni ta wa a jam peelim a ko ale waai meena ale va wa la.>> Kaabteerɔwa a weeni kama ayen, <<Ni kan ko wa Naawen yenni po.>> 15Dila ba yaa yik, wa ase wa le jam paari Wusuma Nansuiŋku nɔi naab yeri la, dula jigini ate ba jam ko wa.
16Jeyoiada yaa jam nye nɔiyeŋ ayen wa ale nuruma ale naawa a chim Naawen nuruba. 17Nuruma meena yaa jam cheŋ Baal bɔglukku yenni a nak di lɔnsi. Ba jam ŋɔriŋ kuŋkuŋtaŋa ale bɔgtaŋa kama ale ko Mattan, Baal kaabteerɔwa kuŋkuŋtaŋa niŋ.
18Jeyoiada yaa pai Naawen yenni tuimaŋa a nyo kaabteerɔma nisima po, baai ale ka Livaima la, baai ate Deevid a te ba tuima Wen yenni po ayen ba a nye juka tiirim a te Naawen ase ku le ŋmarisi dii Moosis Sinsaŋŋa po ale mariŋka ale yiila lennika, ase Deevid ale jam weeni la. 19Wa jam basi ate ka limisidɔba a za Naawen yenni nansuiŋtaŋa mɛ ate nuru waai ale daŋ la a nya suik a baga a jo.
20Wa jam ta ka kpaga ŋaai ale a nya kobsa zuk la ale nuru kpienta ale niŋdeerɔba ale nuruma meena tɛŋka po ale ta naawa a nyini Naawen yenni po, a siŋ tɛŋ. Ba jam va ka Ŋmazuk Nansuiŋku a jo naab yenni po a pai naawa a kali naam zukpaglika zuk. 21Ate nuruma meena tɛŋka po sue a jam peenti. Ate tɛŋ nummu a jam nye nna chorototo, dii nyiŋla ba jam ko Ataliaya kama.

english_text:
King Joash of Judah
(2 Kings 12.1-16)
1Joash was only 7 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled 40 years from Jerusalem. His mother Zibiah was from the town of Beersheba.
2While Jehoiada the priest was alive, Joash obeyed the Lord by doing right. 3Jehoiada even chose two women for Joash to marry so he could have a family.
4Some time later, Joash decided it was time to repair the temple. 5He called together the priests and Levites and said, “Go everywhere in Judah and collect the annual tax from the people. I want this done at once—we need that money to repair the temple.”
But the Levites were in no hurry to follow the king's orders. 6 So he sent for Jehoiada the high priest and asked, “Why didn't you send the Levites to collect the taxes? The Lord's servant Moses and the people agreed long ago that this tax would be collected and used to pay for the upkeep of the sacred tent. 7And now we need it to repair the temple because the sons of that evil woman Athaliah came in and wrecked it. They even used some of the sacred objects to worship the god Baal.”
8Joash gave orders for a wooden box to be made and had it placed outside, near the gate of the temple. 9He then sent letters everywhere in Judah and Jerusalem, asking everyone to bring their taxes to the temple, just as Moses had required their ancestors to do.
10The people and their leaders agreed, and they brought their money to Jerusalem and placed it in the box. 11Each day, after the Levites took the box into the temple, the king's secretary and the high priest's assistant would dump out the money and count it. Then the empty box would be taken back outside.
This happened day after day, and soon a large amount of money was collected. 12Joash and Jehoiada turned the money over to the men who were supervising the repairs to the temple. They used the money to hire stonecutters, carpenters, and experts in working with iron and bronze.
13These workers went right to work repairing the temple, and when they were finished, it looked as good as new. 14They did not use all the tax money for the repairs, so the rest of it was handed over to Joash and Jehoiada, who then used it to make dishes and other gold and silver objects for the temple.
