Sacrifices to please the Lord were offered regularly in the temple for as long as Jehoiada lived. 15He died at the ripe old age of 130 years, 16and he was buried in the royal tombs in Jerusalem, because he had done so much good for the people of Israel, for God, and for the temple.
Joash Turns Away from the Lord
17After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the leaders of Judah went to Joash and talked him into doing what they wanted. 18The people of Judah soon stopped worshiping in the temple of the Lord God and started worshiping idols and the symbols of the goddess Asherah. These sinful things made the Lord God angry with the people of Judah and Jerusalem, 19but he still sent prophets who warned them to turn back to him. The people refused to listen.
20 God's Spirit spoke to Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, and Zechariah told everyone that God was saying: “Why are you disobeying me and my laws? This will only bring punishment! You have deserted me, so now I will desert you.”
21-22King Joash forgot that Zechariah's father had always been a loyal friend. So when the people of Judah plotted to kill Zechariah, Joash joined them and gave orders for them to stone him to death in the courtyard of the temple. As Zechariah was dying, he said, “I pray that the Lord will see this and punish all of you.”
Joash Is Killed
23In the spring of the following year, the Syrian army invaded Judah and Jerusalem, killing all of the nation's leaders. They collected everything of value that belonged to the people and took it back to their king in Damascus. 24The Syrian army was very small, but the Lord let them defeat Judah's large army, because he was punishing Joash and the people of Judah for turning away from him.
25-26Joash was severely wounded during the battle, and as soon as the Syrians left Judah, two of his officials, Zabad and Jehozabad, decided to revenge the death of Zechariah. They plotted and killed Joash while he was in bed, recovering from his wounds. Joash was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs. 27The History of the Kings also tells more about the sons of Joash, what the prophets said about him, and how he repaired the temple. Amaziah son of Joash became king after his father's death.
translation_text:
1Joas jam ta ka bena ŋayopɔi ale chim naab, a dɛ naamu Jerusalem po bena pisinaansi. Wa mawa yuei jam le Zibiya, wa jam nyini ka Beerseba. 2Joas jam nye ka dii ale jam nala Naawen nina po la kaabteerɔwa Jeyoiada benaŋa po meena. 3Jeyoiada a jam lueri ka pooba baye a te wa, ate wa jam ta nidoabilisa ale lieba.
4Ku le beni magadek la, Joas yaa jam zɔk ayen wa ŋman tebi Naawen yenni. 5Wa yaa wi kaabteerɔma ale Livaima jigi yeŋ a weeni ba ayen, <<Cheŋ Juda tɛŋka po a tuesi Izirali demma ale magsi ba tuni ligri ŋaai meena la ate ti pa tebi ni Wen yenni. Nye dila yɔgyɔgla de,>> alege Livaima an deri jam nye bunyi.
6Dila nyiŋ naawa yaa wi Jeyoiada kaabteerɔ kpioŋku a weeni wa ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi an weeni Livaima ayen ba ta lampoowa ate Naawen tomteerɔwa Moosis a jam weeni ayen Izirali tigsuŋku a cheesi a ta nyini Juda ale Jerusalem a jam magsi wen viuku la?>>
7Gaasa nipowa Ataliaya nidoabilisaŋa a jam wɛ kama a jo wen dɔkku po a pai ku ŋan weleŋsaŋa a ta ga te Baal.
8Naawa a weeni ate ba nye cheesika dakari a pai di zaani Naawen yenni nansuiŋku nɔi. 9Moolik ale jam nye Juda ale Jerusalem tɛŋsaŋa po meena ayen ba ta Naawen lampoowa ate Wen tomteerɔwa Moosis a weeni Izirali sagni po ayen ba ta jam la.
10Kpaŋŋa meena ale nuruma meena a jam ta ba cheesuŋku a jam kama ale suipeentik, a lɔnsi dakanni po ate di ga sueri. 11Diipo meena Livaima a dan ta dakanni a jam naawa nisɔmma jigi ate ba nya ayen ligraŋa a zuak, naab yeri teeridɔwa ale kaabteerɔ kpioŋku kpagni a nyiem jam kpiiri ligraŋa kama ale ge daka koruk ale ŋman ta di a cheŋ di jigini. Ba jam a nye kude ka veruveruk a tuesi ligra nna yegayega. 12Naawa ale Jeyoiada yaa jam pai ŋa a te nidoama baai ale jam a tom Naawen yenni tuimaŋa la. Ba jam yaali ka seerɔba ale danagrisa ate ba tom Naawen yenni tuini ate ba tuni ba, ba jam mi a yaali ka baai ale a gebi kuta ale kutuk mɔnuŋ la ate ba tom Wen yenni tuini.
13Nidoa baai ale jam a nya tuini zuk la a jam kpesi badek kama, ate tuini a cheŋ nalimnyiini ba nisa po. Ba jam ŋman sɛ Wen yenni kama ase di ni magsi ba sɛ di dii a nyini piilimka la. 14Ba le jam nueri la, ba yaa ta ligri ŋaai ale tali la meena a jam te naawa ale Jeyoiada, ate ba pai ŋa a nye Naawen yenni ŋantomta. Ŋantomta a magsi tuima ale juka tiirita ale china ale ligmɔniŋ ale kpana ŋanta. Ase Jeyoiada ale jam boro a beni diila, juka tiirimu a jam te a vi chaab ka dila Naawen yenni po.
15Yɔgyɔgla de Jeyoiada a jam kpaŋ kama ate wa benaŋa a piisi. Wa jam ta ka bena kook ale pisita ale kpi. 16Ba jam gu wa a gum ka nalimaŋa po Deevid Tɛŋka po, dii nyiŋla wamaŋsaŋa ate wa jam nye Izirali po a te Wen ale Wen yenni la.
17Jeyoiada kummu ŋaaŋnyiŋ Juda kpaŋŋa meena yaa jam ba sak zula ale naawa ate wa wom ba. 18Ba jam banti Naawen yenni a basi kama, ba koma Wenni ale a va Asera zaŋŋa ale bɔgtaŋa. Ba foolaa wa nyiŋ, Wen suipuurum yaa jam Juda ale Jerusalem po. 19Naawen a jam tom ka biisiteerɔba nuruma jigi ayen wa ta ba a ŋman jam wa jigi ba le jam biisi a kaasi ba la, ba an diem jam wom ya.
20Wen chiika yaa jam kaabteerɔwa Jeyoiada nidoabinni Zakaria jigi. Wa jam zaani ka nuruma niŋ ayen, <<Dii ate Wen a weeni la ale nna: <Ka boa ate nama an siak Naawen wieŋa? Ni kan jigsi. Dii nyiŋla ni zɛri Naawen kama wa mɛ a zɛri ni kama.>>
21Alege ba jam ta chaab ale wa, ate Naawa a te suik ate ba jam yuk wa ale tana ate wa kpi Naawen yenni dabiaka po. 22Naab Joas an jam teeri nyemagsika ate Zakaria kowa Jeyoiada a jam sak wa la alege a ko wa nidoabinni waai ale jam doa a kpi ale weeni ayen, <<Naawen a nya abe wa bek fu ku nyiŋ.>>
23Benni nueka po, Araam tugurik tɔŋdɔma yaa jam gɔk santiri a ta chaab ale Joas, ba jam fɛ jo Juda ale Jerusalem po kama a ko nuruma niŋdeerɔma meena. Ba jam ta ba le koaliŋ ŋan baai meena la a ga te ka ba naawa Damasikus po. 24Araam tugurik tɔŋdɔma a jan jam ale ka nidoaba maga, Naawen a jam pai ka tugurik tɔŋdɔ bori a nyo ba nisa po. Diila Juda a jam zɛri Naawen kama, ba koma Wenni, buusa ale jam Joas zuk. 25Ase Araam demma ale jam ŋmani la, ba jam kɔni Joas ka nna yegayega. Wa kpaŋŋa a jam zɔk kama a ta chaab ale wa, dii nyiŋla wa le ko kaabteerɔwa Jeyoiada nidoabinni la, a ko Joas wa gaduokku zuk. Dila wa jam kpi kama ate ba gu wa Deevid Tɛŋka po alege jam daa nalimaŋa boosutaŋa po.
26Baai ale jam ta chaab ale wa la jam le Zabad, wa jam ka Simeat Amon tɛŋka lie nidoabili ale Moab tɛŋka liewa Simrit nidoabinni Jeyozabad. 27Wa nidoabilisaŋa wie, wie ŋaai ate ba biisi te wa ale wa le ŋman tebi Wen yenni la, a ŋmarisi doa nalima gbaŋka po kama. Joas nidoabinni Amaziya ale jam zaani wa naŋkula po ase naab la.

english_text:
King Amaziah of Judah
(2 Kings 14.1-6)
1Amaziah was 25 years old when he became king, and he ruled 29 years from Jerusalem, the hometown of his mother Jehoaddin.
2Even though Amaziah obeyed the Lord by doing right, he refused to be completely faithful. 3For example, as soon as he had control of Judah, he arrested and killed the officers who had murdered his father. 4 But the children of those officers were not killed; the Lord had commanded in the Law of Moses that only the people who sinned were to be punished.
Edom Is Defeated
(2 Kings 14.7)
5Amaziah sent a message to the tribes of Judah and Benjamin and called together all the men who were 20 years old and older. Three hundred thousand men went to Jerusalem, all of them ready for battle and able to fight with spears and shields. Amaziah grouped these soldiers according to their clans and put them under the command of his army officers. 6Amaziah also paid about 3.4 tons of silver to hire 100,000 soldiers from Israel.
7One of God's prophets said, “Your Majesty, don't let these Israelite soldiers march into battle with you. The Lord has refused to help anyone from the northern kingdom of Israel, 8and so he will let your enemies defeat you, even if you fight hard. He is the one who brings both victory and defeat.”
9Amaziah replied, “What am I supposed to do about all the silver I paid those troops?”
“The Lord will give you back even more than you paid,” the prophet answered.
10Amaziah ordered the troops from Israel to go home, but when they left, they were furious with the people of Judah.
11After Amaziah got his courage back, he led his troops to Salt Valley, where he killed 10,000 Edomite soldiers in battle. 12He captured 10,000 more soldiers and dragged them to the top of a high cliff. Then he pushed them over the side, and they all were killed on the rocks below.
13Meanwhile, the Israelite troops that Amaziah had sent home, raided the towns in Judah between Samaria and Beth-Horon. They killed 3,000 people and carried off their possessions.
14After Amaziah had defeated the Edomite army, he returned to Jerusalem. He took with him the idols of the Edomite gods and set them up. Then he bowed down and offered them sacrifices. 15This made the Lord very angry, and he sent a prophet to ask Amaziah, “Why would you worship these foreign gods that couldn't even save their own people from your attack?”
16But before the prophet finished speaking, Amaziah interrupted and said, “You're not one of my advisors! Don't say another word, or I'll have you killed.”
The prophet stopped. But then he added, “First you sinned and now you've ignored my warning. It's clear that God has decided to punish you!”
Israel Defeats Judah
(2 Kings 14.8-14)
17King Amaziah of Judah talked with his officials, then sent a message to King Jehoash of Israel: “Come out and face me in battle!”
18Jehoash sent back a reply that said:
Once upon a time, a small thornbush in Lebanon arranged the marriage between his son and the daughter of a large cedar tree. But a wild animal came along and trampled the small bush.
19Amaziah, you think you're so powerful because you defeated Edom. But stay at home and do your celebrating. If you cause any trouble, both you and your kingdom of Judah will be destroyed.
20God made Amaziah stubborn because he was planning to punish him for worshiping the Edomite gods. Amaziah refused to listen to Jehoash's warning, 21so Jehoash led his army to the town of Beth-Shemesh in Judah to attack Amaziah and his troops. 22During the battle, Judah's army was crushed. Every soldier from Judah ran back home, 23and Jehoash captured Amaziah.
Jehoash took Amaziah with him when he went to attack Jerusalem. Jehoash broke down the city wall from Ephraim Gate to Corner Gate, a section nearly 200 meters long. 24He carried away the gold, the silver, and all the valuable furnishings from God's temple where the descendants of Obed-Edom stood guard. He robbed the king's treasury, took hostages, then returned to Samaria.
Amaziah Is Killed
(2 Kings 14.15-20)
25Amaziah lived 15 years after Jehoash died. 26Everything else Amaziah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
27As soon as Amaziah started disobeying the Lord, some people in Jerusalem plotted against Amaziah. He was able to escape to the town of Lachish, but another group of people caught him and killed him there. 28His body was taken to Jerusalem on horseback and buried beside his ancestors.
translation_text:
1Amaziya jam ta ka bena pisiye ale ŋanu ale chim naab, a dɛ naam Jerusalem po bena pisiye ale neok. Wa mawa yuei jam le Jeyoaddan, nipowa a jam nyini ka Jerusalem. 2Wa jam nye ka dii ale nala Naawen nina po alege daa wa suinum po meena. 3Naamu ale ga jo wa nisa a paari la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, wa yaa ko kpaga ŋaai meena ale jam ko wa kowa naawa la. 4Wa an jam ko ba nidoabilisaŋa, wa jam nye a ta va chaab ale ka dii ale ŋmarisi sinsaŋŋa po la, Moosis gbaŋka, juijui ate Naawen a jam weeni ayen, <<Ba kan ko koba ba bisa kaasuŋ nyiŋŋa yaase ba ko bisa ba koba kaasuŋ nyiŋla. Waai meena a kpi ka wadek biem nyiŋ.>>
5Amaziya yaa wi Juda Demma meena jigi yeŋ a ta va ba dɔkdemma ale ka diila, ate ba bo kpaga ale a nya tusa ale kpaga ale a nya kobsa la nisa po a te Juda ale Benjamin meena. Wa yaa jam chiini baai ale ta bena pisiye yaase ba gaam di la a nya ale ba jam ka nidoaba tusa kobsita (300,000) a gomsi magsi tugurik tuima, a baga a yik gbaluk ale kpaliŋ ŋanchɔgsinta. 6Wa jam mi a yaali ka tugurik tɔŋdɔba tusa kook (100,000) a nyini Izirali a tuni ba ale kpana boorik dobrim kook.
7Alege Wen nuru ale jan jam wa jigi ayen, <<Naaba, tugurik tommu de ale nyini Izirali la ku a fɛ ate ba kan gok santiri a va fu, diila Naawen an bo ale Izirali demma, wa an bo ale Ɛfraim nuruma wanyi mɛ la. 8Ase fi dan poom cheŋ a kpaliŋ ale fi nyiŋbiiri meena kpaliŋka po, Wen ale pai fu a te dachiaka diila, ka Wen ale ta pagrim a maari yaase wa basi ate ba nak yik fu.
9Amaziya yaa jam bek Wen nuruwa ayen, <<Alege kpana boorik dobrim kooku ate m tuni te Izirali tugurik tommu la?>> Ate Wen nuruwa a tulisi ayen, <<Naawen a baga a te fu ligra a gaam dila kama.>>
10Dila nyiŋ Amaziya yaa basi ate tugurik tommu baai ale nyini Ɛfraim a jam wa jigi la a kuli. Ba sue ale jam a puuri ale Juda demma, a kuli yeri ale suipuurum kpiem.
11Amaziya yaa jam pii nyiŋ a dɛ niŋ a ta wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma, a siŋ Yesa Viaka po. Dula wa jam ko ka Seir nidoaba tusa pi (10,000). 12Juda tugurik tɔŋdɔma mɛ a jam nak yik ka nidoaba tusa pi (10,000) vuta, a ta ba jueli piuŋ zuk a yuk ba basi ate ba lo ŋɔriŋ.
13Alege tugurik tommu ate Amaziya a jam basi ate ba ŋmani an basi ate ba maa nye kpaliŋka la a jam kaasi Juda tɛŋsaŋa kama a nyini Samaria a ga paari Bet Yoron. Ba jam ko ka nuruba tusa ŋata (3,000) ale ji ŋanta yega a ta cheŋ.
14Ase Amaziya ale jam tɔgri Edom demma ale ŋman jam la, wa jam ta ka Seir nuruma wena a jam. Wa jam feri ŋa a zaani kama ase wadek wena la, a koori a zuli ŋa ale a ju kaabka a te ŋa. 15Naawen sui yaa jam a puuri ale Amaziya, ate wa tom biisiteerɔ wa jigi, waai ale jam weeni wa ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi a cheŋ nuruma de wenaŋa jigi yaa, ŋaai ale kan bag a vari ŋadek nuruma fi nisa po a basi la?>>
16Ase wa le diem boro a biisi la, naawa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Tama a lueri ka fi ayen fi a sak naawa? Basi kan daa di fi le kpi.>> Dila biisiteerɔwa yaa basi alege weeni ayen, <<Mi seba ayen Wen a gomsi wa kaasi fi kama, dii nyiŋla fi nye kude kama ale an wom m sinsaŋŋa.>>
17Juda naawa Amaziya ale ga wom nyini wa sagrɔma jigi la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, wa yaa tom weeni Jeyoayaz nidoabinni Joas, ate wa kokpieŋ a nye Jeyu Izirali naawa la ayen, <<Jam ate ti nina a tu chaab.>>
18Alege Izirali naawa Joas a jam tulisi Juda naawa Amaziya ayen, <<Muŋ ale bo Lebanon a te tomtomiŋ Lebanon nyunyoŋ ayen, <Pai fi liewa ate m nidoabinni a faari wa.> Ate Lebanon gɔi duŋ yaa jam tabi muŋka a kaasi. 19Fi weeni fidek ayen mi nya pagrim Edom zuk, ate fi yaa ta kanjanta fi suinum po. Alege yɔgyɔgla de kali yeri. Ka boa ale soa ate fi a bek daanika a te fidek ale Juda mɛ?>>
20Alege Amaziya an jam wom ya, diila ka Wen ale jam nye dila ayen wa pai wa a nyo Joas nisa po, dii nyiŋla ba jam cheŋ ka Edom wenaŋa jigi. 21Dila Izirali naawa Joas yaa siti. Wa ale Juda naawa Amaziya yaa ta chaab Bet Sɛmes ale bo Juda po la. 22Izirali a jam nak yiak Juda kama ate nuru meena a chali kuli wa yeri. 23Izirali naawa Joas a jam nak yik Juda naawa Amaziya ate wa kowa a chim Joas, ate wa kokpieŋka a chim Ayaziya la kama Bet Sɛmes po. Ate wa ta wa jam Jerusalem a ga nak Jerusalem parika a lɔnsi a nyini Ɛfraim Nansuiŋku a ga paari Gugoruk Nansuiŋku. Kauk kuui magsika ale paari anamagib kobsinaaniŋ la. 24Wa jam pai ligmɔniŋka ale kpanaŋa ale ŋantomtaŋa ale jam bo Wen yenni po la kama, baai ale jam bo Obed Edom nisa po la, a gum chaab ale naab yeri ligraŋa ale ligrɔma a ta ŋman cheŋ Samaria.
25Joas nidoabinni Amaziya a jam goa ka bena pi ale ŋanu Jeyoayaz nidoabinni Izirali naawa Joas kummu ŋaaŋnyiŋ. 26Dan ka Amaziya naamu wayoŋ tintila, a nyini piilimka a ga paari kpeglimka, ŋa ŋmarisi doa Juda ale Izirali nalima gbaŋka po kama. 27A nyini diipo ate Amaziya a basi Naawen vaka la, ba jam zɔk kama a ta chaab ale wa Jerusalem po ate wa chali ga bo Lachis po, alege ba diem jam tom nidoaba ate ba saŋ va wa cheŋ Lachis a ko wa dula. 28Ba jam ta wa a ŋman jam ale ka wusum a gu wa a gum wa koma po Juda Tɛŋ nummu po.

english_text:
King Uzziah of Judah
(2 Kings 14.21,22; 15.1-7)
1-3After the death of King Amaziah, the people of Judah crowned his son Uzziah king, even though he was only 16 at the time. Uzziah ruled 52 years from Jerusalem, the hometown of his mother Jecoliah. During his rule, he recaptured and rebuilt the town of Elath.
4He obeyed the Lord by doing right, as his father Amaziah had done. 5Zechariah was Uzziah's advisor and taught him to obey God. And so, as long as Zechariah was alive, Uzziah was faithful to God, and God made him successful.
6While Uzziah was king, he started a war against the Philistines. He smashed the walls of the cities of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod, then rebuilt towns around Ashdod and in other parts of Philistia. 7God helped him defeat the Philistines, the Arabs living in Gur-Baal, and the Meunites. 8Even the Ammonites paid taxes to Uzziah. He became very powerful, and people who lived as far away as Egypt heard about him.
9In Jerusalem, Uzziah built fortified towers at the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate, and the place where the city wall turned inward. 10He also built defense towers out in the desert.
He owned such a large herd of livestock in the western foothills and in the flatlands, that he had cisterns dug there to catch the rainwater. He loved farming, so he had crops and vineyards planted in the hill country wherever there was fertile soil, and he hired farmers to take care of them.
11Uzziah's army was always ready for battle. Jeiel and Maaseiah were the officers who kept track of the number of soldiers, and these two men were under the command of Hananiah, one of Uzziah's officials. 12-13There were 307,500 trained soldiers, all under the command of 2,600 clan leaders. These powerful troops protected the king against any enemy. 14Uzziah supplied his army with shields, spears, helmets, armor, bows, and stones used for slinging. 15Some of his skilled workers invented machines that could shoot arrows and sling large stones. Uzziah set these up in Jerusalem at his defense towers and at the corners of the city wall.
God helped Uzziah become more and more powerful, and he was famous all over the world.
Uzziah Becomes Too Proud
16Uzziah became proud of his power, and this led to his downfall.
One day, Uzziah disobeyed the Lord his God by going into the temple and burning incense as an offering to him. 17Azariah the priest and 80 other brave priests followed Uzziah into the temple 18 and said, “Your Majesty, this isn't right! You are not allowed to burn incense to the Lord. That must be done only by priests who are descendants of Aaron. You will have to leave! You have sinned against the Lord, and so he will no longer bless you.”
19Uzziah, who was standing next to the incense altar at the time, was holding the incense burner, ready to offer incense to the Lord. He became very angry when he heard Azariah's warning, and leprosy suddenly appeared on his forehead! 20Azariah and the other priests saw it and immediately told him to leave the temple. Uzziah realized that the Lord had punished him, so he hurried to get outside.
21Uzziah had leprosy the rest of his life. He was no longer allowed in the temple or in his own palace. That's why his son Jotham lived there and ruled in his place.
22Everything else Uzziah did while he was king is in the records written by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz. 23 Since Uzziah had leprosy, he could not be buried in the royal tombs. Instead, he was buried in a nearby cemetery that the kings owned. His son Jotham then became king.
translation_text:
1Juda nuruma meena yaa yik Yuzaya, waai ale jam ta bena pi ale ŋayuebi la a bobi wa naab wa kowa Amaziya naŋkula po. 2Wa ale jam pilim sɛ Elat a pai ka a te Juda, Amaziya ale jam vuusi a gum wa koma po la ŋaaŋnyiŋ.
3Yuzaya a jam ta ka bena pi ale ŋayuebi ale chim naab, a dɛ naamu Jerusalem po bena pisinu ale ŋaye. Wa mawa yuei jam le Jekolia, wa jam nyini ka Jerusalem. 4Wa jam nye ka dii ale nala Naawen nina po ase wa kowa Amaziya ale jam a nye diila. 5Wa jam gisi Wen kama Zakaria daaŋa po, waai ale jam sak wa Wen yɔgsum chalika la. Ase wa le gisi Naawen a beni diila, Wen a te wa ka nyeboka.
6Wa yaa jam ga nye kpaliŋ ale Filistia demma a wɛ Gat ale Jabne ale Asdod parisaŋa. Wa jam pilim sɛ ka tɛŋsa a moata Asdod ale kab yoŋta Filistia tɛŋka po. 7Wen a jam maari wa kama a tu chaab ale Filistia demma ale Arab demma, baai ale jam bo Gur Baal la ale Meuni demma. 8Ammon demma a jam tuni ka ligra a te Yuzaya, ate wa yuenni a yiti paari Ejipiti tɛŋ banni, dii nyiŋla wa jam ŋmasi pagra kama.
9Yuzaya a jam sɛ ka kiaga Jerusalem parika zuk Gugoruk Nansuiŋku geŋsa ale Viaka Nansuiŋku geŋsa ale parika kpeglimka geŋsa a nye ate si pagra. 10Wa jam maa sɛ ka kiaga gɔnni po ale tu vili boari, dii nyiŋla wa jam ta ka duŋ boari guutaŋa zuima ale peelimmu ale doa nna jalɔ la po. Wa jam ta ka nuruba ate ba a tom wa tattaŋa ale wa kaduksaŋa po guutaŋa zuima ale tɛŋ sii ale poak la po, diila wa jam a yaali ka tɛŋka.
11Yuzaya a jam ta ka tugurik tɔŋdɔ baai ate ba sak ba a paari, a gomsi ba nyini beŋsa a ta va ba ale soa diila ase teeridɔwa Jeiel ale Maaseiya kpagni ate Yanania a jaa sak wa la, wa jam ka naab yeri kpaŋŋa dinyi. 12Dɔkdemma niŋdeerɔma nɔi ale jam ka dii a nya tugurik tɔŋdɔma zuk la jam ka nidoaba tusa ŋaye ale kobsiyuebi (2,600). 13Ba ale jam a nya tugurik tɔŋdɔ baai zuk la jam ka nidoaba tusa kobsita ale ŋayopɔi ale kobsinu (307,500), baai ale jam kpaliŋ ale pagrim kpiem a maari naawa a tu chaab ale dachiaka. 14Yuzaya a jam yaali kpaliŋ ŋanchɔgsinta ale gbatta ale zukchina ale kpaliŋ gatta ale tima ale visiŋ tana a te tugurik tommu meena. 15Jerusalem po wa basi ate ka gobrɔba a nye ŋanta ate ba bo kiaŋa zuima ale gugottaŋa po a kpaliŋ a kasi, a tɔŋ piema ale a yuk tintain kpiema. Wa yuenni a jam yiti kama a cheŋ ti ku yalima, diila wa jam nya ka maarika nna yega a chim pagrɔ.
16Alege Yuzaya ale ga pagra la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, wa kanjantaŋa yaa ta wa lueta jam. Wa jam ka wensie ale Naawen wa Wenni, a jo Naawen yenni po ayen wa ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la ŋan baai nyum ale masa la kuŋkuŋku zuk. 17Kaabteerɔwa Azariya ale Naawen kaabteerɔ tuasa ba chaab pinaanuŋ ale nye zu kooŋ a va wa jo. 18Ba jam weeni wa kama ayen, <<Yuzaya fi ka suik a ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa a te Naawen ya. Kaabteerɔma ale soa dula, Aaron ŋaaŋbisaŋa, baai ate Wen a gomsi ba a magsi ba ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa. Nyini Wen dɔkku po ale fi ka wensie. Naawen fi Wenni a kan zuli fu.>>
19Yuzaya waai ale jam ta juka jaamu wa nisa po a gomsi wa ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la sui yaa jam puuri. Ase wa le jam a na kaabteerɔma ale jam za ŋan baai nyum ale masa la kuŋkuŋku niŋ Naawen yenni po la, gama tuem yaa piilim wa dinni. 20Ase kaabteerɔ kpioŋku Azariya ale kaabteerɔ mbala meena ale zak nya wa la, ba jam nya kama ale gama tuem ale bo wa dinni, dila kpabi a ta wa nyini peelim. Wadek a jam a yeenti wa nyini kama, diila Naawen a te ti ku jo ka wa nyiŋ.
21Naab Yuzaya jam ka gami a ga paari dai dii ate wa kpi la. Wa jam bo ka yeri po wadek wa nyiini ase gami la a kan jo Naawen yenni po. Wa nidoabinni Jotam ale jam a nya naab yenni zuk ale a nya nuruma zuk tɛŋka po.
22Yuzaya naamu wayoŋ tintila a nyini piilimka a ga paari kpeglimka, Amoz nidoabinni biisiteerɔwa Azaya a jam ŋmarisi dueni kama. 23Yuzaya a jam vuusi kama a gum wa koma po, ate ba gu wa a moata ba talim buui ate ba gu nalima du la, nuruma a jam weeni kama ayen, <<Wa ta ka gama tuem. Ate wa nidoabinni Jotam a zaani wa nankula po ase naab la.

english_text:
King Jotham of Judah
(2 Kings 15.32-38)
1Jotham was 25 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 16 years. Jerushah his mother was the daughter of Zadok.
2Jotham obeyed the Lord and did right. He followed the example of his father Uzziah, except he never burned incense in the temple as his father had done. But the people of Judah kept sinning against the Lord.
3Jotham rebuilt the Upper Gate of the temple and did a lot of work to repair the wall near Mount Ophel. 4He built towns in the mountains of Judah and built fortresses and defense towers in the forests.
5During his rule he attacked and defeated the Ammonites. Then every year for the next three years, he forced them to pay 3.4 tons of silver, 1,000 tons of wheat, and 1,000 tons of barley.
6Jotham remained faithful to the Lord his God and became a very powerful king.
7Everything else Jotham did while he was king, including the wars he fought, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel and Judah. 8After he had ruled Judah 16 years, he died at the age of 41. 9He was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
translation_text:
1Jotam jam ta ka bena pisiye ale ŋanu ale chim naab, a dɛ naamu Jerusalem po bena pi ale ŋayuebi. Wa mawa yuei jam le Jerusa wa jam ka Zadok lie. 2Wa jam nye ka dii ale nala Naawen nina po, ase dii dek ate wa kowa Yuzaya jam nye la, alege wa an nye ase wa kowa la a jo Naawen yenni po. Nuruma a diem jam gum du nye a kaasi kama. 3Jotam a ŋman pilim sɛ Ŋmai Nansuiŋku ale bo Naawen yenni geŋsa la ale tom tuima yega parika ale bo Ofel guuku zuk la. 4Wa jam sɛ ka tɛŋ kpieŋsa Juda guutaŋa zuima ale diina ale kiaga daataŋa jigini.
5Jotam a jam nye ka kpaliŋ ale Ammon naawa a nak yik ba. Ben dila Ammon demma a jam tuni ka kpana boorik dobrim kook a te wa ale muma busisa tusa pi (10,000) ale za busisa tusa pi (10,000). Ammon demma a jam ta ka dila dek dek a jam te wa bena ŋayewa ale ŋatawa po.
6Jotam a jam ŋmasi pagra kama dii nyiŋla wa jam va Naawen wa Wenni kama nalimnyiini.
7Jotam naamu wayoŋ tintila, gum chaab ale wa kpaliŋsaŋa meena ale wayoŋtaŋa ate wa nye la, a ŋmarisi doa Izirali ale Juda nalima gbaŋka po kama. 8Wa jam ta ka bena pisiye ale ŋanu ale chim naab, a dɛ naamu Jerusalem po bena pi ale ŋayuebi. 9Jotam a jam vuusi kama a gum wa koma po ate ba gu wa Deevid Tɛŋka po. Ka wa nidoabinni Ayazi ale jam zaani wa nankula po ase naab la.

english_text:
King Ahaz of Judah
(2 Kings 16.1-4)
1Ahaz was 20 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 16 years.
Ahaz was nothing like his ancestor David. Ahaz disobeyed the Lord 2and was as sinful as the kings of Israel. He made idols of the god Baal, 3and he offered sacrifices in Hinnom Valley. Worst of all, Ahaz sacrificed his own sons, which was a disgusting custom of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel. 4Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
Syria and Israel Attack Judah
(2 Kings 16.5,6)
5-6 Ahaz and the people of Judah sinned and turned away from the Lord, the God their ancestors had worshiped. So the Lord punished them by letting their enemies defeat them.
The king of Syria attacked Judah and took many of its people to Damascus as prisoners. King Pekah of Israel later defeated Judah and killed 120,000 of its bravest soldiers in one day. 7During that battle, an Israelite soldier named Zichri killed three men from Judah: Maaseiah the king's son; Azrikam, the official in charge of the palace; and Elkanah, the king's second in command. 8The Israelite troops captured 200,000 women and children and took them back to their capital city of Samaria, along with a large amount of their possessions. They did these things even though the people of Judah were their own relatives.
Oded the Prophet Condemns Israel
9Oded lived in Samaria and was one of the Lord's prophets. He met Israel's army on their way back from Judah and said to them:
The Lord God of your ancestors let you defeat Judah's army only because he was angry with them. But you should not have been so cruel! 10If you make slaves of the people of Judah and Jerusalem, you will be as guilty as they are of sinning against the Lord.
11Send these prisoners back home—they are your own relatives. If you don't, the Lord will punish you in his anger.
12About the same time, four of Israel's leaders arrived. They were Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai. They agreed with Oded that the Israelite troops were wrong, 13and they said:
If you bring these prisoners into Samaria, that will be one more thing we've done to sin against the Lord. And he is already angry enough with us.
14So in front of the leaders and the crowd, the troops handed over their prisoners and the property they had taken from Judah. 15The four leaders took some of the stolen clothes and gave them to the prisoners who needed something to wear. They later gave them all a new change of clothes and shoes, then fixed them something to eat and drink, and cleaned their wounds with olive oil. They gave donkeys to those who were too weak to walk, and led all of them back to Jericho, the city known for its palm trees. The leaders then returned to Samaria.
Ahaz Asks the King of Assyria for Help
(2 Kings 16.7-9)
16-18Some time later, the Edomites attacked the eastern part of Judah again and carried away prisoners. And at the same time, the Philistines raided towns in the western foothills and in the Southern Desert. They conquered the towns of Beth-Shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco, Timnah, and Gimzo, including the villages around them. Then some of the Philistines went to live in these places.
Ahaz sent a message to King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria and begged for help. 19But God was punishing Judah with these disasters, because Ahaz had disobeyed him and refused to stop Judah from sinning. 20So Tiglath Pileser came to Judah, but instead of helping, he made things worse. 21Ahaz gave him gifts from the Lord's temple and the king's palace, as well as from the homes of Israel's other leaders. The Assyrian king still refused to help Ahaz.
The Final Sin of Ahaz and His Death
22Even after all these terrible things happened to Ahaz, he sinned against the Lord even worse than before. 23He said to himself, “The Syrian gods must have helped their kings defeat me. Maybe if I offer sacrifices to those gods, they will help me.” That was the sin that finally led to the downfall of Ahaz, as well as to the destruction of Judah.
24Ahaz collected all the furnishings of the temple and smashed them to pieces. Then he locked the doors to the temple and set up altars to foreign gods on every street corner in Jerusalem. 25In every city and town in Judah he built local shrines to worship foreign gods. All of this made the Lord God of his ancestors very angry.
26Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel. 27 Ahaz died and was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs. His son Hezekiah then became king.
translation_text:
1Ayazi jam ta ka bena pisiye ale chim naab, a dɛ naamu Jerusalem po bena pi ale ŋayuebi. Wa an jam a nye ase wa kowa Deevid la, wa jam nye ka dii ale kan nala Naawen nina po. 2Wa jam a nye ka Izirali nalimaŋa nyeelaŋa ale maa nye kuta bɔgta a magsi Baal kaabka. 3Wa jam nye ka juka kaabka Ben Yinnom Viaka po ale pai wa nidoabilisa a nye kaabka bolim po, a va kisita wie ate tɛŋ kpieŋsa jam a nye ate Naawen a yiak si a basi a te Izirali demma la. 4Wa jam nye ka kaabka ale ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la pimpitima ale guuta zuima ale ti sii ale teeri la kie.
5Dila nyiŋ Naawen wa Wenni yaa pai wa a nyo Araam naawa nisa po. Araam demma a jam nak yik wa kama ale ta wa nuruma yega a cheŋ ase ligrɔba la Damasikus po. Wa jam maa jo Izirali naawa nisa po kama waai ale jam te ku jo wa nyiŋ ale mula. 6Dai yeŋ po Aremaliya nidoabinni a jam ko ka tugurik tɔŋdɔba tusa kook ale pisiye (120,000) Juda po, dii nyiŋla Juda a jam zɛri Naawen, ba koma Wenni kama. 7Ɛfraim tɛŋka kpaliŋ nyeerɔwa Zikri a jam ko naawa nidoabinni Maaseiya kama ale Azrikam kpagni ale jam a nya naab yeri zuk la ale Elkana, waai ale paasaŋ naawa la kama. 8Izirali demma a jam yik ka badek mabisa pooba ale nidoabilisa ale lieba tusa kobsiye (200,000) a ta cheŋ ase ligrɔba la. Ba jam maa ta ka ŋan baai ale ta dobrim la a cheŋ Samaria.
9Alege Naawen biisiteerɔwa yuei ale Oded a jam bo dula, a yaa jam nyini peelim wa tu tugurik tommu ale ŋman jam Samaria la. Wa jam weeni ba kama ayen, <<Naawen, ni koma Wenni sue ale a puuri ale Juda la nyiŋ, ate wa pai ba a nyo ni nisa po. Alege ni pai ka suipuurum a tɔgri ba ate dila a paari wenŋmazuk. 10Yɔgyɔgla de nama a poli kama ayen ni nye Juda ale Jerusalem demma ni yɔm. Alege nama a kan poli mɛ ase ni a nye ka biem a kaasi Naawen ni Wenni la? 11Yɔgyɔgla de ni wom mi, ni basi ate ni tɛŋ dem chaama ate ni yik ase yɔm la a ŋmani, ale Naawen suipuurum kpiemu a cheen ni zuk.>>
12Ate Ɛfraim niŋdeerɔma gela, Jeyoyanan nidoabinni Azariya ale Mesillemot nidoabinni Berekiya ale Sallum nidoabinni Jeyizkia ale Yadlai nidoabinni Amasa yaa weeni baai ale nyini kpaliŋka po a cheen la. 13Ba jam weeni ba kama ayen, <<Ni kan ta ligrɔma a jam dela, ti le nye foolaa Naawen niŋ, nama a yaali ni yaali ka wari a gum ti biemu ale ti foolaawa po? Ti foolaawa a poom zuak kama, ate wa suipuurum kpiemu a jam Izirali zuk.>>
14Dila tugurik tɔŋdɔma yaa pai ligrɔma ale ŋan baai ba pai la a zaani kpaŋŋa niŋ a te tigsuŋku. 15Nidoa baai ate ba ŋmarisi ba yueŋa la yaa ta ligrɔma a lueri gatta a ta nyini ŋantaŋa po a jo baai meena ale ta chaboala la. Ba jam te ba ka gatta ale nuensa ale ŋandiinta ale daam ale tebika tiim. Baai meena ale jam gbaalima la ba jam pai ba ale ka bonsa. Dila ba yaa jam ta ba a ŋmani cheŋ ba tɛŋ demma jigi Jeriko po, kpinkpatta tɛŋka, ale ŋmani cheŋ Samaria.
16Dila po naab Ayazi a jam tom yaali ka maarika a nyini Assiria naawa jigi. 17Edom demma a ŋman pilim jam nye ka kpaliŋ ale Juda demma ligrɔba a cheŋ, 18alege ate Filistia demma a jam vari tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa ale bo guutaŋa zuima ale Juda yeseoku gensa la. Ba jam kali likka Bet Sɛmes ale Aijalon ale Gederot ale Soko ale Timnaya ale Gimzo ale si tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa ale gilim si la. 19Naawen a ta Juda siŋ ka tɛŋ Izirali naawa Ayazi niŋ, diila wa jam basi ate ka gaasa a piisi Juda po ale chim waai ale kan ta wensie ale Naawen la. 20Assiria naawa Tilgat Pilneser yaa jam wa jigi alege wa te wa ka daanika ku le magsi wa maari wa la. 21Ayazi yaa jam pai ŋantaŋa gela a nyini Naawen yenni ale naab yenni po ale nabisaŋa jigi a pai ŋa a te Assiria naawa alege dila an maari wa.
22Va ŋaai ate wa jam bo daanika po la a ŋmasi nye a gum du kama a ka wensie ale Naawen ya. 23Wa jam nye ka kaabka a te Damasikus wenaŋa, ŋaai ale jam nya pagrim wa zuk, wa jam poli kama ayen, <<Ase Araam naawa wenaŋa ale jam maari ba la, m le nye kaabka a te ŋa ate ŋa maari mu.>> Alege ka ŋala ale jam ta wa ale Izirali meena lueta a jam.
24Ayazi yaa jam tigsi ŋantaŋa Wen yenni po a ta cheŋ. Wa jam lik Naawen yenni tuataŋa kama ale sɛ kuŋkuŋta suiduok meena gugoruk po Jerusalem po. 25Juda tɛŋ meena po wa jam sɛ ka pimpitima a ju kaabka a te wen yona a nye ate Naawen, wa koma Wenni sui a puuri.
26Wa naamu wayoŋ tintila ale wa nyeelaŋa meena, a nyini piilimka a ga paari kpeglimka a ŋmarisi doa Juda ale Izirali nalima gbaŋka po kama. 27Ayazi a jam vuusi kama a gum wa koma po ate ba gu wa Jerusalem tɛŋ kpieŋka po, alege ba an jam gu wa Izirali nalima boositaŋa po. Ka Azekaya wa nidoabinni ale jam zaani wa nankula po ase naaba la.

english_text:
King Hezekiah of Judah
(2 Kings 18.1-3)
1Hezekiah was 25 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled 29 years from Jerusalem. His mother was Abijah daughter of Zechariah. 2Hezekiah obeyed the Lord by doing right, just as his ancestor David had done.
The Temple Is Purified
3In the first month of the first year of Hezekiah's rule, he unlocked the doors to the Lord's temple and had them repaired. 4Then he called the priests and Levites to the east courtyard of the temple 5and said:
It's time to purify the temple of the Lord God of our ancestors. You Levites must first go through the ceremony to make yourselves clean, then go into the temple and bring out everything that is unclean and unacceptable to the Lord. 6Some of our ancestors were unfaithful and disobeyed the Lord our God. Not only did they turn their backs on the Lord, but they also completely ignored his temple. 7They locked the doors, then let the lamps go out and stopped burning incense and offering sacrifices to him. 8The Lord became terribly angry with the people of Judah and Jerusalem, and everyone was shocked and horrified at what he did to punish them. Not only were 9our ancestors killed in battle, but our own children and wives were taken captive.
10So I have decided to renew our agreement with the Lord God of Israel. Maybe then he will stop being so angry with us. 11Let's not waste any time, my friends. You are the ones who were chosen to be the Lord's priests and to offer him sacrifices.
12-14When Hezekiah finished talking, the following Levite leaders went to work:
Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah from the Kohath clan; Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel from the Merari clan; Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah from the Gershon clan; Shimri and Jeuel from the Elizaphan clan; Zechariah and Mattaniah from the Asaph clan; Jehuel and Shimei from the Heman clan; Shemaiah and Uzziel from the Jeduthun clan.
15These leaders gathered together the rest of the Levites, and they all went through the ceremony to make themselves clean. Then they began to purify the temple according to the Law of the Lord, just as Hezekiah had commanded.
16The priests went into the temple and carried out everything that was unclean. They put these things in the courtyard, and from there, the Levites carried them outside the city to Kidron Valley.
17The priests and Levites began their work on the first day of the first month. It took them one week to purify the courtyards of the temple and another week to purify the temple. So on the sixteenth day of that same month 18they went back to Hezekiah and said:
Your Majesty, we have finished our work. The entire temple is now pure again, and so is the altar and its utensils, as well as the table for the sacred loaves of bread and its utensils. 19And we have brought back all the things that King Ahaz took from the temple during the time he was unfaithful to God. We purified them and put them back in front of the altar.
Worship in the Temple
20At once, Hezekiah called together the officials of Jerusalem, and they went to the temple. 21They brought with them seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven goats as sacrifices to take away the sins of Hezekiah's family and of the people of Judah, as well as to purify the temple. Hezekiah told the priests, who were descendants of Aaron, to sacrifice these animals on the altar.
22The priests killed the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, then splattered the blood on the altar. 23They took the goats to Hezekiah and the worshipers, and they laid their hands on the animals. 24The priests then killed the goats and splattered the blood on the altar as a sacrifice to take away the sins of everyone in Israel, because Hezekiah had commanded that these sacrifices be made for all the people of Israel.
25Next, Hezekiah assigned the Levites to their places in the temple. He gave them cymbals, harps, and other stringed instruments, according to the instructions that the Lord had given King David and the two prophets, Gad and Nathan. 26 The Levites were ready to play the instruments that had belonged to David; the priests were ready to blow the trumpets.
27As soon as Hezekiah gave the signal for the sacrifices to be burned on the altar, the musicians began singing praises to the Lord and playing their instruments, 28and everyone worshiped the Lord. This continued until the last animal was sacrificed.
29After that, Hezekiah and the crowd of worshipers bowed down and worshiped the Lord. 30Then Hezekiah and his officials ordered the Levites to sing the songs of praise that David and Asaph the prophet had written. And so they bowed down and joyfully sang praises to the Lord.
31Hezekiah said to the crowd, “Now that you are once again acceptable to the Lord, bring sacrifices and offerings to give him thanks.”
The people did this, and some of them voluntarily brought animals to be offered as sacrifices. 32Seventy bulls, 100 rams, and 200 lambs were brought as sacrifices to please the Lord; 33600 bulls and 3,000 sheep were brought as sacrifices to ask the Lord's blessing. 34There were not enough priests to skin all these animals, because many of the priests had not taken the time to go through the ceremony to make themselves clean. However, since all the Levites had made themselves clean, they helped the priests until the last animal was skinned. 35Besides all the sacrifices that were burned on the altar, the fat from the other animal sacrifices was burned, and the offerings of wine were poured over the altar.
So the temple was once again used for worshiping the Lord. 36Hezekiah and the people of Judah celebrated, because God had helped them make this happen so quickly.
translation_text:
1Azekaya jam ta ka bena pisiye ale ŋanu ale chim naab, a dɛ naamu Jerusalem po bena pisiye ale neok. Wa mawa yuei jam le Abaija, wa jam ka Zakaria lie. 2Wa jam nye ka dii ale nala Naawen nina po ase wa kowa Deevid ale jam ka diila.
3Benni piilimka po chiik kaai ale piilim ate wa dɛ naam la, wa yaa lak Naawen yenni tuataŋa a gomsi ti a magsi. 4Wa yaa jam ta kaabteerɔma ale Livaima a jam tigsi ba peelimmu po kori geŋsa 5ayen, <<Ni wom mi Livaiba; ni gomsi gaari nidek abe ni gaari Naawen ni koma Wenni yenni. Ni yeeri ŋan baai meena ale taŋ la a ta nyini Jigi Dii Ale Ta Tuilum La po. 6Ti koma a jam ka wensie, ba jam nye ka biem Naawen ti Wenni nina po ale zɛri wa. Ba jam tulim ba nina kama a ta nyini Naawen boka jigini ale tulim ba ŋaaŋsa a te wa. 7Ba jam lik pɔsutaŋa tuataŋa kama mɛ ale kpimsi zeuŋtaŋa. Ba an jam ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa yaase ba nye juka tiirita Jigi Dii Ale Ta Tuilum La a te Izirali Wenni. 8Dila nyiŋ Naawen suipuurumu yaa lo Juda ale Jerusalem zuk, wa yaa basi ate ba yɔgsa nna yega ale cha ba ale ŋan laanta ase ni le nya ale nidek nina la. 9Kude nyiŋ ate tama koma a kpi ale gebik ate ti nidoabilisaŋa ale ti liema ale ti pooma a bo yɔntidi po la.
10<<Yɔgyɔgla de mi a yaali ayen m nye ka nɔiyeŋ ale Naawen dii ale ka Izirali Wenni la, ate dila ale nye ate wa basi wa suipuurum kpiemu. 11M nidoabilisaa, ni kan chim baai niŋ ale kan bo wari po yɔgyɔgla de, ale Naawen a lueri ka nama ayen ni zaani wa niŋ a tom a te wa, a tom wa niŋ abe ni a ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la.>>
12Livaima de ale jam ba tom tuini la. A nyini Koyat yezukku jam ka Amasai nidoabinni Mayat ale Azariya nidoabinni Joel. A nyini Merari yezukku jam ka Abdi nidoabinni Kis ale Jeyallelel nidoabinni Azariya. A nyini Gerson yezukku jam ka Zimmaya nidoabinni Joa ale Joa nidoabinni Eden. 13A nyini Elizafan ŋaaŋbisaŋa po, jam ka Simri ale Jeiel. A nyini Asaf ŋaaŋbisaŋa po, jam ka Zakaria ale Mattania. 14A nyini Yeman ŋaaŋbisaŋa po, jam ka Jeyiel ale Simei. A nyini Jedutun ŋaaŋbisaŋa po, jam ka Sɛmaiya ale Uzziel.
15Ase ba le jam tigsi ba suataŋa ale gomsi badek a magsi la, ba yaa jam jo a nye ate Naawen yenni a welema ase naawa ale jam weeni dii a ta va Naawen wanni la. 16Kaabteerɔma yaa jo Naawen yenni po ayen ba nye ate di welema. Ba jam ta jaab meena ale kan welema a bo Naawen yenni po la a nyini ka peelim Livaima a jam ji ba kama a ta ga basi Kidron Viaka po. 17Ba jam piilim tuilum tuini chiik kaai ale dɛ niŋ la piilimka danni, ate chiika daa naanika danni, ba jo Naawen pɔsuku po. Ba yaa gaari Naawen yenni daa naaniŋ po, a nueri chiika daa pi ale ŋayuebi dai.
18Ba yaa jam jo Naab Azekaya jigi a weeni wa ayen, <<Ti nye ate Naawen yenni meena a nala kama. Kuŋkuŋku ale magsi juka tiirim la ale ku ŋantomtaŋa meena ale jazaanimu ate tuilum boroboroku a dueni du la ale ku ŋantomtaŋa. 19Ti gomsi ale nye ate ŋan baai meena ate Naab Ayazi an jam yeeri ale wensie diipo ate wa chim naab la ate ba welema. Ba yaa bo ka Naawen kuŋkuŋku niŋ yɔgyɔgla de.>>
20Dai dii ale paasaŋ la saluik yokyokwa Naab Azekaya yaa tigsi tɛŋka kpaŋŋa jigi yeŋ a yaa jueli Naawen yenni po. 21Ba jam ta ka lalisa siyopɔi ale padaasa siyopɔi ale padabilisa siyopɔi ale budukta tiyopɔi a jam ase biem tiirim la a magsi naamu ale Wen yenni ale Juda. Naawa jam weeni kaabteerɔma Aaron ŋaaŋbisaŋa kama ayen ba kaab ŋantaŋa de Naawen kuŋkuŋku zuk. 22Dila ba yaa tɔgri lalisaŋa ate kaabteerɔma a pai ziimu a misi kuŋkuŋku zuk, ba tɔgri padaasaŋa a misi si ziimu kuŋkuŋku zuk, a tɔgri pabisaŋa mɛ a misi si ziimu kuŋkuŋku zuk. 23Booŋa ale magsi biem tiirimu la ba jam ta ŋa a jam ka naawa ale tigsuŋku niŋ a te ba vi nisa ŋa zuk. 24Kaabteerɔwa yaa tɔgri booŋa a pai ŋa ziimu a zaani kuŋkuŋku zuk ase biem tiirim la a nye biem duisi basika a te Izirali meena, diila naawa ale weeni ayen ba nye juka tiirim ale biem tiirimu a te Izirali meena.
25Wa jam pai Livaima a zaani ka Naawen yenni po ale baganiŋsa ale dunduirisa ale kpanta ase dii ate Deevid ale naawa sagrɔwa Gad ale biisiteerɔwa Natan a jam magsi sak ba la, kude ka Naawen ale jam ta va wa biisiteerɔma zuk a biisi. 26Dila Livaima yaa jam za ale Deevid ale ba ŋannagintaŋa ale kaabteerɔma ale ba damunsaŋa.
27Azekaya a jam weeni kama ate ba nye juka kaabka kuŋkuŋku zuk. Ase tiirimu ale piilim la, ba yaa piilim lenni yiila a te Naawen mɛ a gum chaab ale damunsa ale Izirali naawa Deevid ŋannagintaŋa. 28Tigsuŋku meena yaa jam koori tɛŋ a seni ale ge ate yilendisaŋa a lenni ate damunsaŋa mɛ a peeri. Kude meena a jam nye kama a gum du ate ku ga paari diipo ate juka tiirim kaabka a nueri la.
29Ase ba le jam te tiiritaŋa a nueri la, naawa ale waai meena ale jam bo dula ale wa la yaa kpi duna tɛŋ a pak wa. 30Naab Azekaya ale wa kpaŋŋa a yaa weeni ate Livaima a seni Naawen ale Deevid ale Asaf biisiteerɔwa wieŋa. Ba jam lenni kama a seni ale suipeentik a pai ba zuima a su tɛŋ a pak.
31Azekaya yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni yaa pai ka nidek a nyo Naawen nisa po. Ni ta kaabka ale jiam tiirita a jam Naawen yenni po.>> Dila tigsuŋku yaa jam ta kaabka ale jiam tiirita a jam ale baai meena suiniima ale jam a yaali la yaa ta juka tiirita a jam.
32Juka tiiritaŋa nɔi ale jam ka dii ate tigsuŋku a ta jam la ka lalisa pisiyopɔi ale padaasa kook ale padabilisa kobsiye, duŋsaŋa de meena jam ka juka tiirita a te Naawen. 33Duŋsaŋa meena ale jam magsi kaabka la jam ka lalisa kobsiyuebi ale piisa ale bua tusa ŋata (3,000). 34Kaabteerɔma an jam soa dii ya a puli juka tiiritaŋa duŋsaŋa, ka ba kobisaŋa Livaima ale jam maari ba ate ba nueri tuini ate ku paari diipo ate ba lueri kaabteerɔ yonta la, diila Livaima a jam gomsi badek a magsi gaam kaabteerɔma ale jam ka diila kama. 35Juka tiiritaŋa a jam piisi kama a gum chaab ale suiyɔgni tiiritaŋa kpapalaŋa ale nyuka tiiritaŋa ale jam gum juka tiiritaŋa po la. Naawen yenni tuimaŋa a ŋman pilim jam zaani kama. 36Azekaya ale nuruma meena sue a jam peenti kama ale dii ate Wen a ta jam te wa nuruma la, dii nyiŋla ku jam nye ka nna nwuli.

english_text:
Hezekiah Prepares To Celebrate Passover
1-4 Passover wasn't celebrated in the first month, which was the usual time, because many of the priests were still unclean and unacceptable to serve, and because not everyone in Judah had come to Jerusalem for the festival. So Hezekiah, his officials, and the people agreed to celebrate Passover in the second month.
Hezekiah sent a message to everyone in Israel and Judah, including those in the territories of Ephraim and West Manasseh, inviting them to the temple in Jerusalem for the celebration of Passover in honor of the Lord God of Israel. 5Everyone from Beersheba in the south to Dan in the north was invited. This was the largest crowd of people that had ever celebrated Passover, according to the official records.
6Hezekiah's messengers went everywhere in Israel and Judah with the following letter:
People of Israel, now that you have survived the invasion of the Assyrian kings, it's time for you to turn back to the Lord God our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob worshiped. If you do this, he will stop being angry. 7Don't follow the example of your ancestors and your Israelite relatives in the north. They were unfaithful to the Lord, and he punished them horribly. 8Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. Decide now to obey the Lord our God! Come to Jerusalem and worship him in the temple that will belong to him forever. Then he will stop being angry, 9and the enemies that have captured your families will show pity and send them back home. The Lord God is kind and merciful, and if you turn back to him, he will no longer turn his back on you.
10The messengers went to every town in Ephraim and West Manasseh as far north as the territory of Zebulun, but people laughed and insulted them. 11Only a few people from the tribes of Asher, West Manasseh, and Zebulun were humble and went to Jerusalem. 12God also made everyone in Judah eager to do what Hezekiah and his officials had commanded.
Passover Is Celebrated
13In the second month, a large crowd of people gathered in Jerusalem to celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread. 14They took all the foreign altars and incense altars in Jerusalem and threw them into Kidron Valley.
15-17Then, on the fourteenth day of that same month, the Levites began killing the lambs for Passover, because many of the worshipers were unclean and were not allowed to kill their own lambs. Meanwhile, some of the priests and Levites felt ashamed because they had not gone through the ceremony to make themselves clean. They immediately went through that ceremony and went to the temple, where they offered sacrifices to please the Lord. Then the priests and Levites took their positions, according to the Law of Moses, the servant of God.
As the Levites killed the lambs, they handed some of the blood to the priests, who splattered it on the altar.
18-19Most of the people that came from Ephraim, West Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun had not made themselves clean, but they ignored God's Law and ate the Passover lambs anyway. Hezekiah found out what they had done and prayed, “Lord God, these people are unclean according to the laws of holiness. But they are worshiping you, just as their ancestors did. So, please be kind and forgive them.” 20The Lord answered Hezekiah's prayer and did not punish them.
21The worshipers in Jerusalem were very happy and celebrated the Festival for seven days. The Levites and priests sang praises to the Lord every day and played their instruments. 22Hezekiah thanked the Levites for doing such a good job, leading the celebration.
The worshipers celebrated for seven days by offering sacrifices, by eating the sacred meals, and by praising the Lord God of their ancestors. 23Everyone was so excited that they agreed to celebrate seven more days.
24So Hezekiah gave the people 1,000 bulls and 7,000 sheep to be offered as sacrifices and to be used as food for the sacred meals. His officials gave 1,000 bulls and 10,000 sheep, and many more priests agreed to go through the ceremony to make themselves clean. 25Everyone was very happy, including those from Judah and Israel, the priests and Levites, and the foreigners living in Judah and Israel. 26It was the biggest celebration in Jerusalem since the days of King Solomon, the son of David. 27The priests and Levites asked God to bless the people, and from his home in heaven, he did.
translation_text:
1Azekaya yaa jam tom wi Izirali ale Juda demma meena ale ŋmarisi gbaŋsa a te Ɛfraim ale Manasa mɛ, a wi ba ayen ba jam Naawen yenni Jerusalem po a dɛ Naawen, Izirali Wenni Gaambasika Tigini. 2Naawa ale wa kpaŋŋa ale tigsuŋku meena ale bo Jerusalem po la a jam zɔk kama ayen ba dɛ Gaambasika Tigini chiisa siyewa po. 3Ba an jam a dɛ di veruveruk dii nyiŋla kaabteerɔba an jam diem soa dii ya a gomsi badek a magsi ya, nuruma mɛ an diem jam tigsi Jerusalem po. 4Zɔŋŋa a jam nye ase ŋa nala kama a te naawa ale tigsuŋku meena la. 5Ba yaa jam zɔk a tom moolidɔ Izirali meena po a nyini Beerseba a ga paari Dan, a wi nuruma ayen ba jam Jerusalem po a dɛ Gaambasika Tigini a te Naawen, Izirali Wenni. Ba an jam dɛ di ale nuru boari nna nya ya ase dii ale ŋmarisi la.
6Naawa ale weeni la, tintomdɔ yaa cheŋ Izirali ale Juda meena po ale gbaŋsa a nyini naawa ale wa kpaŋŋa jigi ate ba kariŋ ayen, <<Izirali nuruba, ni pilim ŋmani Naawen, Abrayam Wenni ale Aizik Wenni ale Izirali Wenni jigi, ate wa ale ŋmani nama baai ate wa basi ni la jigi, baai ale chali bɛ nyini Assiria naawa nisa po la. 7Ni kan nye ase ni koma ale ni suataŋa la, baai ale jam kan ta wensie ale Naawen, ba koma Wenni la ate wa basi ate ba chim ŋan laanta la. 8Ni kan ta tukpari ase ni koma ale jam ka diila, ni nye baliyaa a te Naawen. Ni jam wa yenni po, dii ate wa nye di nna cheri taam wuu la. Ni tom te Naawen ni Wenni ate wa suipuurum kpiemu ale basi ni. 9Ni dan pilim ŋmani Naawen jigi, ni suataŋa ale ni bisaŋa ale nya jiirim a nyini ba nak yigrɔma jigi a ŋman jam tɛŋka de po, diila Naawen ni Wenni ta ka ŋmantiik ale jiirim. Wa kan viriŋ wa nina a basi nakpiaga ase nama a nin pilim ŋmani wa jigi ya.>>
10Tomtomdɔwa yaa jam cheŋ tɛŋ meena Ɛfraim ale Manasa ale Zebulun po alege nuruma a jam koosi a la ba. 11Ale ge dila meena, Asɛ ale Manasa ale Zebulun diinaŋa nidoama gela a jam yik badek kama a cheŋ Jerusalem po. 12Juda po mɛ Wen nisa a jam bo nuruma zuk kama ayen wa te ba nɔiyeŋ ale popola yena ate ba tom naawa ale wa kpaŋŋa ale weeni diila a ta va Naawen wanni.
13Nuru boari nna yegayega ale jam tigsi Jerusalem po ayen ba ŋɔbi Boroborok Kuui Ate Dabinta A Ka Ku Po La Tigini chiisa siyewa po. 14Ba jam kpiti kuŋkuŋtaŋa kama Jerusalem po ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa la kuŋkuŋtaŋa a yuk basi Kidron Viaka po.
15Ba jam tɔgri Gaambasika pabiika ka chiisa siyewa po ka daa pi ale ŋanaansiwa danni. Chivie ale jam ta kaabteerɔma ale Livaima ate ba gomsi badek nna cheri a ta juka tiirita a jam Naawen yenni po. 16Ba yaa jam tuesi ba le magsi ba nye dii ase ku le ŋmarisi dii Moosis Wen nuruwa Sinsaŋŋa po la. Kaabteerɔma ale jam a misi ziimu ate Livaima a pai nyo ba nisa po la.
17Ase nuru boanni yega ale kan jam nala la, ka Livaima ale jam a ko Gaambasika Tigini pabisaŋa a te baai meena ale kan jam nye cheri ale an baga a nye ate ba pabisaŋa a nye cheri la a te Naawen. 18Nuruma yega baai ale nyini Ɛfraim ale Manasa ale Isaka ale Zebulun la an jam nye badek cheri, ale ge ba jam dɛ Gaambasika Tigini kama ate ku an va dii ale jam ŋmarisi la. Alege Azekaya a jam puusi te ba kama ayen, <<Naawen dii ale nala la vɔŋ te waai meena. 19Waai ale pai wa suinum a gisi Wen, Naawen wa koma Wenni, ase wa nin poom kan welema a ta va Naawen yenni vuutaŋa ale ka diila.>> 20Naawen yaa wom Azekaya a tebi nuruma.
21Izirali demma baai ale jam bo Jerusalem po la a jam ŋɔbi Boroborok Kuui Ate Dabinta A Ka Ku Po La Tigini ka daa ŋayopɔi ale mariŋ kpieŋ ale ge kaabteerɔma ale Livaima a jam lenni yiila a te Naawen daa meena, ale Naawen ŋannagintaŋa a pak wa. 22Azekaya a jam biisi deŋsi Livaima meena kpa kama, baai ale jam sak miŋ chakka ale Naawen tuini la. Daa ŋayopɔiwa ba jam dɛ ka ba charuku ale nye suiyɔgni tiirita a pak Naawen ba koma Wenni.
23Tigsuŋku meena yaa siak ayen ba dɛ tigini daa ŋayopɔi a gum du. Dila daa ŋayopɔi ate ba pai dɛ ale mariŋka. 24Juda naawa Azekaya jam te ka lalisa tusidi ale piisa ale bua tusa ŋayopɔi (7,000) a magsi tigsuŋku ate kpaŋŋa mɛ a te ba lalisa tusidi ale piisa ale bua tusa pi (10,000). Kaabteerɔba ale jam paari dii choa a nye badek cheri. 25Juda tigsuŋku meena a jam a dɛ ka masim a gum chaab ale kaabteerɔma ale Livaima ale baai meena ale nyini Izirali a tigsi la a gum chaab ale nichamma baai ale nyini Izirali ale baai ale bo Juda po la. 26Mariŋka nna yega ale jam bo Jerusalem po, diila a nyini Izirali naawa Deevid nidoabinni Solomon daaŋa po wari an jam nye ase nna la Jerusalem po. 27Kaabteerɔma ale Livaima yaa jam niak nuruma ate Wen a wom ba, diila ba puusaŋa a jam paari wenŋmazuk kama, wa weleŋsa boka jigini.

english_text:
The People Destroy the Local Shrines
(2 Kings 18.4)
1After the Festival, the people went to every town in Judah and smashed the stone images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah. They destroyed all the local shrines and foreign altars in Judah, as well as those in the territories of Benjamin, Ephraim, and West Manasseh. Then everyone went home.
Offerings for the Priests and Levites
2Hezekiah divided the priests and Levites into groups, according to their duties. Then he assigned them the responsibilities of offering sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. He also appointed people to serve at the temple and to sing praises at the temple gates. 3 Hezekiah provided animals from his own herds and flocks to use for the morning and evening sacrifices, as well as for the sacrifices during the Sabbath celebrations, the New Moon Festivals, and the other religious feasts required by the Law of the Lord.
4 He told the people of Jerusalem to bring the offerings that were to be given to the priests and Levites, so that they would have time to serve the Lord with their work. 5As soon as the people heard what the king wanted, they brought a tenth of everything they owned, including their best grain, wine, olive oil, honey, and other crops. 6The people from the other towns of Judah brought a tenth of their herds and flocks, as well as a tenth of anything they had dedicated to the Lord. 7The people started bringing their offerings to Jerusalem in the third month, and the last ones arrived four months later. 8When Hezekiah and his officials saw these offerings, they thanked the Lord and the people.
9Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites about the large amount of offerings. 10The high priest at the time was Azariah, a descendant of Zadok, and he replied, “Ever since the people have been bringing us their offerings, we have had more than enough food and supplies. The Lord has certainly blessed his people. Look at how much is left over!”
11So the king gave orders for storerooms to be built in the temple, and when they were completed, 12-13all the extra offerings were taken there. Hezekiah and Azariah then appointed Conaniah the Levite to be in charge of these storerooms. His brother Shimei was his assistant, and the following Levites worked with them: Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah. 14Kore son of Imnah was assigned to guard the East Gate, and he was put in charge of receiving the offerings voluntarily given to God and of dividing them among the priests and Levites. 15-16He had six assistants who were responsible for seeing that all the priests in the other towns of Judah also got their share of these offerings. They were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah.
Every priest and every Levite over 30 years old who worked daily in the temple received part of these offerings, according to their duties. 17The priests were listed in the official records by clans, and the Levites 20 years old and older were listed by their duties. 18The official records also included their wives and children, because they had also been faithful in keeping themselves clean and acceptable to serve the Lord.
19Hezekiah also appointed other men to take food and supplies to the priests and Levites whose homes were in the pastureland around the towns of Judah. But the priests had to be descendants of Aaron, and the Levites had to be listed in the official records.
20-21Everything Hezekiah did while he was king of Judah, including what he did for the temple in Jerusalem, was right and good. He was a successful king, because he obeyed the Lord God with all his heart.
translation_text:
1Ase kude meena ale jam nueri la, Izirali dem baai ale jam bo dula la yaa jam cheŋ Juda tɛŋsaŋa po a ŋɔriŋ tintain ferima ale che Asera zaŋŋa a lɔnsi. Ba jam kaasi pimpitimaŋa ale kuŋkuŋtaŋa meena kama Jerusalem ale Benjamin ale Ɛfraim ale Manasa po. Ba ale jam kaasi ba meena la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, Izirali demma yaa ŋman cheŋ badek tɛŋsaŋa ale ba ŋantaŋa jigi.
2Azekaya a jam labi kaabteerɔma ale Livaima ka beŋsa a te wanyi meena tuini a ta va chaab ale kaabteerɔma ale Livaima tuimaŋa ale ka diila ayen ba nye juka tiirita ale suiyɔgni tiirita abe ba a tom, abe ba a te jiam a lenni yiila Naawen boka jigini nansuiŋku nɔi. 3Naawa a jam te kama a nyini wadek nitalimu po a magsi saluiku ale junɔinni juka tiiritaŋa ale Vuusum Daaŋa juka tiiritaŋa ale Chiik Paalik ale tigi ŋaai ate wa lueri ase ku le ŋmarisi Naawen Sinsaŋŋa po la.
4Wa jam weeni nuruma ale bo Jerusalem po la ayen ba te kaabteerɔma ale Livaima ba dɛka jigini ate dila ale basi ate ba pai badek a te Naawen Sinsaŋŋa. 5Ase wa le jam weeni diila ale nyini peelim la, Izirali demma a jam te ba ŋan baai ale dɛ niŋ bɛ la kama ale ba da paalimu ale kpaam ale siita ale jabuui meena ate ba nya nyini tɛŋka la, ba jam ta ka ŋanta a zuak ale jaab meena piika a jam. 6Izirali ale Juda nidoama baai ale jam bo Juda tɛŋsaŋa po la mɛ a jam ta ba duŋ buulimu piika a jam ale ba ŋan baai ale ta tuilum ate ba pai nyo Naawen ba Wenni nisima po a pai ba a vi chaab zuk nna kolololo. 7Ba jam piilim kude nyeka ka chiisa sitawa po a ga nueri chiisa siyopɔiwa po. 8Azekaya ale wa kpaŋŋa ale jam nya puulaŋa nna kolololo la, ba yaa pak Naawen ale niak wa nuruma Izirali demma.
9Azekaya yaa jam bek kaabteerɔma ale Livaima puulaŋa wie ate 10Kaabteerɔ kpagni Azariya ale nyini Zadok dɔkdemma buuni po la yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ase nuruma ale piilim ta ba cheesuŋku a jam Naawen yenni po la, ti ta ŋandiinta kama a dɛ ale tali yega a zaani, dii nyiŋla Naawen a niak wa nuruma kama ate ŋantaŋa de a tali zuak.>>
11Azekaya yaa jam weeni ate ba gomsi ŋanta duenika jigi Naawen yenni po, ate ba nye dila. 12Ba yaa jam ta cheesuŋku ale piika ale tiiritaŋa a jam ale wensie a te Konania ale ka Livai la ale jam a nya ŋantaŋa de zuk, ate wa suoku Simei a pai saŋ wa ŋaaŋ. 13Jeyiel ale Azaziya ale Nayat ale Asayel ale Jeremot ale Jozabad ale Eliel ale Ismakia ale Mayat ale Benaya ale jam a nya tuimaŋa zuk, ka Konania ale wa suoku Simei ale jam a nya ba zuk. Ka Naab Azekaya ale Azariya kpagni ale jam a nya Wen yenni zuk la ale lueri ba.
14Livai denɔwa Imnaya nidoabinni Kore, Kori Nansuiŋku nyaarɔwa ale jam a nya suiyɔgni tiiritaŋa ate ba te Wen la zuk ale chari cheesika ate ba nye te Naawen ale tiirim weleŋsaŋa mɛ. 15Eden ale Miniamin ale Jesua ale Sɛmaiya ale Amariya ale Sekania ale jam a maari wa ale wensie kaabteerɔma tɛŋsaŋa po a chari ŋantaŋa a te ba kaabteerɔ chaama a ta va ba labika ale ka diila jakpak ale paalik meena ba jam chari ka wayeŋ.
16A gum du, ba jam chari nidoama ale ta bena ŋata yaase ba gaam di la baai yueŋa ale jam bo ba ŋiaka gbaŋsaŋa po la, baai meena ale jam a jo Naawen yenni po a tom ba tuin dii ale beni ale tomka a ta va ba tuimaŋa ale ba labika ale ka diila. 17Ba jam chari kaabteerɔma ate ba dɔkdemma a jam ŋmarisi ba yueŋa ba ŋiaka gbaŋsaŋa po la ale Livaima mɛ baai ale paari bena pisiye yaase ba gaam di la a ta va ba ale magsi ba a tom diila ale ba labika. 18Ba jam chiini ŋan fiisaŋa meena a gum du kama, nipooma ale nidoabilisaŋa ale liema naakuuni meena po ba jam ŋmarisi kama ŋiak gbaŋsaŋa de po. Diila ba jam ta ka wensie a nye badek cheri.
19Dan ka kaabteerɔma, Aaron ŋaaŋbisaŋa baai ale jam bo tattaŋa tɛŋsaŋa ale gilim ba tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa yaase ba bo tɛŋ yonsa po la, nidoaba ale ba jam ŋmarisi ba yueŋa ate ba chari tɛŋka a te nidoa meena ale bo ba po la ale waai meena yuei ale ŋmarisi bo Livaima ŋiak gbaŋka po la.
20Nyakude ate Azekaya a jam nye Juda meena po la, a nye dii ale nala ale chekki ale wensie la Naawen wa Wenni niŋ. 21Dii meena ate wa jam nye Wen yenni po la ale wa le siak a wom sinsaŋŋa ale wieŋa la, wa jam gisi wa Wenni ale tom ale wa suinum meena. Dila wa yaa jam nya niaka.

english_text:
King Sennacherib of Assyria Invades Judah
(2 Kings 18.13-37; Isaiah 36.1-22)
1After King Hezekiah had faithfully obeyed the Lord's instructions by doing these things, King Sennacherib of Assyria invaded Judah. He attacked the fortified cities and thought he would capture every one of them.
2As soon as Hezekiah learned that Sennacherib was planning to attack Jerusalem, 3-4he and his officials worked out a plan to cut off the supply of water outside the city, so that the Assyrians would have no water when they came to attack. The officials got together a large work force that stopped up the springs and streams near Jerusalem.
5Hezekiah's workers also repaired the broken sections of the city wall. Then they built defense towers and an outer wall to help protect the one already there. The landfill on the east side of David's City was also strengthened.
He gave orders to make a large supply of weapons and shields, 6and he appointed army commanders over the troops. Then he gathered the troops together in the open area in front of the city gate and said to them:
7Be brave and confident! There's no reason to be afraid of King Sennacherib and his powerful army. We are much more powerful, 8because the Lord our God fights on our side. The Assyrians must rely on human power alone.
These words encouraged the army of Judah.
9When Sennacherib and his troops were camped at the town of Lachish, he sent a message to Hezekiah and the people in Jerusalem. It said:
10I am King Sennacherib of Assyria, and I have Jerusalem surrounded. Do you think you can survive my attack? 11Hezekiah your king is telling you that the Lord your God will save you from me. But he is lying, and you'll die of hunger and thirst. 12Didn't Hezekiah tear down all except one of the Lord's altars and places of worship? And didn't he tell you people of Jerusalem and Judah to worship at that one place?
13You've heard what my ancestors and I have done to other nations. Were the gods of those nations able to defend their land against us? 14None of those gods kept their people safe from the kings of Assyria. Do you really think your God can do any better? 15Don't be fooled by Hezekiah! No god of any nation has ever been able to stand up to Assyria. Believe me, your God cannot keep you safe!
16The Assyrian officials said terrible things about the Lord God and his servant Hezekiah. 17Sennacherib's letter even made fun of the Lord. It said, “The gods of other nations could not save their people from Assyria's army, and neither will the God that Hezekiah worships.” 18The officials said all these things in Hebrew, so that everyone listening from the city wall would understand and be terrified and surrender. 19The officials talked about the Lord God as if he were nothing but an ordinary god or an idol that someone had made.
The Death of King Sennacherib
(2 Kings 19.14-19,35-37; Isaiah 37.14-20; 37.36-38)
20Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz begged the Lord for help, 21and he sent an angel that killed every soldier and commander in the Assyrian camp.
Sennacherib returned to Assyria, completely disgraced. Then one day he went into the temple of his god where some of his sons killed him.
22The Lord rescued Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from Sennacherib and also protected them from other enemies. 23People brought offerings to Jerusalem for the Lord and expensive gifts for Hezekiah, and from that day on, every nation on earth respected Hezekiah.
Hezekiah Gets Sick and Almost Dies
(2 Kings 20.1-11; Isaiah 38.1-8)
24About this same time, Hezekiah got sick and was almost dead. He prayed, and the Lord gave him a sign that he would recover. 25But Hezekiah was so proud that he refused to thank the Lord for everything he had done for him. This made the Lord angry, and he punished Hezekiah and the people of Judah and Jerusalem. 26Hezekiah and the people later felt sorry and asked the Lord to forgive them. So the Lord did not punish them as long as Hezekiah was king.
Hezekiah's Wealth
(2 Kings 20.12-19; Isaiah 39.1-8)
27Hezekiah was very rich, and everyone respected him. He built special rooms to store the silver, the gold, the precious stones and spices, the shields, and the other valuable possessions. 28Storehouses were also built for his supply of grain, wine, and olive oil; barns were built for his cattle, and pens were put up for his sheep. 29God made Hezekiah extremely rich, so he bought even more sheep, goats, and cattle. And he built towns where he could keep all these animals.
30It was Hezekiah who built a tunnel that carried the water from Gihon Spring into the city of Jerusalem. In fact, everything he did was successful! 31Even when the leaders of Babylonia sent messengers to ask Hezekiah about the sign God had given him, God let Hezekiah give his own answer to test him and to see if he would remain faithful.
Hezekiah Dies
(2 Kings 20.20,21)
32Everything else Hezekiah did while he was king, including how faithful he was to the Lord, is included in the records kept by Isaiah the prophet. These are written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel. 33When Hezekiah died, he was buried in the section of the royal tombs that was reserved for the most respected kings, and everyone in Judah and Jerusalem honored him. His son Manasseh then became king.
translation_text:
1Azekaya ale jam nye dii meena ale wensie la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, Assiria naawa Sennacherib yaa jam fɛ jo Juda po. Wa jam siti tɛŋsaŋa ate ba sɛ parik a gilim la kama a poli ayen wa le nak yik ba. 2Ase Azekaya ale jam nya ayen Sennacherib a jam kama a poli ayen wa nye kpaliŋ ale Jerusalem tɛŋka la, 3wa yaa zɔk ale wa kpaŋŋa ale tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpaŋŋa ayen ba kasi nyiamu ale bo tɛŋka peelim la ate ba maari wa. 4Nuru boari yaa jam tigsi ate ba kasi nyaataŋa ale buboalisaŋa meena ale chali nyini tɛŋka po a nyini la. Ba weeni ayen, <<Boan nyiŋ ate Assiria naawa a jam nya nyiam nna yegayega? 5Wa yaa jam tom nalimnyiini a ŋman tebi parika kab tii ale lo la meena a sɛ kiaga ka zuk. Wa jam sɛ ka parik ka choa peelim a gilim kala a tom Deevid Tɛŋka po. Wa jam maa nye ka kpaliŋ ŋanchɔgsin kpienta.
6Wa jam lueri ka tugurik tɔŋdɔba kpaga ate ba a nya nuruma zuk ale tigsi ba wa niŋ tɛŋka nansuiŋku nɔi a te ba nyiŋbiiri ale wieŋa de ayen, 7<<Ni pagra abe ni toa. Ni kan chali yɔgsum abe ni jɔk yiila Assiria naawa ale wa tugurik tom boanni nyiŋŋa, ale ka pagrim kpiem ale bo ale tama a gaam ba. 8Wa ta ka nuruba nyiini, alege tama ta ka Naawen ti Wenni ate wa a maari ti a kpaliŋ ti kpaliŋka a te ti.>> Ate nuruma a ta sebchakka ale Juda naawa Azekaya ale weeni diila.
9Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ase Assiria naawa Sennacherib ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena ale jam suk doa Lachis suiku po la, wa yaa jam tom wa kpaŋŋa Jerusalem tɛŋka ale tintomiŋka de ate Juda naawa Azekaya ale Juda nuruma meena ale bo dula la ayen,
10<<Assiria naawa Sennacherib ale weeni diila ale nna: Ka boan jaab zuk ate nama sebchakka a boro ate ni wari suk bo Jerusalem po? 11Ase Azekaya ale jam weeni ayen, <Naawen dii ale ka ti Wen la ale vari ti a ta nyini Assiria naawa nisima po a basi la,> wa a paasi ni kama ayen ni kpi ale kɔm ale nyanyuila. 12Azekaya dek an jam kpiti wenni de pimpitimaŋa ale kuŋkuŋtaŋa kama ale weeni Juda ale Jerusalem demma ayen, <Ku a fɛ ate ni a kaab kuŋkuŋ yeŋ abe ni a nye juka kaabka ku zuk la?>
13<<Nama a zɛ dii ate mi ale m koma a nye tɛŋ sinsila nuruma la? Ba wenaŋa a jam baga a vari ba mi nisa po a basi? 14Tɛŋsaŋa de meena wenaŋa dina ate mi koma a jam kaasi la ale baga a vari di nuru mi jigi ya? Nama wenni abe le nye ka sɛ a vari ni mi nisa po a basi? 15Ni kan basi ate Azekaya a paasi ni a ta ni cheŋ bɛ. Ni kan ta sebchakka ale wa, ale tɛŋ yoŋ yaase naam wen a baga vari di nuruba mi nisa po yaase m koma nisa po a basi. Nama wenni ale nye ka sɛ a vari ni mi nisa po a basi?>>
16Sennacherib kpaŋŋa yaa jam biisi gum du a ta chaab ale Naawen dii ale ka Wenni la ale wa tomteerɔwa Azekaya. 17Naawa a jam ŋmarisi ka gbaŋsa mɛ a lɛ Naawen, Izirali Wenni a biisi wieŋa de a ta chaab ale wa ayen, <<Ase nuru yoŋta wena ale kan baga a vari ŋa nuruba mi nisa po la, dila Azekaya wenni an baga a vari wa nuruma mi nisa po a basi.>> 18Ba yaa wi nuruma ale bo Jerusalem po la ale Yiburu biika baai ale jam bo parika zuk la ayen ba nyigsi ba a nye ate ba yɔksa ate ba nya suik a nak yik tɛŋka. 19Ba jam biisi kaasi Jerusalem Wenni ase ka ba le jam biisi nuru yoŋta wenaŋa ate nuru bisa a nye la.
20Naab Azekaya ale Amoz nidoabinni biisiteerɔwa Azaya yaa jam puusi a kaari a te wenŋmazuk kude nyiŋ. 21Naawen yaa jam tom maarɔ, waai ale jam ko tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale niŋdeerɔma ale kpaŋŋa meena Assiria naawa tigsuŋku jigini. Dila a jam basi kama ate wa ŋman kuli wadek tɛŋka ale chivie. Ase wa le jam ga jo wa wenni yenni po la, wa nidoabilisaŋa gela yaa che wa ale gebik a ko.
22Naawen a jam vari Azekaya ale Jerusalem nuruma Assiria naawa Sennacherib ale nuru yonta nisima po a basi kama. Wa jam a nya ba zuk ka dila jigi meena. 23Yega ale jam ta tiirita a jam te Naawen Jerusalem po ale te Juda naawa Azekaya tiirim tii ale ta yuei la. A nyini dula tɛŋsa meena a jam a zuli wa kama.
24Va ŋala po ate Azekaya a jam a yuak a moata kum. Wa jam puusi kama a te Naawen, waai ale jam tulisi wa a te wa wakinkagli daana. 25Alege Azekaya jam ta ka kanjanta wa suinummu po, wa nina an jam sueri ale wa le nya nyemagsika la, dila nyiŋ Naawen suipuurumu yaa jam wa ale Juda ale Jerusalem demma zuk. 26Azekaya yaa jam tagri basi kanjantaŋa ale bo wa suinummu po la Jerusalem demma mɛ a jam nye ka dila, dila nyiŋ Naawen suipuurumu an jan jam ba jigi Azekaya daaŋa po.
27Azekaya jam jigsi kama nalimnyiini a ta zula, wa jam sɛ ka jigi a magsi wa kpanaŋa ale ligmɔniŋka ale wa tintain ŋaai diak ale pagra la ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa la ale kpaliŋ ŋanchɔgsinta ale ŋan baai meena ale ta dobrim la. 28Wa jam maa sɛ ka diina a magsi kpari ŋanta duenika ale da paalimu ale kpaam ale nye nankpieŋsa a magsi niiga tɔgatɔga ale zoŋta a magsi duŋ buulimu. 29Wa jam sɛ ka tɛŋ kpaŋsa ale ta duŋ buulim nna yegayega diila Wen a jam te wa ka jigsika nna yegayega.
30Ku jam ka Azekaya ale kasi Giyon ŋmazuk nyiam vuuku ale a zaŋti Deevid Tɛŋka yeniŋ geŋsa la. Wa jam nya suik a nye dii meena ate wa a yaali ayen wa nye la kama. 31Alege ase kpaŋŋa ale jam tom nuruba ate ba nyini Babilon ayen ba bek wa wakinkagni ale jam nye tɛŋka po la, Wen a jam basi wa kama ayen wa chamsi wa nya abe wa seba dii meena ale a nye wa suinummu po la.
32Azekaya naamu wayoŋtaŋa ale wa le nye diila a ŋmarisi bo Amos nidoabinni biisiteerɔwa Azaya a jam nya la po kama Juda ale Izirali nalima gbaŋka po. 33Azekaya a jam vuusi kama a gum wa koma po ate ba gu wa guuku zuk juijui ate Deevid ŋaaŋbisaŋa boositaŋa a boro la. Juda ale Jerusalem demma meena a jam zuli wa kama wa le kpi la. Manasa wa nidoabinni ale jam zaani wa nankula po ase naab la.

english_text:
King Manasseh of Judah
(2 Kings 21.1-9,17,18)
1Manasseh was 12 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled 55 years from Jerusalem. 2 Manasseh disobeyed the Lord by following the disgusting customs of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel. 3He rebuilt the local shrines that his father Hezekiah had torn down. He built altars for the god Baal and set up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah. And he continued to worship the stars.
4In the temple, where only the Lord was supposed to be worshiped, Manasseh built altars for the worship of pagan gods 5and the stars. He placed these altars in both courtyards of the temple 6-7 and even set up a stone image of a foreign god. Manasseh practiced magic and witchcraft; he asked fortunetellers for advice and sacrificed his own sons in Hinnom Valley. He did many other sinful things and made the Lord very angry.
Years ago, God had told David and Solomon:
Jerusalem is the place I prefer above all others in Israel. It belongs to me, and there in the temple I will be worshiped forever. 8If my people will faithfully obey all the laws and teaching I gave to my servant Moses, I will never again force them to leave the land I gave to their ancestors.
9But the people of Judah and Jerusalem listened to Manasseh and did even more sinful things than the nations the Lord had wiped out.
10The Lord tried to warn Manasseh and the people about their sins, but they ignored the warning. 11So he let Assyrian army commanders invade Judah and capture Manasseh. They put a hook in his nose and tied him up in chains, and they took him to Babylon. 12While Manasseh was held captive there, he asked the Lord God to forgive him and to help him. 13The Lord listened to Manasseh's prayer and saw how sorry he was, and so he let him go back to Jerusalem and rule as king. Manasseh knew from then on that the Lord was God.
14Later, Manasseh rebuilt the eastern section of Jerusalem's outer wall and made it taller. This section went from Gihon Valley north to Fish Gate and around the part of the city called Mount Ophel. He also assigned army officers to each of the fortified cities in Judah.
15Manasseh also removed the idols and the stone image of the foreign god from the temple, and he gathered the altars he had built near the temple and in other parts of Jerusalem. He threw all these things outside the city. 16Then he repaired the Lord's altar and offered sacrifices to thank him and sacrifices to ask his blessing. He gave orders that everyone in Judah must worship the Lord God of Israel. 17The people obeyed Manasseh, but they worshiped the Lord at their own shrines.
18Everything else Manasseh did while he was king, including his prayer to the Lord God and the warnings from his prophets, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. 19Hozai wrote a lot about Manasseh, including his prayer and God's answer. But Hozai also recorded the evil things Manasseh did before turning back to God, as well as a list of places where Manasseh set up idols, and where he built local shrines and places to worship Asherah. 20Manasseh died and was buried near the palace, and his son Amon became king.
King Amon of Judah
(2 Kings 21.19-26)
21Amon was 22 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 2 years. 22Amon disobeyed the Lord, just as his father Manasseh had done, and he worshiped and offered sacrifices to the idols his father had made. 23Manasseh had turned back to the Lord, but Amon refused to do that. Instead, he sinned even more than his father.
24Some of Amon's officials plotted against him and killed him in his palace. 25But the people of Judah killed the murderers of Amon and made his son Josiah king.
translation_text:
1Manasa jam ta ka bena pi ale ŋaye ale chim naab, wa jam dɛ naamu Jerusalem po ka bena pisinu ale ŋanu. 2Wa jam nye ka biem Naawen nina po a va kisuk nyeelaŋa ate tɛŋ sii ate Naawen a yiak si basi a te Izirali demma la. 3Wa pilim sɛ pimpitimaŋa ate wa kowa a jam ŋɔriŋ la kama, wa jam sɛ ka kuŋkuŋta a te Baal bɔgtaŋa mɛ ale nye zaŋŋa te Asera bɔglukku. Wa jam koori ka tɛŋ a puusi wenŋmazuk chiŋmarisaŋa. 4Wa jam sɛ ka kuŋkuŋta Naawen yenni po, dii ate Naawen ayen, <<Mi Yuenni ale wari bo Jerusalem po taam wuu.>> 5Naawen dabaasa siyewa po wa jam sɛ ka kuŋkuŋta a te wenŋmazuk chiŋmarik boanni. 6Wa jam pai ka wa nidoabilisaŋa a nye bolim kaabka Ben Yinnom Viaka po, a zamsi sampoporinni ale bɔkka ale sakpaŋni ale a bek wie a nyini ninnyaama ale chichirik wiirisa jigi. Wa jam nye ka biem nna yegayega Naawen nina po, a nye ate wa sui a yiti.
7Wa jam pai jaamu ate ba peesi la a zaani ka Wen yenni po dii ate Wen a weeni Deevid ale wa nidoabinni Solomon ayen, <<Yenni de po ale Jerusalem po, juijui ate mi a lueri nyini Izirali buuni meena po la, mi ale basi m Yuenni du taam wuu. 8Mi kan ŋman nye ate Izirali demma naŋtaata a basi tɛŋka ate mi a te ni kokpieŋsaŋa la, ase ba nin kpesi ayen ba nye dii meena ate mi a weeni ba a ta va sinsaŋŋa meena ale ŋmarisika ale kaamka ate Moosis a weeni ni la.>> 9Alege Manasa a jam ta Juda ale Jerusalem nuruma a cheŋ bɛ kama ate dila a nye ate ba ŋmasi nye biem a gaam tɛŋ sii ate Naawen a yiak ba a te Izirali demma la.
