Ka boa ale a daani ni ate ni kasim a nak nanpaga? 4Mi mɛ ate baga a biisi ase nama la kama, ase nama a nin poom bo mi jigini. Mi ti baga a biisi bi maŋsa kama a ta chaab ale ni abe m girinti m zukku. 5Alege mi nɔnni ale te ni nyiŋbiiri, mi nɔnni suiyɔgni ale fasiyaa a jam ni jigi.
6<<Mi dan poom biisi, mi nyiŋdommaŋa a kan basi, ate m dan poom basi biik, ŋa kan cheŋ. 7Chekki, Wen yaa fi basi ate m nye kuligi, fi kaasi m yenni meena kama. 8Fi bobi mu kama ate kula a chim seerɔ, mi nye ka nna wakki ate kula a sak mi ale nye foolaa diila. 9Wen a siti mi kama ale dari mi cheeri ale wa suipuurumu ale a ŋɔbi nyina. Mi dachiaka a nya mi kama ale kisika. 10Nuruba a lak ba nɔi kama a nye mu a la, ba fɔbi ka m tapiak ale nye laka ale gum chaab a ta chaab ale mu. 11Wen a tulim mi a te ka nuru baata ale yuk mi a basi wabaata nyam batta po. 12Jaab meena a jam nala kama te mi alege wa lik mi, wa tik ka mi nyiŋ 13wa tɔŋdɔma a gilim mi kama, ba ka jiirimmoa, ba lu ka mi yiimaŋa ale mobi m yaamu a basi tɛŋ. 14Wa ŋman na pusi mi zuk, wa wuuri a jam mi zuk ase tugurik tɔŋdɔ la.
15<<Mi baali ka boorisa garuk a lik mi nyiŋ gbaŋka ale pai mi dinni a kpi tɛŋ. 16Mi kum kama ate mi ninaŋa a muni ate mi ninaŋa a ji ate mi nina a lo du, 17alege mi nisima an nye vakvak ate mi puusaŋa a nye cheri.
18<<Tɛŋŋa, kan lik mi ziimu. Mi ale kaari a yaali diila a kan nye chorr. 19Yɔgyɔgla de pooma mi seerɔwa a bo ka wenŋmazuk, mi maarɔwa a bo ka ŋmazuk. 20Waai ale biisi a te mi la ka mi doa ase mi ale a kum ale ninyaata a te Wen la. 21Nuru nankula po wa a saalim Wen ase ka nuru ale a saalim a te wa doa diila.
22<<Bena magadega ale taam alege ate mi cheŋ suik kuui ale kaa ŋmani la po.

english_text:
Job Complains to God
My Hopes Have Died
1My hopes have died,
my time is up,
and the grave is ready.
2All I can see are angry crowds,
making fun of me.
3If you, Lord, don't help,
who will pay the price
for my release?
4My friends won't really listen,
all because of you,
and so you must be the one
to prove them wrong.
5They have condemned me,
just to benefit themselves;
now blind their children.
6You, God, are the reason
I am insulted and spit on.
7I am almost blind with grief;
my body is a mere shadow.
8People who are truly good
would feel so alarmed,
that they would become angry
with my worthless friends.
9They would do the right thing
and because they did,
they would grow stronger.
10But none of my friends
show any sense.
11My life is drawing to an end;
hope has disappeared.
12But all my friends can do
is offer empty hopes.
13I could tell the world below
to prepare me a bed.
14Then I could greet the grave
as my father
and say to the worms,
“Hello, mother and sisters!”
15But what kind of hope is that?
16Will it keep me company
in the world of the dead?

3<<Wen yaa, tuni a vari mu a basi. Waai karo a tuni vari mu a basi. 4Fi lik ba popolaŋa kama ate ba kan miŋi, dila nyiŋ fi kan basi ate ba nya pagrimoa. 5Nuru a dan zɛri wa doaba tutuna nyiŋ, wa bisaŋa ale nam ku nyiŋ.
6<<Wen a basi kama ate mi chim waai ate waai meena a ta a biisi, nuru waai ate nuruba a chesi tintueta a basi m nina po. 7Sui kaasuŋ a basi kama ate mi an ŋman nya a paari, mi nyiŋ diokku meena a nye ase ka yisuŋ la. 8Ku cha baai ale ta wensie la kama ate ba meena a bo a mini mi ayen mi a ka Wen ya. 9Ku dan poom ka dii ya wayɔrisima nyama ale yik ba suitaŋa a ta, ate baai nisima ale nye cheri la ale ta pagrim.
10<<Alege, ni meena jam, ni ŋman nye nya. Mi a kan nya yam nuru ni po. 11Mi daaŋa a taam kama, mi zɔŋŋa a kaasi kama, ku be ka dila ale mi suinummu ale a yaali diila. 12Nuruma de a tulim yok ate ku a chim kantueŋ, legi po ba a weeni kama ayen bolim a moata. 13Ase yie dii ate mi a yiili la dan ka vɔrumu, ate mi dan pati m tiaka legini po, 14ase mi daa wi vɔrumu ayen, <Fi ka m ko,> ale a wi nanzuinni ayen, <M ma,> yaase <M tua.> 15Mi yiilaŋa yaa be bo ka bɛ? Ka wana ale wa nya yiila a te mi? 16Ŋa le siŋ vɔrumu po? Ti le siŋ tantaŋa po ale chaaba?>>

english_text:
Bildad's Second Speech
How Long Will You Talk?
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2How long will you talk?
Be sensible! Let us speak.
3Or do you think that we
are dumb animals?
4You cut yourself in anger.
Will that shake the earth
or even move the rocks?
* 5 The lamps of sinful people
soon are snuffed out,
6leaving their tents dark.
7Their powerful legs become weak,
and they stumble on schemes
of their own doing.
* 8Before they know it,
9they are trapped in a net,
10hidden along the path.
11Terror strikes and pursues
from every side.
12Starving, they run,
only to meet disaster,
13then afterwards to be eaten alive
by death itself.
14Those sinners are dragged
from the safety of their tents
to die a gruesome death.
15Then their tents and possessions
are burned to ashes,
16and they are left like trees,
dried up from the roots.
17They are gone and forgotten,
18thrown far from the light
into a world of darkness,
19without any children
to carry on their name.
20Everyone, from east to west,
is overwhelmed with horror.
21Such is the fate of sinners
and their families
who don't know God.
translation_text:
1Suya denɔwa Bildad yaa tulisi ayen, 2<<Ka dimpo ate fi le kpeglim biisaŋa de? Ta yam, ate ti baga a biisi. 3Ka boa ale soa ate fi a pai ti a chim niiga ale a nya ti ase betta la fi nina po. 4Fi waai ale dari fidek a cheeri nna bunabuna ale suipuurum la, ba basi tɛŋka fi nyiŋŋa? Yaase ba zak pinaŋa ŋa jigini?
5<<Wabaata nyɔnɔwa zeuŋku a kpimsi, wa bolim ŋiaka a basi dɛka kama. 6Bolimu ale bo wa viuku po la a kpi kama, zeuŋku ale bo wa gauŋ la a nye ka lim. 7Wa pagrim tabika an ŋman pagra, wadek zɔŋŋa a yuk wa a basi ka tɛŋ. 8Wa naŋtaataŋa a tusi wa a nyo ka ŋmiak po ate wa cheŋ tuiri a jo vɔrup po. 9Baruk ale yik wa nankpanni, baruk ale yik wa naa giŋgiŋ. 10Katorik ate ba pai suk tɛŋ a magsi wa, baruk ale doa wa suiku po. 11Nyinyigsa nyam ale a nyigsi wa jigi meena, ale va wa naŋsa. 12Wa kom ale ta kaasuŋ, kaasuŋ a gomsi kama a magsi wa ase wa nin lo. 13Ku dɛ wa nyiŋ gbaŋka gela kama, kum ale liŋ biak jabuui la a dɛ wa kama. 14Ba cheeri kama a ta wa nyini wa viuku po ate wa gɔk santiri a cheŋ nyinyigsa naawa jigi. 15Bolim ale bo wa viuku po, bolim mɔnuŋ ale waaŋ wa boka jigini. 16Wa tɛŋ naŋsaŋa a kpi kama tɛŋka ate ŋmazuk naŋsaŋa a kpi. 17Wa wie ate ba a poli la a kpi kama tɛŋka zuk, wa ka yuei tɛŋka po. 18Ba yiak wa kama ate wa nyini bolim po a jo legi po ale yiak wa tɛŋzuk de. 19Wa ka bisa yaase ŋaaŋbisa wa nuruma po, waai an tali vua tɛŋ kaai ate wa jam boro la. 20Ku cha nuru baai ale nyini yeniŋ la kama ale wa danni, nuru baai ale nyini kori geŋsa la yɔgsum ale yik ba. 21Chekki nuru biok boka ale ka diila ale la, nuru waai ale kan seba Wen la jigini ale ka diila ale la.>>

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
How Long Will You Torture Me?
1Job said:
2How long will you torture me
with your words?
3Isn't ten times enough
for you to accuse me?
Aren't you ashamed?
4Even if I have sinned,
you haven't been harmed.
5You boast of your goodness,
claiming I am suffering
because I am guilty.
6But God is the one at fault
for finding fault with me.
7Though I pray to be rescued
from this torment,
no whisper of justice
answers me.
8God has me trapped
with a wall of darkness
9and stripped of respect.
10God rips me apart,
uproots my hopes,
11and attacks with fierce anger,
as though I were his enemy.
12His entire army advances,
then surrounds my tent.
I Am Forgotten
* 13God has turned relatives
and friends against me,
14and I am forgotten.
15My guests and my servants
consider me a stranger,
16and when I call my servants,
they pay no attention.
17My breath disgusts my wife;
everyone in my family
turns away.
18Young children can't stand me,
and when I come near,
they make fun.
19 My best friends and loved ones
have turned from me.
20I am skin and bones—
just barely alive.
21My friends, I beg you for pity!
God has made me his target.
22Hasn't he already done enough?
Why do you join the attack?
23I wish that my words
could be written down
24or chiseled into rock.
25I know that my Protector lives,
and at the end
he will stand on this earth.
26My flesh may be destroyed,
yet from this body
I will see God.
27Yes, I will see him for myself,
and I long for that moment.
28My friends, you think up ways
to blame and torment me, saying
I brought it on myself.
29But watch out for the judgment,
when God will punish you!
translation_text:
1Job yaa tulisi ayen, 2<<Ni le namsi mi a paari ka dimpo abe ni ŋɔriŋ mu ale wie? 3Naŋtuok nɔi pi ale nna ate ni toariŋ mu ale ta chaab ale mu a kan chali chivie. 4Ku dan ka wensie nyiŋ mi cheŋ a be kama, mi nyebeka ti ka mi nyiini niŋ wari. 5Ni dan poom zak nidek ŋmai a gaam mi ale pai mi ale kan daa jaab la a biisi mi, 6yaa be seba ayen Wen ale nye mi a kaasi ale dari wa ŋmiaka a gilim mi.
7<<Mi a kum kama ayen, <Ba nye mu kaasi m kan nya tulisika>, mi a wi a yaali maarika alege nyemagsika ka. 8Wa kasi mi suiku kama ate mi a kan baga a taamu, wa lik mi suitaŋa kama legi po. 9Wa yeeri mi zulaŋa kama, ale lak naam zutɔkka mi zukku po. 10Wa a cheeri mi kama a lɔnsi kauk meena ate mi cheŋ ferr, wa dari mi yiilaŋa a voori ase tiib la. 11Wa suinni a dɛ ka nna pɔkpɔk ale mi, wa chiini mi a nyo ka wa dachaasaŋa po. 12Wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma a duŋ kama ale fifiok, ba sɛ ka bimbimi a ta chaab ale mu ale kɔk a gilim m viuku.
13<<Wa yeeri mi suataŋa mi jigi kama, mi ale baai ale magsi chaab la a yeeri ka wossi mi jigi. 14Mi dateerɔma a cheŋ ka meena, mi doama a baŋ mi wari kama. 15Mi nichamma ale mi dɔkliema a baŋ mi wari kama, ba a nya mi ase ka nichaanɔ la. 16Mi wi mi tomteerɔwa kama, alege wa an tulisi ya, mi ale saalim wa ale m dek nɔi la mɛ. 17Mi vuusumu a daani mi powa kama, mi dek suataŋa a kisi mi kama. 18Nidoabili fiisa a nye mi a la kama, mi dan ga na nyini ba a nye mi a lu kama. 19Mi doa baai meena ale moata mi la a kisi mi kama, baai ate mi a yaali la a cheem ta ka chaab ale mi. 20Mi daa jaaboa alege ka nyiŋ gbaŋ ale koba, mi be chali be ale ka mi nyinaŋa nyiŋ gbaŋka nyiini.
21<<Ni ta jiirim ale mu, m doaba, ni ta jiirim ale mu, diila Wen nisa ale nak mu. 22Ka boa ate ni a vi mu ase Wen ale a vi mu la? Nama an namsi mi a magsi ya?
23<<Mi yaali ayen mi wieŋa ate ŋmarisi doa kama, ŋa ti ŋmarisi doa gbaŋ po, 24mi yaali ayen ba ti pai kutuk jaab a kpiiri a dueni kutuk baasuŋ nyiŋ, yaase ba kerisi a dueni piuŋ nyiŋ taam wuu. 25Mi seba ayen m Da Tuesirɔwa a boro kama, ate ku kpeglimka wa le zaani tɛŋka zuk. 26Mi nyiŋ gbaŋka abe dan kaasi ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ mi nyiŋ lammu po mi ale nya Wen. 27Mi dek ale nya wa ale m dek nina, ate mi ale seba wa ale ka waai la. Mi suinummu ale yaali a soa diila.
28<<Ni dan weeni ayen, <Ti le ti nye dii a vi wa la, diila daanika piilimka a boka wa jigi,> 29nama dek a chali gebika, diila suipuurum ale ta gebika namsika a jam, ate ni yaa seba ayen buusa a boro.>>

english_text:
Zophar's Second Speech
Your Words Are Disturbing
1Zophar from Naamah said:
2Your words are disturbing;
now I must speak.
3You have accused
and insulted me,
and reason requires a reply.
4Since the time of creation,
everyone has known
5that sinful people are happy
for only a while.
6Though their pride and power
may reach to the sky,
7they will disappear like dust,
and those who knew them
will wonder what happened.
8 They will be forgotten
like a dream
9and vanish from the sight
of family and friends.
10Their children will have to repay
what the parents took
from the poor.
11Indeed, the wicked will die
and go to their graves
in the prime of life.
Sinners Love the Taste of Sin
12Sinners love the taste of sin;
they relish every bite
13and swallow it slowly.
14But their food will turn sour
and poison their stomachs.
15Then God will make them lose
the wealth they gobbled up.
16They will die from the fangs
of poisonous snakes
17and never enjoy rivers flowing
with milk and honey.
18Their hard work will result
in nothing gained,
19because they cheated the poor
and took their homes.
20Greedy people want everything
and are never satisfied.
21But when nothing remains
for them to grab,
they will be nothing.
22Once they have everything,
distress and despair
will strike them down,
23and God will make them swallow
his blazing anger.
24 While running from iron spears,
they will be killed
by arrows of bronze,
25whose shining tips go straight
through their bodies.
They will be trapped by terror,
26and what they treasure most
will be lost in the dark.
God will send flames
to destroy them in their tents
with all their property.
27The heavens and the earth
will testify against them,
28and all their possessions
will be dragged off
when God becomes angry.
29This is what God has decided
for those who are evil.
translation_text:
1Naama denɔwa Zofar yaa tulisi ayen, 2<<Mi popolaŋa daanika ale choa ate mi a tulisi dii nyiŋla ku daani mi ka yega. 3Mi a wom ka toariŋka ate zula a karo, ate mi dek miŋka po ayen mi tulisi.
4<<Chekki fi seba kama ku le ka dii a nyini dipowa la, diipo meena ate nurubiik a bo tɛŋka zuk la, 5ayen wabaata nyɔnɔwa masimu an soa diiya, waai ale kan ta Wen la suipeentika a kan beni. 6Wa kanjantaŋa a dan poom a paari wenni, ate wa zukku a tiri chiŋmaaŋa, 7wa le kpi taam wuu, ase wadek binta la. Baai ale nya wa la ale weeni ayen, <Wa boka be?> 8Ase gɔdaasima la wa le yiti a be, ba kan ŋman nya wa, a cheŋ ferr ase yok gɔdaasima la. 9Num buui ale nya wa la a kan ŋman nya wa, wa jigini a kan ŋman nya wa. 10Wa bisaŋa ale nye magsi ale ŋanjaksaŋa, wadek nisaŋa ale pai wa jigsika a ŋman te. 11Bimbain pagrimu ale bo wa kobaŋa po la ale duak tantaŋa po ale wa.
12<<Biem poom masa kama wa nɔnni po, ate wa suk bu wa giŋgeluŋku tɛŋ, 13wa an poom baga a basi ate bu a cheŋ ale basi ate bu bo wa nɔnni po, 14ale dila meena wa ŋandiintaŋa ale tulim tua wa ponni po, bu le chim waapiik lɔk wa po. 15Wa le chessi jigsi kaai ate wa nɛ la. Wen ale basi ate wa chiiri ba wa ponni po. 16Wa le dari waapiisaŋa lɔkku, waapiik ŋesɔ ale dom wa ate wa kpi. 17Wa kan nya beli naŋsaŋa masimmoa, beli ŋaai ale a chali ale biisim ale siita la. 18Ŋan baai ate wa nam a nya la wa le pai te wa kan de, wa kan de wa geruŋku nyuentaŋa masimmoa. 19Diila wa namsi ŋanjaksaŋa kama ale basi ba kinla, wa vari yie ŋaai ate wa an sɛ ya.
20<<Wa ka de gaamka nyɔnɔ, wa kan maara a chagi, wa kan baga a nya wa le a yaali ŋan baai la. 21Jaab an tali magsi wa dɛka, wa ŋantaŋa a kan beni. 22Wa ŋanta yega suŋsuŋ sui kaasuŋ ale paari wa, niniga yega ale jam wa zuk. 23Wa dan sueri wa ponni, Wen suipuurum ale jam wa zuk a basi ate nigua a siŋ wa zuk. 24Wa le chali ayen wa bɛ gbaluku alege kutuk mɔnuŋ penni ale yik wa. 25Wa le dari di a yeeri wa ŋaaŋka, di nɔi choarika a yeeri wa paŋni po. Nyinyigsa nyam ale nya pagrim wa zuk. 26Legi ale a limisi wa tuilum ŋantaŋa. Bolim buui ale kan fugi ya ale dɛ wa abe bu dɛ ŋan baai ale tali viuku po la. 27Wenŋmazukku ale lak wa foolaa wa a sak, tɛŋka ale yiti a ta chaab ale wa. 28Pimpanta ale ji wa yenni ta cheŋ, Wen suipuurumu danni nya tii ale a wuuri la ale jam. 29Zubiok kuui choa ate Wen a basi ate wabaata nyama a nya la ale la, nitalim buui ate Wen a te ba la.>>

english_text:
Job's Reply to Zophar
If You Want To Offer Comfort
1Job said:
2If you want to offer comfort,
then listen to me.
3And when I have finished,
you can start your insults
all over again.
4My complaint is against God;
that's why I am impatient.
5Just looking at me is enough
to make you sick,
6and the very thought of myself
fills me with disgust.
7Why do evil people live so long
and gain such power?
8Why are they allowed to see
their children grow up?
9They have no worries at home,
and God never punishes them.
10Their cattle have lots of calves
without ever losing one;
11their children play and dance
safely by themselves.
12These people sing and celebrate
to the sound of tambourines,
small harps, and flutes,
13and they are successful,
without a worry,
until the day they die.
Leave Us Alone!
14Those who are evil say
to God All-Powerful,
“Leave us alone! Don't bother us
with your teachings.
15What do we gain from praying
and worshiping you?
16We succeeded all on our own.”
And so, I keep away from them
and their evil schemes.
17How often does God become angry
and send disaster and darkness
to punish sinners?
18How often does he strike them
like a windstorm
that scatters straw?
19You say, “God will punish
those sinners' children
in place of those sinners.”
But I say, “Let him punish
those sinners themselves
until they really feel it.
20Let God All-Powerful force them
to drink their own destruction
from the cup of his anger.
21Because after they are dead,
they won't care what happens
to their children.”
Who Can Tell God What To Do?
22Who can tell God what to do?
He judges powerful rulers.
* 23Some of us die prosperous,
24enjoying good health,
25while others die in poverty,
having known only pain.
26But we all end up dead,
beneath a blanket of worms.
27My friends, I know that you
are plotting against me.
28You ask, “Where is the home
of that important person
who does so much evil?”
29Everyone, near and far, agrees
30that those who do wrong
never suffer disaster,
when God becomes angry.
31No one points out their sin
or punishes them.
32Then at their funerals,
they are highly praised;
33the earth welcomes them home,
while crowds mourn.
34But empty, meaningless words
are the comfort you offer me.

1Job yaa tulisi ayen, 2<<Kpesi a wom mi wieŋa, basi ate kula chim sui yɔkka a te mu. 3Yik fidek abe mi a biisi ate m biika ŋaaŋnyiŋ, fi daa yaali fi nye mu a la.
4<<M funfɔblaŋa a cheŋ ka nuru jigi ya? Ka boa ale soa ate mi a yik m dega? 5Nya mi ate ku cha fu, ate fi pai nisa a lik fi nɔnni. 6Mi dan poli kude wari, yɔgsum ale ta mi, mi nyiŋka a gɔk kama.
7<<Ka boa ale soa ate wabaata nyam a kasim boro, a kpaŋ alege ate ba pagrimu a kasim a zuak? 8Ba a nya ba bisaŋa ate ba nya badek a kali a gilim ba, a nya ba ŋaaŋsaŋa ale ba nina. 9Ba yeeŋa jaab a kan daani ŋa ate yɔgsum a kan yik ba, Wen doani an bo ba zuwa. 10Ba lalisaŋa a kan biak a kpeeri, ba naab niimaŋa a ta ka bisa ŋa kan biak a basi. 11Ba basi ate ba bisaŋa a cheŋ ase piisa la, ba bi fiisaŋa a gɔk. 12Ba yi ba yiilaŋa a magsi ka kayaksa ale kpanta nakka, ba dɛ masim ale ka paampuuŋta kumsa. 13Ba pai ba benaŋa a ta ka ŋanta a yaa siŋ vɔrumu po ale suiyɔgni. 14Alege ba a weeni Wen ayen, <Basi ti tidek ti nyiini. Ti kan yaali ayen ti seba fi suitaŋa. 15Wen Dii Ale A Niak La ka wana, ate tama a tom a te wa? Ka boan nyuenta ate ti le nya nyini wa puusi teka po?> 16Alege ba ŋan paarika a ka badek nisa po, dila mi yalima kama ale wabaata nyama sinsaŋŋa.
17<<Wabaata nyam yega a kan kpabi a kpi. Ba kan kasim a nya kaasuŋŋoa. Wen sui a kan kasim a puuri ate wa a chari ba ninammoa. 18Viok a kan jam a ji ba a ta cheŋ ase kinkaa la. Va kiliŋ a kan jam a ji ba a ta cheŋ ase vɔtta la. 19Waai weeni kama ayen, <Wen a tigsi nuru wabaata a dueni a magsi ka wa nidoabilisa.> Basi ate Wen dek a tuni wabaata nyɔnɔwa ate wa seba. 20Basi ate wadek nina a nya wa kaasuŋku, basi ate wa nyu Wen Dii Ale A Niak La suipuurumu. 21Nuru kpiuk niŋ a ka dii ale a nye wa dɔkdem la po.
22<<Waai a baga a sak Wen yammoa, wa le toalim a bo baai ale bo wenzuk la buusa la? 23Nuru waai a nyiem ta nyiŋyɔgsa kama ate wari a kan daani wa ate wa ga kpi, 24wa nyiŋka a soa ka dek, wa kobaŋa a ta kpaam. 25Nuru wa choa a kpi ale suipuurum, wa an maa dɛ jamaŋ masimmoa. 26Alege ba meena ase chaab la a duak ka tantaŋa po ate nanzue a lik ba nyiŋsaŋa.
27<<Mi seba kama nalimnyiini ni le a poli diila, zɔk ŋaai ate ni le pai nye mi kaasi la. 28Ni a weeni ayen, <Nuru kpioŋku yenni a bo ka be, vi tii ate wabaata nyam a boro la?> 29Ni baga a zamsi baai ale a nyiem la jigi kama. Ni kpesi a nya ba wieŋa. 30Jaab a kan nye nuru bioku ase Wen sui a nin puuri, wa a nyini Wen namsika po a nyini kama. 31Ka wana ale biisi a zɛri wa nyeelaŋa wa nina po? Ka wana ale pilim a tuni wa, wa le nye diila? 32Ba ji wa a ta cheŋ boosuku po, ate ba a limisi vɔrumu. 33Tantaŋa ale bo viaka po la a masa a te wa, ate nuruba meena a va wa, ate baai ale kan ta chiina a dɛ wa niŋ.
34<<Dila fi le nye ka sɛ a yɔk mi sui ya ale fi betta biika? Jaab a ka fi tulisaŋa po alege ka venta.>>

english_text:
Eliphaz's Third Speech
What Use Are We Humans to God?
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
2 What use are we humans
to God,
even the wisest of us?
3If you were completely sinless,
that would still mean nothing
to God All-Powerful.
4Is he correcting you
for worshiping him?
5No! It's because of
your terrible and endless sins.
6To guarantee payment of a debt,
you have taken clothes
from innocent people.
7And you refused bread and water
to the hungry and thirsty,
8although you were rich,
respected, and powerful.
9You have turned away widows
and have broken the arms
of orphans.
10That's why you were suddenly
trapped by terror,
11blinded by darkness,
and drowned in a flood.
God Lives in the Heavens
12God lives in the heavens
above the highest stars,
where he sees everything.
13Do you think the deep darkness
hides you from God?
14Do thick clouds cover his eyes,
as he walks around heaven's dome
high above the earth?
15Give up those ancient ideas
believed by sinners,
16who were swept away
without warning.
17They rejected God All-Powerful,
feeling he was helpless,
18although he had been kind
to their families.
The beliefs of these sinners
are truly disgusting.
19When God's people see
the godless swept away,
they celebrate, 20saying,
“Our enemies are gone,
and fire has destroyed
their possessions.”
Surrender to God All-Powerful
21Surrender to God All-Powerful!
You will find peace
and prosperity.
22Listen to his teachings
and take them to heart.
23If you return to God
and turn from sin,
all will go well for you.
24So get rid of your finest gold,
as though it were sand.
25Let God All-Powerful
be your silver and gold,
26and you will find happiness
by worshiping him.
27God will answer your prayers,
and you will keep the promises
you made to him.
28He will do whatever you ask,
and life will be bright.
29When others are disgraced,
God will clear their names
in answer to your prayers.
30Even those who are guilty
will be forgiven,
because you obey God.
translation_text:
1Tema denɔwa Elifaz yaa tulisi ayen, 2<<Nuru an baga a ta nyuenta a te Wen ya. Yam nyɔnɔ an poom baga a te wa nyuenta. 3Ase fi dan jam ka wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ kula kan te Wen Dii Ale A Niak La suipeentiga. Wa kan nya nyuenta ase fi nin jam kan ta wakaasuŋŋoa.
4<<Daa fi le pai fidek a te wa la ale soa ate wa toariŋ fu alege ta chaab ale fu. 5Fi wabaataŋa a zuak kama. Fi wabaataŋa a ka kpeglimka. 6Fi yaali ayen fi suataŋa a pai ba ŋanta a dueni abe fi piem ba kinla nyiŋ, fi yeeri nuruba gatta alege ba chaboala. 7Fi an te baai ale jiak la nyiamoa ale peri ŋandiinta an te kɔm ale ta baai la. 8Ate fi le jam ta pagrim la, a ta tɛŋ ate ba a zuli fu, a bo ka po, 9ale basi ate pukɔga a cheŋ ale nikotta ale basi ate baai ale kan ta koba la, ŋman ka jagsim fii fiiga. 10Dila ale soa ate batta a gilim fu, dila ale soa ate biem a diiri fu ate fi kpaziim a nak la, 11dila ale soa ate ku nye legi ate fi kan nya la, ate dila ale soa ate nya pimpanta a lik fu.
12<<Wen an bo daa wenŋmazuk niŋniŋŋa? Nya chiŋmarisaŋa ale bo wenŋmazuk la ale zuak diila. 13Alege fi a weeni ayen, <Wen a seba ka boa? Wa a bo buusa legini de choa po? 14Chiŋma sobta ale lik wa, dila wa kan nya ti ase wa le a cheŋ wenŋmazuk gigilukku po la.> 15Kan kasim ta suik kpakka ate nuru baata a cheŋ ku po la. 16Ba kpi kama alege ate ba danni a paari, ba nyubaŋa nya pimpanta a ji ta cheŋ. 17Ba weeni Wen kama ayen, <Basi ti tidek ti nyiini! Wen Dii Ale A Niak La a baga a nye ka boa a te ti?> 18Alege ka wa abe le sueri ba yeeŋa ale ŋan maŋsa. Dila mi yalima kama ale wabaata nyam sinsaga.
19<<Wayɔrisima nyama a nya ba kaasuŋku kama a naŋ, baai ale kan seba wari nɔi po la a nye ba a la kama a weeni ayen, 20wensie ti dachaasaŋa ba kaasi ba kama, ate bolim a dɛ ba jigsika.
21<<Siak a te Wen abe fi ta suiyɔgni ale wa, suiku de po nye paarika ale jam fi jigi. 22Siak wa nɔi po sinsaga abe fi pai wa wieŋa a nyo fi suinum po. 23Fi dan pilim ŋmani Wen Dii Ale A Niak La jigi wa le tuesi fu. Ase fi dan yeeri biem fi viuku po ate bu yalima, 24ale pai fi ligmɔniŋka a basi tantaŋa po, fi Ofir ligmɔniŋka a basi vooliŋsaŋa pinaŋa po, 25Wen Dii Ale A Niak La yaa le chim fi ligmɔniŋ, kpana ŋaai ale nala a te fu. 26Wensie fi yaa le nya masim Wen Dii Ale A Niak La jigi ate fi le zak zuk a nya Wen. 27Fi le puusi a te wa ate wa wom fu, ate fi le tuni fi pumpuulimaŋa. 28Fi le a poli diila ale nye ate bolim a nyaksi fi suitaŋa po. 29Nuruba a dan siŋ tɛŋ ate fi weeni ayen, zak ba ŋmai, wa le vari baai sue ale kaasi la a basi. 30Wa le poom vari waai ale seba wie nɔi po la a basi, waai ale wa poom nya varibasika fi nisa ale welema la nyiŋ.>>

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
Today I Complain Bitterly
1Job said:
2Today I complain bitterly,
because God has been cruel
and made me suffer.
3If I knew where to find God,
I would go there
4and argue my case.
5Then I would discover
what he wanted to say.
6Would he overwhelm me
with his greatness?
No! He would listen
7because I am innocent,
and he would say,
“I now set you free!”
8I cannot find God anywhere—
in front or back of me,
9to my left or my right.
God is always at work,
though I never see him.
10But he knows what I am doing,
and when he tests me,
I will be pure as gold.
* 11I have never refused to follow
any of his commands,
12and I have always treasured
his teachings.
13But he alone is God,
and who can oppose him?
God does as he pleases,
14and he will do exactly
what he intends with me.
* 15Merely the thought
of God All-Powerful
16makes me tremble with fear.
17God has covered me
with darkness,
but I refuse to be silent.

1Job yaa tulisi ayen, 2<<Jinla mi funfɔblaŋa a poom tua ka na katikati, ale mi ŋuuni ka meena wa nisaŋa a dobra kama mi zuk. 3M dan poom seba ka m nin nya wa juijui la ate mi poom baga a cheŋ ka wa boka jigini. 4M le biisi mi le ta diila a dueni wa niŋ, abe m sueri m nɔnni ale nanpaga. 5M le nya wa le wa tulisi mu diila, abe m poli wa le wa weeni diila, 6Wa le pai pagrim kpiem a ta chaab ale mu? Aaya, wa kan pai wie a duŋ mu a ta chaab ale mu. 7Dula, wayɔrisima nuru ale baga a biisi wa wari a dueni wa niŋ, ate m le nya varibasika a nyini m boteerɔwa jigi.
8<<Alege m dan cheŋ konni po, wa ka dula, m dan cheŋ yeri niŋka, m kan nya wa. 9Wa be dan bo tuima wiilukku geŋ, m kan nya wa, wa be dan cheem cheŋ yeseoku, m kan chiak nya wa yilibi. 10Alege wa seba suik kuui ate mi a va la kama, wa dan chamsi mi a nya mi le nyini du ase ligmɔniŋ la. 11Mi kasim cheŋ a va wa kama, mi kasim va wa suiku kama ale kan cheem nakpiaga. 12Mi an basi wa nɔngbanvaataŋa po sinsaŋŋa, wa nɔnni po wieŋa a nye wari a te mi a gaam mi danni po ŋandiinta kama.
13<<Alege wa za ka wadek wa nyiini, ka wana ale wa tu chaab ale wa? Wa a nye ka dii ate wa a yaali la. 14Wa ta ka wa ŋmarisika a nyini peelim a ta chaab ale mi, alege diem ta zɔga yega ate ŋa doa. 15Dila ale soa ate mi kpaziim a nak wa niŋ, mi a dan poli nna meena, mi a chali wa kama. 16Wen a basi kama ate mi suinum a fuŋti, Wen Dii Ale A Niak La a basi kama ate mi kpaziim a nak. 17Alege legi ale nye nna kpitɔ a lik mi nina la an basi ate mi sina.

english_text:
Job Continues
Why Doesn't God Set a Time?
1Why doesn't God
set a time for court?
Why don't his people know
where he can be found?
2Sinners remove boundary markers
and take care of sheep
they have stolen.
3They cheat orphans and widows
by taking their donkeys
and oxen.
4The poor are trampled
and forced to hide
5in the desert,
where they and their children
must live like wild donkeys
and search for food.
6If they want grain or grapes,
they must go to the property
of these sinners.
7They sleep naked in the cold,
because they have no cover,
8and during a storm
their only shelters are caves
among the rocky cliffs.
9Children whose fathers have died
are taken from their mothers
as payment for a debt.
10Then they are forced to work
naked in the grain fields
because they have no clothes,
and they go hungry.
11They crush olives to make oil
and grapes to make wine—
but still they go thirsty.
12And along the city streets,
the wounded and dying cry out,
yet God does nothing.
Some Reject the Light
13Some rebel and refuse
to follow the light.
14Soon after sunset they murder
the poor and the needy,
and at night they steal.
15Others wait for the dark,
thinking they won't be seen
if they sleep with the wife
or husband of someone else.
16Robbers hide during the day,
then break in after dark
because they reject the light.
17They prefer night to day,
since the terrors of the night
are their friends.
Sinners Are Filthy Foam
18Those sinners are filthy foam
on the surface of the water.
And so, their fields and vineyards
will fall under a curse
and won't produce.
19Just as the heat of summer
swallows the snow,
the world of the dead
swallows those who sin.
20Forgotten here on earth,
and with their power broken,
they taste sweet to worms.
21Sinners take advantage of widows
and other helpless women.
22But God's mighty strength
destroys those in power.
Even if they seem successful,
they are doomed to fail.
23God may let them feel secure,
but they are never
out of his sight.
24Great for a while; gone forever!
Sinners are mowed down
like weeds,
then they wither and die.
25If I haven't spoken the truth,
then prove me wrong.
translation_text:
1<<Ka boa ale soa ate Wen Dii Ale A Niak La a kan dak daa a magsi buusa boka? Ka boa ale soa ate baai ale seba wa la a gisi daa ŋala kinla nyiŋŋa? 2Nuruba a zak tɛŋbana tintana, ba a nya pa ŋaai ate ba zu la zuk. 3Ba yiak kpiŋka boniŋka a ta cheŋ ale tuesi pukɔgini naamu a nya diipo ate wa le tuni wa pamini la. 4Ba fɛ yiak baai ale a silim la suiku po a basi ale fɛ tɛŋka ŋanjaksaŋa meena ate ba suk. 5Dila ŋanjaksaŋa ase bon waarisa la a bo gɔi koruk po ayen ba te ba bisaŋa ŋandiinta. 6Ba a tigsi ŋandiinta laŋsaŋa po ale a yiisi wabaata nyama kaduksaŋa po. 7Ba le a silim gatta la ba bo yokku po meena ale ka chaboala, ba ka jaaboa a lik badek ale ŋootaŋa. 8Ŋmorukku ale a lo pinaŋa zuk la a yɔk ba ka meena, ate ba bobi pinaŋa giŋgiŋ jaab ale kan boro a lik ba la nyiŋ. 9Biik kaai ale kan ta ko la ba chiak wa biisiri ŋoosika po, jajakka bulueku ba fɛ tuesi wa pami nyiŋ. 10Ba le a silim gatta la, ba yaa nyiem ale chaboala, ba ji boba, alege a cheŋ kɔm. 11Ba a ŋmiak yɔna a nya kpaam ale daam, alege badek nyanyuila a ta ba. 12Baai ale a kpi la ŋuunika a jueli kama tɛŋka po, ate baai ale kɔni la a kaari a yaali maarika. Alege Wen a ka wari ale waai nye kaasika.
13<<Baai ale boro a ta chaab ale bolimu, baai ale kan seba bu suitaŋa yaase ba bo bu suitaŋa po. 14Danni kantueŋka a dan cheŋ, nuru koorika a yiti kama a ko ŋanjaksaŋa ale baai ale a silim la, yokku wa a zu kama ase zue la. 15Nidoa kaboŋ nyeerika a limisi ka tɛŋ sob paalik, wa a poli kama ayen, waai a kan nya mi, ale lik wa ninaŋa. 16Legi po, nuruba a wɛ a jo ka yie po, alege kantueŋ ba lik badek a basi dina po, ba ka wari a nye ale bolimoa. 17Legi a nye ase ka saluik a te ba meena, bade ka doaba ale legi nyinyigsaŋa nyama.
18<<Dila meena ba ka puuk nyiam zuk, ba le soa tɛŋka kauk kuui la ka kikaasa, dila waai a kan cheŋ kaduksaŋa jigi ya. 19Ase tuiluk ale kosik ale basi ate ŋmoruk tana a nyaliŋ a bɛ diila, vɔrumu a basi ate wabaata nyama a nye ka dila. 20Luikku a baŋ ba wari, ate nanzue a dɛ ba, ba an ŋmaa teeri nuru baata wari ya alege ba wɛ kama ase tiib la. 21Ku nye kama dii nyiŋla ban nye pukɔga a magsi ya ale an sak jiirim ale baai ale kan ta bisa la. 22Alege Wen a dari baai ale pagra la kama a vuuri ale wa pagrimu a ta cheŋ, ba le ba kali paarika meena, ba zɛ ba nyuvooŋa wari chak ya. 23Dai dii dai wa le basi ate ba vuusi a poli ayen wari a kan daani, alege wa ninaŋa a nya ka ba suitaŋa po. 24Ba le nya zak zaanka magadega ate ba ŋman cheŋ, ba le siŋ tɛŋ ate ba tigsi ba ase nuru yonta la, ba le gebi ba basi ase ŋanbie zuima la.
25<<Kude dan kan daa di, ka wana le wa sak ayen mi a velim ate mi wieŋa a chim kinla?>>

english_text:
Bildad's Third Speech
God Is the One To Fear
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2God is the one to fear,
because God is in control
and rules the heavens.
3Who can count his army of stars?
Isn't God the source of light?
4How can anyone be innocent
in the sight of God?
5To him, not even the light
of the moon and stars
can ever be pure.
6So how can we humans,
when we are merely worms?
translation_text: 1Suya denɔwa Bildad yaa tulisi ayen, 2<<Pagrim ale yɔgsum chala ka Wen ale soa, wa le basi ate yomsi magsika a bo wenŋmazukku niŋniŋŋa. 3Ka wana ale baga wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma a chiini? Ka wana zuk ate wa bolimu a kan nya? 4Nuru yaa be le nye ka sɛ a chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ Wen niŋŋa? Waai ate nipok a biak la ale nye ka sɛ a nye cheri? 5Chiika a dan kan poom a nya ate chiŋmarisaŋa an nye cheri wa nina po, 6alege ka nuru ale kan daa jaaboa alege ka nanzuiri, saalɔ biiga waai ale ka mimenuŋ.>>

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
You Have Really Been Helpful
1Job said:
2You have really been helpful
to someone weak and weary.
3You have given great advice
and wonderful wisdom
to someone truly in need.
4How can anyone possibly speak
with such understanding?
5Remember the terrible trembling
of those in the world of the dead
below the mighty ocean.
6Nothing in that land
of death and destruction
is hidden from God,
7who hung the northern sky
and suspended the earth
on empty space.
8God stores water in clouds,
but they don't burst,
9and he wraps them around
the face of the moon.
10On the surface of the ocean,
God has drawn a boundary line
between light and darkness.
11And columns supporting the sky
tremble at his command.
12By his power and wisdom,
God conquered the force
of the mighty ocean.
13The heavens became bright
when he breathed,
and the escaping sea monster
died at his hands.
14These things are merely a whisper
of God's power at work.
How little we would understand
if this whisper
ever turned into thunder!
translation_text:
1Job yaa tulisi ayen, 2<<Fi bola a maari baai nisima ale kan ta pagrim la kama. Fi vari baai nisima ale kan pagra la a basi kama chekki. 3Sinsak ŋaai chaab ate fi pai te waai ale kan ta yam la, ale nyaasim kpiem buui ate fi sak la. 4Ka wana ale maari fi ate fi biisi wieŋa de? Ka wana chiik abe le biisi fi nɔi po?
5<<Baai ale kpi la a bo ka ninam po, baai ale bo nyaataŋa tɛŋ la ale baai ale bo ba po la. 6Kum ta ka chaboala Wen niŋ, Kaasuŋ a doa kama an lik ya. 7Wa yarinti wiiluk geŋka wenŋmazuimaŋa wenzuk koroku po, wa an pai tɛŋka a yik jaab nyiŋŋa. 8Wa kpamsi nyaataŋa wa chiŋmaaŋa po, alege chiŋmaaŋa a kan na cheeri dobrimu nyiŋŋa. 9Wa lik chiika meena nina, a pati wa chiŋmanni ka zuk. 10Wa daani ka dindaanuŋ woŋ a chibli nyaataŋa zuk, a gaari danni kantueŋka legini po. 11Wenŋmazukku zaŋŋa a choa dii nyiŋla wa toariŋka a cha ba kama. 12Wa pai wa pagrimu a choa nyakpiemu, a pai wa yammu a gebi jachichimini nna munamuna. 13Wa vuusumu ale basi ate wenzuk a nye cheri, ate wa nisaŋa a ko waamu. 14Alege ŋade ka wa pagrimu nyima nyima ate ti a nya, ka waasika nyiini ate ti a wom ka wana ale baga a miŋ wa pagrimu nampaŋsaŋa?>>

english_text:
Job Continues
I Am Desperate
1Job said:
2I am desperate because
God All-Powerful refuses
to do what is right.
As surely as God lives,
3and while he gives me breath,
4I will tell only the truth.
5Until the day I die,
I will refuse to do wrong
by saying you are right,
6because each day my conscience
agrees that I am innocent.
7I pray that my enemies
will suffer no less
than the wicked.
8Such people are hopeless,
and God All-Powerful
will cut them down,
9without listening
when they beg for mercy.
10And that is what God should do,
because they don't like him
or ever pray.
11Now I will explain in detail
what God All-Powerful does.
12All of you have seen these things
for yourselves.
So you have no excuse.
How God Treats the Wicked
13Here is how God All-Powerful
treats those who are wicked
and brutal.
14They may have many children,
but most of them will go hungry
or suffer a violent death.
15Others will die of disease,
and their widows
won't be able to weep.
16The wicked may collect riches
and clothes in abundance
as easily as clay.
17But God's people will wear
clothes taken from them
and divide up their riches.
18No homes built by the wicked
will outlast a cocoon
or a shack.
19Those sinners may go to bed rich,
but they will wake up poor.
20Terror will strike at night
like a flood or a storm.
21Then a scorching wind
will sweep them away
22without showing mercy,
as they try to escape.
23At last, the wind will celebrate
because they are gone.
translation_text:
1Ate Job a diem biisi a cheŋ ayen, 2<<Wen ale sum boro la, waai ale mini mi nyemagsika la, Wen Dii Ale A Niak La waai ale basi ate mi lam tuem nna katikati la, 3ate mi toalim ta nyuvuri la, Wen vuusumu a bo mi nyue vieŋa po la, 4mi nɔngbanvaataŋa a kan biisi biemmoa, ate mi giŋgeluŋku nna a kan biisi venta. 5Mi kan siak ayen ni nye magsi, ate mi ga kpi, mi kan zɛri mi wensieŋa. 6Mi le ta mi wayɔrisimaŋa abe m kan maa basi ate ŋa cheŋ, mi popola abe kan ŋma mi mi boka po meena.
7<<Mi dachaasaŋa abe tu ninam ase wabaata nyama la, mi dachaasaŋa abe nam ase baai ale kan ta nyemagsika la. 8Baai ale kan ta Wen la a ta ka boan yiila ase ba nin gebi wa basi, ase Wen a nin yeeri wa nyuvunni? 9Wen a wom wa kumsa ase daanika a nin jam wa zuwa? 10Wa sui ale peenti ale Wen Dii Ale A Niak La ya? Wa le kasim a wi Wen ya?
11<<M le sak fu Wen pagrimu wari, Wen Dii Ale A Niak La suitaŋa, m kan sugi. 12Ni meena a nya nna kama nidek. Ka boan be le soa a ka kiri biika de?
13<<Charuku de ate Wen a pai a te wabaata nyama, nyeka tuem nyɔnɔwa nitalimu ate wa a tuesi Wen Dii Ale A Niak La jigi la. 14Wa bisaŋa yega charuku ka gebika wa bisaŋa a kan nya ŋandiinta a zuak a de. 15Nyiŋtuila ale ko baai ale vuuk la, ate ba pukɔŋŋa a kan kum ba nyiŋŋa. 16Wa pai ka kpana a vi chaab ase tanta la, ale gatta a vi chaab ase yak la, 17ŋan baai ate wa pai dueni la wayɔrisima nyam ale ba jo ba, ate baai ale kan seba wari nɔi po la a pai kpanaŋa a chari chaab. 18Ye dii ate wa a sɛ la a nye ase ka narik baruk la, a nye ase ka limisidɔ ale ti kusuŋ la. 19Wa doa kama a jigsi, alege wa kan ŋman nye dila, wa dan lak wa ninaŋa jaab meena a cheŋ kama. 20Nyinyigsa nyam ale diiri wa ase nyiam ale mobi la, viok ale ji wa yok a ta cheŋ. 21Kori viok ale ji wa ta cheŋ, ate wa cheŋ, ku ji wa a ta nyini wa jigini a cheŋ. 22Ku le fuk wa a kan ta jiirimmoa ase wa ale a chali ayen wa bɛ la. 23Ku a nak ka nisima ale siak ale a siisi ayen wa nyini wa jigini.

english_text:
Job Continues
Gold and Silver Are Mined
1Gold and silver are mined,
then purified;
2the same is done
with iron and copper.
3Miners carry lanterns
deep into the darkness
to search for these metals.
4They dig tunnels
in distant, unknown places,
where they dangle by ropes.
5Far beneath the grain fields,
fires are built
to break loose those rocks
6that have jewels or gold.
7Miners go to places unseen
by the eyes of hawks;
8they walk on soil unknown
to the proudest lions.
9With their own hands
they remove sharp rocks
and uproot mountains.
10They dig through the rocks
in search of jewels
and precious metals.
11They also uncover
the sources of rivers
and discover secret places.
Where Is Wisdom Found?
12 But where is wisdom found?
13 No human knows the way.
14Nor can it be discovered
in the deepest sea.
* 15It is worth much more
than silver or pure gold
16or precious stones.
17Nothing is its equal—
not gold or costly glass.
18Wisdom is worth much more than
coral, jasper, or rubies.
19All the topaz of Ethiopia
and the finest gold
cannot compare with it.
20Where then is wisdom?
21It is hidden from human eyes
and even from birds.
22Death and destruction
have merely heard rumors
about where it is found.
23 God is the only one who knows
the way to wisdom;
24he alone sees everything
beneath the heavens.
25When God divided out
the wind and the water,
26and when he decided the path
for rain and lightning,
27 he also determined the truth
and defined wisdom.
28 God told us, “Wisdom means
that you respect me, the Lord,
and turn from sin.”
translation_text:
1<<Jigi ale boro ate ba a tu vɔrup a yeeri kpana ate jigi a boro ate ba a soti ligmɔniŋ. 2Ba tu a yeeri kutuk ka tɛŋ, ale nyaliŋ a yeeri kutuk mɔnuŋ tana po. 3Nuruba ta bolim kama a jo legi kpienni po a gisi a paari tɛŋ niŋniŋŋa a tu a yeeri tintana legini po. 4Wa tu ka vɔrup juijui ale yalima ate nuruba a kan boro la, yaase ba nyiem du a nya la. Dula jigini wa a tom ka wadek wa nyiini, a yik miisa golukku po. 5Tɛŋ kaai ate ŋandiinta a nyini du a jam la, bolim a tagri ka kama tɛŋ, 6tintain sobta ale bo pinaŋa po ate ŋa tanta ligmɔniŋ a boro. 7Nuim a karo a seba susuga suik kula, wobik a karo ate ka nina a nya ku. 8Duŋ waarisa an tabi naŋ du, gbeŋli abe an nyiem dula. 9Nuru a tu pina ŋaai ale pagra kama, a tu guuta kie po. 10Wa che piuŋku po a jo, ate wa ninaŋa a nya tuilum ŋanta. 11Wa tu a va benni vuutaŋa, a ta jabuui ale suk la a nyini.
12<<Alege yam a bo ka bɛ? Miŋka a bo ka bɛ? 13Nuru a kan miŋ bu tuilummoa, fi an baga a nya bu ŋanvuta tɛŋka po. 14Juijui ale limisa la a weeni ayen, <Bu ka ale mi>, nyakpiemu a weeni ayen, <Bu ka ale mi.> 15Ba kan da bu ale ligmɔniŋ maŋŋa, yaase bu diaka a magsi ale kpana. 16Ba kan da bu ale Ofir ligmɔniŋka, yaase tintain ŋaai ale gamisi yaase tintain sobta, 17yaase ligmɔniŋ ale tintain salima a magsi chaab ale bu yaase bu da ale ligmɔniŋ ŋansuinta. 18Kanbieŋsa ale tintain mɔnta a poom ka wi ka, yam diak a gaam tintain munta kama. 19Kus tintain ŋaai ale a nye ase dubuulim la a kan magsi chaab ale bu, bu kan da ale ligmɔniŋ maŋŋa.
20<<Yam yaa be nyini ka be? Miŋka a bo ka bɛ? 21Bu suk kama javuk meena nina po, a poom suk wenzuk nuinsaŋa jigi. 22Kaasuŋ ale Kum a weeni kama ayen, <<Ka bu wie ale jo tama tue.>> 23Wen nyiini ale a miŋ suik kuui ale a cheŋ bu jigi la, wa nyiini abe le seba bu le bo juijui la, 24diila wa le a nya tɛŋka kpeglimka meena ale a nya jaab meena ale bo tɛŋzuk la. 25Wa le te vioku pagrim ale magsi nyaataŋa, 26wa le te suik ayen ŋmorukku a ni ale te ŋmoruk vioku suik, 27wa yaa nya yam a weeni bu tuilum ale ka diila, a yaa sak bu wensie ale ka diila ale chamsi bu a nya. 28Ate wa yaa weeni nuru ayen, <<Nyɔnɔwa yɔgsum chalika ka yam, fi be dan zɛri biem ka miŋka.>>

english_text:
Job Continues
I Long for the Past
1Job said:
2I long for the past,
when God took care of me,
3and the light from his lamp
showed me the way
through the dark.
4I was in the prime of life,
God All-Powerful
was my closest friend,
5and all of my children
were nearby.
6My herds gave enough milk
to bathe my feet,
and from my olive harvest
flowed rivers of oil.
* 7When I sat down at the meeting
of the city council,
8the young leaders stepped aside,
* 9while the older ones stood
10and remained silent.
Everyone Was Pleased
11Everyone was pleased
with what I said and did.
12When poor people or orphans
cried out for help,
I came to their rescue.
13And I was highly praised
for my generosity to widows
and others in poverty.
14Kindness and justice
were my coat and hat;
15I was helpful to the blind
and to the lame.
16I was a father to the needy,
and I defended them in court,
even if they were strangers.
17When criminals attacked,
I broke their teeth
and set their victims free.
18I felt certain that I would live
a long and happy life,
then die in my own bed.
19In those days I was strong
like a tree with deep roots
and with plenty of water,
20or like an archer's new bow.
21Everyone listened in silence
to my welcome advice,
22and when I finished speaking,
nothing needed to be said.
23My words were eagerly accepted
like the showers of spring,
24and the smile on my face
renewed everyone's hopes.
25My advice was followed
as though I were a king
leading my troops,
or someone comforting
those in sorrow.
translation_text:
1Job yaa diem biisi a cheŋ ayen,
2<<Mi ale yaali chiik sii ale taam la a soa diila, da ŋaai ate Wen a jam a nya mi zuk la, 3diipo ate wa zeuŋku a nya mi zuk la ate wa bolimu nyiŋ mi cheŋ a va legi po a taam. 4Da ŋaai ate mi diem paala la, ate Wen doataŋa ale mi a ta niauŋ a jam mi yenni la, 5diipo ate Wen Dii Ale A Niak La a jam bo le mi la ate mi bisaŋa a gilim wa la, 6diipo ate mi niiŋa ale mi buaŋa a te biisim yega la ate pinaŋa po mi nya kpaam yega a nyini kpaam tiisaŋa po la.
7<<Mi ale cheŋ tɛŋka nansuiŋku la a yaa kali nuruma po la, 8nidoa paalukku a nya mi a ga zaani nakpiak ate nidoa kpagsaŋa a yiti a zaani. 9Niŋdeerɔma a basi biik ale lik ba noaŋa ale ba nisima. 10Nuru kpientaŋa a nye diki, ate ba giŋgeluŋtaŋa a kpari maŋ ba laŋtisaŋa. 11Nuru waai dek ale wom mi la a biisi mi wie kama ale suipeentik, ate baai ale nya mi la a pak mi, 12dii nyiŋla mi vari ŋanjaksaŋa ale kaari a yaali maarika la kama a basi, ale baai ale kan ta koba ate ba a maari ba la. 13Nuru waai ale jam boro a kpi la a niak mi. Mi basi ate pukɔgini a lenni yiila wa suinummu po. 14Mi wayɔrisimaŋa a nye ase ka gatta la, mi nyemagsika a nye ase garuk woŋ ale mi garuk pali la. 15Mi jam chim ka yeema nina ale gbaruktaŋa naŋsa. 16Mi jam chim ka ko a te baai ale a silim la ale maari nicham ba daanika po. 17Mi wɛ gaasa nyɔnɔwa nyinaŋa kama ale vari baai ate wa ta la a basi.
18<<Mi poli kama ayen, <Mi le kpi mi dek yenni po, mi daaŋa ale piisi dii ase tintain busuŋ zaa la. 19Mi poli kama ayen mi tɛŋ naŋsaŋa ale siŋ a paari nyiamu, ate maglimu ale lo m ŋmazuk naŋsaŋa zuk yokku meena. 20Mi zulaŋa ale bo le mu paalik paaliga, tommu ale kasim paala m nisa po.>
21<<Nuruba a wom mi kama ale a yiili, a sina ale a limisi mi sinsaga. 22Mi ale biisi la ŋaaŋnyiŋ ba an ŋman biisi ya, mi wieŋa a lo kama nna ŋmam ba tueŋa po. 23Ba limisi mi kama ase nuruba ale a limisi ŋmoruk la, a yaa nyu mi wieŋa ase tɛŋsik ŋmoruk la. 24Mi ale nya ba a la la, ku yaa cha ba, mi ninaŋa bolimu a jam ta ka tuilum a te ba. 25Mi yaa lueri suiku a te ba, ale kali ase naab la wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma suŋsuŋ. Mi jam nye ase ka waai ale a yɔk baai ale a kum la sue la.

english_text:
Job Continues
Young People Now Insult Me
1Young people now insult me,
although their fathers
would have been a disgrace
to my sheep dogs.
2And those who insult me
are helpless themselves.
3They must claw the desert sand
in the dark for something
to satisfy their hunger.
4They gather tasteless shrubs
for food and firewood,
5and they are run out of towns,
as though they were thieves.
6Their only homes are ditches
or holes between rocks,
7where they bray like donkeys
gathering around shrubs.
8And like senseless donkeys
they are chased away.
Those Worthless Nobodies
9Those worthless nobodies
make up jokes and songs
to disgrace me.
10They are hateful
and keep their distance,
even while spitting
in my direction.
11God has destroyed me,
and so they don't care
what they do.
12Their attacks never stop,
though I am defenseless,
and my feet are trapped.
13Without any help,
they prevent my escape,
destroying me completely
14and leaving me crushed.
15Terror has me surrounded;
my reputation and my riches
have vanished like a cloud.
I Am Sick at Heart
16I am sick at heart!
Pain has taken its toll.
17Night chews on my bones,
causing endless torment,
18and God has shrunk my skin,
choking me to death.
19I have been thrown in the dirt
and now am dirt myself.
20I beg God for help,
but there is no answer;
and when I stand up,
he simply stares.
21God has turned brutal,
22stirring up a windstorm
to toss me about.
23Soon he will send me home
to the world of the dead,
where we all must go.
24No one refuses help to others,
when disaster strikes.
25I mourned for the poor
and those who suffered.
26But when I beg for relief
and light,
all I receive are disaster
and darkness.
27My stomach is tied in knots;
pain is my daily companion.
28My days are dark and gloomy
and in the city council
I stand and cry out,
29making mournful sounds
like jackals and owls.
30My skin is so parched,
that it peels right off,
and my bones are burning.
31My only songs are sorrow
and sadness.
translation_text:
1<<Alege yɔgyɔgla de ba nye mi a la kama, nuru baai ale paala a gaam mi, baai koba ate mi tin kan yaali ayen ba maari mi baasa a nya mi piisa zuwa. 2Ba nisima pagrimu a ta ka boan tuini a te mi, ba pagrimu ale toalim nyini ba po la? 3Ba le jiak ale ŋanyaalinta ale kɔm la, ba nyiem ka tɛŋ kosikka po tɛŋ kaai ale doa kinla la yokku. 4Gɔnni po ba yaa tigsi va tii ale ta yesa la, ate ba ŋandiintaŋa a chim tiib tɛŋ naŋsaŋa. 5Ba jam yiak ba kama badek nuruma po, a na ba ase zueba la. 6Ba jam fɛ kama a bo beli naŋ kosikka po, pinaŋa po ale tɛŋka vie po. 7Ba yaa a wooli tiisaŋa po ale gurum badek ale yɔgsum tiisaŋa tɛŋ. 8A ka kiri nuru baai ale kan ta yuei ya ate ba yiak ba tɛŋka po.
9<<Ate yɔgyɔgla de ba nidoabilisaŋa a pai yiili a nye mi a la. Mi yaa chim ka ja laam ba po. 10Ba kisi mi kama ale yalima ale mi, ba poom kan kpaliŋ ba chesi tintueta a basi mi nimbie po. 11Yɔgyɔgla de ate Wen a kaasi mi tommu ate mi a wobsa la ba yaa nye ba le a yaali diila a gilim mi. 12Mi juga geŋ buuni a siti mi, a bari mi batta, a gilim ayen ba ko mi. 13Ba wɛ mi suiku kama, ba nya suik kama a kaasi mi alege waai an maari ba. 14Ba kasim a duŋ kama a kasi mi, a kasim a ŋɔriŋ mi. 15Nyigsika a nya ka pagrim mi zuk, mi zulaŋa a cheŋ kama ase viok la, ate mi ale soa m dek diila a muriŋ bɛ ase chiŋmari la.
16<<Yɔgyɔgla de mi nyuvunni a muriŋ a bɛ kama, ninam daa ale yik mi. 17Yɔkku a chub mi kobaŋa kama, mi kan nya vuusum ale mi nyiŋdommaŋa. 18Alege Wen pagrim kpiemu po wa chim ka garuk a te mu, wa a bobi mu ase ka m garukku ŋinni la. 19Wa yuk mi a basi bagta po, ate mi yaa chim tanta ale buntuem.
20<<Mi a kaari a te fu, Wen yaa, alege fi an tulisi ya, mi yiti zaani ŋmai, alege fi an potim a nya mi. 21Fi cheem mi zuk kama ale nyeka tuem, ale fi nisa pagrimu fi siti mu. 22Fi chiak mi wenzuk a yaa yiak mi a basi vioku niŋ, a tɔŋ mi a basi vamuniŋka po. 23Mi seba fi le ta mi siŋ jam kum po, juijui ate fi lueri ate ŋanvuta meena ale cheŋ la.
24<<Chekki nuru a karo a pai nisa a tiri waai ale ŋɔriŋ yaase wa nin kaari a yaali maarika wa daanika po. 25Mi an jam kum te baai ale bo daanika po la? Ku an daani mi chiika ŋanjaksaŋa nyiŋŋa? 26Alege mi ale jam a yiili a limisi nalim la, biem ale jan jam, mi ale jam a gisi bolim la, legi ale jan jam. 27Choa kaai ale bo mi po la kan maara basi, ninam daa ale a tu mu. 28Mi a nyiem kama nna timtim, alege daa wenbinni ale nye ya, mi za ka tigsuŋku po a kaari a yaali maarika. 29Mi yaa chim ka suemkpatta suok, viuta vaanchoa. 30Mi nyiŋ gbaŋka a sobri kama ale a luenti, mi nyiŋka a dɛ kama ale nyiŋ toliŋka. 31Mi kpanuŋku nakka a tagri chim ka kumsa ate m paampuuŋku peerika a chim kaarik.

english_text:
Job Continues
I Promised Myself
1I promised myself
never to stare with desire
at a young woman.
2God All-Powerful punishes
men who do that.
3In fact, God sends disaster
on all who sin,
4and he keeps a close watch
on everything I do.
5I am not dishonest or deceitful,
6and I beg God to prove
my innocence.
7If I have disobeyed him
or even wanted to,
8then others can eat my harvest
and uproot my crops.
9If I have desired someone's wife
and chased after her,
10then let some stranger
steal my wife from me.
11If I took someone's wife,
it would be a horrible crime,
12sending me to destruction
and my crops to the flames.
13When my servants
complained against me,
I was fair to them.
14Otherwise, what answer
would I give to God
when he judges me?
15After all, God is the one
who gave life to each of us
before we were born.
I Have Never Cheated Anyone
16 I have never cheated widows
or others in need,
17and I have always shared
my food with orphans.
18Since the time I was young,
I have cared for orphans
and helped widows.
19I provided clothes for the poor,
20and I was praised
for supplying woolen garments
to keep them warm.
21If I have ever raised my arm
to threaten an orphan
when the power was mine,
22I hope that arm will fall
from its socket.
23I could not have been abusive;
I was terrified at the thought
that God might punish me.
24 I have never trusted
the power of wealth,
25or taken pride in owning
many possessions.
* 26I have never openly or secretly
27worshiped the sun or moon.
28Such horrible sins
would have deserved
punishment from God.
29I have never laughed
when my enemies
were struck by disaster.
30Neither have I sinned
by asking God
to send down on them
the curse of death.
31No one ever went hungry
at my house,
32and travelers
were always welcome.
33Many have attempted to hide
their sins from others—
but I refused.
34And the fear of public disgrace
never forced me to keep silent
about what I had done.
Why Doesn't God Listen?
35Why doesn't God All-Powerful
listen and answer?
If God has something against me,
let him speak up
or put it in writing!
36Then I would wear his charges
on my clothes and forehead.
37And with my head held high,
I would tell him everything
I have ever done.
38I have never mistreated
the land I farmed
and made it mourn.
39Nor have I cheated
my workers
and caused them pain.
40If I had, I would pray
for weeds instead of wheat
to grow in my fields.
After saying these things,
Job was silent.
translation_text:
1<<Mi nye ka nɔiyeŋ ale mi ninaŋa ayen mi kan nya nipokbili ale kɔrisa. 2Nurubiik charuku ka boa a bo Wen jigi wenŋmazuk wa, wa nitalimu Wen Dii Ale A Niak La jigi wenzuk wa? 3Ku daa kaasika a te wabaata nyama, kaasuŋ a te baai ale nye kaasi la? 4Wa kan nya mi suitaŋa, ale a chiini mi naŋsa tabika meena?
5<<Ase mi dan cheŋ venta po yaase mi naŋ a nye mwuli a vi pimpaasima 6basi ate Wen a magsi mu wensie ŋanmagsinta zuk ate wa seba ayen mi a ka kaasuŋŋoa, 7ase mi naŋsa a dan viriŋ a basi suiku, yaase mi ninaŋa a dan tagri mi suinummu yaase mi nisaŋa a taŋ, 8nuru yonta abe dɛ mi ale bori jabuui la, abe ba voori m ŋanborintaŋa.
9<<Ase mi suinummu a dan siak te nipok pimpaasima, yaase m nak waai ale moata mu la tuok, 10m powa abe num nidoa yoŋ zom, abe nuru yonta a goa ale wa. 11Dila ate le chim ka chivie, wabiok kuui ale magsi buusa boka. 12Ka bolim buui ale a dɛ a ga a kaasi, bu ti dɛ m ŋancheentaŋa.
13<<Ase mi dan jam zɛri mi nidoa tomteerɔma ale nipok tomteerɔma nyemagsika kama ba le jam, ta chaab ale mi ale ba funfɔblaŋa, 14mi ale nye ka sɛ ase Wen a nin tu mu? Mi le tulisi ayen ka boa ase wa nin wi mu ayen m tɔgi? 15Daa wa waai ale nye mi luikku po la ale nye ba? Daa wadek ale daani tama ti mama puusa po?
16<<Ase mi nin zɛri an te ŋanjaksaŋa ba ŋan yaalinta yaase m basi ate pukɔga a dɛ niniga, 17ase mi nin peri ŋandiinta a te m dek alege an chari ale kpiŋsa, 18alege a nyini mi biik po mi nya wa zuk kama ase ko la, a nyini m biam po m gani pukɔga. 19Ase mi nin nya waai ate wa a kpi wa le a silim garuk la nyiŋ, yaase nuru waai ale kan ta jaab a lik wa dega, 20ate wa suinum an niak mi mi ale te wa ale m piisaŋa kɔbtaŋa la nyiŋŋa. 21Ase mi nin zak nisa a ta chaab ale kpiŋsa, ale seba ayen mi le biisi buusa dɔkku po a nyini, 22be basi ate m nisimaŋa a passi a lo, basi ate si wɛ si tomaŋa po. 23Diila mi a chali kaasuŋ Wen jigi kama, mi an baga a nye wa ŋala chaaba dii nyiŋla mi a chali ka yɔgsum ale wa nyaksika.
24<<Ase mi nin pai mi mariŋka a basi ligmɔniŋ zuk yaase m weeni ligmɔniŋ kaai ale nye cheri ayen, <Fi ka m ligrɔ,> 25ase mi nin a naŋ m ŋanpaarika nyiŋ, m zusɔŋku nyiŋ ate m nisima a nya nyuen tii la, 26ase mi niŋ a nin bo wenbinni ale di nyaksika po yaase chiika ale ka nalimu po, 27ate dila a suk paasi mi suinum ate mi nisa a te ba zula, 28ŋade meena ate le chim wabaata a magsi buusa boka, dii nyiŋla mi ate kan ta wensie ale Wen dii ale bo wenŋmazuk la.
29<<Ase mi a dan naŋ mi dachiak zubiok nyiŋ yaase m sui a peenti daanika ale jam wa zuk la, 30alege mi an lak mi nɔnni a nye wabiok a ka a te wa. 31Mi yenni demma a nin maa weeni ayen, <Ka wana ale kan de Job ŋandiintaŋa a chak ya?> 32alege nichaanɔ an goa peelim yowa, diila mi tuoku kasim lak a te nyeendɔba. 33Mi an suk m wabaataŋa ase nuruba ale a nye diila, mi an suk m foolaawa m suinum po, 34dii nyiŋla mi a chali nuru boanni kama ate m kpaziim a nak yezuima ale a zɛri mu la ate mi nye diki a kan nyini peelimmoa.
35<<Mi dan ta ka waai ate wa a wom mu. Mi ŋmarisika m yuenni a magsi m varibasika. Wen Dii Ale A Niak La abe tulisi mu. Waai ale a ŋma mu la abe ŋmarisi a nyo gbaŋ po. 36Chekki m le pai ka a yi ka m ŋmankpaluk, m le pai a su ase ka naam zutɔk la. 37M le chiini m naŋ tabika meena a te wa. Ase nabiik la m le cheŋ wa jigi.
38<<Ase mi tɛŋka a dan kaari a ta chaab ale mi ate ka vuutaŋa meena a yɔk ale ninyaata, 39ase mi a dan dɛ ka ŋanta meena alege an tuni ya yaase m kaasi ka baai ale bo tɛŋka po la sue, 40muŋkangɔtisa abe nyini alege daa ŋanbie, wuuta abe nyini alege daa ŋankpaanta.>> Job wieŋa a kpeglim ya.

english_text:
Elihu Is Upset with Job's Friends
1Finally, these three men stopped arguing with Job, because he refused to admit he was guilty.
2Elihu from Buz was there, and he had become upset with Job for blaming God instead of himself. 3He was also angry with Job's three friends for not being able to prove that Job was wrong. 4Elihu was younger than these three, and he let them speak first. 5But he became irritated when they could not answer Job, 6and he said to them:
I am much younger than you,
so I have shown respect
by keeping silent.
7I once believed age
was the source of wisdom;
8now I truly realize
wisdom comes from God.
9Age is no guarantee of wisdom
and understanding.
10That's why I ask you
to listen to me.
I Eagerly Listened
* 11I eagerly listened
to each of your arguments,
12but not one of you proved
Job to be wrong.
13You shouldn't say,
“We know what's right!
Let God punish him.”
14Job hasn't spoken against me,
and so I won't answer him
with your arguments.
15All of you are shocked;
you don't know what to say.
16But am I to remain silent,
just because you
have stopped speaking?
17No! I will give my opinion,
18because I have so much to say,
that I can't keep quiet.
19I am like a swollen wineskin,
and I will burst
20if I don't speak.
* 21I don't know how to be unfair
or to flatter anyone—
22if I did, my Creator
would quickly destroy me!
translation_text:
1Dila nuruba batawa de yaa basi Job tulisika, dii nyiŋla wa jam ka wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ wadek nimbie po. 2Alege Buz denɔwa Barakel nidoabinni Eliyu, ale nyini Aram dɔkdemma po la, sui yaa puuri ale Job wa le weeni ayen wa nye magsi alege daa Wen la. 3Wa sui ale jam puuri mɛ ale Job doaba batawa, dii nyiŋla ba an baga a biisi a gaam Job ale gonti biisi wa a kaasi. 4Eliyu a jam limisi kama an biisi ya diila ba jam kpiem wa kama. 5Alege wa le jam nya ayen nidoaba batawa a ŋman ka wari a weeni la, wa suinni yaa yiti.
6Dila Buz denɔwa Barakel nidoabinni Eliyu yaa weeni ayen, <<Mi paala kama ale bena, alege nama a pak, dila ale soa ate mi a chali yɔgsum, an yaksi ayen m weeni ni mi ale seba diila. 7Mi poli kama ayen, <Kpaŋta a biisi, baai ale pak la a sak ba yammu.> 8Alege ka chiika ale bo nuru po la, Wen Dii Ale A Niak La vuusumu ale a te miŋka. 9Daa baai ale pak la nyiini ale ta yammoa, daa baai ale pak la nyiini ale a miŋ dii ale nala la.
10<<Dila mi a weeni ayen, wom mi. Mi mɛ ale weeni ni mi ale seba diila. 11Mi limisi kama alege ate ni biisi, mi wom ni popolaŋa kama alege ate ni a gisi wie la, 12mi kpesi a wom ni ka meena. Alege ni wanyi mɛ an sak ayen Job a kaasi ya. Ni waai an tulisi wa nampaŋŋa. 13Ni kan weeni ayen, <Tama a nya yammoa, Wen dek ale wa tulisi wa, daa nuru biiga.> 14Alege Job a biisi a te ka nama, daa mi ate mi ale tulisi wa nama ale tulisi diila.
15<<Ba jɔk ka nyiŋbiiri a ka wari a weeni, wie a nye kpeeri kama. 16Ku kan magsi ayen m limisi, yɔgyɔgla de ate ba sinla, yɔgyɔgla de ate ba za dula a ka tulisa la. 17Mi mɛ ale te m nɔi, mi mɛ ale weeni mi ale seba diila. 18Mi ta ka wie nyiini ate chiik kaai ale bo m po la a fɛ mu. 19Mi ponni po a nye ase daam kolini ale lik la, nna se daam bunlɔk paalita ale gomsi naka la. 20Ku a fɛ ate m biisi a foli m dek basi, se m lak m nɔnni a tulisi. 21Mi kan luk a maari waai ya, yaase m pak waai a gaam taamu, 22diila mi dan kperi ale pakka, m Nyeerɔwa ale ta mu cheŋ ku kan beni.

english_text:
Elihu Speaks
Job, Listen to Me!
1Job, listen to me!
Pay close attention.
* 2Everything I will say
3is true and sincere,
4just as surely as the Spirit
of God All-Powerful
gave me the breath of life.
5Now line up your arguments
and prepare to face me.
6We each were made from clay,
and God has no favorites,
7so don't be afraid of me
or what I might do.
I Have Heard You Argue
8I have heard you argue
9that you are innocent,
guilty of nothing.
10You claim that God
has made you his enemy,
11 that he has bound your feet
and blocked your path.
12But, Job, you're wrong—
God is greater
than any human.
13So why do you challenge God
to answer you?
14God speaks in different ways,
and we don't always
recognize his voice.
* 15 Sometimes in the night,
he uses terrifying dreams
16to give us warnings.
17God does this to make us turn
from sin and pride
18and to protect us
from being swept away
to the world of the dead.
19Sometimes we are punished
with a serious illness
and aching joints.
20Merely the thought
of our favorite food
makes our stomachs sick,
21and we become so skinny
that our bones stick out.
22We feel death and the grave
taking us in their grip.
23One of a thousand angels
then comes to our rescue
by saying we are innocent.
24The angel shows kindness,
commanding death to release us,
because the price was paid.
25Our health is restored,
we feel young again,
26and we ask God to accept us.
Then we joyfully worship God,
and we are rewarded
because we are innocent.
27When that happens,
we tell everyone,
“I sinned and did wrong,
but God forgave me
28and rescued me from death!
Now I will see the light.”
29God gives each of us
chance after chance
30to be saved from death
and brought into the light
that gives life.
31So, Job, pay attention
and don't interrupt,
32though I would gladly listen
to anything you say
that proves you are right.
33Otherwise, listen in silence
to my wisdom.
translation_text:
1<<Alege yɔgyɔgla de, Job wom mi ale ta dii ayen m weeni la. Kpesi a wom dii meena ate mi ta ayen m weeni la. 2Mi gomsi kama ayen m biisi dii ale bo m popolaŋa po la. 3Mi wieŋa meena, ka wamaŋsa, mi abe a biisi ka wensie. 4Wen Chiika ale nye mi, Wen Dii Ale A Niak La vuusumu ale a te mi nyuvuri. 5Be tulisi mu ase fi nin baga, gomsi fidek a tu mu. 6Mi a nye ase ka fi la Wen niŋ. Mi mɛ nyini ka yak po. 7Kan te mi yɔgsum chalika a daani fu. Mi kan ta pagrim fi zuwa.
8<<Alege fi weeni kama ate mi wom. Mi wom ka wieŋa de dek. 9<Mi nye ka cheri a ka wabiowa. Mi ka kaasuŋŋoa. Mi yeeri m dek kama foolaa po. 10Alege Wen a nya wie a ta chaab ale mi, wa a nya mi ase ka wa dachiak la. 11Wa bobi mi naŋsa ale chɔrima, wa kasim a nya mi suita meena kama.>
12<<Alege mi a weeni fu kama, kude po fi nye kaasi kama, diila Wen a zuak gaam nuru kama. 13Ka boa ate fi a fɔbili a te wa ayen wa kan tulisi nuru wari bola? 14Wen a kasim a biisi kama alege waai a kan kpesi a wom wa le a weeni diila. 15Yɔk nuruba a daa goa, Wen a biisi kama gɔdaasima po ale pai sakka po. 16Wa le biisi ba tueŋa po a nyigsi ba ale wa kaamka, 17ate ba cheem basi ba nye kaasuŋku abe wa kasi wa wa kanjantaŋa po, 18a kasi wa chiika vɔrumu po siŋ ka, ale wa nyuvunni ate gebik a kan ko wa. 19Wen a tom ka nyiŋtuila ale nyiŋdomma nuru jigi a sak wa. 20Nuru waai ale a yuak la nɔi po a kan masa ale ŋandiinta ate ŋandiin tii ale poom nala wa kan yaali ti nyummoa. 21Wa nyiŋka a kpeeri a bɛ ate wa kobaŋa ale jam kaa nya la a yaa yeeri za. 22Wa yaa torisi a moata ka vɔrumu, ate wa nyuvunni a cheŋ kum tomtomdɔma jigi.
23<<Dai dii dai Wen maarɔ ale jam wa maarika, Wen maarɔma tusini po wanyi, waai ale wa teeri nuruba ba tuima. 24Maarɔwa ale weeni ale jiirim ayen, <Basi wa. Wa an magsi wa siŋ kpilima tɛŋŋa. Tutuna ale nna a vari wa a basi.> 25Ate wa nyiŋka a chim nyiŋ paalik ase biik la. Ka le ŋman jam ase wa bimbain po la. 26Wa le puusi te Wen a nya ŋmanteka ale wa, wa le nya Wen nimbidiak a kaari ale suipeentik, Wen ale ŋman ta wa jam wa wayɔrisimaŋa jigini. 27Wa yaa le jam nuruba jigi a weeni ayen, <Mi tom kaasi kama, ale an nye dii ale magsi la, alege mi an nya dii ale magsi mi la. 28Wa vari mu basi ate mi an siŋ vɔrumu po, ate m le boro a nya masim bolimu po.>
29<<Wen ale a nye wieŋa de meena a te nuru buye, poom ka naŋtuok nɔi buta, 30ayen wa basi ate wa pilim nyini vɔrumu jigi a ŋmani, ate nyuvuri bolimu a nyaksi wa zuk.
31<<Job, kpesi a wom mi, nye diki ate m biisi. 32Fi dan ta wari ayen fi weeni, tulisi mu, biisi, mi a yaali ayen fi biisi a vari ka fidek a basi. 33Alege dan kan daa di, yaa be wom mi, nye diki, ate m sak fu yam.>>

english_text:
Elihu Continues
You Men Think You Are Wise
1Elihu said:
2You men think you are wise,
but just listen to me!
3Think about my words,
as you would taste food.
4Then we can decide the case
and give a just verdict.
5Job claims he is innocent
and God is guilty
of mistreating him.
6Job also argues that God
considers him a liar
and that he is suffering severely
in spite of his innocence.
7But to tell the truth,
Job is shameless!
8He spends his time with sinners,
9because he has said,
“It doesn't pay to please God.”
If Any of You Are Smart
10If any of you are smart,
you will listen and learn
that God All-Powerful
does what is right.
11 God always treats everyone
the way they deserve,
12and he is never unfair.
13From the very beginning,
God has been in control
of all the world.
14If God took back the breath
that he breathed into us,
15we humans would die
and return to the soil.
16So be smart and listen!
17The mighty God is the one
who brings about justice,
and you are condemning him.
18Indeed, God is the one
who condemns unfair rulers.
19And God created us all;
he has no favorites,
whether rich or poor.
20Even powerful rulers die
in the darkness of night
when they least expect it,
just like the rest of us.
God Watches Everything We Do
21God watches everything we do.
22No evil person can hide
in the deepest darkness.
23And so, God doesn't need
to set a time for judgment.
24Without asking for advice,
God removes mighty leaders
and puts others in their place.
25He knows what they are like,
and he wipes them out
in the middle of the night.
26And while others look on,
he punishes them
because they were evil
27and refused to obey him.
28The persons they mistreated
had prayed for help,
until God answered
their prayers.
29When God does nothing,
can any person or nation
find fault with him?
30But still, he punishes rulers
who abuse their people.
31Job, you should tell God
that you are guilty
and promise to do better.
32Then ask him to point out
what you did wrong,
so you won't do it again.
33Do you make the rules,
or does God?
You have to decide—
I can't do it for you;
now make up your mind.
34Job, anyone with good sense
can easily see
35that you are speaking nonsense
and lack good judgment.
36So I pray for you to suffer
as much as possible
for talking like a sinner.
37You have rebelled against God,
time after time,
and have even insulted us.
translation_text:
1Eliyu yaa weeni ayen, 2<<Ni wom mi wieŋa, nama yam nyama, ni wom mi, nama zamsirɔma. 3Diila tuini a chamsi ka wie ase giŋgeluŋku ale a lam ŋandiinta diila. 4Ni basi ate tama a kpesi nya dii ale nala la. Ni basi ate ti gum chaab a zamsi dii ale nala la.
5<<Ti wom Job a weeni ayen, <Mi ka kaasuŋŋoa, alege Wen a mini mi nyemagsika. 6Mi wanni a boro kama, alege mi a chim velimvendik, mi an nye foolaa, alege wa penni a te mi tuem buui ale kaa tebi.> 7Ka nuru boa ale a nye ase Job la, ate wa a nyu a ka zula ase nyiam la? 8Wa a gum ka wabanyeerisa po. Wa a nye ale ka gaasa nyam. 9Diila wa weeni kama ayen, <Ku kan te nuru nyuenta ase wa ale a nye ate Wen sui a peenti.>
10<<Dila wom mi, nama baai ale a miŋ la. Wen an baga a nye biemmoa, Wen Dii Ale A Niak La a kan nye a kaasi. 11Wa pilim a tuni nuru kama dii ate wa nye la. Wa ta ka dii ale a magsi wa nyeelaŋa la a jam wa zuk. 12Wen a kan nye a kaasi Wen Dii Ale A Niak La a kan mini waai nyemagsika. 13Ka wana ale lueri wa ayen wa a nya tɛŋzuk de? Ka wana ale ayen wa a nya tɛŋka meena? 14Dan jam ka wa popola ate wa yeeri wa chiika ale wa vuusumu, 15nurubiik meena ale kpi ate nuru a pilim ŋman tantaŋa po.
16<<Fi dan ta miŋka wom kude, wom mi ale a weeni diila. 17Waai ale kisi nyemagsika a baga a de niŋŋa? Fi le ŋma Nyemagsika Nyɔnɔwa ale Waai ale Zuak la? 18Daa Wa ale a weeni nalima ayen, <Ni ka ŋankayaata,> ale kpaga ayen, <Ni ka gaasa nyama,> 19waai ale kaa luk nabisa ale a sak ŋmanteka ale jigsirɔba ŋanjaksa zuwa, diila ba meena ka wa nisima tuima. 20Ba a kpi ka nna kadi, yok suŋsuŋ, ate nuruma nyiŋsa a gɔk ate ba taam ferr. Nuru kpientaŋa a yeeri kama alege daa nurubisa nisa ale a yeeri ba.
21<<Wa ninaŋa a bo ka nuruba suitaŋa po, wa a nya ba naŋsa tabika meena. 22Legi a karo, birim jigi a karo ate nuru baata a suk. 23Wen a kan yaksi a kpesi nuru biiga, ate ba jam wa niŋ ate wa bo ba buusa. 24Wa kan begi ale a kaasi nuru kpientaŋa ale pai nuru yonta a zaani ba jigini. 25Dii nyiŋla wa a kpesi ba nyeelaŋa kama, wa a yiak ba ka yok ate ba a ŋɔriŋ. 26Wa a namsi ba kama ba wabaataŋa nyiŋ juijui ate waai meena a baga a nya ba la, 27dii nyiŋla ba cheem basi wa vaka kama alege ate ba niŋ a ka wa suitaŋa kuui po. 28Ba a nye kama ate ŋanjaksaŋa kaarika a jam wa jigi, ate dila wa wom baai ale a silim la kaarik. 29Alege wa dan nye diki ka wana ale baga ayen wa an nye magsi ya? Wa dan suk wa nimbidiaka, ka wana ale baga a nya wa? Alege wa ta pagrim nuru ale tɛŋ kpieŋ meena zuk, 30a kasi waai ale kan ta Wen la ate wa kan de kpaŋta ate wa kan dueni batta a bari nuruma.
31<<Ase nuru a dan weeni Wen ayen, <Mi nye ka foolaa alege mi kan ŋman tom kaasi. 32Sak mu dii ate mi an baga a nya la, ase m dan nye kaasi, m kan ŋman nye dila.> 33Wen abe nye fi ale a yaali diila ase fi nin zɛri an tagri ya? Fidek a nye popola, daa mi, dila weeni mi fi le seba diila.
34<<Nuru baai ale ta miŋka a weeni ayen, yam nyam baai ale wom mi la a weeni mi ayen, 35<Job a biisi kama ale ka sebika, wa wieŋa yam a ka du.> 36Poli ku meena po a nya Job ale a weeni diila, fi le nya ayen wa a biisi ase ka nuru biok la. 37Wa a gum ka tuikpari wa wabaataŋa po, wa a nye ka Wen a la ti suŋsuŋ, wie ŋaai nyiŋ ate wa ta chaab ale Wen la a zuak kama.>>

english_text:
Elihu Continues
Are You Really Innocent?
1Elihu said:
2Job, are you really innocent
in the sight of God?
3Don't you honestly believe
it pays to obey him?
4I will give the answers
to you and your friends.
* 5Look up to the heavens
6 and think!
Do your sins hurt God?
7Is any good you may have done
at all helpful to him?
8The evil or good you do
only affects other humans.
9In times of trouble,
everyone begs the mighty God
to have mercy.
10But after their Creator
helps them through hard times,
they forget about him,
11though he makes us wiser
than animals or birds.
12God won't listen to the prayers
of proud and evil people.
13If God All-Powerful refuses
to answer their empty prayers,
14he will surely deny
your impatient request
to face him in court.
15Job, you were wrong to say
God doesn't punish sin.
16Everything you have said
adds up to nonsense.
translation_text:
1Eliyu yaa weeni ayen, 2<<Fi a poli ayen kude a magsi ya? Fi a weeni ayen, <Wen ale pagsi m nɔi.> 3Alege fi a bek wa ayen, <Ku ka boan nyuenta a te mi, ale boan nyuenta ate mi a nya wabaata tomka po?>
4<<Mi a yaali ayen m tulisi fu ale fi doama ale bo ale fu la. 5Zak a nya wenzukku, nya chiŋmaaŋa ale bo fi zuk niŋ la. 6Fi dan tom kaasi, kula a nye wa ka sɛ? Fi wabaataŋa a dan piisi, kula a nye wa ka boa? 7Fi dan ka wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ, fi a te wa ka boa, yaase wa a tuesi ka boan fi nisa po? 8Fi wabaataŋa a nye ka nuru nyiini ase fidek la, ate fi wayɔrisimaŋa a nye saalɔ bisa nyiini.
9<<Nuruba a kum kama ba ninammu nyiŋ, ba a saalim kama a yaali maarika a nyini pagrɔwa nisa po. 10Alege waai a kan weeni ayen, <Wen m Nyeerɔwa a bo ka be, waai ale a te yiila yok la, 11Waai ale sak ti a gaam tɛŋka zuk duŋsa ale basi ate ti ta yam a gaam wenzuk nuinsa?> 12Ba a kaari a yaali maarika alege Wen a kan tulisi dii nyiŋla wabaata nyama a ta ka kanjanta. 13Wensie, Wen a kan wom ba saalim koroku, Wen Dii Ale A Niak La a kan wom du. 14Ku yaa be ku nye ka sɛ ate wa wom ase fi nin weeni ayen fi kan nya wa? Bi kala a bo ka wa jigi be chiib a limisi wa. 15Ale ŋman gum du ayen wa suipuurumu a kan namsi. Wa niŋ kan potim a bo biem po. 16Dila Job a lak wa nɔnni a biisi ka bi koruk, ate wa wieŋa a piisi alege sebika a karo.>>

english_text:
Elihu Continues
Be Patient a While Longer
1Elihu said:
2Be patient a while longer;
I have something else to say
in God's defense.
3God always does right—
and this knowledge
comes straight from God.
4You can rest assured
that what I say is true.
5Although God is mighty,
he cares about everyone
and makes fair decisions.
6The wicked are cut down,
and those who are wronged
receive justice.
7God watches over good people
and places them in positions
of power and honor forever.
8But when people are prisoners
of suffering and pain,
* 9God points out their sin
and their pride,
10then he warns them
to turn back to him.
11And if they obey,
they will be successful
and happy from then on.
12But if they foolishly refuse,
they will be rewarded
with a violent death.
Godless People Are Too Angry
13Godless people are too angry
to ask God for help
when he punishes them.
14So they die young
in shameful disgrace.
15Hard times and trouble
are God's way
of getting our attention!
16And at this very moment,
God deeply desires
to lead you from trouble
and to spread your table
with your favorite food.
17Now that the judgment
for your sins
has fallen upon you,
18don't let your anger
and the pain you endured
make you sneer at God.
19Your reputation and riches
cannot protect you
from distress,
20nor can you find safety
in the dark world below.
21Be on guard! Don't turn to evil
as a way of escape.
22God's power is unlimited.
He needs no teachers
23to guide or correct him.
Others Have Praised God
24Others have praised God
for what he has done,
so join with them.
25From down here on earth,
everyone has looked up and seen
26how great God is—
God is more than we imagine;
no one can count the years
he has lived.
* 27God gathers moisture
into the clouds
28and supplies us with rain.
29Who can understand
how God scatters the clouds
and speaks from his home
in the thunderstorm?
30And when God sends lightning,
it can be seen
at the bottom of the sea.
31By producing such rainstorms,
God rules the world
and provides us with food.
32Each flash of lightning
is one of his arrows
striking its target,
33and the thunder tells
of his anger against sin.
translation_text:
1Eliyu a diem biisi a cheŋ ayen, 2<<Yik fidek maga ale mu ate m sak fu ayen wie yega ale boro ate m le biisi a te Wen. 3Mi nya m sebika a nyini ka niŋ, m le pai nyemagsika a te m Nyeerɔwa. 4Mi ale basi ate fi seba a chak ayen m wieŋa daa venta, waai ale ka chekki ale sebika fi jigi.
5<<Wen a zuaya, alege a kan zɛri nuruba, wa zuaya ale nye giŋgiŋ wa popola po. 6Wa kan basi ate wabanyeerisa a vua alege a te baai ale a nam la ba le soa ŋan baai la. 7Wa kan yeeri wa nina baai ale ka wayɔrisima nyam la zuwa, wa basi ate ba a dɛ naam ale nalima ale zak ba a zaani taam wuu. 8Alege chɔrima a dan bobi nuruba, a yik ba ŋmapi ale namsika miisa, 9wa a weeni ba kama ba le nye diila, ayen ba tom kaasi kama ale kanjanta. 10Wa nye ate ba a wom sinsaga ale a weeni ba laŋ nyeka abe ba basi ba biemu. 11Ba dan zuli ale tom te wa, ba le pai da ŋaai meena ale tali la a nya badek ate ba benaŋa meena ba nina a sueri. 12Alege ba dan kan wom ya, ba le kpi ale gebika, ba le kpi ba kan seba.
13<<Baai ale kan ta Wen la sue ale kasim a puuri ate ba dan poom nya ninam ba kan kum a yaali maarika. 14Ba a kpi ale ba diem paala kama, nidoa taabuksa tangbana suŋsuŋ. 15Alege Wen a va ka ninam po a sak nuruba ale pai namsika a lak ba nina.
16<<Wen a yeeri fu ka daanika po a ta fu a cheŋ juijui ate mirika a ka, ate fi jazaanimu zuk ŋandiin maŋsa a vi du a te fu. 17Alege yɔgyɔgla de buusa ale ji fu a magsi chaab ale biem, buusa ale nyemagsika ale yik fu. 18Kpesi fidek ate waai a kan pai jigsika a paasi fu, kan basi ate diak yega a tulim fu a basi nakpiaga. 19Fi jigsika yaase fi nye zuaka pooma a kan yik fu ate fi kan bo ninam po. 20Kaa yaali yok wa ayen fi dari nuruba a ta nyini ba yie a cheŋ. 21Kpesi fidek ate fi kan cheem a jo biem po, fi ninammu a jam ayen bu kasi fu ka biem po joka.
22<<Teeri Wen pagrimu ale zuak diila, wa ale sagrɔ a gaam waai meena. 23Ka wana ale sak wa wa suitaŋa, yaase a weeni wa ayen, <Fi nye kaasi ya>? 24Teeri ate fi pak wa tuimaŋa, ŋaai ate nuru a siak yiila a pak la. 25Saalɔ meena a nya kama, nuruba a zaani niŋ a nya kama. 26Wen ale soa dii a gaam ti miŋka, wa benaŋa a nak taam ti kpesi miŋka kama.
27<<Ka Wen ale a dari nyiam tɛŋka zuk a tulim bu ate bu a chim ŋmoruk a zi. 28Wa basi ate ŋmorukku a nyini chiŋmaaŋa po a ni a te saalɔ meena. 29Waai an baga a miŋ chiŋmaaŋa ale a cheŋ dii ya yaase nampaŋsaŋa ale a na a kum a cheŋ wenzukku ate Wen a boro la. 30Wa basi ate nyaksika a cheŋ wenzukku meena, alege nyakpiemu tɛŋ a wari chim legi. 31Wa le a nya tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa zuk diila ale nna ale a te ŋandiinta nna yegayega. 32Wa a tuesi nyaksika ale wa nisimaŋa ale a weeni ayen bu na juijui ale magsi la. 33Wa nampanika ale a mooli vioku jamka, niiŋa a poom seba ku le cheen la kama.

english_text:
Elihu Continues
I Am Frightened
1I am frightened
and tremble all over,
2when I hear the roaring voice
of God in the thunder,
3and when I see his lightning
flash across the sky.
4God's majestic voice
thunders his commands,
5creating miracles too marvelous
for us to understand.
6Snow and heavy rainstorms
7make us stop and think
about God's power,
8and they force animals
to seek shelter.
9The windstorms of winter strike,
10and the breath of God
freezes streams and rivers.
11Rain clouds filled with lightning
appear at God's command,
12traveling across the sky
13to release their cargo—
sometimes as punishment for sin,
sometimes as kindness.
Consider Carefully
14Job, consider carefully
the many wonders of God.
15Can you explain why lightning
flashes at the orders
16of God who knows all things?
Or how he hangs the clouds
in empty space?
17You almost melt in the heat
of fierce desert winds
when the sky is like brass.
18God can hammer out the clouds
in spite of the oppressive heat,
but can you?
19Tell us what to say to God!
Our minds are in the dark,
and we don't know how
to argue our case.
20Should I risk my life
by telling God
that I want to speak?
21No one can stare at the sun
after a breeze has blown
the clouds from the sky.
22Yet the glorious splendor
of God All-Powerful
is brighter by far.
23God cannot be seen—
but his power is great,
and he is always fair.
24And so we humans fear God,
because he shows no respect
for those who are proud
and think they know so much.
translation_text:
1<<Kude a basi kama ate mi suinum a nak ale a yiti. 2Wom, wom wa lueluku ale a na la, ku le a wuuri a nyini wa nɔnni po a jam la. 3Wa a tom nyaksika ate ka a cheŋ wenzukku meena, a nyini kauk kunku a taam kauk kunku. 4Dila ŋaaŋnyiŋ wa lueluku wuurika a yaa jam, wa a na kama ale wa naam lueluku. Wa lueluku a dan ŋman kum, wa kan peri jaaboa. 5Wen lueluku a na ka nna kperikperiga, wa a nye ka wa kpiema a gaam ti miŋka. 6Wa a weeni ŋmoruk tana ayen, <Lo tɛŋka zuk,> ale ŋmorukku ayen, <Ku a siŋ nna yegayega.> 7Ate dila nuruba meena ate wa nye la ale seba wa tuimaŋa, wa te waai meena a basi wa tuima. 8Ate duŋsaŋa a nya likka, ŋa a wari ka si boka jiŋŋa. 9Va munsaŋa a nyini ka yeseoku geŋ a jam, ate ŋo tii ale a fuk la a nyini wiilukku geŋ. 10Wen vuusumu a basi ate ka ŋmoruk tana a boro, ate nya tii ale lak la a goa. 11Wa basi ate nyiam a sueri chiŋmaaŋa po, wa basi ate wa nyaksika a waaŋ ba po meena. 12Ba le a cheŋ a va Wen yaalika, ba a nye ka Wen ale a weeni diila, jigi meena tɛŋka po. 13Wa ta ka chiŋma a jam ayen ŋa namsi nuruba, yaase ŋa zaŋti wa tɛŋka abe wa sak wa ŋmanteka.
14<<Job wom kude, zimsi abe fi poli Wen wakinkaglaŋa wie. 15Fi seba Wen ale nye dii a yik chiŋmaaŋa a ta ale basi ate ku a nyaksi la? 16Fi seba chiŋma ale nye dii a cheŋ wenzukku la, Wen yam tuimaŋa ale a cha ti la? 17Fi a nam ka tuilukku po nyiini ase yeseoku vioku a nin namsi tɛŋka. 18Fi baga a maari Wen ate wa a dari wenzukku ale a nye ate ku a pagra ase kutuk ate ba salisi la?
