25If you want too much
and are too lazy to work,
it could be fatal.
26But people who obey God
are always generous.
27 The Lord despises the offerings
of wicked people
with evil motives.
28If you tell lies in court,
you are done for;
only a reliable witness
can do the job.
29Wicked people bluff their way,
but God's people think
before they take a step.
30No matter how much you know
or what plans you make,
you can't defeat the Lord.
31Even if your army has horses
ready for battle,
the Lord will always win.
translation_text:
1Naab suinum ka buboalik nyiam Naawen nisa po, wa te bu a va ka juijui ate wa a yaali la. 2Nurubiik suita po wie meena a nala ka wadek nina po, alege ka Naawen ale a kpesi suiniima meena a nya. 3Ate fi tom wayɔrisima ale wensie tuima la a nala a te Naawen a gaam kaab te ka kama. 4Kayeruk ale kanjanta ale biem nyeela meena ka wabaata. 5Popola maŋsa ale nyiŋbiiri ale ta a cheŋ jigsika po, alege yientika a ta fu tuak ka jaŋsa po.
6Fi dan velim a jigsi, ŋantaŋa a muriŋ a bɛ kama a nyini fi jigi ase pik la ale ŋman a chim kum baruk. 7Gaasa nyama dek wɔkwɔk ale vaari ba ta cheŋ, dii nyiŋla ba zɛri kama ayen ba kan nye dii ale ta wensie la. 8Nye kaasirɔwa a va ka suik goantika, alege waai ale kan seba wari nɔi po la a va ka suik kuui ale yoarisi la. 9Fi gboŋ gugoruk po a zunchoŋŋa ase fi nin bo yeri po ate nipok kpaliŋ kpaliŋdɔ a boro. 10Nuru baata a yaali ka biem, ba vaanchaab a kan nya jiirim a nyini ba jigi ya.
11Ase ba dan dari waai ale koosi nuruba a la la turi, a jɔk po yiila nyama ale ta yam. Fi dan sak yam nyam ba ale ŋmasi a ta yam. 12Wayɔrisima Nyɔnɔwa a kpesi gaasa nyɔnɔwa yenni kama. Wa ale dari gaasa nyɔnɔwa a lɔnsi tɛŋ ate wa kaasi. 13Waai ale kaa lak tue a wom ŋanjaksa kumsa la, wa mɛ ale kum a yaali maarika alege waai a kan wom wa. 14Susugi tiirim a yɔk ka suipuurum, fi deri suk te waai jaab dila a kpimsi ka suipuurum yegayega. 15Chekki tuima ka masim a te wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ, alege ku chim daanika a te biem nyam.
16Nuru waai ale kaa miŋ wie kiri la ale nya wadek ale ka kpilima. 17Baai ale a yaali masim la jaŋsa ale yik ba. Baai ale a yaali daam ale masim ŋanta la a kan jigsi. 18Ba a namsi gaasa nyam a tagri ka wayɔrisima nyam ale a namsi bumbobrɔba a tagri baai ale chim wensie nyam la. 19Fi dan bo gɔi po fidek fi nyiini a zunchoŋ fi ale bo ale nipok waai ale a yaali kpaliŋsa ale funfɔbla. 20Yam nyama a ta ka ŋanta ale masim, alege betta a dɛ ka jaab meena ate ba a nya la.
21Waai ale a gisi wayɔrisima ale yaali maŋ la ale nya ka nyuvuri ale wayɔrisima ale zula. 22Yam nyɔnɔwa a nya nakdeka pagrɔwa tɛŋka zuk kama ale a lɔnsi ba yie pagraŋa ate ba ta mariŋka ale ŋa la. 23Waai ale a yik wa nɔnni ale wa giŋgeluŋku la, a yeeri ka wadek a nyini daanika po. 24Koosi laarɔba ka kanjanta ale nyanueriŋ nyam, jaab karo a kasi ba ate ba kan kuulim. 25Nyiŋworuk nyam ale a yaali diila ale a ko ba, diila ba kan siagi ayen ba pai nisa a tom tuini.
26Nuruba gela a ta ka butuem a yaali yega ayen ba gum ba ale ta diila po, alege baai ale ka Naawen nuruba a yaali ka teka. 27Nuru biok kaabka ka kisuk, be poom ka wa nin ta popola baata a nye kaabka. 28Venta seerɔ ba le gebi wa a basi, alege wensie seerɔ ba le te wa suik ate wa biisi. 29Gaasa nyam a sak ka badek ale ba tuima, alege waai ale za dekki la a poli kama ale a tom wa tuima. 30Nurubiik yam ale sebika ale zɔga an baga a nye Naawen wari ya.
31Wusummu a gomsi magsi kpaliŋka kama, alege nak dɛka bo ka Naawen jigi.

english_text:
The Value of a Good Reputation
1A good reputation and respect
are worth much more
than silver and gold.
2The rich and the poor
are all created
by the Lord.
3When you see trouble coming,
don't be stupid
and walk right into it—
be smart and hide.
4Respect and serve the Lord!
Your reward will be wealth,
a long life, and honor.
5Crooks walk down a road
full of thorny traps.
Stay away from there!
6 Teach your children
right from wrong,
and when they are grown
they will still do right.
7The poor are ruled by the rich,
and those who borrow
are slaves of moneylenders.
8Troublemakers get in trouble,
and their terrible anger
will get them nowhere.
9The Lord blesses everyone
who freely gives food
to the poor.
10Arguments and fights
will come to an end,
if you chase away those
who insult others.
11The king is the friend of all
who are sincere
and speak with kindness.
12The Lord watches over everyone
who shows good sense,
but he frustrates the plans
of deceitful liars.
13Don't be so lazy that you say,
“If I go to work,
a lion will eat me!”
14The words of a bad woman
are like a deep pit;
if you make the Lord angry,
you will fall right in.
15All children are foolish,
but firm correction
will make them change.
16Cheat the poor to make profit
or give gifts to the rich—
either way you lose.
Thirty Wise Sayings
17Here are some sayings
of people with wisdom,
so listen carefully
as I teach.
18You will be glad
that you know these sayings
and can recite them.
19I am teaching them today,
so that you
may trust the Lord.
20I have written thirty sayings
filled with sound advice.
21You can trust them completely
to give you the right words
for those in charge of you.
–1–
22Don't take advantage
of the poor
or cheat them in court.
23The Lord is their defender,
and what you do to them,
he will do to you.
–2–
24Don't make friends with anyone
who has a bad temper.
25You might turn out like them
and get caught in a trap.
–3–
26Don't guarantee to pay
someone else's debt.
27If you don't have the money,
you might lose your bed.
–4–
28Don't move a boundary marker
set up by your ancestors.
–5–
29If you do your job well,
you will work for a ruler
and never be a slave.
translation_text:
1Yuei maŋ luerika a gaam jigsika. Fi yuei dan yiti a gaam kpana ale ligmɔniŋ. 2Jigsirɔma ale ŋanjaksaŋa meena, ka Naawen ale nye ba. 3Yam nyɔnɔ a nya dii ale ta kum cheen la kama a suk wadek, alege beruk a gaa jo du kama a nam. 4Zaab m dek ale Naawen yɔgsum chalika, tutuna ale jigsika ale zula ale nyuvuri. 5Muŋsa ale batta ale bo baai ale za venta suita po la. Waai ale a yik wa chiik la ale yeeri wadek a nyini ŋa po.
6Dak suik maŋka a sak fi bisaŋa ate ba dan jam pak, ba kan pai ku a basi. 7Ase jigsirɔ ale a nya jajak zuk diila, dila mɛ ate peemdɔwa a chim yɔma a te peemteerɔwa. 8Baai ale a bori venta la a che ka kaasuŋ, ate ba wɔkwɔkka ale jam kpeglimka. 9Nuru waai ale a te la ale nya niaka, dii nyiŋla wa a te ŋanjaksaŋa ka ŋandiinta. 10Yiak waai ale a la nuruba la ate wa cheŋ, ate kpaliŋ a maa va cheŋ. Kpaliŋsa ale leeta ale muriŋ bɛ.
11Waai suinum ale peela la, ate yaalika a bo wa biisa po la, ale ta ka naab ase wa doa la. 12Naawen a nya wensie nyama zuk kama, alege wa a yiak venta nyama a basi. 13Nyiŋ wɔrukku nyɔnɔwa a weeni kama ayen, <<M dan nyini peelim, m le zik gbeŋli suiku po ate di ko mu.>> 14Nipok kaasuŋ nɔi ka baruk pagrik. Baai ate Naawen sui a puuri ale ba la a lɔ ka ku po. 15Biik suinum po a sueri ale ka betta, alege ka turi darika ale a yeeri dila a nyini wa po.
16Nuru waai ale a namsi ŋanjaksa ayen wa jigsi yaase wa a te jigsirɔba tiirita la ale kpeglim ale jaŋsa.
17Lak fi tunni a wom yam nyam wieŋa, abe fi basi ate fi suinummu a ta m miŋka. 18Diila ŋa nala ayen fi ta wieŋa de fi suinum po, abe ŋa kasim bo fi nɔi po. 19Jinla danni de po, mi nye kama ate fi a miŋ yam nyama kiri, ate fi ale ta mariŋka ale Naawen. 20M ŋmarisi ka yam wie pisita a te fu, ate sinsaga ale yam wie miŋka a bo ŋa po. 21Suiku de po, fi ale miŋ wensie ate baai ale tom fu la, fi ale ga weeni ba fi ale nya diila.
22Kan vari jajak ŋanta ayen wa jaŋ nyiŋŋa, yaase fi vari waai ale a silim a jam bo buusa dɔkku po la. 23Naawen ale tuesi ba biisaŋa a biisi a te ba, abe wa kɔni waai ale kɔni ba la.
24Kan dɛ doata ale suipuurum nuruba yaase fi a nye wari ale nuru baai sue ale kpabi a puuri la, 25dan kan daa di fi ale zamsi wa suitaŋa a ta fidek a ga jo baruk po.
26Kan siagi ayen fi zaani ate a waai a pai fi nyiŋ a de pami ya, yaase wa dan kan baga a tuni fi ga a tuni a te wa. 27Fi kan jam baga a tuni, ba ale poom a pai fi gaduokku a nyini fi jigi.
28Ni kan yeeri banaŋa ate ni kokpieŋsaŋa a dueni la ate ni baga a zu ni vaanchaama nitalimu.
29Fi nya nuru baai ale seba tuima la a nya ya? Ba ale tom a te ka nalima alege daa nuruba kinla.

english_text:
–6–
1When you are invited
to eat with a king,
use your best manners.
2Don't go and stuff yourself!
That would be just the same
as cutting your throat.
3Don't be greedy for all
of that fancy food!
It may not be so tasty.
–7–
4Give up trying so hard
to get rich.
5Your money flies away
before you know it,
just like an eagle
suddenly taking off.
–8–
6Don't accept an invitation
to eat a selfish person's food,
no matter how good it is.
7People like that take note
of how much you eat.
They say, “Take all you want!”
But they don't mean it.
8Each bite will come back up,
and all your kind words
will be wasted.
–9–
9Don't talk to fools—
they will make fun of you.
–10–
10Don't move a boundary marker
or take the land
that belongs to orphans.
11God All-Powerful is there
to defend them against you.
–11–
12Listen to instruction
and do your best to learn.
–12–
13Don't fail to correct
your children.
You won't kill them
by being firm,
14and it may even
save their lives.
–13–
15My children,
if you show good sense,
I will be happy,
16and if you are truthful,
I will really be glad.
–14–
17Don't be jealous of sinners,
but always honor the Lord.
18Then you will truly have hope
for the future.
–15–
19Listen to me, my children!
Be wise and have enough sense
to follow the right path.
20Don't be a heavy drinker
or stuff yourself with food.
21It will make you feel drowsy,
and you will end up poor
with only rags to wear.
–16–
22Pay attention to your father,
and don't neglect your mother
when she grows old.
23Invest in truth and wisdom,
discipline and good sense,
and don't part with them.
24Make your father truly happy
by living right and showing
sound judgment.
25Make your parents proud,
especially your mother.
–17–
26My son, pay close attention,
and gladly follow
my example.
27Bad women and unfaithful wives
are like a deep pit—
28they are waiting to attack you
like a gang of robbers
with victim after victim.
–18–
29Who is always in trouble?
Who argues and fights?
Who has cuts and bruises?
Whose eyes are red?
30Everyone who stays up late,
having just one more drink.
31Don't even look
at that colorful stuff
bubbling up in the glass!
It goes down so easily,
32but later it bites
like a poisonous snake.
33You will see weird things,
and your mind
will play tricks on you.
34You will feel tossed about
like someone trying to sleep
on a ship in a storm.
35You will be bruised all over,
without even remembering
how it all happened.
And you will lie awake asking,
“When will morning come,
so I can drink some more?”
translation_text:
1Fi dan boro a dɛ ale niŋdeerɔ, kpesi nya ba ale pai jabuui a zaani fi niŋ la. 2Fi dan ka waai ale baga a dɛ, pai gebik a tiik fi tutɔk. 3Kan basi ate fi popola meena a bo ŋandiin maŋsaŋa jigi ya, da dii dai wa a yaali wa nye fu nya kama.
4Kan jiak fidek ayen jigsika nyiŋŋa. Miŋ yam ate fi seba diipo ale magsi ayen fi pai a basi la. 5Jigsika a muriŋ a bɛ ka nna yilibi ase nina kamsika la. Diila ku ale tom ka kinkaŋŋa a yaa yiti jueli wen ase jiiruk la.
6Kan dɛ ŋandiinta ale butuem nyama. Kan te fi kɔrisa a bo ale ba ŋantaŋa. 7Butuem nyam nyiem kasim a poli ka ŋandiinta nyaka wari ale toa diila ate ku a daani ba. Ba le weeni fu ayen a dɛ abe fi a nyu alege ba suinummu po ku daa dila. 8Fi ale chiiri mag kaai ate fi dɛ la a basi ate fi jiirim wieŋa a kan ta kiri.
9Kan biisi wari a basi beruk tue po dii nyiŋla, wa ale yuk fi yam wieŋa a basi.
10Kan zu niwoba yaase kpiŋsa tɛŋsa a yeeri ba kokpieŋsaŋa banaŋa. 11Dii nyiŋla ba Da Tuesirɔwa a pagra kama, wadek ale za wa zaani a biisi a te ba.
12Pai fidek a te sinsaga abe fi chiib a wom yam wie.
13Kan basi fi bisaŋa waalika. Fi dan te ba waalika, ba kan kpi. 14Fi dan pai fiŋ a miiri ba, fi ale vari ba chiisaŋa a nyini kum po.
15M biiga, yam a dan bo fi suinum po, mi mɛ suinummu ale nya masim. 16Fi dan weeni dii ale nala la, jaab meena ale bo mi po la ale dɛ masim.
17Kaa dɛ nyuri ale wabanyeerisa, alege kasim a chali Naawen. 18Fi ale nya tutuna nyakude nyiŋ. Fi yiilaŋa a kan chim kinla.
19Wom de m biiga, ate fi ta yam, ate fi suinummu a va suiku. 20Kan bo ale danyuirisa yaase baai ale baga a dɛ la, 21diila ba bo ka ba suik po a cheŋ jaŋsa po, ate goom yegayega ale chim garuchaasa a lik ba.
22A wom fi kowa waai ale te fu nyuvuri la, abe fi kan zɛri fi mawa ase wa nin jam kpaŋmu. 23Tuesi wensie abe fi kan pai ŋa a da. Be ŋman tuesi yam ale waalika ale wensie buusa boka. 24Ko waai bisa ale bo wayɔrisima po la, ku ka masim a te wa. Ku ka masim ase fi nin ta bisa ate ba ta yam. 25Te fi kowa ale fi mawa masim. Te waai ale biak fu la sui a peenti.
26M biiga te mu fi suinummu, abe fi basi ate fi ninaŋa a kpesi nya m suitaŋa. 27Nipok waai ale pai wadek a te nidoaba a tuesi ŋanta la ka baruk pagrik. Nipok kaboŋ a nye ase ka vili miglik ate nuru a lɔ di po la. 28Wa suk kama ale a limisi ase zue la, a yaali ayen wa nye ate nidoaba yegayega a kan chim wensie nuruba.
29Ka wana ale ta nyiŋdomma? Ka wana ale ta suipuurummoa? Ka wana ale kasim a fɔbili? Ka wana ale ta mula alege zɛ ku kiri ya? Ka wana nimbie ale muni ya? 30Ka baai ale a kali daam zuk a beni la. Baai ale a lam da paalisa a nya la. 31Kaa nya daamoa, a nya bu ale muni dii ya, bu ale a tɔŋ chiima beerika po dii ya, bu ale nyu a siŋ dii ya. 32Ku nueri ka po, bu a dom ase ka waab biok la. Bu be ŋman a dom ase ka waab piik la. 33Fi ale nya ŋanchaŋsa ate fi ale weeni yesiŋsa wie. 34Fi ale nye ase waai ale doa nyakpiemu suŋsuŋ, ate fi kpari maŋ diok woŋ ate ba pai ti zaani ŋaaruŋ zuk diila. 35Ate fi ale weeni ayen, <<Ba nak mu kama, alege ku an jo m nyiŋŋa. Mi a poom zɛ diipo ate ba nak mi la. Mi ale yiti ka dimpo ate m ŋman gisi daam bu choa?>>

english_text:
–19–
1Don't be jealous of crooks
or want to be their friends.
2All they think about
and talk about
is violence and cruelty.
–20–
3Use wisdom and understanding
to establish your home;
4let good sense fill the rooms
with priceless treasures.
–21–
5Wisdom brings strength,
and knowledge gives power.
6Battles are won
by listening to advice
and making a lot of plans.
–22–
7Wisdom is too much for fools!
Their advice is no good.
–23–
8No one but troublemakers
think up trouble.
9Everyone hates senseless fools
who think up ways to sin.
–24–
10Don't give up and be helpless
in times of trouble.
–25–
11Don't fail to rescue those
who are doomed to die.
12Don't say, “I didn't know it!”
God can read your mind.
He watches each of us
and knows our thoughts.
And God will pay us back
for what we do.
–26–
13Honey is good for you,
my children,
and it tastes sweet.
14Wisdom is like honey
for your life—
if you find it,
your future is bright.
–27–
15Don't be a cruel person
who attacks good people
and hurts their families.
16Even if good people
fall seven times,
they will get back up.
But when trouble strikes
the wicked,
that's the end of them.
–28–
17Don't be happy
to see your enemies trip
and fall down.
18The Lord will find out
and be unhappy.
Then he will stop
being angry with them.
–29–
19Don't let evil people
worry you
or make you jealous.
20They will soon be gone
like the flame of a lamp
that burns out.
–30–
21My children, you must respect
the Lord and the king,
and you must not make friends
with anyone who rebels
against either of them.
22Who knows what sudden disaster
the Lord or a ruler
might bring?
More Sayings That Make Good Sense
23Here are some more sayings
that make good sense:
When you judge,
you must be fair.
24If you let the guilty
go free,
people of all nations
will hate and curse you.
25But if you punish the guilty,
things will go well for you,
and you will prosper.
26Giving an honest answer
is a sign
of true friendship.
27Get your fields ready
and plant your crops
before starting a home.
28Don't accuse anyone
who isn't guilty.
Don't ever tell a lie
29or say to someone,
“I'll get even with you!”
30I once walked by the field
and the vineyard
of a lazy fool.
31Thorns and weeds
were everywhere,
and the stone wall
had fallen down.
32When I saw this,
it taught me a lesson:
33 Sleep a little. Doze a little.
Fold your hands
and twiddle your thumbs.
34Suddenly poverty hits you
and everything is gone!
translation_text:
1Kan dɛ nyuri ale nuru baata yaase fi poom yaali ayen fi bo ale ba. 2Diila ba a zɔk ka wɔkwɔk ba suiniimaŋa po, ate ba wieŋa a siti kpaliŋ.
3Yam ate ba pai a sɛ yeri ale a ta pagrim a nyini yam maŋ po. 4A nyini yam wie miŋka ate bu diinaŋa a sueri le jigsika ale ŋan baai ale ta dobrim.
5Yam nyama a zuak a gaam pagrɔba, ate baai ale ta yam wie miŋka la ale kasim a chim ale pagrim. 6Dila nyiŋ kan cheŋ kpaliŋ alege ate ba an sak fu dii ate fi ale nye la. Nakdeka a nyini ka sagrɔba jigi.
7Yam a ka kiri a te betta. A bo niŋdeerɔba tɛŋka nansuiŋku nɔi ba ka wari a weeni.
8Nuru waai ale a poli biem la ba ale nya wa ase ka waai ale a ta daanika a jam la. 9Beruk popola ka biem. Waai meena a kisi waai ale nye nuruba a la la kama.
10Ase ku dan jam miri fu, fi pagrimu an soa dii ya.
11Baai ate ba an va wensie a bo mini ba ayen ba ko ba la vari ba a basi, vari ba a basi ase ba le tuak kum jigi la. 12Kan yaali wari a weeni ayen, <<Nya tama jam zɛ.>> Diila Naawen a miŋ suiniima meena kiri kama, wa abe a nya fu kama. Waai ale a nya fi chiika zuk la a seba ayen fi seba kama. Wa le tuni nuru meena a magsi wa nyeka ale ka diila kama.
13M biiga, a dɛ siita ale ku nala kama, ate samparimaŋa lamka a masa. 14Suik kula dek mɛ po, yam a nala kama a te fi chiika. Fi dan nya bu, fi chumwa ale jam a nala. Ate fi le goa a yiili diila ale sum a nye.
15Kan gu doa nuru maŋ yeri po ayen fi nye wa biem, be kan ga yik nuru maŋka wa yenni po. 16Nuru maŋsa ale sati lɔ naŋtuok nɔi buyopɔi, alege ba ale ŋman yiti. Alege kaasuŋ bunyi nyiini ale te ate gaasa nyam a muriŋ bɛ.
17Kaa dɛ masim ase fi dachaasa nin lɔ. Kan te fi sui a peenti ase ba nin nak naŋŋa. 18Diila Naawen sui a kan peenti ale fu, ate wa ale yeeri wa suipuurumu a nyini ba zuk. 19Kan te wabanyeerisa wie a daani fu. Kaa dɛ nyuri ale gaasa nyama. 20Diila nuru baata a ka chum. Gaasa nyama bolimu ale kpi.
21M biiga, a chali Naawen ale Naawa. Kan pai fidek a gum tukpari nyam po, 22diila kaasuŋ ale kpabi a jam ba zuk. Ka wana ale seba namsi kaai choa ale nyini Naawen ale Naawa jigi a cheen ba zuk la?
23Yam wie gela ale nna ŋmana: Ku an nala ase fi nin boro a bo buusa ate fi luk a sak jiirim ale baai ate fi a yaali la. 24Boteerɔ waai ale a weeni gaasa nyɔnɔwa ayen, <<Fi zɛ wari nɔi po la,>> nuruba yegayega ale ka kikaasa a te wa, ate tɛŋ kpieŋsa ale biisi zɛri wa. 25Alege ku ale cheŋ nalimnyiini a te baai ale basi ate waai ale nye kaasi la a siak wa kaasuŋku la kama. Niaka ale bo ba zuk.
26Wensie tulisika a nye ase ka doaba ale a gbaari chaab diila.
27Nye fi zɔŋŋa abe fi gomsi fi tɛŋka abe fi ge piilim fi yenni sɛka. 28Kan biisi kaasi fi vaanchaab alege ate ba an nye fu wari ya. Kan velim a te ba. 29Be kan weeni ayen, <<Yɔgyɔgla de m le tuni ba dii ate ba pai nye mu la! M le yik ba.
30Mi va ka nyiŋworuk nyɔnɔ laŋ po a taam, nuru waai ale kan ta wadek yam a bo wa kaduk po la. 31Mi jam nya ka muŋsa ale chim ka po, ate wuuta a lik ka, ate ka parisaŋa a lɔ. 32Ate mi ale nya ale poli ka wari la, mi yaa zamsi wanni de: 33Goom nna maga ale goajɔgsika nna maga ale nisa gurumka nna maga ayen fi vuusi, 34ate jaŋsa ale jam fi zuk ase zueba la. Silimka ale jam fi zuk ase varidɔba la.

english_text:
More of Solomon's Wise Sayings
1Here are some more
of Solomon's proverbs.
They were copied by the officials
of King Hezekiah of Judah.
2God is praised
for being mysterious;
rulers are praised
for explaining mysteries.
3Who can fully understand
the thoughts of a ruler?
They reach beyond the sky
and go deep in the earth.
4Silver must be purified
before it can be used
to make something of value.
5Evil people must be removed
before anyone can rule
with justice.
6 Don't try to seem important
in the court of a ruler.
7It's better for the ruler
to give you a high position
than for you to be embarrassed
in front of royal officials.
Be sure you are right
8before you sue someone,
or you might lose your case
and be embarrassed.
9When you and someone else
can't get along,
don't gossip about it.
10Others will find out,
and your reputation
will then be ruined.
11The right word
at the right time
is like precious gold
set in silver.
12Listening to good advice
is worth much more
than jewelry made of gold.
13A messenger you can trust
is just as refreshing
as cool water in summer.
14Broken promises
are worse than rain clouds
that don't bring rain.
15Patience and gentle talk
can convince a ruler
and overcome any problem.
16Eating too much honey
can make you sick.
17Don't visit friends too often,
or they will get tired of it
and start hating you.
18Telling lies about friends
is like attacking them
with clubs and swords
and sharp arrows.
19A friend you can't trust
in times of trouble
is like having a toothache
or a sore foot.
20Singing to someone
in deep sorrow
is like pouring vinegar
in an open cut.
21 If your enemies are hungry,
give them something to eat.
And if they are thirsty,
give them something
to drink.
22This will be the same
as piling burning coals
on their heads.
And the Lord
will reward you.
23As surely as rain blows in
from the north,
anger is caused
by cruel words.
24It's better to stay outside
on the roof of your house
than to live inside
with a nagging wife.
25Good news from far away
refreshes like cold water
when you are thirsty.
26When a good person gives in
to the wicked,
it's like dumping garbage
in a stream of clear water.
27Don't eat too much honey
or always want praise.
28Losing self-control
leaves you as helpless
as a city without a wall.
translation_text:
1Yam wie ale nna ate Solomon a weeni ate ŋmarisidoama baai ale bo Naab Azekaya buusa boka yenni po a bo Juda tɛŋka po la a ŋmarisi. 2Ku ka Naawen suik ate wa lik wie, ku ka naawa suik ate wa lak ŋa. 3Ase wenŋmazuk ale yalima ate tɛŋzuk a limisa diila, ku ka dila ale nalima suiniima fi kan seba dii ale boro la.
4Ase nuruba a dan yeeri yaataŋa a nyini kpana po, tuimtomdɔwa ale pai ku a nye wamaŋsa. 5Yiak gaasa nyɔnɔwa ate wa nyini naawa dabiaka po a nyini, ate wa dɛ naamu a nyini wensie po.
6Kan te nuruba a nya ase fi ale naawa ka bunyi la, yaase fi ga zaani nuru kpienta boka jigi ya. 7Fi dan limisi ate ba wi fu, a zunchoŋŋa ase fi ale cheŋ fidek ate ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ba zɛri fu nuru boari suŋsuŋ po ale chivie. Fi ale nya jaab la nyiŋ, 8kan kpabi a cheŋ buusa boka yeri ya. Da dii dai fi ale ga biisi lɔ fi ale waai ale ta chaab la niŋ ate chivie a ji fu.
9Weeni fi wanni a sak fi ale waai ale ta chaab la nyiini. Kan weeni a sak waai ya, 10dan kan daa di nuruba ale wi fu ayen bumbobrɔ ate fi ale jɔk fi zula.
11Fi dan biisi wamaŋ diipo ale magsi la, ku nala kama ase ligmɔniŋ ale ŋmirisi kpana chin po la. 12Yam kaamka ate waai ale wa wom la a ta dobrim ase ka ligmɔniŋ tukpana yaase ligmɔniŋ baŋsa la.
13Tintomdɔ waai ate ba a mariŋ wa la a nye ase ka wenkarik ŋmoruk la. Wa a te wa kpagni nyiŋbiiri.
14Nuru waai ale ka a te wa puulimka tiirim la a nye ase ka chiŋma ale viok kuui ale kan ta ŋmoruk a jam la.
15Chichiiba a baga a tagri niŋdeerɔ popola kama, fi be dan seba biik wari meena ka moali.
16Fi a yaali siita? Kan de ti yega, ti le basi ate fi yuak. 17Kan kasim a cheŋ fi mabiik jigi daa meena. Wa nyue ale kasim a nyuŋ ale fu. 18Nuru waai ale a biisi venta wie a te wa vaanchoa la, a nye ase ka kpaliŋ tigsuŋ la, yaase gebik woŋ la, yaase pein la.
19Fi dan pai fi sebchakka a basi waai ale kan ta wensie la jigi ku a nye ase ka naboagi nyɔnɔ ale a chaam ŋanta diila, yaase fi a cheŋ naŋ kaai ale wɛ la nyiŋ diila.
20Waai ale a lenni yiila a te waai sui ale kaasi la a nye ase ka waai ale yeeri wa garuk diipo ate ŋoota a boro la, yaase fi le kpiiri kaam a nyo noruk po diila.
21Kɔm a dan ta fi dachiak te wa ŋandiinta ate wa dɛ. Nyanyuila a abe dan ta wa, te wa nyiam ate wa nyu. 22Fi pai ka bolim kaala a vi wa zuk, ate Naawen ale te fu tutuna.
23Wiilukku geŋsa vioku ta ka ŋmoruk a jam ate bumbobrɔ a ta suipuurum a jam.
24Fi bo gboŋ zuk gugoruk po, a zunchoŋŋa ale fi le bo yeri naliŋ po ate nipok tugurik tɔŋdɔba a bo di po.
25Ase nya yɔgsik ale ka dii a te nyanyuila ale ta waai la, ku ka dila ase fi nin wom wapaala maŋsa a ta nyini niŋniŋŋa.
26Ase wayɔrisima nyama a dan siak a te gaasa nyama, ku a nye ase ka bulik nyiam daŋka yaase bulik nyiam poatika la.
27Ku an nala ale fi le de siita yega, ku an nala mɛ ate fi yaali zula a te fi dega.
28Nuru waai ale kan bag wadek a yik la a nye ase ka tɛŋ kpieŋ ale kan ta pagrim diila.

english_text:
Don't Be a Fool
1Expecting snow in summer
and rain in the dry season
makes more sense
than honoring a fool.
2A curse you don't deserve
will take wings and fly away
like a sparrow or a swallow.
3Horses and donkeys
must be beaten and bridled—
and so must fools.
4Don't make a fool of yourself
by answering a fool.
5But if you answer any fools,
show how foolish they are,
so they won't feel smart.
6Sending a message by a fool
is like chopping off your foot
just to spite yourself.
7A fool with words of wisdom
is like an athlete
with legs that can't move.
8Are you going to honor a fool?
Why not shoot a slingshot
with the rock tied tight?
9A thornbush waved around
in the hand of a drunkard
is no worse than a proverb
in the mouth of a fool.
10It's no smarter to shoot arrows
at every passerby
than it is to hire a bunch
of worthless nobodies.
11 Dogs return to eat their vomit,
just as fools repeat
their foolishness.
12There is more hope for a fool
than for someone who says,
“I'm really smart!”
13Don't be lazy and keep saying,
“There's a lion outside!”
14A door turns on its hinges,
but a lazy person
just turns over in bed.
15Some of us are so lazy
that we won't lift a hand
to feed ourselves.
16A lazy person says,
“I am smarter
than everyone else.”
17It's better to take hold
of a mad dog by the ears
than to take part
in someone else's argument.
18It's no crazier to shoot
sharp and flaming arrows
19than to cheat someone and say,
“I was only fooling!”
20Where there is no fuel
a fire goes out;
where there is no gossip
arguments come to an end.
21Troublemakers start trouble,
just as sparks and fuel
start a fire.
22There is nothing so delicious
as the taste of gossip!
It melts in your mouth.
23Hiding hateful thoughts
behind smooth talk
is like coating a clay pot
with a cheap glaze.
24The pleasant talk
of an enemy
hides more evil plans
25than can be counted—
so don't believe a word!
26Everyone will see through
those evil plans.
27 If you dig a pit,
you will fall in;
if you start a stone rolling,
it will roll back on you.
28Watch out for anyone
who tells lies and flatters—
they are out to get you.
translation_text:
1Ase ŋmoruk nika ale kan ta kiri fanɔi vaari po la, dila mɛ ate zula a ka kiri a te beruwa. 2Kikaasa kan jam fi zuwa nin ka fi mɛ nin magsi dila, ŋa ale nye ase ka nuim ale bo wen ale kan zi diila.
3Fiŋ ka wusum ale soa, a pai miik a dari boniŋ mɛ ate doari a soa beruk ŋaaŋ.
4Kan tulisi beruk a magsi chaab ale wa betta, dan kan daa di fi mɛ ale nye ase ka wadek la.
5Tulisi beruk a magsi chaab ale wa betta, dan kan daa di wa ale pai wadek a chim ka yam nyɔnɔ.
6A waai ale pai tomtomiŋ a te beruk la, a che ka wadek naŋsa ale a gisi daanika a te wadek.
7Ase gbaniŋ naŋsa, ale kan ta kiri diila, wamagsini ka dila a te beruk.
8Ase waai ale pai tain a nyo visiŋ po la a nye ase ka waai ale pai zula a te beruk la.
9Ase muŋ ale a lu danyuirik diila. Wamagsini ka dila a bo beruk nɔi po.
10Tuima nyɔnɔ waai ale a pai beruk yaase waai ale za a nya tuimaŋa la a nye ase ka tɔŋdɔ ale tɔŋ a basi dula.
11Ase biak ale ŋman a lak ka chichiita diila, ku ka dila ate beruk kuui nyiem ale ŋman a tom wa betta la.
12Waai ale a poli ayen wa ta yam la, alege ka bu la, betta a gaam wa kama.
13Nyiŋworuk nyɔnɔwa a ta ka wie a weeni ayen, <<Mi a kan nyini peelim dii nyiŋla gbeŋli a baga a bo suiku po kama. Ku sum ka wensie gbeŋli ale boro.>>
14Ase kuta ale a yik tuok ate ku a lik ale a lak diila, dila mɛ ate nyiŋworuk nyɔnɔwa gaduokku a yik wa a tara.
15Nuruba gela nyiŋ wɔrukku a nye kama ate ba nisa nɔi ta juelika a toa a te ba.
16Nyiŋworuk nyam a poli ayen ba seba gaam yam nyam bayopɔi kama.
17Fi ta fidek a jo a waai wari po a nak nanpaga ku nyiŋ alege ate ku an nya fu la, ku ka betta ase fi ale ga yik biak turi diila.
18Ku a nye ase ka yesiŋ ale a tɔŋ tom diila.
19Ka waai ale a weeni venta wie a sak wa doa ale weeni ayen, <<Mi poom a diini kama.>>
20Daata a dan kan boro bolim a kpi kama, ŋaaŋzum mɛ a dan kan boro kpaliŋ a kan boro.
21Kpaliŋ nyeerɔ a piilim kpaliŋ ka nna se bolim a nyiem ale chɔgsi kaala yaase daata diila.
22Ŋaaŋzum nyɔnɔ wie a nye a ase ka ŋandiin masa ale a siŋ a waai poi po diila.
23Gaasa nyɔnɔ ale biisi wamasik a lik wa suinum ase ba ale pai jabuui ale a nyaksi a nye yak liik nyiŋ diila.
24Nuruba ale weeni wie ŋaai ale masa la a lirim ba biem popolaŋa, alege ba a paasi fu kama. 25Ba a nye badek kama nna se ba ka nuru maŋsa la, alege kan ta siaka ale ba. Ba suiniimaŋa a sueri ale ka biem. 26Wa dan poom pai pimpaasima a lik wa gaasaŋa, ŋa ale nye jassi nuru boari suŋsuŋ po.
27Fi dan bari baruk ayen ku yik nuruba, ku ale cheem yik ka fidek. Fi abe dan bilim piuŋ ayen ku bilim a ji a waai zuk, ku ale cheem bilim a ji ka fidek.
28Giŋgeluŋ kuui ale a velim la a kisa baai ale a nye wa wari la kama, ate venta pimpaga a ka kiri ya.

english_text:
Don't Brag about Tomorrow
1 Don't brag about tomorrow!
Each day brings
its own surprises.
2Don't brag about yourself—
let others praise you.
3Stones and sand are heavy,
but trouble caused by a fool
is a much heavier load.
4An angry person is dangerous,
but a jealous person
is even worse.
5A truly good friend
will openly correct you.
6You can trust a friend
who corrects you,
but kisses from an enemy
are nothing but lies.
7If you have had enough to eat,
honey doesn't taste good,
but if you are really hungry,
you will eat anything.
8When you are far from home,
you feel like a bird
without a nest.
9The sweet smell of incense
can make you feel good,
but true friendship
is better still.
10Don't desert an old friend
of your family
or visit your relatives
when you are in trouble.
A friend nearby is better
than relatives far away.
11My child, show good sense!
Then I will be happy
and able to answer anyone
who criticizes me.
12Be cautious and hide
when you see danger—
don't be stupid and walk
right into trouble.
13You deserve to lose your coat
if you loan it to someone
to guarantee payment
for the debt of a stranger.
14A loud greeting
early in the morning
is the same as a curse.
15The steady dripping of rain
and the nagging of a wife
are one and the same.
16It's easier to catch the wind
or hold olive oil in your hand
than to stop a nagging wife.
17Just as iron sharpens iron,
friends sharpen the minds
of each other.
18Take care of a tree,
and you will eat its fruit;
look after your master,
and you will be praised.
19You see your face in a mirror
and your thoughts
in the minds of others.
20Death and the grave
are never satisfied,
and neither are humans.
21Gold and silver are tested
in a red-hot furnace,
but we are tested by praise.
22No matter how hard
you beat a fool,
you can't pound out
the foolishness.
23You should take good care
of your sheep and goats,
24because wealth and honor
don't last forever.
25After the hay is cut
and the new growth appears
and the harvest is over,
26you can sell lambs and goats
to buy clothes and land.
27From the milk of the goats,
you can make enough cheese
to feed your family
and all your servants.
translation_text:
1Kan nak kuusidi chum nyiŋŋa, fi zɛ danni ale ta ka dii cheen la. 2Kan pak fi dega, basi ate nuru yoŋta a nye dila. 3Tana a dobra kama ate tanta a dobra gaam di ate beruk ale a daani diila a dobra a gaam ŋala meena. 4Suipuurum a bie kama ale ŋman a kaasi tuima alege nyuri a pagra a gaam ŋa kama. 5Fi dan toariŋ nuruwa nimbie po a zunchoŋŋa fi le suk a yaali wa.
6Fi doa a dan te fu tuem a zunchoŋŋa fi dachiak ale a gbaari fu.
7Fi dan dɛ chak siita mɛ an poom masa a te fu, alege kom a dan ta fu jabuui ale toa la a masa kama. 8Ase nuim ale a nyini bu tuk po a cheŋ diila, nidoa waai ale a basi wa yeri la mɛ ka dila. 9Kpaam ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa la a basi ate ka fi sui a peenti, doa masim a nyini ka wa sinsak maŋsa jigi. 10Kan baŋ fi doa yaase fi kowa doa wari ya. Ate diipo ate fi a silim la, fi kan bek mabiik ayen wa maari fu. Fi dan cheŋ waai ale moata fu la jigi a zunchoŋ fi le cheŋ fi mabiik waai ale yalima la jigi.
11M biiga, be ta yam, abe fi nye ate m sui a peenti. Ate m baga a tulisi baai ale kan biisi mu a magsi la. 12Waai ale ta yam la nyiem de ka niŋ a nya ayen daanika a cheena ate wa kpesi wadek. Alege beruk nyiem kala a basi du kama ate di jam a diiri wa ate wa yaa ŋma wadek. 13Waai a dan chim beruk ayen wa zaani ate nichaanɔ a tuesi pami jaab, wa magsi wa pai ka wadek nitalim a zaani a magsi pamini tuesika. 14Fi dan tue na puusi waai ale moata fu la saluik yokyokwa, ku a nye ase ka kikaasa la. 15Nipok kpaliŋ kpaliŋdɔ nyeka a puuri ka sui ase ŋmoruk kuui ale kasim a minisi a kan vɔssi la. 16Fi dan ayen fi nye ate wa basi wa funfɔblaŋa, ku a nye ase ka waai ale a yaali ayen wa nye ate vioku a basi la, yaase waai ale a yaali wa yik jaab alege ate kpaam a bo wa nisa po la.
17Ase ba le pai kuta a saasi chaab diila, nuruba mɛ a maari chaab ka dila. 18Ase tuimtomdɔ waai ale a nya tiib zuk a baga a dɛ bu yɔna diila, dila mɛ ate tuimtomdɔ waai ale a nye wa kpagi ale a yaali diila ale nya wa tutuna. 19Ase nuru ale a nya wa nimbidiaka nyiam po diila, dila mɛ ate wa suinummu a dak wa a sak.
20Ase Kum ale Kaasuŋ ale kaa chak diila, dila mɛ ate nuru a kan chak ale ŋanta. 21Bolim ate ba pai chamsi kpana ale ligmɔniŋ a nya, alege ba chamsi nuru a nya ale ka pimpauk. 22Fi dan poom a nak beruk ase ba ale a kuri zaa diila, wa kan basi wa bettaŋa.
23Seba fi piisaŋa ale ka diila a chak, abe fi te ate fi suinum a bo fi niiŋa zuk nyaasim. 24Diila jigsika a kan boro taam wuu, ate naam zutɔk a kan boro a ga paari gaŋ kaai ale pai a saŋ la. 25Ate ba dan ŋari wuuta, ate ŋan bulaŋa ate ba bori laŋsaŋa bo la a nyini, ate ba tigsi guuta wuutaŋa a ta jo dueni, 26ni piisaŋa ale te kɔbta a magsi gatta, ate ni booŋa ale tuni laŋsaŋa nyiŋ. 27Ate ni ale nya booŋa biisim yega ate ku paari ni ale ni dɔkdem ale ni tomteerɔma nipokbilisaŋa.

english_text:
The Law of God Makes Sense
1Wicked people run away
when no one chases them,
but those who live right
are as brave as lions.
2In time of civil war
there are many leaders,
but a sensible leader
restores law and order.
3When someone poor takes over
and mistreats the poor,
it's like a heavy rain
destroying the crops.
4Lawbreakers praise criminals,
but law-abiding citizens
always oppose them.
5Criminals don't know
what justice means,
but all who respect the Lord
understand it completely.
6It's better to be poor
and live right,
than to be rich
and dishonest.
7It makes good sense
to obey the Law of God,
but you disgrace your parents
if you make friends
with worthless nobodies.
8If you make money by charging
high interest rates,
you will lose it all to someone
who cares for the poor.
9God cannot stand the prayers
of anyone who disobeys
his Law.
10By leading good people to sin,
you dig a pit for yourself,
but all who live right
will have a bright future.
11The rich think highly
of themselves,
but anyone poor and sensible
sees right through them.
12When an honest person wins,
it's time to celebrate;
when crooks are in control,
it's best to hide.
13If you don't confess your sins,
you will be a failure.
But God will be merciful
if you confess your sins
and give them up.
14The Lord blesses everyone
who is afraid to do evil,
but if you are cruel,
you will end up in trouble.
15A ruler who mistreats the poor
is like a roaring lion
or a bear hunting for food.
16A heartless leader is a fool,
but anyone who refuses
to get rich by cheating others
will live a long time.
17Don't give help to murderers!
Make them stay on the run
for as long as they live.
18Honesty will keep you safe,
but everyone who is crooked
will suddenly fall.
19Work hard, and you will have
a lot of food;
waste time, and you will have
a lot of trouble.
20God blesses his loyal people,
but punishes all who want
to get rich quick.
21It isn't right to be unfair,
but some people can be bribed
with only a piece of bread.
22Don't be selfish
and eager to get rich—
you will end up worse off
than you can imagine.
23Honest correction
is appreciated
more than flattery.
24If you cheat your parents
and don't think it's wrong,
you are a common thief.
25Selfish people cause trouble,
but you will live a full life
if you trust the Lord.
26Only fools would trust
what they alone think,
but if you live by wisdom,
you will do all right.
27Giving to the poor
will keep you from poverty,
but if you close your eyes
to their needs,
everyone will curse you.
28When crooks are in control,
everyone tries to hide,
but when they lose power,
good people are everywhere.
translation_text:
1Gaasa nyɔnɔwa a chali kama alege ate waai an poom a vi wa, alege wayɔrisima nyɔnɔwa suinummu a pagra kama nna se gbeŋli la. 2Tɛŋ nuruba nyeela a dan kan nala, niŋdeerɔma a jɔk ba naamu kama. Alege yam ale sebika niŋdeerɔba a ta ka zaana nalimnyiini. 3Nuru jak waai ale a namsi jajak la, a nye ase ka ŋmoruk ale ni kaasi ŋankpaanta diila. 4Baai ale a zɛri sinsaŋŋa la, a pakka gaasa nyam, alege baai ale ta sinsaŋŋa la a kpaliŋ ale ka gaasa nyama. 5Nuru baata a kan miŋ wensie kiri ya, alege baai ale a gisi Naawen la a miŋ ku kiri ka nalimnyiini.
6Jajak a dan a cheŋ wa wensie suik po, ku gaam jigsirɔ ale va venta suik po. 7Nuru paalisa baai ale a nye tuewomma a te sinsaŋŋa la, ka yam nyam. Baai ale a va doa baai ale waara la a ta ka chivie a jam ba nyam zuk. 8Waai ale a gebi ligra a nya nyuenta la ale jɔk ŋa. Ku kpeglim ka ŋa le jo ka waai ale ta jiirim ale ŋanjaksa la nisima po. 9Waai ale lik turi a kan wom sinsaŋŋa la, kula nyɔnɔ puusa ka leeta a te Naawen. 10Baai ale a paasi nuru maŋsa a ta ba a jo biem po la ale lɔ ka badek baruk po, alege baai ale za dekki la ale nya ŋan maŋsa.
11Jigsirɔ ale poli ayen wa ta yam ka wadek nina po, alege waai ale jaŋ ale ta miŋ chakka la a seba dii ale nala la kama. 12Ase Wen nuruma a dan nya nyeboka, waai meena sue a peenti kama. Alege gaasa nyam a dan nya pagrim nuruba ale jo ŋooma vie. 13Nuru baai ale a lik ba wabaata la a kan nya ba dega, alege ba dan weeni ale basi ŋa ba ale nya jiirim. 14Niauŋ a bo ale waai ale a chali Naawen diipo meena la jigi, alege waai ale ta tukpari la ale jo ninam po. 15Niŋdeerɔ biok a nye ase ka gbeŋli yaase gɔi biak ale waara diila nuru waai ale jaŋ la jigi.
16Niŋdeerɔ waai ale kan ta miŋka la a namsi ka wa nuruba, alege waai ale kaa yaali venta ŋanta la daaŋa ale wɔŋa. 17Nuru koorik popola a ta wa a daani ka dila a ga a paari wa kum. Kan nya wa zuwa. 18Waai ale a cheŋ wensie suik la ale nya varibasika, alege waai ale kan va wensie po la ale deri lɔ tɛŋ. 19Tuimtomdɔ waai ale ta nyiŋbiiri a kpa la a ta ŋandiinta ka nna yegayega, alege nuru waai ale a va wie kayaata la ale kpeglim ale ka jaŋsa. 20Wensie nuru ale nya niauŋ yegayega, alege nuru waai ale a yaali ayen wa kpabi a jigsi la ale ga jo ka daanika po.
21Fi daa sak lukka ku an nala, alege dɛka nyiŋ nuru a bag nye a kaasi kama. 22Nuru baai ale a yaali de gaamka la a yaali kama ayen ba kpabi a jigsi, alege zɛ ayen ba a cheŋ tuak ka jaŋsa po. 23Waai a dan toariŋ nuru ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ wa le nya pimpauk a gaam waai ale a paasi la. 24Waai ale a zu wa ko ale wa ma alege a weeni ayen, <<Kaasuŋ boa ale bo nya kude po?>> Wa ale nuru koorik ka bunyi. 25De gaamka nyɔnɔ a siti ka kpaliŋ, alege waai ale ta sebchakka ale Naawen la ale nya wadek kama.
26A waai ale ta sebchakka ale wadek popola la ka beruk, alege waai ale a cheŋ yam po la a nya varibasika kama. 27Nuru waai ale a te ŋanjaksa ŋanta la, a kan silim jaaboa, alege waai ale kan cheem a nya ba la ale nya kikaasa yegayega. 28Gaasa nyam a dan bo pagrim po, nuruba a suk kama. Ba dan ta chaab ale kaasuŋ Wen nuruma a piisi kama.

english_text:
Use Good Sense
1If you keep being stubborn
after many warnings,
you will suddenly discover
you have gone too far.
2When justice rules a nation,
everyone is glad;
when injustice rules,
everyone groans.
3If you love wisdom
your parents will be glad,
but chasing after bad women
will cost you everything.
4An honest ruler
makes the nation strong;
a ruler who takes bribes
will bring it to ruin.
5Flattery is nothing less
than setting a trap.
6Your sins will catch you,
but everyone who lives right
will sing and celebrate.
7The wicked don't care
about the rights of the poor,
but good people do.
8Sneering at others is a spark
that sets a city on fire;
using good sense can put out
the flames of anger.
9Be wise and don't sue a fool.
You won't get satisfaction,
because all the fool will do
is sneer and shout.
10A murderer hates everyone
who is honest
and lives right.
11Don't be a fool
and quickly lose your temper—
be sensible and patient.
12A ruler who listens to lies
will have corrupt officials.
13The poor and all who abuse them
must each depend on God
for light.
14Kings who are fair to the poor
will rule a long time.
15Correct your children,
and they will be wise;
children out of control
disgrace their mothers.
16Crime increases
when crooks are in power,
but law-abiding citizens
will see them fall.
17If you correct your children,
they will bring you peace
and happiness.
18Without guidance from God
law and order disappear,
but God blesses everyone
who obeys his Law.
19 Even when servants are smart,
it takes more than words
to make them obey.
20There is more hope for a fool
than for someone who speaks
without thinking.
21Slaves that you treat kindly
from their childhood
will cause you sorrow.
22A person with a quick temper
stirs up arguments
and commits a lot of sins.
23Too much pride brings disgrace;
humility leads to honor.
24If you take part in a crime
you are your worst enemy,
because even under oath
you can't tell the truth.
25Don't fall into the trap
of being a coward—
trust the Lord,
and you will be safe.
26Many try to make friends
with a ruler,
but justice comes
from the Lord.
27Good people and criminals
can't stand each other.
translation_text:
1Nuru waai ale kaa wom sinsaga la ale deri kpi kama wa tukpanni nyiŋ ale kan nyini du a nyini. 2Wen nuruma a dan bo pagrim po, nuruma a de ka masim. Alege gaasa nyama a dan bo pagrim po nuruma a kum kama. 3Waai ale a yaali yam la a nye ate ka wa ko sui a peenti, alege waai ale a yaali nipooba la, a nueri ka wa nitalim. 4Naab waai ale chekki la a yik wa tɛŋka a zaani kama, alege waai ale te ate ba pai ŋanta a da wa la a lɔnsi ka kama. 5Baai ale ta nɔi masim la a bari ka nuruba.
6Wabaata nyam bari yik nuru baata kama, alege ku kan yik wayɔrisima nyama ate ba nyiem yaa nye masim nuemka. 7Wayɔrisima nyɔnɔwa a seba dii ale magsi jajakka la kama, alege gaasa nyɔnɔwa niŋ a poom karo ayen wa miŋ wari ya. 8Baai ale a la nuruba la a nye kama ate tɛŋ a chɔgsi bolim, alege baai ale ta yam la a kpimsi ka suipuurum. 9Ase yam nyɔnɔ a dan ta nanpaga ale beruk, beruku a biisi a basi kama ale a la, ate chim nyeka a kan boro. 10Nuru koorisa a kisa nuru baai ale kan ta ŋmiŋmaasa la kama, alege waai ale za dekki la a yaali ayen wa maari kama.
11Beruk a sak wa suipuurum ka nna nwuli alege yam nyɔnɔ a yik wadek kama. 12Niŋdeerɔ a daa wom venta wie, wa ŋaaŋviirɔma meena a chim ka gaasa nyam. 13Ŋanjaksaŋa ale ba namsidɔma meena ka Naawen ale basi ate ba a nya. 14Naab waai ale a bo ŋanjaksa wensie buusa bo ka la, wa naam zukpaglika ale boro taam wuu. 15Biik waalika a te wa ka yam, alege biik kaai ate ba a basi wa la a ta ka chivie a jam a te wa ma.
16Ase gaasa nyam a dan bo pagrim po, biem a piisi kama. Alege Wen nuruma ale boro a nya ba lueta. 17Te fi biika waalika, ate wa ale basi ate fi vuusi. Wa ale te ate fi chiika a dɛ masim. 18Juijui ate Naawen wanni a ka la, nuruma a nye a kaasi kama, alege waai ale ta sinsaŋŋa la ale nya niauŋ. 19Biik nyiini a kan tagri tomteerɔ, wa dan poom miŋ fi ale a weeni diila, wa kan nye. 20Beruk a ta yiila a gaam a waai ale a biisi ale kan poli la kama.
21Fi daa poagi fi tomteerɔ wa ale yiri a zɛri fi nɔi. 22Waai sui ale kpabi a puuri la, a kpabi a nye ka kpaliŋ ale a nye wie ŋaai ale bie la. 23Nuru kanjanta a ta wa siŋ ka tɛŋ alege nuru waai ale a yik wadek chiik la a te ka zula. 24Fi dan maari zue, fi a nye ka fidek. Ba ale namsi fu ase fi ale weeni kaasuŋ kuui ale nye la, alege kikaasa ale bo fi zuk ase fi a nin kan weeni ya. 25Nurubiik yɔgsum chala ka baruk barika, alege waai ale ta sebchakka ale Naawen la a nya boka dek jigi kama.
26Nuruba yegayega a zak a nya ka kpaga, alege nuru a nya wensie boteka a nyini ka Naawen jigi. 27Wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ a kisi gaasa nyɔnɔwa kama, ate gaasa nyɔnɔwa mɛ a kisa wayɔrisima nyɔnɔwa.

english_text:
The Sayings of Agur
1These are the sayings
and the message
of Agur son of Jakeh.
Someone cries out to God,
“I am completely worn out!
How can I last?
2I am far too stupid
to be considered human.
3I never was wise,
and I don't understand
what God is like.”
4 Has anyone gone up to heaven
and come back down?
Has anyone grabbed hold
of the wind?
Has anyone wrapped up the sea
or marked out boundaries
for the earth?
If you know of any
who have done such things,
then tell me their names
and their children's names.
5Everything God says is true—
and it's a shield for all
who come to him for safety.
6Don't change what God has said!
He will correct you and show
that you are a liar.
7There are two things, Lord,
I want you to do for me
before I die:
8Make me absolutely honest
and don't let me be too poor
or too rich.
Give me just what I need.
9If I have too much to eat,
I might forget about you;
if I don't have enough,
I might steal
and disgrace your name.
10Don't tell a slave owner
something bad about one
of the slaves.
That slave will curse you,
and you will be in trouble.
11Some people curse their father
and even their mother;
12others think they are perfect,
but they are stained by sin.
13Some people are stuck-up
and act like snobs;
14others are so greedy
that they gobble up
the poor and homeless.
15Greed has twins,
each named “Give me!”
There are three or four things
that are never satisfied:
16The world of the dead
and a childless wife,
the thirsty earth
and a flaming fire.
17Don't make fun of your father
or disobey your mother—
crows will peck out your eyes,
and buzzards will eat
the rest of you.
18There are three or four things
I cannot understand:
19 How eagles fly so high
or snakes crawl on rocks,
how ships sail the ocean
or people fall in love.
20An unfaithful wife says,
“Sleeping with another man
is as natural as eating.”
21There are three or four things
that make the earth tremble
and are unbearable:
22A slave who becomes king,
a fool who eats too much,
23a hateful woman
who finds a husband,
and a slave who takes the place
of the woman who owns her.
24On this earth four things
are small but very wise:
25Ants, who seem to be feeble,
but store up food
all summer long;
26badgers, who seem to be weak,
but live among the rocks;
27locusts, who have no king,
but march like an army;
28lizards, which can be caught
in your hand,
but sneak into palaces.
29Three or four creatures
really strut around:
30Those fearless lions
who rule the jungle,
31those proud roosters,
those mountain goats,
and those rulers
who have no enemies.
32If you are foolishly bragging
or planning something evil,
then stop it now!
33If you churn milk
you get butter;
if you pound on your nose,
you get blood—
and if you stay angry,
you get in trouble.
translation_text:
1Jakey biika Agur wieŋa ale nna. M Wen yaa m jiak kama. M dek Wen yaa, m sum a jiak kama ate pagrim a ka m po.
2M ka beruk, ate m ka m dek yam mɛ. 3Mi an zamsi yam yaase m seba Waai Ale Welema la wari ya. 4Ka wana ale jueli wenŋmazuk ale siŋ ya? Ka wana ale baga a gum vioku a ta wa nisima po? Ka wana ale baga a kpamsi nyaataŋa a nyo wa garuk po? Ka wana ale nye tɛŋka kpeglimka meena? Wa yue ale boa, wa biika mɛ yue ale boa. Weeni a sak mu ase fi a nin seba.
5Naawen wari meena ka wensie. Wa chim ka ligrɔ a te baai ale a jam wa jigi ayen wa a nya ba zuk la. 6Kan yaali wari a gum wa wieŋa po, fi dan nye dila fi ka velimvendik, wa le toariŋ fu.
7M Naawen ya, mi a yaali ka wie ŋaye ayen fi nye a te mu. Basi ate m nya ŋa abe m ge a kpi. 8Dii ale a dɛ niŋ la ale maari mu ate m kan velim. Dii ale a saari buye la ale kan te m jaŋ yaase m jigsi. Te ate mi a nya a magsi ate m kan silimu. 9Dii nyiŋla m dan jigsi, m le zɛri fu abe m weeni ayen, <<Ka wana ale Naawen?>> Ate m dan jaŋ, da dii dai m le cheŋ ga zu ate ku ta leeta a jam Naawen yuei weleŋka jigi.
10Kan weeni tomteerɔ kaasuŋ a sak wa kpagi ya. Wa ale ka a te fu ate ku ale sum a va fu. 11Nuruba gela a ka a te ba koba kama ale kan nye ba maba jiamoa. 12Ba nye cheri ka badek nimbie po, alege ba daŋ kama ale an poom sugri ba dega. 13Ba a poli kama ayen ba ka nuru maŋsa, alege ba daa jaaboa. 14Ba nyinaŋa a nye ase ka gebik woŋsa ale gebi fiisa la, a nɛ ŋanjaksa tɛŋka zuk ale baai ale a silim a maa bo nuruba po la.
15Jumbaleok a ta ka noa ŋaye a dari ziim ale a kum a weeni ayen, <<Yegayega>> Ŋanta bata ale boro a kan maara a chagi. Aaya, banaansi ale boro a weeni ayen, <<Ku an magsi ya.>> 16Boosuku ale kirika ale tɛŋ kaai ale kaa jo nyiamoa ale bolim ŋiak. 17Numbiri dii ale a nye ko a la la ale a zɛri ma sinsaga la, tagaarutaŋa ale bo viaka po la ale yeeri bu ate duinsa a dɛ.
18Ŋanta bata ale cha mi. Aaya, ŋanta banaansi ate mi a kan miŋ ku kiri ya. 19Ku ale nye dii ate jiiruk nyiem bo chiŋmaaŋa po ale ku ale nye dii ate waab a bo pina po ale ku ale nye dii ate ŋaaruŋ a cheŋ nyakpiemu zuk ale ku ale nye dii ate nidoa a yaali nipok.
20Nipok kaboŋ nyeerik ale dɛ nidoa kama, a yaa duisi wa nɔnni ale weeni ayen, <<Kaasuŋ boa ale bo nya kude po?>>
21Wie ŋata ale basi ate tɛŋka a choa, aaya, ŋanaansi ale kan baga a zaani. 22Ase yɔma a nin chim naab, ate beruk puuk a sueri ale ŋandiinta, 23nipok waai nyeka ale toa la a nyiem yaa jam nya chorɔ a yali, ate dɔklie nyiem yaa jam tagri wa kpagni.
24Wie ŋanaansi ale fiisa a bo tɛŋzuk de alege a ta yam nna yegayega. 25Nankeriŋsa, si ka pagrimoa, alege si a dueni ŋandiinta fanɔi wen. 26Suensa, ka pagrimoa alege si a nye si yieŋa ka pina po. 27Tintue ŋa ka naaba alege ŋa a va ka chaab. 28Baŋsa, si yikka an toa, alege si bo nalima yie po.
29Ŋanta bata ale boro ate ŋa chelim a nala, aaya, ŋanta banaansi ale a nyiem. 30Gbeŋli ale ka duŋsaŋa naab la, ate di kan viriŋ ayen wari nyiŋla, 31ale kpadiak ale buduk ale naab waai ale de wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma niŋ la.
32Ase fi dan chim beruk ale ta kanjanta yaase fi nye biem, kan nak kuusidi dila nyiŋŋa, pai fi nisaŋa a lik fi nɔnni ale chivie. 33Ase ba ale a nak biisim ate bu a goa diila, ale a tak nyue ate ziim a nyini diila, ka dila ate fi dan nye ate nuruba sue a puuri wɔkwɔk a jam la.

english_text:
What King Lemuel's Mother Taught Him
1These are the sayings
that King Lemuel of Massa
was taught by his mother.
2My son Lemuel, you were born
in answer to my prayers,
so listen carefully.
3Don't waste your life
chasing after women!
This has ruined many kings.
4Kings and leaders
should not get drunk
or even want to drink.
5Drinking makes you forget
your responsibilities,
and you mistreat the poor.
6Beer and wine are only
for the dying or for those
who have lost all hope.
7Let them drink and forget
how poor and miserable
they feel.
8But you must defend
those who are helpless
and have no hope.
9Be fair and give justice
to the poor and homeless.
In Praise of a Good Wife
10A truly good wife
is the most precious treasure
a man can find!
11Her husband depends on her,
and she never
lets him down.
12She is good to him
every day of her life,
13and with her own hands
she gladly makes clothes.
14She is like a sailing ship
that brings food
from across the sea.
15She gets up before daylight
to prepare food for her family
and for her servants.
16She knows how to buy land
and how to plant a vineyard,
17and she always works hard.
18She knows when to buy or sell,
and she stays busy
until late at night.
19She spins her own cloth,
20and she helps the poor
and the needy.
21Her family has warm clothing,
and so she doesn't worry
when it snows.
22She does her own sewing,
and everything she wears
is beautiful.
23Her husband is a well-known
and respected leader
in the city.
24She makes clothes to sell
to the shop owners.
25She is strong and graceful,
as well as cheerful
about the future.
26Her words are sensible,
and her advice
is thoughtful.
27She takes good care
of her family
and is never lazy.
28Her children praise her,
and with great pride
her husband says,
29“There are many good women,
but you are the best!”
30Charm can be deceiving,
and beauty fades away,
but a woman
who honors the Lord
deserves to be praised.
31Show her respect—
praise her in public
for what she has done.
translation_text:
1Naab Lemuel ale weeni bi sii ate wa mawa a sak la ale nna. 2<<M dek biiga, m dek popo biiga, m bek ka Naawen ate wa pai fu a te mu. 3Kan pai fi pagrim a te nipooba, baai ale a kaasi nalima.
4Lemuel, ku an nala ayen nalima a nyu daamoa, yaase kpaga a nyu da pagrisa. 5Diila ba dan nyu, ba ale baŋ wie ate ba kan bo wensie buusa a te baai ate ba ta a namsi la. 6Pai da pagrik a te waai ale cheŋ a bɛ la, abe fi te waai chiik ale bo daanika po la daam. 7Basi ate ba nyu a baŋ ba jaŋsaŋa abe ba kan ŋman teeri ba daanika.
8Biisi a te baai ale kan baga a biisi a te badek la. Tom wensie tuima a te baai ale bo daanika po la. 9Wensie, be biisi a te ŋanjaksa ale baai ale kan ta maarika la, abe fi basi ate wensie buusa boka a tom tuima.
10Ka wana ale wa nya nipok maŋŋa ate wa baga wie a nye? Wa gaam tintain munta. 11Wa chorɔwa a baga a ta sebchakka ale wa kama, ate wa a nye ate wa boka po a nya jigsika nna yegayega. 12Wa boka po meena, wa ta ka ŋandiinta a jam a te wa alege daa daanika. 13Wa gisi a nya ka duŋ kɔbta ale bɔkta a pai a tom wa tuima. 14Wa a nye ase ka geruŋdɔ ŋaaruŋ ale a cheŋ niŋniŋ a ta ŋandiinta a jam la.
15Wa a yiri kama alege ate vanni a veenti a dik ŋandiinta a te wa dɔkdem ale a gomsi danni tuima a te wa dɔkliema. 16Wa a nya laŋ a da kama. Wa pai wa tutunaŋa a bori ŋanta wa kadukka po. 17Wa pagra kama ale ta nyiŋbiiri ale tuima tomka. 18Wa a yaali kama ayen wa ale a nye dii meena la a ta nyuenta a jam a te wa. Wa zeuŋku a baga a toati a paari yok suŋsuŋ kama. 19Wa nisaŋa a kasim a yɔk ka ŋanta ale a nye gattaasa.
20Wa a teeri wa nisa a maari ŋanjaksa ale baai ale a silim la. 21Wa kpaziim a kan nak ale ŋoota wen ya dii nyiŋla wa ta ŋoota gatta kama a te wa dɔkdemma.
22Wa a nye ka wadek gattiak a lik wa gaduokku. Wa a jo ka garuk naliŋsa ate wa garuk woŋtaŋa a chim sobluk ale mɔnuŋ a dam chaab. 23Tɛŋka nansuiŋtaŋa demma a seba wa chorɔwa kama, juijui ate wa a kali ale tɛŋka niŋdeerɔma la.
24Wa a nye ka gatta ale chiak gbana a da a te geruŋdɔba. 25Pagrim ale zula a bo wa po ate wa kpaziim a kan nak ale chum wie.
26Wa dan biisi, yam a bo wa biika po kama ale a te sinsaga ale jiirim.
27Wa a kpesi a nya wa yenni po ŋanta meena ale ka wari a nye ale nyiŋ wɔrukwa. 28Wa bisaŋa a yiti a wi wa ayen suipeentik nyɔnɔ. Wa chorɔwa mɛ a pak wa. 29<<Nipooba yegayega a boro kama ate ba nyeka a nala ale baga wie a nye abo tɛŋka zuk meena, alege fi gaam ba meena kama.>> 30Nyeela maŋsa a baga chim pimpaasima kama, nalim mɛ ka kinla, alege nipok waai ale a chali Naawen la ale magsi pakka. 31Tuni wa ale nye dii meena la nyiŋ. Te wa tuimaŋa nyiŋ nuru meena a pak wa.

english_text:
Nothing Makes Sense
1When the son of David was king in Jerusalem, he was known to be very wise, and he said:
2Nothing makes sense!
Everything is nonsense.
I have seen it all—
nothing makes sense!
3What is there to show
for all of our hard work
here on this earth?
4 People come, and people go,
but still the world
never changes.
5The sun comes up,
the sun goes down;
it hurries right back
to where it started from.
6The wind blows south,
the wind blows north;
round and round it blows
over and over again.
7All rivers empty into the sea,
but it never spills over;
one by one the rivers return
to their source.
8All of life is far more boring
than words could ever say.
Our eyes and our ears
are never satisfied
with what we see and hear.
9Everything that happens
has happened before;
nothing is new,
nothing under the sun.
10Someone might say,
“Here is something new!”
But it happened before,
long before we were born.
11No one who lived in the past
is remembered anymore,
and everyone yet to be born
will be forgotten too.
It Is Senseless To Be Wise
12I said these things when I lived in Jerusalem as king of Israel. 13With all my wisdom I tried to understand everything that happens here on earth. And God has made this so hard for us humans to do. 14I have seen it all, and everything is just as senseless as chasing the wind.
15If something is crooked,
it can't be made straight;
if something isn't there,
it can't be counted.
16 I said to myself, “You are by far the wisest person who has ever lived in Jerusalem. You are eager to learn, and you have learned a lot.” 17Then I decided to find out all I could about wisdom and foolishness. Soon I realized that this too was as senseless as chasing the wind.
18The more you know,
the more you hurt;
the more you understand,
the more you suffer.
translation_text:
1Deevid ale jam ka naab a bo Jerusalem la nidoabinni Sagrɔwa wieŋa ale nna: Sagrɔwa ayen, 2<<Ku ka kiri ya! Ku ka kiri ya! Ku din bola ka kiri ya! Jaab meena a ka kiri ya.>>
3Nuru ale nya ka boa a nyini wa ninammu meena po dii ate wa nam tɛŋzuk de la? 4Gaŋsa a jam kama ate gaŋsa a cheŋ, alege tɛŋzuk de a boro kama taam wuu. 5Wenbinni a pusi kama, wenbinni abe a siŋ kama, ale kpabi a ŋmani a cheŋ di pusika jigini. 6Vioku a fuk a cheŋ yeseoku ale tulim a cheŋ wiilukku geŋsa a gilim a gilim ku le poom liŋ va juijui la. 7Buboalisa meena chali a siŋ ka nyakpiemu po, alege nyakpiemu diem kan sueri. Buboalisaŋa ale nyini juijui la, dula jigini ate si ŋmani a cheŋ. 8Wari meena a ta ka jianta ate waai a kan baga a biisi ŋa wari ya. Numbinni a nya ka dila a kan jiagi, tunni mɛ a wom ka dila di kan jiagi.
9Dii ale liŋ boro la ale pilim boro dii ale liŋ nye la ale ŋman pilim nye. Wari a ka tɛŋzuk de a chim wapaali. 10Wari a boro ate waai ale baga ayen, <<Nya wanni de ka wapaali?>> Di poom liŋ bo dela kama ate ku beni, alege ate tama a jam. 11Ba kan ŋman teeri nuru kpagsa wari ya, ate baai mɛ ale diem cheena la baai ale paasaŋ ba la a kan teeri ba wari ya.
12Mi, sagrɔwa jam ka naab a nya Izirali zuk Jerusalem po. 13Mi jam yik ka m dek a zamsi ale kpesi ayen m gisi ale yam a nya dii meena ale nye tɛŋzuk la. Ka boan jib doabrita ate Naawen a pai ji nuru biiga! 14Mi nya wie ŋaai meena ale jam nye tɛŋzuk de la kama, ŋa meena ka kiri ya ŋa a nye ase ka fi le a vi viok diila.
15Jabuui ale goaliŋ la a ka teentika, jabuui ale kan karo la ba kan chiini.
16Mi yaa weeni m dek ayen, <<Nya m chim kama ale ta yam a gaam waai meena ale nya Jerusalem zuk ale ge te mi la. Mi nya ka yam ale sebika yega.>> 17Mi yaa poli ayen m miŋ yam ale yesiŋsa ale berinni kiri, alege mi yaa miŋ ayen kude mɛ a nye ase fi le a vi viok diila.
18Yam yega a ta ka niniga cheena. Fi dan ta sebika yega, fi a nya ka niniga yega.

english_text:
It Is Senseless To Be Selfish
1I said to myself, “Have fun and enjoy yourself!” But this didn't make sense. 2Laughing and having fun is crazy. What good does it do? 3I wanted to find out what was best for us during the short time we have on this earth. So I decided to make myself happy with wine and find out what it means to be foolish, without really being foolish myself.
4 I did some great things. I built houses and planted vineyards. 5I had flower gardens and orchards full of fruit trees. 6And I had pools where I could get water for the trees. 7 I owned slaves, and their sons and daughters became my slaves. I had more sheep and goats than anyone who had ever lived in Jerusalem. 8 Foreign rulers brought me silver, gold, and precious treasures. Men and women sang for me, and I had many wives who gave me great pleasure.
9 I was the most famous person who had ever lived in Jerusalem, and I was very wise. 10I got whatever I wanted and did whatever made me happy. But most of all, I enjoyed my work. 11Then I thought about everything I had done, including the hard work, and it was simply chasing the wind. Nothing on earth is worth the trouble.
Wisdom Comes from God
12I asked myself, “What can the next king do that I haven't done?” Then I decided to compare wisdom with foolishness and stupidity. 13And I discovered that wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness. 14Wisdom is like having two good eyes; foolishness leaves you in the dark. But wise or foolish, we all end up the same.
15Finally, I said to myself, “Being wise got me nowhere! The same thing will happen to me that happens to fools. Nothing makes sense. 16Wise or foolish, we all die and are soon forgotten.” 17This made me hate life. Everything we do is painful; it's just as senseless as chasing the wind.
18Suddenly I realized that others would someday get everything I had worked for so hard, then I started hating it all. 19Who knows if those people will be sensible or stupid? Either way, they will own everything I have earned by hard work and wisdom. It doesn't make sense.
20I thought about all my hard work, and I felt depressed. 21When we use our wisdom, knowledge, and skill to get what we own, why do we have to leave it to someone who didn't work for it? This is senseless and wrong. 22What do we really gain from all of our hard work? 23 Our bodies ache during the day, and work is torture. Then at night our thoughts are troubled. It just doesn't make sense.
24 The best thing we can do is to enjoy eating, drinking, and working. I believe these are God's gifts to us, 25and no one enjoys eating and living more than I do. 26 If we please God, he will make us wise, understanding, and happy. But if we sin, God will make us struggle for a living, then he will give all we own to someone who pleases him. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_text:
1Mi yaa poli m suinum po ayen, <<Jam yɔgyɔgla de, m le chamsi fu nya ale masim a nya ase ka boa ale jamaŋ.>> Alege dila mɛ a ka kiri ya. 2Mi yaa weeni ayen, <<Laata! Ku ka betta. Masim dɛka a ta ka boan cheena?>> 3Mi yaa piilim a te m dek nyiŋbiiri ale daam nyuka ale kpari maŋ berinni ate m popolaŋa a diem a gani mu ale yam. Mi jam a yaali ayen m nya ka dii ale ka wamaŋ ayen nuruba a nye tɛŋzuk de daa magadek ate ba vua la po.
4Mi yaa nye wakpiema nna yegayega: Mi jam sɛ ka yie a te m dek ale bori kaduksa yega. 5Mi lɔ ka tatta ale peelim nna jalɔ ale vuk yɔna tiisa ti po. 6Mi jam nye gola ate nyiam a bo ŋa po a zaŋti ti sii ale a busim la. 7Mi jam ta ka nidoa yɔm ale nipok yɔm ale ta yɔm ba chaab ate ba biak ba m yenni po. Mi jam ta ka duŋ boari ale duŋ buulim a gaam waai meena ale jam bo Jerusalem po a ta diila. 8Mi jam maa ta ka kpana ale ligmɔniŋ ale ligra a nyini nalima ale tɛŋsa jigi. Mi jam ta ka nidoa yilendisa ale nipok yilendisa ale nipooba boka jigi, nidoa suinum mariŋka jigini. 9Mi jam ta ka yuei a poom gaam baai meena ale liŋ bo Jerusalem po ale ge mi la. M yammu ale jam maari mu nnala meena.
10Jaab meena ate mi jam nya a yaali la a jo m nisa kama. Mi an jɔk masim buui meena ate mi a yaali la. Mi sui a jam peenti ale dii meena ate mi a nye la kama. Masimu de abe jam ka m le chiib a tom la nyiŋ. 11Alege mi ale kpesi nya dii meena ate mi nisaŋa a nye la ale mi ale nam a nye diila, wari meena jam ka kiri ya, ku ka viok chali vika nyuenta ka tɛŋzuk de.
12Mi yaa tulim m popolaŋa a basi yam ale yesiŋsa ale berinni jigi. Ka boa ate waai ale za naawa nankula po la ale ŋman nye a gaam nnala, dii ale poom liŋ nye la? 13Mi yaa nya ale yam a zunchoŋ berinni kama, ase bolim ale zunchoŋ legi diila. 14Yam nyam a nya ba le a cheŋ juijui la kama alege betta a bo ka legini po a gilim. Mi nya dila, yam nyam ale betta nyam kpeglimka ka bunyi.
15Mi yaa poli m suinum po ayen dii ale nye beruku la ale nye mi mɛ kama. Dila ka boan tiirim ale boro ase fi nin ta yammoa?>> Mi weeni midek ayen, <<Fi dan ta yam mɛ ku ka kiri ya.>> 16Yam ale betta nyam meena a kpi kama. Ate waai a kan teeri wanyi wari a beni chum po ba nɔi bayewa ba le baŋ ba wari.
17Dila mi yaa kisa nyeboka, dii nyiŋla ku te mi ka sui kaasuŋ ate mi a poli ayen wari meena tɛŋzuk de a ka kiri ya, ku a nye ase ka fi le chali a vi viok diila. 18Mi kisa jaab meena ate mi nam nya tɛŋzuk de la kama, dii nyiŋla ku a fɛ ate m basi a te waai ale wa boro mi ŋaaŋnyiŋ la. 19Nuru yoŋ ale wa soa ŋan baai ate mi nam tɛŋzuk de a nya la, mi abe zɛ ase wa le ta yam yaase wa ka beruwa. Kude mɛ a ka kiri ya. 20Dila nyiŋ mi suinum yaa piilim a kaasi dii meena ate m nam nye tɛŋzuk de la. 21Nuru ale tom wa tuini ale yam ale sebika ale wa le seba diila, a basi ŋan baai meena ate wa soa la a te waai ale kan tom ba nyiŋla. Kude mɛ a ka kiri ya ale chim zubiok. 22Nuru ale nya ka boa wa tuimaŋa ale wa ninammu nyiŋ tɛŋzuk de? 23Wa daaŋa meena, wa tuini meena ka nyiŋdomma ale niniga, yokku po wa popolaŋa kan vuusi. Kude mɛ a ka kiri ya.
24Wamaŋ kaai ate nuru ale nye la ale wa dɛ abe wa nyu abe wa dɛ masim wa tuini nyiŋ. Mi nya dila kama kude a poom nyini ka Wen jigi. 25Dan kan daa wala, ka wana ale baga a dɛ yaase wa nya masimmoa? 26Ate nuru waai ale nye ate wa sui a yɔk la, Wen a te ka yam ale sebika ale suipeentik, alege wabanyeerika, wa basi kama ate wa tigsi ale su wa paaruŋku a zaani ate wa pai ba a te waai ale nye ate Wen sui a peenti la. Kude mɛ a ka kiri ya, ku a nye ase ka fi le chali a vi viok diila.

english_text:
Everything Has Its Time
1Everything on earth
has its own time
and its own season.
2There is a time
for birth and death,
planting and reaping,
3for killing and healing,
destroying and building,
4for crying and laughing,
weeping and dancing,
5for throwing stones
and gathering stones,
embracing and parting.
6There is a time
for finding and losing,
keeping and giving,
7for tearing and sewing,
listening and speaking.
8There is also a time
for love and hate,
for war and peace.
What God Has Given Us To Do
9What do we gain by all our hard work? 10I have seen what difficult things God demands of us. 11God makes everything happen at the right time. Yet none of us can ever fully understand all he has done, and he puts questions in our minds about the past and the future. 12I know the best thing we can do is to always enjoy life, 13because God's gift to us is the happiness we get from our food and drink and from the work we do. 14Everything God has done will last forever; nothing he does can ever be changed. God has done all this, so that we will worship him.
15Everything that happens
has happened before,
and all that will be
has already been—
God does everything
over and over again.
The Future Is Known Only to God
16Everywhere on earth I saw violence and injustice instead of fairness and justice. 17So I told myself that God has set a time and a place for everything. He will judge everyone, both the wicked and the good. 18I know God is testing us to show us that we are merely animals. 19Like animals we breathe and die, and we are no better off than they are. It just doesn't make sense. 20All living creatures go to the same place. We are made from earth, and we return to earth. 21Who really knows if our spirits go up and the spirits of animals go down into the earth? 22We were meant to enjoy our work, and that's the best thing we can do. We can never know the future.
translation_text:
1Dai ale boro a te wari meena, ate vari a boro a te tuini meena tɛŋzuk de. 2Biam dai a boro kama, ate kum dai a boro. Borik dai a boro kama ate voorika dai mɛ a boro. 3Koka dai a boro kama ate tebika dai a boro. Kaasika dai a boro kama ate sɛka dai mɛ a boro. 4Kumsa dai a boro kama ate laata dai a boro. Kaarik dai a boro kama ate gɔgta dai mɛ a boro.
5Tintana kati waaŋka dai a boro kama ate ŋa tigsika dai a boro. Gbaarika dai a boro kama ate dai mɛ boro an magsi gbaarika. 6Gisika dai a boro kama ate dai a boro an magsi gisika. Yiktaka dai a boro kama ate yukbasika dai mɛ a boro. 7Cheerika dai a boro kama ate maŋka dai a boro. Diki dai a boro kama ate biik dai mɛ a boro. 8Yaalika dai a boro kama ate kisika dai a boro. Kpaliŋ dai a boro kama ate suiyɔgni dai mɛ a boro.
9Ka boa ate tuimtomdɔwa ale nya wa ninammu nyiŋŋa? 10Mi nya gigelika ate Wen a pai ji nurubiik la kama. 11Wen a nye wari meena kama ate di nala diipo ale magsi la. Wa nye kama mɛ ate wenŋmazuk wie a bo nurubisa suiniima po alege ba kan miŋ Wen ale nye dii a nyini piilimka a ga paari kpeglimka. 12Mi seba kama ayen wari a karo a zunchoŋ a te nuru biiga a gaam ba le ta suipeentik ase ba nin a nye wamaŋsa ase ba le vua la. 13Wen a yaali kama ayen ba a dɛ abe ba nyu a ta suipeentik ba tuimaŋa po, dii ale ka tiirim a nyini Wen jigi la. 14Mi seba ayen Wen ale a nye diila ale boro kama taam wuu. Ba kan pai wari a gum du ba be kan yeeri wari a ta a nyini du. Wen a nye dila kama ayen nurubiik a zuli wa.
15Dii ale a nye yɔgyɔgla de la a liŋ nye nya kama, dii abe le kali di nye chum po la a liŋ nye kama. Wen ale basi ate dii ale nye dipo la a ŋman pilim nye.
16Mi nya ka wari dichoa tɛŋzuk de. Buusa boka jigini gaasa ale boro. Nyemagsika jigini gaasa ale boro.
17Mi yaa weeni m dek ayen, Wen a gomsi ka dai a magsi wari meena ale nyeela meena, ate dila ale basi ate wa bo nuru maŋsa ale nuru baata meena buusa.
18Mi yaa ŋman poli ayen, <<Dan ka nurubiik Wen a chamsi ba a nya kama ate dila ale basi ate ba nya ayen ba a nye ase ka duŋsaŋa la. 19Nurubiik a nye ase ka duŋsa la, nyeela ŋala ale a limisi ba nɔi bayewa. Ase wanyiwa ale a kpi la, dila dek ate nwala ale kpi. Ba meena a ta ka vuusum yeŋka la. Nuru a ka wamaŋ a gaam duŋŋa. Wari meena a ka kiri ya. 20Ba meena a cheŋ ka jigi yeŋ, ba meena a nyini ka tanta po, tantaŋa po abe le ba meena ale wari du. 21Ka wana ale seba a chak ase nuru chiik a jueli ka Wen jigi ate duŋ chiik a siŋ tɛŋŋa?>>
22Dila mi yaa nya ayen dii ale zunchoŋ la ale nuruba a dɛ masim ba tuima nyiŋ, dii nyiŋla dii meena ate ba ta la ale la. Nuru an baga a maari wa choa ate wa a nya dii ale di nye chum po la.

english_text:
1I looked again and saw people being mistreated everywhere on earth. They were crying, but no one was there to offer comfort, and those who mistreated them were powerful. 2I said to myself, “The dead are better off than the living. 3But those who have never been born are better off than anyone else, because they have never seen the terrible things that happen on this earth.”
4Then I realized that we work and do wonderful things just because we are jealous of others. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
5Fools will fold their hands
and starve to death.
6Yet a very little food
eaten in peace
is better than twice as much
earned from overwork
and chasing the wind.
7Once again I saw that nothing on earth makes sense. 8For example, some people don't have friends or family. But they are never satisfied with what they own, and they never stop working to get more. They should ask themselves, “Why am I always working to have more? Who will get what I leave behind?” What a senseless and miserable life!
It Is Better To Have a Friend
9You are better having a friend than to be all alone, because then you will get more enjoyment out of what you earn. 10If you fall, your friend can help you up. But if you fall without having a friend nearby, you are really in trouble. 11If you sleep alone, you won't have anyone to keep you warm on a cold night. 12Someone might be able to beat up one of you, but not both of you. As the saying goes, “A rope made from three strands of cord is hard to break.”
13You may be poor and young, but if you are wise, you are better off than a foolish old king who won't listen to advice. 14Even if you were not born into the royal family and have been a prisoner and poor, you can still be king. 15I once saw everyone in the world follow a young leader who came to power after the king was gone. 16His followers could not even be counted. But years from now, no one will praise him—this makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_text:
1Mi yaa ŋman nya namsi kaai meena ale bo tɛŋzuk de la. Mi nya baai ate ba a namsi la ninyaataŋa alege ba ka maarɔ, pagrimu a jam bo ka ba namsidɔma jigi, ba jam ka maarɔ. 2Mi yaa weeni ayen kpiema, baai ale ŋaam kpi la a ta suipeentik a gaam ŋanvutaŋa baai ale diem vua la. 3Alege ba le kan diem biak baai la a zunchoŋ ba nɔi buyewa kama ba an diem nya biem buui ale nye tɛŋzuk de la.
4Ate mi yaa nya ninam ale dii meena ate nuru a nye la ka wa ninŋmaarima ale wa vaanchoa la nyiŋ. Kude mɛ a ka kiri ya, ku a nye ase ka fi le chali a vi viok diila.
5Beruk a pa ka nisa vi chaab a kala a kan tom tuini ate ku a jo wadek nyiŋ. 6Ku zunchoŋ ate fi nina a sueri ale magadekka ate fi ta la. Kan daa di fi le kasim a nam kama fi nya yega, dila abe a nye ase ka fi le chali a vi viok diila.
7Mi ŋman nya ka wari ale di ka kiri tɛŋzuk de. 8Nuru ale jam boro wadek wa nyiini, wa ka nidoabili yaase suokwa. Wa ninammu a ka kpeglimka, dila meena wa nina an sueri ale wa paaruŋku. Wa yaa bek ayen, <<Ka wana ate mi a nam a te, ka boa ate mi a zɛri masim dɛka?>> Kude mɛ a ka kiri ya. Ninam kayiok.
9Nuruba baye a zunchoŋ wanyi kama, dii nyiŋla ba ale nya ka yega ba le a tom ale chaab la nyiŋ. 10Wanyi a dan lo tɛŋ, wa doawa ale maari wa ate wa yiti. Alege ta niniga ale waai ale lo ale ka nuru ate wa a maari wa ate wa a yiti la. 11Baye a dan doa ale chaab ba nyiŋsa a toliŋ kama. Alege nuru yeŋ nyiŋ ale nye ka sɛ a toliŋŋi? 12Ba le baga a nya pagrim wanyi zuk, alege nuruba baye a baga a zɛri badek nyiŋ kama. Miisa sita a dan mɛliŋ chaab si gebika toa kama.
13Bi kaai ale jaŋ ale ta yam la a zunchoŋ naab waai ale pak ale kan wom sinsaga la kama. 14Dai dii dai bi paaluk ale nyini likka dɔk a jam dɛ naam yaase ba biak wa jaŋsa po wa naamu po. 15Mi nya ale baai meena ale boro ale a cheŋ tɛŋzuk de la a va ka bi paalukku, waai ale tagri za naawa nankula po la. 16Nuru baai ale jam dɛ wa niŋ la a ka kpeglimka. Alege baai ale jam ŋaaŋnyiŋ la sue an peenti ale waai ale za naawa nankula po la. Kude mɛ a ka kiri ya, ku a nye ase ka fi ale chali a vi viok diila.

english_text:
Be Careful How You Worship
1Be careful what you do when you enter the house of God. Fools go there to offer sacrifices, because all they do is sin. But it's best just to listen when you go to worship. 2Don't talk before you think or make promises to God without thinking them through. God is in heaven, and you are on earth, so don't talk too much. 3If you keep thinking about something, you will dream about it. If you talk too much, you will say the wrong thing.
4 God doesn't like fools. So don't be slow to keep your promises to God. 5It's better not to make a promise at all than to make one and not keep it. 6Don't let your mouth get you in trouble! And don't say to the worship leader, “I didn't mean what I said.” God can destroy everything you have worked for, so don't say something that makes God angry.
7Respect and obey God! Daydreaming leads to a lot of senseless talk.
8Don't be surprised if the poor of your country are abused, and injustice takes the place of justice. After all, the lower officials must do what the higher ones order them to do. 9And since the king is the highest official, he benefits most from the taxes paid on the land.
10If you love money and wealth, you will never be satisfied with what you have. This doesn't make a bit of sense. 11The more you have, the more everyone expects from you. Your money won't do you any good—others will just spend it for you. 12If you have to work hard for a living, you can rest well at night, even if you don't have much to eat. But if you are rich, you can't even sleep.
13I have seen something terribly unfair. People get rich, but it does them no good. 14Suddenly they lose everything in a bad business deal, then have nothing to leave for their children. 15 They came into this world naked, and when they die, they will be just as naked. They can't take anything with them, and they won't have anything to show for all their work. 16That's terribly unfair. They leave the world just as they came. They gained nothing from running after the wind. 17Besides all this, they are always gloomy at mealtime, and they are troubled, sick, and bitter.
18What is the best thing to do in the short life God has given us? I think we should enjoy eating, drinking, and working hard. This is what God intends for us to do. 19Suppose you are very rich and able to enjoy everything you own. Then go ahead and enjoy working hard—this is God's gift to you. 20God will keep you so happy that you won't have time to worry about each day.
translation_text:
1Kpesi fidek ase fi nin cheŋ fi puusi Wen yenni po. Fi dan wom chak zunchoŋ fi le nye betta kaabka ale poom zɛ ayen fi nye kaasi kama.
2Kan te ate fi nɔi a valima abe fi kpesi fidek fi ale a biisi dii a te Wen la. Wen a bo ka wenŋmazuk ate fi bo tɛŋzuk de, dila biisi magadega. 3Fi daa poli yegayega ku ta ka gɔdaasima a jam, ka betta ale a biisi wie yega.
4Ase fi dan puulim a te Wen, kan beni ale nyeka. Wen sui kan peenti ale betta, nye fi le puulim diila. 5Fi dan kan puulim ya ku zunchoŋ fi le puulim ale kan nye fi ale puulim diila. 6Kan basi ate fi nɔnni a ta fu jo biem po, abe fi kan ta chaab ale biisiteerɔwa Wen yenni po ayen, <<Mi ale puulim diila m nye bɛ kama.>> Fi dan nye dila Wen sui ale puuri ale fu ate wa kaasi jaab meena ate fi nam nya la. 7Gɔdaasima yegayega ale wie yegayega biisika a ka kiri ya. Dila a zuli Wen.
8Fi dan nya ale ba a namsi ŋanjaksa tɛŋ kpieŋ po, ate nyemagsika ale wensie a karo, kan te wa ŋala a cha fu, ale ka kpagi kpien nina ale bo wa zuk, ŋayema zuk ka kpagi kpiema ale diem boro. 9Tɛŋka ŋantaŋa ka ba ale soa ba meena, naawa dek a nya nyuenta ka dula.
10Waai ale a yaali ligra la a kan ta ligra yega, waai ale a yaali jigsika la jigsika a kan paari wa. Kude mɛ a ka kiri ya.
11Ase ŋanta ale a piisi diila, ba dɛɛrɔma mɛ a piisi ka dila. Be ka boan jaab nyuenta a te ba nyɔnɔwa, ka wa pai nina a nya ba?
12Tuimtomdɔ goom a masa kama, wa dɛ maga yaase wa dɛ yega wa a goa kama alege nuru waai ale jigsi la ŋantaŋa a kan te wa suik ate wa a goa.
13Mi nya ka biem ate bu a daani tɛŋzuk de, paaruŋ ka biem a te ku nyɔnɔwa 14yaase paaruŋ a va ka suik yoŋ a muriŋ a be dila wa dan ta nidoabili jaab karo tali a te wa. 15Chaboala ate nuru a nyini wa ma popo a nyini, wa be pilim a cheŋ ka dila dek. Wa kan pai jaab a nyini wa gigelika nyiŋŋa a nyo wa nisaŋa po a cheŋ.
16Kude mɛ ka biem ale ta daanika tɛŋzuk de. Ase nuru ale jam diila, dila dek ate wa a ŋmani, ka boan nyuenta ate wa nya, wa nam a te ka vioku? 17Wa daaŋa meena po wa a dɛ kama legini po ale ninam kayiok ale nyiŋ wula ale suipuurum.
18Mi yaa nya ayen ku nala kama ale chim wamaŋ ayen nuru a dɛ abe wa a nyu a chak wa gigelika ale wa ninammu nyiŋ tɛŋzuk de daa magadega ate Wen a te wa la, ka wa charuk ale la. 19Alege Wen a dan te nuru jigsika ale ŋanta ale maari wa ate wa a dɛ ba ale masim, ate wa tuesi wa paaruŋku ale ta suipeentik, kude ka Wen tiirim. 20Wa nyiem kan poli wa daaŋa ale gela diila wari ya, dii nyiŋla Wen a basi kama ate wa nina a muni ate wa sui a peenti.

english_text:
Don't Depend on Wealth
1There is something else terribly unfair, and it troubles everyone on earth. 2God may give you everything you want—money, property, and wealth. Then God doesn't let you enjoy it, and someone you don't even know gets it all. That's senseless and terribly unfair!
3You may live a long time and have a hundred children. But a child born dead is better off than you, unless you enjoy life and have a decent burial. 4-5That child will never live to see the sun or to have a name, and it will go straight to the world of darkness. But it will still find more rest than you, 6even if you live two thousand years and don't enjoy life. As you know, we all end up in the same place.
