38Naawen a weeni ayen, <<Daaŋa a cheena ate ba le ŋman sɛ tɛŋka de a te mi a zaani Yananel Yewɔŋku a ta ga paari Gugoruk Nansuiŋku. 39Magsika dindaanuŋku ale dari nyini ka dula a yomsi ga paari Gareb guuku a cheem a cheŋ Goya. 40Viaka meena juijui ate ba yuk kpieba ale buntueta a basi du la, ale laŋ sii meena ale ba peelimmu a cheŋ Kidron Viaka kori geŋka a ta ga paari Wusuma Nansuiŋku gugoruku ale ta tuilum kama a te Naawen. Ba kan ŋman dari tɛŋka a dueni yaase ba kaasi ka.>>

english_text:
Jeremiah Buys a Field
1 The Lord spoke to me in the tenth year that Zedekiah was king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year that Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylonia. 2At that time, the Babylonian army had surrounded Jerusalem, and I was in the prison at the courtyard of the palace guards. 3Zedekiah had ordered me to be held there because I told everyone that the Lord had said:
I am the Lord, and I am about to let the king of Babylonia conquer Jerusalem. 4King Zedekiah will be captured and taken to King Nebuchadnezzar, who will speak with him face to face. 5Then Zedekiah will be led away to Babylonia, where he will stay until I am finished with him. So, if you people of Judah fight against the Babylonians, you will lose. I, the Lord, have spoken.
6Later, when I was in prison, the Lord said:
7Jeremiah, your cousin Hanamel, the son of your uncle Shallum, will visit you. He must sell his field near the town of Anathoth, and because you are his nearest relative, you have the right and the responsibility to buy it and keep it in the family.
8Hanamel came, just as the Lord had promised. And he said, “Please buy my field near Anathoth in the territory of the Benjamin tribe. You have the right to buy it, and if you do, it will stay in our family.”
The Lord had told me to buy it 9from Hanamel, and so I did. The price was 17 pieces of silver, and I weighed out the full amount on a scale. 10-11I had two copies of the bill of sale written out: an official copy containing the details of our agreement and another copy, without the details. Some witnesses and I signed the official copy, which was folded and tied, before being sealed shut with hot wax. Then I gave Hanamel the silver. 12And while he, the witnesses, and all the other Jews sitting in the courtyard were still watching, I gave both copies to Baruch son of Neriah.
13-14I told Baruch that the Lord had said:
Take both copies of this bill of sale, one sealed shut and the other open, and put them in a clay jar so they will last a long time. 15I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I promise you that people will once again buy and sell houses, farms, and vineyards in this country.
Jeremiah Questions the Lord
16Then I prayed:
17 Lord God, you stretched out your mighty arm and made the sky and the earth. You can do anything. 18You show kindness for a thousand generations, but you also punish people for the sins of their parents. You are the Lord All-Powerful. 19With great wisdom you make plans, and with your great power you do all the mighty things you planned. Nothing we do is hidden from your eyes, and you reward or punish us as we deserve.
20You are famous because you worked miracles in Egypt, and you are still working them in Israel and in the rest of the world as well. 21You terrified the Egyptians with your miracles, and you reached out your mighty arm and rescued your people Israel from Egypt. 22Then you gave Israel this land rich with milk and honey, just as you had promised our ancestors.
23But when our ancestors took over the land, they did not obey you. And now you have punished Israel with disaster. 24Jerusalem is under attack, and we suffer from hunger and disease. The Babylonians have already built dirt ramps up to the walls of our city, and you can see that Jerusalem will be captured just as you said.
25So why did you tell me to get some witnesses and buy a field with my silver, when Jerusalem is about to be captured by the Babylonians?
The Lord Explains about the Field
26The Lord explained:
27Jeremiah, I am the Lord God. I rule the world, and I can do anything!
28 It is true that I am going to let King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia capture Jerusalem. 29The Babylonian army is already attacking, and they will capture the city and set it on fire. The people of Jerusalem have made me angry by going up to the flat roofs of their houses and burning incense to Baal and offering wine sacrifices to other gods. Now these houses will be burned to the ground!
30-33The kings and the officials, the priests and the prophets, and everyone else in Israel and Judah have turned from me and made me angry by worshiping idols. Again and again I have tried to teach my people to obey me, but they refuse to be corrected.
I am going to get rid of Jerusalem, because its people have done nothing but evil. 34 They have set up repulsive idols in my temple, and now it isn't a fit place to worship me. 35 And they led Judah into sin by building places to worship Baal in Hinnom Valley, where they also sacrificed their sons and daughters to the god Molech. I have never even imagined they would commit such disgusting sins.
36Jeremiah, what you said is true. The people of Jerusalem are suffering from hunger and disease, and so the king of Babylonia will be able to capture Jerusalem.
37I am angry with the people of Jerusalem, and I will scatter them in foreign countries. But someday I will bring them back here and let them live in safety. 38They will be my people, and I will be their God. 39-41I will make their thoughts and desires pure. Then they will realize that, for their own good and the good of their children, they must worship only me. They will even be afraid to turn away from me. I will make an agreement with them that will never end, and I won't ever stop doing good things for them. With all my heart I promise that they will be planted in this land once again. 42Even though I have brought disaster on the people, I will someday do all these good things for them.
43Jeremiah, when you bought the field, you showed that fields will someday be bought and sold again. You say that this land has been conquered by the Babylonians and has become a desert, emptied of people and animals. 44But someday, people will again spend their silver to buy fields everywhere—in the territory of Benjamin, the region around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, and in the hill country, the foothills to the west, and the Southern Desert. Buyers and sellers and witnesses will sign and seal the bills of sale for the fields. It will happen, because I will give this land back to my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
1Naawen yaa biisi ale mi bena piika po ate Zedekia a jam chim Juda naab la. Jam ka Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar naamu bena pi ale naaniŋ po ale la. 2Babilon naawa tugurik tɔŋdɔma a yaa jam a gilim ka Jerusalem, ate biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya ba yaa jam lik wa basi Juda naab yenni limisidɔma dabiaka po.
3Yɔgyɔgla de Juda naawa Zedekia a jam yik wa lik basi ka dula ale weeni ayen, <<Ka boa ale soa ate fi a mooli dila? Fi a weeni ayen, <Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: M za m basi ate ka Babilon naawa a yik tɛŋka de. 4Juda naawa Zedekia a kan yuli bɛ a nyini Kaldiya demma nisima po alege m le pai wa a te Babilon naawa, ate wa nya wa ale nina ate ba tuk chaab a biisi. 5Wa le ta Zedekia a cheŋ Babilon, ate wa wari dula ate m nye ale wa. Naawen ale weeni. Fi dan kpaliŋ ale Kaldiya demma fi kan nak dɛ.> >>
6Jeremaya yaa weeni ayen, <<Naawen wanni a jan jam mi jigi ayen, 7Sallum nidoabinni Yanamel fi kowa suoku ale jam fi jigi a weeni ayen, <Da m tɛŋka ale bo Anatot la, dii nyiŋla fi ale wa ale moata chaab diila a chim suata la fi ta suik kama a da.>
8<<Ase Naawen ale weeni diila, mi suoku yaa jam mi jigi limisidɔma dabiaka po a weeni ayen, <Da m tɛŋka ale bo Anatot Benjamin tɛŋbanni po la. Fi ale toalim ta suik a da a ta la, da te fidek.> Mi jam seba ayen ka Naawen wari ale nna. 9Dila mi yaa da tɛŋka Anatot po m suoku Yanamel jigi a magsi kpana ligbie dobrim pi ale buyopɔi. 10Mi yaa ŋmarisi mi yuenni ale yaali seerɔ ale magsi kpanaŋa ŋanmagsinta zuk. 11Mi yaa pai diaka gbaŋka, kaai ale lik la ate wie ŋaai ti nye magsi chaab la a bo ka po la ale kaai ale kan lik la, 12a pai ka a te Neria nidoabinni Baruk ate wa kokpieŋ a chim Maseiya la, m suoku Yanamel ale seerɔ baai ale ŋmarisi ba yueŋa la ale Juuma meena ale kali limisidɔma dabiaka po la niŋ.
13<<Ba niŋ mi yaa te Baruk sinsaŋŋa de: 14<Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni ale weeni diila ale nna: Pai gbaŋsaŋa de sii ale lik ale sii ale kan lik ya ate si a sak nyemagsika diaka la a pai si a nyo yak samɔniŋ po ate si beni. 15Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni ale weeni diila ale nna: Ba le ŋman da yie ale laŋsa ale kaduksa tɛŋka de po ŋmana.>
16<<Mi ale pai nyemagsika diaka gbaŋka a te Neria nidoabinni Baruk la ŋaaŋnyiŋ mi yaa puusi a te Naawen. 17Nyɔnɔwa Naawen, fi ale nye wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋ ale fi pagrim kpiemu ale fi nisa teerika. Jaab karo a tua a te fu. 18Fi a sak ŋmanteka ale tusa ale ge a namsi nuruba ba koba biem nyiŋ. Wen dii ale zuak ale chim pagrɔ, waai yuei ale chim Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, 19fi zɔŋŋa a zuak kama ale a tom wa kpiema. Fi ninaŋa a lak kama a nya nurubisa suita, fi a tuni waai meena a magsi ka wa nyeelaŋa ale wa tuimaŋa ale magsi diila. 20Fi tom wakinkagla ale wakperikaliisa Ejipiti tɛŋka ale kasim a tom a jam paari jinla, Izirali po ale nurubiik meena suŋsuŋ, a nya yuei dii ale diem ka fi yuei. 21Fi ta fi nuruma Izirali demma a nyini Ejipiti a nyini ale ka wakinkagla ale wakperikaliisa ale ni pagrisa ale nisa teerika ale kpazinagsuk nna yegayega. 22Fi pai tɛŋka de ate fi pɛ ayen fi le te ba kokpieŋsaŋa la a te ba, tɛŋ kaai ate biisim ale siita a bo ka po la. 23Ba jam jo ka po a tuesi ka a ta, alege ba an wom fi nɔiya yaase ba va fi sinsaŋŋa, ba an nye fi le weeni ba ayen ba nye diila. Dila fi yaa ta kaasuŋku de meena a jam ba zuk.
24<<Nya bimbimaŋa ba le sɛ a ta jueli dii ayen ba tuesi tɛŋka la. Gebika ale kɔmmu ale nyiŋtuilaŋa nyiŋ tɛŋka ale jo Kaldiya demma ale a siti ka la nisima po. Fi le weeni diila a nye kama ase fi le a nya yɔgyɔgla de la. 25Tɛŋka ale jo Kaldiya demma nisa, fi Nyɔnɔwa Naawen yaa weeni mi kama ayen, <Da laŋka ale kpana ate diaka a ta seerɔba.> >>
26Naawen wanni yaa jam Jeremaya jigi ayen, 27<<Mi ale Naawen, nurubiik meena Wenni. Wari a boro a tua a te mi? 28Dila la Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: Mi za m pai tɛŋka de a te Kaldiya demma ale Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar waai ale wa tuesi ka la. 29Kaldiya demma ale a siti tɛŋka de la ale jo a ju ka bolim, ba le ju ka meena ale yie ŋaai ate nuruma a ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa ŋa zuk a te Baal ale kpiiri daam tiirita a te wen yona a nye ate m sui a puuri la.
30<<Izirali ale Juda demma an nye wari ya alege ka biem mi nina po a nyini ba bimbain po. Chekki Izirali demma an nye wari ya alege ka ba nye ate ka mi sui a puuri ale ba le pai ba nisima a nye ŋan baai la. Naawen ale weeni. 31A zaani dai dii danni ate ba sɛ ka la a jam paari yɔgyɔgla de, tɛŋka de a nye ate mi sui a yiti ka nna yegayega ate ku a fɛ ayen m yeeri ka m nina po. 32Izirali ale Juda demma a nye ate ka m sui a puuri ale biem buui meena ate ba nye la, badek ale ba nalimaŋa ale kpaŋŋa ale ba kaabteerɔma ale biisiteerɔma ale Juda nuruma ale Jerusalem nuruma. 33Ba cheem ka ba ŋaaŋsa te mi alege daa ba nina. Mi sak ba kama a tulim tulim ba kan wom ba niŋ be ka waalika po. 34Ba pai ka ba bɔgluk tii ate mi a kisa la a zaani yie dii ale ta mi Yuenni la po ale taŋ di. 35Ba sɛ ka kuŋkuŋta a te Baal Ben Yinnom Viaka po a kaab ba nidoabilisaŋa ale ba liema a te Molek, alege mi an weeni ba di yaase ku poom bo mi popola po ayen ba nye kisuk wa dila choa a basi ate Juda a tom kaasi.
36<<Ni a weeni tɛŋka de wari kama ayen, <Gebika ale kɔmmu ale nyiŋtuilaŋa nyiŋ tɛŋka ale jo Babilon naawa nisa,> alege Naawen, Izirali Wenni ale weeni diila ale nna: 37M le sum tigsi ba a ta nyini tɛŋ sii meena ate mi yiak ba basi du m suipuurumu ale m suidomsika nyiŋla, m le ta ba ŋman jam dela a basi ate ba boro sɔŋsɔŋŋoa. 38Ba le chim m nuruba ate mi ale chim ba Wen. 39M le te ba popola yena ate ba a zuli mu a kasim a cheŋ, badek nalim nyiŋ ale ba ŋaaŋsaŋa nalim nyiŋ. 40M le nye nɔiyeŋ kaai ale kan ta kpeglimka ale ba. M kan basi nalim ba nye teka, abe m choa ba ate ba a chali mu, ate ba kan ŋman basi mu. 41M le nye wamaŋsa a te ba ale suipeentik abe m basi ate ba kali paari tɛŋka de po ale m suinum meena.
42<<Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: Ase m ni ta kaasuŋ kpioŋku de meena a jam nuruma de zuk la, m le te ba paaruŋ kuui meena ate m puulim la. 43Ba le da laŋsa tɛŋka de po kaai ate ni a weeni ayen, <Ka ka tɛŋ koruk, a ka nuruba ale duŋsa diila ba pai ka a te ka Kaldiya demma.> 44Nuruba ale da laŋsa ate ba ŋmarisi yue gbaŋsa po a lik si ale seerɔba. Kude ale nye ka Benjamin tɛŋka ale tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa ale gilim Jerusalem la, ale Juda tɛŋsaŋa po, ale tɛŋ sii ale bo guuku zuk la ale guuku chiak la ale Juda yeseok geŋ. M le ta nuruma a ŋman jam ba tɛŋka. Naawen ale weeni.>>

english_text:
The Lord Promises To Give the Land Back to His People
1-2I was still being held prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guards when the Lord told me:
I am the Lord, and I created the whole world. 3Ask me, and I will tell you things that you don't know and can't find out.
4-5Many of the houses in Jerusalem and some of the buildings at the royal palace have been torn down to be used in repairing the walls to keep out the Babylonian attackers. Now there are empty spaces where the buildings once stood. But I am furious, and these spaces will be filled with the bodies of the people I kill. The people of Jerusalem will cry out to me for help, but they are evil, and I will ignore their prayers.
6Then someday, I will heal this place and my people as well, and let them enjoy unending peace. 7I will give this land to Israel and Judah once again, and I will make them as strong as they were before. 8They sinned and rebelled against me, but I will forgive them and take away their guilt. 9When that happens, all nations on earth will see the good things I have done for Jerusalem, and how I have given it complete peace. The nations will celebrate and praise and honor me, but they will also tremble with fear because of the powerful things I have done.
10Jeremiah, you say that this land is a desert without people or animals, and for now, you are right. The towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem are deserted, and people and animals are nowhere to be seen. But someday you will hear 11 happy voices and the sounds of parties and wedding celebrations. And when people come to my temple to offer sacrifices to thank me, you will hear them say:
“We praise you,
Lord All-Powerful!
You are good to us,
and your love never fails.”
The land will once again be productive. 12-13Now it is empty, without people or animals. But when that time comes, shepherds will take care of their flocks in pastures near every town in the hill country, in the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert, in the land of the Benjamin tribe, and around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord's Wonderful Promise
14 The Lord said:
I made a wonderful promise to Israel and Judah, and the days are coming when I will keep it.
15I promise that the time will come
when I will appoint a king
from the family of David,
a king who will be honest
and rule with justice.
16In those days,
Judah will be safe;
Jerusalem will have peace
and will be named,
“The Lord Gives Justice.”
17 The king of Israel will be one of David's descendants, 18 and there will always be priests from the Levi tribe serving at my altar and offering sacrifices to please me and to give thanks.
19Then the Lord told me:
20I, the Lord, have an agreement with day and night, so they always come at the right time. You can't break the agreement I made with them, 21and you can't break the agreements I have made with David's family and with the priests from the Levi tribe who serve at my altar. A descendant of David will always rule as king of Israel, 22and there will be more descendants of David and of the priests from the Levi tribe than stars in the sky or grains of sand on the beach.
23The Lord also said:
24You've heard foreigners insult my people by saying, “The Lord chose Israel and Judah, but now he has rejected them, and they are no longer a nation.”
25Jeremiah, I will never break my agreement with the day and the night or let the sky and the earth stop obeying my commands. 26In the same way, I will never reject the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob or break my promise that they will always have a descendant of David as their king. I will be kind to my people Israel, and they will be successful again.
translation_text:
1Jeremaya ate ba jam diem lik basi limisidɔma dabiaka po la, Naawen wanni yaa jam wa jigi a nye buye. 2<<Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna, waai ale nye tɛŋka la, Naawen ale gomsi ka ale yikka a zaani, Naawen ale wa yuenni. 3<Wi mi ate m tulisi fu, m le weeni fu wakpiema ale wasusuga ate fi zɛ ŋa.> 4Diila Naawen, Izirali Wenni ale weeni diila ale nna a magsi chaab ale yeeŋa ale bo tɛŋka po ale Juda naab yeeŋa ate ba nak lɔnsi bimbimini ale sitika nyiŋla. 5Ba gela ale kpaliŋ ale Kaldiya demma, <Baai ale ba sueri ba yeeŋa ale kpio baai ate mi za m ko ale m suipuurumu la. Mi cheem ka kpai a te tɛŋka de biem buui ate ka nuruma a nye la nyiŋ.
6<< <Alege m le ta nyiŋyɔgsa ale tebika a jam te ka. M le tebi m nuruma abe m basi ate ba nya masim ale suiyɔgni dii ale zuak ale likka. 7M le ta Juda ale Izirali a nyini ba likka jigini a jam abe m ŋman sɛ si ase si ni jam ka diila. 8M le sugri ba biem buui meena ate ba nye la abe m vɔŋ ba tuikpari biemu a te ba. 9Ate tɛŋka de yaa le ta yuei ale suipeentik ale pimpauk ale zula jam te mi ate tɛŋsa meena tɛŋka zuk ale a wom wamaŋ sii ate mi a nye te ka la ate ku cha si nuruma abe ba nyiŋsa a gɔk paaruŋku yega wa ale suiyɔgni ate mi te ka la.>
10<<Naawen ale weeni nna: <Ni a weeni dela wie ayen, <<Ka ka tɛŋ koruk, ka ka nuruba yaase duŋsa.>> Alege Juda tɛŋsaŋa po ale Jerusalem suik duataŋa po ate ba zɛri la, ate nuruba yaase duŋsa a karo la ba le ŋman wom 11masim ale suipeentik nuemka ale nipok ale wa chorɔ lueluta ale baai ale ta jiam tiirita a jam Naawen yenni la a weeni ayen, <<Pai jiam a te Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, diila Naawen a nala kama, wa ŋmanteka boro ka taam wuu.>> Diila m le nye ate tɛŋka a ŋman nya ka dek ase ka le jam ka diila.> Naawen ale weeni.
12<<Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni diila ale nna: <Tɛŋka de po ate ka chim koroku nna ate nuruba yaase duŋsa a ka du la wuuk ale ŋman bo du ate naapeerisa piisa a de. 13Tɛŋ sii ale bo guuku zuk la ale guuku chiak la ale Juda yeseok geŋ ale Benjamin tɛŋka ale tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa ale gilim Jerusalem la ale Juda tɛŋsaŋa naapeerisa ale ŋman chiini ba piisa.> Naawen ale weeni.
14<<Naawen a weeni ayen, <Ku daaŋa a cheena ate m le nye niauŋ pumpuulima ŋaai ale Izirali yenni ale Juda yenni la ale nye.
15<< <Da ŋala po ale dila po m le basi ate wayɔrisima Naŋ a pusi nyini Deevid tomni po, wa le nye dii ale magsi ale yɔrisi tɛŋka po. 16Da ŋala po Juda ale nya varibasika ate Jerusalem a boro sɔŋsɔŋŋoa. Ba le ba a wi ka yuei diila ale nna: Naawen Ti Wayɔrisimaŋa.>
17<<Dii ate Naawen a weeni la ale nna: <Deevid a kan kpeeri nuru nyaka ate wa kali Izirali yenni naam zukpaglika zuwa, 18yaase kaabteerɔma baai ale ka Livaiba la a kan maa kpeeri ale nuru nyaka ate wa zaani mi niŋ a kasim a te juka tiirita abe wa a ju ŋanbie tiirita abe wa a nye kaabsa a te.> >>
19Naawen wanni a yaa jam Jeremaya jigi: 20<<Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <Mi nye ka nɔiyeŋ ale danni ale yokku, ate ŋa a jam diipo ale magsi la ate nɔiyeŋ kala a kan kaasi. 21Suik kula dek po ate mi nye nɔiyeŋ ale mi tomteerɔwa Deevid ayen wa le kasim ta ŋaaŋbiik kama ate wa chim naab, ale nye nɔiyeŋ ale kaabteerɔma a ta nyini Livai buuni po ayen ba le kasim tom a te mi ate nɔiyeŋ sila a kan kaasi. 22M le basi ate m tomteerɔwa Deevid ŋaaŋbisaŋa ale kaabteerɔma ale nyini Livai buuni po la ŋaaŋbisaŋa a piisi ate ku le tua ale ba chiinika ase ku le tua ate fi chiini chiŋmarisaŋa ale bo wenzukku diila yaase fi baga a chiini tintain busuŋ za beli nɔi diila.> >>
23Naawen wanni a jam Jeremaya jigi: 24<<Fi kpesi ayen nuruma de a weeni kama ayen, <Naawen a zɛri Izirali ale Juda kama, dɔkdem buyewa ate mi a lueri la?> Dila ba yaa zɛri mi nuruma ate ba niŋ a ka si po ase tɛŋ la. 25Alege mi Naawen a ta ka nɔiyeŋ ale danni ale yokku ale nye wa ŋaai ale yik tɛŋka ale wenzukku a ta. 26Ase mi ale sum nye nna la, m le ta m nɔiyeŋka ale Jekob ŋaaŋbisaŋa ale mi tomteerɔwa Deevid. M le lueri Deevid ŋaaŋbisaŋa ate ba a nya Abrayam ale Aizik ale Jekob ŋaaŋbisaŋa zuk. M le ta jiirim ale m nuruma abe m basi ate ba ŋman nya badek.> >>

english_text:
Jeremiah Warns Zedekiah
1 King Nebuchadnezzar had a large army made up of people from every kingdom in his empire. He and his army were attacking Jerusalem and all the nearby towns, when the Lord told me 2to say to King Zedekiah:
I am the Lord, and I am going to let Nebuchadnezzar capture this city and burn it down. 3You will be taken prisoner and brought to Nebuchadnezzar, and he will speak with you face to face. Then you will be led away to Babylonia.
4Zedekiah, I promise that you won't die in battle. 5You will die a peaceful death. People will mourn when you die, and they will light bonfires in your honor, just as they did for your ancestors, the kings who ruled before you.
6I went to Zedekiah and told him what the Lord had said. 7Meanwhile, the king of Babylonia was trying to break through the walls of Lachish, Azekah, and Jerusalem, the only three towns of Judah that had not been captured.
The People Break a Promise
8-10King Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Jerusalem made an agreement to free all Hebrew men and women who were slaves. No Jew would keep another as a slave. And so, all the Jewish slaves were given their freedom.
11But those slave owners changed their minds and forced their former slaves back into slavery.
12That's when the Lord told me to say to the people:
13I am the Lord God of Israel, and I made an agreement with your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt, where they had been slaves. 14 As part of this agreement, you must let a Hebrew slave go free after six years of service.
Your ancestors did not obey me, 15-16but you decided to obey me and do the right thing by setting your Hebrew slaves completely free. You even went to my temple, and in my name you made an agreement to set them free. But you have abused my name, because you broke that agreement and forced your former slaves back into slavery.
17You have disobeyed me by not giving your slaves their freedom. So I will give you freedom—the freedom to die in battle or from disease or hunger. I will make you disgusting to all other nations on earth.
18You asked me to be a witness when you made the agreement to set your slaves free. And as part of the ceremony you cut a calf into two parts, then walked between the parts. But you people of Jerusalem have broken that agreement as well as my agreement with Israel. So I will do to you what you did to that calf. 19-20I will let your enemies take all of you prisoner, including the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, the royal officials, the priests, and everyone else who walked between the two parts of the calf. These enemies will kill you and leave your bodies lying on the ground as food for birds and wild animals.
21-22These enemies are King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia and his army. They have stopped attacking Jerusalem, but they want to kill King Zedekiah and his high officials. So I will command them to return and attack again. This time they will conquer the city and burn it down, and they will capture Zedekiah and his officials. I will also let them destroy the towns of Judah, so that no one can live there any longer.
translation_text:
1Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena ale tɛŋ sii meena ale nuru baai meena ate wa a nya la ale jam diem a kpaliŋ ale Jerusalem ale tɛŋ sii meena ale gilim ka la, wanni de yaa nyini Naawen jigi a jam Jeremaya jigi. 2<<Naawen, Izirali Wenni ale weeni diila ale nna: Cheŋ Juda naawa Zedekia jigi a weeni wa ayen, <Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: M za m pai tɛŋka de a te Babilon naawa kama, ate wa ju ka a basi. 3Ni kan be ale wa yikka alege ba le sum a yik ni a pai te wa. Ni le nya Babilon naawa ale nidek nina, ate wa ale ni a nya chaab ate wa biisi ale ni. Ate ni cheŋ Babilon.
4<< <Alege Zedekia Juda naaba, wom Naawen pumpuulimaŋa. Naawen ale biisi dii a magsi chaab ale fu la ale nna: Fi kan kpi ale gebika, 5fi le kpi ale suiyɔgni. Ase nuruba ale jam ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la diipo ate ba jam gu fi kokpieŋsaŋa la, baai ale jam chim nalima alege te fi la, suik kula po ate ba le ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa a te fu. Ba le kum fi zuk a weeni ayen, <<Ti naawa a kpi kama.>> Mi Naawen ale weeni.> >>
6Biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya yaa weeni kude meena a sak Juda naawa Zedekia Jerusalem po, 7alege ate Babilon naawa tugurik tɔŋdɔma a kpaliŋ ale Jerusalem ale Juda tɛŋ sinsila Lachis ale Azeka, sii nyiini ale jam tali pagra la.
8Naawen wanni yaa jam Jeremaya jigi ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ naab Zedekia a yaa nye nɔiyeŋ ale wa nuruma meena Jerusalem a mooli fasiyaa a te yɔmma. 9Waai meena a jam magsi ayen wa basi wa Yiburu yɔm kama, nidoa ale nipok meena, waai a kan yik wa Juu choa a ta. 10Dila kpaŋŋa meena ale nuru baai ale jo nɔiyeŋka de po a siak ayen ba basi ba yɔmma nipooba ale nidoaba abe ba kan ŋman yik ba ta. Ba yaa jam siak a basi ba. 11Alege ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ba tagri ba popolaŋa a yik ba yɔmma ate ba basi ba la ate ba ŋman chim yɔm.
12Naawen wanni yaa jam Jeremaya jigi: 13<<Dii ate Naawen, Izirali Wenni a biisi la ale nna: Mi jam nye ka nɔiyeŋ ale ni kokpieŋsaŋa diipo ate mi a ta ni nyini Ejipiti nyini la, a nyini yɔntidi tɛŋ po a nyini. Mi weeni ayen, 14<Ben dii ale a saari ŋayopɔi meena ku a fɛ ate ni Yiburu choa waai ale pai wadek a da a te ni. Wa dan tom bena ŋayuebi a te fu, ku a fɛ ate fi basi ate wa cheŋ fasiyaa.> Ni koma an jam wom mu yaase ba niŋ jam bo mi po. 15Ku an diem beni ya ni laŋ ka nyeka ale nye dii ale nala la mi nina po. Waai meena a mooli ka fasiyaa a te wa tɛŋ dem. Ni poom a nye ka nɔiyeŋ mi niŋ mi yie dii ale ta mi Yuenni la po. 16Alege yɔgyɔgla de ni ŋman cheem kaasi mi yuenni, waai meena a ŋman tuesi wa yɔma nipok ale nidoa ate ni basi ayen ba cheŋ juijui ate ba a yaali la. Ni fɛ ba kama ate ba ŋman chim ni yɔm.
17<<Dila la, Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: Ni an wom mi nɔiya, ni an mooli fasiyaa a te ni tɛŋ demma. Dila mi yɔgyɔgla de a mooli ka <fasiyaa> a te ni, Naawen ale weeni, <fasiyaa> ayen gebika ale nyiŋtuila ale kɔm ale jam ni jigi. M le basi ate tɛŋsa a kisi ni. 18Nuru baai ale zɛri mi nɔiyeŋka alege an nye nɔiyeŋka wie ate ba nye mi niŋ la, m le nye ba ase ka naabiika ate ba gebi ka buye a cheŋ va suŋsuŋka po a taam diila. 19Juda ale Jerusalem kpaŋŋa ale naab yenni kpaŋŋa ale kaabteerɔma ale tɛŋka nuruma meena ale cheŋ va naabiika suŋsuŋ a taam la, 20m le pai ba a te ba dacha sii ale a gisi ba nyuvooŋa la. Ba nyiŋsaŋa ale chim ka ŋandiinta a te wenzuk nuinsaŋa ale tɛŋzuk duŋsaŋa.
21<<M le pai Juda naawa Zedekia ale wa kpaŋŋa a te ba dacha sii ale a gisi ba nyuvooŋa la, m le pai a te Babilon naawa tugurik tɔŋdɔma baai ale basi ni siti ka la. 22M boro ayen m te ka suik, Naawen ale weeni, abe m ta ba a ŋman jam tɛŋka de. Ba le kpaliŋ ale ka, a yik ka ale ju ka basi. Ate m yaa basi ate Juda tɛŋsaŋa a doa koruk nuru a kan baga a boro.>>

english_text:
Learn a Lesson from the Rechabites
1 When Jehoiakim was king of Judah, the Lord told me, 2“Go to the Rechabite clan and invite them to meet you in one of the side rooms of the temple. When they arrive, offer them a drink of wine.”
3So I went to Jaazaniah, the leader of the clan, and I invited him and all the men of his clan. 4I brought them into the temple courtyard and took them upstairs to a room belonging to the prophets who were followers of Hanan son of Igdaliah. It was next to a room belonging to some of the officials, and that room was over the one belonging to Maaseiah, a priest who was one of the high officials in the temple.
5I set out some large bowls full of wine together with some cups, and then I said to the Rechabites, “Have some wine!”
6But they answered:
No! The ancestor of our clan, Jonadab son of Rechab, made a rule that we must obey. He said, “Don't ever drink wine 7or build houses or plant crops and vineyards. Instead, you must always live in tents and move from place to place. If you obey this command, you will live a long time.”
8-10Our clan has always obeyed Jonadab's command. To this very day, we and our wives and sons and daughters don't drink wine or build houses or plant vineyards or crops. And we have lived in tents, 11except now we have to live inside Jerusalem because Nebuchadnezzar has taken over the countryside with his army from Babylonia and Syria.
12-13Then the Lord told me to say to the people of Judah and Jerusalem:
I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, want you to learn a lesson 14from the Rechabite clan. Their ancestor Jonadab told his descendants never to drink wine, and to this very day they have obeyed him. But I have spoken to you over and over, and you haven't obeyed me! 15You refused to listen to my prophets, who kept telling you, “Stop doing evil and worshiping other gods! Start obeying the Lord, and he will let you live in this land he gave your ancestors.”
16The Rechabites have obeyed the command of their ancestor Jonadab, but you have not obeyed me, 17your God. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I warned you about the terrible things that would happen to you if you did not listen to me. But you have ignored me, so now disaster will strike you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Makes a Promise to the Rechabites
18Then the Lord told me to say to the Rechabite clan:
“I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You have obeyed your ancestor Jonadab, 19so I promise that your clan will be my servants and will never die out.”
translation_text:
1Wanni ale nna a nyini Naawen jigi a jam Jeremaya jigi diipo ate Josia nidoabinni Jeyoiakim a chim naab a nya Juda la. 2<<Cheŋ Arekab dɔkdemma jigi a wi ba ate ba jam Naawen yenni nakpiak diinaŋa kunyi po a te ba daam ate ba nyu.>>
3Mi yaa cheŋ ayen m yik Jeremaya nidoabinni Jaazania ate wa kokpieŋ a nye Yabazzinia ale wa suataŋa ale wa nidoabilisaŋa meena, Arekab dɔkdemma meena. 4Mi yaa ta ba jam Naawen yenni Igdalia Wen nuruwa nidoabinni Yanan nidoabilisaŋa dɔkku po. Ku jam pai saŋ ka kpaŋŋa dɔkku, kuui ale jam bo Sallum nidoabinni Maaseiya waai ale a nya nansuiŋku zuk la dɔkku ŋmai. 5Mi yaa pai taasa a zaani ate daam a sueri ale beerisa Arekab dɔkdemma nidoama niŋ a weeni ba ayen, <<Ni nyu daam.>>
6Alege ba a tulisi ayen, <<Tama a kan nyu daamoa, dii nyiŋla tama kokpieŋka Arekab nidoabinni Jonadab a te ti ka sinsaŋŋa de: <Ku a fɛ ate nama yaase ni ŋaaŋbisa a kan nyu daamoa. 7Ku a fɛ mɛ ate ni kan sɛ yie, ni bori abe ni vuk tiisa, ni kan maa ta ŋantaŋa de alege ku a fɛ ate ni bo viita po. Ni yaa le goa tɛŋka zuk beni juijui ate ni chim nicham la.> 8Ti va wari meena kama ate ti kokpieŋka Arekab nidoabinni Jonadab a weeni ti la. Tama yaase ti pooma yaase ti nidoabilisaŋa ale liema an nyu daam a nya ya 9yaase ti sɛ yie a boro yaase ti ta kaduksa ale laŋsa yaase ŋanbie. 10Ti kasim bo ka viita po ale va ti kokpieŋka Jonadab ale weeni ti dii meena la. 11Alege Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar ale jo tuesi tɛŋka de la, tama weeni kama ayen, <Ni jam, ku a fɛ ate ti cheŋ Jerusalem ate ti bɛ ale Kaldiya tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale Araam tugurik tɔŋdɔma.> Dila tama yaa wari bo Jerusalem.>>
12Naawen wanni yaa jam Jeremaya jigi ayen, 13<<Dii ate Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni a weeni la ale nna: Cheŋ a ga weeni Juda nuruma ale Jerusalem demma ayen, <Nama a kan zamsi wari a va mi wieŋa?> Naawen ale weeni. 14<Arekab nidoabinni Jonadab a weeni wa nidoabilisaŋa kama ayen ba kan nyu daamoa ate ba ta wanni de. A ta jam paari jinla ba an nyu daamoa, dii nyiŋla ba va ka ba kokpieŋka wanni. Alege mi biisi ale ni kama a tulim tulim, alege ni an wom mi nɔiya. 15Mi tom mi tomteerɔma biisiteerɔma kama a tulim tulim ni jigi. Ba weeni ayen, <<Waai meena a cheem basi wa gaasa suita abe wa tagri nyeela, ni kan va wen yona a tom te ŋa. Ate ni yaa le bo tɛŋ kaai po ate mi pai te ni ale ni koma la.>> Alege ni popola a ka mi jigi yaase ni wom mi. 16Arekab nidoabinni Jonadab ŋaaŋbisaŋa a ta ba kokpieŋka wanni ate wa te ba la kama, alege nuruma de an wom m nɔiya.>
17<<Dila, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni a weeni ayen, <Ni wom. Mi za ayen m ta ka kaasuŋ meena ate mi a mooli la a jam Juda ale waai meena ale bo Jerusalem la zuk. Mi jam biisi le ba kama alege ba an wom ya, a wi ba alege ba an tulisi ya.> >>
18Jeremaya yaa weeni Arekab dɔkdemma ayen, <<Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni ale weeni diila ale nna: <Ni wom ka ni kokpieŋka Jonadab ale weeni diila ale va wa sinsaŋŋa meena ale nye dii meena ate wa weeni la.> 19Dila la, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni ale weeni diila ale nna: <Arekab nidoabinni Jonadab a kan kpeeri ale nuru nyaka ate wa tom a te mi.> >>

english_text:
King Jehoiakim Burns Jeremiah's First Scroll
1 During the fourth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah, the Lord said to me, “Jeremiah, 2since the time Josiah was king, I have been speaking to you about Israel, Judah, and the other nations. Now, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you, 3then read it to the people of Judah. Maybe they will stop sinning when they hear what terrible things I plan for them. And if they turn back to me, I will forgive them.”
4I sent for Baruch son of Neriah and asked him to help me. I repeated everything the Lord had told me, and Baruch wrote it all down on a scroll. 5Then I said,
Baruch, the officials refuse to let me go into the Lord's temple, 6so you must go instead. Wait for the next holy day when the people of Judah come to the temple to pray and to go without eating. Then take this scroll to the temple and read it aloud. 7The Lord is furious, and if the people hear how he is going to punish them, maybe they will ask to be forgiven.
8-10In the ninth month of the fifth year that Jehoiakim was king, the leaders set a day when everyone who lived in Jerusalem or who was visiting there had to pray and go without eating. So Baruch took the scroll to the upper courtyard of the temple. He went over to the side of the courtyard and stood in a covered area near New Gate, where he read the scroll aloud.
This covered area belonged to Gemariah, one of the king's highest officials. 11Gemariah's son Micaiah was there and heard Baruch read what the Lord had said. 12When Baruch finished reading, Micaiah went down to the palace. His father Gemariah was in the officials' room, meeting with the rest of the king's officials, including Elishama, Delaiah, Elnathan, and Zedekiah. 13Micaiah told them what he had heard Baruch read to the people. 14Then the officials sent Jehudi and Shelemiah to tell Baruch, “Bring us that scroll.”
When Baruch arrived with the scroll, 15the officials said, “Please sit down and read it to us,” which he did. 16After they heard what was written on the scroll, they were worried and said to each other, “The king needs to hear this!” Turning to Baruch, they asked, 17“Did someone tell you what to write on this scroll?”
18“Yes, Jeremiah did,” Baruch replied. “I wrote down just what he told me.”
19The officials said, “You and Jeremiah must go into hiding, and don't tell anyone where you are going.”
20-22The officials put the scroll in Elishama's room and went to see the king, who was in one of the rooms where he lived and worked during the winter. It was the ninth month of the year, so there was a fire burning in the fireplace, and the king was sitting nearby. After the officials told the king about the scroll, he sent Jehudi to get it. Then Jehudi started reading the scroll to the king and his officials. 23-25But every time Jehudi finished reading three or four columns, the king would tell him to cut them off with his penknife and throw them in the fire. Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah begged the king not to burn the scroll, but he ignored them, and soon there was nothing left of it.
The king and his servants listened to what was written on the scroll, but they were not the least bit afraid, and they did not tear their clothes in sorrow.
26The king told his son Jerahmeel to take Seraiah and Shelemiah and to go arrest Baruch and me. But the Lord kept them from finding us.
Jeremiah's Second Scroll
27I had told Baruch what to write on that first scroll, but King Jehoiakim had burned it. So the Lord told me 28to get another scroll and write down everything that had been on the first one. 29Then he told me to say to King Jehoiakim:
Not only did you burn Jeremiah's scroll, you had the nerve to ask why he had written that the king of Babylonia would attack and ruin the land, killing all the people and even the animals. 30So I, the Lord, promise that you will be killed and your body thrown out on the ground. The sun will beat down on it during the day, and the frost will settle on it at night. And none of your descendants will ever be king of Judah. 31You, your children, and your servants are evil, and I will punish everyone of you. I warned you and the people of Judah and Jerusalem that I would bring disaster, but none of you have listened. So now you are doomed!
32After the Lord finished speaking to me, I got another scroll and gave it to Baruch. Then I told him what to write, so this second scroll would contain even more than was on the scroll Jehoiakim had burned.
translation_text:
1Josia nidoabinni Jeyoiakim Juda naawa naamu bena ŋanaansiwa po wanni de yaa nyini Naawen jigi a jam Jeremaya jigi: 2<<Pai gbaŋ a ŋmarisi wie ŋaai meena ate mi biisi a te fu a magsi chaab ale Izirali ale Juda ale tɛŋ yonsaŋa meena a zaani diipo ate mi piilim a biisi a te fu Josia naamu daaŋa po a jam paari yɔgyɔgla la a nyo ka po. 3Dai dii dai Juda nuruma a dan wom kaasuŋ meena ate mi zɔk ayen m ta jam ba zuk la, ba wanyi meena ale basi wa gaasa suiku, ate m vɔŋ ba gaasaŋa ale ba wabaataŋa a te ba.>>
4Dila Jeremaya a yaa wi Neria nidoabinni Baruk ate Jeremaya ale a biisi wie ŋaai meena ate Naawen a biisi a te wa la ate Baruk a ŋmarisi a nyo gbaŋ po. 5Jeremaya yaa jam weeni Baruk ayen, <<Ba kasi mi kama, mi an baga a cheŋ Naawen yenni. 6Dila cheŋ Naawen yenni nɔi bobika dai a kariŋ Naawen wieŋa gbaŋ po ate mi a biisi ate fi ŋmarisi la a te nuruma. Karim a te Juda nuruma meena ale nyini ba tɛŋsaŋa a jam la. 7Dai dii dai ba le puusi a te Naawen ate ba waai meena a basi wa gaasa suik, diila Naawen ale mooli ale suipuurum buui a basi nuruma zuk la a zuak ka yega.>>
8Neria nidoabinni Baruk yaa nye dii meena ate Jeremaya a weeni wa ayen wa nye la. Naawen yenni po wa kariŋ Naawen wieŋa gbaŋka po kama. 9Josia nidoabinni Jeyoiakim Juda naawa naamu bena ŋanuwa po chiisa neokku po ba yaa mooli nɔi bobika Naawen niŋ a te Jerusalem nuruma meena ale baai ale nyini Juda tɛŋsaŋa a jam la. 10Safan nidoabinni Gemaria gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa dɔkku po ate ku bo ŋmazuk dabiaka po a tuak Wen yenni Nansuiŋ Paalukku jigini la, Baruk yaa kariŋ Jeremaya wieŋa gbaŋka po Naawen yenni po a te nuruma.
11Gemaria nidoabinni Mikaiya ate wa kokpieŋ a nye Safan la ale wom Naawen wieŋa gbaŋka po la, 12wa deri siŋ gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa dɔkku po naawa yenni po, juijui ate kpaŋŋa meena a kala la, Elisama gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa ale Sɛmaiya nidoabinni Delaiya ale Achbor nidoabinni Elnatan ale Safan nidoabinni Gemaria ale Yanania nidoabinni Zedekia ale kpaga m ŋala meena. 13Mikaiya ale weeni dii meena ate wa wom Baruk ale kariŋ a te nuruma gbaŋka po la, 14kpaŋŋa meena yaa tom Jeyudi waai ale ka Netania nidoabili la, Selemia ŋaaŋbiika, Kusi ŋaaŋtulika ayen wa weeni Baruk ayen, <<Ta gbaŋka ate fi kariŋ a te nuruma la a jam.>> Dila Neria nidoabinni Baruk yaa ta gbaŋka wa nisa po a cheŋ. 15Ba yaa weeni ayen, <<Kali tɛŋ, ti a saalim kariŋ a te ti.>> Baruk yaa kariŋ a te ba. 16Ba le wom wieŋa de meena la, ba yaa nya chaab ale yɔgsum a weeni Baruk ayen, <<Ku a fɛ ate ti weeni wieŋa de meena a sak naawa.>> 17Ba yaa bek Baruk ayen, <<Weeni ti, ku zaani ka sɛ ate fi ŋmarisi nna meena? Ka Jeremaya ale biisi ate fi ŋmarisi?>>
18Baruk yaa tulisi ayen, <<Mm, wa le biisi wieŋa de meena a te mi, ate mi a ŋmarisi gbaŋka po.>>
19Kpaŋŋa yaa weeni Baruk ayen, <<Fi ale Jeremaya, ni ga suk. Ni kan basi ate waai a seba ni ale bo juijui la.>>
20Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ba le pai gbaŋka a dueni gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa Elisama dɔkku po la, ba yaa cheŋ naawa jigi dabiaka po a weeni wari meena a sak wa. 21Naawa yaa tom Jeyudi ayen wa ta gbaŋka a jam, ate Jeyudi a ta ka nyini gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa Elisama dɔkku po a jam kariŋ a te naawa ale wa kpaŋŋa meena ale za wa gauŋ la. 22Ku jam ka chiisa neokku po ate naawa a kala ale wa ŋoota garuk, ate bolim a bo bolim samɔniŋ po a za wa niŋ. 23Jeyudi a dan jam kariŋ gbaŋka a paari ka geli naawa a pai ka ŋmarisidoa gebik a gebi a pai a lɔnsi bolim samɔniŋka po, ate gbaŋka meena a ga dɛ bolimu po a nueri. 24Naawa ale baai meena ale tom a te wa la ale wom wieŋa de meena la ba an sak yɔgsummoa, yaase ba cheeri ba gattaŋa. 25Elnatan ale Delaiya ale Gemaria ale weeni naawa ayen wa kan ju gbaŋka la ale dila meena wa an wom ba. 26Naawa a goanti a te ka Jerameel naawa nidoabili ale Azriel nidoabinni Seraiya ale Abdeel nidoabinni Selemia suik ayen ba yik ŋmarisidoawa Baruk ale biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya. Alege Naawen a pai ba a suk.
27Naawa ale ju gbaŋka ate Jeremaya a biisi ate Baruk a ŋmarisi ka wieŋa la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, Naawen wanni yaa jam Jeremaya jigi ayen,
28<<Pai gbaŋ ka choa a ŋmarisi ka po wie ŋaai meena ale liŋ bo niŋ gbaŋka ate Juda naawa Jeyoiakim a ju la. 29Weeni Juda naawa Jeyoiakim mɛ ayen, <Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: Fi ju gbaŋ kala kama ale weeni ayen, <<Ka boa ale soa ate fi ŋmarisi ayen Babilon naawa ale sum jam kaasi tɛŋka de abe wa gebi nuruba ale duŋsa a ta nyini ka po?>> 30Dila la Naawen ale weeni dii a magsi chaab ale Juda naawa Jeyoiakim la ale nna: Wa kan ta waai ate wa kali Deevid naam zukpaglika zuwa, ba le yuk wa nyiŋka a basi ate ka bo kantueŋka tuilukku po ale yokku maglimu po. 31M le namsi wa ale wa bisaŋa ale baai ale tom a te wa la ba gaasaŋa nyiŋ, m le ta kaasuŋ kuui meena ate mi a mooli la a jam ba zuk ale baai ale bo Jerusalem la ale Juda nuruma zuk, dii nyiŋla ba an wom ya.> >>
32Jeremaya yaa pai gbaŋ ka choa a te ŋmarisidoawa Neria nidoabinni Baruk, ate Jeremaya ale a biisi la Baruk a ŋmarisi ka po wa ŋaai dek ale jam bo kaai po ate Juda naawa Jeyoiakim a ju ale bolimu la. Ate wa ŋala chaab dek a maa gum du.

english_text:
King Zedekiah Asks Jeremiah To Pray
1 King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had removed Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim from being the king of Judah and had made Josiah's son Zedekiah king instead. 2But Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Judah ignored everything the Lord had told me.
3-5Later, the Babylonian army attacked Jerusalem, but they left after learning that the Egyptian army was headed in this direction.
One day, Zedekiah sent Jehucal and the priest Zephaniah to talk with me. At that time, I was free to go wherever I wanted, because I had not yet been put in prison. Jehucal and Zephaniah said, “Jeremiah, please pray to the Lord our God for us.”
6-7Then the Lord told me to send them back to Zedekiah with this message:
Zedekiah, you wanted Jeremiah to ask me, the Lord God of Israel, what is going to happen. So I will tell you. The king of Egypt and his army came to your rescue, but soon they will go back to Egypt. 8Then the Babylonians will return and attack Jerusalem, and this time they will capture the city and set it on fire. 9Don't fool yourselves into thinking that the Babylonians will leave as they did before. 10Even if you could defeat their entire army, their wounded survivors would still be able to leave their tents and set Jerusalem on fire.
Jeremiah Is Put in Prison
11The Babylonian army had left because the Egyptian army was on its way to help us. 12So I decided to leave Jerusalem and go to the territory of the Benjamin tribe to claim my share of my family's land. 13I was leaving Jerusalem through Benjamin Gate, when I was stopped by Irijah, the officer in charge of the soldiers at the gate. He said, “Jeremiah, you're under arrest for trying to join the Babylonians.”
14“I'm not trying to join them!” I answered. But Irijah wouldn't listen, and he took me to the king's officials. 15-16They were angry and ordered the soldiers to beat me. Then I was taken to the house that belonged to Jonathan, one of the king's officials. It had been turned into a prison, and I was kept in a basement room.
After I had spent a long time there, 17King Zedekiah secretly had me brought to his palace, where he asked, “Is there any message for us from the Lord?”
“Yes, there is, Your Majesty,” I replied. “The Lord is going to let the king of Babylonia capture you.”
18Then I continued, “Your Majesty, why have you put me in prison? Have I committed a crime against you or your officials or the nation? 19Have you locked up the prophets who lied to you and said that the king of Babylonia would never attack Jerusalem? 20Please, don't send me back to that prison at Jonathan's house. If you do, I will die there.”
21King Zedekiah had me taken to the prison cells in the courtyard of the palace guards. He told the soldiers to give me a loaf of bread from one of the bakeries every day until the city ran out of grain.
translation_text:
1Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar yaa bobi Josia nidoabinni Zedekia Juda naab a tagri Jeyoiakim nidoabinni Konia. 2Alege Zedekia yaase baai ale tom a te wa la yaase tɛŋka nuruma niŋ a bo wie ŋaai ate Naawen a biisi a ta va biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya jigi la.
3Naab Zedekia yaa jam tom Selemia nidoabinni Jeyukal ale Maaseiya nidoabinni kaabteerɔwa Zefania ayen ba cheŋ biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya jigi ale tomtomiŋ ka de: <<Mi a saalim puusi a te Naawen, ti Wenni a te ti.>>
4Yɔgyɔgla de Jeremaya a jam nye fasiyaa kama a jam ale a cheŋ nuruma po, diila ba an diem jam lik wa. 5Faaro tugurik tɔŋdɔma a jam gɔk santiri kama a nyini Ejipiti a nyini, ate Kaldiya demma baai ale jam gilim Jerusalem la ale wom ba wari la ba yaa basi Jerusalem.
6Naawen wanni yaa jam biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya jigi: 7<<Dii ate Naawen, Izirali Wenni a weeni la ale nna: Weeni Juda naawa waai ale tom fu ayen fi bek mi la ayen, <Faaro tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale gɔk santinni a nyini ayen ba maari ni la ale pilim ŋmani badek tɛŋka Ejipiti. 8Kaldiya demma ale ŋman jam a siti tɛŋka de a yik ka a ju basi.>
9<<Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: Ni kan paasi nidega, a poli ayen, <Kaldiya demma a za ba sum basi ti kama.> Ba kan basi ni. 10Babilon tugurik tɔŋdɔ baai meena ale a siti la ba nuru baai ale kɔni la a dan poom tali bo ba viitaŋa po ba le nyini a ju tɛŋka de a basi.>>
11Babilon tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale basi Jerusalem Faaro tugurik tɔŋdɔma la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, 12Jeremaya yaa piilim a basi tɛŋka a cheŋ Benjamin tɛŋka ayen wa tuesi wa charuku nuruma jigi dula. 13Alege wa le paari Benjamin nansuiŋku la, limisidɔwa kpagni, ate wa yuei a chim Irija la Selemia nidoabinni ate wa kokpieŋ a chim Yanania la a yik wa ale weeni ayen, <<Fi basi kama ale a cheŋ Kaldiya demma jigi?>>
14Jeremaya yaa weeni ayen, <<Kula daa wensie. Mi an basi ale a cheŋ Kaldiya demma jigi ya.>> Alege Irija a kan wom wa, wa goanti yik Jeremaya kama a ta wa jam kpaŋŋa jigi. 15Ba sue ale jam a puuri ale Jeremaya a yaa jam nak wa ale lik wa gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa Jonatan yenni po dii ate ba pai chim likka dɔk la.
16Ba jam pai Jeremaya a basi ka tɛŋ likka dɔk po a basi ate wa bo dula a beni. 17Naab Zedekia yaa tom ate ba ta wa jam naab yenni, juijui ate wa bek wadek wa nyiini ayen, <<Wari boro a nyini Naawen jigi ya?>> Jeremaya yaa tulisi ayen, <<Mm, ba le pai fu a te Babilon naawa.>>
18Jeremaya yaa weeni naab Zedekia ayen, <<Boan biem ate m tom a kaasi fu yaase fi kpaŋŋa yaase nuruma de, ate fi lik mu? 19Fi biisiteerɔma a bo ka bɛ? Baai ale mooli a te fu ayen, <Babilon naawa a kan siti fu yaase tɛŋka de la?> 20Alege yɔgyɔgla de, m nyɔnɔ naaba, mi a saalim wom de. Basi ate m saalim fu: Kan te ate m ŋman cheŋ gbaŋ ŋmarisidoawa Jonatan yenni dan kan daa di m le kpi dula.>>
21Naab Zedekia yaa te suik ate ba pai Jeremaya a basi limisidɔma dabiaka po ale a te wa boroborok a nyini seerɔma jigi ate boroborok tɛŋka po meena a nueri. Dila Jeremaya yaa jam wari ka limisidɔma dabiaka po.

english_text:
Jeremiah Is Held Prisoner in a Dry Well
1One day, Shephatiah, Gedaliah, Jehucal, and Pashhur heard me tell the people of Judah 2-3that the Lord had said, “If you stay here in Jerusalem, you will die in battle or from disease or hunger, and the Babylonian army will capture the city anyway. But if you surrender to the Babylonians, they will let you live.”
4So the four of them went to the king and said, “You should put Jeremiah to death, because he is making the soldiers and everyone else lose hope. He isn't trying to help our people; he's trying to harm them.”
5Zedekiah replied, “Do what you want with him. I can't stop you.”
6Then they took me back to the courtyard of the palace guards and let me down with ropes into the well that belonged to Malchiah, the king's son. There was no water in the well, but I sank down in the mud.
7-8Ebedmelech from Ethiopia was an official at the palace, and he heard what they had done to me. So he went to speak with King Zedekiah, who was holding court at Benjamin Gate. 9Ebedmelech said, “Your Majesty, Jeremiah is a prophet, and those men were wrong to throw him into a well. And when Jerusalem runs out of food, Jeremiah will starve to death down there.”
10Zedekiah answered, “Take 30 of my soldiers and pull Jeremiah out before he dies.”
11Ebedmelech and the soldiers went to the palace and got some rags from the room under the treasury. He used ropes to lower them into the well. 12Then he said, “Put these rags under your arms so the ropes won't hurt you.” After I did, 13the men pulled me out. And from then on, I was kept in the courtyard of the palace guards.
King Zedekiah Questions Jeremiah
14King Zedekiah had me brought to his private entrance to the temple, and he said, “I'm going to ask you something, and I want to know the truth.”
15“Why?” I replied. “You won't listen, and you might even have me killed!”
16He said, “I swear in the name of the living Lord our Creator that I won't have you killed. No one else can hear what we say, and I won't let anyone kill you.”
17Then I told him that the Lord had said: “Zedekiah, I am the Lord God All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I promise that if you surrender to King Nebuchadnezzar's officers, you and your family won't be killed, and Jerusalem won't be burned down. 18But if you don't surrender, I will let the Babylonian army capture Jerusalem and burn it down, and you will be taken prisoner.”
19Zedekiah answered, “I can't surrender to the Babylonians. I'm too afraid of the people of Judah who have already joined them. The Babylonians might hand me over to them, and they would torture me.”
20I said, “If you will just obey the Lord, the Babylonians won't hand you over to those Jews. You will be allowed to live, and all will go well for you. 21But the Lord has shown me that if you refuse to obey, 22then the women of your palace will be taken prisoner by Nebuchadnezzar's officials. And those women will say to you:
Friends you trusted led you astray.
Now you're trapped in mud,
and those friends you trusted
have all turned away.
23The Babylonian army will take your wives and children captive, you will be taken as a prisoner to the King of Babylonia, and Jerusalem will be burned down.”
24Zedekiah said, “Jeremiah, if you tell anyone what we have talked about, you might lose your life. 25And I'm sure that if my officials hear about our meeting, they will ask you what we said to each other. They might even threaten to kill you if you don't tell them. 26So if they question you, tell them you were begging me not to send you back to the prison at Jonathan's house, because going back there would kill you.”
27The officials did come and question me about my meeting with the king, and I told them exactly what he had ordered me to say. They never spoke to me about the meeting again, since no one had heard us talking.
28 I was held in the courtyard of the palace guards until the day Jerusalem was captured.
translation_text:
1Mattan nidoabinni Sepatia ale Pasur nidoabinni Gedalia ale Selemia nidoabinni Jukal ale Malkija nidoabinni Pasur ale jam wom dii ate Jeremaya a weeni nuruma meena ase wa le jam weeni ayen, 2<<Naawen abe le weeni diila ale nna: <Waai dek ale a bo tɛŋka de po la ale kpi ale gebika ale kɔm ale nyiŋtuila, alege waai dek ale a cheŋ Kaldiya demma jigi ale boro. Wa le nyini vum nyiŋ, wa le boro.> 3Naawen abe le weeni diila ale nna: <Tɛŋka de m le sum pai te Babilon naawa tugurik tɔŋdɔma ate ba yik ka.> >>
4Kpaŋŋa yaa weeni naawa ayen, <<Nuruwa de a magsi ka koka. Wa basi ate ka tugurik tɔŋdɔ baai ale tali bo tɛŋka po la a jɔk nyiŋbiiri ale nuruma meena ale wa le weeni wie ŋaai a te ba la. Nuruwa de a kan gisi nuruma de nalimmoa alege ka ba kaasuŋ.>>
5Naab Zedekia yaa tulisi ayen, <<Wa bo ni nisima po. Naawa an baga a kasi ni.>>
6Dila ba yaa pai Jeremaya a nyo naawa nidoabinni Malkija vili po, dii ale jam bo limisidɔma dabiaka po la. Ba jam pai ka miisa a bobi wa a basi ate wa siŋ vinni po. Nyiam a jam ka di po, ka bagta nyiini, ate Jeremaya a siŋ bagtaŋa po.
7Alege Kus denɔ Ebed Melek, waai ale ka naawa yenni kpagi la a wom ayen ba pai Jeremaya a basi ka vili po. Naawa ale diem jam kali Benjamin Nansuiŋku la, 8Ebed Melek a nyini naab yenni po a weeni naawa ayen, 9<<M nyɔnɔ naaba, nuruma de a tom ka gaasa tuima ale ba le nye biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya dii meena la. Ba le pai wa basi vinni po la ale basi kama ate wa viiri a kpi ase ŋandiinta a nin kan ŋman bo tɛŋka po.>>
10Naawa yaa weeni Kus denɔ Ebed Melek ayen, <<Yaali nidoaba pisita dela ale fu ate ni yeeri biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya vinni po alege ate wa kpi.>>
11Dila Ebed Melek a yaali nidoama ate ba cheŋ dɔk ate ba a dueni ŋanta du naab yenni po la. Wa yaa pai garucha kpagsa ale garuk tii ale bugi a yaa basi ate ti siŋ Jeremaya jigi vinni po ale miisa. 12Kus denɔwa Ebed Melek a yaa weeni Jeremaya ayen, <<Pai garucha kpagsaŋa de ale garuk tii ale bugi la a su fi nisimaŋa de ate miisaŋa a kan te fu tuemoa.>> Ate Jeremaya a nye dila, 13ate ba dari wa ale miisaŋa a ta nyini vinni po a jueli. Ate Jeremaya a jam wari bo limisidɔwa dabiaka po.
14Naab Zedekia yaa tom ate ba ta biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya a jam nansuiŋ kuui ale saari buta wa a jo Naawen yenni po la. Naawa yaa weeni Jeremaya ayen, <<Mi a yaali ayen m bek fu ka wari. Kan suk wari ale mu.>>
15Jeremaya yaa weeni Zedekia ayen, <<M dan tulisi fu fi kan ko mu? M dan poom sak fu fi kan wom mu.>>
16Alege Zedekia a suk pɛ ale Jeremaya ayen, <<Naawen ale sum boro la nyiŋ, waai ale basi ate ti a vuusi la, m kan ko fu yaase m pai fu a te baai ale a gisi fi nyuvunni la.>>
17Jeremaya yaa weeni Zedekia ayen, <<Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni a weeni ayen, <Fi dan siak a te Babilon naawa kpaŋŋa, fi le nyini vum nyiŋ ate ba kan ju tɛŋka de, ate fi ale fi dɔkdemma ale boro. 18Alege fi dan kan siak a te Babilon naawa kpaŋŋa tɛŋka de, ale jo Kaldiya demma nisa po ate ba ju ka basi, fidek a kan yuli bɛ ba nisima po.> >>
19Naab Zedekia a weeni Jeremaya ayen, <<Mi a chali ka yɔgsum ale Juuma baai ale cheŋ Kaldiya demma jigi la, Kaldiya demma ale pai mu a te ba ate ba nye mu gaasa.>>
20Jeremaya yaa weeni ayen, <<Ba kan pai fu a te, zuli Naawen a nye dii ate mi a weeni fu la. Ate ku cheŋ nalimnyiini a te fu, ate fi nyini vum nyiŋ. 21Alege fi dan zɛri an siak te ya, Naawen ale pai dii a sak mi la ale nna: 22Nipooma meena ale tali bo Juda naawa yenni po la ba le ta ba nyini te Babilon naawa. Nipok bala ale weeni ayen, <Ba ta fu cheŋ bɛ kama a nya pagrim fi zuk, doa baai ate fi mariŋ la. Fi naŋsaŋa a feri bagtaŋa po, fi doama a zɛri fu.>
23<<Ni pooma ale ni bisaŋa ba le ta nyini te Kaldiya demma. Fidek kan yuli bɛ, Babilon naawa ale yik fu, ate tɛŋka de ba ju ka basi.
24Ate Zedekia yaa weeni Jeremaya ayen, <<Kan basi ate waai seba biika de nɔi po, dan kan daa di fi baga a kpi kama. 25Kpaŋŋa a dan wom ayen mi biisi ale fu, ate ba jam fi jigi a weeni ayen, <Weeni ti dii ate fi weeni naawa la ale naawa ale weeni fi diila, kan suk ti dan kan daa di ti le ko fu,> 26weeni ba ayen, <Mi jam a saalim naawa kama ayen wa kan te ti ŋman cheŋ Jonatan yenni ate m kpi dula.> >>
27Kpaŋŋa meena a jan jam Jeremaya jigi kama a bek wa, ate wa weeni ba dii meena ate naawa ayen wa weeni la. Dila ba an ŋman weeni wari ya, diila waai an wom wa ale naawa biika.
28Ate Jeremaya a wari bo limisidɔwa dabiaka po a ga paari Jerusalem sitika danni. Ba le jam kaasi Jerusalem diila ale nna:

english_text:
Jerusalem Is Captured by the Babylonians
(Jeremiah 52.4-16; 2 Kings 25.1-12)
1-3In the tenth month of the ninth year that Zedekiah was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonian army began their attack on Jerusalem. They kept the city surrounded for a year and a half. Then, on the ninth day of the fourth month of the eleventh year that Zedekiah was king, they broke through the city walls.
After Jerusalem was captured, Nebuchadnezzar's highest officials, including Nebo Sarsechim and Nergal Sharezer from Simmagir, took their places at Middle Gate to show they were in control of the city.
4When King Zedekiah and his troops saw that Jerusalem had been captured, they tried to escape from the city that same night. They went to the king's garden, where they slipped through the gate between the two city walls and headed toward the Jordan River valley. 5But the Babylonian troops caught up with them near Jericho. They arrested Zedekiah and took him to the town of Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial, then found him guilty, 6and gave orders for him to be punished. Zedekiah's sons were killed there in front of him, and so were the leaders of Judah's ruling families. 7Then his eyes were poked out, and he was put in chains, so he could be dragged off to Babylonia.
8Meanwhile, the Babylonian army had burned the houses in Jerusalem, including the royal palace, and they had broken down the city walls. 9Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guards, led away everyone from the city as prisoners, even those who had deserted to Nebuchadnezzar. 10Only the poorest people who owned no land were left behind in Judah, and Nebuzaradan gave them fields and vineyards.
11Nebuchadnezzar had given the following orders to Nebuzaradan: 12“Find Jeremiah and keep him safe. Take good care of him and do whatever he asks.”
13Nebuzaradan, Nebushazban, Nergal Sharezer, and the other officers of King Nebuchadnezzar 14sent some of their troops to bring me from the courtyard of the royal palace guards. They put me in the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam and told him to take me to my home. And so I was allowed to stay with the people who remained in Judah.
The Lord Promises To Protect Ebedmelech
15While I was a prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guard, the Lord told me to say 16to Ebedmelech from Ethiopia:
I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I warned everyone that I would bring disaster, not prosperity, to this city. Now very soon I will do what I said, and you will see it happen. 17-18But because you trusted me, I will protect you from the officials of Judah, and when Judah is struck by disaster, I will rescue you and keep you alive. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
1Juda naawa Zedekia bena neokku po chiisa piika po Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena yaa gɔk santiri a ta chaab ale Jerusalem ale gilim kasi ka. 2Ate Zedekia bena pi ale dinyiwa po chiisa sinaansiwa po ka daa neokku danni, ba wɛ tɛŋka parika a jo. 3Babilon naawa kpaŋŋa meena yaa jam tuesi kalisa jigi Suŋsuŋ Nansuiŋku. Kpaŋŋa jam le Nergal Sarezer ale nyini Samgar ale kpagi kpienni Nebo Sarsekim ale Nergal Sarezer niŋdeerɔ kpioŋ ale Babilon naawa kpaga ŋachaab. 4Juda naawa Zedekia ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena ale nya ba la, ba yaa chali. Ba yaa basi tɛŋka yok ale va naawa kadukka po a va parisa siyewa suŋsuŋ nansuiŋku a nyini a duŋ Araba.
5Alege Kaldiya tugurik tɔŋdɔma a vi ba a ga yik Zedekia Jeriko peelimmu po. Ba jam yik wa kama a ta wa ga te Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar Aribla ale bo Yamat la, juijui ate wa mooli ba le ba nye wa diila. 6Babilon naawa yaa tɔgri Zedekia nidoabilisaŋa wa nina po Aribla tɛŋka ale ko Juda kpaŋŋa meena mɛ. 7Wa jam yeeri Zedekia ninaŋa kama ale bobi wa ale kutuk mɔnuŋ chɔrima a ta cheŋ Babilon.
8Kaldiya demma a ju naab yenni ale nuruma yeeŋa bolim ale wɛ Jerusalem parisaŋa a lɔnsi. 9Nebuzaradan ale a nya tugurik tɔŋdɔma zuk la yaa ji nuru baai ale tali tɛŋka po la, ale baai ale jam cheŋ wa jigi la, ale nuru mbala meena a ta cheŋ Babilon. 10Alege Nebuzaradan tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagni a jam tali ka ŋanjaksaŋa gela ale kan ta jaab la a basi Juda tɛŋka po. Dila po wa jam te ba ka kaduksa ale laŋsa.
11Yɔgyɔgla de Babilon naawa Nebukadnezzar a jam te wieŋa de ka tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagni Nebuzaradan a magsi chaab ale Jeremaya: 12<<Ta wa a ga a nya wa zuk, kan nye wa biemmoa alege nye dii meena ate wa a bek la.>> 13Dila tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagni Nebuzaradan ale kpagi kpienni Nebusazban ale niŋdeerɔ kpioŋku Nergal Sarezer ale Babilon naawa kpaga ŋachaama meena 14a yaa tom yeeri Jeremaya dabiaka po. Ba jam pai wa a te ka Gedalia waai ale ka Ayikam nidoabili la ate wa chim Safan nidoabili la ayen wa ta wa cheŋ wa yenni. Dila wa jam bo ale ka wadek nuruba.
15Jeremaya ale jam diem bo dabiaka po la, Naawen wanni a jam wa jigi ayen, 16<<Cheŋ ga weeni Kus denɔwa Ebed Melek ayen, <Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni ale weeni diila ale nna: M le basi ate m wieŋa a chim wensie a va ka kaasuŋ alege daa paaruŋ. Dila po ŋa le nye ni nimbie po. 17Alege m le vari ni a basi da dila danni, Naawen ale weeni. Ba kan pai ni a te baai ate ni a chali yɔgsum la. 18M le vari ni a basi, ba kan ko ni ale gebiga alege ni ale bɛ a nyini vum nyiŋ, dii nyiŋla ni ta sebchakka ale mi kama. Naawen ale weeni.> >>

english_text:
Jeremiah Is Set Free
1I was led away in chains along with the people of Judah and Jerusalem who were being taken to Babylonia. Nebuzaradan was the officer in charge of the guard, and while we were stopped at Ramah, the Lord caused him to set me free. 2Nebuzaradan said:
Jeremiah, the Lord your God warned your people that he would bring disaster on this land. 3But they continued to rebel against him, and now he has punished them just as he threatened.
4Today I am taking the chains off your wrists and setting you free! If you want to, you can come with me to Babylonia, and I will see that you are taken care of. Or if you decide to stay here, you can go wherever you wish. 5King Nebuchadnezzar has chosen Gedaliah to rule Judah. You can live near Gedaliah, and he will provide for you, or you can live anywhere else you choose.
Nebuzaradan gave me a supply of food, then let me leave. 6I decided to stay with the people of Judah, and I went to live near Gedaliah in Mizpah.
The Harvest Is Brought In
7-8 Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, together with Johanan and Jonathan, the two sons of Kareah, had been officers in Judah's army. And so had Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah from Maacah. They and their troops had been stationed outside Jerusalem and had not been captured. They heard that Gedaliah had been chosen to rule Judah, and that the poorest men, women, and children had not been taken away to Babylonia. So they went to Mizpah and met with their new ruler.
9Gedaliah told them, “There's no need to be afraid of the Babylonians. Everything will be fine, if we live peacefully and obey King Nebuchadnezzar. 10I will stay here at Mizpah and meet with the Babylonian officials on each of their visits. But you must go back to your towns and bring in the harvest, then store the wine, olive oil, and dried fruit.”
11-12Earlier, when the Babylonians had invaded Judah, many of the Jews escaped to Moab, Ammon, Edom, and several other countries. But these Jews heard that the king of Babylonia had appointed Gedaliah as ruler of Judah, and that only a few people were left there. So the Jews in these other countries came back to Judah and helped with the grape and fruit harvest, which was especially large that year.
Gedaliah Is Murdered
13One day, Johanan got together with some of the other men who had been army officers, and they came to Mizpah and met with Gedaliah. 14They said, “Gedaliah, we came to warn you that King Baalis of Ammon hired Ishmael to murder you!”
Gedaliah refused to believe them, 15so Johanan went to Gedaliah privately and said, “Let me kill Ishmael. No one will find out who did it. There are only a few people left in Judah, but they are depending on you. And if you are murdered, they will be scattered or killed.”
16Gedaliah answered, “Don't kill Ishmael! What you've said about him can't be true.”
translation_text:
1Wanni yaa nyini Naawen jigi a jam Jeremaya jigi tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagni Nebuzaradan ale lak wa Arama basi la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, wa jam nya kama ayen chɔrima ale bobi Jeremaya ate wa ta bo baai ate ba yik ta nyini Jerusalem ale Juda a jam Babilon la po. 2Kpagni ale nya Jeremaya la, wa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Naawen fi Wenni ale te suik ate kaasuŋku de a jam dela. 3Ate yɔgyɔgla de Naawen a ta ku jam, wa nye ase ka wa le weeni ayen wa nye diila. Kude meena a nye kama dii nyiŋla nama a tom kaasi Naawen kama ale an zuli wa. 4Alege jinla mi a yeeri chɔrimaŋa kama fi nisimaŋa po. Fi daa yaali va mu a jam Babilon ate mi a nya fi zuk, alege fi dan kaa yaali, kan jam. Nya, tɛŋka meena a doa ka fi niŋ, a cheŋ juijui meena ate fi a yaali la.>> 5Jeremaya ale cheem ayen wa cheŋ la, Nebuzaradan yaa gum du ayen, <<Ŋman cheŋ Ayikam nidoabinni Gedalia jigi ate wa kokpieŋ a nye Safan la, waai ate Babilon naawa a lueri ayen wa a nya Juda tɛŋsaŋa zuk la, a bo le wa ale nuruma, yaase jigi meena ate fi a yaali la.>> Ate kpagni a yaa te wa ŋanta ale basi ate wa cheŋ. 6Jeremaya yaa cheŋ Ayikam nidoabinni Gedalia jigi Mizpa a bo ale nuru baai ale jam tali tɛŋka po la.
7Tugurik tɔŋdɔ kpaŋŋa ale ba nuruma ale jam diem bo tɛŋka peelimmu po la yaa wom ayen Babilon naawa a lueri ka Ayikam nidoabinni Gedalia ayen wa a nya tɛŋka zuk la ale nidoama ale nipooma ale bisaŋa baai ale jam jaŋ tɛŋka po la ate ba an jam ji ba a ta cheŋ Babilon la, 8ba yaa jam Mizpa. Dila Netania nidoabinni Ismael ale Karea nidoabilisaŋa Joyanan ale Jonatan ale Tanhumet nidoabinni Seraiya ale Netofat denɔwa Efai nidoabilisaŋa ale Maaka denɔwa nidoabinni Jezaniya ale ba nuruma yaa cheŋ Gedalia jigi Mizpa. 9Ayikam nidoabinni Gedalia ate wa kokpieŋ a nye Safan la a yaa pɛ ayen wa basi ate ba ale ba nuruma a seba chak. Wa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni kan chali yɔgsum ale Kaldiya demma tom teka. Ni kali tɛŋka po a tom a te Babilon naawa, ate ku cheŋ nalimnyiini a te ni. 10Mi dek ale tagri ni zuk a bo Mizpa a magsi Kaldiya demma a nin jam ti jigi, alege nama a su daamu abe ni a tigsi yɔnaŋa ale kpaamu a nyo ni samɔnsaŋa po abe ni bo tɛŋ kpaŋsaŋa po.>>
11Juuma ale bo Moab ale Ammon ale Edom ale tɛŋ sinsila meena la ale wom ayen Babilon naawa a tali nuruba basi Juda ale lueri Ayikam nidoabinni Gedalia ate wa kokpieŋ a nye Safan la ayen wa a nya ba zuk la, 12ba meena yaa ŋman jam Juda tɛŋka Gedalia jigi Mizpa po. Ba jam nyini ka tɛŋ sii meena ate ba jam waaŋ a cheŋ la. Ate ba jam gbesi yɔna piisi ale nya daam yega.
13Karea nidoabinni Joyanan ale tugurik tɔŋdɔ kpaŋŋa ale diem bo tɛŋka peelimmu po la a yaa jam Gedalia jigi Mizpa 14a weeni wa ayen, <<Fi zɛ ayen Ammon demma naawa Baalis a tom ka Netania nidoabinni Ismael ayen wa ko fu?>> Alege Ayikam nidoabinni Gedalia an siak ba le weeni diila.
15Karea nidoabinni Joyanan yaa weeni Gedalia dek wa nyiini Mizpa ayen, <<Basi ate m ga ko Netania nidoabinni Ismael ate waai a kan seba. Ka boa ale soa ate wa ayen wa ko fu abe wa nye ate Juuma meena ale tigsi gilim fu la a waaŋ abe Juda baai ale tali la a kpi?>>
16Alege Ayikam nidoabinni Gedalia a weeni Karea nidoabinni Joyanan ayen, <<Kan nye wa dila choa! Fi le weeni dii a te Ismael la daa wensie.>>

english_text:
1 But in the seventh month, Ishmael came to Mizpah with ten of his soldiers. He had been one of the king's officials and was a member of the royal family. Ishmael and his men were invited to eat with Gedaliah. 2During the meal, Ishmael and his soldiers killed Gedaliah, the man chosen as ruler of Judah by the king of Babylonia. 3Then they killed the Jews who were with Gedaliah, and they also killed the Babylonian soldiers who were there.
4The next day, the murders had still not been discovered, 5when 80 men came down the road toward Mizpah from the towns of Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria. They were on their way to the temple to offer gifts of grain and incense to the Lord. They had shaved off their beards, torn their clothes, and cut themselves, because they were mourning.
6Ishmael went out the town gate to meet them. He pretended to be weeping, and he asked them to come into Mizpah to meet with Gedaliah, the ruler of Judah. 7But after they were inside the town, Ishmael ordered his soldiers to kill them and throw their bodies into a well. 8He let ten of the men live, because they offered to give him supplies of wheat, barley, olive oil, and honey they had hidden in a field. 9The well that he filled with bodies had been dug by King Asa of Judah to store rainwater, because he was afraid that King Baasha of Israel might surround Mizpah and keep the people from getting to their water supply.
10Nebuzaradan, King Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guard, had left King Zedekiah's daughters and many other people at Mizpah, and he had put Gedaliah in charge of them. But now Ishmael took them all prisoner and led them toward Ammon, on the other side of the Jordan River.
11Johanan and the other army officers heard what Ishmael had done. 12So they and their troops chased Ishmael and caught up with him at the large pit at Gibeon. 13When Ishmael's prisoners saw Johanan and the officers, they were happy 14and turned around and ran toward Johanan. 15But Ishmael and eight of his men escaped and went to Ammon.
Johanan Decides To Take the People to Egypt
16Johanan and the officers had rescued the women, children, and royal officials that Ishmael had taken prisoner after killing Gedaliah. Johanan led the people from Gibeon 17-18toward Egypt. They wanted to go there, because they were afraid of what the Babylonians would do when they found out that Ishmael had killed Gedaliah, the ruler appointed by King Nebuchadnezzar.
The People Ask Jeremiah To Pray for Them
On the way to Egypt, we stopped at the town of Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem.
translation_text:
1Chiisa siyopɔiwa po Netania nidoabinni Ismael ate wa kokpieŋ a nye Elisama la ate wa chim naawa dɔkdemma wanyi la ale ŋman chim naawa kpaŋŋa dinyi la a yaa jam Ayikam nidoabinni Gedalia jigi Mizpa ale nuruba pi. Ba le diem boro a de ale chaab la, 2Netania nidoabinni Ismael ale nuruba piika ale jam bo le wa la yaa yiti ko Ayikam nidoabinni Gedalia ate wa kokpieŋ a nye Safan la ale gebik, a ko waai ate Babilon naawa a jam lueri ayen wa a nya tɛŋka zuk la. 3Ismael a jam ko Juuma meena ale jam bo ale Gedalia Mizpa la kama, ale Kaldiya tugurik tɔŋdɔma gela ale jam bo dula la.
4Dai dii ale pai saŋ Gedalia koka la, alege ate waai a seba ku nɔi po la, 5nuruba pinaanuŋ ale chiiri ba teeŋsa, a cheeri ba gatta ale gebi badek a nyini Sikiim ale Siilo ale Samaria a ta ŋanbie tiirita ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa a jam Naawen yenni. 6Netania nidoabinni Ismael yaa jam nyini Mizpa a nyini ayen wa tu ba, a kum a cheŋ. Wa le tu ba la, wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni jam Ayikam nidoabinni Gedalia jigi.>> 7Ba le jo tɛŋka po la, Netania nidoabinni Ismael ale nuru baai ale jam bo le wa la a yaa tɔgri ba a yuk ba basi vili po. 8Alege ba po pi a weeni Ismael ayen, <<Kan ko ti! Ti ta ka wiiti ale barli ale kpaam ale siita a suk laŋka po.>> Dila wa yaa basi ba ale an jam ko ba ale mbala. 9Yɔgyɔgla de vili dii ate wa yuk nuru baai ate wa ko la ale Gedalia a basi du la ka dii ate naab Asa a jam tu a maari wadek Izirali naawa Baasia ale jam a siti wa la. Netania nidoabinni Ismael a jam sueri di ale ka kpieba.
10Ismael yaa yik nuru mbala meena ale bo Mizpa la, naawa liema ale baai meena ale tali dula ate tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagni Nebuzaradan a lueri Ayikam nidoabinni Gedalia ayen wa a nya ba zuk la. Netania nidoabinni Ismael yik ba a yaa ta a duŋ Ammon tɛŋka.
11Karea nidoabinni Joyanan ale tugurik tɔŋdɔ kpaŋŋa ale bo ale wa la ale wom biem buui meena ate Netania nidoabinni Ismael a nye la, 12ba yaa yik ba nuruma meena a cheŋ ba kpaliŋ Netania nidoabinni Ismael. Ba yaa paari ba beli kpienni ale bo Gibeon la. 13Nuru baai meena ate Ismael a yik la ale nya Karea nidoabinni Joyanan ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale bo le wa la ba sue yaa peenti. 14Nuruma meena ate Ismael a yik Mizpa la a ŋmani cheŋ Karea nidoabinni Joyanan jigi. 15Alege Netania nidoabinni Ismael ale wa nuruba naaniŋ a vari Joyanan jigi a chali cheŋ Ammon tɛŋka.
16Karea nidoabinni Joyanan ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔ kpaŋŋa ale bo le wa la yaa de baai ale vuuk la Mizpa ate wa tuesi Netania nidoabinni Ismael jigi wa le ko Ayikam nidoabinni Gedalia la ŋaaŋnyiŋ: ba jam ka tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale nipooma ale bisaŋa ale baai ate ba jɛ ba la ate wa ta nyini Gibeon. 17Ate ba cheŋ a ga wari Gerut Kimyam a moata Betiliyem ba suiku po a cheŋ Ejipiti 18ayen ba bɛ ale Kaldiya demma. Ba jam a chali ba ka yɔgsum dii nyiŋla Netania nidoabinni Gedalia ate Babilon naawa a lueri ayen wa a nya tɛŋka zuk la.

english_text:
1Johanan, Jezaniah, the other army officers, and everyone else in the group, came to me 2and said, “Please, Jeremiah, pray to the Lord your God for us. Judah used to have many people, but as you can see, only a few of us are left. 3Ask the Lord to tell us where he wants us to go and what he wants us to do.”
4“All right,” I answered, “I will pray to the Lord your God, and I will tell you everything he says.”
5They answered, “The Lord himself will be our witness that we promise to do whatever he says, 6even if it isn't what we want to do. We will obey the Lord so that all will go well for us.”
7Ten days later, the Lord gave me an answer for 8Johanan, the officers, and the other people. So I called them together 9and told them that the Lord God of Israel had said:
You asked Jeremiah to pray and find out what you should do. 10I am sorry that I had to punish you, and so I now tell you to stay here in Judah, where I will plant you and build you up, instead of tearing you down and uprooting you. 11Don't be afraid of the King of Babylonia. I will protect you from him, 12and I will even force him to have mercy on you and give back your farms.
13But you might keep on saying, “We won't stay here in Judah, and we won't obey the Lord our God. 14We are going to Egypt, where there is plenty of food and no danger of war.”
15People of Judah, you survived when the Babylonian army attacked. Now you are planning to move to Egypt, and if you do go, this is what will happen. 16-17You are afraid of war, starvation, and disease here in Judah, but they will follow you to Egypt and kill you there. None of you will survive the disasters I will send.
18I, the Lord, was angry with the people of Jerusalem and punished them. And if you go to Egypt, I will be angry and punish you the same way. You will never again see your homeland. People will be horrified at what I do to you, and they will use the name of your city as a curse word.
Jeremiah Gives a Warning
19I told the people:
You escaped the disaster that struck Judah, but now the Lord warns you to stay away from Egypt. 20You asked me to pray and find out what the Lord our God wants you to do, and you promised to obey him. But that was a terrible mistake, 21because now that I have given you the Lord's answer, you refuse to obey him. 22And so, you will die in Egypt from war, hunger, and disease.
translation_text:
1Tugurik tɔŋdɔ kpaŋŋa meena a gum chaab ale Karea nidoabinni Joyanan ale Yosaya nidoabinni Jezaniya ale nuruma meena nuru fiisa ale nuru kpienta a cheŋ, 2biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya jigi a weeni wa ayen, <<Ti a saalim wom ti juisimu a puusi te Naawen fi Wenni a te baai ale tali la ase fi le a nya dii yɔgyɔgla la, ti jam piisi kama alege yɔgyɔgla de maga ale tali. 3Puusi a te Naawen fi Wenni a weeni ti juijui ate ti cheŋ la ale ti le ti nye diila.>>
4Biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya yaa weeni ayen, <<M wom ni kama, m le sum puusi a te Naawen ni Wenni ni le bek diila. M le weeni ni dii meena ate Naawen a weeni la m kan peri wariya.>>
5Ba yaa weeni Jeremaya ayen, <<Naawen abe chim wensie seerɔ a ta chaab ale ti ase ti nin kan nye va dii meena ate Naawen ni Wenni a tom fu ayen fi weeni ti la. 6Ku nala te ti yaase ku an nala te ti, ti le zuli Naawen ti Wenni, waai jigi ate ti a tom fu la, ate ku cheŋ nalimnyiini a te ti, dila ti le zuli Naawen ti Wenni.>>
7Daa pi ŋaaŋnyiŋ Naawen wanni yaa jam Jeremaya jigi. 8Wa yaa wi Karea nidoabinni Joyanan ale tugurik tɔŋdɔ kpaŋŋa meena ale jam bo le wa la a zaani nuru fiisa a ga paari nuru kpienta ate ba jam jigi yeŋ. 9Wa weeni ba ayen, <<Naawen, Izirali Wenni ate ni tom mi wa jigi ayen m pai ni juisimu a te wa la a weeni ayen, 10<Ni dan bo tɛŋka de po, m le yik ni zaani abe m kan dari ni lɔnsi, m le vuk ni abe m kan dari ni voori, diila kaasuŋku ate m pai basi ni zuk la a daani mu kama. 11Ni kan chali Babilon naawa yɔgsummoa, waai ate ni a chali yɔgyɔgla de nna. Ni kan chali wa yɔgsum. Naawen ale weeni. Mi a bo ale ni kama m be le vari ni wa nisa po a basi. 12M le sak jiirim ale ni ate wa sak jiirim ale ni a ta ni ŋmani ni tɛŋka.>
13<<Alege, nama dan weeni ayen, <Ti kan bo tɛŋka de po,>> an zuli Naawen ni Wenni, 14ni be dan weeni ayen, <Aaya, ti le cheŋ a ga bo Ejipiti, juijui ate ti kan nya kpaliŋŋa yaase ti wom damuniŋ peerika yaase kɔm a ta ti,> 15ni yaa be wom Naawen wanni, Juda baai ale tali la. Dii ate Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni a weeni la ale nna: <Ni dan pii nyiŋ ayen ni cheŋ Ejipiti ate ni cheŋ a ga kali dula, 16gebik kaai ate nama a chali yɔgsum la ale paari ni dula, ate kɔm buui ni a chali la ale va ni a jo Ejipiti, ate ni kpi dula. 17Chekki, baai meena ale a pii nyiŋ ayen ba cheŋ Ejipiti a ga kali dula la gebika ale kɔm ale nyiŋtuila ale ko ba, baai a kan vuugi yaase ba bɛ ale kaasuŋku ate mi a ta cheena ba zuk la.> 18Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, Izirali Wenni ale weeni diila ale nna: <Ase mi suipuurumu ale bo baai ale bo Jerusalem zuk diila, ka dila ate mi ale kpiiri m suipuurumu a basi baai ale a cheŋ Ejipiti la zuk. Ni nyaasim ale bie, nuruba ale nye ni a la abe ni yuenni ba a wi ase kikaasa la. Ni kan ŋman nya dela diipo diipo.>
19<<Juda baai ale tali la, Naawen a jam weeni ni ayen, <Ni kan cheŋ Ejipiti.> Ni seba kude a chak: Mi a kaam ni jinla 20ayen ni nye kaasi a jo ka biem ni le tom mi Naawen, ni Wenni jigi a weeni ayen, <Puusi a te Naawen ti Wenni a te ti abe fi weeni ti dii meena ate wa a weeni la ate ti nye.> 21Mi a weeni ni jinla kama, alege ni an diem zuli Naawen ni Wenni dii meena ate wa tom mi ayen m weeni ni la. 22Dila yɔgyɔgla de, ni seba kude a chak: Gebika ale kɔm ale nyiŋtuila ale ko ni juijui ate ni a yaali ayen ni cheŋ a ga kali la.>>

english_text:
The People Go to Egypt
1I told the people everything the Lord had told me. 2But Azariah, Johanan and some other arrogant men said to me, “You're lying! The Lord didn't tell you to say that we shouldn't go to Egypt. 3Baruch son of Neriah must have told you to say that. He wants the Babylonians to capture us, so they can take us away to Babylonia or even kill us.”
