7Dii ale pai saŋ la, wa ŋman ta mi cheŋ dabiaka tuoku nɔi ate mi nya vɔrup siaka nyiŋ. 8Wa yaa weeni ayen nye ate vɔrumu a zuak. Mi le nye la, mi yaa nya le ka tuok nɔi. 9Wa yaa weeni mi ayen, jo a nya wa gbenti sii ate nuruma a nye la. 10Ponni po mi yaa nya duŋ sii ale vuuri a cheŋ la ale duŋ daŋtisa ale bɔgta siaka nyiŋ ate Izirali a kaab la. 11Izirali niŋdeerɔba pisiyopɔi ale za dula ate Safan biika Jaazania maa boro. Ba wanyi meena yaa ta ŋan baai ate ba ju ŋan baai nyum ale masa la. Ate ba nyummu a sueri dɔkku meena.
12Naawen yaa weeni ayen, <<Saalɔ biiga, fi nya wa gbenti sii ate Izirali niŋdeerɔma suk a nye la? Ba diinaŋa a sueri ale ka bɔgta. Ate ba a weeni ayen mi kan nya ba, dii nyiŋla ba a poli ayen mi poom zɛri Izirali kama. 13Alege m le sak ni wari ate ku bie gaam dila.
14Wa ŋman ta mi cheŋ nɔi dii ale bo wiiluk geŋka la ate mi nya nipooba a kum a te bɔgluk ate ba a wi ayen Tammuz. 15Naawen yaa bek mi ayen, <<Saalɔ biiga, fi baga a siak ni pooma de ale a nye diila? Alege m le sak fu wa dii ale ŋmasi bie.>>
16Wa ŋman ta mi cheŋ jo Naawen Yenni dabiaka ponni po ate mi nya nidoaba pisiye ale banu za moata. Ba pai ka ba ŋaaŋsa a te Naawen. Penni a yaa tuk wenbinni ale a pusi la nyiŋ a koori.
17Wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Saalɔ biiga, Juda demma ale a nye diila a bie ka nna yegayega. Alege basi mɛ ate gaasa ale nyeka tuem waaŋ Izirali tɛŋka meena. Ku basi kama ate m sui a puuri nna yegayega. Ba lɛ mu kama a nye mu chivie. 18M suinni ale a puuri la, m le namsi ba. M kan sak jiirimmoa. Ba bi dan kum te mu m kan maari ba.>>

english_text:
The Lord Gives the Command To Punish Jerusalem
1After that, I heard the Lord shout, “Come to Jerusalem, you men chosen to destroy the city. And bring your weapons!”
2I saw six men come through the north gate of the temple, each one holding a deadly weapon. A seventh man dressed in a linen robe was with them, and he was carrying things to write with. The men went into the temple and stood by the bronze altar.
3The brightness of God's glory then left its place above the statues of the winged creatures inside the temple and moved to the entrance. The Lord said to the man in the linen robe, 4 “Walk through the city of Jerusalem and mark the forehead of anyone who is truly upset and sad about the terrible things that are being done here.”
5-6He turned to the other six men and said, “Follow him and put to death everyone who doesn't have a mark on their forehead. Show no mercy or pity! Kill men and women, parents and children. Begin here at my temple, but be sure not to harm those who are marked.”
The men immediately killed the leaders who were standing there.
7Then the Lord said, “Pollute the temple by piling the dead bodies in the courtyards. Now get busy!” They left and started killing the people of Jerusalem.
8I was then alone, so I bowed down and cried out to the Lord, “Why are you doing this? Are you so angry with the people of Jerusalem that everyone must die?”
9The Lord answered, “The people of Israel and Judah have done horrible things. Their country is filled with murderers, and Jerusalem itself is filled with violence. They think that I have deserted them, and that I can't see what they are doing. 10And so I will not have pity on them or forgive them. They will be punished for what they have done.”
11Just then, the man in the linen robe returned and said, “I have done what you commanded.”
translation_text:
1Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ, mi yaa wom le Naawen nɔi ayen, <<Nuru baai ate m lueri ayen ba kaasi tɛŋka la ni jam Jerusalem. Ni ta ni kpaliŋ ŋantaŋa jam.>> 2Mi nya nidoaba bayuebi a va Naawen Yenni nɔi dii ale bo wiiluk geŋ la a jo. Waai meena ta ka kpaliŋ ŋa pagrik wa nisa po. Nuru ale saari bayopɔi a jo garuk ate ku a nyaksi a bo ale ba a ta ŋanta ayen wa ŋmarisi. Nuruma yaa jo Wen Yenni po a zaani kuŋkuŋku tɛŋ.
3Izirali Wen zulaŋa ale wa nalimu ale nyaksika yaa basi javukku ale ta kiŋkaŋŋa ate ba mɛ zaani Wen Yenni po la ale torisi cheŋ nansuiŋka jigini. Naawen yaa weeni waai garukku ale a nyaksi la ayen, 4<<Cheŋ Jerusalem tɛŋka po, baai meena ate waba tii a nye dela a sum a daani ba la, daani ba deeŋa nyiŋ.>> 5-6Wa yaa cheem mbala bayuebiwa jigi a weeni ba ayen, <<Ni va wa a ga ko baai meena ale kan ta daanika ba deeŋa nyiŋla. Ni kan sak jiirimmoa. Ni bi kan ŋman te ba. Ni ko nidoaba ale nipooba, nyam ale ba bisa.>> Ni piilim dela m Yenni tɛŋ abe nuruma deri ko niŋdeerɔma ale za dula la.
7Wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Pai kpiema a vi chaab dueni yenni dabaasaŋa po ate di daŋm. Ni te ni nina muni.>> Ba yaa basi dula ale piilim a ko Jerusalem demma. 8Mi jam ka m dek m nyiini, mi yaa koori tɛŋ a kaari a weeni, <<Nyɔnɔ Naawen yaa! Ka boa ate fi a nye naa? Ka fi sui ale a puuri nna yegayega ale Jerusalem demma ate fi a yaali ayen waai meena kpi?>>
9Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Izirali ale Juda demma a tom ka wabaata nna yegayega. Nuru koorisa ale sueri ba tɛŋka. Jerusalem dek a sueri ale gaasa. Ba a poli ayen, <Naawen zɛri ba kama.> Ba a poli ayen, <Naawen kan nya ba ale a nye diila.> 10Dila nyiŋ m kan ŋman te ba m be kan vɔŋ te ba. M le namsi ba ba le nye diila nyiŋ.>>
11Nuru waai ale jo garuk kuui ale a nyaksi la yaa ŋman jam weeni ayen, m nye fi le weeni ayen, <<M nye diila kama.>>

english_text:
The Lord's Glory Leaves the Temple
1 I saw the dome that was above the four winged creatures, and on it was the sapphire throne. 2 The Lord said to the man in the linen robe, “Walk among the four wheels beside the creatures and pick up as many hot coals as you can carry. Then scatter them over the city of Jerusalem.” I watched him as he followed the Lord's instructions.
3The winged creatures were standing south of the temple when the man walked among them. A cloud filled the inner courtyard, 4and the brightness of the Lord's glory moved from above the creatures and stopped at the entrance of the temple. The entire temple was filled with his glory, and the courtyard was dazzling bright. 5The sound of the creatures' wings was as loud as the voice of God All-Powerful and could even be heard in the outer courtyard.
6The man in the robe was now standing beside a wheel. 7One of the four creatures reached its hand into the fire among them and gave him some of the hot coals. The man took the coals and left.
8I noticed again that each of the four winged creatures had what looked like human hands under their wings, 9 and I saw the four wheels near the creatures. These wheels were shining like chrysolite. 10Each wheel was exactly the same and had a second wheel that cut through the middle of it, 11so that they could move in any direction without turning. The wheels moved together whenever the creatures moved. 12 I also noticed that the wheels and the creatures' bodies, including their backs, their hands, and their wings, were covered with eyes. 13And I heard a voice calling these “the wheels that spin.”
14 Each of the winged creatures had four faces: the face of a bull, the face of a human, the face of a lion, and the face of an eagle. 15-17These were the same creatures I had seen near the Chebar River. They controlled when and where the wheels moved—the wheels went wherever the creatures went and stopped whenever they stopped. Even when the creatures flew in the air, the wheels stayed beside them.
18Then I watched the brightness of the Lord's glory move from the entrance of the temple and stop above the winged creatures. 19They spread their wings and flew into the air with the wheels at their side. They stopped at the east gate of the temple, and the Lord's glory was above them.
20I knew for sure that these were the same creatures I had seen beneath the Lord's glory near the Chebar River. 21-22They had four wings with hands beneath them, and they had the same four faces as those near the River. Each creature moved straight ahead without turning.

1Mi yaa nya gigiluk ale bo ŋan baai ale ta kiŋkaŋŋa ŋanaansiwa la zuk. Dula bi ka naamu kalika jigini a nyaksi. 2Naawen yaa weeni waai ale jo garuk kuui ale a nyaksi la ayen, <<Cheŋ va wiilima ale za ŋan baai ale ta kiŋkaŋŋa la suŋsuŋ a ga pai bolim kaala ŋaai ate wa baga a ji la. Abe fi yaa pai yarinti Jerusalem tɛŋka meena.>> Ate mi ya kpesi a nya wa le va wiilima po.>> 3Ŋan baai ale ta kiŋkaŋŋa la a za ka Wen yenni yeseok geŋka alege ate nuruwa a cheŋ ba suŋsuŋ. Chiŋmari yaa lik ponni po dabiaka ate 4Naawen zulaŋa ale wa nalimu nyaksika yaa va ŋan baai ale ta kiŋkaŋŋa la zuk a ga wari nansuiŋku nɔi. Naawen zulaŋa a kasim lik yenni meena ate dabiaka po mɛ a nyaksi. 5Ŋantaŋa kiŋkaŋŋa nuemka a nye ase ka Wen Dii Ale A Niak La lueluk la ate fi dan za peelim dabiaka po fi wom.
6Wa yaa weeni nuru waai ale jo garuk kuui ale a nyaksi la ayen, <<Pai bolim a nyini wiilima po, a nyini ŋanvutaŋa po, ate wa yaa ga za wiilima gauŋ. 7Baai ale ta kiŋkaŋŋa la wanyi yaa laari nisa pai kaala bolim po a te wa. Nuruwa yaa tuesi kaalaŋa a cheŋ. 8Mi ŋman nya ale ŋan baai banaansiwa ale ta kiŋkaŋŋa la wanyi meena ta ka ŋanta nna ase nurubiik nisima la ba kiŋkaŋŋa po. 9Mi yaa nya wiiliba banaansiwa a moata ŋan baai ale ta kiŋkaŋŋa la. Wiilima de kasim a nyaksi kama ase tintain salima la. 10Wiili meena a neensi ka ku choa ale ŋman ta wiili ku choa ate ku bari bo ku suŋsuŋ. 11Ate ba baga a va jigi meena ale kan cheemu. Ŋan baai ale ta kiŋkaŋŋa la a daa cheŋ, wiilima mɛ a va ka chaab a cheŋ. 12Mi ŋman nya ayen wiilima ale ŋan baai ale ta kiŋkaŋŋa la nyiŋsaŋa ale ba ŋaaŋsaŋa ale ba nisimaŋa ale ba kiŋkaŋŋa ka nina nyiini. 13Mi yaa wom lueluk a wi ayen, wiili baai ale a gilim la. 14Ŋan baai ale ta kiŋkaŋŋa la wanyi meena a ta ka nimbidaasa sinaansi. Wanyi nina a nye ase lalik la, wanyi mɛ nina a nye ase nurubiik la, wanyi nina a nye ase gbeŋli la, nwala ninaŋa a nye ase jiiruk la.
15Ŋan baai ale ta kiŋkaŋŋa la ka baai ate mi liŋ nya Chebar Benni nɔi la. 16Wiilima a cheŋ ka juijui meena ate ŋantaŋa a cheŋ la, ale a zaani juijui ate ŋantaŋa a zaani la. 17Ŋantaŋa a dan poom yiti wiilima sali va ba kama, dii nyiŋla ŋantaŋa chiika a bo ale ba kama.
18Mi yaa nya ale Naawen zulaŋa ale wa nyaksika nyini nansuiŋku jigini a ga bo ŋan baai ale ta kiŋkaŋŋa la zuk. 19Ba yaa lak ba kiŋkaŋŋa a yiti wen ate wiilima mɛ sali va. Ba yaa ga zaani Naawen yenni kori geŋ. Ate Izirali Wen zulaŋa ale nalimu a bo ba zuk.
20Ate mi yaa seba a chak ayen ŋan baai dek ate mi nya Chebar Benni nɔi ate Izirali Wenni zulaŋa a bo ba zuk la ale la. 21Ba ta ka kiŋkaŋŋa ŋanaansi ate nisima a bo ŋa tɛŋ. 22Wanyi meena a ta nimbidaasa sinaansi ase baai ale jam moata Chebar Benni la. Ba wanyi meena a cheŋ ka yorr ale kan cheemu.

english_text:
Ezekiel Condemns Jerusalem's Wicked Leaders
1The Lord's Spirit lifted me up and took me to the east gate of the temple, where I saw 25 men, including the two leaders, Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah. 2The Lord said, “Ezekiel, son of man, these men are making evil plans and giving dangerous advice to the people of Jerusalem. 3They say things like, ‘Let's build more houses. This city is like a cooking pot over a fire, and we are the meat, but at least the pot keeps us from being burned in the fire.’ 4So, Ezekiel, condemn them!”
5The Lord's Spirit took control of me and told me to tell these leaders:
I, the Lord God, know what you leaders are saying. 6You have murdered so many people that the city is filled with dead bodies! 7This city is indeed a cooking pot, but the bodies of those you killed are the meat. And so I will force you to leave Jerusalem, 8and I'll send armies to attack you, just as you fear. 9Then you will be captured and punished by foreign enemies. 10You will be killed in your own country, but not before you realize that I, the Lord, have done these things.
11You leaders claim to be meat in a cooking pot, but you won't be protected by this city. No, you will die at the border of Israel. 12You will realize that while you were following the laws of nearby nations, you were disobeying my laws and teachings. And I am the Lord!
13Before I finished speaking, Pelatiah dropped dead. I bowed down and cried out, “Please, Lord God, don't kill everyone left in Israel.”
A Promise of Hope
14The Lord replied:
15Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in Jerusalem claim that you and the other Israelites who were taken to Babylonia are too far away to worship me. They also claim that the land of Israel now belongs only to them. 16But here is what I want you to tell the Israelites in Babylonia:
It's true that I, the Lord God, have forced you out of your own country and made you live among foreign nations. But for now, I will be with you wherever you are, so that you can worship me. 17And someday, I will gather you from the nations where you are scattered and let you live in Israel again. 18When that happens, I want you to clear the land of all those idols I hate so much. 19 Then I will take away your stubbornness and make you eager to be completely faithful to me. You will want to obey me 20and all my laws and teachings. You will be my people, and I will be your God. 21But those who worship idols will be punished and get what they deserve. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
The Lord's Glory Leaves Jerusalem
22 After the Lord had finished speaking, the winged creatures spread their wings and flew into the air, and the wheels were beside them. The brightness of the Lord's glory above them 23left Jerusalem and stopped at a hill east of the city.
24Then in my vision, the Lord's Spirit lifted me up and carried me back to the other exiles in Babylonia. The vision faded away, 25and I told them everything the Lord had shown me.
translation_text:
1Wen Chiika yaa zak mi wen a ta mi jam Naawen Yenni niŋ geŋ nɔnni ale tuk kori la. Mi yaa nya nidoaba pisiye ale banu tuoku ale lak juijui la. Ba po Azzur nidoabinni Jaazania ale Benaya nidoabinni Pelatia ale jam chim nuruma niŋdeerɔba. 2Wen Chiika yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Saalɔ biiga, nuruma de ale a zɔk biem wie ale a te sinsak baata Jerusalem tɛŋka po. 3Ba a weeni kama ayen, <Ku paari ka diipo ate ku magsi ti a se yie. Tɛŋka de a nye ase ka samɔniŋ ate ba ta a dik la, ate tama dek a nye ase lam maŋsa la.> 4Dila nyiŋ mooli a te ba, mooli, Saalɔ biiga.>>
5Naawen Chiika yaa ŋman jo mi a weeni mi ayen weeni ba ayen, <<Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna; Nama Izirali demma ale weeni wieŋa de m be sebi ni ale a poli diila kama. 6Ni ko ka nuruba yega tɛŋka po ate kpieba sueri suitaŋa niŋ meena. 7Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Nuru baai ate ni ko a basi tɛŋka suŋsuŋ la a nye ase ka lam maŋsa la ate tɛŋka a nye ase samɔniŋ ate ba pai dik la. Alege m le fɛ ate ni nyini tɛŋka po. 8Ni a chali gebik kama, alege m le ta gebik a jam ni po. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.
9<<Mi le fɛ ate ni nyini tɛŋka po nyini abe m pai ni te nicham ate ba namsi ni. 10Ba le ko ni ale ka gebik. M le namsi ni Izirali tɛŋka banni jigini ate ni seba ayen ka Mi ale Naawen. 11Tɛŋka de kan chim ni samɔniŋ kaai le a digi. Nama be kan chim lam maŋsa ka po. M le namsi ni Izirali tɛŋka banni jigini. 12Ate ni yaa seba ayen ka Mi ale Naawen. Ni an va mi ŋmarisika ni boka po, ni be an va m buusaŋa. Ni a nye a magsi chaab ale ka tɛŋ sii ale gilim ni la buusaŋa.>>
13Mi ale mooli la Benaya biika Pelatia a deri kpi. Mi yaa koori tɛŋ a kaari ate ku jueli ayen, <<Aaya, Nyɔnɔ Naawen yaa! Fi a yaali fi ko Izirali demma baai ale tali vua la ka meena?>>
14Naawen yaa biisi wa wanni te mi ayen, 15<<Saalɔ biiga, nuru baai ale diem bo Jerusalem la a biisi fidek buuni ale Izirali demma baai ale ka ligrɔba ale fu la a weeni ayen, <Ba yalima ale Naawen kama. Ba pai tɛŋka de a te ti kama ase nitalim la.> 16Dila la, weeni ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Mi ta nuruma cheŋ ka niŋ a basi ate ba waaŋ tɛŋsaŋa po. Alege ku an beni ya ate m ŋman cheŋ m dek yenni tɛŋ sii ate ba cheŋ la po.> 17Dila weeni ba ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Mi le tigsi ta nyini tɛŋsaŋa po a ta ba jam jigi yeŋ a ya pai Izirali tɛŋka a ŋman te ni.> 18Ba dan jam tɛŋka de po ba le yeeri bɔgluk tii ale ŋan mɛɛnta meena ate m kisi la. 19M le basi ate ba ta yaali kaai ale kaa basi ate ba a zuli mu la abe m pai popoli paala a te ba. Mi ale yeeri tuikpari ba po abe m basi ate ba ta zula. 20Ate ba va m ŋmarisika a boro abe ba a zuli m buusaŋa abe ba ta ŋa. Ba le chim m nuruba ate mi mɛ a chim ba Wen. 21Alege baai ale a yaali ayen ba va bɔgluk baataŋa ale bɔgluk tii tin kisi la, m le tuni ba ba biemu nyiŋ. Mi Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.>>
22Ate ŋanvutaŋa a zak ba kiŋkaŋŋa ale wiilima ale bo ba gauŋ la, ate Izirali Wenni zulaŋa a yaa bo ba zuk. 23Naawen zulaŋa yaa nyini Jerusalem a jueli wari guuku ale bo tɛŋka kori geŋ la zuk. 24Wen Chiika yaa zak mi a ta mi jam nuru baai ate ba ta nyini Juda a jam Kaldiya la jigi. Kude ale nye la ka Wen Chiika ale pai sak mu. Mi ale nya diila yaa kpeglim. 25Mi yaa weeni baai meena ale nyini Juda la Naawen ale pai dii meena a sak mu la.

english_text:
Ezekiel Acts Out Israel's Captivity
1The Lord said:
2 Ezekiel, son of man, you are living among rebellious people. They have eyes, but refuse to see; they have ears, but refuse to listen. 3So before it gets dark, here is what I want you to do. Pack a few things as though you were going to be taken away as a prisoner. Then go outside where everyone can see you and walk around from place to place. Maybe as they watch, they will realize what rebels they are. 4After you have done this, return to your house.
Later that evening leave your house as if you were going into exile. 5Dig through the wall of your house and crawl out, carrying the bag with you. Make sure everyone is watching. 6Lift the bag to your shoulders, and with your face covered, take it into the darkness, so that you cannot see the land you are leaving. All this will be a warning for the people of Israel.
7I did everything the Lord had said. I packed a few things. Then as the sun was going down, and while everyone was watching, I dug a hole through one of the walls of my house. I pulled out my bag, then lifted it to my shoulders and left in the darkness.
8The next morning, the Lord 9reminded me that those rebellious people didn't even ask what I was doing. 10So he sent me back to tell them:
The Lord God has a message for the leader of Jerusalem and everyone living there!
11I have done these things to show them what will happen when they are taken away as prisoners.
12The leader of Jerusalem will lift his own bag to his shoulders at sunset and leave through a hole that the others have dug in the wall of his house. He will cover his face, so he can't see the land he is leaving. 13 The Lord will spread out a net and trap him as he leaves Jerusalem. He will then be led away to the city of Babylon, but will never see that place, even though he will die there. 14His own officials and troops will scatter in every direction, and the Lord will track them down and put them to death.
15The Lord will force the rest of the people in Jerusalem to live in foreign nations, where they will realize that he has done all these things. 16Some of them will survive the war, the starvation, and the deadly diseases. That way, they will be able to tell foreigners how disgusting their sins were, and that it was the Lord who punished them in this way.
A Sign of Fear
17The Lord said:
18Ezekiel, son of man, shake with fear when you eat, and tremble when you drink. 19Tell the people of Israel that I, the Lord, say that someday everyone in Jerusalem will shake when they eat and tremble when they drink. Their country will be destroyed and left empty, because they have been cruel and violent. 20Every town will lie in ruins, and the land will be a barren desert. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
The Words of the Lord Will Come True
21The Lord said:
22Ezekiel, son of man, you've heard people in Israel use the saying, “Time passes, and prophets are proved wrong.” 23Now tell the people that I, the Lord, am going to prove that saying wrong. No one will ever be able to use it again in Israel, because very soon everything I have said will come true! 24The people will hear no more useless warnings and false messages. 25I will give them my message, and what I say will certainly happen. Warn those rebels that the time has come for them to be punished. I, the Lord, make this promise.
26-27Ezekiel, the people of Israel are also saying that your visions and messages are only about things in the future. 28So tell them that my words will soon come true, just as I have warned. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
1Naawen a ŋman biisi wa wanni te mi a weeni ayen, 2<<Saalɔ biiga, fi bo ale ka nuru baai ale kaa zuli mi la. Ba ta nina kama alege kan nya a ta tue alege kan wom, dii nyiŋla ba ka nuru baai ale zɛri mi zula teka. 3Dila nyiŋ, saalɔ biiga, tigsi fi ŋantaŋa ase ba le yik fu ta cheŋ ka jigi la, a yaa cheŋ ase ba yik fu kama la kantueŋ ate nuruba a nya. Nyini fi jigini a cheŋ jigi yoŋ ate nuruma a nya. Ate ba ale zɛri ayen ba kan zuli mi la, da dii dai ba le miŋ ku kiri. 4Ku dan ka kantueŋ ate nuruma a nya, yeeri ŋan baai ate fi tigsi la ase ba yik fu la. Junɔi, nuruma ale a nya la basi fi jigini ase nuruba ate ba yik ba ta nyini ba tɛŋ a cheŋ la. 5Nuruma ale diem a nya fu la, keri vɔrup siaka nyiŋ a ta fi ŋantaŋa va du nyini. 6Zak ba a vi ŋmankpala ate nuruma a nya, a yaa ji ba ta nyini legini po. Lik fi ninaŋa ate fi kaa nya tɛŋka, dii nyiŋla m basi kama ayen fi nye dila a sak Izirali demma.>>
7Mi yaa nye wieŋa de a va dii ate wa weeni la. Kantueŋka mi yaa ji ŋantaŋa ate m tigsi la ase ba yik mu ta a cheŋ la. Junɔinni mi yaa keri vɔrumu siaka nyiŋ ale m nisaŋa. A ta m ŋantaŋa nyini legini po a zak vi ŋmankpala ate nuruma a nya.
8Saluiku ate Naawen biisi wa wanni te mi ayen, 9<<Saalɔ biiga, Izirali dem baai ale zɛri mi zuli ka la an bek ayen, <Ka boa ti fi a nye>? 10Weeni ba ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Wanni de ka naawa ale bo Jerusalem la ale Izirali nuruma ale bo dula la wari.> 11Weeni ba ayen, <Mi a sak ba ka wari.> Wie ŋaai dek ate m nye la, m le nye Jerusalem nuruma ka dila dek. Ba le yik ba ta nyini ba tɛŋka a cheŋ jigi yoŋ. 12Naawa ale pai wa ŋantaŋa a vi ŋmankpala a nyini legini po a cheŋ. Nuruma ale keri vɔrup siaka po a ta wa nyini. Wa le lik wa ninaŋa ate wa kaa nya tɛŋka. 13Alege m le yuk m ŋmiaka a vi wa zuk a yik wa. M yaa le ta wa jam Babilon, Kaldiya demma tɛŋka. Wa kan nya tɛŋ kala, alege wa za wa kpi ka dula. 14Baai meena ale gilim naawa la, wa maarima ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma meena, m le basi ate ba waaŋ jigi meena a yaa ko ba ale m gebika. 15M dan basi ate ba waaŋ tɛŋsaŋa meena po ba le seba ayen ka Mi ale Naawen. 16Alege m le vari ba maga a basi, m kan ko ba ale gebika, yaase m basi ate kɔm ko ba, yaase m basi ate nyiŋtuila a ko ba. Ba yaa le weeni sak tɛŋ sii meena ba cheŋ la gaasa wie ŋaai meena ba nye la. Ate ba yaa seba ayen ka Mi ale Naawen.
17Naawen a ŋman biisi wa wanni a te mi ayen, 18<<Saalɔ biiga, fi daa dɛ ŋandiinta basi ate fi nyiŋka a gɔk, fi be daa nyu nyiam basi ate fi nyiŋka a gɔk ale yɔgsum. 19Abe fi yaa weeni tɛŋka demma ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni dii a magsi chaab ale nuru baai ale bo Jerusalem, Izirali tɛŋka po la. Ba le dɛ ŋandiinta ale yɔgsum abe ba nyu nyiam ale chichama, dii nyiŋla ba tɛŋka kan ŋman ta jaaboa nuruma gaasaŋa ale nyeka tuemu nyiŋ. 20Tɛŋ sii ate nuruba a boro la ale kaasi doa. Tɛŋka ale chim tɛŋ koruk. Ate ni seba ayen ka Mi ale Naawen.> >>
21Naawen a biisi wa wanni te mi a weeni ayen, 22<<Saalɔ biiga, ka boan biik ate ni ta Izirali tɛŋka po nna: <Daaŋa jam a taam ka di alege dii ate Naawen pai sak la kan nye jaaboa>? 23Dila nyiŋ weeni ba ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, M le te ba basi nna wa weeni ka. Waai be kan bo Izirali a ŋman weeni wanni de.> Alege weeni ba ayen, <Ku moata ate dii meena m pai sak la a chim wensie. 24Venta wie nyaasim ale bi sii ale a peenti nuruba sui Izirali tɛŋka po la a kan boro. 25Alege Mi Naawen ale biisi. Mi ale a weeni diila ale nye ku kan beni. Ni zɛri mi zula teka kama ale ni daaŋa po m le biisi abe m nye. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.> >>
26Naawen biisi wa wanni te mi a weeni ayen, 27<<Saalɔ biiga, Izirali demma weeni kama ayen, <Ezekiel ale nya diila ka chum po wie nyiini. Wa a biisi ka chum po wie.> 28Dila be weeni ba ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Wa wieŋa ŋa ŋaai mɛ la kan beni. M le weeni diila m le nye. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.> >>

english_text:
Lying Prophets
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the prophets of Israel who say they speak in my name, but who preach messages that come from their own imagination. Tell them it's time to hear my message.
3I, the Lord God, say those lying prophets are doomed! They don't see visions—they make up their own messages! 4Israel's prophets are no better than jackals that hunt for food among the ruins of a city. 5They don't warn the people about coming trouble or tell them how dangerous it is to sin against me. 6Those prophets lie by claiming they speak for me, but I have not even chosen them to be my prophets. And they still think their words will come true. 7They say they're preaching my messages, but they are full of lies—I did not speak to them!
8So I am going to punish those lying prophets for deceiving the people of Israel with false messages. 9I will turn against them and no longer let them belong to my people. They will not be allowed to call themselves Israelites or even to set foot in Israel. Then they will realize that I am the Lord God.
10 Those prophets refuse to be honest. They tell my people there will be peace, even though there's no peace to be found. They are like workers who think they can fix a shaky wall by covering it with paint. 11But when I send rainstorms, hailstones, and strong winds, the wall will surely collapse. 12People will then ask the workers why the paint didn't hold it up.
13That wall is the city of Jerusalem. And I, the Lord God, am so angry that I will send strong winds, rainstorms, and hailstones to destroy it. 14The lying prophets have tried to cover up the evil in Jerusalem, but I will tear down the city, all the way to its foundations. And when it collapses, those prophets will be killed, and everyone will know that I have done these things.
15The city of Jerusalem and its lying prophets will feel my fierce anger. Then I will announce that the city has fallen and that the lying prophets are dead, 16because they promised my people peace, when there was no peace. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
Women Who Wear Magic Charms
The Lord said:
17Ezekiel, son of man, now condemn the women of Israel who preach messages that come from their own imagination. 18Tell them they're doomed! They wear magic charms on their wrists and scarves on their heads, then trick others into believing they can predict the future. They won't get away with telling those lies. 19They charge my people a few handfuls of barley and a couple pieces of bread, and then give messages that are insulting to me. They use lies to sentence the innocent to death and to help the guilty go free. And my people believe them!
20I hate the magic charms they use to trick people into believing their lies. I will rip those charms from their wrists and set free the people they have trapped like birds. 21I will tear the scarves from their heads and rescue my people from their power once and for all. Then they will know that I am the Lord God.
22They do things I would never do. They lie to good people and encourage them to do wrong, and they convince the wicked to ruin their own lives by not turning from sin. 23I will no longer let these women give false messages and use magic, and I will free my people from their control. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_text:
1Naawen a ŋman biisi wa wanni a te mi a weeni ayen, 2<<Saalɔ biiga, mooli a kaam Izirali biisiteerɔma. Weeni baai ale poli a weeni badek wie la ayen ba wom Naawen wanni. 3Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Ku le bie te biisiteerɔ bettaŋa ale a va badek popola alege an nya wari mi jigi la. 4Izirali demma, ni biisiteerɔma a nye ase ka gɔi baasa ale a gisi ŋanta ayen si ko abe si dɛ yie luema po la. 5Izirali a nye ase ka yeri ale lo kaasi diila, alege ni an ga tebi kab tii ale wie lo la yaase ni tebi saasaŋa. Dila la Izirali ale nye ka sɛ a tu chaab ale dachaasaŋa kpaliŋka po Naawen danni? 6Ni biisiteerɔma a nya ka venta wie ale a biisi venta mɛ. Ba a weeni kama ayen, <<Naawen wari ale nna,>> alege Naawen an poom tom ba. Alege ba a poli ayen ba le weeni diila ale chim wensie. 7Ni nyiem weeni kama ayen, <<Naawen wari ale nna,>> alege ka venta wie ni nya. Ni wieŋa ka venta, dii nyiŋla mi an biisi wari ya.
8<< <Dila la Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, dii nyiŋla nama biisiteerɔma biisi ka venta wie ale nya wie ŋaai ale kaa chim wensie. Mi ta ka chaab ale ni. Mi Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni. 9Mi ale namsi biisiteerɔ baai ale a nya venta wie ale a velim wie la. Ba kan jigi mi nuruma po. Ba yue kan maa ŋmarisi bo Izirali demma wieŋa po, ba be kan jo Izirali tɛŋka. Dila ni le seba ayen ka Mi ale Nyɔnɔwa Naawen la. 10Dii ate mi a nye dila la ba te ti m nuruma a cheŋ a bɛ ale a weeni ayen, <<Suiyɔgni a boro.>> alege suiyɔgni a ka. Nuruma a dan se parik kaai ale kan pagra biisiteerɔma a sa siaka ale peeluk ase parik pagrik la. 11Dila nyiŋ weeni baai ale pai peeluk a sa parik kaai ale kan pagra la ayen, ŋmoruk ale ni yega ate viok ale tana a lo ate va pagrik a wɛ siaka. 12Siaka a dan lo nuruba ale bek fu ayen, <<Peelukku ate fi pai sa siaka la a bo be?>>
13<< <Dila la Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, M le wɛ siaka ale va pagrik. M suinni ale a puuri la nyiŋ m le basi ate ŋmoruk a ni yega abe tintain tuila a kaasi parika. 14M le kabri parik kaai ate ni nye ka peelukku la. Ka le paari tɛŋ ate nuruba nya ka nyubini. Parisaŋa a dan lo, nama dek ale kpi si kiri la. Ate ni seba ayen ka Mi ale Naawen. 15M sui le puuri ale parika ale baai ale pai peelukku a sa ka la. Abe m weeni ni ayen, parika a cheŋ ale baai ale pai peelukku a sa ka la. 16Izirali biisiteerɔma ale mooli a te Jerusalem la ale baai ale nya ayen suiyɔgni a bo tɛŋka po alege suiyɔgni a ka la ale taam meena. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.>> >
17<<Yɔgyɔgla de, Saalɔ biiga nya nipooma ale bo nuruma po la a poli badek wieŋa a weeni la. Biisi te ba. 18Weeni ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Ku le bie a te nipok baai ale a baali ŋan kperisa a su ba nisa ale a nye ŋan nyaara a pai vi ba zuima ayen ba bari yik nuruba la. Ni kaasi mi nuruma nyuvooŋa kama ale ayen ni vari nidek nyuvooŋa. 19<Barli> nisa nɔi ale boroborok maga nyiŋ ate ni an zuli mi m nuruma suŋsuŋŋa. Ni velim te mi nuru baai ale a wom venta la. Ni ko baai ale kan magsi ba kpi ale basi baai ale magsi ba kpi la.
20<< <Dila la Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, wa kan yaali kperisa wie ŋaai ate ba nye a bari a yik nuruba ase nuinsa la. Ayen wa le gebi kperisa ŋantaŋa ba nisaŋa po a vari baai ate ba bari yik ase nuinsa la a basi. 21M le cheeri ba ŋan nyaaraŋa abe m vari m nuruma ni nisa po. Ni kan ŋman bari yik ba ale ni pagrimu. Ate ni seba ayen ka Mi ale Naawen. 22Ba a nye ka wie ate mi a kan nye ŋa. Ba velim kama a te nuru maŋsa ale a te ba nyiŋbiiri ate ba nye a kaasi, ale a paasi wabaata nyama ate ba kasim a nye biem a kaasi ba nyuvooŋa. 23Mi kan basi ate ba ŋman nya venta wie abe ba porisi, ate m vari m nuruma ba nisa po a basi. Ate ba seba ayen, Mi Naawen ale nye wieŋa de.> >>

english_text:
Ezekiel Encourages the People To Turn Back to the Lord
1One day, some of Israel's leaders came to me and asked for a message from the Lord. 2While they were there, the Lord said:
3Ezekiel, son of man, these men have started worshiping idols, though they know it will cause them to sin even more. So I refuse to give them a message!
4Tell the people of Israel that if they sin by worshiping idols and then go to a prophet to find out what I say, I will give them the answer their sins deserve. 5When they hear my message, maybe they will see that they need to turn back to me and stop worshiping those idols.
6Now, Ezekiel, tell everyone in Israel:
I am the Lord God. Stop worshiping those idols I hate so much and come back to me.
7Suppose one of you Israelites or a foreigner living in Israel rejects me and starts worshiping idols. If you then go to a prophet to find out what I say, I will answer 8by turning against you. I will make you a warning to anyone who might think of doing the same thing, and you will no longer belong to my people. Then you will know that I am the Lord and that you have sinned against me.
9If a prophet gives a false message, I am the one who caused that prophet to lie. But I will still reject him and cut him off from my people, 10and anyone who goes to that prophet for a message will be punished in the same way. 11I will do this, so that you will come back to me and stop destroying yourselves with these disgusting sins. So turn back to me! Then I will be your God, and you will be my people. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
Judgment on a Sinful Nation
12The Lord God said:
13Ezekiel, son of man, suppose an entire nation sins against me, and I punish it by destroying the crops and letting its people and livestock starve to death. 14 Even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were living in that nation, their faithfulness would not save anyone but themselves.
15Or suppose I punish a nation by sending wild animals to eat people and scare away every passerby, so that the land becomes a barren desert. 16As surely as I live, I promise that even if these three men lived in that nation, their own children would not be spared. The three men would live, but the land would be an empty desert.
17Or suppose I send an enemy to attack a sinful nation and kill its people and livestock. 18If these three men were in that nation when I punished it, not even their children would be spared. Only the three men would live.
19And suppose I am so angry that I send a deadly disease to wipe out the people and livestock of a sinful nation. 20Again, even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were living there, I, the Lord, promise that the children of these faithful men would also die. Only the three of them would be spared.
21 I am the Lord God, and I promise to punish Jerusalem severely. I will send war, starvation, wild animals, and deadly disease to slaughter its people and livestock. 22And those who survive will be taken from their country and led here to Babylonia. Ezekiel, when you see how sinful they are, you will know why I did all these things to Jerusalem. 23You will be convinced that I, the Lord God, was right in doing what I did.
translation_text:
1Izirali niŋdeerɔ kpagsaŋa gela yaa jam kali mi niŋ. 2Naawen yaa biisi ale mi a weeni ayen, 3<<Saalɔ biiga, nuruma de a yaali ayen ba kaab ka bɔgta. Ba ta ka biem wie ŋaai ale nye ate nuruba a tom biem la. M be te ba suik ate ba bek maarika? 4Dila nyiŋ, biisi weeni ba ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Izirali nuruma baai ale a yaali ba kaab bɔgta abe ba ta biem wie ŋaai ale nye ate nuruba a nye biem alege a jam biisiteerɔwa jigi la, Mi, Naawen dek ale tulisi ba ba bɔgtaŋa kaabka nyiŋ. 5Ate m ŋman nya m nuruma Izirali demma, baai ale basi mu ba bɔgtaŋa nyiŋla.>
6<<Dila nyiŋ weeni Izirali demma ayen, <Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale biisi diila ale nna, Ni tagri ni nyeka ale ni suiniimaŋa abe ni basi bɔgta kaabka. Ni basi wie ŋaai meena ate mi kisi la nyeka.
7<< <Izirali demma baai ale nichamma baai ale bo Izirali tɛŋka po la a daa yaali ba poori badek mi jigi a kaab bɔgta abe ba ta, nye kaai ale a basi ate nuruba a nye biem la. Ba yaa dan jam biisiteerɔwa jigi ayen ba bek mu bega, Mi Naawen ale tulisi ba m dek. 8M le zɛri ba, M le yeeri ba m nuruma po ate ba a nya ba. Dila ni le seba ayen Mi ale Naawen.
9<< <Alege, ba dan paasi biisiteerɔwa ate wa biisi wari ka mi Naawen ale paasi wa ate wa biisi. Dila mi yaa le pai m pagrimu a kaasi wa Izirali demma suŋsuŋ. 10Biisiteerɔwa ale nye bɛ kama ase waai ale bek a yaali maarika la. Ba nɔi bayewa ale nam ba biemu nyiŋ. 11Ate Izirali tɛŋka kan ŋman basi mi yaase ba daŋ badek ale ba wabaataŋa. Ba le chim m nuruba ate mi mɛ a chim ba Wen. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.> >>
12Naawen yaa biisi ale mi a weeni ayen, 13<<Saalɔ biiga, tɛŋ kaai nuruba a dan tom kaasi mi a kan zuli mi, m le tu chaab ale ba ale pagrim. M le kaasi ŋandiintaŋa abe m basi ate kɔm jam ate nuruba ale duŋsa meena a kpi. 14Nuruma de batawa Nowa ale Daniel ale Job a dan poom bo tɛŋ kala po ba tuim maŋsaŋa ale vari ka badek ba nyiini a basi. Nyɔnɔwa Naawen la ale weeni.

Ate nuru a kan va ka po a taamu duŋsaŋa nyiŋ. 16Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale a weeni ayen, Mi le ka waai ale vua la, Nowa ale Daniel ale Job a dan poom bo tɛŋka po ba kan baga a vari badek bisa ale ba lieba a basi, ba le vari ka badek a basi. Ba le vari ka badek a basi alege tɛŋ kala ale doa koruk.
17<<Yaase m ta kpaliŋ jam tɛŋka po. Da dii dai m le weeni ayen, <Kpaliŋ siti tɛŋka po,> a ko nuruma ale duŋsaŋa. 18Mi Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale a weeni ayen, Mi ale vua la, nuru bala batawa a dan poom bo tɛŋ kala po ba kan baga a vari ba bisa ale ba lieba a basi. Ba le vari ka badek a basi.
19<<Yaase m basi ate tuem a waaŋ tɛŋka meena. M sui ale puuri nna yegayega ale ba ate m kaasi abe m ko nuruma ale duŋsa. 20Mi Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni ayen mi ale sum vua la, Nowa ale Daniel ale Job a dan poom bo tɛŋka po ba kan baga vari ba biik yaa ba lie a basi. A ko nuruma ale duŋsaŋa. 22Alege nuruba gela ale nyin du nyin, bisa ale lieba ale nyini. Ba le nyini jam ni jigi ate ni nya ba nyeka ate sui yaa yɔk ale mi ale ta kaasuŋ kuui a jam Jerusalem la. 23Ni dan nya ba nyeka ni sue le yɔk ate ni seba ayen mi an nye basi du alege ka wari nyiŋ. Ka Mi Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ale weeni.

english_text:
Jerusalem Is a Useless Vine
1Some time later, the Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, what happens to the wood of a grapevine after the grapes have been picked? It isn't like other trees in the forest, 3because the wood of a grapevine can't be used to make anything, not even a small peg to hang things on. 4It can only be used as firewood. But after its ends are burnt and its middle is charred, it can't be used for anything. 5The wood is useless before it is burned, and afterwards, it is completely worthless.
6I, the Lord God, promise that just as the wood of a grapevine is burned as firewood, 7I will punish the people of Jerusalem with fire. Some of them have escaped one destruction, but soon they will be completely burned. And when that happens, you, Ezekiel, will know that I am the Lord. 8I will make their country an empty wasteland, because they have not been loyal to me. I, the Lord God, have spoken.

Fi baga a pai a nye kpaasiri a yik jaab du? 4Ase ba dan pai tunuk dabi a yuk basi bolim po ate bu dɛ kaabta buyewa jam suŋsuŋka po a dɛ, fi baga a pai a nye jaaboa. 5Diokku ale chim pumi la, ba an baga a pai nye jaaboa.
