to bite them.
4I'll send a sword to kill them,
wherever their enemies
drag them off as captives.
I'm determined to hurt them,
not to help them.”
His Name Is the Lord
5When the Lord God All-Powerful
touches the earth, it melts,
and its people mourn.
God makes the earth rise
and then fall,
just like the Nile River.
6He built his palace in the heavens
and let its foundations
rest on the earth.
He scoops up the ocean
and empties it on the earth.
His name is the Lord.
The Lord Is God
7Israel, I am the Lord God,
and the Ethiopians
are no less important to me
than you are.
I brought you out of Egypt,
but I also brought
the Philistines from Crete
and the Arameans from Kir.
8My eyes have seen
what a sinful nation you are,
and I'll wipe you out.
But I will leave a few
of Jacob's descendants.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
9At my command, all of you
will be sifted like grain.
Israelites who remain faithful
will be scattered
among the nations.
And the others will be trapped
like trash in a sifter.
10Some of you are evil,
and you deny
that you will ever get caught.
But you will be killed.
The Lord's Promise to Israel
11 In the future, I will rebuild
David's fallen kingdom.
I will build it from its ruins
and set it up again,
just as it used to be.
12Then you will capture Edom
and the other nations
that are mine.
I, the Lord, have spoken,
and my words will come true.
13You will have such a harvest
that you won't be able
to bring in all of your wheat
before plowing time.
You will have grapes left over
from season to season;
your fruitful vineyards
will cover the mountains.
14I'll make Israel prosper again.
You will rebuild your towns
and live in them.
You will drink wine
from your own vineyards
and eat the fruit you grow.
15I'll plant your roots deep
in the land I have given you,
and you won't ever
be uprooted again.
I, the Lord God, have spoken!
translation_text:
1Mi nya ka Nyɔnɔwa ale wa za kuŋkuŋku gauŋ a weeni ayen, <<Nak Nyɔnɔwa yenni zaŋŋa ŋmanni ale nyubini a choa. Ŋa ale lo nuru baai ale bo yenni po la meena zuk. Baai ale a tali la m le ko ba ale gebik. Ba waai a kan cheŋŋi. Ba wanyi mɛ a kan chali bɛ. 2Ba dan poom a tu vie a paari kpiluŋ a ga suk dula, mi ale cheŋ a ga yik ba dula. Ba dan chali a jueli wenŋmazuk, dula ate mi ale kasi ba a lɔnsi tɛŋ. 3Ba dan jueli Karmel guuku, mi ale yik ba meena a ta ba siŋ tɛŋ. Ba dan suk badek nyakpiemu tɛŋ dula mi ale basi ate waab a dom ba. 4Ba dachaasaŋa ale yik ba ta ga basi badek tɛŋ po ate m le te ba ko ba. M kan maari ba. M za m kaasi ba kama. M le pai biem nina a nya ba alege daa nalimmoa.>>
5Nyɔnɔwa, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, waai ale a tiri tɛŋka ate ka a nyaliŋ la, ate baai meena ale bo ka po la a kum. Tɛŋka meena a yiti kama ase Nile benni la, a yaa siŋ ase Ejipiti benni la. 6Naawen dii ale sɛ wa yenni wenŋmazuk la ale nye di nyubini tɛŋka zuk la, waai ale basi ate nyakpiemu nyaataŋa a tagli tɛŋka meena la. Wa yuei ale Naawen.
7Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna, <<Izirali demma, nama ale tɛŋ yoŋ dem, ase Kus demma daa bunyi? Mi a yeeri Izirali demma a nyini yontidi po Ejipiti tɛŋka po, Filistia demma nyini Kaftor po ate Araam demma nyini Kir tɛŋka po?
8<<Chekki Nyɔnɔwa Naawen a nya Izirali tɛŋka demma wabaataŋa kama m be za m kaasi ba kama a ta nyini tɛŋka zuk. Alege m kan kaasi Jekob ŋaaŋsaŋa meena.>> Ka Naawen ale weeni. 9<<Mi ale te ka nɔi, ayen tɛŋ yonsa demma a nye Izirali demma ase ba ale a yɛliŋ zom diila a yeeri baai ale kan ta kiri la a basi. 10Wabaata nyama ale maa pulim nuruma po la meena a za ba kpi kama kpaliŋ po, ale baai mɛ ale weeni ayen kaasuŋ a kan paari ba la mɛ la meena.>>
11Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna, <<Dai ale jam ate mi ale ŋman pilim pai Izirali demma pagrimu a te ni ase diipo ate Deevid a jam ka naab la. Ba yie ŋaai ale lo la, mi ale pilim a sɛ ŋa ate ŋa pilim a nye ase ŋa nyiem ale jam ka diila. 12Ate ba pilim a nak tuesi Edom demma ale bo tɛŋ sii po la meena ale tɛŋ sii meena ale ta mi yuenni la.>> Ka Naawen dii ale wa nye wieŋa de la ale weeni.
13Naawen ale weeni ayen, <<Daaŋa a cheena ate naa kpaarɔwa ale gaam cheerɔwa a taam. Ate yɔn pisidɔwa a gaam vukdɔwa a taam. Da paalik ale nyini pinaŋa po a tagli guutaŋa meena zuk. 14M nuruma Izirali demma ale bo tɛŋ yoŋ po la, m le ŋman ta ba a jam badek tɛŋka po. Ba tɛŋsaŋa ale kaasi la mi ale pilim a sɛ si ate ba ale bo si po. Ba ale nya daam a nyu a nyini yɔna ti sii ate ba vuk la po. Ba ale kpa ŋan baai la ale ta ŋandiinta a jam te ba. 15Mi ale te Izirali demma a kali ba tɛŋka po waai a kan ŋman yiak ba a nyini tɛŋ kaai ate mi a pai a te ba la.>> Ka Naawen fi Wenni ale weeni.

english_text:
Edom's Pride and Punishment
1 The Lord God gave Obadiah
a message about Edom,
and this is what we heard:
“I, the Lord, have sent
a messenger
with orders for the nations
to attack Edom.”
2The Lord said to Edom:
I will make you the weakest
and most despised nation.
3You live in a mountain fortress,
because your pride
makes you feel safe from attack,
but you are mistaken.
4I will still bring you down,
even if you fly higher
than an eagle
or nest among the stars.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
5If thieves break in at night,
they steal
only what they want.
And people who harvest grapes
always leave some unpicked.
But, Edom, you are doomed!
6Everything you treasure most
will be taken from you.
7Your allies can't be trusted.
They will force you out
of your own country.
And your best friends
will trick and trap you,
even before you know it.
8Edom, when this happens,
I, the Lord, will destroy
all your marvelous wisdom.
9Warriors from the city of Teman
will be terrified,
and you descendants of Esau
will be wiped out.
The Lord Condemns Edom's Cruelty
10You were cruel to your relatives,
the descendants of Jacob.
Now you will be destroyed,
disgraced forever.
11You stood there and watched
as foreigners entered Jerusalem
and took what they wanted.
In fact, you were no better
than those foreigners.
12Why did you celebrate
when such a dreadful disaster
struck your relatives?
Why were you so pleased
when everyone in Judah
was suffering?
13They are my people,
and you were cruel to them.
You went through their towns,
sneering and stealing
whatever was left.
14In their time of torment,
you ambushed refugees
and handed them over
to their attackers.
The Lord Will Judge the Nations
15The day is coming
when I, the Lord,
will judge the nations.
And, Edom, you will pay in full
for what you have done.
16I forced the people of Judah
to drink the wine of my anger
on my sacred mountain.
Soon the neighboring nations
must drink their fill—
then vanish without a trace.
Victory for Israel
17The Lord's people who escape
will go to Mount Zion,
and it will be holy.
Then Jacob's descendants
will capture the land of those
who took their land.
18Israel will be a fire,
and Edom will be straw
going up in flames.
The Lord has spoken!
19The people of Israel
who live in the Southern Desert
will take the land of Edom.
Those who live in the hills
will capture Philistia,
Ephraim, and Samaria.
And the tribe of Benjamin
will conquer Gilead.
20Those who return from captivity
will control Phoenicia
as far as Zarephath.
Captives from Jerusalem
who were taken to Sepharad
will capture the towns
of the Southern Desert.
21Those the Lord has saved
will live on Mount Zion
and rule over Edom.
Then the kingdom will belong
to the Lord.
translation_text:
1Obadia ale jam gɔdaasim diila ale nna. Nya kude ate Nyɔnɔwa Naawen a weeni a magsi chaab ale Edom. Ti wom ka wari a nyini Naawen jigi ayen, Waai ale ba tom ayen wa cheŋ tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa po a ga weeni ayen, <<Yiti, ate ti cheŋ a ga siti tugurik ale wa.>>
2<<Nya, m le nye ate fi fiisa tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa po. Ba ale valiŋ fu. 3Fi suinummu kanjantaŋa a paasi fu kama, fi waai ale bo pinaŋa po ale sɛ fi yenni ŋmai la, fi weeni ka fidek ayen, <Ka wana ale wa ta mi a siŋ tɛŋŋa?> 4Fi poom a yiri wen ase ka jiiruk la ale a yɔk fi tukku chiŋmarisaŋa po, dula ate m le ta fu a siŋ tɛŋ,>> Ka Naawen ale weeni.
5<<Ase zueba nin jam fi jigi, ate varidɔba a jam fi jigi yok. Ka boa kaasuŋ choa ate fi za fi tu. Ba kan zu koalim daa jaab buuri meena ate ba a yaali la? Yɔn pisidɔba a dan jam fi jigi, ba kan pisi abe ba tali gela a basi? 6Alege nya ba ale vari Iisɔ dii yaa, ba koalim wa nitalimu ate wa pai suk la kama. 7Fi sɔmma meena ale fɛ fu a ta cheŋ tɛŋka banni. Fi doama ale paasi fu a nya pagrim fi zuk. Baai ale a dɛ fi ŋandiintaŋa la ale bari fu alege fi kan miŋ ku.
8Naawen weeni ayen, <<Dai dila danni m kan kaasi Edom nuru baai ale ta yam la ale nuru baai ale ta miŋka a bo Iisɔ guutaŋa po la. 9Teman, fi tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpaziita ale nak, ate waai meena ale bo Iisɔ guutaŋa po la ale kpi tugurik po. 10Wɔkwɔkka ate fi jam nye ale fi suoku Jekob la nyiŋ, chivie ale lik fu. Fi ale kaasi kama taam wuu. 11Fi jam nye ase ka ba la la, dai dila danni fi jam za a nya kama ate nicham a ji ba jigsika ŋantaŋa, ate nicham a va ba nansuiŋtaŋa a jo a nak gbaŋ Jerusalem nyiŋ. 12Ku an magsi ayen fi valiŋ fi suoku dai dii danni ate wa bo daanika po la, yaase fi dɛ masim dai dii danni ate Juda demma a bo kaasuŋ po la, yaase fi kuulim nna yegayega ba daanika danni po. 13Ku an magsi ayen fi gɔk santiri a gilim m nuruma nansuiŋtaŋa dai dii danni ate ku kaasi ba jigi la, yaase fi valiŋ ba ba daanika po ate ku kaasi ba jigi la, yaase ni peri ba jigsika ŋantaŋa a ta dai dii danni ate ba bo kaasuŋ po la. 14Ku an magsi ayen fi za suimagsa po a yik baai ale chali a bɛ la, yaase fi pai baai ale vuuk la a nyo ba nisa po.
15<<Naawen danni a moata kama a te tɛŋ kpieŋsa meena. Ase fi ale nye diila, ba ale nye fi mɛ dila. Fi tuimaŋa ale ŋman pilim siŋ fidek zuk po. 16Ase fi ale jam nyu daam m tuilum guuku zuk diila, dila mɛ ate tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa meena ale kasim a nyu daam. Ba ale kasim a nyu kama ate ku ale nye ba jigi nna se ba an poom nyu daam a nya la. 17Alege varibasika ale bo Zayon Guuku zuk. Ka ale ta tuilum ate Jekob yenni ale soa ka nitalimu. 18Naawen a weeni kama ayen, Jekob yenni ale chim ka bolim ate Josefi yenni a chim bolim ŋiak. Iisɔ yenni le chim ka kinkaa, ate ba pai a cheem bolim te ba dɛ a kaasi. Waai a kan vuuk a nyini Iisɔ yenni po.>>
19Nuru baai ale nyini Negev la ale bo Iisɔ guutaŋa, ate nuru baai ale nyini guutaŋa tɛŋsa la ale soa Filistia demma tɛŋka. Ba ale tuesi Ɛfraim ale Samaria kaduksaŋa, abe Benjamin a soa Gilead. 20Izirali dem baai ale bo Keenan la ale soa tɛŋka a ga paari Zarefat. Nuru baai ale nyini Jerusalem ale ga bo Sefarad la ale soa Negev tɛŋ fiisaŋa. 21Varibasidɔba le cheŋ jueli Zayon Guuku zuk a nya Iisɔ guutaŋa zuk. Ate Naawen ale soa naamu.

english_text:
Jonah Runs from the Lord
1 One day the Lord told Jonah, the son of Amittai, 2to go to the great city of Nineveh and say to the people, “The Lord has seen your terrible sins. You are doomed!”
3Instead, Jonah ran from the Lord. He went to the seaport of Joppa and found a ship that was going to Spain. So he paid his fare, then got on the ship and sailed away to escape.
4But the Lord made a strong wind blow, and such a bad storm came up that the ship was about to be broken to pieces. 5The sailors were frightened, and they all started praying to their gods. They even threw the ship's cargo overboard to make the ship lighter.
All this time, Jonah was down below deck, sound asleep. 6The ship's captain went to him and said, “How can you sleep at a time like this? Get up and pray to your God! Maybe he will have pity on us and keep us from drowning.”
7Finally, the sailors got together and said, “Let's ask our gods to show us who caused all this trouble.” It turned out to be Jonah.
8They started asking him, “Are you the one who brought all this trouble on us? What business are you in? Where do you come from? What is your country? Who are your people?”
9Jonah answered, “I'm a Hebrew, and I worship the Lord God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.”
10When the sailors heard this, they were frightened, because Jonah had already told them he was running from the Lord. Then they said, “Do you know what you have done?”
11The storm kept getting worse, until finally the sailors asked him, “What should we do with you to make the sea calm down?”
12Jonah told them, “Throw me into the sea, and it will calm down. I'm the cause of this terrible storm.”
13The sailors tried their best to row to the shore. But they could not do it, and the storm kept getting worse every minute. 14So they prayed to the Lord, “Please don't let us drown for taking this man's life. Don't hold us guilty for killing an innocent man. All of this happened because you wanted it to.” 15Then they threw Jonah overboard, and the sea calmed down. 16The sailors were so terrified that they offered a sacrifice to the Lord and made all kinds of promises.
17 The Lord sent a big fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was inside the fish for three days and three nights.

1Naawen a yaa biisi ale Amittai nidoabinni Jona ayen, 2<<Cheŋ tɛŋ kpieŋka Niineve a ga biisi ale ka nuruma, dii nyiŋla ka nuruma biemu a zuak kama m niŋ.>> 3Alege Jona a yiti chali a bɛ Naawen niŋ. Wa jam chali a cheŋ ka Tarsis tɛŋka. Wa abe liŋ jam cheŋ ka Jopa tɛŋka a yaa nya ŋaaruŋ ale ku a cheŋ Tarsis. Wa yaa tuni ale ge jueli ate ku ta wa a cheŋ Tarsis ayen wa chali bɛ Naawen.
4Naawen a yaa basi ate va pagrik a fuk nyiamu ate ŋaaruŋku a tali maga ate ku mobi kabakaba. 5Baai meena ale jam a dam ŋaaruŋku la kpaziim a yaa jam a nak nna lɔlɔ ate ba yaa piilim a kaari a wi wa wen wa wen ayen ŋa maamaari ba. Ba pai kɔlimaŋa ale bo ŋaaruŋku po la a yuk a basi nyiamu po ayen dila a maari ate ŋaaruŋku a valima. Nya kude ale nye la, alege Jona a daam nya ka ŋaaruŋku gugoruk po a doa ate goom a chiak wa. 6Nuru waai ale chim kpagi a nya ŋaaruŋku zuk la, a yaa cheŋ wa jigi a ga weeni wa ayen, <<Ka boan nyiŋ ate fi doa goa? Yiti ŋmai a wi fi wenni. Fi wenni ale naam chali ti jiirim a vari ti a basi ate ti kan kpi.>>
7Ŋaaruŋku damdɔma a yaa wi chaab a weeni chaab ayen, <<Ni jam ate ti nak gbaŋ ate ti nya ase ka wana ale soa ate wapagni de a paari ti.>> Ba yaa nak gbaŋka ate ka za lɔ Jona zuk. 8Ba yaa bek wa ayen, a weeni, <<Ka wana ale soa ate ninammu de a jam tama zuwa? Fi nye ka boa? Fi nyini ka be? Fi nyini ka tɛŋ kana? Fi ka boan buuri?>> 9Wa yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<Mi ka Yiburu denɔ, a puusi Naawen, Wen dii ale soa wenŋmazuk la, waai ale nye nyakpiemu ale tɛŋka la.>> 10Jona tulisaŋa a yaa nak ba kpaziim ate ba yaa bek wa ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi nye?>> Ba poom jam seba kama ayen Jona a chali a bɛ kama Naawen niŋ dii nyiŋla wa ŋaam jam weeni ba kama.
11Ŋaaruŋku damdɔma ale a biisi ale Jona la, nyiamu choaka a ŋman ŋmasi a gaam di. Ba yaa bek wa ayen, <<Ti be ti nye fu ka sɛ ate nyiamu a baliŋ a te ti?>> 12Wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni koati mu a lɔnsi nyiamu po dila ale bu baliŋ. Mi seba ayen ka mi nyiŋ ale soa ate daanika de a paari ni.>> 13Jona ale biisi nnala a nueri la, ŋaaruŋku damdɔma a diem pii ka nyiŋ ayen ba dam ŋaaruŋku a ta ŋmani jueli kunkɔŋi alege ba an jam baga dii nyiŋla nyiamu choaka a jam pagra ka nna yegayega a gaam bu nyiem ale ka dii la. 14Ba yaa kum te Naawen weeni ayen, <<Naawen yaa, kan ko ti ase tama a nin ko nuruwa de. Kan te ti pamiya ase tama a nin ko nuru waai ale kan kaasi tuini la, dii nyiŋla ka fi Naawen yaa, ale tom fidek ale a yaali diila.>> 15Ba yaa koati Jona a lɔnsi nyiamu po ate nyiamu ale a dɛ bu tuemu la a yaa deri baliŋ. 16Damdɔma ale nya ale nyiamu a baliŋ la, ba yaa chali yɔgsum ale Naawen ate ba nye kaabka a te Naawen ale puulim ayen ba le kasim a zuli wa.
17Alege Naawen a gomsi jum kpioŋ ate bu nɛ Jona. Jona jam bo jummu poni po ka daa ŋata.

english_text:
Jonah's Prayer
1From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the Lord his God:
2When I was in trouble, Lord,
I prayed to you,
and you listened to me.
From deep in the world
of the dead,
I begged for your help,
and you answered my prayer.
3You threw me down
to the bottom of the sea.
The water was churning
all around;
I was completely covered
by your mighty waves.
4I thought I was swept away
from your sight,
never again to see
your holy temple.
5I was almost drowned
by the swirling waters
that surrounded me.
Seaweed had wrapped
around my head.
6I had sunk down deep
below the mountains
beneath the sea.
I knew that forever,
I would be a prisoner there.
But, you, Lord God,
rescued me from that pit.
7When my life was slipping away,
I remembered you—
and in your holy temple
you heard my prayer.
8All who worship worthless idols
turn from the God
who offers them mercy.
9But with shouts of praise,
I will offer a sacrifice
to you, my Lord.
I will keep my promise,
because you are the one
with power to save.
10 The Lord commanded the fish to vomit up Jonah on the shore. And it did.
translation_text:
1Jona yaa duak jummu poni po a puusi te Naawen wa Wenni. 2Wa weeni ayen, <<M ninammu po m wi Naawen Yuei ate wa tulisi mu. M le bo vɔrumu po la, m wi wa a bek maarika, ate fi wom m kumsa. 3Fi yuk mu a basi nyakpiemu po juijui ate nyiamu ale nya miisaŋa a gilim mu.
4<<M weeni ayen, <Fi zɛri mu kama, alege m diem za ayen m cheŋ fi yenni po kama a puusi fu.> 5Nya buui ale a lim a gilim mu la a paari ka m ŋiri, liuŋku a gilim mu kama, beni wuutaŋa a bobi m zukku mɛ. 6M siŋ paari ka nyiamu niŋniŋa ase gu kpioŋ chiak ate m za la juijui ate ba lik tɛŋka tuataŋa diipo meena wuu. Naawen m Wen yaa, alege fi dari mu yeeri vɔrumu po a pilim te mu vum. 7M daam le boro a jɔk m nyuvunni la, Naawen yaa, m teeri fi wari, a yaa jo fi yenni po a puusi a te fu. 8Baai ale pai badek a seeri bɔgta la a yeeri badek Naawen jigi kama a kan nya wa jiirimu. 9Alege mi, ale pai ka yiila a nye kaabka a te fu. M le puulim ayen mi le nye diila, mi le nye ate ku nala. Varibasika a nyini ka Naawen jigi.>> 10Jona ale puusi nnala a nueri jummu poni po la, Naawen a yaa weeni jummu ate bu ta Jona jueli kunkɔŋi a chiiri wa dueni vuta.

english_text:
Jonah Goes to Nineveh
1Once again the Lord told Jonah 2to go to that great city of Nineveh and preach his message of doom.
3Jonah obeyed the Lord and went to Nineveh. The city was so big that it took three days just to walk through it. 4 After walking for a day, Jonah warned the people, “Forty days from now, Nineveh will be destroyed!”
5They believed God's message and set a time when they would go without eating to show their sorrow. Then everyone in the city, no matter who they were, dressed in sackcloth.
6When the king of Nineveh heard what was happening, he also dressed in sackcloth; he left the royal palace and sat in dust. 7-9Then he and his officials sent out an order for everyone in the city to obey. It said:
None of you or your animals may eat or drink a thing. Each of you must wear sackcloth, and you must even put sackcloth on your animals.
You must also pray to the Lord God with all your heart and stop being sinful and cruel. Maybe God will change his mind and have mercy on us, so we won't be destroyed.
10When God saw that the people had stopped doing evil things, he had pity and did not destroy them as he had planned.
translation_text:
1Naawen a yaa ŋman biisi ale Jona ku naŋtuok nɔi buye. 2<<Cheŋ Niineve tɛŋ kpieŋka a weeni ba wa dii ate m pai te fu ayen fi weeni ba la.>> 3Jona a yaa siak Naawen nɔi a yaa cheŋ Niineve. Niineve jam ka tɛŋ kpieŋ. Ba pai ka daa ŋata a cheŋ a paari ka. 4Jona ale cheŋ paari Niineve wa pai ka dai a cheŋ mooli Naawen ale weeni wa diila ayen, <<Da pisinaansi ale tali ate Naawen yik Niineve nuruma ale ka jaab meena kaasi.>> 5Jona ale biisi nnala a nueri la, Niineve nuruma a yaa siak Naawen lueluku. Ba yaa nya chaab a zɛri ŋandiinta dɛka. A zaani ba ŋankpagsa ta ga paari ba bimbaansa meena a yaa pai boorisa gatta a jo ayen ku sak ayen ba sue a kaasi ale ba wabaataŋa kama.
6Ba le weeni ate ku paari Niineve naawa, Naawen ale weeni diila, wa yaa yeeri wa naamu gattaŋa ale yaali boorisa gatta a jo a yiri wa naamu zaŋgɔŋka zuk a siŋ kala tantaŋa po. 7Wa yaa ŋmarisi gbaŋ a weeni wa tɛŋka demma ayen, <<Naawa ale wa nisɔmma ale a te gbaŋka de a weeni ayen nuru waai kan dɛ jaab tɛŋka po. Waai mɛ la bi kan ta niiga yaase duŋ buulim a nyini ate ŋa dɛ jaaboa yaase ŋa nyu nyiamoa. 8Alege nurubiik ale duŋsa meena a jo boorisa gatta. Waai meena a juisi Wen ale ninmuna. Waai meena a basi tuim kaasima ale nyeka tuem. 9Ka wana ale seba? Wen bag kama a tagri wa popolaŋa a ta jiirim ale ti a kan pai wa suinni a ko ti.>>
10Wen ale nya ba le nye diila, ale ba le pai ba biemu nyeka a basi la, Wen jiirim a yaa dari ba ate wa an ŋman ta kaasika jam ba jigi ya ase wa le poom piilim poli ayen wa kaasi ba diila.

english_text:
Jonah Gets Angry with the Lord
1Jonah was really upset and angry. 2 So he prayed:
Our Lord, I knew from the very beginning that you wouldn't destroy Nineveh. That's why I left my own country and headed for Spain. You are a kind and merciful God, and you are very patient. You always show love, and you don't like to punish anyone.
3 Now let me die! I'd be better off dead.
4The Lord replied, “What right do you have to be angry?”
5Jonah then left through the east gate of the city and made a shelter to protect himself from the sun. He sat under the shelter, waiting to see what would happen to Nineveh.
6The Lord made a vine grow up to shade Jonah's head and protect him from the sun. Jonah was very happy to have the vine, 7but early the next morning the Lord sent a worm to chew on the vine, and the vine dried up. 8During the day the Lord sent a scorching wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah's head, making him feel faint. Jonah was ready to die, and he shouted, “I wish I were dead!”
9But the Lord asked, “Jonah, do you have the right to be angry about the vine?”
“Yes, I do,” he answered, “and I'm angry enough to die.”
10But the Lord said:
You are concerned about a vine that you did not plant or take care of, a vine that grew up in one night and died the next. 11In that city of Nineveh there are more than 120,000 people who cannot tell right from wrong, and many cattle are also there. Don't you think I should be concerned about that big city?
translation_text:
1Alege Jona sui a jam kaasi ate wa sui a puuri nna yegayega. 2Wa yaa puusi a te Naawen a weeni ayen, <<Naawen yaa, daa m ni poom bo yeri a weeni diila ale la? Ka fi nye ka de nyiŋ ale soa ate mi din banti ale chali a cheŋ Tarsis la. Mi seba kama ayen fi ka jiirim kpiem nyɔnɔ ate fi sui yirika a toa ate fi ŋmanteka mɛ a ka bain ya, fi ka Wen dii ale ka a daliŋ fi vɔŋ te la. 3Naawen yaa, dila nyiŋla ko mu yɔgyɔgla de. Ale m dan jɔk kpi, ku zunchoŋ kama a gaam m le boro.>> 4Alege Naawen a ya tulisi wa ayen, <<Ka din dek nyiŋ ale soa ate fi basi ate fi sui a puuri?>> 5Jona yaa nyini tɛŋka po a nyini a taam ka kori geŋ a ti viuk a yaa jo kali ku po a limisi ase Naawen ale kaasi tɛŋka ya.
6Naawen dii ale ka Wen la yaa basi ate tunuŋ a nyini chim yɔgsum a liŋ Jona zukku ate wa yaa kala. Jona sui jam peenti ka nna yegayega ale tunuku yɔgsummu. 7Vari ale veenti la, saluik yokyokwa Wen a yaa basi nanzuiri ate di dɛ tunuku kinni ate ku kpi. 8Wenbinni ale pusi la, Wen a yaa basi ate kantueŋ wuluk a ŋari nyini koni po a nak Jona zukku ate wa buk nna zana. Wa jaa yaa ka kum nyiini. Wa yaa weeni ayen, <<M dan jɔk kpi a zunchoŋ m le vua la kama.>>
9Naawen a yaa bek Jona ayen, <<Fi ta suik a basi ate fi sui a puuri ale tunuku ale kpi la nyiŋŋa?>> Jona yaa tulisi ayen, M ta suik kama. M suinni ale puuri diila m yaa a yaali ka kum nyiini.>> 10Naawen yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Tunuku ale nyini la, fi a kpa gilim ku, fi a nyo bibaam ku tɛŋa. Ku pai ka yok yeŋ a nyini, a ŋman pai yok yeŋ a kpi, alege fi basi ate fi sui a puuri ale ku kum. 11Alege Niineve a ta ka nuruba ate ba piisi gaam tusa kook ale pisiye (120,000) ate ba zɛ ba juga ale ba gala. Ba bi ta niiga mɛ kama a piisi. Ku a magsi ayen m basi ate m jiirim a dari tɛŋ kpieŋ ka dɛ?>>

english_text:
1 I am Micah from Moresheth. And this is the message about Samaria and Jerusalem that the Lord gave to me when Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah.
Judgment on Samaria
2Listen, all of you!
Earth and everything on it,
pay close attention.
The Lord God accuses you
from his holy temple.
3And he will come down
to crush underfoot
every pagan altar.
4Mountains will melt
beneath his feet
like wax beside a fire.
Valleys will vanish like water
rushing down a ravine.
5This will happen because of
the terrible sins of Israel,
the descendants of Jacob.
Samaria has led Israel to sin,
and pagan altars at Jerusalem
have made Judah sin.
6So the Lord will leave Samaria
in ruins—
merely an empty field
where vineyards are planted.
He will scatter its stones
and destroy its foundations.
7Samaria's idols will be smashed,
and the wages
of temple prostitutes
will be destroyed by fire.
Silver and gold from those idols
will then be used by foreigners
as payment for prostitutes.
Judah Is Doomed
8Because of this tragedy,
I go barefoot and naked.
My crying and weeping
sound like howling wolves
or ostriches.
9The nation is fatally wounded.
Judah is doomed.
Jerusalem will fall.
10Don't tell it in Gath!
Don't even cry.
Instead, roll in the dust
at Beth-Leaphrah.
11Depart naked and ashamed,
you people of Shaphir.
The town of Bethezel mourns
because no one from Zaanan
went out to help.
12Everyone in Maroth
hoped for the best,
but the Lord sent disaster
down on Jerusalem.
13Get the war chariots ready,
you people of Lachish.
You led Jerusalem into sin,
just as Israel did.
14Now you will have to give
a going-away gift
to Moresheth.
Israel's kings will discover
that they cannot trust
the town of Achzib.
15People of Mareshah,
the Lord will send someone
to capture your town.
Then Israel's glorious king
will be forced to hide
in Adullam Cave.
16Judah, shave your head
as bald as a vulture
and start mourning.
Your precious children
will be dragged off
to a foreign country.
translation_text:
1Naawen wa dii ale jan jam Maika ale nyini Moreset la jigi. Di jam ka va ŋaai po ate Jotam dɛ naam ate Ayazi a jam dɛ ate Azekaya mɛ a jam dɛ Juda la. Wa le jam nya wa dii a magsi chaab ale Samaria ale Jerusalem la ale nna:
2Nuruba, ni wom, ni meena abe wom, tɛŋzuk de ale baai meena ale bo ka po la, ayen Nyɔnɔwa Naawen a nya ni ale nye dii a kaasi la kama. Nyɔnɔwa a nyini ka wa yenni po. 3Nya! Naawen a nyini ka wa bo ka jigini a cheena. Wa siŋ cheen kama ayen wa tabi tɛŋzuk de guutaŋa zuk. 4Guutaŋa a nyaliŋ kama wa naŋtaata po, ate vaasaŋa a lab ase bolim ale paari zirima diila ase nyiam ale va churintika jigi a siŋ diila. 5Nya kude meena ka Jekob nye kaasuŋku ale Izirali wabaataŋa nyiŋ. Ka boa ale Jekob nye kaasuŋku? Ku daa Samaria? Ka boa ale Juda puusika jigini? Daa Jerusalem?
6<<Dila nyiŋ m le nye ate Samaria a chim guura, a chim kaduk ate ba a bori ŋanta ka po. M le kpiiri ka tanaŋa a basi viaka po ate ka nyubaŋa a doa jassi. 7Ka bɔgtaŋa meena ale ŋɔriŋ nna bunabuna. Ka yenni tiiritaŋa meena ale dɛ bolim. M le kaasi ka ŋanmɛɛntaŋa meena. Ka ale toalim a tigsi ka tiiritaŋa a nyini ka taabuksa tutuna jigi la, ase taabuksa tutuna la ate ba ale ŋman pai ŋa a tom.>>
8Nya kude nyiŋ m le kum abe m wooli. M le cheŋ naŋta bie ale chaboala. M le wooli ase gɔi biak la, abe m siŋti ase viuk la. 9Diila wa niraŋa a kan nueri. Ku cheŋ paarika Juda. Ku paarika m nuruma Jerusalem dek nansuiŋku nɔi. 10Kan weeni ku Gat po. Kan poom kum. Bilim fidek Bet Ofra paasuku po. 11Nama baai ale bo Safir po la, ni cheŋ chaboala ale chivie. Baai ale bo Zaanan po la a kan nyini peelim. Bet Ezel a bo ka kumsa po. Ba pai jabuui ale a nya ba zuk la kama ta cheŋ. 12Baai ale bo Marot la a viriŋ ale ka nyiŋdomma a limisi nyiŋyɔgsa, dii nyiŋla kaasuŋ a nyini ka Naawen jigi a jam, a poom ga paari Jerusalem nansuiŋku nɔi. 13Nama baai ale bo Lachis la, ni bobi wusumaŋa a maŋ torokowa. Nama ale piilim a nye Zayon Liewa biem. Dii nyiŋla ba nya Izirali wabaataŋa ka fi po. 14Dila nyiŋ ni ale te Moreset Gat basika tiirita. Akzib tɛŋka ale paasi Izirali nalimaŋa. 15M le basi ate nakdeerɔ a jam nama baai ale bo Maresa po la zuk. Waai ale ka Izirali zula la ale jam Adullam. 16Ni poni ni zuimaŋa abe ni a kum ni bisaŋa ate ni ta suipeentik ba nyiŋla. Ni nye ate ni zuimaŋa a kpa ase duiŋ la, diila bisaŋa ale nyini ni jigi kama a cheŋ tɛŋ yoŋ po.

english_text:
Punishment for Those Who Abuse Their Power
1Doomed! You're doomed!
At night you lie in bed,
making evil plans.
And when morning comes,
you do what you've planned
because you have the power.
2You grab any field or house
that you want;
you cheat families
out of homes and land.
3But here is what the Lord says:
“I am planning trouble for you.
Your necks will be caught
in a noose,
and you will be disgraced
in this time of disaster.”
4When that happens,
this sorrowful song
will be sung about you:
“Ruined! Completely ruined!
The Lord has taken our land
and given it to traitors.”
5And so you will never again
own property
among the Lord's people.
6“Enough of your preaching!”
That's what you tell me.
“We won't be disgraced,
so stop preaching!”
7Descendants of Jacob,
is it right for you to claim
that the Lord did what he did
because he was angry?
Doesn't he always bless
those who do right?
8My people, you have turned against
one another!
You have even stolen
clothes right off the backs
of innocent neighbors
who pass by in peace.
9You take over lovely homes
that belong to the women
of my nation.
Then you cheat their children
out of the inheritance
that comes from the Lord.
10Get out of here, you crooks!
You'll find no rest here.
You're not fit to belong
to the Lord's people,
and you will be destroyed.
11The only prophet you want
is a liar who will say,
“Drink and get drunk!”
A Promise of Hope
12I, the Lord, promise
to bring together
the people of Israel
who have survived.
I will gather them,
just as a shepherd
brings sheep together,
and there will be many.
13I will break down the gate
and lead them out—
then I will be their king.
translation_text:
1Ku ale toa a te baai ale a zɔk wabaata ale baai ale a zɔk biem ba gaduata zuk la! Saluiku po ba nyiem yaa ji kama a ta nyini dii nyiŋla ba ta pagrim kama a nye di. 2Ba nina a muni ale nuruba kaduksa ale a vari ba yieŋa. Ba a vari nuru wa yeri po ale a vari wa vaanchoa nitalim.
3Dila nyiŋ, Naawen a weeni kama ayen, <<M boro a zɔk ka kaasuŋ nuruma de zuk ate ba kan baga a vari badek a basi. Ni kan ŋman cheŋ kanjanta po, diila va ŋala ale chim ka kaasuŋ. 4Dai dila danni nidoaba ale nye fu a la. Ba ale nye ate ni sue a puuri ale kumsa yiini de ayen, <Ti kaasi kama. Ba lab m nuruma ŋantaŋa a te ka chaab. Wa pai a nyini m jigi! Wa pai ti kaduksaŋa te bumbobrɔba.>> 5Dila nyiŋ fi kan nya waai Naawen nuruma po ate wa nak gbaŋ a lab tɛŋka.
6Ba biisiteerɔma a weeni kama ayen, <<Ni kan biisi. Ni kan biisi ŋantaŋa de wie. Chivie a kan bag ti.>> 7Jekob yenni ale weeni ayen, <<Naawen Chiika sui a puuri kama? Wa a nye ŋade chaab kama? Mi wieŋa kan nye nalim a te waai suita ale nala la? 8Mi nuruma a yiti ka yɔgyɔgla de ase dachiak la. Ni vari jigsika garukku a nyini baai ale va suiku a taam la ate ni niŋ a poom ka ba po nna se nidoaba ale nyini kpaliŋ po a cheena la. 9Ni yiak m nuruma nipooma a nyini ba yie naliŋsaŋa po. Ni pai m niauŋku a nyini ba bisaŋa jigi taam wuu. 10Ni yiti zaani, cheŋ niŋ! Diila dela daa ni vuusum jigi ya, dii nyiŋla ka daŋ kama. Ka kaasi kama ate jaab karo a yik ka nye a magsi. 11Ase velimvendik ale pimpaasirɔ a dan jam weeni ayen, <Mi le mooli ate daam ale buui ale a buk la a jam ni jigi.> Wa le chim ka biisiteerɔ waai ate nuruma de a yaali la!
12<<Jekob, m le sum a tigsi ni meena. M le sum a ta Izirali dem baai ale tali la a jam jigi yeŋ. M le ta ba a jam jigi yeŋ ase piisa ale bo zɔŋ po diila. Ba ale bo jigi yeŋ ase piisa ale bo wuyɔgsuk po diila. Nuruba ale sueri jigini. 13Waai ale wɛ a nyini la ale wa lak suiku a ga dɛ ba niŋ. Ba ale wɛ nansuiŋ tuoku a ga nyini. Ba naawa ale taam a ga dɛ ba niŋ. Naawen ale bo ba zuk.>>

english_text:
Evil Rulers and Lying Prophets
1Listen to me,
you rulers of Israel!
You know right from wrong,
2but you prefer to do evil
instead of what is right.
You skin my people alive.
You strip off their flesh,
3break their bones,
cook it all in a pot,
and gulp it down.
4Someday you will beg the Lord
to help you,
but he will turn away
because of your sins.
5You lying prophets promise
security for anyone
who gives you food,
but disaster for anyone
who refuses to feed you.
Here is what the Lord says
to you prophets:
6“You will live in the dark,
far from the sight of the sun,
with no message from me.
7You prophets and fortunetellers
will all be disgraced,
with no message from me.”
8But the Lord has filled me
with power and his Spirit.
I have been given the courage
to speak about justice
and to tell you people of Israel
that you have sinned.
9So listen to my message,
you rulers of Israel!
You hate justice
and twist the truth.
10You make cruelty and murder
a way of life in Jerusalem.
11You leaders accept bribes
for dishonest decisions.
You priests and prophets
teach and preach,
but only for money.
Then you say,
“The Lord is on our side.
No harm will come to us.”
12 And so, because of you,
Jerusalem will be plowed under
and left in ruins.
Thorns will cover the mountain
where the temple now stands.
translation_text:
1Ate mi yaa weeni ayen, <<Nama Jekob niŋdeerɔma ale Izirali yenni kpaŋŋa ni wom. Ni kan seba nyemagsika, 2nama baai ale kisa nalim ale a yaali biem la. Nama baai ale a puli nyiŋ gbaŋ a nyini m nuruma jigi ale ba nyiŋ lammu a nyini ba kobaŋa po la. 3Nama baai ale a ŋɔbi m nuruma nyiŋlanta ale a puli ba nyiŋ gbaŋsaŋa ale a che ba kobaŋa nna bunabuna a magsi dikka, ase lam ate ba dik la?>>
4Ate ba yaa le kaari a te Naawen, alege wa a kan wom ba. Dila po wa ale suk wa nimbidiaka a nyini ba jigi, dii nyiŋla biemu ate ba nye la nyiŋ.
5Nya kude ate Naawen a weeni ayen, <<Dan ka biisiteerɔ baai ale ta mi nuruma a cheŋ a bɛ la, ase ba wanyi a dan te ba ŋandiinta, ba a mooli ka suiyɔgni. Ate wa dan kan nye ya, ba a gomsi kama ayen ba nye kpaliŋ ale wa. 6Dila nyiŋ yok ale jam fi zuk, ate fi kan nya, ate legi ale nye ate fi kan baga a porisi. Wenbinni ale siŋ biisiteerɔma zuk, ate danni ale chim legi a te ba. 7Chivie ale yik biisiteerɔma ate kanpiinta ale dɛ sampoporisaŋa. Ba meena ale lik ba nimbidaasaŋa dii nyiŋla tulisika a kan nyini Wen jigi ya.>> 8Alege dan ka mi, mi sueri ale ka pagrim ale Naawen Chiika ale nyemagsika ale zuaka ayen m weeni Jekob nye kaasuŋku ale Izirali wa biemu. 9Wom de, Jekob yenni niŋdeerɔma ale Izirali yenni kpaŋŋa baai ale a zɛri nyemagsika ale yik dii meena ale magsi a tagri la. 10Baai ale a ko nuruba a sɛ Zayon ale ziim ale a sɛ Jerusalem ale gaasa la. 11Wa niŋdeerɔma a tuesi ŋanta nuruba jigi alege a bo buusa, ate wa kaabteerɔma a tuesi ŋanta alege a sak, ate wa biisiteerɔma a tuesi ligra alege a porisi. Alege ba a sali ka Naawen ale a weeni ayen, <<Naawen an bo ale ti? Kaasuŋ a kan jam ti zuwa.>> 12Dila nyiŋ nama nyiŋ, ba ale kpa Zayon ase ka laŋ la. Jerusalem ale nye ase ka guura la, Naawen yenni a chim guuk ate tiisa a chim lik.

english_text:
Peace and Prosperity
1In the future, the mountain
with the Lord's temple
will be the highest of all.
It will reach above the hills,
and every nation
will rush to it.
2People of many nations
will come and say,
“Let's go up to the mountain
of the Lord God of Jacob
and worship in his temple.”
The Lord will teach us his Law
from Jerusalem,
and we will obey him.
3 He will settle arguments
between distant
and powerful nations.
They will pound their swords
and their spears
into rakes and shovels;
they will never again make war
or attack one another.
4 Everyone will find rest
beneath their own fig trees
or grape vines,
and they will live in peace.
This is a solemn promise
of the Lord All-Powerful.
5Others may follow their gods,
but we will always follow
the Lord our God.
The Lord Will Lead His People Home
6The Lord said:
At that time
I will gather my people—
the lame and the outcasts,
and all others into whose lives
I have brought sorrow.
7Then the lame and the outcasts
will belong to my people
and become a strong nation.
I, the Lord, will rule them
from Mount Zion forever.
8Mount Zion in Jerusalem,
guardian of my people,
you will rule again.
9Jerusalem, why are you crying?
Don't you have a king?
Have your advisors gone?
Are you suffering
like a woman in childbirth?
10Keep on groaning with pain,
you people of Jerusalem!
If you escape from your city
to the countryside,
you will still be taken
as prisoners to Babylonia.
But later I will rescue you
from your enemies.
11Zion, because of your sins
you are surrounded
by many nations who say,
“We can hardly wait
to see you disgraced.”
12But they don't know
that I, the Lord,
have gathered them here
to grind them like grain.
13Smash them to pieces, Zion!
I'll let you be like a bull
with iron horns
and bronze hoofs.
Crush those nations
and bring their wealth to me,
the Lord of the earth.
translation_text:
1Dai kpeglimaŋa po, Naawen yenni guuku ale zaani ase naab la guutaŋa po. Ku ale zak ŋmai a gaam guutaŋa, ate tɛŋsa meena ale chuiri a cheŋ ku jigi.
2Tɛŋ kpieŋsa yega ale jam a weeni ayen, <<Ni jam ate ti jueli Naawen guuku, ti jueli Jekob Wen yenni. Wa ale sak ti Wa suitaŋa ate ti baga a cheŋ ti po.>> Wa sinsaŋŋa ale nyini Zayon a cheŋ. Ate Naawen wanni ale nyini Jerusalem. 3Wa ale bo nuru boari buusa. Wa le yik tɛŋ pagrisa wie a yomsi. Ba ale kuri ba gebisaŋa a nye niiga kua. Ba gbattaŋa ale labri a chim gebisa ate ba pai a yoarisi tiisa. Tɛŋ a kan pai gebik a ta chaab ale tɛŋ ka choa, yaase ba ŋman sak badek a magsi kpaliŋ diipo diipo. 4Nuru meena ale kali wadek yɔna tiib tɛŋ ale wadek kiŋkaŋ tɛŋ, ate waai a kan nye ate ba kpaziim kasim a nak, dii nyiŋla ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni. 5Tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa meena ale cheŋ ba wenaŋa yuenni nyiŋ, alege tama ale cheŋ ka Naawen ti Wenni yuenni nyiŋ taam wuu.
6Naawen ti Wenni a weeni kama ayen, <<Dai dila danni m le tigsi gbansa, abe m tigsi baai ale basi ba tɛŋsa la ale baai ate m daani ba la. 7M le basi ate gbansaŋa a tali, abe baai ate ba yiak basi la tɛŋ pagrik. Naawen ale nya ba zuk Zayon po a nyini dai dila danni a taa cheŋ. 8Dan ka fi, piisaŋa yewɔŋku, Zayon liewa pagrimu, fi a ŋman nya fi pagrim kpakka. Naam ale jam Jerusalem Liewa jigi.
9Boan nyiŋ ate fi a kaari? Fi a ka naabaa? Fi sagrɔwa a bɛ kama? Nyiŋ dommaŋa de a nye fi ase ka nipok waai ale boro a biak la? 10Zayon Liewa, a bilim tɛŋka ale nyiŋdomma, ase nipok ale boro a biak diila. Diila yɔgyɔgla de fi magsi fi basi tɛŋka kama a ga kali peelim. Fi ale cheŋ Babilon, ate fi ale nya varibasika dula. Naawen ale da fu a tuesi dula a nyini fi dachaasaŋa nisa po.
11Alege yɔgyɔgla de tɛŋ kpieŋsa yega a nya ka chaab ayen si nye kpaliŋ ale fu. Ba a weeni kama ayen, <<Basi ate wa taŋ, basi ate ti ninaŋa a naŋ Zayon zuk. 12Alege ba zɛ Naawen popola. Ba kan miŋ wa zɔŋŋa. Ka wala ale a tigsi ba ase boba la a taa cheŋ fɔbika jigini.
13Zayon Liewa, yiti a fɔbi, diila m le te fu ka kutuk nyiila ale kutuk mɔnuŋ naŋsaba, ate fi ale kaasi tɛŋ kpieŋsa nna yegayega.>> Ni ale pai ba nyuentaŋa ate ni nak vari la a te Naawen ale ba jigsika ŋantaŋa a te tɛŋzuk de meena Nyɔnɔwa.

english_text:
A Promised Ruler
1Jerusalem, enemy troops
have surrounded you;
they have struck Israel's ruler
in the face with a stick.
2 Bethlehem Ephrath,
you are one of the smallest towns
in the nation of Judah.
But the Lord will choose
one of your people
to rule the nation—
someone whose family
goes back to ancient times.
3The Lord will abandon Israel
only until this ruler is born,
and the rest of his family
returns to Israel.
4Like a shepherd
taking care of his sheep,
this ruler will lead
and care for his people
by the power and glorious name
of the Lord his God.
His people will live securely,
and the whole earth will know
his true greatness,
5because he will bring peace.
Assyria Will Be Defeated
Let Assyria attack our country
and our palaces.
We will counterattack,
led by a number of rulers
6 whose strong army will defeat
the nation of Assyria.
Yes, our leaders will rescue us,
if those Assyrians
dare to invade our land.
The Survivors Will Be Safe
7A few of Jacob's descendants
survived and are scattered
among the nations.
But the Lord will let them
cover the earth like dew and rain
that refreshes the soil.
8At present they are scattered,
but later they will attack,
as though they were fierce lions
pouncing on sheep.
Their enemies will be torn
to shreds,
with no one to save them;
9they will be helpless,
completely destroyed.
Idols Will Be Destroyed in Israel
10The Lord said:
At that time I will wipe out
your cavalry and chariots,
11as well as your cities
and your fortresses.
12I will stop you
from telling fortunes
and practicing witchcraft.
13You will no longer worship
the idols or stone images
you have made—
I will destroy them,
14together with the sacred poles
and even your towns.
15I will become furious
and take revenge on the nations
that refuse to obey me.
translation_text:
1Tigsi fi tugurik tɔŋdɔma, tugurik tɔŋdɔba tɛŋ nummoa, diila ba gilim kama a ta chaab ale ti. Ba le fɔbi Izirali niŋdeerɔwa tapiak ale doari.
2<<Alege fi Betiliyem Efrata, Juda buuni po fi ale pɔsima, a nyini fi po ate niŋdeerɔ ale nya Izirali zuk a te mi. Waai kiri ale nyini ŋiak po.>>
3Dila nyiŋ ba za ba zɛri Izirali kama ate ku ga paari diipo ate nipok waai ale a dom la a ga biak, ate wa soa tii ale tali la a pilim ŋmani a ga gum Izirali demma po.
4Wa ale zaani a kasi wa piisaŋa Naawen pagrimu nyiŋ ale Naawen wa Wenni zula yuenni nyiŋ. Ate ba ale bo sukka dek jigi, ate wa zuaka ale paari tɛŋka kpeglimka. 5Ate wala ale chim ba suiyɔgni. Ase Assiria demma nin wɛ jɔ ti tɛŋka po a gɔk santiri a gilim ti yie pagrisaŋa, ti ale siti ka naapeerisa bayopɔi dan poom ka nidoaba naaniŋ a basi ba zuk. 6Ba ale pai gebika a nya Assiria tɛŋka zuk, abe ba dari gebik a yeeri fook po a nya Nimrod tɛŋka zuk. Wa ale vari ti a nyini Assiria demma nisa po a basi ase ba nin wɛ jo ti tɛŋka po a gɔk santiri va ti tɛŋ banaŋa po.
7Jekob nuru baai ale tali la ale bo nuru boari po ase maglim ale nyini Naawen jigi diila, abe ba ŋman nye ase ŋmoruk ale ni a basi wuuk zuk diila, ale kan limisi nuru yaase nurubiik zuk nyaka la. 8Jekob nuru baai ale a tali la ale bo ka tɛŋsaŋa po, nuru boari suŋsuŋ po ase gbeŋli ale bo gɔi po ale duŋsa diila, abe ba ŋman nye ase gbeŋ paali ale bo ale piisa a na ale dari a ŋasi nna bunabuna ate waai karo ale vari ŋa a basi la. 9Fi ale zagri fi nisaŋa ŋmai nakdeka po fi dachaasaŋa zuk, ate fi dachaasaŋa meena ale kaasi.
10Naawen ale a weeni ayen, <<Dai dila danni m le kaasi ni wusumaŋa ni suŋsuŋ, abe m ŋɔriŋ ni torokoma. 11M le kaasi ni tɛŋka tɛŋ ninaŋa abe m dari ni pagrimu ale bo juijui la meena a lɔnsi tɛŋ. 12M le kaasi ni sakpaŋni ate ni kan ŋman baga a tom sampoporinni. 13M le kaasi ni bɔgtaŋa ale ni tuilum tanaŋa ni suŋsuŋ. Ni kan ŋman koori tɛŋ a te ni nisa tuima. 14M le voori Asera zaŋŋa ni suŋsuŋ abe m kaasi ni tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa. 15Suipuurum po ate m le nye tuni tɛŋ kpieŋ sii meena ale kan wom mi la.>>

english_text:
The Lord's Challenge to His People
1The Lord said to his people:
Come and present your case
to the hills and mountains.
2Israel, I am bringing charges
against you—
I call upon the mountains
and the earth's firm foundation
to be my witnesses.
3My people, have I wronged you
in any way at all?
Please tell me.
4 I rescued you from Egypt,
where you were slaves.
I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
to be your leaders.
5 Don't forget the evil plans
of King Balak of Moab
or what Balaam son of Beor
said to him.
Remember how I, the Lord,
saved you many times
on your way from Acacia
to Gilgal.
True Obedience
6What offering should I bring
when I bow down to worship
the Lord God Most High?
Should I try to please him
by sacrificing
calves a year old?
7Will thousands of sheep
or rivers of olive oil
make God satisfied with me?
Should I sacrifice to the Lord
my first-born child as payment
for my terrible sins?
8The Lord God has told us
what is right
and what he demands:
“See that justice is done,
let mercy be your first concern,
and humbly obey your God.”
Cheating and Violence
9I am the Lord,
and you are wise to respect
my power to punish.
So listen to my message
for the city of Jerusalem:
10You store up stolen treasures
and use dishonest scales.
11But I, the Lord, will punish you
for cheating with weights
and with measures.
12You rich people are violent,
and everyone tells lies.
13Because of your sins,
I will wound you and leave you
ruined and defenseless.
14You will eat,
but still be hungry;
you will store up goods,
but lose everything—
I, the Lord, will let it all
be captured in war.
15You won't harvest what you plant
or use the oil
from your olive trees
or drink the wine
from grapes you grow.
16 Jerusalem, this will happen
because you followed
the sinful example
of kings Omri and Ahab.
Now I will destroy you
and your property.
Then the people of every nation
will make fun and insult you.
translation_text:
1Wom Naawen ale a weeni diila. <<Ni yiti zaani, ni weeni ni wanni ate guutaŋa wom. Ni basi ate pinaŋa a wom ni ale a yaali ayen ni weeni diila. 2Guutaŋa, ni wom, Naawen ale ta dii a weeni ayen ni nye kaasi la. Ni wom, nama tɛŋ nyuba ŋaai ale boro taam wuu la. Diila Naawen a ta ka wari ale wa nuruma. Wa pai ka wari a ta chaab ale Izirali.
3<<M nuruba, ka boan wari ate m pai nye ni? M te ni ka boan jiboa? Ni tulisi mu. 4M ta ni nyini Ejipiti ale ŋman da tuesi ni a nyini yɔntidi tɛŋ po. Mi jam tom Moosis ate wa dɛ ni niŋ, a ŋman tom Aaron ale Miriam. 5M nuruba, ni teeri Moab naawa Belak ale jam zɔk dii ayen wa nye la, ate Biio nidoabinni Balaam a jam tulisi diila. Ni teeri ni suiku chelimu a nyini Sittim a ga paari Gilgal ate ni baga a miŋ Naawen wayɔrisima tuimaŋa ale ka dii la.>>
6Ka boa ate m le ta jam Naawen niŋ abe m koori wenŋmazukku Wenni niŋŋa? M jam wa niŋ ale ben yeŋ naabisa juka tiirita? 7Naawen sui ale peenti ale padaasa tusa ale kpaam bela tusa pi (10,000)? M pai m bikpagni a nye kaabka m wabaataŋa nyiŋŋa, m le liŋ biak waai la m chiika biem nyiŋŋa?
8Nuru, wa sak fu ka dii ale nala la. Be ka boa ate Naawen a yaali a nyini fi jigi yaa? Fi nye a magsi abe fi a yaali jiirim abe fi yik fidek a cheŋ ale fi Wenni.
9Ni wom! Naawen a wi ka tɛŋ nummu, ate fi daa chali wa yuenni yɔgsum ka yam. <<Ni zuli tachekka ale waai ale lueri ka la. 10Gaasa yeri yaa, mi diem za m baŋ ni varuk ŋantaŋa ale ni ŋanmagsin gelaŋa ale ka kisuk la kama? 11M siak a te nuru waai ale ta venta ŋanmagsinta ale venta boorik kaai dobrim ale kan daa wensie la ayen ku magsi yaa? 12Wa nuru baai ale jigsi la ka wɔkwɔk nuruba. Wa nuruma ka velimvendisa ale a paasi nuruba. 13Dila nyiŋ m piilim kama ayen m kaasi fu, fi wabaataŋa nyiŋ. 14Fi ale dɛ alege fi kan chagi. Fi puuka ale chim ka pu koruk. Fi ale dueni ŋanta alege jaab a kan boro a te fu, dii nyiŋla fi ale a dueni ŋan baai la m le pai ŋa a te kpaliŋ po. 15Fi ale bori alege fi kan nya che. Fi ale ŋmiak kpaam alege fi kan pai bu a tom tuini. Fi ale ŋmiak yɔna alege fi kan nyu ŋa daamoa. 16Fi va ka Omri ŋmarisika ale Ayab yenni ale a nye dii meena la ale va ba ŋiak wieŋa. Dila nyiŋ m le kaasi ni, ate fi nuruma ale chim nuru valiŋsa. Tɛŋ kpieŋsa meena ale nye ni a la.>>

english_text:
Israel Is Corrupt
1I feel so empty inside—
like someone starving
for grapes or figs,
after the vines and trees
have all been picked clean.
2No one is loyal to God;
no one does right.
Everyone is brutal
and eager to deceive
everyone else.
3People cooperate to commit crime.
Judges and leaders demand bribes,
and rulers cheat in court.
4The most honest of them
is worse than a thorn patch.
Your doom has come!
Lookouts sound the warning,
and everyone panics.
5Don't trust anyone,
not even your best friend,
and be careful what you say
to the one you love.
6 Sons refuse to respect
their own fathers,
daughters rebel against
their own mothers,
and daughters-in-law despise
their mothers-in-law.
Your family is now your enemy.
7But I trust the Lord God
to save me,
and I will wait for him
to answer my prayer.
The Nation Turns to God
8My enemies, don't be glad
because of my troubles!
I may have fallen,
but I will get up;
I may be sitting in the dark,
but the Lord is my light.
9I have sinned against the Lord.
And so I must endure his anger,
until he comes to my defense.
But I know that I will see him
making things right for me
and leading me to the light.
10You, my enemies, said,
“The Lord God is helpless.”
Now each of you
will be disgraced
and put to shame.
I will see you trampled
like mud in the street.
A Bright Future
11Towns of Judah, the day is coming
when your walls will be rebuilt,
and your boundaries enlarged.
12People will flock to you
from Assyria and Egypt,
from Babylonia
and everywhere else.
13Those nations will suffer disaster
because of what they did.
Micah's Prayer and the Lord's Answer
14Lead your people, Lord!
Come and be our shepherd.
Grasslands surround us,
but we live in a forest.
So lead us to Bashan and Gilead,
and let us find pasture
as we did long ago.
15I, the Lord, will work miracles
just as I did when I led you
out of Egypt.
16Nations will see this
and be ashamed because
of their helpless armies.
They will be in shock,
unable to speak or hear,
17because of their fear of me,
your Lord and God.
Then they will come trembling,
crawling out of their fortresses
like insects or snakes,
lapping up the dust.
No One Is Like God
The people said:
18Our God, no one is like you.
We are all that is left
of your chosen people,
and you freely forgive
our sin and guilt.
You don't stay angry forever;
you're glad to have pity
19and pleased to be merciful.
You will trample on our sins
and throw them in the sea.
20You will keep your word
and be faithful to Jacob
and to Abraham,
as you promised our ancestors
many years ago.
translation_text:
1Niniga nuru ale mi! Mi a nye ase ka waai ale a yiisi yɔna kaduk po wenkarik diila. Yɔn saga a karo ate m le dɛ. Kinkama ŋaai ale kpabi a yɔni ate m ta koarisa ale ŋa la mɛ karo. 2Wensie nuruba a ka tɛŋka zuwa. Wanyi mɛ la an tali ya. Nuru meena kali kama a yaali kpaliŋ a pai ŋmiak a yik wa suok. 3Ba nisaŋa meena a korisi ale biem nyeka kama. Kpagni a yaali tiirita, ate waai ale a bo buusa la a tuesi ŋan baai ate ba pai a da wa la. Pagrɔma ale a sak ba ale a yaali jabuui la. Ba a nya ka chaab a tom ba tuimaŋa. 4Waai ale nala ba po la a nye ase ka wobi la, ate nuru maŋka ba po a gaam muŋ. Fi limisidɔma danni a paari ya, di danni ate Wen ale jam fi jigi la. Yɔgyɔgla de ale ba butimka dai. 5Kan ta mariŋka ale waai ale kali moata fu. Kan ta sebchakka ale fi doa. Poom le waai ale a duak fi nigoruk po. Be kpesi fi wieŋa a paari abe fi ge a biisi. 6Diila nidoabili a kan zuli wa ko, ate lie ale yiti a ta chaab ale wa ma, ate sampok ale yiti a ta chaab ale wa ŋiak nipok. Nuru dachiak a nyini ka wadek yeri po.
7Alege dan ka mi, m yiilaŋa a bo ka Naawen jigi. Mi a limisi ka Wen m varibasidɔwa. M Wenni ale wom mu.
8M dachiagaa, kan te fi sui a peenti ale m lueta. M dan poom lo, m le ŋman yiti. M dan poom kala legi po, Naawen ale chim m bolim. 9Dii nyiŋla m tom kaasi wa kama, ate ku magsi ayen m tu chaab ale wa suipuurumu, ate ku ga paari diipo ate wa le biisi te mu a ŋman nye mu a magsi la. Wa ale ta mu a nyini peelim ale bolim. M le nya wa wayɔrisimaŋa. 10Ate m dachiaka ale nya ate chivie a yik wa, ate waai ale jam weeni mi ayen, <<Naawen fi Wenni a boka be la?>> M ninaŋa ale nya wa lueta. Ba poom ŋaam tabi wa kama ase tantaŋa ale doa suiku po diila.
11Fi parisaŋa sɛka danni ale paari. Fi tɛŋ banaŋa lagrika danni a cheena. 12Dai dila danni nuruba ale nyini Assiria ale Ejipiti tɛŋ ninaŋa a ŋman nyini Ejipiti a ga paari Benni a jam fi jigi a nyini nyakpiem a ga paari nyakpiem, a nyini guuk a ga paari guuk. 13Tɛŋzuk de a doa koruk ka nuruma tuimaŋa nyiŋ.
14Pai fi tachekka a kasi fi nuruma. Duŋsaŋa ale fi nitalim ate si dek a bo gɔi tɛŋ maŋka ate wuyɔgsuk a boro la. Basi ate si a dɛ Basan ale Gilead ase dila po wa la.
15<<M le sak ni m wakinkaglaŋa ase diipo ate ni jam nyini Ejipiti a jam la.>>
16Tɛŋ kpieŋsa ale nya ate chivie a yik ba, ate ba pagrimu ale yalima ale ba. Ba ale pai ba nisa a vi ba noaŋa zuk ate ba tueŋa ale kpari. 17Ba ale leeli tanta ase waab la, abe ba kuuk tɛŋ ase duŋsaŋa la. Ba le nyini ba diinaŋa po ale kpazinagsuk. Ba ale viriŋ cheŋ Naawen ti Wenni jigi ale kpazinagsuk ate ba ale chali fu. 18Wen dina ale a nye ase fi la, ate fi a vɔŋ fi nuru baai ale tali boro la wabaata ale ba nye kaasuŋ a te ba? Fi sui a kan puuri gaam a taam, dii nyiŋ la fi kasim a yaali ŋmanteka kama. 19Fi ale ŋman ta jiirim ale ti. Fi ale tabi ti wabaataŋa zuk abe fi yuk ti biemu meena a basi nyakpiemu liuŋku po. 20Fi ale ta wensie ale Jekob, abe fi sak ŋmanteka ale Abrayam ase fi ale jam puulim a te ti koma dipo diila.

english_text:
1 I am Nahum from Elkosh. And this is the message that I wrote down about Nineveh.
The Fierce Anger of the Lord
2The Lord God demands loyalty.
In his anger, he takes revenge
on his enemies.
3The Lord is powerful,
yet patient;
he makes sure that the guilty
are always punished.
He can be seen in storms
and in whirlwinds;
clouds are the dust from his feet.
4At the Lord's command,
oceans and rivers dry up.
Bashan, Mount Carmel,
and Lebanon wither,
and their flowers fade.
5At the sight of the Lord,
mountains and hills
tremble and melt;
the earth and its people
shudder and shake.
6Who can stand the heat
of his furious anger?
It flashes out like fire
and shatters stones.
The Power of Assyria Will Be Broken
7The Lord is good.
He protects those who trust him
in times of trouble.
8But like a roaring flood,
the Lord chases his enemies
into dark places
and destroys them.
9So don't plot against the Lord!
He wipes out his enemies,
and they never revive.
10They are like drunkards
overcome by wine,
or like twisted thornbushes
burning in a fire.
11Assyria, one of your rulers
has made evil plans
against the Lord.
12But the Lord says, “Assyria,
no matter how strong you are,
you will be cut down!
My people Judah,
I have troubled you before,
but I won't do it again.
13I'll snap your chains
and set you free
from the Assyrians.”
14Assyria, this is what else
the Lord says to you:
“Your name will be forgotten.
I will destroy every idol
in your temple,
and I will send you to the grave,
because you are worthless.”
15 Look toward the mountains,
people of Judah!
Here comes a messenger
with good news of peace.
Celebrate your festivals.
Keep your promises to God.
Your evil enemies are destroyed
and will never again
invade your country.
translation_text:
1Nayum ale nyini Elkos tɛŋka la ale nya wanni de a magsi chaab ale Niineve tɛŋka.
2Naawen ka nyuri dɛka Wen a kan yaali ŋaan chaaba. Naawen a namsi baai meena ale ka wa dachaasa la kama. Naawen suinni dan puuri wa a tuni ba kama. 3Naawen sui a kan kpabi a puuri, alege ta pagrim a kan basi baai ale nye kaasi la namsika. Juijui ate Naawen a cheŋ la, va pagrik ale a yiti. Chiŋmaaŋa ka nyuŋ a yiti wa naŋsa po. 4Wa dan na biisi nyakpiemu a kpeeri kama. Wa basi kama ate belaŋa a kpeeri. Basan tɛŋsaŋa ale Karmel guuku a ko ka chekchek ale Lebanon wuutaŋa ale ti puutaŋa a kpi meena. 5Guuta a choa Naawen niŋ. Gu tii meena ale jueli a nyaliŋ Naawen niŋ. Naawen a dan na nyini tɛŋka a choa kama ate tɛŋka meena nuruma nyiŋsa a gɔk. 6Wa sui a dan puuri ka wana le wa vuugi? Ka wana le wa lati ale wa suipuurumu nna? Wa suinni kasim a yiti ase ka bolim ŋiak la, ate pina a mobi wa niŋ.
7Naawen a nala ale a lik wa nuruma daanika po. Baai ale pilim a jam wa jigi la wa a nya ba zuk kama. 8Wa nyiem deri kaasi wa dachaasaŋa kama ase nyiam ale tagli jigi meena a pai nna pilim pilim la. Wa le vi wa dachaasaŋa a ga ko ba meena.
9Ka boa ate ni a zɔk ayen ni tu chaab ale Naawen yaa? Wa le kaasi ni. Nuru karo a daani wa a saari buye. 10Wa le ju ni ase munsa ale wukosik la. 11Nuru ale nyini Niineve ale popola baata a kisi Naawen ale ta gaasa sinsaga.
12Naawen ale weeni dii a te Juda demma la ale nna, <<Assiria demma a dan poom pagra ale piisi m le kaasi ba ate ba muriŋ bɛ. Nama mi dek nuruma m namsi ni kama alege m kan nye di ŋmana. 13Assiria ale ta pagrim buui ni zuk la, m le kpeglim bu abe m gebi chɔrima ŋaai ale bobi ni la.
14Naawen ale weeni dii dueni a magsi Niineve la ale nna, <<Ba kan nya ŋaaŋsa ate ba diem ta ba yuenni. M le kaasi ba bɔgtaŋa ale bo ni wenaŋa yenni po la. M boro a gomsi ka vɔrup a magsi Assiria demma. Ba an magsi boka.>>
15A nya, nuru ale nyini guutaŋa zuk a cheena ale wa paala. Wa bo ka suik cheena ayen wa mooli nak dɛka. Juda demma, ni a dɛ ni tiŋŋa abe ni pai jabuui ate ni puulim ayen ni te wa la a te. Nye ka tuem nyama a kan ŋman tuesi ni tɛŋka. M kaasi ba ka meena.

english_text:
Nineveh Will Fall
1Nineveh, someone is coming
to attack and scatter you.
Guard your fortresses!
Watch the road! Be brave!
Prepare for battle!
2Judah and Israel are like trees
with branches broken
by their enemies.
But the Lord is going to restore
their power and glory.
* 3Nineveh, on this day of attack,
your enemies' shields are red;
their uniforms are crimson.
4Their horses prance,
and their armored chariots
dart around like lightning
or flaming torches.
5An officer gives a command.
But his soldiers stumble,
as they hasten to build
a shelter to protect themselves
against rocks thrown down
from the city wall.
6The river gates fly open,
and panic floods the palace.
7Nineveh is disgraced.
The queen is dragged off.
Her servant women mourn;
they moan like doves,
and they beat their breasts
in sorrow.
8Nineveh is like a pond
with leaking water.
Shouts of “Stop! Don't go!”
can be heard everywhere.
But everyone is leaving.
9Enemy soldiers shout,
“The city is full of treasure
and all kinds of wealth.
Steal her silver! Grab her gold!”
10Nineveh is doomed! Destroyed!
Her people tremble with fear;
their faces turn pale.
11What happened to this city?
They were safer there
than powerful lions in a den,
with no one to disturb them.
12These are the same lions
that ferociously attacked
their victims,
then dragged away the flesh
to feed their young.
13The Lord All-Powerful
is against you, Nineveh.
God will burn your chariots
and send an army to kill
those young lions of yours.
You will never again
make victims of others
or send messengers to threaten
everyone on this earth.
translation_text:
1Nama Niineve demma kaasirɔwa cheena ayen wa siti ni. Pagrim buui ale bu kaasi ni la a jam ya. Ni lik ŋan kasintaŋa. Ni kasi suiku. Ni gomsi magsi kpaliŋ.
2Naawen a yaali wa ŋman te Izirali zulaŋa kama ase ba le jam ka dii alege ate ba dachaasaŋa a yik ba la. 3Dachaasaŋa a jam ta ka ŋanchɔgsin mɔnta ale jo garuk mɔnta. Ba gomsi kama ayen ba choa ba. Ba torokoma a nyaksi ase ka bolim la. Ba wusumaŋa a yɔk namaga. 4Torokoma a chali tɛŋka suitaŋa po a cheŋ niŋ ale ŋaaŋ tɛŋka gugorutaŋa po. A nyaksi ase bolim ale a nye nna yilibi yilibi ase bolim ale a kamsi la.
5Ba wi ba kpaŋŋa kama ate baa cheŋ niŋ geŋ ale a nak naŋsa a lo. Tugurik tɔŋdɔma a chali ga parika jigini ayen ba kasi ŋan baai ba a yuk la. 6Nansuiŋ tii ale bo benni jigini la a lagri Naawa yenni po niniga nyiini ale sueri. 7Nipok naawa ba yik ate wa yɔmma a kum ase nangbaŋsa la a nak ba kuusa ale niniga. 8Niineve demma a daa chali kama ase mɔgi ale ŋɔsi la. Ba yaa kaari ayen, basi basi, alege waai an viriŋ ŋaaŋŋa. 9Ni vari kpanaŋa. Ni vari ligmɔniŋka. Tɛŋka jigsi kama ale ŋanta. 10Niineve a kaasi kama a dua. Ate nuruma nyiŋsa a gɔk ate ba duna a nak chaab, pagrim a bɛ. Ate nimbidaasa a peenti.
11Tɛŋ kaai ale jam a nye ase gbeŋma boka jigi la a boka be yɔgla, juijui ate gbeŋma bisa a dɛ ŋandiinta la, juijui ate gbeŋduata ale gbeŋniima a cheŋ ate jaab a kan nye ŋa bisaŋa wari la? 12Gbeŋli a ko ka lanta yega a te di bisaŋa ale di vaanchoawa, ale sueri di boka jigini ale lanta.
13Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La yaa weeni ayen, <<Mi ka ni dachiak. M le ju ni torokoma. Ba le ko ni tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpaliŋ po abe m tuesi jaab meena ate ni tuesi nuru yonta jigi la. Ba kan ŋman wom baai ate ni a tom la luelita.>>

english_text:
Punishment for Nineveh
The Lord said:
1Doom to the crime capital!
Nineveh, city of murder
and treachery,
2here is your fate—
cracking whips,
churning wheels;
galloping horses,
roaring chariots;
3cavalry attacking,
swords and spears flashing;
soldiers stumbling
over piles of dead bodies.
4You were nothing more
than a prostitute
using your magical charms
and witchcraft
to attract and trap nations.
5But I, the Lord All-Powerful,
am now your enemy.
I will pull up your skirt
and let nations and kingdoms
stare at your nakedness.
6I will cover you with garbage,
treat you like trash,
and rub you in the dirt.
7Everyone who sees you
will turn away and shout,
“Nineveh is done for!
Is anyone willing to mourn
or to give her comfort?”
Nineveh's Fate Is Sealed
8Nineveh, do you feel safer
than the city of Thebes?
The Nile River
was its wall of defense.
9Thebes trusted the mighty power
of Ethiopia and Egypt;
the nations of Put and Libya
were her allies.
10But she was captured and taken
to a foreign country.
Her children were murdered
at every street corner.
The members of her royal family
were auctioned off,
and her high officials
were bound in chains.
11Nineveh, now it's your turn!
You will get drunk and try to hide
from your enemy.
12Your fortresses are fig trees
with ripe figs.
Merely shake the trees,
and fruit will fall
into every open mouth.
13Your army is weak.
Fire has destroyed the crossbars
on your city gates;
now they stand wide open
to your enemy.
14Your city is under attack.
Haul in extra water!
Strengthen your defenses!
Start making bricks!
Stir the mortar!
15You will still go up in flames
and be cut down by swords
that will wipe you out like a field
attacked by grasshoppers.
So, go ahead and increase
like a swarm of locusts!
16More merchants are in your city
than there are stars
in the sky—
but they are like locusts
that eat everything,
then fly away.
17Your guards and your officials
are swarms of locusts.
On a chilly day
they settle on a fence,
but when the sun comes out,
they take off
to who-knows-where.
18King of Assyria,
your officials and leaders
are sound asleep,
while your people are scattered
in the mountains.
Yes, your people are sheep
without a shepherd.
19You're fatally wounded.
There's no hope for you.
But everyone claps
when they hear this news,
because your constant cruelty
has caused them pain.
translation_text:
1Ku le bie te Niineve tɛŋka diila ba ko ka nuruba yega. Ka ka venta nyiini alege zu tɛŋ yonsa ŋanta. Ka kasim a ko kama. 2A wom finsaŋa miirika ale torokoma naŋsaŋa nuemka. Wom wusumaŋa ale yɔk a tabi la ale torokoma ale dari a nuem la. 3Wusuma nyiŋsa a toariŋ ate gebik woŋsa a nyaksi ate gbatta mɛ a nyaksi. Nuruba yega ale kpi a vi chaab zuk a ka chiina. Ate nuruba a tabi ba zuk a lo a yiti. 4Tɛŋka a nye ka nna ase nipok kaasuŋ la. A yaali porisika ale a nye nuruba ale tiita. A pai ka kaasuŋ nyeka ale sakpaŋni a basi ate tɛŋsa a chim ka yɔm.
5Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni ayen, <<Mi ta ka chaab ale ni, nama Niineve demma. M le nye ni gattaŋa a ta jueli lik ni ninaŋa a pai ni chaboalaŋa a sak tɛŋsaŋa ate si nya ni chivieŋa. 6M le nye ni m kan sak zula abe m lik ni ale daŋta ate nuruba kasim a nya ni. 7Waai meena a dan nya ni ba le yiti a chali abe ba a weeni ayen, <Niineve a kaasi ya.> Ka wana le wa kum ka nyiŋŋa? Niineve demma, mi ale nya ka wana ate wa nye ate ni sue yɔk.>>
8Ni an zunchoŋ Tebes tɛŋka ale moata Nile benni ate nyiam gilim ka la. Nyiamu, ale jam kasi ka. Nyiamu jam a nye ase ka parik la gilim ka. 9Kus ale Ejipiti a te ba pagrim buui ale kaa nueri. Put ale Libia mɛ a maa maari ka. 10Alege ba yik Tebes demma ate ba ga bo tɛŋ yoŋ. Ba bimbaan fiisaŋa ba nak ba ko dueni suitaŋa niŋsa. Ba niŋdeerɔma ba yik ba ale chɔrima a ta cheŋ. 11Niineve demma ni le nyu daam buk. Ni le suk. Ni le gisi yaali jigi ayen dachaasaŋa kan nya ni.
12Ni ŋan kasintaŋa meena a nye ase kinkaŋsa ale ta moota la. Ba dan zaŋ tiimu, yɔnaŋa deri lo dɛɛrɔwa nɔi po. 13Ni nya ni tugurik tɔŋdɔma. Ba meena ka nipooba. Ni tɛŋka tuataŋa a lak kama a magsi ayen dachaasaŋa a jo. Bolim a dɛ ni tuataŋa daataŋa.
14Ni ŋari nyiam zuak alege ti kpaliŋ le za ka beni la piilim. Ni basi ate ni ŋan kasintaŋa a pagra. Ni yaali yak a dam ni tanta a nak peela. 15Dula jigini bolimu ale dɛ ni. Gebika ale ko ni. Kpaliŋka ale ko ni ka meena ase nanchoŋta ale dɛ ŋanta vaata diila. Ni be piisi yega ase nanchoŋta ale yɔk a cheŋ. Ni piisi yega ase tintue la. 16Ni geruŋdɔma a piisi a gaam chiŋmarisaŋa ale bo wenzukku la kama, alege a nye ase tintue la, a dɛ jaab meena ale yiti cheŋ. 17Ni limisidɔma a nye ase ka tintue la a bo saasaŋa nyiŋ da di dai ate ku yɔk la. Alege kantueŋka a dan jam ŋa yiti cheŋ ate waai zɛ ŋa le ga juijui la.
18Assiria naaba, fi kpaŋŋa kpi kama ate fi nuru baai ale ta zula la a goa takakaka. Fi nuruma a waaŋ bo guutaŋa zuima ate waai karo a ta ba a jam yeri ŋmana. 19Ni le kɔni ale nya tueta la tebika karo ate ni a nya nyiŋyɔgsa. Baai meena le wom ni tɛŋka kaasika la a nak ka nichaala a naŋ diila waai meena ku jo wa nyiŋ kama ale ni nyeka tuemu ale kaa nueri la.

english_text:
1I am Habakkuk the prophet. And this is the message that the Lord gave me.
Habakkuk Complains to the Lord
2Our Lord, how long must I beg
for your help
before you listen?
How long before you save us
from all this violence?
3Why do you make me watch
such terrible injustice?
Why do you allow violence,
lawlessness, crime, and cruelty
to spread everywhere?
4Laws cannot be enforced;
justice is always the loser;
criminals crowd out honest people
and twist the laws around.
The Lord Answers Habakkuk
5 Look and be amazed
at what's happening
among the nations!
Even if you were told,
you would never believe
what's taking place now.
6 I am sending the Babylonians.
They are fierce and cruel—
marching across the land,
conquering cities and towns.
7How fearsome and frightening.
Their only laws and rules
are the ones they make up.
8Their cavalry troops are faster
than leopards,
more ferocious than wolves
hunting at sunset,
and swifter than hungry eagles
suddenly swooping down.
9They are eager to destroy,
and they gather captives
like handfuls of sand.
10They make fun of rulers
and laugh at fortresses,
while building dirt mounds
so they can capture cities.
11Then suddenly they disappear
like a gust of wind—
those sinful people who worship
their own strength.
Habakkuk Complains Again
12Holy Lord God, mighty rock,
you are eternal,
and we are safe from death.
You are using those Babylonians
to judge and punish others.
13But you can't stand sin or wrong.
So don't sit by in silence
while they gobble up people
who are better than they are.
14The people you put on this earth
are like fish or reptiles
without a leader.
15Then an enemy comes along
and takes them captive
with hooks and nets.
It makes him so happy
16that he offers sacrifices
to his fishing nets,
because they make him rich
and provide choice foods.
17Will he keep hauling in his nets
and destroying nations
without showing mercy?
translation_text:
1Wa dii ate Naawen a pai sak wa biisiteerɔwa Yabakkuk la, 2Naawen, mi ale saalim fi soa ka sɛ a weeni ayen fi maari ti alege ate fi yaa wom? Ku le beni ka sɛ alege ate fi vari ti gaasaŋa dɛ po basi? 3Ka boa ale soa ate fi basi ate mi a nya daanika de meena? Ka boa ale soa ate fi a nya nye kaasika de meena? Kaasuŋ ale gaasa ale kasim gilim mu, ate kpaliŋ ale nanpaga kasim bo jigi meena. 4Sinsaŋŋa ŋman ka kiriya, ŋa kan ŋma tomu, wensie tuima ka. Nuru baataŋa a goanti a nya badek alege nuru maŋsaŋa a lo ate boteerɔma kan bo buusa a magsi.
5Ate Naawen yaa weeni wa nuruma ayen, <<Ni a nya tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa ale gilim ni la. Ni le a nya diila le cha ni. M le za m nye diila ni kan siagi ase ni nin poom wom. 6Kaldiya demma baai nyeka ale toa nna yegayega la, m le te ba pagrim. Ba gɔk ka santiri a diak a nak tɛŋ kpieŋsa ale tɛŋ fiisa a cheŋ. 7Ba kasim a nyigsi ka nuruba. Ba a nyeka ba le a yaali diila. Ba le ba kanjantaŋa ba chim nuru maŋsa te ka badek. 8Ba wusumaŋa a korisi gaam yɔŋma ate ŋa nyeka mɛ toa ase kom ale ta piina la. Ba wusum duerisaŋa nyiem deri jam diiri kama. Ba nyini ka niŋniŋŋa. Ba nyiem jam diiri kama ase jiiruk ale diiri jaab diila. 9Ba meena jam ka kpaliŋ. Jaab karo a kasi ba. Ba ligrɔma a piisi ase ka tintain busuŋ la. 10Ba a la nalima kama ale a nye kpaga a la. Ba a la tɛŋ sii meena ale ta pari pagrisa a gilim ba la Kama. Ba nyiem dueni ka tanta a jueli paari noawaaŋa a jo yik ba. 11Ate ba yaa boro ase viok la a cheŋ. Nuru ba tii ale a zuli badek pagrim la.>>
12Naawen yaa, fi ka Naawen a nyini piilimka po meena. Fi ka m Wen, a Welema ale ka kpeglimka. Ti kan kpi. Naawen yaa m ligrɔ, fi ale lueri Kaldiya demma a te ba pagrim ayen ba namsi ti. 13Fi be welema ka yega ale biem nyaka. Fi kan baga a nya baai ale tom a kaasi la. Dila nyiŋ fi le nye ka sɛ a nye ale biem nyama? Fi le nye ka sɛ sina ate ba a ko baai ale diem chim nuru maŋsa a gaam ba la? 14Fi a nye nuruba nna se ka jumaŋa ale bo nyiamu po la, nna se ŋan baai ale bo nyiam po a ka niŋdeerɔ la. 15Kaldiya demma a yik nuruba ale ka goatisa ase juma la. A yaa dari ale ba ŋmaasaŋa ale a kaari ale suipeentik ba le yik la. 16Ba poom a zuli ba ŋmaasaŋa kama ale a kaab si, si ale a te ba dii meena ate ba a yaali la. 17Ba le kasim pai ba gebisaŋa a kaasi tɛŋsaŋa kama a cheŋ alege kan sak jiirimmoa?

english_text:
The Lord Answers Habakkuk Again
1While standing guard
on the watchtower,
I waited for the Lord's answer,
before explaining the reason
for my complaint.
2Then the Lord told me:
“I will give you my message
in the form of a vision.
Write it clearly enough
to be read at a glance.
3 At the time I have decided,
my words will come true.
You can trust what I say
about the future.
It may take a long time,
but keep on waiting—
it will happen!
4 “I, the Lord, refuse to accept
anyone who is proud.
Only those who live by faith
are acceptable to me.”
Trouble for Evil People
5Wine is treacherous,
and arrogant people
are never satisfied.
They are no less greedy
than death itself—
they open their mouths as wide
as the world of the dead
and swallow everyone.
6But they will be mocked
with these words:
You're doomed!
You stored up stolen goods
and cheated others
of what belonged to them.
7But without warning,
those you owe
will demand payment.
Then you will become
a frightened victim.
8You robbed cities and nations
everywhere on earth
and murdered their people.
Now those who survived
will be as cruel to you.
9You're doomed!
You made your family rich
at the expense of others.
You even said to yourself,
“I'm above the law.”
10But you will bring shame
on your family
and ruin to yourself
for what you did to others.
11The very stones and wood
in your home
will testify against you.
12You're doomed! You built a city
on crime and violence.
13 But the Lord All-Powerful
sends up in flames
what nations and people
work so hard to gain.
14 Just as water fills the sea,
the land will be filled
with people who know
and honor the Lord.
15You're doomed!
You get your friends drunk,
just to see them naked.
16Now you will be disgraced
instead of praised.
The Lord will make you drunk,
and when others see you naked,
you will lose their respect.
17You destroyed trees and animals
on Mount Lebanon;
you were ruthless to towns
and people everywhere.
Now you will be terrorized.
Idolatry Is Foolish
18What is an idol worth?
It's merely a false god.
Why trust a speechless image
made from wood or metal
by human hands?
19What can you learn from idols
covered with silver or gold?
They can't even breathe.
Pity anyone who says to an idol
of wood or stone,
“Get up and do something!”
20Let all the world be silent—
the Lord is present
in his holy temple.
translation_text:
1Mi ale jueli ka gboŋ a za ase limisidɔ la a limisi ate m nya Naawen ale wa weeni mu diila ale wa le wa tulisi m funfɔblaŋa diila.
2Naawen yaa tulisi mi a weeni ayen, <<Ŋmarisi dii ate fi nya la dueni. Ŋmarisi cheri a dueni tintain paglak nyiŋ ate waai dek ale a karim la a chali ga weeni ba gela. 3Ku an diem paari diipo ate wanni ale chim wensie la, alege ku cheena ate wanni a chim wensie. Ku a nye ase ku a beni kama la, alege yik fidek a limisi, dii nyiŋla ku le sum jam, ku kan beni.
4<<Kanjanta nyɔnɔ nyeelaŋa an nala alege wayɔrisima nyɔnɔwa a vuuk kama wa siaka nyiŋ. 5Daam ale baga a paasi nuru la, wabaata nyama a kan benni, diila ba a yaali ŋanta ase ka vɔrup ale a yaali kum diila, kum abe kasim a yaali ka kpieba yega. Ba tigsi tɛŋsaŋa meena nuruma a ta jam jigi yeŋ a ta ba.
6<<Alege tɛŋ sii meena ate Kaldiya a basi ate ko jo ba nyiŋla ale cheem la ba. Ba le nye ba a la abe ba a weeni ayen ku le bie te baai ale a zu ŋanta yegayega la. Tɛŋ kala demma ate ba jigsi a paari ka dimpo a fɛ nuruba ayen ba a tuni ba? 7Dai yeŋ nuru baai ate ni a tuesi ligra ba jigi la ale tulim ta chaab ale ni. Ba le miŋ dii meena ale a nye la a basi ate yɔgsum yik ni ate ni nyiŋsa a gɔk. Ate ba yaa tuesi jaab meena ate ni ta la. 8Ni be le zu tɛŋsa yegayega la, baai ale tali la ale tuesi yegayega ni jigi. Dii nyiŋla ni ko nuruba yega a kaasi tɛŋ kpieŋsa ale nuru baai meena ale bo si po la.
9<<Ku le ku bie dii ale tɛŋ kaai ale va biem nyiŋ a jigsi la, ale a poli ayen ba le bo kauk kuui ate ba nyini biem po la. 10Ni be le a zɔk ayen ni ko nuruba yega la ni nye kama ate chivie a yik nidek dɔkdemma. Dila nyiŋ ni le jɔk ni nyuvooŋa. 11Saasaŋa tintanaŋa ale kaari a weeni ayen ni an nye magsi ya, da pilintaŋa ale siak ayen ni nye kaasi kama.
12<<Tɛŋ kaai ale a ko nuruba ayen ba va dila nyiŋ a sɛ ba tɛŋka la, ku le bie ba jigi, ale nye nuru yonta a kaasi, ayen ba piilim ba tɛŋka la. 13Naawen dii ale ka Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋdeerɔ ale basi ate bolim jam kaasi ba le se ŋan baai meena la, ate ba tuimaŋa meena a chim kinla. 14Ate nya kpiem ale taari lik dua ate ba a nya diila, nuruba ale bo jigi meena la ale nya Naawen zulaŋa ale wa nalimu.
15<<Tɛŋ kaai nuruba ale a basi ate ba chaab a nyu daam a buk la ku le bie ba jigi, a kasim a kpiiri bu daam yuini po a te ate ba ga buk ate ba yaa a nya ba chaboala la. 16Nama Kaldiya demma chivie ale yik ni chekki, ni kan nya zula. Ku tulim jam kama ayen nama mɛ nyu buk lo tɛŋ ase da bugrik la. Suipuurum beerika ale bo Naawen juga nisa po la cheen ni jigi. Ni le tuesi chivie, daa zula. 17Ni te ti ku jo nuruba nyiŋ Lebanon po, alege yɔgyɔgla de ku le jo nama mɛ nyiŋ. Ni che tiisaŋa meena ale ko duŋsa yegayega dula, yɔgyɔgla de yɔgsum le yik ni dii ate ni nye tɛŋ kala ale ka tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa, ale nuruma ale bo si po la.
18<<Bɔgluk a kan nye wamaŋa, diila nurubiik ale nye ku, ku ka jameem buui ale a sak venta. Waai ale nye ku la a ta sebchakka kama ayen wadek tuini maari wa, alege wa a nye ka bɔgluk tii ale kan poom a biisi. 19Waai ale a weeni bɔgluk ate ba nye ale diok la, ayen vari mu a basi la, ku le bie wa jigi. Waai ale a weeni tintain ayen yiti ŋmai la, ku le bie wa jigi. Di an baga a weeni fi le fi nye dii ya. Ka jaab kama ate ba pai ligmɔniŋ ale kpana nye lik ku nyiŋka, nyuvuri ka ku po. 20Naawen a bo ka wa yenni po, tɛŋka nuruma meena nye diki wa niŋ.>>

english_text:
Habakkuk's Prayer
1This is my prayer:
2I know your reputation, Lord,
and I am amazed
at what you have done.
Please turn from your anger
and be merciful;
do for us what you did
for our ancestors.
3You are the same Holy God
who came from Teman
and Paran to help us.
The brightness of your glory
covered the heavens,
and your praises were heard
everywhere on earth.
4Your glory shone like the sun,
and light flashed from your hands,
hiding your mighty power.
5Dreadful diseases and plagues
marched in front
and followed behind.
6When you stopped,
the earth shook;
when you stared,
nations trembled;
when you walked
along your ancient paths,
eternal mountains and hills
crumbled and collapsed.
7The tents of desert tribes
in Cushan and Midian
were ripped apart.
8Our Lord, were you angry
with the monsters
of the deep?
You attacked in your chariot
and wiped them out.
9Your arrows were ready
and obeyed your commands.
You split the earth apart
with rivers and streams;
10mountains trembled
at the sight of you;
rain poured from the clouds;
ocean waves roared and rose.
11The sun and moon stood still,
while your arrows and spears
flashed like lightning.
12In your furious anger,
you trampled on nations
13to rescue your people
and save your chosen one.
You crushed a nation's ruler
and stripped his evil kingdom
of its power.
14His troops had come like a storm,
hoping to scatter us
and glad to gobble us up.
To them we were refugees
in hiding—
but you smashed their heads
with their own weapons.
15Then your chariots churned
the waters of the sea.
Habakkuk's Response to God's Message
16When I heard this message,
I felt weak from fear,
and my lips quivered.
My bones seemed to melt,
and I stumbled around.
But I will patiently wait.
Someday those vicious enemies
will be struck by disaster.
Trust in a Time of Trouble
17Fig trees may no longer bloom,
or vineyards produce grapes;
olive trees may be fruitless,
and harvest time a failure;
sheep pens may be empty,
and cattle stalls vacant—
18but I will still celebrate
because the Lord God
is my Savior.
19 The Lord gives me strength.
He makes my feet as sure
as those of a deer,
and he helps me stand
on the mountains.
To the music director:
Use stringed instruments.
translation_text:
1Puusa ŋaai ate Naawen biisiteerɔwa Yabakkuk a puusi la ale nna, 2Naawen, mi wom fi wie kama. Fi le nye diila a cha mu kama. Naawen nye wa kpiema ŋmana tama daaŋa po, basi ate wa ŋala ŋman nye tama daaŋa po. Fi sui dan poom a puuri, be teeri a ta jiirim.
3Naawen a nyini Teman a cheena, Weleŋsa Nyɔnɔwa a nyini Paran Guuku zuk cheena. Wa zulaŋa ale nalimu a lik wenŋmazukku ate wa pimpaukku a sueri tɛŋka. 4Wa a nye ase ka bolim la nna cha. Bolim ale a nyaksi wa nisa po nna ziriziri, ate wa yaa suk wa pagrimu dula. 5Nyiŋtuila ale dɛ wa niŋ a cheŋ ate tueta a bo wa ŋaaŋ a vi. 6Wa za kama a choa tɛŋka. A nya ate tɛŋsaŋa a choa ale a chali yɔgsum Guuk tii ale dua nyini diipo la a waaŋ buk buk, Guuk kpagsaŋa a lo tɛŋ. Ka Naawen le kasim a nye nna. 7Mi yaa nya Kusan nuruma ale Midian nuruma nyiŋsa kasim a gɔk.
8Naawen yaa, ka fi sui ale a puuri ale beli kpiemaŋa yaa fi sui ale a puuri ale beli fiisaŋa? Ka fi sui ale jam a puuri ale nyakpiemu ate fi do wusumaŋa ale ŋa torokoma a nya nakdeka la? 9Fi basi ate ba nya fi tomu alege ayen ba ta peema yega jam te fu. Fi poori tɛŋka kama ale bela. 10Guutaŋa nya fu kama a choa ale yɔgsum. Nyaataŋa a chali a cheŋ. Nyakpiemu a wuuri a nuem ate nya miisaŋa a yiti a jueli wen.
11Wenbinni ale chiika deri wari za wenzukku; ba le nya fi tɔŋ peemaŋa ate ŋa nyaksi a cheŋ la, ale fi gbaluku ale nyaksi a cheŋ la, ba deri wari za. 12Suipuurum nyiŋ ate fi tabi tɛŋka zuk a taam, suipuurum nyiŋ ate fi namsi tɛŋsaŋa. 13Fi nyini kama ayen fi vari fi nuruma basi, fi vari baai ate fi lueri la. Fi ŋɔriŋ wabaata nyama niŋdeerɔwa kama alege tuesi wa le ta ŋan baai la, A zaani wa zuk ta siŋ paari wa naŋsa. 14Fi pai dachiaka dek gbaluku a chub wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma niŋdeerɔwa. Wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma vuri kama nyini ase vamuniŋ la ayen ba choa ti waaŋ. Ba sui jam peenti kama ba le suk a zu ŋanjaksaŋa la. 15Alege fi tabi va nyakpiemu po ale fi wusumaŋa a damu nya kpientaŋa.
16Mi yaa wom wieŋa de ate m nyiŋka a gɔk, m le wom la m nɔnni a gɔk. M kobaŋa po a kpi nna limalima, ate m naŋsaŋa a gɔk. Alege m chiibi kama a limisi da dii danni ate kaasuŋ a cheena nuru baai ale a namsi ti la zuk la.
17Kinkaŋsa baga kama a kan yɔni kinkama, ate yɔna buuri a kan bo tiisa naŋsa nyiŋŋa, ate ŋandiinta kan bo kaduksaŋa po. Ate piisa a kan bo zoŋtaŋa po, ate niiga mɛ a kan bo nankpieŋsaŋa po. 18Alege dila meena m sui le diem peenti ale Naawen. M sui ale peenti ale Wen m Varibasidɔwa. 19Nyɔnɔwa Naawen ka m pagrim. Wa basi ate mi a nye ase ka walik ale ka a nak naŋ a lo diila, ate m baga a cheŋ guuta zuima. Ku cheŋ waai ale a nya yiilaŋa zuk la jigi. Puusaŋa de a cheŋ ale ka kpanta buuri.

english_text:
1 I am Zephaniah, the son of Cushi, the grandson of Gedaliah, the great-grandson of Amariah, and the great-great-grandson of Hezekiah.
When Josiah son of Amon was king of Judah, the Lord gave me this message.
Judgment on Judah
2I, the Lord, now promise
to destroy everything
on this earth—
3people and animals,
birds and fish.
Everyone who is evil
will crash to the ground,
and I will wipe out
the entire human race.
4I will reach out to punish
Judah and Jerusalem—
nothing will remain
of the god Baal;
