nothing will be remembered
of his pagan priests.
5Not a trace will be found
of those who worship stars
from their rooftops,
or bow down to the god Milcom,
while claiming loyalty
to me, the Lord.
6Nothing will remain of anyone
who has turned away
and rejected me.
7Be silent! I am the Lord God,
and the time is near.
I am preparing
to sacrifice my people
and to invite my guests.
8On that day I will punish
national leaders
and sons of the king,
along with all who follow
foreign customs.
9I will punish worshipers
of pagan gods
and cruel palace officials
who abuse their power.
10I, the Lord, promise
that on that day
noisy crying will be heard
from Fish Gate, New Town,
and Upper Hills.
11Everyone in Lower Hollow
will mourn loudly,
because merchants
and money changers
will be wiped out.
12I'll search Jerusalem with lamps
and punish those people
who sit there unworried
while thinking,
“The Lord won't do anything,
good or bad.”
13Their possessions will be taken,
their homes left in ruins.
They won't get to live
in the houses they build,
or drink wine from the grapes
in their own vineyards.
A Terrible Day
14The great day of the Lord
is coming soon, very soon.
On that terrible day,
fearsome shouts of warriors
will be heard everywhere.
15It will be a time of anger—
of trouble and torment,
of disaster and destruction,
of darkness and despair,
of storm clouds and shadows,
16of trumpet calls
and battle cries
against fortified cities
and mighty fortresses.
17The Lord warns everyone
who has sinned against him,
“I'll strike you blind!
Then your blood and your insides
will gush out like vomit.
18Not even your silver or gold
can save you on that day
when I, the Lord, am angry.
My anger will flare up
like a furious fire
scorching the earth
and everyone on it.”
translation_text:
1Naawen wanni yaa jan jam Kusi nidoabinni Zefania jigi. Gedalia nidoabili ale nye Kusi ate Amariya nidoabili a nye Gedalia ate Azekaya nidoabili a nye Amariya. Di jam ka diipo ate Amon nidoabinni Josia a jam chim Juda naab la. 2<<Mi ale yiak jaab meena ale bo tɛŋka zuk la a ta cheŋ.>> Ka Naawen ale weeni.
3<<Mi ale yiak nidoaba ale duŋsa meena a ta cheŋ, mi ale yiak nuinsaŋa ale bo wenzukku la ale jumaŋa ale bo nyakpiemu po la a ta cheŋ. Gaasa nyama ale nya ka kaasuŋ ase mi a nin yeeri nurubiik a ta nyini tɛŋka zuk.>> Ka Naawen ale weeni.
4<<Mi ale teeri m nisaŋa a ta chaab ale Juda abe m ta chaab ale baai meena ale bo Jerusalem po la. Mi ale gebi dela jigini Baal nuru baai ale tali la basi, bɔgluk kaarisaŋa yueŋa ale bɔgta kaabteerɔma, 5baai ale a koori tɛŋ diina zuima a puusi wenzuk chiŋmari boanni la, baai ale a koori tɛŋ a pɛ Naawen yuenni nyiŋ ale a pɛ Milkom wenni yuei nyiŋla, 6baai ale basi Naawen vaka ale kan gisi Naawen yaase ba kpesi a nyini wa jigi la. 7Ni nye diki Nyɔnɔwa Naawen niŋ ale wa jam ka a moata kama. Naawen a gomsi wa kaabka kama, wa nye baai ate wa wi la kama ate ba welema a te wadek. 8Naawen kaabka daaŋa po, mi ale namsi nabisa ale naawa nidoabilisaŋa ale baai meena ale jo garuk chaŋsa la. 9Dai dila danni mi ale namsi baai meena ale jo a sueri ba wenaŋa yenni po ale nyeka tuem ale pimpaasima la.
10Naawen weeni ayen, <<Dai dila danni kaarik ale nyini Juma Nansuiŋku, a wooli a nyini Jigi Paalika, ate ŋɔriŋ kpieŋ ale nyini guutaŋa zuima. 11Nama baai ale bo yabaŋa geŋsa la ni a kaari, nama geruŋdɔma meena a kala ni kpi kama ate baai meena ale a gerim ale kpana la ale nueri. 12Va ŋala po mi ale gisi Jerusalem ale zeuŋta abe m namsi baai ale ta sebchakka la, baai ale a poli ayen Naawen a kan nye wari ase nalim yaase kaasuŋ la. 13Ba le koalim ba paaruŋku a ta cheŋ, ba yieŋa ale ŋɔriŋ. Ba le sɛ yie alege ba kan bo ŋa po, ba le vuk tiisa ba kaduksaŋa po alege ba kan nyu si daamu.
14Naawen dai kpienni a moata kama, a moata ale cheena nna nwuli. Ni wom Naawen danni kaarika a za ka toa kama nna katikati, tugurik tɔŋdɔma neakka. 15Dai dila danni ale chim ka suipuurum dai, nyinyigsa ale daanika dai, dai kaasuŋ ale koka, legi ale paasuk dai, chiŋma ale sobluk dai, 16damunsa ale kpaliŋ kaarik a siti tɛŋka ate ba sɛ parik pagrik a gilim ka la a ta chaab ale gboŋ woŋku ale za gugoruku po la. 17Mi ale ta daanika a jam nuruma po ate ba a cheŋ ase yeeba la, dii nyiŋla ba nye ka biem a kaasi Naawen. Ba ziimu ale waaŋ ase nyuŋ la ate ba puusaŋa po a poak. 18Ba kpanaŋa yaase ba ligmɔniŋka a kan baga vari ba a basi Naawen suipuurumu danni. Wa nyuri dɛka bolimu po, tɛŋzuk meena bolim ale dɛ, diila wa le basi ate baai meena ale bo tɛŋzuk de la a kpeglim nna kadi.>>

english_text:
Turn to the Lord
1You disgraceful nation,
gather around,
2before it's too late.
The Lord has set a time
when his fierce anger
will strike like a storm
and sweep you away.
3If you humbly obey the Lord,
then come and worship him.
If you do right and are humble,
perhaps you will be safe
on that day when the Lord
turns loose his anger.
Judgment on Philistia
4 Gaza and Ashkelon
will be deserted
and left in ruins.
Ashdod will be emptied
in broad daylight,
and Ekron uprooted.
5To you people of Philistia
who live along the coast,
the Lord has this to say:
“I am now your enemy,
and I'll wipe you out!”
6Your seacoast will be changed
into pastureland
and sheep pens.
7The Lord God hasn't forgotten
those survivors in Judah,
and he will help them—
his people will take your land
to use for pasture.
And when evening comes,
they will rest
in houses at Ashkelon.
Judgment on Moab and Ammon
* 8 The Lord All-Powerful,
the God of Israel, said:
I've heard Moab and Ammon
insult my people
and threaten their nation.
9 And so, I swear by my very life
that Moab and Ammon will end up
like Sodom and Gomorrah—
covered with thornbushes
and salt pits forever.
Then my people who survive
will take their land.
10This is how Moab and Ammon
will at last be repaid
for their pride—
and for sneering at the nation
that belongs to me,
the Lord All-Powerful.
11I will fiercely attack.
Then every god on this earth
will shrink to nothing,
and everyone of every nation
will bow down to me,
right where they are.
Judgment on Ethiopia
12 People of Ethiopia,
the sword of the Lord
will slaughter you!
Judgment on Assyria
13 The Lord will reach to the north
to crush Assyria
and overthrow Nineveh.
14Herds of wild animals
will live in its rubble;
all kinds of desert owls
will perch on its stones
and hoot in the windows.
Noisy ravens will be heard
inside its buildings,
stripped bare of cedar.
15This is the glorious city
that felt secure and said,
“I am the only one!”
Now it's merely ruins,
a home for wild animals.
Every passerby simply sneers
and makes vulgar signs.
translation_text:
1Ni tigsi jigi yeŋ ni tigsi jigi yeŋ chivie tɛŋa, 2ni nye dila abe ni ge ate wa le dak diipo la a jam, dai dii dai ate nama ale chuiri a taam ase vɔtta la a paari, alege ate Naawen suipuurumu a jam ni zuk. 3Ni gisi Naawen nama baai meena ale yik nidek tɛŋka po la, nama baai ale a nye dii ate wa weeni la. Ni a gisi wayɔrisima, ni gisi yik m dek, dai dii dai ni le lik nidek Naawen suipuurumu danni.
4Ba le banti Gaza tɛŋka a basi ate Askelon a kaasi. Kantueŋ suŋsuŋ Asdod ale duak koruk ate Ekron ale basi ka le bo juijui la. 5Ku le bie a te nama baai ale bo nyakpiemu nɔi la Keret nuruba, Naawen wanni a ta ka chaab ale ni Keenan Filistia demma tɛŋka. <<Mi ale kaasi ni ate waai a kan tali.>>
6Tɛŋka ale bo nyakpiemu nɔi la juijui ate Keret demma a boro la ale chim ka naapeerisa jigi ale piisa zɔŋta. 7Ka Juda dem baai ale tali la ale kala ba soa ŋa. Dula jigini ba le nya wuyɔgsuk. Junɔi ba le duak Askelon yieŋa po. Naawen ba Wenni ale nya ba zuk, wa le ŋman te ba ba zumasuku.
8<<Mi wom Moab leetaŋa ale Ammon demma nye laka kama baai ale lɛ mi nuruma ale a nyigsi ba tɛŋka la. 9Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La Izirali Wenni ayen, <<Chekki ase mi ale boro la Moab tɛŋka ale nye ase ka Sodom la ate Ammon tɛŋka a nye ase Gomora la juijui ale ka wuuta ale yesa gola a kaasi taam wuu. Mi nuru baai ale tali vua la ale koalim ba, baai ale tali vua mi tɛŋka po la ale tuesi ba tɛŋka.>>
10Ka nnala ale ku jam ba jigi ba kanjantaŋa nyiŋ, ba ale lɛ ale nye Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La nuruma a la la nyiŋ. 11Naawen ale chim nyinyigsa a te ba ase wa nin kaasi tɛŋka wenaŋa meena. Tɛŋsa meena ale bo kunkɔŋni la ale puusi wa, waai meena wadek tɛŋ po.
12<<Nama Kus demma mɛ mi gebika ale basi ate ni nye diki.>>
13Wa le teeri wa nisaŋa a ta chaab ale wiilukku geŋsa demma a kaasi Assiria tɛŋka, a basi ate Niineve a kaasi chessi abe ka nye ase gɔi kosik la. 14Duŋ boari ale duak dula, ŋan nyeenta nna tɔgatɔga. Sagi po viuk ale viuk mɔnuŋ ale kali si zaŋŋa zuk, si kumsaŋa ale nuem va takpataŋa a nyini, tuataŋa nɔi tintana ale boro, ate nyunyoŋ chibsaŋa a nya peelim. 15Tɛŋ kaai ale jam boro fasiyaa la ale nna, kaai ale boro ate wari a kan daanika la. Ka jam weeni ka dek kama ayen, <<Ka mi, waai karo a gum mi po.>> Nya ka le kaasi dii ya, ate gɔi duŋsa a duak ka po. Baai meena ale va ka tɛŋ a taam la a nye ka a la kama ale a kpaanti ba naŋtaata.

english_text:
Sinful Jerusalem
1Too bad for that disgusting,
corrupt, and lawless city!
2Forever rebellious
and rejecting correction,
Jerusalem refuses to trust
or obey the Lord God.
3Its officials are roaring lions,
its judges are wolves;
in the evening they attack,
by morning nothing is left.
4Jerusalem's prophets are proud
and not to be trusted.
The priests have disgraced
the place of worship
and abused God's Law.
5All who do evil are shameless,
but the Lord does right
and is always fair.
With the dawn of each day,
God brings about justice.
6The Lord wiped out nations
and left fortresses
crumbling in the dirt.
Their streets and towns
were reduced to ruins
and emptied of people.
7God felt certain that Jerusalem
would learn to respect
and obey him.
Then he would hold back
from punishing the city
and not wipe it out.
But everyone there was eager
to start sinning again.
Nations Will Turn to the Lord
8The Lord said:
Just wait for the day
when I accuse you nations.
I have decided on a day,
when I will bring together
every nation and kingdom
and punish them all
in my fiery anger.
I will become furious
and destroy the earth.
9I will purify each language
and make those languages
acceptable for praising me.
Then, with hearts united,
everyone will serve
only me, the Lord.
10From across the rivers
of Ethiopia,
my scattered people,
my true worshipers,
will bring offerings to me.
11When that time comes,
you won't rebel against me
and be put to shame.
I'll do away with those
who are proud and arrogant.
Never will any of them
strut around
on my holy mountain.
12But I, the Lord, won't destroy
any of your people
who are truly humble
and turn to me for safety.
13 The people of Israel who survive
will live right
and refuse to tell lies.
They will eat and rest
with nothing to fear.
A Song of Celebration
14Everyone in Jerusalem and Judah,
celebrate and shout
with all your heart!
15Zion, your punishment is over.
The Lord has forced your enemies
to turn and retreat.
Your Lord is King of Israel
and stands at your side;
you don't have to worry
about any more troubles.
16Jerusalem, the time is coming,
when it will be said to you:
“Don't be discouraged
or grow weak from fear!
17The Lord your God
wins victory after victory
and is always with you.
He celebrates and sings
because of you,
and he will refresh your life
with his love.”
The Lord's Promise to His People
18The Lord has promised:
Your sorrow has ended,
and you can celebrate.
19I will punish those
who mistreat you.
I will bring together the lame
and the outcasts,
then they will be praised,
instead of despised,
in every country on earth.
20I will lead you home,
and with your own eyes
you will see me bless you
with all you once owned.
Then you will be famous
everywhere on this earth.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_text:
1Ku le bie a te tɛŋ kaai ale a namsi, a ta tukpari ale ka nuruma ale a taŋ ka, 2ka kan wom waai nɔi ya, ka kan siak sinsaga, ka an ta sebchakka ale Naawen ya, ka kan cheŋ a moata ka Wenni. 3Ka kpaŋŋa ka gbeŋ ŋaai ale a ŋuuni, ka niŋdeerɔma ka junɔi piina baai ale ka a tali jaab a magsi saluiwa. 4Ka biisiteerɔma ta ka kayerinni, ba ka nuru baai ale suk a nye biem. Ka kaabteerɔma a taŋ Wen dɔkku kama ale kaasi sinsaŋŋa. 5Naawen ale bo ka po la ka wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ, wa kan nye a kaasi. Saluik meena wa a nye ka wa wensieŋa, dai paali meena wa kan nye wari a kpeeri. Ale ge baai ale kan daa wayɔrisima nyam la a zɛ chivie.
6<<Mi kaasi ka tɛŋsa, si parik pagrisaŋa a ŋɔriŋ kama, mi basi ate ba suiduataŋa a doa koruk ate waai a kan cheŋ ti po. Ba tɛŋ ninaŋa a kaasi ya, nuru yeŋ mɛ la a kan tali, waai a kan tali. 7Mi weeni tɛŋ nummu ayen, <Chekki ni le chali mi abe ni siak sinsaga!> Ate ba le bo juijui la m kan kaasi dula, yaase m namsika meena a jam ka zuwa. Alege ba nyiŋsa ale diem a zeenti ayen ba nye kaasi dii meena ate ba a nye la po.>> 8Naawen weeni ayen, <<Dila nyiŋ ni limisi wa ale dai cheena m le zaan a biisi. Mi zɔk kama ayen m tigsi tɛŋsa, m tigsi naata ate m suipuurumu a jam ba zuk, m suipuurumu meena. Tɛŋka meena mi nyuri dɛka suipuurumu ale dɛ ba a ko.
9<<Ate m yaa le nye ate nuruma nɔngbanvaataŋa a nye cheri, ate ba meena ale wi Naawen yuenni a maa chaab a puusi wa. 10A nyini Kus beli naŋsaŋa geŋsa mi puusirɔma, mi nuruma ale waaŋ la ale ta tiirita a jam te mi. 11A zaani dai dila danni ni kan jo chivie po dii meena ate ni nye kaasi mi, dii nyiŋla m le yeeri baai meena ale dɛ masim ba kanjantaŋa nyiŋla tɛŋka po. Nama a kan ŋman ta kanjanta m tuilum guuku zuwa. 12Alege mi ale basi ate baai ale kaa yaali biik la ale baai ale a yik badek la a bo ni po, baai ale ta sebchakka ale Naawen yuenni la. 13Izirali demma ale tali vua la a kan ŋman nye kaasi, ba kan velimu yaase pimpaasima a bo ba noaŋa po. Ba le dɛ abe ba duak ate waai a kan nye ate ba a yɔgsa.>>
14A leni yiila Zayon Lie, Izirali na ate ku jueli basi ate fi sui a peenti abe fi a dɛ masim ale fi suinum meena Jerusalem Lie. 15Naawen a yeeri fi namsika kama, wa yiak fi dachiaka kama. Naawen, Izirali Naawa a bo le fu kama, fi a kan ŋman chali daanika. 16Dai dila danni ba le weeni Jerusalem ayen, <<Kan chali yɔgsummoa Zayon. Kan basi ate fi nisaŋa a jiagi. 17Naawen, fi Wenni a bo le fu kama, wa zuak kama a vari a basi. Wa le dɛ masim fi nyiŋ, wa le sueri fu ale wa yaalika, wa le dɛ masim fi nyiŋ ale yiila lennika.>>
18<<Tigi ŋaai ate mi a lueri la niniŋŋa m le yeeri ŋa fi jigi, ŋa ka jibta ale chivie a te fu. 19Va ŋala po m le nye ale baai meena ale namsi fu la, m le vari gbansaŋa a basi abe m tigsi baai ale waaŋ la jigi yeŋ. M le pai pimpauk ale zula a te ba tɛŋ sii meena po ate ba jam pai ba nyo chivie po la. 20Va ŋala po m le tigsi ni, va ŋala po m le ta ni jam yeri. M le te ni zula abe pimpauk nuruma meena po tɛŋzuk de ase m nin ŋman te ni zumasuk nidek nimbie po.>> Ka Naawen ale weeni.

english_text:
Rebuild the Temple
1 On the first day of the sixth month of the second year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord told Haggai the prophet to speak his message to the governor of Judah and to the high priest.
So Haggai told Governor Zerubbabel and High Priest Joshua 2-5that the Lord All-Powerful had said to them and to the people:
You say this isn't the right time to build a temple for me. But is it right for you to live in expensive houses, while my temple is a pile of ruins? Just look at what's happening. 6You harvest less than you plant, you never have enough to eat or drink, your clothes don't keep you warm, and your wages are stored in bags full of holes.
7Think about what I have said! 8But first, go to the hills and get wood for my temple, so I can take pride in it and be worshiped there. 9You expected much, but received only a little. And when you brought it home, I made that little disappear. Why have I done this? It's because you hurry off to build your own houses, while my temple is still in ruins. 10That's also why the dew doesn't fall and your harvest fails. 11And so, at my command everything will become barren—your farmland and pastures, your vineyards and olive trees, your animals and you yourselves. All your hard work will be for nothing.
12Zerubbabel and Joshua, together with the others who had returned from exile in Babylonia, obeyed the Lord's message spoken by his prophet Haggai, and they started showing proper respect for the Lord. 13Haggai then told them that the Lord had promised to be with them. 14So the Lord God All-Powerful made everyone eager to work on his temple, especially Zerubbabel and Joshua. 15And the work began on the twenty-fourth day of that same month.
translation_text:
1Naab Darius ale dɛ wa naamu a paari bena ŋayewa po la chiisa siyuebiwa piilimka danni, Naawen wanni yaa jam biisiteerɔwa Aggai jigi ate wa biisi te Sealtiel nidoabinni Zerubabel waai ale jam a nya Juda zuk la ale Jeyozadak nidoabinni kaabteerɔ kpioŋku Josua ayen, 2Dii ate Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La a weeni la ale nna, <<Nuruma de ayen, <Ku an diem paari diipo ale magsi Naawen yenni sɛka la.> >>
3Ate Naawen wanni yaa jam biisiteerɔwa Aggai jigi ayen, 4<<Ku ka diipo ale magsi ayen ni bo yie naliŋsa po ale ge ate Naawen yenni a kaasi?>>
5Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La abe le weeni diila ale nna, <<Ŋmasi kpesi fi ale poli diila zuk. 6Fi bori ka yega alege che fiifiiga. Fi dɛ alege an chagi ya. Fi nyu ale an ko fi koarisaŋa. Fi jo gatta alege fi nyiŋka an toliŋ ya. Fi nya nyuenta a pai nyo fook kuui ale a yuli la po.>>
7Dii ate Naawen a weeni la ale nna: <<Ŋmasi kpesi fi ale poli diila zuk. 8Jueli guutaŋa zuima a ta daata jam sɛ Naawen yenni ate m dɛ masim abe m nya zula.>> Ka Naawen ale weeni. 9Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ayen, <<Fi a yiili ka yega ale nya, ku tulim chim ka fiifiiga. Fi ale ta dii jo dɔk la, mi pobisi basi kama. Boan nyiŋŋa? Mi yenni ale kaasi ale ge ni wanyi meena nina a muni ale wadek yeri la nyiŋ. 10Dila, nama nyiŋ wenŋmazuk an basi ate maglim a lo ya, tɛŋzuk de mɛ an basi ate ŋanta a bɛ ya. 11Mi ale basi ate kantueŋ a zaani ate tattaŋa ale guutaŋa zuima ale ŋan kpaantaŋa ale da paalimu ale kpaamu ale jabuui meena ate ni nya a nyini tɛŋka zuk la ale nuruma ale niiŋa ale ni nisa tuima meena zuk ayen ni kan nya jaaboa.>>
12Sealtiel nidoabinni Zerubabel ale Jeyozadak nidoabinni kaabteerɔ kpioŋku Josua ale nuru baai meena ale tali vua la yaa va Naawen, ba Wenni lueluku ale biisiteerɔwa Aggai wanni dii nyiŋla Naawen ba Wenni ale tom wa. Ate nuruma yaa jam a chali Naawen yɔgsum.
13Naawen tomteerɔwa Aggai yaa jam pai Naawen wanni a te nuruma ayen, <<Mi a bo ale ni kama.>> Ka mi Naawen ale weeni. 14Naawen yaa choa Sealtiel nidoabinni Zerubabel Juda tɛŋka nyɔnɔwa chiika ale Jeyozadak nidoabinni kaabteerɔ kpioŋku Josua chiika ale nuru baai meena ale tali vua la chiisaŋa. Ba yaa jam piilim ba tom Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, ba Wenni tuimaŋa, 15chiisa siyuebiwa po ka daa pisiye ale ŋanaansiwa danni naab Darius naamu bena ŋayewa po ale la.

english_text:
The Glorious New Temple
1-2On the twenty-first day of the next month, the Lord told Haggai the prophet to speak this message to Governor Zerubbabel, High Priest Joshua, and everyone else:
3 Does anyone remember how glorious this temple used to be? Now it looks like nothing. 4But cheer up! Because I, the Lord All-Powerful, will be here to help you with the work, 5 just as I promised your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt. Don't worry. My Spirit is right here with you.
6 Soon I will again shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land. 7I will shake the nations, and their treasures will be brought here. Then the brightness of my glory will fill this temple. 8All silver and gold belong to me, 9and I promise that this new temple will be more glorious than the first one. I will also bless this city with peace.
The Past and the Future
10On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the Lord God All-Powerful told the prophet Haggai 11to ask the priests for their opinion on the following matters:
12Suppose meat ready to be sacrificed to God is being carried in the folds of someone's clothing, and the clothing rubs against some bread or stew or wine or olive oil or any other food. Would those foods that were touched then become acceptable for sacrifice?
“Of course not,” the priests answered.
13 Then Haggai said, “Suppose someone has touched a dead body and is considered unacceptable to worship God. If that person touches these foods, would they become unclean?”
“Of course they would,” the priests answered.
14So the Lord told Haggai to say:
That's how it is with this entire nation. Everything you do and every sacrifice you offer is unacceptable to me. 15But from now on, things will get better. Before you started laying the foundation for the temple, 16you recalled what life was like in the past. When you wanted 200 kilograms of wheat, there were only 10, and when you wanted 50 jars of wine, there were only 20. 17I made all of your hard work useless by sending mildew, mold, and hail—but you still did not return to me, your Lord.
18Today you have completed the foundation for my temple, so listen to what your future will be like. 19Although you have not yet harvested any grain, grapes, figs, pomegranates, or olives, I will richly bless you in the days ahead.
God's Promise to Zerubbabel
20That same day the Lord spoke to Haggai again and said:
21Tell Governor Zerubbabel of Judah that I am going to shake the heavens and the earth 22and wipe out kings and their kingdoms. I will overturn war chariots, and then cavalry troops will start slaughtering each other. 23But tell my servant Zerubbabel that I, the Lord All-Powerful, have chosen him, and he will rule in my name.
translation_text:
1Chiisa siyopɔiwa po, daa pisiye ale dinyiwa danni, Naawen wanni yaa jam biisiteerɔwa Aggai jigi ayen, 2<<Biisi a te Sealtiel nidoabinni Zerubabel Juda tɛŋka nyɔnɔwa ale Jeyozadak nidoabinni kaabteerɔ kpioŋku Josua ale nuru baai ale tali vua la. Bek ba ayen, 3<Ka ni wana ale tali waai ale jam nya yenni de ale jam ta yuei diila? Nama a nya di ka sɛ yɔgyɔgla de? 4Alege yɔgyɔgla de bi pagra Zerubabel.> Ka Naawen ale weeni. <Bi pagra, Jeyozadak kaabteerɔ kpioŋku nidoabinni Josua.> Ni pagra nama tɛŋka nuruba meena. Ka Naawen ale weeni. <Abe ni a tom. Ale mi bo ale ni kama.> Ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni. 5<Nnala ate mi jam nye nɔiyeŋka ale ni ase ni le jam basi Ejipiti la. Ate m Chiika a diem jam bo ale ni. Ni kan chali yɔgsummoa.>
6<<Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni diila ale nna: <Ku kan beni m le ŋman choa wenŋmazukku ale tɛŋzuk de ale nyakpiemu ale tɛŋ kosikka. 7M le choa tɛŋsa meena ate tɛŋsa meena koarisa ale jam ate mi ale basi ate yenni de a sueri ale pimpauk.> Ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni. 8<Kpanaŋa ka mi ale soa, ligmɔniŋka mɛ ka mi ale soa.> Ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni. 9<Yenni de pimpaukku yɔgyɔgla de ale gaam yie kpakka pimpaukku.> Ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni. <Dela jigini mi ale te suiyɔgni.> Ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni.
10Bena ŋayewa po, chiisa neokku po, daa pisiye ale ŋanaansiwa danni, ate Darius a dɛ wa naamu la, Naawen wanni yaa jam biisiteerɔwa Aggai jigi ate wa weeni ayen, 11<<Dii ate Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La a weeni la ale nna: <Bek kaabteerɔwa sinsaŋŋa ale weeni diila. 12Ase nuru a dan pai tuilum lam a nyo wa garuk lɔk po, ate dula a tiri ŋandiinta yaase jenta yaase daam yaase kpaam yaase ŋandiin yonta, ŋan bala ale ta tuilum?>> Ate kaabteerɔwa a tulisi ayen, <<Aaya.>>
13Aggai yaa weeni ayen, <<Ase nuru a dan tiri jakpiuk a taŋ wadek ate wa nyiŋka a tiri ŋantaŋa de wanyi, ba mɛ a taŋ kama?>> Ate kaabteerɔwa a tulisi ayen, <<Mm, ba mɛ a taŋ kama.>>
14Ate Aggai yaa weeni ayen, <<Ka Naawen ale weeni, <Ku ka dila ale nuruma de ale tɛŋka de mi jigi. Dii meena ate ba nye ale jabuui meena ate ba a te la taŋka a boro kama. 15Yɔgyɔgla de ni kpesi poli kude zuk a nyini danni de a cheŋ, ni teeri wie ale jam ka dii ale ge ate tana a vi chaab zuk Naawen yenni po la. 16Ase nuru a dan poli ayen wa le nya ŋanta a paari busisa pisiye, wa a nya ka pi nyiini, nuru a dan cheŋ daam ŋmiaka jigi a yiili ayen wa le nya paari ka leŋsa pisinu, wa le nya ka pisiye nyiini dula. 17Mi kaasi ni nisima tuima ale chutika ale kɔlika tuem ale ŋmoruk tana ale ge nama an diem ŋmani mi jigi ya.> Ka Naawen ale weeni. 18<A nyini jinla danni a ta a cheŋ, a nyini daa pisiye ale ŋanaansiwa de danni chiisa neokku po, ni kpesi poli danni de zuk dii ate ni dueni Naawen yenni nyubini la ni kpesi a poli. 19Biri a diem tali bo bunni po? Ka yɔgyɔgla de ni tunuku ale kinkaŋsaŋa ale yɔn gilimaŋa ale kpaam tiisaŋa an diem yɔni ya. A nyini jinla danni a ta a cheŋ m le niak ni.> >>
20Naawen wanni yaa jam Aggai jigi a nye buye chiika daa pisiye ale ŋanaansiwa danni ayen, 21<<Weeni Zerubabel Juda tɛŋka nyɔnɔwa ayen mi ale choa wenŋmazukku ale tɛŋzuk de. 22Mi ale yeeri nalima ba naam zukpagliksa zuk abe m kaasi tɛŋ chaŋsa naata. Mi ale nak yiak torokoba ale ŋa damdɔba ale wusuma ate ŋa duerɔba ale kpi, wanyi meena suok ale ko wa ale gebik.
23<<Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni ayen, <Dai dila danni, mi ale fi, Sealtiel nidoabinni Zerubabel.> Ka Naawen ale weeni. <Mi ale nye fu ase ka m nifelinni la, dii nyiŋla mi lueri fu kama.> Ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni.>>

english_text:
Turn to the Lord
1 I am the prophet Zechariah, the son of Berechiah and the grandson of Iddo.
In the eighth month of the second year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord told me to say:
2-3Israel, I, the Lord All-Powerful, was very angry with your ancestors. But if you people will return to me, I will turn and help you. 4Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. They were warned by the earlier prophets to give up their evil and turn back to me, but they paid no attention.
5Where are your ancestors now? Not even prophets live forever. 6But my warnings and my words spoken by the prophets caught up with your ancestors. So they turned back to me and said, “Lord All-Powerful, you have punished us for our sins, just as you had planned.”
First Vision: Horses and Riders
7-8 On the twenty-fourth day of Shebat, which was the eleventh month of that same year, the Lord spoke to me in a vision during the night: In a valley among myrtle trees, I saw someone on a red horse, with riders on red, brown, and white horses behind him. 9An angel was there to explain things to me, and I asked, “Sir, who are these riders?”
“I'll tell you,” the angel answered.
10At once, the man standing among the myrtle trees said, “These are the ones the Lord has sent to find out what's happening on earth.”
11Then the riders spoke to the Lord's angel, who was standing among the myrtle trees, and they said, “We have gone everywhere and have discovered that the whole world is at peace.”
12At this, the angel said, “Lord All-Powerful, for 70 years you have been angry with Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. When are you ever going to have mercy on them?”
13The Lord's answer was kind and comforting. 14So the angel told me to announce:
I, the Lord All-Powerful, am very protective of Jerusalem. 15For a while I was angry at the nations, but now I am furious, because they have made things worse for Jerusalem and are not the least bit concerned. 16And so, I will have pity on Jerusalem. The city will be completely rebuilt, and my temple will stand again. 17I also promise that my towns will prosper—Jerusalem will once again be my chosen city, and I will comfort the people of Zion.
Second Vision: Animal Horns
18Next, I saw four animal horns. 19-21The angel who was sent to explain was there, and so I asked, “What do these mean?”
His answer was, “These horns are the nations that scattered the people of Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem, and took away their freedom.”
Then the Lord showed me four blacksmiths, and I asked, “What are they going to do?”
He replied, “They are going to terrify and crush those horns.”
translation_text:
1Chiisa naanika po, Naab Darius naamu bena ŋayewa po, ate Naawen wanni a jan jam Wen biisiteerɔwa Zakaria waai ale ka Berekiya nidoabili la ate wa kokpieŋ a nye Iddo la jigi.
2<<Naawen sui a jam puuri ale fi kokpieŋsaŋa kama. 3Dila nyiŋla weeni nuruma ayen: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale a weeni diila ale nna: <Ni pilim a jam mi jigi,> Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni dila, <Ate mi mɛ ale ŋman jam ni jigi.> Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni dila. 4Ni kan nye ase ni kokpieŋsaŋa ate Naawen biisiteerɔma a weeni ba ayen: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni nna: <Ni tagri nyini ni suibaataŋa ale tuimbaataŋa po.> Alege ba an jam a wom mi ale jam a weeni ba diila. Mi Naawen ale weeni dila. 5Ni kokpieŋsaŋa yɔgyɔgla de a bo ka bɛ? Ale Wen biisiteerɔma, ba jam boro taam wuu? 6Alege mi wieŋa ale m ŋmarisika ate m jam pai te m tomteerɔma biisiteerɔma la ni kokpieŋsaŋa an jam a siak te ŋa? Ba yaa jam tagri kama a yaa weeni ayen, <Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La a nye ti magsi ka chaab ale ti suitaŋa ale ti tuimaŋa ale ka diila, ase wa ale a poli diila ate wa a nye.> >>
7Daa pisiye ale ŋanaansiwa danni, chiisa pi ale kanyiwa po, Sebat chiika po ale la Darius naamu bena ŋayewa po ate Naawen wanni a jam Wen biisiteerɔwa Zakaria jigi waai ale ka Berekiya nidoabili la ate wa kokpieŋka mɛ a nye Iddo la.
8Yɔkku po ate mi a jam nya pa sakka ale nuru a do wusum mɔnuŋ a bo mi niŋ. Wa jam za ka, ti puuta suŋsuŋ vooliŋ po. Wusum mɔnta ale wusum busumbooŋta ale wusum peeta ale jam za wa ŋaaŋ. 9Mi yaa bek ayen, <<Ka boa ale la, m nyɔnɔ?>> Wen maarɔ waai ale jam biisi ale mi la yaa tulisi ayen, <<M le sak fu ŋa kiri.>>
10Ate nuru waai ale jam za ti puutaŋa po la yaa tɔk ŋa kiri ayen, <<Ba ka baai ate Naawen a tom ba ayen ba cheŋ tɛŋka meena.>> 11Ba yaa ŋman ga weeni Naawen maarɔ waai ale za ti puutaŋa po la ayen, <<Ti cheŋ tɛŋka meena kama a gilim, ti be nya kama ayen tɛŋka demma meena a ta vuusum kama ate suiyɔgni mɛ a bo ba jigi.>>
12Naawen maarɔwa yaa weeni ayen, <<Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La, ka dimpo ate fi ale peri jiirim a nyini Jerusalem ale Juda tɛŋsaŋa, daa bena pisiyopɔi ate fi suinni a kasim a puuri ale ba?>> 13Dila nyiŋ Naawen a yaa weeni nalim ale suiyɔgni wie a te Wen maarɔ waai ale biisi ale mi la.
14Ate Wen maarɔ waai ale jam biisi ale mi la yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Weeni wieŋa de: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni nna: <M ta nyuri ale Jerusalem ale Zayon 15alege mi sui ale jam a puuri ale ba tɛŋ kpieŋ sii ale nya badek nna se ba nya likka la alege ba nye kama ate ba ninammu a zuak.>
16<<Dila nyiŋla, Naawen ale a weeni diila ale nna: Mi ale ŋman jam sak jiirim ale Jerusalem demma ate m yenni ale pilim ŋman sɛ. Jamagsimmu ale vi Jerusalem zuk, Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni dila.
17<<Ŋman pilim weeni nna: Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni diila ale nna: <M tɛŋsaŋa ale ŋman pilim jigsi ate Naawen ale ŋman yɔk Zayon suinum abe wa lueri Jerusalem.> >>
18Ate mi zak nya wenŋmazuk ale ka duŋsa ale nyiila ŋanaansi ale za mi niŋ 19mi yaa bek maarɔwa ayen ka wana ale a biisi ale mi la. <<Ŋade kiri ale boa?>> Wa yaa tulisi mi ayen, <<Ka m nyiilaŋa de ale jam kati Juda ale Izirali ale Jerusalem a waaŋ la.>>
20Ate Naawen yaa sak mi nidoa yɔgdɔba banaansi. 21Mi yaa bek ayen, <<Ŋade kiri ale boa, bade cheena ayen ba nye ka boa?>> Ate wa tulisi ayen, <<Ka m nyiilaŋa de ale jam kati Juda waaŋ ate waai an jam baga a zak wa zuk la, alege yɔgdɔma a jam kama ayen ba siti ba abe wa yuk tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa nyiilaŋa ale yiti ta chaab ale Juda ayen ba waaŋ ka nuruma la.>>

english_text:
Third Vision: A Measuring Line
1This time I saw someone holding a measuring line, 2and I asked, “Where are you going?”
“To measure Jerusalem,” was the answer. “To find out how wide and long it is.”
3The angel who had spoken to me came toward me, when another angel came up to him 4and said, “Hurry! Tell that man with the measuring line that Jerusalem won't have any boundaries. It will be too full of people and animals even to have a wall. 5The Lord himself has promised to be a protective wall of fire surrounding Jerusalem, and he will be its shining glory in the heart of the city.”
A Call to Action
6The Lord says to his people, “Run! Escape from the land in the north, where I scattered you to the four winds. 7Leave Babylonia and hurry back to Zion.”
8Then the glorious Lord All-Powerful ordered me to say to the nations that had raided and robbed Zion:
Zion is as precious to the Lord as are his eyes. Whatever you do to Zion, you do to him. 9And so, he will put you in the power of your slaves, and they will raid and rob you. Then you will know that I am a prophet of the Lord All-Powerful.
10City of Zion, sing and celebrate! The Lord has promised to come and live with you. 11When he does, many nations will turn to him and become his people. At that time you will know that I am a prophet of the Lord All-Powerful. 12Then Judah will be his part of the holy land, and Jerusalem will again be his chosen city.
13Everyone, be silent!
The Lord is present
and moving about
in his holy place.
translation_text:
1Mi yaa zak nya wenŋmazuk ale nuru ale ta jamagsim wa nisa po a za mi niŋ! 2Mi yaa bek wa ayen, <<Fi a cheŋ ka be?>> Wa yaa tulisi mi ayen, <<Mi a cheŋ m magsi ka Jerusalem, a nya ka labsimu ale ka woglimmu ale ka diila.>>
3Ate Wen maarɔ waai ale a biisi ale mi la yaa cheŋ, ate maarɔ wa choa a tu wa, 4a weeni wa ayen, <<Chali cheŋ, ga weeni nidoabili paalika ayen, <Jerusalem tɛŋka a kan ta parisa a gilim ka, dii nyiŋla nuruba ale duŋsaŋa ale piisi dii a bo ka po la nyiŋ. 5Ate mi dek ale chim ka bolim parik a gilim ka,> Naawen ale weeni dila, <Ate mi ale chim ka zula a bo ka po.>
6<<Ni jam! Ni jam! Ni chali nyini wiiluk geŋka tɛŋka po.>> Naawen ale a weeni ayen, <<Dii nyiŋla mi basi kama ate ni waaŋ jigi meena.>> Naawen ale a weeni.
7<<Jam Zayon! Ni chali be, nama baai ale bo Babilon tɛŋka po la.>> 8Diila Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni ayen, <<Wa dan zuli mi a tom mi a ta chaab ale tɛŋ kpieŋ sii ale kɔlim fu la. Diila waai a dan tiri fu, wa tiri ka wa numbinni. 9Mi ale zak nisa ba zuk ate baai ale jam chim ba yɔm la ale ŋman cheem a namsi ba. Ate nama ale seba ayen Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale sum tom mi.
10<<Zayon Liewa, nuem abe fi te ate fi sui a peenti. Dii nyiŋla mi cheena kama ayen m bo ale fu.>> Naawen ale weeni. 11<<Tɛŋsa yegayega ale gum chaab ale Naawen dai dila danni, ate ba ale chim mi nuruba. Mi ale bo ale ni ate ni ale miŋ ayen Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La a sum tom mi ka ni jigi. 12Juda tɛŋka ale chim ka Naawen nitalim a bo tuilum tɛŋka zuk abe wa ŋman lueri Jerusalem. 13Nuru meena abe zaani Naawen niŋ dii nyiŋla wa nyini ka wa boka jigini a cheena.>>

english_text:
Fourth Vision: Joshua and Satan
1 I was given another vision. This time Joshua the high priest was standing in front of the Lord's angel. And there was Satan, standing at Joshua's right side, ready to accuse him. 2 But the Lord said, “Satan, you are wrong. Jerusalem is my chosen city, and this man was rescued like a stick from a flaming fire.”
3Joshua's clothes were filthy. 4So the angel told some of the people to remove Joshua's filthy clothes. Then he said to Joshua, “This means you are forgiven. Now I will dress you in priestly clothes.”
5I spoke up and said, “Also put a clean priestly turban on his head.” Then they dressed him in priestly clothes and put the turban on him, while the Lord's angel stood there watching.
6After this, the angel encouraged Joshua by telling him that the Lord All-Powerful had promised:
7If you truly obey me, I will put you in charge of my temple, including the courtyard around it, and you will be allowed to speak at any time with the angels standing beside me. 8 Listen carefully, High Priest Joshua and all of you other priests. You are a sign of things to come, because I am going to bring my servant, the Chosen King.
9Joshua, I have placed in front of you a stone with seven sides. I will engrave something on that stone, and in a single day I will forgive this guilty country. 10 Then each of you will live at peace and entertain your friends in your own vineyard and under your own fig trees.
translation_text:
1Ate wa jam sak mi kaabteerɔ kpioŋku Josua, ale za Naawen maarɔwa niŋ la, ate Sitaana mɛ a za wa juga geŋ ayen wa ŋma wa. 2Naawen a yaa weeni Sitaana ayen, <<Naawen a toariŋ fu kama, fi Sitaana! Naawen dii ale lueri Jerusalem la, a toariŋ fu kama! Nuruwa de a kan nye ase ka diok kosik ate ba chiak bolim po la?>>
3Yɔgyɔgla Josua a jam jɔ ka garuk daŋtisa ase wa ale jam za maarɔwa niŋ la. 4Maarɔwa a jam weeni baai ale za wa niŋ la ayen, <<Ni yeeri garuk daŋtisaŋa wa nyiŋka po.>> Ate wa yaa weeni Josua ayen, <<Nya, mi yeeri fi wabiokku fi jigi kama, mi ale pai ka jigsika gatta a jo fu.>>
5Ate mi jam weeni ayen, <<Ba pai zutɔk naliŋ a vuk wa zukku.>> Ate ba sum pai zutɔk naliŋ a vuk wa zukku ale pai garuk a jo wa, alege ate Naawen maarɔwa mɛ a za. 6Naawen maarɔwa yaa jam weeni Josua ayen, 7<<Nya kude ate Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La a weeni ayen, <Ase fi dan siak a va mi suitaŋa, ale ta dii ate mi a yaali la, fi abe le kasim a nya mi yenni zuk, abe fi a nya m dabaasaŋa zuk. Abe m te fu jigi baai ale za dela la po.
8<< <Wom, kaabteerɔ kpioŋ Josua ale fi maarɔwa ale kala fi niŋ la, baai ale ka nidoaba a chim daana a magsi chaab ale ŋan baai ale za ŋa nye la. M za m ta ka m tomteerɔwa ale ka Naŋ la a jam. 9Nya, buntain dii ate mi pai dueni Josua niŋ la! Ka nina ŋayopɔi ale bo tain yeŋka nyiŋ, ate m le ŋmarisi wari a dueni di nyiŋ.> Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni dila, <Ate mi ale pai ka dai yeŋ a yeeri ba wabiokku ba tɛŋka zuk. 10<< <Dai dila danni waai meena ale wi ka wa vaanchoa ayen wa kali wa yɔna tiib ale wa kinkaŋ tɛŋ.> Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni dila.>>

english_text:
Fifth Vision: A Lampstand and Olive Trees
1The angel who explained the visions woke me from what seemed like sleep. 2Then he asked, “What do you see?”
“A solid gold lampstand with an oil container above it,” I answered. “On the stand are seven lamps, each with seven flames. 3 One olive tree is on the right side and another on the left of the oil container. 4But, sir, what do these mean?”
5Then he asked, “Don't you know?”
“No sir,” I replied.
6 So the angel explained that it was the following message of the Lord to Zerubbabel:
I am the Lord All-Powerful. So don't depend on your own power or strength, but on my Spirit. 7Zerubbabel, that mountain in front of you will be leveled to the ground. Then you will bring out the temple's most important stone and shout, “God has been very kind.”
8The Lord spoke to me again and said:
9Zerubbabel laid the foundation for the temple, and he will complete it. Then everyone will know that you were sent by me, the Lord All-Powerful. 10 Those who have made fun of this day of small beginnings will celebrate when they see Zerubbabel holding this important stone.
Those seven lamps represent my eyes—the eyes of the Lord—and they see everything on this earth.
11 Then I asked the angel, “What about the olive trees on each side of the lampstand? What do they represent? 12And what is the meaning of the two branches from which golden olive oil flows through the two gold pipes?”
13“Don't you know?” he asked.
“No sir, I don't,” was my answer.
14Then he told me, “These branches are the two chosen leaders who stand beside the Lord of all the earth.”
translation_text:
1Ate Wen maarɔ waai ale biisi ale mi la a ŋman jam mi jigi a nak mi a yiti, ase nuru nyiem ale a goa ate ba nak wa a yiti diila. 2Wa yaa bek mi ayen, <<Fi nya ka boa?>> Mi yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Mi nya ka zeuŋ ate ba pai ligmɔniŋ a nye ku, kpaam ale bo taasidi po a za ku ŋma zukku, zeuŋku a ta ka naŋsa siyopɔi ate ba pai boomsa a tuiri ti ate ba baga pai ti a toati bolim. 3Kpaam tiisa siye ale jam za ku tɛŋ, tiisaŋa de bunyi a jam za ka zeuŋku juga geŋ ate bunyi mɛ a za ku gala geŋ.>>
4Mi yaa bek Wen maarɔ waai ale biisi ale mi la ayen, <<Kude kiri ale boa, m nyɔnɔ?>> 5Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Fi a zɛ ŋade kiri ya?>> Mi ŋman tulisi ayen, <<M nyɔnɔ, mi zɛ.>>
6Ate wa yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Naawen wanni ate wa weeni Zerubabel la ale nna, <Ku daa zuaka yaase pagrimoa, alege ka mi Chiika.> Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni dila. 7Guuk kpioŋŋoa, ka boa ale fi? Fi za fi chalisi kama a magsi chaab ale tɛŋka Zerubabel niŋ. Ate wa yaa dueni buntain dii ale a kpeglim la a nuem ayen Wen a niak di! Wen a niak di!>>
8Ate Naawen wanni a jam mi jigi ayen, 9<<Zerubabel nisaŋa ale dueni Wen yenni de, nyubini wa nisaŋa ale sɛ di a tuk. Ate nama ale miŋ ayen Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale tom mi ni jigi. 10Ka wana ale wa zɛri dai dii dai ate fi pai maga a piilim wari ayen fi pai a tom tuima la? Nuruba ale dɛ masim ase ba nin nya Zerubabel a ta jamagsim buui ate ba pai a sɛ la wa nisima po. Zeuŋtaŋa tiyopɔiwa a sak ka Naawen nina ŋayopɔi ŋaai ale a nya tɛŋzuk meena la.>>
11Ate mi yaa bek maarɔwa ayen, <<Kpaam tiisa siyewa ale za zeuŋku jazaanimu gala ale juga la kiri ale boa?>> 12Mi ŋman pilim bek ayen, <<Kpaam tiimu naŋsa siyewa ale za ligmɔniŋ naŋsa siyewa tɛŋ ate kpaam a kpiiri a nyini du la kiri ale boa?>> 13Wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Fi zɛ ŋade kiri ya?>> Mi yaa weeni ayen, <<Aaya, m nyɔnɔ. 14Ate wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Bade bayewa ka baai ate mi kpiiri kpaam ba zuk a gomsi ba ayen ba zaani tɛŋzuk de meena a tom a te mi la.>>

english_text:
Sixth Vision: A Flying Scroll
1When I looked the next time, I saw a flying scroll, 2and the angel asked, “What do you see?”
“A flying scroll,” I answered. “About nine meters long and four and a half meters wide.”
3Then he told me:
This scroll puts a curse on everyone in the land who steals or tells lies. The writing on one side tells about the destruction of those who steal, while the writing on the other side tells about the destruction of those who lie.
4The Lord All-Powerful has said, “I am sending this scroll into the house of everyone who is a robber or tells lies in my name, and it will remain there until every piece of wood and stone in that house crumbles.”
Seventh Vision: A Woman in a Basket
5Now the angel who was there to explain the visions came over and said, “Look up and tell me what you see coming.”
6“I don't know what it is,” was my reply.
“It's a big basket,” he said. “And it shows what everyone in the land has in mind.”
7The lead cover of the basket was opened, and in the basket was a woman. 8“This woman represents evil,” the angel explained. Then he threw her back into the basket and slammed the heavy cover down tight.
9Right after this I saw two women coming through the sky with wings outstretched like a stork in the wind. Suddenly they lifted the basket into the air, 10and I asked the angel, “Where are they taking the basket?”
11“To Babylonia,” he answered, “where they will build a house for the basket and set it down inside.”
translation_text:
1Mi ŋman nya ale ka gbaŋ ale yiti a bo wenŋmazuk! 2Wa yaa bek mi ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi nya?>> Mi yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Mi nya ka gbaŋ ale wɔŋa a paari anamagib pisinaansi ale ŋman labsa a paari anamagib pisiye a bo wenŋmazuk.>>
3Ate wa weeni sak mi ayen, <<Gbaŋka nyiŋka a ŋmarisi ka kika sii ale za si jam tɛŋka meena zuk. Ku ŋmarisi kama ayen, ba za ba yiak zueba ale baai ale a nye venta pɛka a bo tɛŋka po la kama. 4Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni ayen, <M le tom m wanni ate di jo zuewa yenni po ale waai ale pai mi yuenni a nye venta pɛka la yenni po. Di ale wari a bo wa yenni a ga kaasi di, di ale kaasi di daataŋa ale di tanaŋa meena.> >>
5Ate Wen maarɔ waai ale a biisi ale mi la yaa jam zaani mi niŋ, a weeni sak mi ayen, <<Zak nya wenŋmazuk dii ale a nye la.>> 6Mi yaa bek ayen, <<Ka boa ale la?>> Wa yaa tulisi mi ayen, <<Ka magsika busik.>> Ate wa ŋman weeni a gum du ayen, <<Kude a sak ka nuruma meena ale bo tɛŋka po la wabaataŋa ale soa diila.>> 7Ba ale lak busika kuta nanlikka la, nipok ale jam kala busika po! 8Wenŋmazuk maarɔwa jaa weeni kama ayen, <<Nipowa de a magsi chaab ale ka gaasa,>> Ate wa ŋman tusi wa a basi ka po a yaa pai nanlikka a lik wa basi du.
9Ate mi zak nya wenŋmazuk ale nipooba baye ale viok a bo ba kiŋkaŋŋa po ase jumbaliiruk la, ba yaa zak busika wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋzuk suŋsuŋ. 10Mi yaa jam bek maarɔwa ayen, <<Ba ta busika a cheŋ ka bɛ?>> 11Wa yaa jam tulisi mi ayen, <<Mi ta a cheŋ ka Sinar demma tɛŋka ayen m sɛ yeri a te ka. Ase ku dan gomsi a nueri, busika ale bo dula ka jigini.>>

english_text:
Eighth Vision: Four Chariots
1Finally, I looked up and saw four chariots coming from between two bronze mountains. 2 The first chariot was pulled by red horses, and the second by black horses; 3 the third chariot was pulled by white horses, and the fourth by spotted gray horses.
4“Sir,” I asked the angel. “What do these stand for?”
5 Then he explained, “These are the four winds of heaven, and now they are going out, after presenting themselves to the Lord of all the earth. 6The chariot with black horses goes toward the north, the chariot with white horses goes toward the west, and the one with spotted horses goes toward the south.”
7The horses came out eager to patrol the earth, and the angel told them, “Start patrolling the earth.”
When they had gone on their way, 8he shouted to me, “Those that have gone to the country in the north will do what the Lord's Spirit wants them to do there.”
The Chosen Leader
9The Lord said to me:
10-11Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah have returned from Babylonia. Collect enough silver and gold from them to make a crown. Then go with them to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah and put the crown on the head of the high priest Joshua son of Jehozadak. 12-13 Tell him that I, the Lord All-Powerful, say, “Someone will reach out from here like a branch and build a temple for me. I will name him ‘Branch,’ and he will rule with royal honors. A priest will stand beside his throne, and the two of them will be good friends. 14This crown will be kept in my temple as a reminder and will be taken care of by Heldai, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Josiah.”
15When people from distant lands come and help build the temple of the Lord All-Powerful, you will know that the Lord is the one who sent me. And this will happen, if you truly obey the Lord your God.
translation_text:
1Mi ŋman pilim nya wenŋmazuk ale ka wusuma torokoba banaansi ale za mi niŋ, ba jam nyini ka guuta tiye suŋsuŋ po, ti jam ka kutuk mɔnta guuta. 2Wusum toroko kuui ale dɛ niŋ la a jam ta ka wusum mɔnta, ate buui ale saari buyewa la a ta sobluk 3ate buui ale saari butawa la a ta peeluk, ate buui ale saari bunaansiwa la nyiŋka a jam ka ŋmiŋmiruk. Ba meena a jam pagra kama. 4Mi yaa bek maarɔwa ayen ka wana ale poom a biisi ale mi la, <<M nyɔnɔ, ŋade ale boa?>
5Wenŋmazuk maarɔwa yaa tulisi mi ayen, <<Wenŋmazuk vaata tinaansiwa ale nna, a nyini nyɔnɔwa jigi a cheŋ tɛŋka meena. 6Waai ale ta wusum sobtaŋa la a cheŋ ka tɛŋ kaai ale bo wiilukku geŋsa la po, waai ale ta wusum peetaŋa la, a cheŋ va yeniŋ geŋsa, ate waai ale ta wusum ŋmiŋmiritaŋa la mɛ a cheŋ a va yeseoku geŋsa.>>
7Ase wusum ŋaai ale pagra la ale ga nyini la, ŋa kasim jaa yienti kama ayen ŋa nyini a kpesi tɛŋka meena ale ka diila. Wenŋmazuk maarɔwa yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni be cheŋ ga kpesi ka.>> Dila nyiŋ ŋa be sum jam cheŋ tɛŋka meena kama. 8Ate wa yaa ŋman wi mi ayen, <<Baai ale a cheŋ wiiluk tɛŋka geŋsa la mi Chiika ale vuusi wiiluk tɛŋka po.>>
9Naawen wanni a jan jam mi jigi ayen, 10<<Tuesi kpana ale ligmɔniŋ a nyini Yeldai ale Tobijaya ale Jedaya ale jam cheŋ ga bo Babilon ale ŋman pilim jam la jigi. Dai dila danni dek cheŋ Zefania nidoabinni Josia yenni. 11Pai kpana ale ligmɔniŋ a nye naam zutɔk a ta cheŋ ga vuk Josua kaabteerɔ kpioŋku ale ka Jeyozadak nidoabinni la zuk. 12Weeni wa ayen Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale a weeni ayen, <Nuruwa de ate ba a wi wa ayen, Tiimu Naŋka La, naŋ kala ale ka teeri a sɛ Naawen yenni. 13Ka wala ale za wa sɛ Naawen yenni, ate ba ale pai nalima gatta a jo wa ate wa ale kali naam zukpaglika zuk a dɛ wa naamu. Wa ale chim ka kaabteerɔ wa naam zukpaglika zuk. Ate nɔiyeŋ ale bo bayewa suŋsuŋ.> 14Naam zutɔkka ale te ka Yelem ale Tobijaya ale Jedaya ale Yen ale ka Zefania nidoabinni la teerika Naawen yenni po. 15Baai ale yalima la ale jam a maari ate Naawen yenni a sɛ, ate nama ale miŋ ayen Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale sum tom mi ni jigi, kude ale nye kama ase nama nin kasim a zuli mi Naawen ni Wenni.>>

english_text:
A Question about Going without Eating
1On the fourth day of Chislev, the ninth month of the fourth year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord again spoke to me. 2-3It happened after the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer with Regem-Melech and his men to ask the priests in the Lord's temple and the prophets to pray for them. So they prayed, “Should we mourn and go without eating during the fifth month, as we have done for many years?”
4-5It was then that the Lord All-Powerful told me to say to everyone in the country, including the priests:
For 70 years you have gone without eating during the fifth and seventh months of the year. But did you really do it for me? 6And when you eat and drink, isn't it for your own enjoyment? 7My message today is the same one I commanded the earlier prophets to speak to Jerusalem and its villages when they were prosperous, and when all of Judah, including the Southern Desert and the hill country, was filled with people.
8-9So once again, I, the Lord All-Powerful, tell you, “See that justice is done and be kind and merciful to one another! 10Don't mistreat widows or orphans or foreigners or anyone who is poor, and stop making plans to hurt each other.”
11-12But everyone who heard those prophets, stubbornly refused to obey. Instead, they turned their backs on everything my Spirit had commanded the earlier prophets to preach. So I, the Lord, became angry 13and said, “You people paid no attention when I called out to you, and now I'll pay no attention when you call out to me.”
14That's why I came with a whirlwind and scattered them among foreign nations, leaving their lovely country empty of people and in ruins.
translation_text:
1Ku bena ŋanaansi po ate Naab Darius jam bo wa naamu po la, ate Naawen wanni jan jam Zakaria jigi chiisa neokku Kislev chiika ka daa ŋanaansiwa po. 2Betel demma a jam tom Sarezer ale Aregem Melek ale ba nidoama ayen ba bek nyini Naawen jigi, 3ate kaabteerɔma ale bo Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La yenni po ale wa biisiteerɔma la ayen, <<M baga a kum a ŋman baga a bobi nɔi chiisa sinuwa po ase m le kasim jam a nye dii bena yega ale taam la?>>
4Ate Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La wanni a jam mi jigi ayen, 5<<Bek nuruma meena ale bo tɛŋka po la ale kaabteerɔma ayen, ase ba ale jam bobi ba noaŋa ale kum chiisa sinu ale siyopɔiwa po bena pisiyopɔiwa ale taam la, ku jam ka mi nyiŋ ate ni jam bobi ni noaŋa? 6Ase ni ale jam boro a dɛ ale a nyu la, ni a jam a nye daa nidek masim nyiŋŋa? 7Daa Naawen wieŋa ale la ate Wen biisiteerɔ baai ale dɛ niŋ la a mooli ase Jerusalem ale ka gilagila tɛŋsaŋa a jam bo vuusum ale jigsika po, ate Negev ale yeniŋ demma a jam kali la?>>
8Ate Naawen wanni ŋman jam Zakaria jigi ayen, 9<<Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni diila ale nna: <Ni ta wensie nyemagsika, a sak jiirim ale ŋmanteka ale chaab. 10Ni kan namsi pukɔga ale baai ale kan ta koba la ale nicham yaase ŋanjaksa. Ni kan poli biem ni suiniima po a te chaaba.>
11<<Alege ba an jam wom ya. Ba jam a nye ka tukpari ale cheem ba ŋaaŋsa a te mi ale mi wanni ale ŋman jam lik ba tueŋa. 12Ba basi kama ate ba suiniima a pagra ase tain chesinni la ate ba poom kan wom sinsaŋŋa yaase wie ŋaai ate Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La a pai wa Chiika a weeni ta va wa biisiteerɔma zuk baai ale dɛ niŋ la. Di la nyiŋ Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La sui yaa jam puuri ale ba nna yegayega.
13<< <Mi ale jam wi ba la, ba an jam wom mi: Dila nyiŋla, ba mɛ dan wi mi, m kan wom ba,> Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni diila ale la. 14<M yiak ba kama ale va kiliŋ a basi tɛŋ kpieŋsa meena po ate ba chim nicham. Tɛŋka a jam doa ka koruk ba ŋaaŋnyiŋ ate nuru a kan jam yaase wa cheŋ. Ba ale nye dii a kaasi tɛŋ maŋka de la ale la.> >>

english_text:
The Lord's Promises to Zion
1The Lord All-Powerful said to me:
2I love Zion so much that her enemies make me angry. 3I will return to Jerusalem and live there on Mount Zion. Then Jerusalem will be known as my faithful city, and Zion will be known as my holy mountain.
4Very old people with walking sticks will once again sit around in Jerusalem, 5while boys and girls play in the streets. 6This may seem impossible for my people who are left, but it isn't impossible for me, the Lord All-Powerful. 7I will save those who were taken to lands in the east and the west, 8and I will bring them to live in Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God, faithful to bring about justice.
9I am the Lord All-Powerful! So don't give up. Think about the message my prophets spoke when the foundation of my temple was laid. 10Before that time, neither people nor animals were rewarded for their work, and no one was safe anywhere, because I had turned them against each other.
11My people, only a few of you are left, and I promise not to punish you as I did before. 12Instead, I will make sure that your crops are planted in peace and your vineyards are fruitful, that your fields are fertile, and the dew falls from the sky. 13People of Judah and Israel, you have been a curse to the nations, but I will save you and make you a blessing to them. So don't be afraid or lose courage.
14When your ancestors made me angry, I decided to punish you with disasters, and I didn't hold back. 15Now you no longer need to be afraid. I have decided to treat Jerusalem and Judah with kindness. 16 But you must be truthful with each other, and in court you must give fair decisions that lead to peace. 17Don't ever plan evil things against others or tell lies under oath. I, the Lord, hate such things.
A Time of Celebration
18The Lord All-Powerful told me to say:
19People of Judah, I, the Lord, demand that whenever you go without food as a way of worshiping me, it should become a time of celebration. No matter if it's the fourth month, the fifth month, the seventh month, or the tenth month, you should have a joyful festival. So love truth and live at peace.
20I tell you that people will come here from cities everywhere. 21Those of one town will go to another and say, “We're going to ask the Lord All-Powerful to treat us with kindness. Come and join us.”
22Many people from strong nations will come to Jerusalem to worship me and to ask me to treat them with kindness. 23When this happens, ten people from nations with different languages will grab a Jew by his clothes and say, “Let us go with you. We've heard that God is on your side.” I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken!
translation_text:
1Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La wanni yaa ŋman pilim jam mi jigi. 2Ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni diila ale nna, <<Mi a dɛ ka nyuri nna yegayega a te Zayon, nyuri nna yegayega ale kasim a dɛ mu ta va ba nyiŋ.>> 3Naawen ale weeni diila ale nna: <<Mi ale ŋman jam Zayon ate m boka jigini ale chim Jerusalem tɛŋka. Ate ba ale wi Jerusalem tɛŋka ayen Wensie Tɛŋ ate ba ale wi Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La guuku ayen tuilum guuku.>>
4Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale a weeni diila ale nna: <<Nidoa baai ale nipok baai ale kpaŋ paari la a za ba kali ka Jerusalem suitaŋa nɔi ate ba wanyi wanyi za wa ta ka dachek dii nyiŋla ba kpaŋ kama ate chelim a toa a te ba. 5Nidoabili paalisa ale nipokbili paalisa ale za ba bo tɛŋ kpieŋka suitaŋa niŋsa a diini ale chaab.>>
6Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale a weeni diila ale nna: <<Ku za ku chim ka wakinkagli a te tɛŋka demma baai ale za ba tali la po, alege ku ale chim wakinkagli a te mi?>> Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni dila.
7Ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale a weeni diila ale nna: <<Mi ale vari m nuruma baai meena ale bo yontidi po tɛŋka kori ale yeniŋ la a basi. 8Mi ale ŋman ta ba jam Jerusalem ate ba ale kali dula. Ba ale chim m nuruba ate mi ale ta wensie ale wayɔrisima ale ba ase ba Wen la.>>
9Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale a weeni diila ale nna: <<Nama baai yaa le a wom wie ŋaai ate biisiteerɔma baai ale jam boro diipo ate ba jam dueni nyubini ayen ba sɛ Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La yenni la, ni te ate ni nisima a pagra ate ni baga a sɛ Wen yenni a tuk. 10Piilimka po tutuna a jam karo a te nuru yaase duŋŋa. Waai an jam baga a tom wa tuima ale nalim wa dachaasa nyiŋŋa, diila m basi kama ate nuru meena a ta chaab ale wa vaanchoa. 11Alege yɔgyɔgla de mi a kan ŋman nye m nuru baai ale tali tɛŋka po la ase m le jam a nye ale ba diila.>> Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni diila ale la.
12<<Binni ale nyini a chim nalimnyiini, ate tiimu ale yɔni bu yɔnaŋa, ate tɛŋka ŋankpaantaŋa ale bɛ, ate wenŋmazukku maglimu a lo. Mi le pai ŋantaŋa de meena ale tali la a te nuruma de ale tali la. 13Nama Juda ale Izirali demma ale chim kikaasa tɛŋsaŋa po la, mi ale vari ni basi ate nama ale chim niauŋ nuruba. Ni be kan chali yɔgsummoa alege ni te ate ni nisima a pagra.>>
14Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale a weeni diila ale nna: <<Ase mi ale jam poli ayen m ta kaasuŋ a jam ni jigi ate m poom kan sak jiirim maga mɛ ale ni la diipo ate ni koma a jam nye ate m suinni a jam puuri ale ba la,>> Ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni nna, 15<<Dila nyiŋ, yɔgyɔgla de m ŋman poli kama ayen m ŋman nye wamaŋsa a te Jerusalem ale Juda. Ni kan chali yɔgsummoa. 16Ni magsi kama ayen ni nye nna: Ni a biisi wensie ale chaab abe ni a bo wensie buusa ni buusa yieŋa po. 17Kan poli ayen fi nye fi vaanchoa biemmoa, kan yaali venta pɛka. Mi a kisi wieŋa de kama,>> Naawen ale weeni diila.
18Ate Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La wanni ŋman jam mi jigi, 19Ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni diila ale nna. <<Chiisa sinaansiwa po ale sinuwa po ale siyopɔiwa po ale piika po ate ni nyiem a bobi nɔi la a za ku chim ka suipeentik tigi a te Juda. Dila nyiŋla ni be yaali wensie ale suiyɔgni.>>
20Ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni diila ale nna, <<Nuru boari ale bo tɛŋ kpieŋsa po la ale za ba jam 21ate tɛŋka choa nuruba ale weeni tɛŋ yoŋ dem ayen, <Te ti cheŋ a ga puusi Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La abe ti ŋman gisi wa. Mi mɛ dek mɛ a cheŋ kama.> 22Ate nuru boari ale satɛŋ sii ale pagra la ale jam Jerusalem a gisi Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La abe ba ŋman puusi wa.>>
23Nya kude ate Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La a weeni ayen, <<Va ŋala po nidoaba pi a nyini biisa meena ale tɛŋ kpieŋsa po la, ale yik Juu denɔ garuk nɔi nna giŋgiŋ a weeni ayen, <Basi ate ti cheŋ ale fu, dii nyiŋla ti wom kama ayen Wen a bo ale fu kama.> >>

english_text:
Israel's Enemies Will Be Punished
1 This is a message
from the Lord:
His eyes are on everyone,
especially the tribes
of Israel.
So he pronounces judgment
against the cities
of Hadrach and Damascus.
2Judgment will also fall
on the nearby city
of Hamath,
as well as on Tyre and Sidon,
whose people are clever.
3Tyre has built a fortress
and piled up silver and gold,
as though they were dust
or mud from the streets.
4Now the Lord will punish Tyre
with poverty;
he will sink its ships
and send it up in flames.
5 Both Ashkelon and Gaza
will tremble with fear;
Ekron will lose all hope.
Gaza's king will be killed,
and Ashkelon emptied
of its people.
6A mob of half-breeds
will settle in Ashdod,
and the Lord himself
will rob Philistia of pride.
7No longer will the Philistines
eat meat with blood in it
or any unclean food.
They will become part
of the people of our God
from the tribe of Judah.
And God will accept
the people of Ekron,
as he did the Jebusites.
8God says, “I will stand guard
to protect my temple from those
who come to attack.
I know what's happening,
and no one will mistreat
my people ever again.”
The Lord Tells about the Coming King
9 Everyone in Jerusalem,
celebrate and shout!
Your king has won a victory,
and he is coming to you.
He is humble
and rides on a donkey;
he comes on the colt
of a donkey.
10 I, the Lord, will take away
war chariots and horses
from Israel and Jerusalem.
Bows that were made for battle
will be broken.
I will bring peace to nations,
and your king will rule
from sea to sea.
His kingdom will reach
from the Euphrates River
across the earth.
The Lord Promises To Rescue Captives
11 When I made a sacred agreement
with you, my people,
we sealed it with blood.
Now some of you are captives
in waterless pits,
but I will come to your rescue
12and offer you hope.
Return to your fortress,
because today I will reward you
with twice what you had.
13I will use Judah as my bow
and Israel as my arrow.
I will take the people of Zion
as my sword
and attack the Greeks.
The Lord Will Protect His People
14Like a cloud, the Lord God
will appear over his people,
and his arrows will flash
like lightning.
God will sound his trumpet
and attack in a whirlwind
from the south.
15The Lord All-Powerful
will protect his people,
and they will trample down
the sharpshooters
and their slingshots.
They will drink and get rowdy;
they will be as full as a bowl
at the time of sacrifice.
16The Lord God will save them
on that day,
because they are his people,
and they will shine on his land
like jewels in a crown.
17How lovely they will be.
Young people will grow there
like grain in a field
or grapes in a vineyard.
translation_text:
1Naawen wanni a ta ka chaab ale Yadrak tɛŋka demma ate ku ale maa paari Damasikus mɛ dii nyiŋla nuruba ale Izirali buuni meena nina a doa ka Naawen zuk. 2Yamat tɛŋka mɛ ale nye bain ale ba mɛ la a gum du kama. Taaya ale Saidon ba ale ba tuimaŋa sebika mɛ ale maa gum du kama. 3Taaya demma a se ka parik kpieŋ a gilim ba tɛŋka ale ŋman tigsi kpana ase tana la ale nye ligmɔniŋ ase tanta ale bo suik po diila. 4Alege Nyɔnɔwa ale tuesi ba nitalimu abe wa kaasi wa pagrimu ale bo nyakpiemu nɔi la ate bolim ale dɛ wa a kaasi.
5Askelon ale nya ate yɔgsum a yik ba. Gaza ale nya ate ku ale te ba nyiŋdomma ate Ekron mɛ ale jɔk yiila. Gaza ale jɔk wa naawa, ate ba ale zɛri Askelon. 6Nicham ale kali Asdod ate mi ale gebi Filistia demma kanjantaŋa a basi. 7Mi ale pai ziim a nyini ba noaŋa po, ŋandiin tii ale ta kisuk la ba nyinaŋa po. Nuru baai ale za ba tali la za ba chim ka Wen nuruba. Ate ba ale chim Juda niŋdeerɔba, ate Ekron demma ale nye ase ka Jebus demma la. 8Alege mi ale maari m yenni demma mi ale nya ba zuk ate tugurik tɔŋdɔba a kan baga a jo ba po. Mi kan ŋman te ate waai a namsi m nuruma, dii nyiŋla mi a nya ba zuk kama.
9Dɛ masim nna yegayega Zayon Lie! Nuem ale masim Jerusalem Lie! Nya, fi naawa a cheena fi jigi, wa ta ka wayɔrisima ale varibasika, wa abe a nye ka nna ŋmam ale dɔ boniŋ kaai ale ka bonpaalik. 10Mi ale tuesi wusum torokoma Ɛfraim jigi ale kpaliŋ wusumaŋa Jerusalem jigi, abe m wɛ kpaliŋka tommu. Wa ale mooli suiyɔgni a te tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa. Wa naamu dɛka ale nyini nyakpiem a cheŋ nyakpiem, a ŋman nyini Benni a ga paari tɛŋzuk de kpeglimka. 11Alege nama, m nɔiyeŋka ziimu nyiŋ, m le yeeri ni ligrɔma vɔrup buui ate nyiam a ka bu po la a basi.
12Ni ŋman cheŋ ni yie pagrisaŋa. Nama ligrɔ baai ale ta yiila la. Yɔgyɔgla de m poom weeni kama ayen m le ŋman te ni ku naŋtuok nɔi buye a poom gaam dila. 13M le gbeeri Juda ase m le a gbeeri m tommu diila, abe m pai Ɛfraim a su bu po. Zayon m le pai fi nidoabilisaŋa a kpaliŋ ale Girik nidoabilisaŋa abe m nye ni ase kpaliŋ nyeerɔ gebik la.
14Naawen yaa ale jam ba jigi. Wa tommu penni ale cheŋ ase ka ŋmoruk nyaksika la. Nyɔnɔwa waai ale ka Naawen la peeri wa damuniŋka. Wa ale gɔk santiri kori vaataŋa po, 15ate Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale lik ba. Ba ale pai visiŋ tana a kaasi ba a nya nakdeka ba zuk. Ba ale kaari kpaliŋ po ase danyuirisa la, ate ba ale ko ba dachaasaŋa ate ba ziimu a sueri chin dii ate ba pai a misi kuŋkuŋku gugottaŋa la.
16Naawen ba Wen ale vari ba a basi da dila danni ase naapeerik ale vari wa piisa a basi diila. Ba ale nye ase ka tana naam zutɔk la ate ba zak a zaani ase daana tɛŋka zuk la. 17Ba nalimu nyiŋ nuruba ale yaali ayen ba a nya. Nidoabili paalisaŋa ale dɛ ŋanbie a nya pagrim ale nyiŋyɔgsa, ate nipokbili paalisaŋa ale nyu da paalib.

english_text:
A Bright Future for Judah and Israel
1I, the Lord, am the one
who sends storm clouds
and showers of rain
to make fields produce.
So when the crops need rain,
you should pray to me.
2 You can't believe idols
and fortunetellers,
or depend on the hope
you receive from witchcraft
and interpreters of dreams.
But you have tried all of these,
and now you are like sheep
without a shepherd.
3I, the Lord All-Powerful,
am fiercely angry
with you leaders,
and I will punish you.
I care for my people,
the nation of Judah,
and I will change
this flock of sheep
into charging war horses.
4From this flock will come leaders
who will be strong
like cornerstones and tent pegs
and weapons of war.
5They will join in the fighting,
and together they will trample
their enemies like mud.
They will fight,
because I, the Lord,
will be on their side.
And they will crush
the enemy cavalry.
6I will strengthen
the kingdoms of Judah
and Israel.
And I will show mercy
because I am the Lord,
their God.
I will answer their prayers
and bring them home.
Then it will seem as though
I had never rejected them.
7Israel will be like
a tribe of warriors
celebrating with wine.
When their children see this,
they will also be happy
because of me, the Lord.
8I will give a signal
for them to come together
because I have rescued them.
And there will be as many
as ever before.
9 Although I scattered my people
in distant countries,
they won't forget me.
Once their children are raised,
they will return—
10I will bring them home
from Egypt and Assyria,
then let them settle
as far as Gilead and Lebanon,
until the land overflows
with them.
11My people will go through
an ocean of troubles,
but I will overcome the waves
and dry up the deepest part
of the Nile.
Assyria's great pride
will be put down,
and the power of Egypt
will disappear.
12I'll strengthen my people
because of who I am,
and they will follow me.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_text:
1Ku dan paari borik ni abe bek Naawen ate wa basi ate ŋmoruk a ni. Ka Naawen ale baga a nye ate viok a chim chiŋma. Wala ale a te nuruba nyiam a ŋman a nye ate ŋankpaanta a bo tata po a te nuruba meena. 2Bɔgtaŋa a weeni ka venta wie, sampoporisaŋa a nya ka venta wie. Ba a weeni ka venta gɔdaasima, suiyɔgni wie ŋaai ate ba a weeni a te nuruba la ka koruk. Dila nyiŋla nuruma a cheŋ bɛ kama a yaa ta chichama ase piisa ale cheŋ tuiri gɔi po dii nna se ŋa ka naapeerik la.
3<<Mi sui ale a dɛ ale naapeerisaŋa, ate mi ale namsi niŋdeerɔma. Ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale a nya Juda yenni zuk ale nye ba, ate ba nye ase wusum buui ale ta kanjanta kpaliŋ po la. 4A nyini Juda po ate ti ale nya gugoruku buntanni ale viuku kpaasini ale kpaliŋ tommu ale kpaga meena. 5Ba ale gum ka chaab a chim nuru kpienta, a tabi sui tii ate bagta a bo ti po ate ba a nye kpaliŋsa. Dii nyiŋla Naawen a bo ale ba kama ba ale kpaliŋ kama, ba ale kpaliŋ a nya a nakdeka wusum duerɔma zuk.
6<<Mi ale te Juda yenni pagrim, abe m vari Josefi yenni a basi. M le ŋman pai ba a zaani ba nyiem ale ka diila po, dii nyiŋla mi ta ka jiirim ale ba. Ba ale nye nna se mi an zɛri ba a nya la. Diila Mi ale Naawen ba Wen ate m le tulisi ba. 7Ɛfraim demma ale nye ase ka nidoa kpienta la, ate ba suiniima ale peenti ase ba nyu daam la. Ba bisaŋa ale nya ate ku te ba masim. Ba suiniimaŋa ale dɛ masim Naawen po. 8Mi ale wi ba a ta jam jigi yeŋ. Chekki wensie mi ale vari ba a basi. Ba ale ŋman piisi ase ba nyiem ale ka diila. 9Mi dan poom a nye ate ba waaŋ a bo nuruba po, ate satɛŋsaŋa a yalima pooma, ba ale ŋman a teeri mi. Ba ale ba bisaŋa ale vuuk ate ba ale ŋman pilim jam badek tɛŋka po.
10Mi ale ta ba ŋman nyini Ejipiti a jam, a tigsi ba a nyini Assiria. M le ta ba cheŋ Gilead ale Lebanon, ate ba kan nya jigi a te ba. 11Ba ale cheŋ va nyakpiemu daanika po. Nyakpiemu nanpansaŋa ale baliŋ, ate Nile nyaliuŋtaŋa meena ale kpeeri. Assiria kanjantaŋa ale siŋ tɛŋ, ate Ejipiti tachekka a kan ŋman boro. 12Mi ale te ba Naawen pagrimu ate ba ale cheŋ ale wa yuenni.>> Ka Naawen ale weeni.

english_text:
Trouble for Israel's Enemies
1Lebanon, open your gates!
Let the fire come in
to destroy your cedar trees.
2Cry, you cypress trees!
The glorious cedars have fallen
and are rotting.
Cry, you oak trees of Bashan!
The dense forest
has been chopped down.
3Listen! Shepherds are crying.
Their glorious pastures
have been ruined.
Listen! Lions are roaring.
The forests of the Jordan Valley
are no more to be found.
Worthless Shepherds
4The Lord my God said to me:
Tend those sheep doomed for slaughter! 5The people who buy and butcher them go unpunished, while everyone who sells them says, “Praise the Lord! I'm rich.” Not even their shepherds have pity on them.
6Tend those sheep because I, the Lord, will no longer have pity on the people of this earth. I'll turn neighbor against neighbor and make them slaves of a king. They will bring disaster on the earth, and I'll do nothing to rescue any of them.
7So I became a shepherd of those sheep doomed to be slaughtered by the sheep dealers. And I gave names to the two sticks I used for tending the sheep: One of them was named “Mercy” and the other “Unity.” 8In less than a month, I became impatient with three shepherds who didn't like me, and I got rid of them. 9Then I said, “I refuse to be your shepherd. Let the sheep that are going to die, go on and die, and those that are going to be destroyed, go on and be destroyed. Then let the others eat one another alive.”
10On that same day, I broke the stick named “Mercy” to show that the Lord had canceled his agreement with all people. 11The sheep dealers who saw me knew at once that this was a message from the Lord. 12-13 I told them, “Pay me my wages, if you think you should; otherwise, forget it.” So they handed me my wages, a measly 30 pieces of silver.
Then the Lord said, “Throw the money into the treasury.” So I threw the money into the treasury at the Lord's temple. 14Then I broke the stick named “Unity” and canceled the ties between Judah and Israel.
15Next, the Lord said to me, “Act like a shepherd again—this time a worthless shepherd. 16Once more I am going to let a worthless nobody rule the land—one who won't care for the strays or search for the young or heal the sick or feed the healthy. He will just dine on the fattest sheep, leaving nothing but a few bones.”
17You worthless shepherd,
deserting the sheep!
I hope a sword
will cripple your arm
and blind your right eye.
translation_text:
1Lebanon ni lak ni tuataŋa, ate bolim a dɛ ni nyunyoŋku. 2Dapeelita tiimu, abe kum, diila nyunyoŋku a lo kama ti naliŋsaŋa a kaasi kama. Basan dapagrisa tiisa a kum. Ba che gɔi kpienni a lɔnsi ka tɛŋ. 3Ni wom naapeerisaŋa kumsaŋa, ba wuyɔgsuku meena a kaasi kama. Ni wom gbeŋmaŋa ale a wooli la. Jodan tiiku a kaasi kama.
4Ka Naawen mi Wenni ale weeni diila ale nna: <<Cheŋ ga a nya pa ŋaai ate ba za ba togri la zuk. 5Baai ale da ŋa la a yik ŋa kama a togri alege ate waai an poom a namsi ba. Ba pai ŋa lantaŋa a da kama a yaa le a weeni ayen, <Pak Naawen, mi yaa jigsi kama.> Badek naapeerisaŋa an jam basi ba. 6Ate dila nyiŋ mi a kan ŋman ta jiirim ale m nuru baai ale bo tɛŋka po la.>> Ka Naawen ale a weeni ayen, <<M le pai waai meena a te wa vaanchoa ale wa naab. Ba ale namsi tɛŋka ate m kan vari ba a nyini ba nisima po a basi.>>
7Ate mi yaa a nya pa ŋaai ate ba te ŋa daana ayen ba tɔgri la, ku jam potim ka pa ŋaai ate ba jam a namsi la ate mi jam a nya. Ate mi yaa pai tacheksa siye a wi kanyi ayen Ŋmantiik ale wi m kala mɛ ayen Nɔiyeŋ ale a nya piisaŋa zuk. 8Chiik yeŋ po mi jam yiak naapeerisa sita a basi kama. Piisaŋa a yaa jam kisi mi, ate mi yaa jam jiak ale ŋa 9ate mi weeni ayen, <<Mi kan chim ni naapeerik ŋmana. Baai ale za ba kpi la abe kpi, ate baai mɛ ale za ba bɛ la abe bɛ. Baai ale a boro la abe ko chaab a ŋɔbi chaab nyiŋlam.>>
10Ate mi yaa pai mi tachek kaai ale ka Jiirim la a yik wɛ, ayen mi ko nɔiyeŋ kaai ate mi ta ale tɛŋsaŋa meena la. 11Ka dai dila danni ate mi jam a ko nɔiyeŋka a basi, ate baai ale namsi piisaŋa la ale jam nya mi la a jam miŋ kama ayen ka Naawen wari ale la.
12Mi yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ase ni dan poli ayen dila nala, ni te mu mi tutunaŋa. Ku be dan kan nala, ni tanla.>> Dila nyiŋla ba jam tuni mi ka kpana ligbie pisita. 13Ate Naawen yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Yuk ŋa a te ligtaarɔwa.>> Da magsika ate ba dak mi la a magsi kama. Ate mi yaa pai kpana ligbie pisitawa a yuk basi Naawen yenni po a te ligtaarɔwa. 14Ate mi ŋman pilim wɛ m tachek kaai ale a saari buyewa la ate ba a wi ayen Nɔiyeŋ la a kaasi Juda ale Izirali suataŋa.
15Ate Naawen yaa ŋman jam weeni mi ayen, <<Ŋman tuesi naapeerik beruku kɔlimaŋa. 16Diila m za m te ate ka naapeerik a bo tɛŋka zuk ate wa niŋ a kan bo ŋaai ale koani la po, yaase wa te ŋaai ale ta nyiŋyɔgsa la ŋandiinta, alege wa ale yik ka pa ŋaai ale nala naŋsabaŋa a dari fɔgri abe wa ŋɔbi ŋa lanta.
17<<Naapeerik kaai ale kan ta kiri ale bo ka kikaasa po, wa ale zɛri piisaŋa la nyiŋ! Gebik ale gebi wa ŋmankpalaŋa a ŋman yeeri wa juga nummu! Wa ŋmankpalaŋa ale kasim a kpi kama ate wa juga nummu ale kasim fak!>>

english_text:
Victory for Jerusalem
1This is a message from the Lord about Israel:
I am the Lord! I stretched out the heavens; I put the earth on its foundations and gave breath to humans. 2I have decided that Jerusalem will become a bowl of wine that makes the neighboring nations drunk. And when Jerusalem is attacked, Judah will also be attacked. 3But I will turn Jerusalem into a heavy stone that crushes anyone who tries to lift it.
When all nations on earth surround Jerusalem, 4I will blind every horse and make them panic, and every rider will be confused. But at the same time, I will watch over Judah. 5Then every clan in Judah will realize that I, the Lord All-Powerful, am their God, and that I am the source of their strength.
6At that time I will let the clans of Judah be like a ball of fire in a wood pile or a fiery torch in a hay stack. Then Judah will send the surrounding nations up in smoke. And once again the city of Jerusalem will be filled with people.
7But I will first give victory to Judah, so the kingdom of David and the city of Jerusalem in all of their glory won't be thought of more highly than Judah itself. 8I, the Lord God, will protect Jerusalem. Even the weakest person there will be as strong as David, and David's kingdom will rule as though my very own angel were its leader. 9I am determined to wipe out every nation that attacks Jerusalem.
Mourning for the One Pierced with a Spear
10 I, the Lord, will make the descendants of David and the people of Jerusalem feel deep sorrow and pray when they see the one they pierced with a spear. They will mourn and weep for him, as parents weep over the death of their only child or their first-born. 11On that day the people of Jerusalem will mourn as much as everyone did for Hadad Rimmon on the flatlands near Megiddo. 12Everyone of each family in the land will mourn, and the men will mourn separately from the women. This includes those from the family of David, and the families of Nathan, 13Levi, Shimei, 14and all other families as well.
translation_text:
1Naawen wari ale nna a ta va Izirali nyiŋ. Naawen dii ale nye wenzuk, ale ŋman dueni tɛŋzuk de nyubini la, ate ku nyini wadek po ate wa nye nurubiik chiik la, waai meena abe seba dila kama. Wa ale a weeni diila ale nna: 2<<Mi ale nye Jerusalem ase ka daam ale bo beerik po la: tɛŋ sii ale moata ka la a dan nyu, ba ale nyiem a ja kama ase danyuirisa la. Ba le gilim Juda ale Jerusalem a siti ba. 3Dai dila danni, tɛŋsaŋa meena ale ta ka chaab ale Jerusalem. Mi ale nye Jerusalem ase ka piuŋjaaliŋ kuui ale kaa choa la a te tɛŋsaŋa meena. Baai ale za ba voori ku la za ba kɔni ka badek. 4Dai dila danni mi ale nye kama ate wusuma kpaziita a nak ate baai ale ba dɔ ŋa la ale chim yesiŋsa.>> Ka Naawen ale weeni dila. <<Mi nina ale kasim a nya Juda demma zuk kama, alege mi ale nye ate tɛŋsaŋa meena wusumaŋa ninaŋa a yi. 5Kula nyiŋ Juda niŋdeerɔma ale weeni ba suiniima po ayen, <Jerusalem demma a ta pagrim la, dii nyiŋla Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale ka ba Wen la nyiŋ.>
6<<Dai dila danni mi ale nye Juda ase ka bolim ale bo daata po a dɛ diila, ate ba ŋman a nye ase bolim ŋiak ale chogsi ŋan kosa a dɛ diila. Bu za bu kasim a dɛ ka nuruma a gala ale a juga meena alege jaab a kan maa nye Jerusalem demma ale ba tɛŋka. 7<<Naawen ale dɛ ka niŋ a vari Juda demma a basi, ate Deevid ŋaaŋbisaŋa ale Jerusalem demma zula ŋaai ate ba za ba nya la a kan gaam Juda demma. 8Dai dila danni Naawen ale lik baai ale bo Jerusalem la kama, ate nuru baai ale wobsa a maa bo ba po la ale nya pagrim ase Deevid la, ate Deevid yenni ale dɛ ba niŋ ase Naawen Maarɔ la. 9Dai dila danni, mi ale kaasi tɛŋ kpieŋ sii meena ale ta chaab ale Jerusalem la kama.
10<<Ate mi ale pai chiik a basi Deevid yenni ale Jerusalem demma zuk, ka ale chim ka niauŋ ale puusa chiik. Ba ale nya mi, mi waai ate ba jam pai gbaluku a chub la, ate ba ale kum ase waai ale a kum wa biik yeŋ nyiŋ diila, ate ba ale kum ka nna yegayega nna se waai ale a kum wa biik kpagi nyiŋ diila. 11Dai dila danni Jerusalem demma a za ba a kum ka nna yegayega. Kumsaŋa de za ŋa pagra kama ase Yadad Arimmon ale bo Megiddo peelimmu po la. 12Tɛŋka dɔkdemma wanyi wanyi ale ba pooba za ba kum kama: Deevid dɔkdemma ale ba pooba ale kum Natan dɔkdemma ale ba pooba mɛ ale kum. 13Livai dɔkdemma ale ba pooba ale kum, Simei dɔkdemma ale ba pooba ale kum, 14ale dɔkdemma baai meena ale tali la ale ba pooba meena ale kum.

english_text:
Getting Rid of Idols and False Prophets
1In the future there will be a fountain, where David's descendants and the people of Jerusalem can wash away their sin and guilt.
2The Lord All-Powerful says:
When that time comes, I will get rid of every idol in the country, and they will be forgotten forever. I will also do away with their prophets and those evil spirits that control them. 3If any such prophets ever appear again, their own parents must warn them that they will die for telling lies in my name—the name of the Lord. If those prophets don't stop speaking, their parents must then kill them with a sword.
4Those prophets will be ashamed of their so-called visions, and they won't deceive anyone by dressing like a true prophet. 5Instead, they will say, “I'm no prophet. I've been a farmer all my life.”
6And if any of them are asked why they are wounded, they will answer, “It happened at the house of some friends.”
A Wounded Shepherd and Scattered Sheep
7 The Lord All-Powerful said:
My sword, wake up! Attack
my shepherd and friend.
Strike down the shepherd!
Scatter the little sheep,
and I will destroy them.
8Nowhere in the land
will more than a third of them
be left alive.
9Then I will purify them
and put them to the test,
just as gold and silver
are purified and tested.
They will pray in my name,
and I will answer them.
I will say, “You are my people,”
and they will reply,
“You, Lord, are our God!”
translation_text:
1<<Dai dila danni, mi ale lagri nyiam a te Deevid ŋaaŋbisaŋa ale Jerusalem demma, ate nya bula ale sugri ba biem ale daŋta tuima a basi.
2<<Dai dila danni, mi le yeeri bɔgtaŋa yueŋa tɛŋka zuk, ate ba a kan ŋman teeri ti wari ya.>> Ka Naawen Dii Ale A Dɛ Tugurik Tɔŋdɔma Niŋ La ale weeni. Wa ŋman weeni kama ayen, <M le yeeri biisiteerɔma ale baai ale ta chiik daŋtisa la tɛŋka zuk.>> 3Ate waai dan diem a weeni chum po wie, kula choa nyɔnɔwa ko ale wa ma ale weeni wa ayen ba ko wa dii nyiŋla wa pai ka Naawen yuenni a weeni venta wie.
