13<<Nama Sinsak sagrɔma ale Farisiima, ku le jam bie kama ni jigi. Ni ka sakpaŋ zula nyam. Nama ale a sak nuruma diila a nye ase nama a yik ka Wen naamu nansuiŋku tuoku a lik ba nimbie po la. Nama dek a kan yaali ayen ni jo du, ni be kan basi ate nuruba a jo du. 14Nama Sinsak sagrɔma ale Farisiima, ku le jam bie kama ni jigi. Ni ka sakpaŋ zula nyam. Nama nyiem a ga a paasi ka pukɔga a tuesi ba ŋanta ale ge a paasi waai meena a puusi puusi woŋta a te Wen. Dila nyiŋla, wa dan jam ayen wa bo ni buusa, ni waalika le zuak yegayega.
15<<Nama Sinsak sagrɔma ale Farisiima, ku le jam bie kama ni jigi. Ni ka sakpaŋ zula nyam. Nama nina a muni ka nna yegayega ayen ni nye ate nuruba a tagri a va nama Wen puusika suiku. Ba dan va nama nyeka ba yaa tom tuimbaata a nya waalika a gaam nama.
16<<Nama yeema nna, baai ale a de nuruba niŋ la. Ku le jam bie kama ni jigi. Nama a sak kama ayen, <Nuru waai a dan wi Wen yenni yuei a pɛ ŋmoruk, ku daa wari ya. Alege wa dan wi ligmɔniŋka ale bo Wen yenni po la yuei a pɛ ŋmoruk, ku ka wakpienni.> 17Nama yeo bettaŋa nna, ka ba wana ale gaam wa choa? Wen yenni yaa ligmɔniŋka ale bo di po la? Ka Wen yenni ale a basi ate ligmɔniŋka a nala. 18Ni be ŋman sak mɛ ayen, <Waai a dan wi kuŋkuŋku yuei a pɛ ŋmoruk ku daa wari ya. Alege waai a dan wi Wen tiirim buui ale bo wa yenni po la yuei a pɛ, ku ka wari.> 19Ni ka yeeba. Ka ba wana ale gaam wa choa? Tiirimu yaa jabuui zuk ate tiirimu a dua la? Ka kuŋkuŋku ale a nye ate tiirimu a welema. 20Nuru waai a dan wi kuŋkuŋku yuei a pɛ, wa maa pɛ ka kuŋkuŋku ale jaab meena ale dua ku zuk la yuei mɛ nyiŋ. 21Nuru waai abe dan wi Wen yenni yuei a pɛ, wa maa pɛ ka Wen yenni ale waai ale bo di po la mɛ yuei nyiŋ. 22Nuru waai a dan wi wenŋmazuk yuei a pɛ, wa maa pɛ ka Wen zukpaglika ale waai ale kali ka zuk la, yuei mɛ nyiŋ.
23<<Nama Sinsak sagrɔma ale Farisiima, ku le jam bie kama ni jigi. Ni ka sakpaŋ zula nyam. Ni a sak kama ayen ŋan baai ate ni pai a nyo jenta po la, ni a lueri ku nɔi piwa po bunyi a te Wen. Alege nyemagsika ale jiirim ale wensie ale nye wari yegayega la ni zɛri. Wie ŋaai ale magsi ayen ni a nye la ale la ase ni a nin poom a nye nŋala. 24Ni a nye ase ka yeeba la. Nama nyiem zɛri ka nanjuŋ nɛka alege nɛ laalaakomi.
25<<Nama Sinsak sagrɔma ale Farisiima, ku le jam bie kama ni jigi. Ni ka sakpaŋ zula nyam. Ku a nye ka nna ase ni ale a nari beerisa ale china ŋaaŋ alege a basi puusaŋa po diila. Ni suiniimaŋa po a sueri ale ka varuk ale butuem nyeka nyiini. 26Nama Farisiima a nye ase ka yeeba la. Ni liŋ sugri ni suiniimaŋa po ate nuruba a sum seba ayen nama a tom ka tuimaŋsa.
27<<Nama Sinsak sagrɔma ale Farisiima, ku le jam bie kama ni jigi. Ni ka sakpaŋ zula nyam. Nama a nye ase ka boosi tii nyiŋsa ale a nyaksi alege ti puusaŋa po a sueri ale koba nyiini ale daŋ mɛ nna yegayega la. 28Suik kula po ate nama a nyiem a paasi nuruba ayen nama a tom ka tuimaŋsa, alege ni suiniimaŋa po a sueri ale ka sakpaŋ zula ale tuimbaata nyiini.
29<<Nama Sinsak sagrɔma ale Farisiima, ku le jam bie kama ni jigi. Ni ka sakpaŋ zula nyam. Nama a nye ate Wen biisiteerɔma ale nuru maŋsa baai ale kpi dipo la, boositaŋa a kasim a nyaksi. 30Ni nyiem a kasim a weeni chaab ayen ase tama a dan jam maa bo ka ti kokpieŋsaŋa tɛŋka po, tama ate an jam maa gum ba po a ko Wen biisiteerɔma. 31Nama a siak kama ayen nama ka baai ale ko Wen biisiteerɔma la, ŋaaŋbisa. 32Ni kokpieŋsaŋa ale piilim diila, ni kasim tom nueri. 33Ni a nye ase ka wiiga la. Ni ka waapiisa buuri. Nama a poli ayen nama ale nye ka sɛ a chali bɛ ale bolim buui ale kan maara kpimsi la po joka?
34<<Mi a weeni ni kama ayen, mi ale tom Wen biisiteerɔba ale yam nyam ale sagrɔba ate ba jam ni jigi. Nama ale pai ba gela a yik ŋanbarinta nyiŋsa a ko ba, abe ni miiri ba gela ale fiŋsa ni tuka dɔkku po abe ni yiak ba ate ba nyini ni tɛŋsaŋa po a nyini. 35Ni kokpieŋsaŋa a liŋ jam ko ka nuru wanyi waai ate ba a wi ayen Abel ate wa an jam a kaasi wari la. Ba jam ko nuru maŋsa yegayega. Nuru waai ate ba jam ko kpeglim la a jam le Barakaya nidoabinni Zakaria. Ba jam ko wa ka kuŋkuŋku ale Wen yenni suŋsuŋ. Wen ale te ni waalika abe wa weeni ayen nama ale soa baai meena ale jam kan kaasi wari la, kummu. 36Wensie ate mi a weeni ni Wen ale te Juuma baai ale diem boro jinla la waalika abe wa weeni ayen bala ale soa ate wieŋa de meena a nye.
37<<Jerusalem, Jerusalem, nama a ko Wen biisiteerɔma ale yuk baai ate Wen a tom ba ni jigi la ale tana, ka bu dina ate mi ale tigsi ni bisaŋa jigi yeŋ ase kpiak ale a pɔbi ka bisa diila alege nama a kan siagi? 38Ku kan beni ate Wen yenni a kaasi. 39Mi a weeni nama kama yɔgyɔgla de ayen ni kan ŋman nya mi see ka m ŋman jamka danni. Da dila danni a dan paari, nama ale weeni ayen, <Niaka a bo waai ale cheena Naawen yuenni nyiŋla.> >> (Yiila 118:26)

english_text:
The Temple Will Be Destroyed
(Mark 13.1,2; Luke 21.5,6)
1After Jesus left the temple, his disciples came over and said, “Look at all these buildings!”
2Jesus replied, “Do you see these buildings? They will certainly be torn down! Not one stone will be left in place.”
Warning about Trouble
(Mark 13.3-13; Luke 21.7-19)
3 Later, as Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, his disciples came to him in private and asked, “When will this happen? What will be the sign of your coming and of the end of the world?”
4Jesus answered:
Don't let anyone fool you. 5Many will come and claim to be me. They will say they are the Messiah, and they will fool many people.
6You will soon hear about wars and threats of wars, but don't be afraid. These things will have to happen first, but that isn't the end. 7 Nations and kingdoms will go to war against each other. People will starve to death, and in some places there will be earthquakes. 8But this is just the beginning of troubles.
9 You will be arrested, punished, and even killed. Because of me, you will be hated by people of all nations. 10Many will give up and will betray and hate each other. 11Many false prophets will come and fool a lot of people. 12Evil will spread and cause many people to stop loving others. 13 But if you keep on being faithful right to the end, you will be saved. 14When the good news about the kingdom has been preached all over the world and told to all nations, the end will come.
The Horrible Thing
(Mark 13.14-23; Luke 21.20-24)
15 Someday you will see that “Horrible Thing” in the holy place, just as the prophet Daniel said. Everyone who reads this must try to understand! 16If you are living in Judea at that time, run to the mountains. 17 If you are on the roof of your house, don't go inside to get anything. 18If you are out in the field, don't go back for your coat. 19It will be a terrible time for women who are expecting babies or nursing young children. 20And pray that you won't have to escape in winter or on a Sabbath. 21 This will be the worst time of suffering since the beginning of the world, and nothing this terrible will ever happen again. 22If God doesn't make the time shorter, no one will be left alive. But because of God's chosen ones, he will make the time shorter.
23Someone may say, “Here is the Messiah!” or “There he is!” But don't believe it. 24False messiahs and false prophets will come and work great miracles and signs. They will even try to fool God's chosen ones. 25But I have warned you ahead of time. 26 If you are told the Messiah is out in the desert, don't go there! And if you are told he is in some secret place, don't believe it! 27The coming of the Son of Man will be like lightning that can be seen from east to west. 28 Where there is a corpse, there will always be vultures.
When the Son of Man Appears
(Mark 13.24-27; Luke 21.25-28)
29 Right after those days of suffering,
“The sun will become dark,
and the moon
will no longer shine.
The stars will fall,
and the powers in the sky
will be shaken.”
30 Then a sign will appear in the sky. And there will be the Son of Man. All nations on earth will weep when they see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. 31At the sound of a loud trumpet, he will send his angels to bring his chosen ones together from all over the earth.
A Lesson from a Fig Tree
(Mark 13.28-31; Luke 21.29-33)
32Learn a lesson from a fig tree. When its branches sprout and start putting out leaves, you know summer is near. 33So when you see all these things happening, you will know the time has almost come. 34I can promise you that some of the people of this generation will still be alive when all this happens. 35The sky and the earth won't last forever, but my words will.
No One Knows the Day or Time
(Mark 13.32-37; Luke 17.26-30,34-36)
36No one knows the day or hour. The angels in heaven don't know, and the Son himself doesn't know. Only the Father knows. 37 When the Son of Man appears, things will be just as they were when Noah lived. 38People were eating, drinking, and getting married right up to the day the flood came and Noah went into the big boat. 39 They didn't know anything was happening until the flood came and swept them all away. This is how it will be when the Son of Man appears.
40Two men will be in the same field, but only one will be taken. The other will be left. 41Two women will be together grinding grain, but only one will be taken. The other will be left. 42So be on your guard! You don't know when your Lord will come. 43 Homeowners never know when a thief is coming, and they are always on guard to keep one from breaking in. 44Always be ready! You don't know when the Son of Man will come.
Faithful and Unfaithful Servants
(Luke 12.35-48)
45Who are faithful and wise servants? Who are the ones the master will put in charge of giving the other servants their food supplies at the proper time? 46Servants are fortunate if their master comes and finds them doing their job. 47You may be sure a servant who is always faithful will be put in charge of everything the master owns. 48But suppose one of the servants thinks the master won't return until late. 49Suppose this evil servant starts beating the other servants and eats and drinks with people who are drunk. 50If that happens, the master will surely come on a day and at a time when the servant least expects him. 51This servant will then be punished and thrown out with the ones who only pretended to serve their master. There they will cry and grit their teeth in pain.
translation_text:
1Yeezu ale yiti Wen yenni po a nyini la, wa ŋaaŋviirɔma yaa dak Wen yenni a sak wa. 2Wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni basi ate m weeni a sak ni. Ku danni a cheena kama ate nuruba a jam kaasi jaabuuri ale bo dela la. Ba kan basi tintain yeŋ mɛ di choa zuwa.>>
3Yeezu ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔma nyiini yaa cheŋ ga jueli kala Olivi Guuku zuk. Ba yaa bek wa ayen, <<Weeni ti, ka dimpo ate wieŋa de meena ale nye, be ka boa ale ku nye ate ku sak ti ayen fi jamka ale tɛŋka zuk meena kpeglimka danni a moata kama?>>
4Wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni kpesi nidek ate waai kan paasi ni. 5Nuruba yegayega ale jam pai mi yuenni nyiŋ a wi badek a weeni ayen ba ka Kirisitawa abe ba paasi nuruba yegayega. Ku a fɛ kama ayen nama a kan va ba. 6Ni dan wom kpaliŋsa wie ate si gela a moata ale ge si gela mɛ a bo niŋniŋa, ni kan chali yɔgsummoa. Kula ale sak ni ayen tɛŋka kpeglimka danni a moata kama. 7Tɛŋsa ale yiti a ta chaab ate naata mɛ a yiti a ta chaab. Ate kɔm a boro ate tɛŋka choa jigi meena. 8Wieŋa de meena a nye ase ka nipok lɔgi ale a dom alege ate wa a biak la.
9<<Nuruba ale yik ni a ta ni ga nyo baai ale ba basi ate ni nya ninam la nisima po ate ba ko ni. Waai meena ale kisi ni mi vaka nyiŋ. 10Va ŋala po nuruba yegayega baai ale jam ta siaka ale mi la, ale ŋmani mi ŋaaŋ vaka. Ba le kisi chaab abe ba bobri chaab a sak. 11Biisiteerɔba yegayega baai ale kan seba Wen la, ale jam paasi nuruba yegayega. 12Nuruba yegayega ale jam basi chaab yaalika, dii nyiŋla nuruba tuimbaata ale jam waaŋ a tagli jigi meena. 13Waai a dan pik a ga paari ku nueri ka, Wen ale vari wa a basi. 14Nuruba ale jam pai Wen wamaŋsaŋa a sak nuruba Wen naamu wie. Waai meena ale bo tɛŋka zuk la le liŋ wom wa wamaŋsaŋa wieŋa ale ge ate tɛŋka meena a kpeglim.
15<<Ni wom mi wieŋa de nalimnyiini. Wen biisiteerɔwa Daniel, a jam ŋmarisi wabiok kuui ale ku jam basi ate nuruba a nam la wie kama Wen gbaŋka po dipo. Nama ale nya ale ku za juijui ale kan magsi ku za la.>> Nuru waai ale a karim wieŋa de la, abe miŋ chak. 16<<Baai meena ale bo Judia tɛŋka po la, yiti a pii nyiŋ chali nna yegayega a ga suk guutaŋa po. 17Baai ale bo ba gbirima zuima la dan wom wabiokku de wie, ba kan ŋman yaali ayen ba siŋ a jo ba diinaŋa po a pai ba ŋanta. 18Baai mɛ ale bo ba kaduksa po la dan wom wanni de, ba mɛ kan ŋman jo ba diinaŋa po ayen ba pai ŋanta. 19Da ŋala po ku le jam pagra nna yegayega a te nipok puusa ale baai ale ta buluata la. 20Ni a puusi a te Wen ate kude a kan jam nye ŋoota wein ya yaase ba Vuusum Danni. 21Ku dan paari da ŋala ninam buui ate nuruba ale nam la ale gaam ninam meena ate nuruba, a nam a ta nyini diipo ate Wen a nye tɛŋka la. Ninam bula choa a kan ŋman jam. 22Wen poom yeeri ninam daaŋa po ŋa gela a basi kama, dii nyiŋla baai ate wa lueri ayen ba jam va wa la nyiŋ. Wa dan kan yeeri ninammu daaŋa gela a basi ya, waai ate kan nyini ninammu po a nyini.
23<<Da ŋala po waai dan weeni ayen, <Ni nya, Kirisitawa ale nna,> yaase <Ni nya, Kirisitawa ale la,> ni kan wom wa. 24Nuruba gela ale jam yiti a paasi nuruba ayen ba ale Kirisitawa. Ba baai mɛ le jam a weeni ayen ba ka Wen biisiteerɔba. Ba le jam a tom wakperikaliisa nna yegayega a yaali ayen ba dan poom baga ba paasi baai ate Wen a lueri ayen ba va wa la. 25Ni wom mi wieŋa de nalimnyiini. Mi poom liŋ weeni ni ba le cheena ayen ba nye ni diila kama. 26Va ŋala po nuru wanyi ale weeni ayen, <Ni nya, Kirisitawa a bo ka sagni po.> Wa chɔ mɛ ale weeni ni ayen, <Ni nya, Kirisitawa a suk bo ka dewa.> Nama kan a wom ba. 27Mi Saalɔbiika ŋman jamka ale nye a ase ka nyaksika la a nyini kori a taam siŋ yeniŋ ate nuruba nya. 28Ni seba ayen jakpiuk ale dua juijui la duinsa a bo ka dula.
29<<Alege ninammu daaŋa a dan jam taam, Wenbinni ale sobri ate chiika a kan nya. (Azaya 13:10) Chiŋmarisaŋa le nyini wenŋmazuk a lo ate ŋan baai meena ale bo wenŋmazuk a ta pagrim la mɛ a choa. 30Saalɔbiika jam ka daanaŋa ale jam chiŋmaaŋa po, ate tɛŋka meena demma ale kum, dii nyiŋla ba le nya Mi Saalɔbiika ale m nyini chiŋmaaŋa po a cheena ale pagrim ale zula yega. 31Mi ale tom maarɔma ale damuniŋ peerika ate ba tigsi nuru baai ate Wen lueri a ta nyini tɛŋka meena la.
32<<Ni basi ate kiŋkaŋ a sak ni wari kiri. Ni nyiem a dan nya ale ka boro a pusi vaata, ni seba ayen kpari wein a moata kama. 33Suik kula po mɛ, ni dan nya wieŋa de meena ale ŋa boro a nye, ni le seba ayen da ŋala a moata kama. 34Wensie ate mi a weeni ni gaŋka de a kan sum taam ka wieŋa de meena a nin nye. 35Wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋzuk meena ale jam taam dai yeŋ po, alege mi wieŋa a kan taam diipo diipo.
36<<Nuru waai a zɛ Mi Saalɔbiika ŋman jamka danni. Mi ale Wen maarɔma mɛ dek a zɛ, alege ka m Kowa nyiini ale seba. 37Mi ŋman jamka ale nye ase ka dii ale jam nye ase ka Nowa daaŋa po la. 38Ase Nowa ale jam boro a nye wa ŋaaruŋ kpioŋku la, waai meena jam boro a nye ka wadek ale a yaali diila. Ba jam kasim a dɛ ŋandiinta ale a nyu ate nidoaba me a faari nipooba. Ba kasim a nye ka dila a ta ga paari diipo ate Nowa a jo wa ŋaaruŋku po alege ate nyiam a jam la. 39Ba jam zɛ ayen Wen ale basi ate nyiam jam a sueri tɛŋka meena a gbiti ba ko. Mi Saalɔbiika jamka ale nye ase ka dai dila danni la. 40Dai dila dek danni nuruba baye ale bo ba kaduksa po a kpa, ate Wen a pai wanyi a ta cheŋ abe wa ge wanyi wa. 41Nipooba baye ale bo nanzuk po a num zom, ate wa pai wanyi abe wa ge wanyi wa.
42<<Ni kpesi nidek abe ni a limisi, dii nyiŋla ni zɛ dai dii danni ate ni Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita a cheena la. 43Ni basi ate m weeni ni ayen ase yeri nyɔnɔ a dan seba ayen zueba ale jam wa yeri, wa ale kasim a nya kama ate zuema a kan baga a jo zu. Wa kan goa see ka wa nin yik ba. 44Diipo ate nama a kan ŋman poli ayen Mi Saalɔbiika ale jam la, dila po ale m cheena. Ka dila ale soa ayen ni gomsi a magsi a limisi la.
45<<Ka nama wana dek ale wa chim wensie ale yam nyɔnɔ wieŋa de meena po? Ku a nye ase ka yeri nyɔnɔ waai ale lueri wa tomteerɔma po wanyi ayen wa chim kpagi mbala zuk abe wa a te ba ŋandiinta diipo ale magsi la. 46Tomteerɔ waai ate wa kpagi a jam paari ale wa a tom wa tuini la a ta suipeentik kama. 47Wensie ate mi a weeni ni, yenni nyɔnɔwa yaa le basi ate wa a nya wa yenni ŋantaŋa meena zuk a te wa. 48Alege tomteerɔwa waai ate yenni nyɔnɔwa a lueri la, a dan ka nyiŋworuk nyɔnɔ, wa a weeni wadek kama ayen wa nyɔnɔwa a kan jamu nwuli. 49Dila nyiŋla wa yaa yik wa tomteerɔ chaama a nak kama alege cheŋ a ga gum baai ale boro a dɛ ŋandiinta ale a nyu daata a bugi la jigi. 50Dai dii danni ate wa kan poli ayen wa nyɔnɔwa a cheena la, dai dila danni dek ate wa cheena. 51Wa nyɔnɔwa a dan jam nya dii ate wa tom la, wa sui ale puuri nna yegayega ale wa, ate wa namsi wa abe wa pai wa a gum chaab ale sakpaŋ zula nyama. Wa ale bo ka dula a kum abe wa a ŋɔbi wa nyinaŋa.

english_text:
A Story about Ten Young Women
1 The kingdom of heaven is like what happened one night when ten young women took their oil lamps and went to a wedding to meet the groom. 2Five of them were foolish and five were wise. 3The foolish ones took their lamps, but no extra oil. 4The ones who were wise took along extra oil for their lamps.
5The groom was late arriving, and the young women became drowsy and fell asleep. 6Then in the middle of the night someone shouted, “Here's the groom! Come to meet him!”
7When the women got up and started getting their lamps ready, 8the foolish ones said to the others, “Let us have some of your oil! Our lamps are going out.”
9Those who were wise answered, “There's not enough oil for all of us! Go and buy some for yourselves.”
10While the foolish ones were on their way to get some oil, the groom arrived. The five who were ready went into the wedding, and the doors were closed. 11 Later the others returned and shouted, “Sir, sir! Open the door for us!”
12But the groom replied, “I don't even know you!”
13So, my disciples, always be ready! You don't know the day or the time when all this will happen.
A Story about Three Servants
(Luke 19.11-27)
14 The kingdom is also like what happened when a man went away and put his three servants in charge of all he owned. 15The man knew what each servant could do. So he handed 5,000 coins to the first servant, 2,000 to the second, and 1,000 to the third. Then he left the country.
16As soon as the man had gone, the servant with the 5,000 coins used them to earn 5,000 more. 17The servant who had 2,000 coins did the same with his money and earned 2,000 more. 18But the servant with 1,000 coins dug a hole and hid his master's money in the ground.
19Some time later the master of those servants returned. He called them in and asked what they had done with his money. 20The servant who had been given 5,000 coins brought them in with the 5,000 that he had earned. He said, “Sir, you gave me 5,000 coins, and I have earned 5,000 more.”
21“Wonderful!” his master replied. “You are a good and faithful servant. I left you in charge of only a little, but now I will put you in charge of much more. Come and share in my happiness!”
22Next, the servant who had been given 2,000 coins came in and said, “Sir, you gave me 2,000 coins, and I have earned 2,000 more.”
23“Wonderful!” his master replied. “You are a good and faithful servant. I left you in charge of only a little, but now I will put you in charge of much more. Come and share in my happiness!”
24The servant who had been given 1,000 coins then came in and said, “Sir, I know that you are hard to work for. You harvest what you don't plant and gather crops where you haven't scattered seed. 25I was frightened and went out and hid your money in the ground. Here is every single coin!”
26The master of the servant told him, “You are lazy and good-for-nothing! You know I harvest what I don't plant and gather crops where I haven't scattered seed. 27You could have at least put my money in the bank, so I could have earned interest on it.”
28Then the master said, “Now your money will be taken away and given to the servant with 10,000 coins! 29 Everyone who has something will be given more, and they will have more than enough. But everything will be taken from those who don't have anything. 30 You are a worthless servant, and you will be thrown out into the dark where people will cry and grit their teeth in pain.”
The Final Judgment
31 When the Son of Man comes in his glory with all his angels, he will sit on his royal throne. 32The people of all nations will be brought before him, and he will separate them, as shepherds separate their sheep from their goats.
33He will place the sheep on his right and the goats on his left. 34Then the king will say to those on his right, “My father has blessed you! Come and receive the kingdom that was prepared for you before the world was created. 35 When I was hungry, you gave me something to eat, and when I was thirsty, you gave me something to drink. When I was a stranger, you welcomed me, 36and when I was naked, you gave me clothes to wear. When I was sick, you took care of me, and when I was in jail, you visited me.”
37Then the ones who pleased the Lord will ask, “When did we give you something to eat or drink? 38When did we welcome you as a stranger or give you clothes to wear 39or visit you while you were sick or in jail?”
40The king will answer, “Whenever you did it for any of my people, no matter how unimportant they seemed, you did it for me.”
41Then the king will say to those on his left, “Get away from me! You are under God's curse. Go into the everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels! 42I was hungry, but you did not give me anything to eat, and I was thirsty, but you did not give me anything to drink. 43I was a stranger, but you did not welcome me, and I was naked, but you did not give me any clothes to wear. I was sick and in jail, but you did not take care of me.”
44Then the people will ask, “Lord, when did we fail to help you when you were hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in jail?”
45The king will say to them, “Whenever you failed to help any of my people, no matter how unimportant they seemed, you failed to do it for me.”
46 Then Jesus said, “Those people will be punished forever. But the ones who pleased God will have eternal life.”

1<<Wen naamu ale nye ase ka nipokbilisa piwa baai ale yiti pai ba zeuŋta a ta cheŋ ayen ba tu nipok fiaka nyɔnɔwa la. 2Ba piwa po ka banu ale jam ta yam, alege mbala banuwa me a jam chim betta. 3Bettaŋa tinuwa a yaa pai ba zeuŋtaŋa alege ba an pai kpaam a magsi ase mbula a dan nueri abe ba pai nyoro la. 4Alege yammu nyama a ta kpaam a gum du a magsi ayen mbula a dan nueri abe ba pai nyoro. 5Nipok fiaka nyɔnɔwa a yaa an jam nwuli, ate nipokbilisaŋa yaa doa a goa.
6<<Ku le jam paari goota suŋsuŋ la, nuru wanyi yaa kaari ayen, <Nipok fiaka nyɔnɔ a cheena. Ni yiti nwuli ate ni ga tu wa.> 7Nipokbilisaŋa piwa yaa deri yiti nna nwuli a viriŋ ayen ba nya ase ba zeuŋtaŋa diem a dɛ ya. 8Bettaŋa nyama zeuŋtaŋa kpaamu nyiini ale jam nueri, ate ba yaa weeni yammu nyama ayen ba nye ba kpaamu a te ba ate ba nyo ba zeuŋtaŋa po. 9Yammu nyama yaa weeni ba ayen, <Tama kpaamu an soa diiya. Dila nyiŋ, ni cheŋ yeeŋa po a ga da kpaam.> 10Bettaŋa yaa cheŋ ayen ba da ba kpaamu. Ba le cheŋ a ga nueri la, nipok fiaka nyɔnɔwa a yaa jam. Yammu nyama ale poom ta ba kpaamu a magsi la, yaa deri va nipok fiaka nyɔnɔwa a jo yenni po ayen ba maa dɛ nipok fiak ŋandiintaŋa. Ba meena ale jo yenni po a nueri la, ba yaa yik nansuiŋku tuoku a lik. 11Ku le ga nye magadek la, bettaŋa tinuwa yaa le ŋmani jam paari la ale tuoku a lik kama. Ba yaa za tuoku nɔi a nak ale a wi ayen ba jam lagri a te ba. 12Nipok fiaka nyɔnɔwa ale wom ba luelutaŋa la, wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <Ni goori ni wanni abe ni cheŋ du. Mi zɛ ni ale ka baai la.> 13Ni chiib a limisi, dii nyiŋla ni zɛ diipo ate mi a cheena la.
14<<Mi dan ŋman jam, Wen naamu ale nye ase ka nuru waai ale gomsi a magsi ayen wa nyiem la. Wa le gomsi nueri la, wa yaa wi wa tomteerɔma batawa yaa pai wa ŋantaŋa meena a nyo ba nisima po ayen ba a nya ba zuk ate wa jam. 15Wa yaa pai wa ŋantaŋa a chari ba a va waai meena ale a tom wa tuima diila. Wa yaa te niŋ nyɔnɔwa ligra tusa ŋanu (5,000), ale te waai ale pai saŋ la ligra tusa ŋaye (2,000), ale ge te butawa nyɔnɔwa ligra tusidi. Wa le chari ba nueri la, wa yaa cheŋ. 16Tomteerɔ waai ale tuesi ligra tusa ŋanuwa (5,000) la, a pai ŋa kama a gerim a nya ligra tusa ŋanu (5,000) nyuenta. 17Buyewa nyɔnɔwa mɛ ale tuesi ligra tusa ŋayewa (2,000) la, a pai ŋa kama a gerim a nya ligra tusa ŋaye (2,000) mɛ nyuenta. 18Alege tomteerɔ waai ale tuesi ligra tusini la a pai wa nyɔnɔwa ligraŋa kama a tu tɛŋ a gu.
19<<Ku yaa ale ga beni ate ba nyɔnɔwa a nyini wa nyeerimu jigini a jam la ate wa yaa wi ba ayen ba jam wa jigi. Ba le jam wa jigi la, wa yaa bek ba ayen wa a yaali kama ayen wa nya waai meena ale pai wa ligra a gerim a nya dii nyuenta la. 20Tomteerɔwa waai ale tuesi ligra tusa ŋanuwa (5,000) la, yaa nyini a weeni wa ayen, <M nyɔnɔ, fi daam pai ka ligra tusa ŋanu (5,000) a te mi ate mi yaa pai ŋa a gerim a nya ligra tusa ŋanu (5,000) nyuenta a ŋman gum du.> 21Wa nyɔnɔwa yaa weeni wa ayen, <Fi ka nuru maŋ ale nye ate ku nala. Mi daam pai ka ligra maga dega a nyo fi nisima po alege fi yaa baga a nye ate ŋa zuak a gum du. Yɔgyɔgla de mi a yaali kama ayen m pai ligra yegayega a nyo fi nisima po ate fi ale mi ta suipeentik.>
22<<Tomteerɔwa waai ale tuesi ligra tusa ŋayewa (2,000) la, mɛ yaa nyini a weeni ayen, <M nyɔnɔ, fi daam pai ka ligra tusa ŋaye (2,000) a te mi ate mi yaa pai ŋa a gerim a nya ligra tusa ŋaye (2,000) nyuenta a ŋman gum du.> 23Wa nyɔnɔwa yaa weeni wa ayen, <Fi mɛ ka nuru maŋ ale nye ate ku nala. Mi daam pai ka ligra maga dega a nyo fi nisima po, alege fi a yaa baga a nye ate ŋa zuak a gum du. Yɔgyɔgla de mi a yaali kama ayen m pai ligra yegayega a nyo fi nisima po, ate fi ale mi a ta suipeentik.>
24<<Tomteerɔwa waai ale tuesi ligra tusini la, mɛ yaa nyini a taam zaani wa niŋ a weeni ayen, <M nyɔnɔ, m seba ayen fi nyeka tua kama, dii nyiŋla fi a che ka za ŋaai ate fi an bori la ale a vaari za ŋaai mɛ ate fi an fɔbi la. 25Fi le pai ligraŋa a te mi la, mi daam a chali ka yɔgsum yaa ta ŋa a ga tu tɛŋ a gu. Nya, lig ŋaai ate fi daam a pai te mi la ale nna.>
26<<Wa nyɔnɔwa ale wom dii ate wa weeni la, wa sui yaa jam puuri nna yegayega ale wa ate wa yaa weeni wa ayen, <Fi ka nuru biok ale nyiŋworuk nyɔnɔ. Fi a poli kama ayen mi a che ka za ŋaai ate mi an bori la ale a vaari za ŋaai mɛ ate mi an fɔbi la. 27Ku magsi kama ayen fi daam ate pai m ligraŋa a te ka nuru waai ale wa pai ŋa a gerimu a nya nyuenta a gum du a te mu la. 28Tuesi ligraŋa wa jigi a pai ŋa a te m tomteerɔma wanyi wa waai ale ta ligra tusa piwa (10,000) la.
29<<Nuru waai ale a pii nyiŋla, ale nya ŋanta a gum du, alege waai ale kan a pii nyiŋla a kan nya jaaboa. 30Ni yik nyiŋworuk nyɔnɔwa de a ta wa a nyini peelim a yuk basi legini po. Dula jigini wa le kum nna yegayega, abe wa a ŋɔbi wa nyinaŋa.>
31<<Alege Mi Saalɔbiika a dan jam ale m zulaŋa ale wa maarɔma m le jam a kala ka m naamu zukpaglika zuk a yaa soa tɛŋka meena. 32Abe m wi waai meena ate ba tigsi a jam m tɛŋ. M le poori ba buye ase naapeerik ale a poori wa piisa ale wa bua diila. 33M le yik baai ale a nye ase piisa la a zaani m juga geŋ, abe m yik baai mɛ ale a nye ase bua la a zaani m gala geŋ.
34<<Naawa yaa weeni baai ale bo m juga geŋ la ayen, <M Kowa a maari ni abe wa niak ni. Wa le jam a nye tɛŋzuk meena la, wa gomsi ka ŋanta a zaani a te ni. Ni be jam a tuesi ba yɔgyɔgla de. 35Kɔm ale jam ta mi la, nama a te mu ŋandiinta ate m dɛ. Nyanyuila mɛ ale jam ta mu la, ni te mu nyiam ate m nyu. M le jam ka nichaanɔ la, ni nye m tia ale ta mu a jo ni yeeŋa po. 36Mi ale jam kan ta gatta la, ni te mu gatta ate m jo. Mi ale jam a yuak la, ni nya m zuk. Ba le jam yik mu a lik la, ni jam a puusi mu.> 37Baai ale ka wayɔrisima nyam a za m juga geŋ la, ba wanyi ale weeni mu ayen, <Naawen yaa, ka dimpo ate tama a nya fu ale kɔm a ta fu ate ti te fu ŋandiinta ate fi dɛ? Ka dimpo mɛ ate tama a nya fu ale nyanyuila a ta fu ate ti te fu nyiam ate fi nyu? 38Ka dimpo ate tama a nya fu ale fi chim nichaanɔ ate tama a nye fi tia ale yik fu a ta jo ti yeeŋa po? Ka dimpo mɛ ate tama a nya fu ale fi an jo gatta ate tama a te fu gatta ayen fi jo? 39Ka dimpo mɛ ate tama a nya fu ale fi a yuak yaase ba yik fu a lik ate tama a jam puusi fu?> 40Naawa weeni ba ayen, <Wensie ate mi a weeni ni ayen dii meena ate nama a nye a te mi ŋaaŋviirɔma po baaŋka mɛ dek la, ni nye a te ka mi dila.>
41<<Dula jigini m le cheem a weeni tuimbaata nyama baai ale bo m gala geŋ la ayen, <Nama baai ate Naawen a ka te ni la, ni cheŋ du mi tɛŋ a cheŋ bolim buui ale kan maara kpimsi ate Naawen a gomsi a magsi a te jabioku ale wa maarɔma. 42Kɔm ale jam ta mu la, nama an te mi ŋandiinta ayen m dɛ. Nyanyuila ale jam ta mu la, nama an te mi nyiam ayen m nyu. 43Mi le jam ka nichaanɔ la, nama an te mi tia ale ta mu a jo ni yeeŋa po. Mi le jam kan ta gatta a jo la, nama an te mi gatta ayen m jo. Mi le jam a yuak ale bo likka dɔk po mɛ la, nama an jam ayen ni nya mi zuwa.> 44Baai ale jam za m gala geŋ la, ba wanyi ale weeni mu ayen, <Naawen yaa, ka dimpo ate tama a nya fu ale kom a yaase nyanyuila a ta fu? Ka dimpo mɛ ate tama a nya fu ale fi ka nichaanɔ yaase fi ka gatta a jo? Ka dimpo ate tama a nya fu ale fi a yuak yaase ba yik fu a lik dɔk po, alege tama an maari fu?> 45M le ŋman weeni ba ayen, <Wensie ate mi a weeni ni ayen diipo meena ate nama an jam maari mi ŋaaŋviirɔma po baaŋka mɛ dek la, nama an maari daa mi.> 46Bade ale jɔk ninam buui ale kan ta kpeglimka la, alege wayɔrisima nyama ale nya nyuvuri dii ale kan ta kpeglimka la.>>

english_text:
The Plot To Kill Jesus
(Mark 14.1,2; Luke 22.1,2; John 11.45-53)
1When Jesus had finished teaching, he told his disciples, 2 “You know two days from now will be Passover. This is when the Son of Man will be handed over to his enemies and nailed to a cross.”
3At that time the chief priests and the nation's leaders were meeting at the home of Caiaphas the high priest. 4They planned how they could sneak around and have Jesus arrested and put to death. 5But they said, “We must not do it during Passover, because the people will riot.”
At Bethany
(Mark 14.3-9; John 12.1-8)
6Jesus was in the town of Bethany, eating at the home of Simon, who had leprosy. 7 A woman came in with a bottle of expensive perfume and poured it on Jesus' head. 8But when his disciples saw this, they became angry and complained, “Why such a waste? 9We could have sold this perfume for a lot of money and given it to the poor.”
10Jesus knew what they were thinking, and he said:
Why are you bothering this woman? She has done a beautiful thing for me. 11 You will always have the poor with you, but you won't always have me. 12She has poured perfume on my body to prepare it for burial. 13You may be sure that wherever the good news is told all over the world, people will remember what she has done. And they will tell others.
Judas and the Chief Priests
(Mark 14.10,11; Luke 22.3-6)
14Judas Iscariot was one of the twelve disciples. He went to the chief priests 15 and asked, “How much will you give me if I help you arrest Jesus?” They paid Judas 30 silver coins, 16and from then on he started looking for a good chance to betray Jesus.
Jesus Eats the Passover Meal with His Disciples
(Mark 14.12-21; Luke 22.7-13; John 13.21-30)
17On the first day of the Festival of Thin Bread, Jesus' disciples came to him and asked, “Where do you want us to prepare the Passover meal?”
18Jesus told them to go to a certain man in the city and tell him, “Our teacher says, ‘My time has come! I want to eat the Passover meal with my disciples in your home.’ ” 19They did as Jesus told them and prepared the meal.
20-21When Jesus was eating with his twelve disciples that evening, he said, “One of you will surely hand me over to my enemies.”
22The disciples were very sad, and each one said to Jesus, “Lord, you can't mean me!”
23 He answered, “One of you men who has eaten with me from this dish will betray me. 24The Son of Man will die, as the Scriptures say. But it's going to be terrible for the one who betrays me! That man would be better off if he had never been born.”
25Judas said, “Teacher, you surely don't mean me!”
“That's what you say!” Jesus replied. But later, Judas did betray him.
The Lord's Supper
(Mark 14.22-26; Luke 22.14-23; 1 Corinthians 11.23-25)
26During the meal Jesus took some bread in his hands. He blessed the bread and broke it. Then he gave it to his disciples and said, “Take this and eat it. This is my body.”
27Jesus picked up a cup of wine and gave thanks to God. He then gave it to his disciples and said, “Take this and drink it. 28 This is my blood, and with it God makes his agreement with you. It will be poured out, so that many people will have their sins forgiven. 29From now on I am not going to drink any wine, until I drink new wine with you in my Father's kingdom.” 30Then they sang a hymn and went out to the Mount of Olives.
Peter's Promise
(Mark 14.27-31; Luke 22.31-34; John 13.36-38)
31 Jesus said to his disciples, “During this very night, all of you will reject me, as the Scriptures say,
‘I will strike down
the shepherd,
and the sheep
will be scattered.’
32 But after I am raised to life, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.”
33Peter spoke up, “Even if all the others reject you, I never will!”
34Jesus replied, “I promise you before a rooster crows tonight, you will say three times that you don't know me.” 35But Peter said, “Even if I have to die with you, I will never say I don't know you.”
All the others said the same thing.
Jesus Prays
(Mark 14.32-42; Luke 22.39-46)
36Jesus went with his disciples to a place called Gethsemane. When they got there, he told them, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”
37Jesus took along Peter and the two brothers, James and John. He was very sad and troubled, 38and he said to them, “I am so sad that I feel as if I am dying. Stay here and keep awake with me.”
39Jesus walked on a little way. Then he knelt with his face to the ground and prayed, “My Father, if it is possible, don't make me suffer by drinking from this cup. But do what you want, and not what I want.”
40He came back and found his disciples sleeping. So he said to Peter, “Can't any of you stay awake with me for just one hour? 41Stay awake and pray that you won't be tested. You want to do what is right, but you are weak.”
42Again Jesus went to pray and said, “My Father, if there is no other way, and I must suffer, I will still do what you want.”
43Jesus came back and found them sleeping again. They simply could not keep their eyes open. 44He left them and prayed the same prayer once more.
45Finally, Jesus returned to his disciples and said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? The time has come for the Son of Man to be handed over to sinners. 46Get up! Let's go. The one who will betray me is already here.”
Jesus Is Arrested
(Mark 14.43-50; Luke 22.47-53; John 18.3-12)
47Jesus was still speaking, when Judas the betrayer came up. He was one of the twelve disciples, and a large mob armed with swords and clubs was with him. They had been sent by the chief priests and the nation's leaders. 48Judas had told them ahead of time, “Arrest the man I greet with a kiss.”
49Judas walked right up to Jesus and said, “Hello, teacher.” Then Judas kissed him.
50Jesus replied, “My friend, do what you came for.”
The men grabbed Jesus and arrested him. 51One of Jesus' followers pulled out a sword. He struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his ear.
52But Jesus told him, “Put your sword away. Anyone who lives by fighting will die by fighting. 53Don't you know that I could ask my Father, and he would at once send me more than twelve armies of angels? 54But then, how could the words of the Scriptures come true, which say this must happen?”
55 Jesus said to the mob, “Why do you come with swords and clubs to arrest me like a criminal? Day after day I sat and taught in the temple, and you didn't arrest me. 56But all this happened, so that what the prophets wrote would come true.”
All Jesus' disciples left him and ran away.
Jesus Is Questioned by the Council
(Mark 14.53-65; Luke 22.54,55,63-71; John 18.13,14,19-24)
57After Jesus had been arrested, he was led off to the house of Caiaphas the high priest. The nation's leaders and the teachers of the Law of Moses were meeting there. 58But Peter followed along at a distance and came to the courtyard of the high priest's palace. He went in and sat down with the guards to see what was going to happen.
59The chief priests and the whole council wanted to put Jesus to death. So they tried to find some people who would tell lies about him in court. 60But they could not find any, even though many did come and tell lies. At last, two men came forward 61 and said, “This man claimed he could tear down God's temple and build it again in three days.”
62The high priest stood up and asked Jesus, “Why don't you say something in your own defense? Don't you hear the charges they are making against you?” 63But Jesus did not answer. So the high priest said, “With the living God looking on, you must tell the truth. Are you the Messiah, the Son of God?”
64 “That is what you say!” Jesus answered. “But I tell all of you,
‘Soon you will see
the Son of Man
sitting at the right side
of God All-Powerful
and coming on the clouds
of heaven.’ ”
65 The high priest then tore his robe and said, “This man claims to be God! We don't need any more witnesses! You have heard what he said. 66What do you think?”
They answered, “He is guilty and deserves to die!” 67 Then they spit in his face and hit him with their fists. Others slapped him 68and said, “You think you are the Messiah! So tell us who hit you!”
Peter Says He Doesn't Know Jesus
(Mark 14.66-72; Luke 22.56-62; John 18.15-18,25-27)
69While Peter was sitting out in the courtyard, a servant girl came up to him and said, “You were with Jesus from Galilee.”
70But in front of everyone Peter said, “That isn't so! I don't know what you are talking about!”
71When Peter had gone out to the gate, another servant girl saw him and said to some people there, “This man was with Jesus from Nazareth.”
72Again Peter denied it, and this time he swore, “I don't even know that man!”
73A little while later some people standing there walked over to Peter and said, “We know you are one of them. We can tell it because you talk like someone from Galilee.”
74Peter began to curse and swear, “I don't know that man!”
Right then a rooster crowed, 75and Peter remembered that Jesus had said, “Before a rooster crows, you will say three times you don't know me.” Then Peter went out and cried bitterly.
translation_text:
1Yeezu ale jam sak wa ŋaaŋviirɔma wieŋa de meena a nueri la, wa yaa weeni ba ayen, 2<<Ni seba ayen tali ka da ŋaye ate Gaambasika Tigini a paari. Ba le yik Mi Saalɔbiika a te ate ba kpi wa jabarim nyiŋ.>>
3Va ŋala po kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa ale Juuma nisɔmma yaa tigsi chaab kaabteerɔ kpioŋku Kayafas dabiaka po, 4ayen ba poli a nya suik ate ba va a suk yik Yeezu a ko. 5Alege ba yaa ŋman weeni chaab ayen, <<Ase ti dan yik wa nuru boanni baai ale tigsi chaab ayen ba dɛ tigini dɛ la suŋsuŋ, ba le jam yiti ale nɔiyeŋ a nyiem a kaasi tuima tɛŋka po.>>
6Dai yeŋ po ate Yeezu yaa jam bo Simon yenni po Betani tɛŋka. Simon wala a jam ta ka gama tuem. 7Nipok wanyi yaa nyini peelim a ta kpa buui nyum ale masa nna yegayega la a jam jo Yeezu jigi a kpiiri bu a nyo wa zuk. 8Yeezu ŋaaŋviirɔma ale ga nya nipowa ale nye diila, ba sue yaa puuri ale wa. Ba yaa jam a poli ba suiniima po ayen, <<Ka boa ale soa ate nipowa de a pai kpaamu a yik kaasi nna la? 9Wa dan poom a pai bu a da ligra yegayega a pai ŋa a te ŋanjaksaŋa, dila an zunchoŋŋa?>>
10Yeezu yaa jam seba dii ate ba a poli la, a yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ka boa ate wa le nye diila a daani nama? Ni basi wa, dii nyiŋla wa tom ka wamaŋ a te mi. 11Niwomma a kasim bo ale nama kama daa meena, alege mi a kan bo ale ni a ta a cheŋŋi. 12Nipowa de a kpiiri kpaamu a nyo mi zuk a gomsi mi nyiŋka a magsi ka guka. 13Wensie ate mi a weeni ni, juijui meena ate nuruba a sak Wen wamaŋsaŋa la, ba le weeni nipowa de ale nye dii a te mi la. Ba le kasim a teeri wa yuei diipo meena wuu.>>
14Da ŋala po Yeezu ŋaaŋviirɔma pi ale bayewa po wanyiwa waai ate ba a wi wa ayen Judas Iskariot la, a jam yiti a cheŋ kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa jigi, 15a weeni ba ayen, <<Ase mi a dan baga a yik Yeezu a ta wa a jam a nyo ni nisima po, nama ale te mu ka boa?>> Wa le bek ba dila la, ba yaa deri chiini ligbie pisita a te wa dula jigini. 16A nyini da ŋala po a ta a cheŋ, Judas yaa nyiem a gisi ka suik ayen wa ta Yeezu a ga bobri a sak.
17Yeezu ŋaaŋviirɔma yaa jam wa jigi tigi dii ate ba a ŋɔbi boroborok kuui ale kan ta dabinta la piilimka danni a weeni ayen, <<Ka bɛ ate fi a yaali ayen ti ga gomsi Gaambasika Tigini ŋandiintaŋa ate ti dɛ?>>
18Wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni cheŋ nuru wanyi jigi tɛŋka po a ga weeni wa ayen, <Ti Sagrɔwa ale tom ti ayen ti jam a weeni fu ayen wa kummu danni a moata kama. Tama ale wa ale a yaali ayen ti dɛ Gaambasika Tigini ŋandiintaŋa fi yenni po.> >>
19Wa ŋaaŋviirɔma yaa cheŋ ga nye dii ate wa weeni la a yaa gomsi Gaambasika Tigini ŋandiintaŋa.
20Wenni ale jam siŋ la, Yeezu ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔma pi ale bayewa yaa tigsi chaab a kala a dɛ ŋandiintaŋa. 21Ba le jam boro a dɛ la, wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Wensie ate mi a weeni ni, nama po wanyi ale a yaali ayen wa ta mi a ga bobri sak.>>
22Wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ale wom dii ate wa weeni ba la, ba meena sue yaa jam kaasi ate ba yaa bek wa wanyi wanyi ayen, <<M Nyɔnɔ Yeezu Kirisita, ka mi?>>
23Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Nuru waai ale kala dela pai wa boroborok a maari a suiik jentaŋa ale mi dek la, ale wa ta mu a ga bobri sak. 24Mi Saalɔbiika ale kpi ase ka ba ale ŋmarisi dii Wen gbaŋka po la. Alege ku le pagra kama a te waai dek ale wa ta mu a ga bobri sak la. Ku zunchoŋ kama ale ba nin poom kan biak wa.>>
25Judas waai ale jam a yaali ayen wa ta Yeezu a ga bobri la yaa bek wa ayen, <<M Sagrɔ, ka mi?>> Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Ka fi.>>
26Ba ale boro a dɛ ŋandiintaŋa la, Yeezu yaa pai boroborok a puusi a te Wen a nye wa jiam, alege ŋmari ku a chari wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ale weeni ba ayen, <<Ni ŋoa ŋɔbi, mi nyiŋka ale nna.>>
27Wa yaa ŋman pai beerik ale daam a puusi a te Wen jiam, alege pai te ba ate ba nyu, wa yaa weeni ba ayen, 28<<Ka mi nɔiyeŋ paalika ziimu ale nna. Buui ale a nyini nuruba yega nyiŋla, ate Wen a vɔŋ ba tuimbaataŋa a te ba. 29Mi a weeni ni, m kan ŋman nyu daamu de nin ka dai dii danni ate m ŋman a nyu da paalimu m Kowa naamu po la.>>
30Ba yaa yi yiili alege a nyini ga jueli Olivi Guuku zuk.
31Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni meena ale chali waaŋ chaab mi nyiŋ yokku de. Diila ba ŋmarisi kama ayen, M le siti naapeerika ate piisa a waaŋ chaab. (Zakaria 13:7) 32Alege m dan yiti kum po, m le dɛ ni niŋ a cheŋ Galili tɛŋka.>> 33Piita yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Fi ŋaaŋviirɔma meena a dan basi fu, mi kan maara basi fu diipo.>> 34Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Basi ate m weeni fu, yokku de fi ale pagsi ku nɔi buta ayen fi zɛ mi, alege ate vari kpadiaka a kum.>> 35Piita yaa ŋman weeni wa ayen, <<Mi kan weeni ayen m zɛ fu. Mi dan poom ayen m kpi ale fu, mi kan weeni dila.>> Wa ŋaaŋviirɔma meena mɛ a weeni dila dekdega.
36Ba yaa jam paari jigi ate ba a wi ayen Getsemani, ate Yeezu yaa weeni wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ayen, <<Ni kali dela ate m cheŋ a ga puusi a te Naawen abe m jam.>> 37Wa le a cheŋ la, wa yaa basi ate Piita ale Jeemsi ale wa suoku Jɔɔn, Zebedi nidoabilisaŋa a va wa. Ku yaa piilim a daani wa ate wa sui a kaasi. 38Wa weeni ba ayen, <<M sui ale kaasi nna yegayega, ate ku a nye nna ase mi a yaali ayen m kpi kama la. Ni be limisi dela ate m jam, abe ni kpesi a nya.>>
39Wa le ŋman cheŋ magadek la, wa yaa kpi duna tɛŋ a puusi a te Wen ayen, <<M Koa, mi a saalim ayen ku dan ka fi popeentik, be yeeri ninammu de mi jigi a basi. Nye fidek ale a yaali diila, alege daa mi ale a yaali diila.>>
40Wa le ŋman pilim a nyini wa puusika jigini a jam la, wa yaa nya wa ŋaaŋviirɔma batawa a doa goa. Wa yaa weeni Piita ayen, <<Ka boa ate nama an baga a kali a limisi maga ale ge a goa? 41Ni a kpesi abe ni a puusi a te ni kan jo nyenyaka po, chiika a yaali kama alege nyiŋka a wobsa.>>
42Wa yaa ŋman pilim cheŋ wa puusika jigini a ga puusi a te Wen ayen, <<M Koa, ku dan kan ta nyeka alege ate fi a yaali ayen m nam bɛ basi ate fi ale a yaali diila a nye.>> 43Wa yaa ŋman pilim jam paari ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔma a doa a goa, dii nyiŋla goom ale jam ta ba nna yegayega.
44Yeezu yaa ŋman pilim cheŋ a ga puusi a te Naawen ase wa le poom a puusi diila. 45Butawa po Yeezu yaa ŋman pilim jam paari a bek ba ayen, <<Ni diem a doa a goa kama? Wie meena a nueri kama. Di danni a paari ya ate ba ayen ba yik Mi Saalɔbiika a nyo tuimbaata nyam nisima po. 46Ni yiti ate ti cheŋ. Nuru waai ale ta mu a ga bobri sak la ale la a cheena.>> 47Yeezu ale diem boro a biisi la, Judas waai ale jam ka Yeezu ŋaaŋviirɔma pi ale bayewa po wanyi la, yaa jam wa jigi ale nuru boari yegayega. Kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa ale Juuma nisɔmma ale tom ba. Ba jam ta ka gebi kpieŋsa ale dua a jam ayen ba yik wa. 48Bumbobrɔwa a poom weeni ba kama ayen, <<Ti dan ga paari ba, nuru waai ate mi a puusi ale a gbaari wa la, ka wala ale la. Ni yik wa ale pagrim.>> 49Ba ale ga paari Yeezu la, Judas yaa deri ga wa jigi a wi wa ayen, <<M Sagrɔ,>> a yaa alege a puusi ale gbaari wa.>>
50Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<M doa, nye dii ate fi a poli ayen fi nye mu la.>> Baai ale jam va Judas la, a yaa yik wa ale pagrim. 51Yeezu ŋaaŋviirɔma po wanyi a deri yeeri wa gebi kpieŋ a che kaabteerɔ kpioŋku yɔmma po wanyi turi a gebi lɔnsi tɛŋ. 52Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Pa fi gebika a ŋman su ka fooku po. Diila baai ale a pai gebik la a kpi ale ka gebik. 53Nama a zɛ ayen mi baga kama a wi M Kowa ayen wa tom wa maarɔma baai ale piisi nna yegayega la ate ba jam a maari mu? 54M dan nye dila, wie ŋaai ate ba ŋmarisi mi wie Wen Gbaŋka po dipo la a kan chim wensie.>>
55Yeezu yaa viriŋ a bek nuru boanni ayen, <<Mi ka zue ate nama a ta gebi kpieŋsa ale dua a jam ayen ni yik mu? Daa meena mi kasim bo ale ni Wen Yenni po a sak ni kama, alege nama an jam yik mu. 56Ba le ŋmarisi Wen biisiteerɔma Gbaŋka po diila a sum chim ka wensie jinla.>> Dula jigini wa ŋaaŋviirɔma meena a yiti chali ale ge wa.
57Ba yaa ta Yeezu a cheŋ kaabteerɔ kpioŋku Kayafas jigi. Ba le jam ga paari dula la, Sinsak sagrɔma ale Juuma nisɔmma yaa jam tigsi chaab. 58Piita yaa mak va ba ŋaaŋ a jam jo kaabteerɔ kpioŋku yenni dabiaka po a cheŋ a ga kala ale kpagni limisidɔma ayen wa nya dii ale di nye la. 59Kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa ale Nisɔmma meena a jam bo dula a gisi nuru ayen wa weeni a sak ba ayen wa nya Yeezu ale wa boro a tom wabiok ate ba baga a nya suik a ko wa. 60Ba yaa gisi a kpeeri. Alege nuruba yegayega a diem nyini a jam za ba niŋ ayen ba velim wie a te wa. Kula ŋaaŋnyiŋ nuruba baye yaa nyini a jam za ba niŋ. 61A weeni ayen, <<Tama a wom ale Yeezu a weeni ayen wa baga a kaasi Wen yenni, abe wa ŋman se di daa ŋata po.>>
62Kaabteerɔ kpioŋku yaa yiti a cheŋ a ga zaani a bek ayen, <<Fi ka wari a tulisi ale ŋaai meena ate ba a biisi a te fu la?>> 63Alege Yeezu yaa sina. Kaabteerɔ kpioŋku yaa ŋman weeni wa ayen, <<Mi a yaali kama ayen fi pɛ Wen dii ale boro la yuenni nyiŋ abe fi weeni mu wensieŋa.>> Wa yaa bek Yeezu ayen, <<Fi ka Wen Nidoabinni waai ate ba a wi ayen Kirisita la?>> 64Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Mm, mi ale la. Ni basi ate m weeni ni ayen dai yeŋ po fi le nya Mi Saalɔbiika ale m kala Wen juga geŋ. Fi le ŋman nya mu ale m nyini Wen jigi chiŋmaaŋa po a cheena.>>
65Wa le weeni dila la, kaabteerɔ kpioŋku yaa yik wa garukku a dari cheeri ale weeni ba ayen, <<Ti kan ŋman a yaali seerɔba. Ni meena wom wa le pai wadek a magsi chaab ale Wen la. 66Nama a poli ka sɛ, wa lo yaa wa an loya?>> Ba meena yaa weeni ayen, <<Wa lo kama. Ku magsi ba ko wa kama.>>
67Nuruma ba gela yaa chesi tintueta a basi wa nyiŋ ale a nak wa. 68A weeni ayen, <<Fi a weeni ayen fi ale Kirisitawa. Be miŋ baai ale a nak fu la.>>
69Ba le ta Yeezu a nye nya kude meena la, Piita a diem bo ka yenni dabiaka po. Nipokbili wanyi a yaa jam boro. Wa jam ka kaabteerɔ kpioŋku dɔkliema po wanyi. Wa yaa nya Piita a weeni wa ayen, <<Daa fi ale poom va Galili tɛŋka denɔwa Yeezu la?>>
70Wa yaa pagsi ale baai meena ale za dula la nimbie po ale weeni wa ayen, <<Mi zɛ fi ale a biisi diila.>> 71Wa le weeni dila la, wa yaa yiti a cheŋ ga za nansuiŋku nɔi. Nipokbili wa choa a ŋman diem nya wa dula jigini ale wa za ate wa yaa weeni nuru baai ale za moata wa la ayen, <<Nuruwa de ka Yeezu ŋaaŋviirɔma po wanyi.>>
72Piita yaa ŋman pagsi ayen, <<M pɛ ya, mi zɛ nuruwa de.>>
73Ku an jam beniya ate baai ale jam za moata wa la wanyi a yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Fi ka ba wanyi, dii nyiŋla fi a biisi ase ka Galili denɔ la.>> 74Piita yaa weeni wa ayen, <<M pɛ ya, ka wensie ate mi a biisi. Mi zɛ nuru waai wie ate fi a biisi la.>> Wa le weeni dila a ga nueri la, vari kpadiaka yaa deri kum. 75Ate Piita yaa teeri dii ate Yeezu a poom weeni wa ayen wa le pagsi ku nɔi buta ayen wa zɛ wa, ale ge ate vari kpadiaka a kum la. Wieŋa de meena yaa nye ate Piita sui a kaasi ate wa yaa deri nyini a kum nna yegayega.

english_text:
Jesus Is Taken to Pilate
(Mark 15.1; Luke 23.1,2; John 18.28-32)
1Early the next morning all the chief priests and the nation's leaders met and decided that Jesus should be put to death. 2They tied him up and led him away to Pilate the governor.
The Death of Judas
(Acts 1.18,19)
3 Judas had betrayed Jesus, but when he learned that Jesus had been sentenced to death, he was sorry for what he had done. He returned the 30 silver coins to the chief priests and leaders 4and said, “I have sinned by betraying a man who has never done anything wrong.”
“So what? That's your problem,” they replied. 5Judas threw the money into the temple and then went out and hanged himself.
6The chief priests picked up the money and said, “This money was paid to have a man killed. We can't put it in the temple treasury.” 7Then they had a meeting and decided to buy a field that belonged to someone who made clay pots. They wanted to use it as a graveyard for foreigners. 8This is why people still call that place “Field of Blood.” 9 So the words of the prophet Jeremiah came true,
“They took
the thirty silver coins,
the price of a person
among the people of Israel.
10They paid it
for a potter's field,
as the Lord
had commanded me.”
Pilate Questions Jesus
(Mark 15.2-5; Luke 23.3-5; John 18.33-38)
11Jesus was brought before Pilate the governor, who asked him, “Are you the king of the Jews?”
“Those are your words!” Jesus answered. 12And when the chief priests and leaders brought their charges against him, he did not say a thing.
13Pilate asked him, “Don't you hear what crimes they say you have done?” 14But Jesus did not say anything, and the governor was greatly amazed.
The Death Sentence
(Mark 15.6-15; Luke 23.13-26; John 18.39—19.16)
15During Passover the governor always freed a prisoner chosen by the people. 16At that time a well-known terrorist named Jesus Barabbas was in jail. 17So when the crowd came together, Pilate asked them, “Which prisoner do you want me to set free? Do you want Jesus Barabbas or Jesus who is called the Messiah?” 18Pilate knew the leaders had brought Jesus to him because they were jealous.
19While Pilate was judging the case, his wife sent him a message. It said, “Don't have anything to do with that innocent man. I have had nightmares because of him.”
20But the chief priests and the leaders convinced the crowds to ask for Barabbas to be set free and for Jesus to be killed. 21Pilate asked the crowd again, “Which of these two men do you want me to set free?”
“Barabbas!” they shouted.
22Pilate asked them, “What am I to do with Jesus, who is called the Messiah?”
They all yelled, “Nail him to a cross!”
23Pilate answered, “But what crime has he done?”
“Nail him to a cross!” they yelled even louder.
24 Pilate saw that there was nothing he could do and that the people were starting to riot. So he took some water and washed his hands in front of them and said, “I won't have anything to do with killing this man. You are the ones doing it!”
25Everyone answered, “We and our own families will take the blame for his death!”
26Pilate set Barabbas free. Then he ordered his soldiers to beat Jesus with a whip and nail him to a cross.
Soldiers Make Fun of Jesus
(Mark 15.16-21; John 19.2,3)
27The governor's soldiers led Jesus into the fortress and brought together the rest of the troops. 28They stripped off Jesus' clothes and put a scarlet robe on him. 29They made a crown out of thorn branches and placed it on his head, and they put a stick in his right hand. The soldiers knelt down and pretended to worship him. They made fun of him and shouted, “Hey, you king of the Jews!” 30Then they spit on him. They took the stick from him and beat him on the head with it.
Jesus Is Nailed to a Cross
(Mark 15.22-32; Luke 23.27-43; John 19.17-27)
31When the soldiers had finished making fun of Jesus, they took off the robe. They put his own clothes back on him and led him off to be nailed to a cross. 32On the way they met a man named Simon who was from Cyrene, and they forced him to carry Jesus' cross.
33They came to a place named Golgotha, which means “Place of a Skull.” 34 There they gave Jesus some wine mixed with a drug to ease the pain. But when Jesus tasted what it was, he refused to drink it.
35 The soldiers nailed Jesus to a cross and gambled to see who would get his clothes. 36Then they sat down to guard him. 37Above his head they put a sign that told why he was nailed there. It read, “This is Jesus, the King of the Jews.” 38The soldiers also nailed two criminals on crosses, one to the right of Jesus and the other to his left.
39 People who passed by said terrible things about Jesus. They shook their heads and 40 shouted, “So you're the one who claimed you could tear down the temple and build it again in three days! If you are God's Son, save yourself and come down from the cross!”
41The chief priests, the leaders, and the teachers of the Law of Moses also made fun of Jesus. They said, 42“He saved others, but he can't save himself. If he is the king of Israel, he should come down from the cross! Then we will believe him. 43 He trusted God, so let God save him, if he wants to. He even said he was God's Son.” 44The two criminals also said cruel things to Jesus.
The Death of Jesus
(Mark 15.33-41; Luke 23.44-49; John 19.28-30)
45At noon the sky turned dark and stayed that way until three o'clock. 46 Then about that time Jesus shouted, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?” which means, “My God, my God, why have you deserted me?”
47Some of the people standing there heard Jesus and said, “He's calling for Elijah.” 48 One of them at once ran and grabbed a sponge. He soaked it in wine, then put it on a stick and held it up to Jesus.
49Others said, “Wait! Let's see if Elijah will come and save him.” 50Once again Jesus shouted, and then he died.
51 At once the curtain in the temple was torn in two from top to bottom. The earth shook, and rocks split apart. 52Graves opened, and many of God's people were raised to life. 53They left their graves, and after Jesus had risen to life, they went into the holy city, where they were seen by many people.
54The officer and the soldiers guarding Jesus felt the earthquake and saw everything else that happened. They were frightened and said, “This man really was God's Son!”
55 Many women had come with Jesus from Galilee to be of help to him, and they were there, looking on at a distance. 56Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of James and John were some of these women.
Jesus Is Buried
(Mark 15.42-47; Luke 23.50-56; John 19.38-42)
57That evening a rich disciple named Joseph from the town of Arimathea 58went and asked for Jesus' body. Pilate gave orders for it to be given to Joseph, 59who took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth. 60Then Joseph put the body in his own tomb that had been cut into solid rock and had never been used. He rolled a big stone against the entrance to the tomb and went away.
61All this time Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were sitting across from the tomb.
62On the next day, which was a Sabbath, the chief priests and the Pharisees went together to Pilate. 63 They said, “Sir, we remember what this liar said while he was still alive. He claimed in three days he would come back from death. 64So please order the tomb to be carefully guarded for three days. If you don't, his disciples may come and steal his body. They will tell the people he has been raised to life, and this last lie will be worse than the first one.”
65Pilate said to them, “All right, take some of your soldiers and guard the tomb as well as you know how.” 66So they sealed it tight and placed soldiers there to guard it.
translation_text:
1Vanni ale veenti la, kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa ale Juuma nisɔmma meena a ŋman tigsi chaab ayen ba poli ba le ba nye dii a ko Yeezu la. 2Ba yaa bobi wa nisimaŋa a ta wa cheŋ Gominawa Paalɔt jigi.
3Judas waai ale jam ta Yeezu a ga bobri sak la, ale nya ba le bo Yeezu buusaŋa diila, wa sui yaa jam kaasi, ate wa yaa ŋman pilim cheŋ kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa ale Juuma nisɔmma jigi ayen wa pai ba ligbieŋa pisitawa a te ba. 4Wa le ga paari dula la, wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Wen a nya mi kaasuŋku kama, dii nyiŋla mi ta ka nuru waai ale kan kaasi wari la, a jam bobri sak nama. Yɔgyɔgla de nama mɛ a yaa bo wa kum buusa.>> Ba yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Kula a daa tama niŋŋa, alege ka fidek niŋ.>> 5Judas ale ga wom dii ate ba weeni la, wa yaa pai ligraŋa a yuk basi Wen yenni suŋsuŋ, ale ge a nyini a ga bobi miik a kpi.
6Judas ale ga nyini la, kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa yaa yiti a pisi ligraŋa ale weeni chaab ayen, <<Ligraŋa de tama pai ŋa a da ka nuru nyuvuri. Ti Sinsaŋŋa a kan siak ayen ti pai ŋa a maa gum Wen yenni ligraŋa po.>> 7Ba yaa pai ligraŋa a da tɛŋ kaai ate ba a wi ayen Samɔnsa Meka jigi la. Ba jam a yaali kama ayen ba pai dula jigini a chim nicham guka jigi. 8Ka dila ale soa ate nuruba a diem a wi dula jigini ayen Ziimu Jigini la. 9Ate Biisiteerɔwa Jeremaya ale biisi diila a chim wensie ayen, <<Ba pai ligbie pisita ŋaai ate Izirali nidoabilisaŋa gela a siak da wa la. 10Ba pai te a magsi samɔnsa mɛka jigi ase Naawen ale dak mi diila.>>
11Yeezu yaa jam taam zaani Paalɔt niŋ. Paalɔt yaa bek wa ayen, <<Ka fi ale Juuma naawa la?>> Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Ka fi ale a weeni dila.>> 12Alege kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa ale Juuma nisɔmma ale jam a ŋma wa la, wa an jam weeni wari ya. 13Paalɔt yaa bek wa ayen, <<Fi kan wom ba ale a ŋma fu ale wie ŋaai meena la?>> 14Alege Yeezu an jam tulisi wa yeŋ mɛ la. Ku yaa jam cha Paalɔt nna yegayega ale wa ale kan a tulisi wari la.
15Bena meena Gaambasika Tigini a nyiem dan paari, gominawa Paalɔt a nyiem lak nuru waai ate tɛŋka demma a yaali ayen wa lak ate wa nyini likka dɔkku po a nyini la a basi kama. 16Nuru wanyi ale jam boro ate ba a wi ayen Barabasi ate ba jam maa yik wa a lik. Nuruba a jam seba wa ka nna yegayega. 17Paalɔt yaa bek nuru baai meena ale tigsi chaab la ayen, <<Nama a yaali ayen m basi ka ba wana? Barabasi yaa Yeezu waai ate ba a wi ayen Kirisitawa la?>> 18Paalɔt jam seba ayen ka kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa nyunni nyiŋ ale soa ate ba yik Yeezu a ta jam wa jigi.
19Paalɔt ale jam diem kala boteka dɔkku po la, wa powa yaa tom weeni wa ayen, <<Kan nye nuruwa de jaaboa ale wa an kaasi wari ya. Dii nyiŋla deemwa yokku mi gɔdaasim wa wari kama ate ku daani mi nna yegayega.>> 20Kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa ale Juuma nisɔmma yaa weeni nuru boanni ayen ba saalim ate wa lak Barabasi a basi abe wa ge ate ba ko Yeezu. 21Paalɔt yaa bek nuru boanni ayen, <<Nuruma de bayewa, nama a yaali ayen m basi ka ba wana?>> Ba yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Ti a yaali ayen fi basi ka Barabasi.>> 22Wa yaa ŋman bek ayen, <<M be nye Yeezu waai ate ba a wi ayen Kirisitawa la ka sɛ?>> Ba meena yaa tulisi ayen, <<Basi ate ba kpi wa jabarimu nyiŋ ate wa kpi.>> 23Wa ŋman bek ba ayen, <<Ka boan jaab wabiok ate wa nye?>> Ba yaa kaari nna yegayega ayen, <<Basi ate ba kpi wa jabarimu nyiŋ ate wa kpi.>>
24Paalɔt yaa nya ayen wa an baga a nye wari ya dii nyiŋla, ba nuemka ale ta kpaliŋ a jam. Wa yaa pai nyiam a nari wa nisaŋa nuru boanni niŋ, ale weeni ba ayen, <<Mi niŋ maa ka nuruwa dɛ kum po, ku bo ka nama dek jigi.>> 25Nuru boanni yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Basi ate wa kummu nyiŋ ninammu a jam tama ale ti bisaŋa jigi.>> 26Paalɔt yaa lak Barabasi a basi ale basi ate ba miiri Yeezu. Ba ale miiri wa nueri la, wa yaa pai wa te ayen ba ta wa ga kpi jabarimu nyiŋ.
27Paalɔt tugurik tɔŋdɔma yaa yik Yeezu a ta jo ba gominawa yenni dabiaka po ate ba meena a yaa gilim wa. 28Ba yaa yeeri wa gattaŋa ale pai garuk mɔnuŋ a jo wa. 29A pai munsa a yɔk zutɔk a pai vuk wa zukku ale pai tachek a nyo wa juga nisaŋa po. Ba yaa kpi duna wa niŋ a nye wa a la, ale a weeni ayen, <<Juuma naawa, kasim boro taam wuu.>> 30Ba jam chesi tintueta a basi wa nyiŋ ale pai diok a nak wa zukku. 31Ba ale nye wa la a ga nueri la, ba yaa yeeri garuk mɔnuŋku ale pai wadek gattaŋa a jo wa a ta wa nyini cheŋ ayen ba kpi wa jabarimu nyiŋ.
32Ba ale jam bo suiku po a cheŋ la, ba yaa zik Simon ale wa cheena tɛŋka po ate tugurik tɔŋdɔma a fɛ wa ate wa tuesi Yeezu jabarimu ji. Simon a jam Sairini tɛŋka denɔ.
33Ba yaa ga paari juijui ate ba a wi ayen Golgota la. Ku kiri ale Zukoluku Jigini. 34Ba yaa pai tiim a nyo daam po a lam nya ale pai te Yeezu ayen wa nyu alege wa an jam nyu ya.
35Ba yaa yik Yeezu a kpi wa jabarimu nyiŋ, ale pai wa gattaŋa a chari chaab. Ba jam nak ka gbaŋ a nya waai ale magsi garuk kuui dek la. 36Ba ale nak gbaŋka wa gattaŋa nyiŋ a nueri la, ba yaa kala a limisi ayen waai a kan vari wa a basi. 37Ba yaa pai tapagi a ŋmarisi di nyiŋ ayen, <<Ka Yeezu, Juuma Naawa Ale Nna,>> a pai di kpi jabarimu zuk.
38Ba jam maa kpi ka zueba baye ŋanbarinta nyiŋ a gum Yeezu po, ate ba wanyi a bo wa juga, nwala mɛ a bo wa gala. 39Nuru baai ale jam va dula a taam la a yaa zak zuk nya wa a mati ba noa ale a lɛ wa ayen, 40<<Fi weeni ayen fi le kaasi Wen yenni abe fi ŋman sɛ di a nueri daa ŋata po. Fi dan ka Wen Nidoabili bɛ nyini jabarimu zuk a siŋ a vari fidek a basi.>> 41Kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa ale Sinsak sagrɔma, ale Juuma nisɔmma me a jam a la wa ale a weeni ayen, 42<<Wa jam baga a vari nuruba a basi kama, alege wa an baga a vari wadek a basi. Daa wa ale Izirali Naawa? Wa dan nyini jabarimu zuk a siŋ ti yaa le ta siaka ale wa. 43Wa ta siaka kama ayen Wen ale bo le wa ale weeni ayen wa ka Wen Nidoabili. Ti be le nya ase Wen ale vari wa a basi ya.>> 44Zue baai ate ba jam kpi ba a gum Yeezu po la, mɛ a lɛ wa dila dekdega.
45Ku ale jam paari kantueŋ baŋ pi ale buye la, tɛŋka meena yaa jam nye legi nna kpitɔ a ta ga paari kantueŋ baŋ buta. 46Baŋ butawa po, Yeezu yaa kaari ate ku jueli a weeni ale wadek tɛŋka biika ayen, <<Eloi, Eloi, Lama Sabagtani.>> Ku kiri ale, <<Mi Wen yaa, mi Wen yaa, ka boa ate fi zɛri mu?>> (Yiila 22:1)
47Nuru baai ale jam za dula jigini la gela a wom dii ate wa weeni la kama. Ba yaa weeni ayen, <<Wa a wi ka Elaja.>> 48Ba po wanyi yaa chali cheŋ ga pai sosok a lusi damiisiŋ po a pai yik diok woŋ nyiŋ a zak ta jueli Yeezu nɔi. 49Nuru mbala yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni basi ate ti limisi a nya ase Elaja ale jam a yik wa a ta nyini jabarimu zuk a siŋ tɛŋ ya.>>
50Yeezu yaa ŋman kaari nna yegayega a yaa le ge kpi. 51Wa ale jam kpi la, garuk panni dii ate ba jam pai a kasi Wen yenni po la, a yaa jam cheeri di ŋmazuk a ta siŋ paari di tɛŋ. Wen jam basi kama ate tɛŋka a choa ate pinaŋa a na a mobi, 52ate nuruba yega ale jam va Wen alege a kpi la boositaŋa a lagri ate ba yiti kum po, 53alege basi boositaŋa. Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ate Yeezu a yiti kum po la ba yaa jo Jerusalem tɛŋka po. Nuruba yegayega ale jam nya ba. 54Tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagni ale tugurik tɔŋdɔ baai ale jam a limisi la ale nya tɛŋka choka ale dii meena ale nye la ku yaa cha ba nna yegayega. Ba yaa weeni ayen, <<Wensie, nuruwa de sum ka Wen Nidoabili.>>
55Nipok baai ale jam maari Yeezu Galili tɛŋka po la a jam za moata dula a nya dii meena ale nye la kama. 56Baai ale jam bo ba po la ale Mɛɛri Magdalene ale Mɛɛri, Jeemsi ale Josefi mawa ale Zebedi nidoabilisaŋa mawa.
57Jigsirɔ wanyi ale jam nyini tɛŋ ate ba a wi ayen, Arimatia. Wa yuei jam ale Josefi. Wa jam ka waai ale ta siaka ale Yeezu. 58Da dila danni junɔi ate wa yaa cheŋ Paalɔt jigi a saalim wa ayen wa basi ate wa ga yeeri Yeezu nyiŋka jabarimu zuk a ta cheŋ ga gu ate Paalɔt yaa siak. 59Josefi yaa cheŋ ga yeeri Yeezu nyiŋka jabarimu zuk yaa pai garuk pali naliŋ a vili ka 60a ta ga dueni piuŋ vɔrup paalik po. Wa yaa bilim tintain kpienni a lik piuŋku vɔrumu nɔnni. 61Mɛɛri Magdalene ale Mɛɛri nwala a jam kali ka dula a tuk vɔrumu nyiŋ.
62Vari ale ŋman veenti la, ba Vuusum Danni saluiku kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa ale Farisiima yaa cheŋ Paalɔt jigi a weeni wa ayen, 63<<Ti diem a teeri velimvendika ale jam boro la wa weeni ayen, <M le yiti kum po ku daa ŋata dai.> 64Be basi ate ba ga a limisi vɔrumu ate ku paari daa ŋata ate wa ŋaaŋviirɔma a kan mak yeeri wa abe ba weeni nuruma ayen wa yiti kum po. Dan kan daa di ventaŋa de ale gaam wa le liŋ velim diila.>> 65Paalɔt yaa siak ale basi ayen tugurik tɔŋdɔba cheŋ a ga ŋmasi a limisi vɔrumu. 66Ba yaa cheŋ ga daani tintanni ayen waai dan bilim di abe ba miŋ a yaa le basi ate tugurik tɔŋdɔma a limisi vɔrumu.

english_text:
Jesus Is Alive
(Mark 16.1-8; Luke 24.1-12; John 20.1-10)
1The Sabbath was over, and it was almost daybreak on Sunday when Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to see the tomb. 2Suddenly a strong earthquake struck, and the Lord's angel came down from heaven. He rolled away the stone and sat on it. 3The angel looked as bright as lightning, and his clothes were white as snow. 4The guards shook from fear and fell down, as though they were dead.
5The angel said to the women, “Don't be afraid! I know you are looking for Jesus, who was nailed to a cross. 6He isn't here! God has raised him to life, just as Jesus said he would. Come, see the place where his body was lying. 7Now hurry! Tell his disciples he has been raised to life and is on his way to Galilee. Go there, and you will see him. This is what I came to tell you.”
8The women were frightened and yet very happy, as they hurried from the tomb and ran to tell his disciples. 9Suddenly Jesus met them and greeted them. They went near him, held on to his feet, and worshiped him. 10Then Jesus said, “Don't be afraid! Tell my followers to go to Galilee. They will see me there.”
Report of the Guard
11While the women were on their way, some soldiers who had been guarding the tomb went into the city. They told the chief priests everything that had happened. 12So the chief priests met with the leaders and decided to bribe the soldiers with a lot of money. 13They said to the soldiers, “Tell everyone that Jesus' disciples came during the night and stole his body while you were asleep. 14If the governor hears about this, we will talk to him. You won't have anything to worry about.” 15The soldiers took the money and did what they were told. The people of Judea still tell each other this story.
What Jesus' Followers Must Do
(Mark 16.14-18; Luke 24.36-49; John 20.19-23; Acts 1.6-8)
16 Jesus' eleven disciples went to a mountain in Galilee, where Jesus had told them to meet him. 17They saw him and worshiped him, but some of them doubted.
18Jesus came to them and said:
I have been given all authority in heaven and on earth! 19 Go to the people of all nations and make them my disciples. Baptize them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, 20and teach them to do everything I have told you. I will be with you always, even until the end of the world.
translation_text:
1Vuusum Danni ale taam la, bakoanni piilimka danni, Mɛɛri Magdalene ale Mɛɛri nwala yaa cheŋ ba nya juijui ate ba gu Yeezu la. 2Tɛŋka yaa jam choa nna yegayega, ate Naawen maarɔ a nyini wenŋmazuk a siŋ bilim tintanni a dueni nakpiak a kali di zuk. 3Maarɔwa a jam kasim a nyaksi kama ase wein ale a nyaksi diila. Wa gattaŋa mɛ a peenti nna yegayega. 4Yɔgsum yaa yik baai ale a limisi vɔrumu la nna yegayega ate ba nyiŋsaŋa a gɔk ate ba nye nna ase ba kpi la. 5Maarɔwa yaa weeni nipooma ayen, <<Ni kan chali yɔgsummoa, mi seba ayen ni a gisi ka Yeezu waai ate ba kpi wa jabarimu nyiŋ la. 6Wa ka dela jigini, wa yiti kum po kama ase wa ale liŋ weeni ni diila. Ni jam a nya juijui ate ba pai wa a dueni la. 7Ni cheŋ nwuli a ga weeni wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ayen wa yiti kum po kama, wa be dɛ ka niŋ a cheŋ Galili tɛŋka. Ni le nya wa dula jigini. Ni teeri m le weeni ni diila.>>
8Ba yaa basi dula jigini ale suipeentik a ga weeni wa ŋaaŋviirɔma dii meena ate maarɔwa a weeni ba la. 9Yeezu yaa tu ba dula jigini a weeni ba ayen, <<Suiyɔgni a bo ale ni.>> Ba yaa domsi kali a puusi wa. 10Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni kan chali yɔgsummoa abe ni ga weeni m suataŋa ayen ba cheŋ Galili tɛŋka a ga tu mu dula jigini.>>
11Nipooma ale bo suik po a cheŋ la, tugurik tɔŋdɔma gela yaa cheŋ tɛŋka po a ga weeni kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa dii meena ale nye la. 12Kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa yaa tu chaab ale Tɛŋka nisɔmma ate ba pai ligra yegayega a te tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale weeni ba ayen, 13<<Ni weeni ayen nama a doa a goa kama ate wa ŋaaŋviirɔma a jam zu pai wa. 14Gominawa a dan poom wom ti le biisi a vari ni basi.>> 15Tugurik tɔŋdɔma yaa tuesi ligraŋa ale weeni ate ku paari Juuma meena a ta jam paari jinla danni.
16Wa ŋaaŋviirɔma pi ale wanyiwa yaa cheŋ a ga jueli guuk kunyi zuk Galili tɛŋka po juijui ate Yeezu a weeni ba ayen ba cheŋ la. 17Ba ale nya wa dula jigini la ba yaa puusi wa. Ba gela a jam diem ta ka chichama. 18Yeezu yaa forisi paari ba a weeni ba ayen, <<Wen a te mi pagrim kama wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋzuk meena. 19Ni cheŋ tɛŋsa meena a sak nuruba ate ba va mi, abe ni a te ba soka Kowa ale wa Nidoabinni ale wa Chiika yuei nyiŋ. 20Ni sak ba ate ba va wie ŋaai meena ate mi a sak ni la. M le bo ale ni a ga paari tɛŋka kpeglimka.>>

english_text:
The Preaching of John the Baptist
(Matthew 3.1-12; Luke 3.1-18; John 1.19-28)
1This is the good news about Jesus Christ, the Son of God. 2 It began just as God had said in the book written by Isaiah the prophet,
“I am sending my messenger
to get the way ready
for you.
3 In the desert
someone is shouting,
‘Get the road ready
for the Lord!
Make a straight path
for him.’ ”
4So John the Baptist showed up in the desert and told everyone, “Turn back to God and be baptized! Then your sins will be forgiven.”
5From all Judea and Jerusalem crowds of people went to John. They told how sorry they were for their sins, and he baptized them in the Jordan River.
6 John wore clothes made of camel's hair. He had a leather strap around his waist and ate grasshoppers and wild honey.
7John also told the people, “Someone more powerful is going to come. And I am not good enough even to stoop down and untie his sandals. 8I baptize you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit!”
The Baptism of Jesus
(Matthew 3.13-17; Luke 3.21,22)
9About that time Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee, and John baptized him in the Jordan River. 10As soon as Jesus came out of the water, he saw the sky open and the Holy Spirit coming down to him like a dove. 11 A voice from heaven said, “You are my own dear Son, and I am pleased with you.”
Jesus and Satan
(Matthew 4.1-11; Luke 4.1-13)
12At once God's Spirit made Jesus go into the desert. 13He stayed there for 40 days while Satan tested him. Jesus was with the wild animals, but angels took care of him.
Jesus Begins His Work
(Matthew 4.12-17; Luke 4.14,15)
14After John was arrested, Jesus went to Galilee and told the good news that comes from God. 15 He said, “The time has come! God's kingdom will soon be here. Turn back to God and believe the good news!”
Jesus Chooses Four Fishermen
(Matthew 4.18-22; Luke 5.1-11)
16As Jesus was walking along the shore of Lake Galilee, he saw Simon and his brother Andrew. They were fishermen and were casting their nets into the lake. 17Jesus said to them, “Follow me! I will teach you how to bring in people instead of fish.” 18Right then the two brothers dropped their nets and went with him.
19Jesus walked on and soon saw James and John, the sons of Zebedee. They were in a boat, mending their nets. 20At once Jesus asked them to come with him. They left their father in the boat with the hired workers and went with him.
A Man with an Evil Spirit
(Luke 4.31-37)
21Jesus and his disciples went to the town of Capernaum. Then on the next Sabbath he went into the synagogue and started teaching. 22 Everyone was amazed at his teaching. He taught with authority, and not like the teachers of the Law of Moses. 23Suddenly a man with an evil spirit in him entered the synagogue and yelled, 24“Jesus from Nazareth, what do you want with us? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are! You are God's Holy One.”
25Jesus told the evil spirit, “Be quiet and come out of the man!” 26The spirit shook him. Then it gave a loud shout and left.
27Everyone was completely surprised and kept saying to each other, “What is this? It must be some new kind of powerful teaching! Even the evil spirits obey him.” 28News about Jesus quickly spread all over Galilee.
Jesus Heals Many People
(Matthew 8.14-17; Luke 4.38-41)
29As soon as Jesus left the synagogue with James and John, they went home with Simon and Andrew. 30When they got there, Jesus was told that Simon's mother-in-law was sick in bed with fever. 31Jesus went to her. He took hold of her hand and helped her up. The fever left her, and she served them a meal.
32That evening after sunset, all who were sick or had demons in them were brought to Jesus. 33In fact, the whole town gathered around the door of the house. 34Jesus healed all kinds of terrible diseases and forced out a lot of demons. But the demons knew who he was, and he did not let them speak.
35Very early the next morning before daylight, Jesus got up and went to a place where he could be alone and pray. 36Simon and the others started looking for him. 37And when they found him, they said, “Everyone is looking for you!”
38Jesus replied, “We must go to the nearby towns, so that I can tell the good news to those people. This is why I have come.” 39 Then Jesus went to their synagogues everywhere in Galilee, where he preached and forced out demons.
Jesus Heals a Man
(Matthew 8.1-4; Luke 5.12-16)
40A man with leprosy came to Jesus and knelt down. He begged, “You have the power to make me well, if only you wanted to.”
41Jesus felt sorry for the man. So he put his hand on him and said, “I want to! Now you are well.” 42At once the man's leprosy disappeared, and he was well.
43After Jesus strictly warned the man, he sent him on his way. 44 He said, “Don't tell anyone about this. Just go and show the priest that you are well. Then take a gift to the temple as Moses commanded, and everyone will know that you have been healed.”
45The man talked about it so much and told so many people, that Jesus could no longer go openly into a town. He had to stay away from the towns, but people still came to him from everywhere.
translation_text:
1Naawen nidoabinni Yeezu Kirisita wapaalaŋa piilimka ale nna. 2Ase ku ale ŋmarisi Wen biisiteerɔwa Azaya gbaŋka po ayen, <<Nya, m tom ka tomtomdɔ waai ale wa gomsi suiku la ayen wa dɛ fi niŋ.>> (Malakai 3:1) 3<<Waai lueluk ale kasim a kaari gɔnni po a weeni ayen gomsi Naawen suiku abe fi nye ate wa suitaŋa a teenti.>> (Azaya 40:3)
4Jɔɔn Sokateerɔwa ale nyini gɔnni po, a mooli ayen ba laŋ nyeka a tuesi soka a nya vɔŋteka. 5Nuruba yegayega yaa nyini tɛŋ kpieŋka Jerusalem ale tɛŋ sii meena ale gilim ka Judia po la a jam Jɔɔn jigi. Ba ale wom wa sinsaŋŋa la, ba yaa tɔk ba tuimbaataŋa meena a sak Naawen alege ate Jɔɔn yaa te ba soka Jodan benni po. 6Ba jam pai ka laalaakomi kɔbta a nye Jɔɔn garukku. Wa jam pai ka chiak gbain a bobi wa chiaka. Wa jam a ŋɔbi ka tintue ale a dɛ siita mɛ. 7Wa jam a mooli kama ayen, <<Nuru wanyi ale bo mi ŋaaŋ a cheena. Wa ta pagrim a gaam mi kama. Mi pɔsima ale mi ale domsi a kali wa niŋ a yeeri wa nuensaŋa a te wa. 8Nyiam ate mi pai a te ni soka, alege waai ale cheena la, ale pai ka Wen Chiika a te ni soka.>>
9Da ŋala po Yeezu a jam nyini ka Nazaret ale bo Galili po la. Wa yaa jam Jɔɔn jigi ayen Jɔɔn a te wa soka Jodan benni po. 10Jɔɔn ale te wa soka a nueri ate Yeezu a yaa nyini nyiamu po a jueli la, wa yaa deri nya wenŋmazukku ale ku lagri ate wa nya Wen Chiika a siŋ jam kali wa zuk nna ase nangbaŋ la, 11ate lueluk a yaa nyini wenŋmazukku po a weeni Yeezu ayen, <<Fi ale m nidoabili dii ate mi a yaali la. M sui a peenti ale fu kama.>>
12Wen Chiika yaa ta Yeezu a ga jo gɔnni po. 13Wa jam bo dula jigini ate ku paari ka da pisinaansi. Ate Sitaana yaa jam nye wa a nya. Wa jam bo ale ka gɔi duŋsa ate Wen yaa tom maarɔba ate ba jam maari wa.
14Dai yeŋ po nuruba a yaa yik Jɔɔn a ta wa ga lik dɔk po. Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ate Yeezu yaa jam Galili tɛŋka po a mooli Wen wamaŋsaŋa ayen, 15<<Da ŋaai ate Wen dak ayen wa naamu le jam la, a moata kama. Ni basi ni tuimbaataŋa abe ni ta siaka ale wa wamaŋsaŋa.>>
16Yeezu ale va Galili nyakpiemu nɔi a taam la, wa yaa nya Simon ale wa suoku Andiru ale ba za a yuk ba ŋmiak a basi nyiamu po diila ba jam ka jum yigrisa. 17Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni jam va mu ate m basi ate ni ta nuruba a jam m jigi.>> 18Ate ba deri basi ba ŋmaasaŋa ale va wa.
19Wa le cheŋ magadek la, wa yaa nya Jeemsi ale wa suoku Jɔɔn ale jam ka Zebedi nidoabilisa la ale ba bo ba ŋaaruŋ po a laŋ ba ŋmaasaŋa. 20Yeezu yaa wi ba ate ba deri basi ba kowa Zebedi ŋaaruŋku po ale wa tomteerɔma ale ga va wa.
21Yeezu ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔma yaa ga jo Kapernaum tɛŋka po. Juuma Vuusum Danni ale jam paari la, Yeezu yaa ga jo ba tuka dɔkku po a boro a sak ba Wen wie. 22Nuruma ale wom wa sinsaŋŋa la, ku yaa cha ba, dii nyiŋla wa sak kama ase waai ale jam ta pagrim la ale kan nye ase Sinsak sagrɔma la. 23Nuru ale jam ta chichirik biok a maa bo tuka dɔkku po. Wa yaa kaari 24ayen, <<Yeezu Nazaret denɔwa, fi a yaali ka boa ti jigiya? Fi jam ayen fi kaasi ti kama? M seba fi ale ka waai la kama, fi ka Nuru Weleŋ a nyini Wen jigi.>>
25Alege Yeezu yaa toariŋ chichirik bioku ayen, <<Goori abe fi nyini wa po a nyini.>> 26Chichirik bioku a deri basi ate nuruwa nyiŋka a gɔk a yaa kaari a nyini wa po a nyini.
27Ku yaa cha nuruma meena ale jam bo dula la, ate ba weeni ayen, <<Ni nya nuruwa de ta pagrim a weeni chichirik baata ate ti a wom wa nɔi a nyini nuruba po a nyini.>> Ba yaa bek chaab mɛ ayen, <<Ka boan jaab sinsak paala ale nna?>> 28Galili tɛŋka po nuruma yegayega a jam wom Yeezu ale tom diila kama.
29Yeezu yaa deri basi tuka dɔkku ale cheŋ. Wa ale Jeemsi ale Jɔɔn yaa ga jo Simon ale Andiru yenni po. 30Yeezu ale jo yenni po la, ba yaa deri weeni wa ayen Simon ŋanuba ale a yuak. Wa nyiŋka jam toliŋ ka nna bakki ate wa dua wa dɔkku po. 31Yeezu yaa jo nipowa dɔkku po a yik wa nisaŋa a zak ate wa yiti ŋmai. Wa ale nye dila la, wa nyiŋka yaa deri yɔk ate wa yiti yaali nyiam a te ba.
32Wenni ale siŋ la, tɛŋka po demma a pai ba yɔgnyieŋsa ale baai ate chichirik baata a jam ta ba la a jam Yeezu jigi. 33Tɛŋka po demma meena a yaa tigsi chaab a jam yeri diipo ate Yeezu a boro la. 34Wa tebi nuruba yegayega baai ate nyiŋtuila tɔgatɔga a jam ta ba la, ale a yiak chichirik baata yegayega nuruba po a basi. Yeezu an jam te chichirik baataŋa suik ate ti weeni wari ya, dii nyiŋla ti poom seba wa ale ka waai la kama.
35Saluik yokyok ate vanni an diem jam veenti la, Yeezu yaa yiti a nyini tɛŋka po a cheŋ juijui ate nuru a karo la a puusi a te Wen dula jigini. 36Simon ale wa vaanchaama yaa nyini gisi wa. 37Ba ale nya wa la, ba yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Waai meena a gisi fu kama.>>
38Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni te ti cheŋ tɛŋ sii ale moata la ate m sak nuruma Wen wie ate ba wom. Ka dila nyiŋ ate m jam.>> 39Wa yaa nyiem a gilim Galili tɛŋka a sak nuruba Wen wieŋa ba tuka diinaŋa po. Wa jam yiak chichirik baata nuruba po a basi mɛ.
40Gami yaa jam Yeezu jigi a kpi duna wa niŋ a saalim wa ayen, <<Fi dan siak, fi baga a tebi mu kama, ate m nya nyiŋyɔgsa.>>
