Ku abe ŋmarisi a va Saalɔbiika nyiŋ kama ayen wa le nam wie yegayega nyiŋ abe ba nye ate wa chim javaliŋ. 13Alege mi a weeni ni kama ayen Elaja a poom ŋaam jam kama ate ba nye wa badek ale a yaali diila. Ase ba ale ŋmarisi dii a ta va wa nyiŋ la.>>
14Ba yaa jam gum chaab ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔ mbala ate nuru boari yegayega a za gilim ba ate Sinsak sagrɔma gela yaa ta nanpaga ale ba. 15Nuru boanni ale jam nya Yeezu la, ku yaa cha ba nna yegayega ate ba yaa chali ga tu wa a puusi wa.
16Yeezu yaa bek wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ayen, <<Ka boan daluŋ ate ni ta ale Sinsak sagrɔma?>>
17Nuru yaa jam bo nuru boanni po a weeni wa ayen, <<Sagrɔ, m ta ka m nidoabili a jam fi jigi. Chichirik biok ale bo wa po ate wa an baga a biisi. 18Chichirik bioku a dan ga yiti, ku nyiem a pai wa kama a kasim a fɔbi tɛŋ diipo meena ate tintupuuk a nyini wa nɔnni po a nyini ate wa a ŋɔbi wa nyinaŋa ate wa nyiŋka mɛ a deri ate m yaa saalim fi ŋaaŋviirɔma ayen ba yiak chichirik bioku wa po a basi alege ba an baga a nyeya.>>
19Yeezu yaa tulisi ayen, <<Nama gaŋ kaai ale kan ta siaka la, mi ale bo ale nama a beni ka sɛ abe mi a ŋmagli ale ni? Ta fi nidoabinni a jam de.>>
20Wa yaa ta wa a jam Yeezu jigi. Chichirik bioku ale ga nya Yeezu la, ku yaa deri yiti nna yegayega a pai biika a fɔbi tɛŋka ate wa a bilim ate tintupuuk a nyini wa nɔnni po a nyini.
21Yeezu yaa bek biika kowa ayen, <<Chichirik bioku ale jo fi biika la, ka benaŋa dina?>> Wa kowa yaa weeni Yeezu ayen, <<Ku jo wa ka wa bi fiik po. 22Dai po dai po ku a yuk wa kama a lɔnsi bolim po ale nyiam po ayen ku ko wa. Fi dan baga a maari ti, ta jiirim ale ti abe fi maari ti.>>
23Yeezu yaa ŋman bek wa ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi a bek ayen m nin baga? Wie meena a baga a nye kama a te nuru waai ale ta siaka la.>>
24Biika kowa yaa deri kaari a weeni ayen, <<Mi ta siaka kama, alege m siaka an soa diiya. Maari mu ate m ta siaka a gum du.>>
25Yeezu ale nya ale nuru boari a chali cheena jigini la, wa yaa toariŋ chichirik bioku ayen, <<Fi chichirik biok kuui ale basi ate biika de an baga a biisi ale kan wom la, mi a biisi ale ka fi. Nyini biika jigi a nyini abe fi kan ŋman jo a bo ale wa.>>
26Chichirik bioku yaa deri kaari nna yegayega a yuk wa lɔnsi alege yaa nyini biika nyiŋka po a nyini, alege ate wa dua ase wa kpi la ate nuruba yegayega a jam a weeni ayen, <<Wa kpi kama.>> 27Yeezu yaa yik wa nisaŋa a zak wa a zaani ŋmai.
28Yeezu ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ale cheŋ a ga jo dɔk po badek ba nyiini la, ba yaa bek wa ayen, <<Ka boa ale soa ate tama an baga yiak chichirik bioku ate ku nyini biika jigiya?>>
29Wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Chichirik bioku de choawa ni dan kan bobi nɔi ale puusi a te Wen nalimnyiini, ni an baga a yiak ate ku a nyini.>>
30Yeezu ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔma yaa basi dula ale cheŋ taam Galili tɛŋka po. Yeezu an jam a yaali ayen nuru seba ba ale a cheŋ juijui la, 31dii nyiŋla wa jam a sak ka wa ŋaaŋviirɔma. Wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Nuruba le jam yik Mi Saalɔbiika, a ta ga nyo nuru baai ale ba ko mu la nisa po, alege daa ŋata dan paari, m le yiti kum po.>> 32Wa ale weeni dila la, ba an jam miŋ dii ate wa a biisi la kiriya, alege ba jam a chali ka yɔgsum ale wa bekka.
33Ba yaa jam paari Kapernaum tɛŋka po a ga jo yeri po. Yeezu yaa bek ba ayen, <<Ti ale poom bo suiku po a cheena la, ka boan jaab nanpaga ate nama poom a nagi?>> 34Alege ba an weeni wa wari ya, dii nyiŋla ba ale poom bo suiku po la, ba ta ka nanpaga ase ka ba wana ale wa chim kpagi a gaam ba meena.
35Yeezu yaa kali tɛŋ a wi wa ŋaaŋviirɔma pi ale bayewa ate ba jam wa jigi ate wa weeni ba ayen, <<Nuru waai ale a yaali ayen wa chim niŋdeerɔ la, ku a fɛ ate wa pai wadek a zaani ŋaaŋ abe wa chim ba meena tomteerɔ.>>
36Wa yaa yik biik wanyi a ta jam zaani ba suŋsuŋ a pai wa nisaŋa a gbaari wa ale weeni ba ayen, 37<<Nuru waai ale a tuesi biik ase biika de la mi nyiŋ, wa tuesi ka mi dila. Waai mɛ abe ale a tuesi mi la, a tuesi ka waai mɛ ale tom mi ate m jam la.>>
38Jɔɔn yaa weeni Yeezu ayen, <<Sagrɔ, tama nya ka nuru wanyi ale wa pai fi yuenni nyiŋ a yiak chichirik baata nuruba po a basi, ate tama yaa weeni wa ayen wa basi, dii nyiŋla wa daa tama po wanyi.>>
39Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni dan ŋman nya wa ase dila la, ni basi wa abe ni kan weeni wa ate wa basi. Nuru waai a dan pai mi yuenni nyiŋ a baga a tom wakperikaliik kula nyɔnɔwa a kan ŋman baga a kpabi kaasi mi yuenni. 40Nuru waai ale kan ta chaab ale ti la, kula nyɔnɔwa va ti kama. 41Wensie ate mi a weeni ni, nuru waai a dan nye nyiam fii fiiga a te ni, ni ale ka mi ŋaaŋviirɔba la nyiŋ, Wen le tuni wa.
42<<Nuru waai abe dan nye ate bisaŋa de wanyi a jɔk wa siaka, ku le zunchoŋ kama a te kula nyɔnɔwa ase ba nin pai niri kpien a bobi yik wa ŋiri a ta wa ga yuk basi nyakpiemu po. 43Nuru waai nisima a dan a nye ayen wa jɔk wa siaka, kula nyɔnɔwa a gebi ni sila a basi, dii nyiŋla, ku zunchoŋ kama ate kula nyɔnɔwa nya Wen nyuvuri dii ale kan a kpeglim la ale ni yeŋ a gaam wa nin ta nisima siye alege cheŋ ninam jigi, juijui ate bolim boro a kan maara kpi la. 44Nanzue ŋaai ale bo dula a dɛ ba la a kan maari a kpi. Bolim buui mɛ ale bo dula a dɛ la a kan maari a kpimsi. 45Nuru waai naŋ a dan a nye ayen wa jɔk wa siaka, kula nyɔnɔwa a gebi naŋ kala a basi, dii nyiŋla, ku zunchoŋ kama ate kula nyɔnɔwa nya nyuvuri dila ale naŋ yeŋ a gaam wa nin ta naŋsa siye alege cheŋ ninam jigi. 46Nanzue ŋaai ale bo dula a dɛ ba la a kan maari a kpi. Bolim buui mɛ ale bo dula a dɛ la a kan maari a kpimsi. 47Nuru waai mɛ num a dan a nye ayen wa jɔk wa siaka, kula nyɔnɔwa a yeeri num bula a basi, dii nyiŋla, ku zunchoŋ kama ate kula nyɔnɔwa jo Wen naamu po ale num bunyi a gaam wa nin ta nina ŋaye alege cheŋ ninam jigi. 48Nanzue ŋaai ale bo dula a dɛ ba la a kan maari a kpi. Bolim buui mɛ ale bo dula a dɛ la a kan maari a kpimsi. 49<<Waai meena tuima ale chamsi nya ale bolim.>>
50Yesa masa kama. Yesaŋa masimu a dan jam nueri, ni le nye ka sɛ a ŋman te si masimmoa? Ase yesa ale a te jenta masim diila, ku a fɛ kama ate nama dek meena a ta nyemagsika ale chaab ate ni boro ale suiyɔgni.>>

english_text:
Teaching about Divorce
(Matthew 19.1-12; Luke 16.18)
1After Jesus left, he went to Judea and then on to the other side of the Jordan River. Once again large crowds came to him, and as usual, he taught them.
2Some Pharisees wanted to test Jesus. So they came up to him and asked if it was right for a man to divorce his wife. 3Jesus asked them, “What does the Law of Moses say about this?”
4 They answered, “Moses allows a man to write out divorce papers and send his wife away.”
5Jesus replied, “Moses gave you this law because you are so heartless. 6 But in the beginning God made a man and a woman. 7 That's why a man leaves his father and mother and gets married. 8He becomes like one person with his wife. Then they are no longer two people, but one. 9And no one should separate a couple that God has joined together.”
10When Jesus and his disciples were back in the house, they asked him about what he had said. 11 He told them, “A man who divorces his wife and marries someone else is unfaithful to his wife. 12A woman who divorces her husband and marries again is also unfaithful.”
Jesus Blesses Little Children
(Matthew 19.13-15; Luke 18.15-17)
13Some people brought their children to Jesus so he could bless them by placing his hands on them. But his disciples told the people to stop bothering him.
14When Jesus saw this, he became angry and said, “Let the children come to me! Don't try to stop them. People who are like these little children belong to the kingdom of God. 15 I promise you that you cannot get into God's kingdom, unless you accept it the way a child does.” 16Then Jesus took the children in his arms and blessed them by placing his hands on them.
A Rich Man
(Matthew 19.16-30; Luke 18.18-30)
17As Jesus was walking down a road, a man ran up to him. He knelt down, and asked, “Good teacher, what can I do to have eternal life?”
18Jesus replied, “Why do you call me good? Only God is good. 19 You know the commandments. ‘Do not murder. Be faithful in marriage. Do not steal. Do not tell lies about others. Do not cheat. Respect your father and mother.’ ”
20The man answered, “Teacher, I have obeyed all these commandments since I was a young man.”
21Jesus looked closely at the man. He liked him and said, “There's one thing you still need to do. Go sell everything you own. Give the money to the poor, and you will have riches in heaven. Then come with me.”
22When the man heard Jesus say this, he went away gloomy and sad because he was very rich.
23Jesus looked around and said to his disciples, “It's hard for rich people to get into God's kingdom!” 24The disciples were shocked to hear this. So Jesus told them again, “It's terribly hard to get into God's kingdom! 25In fact, it's easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to get into God's kingdom.”
26Jesus' disciples were even more amazed. They asked each other, “How can anyone ever be saved?”
27Jesus looked at them and said, “There are some things that people cannot do, but God can do anything.”
28Peter replied, “Remember, we left everything to be your followers!”
29Jesus told him:
You can be sure that anyone who gives up home or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or land for me and for the good news 30will be rewarded. In this world they will be given 100 times as many houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and pieces of land, though they will also be mistreated. And in the world to come, they will have eternal life. 31 But many who are now first will be last, and many who are now last will be first.
Jesus Again Tells about His Death
(Matthew 20.17-19; Luke 18.31-34)
32The disciples were confused as Jesus led them toward Jerusalem, and his other followers were afraid. Once again, Jesus took the twelve disciples aside and told them what was going to happen to him. He said:
33We are now on our way to Jerusalem where the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the teachers of the Law of Moses. They will sentence him to death and hand him over to foreigners, 34who will make fun of him and spit on him. They will beat him and kill him. But three days later he will rise to life.
The Request of James and John
(Matthew 20.20-28)
35James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came up to Jesus and asked, “Teacher, will you do us a favor?”
36Jesus asked them what they wanted, 37and they answered, “When you come into your glory, please let one of us sit at your right side and the other at your left.”
38 Jesus told them, “You don't really know what you're asking! Are you able to drink from the cup that I must soon drink from or be baptized as I must be baptized?”
39“Yes, we are!” James and John answered.
Then Jesus replied, “You certainly will drink from the cup from which I must drink. And you will be baptized just as I must! 40But it isn't for me to say who will sit at my right side and at my left. This is for God to decide.”
41When the ten other disciples heard this, they were angry with James and John. 42 But Jesus called the disciples together and said:
You know that those foreigners who call themselves kings like to order their people around. And their great leaders have full power over the people they rule. 43 But don't act like them. If you want to be great, you must be the servant of all the others. 44And if you want to be first, you must be everyone's slave. 45 The Son of Man did not come to be a slave master, but a slave who will give his life to rescue many people.
Jesus Heals Blind Bartimaeus
(Matthew 20.29-34; Luke 18.35-43)
46Jesus and his disciples went to Jericho. And as they were leaving, they were followed by a large crowd. A blind beggar by the name of Bartimaeus son of Timaeus was sitting beside the road. 47When he heard that it was Jesus from Nazareth, he shouted, “Jesus, Son of David, have pity on me!” 48Many people told the man to stop, but he shouted even louder, “Son of David, have pity on me!”
49Jesus stopped and said, “Call him over!”
They called out to the blind man and said, “Don't be afraid! Come on! He is calling for you.” 50The man threw off his coat as he jumped up and ran to Jesus.
51Jesus asked, “What do you want me to do for you?”
The blind man answered, “Master, I want to see!”
52Jesus told him, “You may go. Your eyes are healed because of your faith.”
At once the man could see, and he went down the road with Jesus.
translation_text:
1Yeezu yaa basi dula jigini alege va Judia tɛŋka po a taam paari Jodan benni kauk kunkula. Nuru boari yegayega yaa tigsi chaab a jam wa jigi ate wa sak ba ase wa nyiem ale poom a sak ba diila.
2Farisiima gela yaa jam wa jigi ayen ba choa wa nɔi a nya. Ba yaa bek wa ayen, <<Ti Sinsaŋŋa a siak ayen nuru a basi wa powa?>>
3Yeezu yaa bek ba ayen, <<Moosis a sak ni ka sɛ?>> 4Ba yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Wa sak ti kama ayen wa ŋmarisi gbaŋ a basi ti wa cheŋ.>>
5Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Moosis a sak ni kama, ayen ni va suik kula dii nyiŋla, ni ta ka tukpari. 6Alege ku piilimka po ate Wen a nye tɛŋka meena la, <Wa nye ŋanta meena ka jaduok ale jasari, nidoa ale nipok.> (Piilimka 1:27) 7A yaa weeni ayen, <Ku nala kama ate nidoa a basi wa ko ale wa ma ale ge a ga faari nipok ate 8ba nɔi bayewa a chim bunyi.> (Piilimka 2:24) Ba ŋman daa nuruba baye, ba yaa ka nuru yeŋ. 9Dila nyiŋla baai ate Wen a basi ate ba chim nuru yeŋ la, ku an magsi ayen nuru a poori ba.>>
10Yeezu ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔma yaa ŋman ga jo yeri po ate ba bek wa dii ate wa poom weeni ba la kiri. 11Wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Nuru waai a dan basi wa pok alege a ŋman faari wa choa, wa nye wa powa a kaasi kama. Wa nye ka kaboŋ, 12ate wa dan basi wa chorɔwa ale yali nuru yoŋ, nipowa a nye ka kaboŋ.>>
13Dula jigini nuruba gela yaa pai bisa a ta jam Yeezu jigi ayen wa niak ba. Ba ale nye dila la, wa ŋaaŋviirɔma yaa toariŋ ba. 14Yeezu ale ga nya dii ate ba nye la, wa sui yaa jam a puuri nna yegayega ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ate wa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni te bisaŋa suik ate ba jam mi jigi. Ni kan yiak ba, ale ka bala ale soa Wen naamu. 15Wensie ate mi a weeni ni, waai a dan kan tuesi Wen naamu ase biik la wa kan baga a jo bu po.>> 16Yeezu yaa pai ba a nyo wa nigoruk po yaa pai wa nisaŋa a ji ba zuima a niak ba.
17Yeezu ale basi dula jigini ale a cheŋ la, nuru yaa chali jam tu wa a kpi duna tɛŋ wa niŋ a bek wa ayen, <<Sagrɔ maŋŋa, mi le nye ka sɛ ate m nya nyuvuri dii ale kan ta kpeglimka la?>>
18Yeezu yaa bek wa ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi a wi mu ayen nuru maŋŋa? Nuru waai karo a chim nuru maŋŋa, ka Wen dek nyiini. 19Fi poom seba Moosis Sinsaŋŋa kama. Naawen a weeni ayen kan ko nuru, kan nye kaboŋsa, kan zu, kan chim seerɔ waai ale a velim la, kan a yaali degaamka. Ku a fɛ ate fi zuli fi ko ale fi ma.>>
20Nuruwa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Sagrɔ, mi kasim va sinsaŋŋa de meena kama a ta nyini m paalim po a jam paari jinla.>> 21Yeezu yaa nya wa ate wa jiirim dari wa ate wa weeni wa ayen, <<Wa yeŋ dekki ale tali fi jigi. Cheŋ a ga pai fi ŋantaŋa meena a da a tuesi ligraŋa a te niwomma. Fi dan nye dila alege jam va mi, fi le jigsi wenŋmazuk.>>
22Yeezu ale weeni wa dila la wa sui yaa deri kaasi ate wa yaa deri cheŋ ale sui kaasuŋ dii nyiŋla wa jam ka ŋanta nyɔnɔ a kan siak wa ŋantaŋa nyiŋŋa.
23Yeezu yaa nya wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ale weeni ba ayen, <<Ku toa kama ate ŋanta nyam a baga a jo Wen naamu po.>>
24Wa ale weeni dila la ku yaa cha ba. Wa yaa ŋman weeni ba ayen, <<M bisa, ku toa kama ale Wen naamu po joka. 25Ku ka moali ate laalaakomi a baga va garuk pein vɔrup po a nyini a gaam jigsirɔ a nin baga a jo Wen naamu po.>>
26Yeezu ale weeni ba dila la, ku yaa cha ba. Ba yaa weeni chaab ayen, <<Ku be dan ka dila, ka wana le wa baga nya varibasika?>>
27Yeezu yaa nya ba a weeni ayen, <<Ku toa kama nurubiik jigi, alege ku ka moali Wen jigi, dii nyiŋla Wen baga wie meena a nye kama.>>
28Dula jigini Piita yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Nya, tama basi ka ti ŋanta meena ale jam va fu.>>
29Yeezu yaa ŋman weeni ba ayen, <<Wensie ate mi a weeni ni, nuru waai ale basi wa yeri ale wa ko ale wa ma ale wa suata ale wa toaba ale wa bisa ale wa kaduksa, mi ale Wen wamaŋsaŋa nyiŋla, 30wa le nya ŋanta ale nuruba nna yegayega jinla a gaam baai meena ate wa basi la. Wa le ŋman nya yie, ale maba ale suata ale toaba ale bisa ale kaduksa alege wa le nya ninam mɛ nna yegayega abe chum diipo wa yaa nya nyuvuri dii ale kan ta kpeglimka la. 31Baai ale dɛ niŋ la yega ale jam wari ŋaaŋ ate baai ale wari ŋaaŋ la jam dɛ niŋ.>>
32Ba ale jam bo suiku po a cheŋ Jerusalem tɛŋka la, Yeezu yaa dɛ ba niŋ ate ba a cheŋ. Baai meena ale jam va wa la, ku yaa cha ba alege baai ale va la jam a chali yɔgsum. Wa yaa poori wa ŋaaŋviirɔma pi ale bayewa a weeni ba dii ate nuruba ayen ba nye wa la. 33Wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni nya, ti a cheŋ ka Jerusalem tɛŋka. Ti dan paari dula jigini, nuruba ale yik Mi Saalɔbiika a ta mu a ga nyo kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa ale Sinsak sagrɔma nisima po. Ba le bo m kum buusa abe ba ta mu a ga nyo baai ale kan daa Juuba la nisima po. 34Ba le la mu abe ba chesi tintueta a basi m nyiŋ, a nak mu abe ba yaa ko mu. Daa ŋata a dan paari mi le yiti kum po.>>
35Dula jigini Zebedi nidoabilisaŋa Jeemsi ale Jɔɔn, yaa jam Yeezu jigi a weeni wa ayen, <<Ti Sagrɔ, ti a yaali ayen ti saalim fu kama ate fi nye wari a te ti.>>
36Wa yaa bek ba ayen, <<Ka boa ate nama a yaali ayen mi nye a te ni?>>
37Ba yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Fi dan jam chim naab a soa nuru meena zuk a nya, ti a yaali kama ayen fi basi ate ti wanyi a kali fi juga, wanyi mɛ a kali fi gala.>>
38Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Nama zɛ dii ate ni a bek la. Ni ale baga a nyu beerik kaai ate mi ale nyu laa yaase so kaai ate mi ale so laa?>>
39Ba yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Ti le baga a maa nam.>> Yeezu yaa ŋman weeni ba ayen, <<Wensie ni ale nyu beerik kaai ate mi ale nyu la abe ni so, so kaai ate mi ale so la. 40Alege mi ka suik a lueri baai ale ba kali mi juga ale mi gala la. Ka Wen le wa pai dula a te baai ate wa gomsi magsi ba la.>>
41Wa ŋaaŋviirɔ mbala piwa ale wom Jeemsi ale Jɔɔn ale bek Yeezu diila, ba sue yaa puuri nna yegayega ale ba. 42Yeezu yaa wi ba ate ba jam tigsi chaab wa jigi ate wa weeni ba ayen, <<Tɛŋzuk de nalima ta pagrim ba nuruma zuk kama a nye ba ale a yaali diila. Ba kpaŋŋa mɛ ta pagrim ba zuk kama. 43Alege ku an magsi ayen ku chim dila nama jigiya. Nuru waai a dan a yaali ayen wa chim nama kpagi, ku a fɛ ate wa chim ni meena tomteerɔ. 44Nuru waai a daa a yaali ayen wa chim nama kpagi, ku a fɛ ate wa chim nama meena yɔma. 45Mi Saalɔbiika an jam ayen ka nuruba a tom a te mu alege ka m tom a te nuruba. M jam ayen m tom a te ka tɛŋka meena demma abe m kpi a tuesi ba a basi.>>
46Ba yaa jam paari Jeriko tɛŋka, ate nuruba yegayega yaa tigsi chaab a jam Yeezu jigi. Ba le jam basi dula jigini ale a nyini la, ba yaa nya yio ale wa kala suiku nɔi a juisi. Wa yuei jam le Baatimiusi. Di kiri ale Timiusi nidoabili. 47Wa ale wom ayen ka Yeezu Nazaret denɔwa ale a taam la, wa yaa kaari a wi wa ayen, <<Yeezu, fi Deevid nidoabinni, ta jiirim ale mu.>>
48Nuruma yega yaa weeni wa ayen wa goori wa wanni, alege wa zɛri ale a kaari nna yegayega a gum du a weeni wa ayen, <<Deevid Nidoabinni, ta jiirim ale mu.>>
49Yeezu yaa zaani a weeni ba ayen ba wi wa ate wa yiti jam wa jigi. Ba yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Te fi sui peenti abe fi yiti jam, dii nyiŋla wa a wi fu kama.>> 50Yiowa yaa yeeri wa kasaauku a dueni, ale yiti a zaani ŋmai a cheŋ Yeezu jigi.
51Yeezu yaa bek wa ayen, <<Fi a yaali ayen mi nye ka boa a te fu?>> Wa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Sagrɔ, mi a yaali ayen fi nye kama ate m ninaŋa a lagri a te mu.>>
52Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Be cheŋ. Fi ale ta siaka ale mu diila a basi kama ate fi ninaŋa a lagri.>> Wa ninaŋa yaa deri lagri ate wa yaa va Yeezu a cheŋ.

english_text:
Jesus Enters Jerusalem
(Matthew 21.1-11; Luke 19.28-40; John 12.12-19)
1Jesus and his disciples reached Bethphage and Bethany near the Mount of Olives. When they were getting close to Jerusalem, Jesus sent two of them on ahead. 2He told them, “Go into the next village. As soon as you enter it, you will find a young donkey that has never been ridden. Untie the donkey and bring it here. 3If anyone asks why you are doing this, say, ‘The Lord needs it and will soon bring it back.’ ”
4The disciples left and found the donkey tied near a door that faced the street. While they were untying it, 5some of the people standing there asked, “Why are you untying the donkey?” 6They told them what Jesus had said, and the people let them take it.
7The disciples led the donkey to Jesus. They put some of their clothes on its back, and Jesus got on. 8Many people spread clothes on the road, while others spread branches they had cut from the fields.
9 In front of Jesus and behind him, people went along shouting,
“Hooray!
God bless the one who comes
in the name of the Lord!
10God bless the coming kingdom
of our ancestor David.
Hooray for God
in heaven above!”
11After Jesus had gone to Jerusalem, he went into the temple and looked around at everything. But since it was already late in the day, he went back to Bethany with the twelve disciples.
Jesus Puts a Curse on a Fig Tree
(Matthew 21.18,19)
12When Jesus and his disciples left Bethany the next morning, he was hungry. 13From a distance Jesus saw a fig tree covered with leaves, and he went to see if there were any figs on the tree. But there were none, because it wasn't the season for figs. 14So Jesus said to the tree, “Never again will anyone eat fruit from this tree!” The disciples heard him say this.
Jesus in the Temple
(Matthew 21.12-17; Luke 19.45-48; John 2.13-22)
15After Jesus and his disciples reached Jerusalem, he went into the temple and began chasing out everyone who was selling and buying. He turned over the tables of the moneychangers and the benches of those who were selling doves. 16Jesus would not let anyone carry things through the temple. 17 Then he taught the people and said, “The Scriptures say, ‘My house should be called a place of worship for all nations.’ But you have made it a place where robbers hide!”
18The chief priests and the teachers of the Law of Moses heard what Jesus said, and they started looking for a way to kill him. They were afraid of him, because the crowds were completely amazed at his teaching.
19That evening, Jesus and the disciples went outside the city.
A Lesson from the Fig Tree
(Matthew 21.20-22)
20As the disciples walked past the fig tree the next morning, they noticed that it was completely dried up, roots and all. 21Peter remembered what Jesus had said to the tree. Then Peter said, “Teacher, look! The tree you put a curse on has dried up.”
22Jesus told his disciples:
Have faith in God! 23 If you have faith in God and don't doubt, you can tell this mountain to get up and jump into the sea, and it will. 24Everything you ask for in prayer will be yours, if you only have faith.
25-26 Whenever you stand up to pray, you must forgive what others have done to you. Then your Father in heaven will forgive your sins.
A Question about Jesus' Authority
(Matthew 21.23-27; Luke 20.1-8)
27Jesus and his disciples returned to Jerusalem. And as he was walking through the temple, the chief priests, the nation's leaders, and the teachers of the Law of Moses came over to him. 28They asked, “What right do you have to do these things? Who gave you this authority?”
29Jesus answered, “I have just one question to ask you. If you answer it, I will tell you where I got the right to do these things. 30Who gave John the right to baptize? Was it God in heaven or merely some human being?”
31They thought it over and said to each other, “We can't say that God gave John this right. Jesus will ask us why we didn't believe John. 32On the other hand, these people think that John was a prophet. So we can't say it was merely some human who gave John the right to baptize.”
They were afraid of the crowd 33and told Jesus, “We don't know.”
Jesus replied, “Then I won't tell you who gave me the right to do what I do.”
translation_text:
1Ba yaa jam paari Betfaaji ale Betani tɛŋsaŋa ale Olivi Guuku. Tɛŋsaŋa ale guuku a jam moata ka Jerusalem tɛŋka. Yeezu yaa wi wa ŋaaŋviirɔma po baye a weeni ba ayen, 2<<Ni cheŋ a ga jo tɛŋ fiik kaai ale bo ni niŋ la. Ni dan deri ga jo dula, ni le nya bonpaalik ate ba bobi ka zaani. Nuru an diem a dɔ ka nyaya. Ni foli ka a ta jam te mu. 3Ni dan boro a foli ka, ate nuru bek ni dii nyiŋ ate ni a foli ka la, ni weeni wa ayen ka Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita ale a yaali ka. Wa be dan nueri ale ka wa le ŋman basi ate ba ta ka a jam nwuli.>>
4Ba yaa cheŋ ga nya bonpaalik ale ka bobi za yeri nansuiŋ nɔi ate ba yaa foli ka. 5Nuru baai ale jam za dula jigini la, yaa nya ba a bek ayen, <<Ka boa ale soa ate nama a foli ka?>> 6Ba yaa weeni ba dii ate Yeezu a poom weeni ba la, ate nuruma yaa basi ate ba foli ka a ta cheŋ ga te wa. 7Ba yaa ta bonpaalika a ga te Yeezu, yaa yeeri ba gattaŋa a pai vi bonpaalika chiaka zuk ate Yeezu yaa doa. 8Nuruba yegayega yaa jam pai ba gattaŋa a pati suiku niŋ ayen Yeezu a ta wa bonika a cheŋ va ti zuk a taam. Ba gela mɛ a cheŋ suiku nakpiak a ga che tiisa vaata a ta jam pati suiku niŋ. 9Ba ale jam bo suiku po a cheŋ la baai ale jam dɛ niŋka la ale baai mɛ ale jam bo ŋaaŋka la, meena yaa zuli wa a kaari ayen, <<Naawen vari ti a basi. Niaka a bo waai ale cheena Naawen yuenni nyiŋla. (Yiila 118:25-26) 10Naawen niak waai ale cheena ayen wa soa ti kokpieŋka Deevid naam buui ale cheena la. Fi, Naawen dii ale bo wenŋmazuk la, a vari ti a basi.>>
11Yeezu ale jam paari Jerusalem tɛŋka la, wa yaa cheŋ ga jo Wen Yenni po a nyiem nya jaabuuri meena ale bo di po la ale ŋman nyini. Yeezu ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔma pi ale bayewa an jam bo dula jigini a beniya, dii nyiŋla, wenni a jam a siŋ kama. Ba yaa basi dula jigini ale ŋman cheŋ Betani.
12Vari ale jam veenti la, ba yaa ŋman yiti a basi Betani ale nyini. Kom yaa jam ta Yeezu. 13Wa yaa nya kiŋkaŋ a za niŋniŋ ate vaata a lik ka. Wa yaa cheŋ ga paari ka tɛŋ ayen wa nya ase ka ta moota ya ate wa dɛ, alege jaab a jam ka ka zuwa. Ka vaata nyiini ale jam boro, dii nyiŋla ku jam daa moota wein ya. 14Yeezu yaa weeni kiŋkaŋka ayen, <<A nyini jinla danni a ta a cheŋ diipo meena wuu, nuru a kan ŋman nya fi moota a dɛ.>> Wa ŋaaŋviirɔma yaa wom dii ate wa weeni la.
15Ba ale ŋman jam paari Jerusalem tɛŋka la, Yeezu yaa ŋman ga jo Wen Yenni po. Nuruba ale jam bo di po a gerim. Wa yaa yiak ba meena ate ba nyini dula jigini a nyini, a zak nuru baai ale jam ta ligraŋa a tagri la ŋanzaanitaŋa a tulim kpib, a tusi baai ale ta nangbaŋsaŋa a da la zukpagliksaŋa mɛ a lɔnsi. 16Wa an jam siak ayen geruŋdɔba a ji ŋanta a va Wen Yenni po a taam nyini. 17Wa yaa sak nuruma ale bek ba ayen, <<Ba an ŋmarisi kama ayen, <Mi yenni ba le wi di ayen ka tɛŋsa meena puusa yeri la,> (Azaya 56:7) alege nama a pai di chim zueba boka jigi ya?>> (Jeremaya 7:11)
18Yeezu ale ga weeni dila ate kaabteerɔ kpagni ale Sinsak sagrɔma wom la, ba yaa jam a gisi suik ayen ba ko wa. Alege yɔgsum ale jam yik ba ale Yeezu ate ba an jam baga a nya suik a tiri wa. Dii nyiŋla wa sinsaŋŋa a jam cha nuruma kama.
19Junɔi ale jam paari la, Yeezu ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔma a yaa basi Jerusalem tɛŋka ale nyini cheŋ.
20Vari ale ŋman veenti la, ba yaa va suiku a taam a nya kiŋkaŋka ale ka kpi za. 21Piita yaa teeri Yeezu diem ale weeni diila, a yaa weeni wa ayen, <<M Sagrɔ, nya, kiŋkaŋ kaai ate fi diem a ka te la, ka meena a kpi kama.>>
22Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni ta siaka ale Wen. 23Wensie ate mi a weeni ni, waai ale ta siaka ale Wen ale ka chichama ale sum siak ayen wa ale weeni diila le nye la, a baga a weeni gu kpioŋku kama ayen ku voori dula jigini a ga lo nyakpiemu po ate Wen sum nye a te wa. 24Dila nyiŋ ni dan puusi a te Wen a juisi jaab, ni ta siaka ayen ni nya jaamu kama ate Wen yaa pai a te ni. 25Diipo meena ni daa ni puusi a te Wen ni dɛ niŋ a vɔŋ te baai ale nye ni a kaasi la, abe ni ge a puusi a te Kowa waai ale bo wenŋmazuk la ate wa mɛ a vɔŋ te ni. 26Ni dan kan nye dila, ni Kowa waai ale bo wenŋmazuk la abe kan vɔŋ te nama mɛ.>>
27Ba yaa ŋman jam Jerusalem tɛŋka a ga jo Wen Yenni po. Yeezu ale bo di po a nyiem la, kaabteerɔ kpagni ale Sinsak sagrɔma ale tɛŋka nisɔmma meena yaa tigsi chaab a jam wa jigi 28a bek wa ayen, <<Ka boan pagrim ate fi ta a tom wieŋa de? Ka wana ale te fu suik ate fi a nyiem a tom wieŋa de?>>
29Yeezu yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<Mi mɛ le bek ni wari. M dan bek ni ate ni siak a tulisi mu, mi mɛ le weeni sak ni pagrim buui ate mi ta a tom wieŋa de la. 30Jɔɔn ale jam a te nuruba soka la, ka Wen ale jam te wa pagrimu yaa ka nuru biiga?>>
31Wa le bek ba dila la, ba yaa ta nanpaga ale chaab ayen, <<Ti dan weeni wa ayen ka Wen ale te wa pagrimu, wa le bek ti ayen, <Be ka boa ale soa ate ti an siak a te wa?> 32Ti be an baga a weeni mɛ ayen ka nurubiik ale te wa pagrimu dii nyiŋla, waai meena a seba wa ale jam ka Wen biisiteerɔ la kama.>> Ate ba yaa chali yɔgsum. 33Ba yaa tulisi Yeezu ayen, <<Tama zɛ.>> Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Mi mɛ a kan weeni ni pagrim buui ate mi ta a tom wieŋa de la.>>

english_text:
Renters of a Vineyard
(Matthew 21.33-46; Luke 20.9-19)
1 Jesus then told them this story:
A farmer once planted a vineyard. He built a wall around it and dug a pit to crush the grapes in. He also built a lookout tower. Then he rented out his vineyard and left the country.
2When it was harvest time, he sent a servant to get his share of the grapes. 3The renters grabbed the servant, beat him up, and sent him away without a thing.
4The owner sent another servant, but the renters beat him on the head and insulted him terribly. 5Then the man sent another servant, and they killed him. He kept sending servant after servant. They beat some of them and killed some.
6The owner had a son he loved very much. Finally, he sent his son to the renters because he thought they would respect him. 7But they said to themselves, “Someday he will own this vineyard. Let's kill him! That way we can have it all for ourselves.” 8So they grabbed the owner's son, killed him, and threw his body out of the vineyard.
9Jesus asked, “What do you think the owner of the vineyard will do? He will come and kill those renters and let someone else have his vineyard. 10 You surely know that the Scriptures say,
‘The stone the builders
tossed aside
is now the most important
stone of all.
11This is something
the Lord has done,
and it is amazing to us.’ ”
12The leaders knew that Jesus was really talking about them, and they wanted to arrest him. But because they were afraid of the crowd, they let him alone and left.
Paying Taxes
(Matthew 22.15-22; Luke 20.20-26)
13The Pharisees got together with Herod's followers. Then they sent some men to trick Jesus into saying something wrong. 14They went to him and said, “Teacher, we know that you are honest. You treat everyone with the same respect, no matter who they are. And you teach the truth about what God wants people to do. Tell us, should we pay taxes to the Emperor or not?”
15Jesus knew what they were up to, and he said, “Why are you trying to test me? Show me a coin!”
16They brought him a silver coin, and he asked, “Whose picture and name are on it?”
“The Emperor's,” they answered.
17Then Jesus told them, “Give the Emperor what belongs to him and give God what belongs to God.” The men were amazed at Jesus.
Life in the Future World
(Matthew 22.23-33; Luke 20.27-40)
18 The Sadducees did not believe that people would rise to life after death. So some of them came to Jesus and said:
19 Teacher, Moses wrote that if a married man dies and has no children, his brother should marry the widow. Their first son would then be thought of as the son of the dead brother. 20There were once seven brothers. The first one married, but died without having any children. 21The second brother married his brother's widow, and he also died without having children. The same thing happened to the third brother, 22and finally to all seven brothers. At last the woman died. 23When God raises people from death, whose wife will this woman be? After all, she had been married to all seven brothers.
24Jesus answered:
You are completely wrong! You don't know what the Scriptures teach. And you don't know anything about the power of God. 25When God raises people to life, they won't marry. They will be like the angels in heaven. 26 You surely know about people being raised to life. You know that in the story about Moses and the burning bush, God said, “I am the God worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” 27He isn't the God of the dead, but of the living. You Sadducees are all wrong.
The Most Important Commandment
(Matthew 22.34-40; Luke 10.25-28)
28 One of the teachers of the Law of Moses came up while Jesus and the Sadducees were arguing. When he heard Jesus give a good answer, he asked him, “What is the most important commandment?”
29 Jesus answered, “The most important one says: ‘People of Israel, you have only one Lord and God. 30You must love him with all your heart, soul, mind, and strength.’ 31 The second most important commandment says: ‘Love others as much as you love yourself.’ No other commandment is more important than these.”
32 The man replied, “Teacher, you are certainly right to say there is only one God. 33 It is also true that we must love God with all our heart, mind, and strength, and that we must love others as much as we love ourselves. These commandments are more important than all the sacrifices and offerings that we could possibly make.”
34When Jesus saw that the man had given a sensible answer, he told him, “You are not far from God's kingdom.” After this, no one dared ask Jesus any more questions.
About David's Son
(Matthew 22.41-46; Luke 20.41-44)
35As Jesus was teaching in the temple, he said, “How can the teachers of the Law of Moses say the Messiah will come from the family of King David? 36 The Holy Spirit led David to say,
‘The Lord said to my Lord:
Sit at my right side
until I make your enemies
into a footstool for you.’
37If David called the Messiah his Lord, how can the Messiah be his son?”
The large crowd enjoyed listening to Jesus teach.
Jesus Condemns the Pharisees and the Teachers of the Law of Moses
(Matthew 23.1-36; Luke 20.45-47)
38As Jesus was teaching, he said:
Guard against the teachers of the Law of Moses! They love to walk around in long robes and be greeted in the market. 39They like the front seats in the synagogues and the best seats at banquets. 40But they cheat widows out of their homes and pray long prayers just to show off. They will be punished most of all.
A Widow's Offering
(Luke 21.1-4)
41Jesus was sitting in the temple near the offering box and watching people put in their gifts. He noticed that many rich people were giving a lot of money. 42Finally, a poor widow came up and put in two coins worth only a few pennies. 43Jesus told his disciples to gather around him. Then he said:
I tell you that this poor widow has put in more than all the others. 44Everyone else gave what they didn't need. But she is very poor and gave everything she had. Now she doesn't have a cent to live on.
translation_text:
1Yeezu yaa magsi wamagsima a sak ba ayen, <<Nuru ale jam kpa wa kaduk, a vuk tiisa ka po ayen si a yɔni. Wa yaa che daata a ti gilim ka meena ale tu goluk a magsi daam ŋmiaka ale sɛ yie woŋ. (Azaya 5:1-2) Wa ale nye dila a ga nueri la, wa yaa yaali nuruba ayen ba a limisi ka abe ba a tom ka po alege nyiem a cheŋ tɛŋ nna niŋniŋa. 2Wa kadukka tiisaŋa yɔnaŋa pisika ale jam paari la, wa yaa tom tomteerɔ ayen wa ga tuesi yɔna ŋaai ate wa soa la wa nuruma jigi a ta jam te wa. 3Nuruma yaa yik wa a nak yiak wa ate wa cheŋ ale nisim koruta. 4Kadukka nyɔnɔwa yaa ŋman tom tomteerɔ wa choa ba jigi ate ba ŋman yik wa mɛ a nak wa zukku, a pai wa a nyo chivie po. 5Wa yaa ŋman pilim tom wa choa ba jigi ate ba ko wala. Ba jam a nye ka nuruba yega dila a nak ba gela ale ko ba gela mɛ.
6<<Waai nyiini ale jam tali ayen wa tom la ale wadek nidoabinni, waai ate wa a yaali la. Wa yaa weeni wadek ayen, <M dan tom m dek nidoabinni, ba le te wa zula.> Wa yaa tom wa ate wa cheŋ ba jigi.
7<<Alege nuruma ale nya wa nidoabinni la, ba yaa weeni chaab ayen, <Nidoabinni kowa a dan kpi, wala le wa soa wa ŋantaŋa meena. Dila nyiŋ ni basi ate ti ko wa ate wa kowa chum dan kan boro abe tama soa wa ŋantaŋa.> 8Ba yaa yik wa a ko a vuuri wa a ta nyini kadukka po a nyini peelim. 9Nama seba kadukka nyɔnɔwa le wa nye ba diila? Wa le jam ko ba kama abe wa ŋman pai wa kadukka a te nuru yonta. 10Nama an diem a karim kude Wen gbaŋka po? <Tain dii ate seerɔma a zɛri ayen di an nala la, tain dila dek ale tulim a chim tain maŋ. 11Naawen ale nye dila. Di ka wakperikaliik ti nina po.> >> (Yiila 118:22-23)
12Ba yaa deri miŋ ayen ka ba jigi ate wa pai wamagsini de a magsi dii nyiŋla, ba zɛri wa kama. Ba yaa jam a yaali ayen ba yik wa, alege ba jam a chali nuru boanni yɔgsum, ate ba yaa jam basi wa ale ge cheŋ.
13Ba yaa tom Farisiima gela ale naawa Ayerod nuruma gela ayen ba ga choa Yeezu nɔi a wom. 14Ba yaa jam weeni wa ayen, <<Sagrɔ, ti seba ayen fi ka wensie nyɔnɔ. Fi niŋ ka dii meena ate nuruba a poli la po. Nuruba kpaŋta kan basi ate fi a tagri fi popola. Fi a sak Wen wieŋa kama ale wensie. Ku magsi ayen ti tuni ti lampoowa a te naab kpioŋku Siiza, yaa ku an magsi ya? Ti a tuni yaa ti kan a tuni?>> 15Yeezu a poom seba ba kiri kama ate wa yaa bek ba ayen, <<Ka boa ate ni a yaali ayen ni choa m nɔi a wom? Ni ga ta ligbiri a jam te mu.>> 16Ba yaa ta ligbiri dinyi a jam te wa. Wa yaa bek ba ayen, <<Ka wana zuk ale wa yuei ale dua ligni nyiŋŋa?>> Ba yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Ka Siiza zuk ale wa yuei ale dua du.>>
17Wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni pai ŋan baai ate Siiza a soa la a te wa, abe ni pai ŋan baai mɛ ate Wen a soa la a te Wen.>> Ba ale wom dila la, ku yaa cha ba.
18Sajusiima baai ale jam weeni ayen nuruba kan yiti kum po la, yaa jam Yeezu jigi ale bega. 19Ba bek Yeezu ayen, <<Moosis a ŋmarisi wa gbaŋka po kama ayen, <Nuru waai a dan faari nipok ate wa ale wa an biak a nyaya alege ate wa kpi, ti a basi kama ate wa yuawa a faari nipowa a biak bisa a te wa ate wa yuenni a kan be.> 20Nuruba bayopɔi ale jam boro a chim suata ate ba suok kpagni a faari nipok ate ba an biaya alege ate wa kpi. 21Waai ale pai saŋ la yaa faari wa suoku powa, alege nipowa ale wa mɛ an biak a nyaya alege ate wa mɛ a kpi. Ba suok kuui ale pai saŋ butawa la mɛ a nye dila dekdega. 22Ba meena bayopɔiwa a jam faari nipowa kama a taam tu, alege ba waai an biak ale wa alege kpi ya. Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ate nipowa mɛ a yaa kpi. 23Yɔgyɔgla de ate nuruba bayopɔiwa de meena a faari wa a nya la, dai dii dai ate nuruba meena a yiti kum po la, ka ba wana dek chekki ale wa soa nipowa de?>>
24Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Nama an diem a miŋ Wen gbaŋka po wieŋa chagiya. Ka dila ale soa ate ni bɛ suiku. Ni zɛ Wen pagrimu mɛ ale ka diila. 25Dai dii dai ate nuruba meena ale yiti kum po la, ba meena le tagri kama a nye ase Wen maarɔma baai ale bo wenŋmazuk la. Nidoa a kan ŋman faari nipowa. Nipok mɛ abe kan ŋman yali chora. 26Yɔgyɔgla de, a magsi chaab ale nuruba le ba yiti kum po la, nama an karim Moosis gbaŋka kauk kuui ale a biisi a magsi chaab ale ti fiika ate bolimu jam a nye nna ase bu a dɛ bu la? Dula jigini ku ŋmarisi kama ayen Wen weeni Moosis kama ayen, <Wa ale Abrayam ale Aizik ale Jekob Wenni.> (Nyinika 3:6) 27Dila a sak kama ayen wa daa kpilima Wen yaa, wa ka ŋanvuta Wen, dila nyiŋ ni bɛ suiku kama.>>
28Sinsak sagrɔma wanyi a yaa wom ba ale a biisi diila. Wa ale wom ale Yeezu a tulisi ba magsi la, wa yaa jam bek Yeezu ayen, <<Ka Wen Sinsaŋŋa po ŋa ŋan dek ale chim sinsak kpiema a gaam ŋa meena?>>
29Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Sinsaŋŋa de ale chim sinsak kpiema a gaam ŋa meena. <Ni wom dɛ Izirali demma: Naawen ka ti Wen. Naawen ka wanyi. 30Yaali Naawen fi Wenni ale fi suinum meena ale fi chiik meena ale fi popola meena ale fi pagrim meena.> (Teerika 6:4-5) 31Sinsaŋ ŋaai ale gaam ale pai saŋ la ale nna, <Yaali fi vaanchoa ase fi ale a yaali fidek diila.> (Kaabka 19:18) Sinsaŋŋa ŋman karo a chim sinsak kpiema a gaam sinsaŋŋa de ŋayewa.>>
32Sinsak sagrɔwa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Sagrɔ, fi wieŋa ka wensie. Wen sum ka dinyi dekki. Wen di choa a ŋman karo a gum wa po. 33Abe fi a yaali wa ale fi suinum meena ale fi miŋka meena ale fi pagrim meena ale yaali fi vaanchoa mɛ ase fidek la, dila ka wari kpienni a gaam fi ale a ko duŋsa ale pai ŋanta ba chaab a kaab a te wa la kama.>>
34Nuruwa ale weeni dila la, Yeezu yaa seba ayen wa tulisi wa ka nalimnyiini ate wa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Ku tali ka magadega ate fi jo Wen naamu po.>> A zaani dila waai an ŋman jam be wa bega.
35Ase Yeezu ale jam a sak Wen Yenni po la, wa yaa bek ayen, <<Ka boa ale soa ate Sinsak sagrɔma a weeni ayen Kirisitawa ale chim ka Deevid nidoabili yaa? 36Wen Chiika jam basi kama ate Deevid weeni ayen, Naawen a weeni mi Nyɔnɔwa ayen, <Kali m juga nisa geŋ a ta cheena diipo ate m le basi ate fi nya pagrim fi dachaasaŋa zuk.> (Yiila 110:1)
37<<Ase Deevid dek dan wi Kirisitawa ayen wa Nyɔnɔ, ku be zaani ka sɛ ate Kirisita a baga a chim Deevid nidoabili yaa?>> Nuru boari nna yegayega ale jam boro a wom Yeezu sinsaŋŋa ale suipeentik.
38Wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni kpesi nidek ate Sinsak sagrɔma a kan paasi ni. Ba a yaali kama ayen ba jo ba garuk woŋtaŋa a bo yabaŋa po a nyiem a cheŋ ate nuruba a puusi ba abe ba a te ba zula mɛ. 39Ba a yaali kama ayen ba nyiem a kali zukpaglik sii ate nuru kpientaŋa a kali la zuima ba tuka diinaŋa po. Ba nyiem a dan boro a nye tigi ba a yaali kama ayen ba a kali zukpaglik sii ate ba kpaŋŋa a kali la zuk. 40Ba be ka baai mɛ ale a yaali pukɔga paasi dɛka la, ale baai mɛ ale a puusi Wen venta puusa woŋta la. Bala chaab waalika le gaam taam ka nna yegayega.>>
41Yeezu a jam kala ka Wen Yenni po a moata juijui ate nuruba ta ba ligra a jam a nyoro a te Wen la, a yaa a nya. Ligra nyam yegayega ale jam maa bo Wen Yenni po. Ba mɛ yaa jam maa ta ligra nna yegayega a jam a nyoro. 42Pukɔgi niwobwa yaa jam boro a ta wa ligbie ŋaye a jam nyoro. Ŋa an jam soa diiya.
43Ate wa yaa wi wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ate ba jam wa jigi weeni ba ayen, <<Wensie, mi ale a weeni ayen pukɔgi jakka de a te gaam baai meena ale te diila kama. 44Dii nyiŋ la ba meena a te kama ale diem tali nna yegayega, alege nipowa de a pai dii meena ate wa ta la a te.>>

english_text:
The Temple Will Be Destroyed
(Matthew 24.1,2; Luke 21.5,6)
1As Jesus was leaving the temple, one of his disciples said to him, “Teacher, look at these beautiful stones and wonderful buildings!”
2Jesus replied, “Do you see these huge buildings? They will certainly be torn down! Not one stone will be left in place.”
Warning about Trouble
(Matthew 24.3-14; Luke 21.7-19)
3Later, as Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives across from the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew came to him in private. 4 They asked, “When will these things happen? What will be the sign that they are about to take place?”
5Jesus answered:
Watch out and don't let anyone fool you! 6Many will come and claim to be me. They will use my name and fool many people.
7When you hear about wars and threats of wars, don't be afraid. These things will have to happen first, but that isn't the end. 8Nations and kingdoms will go to war against each other. There will be earthquakes in many places, and people will starve to death. But this is just the beginning of troubles.
9 Be on your guard! You will be taken to courts and beaten with whips in their synagogues. And because of me, you will have to stand before rulers and kings to tell about your faith. 10But before the end comes, the good news must be preached to all nations.
11When you are arrested, don't worry about what you will say. You will be given the right words when the time comes. But you will not really be the ones speaking. Your words will come from the Holy Spirit.
12Brothers and sisters will betray each other and have each other put to death. Parents will betray their own children, and children will turn against their parents and have them killed. 13 Everyone will hate you because of me. But if you keep on being faithful right to the end, you will be saved.
The Horrible Thing
(Matthew 24.15-21; Luke 21.20-24)
14 Someday you will see that “Horrible Thing” where it should not be. Everyone who reads this must try to understand! If you are living in Judea at that time, run to the mountains. 15 If you are on the roof of your house, don't go inside to get anything. 16If you are out in the field, don't go back for your coat. 17It will be an awful time for women who are expecting babies or nursing young children. 18Pray that it won't happen in winter. 19 This will be the worst time of suffering since God created the world, and nothing this terrible will ever happen again. 20If the Lord doesn't make the time shorter, no one will be left alive. But because of his chosen and special ones, he will make the time shorter.
21If someone should say, “Here is the Messiah!” or “There he is!” don't believe it. 22False messiahs and false prophets will come and work miracles and signs. They will even try to fool God's chosen ones. 23But be on your guard! That's why I am telling you these things now.
When the Son of Man Appears
(Matthew 24.29-31; Luke 21.25-28)
24 In those days, right after this time of suffering,
“The sun will become dark,
and the moon
will no longer shine.
25 The stars will fall,
and the powers in the sky
will be shaken.”
26 Then the Son of Man will be seen coming in the clouds with great power and glory. 27He will send his angels to gather his chosen ones from all over the earth.
A Lesson from a Fig Tree
(Matthew 24.32-35; Luke 21.29-33)
28Learn a lesson from a fig tree. When its branches sprout and start putting out leaves, you know summer is near. 29So when you see all these things happening, you will know that the time has almost come. 30You can be sure that some of the people of this generation will still be alive when all this happens. 31The sky and the earth will not last forever, but my words will.
No One Knows the Day or Time
(Matthew 24.36-44)
32 No one knows the day or the time. The angels in heaven don't know, and the Son himself doesn't know. Only the Father knows. 33So watch out and be ready! You don't know when the time will come. 34 It is like what happens when a man goes away for a while and places his servants in charge of everything. He tells each of them what to do, and he orders the guard to keep alert. 35So be alert! You don't know when the master of the house will come back. It could be in the evening or at midnight or before dawn or in the morning. 36But if he comes suddenly, don't let him find you asleep. 37I tell everyone just what I have told you. Be alert!
translation_text:
1Yeezu yaa ale jam nyini Wen Yenni po a nyini la, wa ŋaaŋviirɔma po wanyi yaa weeni ayen, <<Sagrɔ, nya tanaŋa ale zuak diiya, nya yenni ale nala diila?>>
2Yeezu yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ni nya yeri kpienni de? Dai cheena ate ba le nak di meena a lɔnsi. Tain yeŋ mɛ la a kan ŋman dua di choa zuwa.>>
3Ba yaa cheŋ ga jueli Olivi Guuku zuk a kala dula jigini a nya Wen Yenni. Piita ale Jɔɔn ale Jeemsi ale Andiru yaa bek Yeezu badek ba nyiini ayen, 4<<Ka dimpo ate wieŋa de meena ale nye? Ka boa ale ku nye ate ku sak ti ayen danni a moata?>>
5Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni kpesi nidek ate waai a kan paasi ni. 6Nuruba yegayega le jam mi yuenni nyiŋ a weeni ayen, <<Ka mi ale Kirisitawa.>> Ba le paasi nuruba yegayega ayen ba va ba. 7Ni dan wom kpaliŋsa wie ate si gela moata alege si gela mɛ a bo niŋniŋa, ni kan a chali yɔgsummoa. Ku a fɛ kama ayen nyaŋa de meena a nye, alege ku kan sak kama ayen tɛŋka kpeglimka a moata kama. 8Tɛŋsa le yiti a ta chaab ate naata a yiti ta chaab. Tɛŋka mɛ le choa m na yegayega ate kɔm a jam tɛŋka meena po. Ase nipok ale dɛ niŋ a dom dii alege a biak la, ku a fɛ kama ayen wieŋa de meena mɛ dɛ niŋ nye alege ate tɛŋka a jam kpeglim.
9<<Ni kpesi nidek dii nyiŋla, nuruba ale jam yik ni ale pagrim a ta ni cheŋ ba tuka diinaŋa kpaŋŋa jigi ate ba bo ni buusa abe ba nak ni. Ni ale a va mi la nyiŋ, ba le ta ni mɛ a cheŋ ga zaani nalima niŋ ate ba mɛ bo ni buusa, ate ni nya suik a mooli Wen wamaŋsaŋa a sak ba. 10Ku a fɛ kama ayen nuru meena a liŋ wom Wen wamaŋsaŋa alege ate tɛŋka a kpeglim. 11Ba dan ta ni a cheŋ ga jo buusa boka dɔkku po, ni kan basi ate ni le ni biisi diila a daani ni. Ni biisi dii meena ate Wen le basi ate ni biisi la dii nyiŋla, ka Wen Chiika le ka sak ni ate ni biisi daa nama dega.
12<<Kula danni a dan paari, suata le yik chaab a te nuruba ate ba ko ba. Koba mɛ ale nye ba bisa dila, ate bisa mɛ a nye ba koba ale ba maba dila. 13Waai meena le kisi ni kama ni ale a va mi la nyiŋ. Alege waai a dan baga a chiib zaani a tu ninammu de meena a ga nueri, Wen le vari wa a basi.
14<<Dai yeŋ ni le nya jabuui ate Wen kisa la ale wa za juijui ale kan magsi ayen wa zaani la. Ni dan nya dila ku a fɛ kama ate nama baai meena ale bo Judia tɛŋka po la a chali ga suk guutaŋa suŋsuŋ.>> Nuru waai le wa karim nya kude la, a ŋmasi miŋ chak. 15<<Waai a dan za wa gboŋ zuk kan ŋman daani wadek ayen wa siŋ a pai jaaboa. 16Waai mɛ ale bo wa kaduk po la, a kan ŋman kuli yeri ayen wa pai wa garuwa. 17Da ŋala po ku le jam tua ka nna yegayega a te nipok puusa ale baai ale ta buluata la. 18Ni a puusi a te Wen ate nya kude a kan jam nye ŋoota wein ya. 19A zaani diipo ate Wen a nye tɛŋka la a ta jam paari jinla, ninammu de le gaam ninam meena ate nurubiik a nam ale diem kala ayen wa nam la kama. 20Alege Naawen a yeeri ninammu daaŋa gela a basi kama, baai ate wa lueri ayen ba jam va wa la nyiŋ. Wa dan kan yeeri ninammu daaŋa gela a basiya, waai kan nyini ninammu po a nyini. 21Da ŋala po waai dan weeni ayen, <Ni nya, Kirisitawa ale nna,> yaase <Ni nya, Kirisitawa ale la,> ni kan wom wa. 22Nuruba gela ale jam yiti a paasi nuruba ayen ba ale Kirisitawa. Ba baai mɛ le jam a weeni ayen ba ka Wen biisiteerɔba. Ba le jam a tom wakperikaliisa nna yegayega a yaali ayen ba dan poom baga ba paasi baai ate Wen a lueri ayen ba va wa la. 23Ni be kpesi nidek, dii nyiŋla m ŋaam weeni wieŋa de meena kama ale ŋa an diem nyeya.
24<<Alege ninammu daaŋa a dan jam taam, Wenbinni ale sobri ate chiika a kan nya. (Azaya 13:10) 25Chiŋmarisaŋa le nyini wenŋmazuk a lo ate ŋan baai meena ale bo wenŋmazuk a ta pagrim la mɛ a choa.
26<<Dila po nuruba ale nya Mi Saalɔbiika ale nyini chiŋmaaŋa po a cheena ale pagrim yega ale zula. 27Mi ale tom maarɔma ate ba jam tɛŋka meena po a tigsi nuru baai ate Wen a lueri ayen ba va wa la.
28<<Ni basi ate kiŋkaŋ a sak ni wari kiri. Ni nyiem a dan nya ale ka boro a pusi vaata, ni seba ayen yoe a moata kama. 29Ni be dan nya wieŋa de ale ŋa piilim a nye, ni yaa be seba ayen m jamka moata kama. 30Wensie ate mi a weeni ni gaŋka de a kan sum taam ka wieŋa de meena a nin nye. 31Wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋzuk meena ale jam taam dai yeŋ po, alege mi wieŋa a kan taam diipo diipo.
32<<Nuru waai a zɛ Mi Saalɔbiika ŋman jamka danni. Mi ale Wen maarɔma mɛ dek a zɛ, alege ka m Kowa nyiini ale seba. 33Ni kpesi nidek abe ni a limisi dii nyiŋla, ni zɛ m jamka daiya. 34Ku a nye se ka nuru ale gomsi ayen wa nyiem a cheŋ satɛŋ niŋniŋ la. Wa yaa te wa tomteerɔma meena tuima ale weeni waai ale a nya yenni zuk la ayen wa a limisi.
35<<Ba nyɔnɔwa a baga a jam junɔi geŋsa yaase goota suŋsuŋ yaase kpadaasa kumsa po yaase wenbinni ale a pusi diipo la kama. Ba waai zɛ wa le cheena diipo la. Suik kula po mɛ, nama waai a kan seba mi ŋman jamka danni. Dila nyiŋla, ni kpesi nidek abe 36ni kan basi ate ni nyɔnɔwa a jam diiri ni ale ni dua a goa. 37M kan weeni ka nama nyiini, mi a weeni ka waai meena. Ni kpesi nidek abe ni a limisi.>>

english_text:
A Plot To Kill Jesus
(Matthew 26.1-5; Luke 22.1,2; John 11.45-53)
1 It was now two days before Passover and the Festival of Thin Bread. The chief priests and the teachers of the Law of Moses were planning how they could sneak around and have Jesus arrested and put to death. 2They were saying, “We must not do it during the festival, because the people will riot.”
At Bethany
(Matthew 26.6-13; John 12.1-8)
3 Jesus was eating in Bethany at the home of Simon, who once had leprosy, when a woman came in with a very expensive bottle of sweet-smelling perfume. After breaking it open, she poured the perfume on Jesus' head. 4This made some of the guests angry, and they complained, “Why such a waste? 5We could have sold this perfume for more than 300 silver coins and given the money to the poor!” So they started saying cruel things to the woman.
6But Jesus said:
Leave her alone! Why are you bothering her? She has done a beautiful thing for me. 7 You will always have the poor with you. And whenever you want to, you can give to them. But you won't always have me here with you. 8She has done all she could by pouring perfume on my body to prepare it for burial. 9You may be sure that wherever the good news is told all over the world, people will remember what she has done. And they will tell others.
Judas and the Chief Priests
(Matthew 26.14-16; Luke 22.3-6)
10Judas Iscariot was one of the twelve disciples. He went to the chief priests and offered to help them arrest Jesus. 11They were glad to hear this, and they promised to pay him. So Judas started looking for a good chance to betray Jesus.
Jesus Eats with His Disciples
(Matthew 26.17-25; Luke 22.7-14,21-23; John 13.21-30)
12It was the first day of the Festival of Thin Bread, and the Passover lambs were being killed. Jesus' disciples asked him, “Where do you want us to prepare the Passover meal?”
13Jesus said to two of the disciples, “Go into the city, where you will meet a man carrying a jar of water. Follow him, 14and when he goes into a house, say to the owner, ‘Our teacher wants to know if you have a room where he can eat the Passover meal with his disciples.’ 15The owner will take you upstairs and show you a large room furnished and ready for you to use. Prepare the meal there.”
16The two disciples went into the city and found everything just as Jesus had told them. So they prepared the Passover meal.
17-18 While Jesus and the twelve disciples were eating together that evening, he said, “The one who will betray me is now eating with me.”
19This made the disciples sad, and one after another they said to Jesus, “You surely don't mean me!”
20He answered, “It is one of you twelve men who is eating from this dish with me. 21The Son of Man will die, just as the Scriptures say. But it is going to be terrible for the one who betrays me. That man would be better off if he had never been born.”
The Lord's Supper
(Matthew 26.26-30; Luke 22.14-23; 1 Corinthians 11.23-25)
22During the meal Jesus took some bread in his hands. He blessed the bread and broke it. Then he gave it to his disciples and said, “Take this. It is my body.”
23Jesus picked up a cup of wine and gave thanks to God. He gave it to his disciples, and they all drank some. 24 Then he said, “This is my blood, which is poured out for many people, and with it God makes his agreement. 25From now on I will not drink any wine, until I drink new wine in God's kingdom.” 26Then they sang a hymn and went out to the Mount of Olives.
Peter's Promise
(Matthew 26.31-35; Luke 22.31-34; John 13.36-38)
27 Jesus said to his disciples, “All of you will reject me, as the Scriptures say,
‘I will strike down
the shepherd,
and the sheep
will be scattered.’
28 But after I am raised to life, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.”
29Peter spoke up, “Even if all the others reject you, I never will!”
30Jesus replied, “This very night before a rooster crows twice, you will say three times that you don't know me.”
31But Peter was so sure of himself that he said, “Even if I have to die with you, I will never say I don't know you!”
All the others said the same thing.
Jesus Prays
(Matthew 26.36-46; Luke 22.39-46)
32Jesus went with his disciples to a place called Gethsemane, and he told them, “Sit here while I pray.”
33Jesus took along Peter, James, and John. He was sad and troubled and 34told them, “I am so sad that I feel as if I am dying. Stay here and keep awake with me.”
35-36Jesus walked on a little way. Then he knelt down on the ground and prayed, “Father, if it is possible, don't let this happen to me! Father, you can do anything. Don't make me suffer by drinking from this cup. But do what you want, and not what I want.”
37When Jesus came back and found the disciples sleeping, he said to Simon Peter, “Are you asleep? Can't you stay awake for just one hour? 38Stay awake and pray that you won't be tested. You want to do what is right, but you are weak.”
39Jesus went back and prayed the same prayer. 40But when he returned to the disciples, he found them sleeping again. They simply could not keep their eyes open, and they did not know what to say.
41When Jesus returned to the disciples the third time, he said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Enough of this! The time has come for the Son of Man to be handed over to sinners. 42Get up! Let's go. The one who will betray me is already here.”
Jesus Is Arrested
(Matthew 26.47-56; Luke 22.47-53; John 18.3-12)
43Jesus was still speaking, when Judas the betrayer came up. He was one of the twelve disciples, and a mob of men armed with swords and clubs were with him. They had been sent by the chief priests, the nation's leaders, and the teachers of the Law of Moses. 44Judas had told them ahead of time, “Arrest the man I greet with a kiss. Tie him up tight and lead him away.”
45Judas walked right up to Jesus and said, “Teacher!” Then Judas kissed him, 46and the men grabbed Jesus and arrested him.
47Someone standing there pulled out a sword. He struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his ear.
48Jesus said to the mob, “Why do you come with swords and clubs to arrest me like a criminal? 49 Day after day I was with you and taught in the temple, and you didn't arrest me. But what the Scriptures say must come true.”
50All of Jesus' disciples ran off and left him. 51One of them was a young man who was wearing only a linen cloth. And when the men grabbed him, 52he left the cloth behind and ran away naked.
Jesus Is Questioned by the Council
(Matthew 26.57-68; Luke 22.54,55,63-71; John 18.13,14,19-24)
53Jesus was led off to the high priest. Then the chief priests, the nation's leaders, and the teachers of the Law of Moses all met together. 54Peter had followed at a distance, and when he reached the courtyard of the high priest's house, he sat down with the guards to warm himself beside a fire.
55The chief priests and the whole council tried to find someone to accuse Jesus of a crime, so they could put him to death. But they could not find anyone to accuse him. 56Many people did tell lies against Jesus, but they did not agree on what they said. 57Finally, some men stood up and lied about him. They said, 58 “We heard him say he would tear down this temple that we built. He also claimed that in three days he would build another one without any help.” 59But even then they did not agree on what they said.
60The high priest stood up in the council and asked Jesus, “Why don't you say something in your own defense? Don't you hear the charges they are making against you?” 61But Jesus kept quiet and did not say a word. The high priest asked him another question, “Are you the Messiah, the Son of the glorious God?”
62 “Yes, I am!” Jesus answered.
“Soon you will see
the Son of Man
sitting at the right side
of God All-Powerful,
and coming with the clouds
of heaven.”
63At once the high priest ripped his robe apart and shouted, “Why do we need more witnesses? 64 You heard him claim to be God! What is your decision?” They all agreed he should be put to death.
65Some of the people started spitting on Jesus. They blindfolded him, hit him with their fists, and said, “Tell us who hit you!” Then the guards took charge of Jesus and beat him.
Peter Says He Doesn't Know Jesus
(Matthew 26.69-75; Luke 22.56-62; John 18.15-18,25-27)
66While Peter was still in the courtyard, a servant girl of the high priest came up 67and saw Peter warming himself by the fire. She stared at him and said, “You were with Jesus from Nazareth!”
68Peter replied, “That isn't true! I don't know what you're talking about. I don't have any idea what you mean.” He went out to the gate, and a rooster crowed.
69The servant girl saw Peter again and said to the people standing there, “This man is one of them!”
70“No, I'm not!” Peter replied.
A little while later some of the people said to Peter, “You certainly are one of them. You're a Galilean!”
71This time Peter began to curse and swear, “I don't even know the man you're talking about!”
72At once the rooster crowed a second time. Then Peter remembered that Jesus had told him, “Before a rooster crows twice, you will say three times that you don't know me.” So Peter started crying.
translation_text:
1Ku jam tali ka daa ŋaye ate Gaambasika Tigini ale Boroborok Kuui Ale Kan Ta Dabinta La Tigini a paari, ate kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa ale Sinsak sagrɔma a gisi suik ayen ba mak yik Yeezu a ko. 2Ba yaa weeni ayen, <<Ti kan yik wa tigini po, kan daa di nuruma le nye kpaliŋ kpieŋ.>>
3Yeezu yaa cheŋ Betani tɛŋka a ga jo Simon, waai ate gama tuem a jam yik wa la yenni po. Wa yaa jam kala a dɛ ŋandiinta ate nipok wanyi a ta kpaam jam. Kpaamu nyummu a jam masa kama ate bu diak a pagra. Nipowa yaa pai kpaamu a kpiiri basi Yeezu zuk.
4Nuru baai ale jam kala dula jigini la gela yaa nya dii ate nipowa a nye la, ate ba sue yaa puuri ale wa. Ba yaa poli ba zuima po ayen, <<Ka boa ate nipowa de a pai kpaamu a yik kaasi dila? 5Wa dan pai bu a da kama nna, wa ti le nya ligra ka nna yegayega a te ŋanjaksaŋa. Kula a gaam dii ate wa nye la kama.>> Ba yaa jam toariŋ wa.
6Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni basi wa. Ka boa ate ni a daani wa? Wa nye ka wamaŋ a te mu. 7Niwomma a bo ale ni kama daa meena ate ni daa a yaali ni baga a maari ba. Alege mi a kan kasim bo ale ni. 8Wa nye ka wa ale baga a nye dii meena la a te mu. Wa kpiiri kpa masika de mi nyiŋka kama a gomsi ka a magsi guka. 9Wensie ate mi a weeni ni, juijui meena ate nuruba a sak Wen wamaŋsaŋa la, ba le weeni nipowa de ale nye dii a te mi la. Ba le kasim a teeri wa yuei diipo meena wuu.>>
10Dula jigini Yeezu ŋaaŋviirɔma pi ale bayewa po wanyi, Judas Iskariot yaa cheŋ kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa jigi a ga weeni ba ayen wa baga a maari ba kama ate ba a yik Yeezu. 11Ba ale ga wom dila la, ba sue yaa peenti nna yegayega, ate ba weeni wa ayen wa dan baga a maari ba, ba le te wa ligra. Judas yaa basi dula jigini ale a gisi suik kuui wa le wa va ate ba baga a yik Yeezu la.
12Yeezu ŋaaŋviirɔma yaa jam wa jigi tigi dii ate ba a ŋɔbi boroborok kuui ale kan ta dabinta la piilimka danni. Da dila mɛ ale ba a ko Gaambasika Tigini piisaŋa. Ba yaa bek Yeezu ayen, <<Ka be ate fi a yaali ayen ti ga gomsi Gaambasika Tigini ŋandiintaŋa ate ti dɛ?>>
13Wa yaa weeni wa ŋaaŋviirɔma po baye ayen, <<Ni cheŋ a ga jo tɛŋka po. Dula jigini ni le nya nidoa a ji nyiam ale samɔniŋ. 14Ni va wa a ga jo yeri diipo ate wa a jo la. Ni dan ga jo ni weeni yenni nyɔnɔwa ayen, <Ti Sagrɔwa ale tom ti ayen ti jam bek fu dɔk kuui po ate wa ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ayen ba jam dɛ Gaambasika Tigini ŋandiintaŋa la.> 15Wa le dak ŋmazuk dɔk kpioŋ kunyi a ta ŋanta meena ku po a magsi. Ni gomsi a magsi ti dula jigini.>>
16Ba yaa cheŋ ga jo tɛŋka po a nya dii meena ate Yeezu a poom weeni ba la, ate ba yaa gomsi ba Gaambasika Tigini ŋandiintaŋa.
17Junɔi ale jam paari la, Yeezu ale wa ŋaaŋviirɔma pi ale bayewa yaa jam kala a dɛ. 18Ba ale boro a dɛ la, Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Wensie ate mi a weeni ni meena ale kala a dɛ ale mu la, ni po wanyi le wa ta mu a ga bobri sak m dachaasaŋa.>>
19Wa ŋaaŋviirɔma sui yaa kaasi ate ba bek wa wanyi wanyi ayen, <<Ka mi? Ka mi?>>
20Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ku le chim ka nama pi ale bayewa po wanyi, waai ale a ŋmari boroboroku a suiik jentaŋa ale mu la, ale wa ta mu a ga bobri sak. 21Mi Saalɔbiika ale kpi ase ka ba ale ŋmarisi dii Wen gbaŋka po la. Alege ku le pagra kama a te waai dek ale wa ta mu a ga bobri sak la. Ku zunchoŋ kama ale ba nin poom kan biak wa.>>
22Ba ale boro a dɛ ŋandiintaŋa la, Yeezu yaa pai boroborok a puusi a te Wen a nye wa jiam, alege ŋmari ku a chari wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ale weeni ba ayen, <<Ni ŋoa ŋɔbi, mi nyiŋka ale nna.>>
23Wa yaa ŋman pai beerik ale daam a puusi a te Wen jiam, alege pai te ba ate ba nyu. 24Wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ka mi nɔiyeŋ paalika ziimu ale nna. Buui ale a nyini nuruba yega nyiŋla. 25Wensie ate mi a weeni ni, m kan ŋman nyu daamu de nin ka dai dii danni ate m ŋman a nyu da paalimu Wen naamu po la.>>
26Ba yaa yi yiili alege a nyini ga jueli Olivi Guuku zuk.
27Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni meena ale chali abe ni ge mu dii nyiŋla ba ŋmarisi Wen gbaŋka po kama ayen, <Naawen le jam ko naapeerika, ate piisaŋa yaa chali waaŋ chaab.> (Zakaria 13:7) 28Alege m dan yiti kum po, m le dɛ ni niŋ a cheŋ Galili tɛŋka.>>
29Piita yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Mbala meena a dan poom basi fu, mi kan maa basi fu diipo diipo.>> 30Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Basi ate m weeni a sak fu ayen, yokku de fi le pagsi mu ku nɔi buta ayen fi zɛ mu, alege ate vari kpadiaka a kum a nye buye.>>
31Piita yaa pii nyiŋ a ŋman weeni wa ayen, <<Mi kan weeni diipo diipo ayen m zɛ fu. Mi dan poom ayen m kpi ale fu, mi kan weeni dila.>> Wa ŋaaŋviirɔ mbala meena mɛ yaa weeni dila dekdega.
32Ba yaa jam paari Getsemani, ate Yeezu yaa weeni wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ayen, <<Ni kali dela ate m ga puusi a te Wen abe m jam.>> 33Wa ale a cheŋ la, wa yaa basi ate Piita ale Jeemsi ale Jɔɔn a va wa. Wa sui yaa jam kaasi nna yegayega, ate 34wa weeni ba ayen, <<M sui ale kaasi nna yegayega, ate ku a nye nna ase mi a yaali ayen m kpi kama la. Ni be limisi dela ate m jam, abe ni kpesi a nya.>>
35Wa ale ga cheŋ magadek la, wa yaa kpi duna tɛŋ a puusi a te Wen ayen dan ka dii wa yeeri ninam buui ate wa za wa nam la wa jigi a basi. 36Wa puusi a te Wen kama ayen, <<M Koa, fi baga a nye wari meena kama. Yeeri ninam beerika de m jigi a basi. Alege, nye fidek ale a yaali diila, daa mi ale a yaali diila.>>
37Wa yaa pilim jam a paari wa ŋaaŋviirɔma batawa ale ba dua a goa. Wa yaa weeni Piita ayen, <<Simon, ni a goa kama? Nama an baga nya ate ku a beni fiik fiik ale kan goa? 38Ni a kpesi abe ni a puusi a te ni kan jo nyenyaka po, chiika a yaali kama alege nyiŋka a wobsa.>>
39Wa yaa ŋman ga puusi a te Wen a weeni wa ale poom a weeni diila. 40Wa yaa ŋman jam wa ŋaaŋviirɔma jigi ale ba ŋman dua a goa, dii nyiŋla, goom ale jam ta ba nna yegayega, ate ba zɛ ba ale ba weeni wa diila.
41Wa ale ŋman jam ku nɔi butawa la, wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni diem a goa kama? Ku magsi ya. Di danni a paari ya. Ba le bobri Mi Saalɔbiika a nyo nuru baata nisima po. 42Ni yiti ate ti cheŋ. Nuru waai ale ta mu a ga bobri sak la ale la a cheena.>>
43Yeezu ale diem boro a biisi la, wa ŋaaŋviirɔma pi ale bayewa po wanyiwa Judas, yaa jam wa jigi ale nuru boari. Kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa ale Sinsak sagrɔma ale tɛŋka kpaŋŋa ale tom ba. Ba jam ta ka gebi kpieŋsa ale dua a jam ayen ba yik wa.
44Bumbobrɔwa a poom weeni ba kama ayen, <<Ti dan ga paari ba, nuru waai ate mi a puusi ale a gbaari wa la, ka waai ate ni a yaali la ale la. Ni yik wa a ta cheŋ abe ni kan te wa bɛ.>> 45Ba ale ga paari Yeezu la, Judas yaa deri ga wa jigi a wi wa ayen, <<M Sagrɔ,>> a yaa alege a puusi ale gbaari wa. 46Judas ale nye dila la, nuruma yaa deri yik Yeezu ale pagrim. 47Yeezu ŋaaŋviirɔma po wanyi yaa deri yeeri wa gebi kpieŋ a che kaabteerɔ kpioŋku tomteerɔwa turi a lɔnsi tɛŋ.
48Yeezu yaa bek nuru boanni ayen, <<Mi ka zue ate ni ta gebi kpieŋsa ale dua a jam ayen ni yik mu? 49Daa meena mi kasim bo ale ni kama Wen Yenni po a sak nuruba, alege ni an yik mu. Alege ku a fɛ kama ayen ba ale ŋmarisi Wen gbaŋka po diila, a jam chim wensie.>> 50Dula jigini Yeezu ŋaaŋviirɔma meena yaa chali alege wa.
51Nidoa wanyi ale jam maa va Yeezu a yulum gatta peelik. Ba jam a yaali ayen ba yik wa kama, 52ate wa foli gattiaka a basi te ba alege chali ale chaboala.
53Ba yaa ta Yeezu a cheŋ kaabteerɔ kpioŋku yenni. Kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa ale tɛŋka kpaŋŋa ale Sinsak sagrɔma yaa jam tigsi chaab. 54Piita yaa mag va ba ŋaaŋ a ga jo kaabteerɔ kpioŋku yenni dabiaka po a ga kala ale limisidɔma a ŋuuŋ bolim.
55Kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa ale nisɔmma meena yaa jam bek nuruba ayen ba wom Yeezu wakaasuŋ ba jigi ate ba nya suik a ko wa. Alege ba an baga a nya wari ya. 56Nuruba yegayega a jam velim wie a te wa kama alege ba noaŋa jam daa bunyi.
57Ba gela a nyini biisi venta wie ayen, 58<<Tama wom ale wa a weeni ayen wa baga a kaasi Wen Yenni dii ate nuruba a sɛ la kama, abe wa ŋman sɛ di daa ŋata po. Wa be kan pai nuruba ate ba sɛ di.>> 59Alege ba mɛ wieŋa a jam daa nɔiyeŋ wie.
60Kaabteerɔ kpioŋku yaa yiti zaani ba meena niŋ a bek Yeezu ayen, <<Fi ka wari a tulisi wieŋa de meena ate ba a biisi la po?>> 61Yeezu yaa sina. Wa ŋman bek wa ayen, <<Ka fi ale Kirisitawa Niauŋ Nyɔnɔwa Nidoabinni?>>
62Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Mm, mi ale la. Dai yeŋ ni le nya Mi Saalɔbiika ale m kali Wen Kpienni juga geŋ a nyini chiŋmaaŋa po a cheena.>>
63Kaabteerɔ kpioŋku yaa yik wadek garukku a dari cheeri ale weeni ayen, <<Ti an ŋmaa yaali seerɔba. 64Ni meena a wom wa ale pai wadek a magsi chaab ale Wen la kama. Nama a poli ka sɛ? Wa lɔ yaa wa an lɔ ya?>> Ba meena a yaa bo mini wa ayen ku a magsi kama ayen wa kpi. 65Nuruma gela yaa chesi tintueta a basi wa nyiŋ ale pai garuk a bobi lik wa ninaŋa a nak wa ale a bek ayen, <<Fi seba waai dek ale nak fu la?>> Nuru baai mɛ ale ga yik Yeezu la yaa fɔbi wa a gum du.
66Piita ale diem jam bo yenni dabiaka po la, kaabteerɔ kpioŋku dɔkliema wanyi a yaa nya wa. 67Wa ale nya Piita ale wa kala a ŋuuŋ bolimu la, wa yaa nya wa ziin a weeni wa ayen, <<Fi mɛ ka Yeezu Nazaret denɔwa ŋaaŋviirɔma po wanyi.>>
68Piita yaa pagsi ayen, <<Mi zɛ fi ale a weeni diila.>> Wa yaa yiti a cheŋ ga za pɔsuku nɔi.
69Nipokbinni ale ŋman nya wa ale wa za dula jigini la wa yaa weeni baai ale za dula la ayen, <<Nuruwa de ka Yeezu ŋaaŋviirɔma po wanyi.>> 70Piita yaa ŋman pagsi ayen wa daa Yeezu ŋaaŋviirɔma po wanyi. Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ, nuru baai ale jam za moata wa la yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Fi ka ba po wanyi, dii nyiŋla fi mɛ nyini ka Galili tɛŋka.>>
71Piita yaa pɛ ayen wa zɛ nuru waai ate ba a weeni wa wie la.
72Vari kpadiaka yaa deri kum a nye buye ate Piita teeri dii ate Yeezu a poom weeni wa ayen, wa le pagsi ku nɔi buta ayen wa zɛ wa alege ate vari kpadiaka a kum a nye buye la. Piita sui yaa kaasi ate wa kum.

english_text:
Pilate Questions Jesus
(Matthew 27.1,2,11-14; Luke 23.1-5; John 18.28-38)
1Early the next morning the chief priests, the nation's leaders, and the teachers of the Law of Moses met together with the whole Jewish council. They tied up Jesus and led him off to Pilate.
2He asked Jesus, “Are you the king of the Jews?”
“Those are your words,” Jesus answered.
3The chief priests brought many charges against Jesus. 4Then Pilate questioned him again, “Don't you have anything to say? Don't you hear what crimes they say you have done?” 5But Jesus did not answer, and Pilate was amazed.
The Death Sentence
(Matthew 27.15-26; Luke 23.13-25; John 18.39—19.16)
6During Passover, Pilate always freed one prisoner chosen by the people. 7And at that time there was a prisoner named Barabbas. He and some others had been arrested for murder during a riot. 8The crowd now came and asked Pilate to set a prisoner free, just as he usually did.
9Pilate asked them, “Do you want me to free the king of the Jews?” 10Pilate knew that the chief priests had brought Jesus to him because they were jealous.
11But the chief priests told the crowd to ask Pilate to free Barabbas.
12Then Pilate asked the crowd, “What do you want me to do with this man you say is the king of the Jews?”
13They yelled, “Nail him to a cross!”
14Pilate asked, “But what crime has he done?”
“Nail him to a cross!” they yelled even louder.
15Pilate wanted to please the crowd, so he set Barabbas free. Then he ordered his soldiers to beat Jesus with a whip and nail him to a cross.
Soldiers Make Fun of Jesus
(Matthew 27.27-30; John 19.2,3)
16The soldiers led Jesus inside the courtyard of the fortress and called together the rest of the troops. 17They put a purple robe on him, and on his head they placed a crown they had made out of thorn branches. 18They made fun of Jesus and shouted, “Hey, you king of the Jews!” 19Then they beat him on the head with a stick. They spit on him and knelt down and pretended to worship him.
20When the soldiers had finished making fun of Jesus, they took off the purple robe. They put his own clothes back on him and led him off to be nailed to a cross. 21 Simon from Cyrene happened to be coming in from a farm, and they forced him to carry Jesus' cross. Simon was the father of Alexander and Rufus.
Jesus Is Nailed to a Cross
(Matthew 27.31-44; Luke 23.27-43; John 19.17-27)
22The soldiers took Jesus to Golgotha, which means “Place of a Skull.” 23There they gave him some wine mixed with a drug to ease the pain, but he refused to drink it.
24 They nailed Jesus to a cross and gambled to see who would get his clothes. 25It was about nine o'clock in the morning when they nailed him to the cross. 26On it was a sign that told why he was nailed there. It read, “This is the King of the Jews.” 27-28 The soldiers also nailed two criminals on crosses, one to the right of Jesus and the other to his left.
29 People who passed by said terrible things about Jesus. They shook their heads and shouted, “Ha! So you're the one who claimed you could tear down the temple and build it again in three days. 30Save yourself and come down from the cross!”
31The chief priests and the teachers of the Law of Moses also made fun of Jesus. They said to each other, “He saved others, but he can't save himself. 32If he is the Messiah, the king of Israel, let him come down from the cross! Then we will see and believe.” The two criminals also said cruel things to Jesus.
The Death of Jesus
(Matthew 27.45-56; Luke 23.44-49; John 19.28-30)
33About noon the sky turned dark and stayed that way until around three o'clock. 34 Then about that time Jesus shouted, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which means, “My God, my God, why have you deserted me?”
35Some of the people standing there heard Jesus and said, “He is calling for Elijah.” 36 One of them ran and grabbed a sponge. After he had soaked it in wine, he put it on a stick and held it up to Jesus. He said, “Let's wait and see if Elijah will come and take him down!” 37Jesus shouted and then died.
38 At once the curtain in the temple tore in two from top to bottom.
39A Roman army officer was standing in front of Jesus. When the officer saw how Jesus died, he said, “This man really was the Son of God!”
40-41 Some women were looking on from a distance. They and many others had come with Jesus to Jerusalem. But even before this they had been his followers and had helped him while he was in Galilee. Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of the younger James and of Joseph were two of these women. Salome was also one of them.
Jesus Is Buried
(Matthew 27.57-61; Luke 23.50-56; John 19.38-42)
42It was now the evening before the Sabbath, and the Jewish people were getting ready for that sacred day. 43A man named Joseph from Arimathea was brave enough to ask Pilate for the body of Jesus. Joseph was a highly respected member of the Jewish council, and he was also waiting for God's kingdom to come.
44Pilate was surprised to hear that Jesus was already dead, and he called in the army officer to find out if Jesus had been dead very long. 45After the officer told him, Pilate let Joseph have Jesus' body.
46Joseph bought a linen cloth and took the body down from the cross. He had it wrapped in the cloth, and he put it in a tomb that had been cut into solid rock. Then he rolled a big stone against the entrance to the tomb.
47Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joseph were watching and saw where the body was placed.
translation_text:
1Vari ale veenti la, saluik yokyokwa kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa ale tɛŋka nisɔmma ale Sinsak sagrɔma ale nisɔmma meena yaa ŋman kpabi tu chaab a zɔk ba le ba nye Yeezu diila. Ba yaa bobi wa nisimaŋa a ta wa cheŋ tɛŋka Gominawa Paalɔt jigi.
2Ba ale ga paari la, Paalɔt yaa bek Yeezu ayen, <<Ka fi ale Juuma naawa la?>> Yeezu yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Ka fidek ale weeni dila.>>
3Kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa jam chiini ka wie nna yegayega ayen Yeezu a nye kaasi. 4Dila nyiŋ Paalɔt yaa ŋman bek wa ayen, <<Fi kan wom ba ale a chiini wieŋa nna yegayega a te fu la? Fi ka wari a tulisi ba?>> 5Alege Yeezu a jam sina. Wa an jam weeni wari ya. Ku yaa cha Paalɔt.
6Bena meena ba Gaambasika Tigini a nyiem dan paari, Gominawa Paalɔt a nyiem lak nuru waai ate tɛŋka demma a yaali ayen wa lak ate wa nyini likka dɔkku po a nyini la a basi kama. 7Nuru wanyi ale jam boro ate ba a wi ayen Barabasi ate ba jam maa yik wa a lik dii nyiŋla, wa jam maa nye ka nɔiyeŋ ale wa tɛŋka demma ate ba nye kpaliŋ ale baai ale a nya ba tɛŋka zuk la. Ba ale jam boro a nye kpaliŋka la, ba jam ko ka nuruba gela. 8Nuruba yegayega yaa tigsi chaab a jam Paalɔt jigi a saalim wa ayen wa nye dii ate wa nyiem poom a nye tigini danni la a te ba.
9Wa yaa bek ba ayen, <<Nama a yaali ayen m basi ka Juuma naawa?>> 10Paalɔt a jam seba ayen ka kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa nyunni nyiŋ ale soa ate ba yik Yeezu a ta jam wa jigi. 11Kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa yaa weeni nuru boanni ayen ba a saalim ayen wa lak Barabasi.
12Paalɔt yaa bek ba ayen, <<Nuru waai ate nama wi ayen Juuma naab la, m nye wa se?>> 13Ba meena yaa kaari nna yegayega ayen, <<Ko wa.>>
14Paalɔt yaa bek ba ayen, <<Ka boan jaab wabiok ate wa tom?>> Ba yaa kaari a gaam dila a weeni ayen, <<Ko wa.>>
15Paalɔt a jam a yaali kama ayen wa nye ate nuru boanni suipeentik. Wa yaa lak Barabasi a basi, alege basi ate ba miiri Yeezu ale kpaasa alege pai wa a te, ayen ba ta wa ga ko.
16Paalɔt tugurik tɔŋdɔma yaa yik Yeezu a ta jo ba Gominawa yenni dabiaka po a wi ba tugurik tɔŋdɔ chaama ate ba jam. 17Ba yaa pai garuk mɔnuŋ a jo wa ale pai munsa a yɔk zutɔk a vuk wa zukku, 18a yaa puusi wa a weeni ayen, <<Juuma naawa kasim boro taam wuu.>> 19Ba yaa pai diok, a nak wa zukku ale chesi tintueta a basi wa nyiŋ ale kpi duna wa niŋ a potim a nye nna ase ba a te wa ka zula la. 20Ba ale nye wa la a ga nueri la, ba yaa yeeri garuk mɔnuŋku ale pai wadek gattaŋa a jo wa a ta wa nyini cheŋ ayen ba ko.
21Ba ale jam bo suiku po a cheŋ la, ba yaa zik Simon ale wa cheena tɛŋka po ate tugurik tɔŋdɔma a fɛ wa ate wa tuesi Yeezu jabarimu ji. Simon jam ka Sairini tɛŋka denɔ. Wa jam ka Alezanda ale Arufusi ko. 22Ba yaa ta Yeezu a ga paari juijui ate ba a wi ayen Golgota la. Ku kiri ale <<Zukoluku Jigini.>> 23Ba yaa pai tiim a nyo daam po ayen Yeezu nyu, alege wa an jam nyuya. 24Ate ba yaa kpi wa jabarimu zuk ale labi wa gattaŋa a chari chaab. Ba jam a nak ka gbaŋ ayen ba baga a miŋ dii ale magsi ayen waai meena a pai la.
25Ku jam ka baŋ neok saluik ate ba jam ko wa. 26Ba yaa pai tapagi a ŋmarisi di nyiŋ ayen, <<Ka Juuma Naawa Ale Nna,>> a pai di kpi jabarimu nyiŋ. 27Ba jam maa kpi ka zueba baye ŋanbarinta nyiŋ a gum Yeezu po, ate ba wanyi a bo wa juga, nwala mɛ a bo wa gala. 28Ate ba le jam ŋmarisi dii Wen gbaŋka po ayen, <<Ba nye wa ase ka zue la yaa jam chim wensie.>> 29Nuru baai ale jam va dula a taam la yaa zak zuk nya wa a mati ba noa ale a lɛ wa ayen, <<Mm, daa fi ale weeni ayen fi le kaasi Wen Yenni abe fi ŋman sɛ di a nueri daa ŋata po la? 30Nyini jabarimu zuk a siŋ a vari fidek a basi ate ti nya.>>
31Kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa ale Sinsak sagrɔma mɛ a jam a la wa ale a weeni chaab ayen, <<Wa jam baga a vari nuruba a basi kama, alege wa an baga a vari wadek a basi. 32Basi ate Kirisitawa de, Izirali Naawa de, a nyini jabarimu zuk a siŋ yɔgyɔgla de, ate tama nya a siak te wa.>> Zuema bayewa baai ate ba jam kpi ba a gum Yeezu po la, mɛ a lɛ wa.
33Ku ale jam paari kantueŋ baŋ pi ale buye la, tɛŋka meena yaa jam nye legi nna kpitɔ a ta ga paari kantueŋ baŋ buta. 34Baŋ butawa po, Yeezu yaa kaari ate ku jueli a weeni ale wadek tɛŋka biika ayen, <<Eloi, Eloi, Lama Sabagtani.>> Ku kiri ale, <<Mi Wen yaa, mi Wen yaa, ka boa ate fi zɛri mu?>> (Yiila 22:1)
35Nuru baai ale jam za dula jigini la gela a wom dii ate wa weeni la kama. Ba yaa weeni ayen, <<Wa a wi ka Elaja.>>
36Ba po wanyi yaa chali cheŋ ga pai sosok a lusi damiisiŋ po a pai yik diok woŋ nyiŋ a zak ta jueli Yeezu nɔi. Wa ale diem zak diokku ta la wa yaa cheem weeni baai ale jam za la ayen, <<Ni basi ate ti limisi a nya ase Elaja ale jam yik wa ta nyini jabarimu zuk a siŋ tɛŋ ya.>>
