Ba be le ko biisiteerɔma ale tuimtomdɔma de ba gela abe ba basi ate ba gela a nya ninam. 50Biisiteerɔma ziimu ale nyini tɛŋka nyubini piilimka la nyiŋ, gaŋka de ale nya waalika 51a ta nyini Abel a ga paari Zakaria ate ba jam ko Wen yenni kuŋkuŋku ale weleŋsaŋa jigini suŋsuŋ la. Mi diem a weeni kama ayen gaŋka de ale nya waalika.> 52Ku ale bie a te nama Sinsak sagrɔma, ni ale pai yam saafiika, nama dek an jo ya, ale kasi baai ale a yaa ba jo la.
53Yeezu ale ga basi dula jigini ale cheŋ la, Sinsak sagrɔma ale Farisiima a jam a toariŋ wa kama nalimnyiini a bek wa beka nna yegayega 54a pii nyiŋ a nye ayen wa biisi kaasi ate ba nya suik a bo wa buusa.

english_text:
Warnings
1 As thousands of people crowded around Jesus and were stepping on each other, he told his disciples:
Be sure to guard against the dishonest teaching of the Pharisees! It is their way of fooling people. 2 Everything that is hidden will be found out, and every secret will be known. 3Whatever you say in the dark will be heard when it is day. Whatever you whisper in a closed room will be shouted from the housetops.
The One To Fear
(Matthew 10.28-31)
4 My friends, don't be afraid of people. They can kill you, but after that, there is nothing else they can do. 5God is the one you must fear. Not only can he take your life, but he can throw you into hell. God is certainly the one you should fear!
6Five sparrows are sold for only a few cents, but God doesn't forget a single one of them. 7Even the hairs on your head are counted. So don't be afraid! You are worth much more than many sparrows.
Telling Others about Christ
(Matthew 10.32,33; 12.32; 10.19,20)
8If you tell others that you belong to me, the Son of Man will tell God's angels that you are my followers. 9But if you reject me, you will be rejected in front of them. 10 If you speak against the Son of Man, you can be forgiven, but if you speak against the Holy Spirit, you cannot be forgiven.
11 When you are brought to trial in the synagogues or before rulers or officials, don't worry about how you will defend yourselves or what you will say. 12At that time the Holy Spirit will tell you what to say.
A Rich Fool
13A man in a crowd said to Jesus, “Teacher, tell my brother to give me my share of what our father left us when he died.”
14Jesus answered, “Who gave me the right to settle arguments between you and your brother?”
15Then he said to the crowd, “Don't be greedy! Owning a lot of things won't make your life safe.”
16So Jesus told them this story:
A rich man's farm produced a big crop, 17and he said to himself, “What can I do? I don't have a place large enough to store everything.”
18Later, he said, “Now I know what I'll do. I'll tear down my barns and build bigger ones, where I can store all my grain and other goods. 19 Then I'll say to myself, ‘You have stored up enough good things to last for years to come. Live it up! Eat, drink, and enjoy yourself.’ ”
20But God said to him, “You fool! Tonight you will die. Then who will get what you have stored up?”
21“This is what happens to people who store up everything for themselves, but are poor in the sight of God.”
Worry
(Matthew 6.25-34)
22Jesus said to his disciples:
I tell you not to worry about your life! Don't worry about having something to eat or wear. 23Life is more than food or clothing. 24Look at the crows! They don't plant or harvest, and they don't have storehouses or barns. But God takes care of them. You are much more important than any birds. 25Can worry make you live longer? 26If you don't have power over small things, why worry about everything else?
27 Look how the wild flowers grow! They don't work hard to make their clothes. But I tell you Solomon with all his wealth wasn't as well clothed as one of these flowers. 28God gives such beauty to everything that grows in the fields, even though it is here today and thrown into a fire tomorrow. Won't he do even more for you? You have such little faith!
29Don't keep worrying about having something to eat or drink. 30Only people who don't know God are always worrying about such things. Your Father knows what you need. 31But put God's work first, and these things will be yours as well.
Treasures in Heaven
(Matthew 6.19-21)
32My little group of disciples, don't be afraid! Your Father wants to give you the kingdom. 33Sell what you have and give the money to the poor. Make yourselves moneybags that never wear out. Make sure your treasure is safe in heaven, where thieves cannot steal it and moths cannot destroy it. 34Your heart will always be where your treasure is.
Faithful and Unfaithful Servants
(Matthew 24.45-51)
35 Be ready and keep your lamps burning 36 just like those servants who wait up for their master to return from a wedding feast. As soon as he comes and knocks, they open the door for him. 37Servants are fortunate if their master finds them awake and ready when he comes! I promise you he will get ready and let his servants sit down so he can serve them. 38Those servants are really fortunate if their master finds them ready, even though he comes late at night or early in the morning. 39 You would surely not let a thief break into your home, if you knew when the thief was coming. 40So always be ready! You don't know when the Son of Man will come.
41Peter asked Jesus, “Did you say this just for us or for everyone?”
42The Lord answered:
Who are faithful and wise servants? Who are the ones the master will put in charge of giving the other servants their food supplies at the proper time? 43Servants are fortunate if their master comes and finds them doing their job. 44A servant who is always faithful will surely be put in charge of everything the master owns.
45But suppose one of the servants thinks that the master won't return until late. Suppose that servant starts beating all the other servants and eats and drinks and gets drunk. 46If that happens, the master will come on a day and at a time when the servant least expects him. That servant will then be punished and thrown out with the servants who cannot be trusted.
47If servants are not ready or willing to do what their master wants them to do, they will be beaten hard. 48But servants who don't know what their master wants them to do will not be beaten so hard for doing wrong. If God has been generous with you, he will expect you to serve him well. But if he has been more than generous, he will expect you to serve him even better.
Not Peace, but Trouble
(Matthew 10.34-36)
49I came to set fire to the earth, and I wish it were already on fire! 50 I am going to be put to a hard test. And I will have to suffer a lot of pain until it is over. 51Do you think that I came to bring peace to earth? No indeed! I came to make people choose sides. 52A family of five will be divided, with two of them against the other three. 53 Fathers and sons will turn against one another, and mothers and daughters will do the same. Mothers-in-law and daughters-in-law will also turn against each other.
Knowing What To Do
(Matthew 16.2,3; 5.25,26)
54Jesus said to all the people:
As soon as you see a cloud coming up in the west, you say, “It's going to rain,” and it does. 55When the south wind blows, you say, “It's going to get hot,” and it does. 56Are you trying to fool someone? You can predict the weather by looking at the earth and sky, but you don't really know what's going on right now. 57Why don't you understand the right thing to do? 58When someone accuses you of something, try to settle things before you are taken to court. If you don't, you will be dragged before the judge. Then the judge will hand you over to the jailer, and you will be locked up. 59You won't get out until you have paid the last cent you owe.
translation_text:
1Dila po, nuru boanni a kasim jam dɛ ka tusa diichoa jigi yeŋ a tabi chaab zuk, Yeezu a yaa dɛ niŋ a weeni wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ayen, <<Ni kpesi nidek ale Farisiima dabintaŋa, mi a weeni ka ba sakpaŋ zulaŋa. 2Wari karo a suk dua a kan nyini peelim chum diipo. Wari dii meena mɛ ale chim wasusugi la, ku ale nyini peelim ate nuruba seba. 3Dila nyiŋla, fi dan biisi wari legi po, kantueŋ ba le wom di. Wari dii mɛ ate fi waasi dɔk po la, ale jueli gboŋ ate nuruba wom.
4<<M doaba, ni kan a chali yɔgsum ale baai ale baga a ko fi nyiŋka alege ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ wa an ŋman baga a nye fi wari di choa. 5Ni basi ate m kaam ni waai ale magsi ayen ni a chali yɔgsum la, wala ale Wen, waai ale wa ko fu ale ta pagrim a ŋman pai fu a yuk a basi bolim buui ale kan maari a kpi la po. Mm, mi a weeni ni, ni a chali wa la. 6Nuin fiisa sinu a kan da daa ligbie ŋaye yaa? Wen a kan baŋ si bunyi mɛ la wari ya. 7Wensie, Wen a chiini ni zuisaŋa meena ni zuimaŋa po kama. Nya kude nyiŋ nama kan a chali yɔgsum. Ni gaam nuinsaŋa ka nna yegayega Wen nimbie po.
8<<Nuru waai a dan nyini peelim nuruba niŋ a weeni ayen wa va ka mi, Mi Saalɔbiika mɛ ale nye ka dila dekdega Wen maarɔma niŋ. 9Alege waai mɛ a dan nyini peelim nuruba niŋ a zɛri mi, Mi mɛ ale nyini ka peelim a zɛri wa mɛ Wen maarɔma niŋ. 10Nuru waai a dan lɛ Mi Saalɔbiika kula nyɔnɔwa ale nya vɔŋteka kama, alege waai a dan lɛ Wen Chiika, kula nyɔnɔwa kan nya vɔŋteka. 11Nuruba dan yik fu a ta jam zaani tuka diinaŋa po yaase nalima niŋ yaase kpaga niŋ, ayen ba bek fu bega, kan basi ate ku daani fu ale fi le fi nye dii a biisi nyini la yaase fi le fi biisi diila, 12dii nyiŋla, dipo, Wen Chiika ale sak fu ate fi biisi.>>
13Nuru yaa nyini nuru boanni po a bek Yeezu ayen, <<Sagrɔ, weeni m suoku ate wa basi ate ti labi ti kowa nitalimu a chari chaab.>> 14Alege wa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<M doa, ka wana ale te mi suik ayen m bo nama buusa yaase m lueri ŋanta a chari nama niyewa?>> 15Yeezu yaa weeni nuru boanni meena ayen, <<Ni kpesi nidek ate ni kan chim ŋan yaalisa dii nyiŋla, nyuvuri potim daa fi nin nya ŋanta yegayega.>> 16Yeezu yaa magsi wamagsini ayen, <<Jigsirɔ ale jam ta wa talim ate bu yaa ta ŋanta nna yegayega. 17Wa yaa poli ayen, <M ka jigi a nyo m ŋantaŋa de meena du. M le nye ka sɛ?> 18Wa yaa ŋman weeni wadek ayen, <M le nye ka nna: M le nak ka m buaŋa a lɔnsi abe m sɛ bu kpiema a pai m ŋantaŋa meena a nyoro. 19M dan nye dila a nueri, m yaa weeni m dek ayen, m dega, fi ta ŋandiinta ka nna yegayega a dɛ ate ku ga a paari bena yegayega. Kan a yiili, a dɛ abe fi a nyu abe fi a nye fi yaalika.> 20Alege Wen yaa weeni wa ayen, <Fi ka beruk, yokku de fi ale kpi. Be ka wana ale wa soa fi ŋantaŋa de meena ate fi gomsi zaani la?> 21Ku be ka dila ale baai ale kasim pai ŋanta a zaani a jigsi alege an jigsi Wen nimbie po la.>>
22Yeezu yaa weeni wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ayen, <<Dila abe ale soa ate mi a weeni ni ayen ni kaa a yiili ni nyuvooŋa, ayen ni le nya ŋandiinta ka bɛ a dɛ vuugi, yaase gatta a jo lik ni nyiŋsaŋa. 23Dii nyiŋla, nyuvuri a gaam ŋandiinta kama, fi nyiŋka mɛ abe gaam gatta kama. 24Nama dek abe nya tɛŋka nuinsaŋa, si kan bori ŋanta yaase si a che ŋanta, si ka bua ayen si pai ŋanta a nyoro, alege Wen ale a te si ŋandiinta. Nama abe gaam nuinsa kama! 25Ka ni wana ale a yiili ate dila a gum dai du a te wa? 26Fi be dan kan baga a nye wa fiika de, ka boan ale soa ate fi a yiili nyaŋa de meena. 27Ni ŋman nya tiisaŋa ale wuutaŋa ale a nye ba puutaŋa la, ba kan tom yaase ba a yɔk gatta, alege ni basi ate m weeni ni ayen Solomon ale jam jigsi dii nna yegayega la, wa jam ka gatta ate ti nala a paari tiisaŋa ale wuutaŋa de puutaŋa. 28Alege Wen abe dan a te ti ga tila chaab wuutaŋa de tii nyiem ale boro jinla alege chum ba ŋman pai ti nyo bolim po la, ku a fɛ kama ayen wa te nama mɛ gatta. Ka boa ale soa ate nama siaka an soa diiya? 29Dila nyiŋ ni kan kasim a yiili abe ni pai ni popola meena a basi ni ale ni dɛ abe ni nyu jabuui la jigiya. 30Dii nyiŋla, ka baai ale kan seba Wen la ale kasim chali a vi ŋantaŋa de, alege nama Kowa poom seba ayen nama mɛ a yaali ŋantaŋa de kama. 31Dila nyiŋ ni dɛ niŋ a pai ni popola meena a basi Wen naamu po alege ate Wen a yaa basi ate ŋantaŋa de meena mɛ a jo ni nisa po.>> 32Ni kan chali yɔgsummoa, m bisaa, ale ku ka ni Kowa yaalika ayen wa pai naamu a te ni.
33<<Ni pai ni ŋan baai ate ni ta la a da a pai ligraŋa a te ŋanjaksa. Ni yaali ligra foruk tii ale kan maari a kaasi la, ate ni jigsika meena a bo wenŋmazuk juijui ate ŋanta kasim boro taam wuu ate zueba an baga a zu la, yaase ŋanta an baga a de ba la. 34Dii nyiŋla, ni jigsika ale bo juijui la, ni suiniima mɛ a bo ka dula.
35<<Ni gomsi magsi tuima abe ni basi ate ni bolimu a nyaksi. 36Abe ni a nye ase nuruba ale a limisi ba kpagi a nyini yalika tigi a jam diila. Wa dan jam a nak, tuimtomdisaŋa a nye ka nwuli a lak tuoku a te wa. 37Niauŋ ale tuimtomdɔ bala baai ate kpagni a jam paari ale ba kan goa la, wensie ate mi a weeni, wa le basi ate ba kali ate wa ta ŋandiinta a jam chari ba. 38Ba nyɔnɔwa a dan ŋman pilim jam a paari yok diipo ale ba kan goa, tomteerɔ bala ta niauŋ kama.
39<<Alege ni seba kude, ni basi ate m weeni a sak ni ayen, yenni nyɔnɔwa a dan seba diipo ate zuewa ale jam wa yenni la, wa te kan goa alege basi ate ba a kaasi wa yenni a jo di po. 40Dila nyiŋla, nama mɛ gomsi nidek a magsi dii nyiŋla, Mi Saalɔbiika ale jam ka diipo ate ni kan poli ayen m le jam la.>>
41Piita yaa bek Yeezu ayen, <<M Nyɔnɔ Yeezu Kirisita, fi a weeni wamagsini de a sak ka tama nyiini yaa waai meena?>> 42Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita yaa weeni ayen, <<Ka wana ale wensie ale yam tomteerɔwa de, waai ate wa kpagni a ta sebchakka ale wa ayen wa pai ŋandiinta a te tomteerɔ ba chaab diipo ale magsi la? 43Tomteerɔ waai ate wa kpagi a jam paari ale wa a tom wa tuini la a ta suipeentik kama. 44Wensie, ate mi a weeni fu ayen wa nyɔnɔwa ale pai wa ŋantaŋa meena a nyo ka wa nisa po ayen wa a nya. 45Alege tomteerɔwa a dan weeni ayen wa nyɔnɔwa goa a beni ka yegayega ale jamka, ate wa yaa yiri a nak wa tomteerɔ chaama, nidoama ale nipooma meena a gum chaab alege nye ŋandiinta a dɛ ale a nyu daam a buk, 46wa nyɔnɔwa ale ŋman pilim a jam ka da dii danni ate wa kan poli ayen wa le jam la. Wa nyɔnɔwa a dan jam paari, wa le te tomteerɔwa de ka waalika ase baai ale kan a va Wen nɔi la. 47Tomteerɔ waai ale seba wa nyɔnɔwa yaalika alege an gomsi a nye wa yaalika la, ale nya ka waalika ale nagta nna yegayega. 48Alege tomteerɔ waai ale kan seba wa nyɔnɔwa ale a yaali ayen wa nye dii a te wa alege wa nye wari dii ale magsi wa nya nagta la, wa le nya ka nagta nna maga. Nuru dan te fu yegayega, wa a poli ayen wa tuesi fi jigi ka yegayega mɛ. Wa be dan te fu nna yegayega gaam taam, wa poli ayen wa tuesi fi jigi ka nna yegayega mɛ a gaam taam.
49<<Mi jam ayen m cheem ka bolim tɛŋzuk de, mi be a yaali ayen bu ti poom ŋaam toati kama. 50M ta ka ninam ayen m nam bu po, ku abe a daani mu ka nna yegayega ka bu nin ga nueri. 51Nama a poli ayen mi jam ayen m ta ka suiyɔgni a jam tɛŋzuk de? Aaya, m jam ayen m poorika kama. 52A ta nyini yɔgyɔgla a cheŋ, nuruba banu a dan bo ba yeri po, ba le poori ka tɔgatɔga ate nuruba bata (3) a maa chaab a ta chaab ale nuruba baye. 53Ate ko ale ta chaab ale wa biik ate biika mɛ a ta chaab ale ka kowa. Ate ma ale ta chaab ale wa lie ate liewa mɛ a ta chaab ale wa mawa. Ate ŋianipɔk ale ta chaab ale wa sampok ate sampowa mɛ a ta chaab ale wa ŋianipowa.>>
54Yeezu yaa weeni nuru boanni ayen, <<Nama a dan nya chiŋmari ale di sobri yeniŋka ni a poli kama ayen ŋmoruk ale a yaali ku ni ate ku sum ni. 55Ni nyiem a dan nya ale viok a nyini yeseok geŋ a cheena, ni a poli kama ayen wulum wein a moata kama ate bu sum jam. 56Ni ka sakpaŋ zula nyam. Ni baga a nya tɛŋka ale chiŋmaaŋa kama a baga a seba ku ale ka diila. Be ka boa ale soa ate ni an baga a miŋ wie ŋaai ale a nye yɔgyɔgla de la?
57<<Ka boa ale soa ate ni an baga a weeni nidek dii ale magsi nyeka la? 58Ase fi ŋmaarɔwa a dan ta fu a cheŋ buusa boka jigi, pii nyiŋ ate fi nya wanni zuk suiku po, kan daa di wa pai fu a te ka buusa boorɔwa, ate wala a pai fu a te kpagni ate kpagni ale pai fu a nyo likka dɔk po. 59Mi a weeni fu, fi kan nyini, ka fi nin tuni pamini.>>

english_text:
Turn Back to God
1About this same time Jesus was told that Pilate had given orders for some people from Galilee to be killed while they were offering sacrifices. 2Jesus replied:
Do you think that these people were worse sinners than everyone else in Galilee just because of what happened to them? 3Not at all! But you can be sure that if you don't turn back to God, every one of you will also be killed. 4What about those 18 people who died when the tower in Siloam fell on them? Do you think they were worse than everyone else in Jerusalem? 5Not at all! But you can be sure that if you don't turn back to God, every one of you will also die.
A Story about a Fig Tree
6Jesus then told them this story:
A man had a fig tree growing in his vineyard. One day he went out to pick some figs, but he didn't find any. 7So he said to the gardener, “For three years I have come looking for figs on this tree, and I haven't found any yet. Chop it down! Why should it take up space?”
8The gardener answered, “Master, leave it for another year. I'll dig around it and put some manure on it to make it grow. 9Maybe it will have figs on it next year. If it doesn't, you can have it cut down.”
Healing a Woman on the Sabbath
10One Sabbath, Jesus was teaching in a synagogue, 11and a woman was there who had been crippled by an evil spirit for 18 years. She was completely bent over and could not straighten up. 12When Jesus saw the woman, he called her over and said, “You are now well.” 13He placed his hands on her, and at once she stood up straight and praised God.
14 The man in charge of the synagogue was angry because Jesus had healed someone on the Sabbath. So he said to the people, “Each week has six days when we can work. Come and be healed on one of those days, but not on the Sabbath.”
15The Lord replied, “Are you trying to fool someone? Won't any one of you untie your ox or donkey and lead it out to drink on a Sabbath? 16This woman belongs to the family of Abraham, but Satan has kept her bound for 18 years. Isn't it right to set her free on the Sabbath?” 17Jesus' words made his enemies ashamed. But everyone else in the crowd was happy about the wonderful things he was doing.
A Mustard Seed and Yeast
(Matthew 13.31-33; Mark 4.30-32)
18Jesus said, “What is God's kingdom like? What can I compare it with? 19It is like what happens when someone plants a mustard seed in a garden. The seed grows as big as a tree, and birds nest in its branches.”
20Then Jesus said, “What can I compare God's kingdom with? 21It is like what happens when a woman mixes yeast into three batches of flour. Finally, all the dough rises.”
The Narrow Door
(Matthew 7.13,14,21-23)
22As Jesus was on his way to Jerusalem, he taught the people in the towns and villages. 23Someone asked him, “Lord, are only a few people going to be saved?”
Jesus answered:
24Do all you can to go in by the narrow door! A lot of people will try to get in, but will not be able to. 25Once the owner of the house gets up and locks the door, you will be left standing outside. You will knock on the door and say, “Sir, open the door for us!”
But the owner will answer, “I don't know a thing about you!”
26Then you will start saying, “We dined with you, and you taught in our streets.”
27 But he will say, “I really don't know who you are! Get away from me, you evil people!”
28 Then when you have been thrown outside, you will weep and grit your teeth because you will see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in God's kingdom. 29People will come from all directions and sit down to feast in God's kingdom. 30 There the ones who are now least important will be the most important, and those who are now most important will be least important.
Jesus and Herod
31At that time some Pharisees came to Jesus and said, “You had better get away from here, because Herod wants to kill you!”
32Jesus said to them:
Go tell that fox, “I am going to force out demons and heal people today and tomorrow, and three days later I'll be through.” 33But I am going on my way today and tomorrow and the next day. After all, Jerusalem is the place where prophets are killed.
Jesus Loves Jerusalem
(Matthew 23.37-39)
34 Jerusalem, Jerusalem! Your people have killed the prophets and have stoned the messengers who were sent to you. I have often wanted to gather your people, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings. But you wouldn't let me. 35 Now your temple will be deserted. You won't see me again until the time when you say,
“Blessed is the one who comes
in the name of the Lord.”
translation_text:
1Yeezu ale jam boro a biisi la, nuruba gela a yaa jam weeni a sak wa naawa Paalɔt ale ko Galili demma ba gela ba ale jam boro a nye kaabka a te Wen diila. 2Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Nama a poli ayen Galili demma de, a chim ka tuimbaata nyam a gaam Galili demma mbala? 3Aaya, ni be dan kan basi ni tuimbaataŋa tomka, nama mɛ le kpi ka bala ale kpi diila. 4Nama a poli ayen nuruba pi ale naanika ate Jerusalem tɛŋka Sailom yeri kpienni a jam lo ba zuk a ko ba la a chim ka tuimbaata nyam a gaam nuru baai meena ale bo Jerusalem tɛŋka po la? 5Aaya, alege mi a weeni kama ayen ni dan kan basi ni tuimbaataŋa nama mɛ le kpi kama.>>
6Yeezu yaa magsi wamagsini ayen, <<Nuru ale jam ta kiŋkaŋ wa kaduk po. Nuruwa yaa yiri dai yeŋ a yaali moota alege wa an nya jaaboa. 7Wa yaa weeni waai ale a nya kadukka zuk la, ayen, <Nya de, bena ŋata ale nna ate mi kasim a yaali moota kiŋkaŋka de zuk alege kan nya jaaboa. Che ka lɔnsi, ale mi zɛ jabuui nyiŋ ale soa ate ka a dɛ tɛŋka ŋandiintaŋa la.> 8Wa yaa tulisi wa ayen, <M nyɔnɔ, basi ate ka zaani benni de ate m tu gilim ka a nye bibaam a yuk gilim ka. 9Bein a dan ŋman paari ate ka yɔni, ku nala, alege bu dan kan yɔni ya, fi yaa che lɔnsi.> >>
10Yeezu yaa jam boro a sak nuruba ba tuka diinaŋa kunyi po. 11Nipok wanyi ale jam boro ate chichirik biok a basi ate wa chim gbaruk bena pi ale naaniŋ. Tuemu a jam nye kama ate wa gori an ŋman baga a teenti wadek a zaani. 12Yeezu ale ga nya wa la, wa yaa wi nipowa ayen, <<Nipowa, fi nya nyiŋyɔgsa kama,>> 13a yaa pai wa nisaŋa a vi nipowa zuk ate wa yaa deri teenti wadek a yiri zaani ŋmai a te Wen pimpauk. 14Alege tuka dɔkku kpagni ale ga nya dila la, wa sui yaa puuri dii nyiŋla, ku jam ka ba Vuusum Dai ate Yeezu nye dila. Tuka dɔkku kpagni a yaa weeni nuruma ayen, <<Daa ŋayuebi ale boro ate ti pai ŋala a tom tuima. Nuru waai a dan a yaali ayen wa nya tebika wa jam daaŋa de po. Ku daa ti Vuusum Danni ate ba a nye dila!>> 15Yeezu yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Nama ka sakpaŋ zula nyam, nama wanyi wanyi a foli ni niiga ale ni bonsaŋa kama a ta a cheŋ ate ba a nyu nyiam ni Vuusum Danni. 16Ka boa ate nipowa de, ale ka Abrayam lie la ate Sitaana bobi wa bena pi ale naaniŋ la, a kan nya tebika Vuusum Danni?>> 17Yeezu tulisika de a jam pai wa dachaasaŋa nyo ka chivie po ate nuruma sue a jam peenti ale wakperikaliik sii ate Yeezu jam nye la.
18Yeezu yaa bek ayen, <<Wen naamu a nye ase ka boan la? M le pai ka boan jaab a magsi chaab ale bu? 19Bu a nye ase ka biri dii ate ba a wi ayen, mastad, ate nuru yaa pai bori wa talim po la. Binni a yaa nyini a chim tiib ate nuinsa yaa jam a yɔk si tugta bu naŋsaŋa nyiŋ.>>
20Yeezu ŋman bek ayen, <<M be le ŋman pai ka boa a magsi chaab ale Wen naamu? 21Bu a nye ase ka dabinta ate nipok a pai nyo taasi kpienni ale boroborok zom po ate bu fuusi a sueri di meena diila.>>
22Yeezu yaa va tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa ale tɛŋ fiisaŋa po a cheŋ Jerusalem ale a sak nuruma. 23Nuru wanyi a yaa bek wa ayen, <<M Nyɔnɔ Yeezu Kirisita, nuru baai ale ba nya varibasika la an soa diiya?>> Yeezu yaa tulisi ba ayen, 24<<Ni pii nyiŋ a va tuok miglika a jo, mi a weeni kama ayen nuru boari ale a gisi ba va dula a jo, alege ba kan baga. 25Yenni nyɔnɔwa yaa dan yiri lik dɔkku nɔnni ni yaa weeni ayen, <M nyɔnɔ lak dɔkku nɔnni a te ti.> Ate wa le tulisi ni ayen, <Mi zɛ ni ale nyini ka juijui la.> 26Ate ni yaa weeni wa ayen, <Tama ale fi a dɛ ŋandiinta ale chaab kama. Fi be sak nuruba tama tɛŋka kama.> 27Alege wa le ŋman tulisi ayen, <Mi zɛ ni ale nyini ka juijui la. Nama gaasa nyama, ni bɛ mi niŋ!> 28Ni ni a kum kama abe ni a ŋɔbi nyina ase ni nin nya Abrayam ale Aizik ale Jekob ale Wen biisiteerɔma meena a bo Wen naamu po. Alege ate nama bo bu peelim. 29Nuruba ale nyini kori ale yeniŋ ale wiilukku ale yeseoku geŋsa a jam kali Wen naamu po. 30Ate ba gela ale wari ŋaaŋ la ale dɛ niŋ ate baai ale dɛ niŋ la a wari ŋaaŋ.>>
31Yeezu ale boro a biisi la, Farisiima gela a yaa jam wa jigi a weeni wa ayen, <<Basi dela jigini abe fi nyini a cheŋ jigi yoŋ dii nyiŋla, Naawa Ayerod a yaali ayen wa ko fu kama.>>
32Yeezu yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<Ni ga weeni pimpaasima nyɔnɔwa ayen m bo ka dela a yiak chichirik baata nuruba zuima po a basi ale a tebi ba gela mɛ jinla ale chum ate vɔnuŋ a dan paari abe m nueri m tuimaŋa. 33Alege ku a fɛ kama ayen m bo m suiku po a cheŋ jinla ale chum ale vɔnuŋ dii nyiŋla, ku an magsi ayen Wen biisiteerɔwa a kpi jigi jigiya, ka Jerusalem tɛŋka po ate wa le kpi.>>
34<<Jerusalem, Jerusalem, nama a ko Wen biisiteerɔma ale yuk baai ate Wen a tom ba ni jigi la ale tana, ka bu dina ate mi ale tigsi ni bisaŋa jigi yeŋ ase kpiak ale a pɔbi ka bisa diila alege nama a kan siagi? 35Ni be nya m banti ni yenni kama, mi ale a weeni ni ni kan ŋman nya mi, ka nama a nin weeni ayen, <Niaka a bo waai ale cheena Naawen yuenni nyiŋ la.> >> (Yiila 118:26)

english_text:
Jesus Heals a Sick Man
1One Sabbath, Jesus was having dinner in the home of an important Pharisee, and everyone was carefully watching Jesus. 2All of a sudden a man with swollen legs stood up in front of him. 3Jesus turned and asked the Pharisees and the teachers of the Law of Moses, “Is it right to heal on the Sabbath?” 4But they did not say a word.
Jesus took hold of the man. Then he healed him and sent him away. 5 Afterwards, Jesus asked the people, “If your son or ox falls into a well, wouldn't you pull him out at once, even on the Sabbath?” 6There was nothing they could say.
How To Be a Guest
7Jesus saw how the guests had tried to take the best seats. So he told them:
8 When you are invited to a wedding feast, don't sit in the best place. Someone more important may have been invited. 9Then the one who invited you will come and say, “Give your place to this other guest!” You will be embarrassed and will have to sit in the worst place.
10When you are invited to be a guest, go and sit in the worst place. Then the one who invited you may come and say, “My friend, take a better seat!” You will then be honored in front of all the other guests. 11 If you put yourself above others, you will be put down. But if you humble yourself, you will be honored.
12Then Jesus said to the man who had invited him:
When you give a dinner or a banquet, don't invite your friends and family and relatives and rich neighbors. If you do, they will invite you in return, and you will be paid back. 13When you give a feast, invite the poor, the paralyzed, the lame, and the blind. 14They cannot pay you back. But God will bless you and reward you when his people rise from death.
The Great Banquet
(Matthew 22.1-10)
15After Jesus had finished speaking, one of the guests said, “The greatest blessing of all is to be at the banquet in God's kingdom!”
16Jesus told him:
A man once gave a great banquet and invited a lot of guests. 17When the banquet was ready, he sent a servant to tell the guests, “Everything is ready! Please come.”
18One guest after another started making excuses. The first one said, “I bought some land, and I've got to look it over. Please excuse me.”
19Another guest said, “I bought five teams of oxen, and I need to try them out. Please excuse me.”
20Still another guest said, “I've just now married, and I can't be there.”
21The servant told his master what happened, and the master became so angry he said, “Go as fast as you can to every street and alley in town! Bring in everyone who is poor or paralyzed or blind or lame.”
22When the servant returned, he said, “Master, I've done what you told me, and there is still plenty of room for more people.”
23His master then told him, “Go out along the back roads and make people come in, so my house will be full. 24Not one of the guests I first invited will get even a bite of my food!”
Being a Disciple
(Matthew 10.37,38)
25Large crowds were walking along with Jesus, when he turned and said:
26 You cannot be my disciple, unless you love me more than you love your father and mother, your wife and children, and your brothers and sisters. You cannot follow me unless you love me more than you love your own life.
27 You cannot be my disciple unless you carry your own cross and follow me.
28Suppose one of you wants to build a tower. What is the first thing you will do? Won't you sit down and figure out how much it will cost and if you have enough money to pay for it? 29Otherwise, you will start building the tower, but not be able to finish. Then everyone who sees what is happening will laugh at you. 30They will say, “You started building, but could not finish the job.”
31What will a king do if he has only 10,000 soldiers to defend himself against a king who is about to attack him with 20,000 soldiers? Before he goes out to battle, won't he first sit down and decide if he can win? 32If he thinks he won't be able to defend himself, he will send messengers and ask for peace while the other king is still a long way off. 33So then, you cannot be my disciple unless you give away everything you own.
Salt and Light
(Matthew 5.13; Mark 9.50)
34Salt is good, but if it no longer tastes like salt, how can it be made to taste salty again? 35It is no longer good for the soil or even for the manure pile. People simply throw it out. If you have ears, pay attention!
translation_text:
1Vuusum Daaŋa dinyi ate Yeezu yaa cheŋ Farisiima wanyi yeri ayen wa dɛ ŋandiinta. Nuruwa jam ka kpagi. Dila danni Farisiima ale Sinsaŋŋa sagrɔma yaa kasim jam a nya Yeezu ase wa le nye wari ya. 2Nuru wanyi a yaa boro ate wa nisima ale wa naŋsa a jam fuusi nna yegayega a yaa za Yeezu niŋ 3ate Yeezu yaa bek Sinsak sagrɔma ale Farisiima ayen, <<Sinsaŋŋa a siak ate nuru a tebi yɔgnyieŋsa Vuusum Danni yaa ŋa kan siagi?>> 4Alege ba an tulisi wari ya. Yeezu yaa tebi nuruwa ate wa kuli. 5Yeezu yaa bek ba ayen, <<Ase ni wanyi a nin ta nidoabili yaase naab ate ba wanyi a lo vili po Vuusum Danni, ni kan yeeri nidoabinni yaase naamu Vuusum Danni dila dekdega a ta a nyini?>> 6Alege ba an jam baga a tulisi wa beŋŋa de mɛ.
7Ba ale jam a kali ayen ba dɛ la, Yeezu yaa nya ale nichamma ba gela a lueri jigi maŋsaŋa a kali. Yeezu ale nya dila la, wa yaa biisi magsi wamagsini ayen, 8<<Nuru a dan wi fu ayen fi jam maa dɛ tigi ŋandiinta, kan kali jigi maŋŋa. Dii nyiŋla, ku baga a nye kama ate nuru waai ale ŋman chim nuru kpioŋ a gaam fi la a jam ayen wa maa dɛ tigini ŋandiintaŋa. 9Nuru waai ale wi fu ayen fi jam a maa dɛ tigini ŋandiintaŋa la, ale jam ŋaaŋnyiŋ a weeni fu ayen fi yiri abe fi ge ate nuru waai ale ŋman gaam fu la a kali. Dila abe ta ka chivie a jam fi jigi, wa ale weeni fu ate fi siŋ tɛŋ la nyiŋ. 10Alege, fi dan cheŋ, ga kali juijui ale kan magsi fi kali la, ate waai ale wi fu la yaa jam fi jigi a weeni fu ayen, <M doa, yiti jueli jam kali jigi maŋka de.> Nna le ta zula a jam fi jigi ate waai meena nya. 11Nuru waai ale pai wadek a chim nuru kpioŋ la, ba le zaab wa, alege nuru waai ale a zaab wadek la, ale chim ka nuru kpioŋ.>>
12Yeezu yaa weeni nuru waai ale wi wa ayen wa jam ate ba dɛ la ayen, <<Fi dan nye kantueŋ yaase yok ŋandiinta kan wi fi doaba yaase fi suata yaase fi mabisa yaase fi kalimɔtidɔ yaase jigsirɔba, bala meena waai a dan nye ŋandiinta tigi, ase dila la ba pilim a wi fi mɛ kama. Dila abe dan nye, ku a sak ase fi nya fi ale nye diila tutuna kama. 13Fi dan ta ŋandiinta tigi, wi ŋanjaksa ale gbattaŋa ale gbansa ale yeeba 14ate fi nya niaka, dii nyiŋla, bala waai an baga nye wari a tuni fu. Ka Naawen ale wa tuni fu dai dii danni ate wayɔrisima nyam le yiti kum po la.>>
15Nidoama wanyi ale jam maa kala a dɛ ŋandiintaŋa la a yaa wom dii ate Yeezu a weeni la a yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Niauŋ ale waai ale wa dɛ ŋandiintaŋa Wen naamu po la.>>
16Alege wa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Nuru ale jam nye tigi kpien a wi nuruba yega. 17Ba ale ga dik ŋandiintaŋa a nueri la, wa yaa tom wa tomteerɔwa ayen wa nyiem a weeni baai meena ate wa wi la ayen ba jam ale jaab meena a gomsi magsi kama. 18Alege ba meena wanyi wanyi a yaa tulisi ayen ba kan nya suik a jam. Waai ate tomteerɔwa a dɛ niŋ ga weeni la, yaa weeni ayen, <M da ka tɛŋ ate ku a fɛ ayen m ga nya ka. Mi a saalim, mi an baga a jam.> 19Wanyi mɛ a jam weeni ayen, <M da ka m lalik kpaansa bunu ate mi a cheŋ ayen m ga pai si kpa nya. Mi a saalim, mi an baga a jam.> 20Wa choa mɛ a jam weeni ayen, <M faari ka nipok, dila nyiŋ mi an baga a jam.> 21Dila tomteerɔwa yaa ŋman jam weeni wa kpagni kude. Kpagni yaa weeni wa tomteerɔwa ale suipuurum ayen, <Cheŋ suiduataŋa po nwuli tɛŋ kpieŋka a ta ŋanjaksaŋa ale gbattaŋa ale yeema ale gbansaŋa a jam.> 22Tomteerɔwa yaa weeni ayen, <M nyɔnɔ, fi ale weeni m nye diila mi nye kama alege dɔkku an diem sueri ya.> 23Ate kpagni yaa weeni tomteerɔwa ayen, <Cheŋ tɛŋka suiduataŋa po a weeni abe fi fɛ nuruba ate ba jam ate m yenni a sueri. 24Mi ale a weeni ni ayen baai meena ate m liŋ wi la, ba wanyi mɛ la nɔi a kan tiri mi ŋandiintaŋa de.> >>
25Nuru boari yaa jam va Yeezu a cheŋ ate wa cheem a weeni ba ayen, 26<<Nuru waai dan jam mi jigi ale an kisa wadek ko ale ma ale pok ale bisa ale suata ale toaba ale wadek nyuvunni, wa kan baga a chim mi ŋaaŋviirɔ. 27Waai a dan kan gomsi wadek a magsi ninammoa, kula nyɔnɔwa an baga chim mi ŋaaŋviirɔ. 28Ase ni wanyi a dan a poli yie woŋ sɛka, wa a kan kali tɛŋ a poli wa ale wa pai jabuui ale jabuui a sɛ yenni a nueri la? 29Kan daa di, wa dan nyubi nyubini alege wa an baga a sɛ nueri ya waai meena ale nya wa ale nye diila a la wa kama 30a weeni ayen, <Ni nya nuruwa de ale piilim wa yeri sɛka alege an baga a sɛ nueri ya.> 31Naab abe dan nyini peelim ale nuruba tusa pi (10,000) ayen wa kpaliŋ chaab ale naab wa choa waai ale ta nuruba tusa pisiye (20,000) la, ku a fɛ kama ate wa kali tɛŋ a poli zimm nya ase wa ta pagrim yegayega a baga tu chaab ale naab nwala ya. 32Wa be dan nya ale wa an baga, wa a tom ka nuruba ate ba dɛ niŋ a ga tu naab nwala suiku po a saalim wa ate ba nye magsi chaab alege ate naawa dek a diem bo suiku po niŋniŋ a cheena. 33Dila nyiŋla mi a weeni ni kama ayen ni wanyi mɛ la an baga chim mi ŋaaŋviirɔ, ka wa nin yeeri wa nisa jaabuuri meena ate wa ta la po.
34<<Yesa masa kama, alege si masimu a dan kan boro fi an ŋman baga nye ate si a masa. 35Si ŋman ka kiri a te tɛŋka yaase tampoi ya, ba yuk si a basi kama. Waai abe le ta turi a wom la, abe wom.>>

english_text:
One Sheep
(Matthew 18.12-14)
1 Tax collectors and sinners were all crowding around to listen to Jesus. 2So the Pharisees and the teachers of the Law of Moses started grumbling, “This man is friendly with sinners. He even eats with them.”
3Then Jesus told them this story:
4If any of you has 100 sheep, and one of them gets lost, what will you do? Won't you leave the 99 in the field and go look for the lost sheep until you find it? 5And when you find it, you will be so glad that you will put it on your shoulder 6and carry it home. Then you will call in your friends and neighbors and say, “Let's celebrate! I've found my lost sheep.”
7Jesus said, “In the same way there is more happiness in heaven because of one sinner who turns to God than over 99 good people who don't need to.”
One Coin
8Jesus told the people another story:
What will a woman do if she has ten silver coins and loses one of them? Won't she light a lamp, sweep the floor, and look carefully until she finds it? 9Then she will call in her friends and neighbors and say, “Let's celebrate! I've found the coin I lost.”
10Jesus said, “In the same way God's angels are happy when even one person turns to him.”
Two Sons
11Jesus told them yet another story:
Once a man had two sons. 12The younger son said to his father, “Give me my share of the property.” So the father divided his property between his two sons.
13Not long after that, the younger son packed up everything he owned and left for a foreign country, where he wasted all his money in wild living. 14He had spent everything, when a bad famine spread through that whole land. Soon he had nothing to eat.
15He went to work for a man in that country, and the man sent him out to take care of his pigs. 16He would have been glad to eat what the pigs were eating, but no one gave him a thing.
17Finally, he came to his senses and said, “My father's workers have plenty to eat, and here I am, starving to death! 18I will go to my father and say to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against God in heaven and against you. 19I am no longer good enough to be called your son. Treat me like one of your workers.’ ”
20The younger son got up and started back to his father. But when he was still a long way off, his father saw him and felt sorry for him. He ran to his son and hugged and kissed him.
21The son said, “Father, I have sinned against God in heaven and against you. I am no longer good enough to be called your son.”
22But his father said to the servants, “Hurry and bring the best clothes and put them on him. Give him a ring for his finger and sandals for his feet. 23Get the best calf and prepare it, so we can eat and celebrate. 24This son of mine was dead, but has now come back to life. He was lost and has now been found.” And they began to celebrate.
25The older son had been out in the field. But when he came near the house, he heard the music and dancing. 26So he called one of the servants over and asked, “What's going on here?”
27The servant answered, “Your brother has come home safe and sound, and your father ordered us to kill the best calf.” 28The older brother got so angry that he would not even go into the house.
His father came out and begged him to go in. 29But he said to his father, “For years I have worked for you like a slave and have always obeyed you. But you have never even given me a little goat, so that I could give a dinner for my friends. 30This other son of yours wasted your money on prostitutes. And now that he has come home, you ordered the best calf to be killed for a feast.”
31His father replied, “My son, you are always with me, and everything I have is yours. 32But we should be glad and celebrate! Your brother was dead, but he is now alive. He was lost and has now been found.”
translation_text:
1Dai yeŋ ate lampoo cheesirɔba ale wabaata nyam meena yaa jam torisi paari kpaŋŋa ayen ba wom Yeezu sinsaŋŋa. 2Farisiima ale Sinsak sagrɔma a yaa maa chaab a ŋuuni a weeni ayen, <<Nuruwa de a pai wadek a gum chaab ale ka wabaata nyam ale a dɛ ale ba mɛ.>>
3Wa yaa weeni ba wamagsini de ayen, 4<<Ase ni wanyi a nin ta piisa kook, ate kunyi a bɛ, wa a nye ka sɛ? Wa le basi ka piisa pineok ale neokku sagni po alege yaa nyiem a gisi kuui ale bɛ la ate wa nya ku. 5Ase wa dan nya ku, wa pai ku a tuk ka ŋmankpaluk ale suipeentik. 6Wa dan jam yeri, wa a wi ka wa doama ale wa kali mɔtidɔma jigi yeŋ a weeni ba ayen, <Ni a dɛ masim ale mu ale m nya m posuku ale bɛ la kama.> 7Ku abe ka dila ate mi a weeni ni, suipeentik nna yega ale ka bo wenŋmazuk ase wabaata nyɔnɔ a nin basi wa biemu a gaam wayɔrisima nyam pineok ale neok baai ale kan ŋman magsi tagrika la kama.>>
8Yeezu yaa ŋman magsi wamagsini di choa ayen, <<Ase nipok wanyi a nin ta ligbie pi ate ligbinni dinyi a yaa bɛ wa a nye ka sɛ? Wa toati ka bolim a vaari dɔkku meena gisi nalimnyiini ate wa ga nya di? 9Wa dan ga nya di wa ale wi wa doama ale baai ale kali moata wa ate ba jam jigi yeŋ a weeni ba ayen, <M sui peenti yegayega dii nyiŋla, m nya m ligbi dii ale bɛ la kama. Ni be basi ate ti sue peenti.> 10Suipeentik kala dega dega ate Wen maarɔma a tara ase tuimbaata nyɔnɔ wanyi a nin basi wa tuimbaata tomka.>>
11Yeezu yaa weeni ayen, <<Nuru ale boro a ta wa nidoabilisa baye. 12Wa bibaaŋka a yaa weeni wa ayen, <M koa, ŋan baai ate fi ale lueri a chari mi ale m suoku la, pai mi ŋantaŋa a te mi yɔgyɔgla.> Nuruwa yaa siak a yaa chari ba wa ŋantaŋa. 13Daa maga ale ga taam la, bibaaŋka a yaa pai wa ŋantaŋa meena a cheŋ satɛŋ nna niŋniŋŋa. Dula jigini wa yaa nye nanbolini a kaasi wa ligraŋa meena. 14Wa ale ga dɛ wa ŋantaŋa meena a nueri la, kom nna yegayega a yaa jam tɛŋ kala alege wa ŋman ka jaaboa. 15Wa yaa cheŋ tɛŋ kala nuru wanyi jigi ate nuru wala a yaa ta wa a cheŋ wa talim ayen wa a nya die zuk. 16Wa sui ate jam peenti kama yegayega ase wa nin nya suik a maari a dɛ deeŋa ŋandiintaŋa, alege nuru an jam te wa jaaboa.
17<<Alege ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ate wa yammu jam la, wa yaa weeni wadek ayen, <M kowa tomteerɔma meena a ta ŋandiinta ka nna yegayega a gaam ba dɛka alege mi bo dela ayen m kpi ale kom. 18M le yiri kama a kuli ga weeni m kowa ayen, M Koa, m tom ka wabiok Wen ale fi jigi. 19Ku an ŋman magsi fi ale wi mu ayen fi biiga, a nye mu ase fi tomteerɔma po wanyi la.> 20Wa yaa deri yiti a kuli wa kowa jigi. Wa ale jam bo suiku po a cheena yeri la, wa kowa a yaa nya wa ate jiirim a yaa yik wa kowa ate wa chali nyini a ga tu wa suiku niŋ a gbaari wa a puusi wa. 21Nidoabinni yaa weeni ayen, <M koa, m tom ka wabiok Wen ale fi jigi. Ku an ŋman magsi ayen fi wi mu ayen fi biiga.> 22Alege wa kowa yaa wi tomteerɔma ayen ba nye nwuli a ta garuk kuui ale nala nna yegayega wa gattaŋa meena po la a jam jo wa. Wa weeni ba ayen, <Ni pai nifelinni a su wa nisaŋa abe ni pai nuensa a su wa. 23Ni ga yik naabiik kaai ale biigi la a ta jam ko. Ate ti nye ŋandiin kpienta tigi ate ti nye suipeentik ale chaab. 24Dii nyiŋla, m nidoabinni de a jam kpi kama, alege yɔgyɔgla de wa vua kama, wa jam bɛ kama alege yɔgyɔgla de ti nya wa kama.> Ba yaa deri piilim ba ŋandiintaŋa dɛka ale diinta.
25<<Ba ale jam boro a nye nyaŋa de meena la, wa bikpagni a diem jam bo ka talim. Wa yaa ale jam nyini peelim a cheena a jam moata yeri la, wa yaa wom yiilaŋa ale gɔgtaŋa. 26Wa ale jam paari la, wa yaa wi tomteerɔma wanyi a bek wa ayen, <Ka boan ale a nye?> Tomteerɔwa yaa tulisi wa ayen, 27<Ka fi yuawa ale ŋman pilim jam ate fi kowa yaa ko naabiik tanjaŋini, dii nyiŋla wa nya biika kama ale jaab ka wa, wa ta nyiŋyɔgsa kama.> 28Alege bikpagni sui a yaa a puuri nna yegayega ate wa zɛri ayen wa kan ŋman jo yenni po. Wa kowa yaa nyini saalim wa ayen wa jo. 29Alege wa tulisi wa kowa ayen, <Nya de, benaŋa de meena wuu ate mi tom te fu nna ase yɔma la, m be an zɛri fi nɔi mɛ. Ka boan jaab ate fi nye te mi? Ale buli mɛ la, fi an te mi ayen m nye ŋandiinta tigi ale m doama. 30Alege fi nidoabinni de waai ale ta fi ŋantaŋa a cheŋ ga yik kaasi nipok kaasuŋta zuk la, a yaa dan pilim jam fi yiri yik naabiik kaai ale zuak nna yegayega la, a ko te wa!> 31Wa kowa yaa tulisi wa ayen, <M biigaa, fi kasim bo ale mi ka daa meena, m be ale ta jabuui meena la, ka fi abe ale soa. 32Alege ku magsi kama ayen ti boro a dɛ ale a gɔk dii nyiŋla, fi yuawa a daam kpi kama alege yɔgyɔgla de wa vua kama, wa daam bɛ kama alege yɔgyɔgla de ti nya wa kama.> >>

english_text:
A Dishonest Manager
1Jesus said to his disciples:
A rich man once had a manager to take care of his business. But he was told that his manager was wasting money. 2So the rich man called him in and said, “What is this I hear about you? Tell me what you have done! You are no longer going to work for me.”
3The manager said to himself, “What shall I do now that my master is going to fire me? I can't dig ditches, and I'm ashamed to beg. 4I know what I'll do, so that people will welcome me into their homes after I've lost my job.”
5Then one by one he called in the people who were in debt to his master. He asked the first one, “How much do you owe my master?”
6“A hundred barrels of olive oil,” the man answered.
So the manager said, “Take your bill and sit down and quickly write ‘50.’ ”
7The manager asked someone else who was in debt to his master, “How much do you owe?”
“A thousand sacks of wheat,” the man replied.
The manager said, “Take your bill and write ‘800.’ ”
8The master praised his dishonest manager for looking out for himself so well. That's how it is! The people of this world look out for themselves better than the people who belong to the light.
9 My disciples, I tell you to use wicked wealth to make friends for yourselves. Then when it is gone, you will be welcomed into an eternal home. 10Anyone who can be trusted in little matters can also be trusted in important matters. But anyone who is dishonest in little matters will be dishonest in important matters. 11If you cannot be trusted with this wicked wealth, who will trust you with true wealth? 12And if you cannot be trusted with what belongs to someone else, who will give you something that will be your own? 13 You cannot be the slave of two masters. You will like one more than the other or be more loyal to one than to the other. You cannot serve God and money.
Some Sayings of Jesus
(Matthew 11.12,13; 5.31,32; Mark 10.11,12)
14The Pharisees really loved money. So when they heard what Jesus said, they made fun of him. 15But Jesus told them:
You are always making yourselves look good, but God sees what is in your heart. The things that most people think are important are worthless as far as God is concerned.
16 Until the time of John the Baptist, people had to obey the Law of Moses and the Books of the Prophets. But since God's kingdom has been preached, everyone is trying hard to get in. 17 Heaven and earth will disappear before the smallest letter of the Law does.
18 It is a terrible sin for a man to divorce his wife and marry another woman. It is also a terrible sin for a man to marry a divorced woman.
Lazarus and the Rich Man
19There was once a rich man who wore expensive clothes and every day ate the best food. 20But a poor beggar named Lazarus was brought to the gate of the rich man's house. 21He was happy just to eat the scraps that fell from the rich man's table. His body was covered with sores, and dogs kept coming up to lick them. 22 The poor man died, and angels took him to the place of honor next to Abraham.
The rich man also died and was buried. 23 He went to hell and was suffering terribly. When he looked up and saw Abraham far off and Lazarus at his side, 24he said to Abraham, “Have pity on me! Send Lazarus to dip his finger in water and touch my tongue. I'm suffering terribly in this fire.”
25Abraham answered, “My friend, remember that while you lived, you had everything good, and Lazarus had everything bad. Now he is happy, and you are in pain. 26And besides, there is a deep ditch between us, and no one from either side can cross over.”
27But the rich man said, “Abraham, then please send Lazarus to my father's home. 28Let him warn my five brothers, so they won't come to this horrible place.”
29Abraham answered, “Your brothers can read what Moses and the prophets wrote. They should pay attention to that.”
30Then the rich man said, “No, that's not enough! If only someone from the dead would go to them, they would listen and turn to God.”
31So Abraham said, “If they won't pay attention to Moses and the prophets, they won't listen even to someone who comes back from the dead.”
translation_text:
1Wa yaa ŋman weeni wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ayen, <<Jigsirɔ ale jam boro a ta tomteerɔ, ate ŋmiŋmaasa yaa paari wa ayen nuruwa de kaasi wa ŋantaŋa kama. 2Jigsirɔwa yaa wi wa a bek ayen, <Ka boan jaab wari ate mi a wom a magsi chaab ale fi dila? Pai m ŋantaŋa meena a te mu, fi an ŋman baga a chim waai ale a nya m ŋantaŋa meena zuk la.> 3Tomteerɔwa yaa weeni wadek ayen, <M nyɔnɔwa a yaali ayen wa yiak mu kama tuimaŋa po. M be le nye ka sɛ? M be ka pagrim a kpa, chivie abe ta mu ase m nin nyiem a juisi. 4M seba m le m nye dii yɔgyɔgla de la, ate m dan jɔk m tuimaŋa abe m ta doaba baai ale ba nye m tia ase m nin cheŋ ba yeeŋa la.> 5Wa yaa wi nuru baai meena ale ta wa nyɔnɔwa pama la, ate ba jam wa nyɔnɔwa jigi a bek niŋ denɔwa ayen, <Fi ta m nyɔnɔwa pami ka dina?> 6Nuruwa yaa tulisi ayen, <M ta ka kpaam samɔnsa kook pami.> Wa yaa weeni wa ayen, <Pai fi pamini gbaŋka nwuli a ŋmarisi ka po ayen fi ta ka kpaam samɔnsa pisinu pami.> 7Wa ŋman pilim bek nuru wa choa dila dekdega, ate nuruwa tulisi wa ayen, <Mi ta ka ŋanbie busisa tusidi pami.> Wa ŋman pilim weeni wa mɛ ayen, <Wa ŋmarisi a nyo wa pamini gbaŋka po nwuli ayen wa ta ka ŋanbie busisa kobsinaaniŋ pami.> 8Kpagni yaa pak wa, wa korisika nyiŋ ayen tɛŋka po demma a korisi ale badek wie a gaam baai ale seba Wen kama. 9Dila nyiŋ, Mi a weeni kama ayen ni pai tɛŋzuk de jigsika a dɛ doata ale nuruba ate jigsika a dan kan boro, abe ba nye ni tia wenŋmazuk yeeŋa po.
10<<Nuru waai ale ta wensie wie fiisa zuk la, a ta wensie kama mɛ ale wakpiema. Waai mɛ abe ale kan ta wensie wie fiisa zuk la, a ka wensie mɛ ale wakpiema. 11Ni be dan ta wensie ale tɛŋzuk de jigsika, ka wana ale wa pai wensie jigsika a te fu? 12Ni be dan kan ta wensie ale nuru yoŋta ŋanta, ka wana ale wa pai ŋan baai ate fidek soa la a te fu? 13Tomteerɔ an baga a tom a te kpaga ŋaye, wa le kisa ka wanyi abe wa a yaali nwala yaase wa le va ka wanyi abe wa zɛri wanyi. Fi kan baga a tom a te Wen ale a yaali ligra.>>
14Farisiima ale wom nyaŋa de meena la, ba yaa nye wa a la dii nyiŋla, ba ka nuru baai ale a yaali ligra nna yegayega la. 15Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Nama ka baai ale chim nuruba nimbie po ayen ba pai ni chim nuru maŋsa alege ka Wen nyiini ale seba ni suiniimaŋa po ale ka diila. Dii nyiŋla, wie ŋaai ate nurubiik a pai ŋa a chim wamaŋsa la, ŋa ka ŋaai ate Wen kisa la.
16<<Moosis Sinsaŋŋa ale Wen biisiteerɔma biisaŋa a jam boro kama a ta jam paari diipo ate Jɔɔn Sokateerɔwa a jam boro la, alege a zaani dipo, nuruba a kasim a wom Wen naamu wamaŋsaŋa sinsaŋŋa kama ate waai meena a fɛ ayen ba jo bu po. 17Ku le nye moali ate wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋzuk de a muriŋ bɛ alege ku pagra kama ate Sinsaŋŋa wa fiik a muriŋ bɛ.
18<<Nuru waai a dan zɛri wa pok alege faari wa choa, kula nyɔnɔwa a nye ka kaboŋ. Nuru waai mɛ abe ale a faari nipok waai ate ba zɛri la, a nye ka kaboŋ mɛ.
19<<Jigsirɔ ale jam boro a kasim a jo garuk tii diak ale pagra nna yegayega la. Daa meena wa kasim jam a dɛ ka masim. 20Wa nansuiŋku nɔi jajak ale jam kasim a duak du, wa yuei jam le Lazarus, wa nyiŋka meena jam ka nira, 21wa jam a dɛ ka ŋandiin tii ale nyini jigsirɔ wa dɛka jigini a lo tɛŋka la ate baasaŋa mɛ a leeli wa niraŋa. 22Jajakka yaa jam kpi ate Wen maarɔma a ta wa ga nyo Abrayam nigoruk po. Ku an beni ya ate jigsirɔwa mɛ a kpi ate ba gu wa. 23Kpiluŋ tɛŋ wa jam bo ka nyiŋdomma po, jigsirɔwa yaa nya Abrayam niŋniŋŋa ale Lazarus a bo wa gauŋ. 24Wa yaa kaari a wi Abrayam ayen, <M koa Abrayam, ta jiirim ale mu abe fi tom ate Lazarus pai wa nandummu a lusi nyiam po ate bu zi m giŋgeluŋ ku nyiŋ, m nyiŋka meena ale a dom nna yegayega bolimu de po.>
25<<Alege Abrayam yaa tulisi wa ayen, <M biiga, a teeri diipo ate fi jam vua la, fi jam ta ka ŋanmaŋsaŋa meena alege Lazarus a jam soa ŋanbaataŋa meena. Alege yɔgyɔgla de, wa boro a dɛ ka masim dela jigini, alege ate fi ta nyiŋdomma. 26Daa dila nyiini, ka goluk ale limisa a dua tama ale fi suŋsuŋ, ate baai ale a yaali ayen ba nyini dela a jam fi jigi la, an baga a taamu, yaase waai mɛ abe dan a yaali ayen wa nyini fi jigi a jam tama jigi wa an baga a taamu.> 27Jigsirɔwa yaa weeni ayen, <Mi a saalim kama m koa ayen fi tom Lazarus ate wa cheŋ m kowa yenni, 28Mi ta ka m suata tinu. Tom ate wa ga kaam ba, kan daa di ba mɛ a cheena ka ninammu po.> 29Alege Abrayam yaa tulisi wa ayen, <Fi suataŋa a ta Moosis ale Wen biisiteerɔma sinsaŋŋa kama ate ŋa a kaam ba ayen ba lak tue a wom ŋa ale a weeni ba diila.> 30Jigsirɔwa a yaa ŋman tulisi ayen, <M koa Abrayam, aaya, alege nuru a dan yiri tama baai ale ka kpilima la po a cheŋ ga weeni ba ku a fɛ kama ayen ba basi ba tuimbaataŋa tomka.> 31Abrayam ŋman tulisi wa ayen, <Ba dan kan a yaali ayen ba wom Moosis ale Wen biisiteerɔma sinsaŋŋa ale a weeni diila, nuru a dan poom yiri kpilima po mɛ a ga weeni ba, ba kan diem a wom.> >>

english_text:
Faith and Service
(Matthew 18.6,7,21,22; Mark 9.42)
1Jesus said to his disciples:
There will always be something that causes people to sin. But anyone who causes them to sin is in for trouble. A person who causes even one of my little followers to sin 2would be better off thrown into the ocean with a heavy stone tied around their neck. 3 So be careful what you do.
Correct any followers of mine who sin, and forgive the ones who say they are sorry. 4Even if one of them mistreats you seven times in one day and says, “I am sorry,” you should still forgive that person.
5The apostles said to the Lord, “Make our faith stronger!”
6Jesus replied:
If you had faith no bigger than a tiny mustard seed, you could tell this mulberry tree to pull itself up, roots and all, and to plant itself in the ocean. And it would!
7If your servant comes in from plowing or from taking care of the sheep, would you say, “Welcome! Come on in and have something to eat”? 8No, you wouldn't say that. You would say, “Prepare me something to eat. Get ready to serve me, so I can have my meal. Then later on you can eat and drink.” 9Servants don't deserve special thanks for doing what they are supposed to do. 10And that's how it should be with you. When you've done all you should, then say, “We are merely servants, and we have simply done our duty.”
Ten Men with Leprosy
11On his way to Jerusalem, Jesus went along the border between Samaria and Galilee. 12As he was going into a village, ten men with leprosy came toward him. They stood at a distance 13and shouted, “Jesus, Master, have pity on us!”
14 Jesus looked at them and said, “Go show yourselves to the priests.”
On their way they were healed. 15When one of them discovered that he was healed, he came back, shouting praises to God. 16He bowed down at the feet of Jesus and thanked him. The man was from the country of Samaria.
17Jesus asked, “Weren't ten men healed? Where are the other nine? 18Why was this foreigner the only one who came back to thank God?” 19Then Jesus told the man, “You may get up and go. Your faith has made you well.”
God's Kingdom
(Matthew 24.23-28,37-41)
20Some Pharisees asked Jesus when God's kingdom would come. He answered, “God's kingdom isn't something you can see. 21There is no use saying, ‘Look! Here it is’ or ‘Look! There it is.’ God's kingdom is here with you.”
22Jesus said to his disciples:
The time will come when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, but you will not. 23When people say to you, “Look there,” or “Look here,” don't go looking for him. 24The day of the Son of Man will be like lightning flashing across the sky. 25But first he must suffer terribly and be rejected by the people of today. 26 When the Son of Man comes, things will be just as they were when Noah lived. 27 People were eating, drinking, and getting married right up to the day when Noah went into the big boat. Then the flood came and drowned everyone on earth.
28 When Lot lived, people were also eating and drinking. They were buying, selling, planting, and building. 29But on the very day Lot left Sodom, fiery flames poured down from the sky and killed everyone. 30The same will happen on the day when the Son of Man appears.
31 At that time no one on a rooftop should go down into the house to get anything. No one in a field should go back to the house for anything. 32 Remember what happened to Lot's wife.
33 People who try to save their lives will lose them, and those who lose their lives will save them. 34On that night two people will be sleeping in the same bed, but only one will be taken. The other will be left. 35-36Two women will be together grinding wheat, but only one will be taken. The other will be left.
37Then Jesus' disciples spoke up, “But where will this happen, Lord?”
Jesus said, “Where there is a corpse, there will always be vultures.”
translation_text:
1Yeezu yaa weeni wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ayen, <<Dii ale basi ate biem a nye la ale jam, alege ku ale bie a te waai ale basi ate biem a nye la. 2Ba dan pai ni kpienni a bobi wa ŋiri a yuk basi nyakpiemu po a zunchoŋŋa fi le nye ate bifiisaŋa de wanyi a nye biem. 3Dila nyiŋla, ni kpesi nidek ale wa dii meena ate ni a nye la. <<Fi suok a dan nye wabiok, toariŋ wa ale nin muna ate wa dan basi wa wabaataŋa tomka fi vɔŋ te wa. 4Wa be dan nye kaasi fu a paari ku nɔi buyopɔi dai yeŋ ale ŋman weeni fu ku nɔi buyopɔi ayen wa siak wa kaasuŋku, ku a fɛ kama ayen fi vɔŋ te wa.>>
5Tuimtomdɔma yaa weeni Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita ayen, <<Nye ate ti siaka a zuak a nyoro.>> 6Ate wa mɛ yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<Ni siaka a dan soa ase mastad biri la, ni baga weeni kiŋkaŋka de kama ayen, <Voori fidek a yiri ga zaani nyakpiemu po>, ate ka sum nye dila.
7<<Ka ni wana a nin ta tomteerɔ ate wa a kpa yaase wa a kasi piisa ate wa nyini peelim a jam jo ate fi deri weeni wa ayen, <Jam kali a dɛ ŋandiinta?> 8Wa kan goanti a weeni wa kama ayen, <Dik junɔi ŋandiinta a te mu abe fi gomsi fidek a limisi mu ate m ga dɛ abe m nyu nueri, dila ŋaaŋnyiŋ abe fi mɛ a dɛ abe fi nyu.> 9Wa kan nye tomteerɔwa jiam, dii nyiŋ la wa nye ka dii ale magsi la. 10Ku be ka dila, nama mɛ jigi. Ni dan tom Wen ale weeni ni ayen ni tom diila a nueri, ni weeni nidek ayen, <Tama ka tomteerɔba. Dila nyiŋla ku an magsi wa nye ti jiam. Ti tom ka dii ale magsi ayen ti tom la.> >>
11Yeezu ale jam bo suiku po a cheŋ Jerusalem la, wa jam va ka Samaria ale Galili tɛŋsa suŋsuŋ po a cheŋ. 12Wa jam boro a jo ka tɛŋ fiik po a yaa ga zik gama pi ate ba za nna niŋniŋa, 13a kaari ate ku a jueli ayen, <<Ti Nyɔnɔ, Yeezu, ta jiirim ale ti.>> 14Yeezu ale nya ba la, wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Ni cheŋ a ga pai nidek a sak kaabteerɔma.>> Ba ale cheŋ la ba yaa deri nya nyiŋyɔgsa. 15Ba wanyi ale chuiri nya ale wa ta nyiŋyɔgsa la, wa yaa pilim ŋmani ale a pak Wen ate ku a jueli nna yegayega 16a yaa jam paari Yeezu a lo wa naŋsa tɛŋ a nye wa jiam. Nuruwa a jam ka Samaria denɔ. 17Yeezu yaa bek wa ayen, <<Daa nuruba pi ale nya nyiŋyɔgsa la? Mbala neokku a bo ka bɛ? 18Ba wanyi mɛ la an baga pilim ŋman jam a te Wen pimpaukwa ka nichaanɔwa dɛ nyiini?>> 19Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Yiri zaani a cheŋ. Fi siaka ale basi ate fi nya nyiŋyɔgsa.>>
20Farisiima gela yaa bek Yeezu ayen, <<Ka dimpo ate Wen naamu ale jamu?>> Yeezu yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<Wen naamu an cheena ale daana ayen ni kpesi nya, 21yaase nuru kan weeni ayen, <Nya de, bu bo ka dela,> yaase <Bu bo ka dula.> Wen naamu a bo ka ni suŋsuŋ.>>
22Wa yaa weeni wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ayen, <<Daa cheena kama ate ni le kasim a yaali ayen ni nya Mi Saalɔbiika danni dinyi, alege ni kan nya. 23Nuruba abe le weeni ni ayen, <Ni nya dula, ni nya dela.> Ba dan weeni dila, ni kan cheŋ, ni be kan va ba mɛ. 24Ase ŋmoruk a nyiem ale a ni ate wenni a nyaksi taam de a ŋman nyaksi taam de la, Mi Saalɔbiika mɛ danni a dan jam ku le nye ka dila dekdega. 25Alege wa le dɛ niŋ a nam nna yegayega ate gaŋka de ale zɛri wa. 26Ase ku ale jam ka dii Nowa vaaŋa po la, ku ale chim ka dila dekdega Mi Saalɔbiika daaŋa po. 27Nowa daaŋa po, nuruma a jam a dɛ kama ale nyu a buk ale a faari nipooba ale pai ba liema a yalisi ate ku paari dii ate Nowa a jo ŋaaruŋku po alege ate nyiamu a jam kaasi jaab meena. 28Ku jam nye ka dila dekdega Lɔti daaŋa po. Dila po wa, waai meena a kasim jam a dɛ kama ale a nyu ale a da diak mɛ ale a bori ale a sɛ yie. 29Da dii danni ate Lɔti basi Sodom tɛŋka la, bolim ale tintain tuila ale jam nyini wenŋmazuk a jam ko ba meena. 30Ku le nye ka dila dekdega da dii dai ate Mi Saalɔbiika ale pai m dek a sak nuruba la.
31<<Da dila danni, nuru waai a dan bo wa gboŋ zuk wa kan ŋman siŋ jo wa dɔkku po ayen wa pai wa ŋanta, dila dekdega nuru waai mɛ ale bo peelim wa talim po la, a kan ŋman pilim jam yeri ya. 32Ni teeri Lɔti powa wari! 33Nuru waai ale pii nyiŋ a nye ayen wa vari wadek nyuvuri a basi la, ale jɔk di kama. Waai mɛ abe ale a jɔk wa nyuvuri la, le vari di a basi kama. 34Mi a weeni ayen yok ku la, nuruba baye ale ba dua ta yeŋ po a goa, ate Wen jam pai ba wanyi a ta cheŋ alege nwala a dueni. 35Nipooba baye mɛ ale maa chaab a boro a num zom ate Wen jam pai ba wanyi a ta cheŋ alege nwala a zaani. 36Nuruba baye ale bo kaduk po a kpa ate Wen jam pai ba wanyi a ta cheŋ alege nwala a zaani.>> 37Wa ŋaaŋviirɔma yaa bek wa ayen, <<Ti Nyɔnɔ Yeezu Kirisita, ka bɛ ate nyaŋa de ale nye?>> Wa yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<Jakpiuk ale dua juijui la, duinsa a bo ka dula.>>

english_text:
A Widow and a Judge
1Jesus told his disciples a story about how they should keep on praying and never give up:
2In a town there was once a judge who didn't fear God or care about people. 3In that same town there was a widow who kept going to the judge and saying, “Make sure that I get fair treatment in court.”
4For a while the judge refused to do anything. Finally, he said to himself, “Even though I don't fear God or care about people, 5I will help this widow because she keeps on bothering me. If I don't help her, she will wear me out.”
6The Lord said:
Think about what that crooked judge said. 7 Won't God protect his chosen ones who pray to him day and night? Won't he be concerned for them? 8He will surely hurry and help them. But when the Son of Man comes, will he find on this earth anyone with faith?
A Pharisee and a Tax Collector
9Jesus told a story to some people who thought they were better than others and who looked down on everyone else:
10Two men went into the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee and the other a tax collector. 11The Pharisee stood over by himself and prayed, “God, I thank you that I am not greedy, dishonest, and unfaithful in marriage like other people. And I am really glad that I am not like that tax collector over there. 12I go without eating for two days a week, and I give you one tenth of all I earn.”
13 The tax collector stood off at a distance and did not think he was good enough even to look up toward heaven. He was so sorry for what he had done that he pounded his chest and prayed, “God, have pity on me! I am such a sinner.”
14 Then Jesus said, “When the two men went home, it was the tax collector and not the Pharisee who was pleasing to God. If you put yourself above others, you will be put down. But if you humble yourself, you will be honored.”
Jesus Blesses Little Children
(Matthew 19.13-15; Mark 10.13-16)
15Some people brought their little children for Jesus to bless. But when his disciples saw them doing this, they told the people to stop bothering him. 16So Jesus called the children over to him and said, “Let the children come to me! Don't try to stop them. People who are like these children belong to God's kingdom. 17You will never get into God's kingdom unless you enter it like a child!”
A Rich and Important Man
(Matthew 19.16-30; Mark 10.17-31)
18An important man asked Jesus, “Good Teacher, what must I do to have eternal life?”
19Jesus said, “Why do you call me good? Only God is good. 20 You know the commandments: ‘Be faithful in marriage. Do not murder. Do not steal. Do not tell lies about others. Respect your father and mother.’ ”
21He told Jesus, “I have obeyed all these commandments since I was a young man.”
22When Jesus heard this, he said, “There is one thing you still need to do. Go and sell everything you own! Give the money to the poor, and you will have riches in heaven. Then come and be my follower.” 23When the man heard this, he was sad, because he was very rich.
24Jesus saw how sad the man was. So he said, “It's terribly hard for rich people to get into God's kingdom! 25In fact, it's easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to get into God's kingdom.”
26When the crowd heard this, they asked, “How can anyone ever be saved?”
27Jesus replied, “There are some things that people cannot do, but God can do anything.”
28Peter said, “Remember, we left everything to be your followers!”
29Jesus answered, “You can be sure that anyone who gives up home or wife or brothers or family or children because of God's kingdom 30will be given much more in this life. And in the future world they will have eternal life.”
Jesus Again Tells about His Death
(Matthew 20.17-19; Mark 10.32-34)
31Jesus took the twelve apostles aside and said:
We are now on our way to Jerusalem. Everything that the prophets wrote about the Son of Man will happen there. 32He will be handed over to foreigners, who will make fun of him, mistreat him, and spit on him. 33They will beat him and kill him, but three days later he will rise to life.
34The apostles did not understand what Jesus was talking about. They could not understand, because the meaning of what he said was hidden from them.
Jesus Heals a Blind Beggar
(Matthew 20.29-34; Mark 10.46-52)
35When Jesus was coming close to Jericho, a blind man sat begging beside the road. 36The man heard the crowd walking by and asked what was happening. 37Some people told him that Jesus from Nazareth was passing by. 38So the blind man shouted, “Jesus, Son of David, have pity on me!” 39The people who were going along with Jesus told the man to be quiet. But he shouted even louder, “Son of David, have pity on me!”
40Jesus stopped and told some people to bring the blind man over to him. When the blind man was getting near, Jesus asked, 41“What do you want me to do for you?”
“Lord, I want to see!” he answered.
42Jesus replied, “Look and you will see! Your eyes are healed because of your faith.” 43At once the man could see, and he went with Jesus and started thanking God. When the crowds saw what happened, they praised God.
translation_text:
1Yeezu yaa magsi wamagsini a sak wa ŋaaŋviirɔma. Wa weeni wamagsini kama ayen di deŋsi ba kpa ate ba kasim a puusi Wen. 2Wa weeni ayen, <<Tɛŋ kpieŋ po ate buteerɔ a jam boro waai ale kaa chali Wen yaase wa niŋ a bo nuru po. 3Pukɔgi mɛ ale jam bo tɛŋ kala po a kasim a cheŋ nuruwa de jigi a saalim wa ayen wa maari wa ate wa nye buusa ale wa dachiak. 4Ku jam beni ka nna yegayega alege wa jam zɛri wa maarika kama. Alege ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ wa weeni wadek ayen, <M seba ayen m kan chali Wen ya, m be kan zuli nurubiik mɛ 5alege, pukɔgini de ale kasim a daani mu diila, m le nya ku zuk ate wa nya wa ale a yaali diila. M dan kan nye dila, wa ale kasim a jam kama ate m ga jiak.> >> 6Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita yaa weeni ayen, <<Ni wom buteerɔ bioku de ale weeni diila. 7Nama a poli ayen, Wen a kan vari wadek nuruma a basi, baai ale kaari a te wa kantueŋ ale yok la? Wa ale beni? 8Basi ate m weeni a sak ni ayen wa le bo buusa a te ba ka nna nwuli. Alege Mi Saalɔbiika a dan ŋman pilim jam tɛŋzuk de m le nya siaka nuruba jigiya?>>
9Yeezu yaa ŋman jam magsi wamagsini di choa a te nuru baai ale jam a poli ayen ba ka wayɔrisima nyam ale kan pai waai meena a chim nuru la. Wa yaa magsi wamagsini ayen, 10<<Nuruba baye ale jam Wen yenni po ayen ba puusi Wen. Ba wanyi a jam ka Farisii, wanyi mɛ lampoo cheesirɔ. 11Farisiiwa a yaa yiti zaani wadek wa nyiini a puusi Wen ayen, <Wen ya, mi a nye fi jiam, m daa nuru baai chaab ale a vari la, yaase baai ale kan ta wensie la, yaase kaboŋ nyeerɔba la. Mi a te fi jiam mɛ ayen m daa lampoo cheesirɔwa ale za dula la. 12Mi a bobi nɔi ka buye bakoai po, mi a labi m ŋantaŋa ka pi a pai bunyi a te Wen.> 13Alege lampoo cheesirɔwa a za niŋniŋ a kan poom a yaali ayen wa zak zuk a nya wenŋmazuwa, a nak wa suinummu weeni ayen, <Wen, ta jiirim ale mu diila, m ka wabaata nyɔnɔ.> 14Basi ate m weeni a sak ni ayen daa Farisiiwa alege ka lampoo cheesirɔwa de ate Wen vɔŋ wa wabaataŋa a te wa, alege ate wa yaa kuli yeri. Nuru waai ale a pai wadek a chim nuru kpioŋ la, ba le zaab wa alege waai ale a zaab wadek la, ale chim ka nuru kpioŋ.>>
15Nuru ba gela a yaa ta ba buluata a jam Yeezu jigi ayen wa pai wa nisa a vi ba zuk. Wa ŋaaŋviirɔma ale nya dila la, ba yaa toariŋ ba, 16alege Yeezu yaa wi ba ate ba jam wa jigi ayen, <<Ni basi ate bisaŋa jam mi jigi. Ni kan yiak ba, ale ka bala ale soa Wen naamu. 17Wensie ate mi a weeni ni, waai a dan kan tuesi Wen naamu ase biik la wa kan baga a jo bu po.>>
18Dai yeŋ ate kpagi dinyi a yaa bek Yeezu ayen, <<Sagrɔ maŋŋa, m nin nye se ale m nya nyuvuri dii ale kan ta kpeglimka la?>> 19Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi a wi mu ayen nuru maŋŋa? Nuru maŋ a karo, ka Wen nyiini. 20Fidek a seba Sinsaŋŋa kama, ŋa weeni kama ayen, <Kan nye kaboŋsa, kan ko nuru, kan zu, kan chim seerɔ waai ale a velim la. Zuli fi ko ale fi ma.> >> 21Ate wa weeni ayen, <<Ŋade meena mi va ŋa kama a nyini m paalim po.>> 22Yeezu ale wom nna la, wa yaa weeni nuruwa ayen, <<Fi tali ka wayeŋ ate fi nye. Pai jaab meena ate fi ta la a da a pai ligraŋa a te ŋanjaksa ate fi nya jigsika wenŋmazuk. Fi dan nye dila, fi yaa va mi.>> 23Nuruwa ale wom nna la, wa sui a yaa deri kaasi dii nyiŋla, wa jam ka jigsirɔ. 24Yeezu ale nya ale wa sui kaasi la, wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Ku toa kama ate ŋanta nyam a baga a jo Wen naamu po. 25Ku ka moali ate laalaakomi a baga va garuk pein vɔrup po a nyini a gaam jigsirɔ a nin baga a jo Wen naamu po.>> 26Baai ale jam wom nna la a yaa bek ayen, <<Be ka wana ale wa nya varibasika?>> 27Alege Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Dii ate nurubiik an baga nye la, Wen baga nye kama.>>
28Piita yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Nya, tama basi ti yeeŋa kama ale jam va fu.>> 29Yeezu yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Nuru waai a dan basi wa yeri ale wa pok ale wa suata ale wa ko ale wa ma yaase wa bisa Wen naamu nyiŋ, 30Wen ale te kula nyɔnɔwa ŋanta bala chaab nna yegayega gaam taam wa ale poom ta diila, ate chum diipo wa nya nyuvuri dii ale kan ta kpeglimka la.>>
31Wa yaa weeni wa ŋaaŋviirɔma pi ale bayewa ayen, <<Ni nya ti a cheŋ ka Jerusalem tɛŋka, ate Wen biisiteerɔma ale ŋmarisi dii meena a ta va Saalɔbiika la a chim wensie. 32Boan nyiŋŋa, ba le sum yik mu kama, a pai mu nyo nuru baai ale kan daa Juuba la nisima po ba ale la mu, a chesi tintueta a basi m nyiŋ 33ba ale miiri mu abe ba ko mu, alege daa ŋata dai, m le yiti kum po.>> 34Yeezu ale biisi nna la, wa ŋaaŋviirɔma an jam miŋ ku kiriya. Dii nyiŋla Wen an jam lak ku kiri a sak ba, ate ba an miŋ wa ale a biisi diila.
35Yeezu ale jam moata Jeriko tɛŋka la, yio ale jam kala suiku niŋ a juisi. 36Wa ale wom ale nuru boanni a va wa tɛŋ a taam la, wa yaa bek ayen, <<Ka boa ale la?>> 37Nuruma yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Ka Yeezu Nazaret denɔwa ale a taam.>> 38Yiowa yaa kaari a weeni ayen, <<Yeezu, Deevid nidoabinni, ta jiirim ale mu.>> 39Nuruma ale jam dɛ niŋka la a yaa weeni wa ayen wa goori wa wanni alege wa zɛri ale a kaari nna yegayega a gum du a weeni wa ayen, <<Deevid Nidoabinni, ta jiirim ale mu.>> 40Yeezu yaa zaani a weeni ayen ba ta nuruwa a jam wa jigi. Wa ale jam paari la, Yeezu yaa bek wa ayen, 41<<Fi a yaali ayen m nye ka boa a te fu?>> Wa yaa weeni wa ayen, <<M Nyɔnɔ Yeezu Kirisita, mi a yaali ayen fi nye kama ate m ninaŋa a lagri a te mu.>> 42Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Be a nya. Fi siaka a basi kama ate fi nya nyiŋyɔgsa.>> 43Yeezu ale weeni dila la, wa ninaŋa deri lagri ate wa a nya, ate wa yaa va Yeezu a te Wen pimpauk. Nuru boanni ale nya nna la, ba meena yaa te Wen pimpauk.

english_text:
Zacchaeus
1Jesus was going through Jericho, 2where a man named Zacchaeus lived. He was in charge of collecting taxes and was very rich. 3-4Jesus was heading his way, and Zacchaeus wanted to see what he was like. But Zacchaeus was a short man and could not see over the crowd. So he ran ahead and climbed up into a sycamore tree.
5When Jesus got there, he looked up and said, “Zacchaeus, hurry down! I want to stay with you today.” 6Zacchaeus hurried down and gladly welcomed Jesus.
7Everyone who saw this started grumbling, “This man Zacchaeus is a sinner! And Jesus is going home to eat with him.”
8Later that day Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord, “I will give half of my property to the poor. And I will now pay back four times as much to everyone I have ever cheated.”
9Jesus said to Zacchaeus, “Today you and your family have been saved, because you are a true son of Abraham. 10 The Son of Man came to look for and to save people who are lost.”
A Story about Ten Servants
(Matthew 25.14-30)
11 The crowd was still listening to Jesus as he was getting close to Jerusalem. Many of them thought that God's kingdom would soon appear, 12and Jesus told them this story:
A prince once went to a foreign country to be crowned king and then to return. 13But before leaving, he called in ten servants and gave each of them some money. He told them, “Use this to earn more money until I get back.”
14But the people of his country hated him, and they sent messengers to the foreign country to say, “We don't want this man to be our king.”
15After the prince had been made king, he returned and called in his servants. He asked them how much they had earned with the money they had been given.
16The first servant came and said, “Sir, with the money you gave me I have earned ten times as much.”
17“That's fine, my good servant!” the king said. “Since you have shown that you can be trusted with a small amount, you will be given ten cities to rule.”
18The second one came and said, “Sir, with the money you gave me, I have earned five times as much.”
19The king said, “You will be given five cities.”
20Another servant came and said, “Sir, here is your money. I kept it safe in a handkerchief. 21You are a hard man, and I was afraid of you. You take what isn't yours, and you harvest crops you didn't plant.”
22“You worthless servant!” the king told him. “You have condemned yourself by what you have just said. You knew I am a hard man, taking what isn't mine and harvesting what I've not planted. 23Why didn't you put my money in the bank? On my return, I could have had the money together with interest.”
24Then he said to some other servants standing there, “Take the money away from him and give it to the servant who earned ten times as much.”
25But they said, “Sir, he already has ten times as much!”
26 The king replied, “Those who have something will be given more. But everything will be taken away from those who don't have anything. 27Now bring me the enemies who didn't want me to be their king. Kill them while I watch!”
Jesus Enters Jerusalem
(Matthew 21.1-11; Mark 11.1-11; John 12.12-19)
28When Jesus had finished saying all this, he went on toward Jerusalem. 29As he was getting near Bethphage and Bethany on the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples on ahead. 30He told them, “Go into the next village, where you will find a young donkey that has never been ridden. Untie the donkey and bring it here. 31If anyone asks why you are doing this, just say, ‘The Lord needs it.’ ”
32They went off and found everything just as Jesus had said. 33While they were untying the donkey, its owners asked, “Why are you doing that?”
34They answered, “The Lord needs it.”
35Then they led the donkey to Jesus. They put some of their clothes on its back and helped Jesus get on. 36And as he rode along, the people spread clothes on the road in front of him. 37When Jesus started down the Mount of Olives, his large crowd of disciples were happy and praised God because of all the miracles they had seen. 38 They shouted,
“Blessed is the king who comes
in the name of the Lord!
Peace in heaven
and glory to God.”
39Some Pharisees in the crowd said to Jesus, “Teacher, make your disciples stop shouting!”
40But Jesus answered, “If they keep quiet, these stones will start shouting.”
41When Jesus came closer and could see Jerusalem, he cried 42and said:
It is too bad that today your people don't know what will bring them peace! Now it is hidden from them. 43Jerusalem, the time will come when your enemies will build walls around you to attack you. Armies will surround you and close in on you from every side. 44They will level you to the ground and kill your people. Not one stone in your buildings will be left on top of another. This will happen because you did not see that God had come to save you.
Jesus in the Temple
(Matthew 21.12-17; Mark 11.15-19; John 2.13-22)
45When Jesus entered the temple, he started chasing out the people who were selling things. 46 He told them, “The Scriptures say, ‘My house should be a place of worship.’ But you have made it a place where robbers hide!”
47 Each day, Jesus kept on teaching in the temple. So the chief priests, the teachers of the Law of Moses, and some other important people tried to have him killed. 48But they could not find a way to do it, because everyone else was eager to listen to him.
translation_text:
1Yeezu yaa ga jo Jeriko tɛŋka a va ka po a taam. 2Nuru ale jam boro wa yuei ale Zakiyos. Wa jam ka lampoo cheesirɔba kpagi a jigsi nna yegayega. 3Wa yaa jam a yaali ayen wa nya Yeezu alege wa an jam baga dii nyiŋla, wa jam gela kama ate nuru boanni a yaa jam lik wa. 4Wa yaa chali dɛ niŋ a ga jueli kiŋkaŋ ayen wa nya wa dii nyiŋla Yeezu jam va ka dula a taam. 5Yeezu ale jam paari dula jigini la, wa yaa zak nya wa weeni wa ayen, <<Zakiyos, nye nwuli a siŋ tɛŋ, dii nyiŋla, ku a fɛ kama ayen m goa fi yenni jinla.>> 6Wa yaa nye nwuli a siŋ a tuesi wa nalimnyiini. 7Nuru baai ale jam nya dila la, yaa jam a ŋuuni a weeni ayen, <<Wa jo ayen wa chim ka tuimbaata nyɔnɔwa de nichaanɔ.>> 8Zakiyos yaa yiri zaani a weeni Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita ayen, <<Wom, m Nyɔnɔ Yeezu Kirisita, m le pai ŋan baai meena ate mi ta la geli a te ŋanjaksa, abe m daam dan velim tuesi nuru jaab, m le tuni wa jaab wala dekdega ku nɔi bunaansi.>> 9Yeezu yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Varibasika jam yenni de po jinla kama, wa ale maa ka Abrayam nidoabinni po wanyi la nyiŋ. 10Boan nyiŋŋa, Mi Saalɔbiika a jam ayen m gisi abe m vari baai ale bɛ la a basi.>>
11Nuruma ale jam wom wieŋa de la, wa yaa magsi wamagsini, dii nyiŋla wa jam moata Jerusalem tɛŋka kama, ate ba jam a poli ayen Wen naamu ale jam ka nwuli. 12Wa yaa weeni ayen, <<Nuru kpioŋ ale jam boro, a yaa yiri dai yeŋ a cheŋ satɛŋ nna niŋniŋa ayen ba bobi wa naam abe wa ŋman pilim jam. 13Wa yaa wi wa tomteerɔma po pi a chari ba wanyi wanyi ligra a soa si chaab la alege weeni ba ayen, <Ni pai ligraŋa de a gerim ate m cheŋ abe m pilim jam.> 14Wa tɛŋka demma a jam kisi wa kama, ate ba yaa tom nuruba ate ba saŋ wa ŋaaŋ a ga weeni ayen, <Ti kan yaali nuruwa de ayen wa chim ti naaba.> 15Ba yaa jam bobi nuruwa naamu ate wa pilim jam. Wa ale jam paari la, wa yaa wi wa tomteerɔma ayen ba jam ate wa bek ba nya ase ba gerim a nya ka boan nyuenta. 16Ba wanyi a yaa dɛ niŋ a jam weeni ayen, <Nyɔnɔ, fi ligraŋa vi ka ku nɔi pi a gum du.> 17Nuruwa yaa weeni wa ayen, <Fi nye wamaŋ, tomteerɔ. Fi ale ta wensie ale wie fiisa la nyiŋ ale soa ate mi a pai tɛŋ kpieŋsa pi a nyo fi nisima po ayen fi a nya si meena zuk.> 18Tomteerɔ waai ale pai a saŋ la a jam weeni wa ayen, <Nyɔnɔ, fi ligraŋa vi ka ku nɔi bunu.> 19Wa yaa weeni tomteerɔ wala mɛ ayen, <Fi soa ka tɛŋ kpieŋsa sinu zuk a nya.> 20Tomteerɔ wanyi mɛ a jam weeni wa ayen, <M nyɔnɔ, fi ligraŋa ale nna. Mi pai di a bobi ka lakki po a dueni fu. 21Mi a chali fu kama, dii nyiŋla, fi nyeka toa kama, fi a tuesi ka ŋan baai ale kan daa fi ŋanta la nuruba jigi ale a che ŋan baai mɛ ate fi an bori la.>
22<<Wa nyɔnɔwa yaa weeni wa ayen, <Fi ka tomteerɔ kaasuŋ, m le pai ka fidek biika a dak fi kaasuŋku a sak fu. Fi ale seba ayen mi nyeka toa, a tuesi ŋan baai ale kan daa m ŋanta la nuruba jigi ale a che jabuui ate mi an bori la. 23Be ka boa ale soa ate fi an pai m ligni a te nuru ate wa ta a tom ate diipo ate m le pilim jam la m nya nyuenta di po?> 24Wa yaa weeni nuru baai ale jam za dula la ayen, <Ni tuesi ligbinni ale bo wa jigi la a te tomteerɔ waai ale ta ligbie piwa la.> 25Ba yaa weeni wa ayen, <M nyɔnɔ, wa ta ka ligbie pi?> 26Mi a weeni ayen waai nisa po ale ta la, wala ale ŋman nya ŋanta ka nna yegayega a gum du, alege waai nisa po ale poom kan ta la, kula nyɔnɔwa ale poom ta dii maga la, wa ale jɔk bala mɛ kama a gum du. 27Alege mi dachaasaŋa, baai ale jam kan a yaali ayen mi chim ba Naab la, ta ba a jam dela a ko ba ate m nya.>>
28Yeezu ale biisi wanni de a nueri la, wa yaa dɛ niŋ a cheŋ Jerusalem tɛŋka.
29Wa ale jam moata tɛŋ fiisaŋa, Betfaaji ale Betani ate si moata Olivi Guuku la, Yeezu yaa tom wa ŋaaŋviirɔma po baye 30a weeni ba ayen, <<Ni cheŋ tɛŋ fiik kaai ale bo ni niŋ la. Ni dan ga jo ka po ni le nya boniŋ ate nuru waai an diem do ka nya la ale ka bobi za.
