10Paul went down and bent over Eutychus. He took him in his arms and said, “Don't worry! He's alive.” 11After Paul had gone back upstairs, he broke bread, and ate with us. He then spoke until dawn and left. 12Then the followers took the young man home alive and were very happy.
The Voyage from Troas to Miletus
13Paul decided to travel by land to Assos. The rest of us went on ahead by ship, and we were to take him aboard there. 14When he met us in Assos, he came aboard, and we sailed on to Mitylene. 15The next day we came to a place near Chios, and the following day we reached Samos. The day after that we sailed to Miletus. 16Paul had decided to sail on past Ephesus, because he did not want to spend too much time in Asia. He was in a hurry and wanted to be in Jerusalem in time for Pentecost.
Paul Says Goodbye to the Church Leaders of Ephesus
17From Miletus, Paul sent a message for the church leaders at Ephesus to come and meet with him. 18When they got there, he said:
You know everything I did during the time I was with you when I first came to Asia. 19Some of the Jews plotted against me and caused me a lot of sorrow and trouble. But I served the Lord and was humble. 20When I preached in public or taught in your homes, I didn't hold back from telling anything that would help you. 21I told Jews and Gentiles to turn to God and have faith in our Lord Jesus.
22I don't know what will happen to me in Jerusalem, but I must obey God's Spirit and go there. 23In every city I visit, I am told by the Holy Spirit that I will be put in jail and will be in trouble in Jerusalem. 24 But I don't care what happens to me, as long as I finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me to do. And this work is to tell the good news about God's gift of undeserved grace.
25I have gone from place to place, preaching to you about God's kingdom, but now I know that none of you will ever see me again. 26I tell you today I am no longer responsible for any of you! 27I have told you everything God wants you to know. 28Look after yourselves and everyone the Holy Spirit has placed in your care. Be like shepherds to God's church. It is the flock he bought with the blood of his own Son.
29I know that after I am gone, others will come like fierce wolves to attack you. 30Some of your own people will tell lies to win over the Lord's followers. 31Be on your guard! Remember how day and night for three years I kept warning you with tears in my eyes.
32I now place you in God's care. Remember the message about his gift of undeserved grace! This message can help you and give you what belongs to you as God's people. 33I have never wanted anyone's money or clothes. 34You know how I have worked with my own hands to make a living for myself and my friends. 35By everything I did, I showed how you should work to help everyone who is weak. Remember that our Lord Jesus said, “More blessings come from giving than from receiving.”
36After Paul had finished speaking, he knelt down with all of them and prayed. 37Everyone cried and hugged and kissed him. 38They were especially sad because Paul had told them, “You will never see me again.”
Then they went with him to the ship.
translation_text:
1Wɔkwɔkka de ale ga nueri la, Pɔɔl yaa wi Kirisita bisaŋa jigi yeŋ a biisi deŋsi ba kpa ale ge a banti ba ale a cheŋ Masidoniya. 2Wa ale nyiem gilim Masidoniya tɛŋka meena a biisi deŋsi ba kpa la, wa yaa cheŋ Girik tɛŋka. 3Dula jigini, wa jam goa ka chiisa sita. Wa ale jam boro a gomsi ayen wa jueli ŋaaruŋ a cheŋ Siriya tɛŋka la, wa yaa miŋ ayen Juuma a jam a poli ka wa sitika. Wa yaa tagri wa popolaŋa a pilim ŋmani va Masidoniya a taam cheŋ Siriya. 4Nuru wanyi ale jam boro ate ba a wi wa ayen Pirrus. Wa nyini ka Beria tɛŋka. Wa biik yuei jam ale Sopaata. Biika de ale jam maa va Pɔɔl a cheŋ. Baai mɛ ale jam maa va wa a cheŋ la, ale Arisitaakus ale Sekundus. Bala nyini ka Tesalonika. Mbala jam ale Gayus, wa nyini ka Daabe tɛŋka, ale Tikikus ale Torofimus. Bala mɛ nyini ka Asia tɛŋka. Timoti mɛ a jam maa va wa cheŋ kama. 5Bade a jam dɛka niŋ cheŋ ga bo Torowas a limisi tama. 6Alege tama a basi Filipai tɛŋka a lo benni a jueli ba le jam de tigi dii ate ba kan nyo dabinta di ŋandiintaŋa po la ŋaaŋnyiŋ. Daa ŋanu dai ti yaa paari ba Torowas tɛŋka po, ti jam bo dula ka daa ŋayopɔi.
7Bakoanni piilimka dai, ti meena yaa tu chaab ti de ŋandiinta ate Pɔɔl yaa biisi te tigsuŋku. Dii nyiŋla wa jam a poli kama ayen dai dii ale paasaŋ la wa basi dula jigini. Wa jam kasim a biisi kama ate ku paari yok suŋsuŋ. 8Zeuŋta yegayega ate ba jam toati zaani ŋmazuk kiari po ate tama jam tigsi kala. 9Nidoabili wanyi ale jam maa kala dɔkku tuokparuku zuk diipo ate Pɔɔl jam boro a biisi la. Nuruwa de yuei ale Yutikus. Goom yaa jam yik wa ate wa goa a baŋ wadek a yaa nyini kiari dii ale saari butawa la zuk a jam lo tɛŋ. Ba ale jam zak wa la, ba ga a nya ale wa kpi kama. 10Pɔɔl yaa siŋ tɛŋ a kpi duna tɛŋ gbaari wa ale ge weeni ayen, <<Ni kan basi ate ku daani ni, wa vua kama.>> 11Pɔɔl yaa ŋman jueli gboŋku zuk ate wa ale ŋaaŋviirɔma mbala a maa chaab a dɛ ŋandiintaŋa. Wa ale ga biisi ale ba ate ku beni nna yegayega ate wenbinni a poom moata pusika la, wa yaa basi ba ale cheŋ jigi yoŋ. 12Ba yaa ta nidoabinni a kuli yeri ale suipeentik. Wa an jam kpi ya.
13Ti yaa cheŋ ga jo ŋaaruŋku po a cheŋ Asos tɛŋka. Pɔɔl jam nye wa popola kama wa va suik a cheŋ Asos ate ti yaa jam paari wa dula jigini ate ti cheŋ. 14Wa yaa ale jam paari tama Asos tɛŋka la, ti yaa pai wa a nyo ŋaaruŋku po a cheŋ Mitiliini. 15Ti yaa jueli ŋaaruŋku a cheŋ dila veenti vari a va Kiyos tɛŋka a taam paari Samos tɛŋka. Vari ale ga veenti la, ti yaa paari Militus. 16Ti jam gaam Efisos kama dii nyiŋla wa kan jam a yaali ayen wa beni Asia tɛŋka. Dii nyiŋ ate wa jam a kpabi la, wa jam a yaali kama ayen wa paari Jerusalem ate wa dan baga abe wa paari Daa Pisinu Tigini.
17Pɔɔl yaa zaani Militus a tom tuntomiŋ a te Efisos a weeni Efisos Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab la kpaŋŋa ayen ba tu wa Militus. 18Ba ale jam tu wa la, wa yaa weeni ba ayen, <<Nama dek seba mi boka ale ka diila kama a zaani da dii danni ate mi jam Asia tɛŋka meena po dela la. 19Nama dek seba ayen m jam zaabi m dek ka nna yegayega, m kasim a kum ka ninyiam a tom m tuimaŋa ase yɔma la a te Naawen. Diipo ate m jam a tom dila la, ninam nna yegayega ale jam m jigi dii nyiŋla Juuma ale jam a nye mu gaasa. 20Nama dek abe seba mɛ ayen diipo ate m jam nyini peelim ale maa jo ni yeeŋa po a sak ni la, mi an zɛri ni sakka wa dii ale di te ni maarika la. 21M jam weeni Juuma ale baai ale kan daa Juuma la, ayen ku a fɛ kama ayen ba basi ba wabaataŋa tomka abe ba va Naawen a pai badek a te Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu. 22Yɔgyɔgla de ka Wen Chiika ale weeni mu ayen m cheŋ Jerusalem ate m siak alege m zɛ dii ale di nye mu dula la. 23Alege m seba kama ayen Wen Chiika ale kaam mu ayen m seba ale jigi meena ate mi a cheŋ la, ba le yik mu a lik, daanika mɛ le jam m jigi. 24Alege mi dek nyuvunni, mi kan nya di ase di ka jaab mi jigi la. Mi a yaali kama ayen m tom tuin dii ate Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu a te mu la a nueri. Tuini de ale m weeni a sak nuruba wapaala wamaŋsaŋa a magsi chaab ale wamaŋ sii ate wa nye a te nuruba ŋmanteka nyiŋla.
25<<M nyiem nama meena po kama a sak Wen naamu wie. Yɔgyɔgla de, m be seba kama ayen ni wanyi la kan ŋman nya mu. 26Dila nyiŋla, mi a weeni ni kama ayen ni wanyi abe dan bɛ kula daa mi niŋ ale la. 27Dii nyiŋla, mi an tali wari a magsi chaab ale Wen ale a poli ayen wa nye diila. 28Dila nyiŋla, ni be ŋmasi a nya nidek ale nuru baai ate Wen Chiika a pai te ni la zuk nalimnyiini. Wen pai ka wadek biika ziimu a da Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab la. Ni be a nya ba zuk ase naapeerik ale a nya wa piisa zuk diila. 29M seba a chak kama ayen mi dan basi ni ale cheŋ, nuruba ale jam jo ni suŋsuŋ. Ba a nye ase ka piina ale jo piisa suŋsuŋ a kaasi ŋa diila. 30Di danni cheena ate nuruba nyini nidek po a nyini a velim a paasi ni ate nya kude basi ate Kirisita bisaŋa a basi ba suiku abe ba maa va ba. 31Dila nyiŋla, ni be kpesi nidek abe ni a teeri diipo yok ale kantueŋ ate m kasim a kum ale a kaam ni wanyi wanyi ate ku ga paari bena ŋata la.
32<<Yɔgyɔgla de, m pai ni a nyo Wen nisima po ale wa ŋmanteka wanni, dii ale di basi ate ni zaani paari abe wa te ni nitalimu a nyini baai meena ale nye cheri la po. 33Mi an jam vari ni waai ligra yaase wa gatta. 34Nama dek abe seba ayen mi pai ka m dek nisimaŋa dɛ a tom tuima a nya jaab meena ate mi ale m vaanchaama a jam a yaali la. 35Wari meena po, mi sak ni kama ayen, ku a fɛ kama ayen ti a maari niwoba abe ni a teeri, Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu wieŋa, wa weeni ayen, <Niauŋ yega a bo teka po a gaam tuesika kama.> >>
36Pɔɔl ale ga biisi nueri la, wa yaa kpi duna tɛŋ a puusi ale ba meena. 37Ba meena yaa jam a kum ale gbaari wa. 38Dii ale potim jam kaasi ba sue la ale Pɔɔl ale weeni ba dii ayen ba kan ŋman nya wa diipo diipo la. Ba yaa bani wa a ta cheŋ ŋaaruŋku jigini ayen wa jueli cheŋ.

english_text:
Paul Goes to Jerusalem
1After saying goodbye, we sailed straight to Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes and from there sailed on to Patara. 2We found a ship going to Phoenicia, so we got on board and sailed off.
3We came within sight of Cyprus and then sailed south of it on to the port of Tyre in Syria, where the ship was going to unload its cargo. 4We found the Lord's followers and stayed with them for a week. The Holy Spirit had told them to warn Paul not to go on to Jerusalem. 5But when the week was over, we started on our way again. All the men, together with their wives and children, walked with us from the town to the seashore. We knelt on the beach and prayed. 6Then after saying goodbye to each other, we got into the ship, and they went back home.
7We sailed from Tyre to Ptolemais, where we greeted the followers and stayed with them for a day. 8 The next day we went to Caesarea and stayed with Philip, the preacher. He was one of the seven men who helped the apostles, 9and he had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.
10 We had been in Caesarea for several days, when the prophet Agabus came to us from Judea. 11He took Paul's belt, and with it he tied up his own hands and feet. Then he told us, “The Holy Spirit says that some of the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt. They will also hand him over to the Gentiles.” 12After Agabus said this, we and the followers living there begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
13But Paul answered, “Why are you crying and breaking my heart? I am not only willing to be put in jail for the Lord Jesus, but I am even willing to die for him in Jerusalem!”
14Since we could not get Paul to change his mind, we gave up and prayed, “Lord, please make us willing to do what you want.”
15Then we got ready to go to Jerusalem. 16Some of the followers from Caesarea went with us and took us to stay in the home of Mnason. He was from Cyprus and had been a follower from the beginning.
Paul Visits James
17When we arrived in Jerusalem, the Lord's followers gladly welcomed us. 18Paul went with us to see James the next day, and all the church leaders were present. 19Paul greeted them and told how God had used him to help the Gentiles. 20Everyone who heard this praised God and said to Paul:
My friend, you can see how many tens of thousands of our people have become followers! And all of them are eager to obey the Law of Moses. 21But they have been told that you are teaching those who live among the Gentiles to disobey this Law. They claim that you are telling them not to circumcise their sons or to follow our customs.
22What should we do now that our people have heard you are here? 23 Please do what we ask, because four of our men have made special promises to God. 24Join with them and prepare yourself for the ceremony that goes with the promises. Pay the cost for their heads to be shaved. Then everyone will learn that the reports about you are not true. They will know you do obey the Law of Moses.
25 Some while ago we told the Gentile followers what we think they should do. We instructed them not to eat anything offered to idols. They were told not to eat any meat with blood still in it or the meat of an animal that has been strangled. They were also told not to commit any terrible sexual sins.
26The next day Paul took the four men with him and got himself ready at the same time they did. Then he went into the temple and told when the final ceremony would take place and when an offering would be made for each of them.
Paul Is Arrested
27When the period of seven days for the ceremony was almost over, some of the Jewish people from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They got a large crowd together and started attacking him. 28They were shouting, “Friends, help us! This man goes around everywhere, saying bad things about our nation and about the Law of Moses and about this temple. He has even brought shame to this holy temple by bringing in Gentiles.” 29 Some of them thought that Paul had brought Trophimus from Ephesus into the temple, because they had seen them together in the city.
30The whole city was in an uproar, and the people turned into a mob. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Then suddenly the doors were shut. 31The people were about to kill Paul when the Roman army commander heard that all Jerusalem was starting to riot. 32So he quickly took some soldiers and officers and ran to where the crowd had gathered.
As soon as the mob saw the commander and soldiers, they stopped beating Paul. 33The army commander went over and arrested him and had him bound with two chains. Then he tried to find out who Paul was and what he had done. 34Part of the crowd shouted one thing, and part of them shouted something else. But they were making so much noise that the commander could not find out a thing. Then he ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress. 35As they reached the steps, the crowd became so wild that the soldiers had to lift Paul up and carry him. 36The crowd followed and kept shouting, “Kill him! Kill him!”
Paul Speaks to the Crowd
37When Paul was about to be taken into the fortress, he asked the commander, “Can I say something to you?”
“How do you know Greek?” the commander asked. 38“Aren't you that Egyptian who started a riot not long ago and led 4,000 terrorists into the desert?”
39“No!” Paul replied. “I am a Jew from Tarsus, an important city in Cilicia. Please let me speak to the crowd.”
40The commander told him he could speak, so Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the people. When they were quiet, he spoke to them in Aramaic:
translation_text:
1Ti ale ga banti ba nueri la, ti yaa jueli ŋaaruŋku a cheŋ yɔrr a jam paari Kosi tɛŋka. Vari ale veenti la, ti yaa paari Aroodisi tɛŋka a zaani dula a taam paari Pataara tɛŋka. 2Dula jigini, ti yaa nya ŋaaruŋ ale ku a cheŋ Fonisia tɛŋka. Ti yaa jueli ŋaaruŋ kula a maa va cheŋ. 3Ŋaaruŋku yaa le paari jigi ate ti jam baga nya Saipurus tɛŋka la, a yaa dam va tɛŋ kala yeniŋ a juga geŋ a ga paari Siriya tɛŋka. Ti ale jam paari Taaya la, ti yaa siŋ dii nyiŋla ka dula jigini ate ŋaaruŋku nyama a jam a yaali ayen ba yeeri ba kɔlimaŋa. 4Dula jigini, ti yaa gisi nya Kirisita bisa a goa dula ale ba ate ku paari daa ŋayopɔi. Wen Chiika yaa basi ate ba kaam Pɔɔl ayen wa kan cheŋ Jerusalem. 5Ti ale jam boro ale ba ate ti danni jam paari ayen ti basi ba la, ti yaa banti ba ale ŋman lo ti chelimu po. Ti ale jam banti ba ale ge ayen ti cheŋ la, ba meena ale ba pooba ale ba bisa ale jam ta ti a nyini tɛŋka po a ta ti jam paari nyakpiemu nɔi. Dula jigini ti meena yaa maa chaab a kpi duna tɛŋ a puusi 6ale ge banti chaab ate tama mɛ jueli ŋaaruŋku a cheŋ ale ge ate ba ŋman a kuli.
7Ti yaa ŋman lo ti chelimu po a zaani Taaya a jueli ŋaaruŋ a cheŋ Tolomayas tɛŋka. Dula jigini ti yaa puusi Kirisita bisaŋa ale ge goa dai yeŋ. 8Vari ale ga veenti la, ti yaa basi dula ale ŋman cheŋ Siizariya. Dula jigini, ti yaa jam boro ale Filip waai ale ka Naawen wieŋa moolidɔwa la. Wa jam ka bayopɔiwa po wanyi baai ate Kirisita bisaŋa a lueri ayen ba a nya ligraŋa zuk la. 9Filip jam ta ka lieba banaansi. Ba waai an jam yali nyaya. Ba jam ka Wen biisiteerɔba. 10Ti ale jam goa dula ate ku beni maga la, Wen biisiteerɔ wanyi yaa jam nyini Judia a jam tama jigi. Wa yuei ale Agabus. 11Wa yaa jam pai Pɔɔl chiak gbanni a bobi wadek naŋsa ale wa nisima ale weeni tama ayen, <<Wen Chiika ale weeni diila, ale nna, ayen, Juuma Jerusalem tɛŋka po ale yik ka di nyɔnɔwa a bobi ase nna la a yaa pai wa a te baai ale kan daa Juuba la.>>
12Ti ale wom nna la, tama ale mbala ale jam maa bo dula la, yaa maa chaab a saalim Pɔɔl ayen wa kan cheŋ Jerusalem. 13Alege wa yaa tulisi ayen, <<Ka boa ate nama a nye dila, a nye ate m popola a kaasi? Mi poom gomsi magsi kama ayen ba kan bobi mu bobika nyiini Jerusalem, alege m poom gomsi magsi kama ayen m kpi dula jigini Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu yuenni nyiŋ.>>
14Ti an jam baga fɛ wa ate wa wari ya. Ti yaa pai dila basi ale weeni wa ayen, <<Ti a saalim Naawen ayen ku meena abe nye magsi ale wadek ale a yaali diila.>>
15Ti le jam goa dula jigini ate ku beni maga la, ti yaa ŋman gomsi ti kɔlimaŋa a magsi a yiti cheŋ Jerusalem. 16Yeezu ŋaaŋviirɔma baai ale jam nyini Siizariya la gela yaa ta ti cheŋ nuru waai yenni ate ti jam a poli ayen ti goa la. Nuruwa yuei ale Minaason. Wa nyini ka Saipurus. A ta nyini diipo ate Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab la a piilim boro la ale nuruwa a chim ka Kirisita biik.
17Ti ale jam paari Jerusalem la, ti suataŋa Kirisita bisaŋa a jam nye ti tia ka nalimnyiini ale suipeentik. 18Vari ale veenti la Pɔɔl yaa maa va ti a cheŋ ayen wa nya Jeemsi. Kirisita bisaŋa ale a tu chaab la nisɔmma meena a jam maa boro kama. 19Pɔɔl yaa puusi ba ale ge a tɔgi wari meena dinyi dinyi a sak ba Wen ale va wa tuimaŋa nyiŋ a tom dii a te baai ale kan daa Juuba jigi la. 20Ba ale wom wa a nueri la, ba meena yaa te Wen pimpauk. Ba yaa weeni ayen, <<Ti suowa, fi nya Juuma ale piisi dii chim Kirisita bisa la kama. Fidek be nya ba ale kasim a yaali ayen nuruba a va sinsaŋŋa la kama. 21Nuruba weeni ba kama ayen ka fi ale a sak Juuma meena baai ale bo tɛŋ sii ale kan daa Juuba tɛŋsa la, ayen ba kan a va Moosis Sinsaŋŋa abe ba kan a gebi ba bisaŋa yoaŋa yaase ba kan a va Juuma kisitaŋa. 22Yɔgyɔgla de ti ale nye ka sɛ? Ku a fɛ kama ayen ba wom ayen fi jam ya. 23Tama ale a yaali ayen fi nye diila ale nna. Nuruba banaansi ale bo dela jigini a puulim ale Wen. 24Maa va ba a pai fidek a gum ba po a cheŋ a ga nye ba ale ba nye dii ate ba welema Wen jigi la. Tuni pami dii meena ate ba le tuni abe ba nya weleŋsaŋa dɛ la. Fi dan nye dila ba le nya suik a poni ba zuimaŋa yɔgla. Suik kula po, nuruba yaa le seba ayen wie ŋaai meena ate nuruba weeni a magsi chaab ale fi la, wensie fiik fiik la a ka ba biika po, alege ba le nya ayen fidek fi boka po, fi a va ka Moosis Sinsaŋŋa ale a weeni diila. 25Alege baai ale kan daa Juuba a yaa chim Kirisita bisa la, gbaŋ kaai ate tama ŋmarisi ayen fi ta ga te ba la, ti weeni ba kama ayen, ba kan a dɛ bɔgta ŋandiinta, ba kan a dɛ ziim ba a kan ŋɔbi jabuui ate ba an tɔgri la lammoa, abe ba kan a bobi nipok baai ale kan daa ba pooba la a goa.>>
26Vari ale veenti la, Pɔɔl yaa dɛ nuruma niŋ ate ba cheŋ a ga nye dii ale dii ale di basi ate ba chim cheri nuruba. Pɔɔl yaa jo Wen yenni po a weeni ku a le pai daa ŋaai ate cheri nyaka tigini de a nueri abe ku ge ate ba yaa nya suik ate ba nye kaabka a te ba wanyi wanyi la.
27Ku jam pai ka daa ŋayopɔi ate weleŋsa nyaka tigini de a taam. Alege ku ale jam tali maga ate ŋa nueri la, Juuma gela baai ale jam nyini Asia la yaa nya Pɔɔl Wen yenni po. Ba yaa choa nuru boanni meena a yik Pɔɔl ale pagrim, 28a yaa nuem ate ku a jueli ayen, <<Izirali demma, ni maari ti, nuruwa de ale a nyiem jigi meena a sak ayen Moosis Sinsaŋŋa daa sinsak maŋsa ale biisi a kaasi ti nuruma ale Wen yenni. Wa ta ka baai ale kan daa Juuba la a jam Wen yenni po ale nye ate jigi weleŋka a taŋ.>> 29Ba jam weeni kude kama dii nyiŋla, ba jam nya ka Torofimus waai ale nyini Efisos la ale wa va ka Pɔɔl a nyiem tɛŋka po ate ba yaa deri poli ayen da dii dai Pɔɔl a ta wa jam jo ka Wen yenni po.
30Nuruma meena Jerusalem po sue yaa jam puuri. Ba yaa gum chaab chali ga yik Pɔɔl a vuuri wa a ta nyini Wen yenni po a nyini ale lik di tuataŋa. 31Ba ale jam boro a poli ayen ba ko Pɔɔl la, tuntomiŋ yaa jam paari Aroom tɛŋka tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagi kpienni ayen wa nya Jerusalem tɛŋka meena demma boro a nye ka kpaliŋ nna ŋaglam. 32Kpagi kpienni yaa deri yik kpaga fiisaŋa gela ale tugurik tɔŋdɔba ate ba yaa chali siŋ nuru boanni jigi. Nuru boanni ale nya wa ale tugurik tɔŋdɔma la, ba yaa basi Pɔɔl nagta. 33Kpagi kpienni yaa taam cheŋ Pɔɔl jigi a yik wa ale pagrim a yaa weeni ayen tugurik tɔŋdɔma pai chɔrima ŋaye a bobi wa. Wa yaa bek ayen, <<Ka be denɔ ale nna? Wa nye ka sɛ?>> 34Nuru boanni yaa deri a nuem ate ku a jueli. Ba gela a nuem a weeni wari di choa, ba gela mɛ a nuem a weeni di choa. Juuma yaa nye nna ŋaglam ate kpagi kpienni an jam baga miŋ wari dii ate Pɔɔl nye la. Wa yaa weeni wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma ayen ba ta Pɔɔl cheŋ juijui ate tugurik tɔŋdɔma boro la. 35Ba ale jam ta wa a jueli dɔkku tiilaŋa zuk la, nuru boanni sue yaa ŋman ŋmasi jam a puuri nna yegayega. Dila nyiŋ ku yaa jam fɛ tugurik tɔŋdɔma ate ba koati Pɔɔl a ji. 36Nuru boanni a kasim jam a vi wa kama ale a kaari a weeni ayen, <<Ko wa.>>
37Tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale jam tali maga ate ba ta wa jo yenni po la, Pɔɔl yaa weeni kpagi kpienni ayen, <<Mi a saalim, m weeni wari a sak fu?>> Kpagni yaa bek wa ayen, <<Fi a wom Girik biika kama? 38Mi poli ayen fi ka Ejipiti denɔ waai dipo ale jam nye kpaliŋka ale tɛŋka nyɔnɔwa ate ku an diem beni la, a ta nuru koorisa tusa ŋanaansi (4,000) a nyini sagni po a nyini la?>>
39Pɔɔl yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Aaya, mi daa wala, mi ka Juu. Ba biak mu ka Taasus tɛŋka kaai ale bo Silisiya po la. M be nyini ka tɛŋ kpieŋ kaai yuei ale yiti nna yegayega la po. Mi a saalim ayen fi te mu suik ate m biisi ale nuruma.>>
40Kpagi kpienni yaa te wa suik ate Pɔɔl yaa zaani tiini zuk a zak nisima ayen nuruma goori ate wa biisi. Ba ale ga goori la, Pɔɔl yaa pai Juuma biika Yiburu a biisi ale ba.

english_text:
1“My friends and leaders of our nation, listen as I explain what happened!” 2When the crowd heard Paul speak to them in Aramaic, they became even quieter. Then Paul said:
3 I am a Jew, born in the city of Tarsus in Cilicia. But I grew up here in Jerusalem where I was a student of Gamaliel and was taught to follow every single law of our ancestors. In fact, I was just as eager to obey God as any of you are today.
4 I made trouble for everyone who followed the Lord's Way, and I even had some of them killed. I had others arrested and put in jail. I didn't care if they were men or women. 5The high priest and all the council members can tell you this is true. They even gave me letters to the Jewish leaders in Damascus, so that I could arrest people there and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
6 One day about noon I was getting close to Damascus, when a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed around me. 7I fell to the ground and heard a voice asking, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me?”
8“Who are you?” I answered.
The Lord replied, “I am Jesus from Nazareth! I am the one you are so cruel to.” 9Those who were traveling with me saw the light, but did not hear the voice.
10I asked, “Lord, what do you want me to do?”
Then he told me, “Get up and go to Damascus. When you get there, you will be told what to do.” 11The light had been so bright that I couldn't see. And the others had to lead me by the hand to Damascus.
12In that city there was a man named Ananias, who faithfully obeyed the Law of Moses and was well liked by all the Jewish people living there. 13He came to me and said, “Saul, my friend, you can now see again!”
At once I could see. 14Then Ananias told me, “The God that our ancestors worshiped has chosen you to know what he wants done. He has chosen you to see the One Who Obeys God and to hear his voice. 15You must tell everyone what you have seen and heard. 16What are you waiting for? Get up! Be baptized, and wash away your sins by praying to the Lord.”
17After this I returned to Jerusalem and went to the temple to pray. There I had a vision 18of the Lord who said to me, “Hurry and leave Jerusalem! The people won't listen to what you say about me.”
19I replied, “Lord, they know that in many of our synagogues I arrested and beat people who had faith in you. 20 Stephen was killed because he spoke for you, and I stood there and cheered them on. I even guarded the clothes of the men who murdered him.”
21But the Lord told me to go, and he promised to send me far away to the Gentiles.
22The crowd listened until Paul said this. Then they started shouting, “Get rid of this man! He doesn't deserve to live.” 23They kept shouting. They waved their clothes around and threw dust into the air.
Paul and the Roman Army Commander
24The Roman commander ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress and beaten with a whip. He did this to find out why the people were screaming at Paul.
25While the soldiers were tying Paul up to be beaten, he asked the officer standing there, “Is it legal to beat a Roman citizen before he has been tried in court?”
26When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and said, “What are you doing? This man is a Roman citizen!”
27The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?”
“Yes,” Paul answered.
28The commander then said, “I paid a lot of money to become a Roman citizen.”
But Paul replied, “I was born a Roman citizen.”
29The men who were about to beat and question Paul quickly backed off. And the commander himself was frightened when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains.
Paul Is Tried by the Council
30The next day the commander wanted to know the real reason why the Jewish leaders had brought charges against Paul. So he had Paul's chains removed, and he ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet. Then he had Paul led in and made him stand in front of them.

1Pɔɔl yaa piilim wa biika ayen, <<M suata ale m koba, ni lak tue wom mi ale za ni niŋ ayen m biisi a vari m dek a basi diila.>> 2Ba ale wom ale wa a biisi ale badek biika Yiburu la, ba yaa ŋmasi goori nna chorototo ale ge ate Pɔɔl a biisi a cheŋ a weeni ayen,
3<<Mi ka Juu. Ba biak mu ka Taasus tɛŋka kaai ale bo Silisiya po la. Alege mi chim ka Jerusalem dela a zamsi nyini sagrɔ waai ate ba a wi ayen Gamaliil la jigi, waai ale kpesi sak mu wari meena a ta va ti kokpieŋsaŋa sinsaŋŋa. Mi jam tom a te Wen ale ka nimmuna, ase nama baai ale bo dela jinla de la. 4Mi namsi baai ale a va Yeezu la ka nna yegayega a poom jam a bobi ba gela nidoaba ale nipooba ta ba ga a lik, ale ko ba gela mɛ. 5Ni dan bek Wen yenni kpagi kpienni ale kpaŋŋa meena, ba le siak ayen mi ale a biisi diila ka wensie. M jam tuesi gbaŋsa ba jigi ate ba ŋmarisi a te ti mabisaŋa Juuma mɛ baai ale bo Damasikus tɛŋka la ayen mi cheŋ dula a ga yik baai ale a va Yeezu la a pai chɔrima bobi ba a ta jam Jerusalem ate ba nya waalika.
6<<Ase mi ale jam bo suiku po a cheŋ moata Damasikus tɛŋka la, wenbinni jam bo ka wein zuk suŋsuŋ ate wenŋmazuk a deri nyaksi a gilim mu. 7Mi yaa lo tɛŋ a wom ale lueluk a weeni mi ayen, <Sɔɔl, Sɔɔl, ka boa ate fi a namsi mu nna?> 8Ate mi yaa bek wa ayen, <Ka wana, m Nyɔnɔ?> Wa yaa tulisi ayen, <Ka mi, Yeezu, Nazaret denɔwa ate fi a namsi dila.> 9Nidoa baai ale jam maa va mi a cheŋ la, a jam nya nyaksika kama alege ba an jam wom lueluku ale jam a biisi dii ale mi la. 10Mi yaa bek ayen, <Mi le nye ka sɛ m Naawen yaa?> ate ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita yaa weeni ayen, <Yiti cheŋ Damasikus. Dula jigini fi le wom dii meena ate mi a poli ayen fi nye la.> 11Nyaksi kaai ale jam nyaksi la, a jam basi kama ate m deri yi. M vaanchaama baai ale jam maa va mu la, a yaa yik m nisima a ta mu cheŋ Damasikus.
12<<Dula jigini, nuru wanyi, wa yuei jam le Ananaiyas. Wa jam ka wensuik nyɔnɔ. Wa jam a zuli Moosis Sinsaŋŋa kama. Juuma meena ale jam bo dula la a jam a te wa zula kama. 13Wala yaa jam mi jigi a zaani m tɛŋ a yaa weeni mu ayen, <M suok Sɔɔl, lak fi ninaŋa.> Mi yaa deri lagri ŋa a yaa nya wa 14ate wa deri weeni mi ayen, <Ti kokpieŋsaŋa Wenni ale lueri fu ayen fi seba wa ale a yaali diila, abe fi nya wayɔrisima Tomteerɔwa, abe fi wom wadek lueluku. 15Fi ale chim wa seerɔ a weeni waai meena fi ale nya ale wom diila. 16Fi be ŋman a limisi ka boa jaab yɔgyɔgla de? Yiti, a tuesi soka abe fi puusi a wi wa yuenni ate wa sugri fi wabaataŋa a basi.>
17<<Mi ale ŋmani Jerusalem la, mi yaa bo Wen yenni po a puusi, ku yaa nye mi jigi nna ase gɔdaasima la 18ate mi nya ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita ate wa yaa weeni mi ayen, <Nye nwuli basi Jerusalem yɔgyɔgla de dii nyiŋla nuruma dela jigini a kan siak fi ale a biisi dii a magsi chaab ale mi la.> 19Mi yaa weeni Wa ayen, <M Nyɔnɔ Yeezu, ba seba chak kama ayen ka mi ale cheŋ tama tuka yeeŋa po a yik baai ale ta siaka ale fi la a nak ale a lik ba mɛ. 20Ba ale jam yik Sitiven a ko ayen wa ale jam a sak nuruba fi wieŋa la nyiŋ, ka mi dek abe ale jam maa boro a siak ayen ba ko wa. Be ka mi ale jam a nya baai ale ko wa la kasaautaŋa zuk.> 21Ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita yaa weeni mi ayen, <M le basi ate fi cheŋ nna niŋniŋa baai ale kan daa Juuma la jigi.> >>
22Nuru boanni a jam a wom Pɔɔl kama ate wa ga biisi nna la. Ba yaa piilim a na ayen, <<Ni ko wa, ni yeeri wa tɛŋzuk de a basi, ni kan basi ate wa vua.>> 23Ba yaa jam a kaari a yik ba gattaŋa a kpaanti ale ŋari tintanta a yuk a basi wenzuk. 24Aroom tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagi kpienni yaa weeni wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma ayen ba ta Pɔɔl a ga jo tugurik tɔŋdɔma yenni po, a miiri wa ate wa weeni a sak ba jabuui nyiŋ ale soa ate Juuma a kaari ayen ba kan yaali wa la. 25Ase tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale chamsi wa a nya a gomsi ba miiri wa la, Pɔɔl yaa weeni kpagi dinyi ale jam moata wa la ayen, <<Fi ta suik a nak Aroom tɛŋka denɔ waai ale kan kaasi wari yaa?>>
26Tugurik tɔŋdɔba kpagni ale wom nna la, wa yaa ga bek Tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagi kpienni ayen, <<Fi a nye ka boan dila? Fi zɛ ayen nuruwa dɛ ka Aroom denɔ?>>
27Kpagi kpienni yaa cheŋ Pɔɔl jigi a ga bek wa ayen, <<Weeni a sak mu, fi ka Aroom denɔ?>> Pɔɔl mɛ yaa tulisi ayen, <<Mm.>>
28Kpagi kpienni yaa weeni ayen, <<Mi tuni ka ligra nna yegayega ale ge a chim Aroom denɔ.>> Pɔɔl yaa tulisi ayen, <<Alege a nyini mi biam po mi ka Aroom denɔ.>>
29Nuru baai ale jam gomsi ayen ba miiri Pɔɔl la ale wom nna la, yaa pilim ŋmani ŋaaŋ ale ge basi Pɔɔl. Yɔgsum yaa yik kpagi kpienni dii nyiŋla wa ale jam miŋ ayen Pɔɔl ka Aroom denɔ alege bobi wa ayen ba nak wa la.
30Wa jam a yaali kama ayen wa seba a chak dii nyiŋ ale soa ate Juuma a ŋma Pɔɔl la. Dila nyiŋ vari ale ga veenti la, wa yaa foli Pɔɔl chɔrimaŋa ale ge a wi kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa ale Juuma tɛŋka kpaŋŋa ayen ba nye tuka. Wa yaa ta Pɔɔl a cheŋ ga zaani ba niŋ.

english_text:
1Paul looked straight at the council members and said, “My friends, to this day I have served God with a clear conscience!”
2Then Ananias the high priest ordered the men standing beside Paul to hit him on the mouth. 3 Paul turned to the high priest and said, “You whitewashed wall! God will hit you. You sit there to judge me by the Law of Moses. But at the same time you order men to break the Law by hitting me.”
4The men standing beside Paul asked, “Don't you know you are insulting God's high priest?”
5 Paul replied, “Oh! I didn't know he was the high priest. The Scriptures do tell us not to speak evil about a leader of our people.”
6 When Paul saw that some of the council members were Sadducees and others were Pharisees, he shouted, “My friends, I am a Pharisee and the son of a Pharisee. I am on trial simply because I believe that the dead will be raised to life.”
7As soon as Paul said this, the Pharisees and the Sadducees got into a big argument, and the council members started taking sides. 8 The Sadducees do not believe in angels or spirits or that the dead will rise to life. But the Pharisees believe in all of these, 9and so there was a lot of shouting. Some of the teachers of the Law of Moses were Pharisees. Finally, they became angry and said, “We don't find anything wrong with this man. Maybe a spirit or an angel really did speak to him.”
10The argument became fierce, and the commander was afraid that Paul would be pulled apart. So he ordered the soldiers to go in and rescue Paul. Then they took him back into the fortress.
11That night the Lord stood beside Paul and said, “Don't worry! Just as you have told others about me in Jerusalem, you must also tell about me in Rome.”
A Plot To Kill Paul
12-13The next morning more than 40 Jewish men got together and vowed that they would not eat or drink anything until they had killed Paul. 14Then some of them went to the chief priests and the nation's leaders and said, “We have promised God that we would not eat a thing until we have killed Paul. 15You and everyone in the council must go to the commander and pretend that you want to find out more about the charges against Paul. Ask for him to be brought before your court. Meanwhile, we will be waiting to kill him before he gets there.”
16When Paul's nephew heard about the plot, he went to the fortress and told Paul about it. 17So Paul said to one of the army officers, “Take this young man to the commander. He has something to tell him.”
18The officer took him to the commander and said, “The prisoner named Paul asked me to bring this young man to you, because he has something to tell you.”
19The commander took the young man aside and asked him in private, “What do you want to tell me?”
20He answered, “Some men are planning to ask you to bring Paul down to the Jewish council tomorrow. They will claim they want to find out more about him. 21But please don't do what they say. More than 40 men are going to attack Paul. They have made a vow not to eat or drink anything until they have killed him. Even now they are waiting to hear what you decide.”
22The commander sent the young man away after saying to him, “Don't let anyone know you told me this.”
Paul Is Sent to Felix the Governor
23The commander called in two of his officers and told them, “By nine o'clock tonight have 200 soldiers ready to go to Caesarea. Take along 70 men on horseback and 200 foot soldiers with spears. 24Get a horse ready for Paul and make sure he gets safely through to Felix the governor.”
25The commander wrote a letter that said:
26Greetings from Claudius Lysias to the Honorable Governor Felix:
27Some Jews grabbed this man and were about to kill him. But when I found out that he was a Roman citizen, I took some soldiers and rescued him.
28I wanted to find out what they had against him. So I brought him before their council 29and learned that the charges concern only their religious laws. This man isn't guilty of anything for which he should die or even be put in jail.
30As soon as I learned that there was a plot against him, I sent him to you and told their leaders to bring charges against him in your court.
31The soldiers obeyed the commander's orders, and that same night they took Paul to the city of Antipatris. 32The next day the foot soldiers returned to the fortress and let the soldiers on horseback take him the rest of the way. 33When they came to Caesarea, they gave the letter to the governor and handed Paul over to him.
34The governor read the letter. Then he asked Paul and found out that he was from Cilicia. 35The governor said, “I will listen to your case as soon as the people come to bring their charges against you.” After saying this, he gave orders for Paul to be kept as a prisoner in Herod's palace.

1Pɔɔl yaa nya tigsuŋku po a weeni ba ayen, <<M mabisa, Izirali demma, mi seba chak kama nalimnyiini ayen a zaani diipo ate mi kasim boro a jam paari jinla la, Wen jigi mi ka wari ya.>> 2Kaabteerɔ kpioŋku Ananaiyas yaa weeni baai ale jam za moata Pɔɔl la ayen, ba fɔbi wa nɔnni. 3Pɔɔl yaa weeni Ananaiyas ayen, <<Wen ale fɔbi fi mɛ. Fi ka pimpaasirɔ. Fi kala ka dula a pai Moosis Sinsaŋŋa a bo mi buusa alege fi zɛ ayen fi a kaasi ka Moosis Sinsaŋŋa ale fi ale a weeni ayen ba fɔbi mi nɔnni la?>>
4Nuru baai ale jam za moata Pɔɔl la a yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Fi kan baga a lɛ Wen kaabteerɔ kpioŋku dila?>>
5Pɔɔl yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<M mabisa, mi poom zɛ ayen wa ka kaabteerɔ kpioŋŋoa. Dii nyiŋla, Wen Gbaŋka a weeni ayen, <Ku a fɛ kama ayen nuru waai kan biisi kpagi dii ale a nya ba zuk la a kaasi.> >>
6Pɔɔl ale ga nya ale nuruma gela ka Sajusiiba, ba gela mɛ Farisiiba la, wa yaa biisi ate ku jueli a weeni kpaŋŋa ayen, <<M mabisa, mi ka Farisii, mi be ka Farisii biik. M be za dela kama ayen ba bo mu buusa boan nyiŋŋa, mi ta yiila kama ayen baai ale kpi la le ŋman yiti kum po kama a ta nyuvuri.>>
7Wa ale weeni dila a magsi chaab ale kpieba le ba ŋman yiti a vua la, Farisiima ale Sajusiiba a yaa deri piilim ta chaab ate dila yaa nye ate ba poori chaab. 8Sajusiiba a weeni kama ayen nuruba a kan ŋman yiti kum po a vua, ba a weeni kama mɛ ayen Wen Maarɔba ale chichirisa karo. Alege Farisiima ta siaka kama ayen nuruba le yiti kum po kama, Wen Maarɔba ale chichirisa boro kama. 9Nuemka yaa jam a jueli nna yegayega ate Sinsak sagrɔma gela baai ale jam maa ka Farisiima la yaa yiti weeni ale pagrim ayen, <<Tama an nya wari dii ate nuruwa de kaasi la. Da dii dai ku ka wensie ayen chichirik yaase Wen maarɔ ale sum jam biisi ale wa.>>
10Nanpaŋŋa a jam pagra ka nna yegayega ate tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagi kpienni a jam a chali yɔgsum ayen ba nin zaan yik Pɔɔl a dari passi. Wa yaa weeni wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma ayen ba siŋ nuru boanni po a vari Pɔɔl ba jigi a ta jam a nyo yenni po.
11Yok kula dek ate Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita jam zaani Pɔɔl tɛŋ a weeni wa ayen, <<Pɔɔl kan a chali yɔgsum. Fi weeni m wie kama a sak nuruba Jerusalem tɛŋka po. Ku be a fɛ kama mɛ ayen fi nye dila dekdega Aroom tɛŋka.>>
12Vari ale ga veenti la, Juuma gela yaa nye tuka ayen ba ko Pɔɔl. Ba yaa jam pɛ ayen ba waai kan dɛ ŋandiinta yaase ba nyu nyiam ka ba nin ko Pɔɔl nueri abe ba dɛ yaase ba nyu. 13Nuru baai ale jam maa chaab a poli nna la, a jam gaam pisinaansi kama. 14Ba yaa cheŋ Juuma Yenni kpaŋŋa ale nisɔmma jigi a weeni ba ayen, <<Tama maa ka chaab a pɛ ayen ti kan dɛ jaaboa ka ti nin ko Pɔɔl. 15Yɔgyɔgla de, ni ale kpaŋŋa meena abe tom weeni Aroom tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagi kpienni ayen wa ta Pɔɔl jam. Paasi wa ayen ni a yaali kama ayen ni ŋmasi wom chak dii dek ale boro a magsi chaab ale wa la. Alege tama ale poom gomsi magsi kama ate ti ko wa ale ge ate wa poom nya suik a paari dela jigini.>>
16Alege ba ale jam a biisi nna meena la, Pɔɔl toa biik, yaa wom ba ale a biisi dii la, a yaa cheŋ yeri diipo ate ba lik Pɔɔl la a weeni sak wa. 17Pɔɔl yaa wi tugurik tɔŋdɔba kpaŋŋa wanyi ayen, <<Ta nidoabinni nna a cheŋ ni kpagi kpienni jigi ale wa ta ka wari ayen wa weeni a sak kpagni.>> 18Tugurik tɔŋdɔba kpagni yaa ta wa cheŋ kpagi kpienni jigi a weeni wa ayen, <<Pɔɔl waai ate ti yik a lik la ale weeni ayen m ta nidoabinni de a jam fi jigi ale wa ta ka wari ayen wa weeni a sak fu.>>
19Kpagi kpienni dek yaa yik nidoabinni nisima a ta wa a taam nakpiak a bek wa ayen, <<Ka boa ate fi tara ayen fi weeni a sak mu?>>
20Nidoabinni yaa weeni wa ayen, <<Juuma kpaŋŋa a maa chaab a siak kama ayen, ba bek fu ate fi dan siak abe fi ta Pɔɔl a cheŋ kpagi kpiemaŋa jigi chum. Ba be ale paasi fu kama ase kpagi kpiemaŋa ale sum a yaali wa ayen ba ŋmasi wom dii dek chekki ale boro a magsi chaab ale wa la. 21Alege ba dan weeni dila, kan wom ba, dii nyiŋla, nuruba ale gaam pisinaansi a suk suik a limisi ayen wa dan jam paari abe ba ko wa. Ba pɛ kama ayen ba kan dɛ yaase ba nyu, ka ba nin ko wa. Yɔgyɔgla de ba be gomsi badek a magsi kama a limisi ayen ba wom fi ale ta dii ayen fi weeni a magsi chaab ale wanni de la.>>
22Kpagi kpienni yaa weeni nidoabinni ayen, <<Kan weeni a sak nuru ayen fi weeni wanni de a sak mi.>> Kpagni yaa weeni dila ale ge basi ate nidoabinni kuli.
23Tugurik tɔŋdɔba kpagni yaa wi wa tugurik tɔŋdɔba kpaŋŋa baye a weeni ba ayen, <<Gomsi tugurik tɔŋdɔba kobsiye a magsi ate ba cheŋ Siizariya. Gomsi wusum duerɔba pisiyopɔi ale ba wusumaŋa ale nuruba kobsiye baai ale a kpaliŋ ale gbatta la ate bala meena a gum chaab ale tugurik tɔŋdɔba kobsiyewa ate ku dan nak yok baŋ neok abe fi ta ba cheŋ. 24Ni ta wusuma jam ate Pɔɔl do. Ni ta wa paari du ale nyiŋyɔgsa a ga te Gominawa Feliksi.>> 25Kpagni yaa weeni dila ale ge yaa ŋmarisi gbaŋ ayen ba ta ga te Gominawa. Wa ale ŋmarisi gbaŋka a weeni diila ale nna ayen,
26<<Mi, Kilɔdiyus Lisiyas ale a ŋmarisi gbaŋka de a te fi Feliksi waai ale ka Gomina a nya ti meena zuk la.
<<Mi a puusi fu nalimnyiini.
27<<Juuma a yik nuruwa de, Pɔɔl kama ale pagrim ayen ba ko. M be wom kama ayen wa ka Aroom denɔ ate mi yaa cheŋ wa jigi ale tugurik tɔŋdɔma ayen m vari wa a basi. 28Mi abe jam a yaali kama ayen m miŋ wa dii ate wa kaasi la ate ba a toariŋ wa la. Dila nyiŋ ate mi yaa ta wa cheŋ ba kpagi kpiemaŋa jigi.
29<<M be nya kama ale wa an nye wa dii ale magsi ba ko wa yaase ba ta wa ga lik la. Ka badek Sinsaŋŋa vaka nyiŋ ale soa ate ba a toariŋ wa.
30<<Mi ale wom ale ba a poli ayen ba paasi a ko wa la, m yaa deri weeni m tugurik tɔŋdɔma ayen ba ta wa jam fi jigi. M be weeni baai ale a toariŋ wa la kama ayen ba ta beŋŋa meena jam bek wa fi niŋ.>>
31Tugurik tɔŋdɔma yaa nye ba kpagni ale weeni ba diila. Ba yaa yik Pɔɔl yok kula a cheŋ dila a ga paari Antipatirisi. 32Vari ale veenti la, tugurik tɔŋdɔ baai ale jam a cheŋ naŋsa la, yaa pilim ŋmani Jerusalem ale ge basi tugurik tɔŋdɔba baai ale jam do wusumaŋa la ate ba a cheŋ ale wa. 33Ba yaa ta Pɔɔl cheŋ Siizariya a ga paari, pai gbaŋka a te Gominawa a yaa pai Pɔɔl a nyo wa nisima po. 34Gomina yaa karim gbaŋka ale ge yaa bek Pɔɔl ayen, <<Fi nyini ka tɛŋ boa?>> Gominawa ale miŋ ayen Pɔɔl nyini ka Silisiya la, wa yaa weeni Pɔɔl ayen, 35<<Mi le wom dii ate fi ta la ase baai ale a toariŋ fu la a nin jam.>> Gominawa yaa weeni tugurik tɔŋdɔba ayen ba basi Pɔɔl yenni po abe ba nya wa zuk nalimnyiini. Ye kpienni de jam ka Naawa Ayerod ale se di.

english_text:
Paul Is Accused in the Court of Felix
1Five days later Ananias the high priest, together with some of their leaders and a lawyer named Tertullus, went to the governor to present their case against Paul. 2So Paul was called in, and Tertullus stated the case against him:
Honorable Felix, you have brought our people a long period of peace, and because of your concern our nation is much better off. 3All of us are always grateful for what you have done. 4I don't want to bother you, but please be patient with us and listen to me for just a few minutes.
5This man has been found to be a real pest and troublemaker for our people all over the world. He is also a leader of a group called Nazarenes. 6-8When he tried to disgrace the temple, we arrested him. If you question him, you will find out for yourself that our charges are true.
9The Jewish crowd spoke up and agreed with what Tertullus had said.
Paul Defends Himself
10The governor motioned for Paul to speak, and he began:
I know that you have judged the people of our nation for many years, and I am glad to defend myself in your court.
11It was no more than twelve days ago that I went to worship in Jerusalem. You can find this out easily enough. 12Never once did the Jews find me arguing with anyone in the temple. I didn't cause trouble in the synagogues or in the city itself. 13There is no way that they can prove these charges they are now bringing against me.
14I admit that their leaders think the Lord's Way which I follow is based on wrong beliefs. But I still worship the same God that my ancestors worshiped. And I believe everything written in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets. 15I am just as sure as these people are that God will raise from death everyone, good or evil. 16And because I am sure, I try my best to have a clear conscience in whatever I do for God or for people.
17 After being away for several years, I returned here to bring gifts for the poor people of my nation and to offer sacrifices. 18This is what I was doing when I was found going through a ceremony in the temple. I wasn't with a crowd, and there was no uproar.
19Some Jews from Asia were there at that time, and if they have anything to say against me, they should be here now. 20Or ask the ones who are here. They can tell you that they didn't find me guilty of anything when I was tried by their own council. 21 The only charge they can bring against me is what I shouted out in court, when I said, “I am on trial today because I believe that the dead will be raised to life!”
22Felix knew a lot about the Lord's Way. But he brought the trial to an end and said, “I will make my decision after Lysias the commander arrives.” 23He then ordered the army officer to keep Paul under guard, but not to lock him up or to stop his friends from helping him.
Paul Is Kept under Guard
24Several days later Felix and his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, went to the place where Paul was kept under guard. They sent for Paul and listened while he spoke to them about having faith in Christ Jesus. 25But Felix was frightened when Paul started talking to them about doing right, about self-control, and about the coming judgment. So he said to Paul, “That's enough for now. You may go. But when I have time I will send for you.” 26After this, Felix often sent for Paul and talked with him, because he hoped that Paul would offer him a bribe.
27Two years later Porcius Festus became governor in place of Felix. But since Felix wanted to do the Jewish leaders a favor, he kept Paul in jail.
translation_text:
1Daa ŋanu ale jam taam la, kaabteerɔ kpioŋku Ananaiyas ale tɛŋka nisɔmma gela yaa va chaab a cheŋ Siizariya. Ba jam ta ka Tetuulos cheŋ ayen wa biisi te ba. Ba yaa jam Gominawa Feliksi jigi a jam zaani wa niŋ a weeni dii nyiŋ ale soa ate ba a toariŋ Pɔɔl la. 2Ba yaa wi ate Pɔɔl jo ate Tetuulos yaa deri piilim a ŋma wa ayen, <<Feliksi, fi yam buui ate fi pai a nya ti zuk la a basi kama ate ti boro ale suiyɔgni a ta nyini dipo. Ti be seba kama mɛ ayen ka fi yammu nyiŋ ate tagrika kasim a jam ti tɛŋka po ate ti boro ale suiyɔgni. 3Diipo meena wuu ale jiga meena wuu ti kasim a nye ka fi jiam ŋa nyiŋ. 4M be kan yaali ayen m beni fu, alege mi a saalim fu ayen fi le te ti zula a lak tue a wom ti biik gelika de. 5Tama nya kama ale nuruwa de ka nuru biok a ta daanika a jam ti tɛŋka po. Wa a deŋsi ka Juuma ale bo tɛŋzuk de meena la kpa ayen ba nye kpaliŋ ale Aroom demma. Wa be ka nuru baai ate ba a wi ayen Nazaretba la kpagi. 6Wa kasim jam pii ka nyiŋ a nye ayen wa taŋ yenni ate tama yik wa. 7Alege Lisiyas tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagi kpienni a yaa jam tuesi wa ale pagrim tama jigi. 8Fi dek a dan bek wa bega, fi yaa le miŋ ase ŋade meena ka wensie ya.>> 9Juuma yaa jam pai badek a gum ba po ate ba meena a weeni ayen dii meena ate ba a weeni la ka wensie.
10Gominawa yaa te Pɔɔl suik ayen wa biisi. Pɔɔl yaa piilim ayen,
<<M seba ayen fi chim boteerɔ tɛŋka de ate ku beni ka nna yegayega. Dila nyiŋla, ku te mu suipeentik ate m zaani fi niŋ a biisi vari m dek a basi. 11Yɔgyɔgla de ase fidek a dan bek nuruba wieŋa de fi le wom ayen ka ku da pi ale ŋaye nyiini ale jinla ate mi daam yiti a cheŋ Jerusalem ayen m puusi. 12Diipo ate mi jam jo Wen yenni po la, yaase ba tuka diinaŋa po la, yaase tɛŋka po la, Juuma an nya ale mi a nak nanpaga ale nuru yaase m nye wari dii ale basi ate nuruba tigsi chaab jigi yeŋ la. 13Ba an baga ale sak fu ayen wieŋa de meena ate ba a toariŋ mi la ka wensie. 14Alege mi a weeni nya kude a sak fu kama ayen mi a va ka Kirisita bisaŋa suik kuui ate nuruma de a weeni ayen ku ka venta la, a puusi ti kokpieŋsaŋa Wenni. M be maa ta siaka kama ale Moosis Sinsaŋŋa ale a weeni dii meena la kama. Wen biisiteerɔma mɛ ale ŋmarisi ba gbaŋsaŋa a weeni ŋaai meena la, m ta siaka kama mɛ ale ŋa. 15Mi be ta yiila kama ase nuruma de dek ale ta yiila diila ayen, waai meena, nuru maŋsa ale nuru baata le yiti kum po kama. 16Dila nyiŋla, mi nyiem kasim a pii ka nyiŋ m boka meena po ale m popola po ayen m nye dii ale ka wamaŋ Wen ale nurubiik niŋ la.
17<<Mi ale ga basi Jerusalem ate ku beni maga la, m jam cheŋ kama ayen m te m Kirisita bisa vaanchaama ligra abe m te Wen tiirim. 18Diipo ate mi jam bo Wen yenni po a nye dila la ate Juuma yaa nya mi du. Dila powa ale mi nye weleŋsa nyeka tuini a nueri kama. Dila powa mɛ, nuru boari yaase daanika a jam karo. 19Alege Juuma gela ale jam nyini Asia tɛŋka a jam maa boro. Ku a fɛ kama ayen bala dek a dan ta wari ayen ba toariŋ mu di nyiŋ ba be jam zaani fi niŋ a weeni wa dii ate mi nye kaasi la. 20Yaase fi basi ate nuruma ale za dela la a weeni sak fu diipo ate mi jam zaani kpagi kpiemaŋa niŋ ate ba nya mu la m nin nye wari kaasi. 21Kan daa ka wari dinyi dekki ate mi jam weeni dipo ayen, <Jinla ate mi za nama niŋ ate ni a bek mu beŋŋa de mi ale weeni ayen baai ale kpi la a le yiti kum po kama a ŋman vua la nyiŋ.> >>
22Alege Feliksi a jam seba Yeezu suiku kama, a yaa dak da yoŋ ayen ba biisi biika ale ge a weeni ba ayen, <<Tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagi kpienni Lisiyas a dan jam, abe m yaa poli nya dii ate m le weeni la.>> 23Feliksi yaa weeni tugurik tɔŋdɔ waai ale a nya Pɔɔl zuk la ayen wa ŋmasi nya Pɔɔl zuk nalimnyiini abe wa basi wa nna fasiyaa yenni po, abe wa basi mɛ ate wa doama a te wa jaabuuri meena ate wa a yaali la.
24Daa maga ale taam la, Feliksi yaa jam ale wa powa Durusila, wa jam ka Juu, a yaa weeni ayen ba ta Pɔɔl a jam wa jigi. Wa jam wom kama ale Pɔɔl a weeni kama ayen ba ta siaka ale Yeezu Kirisitawa. 25Alege Pɔɔl ale a biisi nyemagsika ale seba fidek yikka ale buusa boka la, yɔgsum yaa yik Feliksi ate wa yaa weeni Pɔɔl ayen, <<Fi baga cheŋ yɔgyɔgla de kama. M le ŋman wi fu ate fi jam ase m nin nya suik.>> 26Feliksi ale jam weeni dila la, wa jam a poli mɛ kama ayen da dii dai Pɔɔl ale te wa ligra. Dila nyiŋ wa yaa kasim jam a tom a wi Pɔɔl maga maga a daliŋ ale wa.
27Alege bena ŋaye ale taam la, Gominawa choa yaa jam tagri Feliksi zuk. Gominawa de yuei a jam le Poosiyos Fesitos. Dila powa Feliksi a jam a yaali kama ayen wa nye wari ate Juuma suipeentik. Dila nyiŋ, wa yaa basi ate Pɔɔl bo tugurik tɔŋdɔma nisima po.

english_text:
Paul Asks To Be Tried by the Roman Emperor
1Three days after Festus had become governor, he went from Caesarea to Jerusalem. 2There the chief priests and some Jewish leaders told him about their charges against Paul. They also asked Festus 3if he would be willing to bring Paul to Jerusalem. They begged him to do this because they were planning to attack and kill Paul on the way. 4But Festus told them, “Paul will be kept in Caesarea, and I am soon going there myself. 5If he has done anything wrong, let your leaders go with me and bring charges against him there.”
6Festus stayed in Jerusalem for eight or ten more days before going to Caesarea. Then the next day he took his place as judge and had Paul brought into court. 7As soon as Paul came in, the leaders from Jerusalem crowded around him and said he was guilty of many serious crimes. But they could not prove anything. 8Then Paul spoke in his own defense, “I have not broken the Law of my people. And I have not done anything against either the temple or the Emperor.”
9Festus wanted to please the leaders. So he asked Paul, “Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried by me on these charges?”
10Paul replied, “I am on trial in the Emperor's court, and that's where I should be tried. You know very well I have not done anything to harm the Jewish nation. 11If I had done something deserving death, I would not ask to escape the death penalty. But I am not guilty of any of these crimes, and no one has the right to hand me over to these people. I now ask to be tried by the Emperor himself.”
12After Festus had talked this over with members of his council, he told Paul, “You have asked to be tried by the Emperor, and to the Emperor you will go!”
Paul Speaks to Agrippa and Bernice
13A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to visit Festus. 14They had been there for several days, when Festus told the king about the charges against Paul. He said:
Felix left a man here in jail, 15and when I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the Jewish leaders came and asked me to find him guilty. 16I told them it isn't the Roman custom to hand a man over to people who are bringing charges against him. He must first have the chance to meet them face to face and to defend himself against their charges.
17So when they came here with me, I wasted no time. On the very next day I took my place on the judge's bench and ordered him to be brought in. 18But when the men stood up to make their charges against him, they did not accuse him of any of the crimes that I thought they would. 19Instead, they argued with him about some of their beliefs and about a dead man named Jesus, who Paul said was alive.
20Since I did not know how to find out the truth about all this, I asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and be put on trial there. 21But Paul asked to be kept in jail until the Emperor could decide his case. So I ordered him to be kept here until I could send him to the Emperor.
22Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would also like to hear what this man has to say.”
Festus answered, “You can hear him tomorrow.”
23The next day Agrippa and Bernice made a big show as they came into the meeting room. High ranking army officers and leading citizens of the town were also there. Festus then ordered Paul to be brought in 24and said:
King Agrippa and other guests, look at this man! Every Jew from Jerusalem and Caesarea has come to me, demanding for him to be put to death. 25I have not found him guilty of any crime deserving death. But because he has asked to be judged by the Emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.
26I have to write some facts about this man to the Emperor. So I have brought him before all of you, but especially before you, King Agrippa. After we have talked about his case, I will then have something to write. 27It makes no sense to send a prisoner to the Emperor without stating the charges against him.
translation_text:
1Fesitos ale ga dɛ wa naamu a yaa soa tɛŋka la, ku daa ŋata dai ate wa basi Siizariya ale ge cheŋ Jerusalem. 2Kaabteerɔ kpioŋku ale Juuma kpaŋŋa a yaa jam wa jigi a weeni wa wie ŋaai meena ate Pɔɔl kaasi la. Ba meena jam a saalim Fesitos ayen, 3wa maa maari ba ate ba ta Pɔɔl a jam Jerusalem. Ba jam weeni dila kama a poli ayen ba le basi kama ate nuruba suk suiku niŋ ate wa dan jam a taam abe ba ko wa. 4Fesitos yaa tulisi ba ayen, <<Ba yik Pɔɔl a lik ka Siizariya. Mi dek abe le cheŋ dula ka yɔgyɔgla de. 5Ni basi ate ni kpaŋŋa a va mu cheŋ Siizariya ate ni ga ŋma wa dula jigini ase wa nin kaasi wari.>>
6Fesitos a ŋman goa ale ba daa naaniŋ yaase daa pi a gum du ale ge cheŋ Siizariya. Wa ale ga paari Siizariya ate vari veenti la, wa yaa jo biisaŋa dɔkku po a kali wa zukpaglika zuk a weeni wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma ayen ba ta Pɔɔl jam. 7Pɔɔl ale ga jam la, Juuma baai ale jam maa nyini Jerusalem a jam la, a yaa jam za gilim Pɔɔl a weeni ayen wa kaasi ka wie nna yegayega alege ba an jam baga sak ayen ŋaai ate ba a weeni a magsi chaab ale Pɔɔl la ka wensie. 8Pɔɔl yaa biisi ayen wa vari wadek a basi, wa weeni ayen, <<Mi an kaasi Juuma Sinsaŋŋa yaase Wen yenni yaase m biisi naab kpioŋku Siiza a kaasi ya.>>
9Alege Fesitos ale jam a yaali ayen wa nye wari ate Juuma suipeentik la, wa yaa bek Pɔɔl ayen, <<Fi ale siak a cheŋ Jerusalem ate m bek fu a wom ba ale a biisi ŋaai meena a te fu la?>>
10Pɔɔl yaa tulisi ayen, <<Mi za ka waai ale tagri naab kpioŋku Siiza la niŋ, ale wadek buusa boka dɔkku po juijui ale magsi ayen wa bo mi buusa la. Fidek abe seba chak kama ayen mi an nye Juuma wari a kaasi ya. 11M be dan kaasi ka wari ate dila nyiŋ ku magsi ayen m kpi, m kan weeni ayen m kan kpi. Alege wensie abe dan kan boro ale ba ale a ŋma mu la, nuru karo a baga pai mi a nyo ba nisima po. Mi a yaali kama ayen ti cheŋ naab kpioŋku Siiza jigi ate wala bo mi buusa.>>
12Fesitos yaa nya chaab ale wa nuruma baai ale bo ale wa a sak wa a magsi chaab ale wa tuimaŋa la a nueri ale ge a weeni Pɔɔl ayen, <<Fi weeni kama ayen fi yaali ayen fi cheŋ ka naab kpioŋku Siiza jigi, fi abe le cheŋ ka wa jigi.>>
13Ku ale ga beni maga la, Naab Agiripa ale wa toawa Beniis yaa cheŋ Siizariya ayen ba puusi Fesitos abe ba nye wa tia. 14Ba ale bo dula ate ku paari da boari la, Fesitos ya tɔk Pɔɔl wanni kiri a sak Naab Agiripa ayen, <<Nuru ale bo dela ate Feliksi jam yik wa lik. 15Mi ale cheŋ Jerusalem la, kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa ale Juuma nisɔmma ale jam a ŋma nuruwa de ayen wa nye wie kaasi ate ba yaa jam mi jigi ayen m bo wa buusa. 16Mi mɛ yaa tulisi ba ayen tama Aroom demma sinsaŋŋa a weeni kama ayen nuru waai ate nuru a ŋma wa ayen wa kaasi wari la, bala bayewa a tu chaab a nya chaab ate waai ate ba a ŋma la a biisi vari wadek a basi ale ge ate ti yaa bo ba buusa. 17Nuruma de ale va mi a jam Siizariya ayen ti chamsi wa nya la, mi an beni du. Dai dii ale pasaŋ la mi yaa kali buusa zukpaglika zuk a weeni ayen ba ta nuruwa a jam. 18Wa dachaasaŋa ale ga yiti zaani ayen ba biisi la, ba an poom biisi wakaasima ŋaai ate mi jam a poli ayen ba ale biisi a magsi chaab ale wa la. 19Ba ale jam a biisi dii meena la ale nanpaga nakka a magsi chaab ale badek wensuik vaka wie ale nuru wanyi ate ba a wi wa ayen Yeezu ate wa kpi alege Pɔɔl a weeni ayen wa vua kama. 20Mi ale kan jam seba mi ale m tulisi beŋŋa dii la, mi yaa bek Pɔɔl, <Fi a yaali fi cheŋ Jerusalem ate ba bo fi buusaŋa dula?> 21Alege Pɔɔl a jam weeni kama ayen wa a yaali kama ayen wa wari dela ate Naab Kpioŋku a poli nya wa ale wa nye wanni de diila. Dila nyiŋ ate mi yaa weeni ayen ba a limisi wa ate m yaa tom ate wa cheŋ naab kpioŋku Siiza jigi.>>
22Agiripa yaa weeni Fesitos ayen, <<Mi a yaali kama ayen midek a wom nuruwa de biik.>> Fesitos mɛ yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Chum fi be le wom wa.>>
23Vari ale ga veenti la, Agiripa ale Beniis yaa va chaab a jam ate nuruba nna yegayega a vi ba ŋaaŋ a te ba zula. Bala meena yaa va chaab ale tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagi kpiemaŋa ale tɛŋka nisɔm kpientaŋa yaa maa jo dɔk kpioŋ kuui ate nuru boari a jo ku po a nye tuka la. Fesitos yaa weeni ate ba ta Pɔɔl a jo jam. 24Fesitos yaa weeni ayen, <<Naab Agiripa ale baai meena ale bo dela jigini ale ti la, ni meena nya nuruwa de waai ate Juuma ale bo dela ale Jerusalem tɛŋka la a yaa maa chaab a ta wa wie a jam mi jigi, a kaari a weeni ayen, ku an poom ŋman magsi ayen nuruwa de a ŋman bo tɛŋzuk de diipo diipo. 25Alege mi abe nya kama ale wari karo a magsi nuruwa kummoa. Alege wadek ale weeni ayen wa a yaali ayen wa cheŋ Naab Kpioŋku jigi la, ate mi yaa poli ayen m basi ate wa cheŋ Aroom. 26Alege mi potim ka wari ayen m ŋmarisi a magsi chaab ale wa a te Naab Kpioŋku. Dila nyiŋ ate m ta wa jam nama meena jigi a potim jam fi jigi Naab Agiripa ayen fi dan bek wa wanni a wom, abe mi yaa ta wari a ŋmarisi. 27Mi jigi, yam ka ku po ate m tom ligrɔ ale ge kan weeni ate ku a lagri dii dek chekki ate nuruba a weeni ayen wa kaasi la.>>

english_text:
Paul's Defense before Agrippa
1Agrippa told Paul, “You may now speak for yourself.”
Paul stretched out his hand and said:
2King Agrippa, I am glad for this chance to defend myself before you today on all these charges my own people have brought against me. 3You know a lot about our religious customs and the beliefs that divide us. So I ask you to listen patiently to me.
4-5 All the Jews have known me since I was a child. They know what kind of life I have lived in my own country and in Jerusalem. And if they were willing, they could tell you I was a Pharisee, a member of a group that is stricter than any other. 6Now I am on trial because I believe the promise God made to our people long ago.
7Day and night our twelve tribes have earnestly served God, waiting for his promised blessings. King Agrippa, because of this hope, some of our leaders have brought charges against me. 8 Why should any of you doubt that God raises the dead to life?
9 I once thought that I should do everything I could to oppose Jesus from Nazareth. 10I did this first in Jerusalem, and with the authority of the chief priests I put many of God's people in jail. I even voted for them to be killed. 11I often had them punished in our synagogues, and I tried to make them give up their faith. In fact, I was so angry with them, that I went looking for them in foreign cities.
12King Agrippa, one day I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and permission of the chief priests. 13About noon I saw a light brighter than the sun. It flashed from heaven on me and on everyone traveling with me. 14We all fell to the ground. Then I heard a voice say to me in Aramaic, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me? It's foolish to fight against me!”
15“Who are you?” I asked.
Then the Lord answered, “I am Jesus! I am the one you are so cruel to. 16Now stand up. I have appeared to you, because I have chosen you to be my servant. You are to tell others what you have learned about me and what I will show you later.”
17The Lord also said, “I will protect you from the Jews and from the Gentiles that I am sending you to. 18I want you to open their eyes, so they will turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God. Then their sins will be forgiven, and by faith in me they will become part of God's holy people.”
19King Agrippa, I obeyed this vision from heaven. 20 First I preached to the people in Damascus, and then I went to Jerusalem and all over Judea. Finally, I went to the Gentiles and said, “Stop sinning and turn to God! Then prove what you have done by the way you live.”
21That is why some men grabbed me in the temple and tried to kill me. 22But all this time God has helped me, and I have preached both to the rich and to the poor. I have told them only what the prophets and Moses said would happen. 23 I told them how the Messiah would suffer and be the first to be raised from death, so he could bring light to his own people and to the Gentiles.
24Before Paul finished defending himself, Festus shouted, “Paul, you're crazy! Too much learning has driven you out of your mind.”
25But Paul replied, “Honorable Festus, I am not crazy. What I am saying is true, and it makes sense. 26None of these things happened off in a corner somewhere. I am sure that King Agrippa knows what I am talking about. That's why I can speak so plainly to him.”
27Then Paul said to Agrippa, “Do you believe what the prophets said? I know you do.”
28Agrippa asked Paul, “In such a short time do you think you can talk me into being a Christian?”
29Paul answered, “Whether it takes a short time or a long time, I wish you and everyone else who hears me today would become just like me! Except, of course, for these chains.”
30Then King Agrippa, Governor Festus, Bernice, and everyone who was with them got up. 31But before they left, they said, “This man isn't guilty of anything. He doesn't deserve to die or to be put in jail.”
32Agrippa told Festus, “Paul could have been set free, if he had not asked to be tried by the Roman Emperor.”
translation_text:
1Agiripa yaa weeni Pɔɔl ayen, <<Fi ta suik kama a biisi a te fidek.>> Pɔɔl yaa zak wa nisima a puusi a piilim ayen wa biisi a vari wadek a basi. Wa yaa piilim ayen,
2<<Naab Agiripa, mi a poli ayen mi ta ka wein ate jinla mi zaani fi niŋ ayen mi biisi a vari m dek a basi ale Juuma ale a ŋma mu ayen mi kaasi la. 3Fidek abe seba Juuma ŋiak wieŋa ale ba beŋŋa a magsi chaab ale ba wensuiku vaka a chak kama. Dila nyiŋ ate mi a saalim fu ayen fi wom mi ale suduŋni.
4<<Juuma meena seba mi boka ale ka diila kama a ta nyini m bi fiik po a ta paari diipo ate mi jam bo m dek tɛŋka ate ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ate mi bo Jerusalem tɛŋka la. 5Ba seba mu ate ku beni kama. Ba daa yaali ba le weeni fu ayen mi jam ka Farisii. Farisiima abe a zuli mi tɛŋka sinsaŋŋa kama chekki a gaam tigsuŋ meena. 6Yɔgyɔgla de m be za ka dela ayen ni bo mu buusa dii nyiŋla, mi ta yiila kama ale Wen ale jam puulim dii ale ti kokpieŋsaŋa la. 7Pumpuulimaŋa de abe le tama nuruma diina pi ale buyewa a yiili ba nya ase ba le tom a te Wen danni po ale yok la. Naabaa, ba ŋma mu ka m ni ta yiilaŋa de dek la nyiŋ. 8Ka boa abe ale soa ate nama ayen ku daa moali ate Wen nak kpilima a yiti kum po?
9<<Mi dek abe jam poli kama ayen m nye dii meena ale di kaasi Yeezu Nazaret denɔwa yuei la. 10M be ale jam nye dii Jerusalem tɛŋka la ale la. M jam tuesi ka suik kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa jigi a yik Kirisita bisaŋa yegayega a lik. Daa likka nyiini alege, ti ale jam poli ayen ku ka wamaŋ ate ti ko ba la, mi mɛ abe ale jam siak ayen ba ko ba. 11Daa dila nyiini, mi jam te ba waalika ti tuka diinaŋa po ate ku paari ka diichoa, a kasim a nye dila ayen ba lɛ Yeezu. M suinni kasim ŋmasi jam a de ka nna yegayega ale ba ate mi nyiem poom jam cheŋ satɛŋ yonsa juijui ate ba boro la a te ba waalika.
12Mi jam tuesi ka suik ale pagrim kaabteerɔ kpaŋŋa jigi ayen m cheŋ Damasikus tɛŋka. 13Mi ale bo suiku po a cheŋ dula la, wentueŋ suŋsuŋ, mi yaa nya ku nyagsi a nyini wenŋmazuk. Ku jam nyagsi a gaam wenbinni kama a nyagsi a gilim mi ale baai meena ale jam va mi a cheŋ la. 14Ate ti meena yaa lo tɛŋ ate mi wom ale lueluk a weeni mi ale Juuma biika Yiburu ayen, <Sɔɔl, Sɔɔl, ka boa ate fi a namsi mu nna? Fi a namsi ka fidek dila.> 15Mi yaa bek ayen, <Fi ka wana Nyɔnɔ?> Ate ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita yaa tulisi ayen, <Ka mi Yeezu ate fi a namsi. 16Alege, yiti zaani ŋmai. M pai m dek a sak fu kama yɔgyɔgla de ayen ku sak ayen m lueri fu kama ale tom fu mɛ ayen fi chim m tomteerɔ. Ku a fɛ kama ayen fi weeni a sak nuruba ba chaab dii ate fi nya a magsi chaab ale mi jinla la ale m nin m sak fu dii chum diipo la. 17M le vari fu fidek nuruma Juuma nisima po a basi ale baai mɛ ale kan daa Juuba ate mi le tom fu ba jigi la nisima po mɛ a basi. 18M dan tom fu, mi le basi ate fi lagri ba ninaŋa ate ba tagri nyini legini po a nyini jam peelim niŋ. Ba ale tagri nyini Sitaana nisima po a nyini a jam Wen nisima po ate ba ta siaka ale mu ate ba nya wabaataŋa vɔŋteka ate ba yaa maa bo nuru baai ate Wen lueri la po.>
19<<Naab Agiripa, mi a be an zɛri dii ale nyini wenŋmazuk a jam ate mi nya di ase m goadaasim kama la. 20Mi yaa piilim Damasikus ale Jerusalem tɛŋsaŋa po ale ge yaa paari Judia tɛŋka meena ale baai mɛ ale kan daa Juuba la, a sak ba ayen ku a fɛ kama ate ba basi ba wabaataŋa tomka abe ba pai badek a te Naawen abe ba a tom tuim ŋaai ale a sak ayen ba tagri kama la. 21Ku be jam ka sinsaŋŋa de nyiŋ ate Juuma a jam yik mi diipo ate mi jam bo Wen yenni po la a pii nyiŋ ayen ba ko mu. 22Alege zaani dipo a jam paari jinla, ka Wen ale jam a maari mi. Ka dila nyiŋ ate mi za dela ayen m biisi wensie a sak waai meena, nuru fiik yaase nuru kpioŋ. Mi ale a biisi diila ale dila dekdega ate Wen biisiteerɔma ale Moosis a jam weeni ayen ku le nye la, 23ayen Kirisitawa ale kpi, ase wa ale waai ale wa dɛ niŋ a yiti kum po la, wa le ta bolim a jam te nuru meena.>>
24Ase Pɔɔl ale a biisi wieŋa de wa vari wadek a basi la, Fesitos yaa weeni ate ku jueli ayen, <<Pɔɔl fi zukku karo, zamsika yegayega a basi kama ate fi a yesim.>>
25Pɔɔl yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<M koa, mi kan yesimu. Wie ŋaai ate mi a biisi la ka wensie ale yam. 26Mi baga a nyini ka peelim a biisi ale fi Naab Agiripa dii nyiŋla fidek seba wieŋa de nɔi po kama. M seba chak kama ayen fi ŋmasi kpesi wieŋa de dinyi dinyi kama, dii nyiŋla, wanni de an suk nye ka gugoruk po. 27Naab Agiripa, fi ta siaka ale Wen biisiteerɔma ale a biisi diila? M seba ayen fi ta siaka kama.>>
28Agiripa yaa bek Pɔɔl ayen, <<Ku an diem bula beniya ale ge fi a poli ayen fi nye kama ate mi chim Kirisita biik, yaa boa?>>
29Pɔɔl yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Ku beni yaa ku an beniya, mi a puusi a te ka Wen ayen fi ale baai meena ale kali dela jigini a wom mi jinla danni la, nama ale chim ase mi ale ka nuru waai jinla la. Alege m kan poli ayen ni le ta chɔrima ase mi ale ta diila.>>
30Naawa ale Gominawa ale Beniis ale mbala meena a yaa yiti nyini. 31Ba ale nyini nueri la, ba yaa weeni chaab ayen, <<Nuruwa an nye wari a magsi wa kpi yaase ba yik wa a ligi.>> 32Agiripa yaa weeni Fesitos ayen, <<Nuruwa de a poom magsi ka ti basi wa ase wa nin poom kan weeni ayen wa a yaali ayen ka wa cheŋ Siiza jigiya.>>

english_text:
Paul Is Taken to Rome
1When it was time for us to sail to Rome, Captain Julius from the Emperor's special troops was put in charge of Paul and the other prisoners. 2We went aboard a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail to some ports along the coast of Asia. Aristarchus from Thessalonica in Macedonia sailed on the ship with us.
3The next day we came to shore at Sidon. Captain Julius was very kind to Paul. He even let him visit his friends, so they could give him whatever he needed. 4When we left Sidon, the winds were blowing against us, and we sailed close to the island of Cyprus to be safe from the wind. 5Then we sailed south of Cilicia and Pamphylia until we came to the port of Myra in Lycia. 6There the army captain found a ship from Alexandria that was going to Italy. So he ordered us to board that ship.
7We sailed along slowly for several days and had a hard time reaching Cnidus. The wind would not let us go any farther in that direction, so we sailed past Cape Salmone, where the island of Crete would protect us from the wind. 8We went slowly along the coast and finally reached a place called Fair Havens, not far from the town of Lasea.
9By now we had already lost a lot of time, and sailing was no longer safe. In fact, even the Great Day of Forgiveness was past. 10Then Paul spoke to the crew of the ship, “Men, listen to me! If we sail now, our ship and its cargo will be badly damaged, and many lives will be lost.” 11But Julius listened to the captain of the ship and its owner, rather than to Paul.
12The harbor at Fair Havens wasn't a good place to spend the winter. Because of this, almost everyone agreed that we should at least try to sail along the coast of Crete as far as Phoenix. It had a harbor that opened toward the southwest and northwest, and we could spend the winter there.
The Storm at Sea
13When a gentle wind from the south started blowing, the men thought it was a good time to do what they had planned. So they pulled up the anchor, and we sailed along the coast of Crete. 14But soon a strong wind called “The Northeaster” blew against us from the island. 15The wind struck the ship, and we could not sail against it. So we let the wind carry the ship.
16We went along the island of Cauda on the side that was protected from the wind. We had a hard time holding the lifeboat in place, 17but finally we got it where it belonged. Then the sailors wrapped ropes around the ship to hold it together. They lowered the sail and let the ship drift along, because they were afraid it might hit the sandbanks in the gulf of Syrtis.
18The storm was so fierce that the next day they threw some of the ship's cargo overboard. 19Then on the third day, with their bare hands they threw overboard some of the ship's gear. 20For several days we could not see either the sun or the stars. A strong wind kept blowing, and we finally gave up all hope of being saved.
21Since none of us had eaten anything for a long time, Paul stood up and told the men:
You should have listened to me! If you had stayed on in Crete, you would not have had this damage and loss. 22But now I beg you to cheer up, because you will be safe. Only the ship will be lost.
23I belong to God, and I worship him. Last night he sent an angel 24to tell me, “Paul, don't be afraid! You will stand trial before the Emperor. And because of you, God will save the lives of everyone on the ship.” 25Cheer up! I am sure that God will do exactly what he promised. 26But we will first be shipwrecked on some island.
27For 14 days and nights we had been blown around over the Mediterranean Sea. But about midnight the sailors realized we were getting near land. 28They measured and found that the water was about 40 meters deep. A little later they measured again and found it was only about 30 meters. 29The sailors were afraid that we might hit some rocks, and they let down four anchors from the back of the ship. Then they prayed for daylight.
30The sailors wanted to escape from the ship. So they lowered the lifeboat into the water, pretending that they were letting down some anchors from the front of the ship. 31But Paul said to Captain Julius and the soldiers, “If the sailors don't stay on the ship, you won't have any chance to save your lives.” 32The soldiers then cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it fall into the sea.
33Just before daylight Paul begged the people to eat something. He told them, “For 14 days you have been so worried that you haven't eaten a thing. 34I beg you to eat something. Your lives depend on it. Do this and not one of you will be hurt.”
35After Paul had said this, he took a piece of bread and gave thanks to God. Then in front of everyone, he broke the bread and ate some. 36They all felt encouraged, and each of them ate something. 37There were 276 people on the ship, 38and after everyone had eaten, they threw the cargo of wheat into the sea to make the ship lighter.
The Shipwreck
39Morning came, and the ship's crew saw a coast they did not recognize. But they did see a cove with a beach. So they decided to try to run the ship aground on the beach. 40They cut the anchors loose and let them sink into the sea. At the same time they untied the ropes that were holding the rudders. Next, they raised the sail at the front of the ship and let the wind carry the ship toward the beach. 41But it ran aground on a sandbank. The front of the ship stuck firmly in the sand, and the rear was being smashed by the force of the waves.
42The soldiers decided to kill the prisoners to keep them from swimming away and escaping. 43But Captain Julius wanted to save Paul's life, and he did not let the soldiers do what they had planned. Instead, he ordered everyone who could swim to jump into the water and head for shore. 44Then he told the others to hold on to planks of wood or parts of the ship. At last, everyone safely reached shore.
translation_text:
1Gominawa ale jam poli ayen ti jueli ŋaaruŋ a cheŋ Itali la, ba yaa pai Pɔɔl ale ligrɔba ba chaab a nyo Juliyos nisima po. Juliyos jam ka Aroom tɛŋka tugurik tɔŋdɔma beŋ kanyi kpagi. 2Ti jam zaani ka Siizariya tɛŋka a jueli ŋaaruŋ. Ku jam nyini ka Adiramitiyom. Ŋaaruŋku a jam gomsi magsi ayen ku cheŋ ka jigi ŋaai meena ate ŋaaruŋta a zaani Asia tɛŋka la. Nuru ale jam maa va ti a cheŋ, wa yuei ale Arisitaakus wa jam ka Tesalonika denɔ. 3Vari ale veenti la, ti yaa paari Saidon. Juliyos a jam ta zula ale Pɔɔl a yaa siak ayen Pɔɔl ga nya wa doama ate ba te wa jabuui ate wa a yaali la. 4Ti yaa basi ale lo jueli moata Saipurus tɛŋka diila viok ale jam a fɔb ti. 5Ti yaa lo Silisiya nyakpiemu jueli cheŋ Pamfiliya a ga paari Mira tɛŋ kpieŋka ale bo Lisia po la. 6Dula jigini ate tugurik tɔŋdɔba kpagni a yaa nya ŋaaruŋ ale ku nyini Alezandiria a taam a cheŋ Itali. Wa yaa pai ti nyo ku po.
7Ŋaaruŋ kula po, ti kasim jam a cheŋ ka nna maga maga ate daaŋa jam paari da boari ate ti nam ale ge yaa paari Kinides tɛŋka. Ka an jam yalima ale ti. Vioku a jam pagra ka nna yegayega ate ti an ŋman jam baga a va suik kuui ate ti jam va la, ate ti yaa ŋmeriŋ va Kariti tɛŋka juijui ate vioku an jam pagra la a jam va jigi di choa ate ba a wi ayen Salomoni. 8Ti le jam sali va kunkɔŋni a cheŋ la, ku jam tua kama a te ti ate ti yaa jam paari jigi ate ba a wi ayen Ŋaaruŋta Zaani Maŋ jigi a moata Lasia tɛŋka.
9Ti jam beni ka nna yegayega ate ku ga paari diipo ate ku pagra ale ti chelimu la. Dii mɛ la, dai dii danni ate ba a nye Juuma tigi dii a magsi chaab ale wabaataŋa vɔŋteka la a jam poom taam kama. Dila ŋaaŋnyiŋ, vioku a ŋmasi pagra kama. Pɔɔl yaa te ba sinsaŋŋa de ayen, 10<<M doaba, mi nya kama ale ti chelimu a zaani dela a cheŋ a kan nala. Kɔlimaŋa ale ŋaaruŋku le kaasi kama, kum mɛ abe le jam ti jigi.>> 11Alege tugurik tɔŋdɔba kpagni a jam ka siaka ale Pɔɔl ale weeni dii la. Ŋaaruŋku damdɔwa ale ku nyɔnɔwa ale jam weeni diila ale jam basi ate tugurik tɔŋdɔba kpagni a siak te ba. 12Ba jam weeni ayen juijui ate ba jam za la, an jam nala a magsi ba wari dula ŋoota wenni. Dila nyiŋla, nuruma yegayega a jam a yaali kama ayen ku dan siak a nye ba dam a paari Foniksi tɛŋka ate ba wari dula ŋoota wenni a vuusi. Foniksi bo ka Kariti tɛŋka juijui ate ŋaaruŋta a nyiem zaani a vuusi la. Jigini de a tuk ka yeniŋ geŋ.
13Viok yaa nyini yeniŋ a gala geŋ a fuk nna balibali ate ba yaa poli ayen nya kude ale deri basi kama ate ba nye ba ale poom a yaali dii ayen ba cheŋ la. Ba yaa pai kutuk kpioŋ kuui ate ba nyiem pai a yik ŋaaruŋku a zaani la a yeeri ku a ta nyini nyiamu po a jueli. Ba yaa jam cheŋ va kunkɔŋni nɔi nna farafara a moata Kariti tɛŋka. 14Alege ku an bula beniya ate viok kpioŋ a yaa nyini a gala geŋ kori nummu po kunkɔŋni a jam 15fɔbi ŋaaruŋku. Ku be ale jam pagra nna yegayega ate ti an jam baga dam la, ti yaa basi ate ku ji ŋaaruŋku a ta a cheŋ. 16Ti ale jam paari tɛŋ fiik kanyi ate ba a wi ayen Kɔda ate nyiam a gilim ka la ate vioku an jam pagra, ti yaa nam nna yegayega ale ge baga a yaa yik ŋaaruŋku ŋaaruŋ fiika a zaani. 17Ba yaa dari ate ku jueli ŋaaruŋ kpioŋku zuk. Ba yaa pai mi pagrisa a bobi gilim ŋaaruŋ kpioŋku. Yɔgsum ale jam ta ba ayen dai dii dai ba ŋaaruŋku a nin zaan a chali ga feri tintain tii ale vi chaab a jueli dua nyiamu tɛŋ a moata Libia nyiamu kunkɔŋni nɔi la. Dila nyiŋ, ba yaa jam a cheŋ maga maga ale basi ate vioku a tusi ŋaaruŋku a ta a cheŋ. 18Va kpioŋku kasim jam a fɔbi ka dila ate nyamiisaŋa a yiri a jueli wein a jam a lo. Vari ale ga veenti la, ba yaa piilim a kɔlim ŋantaŋa ŋaaruŋku po a yuk a basi nyiamu po. 19Daa ŋatawa danni ba yaa pai nisima a pai ŋan baai ate ti ta a nye ate ŋaaruŋku a zaani ale a cheŋ la gela a yuk basi nyiamu po. 20Daaŋa a jam piisi ka nna yegayega alege ti an jam baga a pai nimbiri tu wenbinni yaase chiŋmarisa. Vioku mɛ abe kasim jam a fɔbi ka dila. Ti ŋman jam ka yiila ayen ti le vuugi.
21Ba ale ga cheŋ ate ku beni alege ba an dɛ ŋandiinta la, Pɔɔl yaa yiti zaani ba niŋ a weeni ba ayen, <<Nidoaba, ku poom magsi ka ni ti wom mi ate ti kan poom ŋman zaani Kariti a dam cheŋ. Nna po de ti ti poom kan nya kaasuŋku de ale ŋantaŋa de ate ti jɔk la. 22Alege yɔgyɔgla de, ni yik nidek. Ni wanyi mɛ a kan kpi. Ka ŋaaruŋku nyiini ale ku kaasi. 23Deemwa yokku Wen maarɔ ale nyini Wen dii ale soa mi ate mi a puusi wa la a jam mi jigi 24a weeni mi ayen, <Pɔɔl, kan chali yɔgsum, ku a fɛ kama ate fi zaani Siiza niŋ. Wen abe tulisi fi puusaŋa kama ayen nuruma de wanyi mɛ la a kan kpi.> >>
25Pɔɔl yaa weeni nuruma ayen, <<Dila nyiŋla, nidoaba, ni yik nidek, m ta siaka ale Wen kama ayen wa ale weeni mi diila, dila dekdega le ku nye. 26Alege ti cheŋ paari tɛŋ kanyi ate nyiam gilim ka la.>>
27Ti kasim jam bo ka nyakpiem buui po ate ba a wi ayen Adariya la po a va vioku ate ku fɔbi ti a ta a cheŋ la. Ku jam ka yok kuui ale saari yogta pi ale tinaansiwa la goota suŋsuŋ ate baai ale a tom ŋaaruŋku po la, a yaa poli ayen ti boro a moata tɛŋ yɔgla. 28Dila nyiŋla, ba yaa pai miik a bobi jaab dobruk nyiŋ a yaa basi ate ku siŋ nyiamu po a nya ale ku limisa ka nna yegayega. Ku ale ga nye magadek la, ba yaa ŋman magsi nya ate ku ŋman limisa yegayega. 29Damdɔma a jam yɔgsa kama ayen ti le nak ka pinaŋa, dila ba yaa pai kutuk dobrita tinaansi a bobi basi nyiamu po ale a puusi ayen vari veenti. 30Baai ale a tom ŋaaruŋku po la, a jam pii ka nyiŋ ayen ba chali bɛ. Ba yaa foli ŋaaruŋ fiika a basi nyiamu po ale ge yaa velim ayen ba boro a foli ka kuta dobrita ti chaab ŋaaruŋku niŋ. 31Alege Pɔɔl yaa weeni tugurik tɔŋdɔba kpagni ale tugurik tɔŋdɔma ayen, <<Ŋaaruŋku tuimtomdɔma de a dan kan bo ŋaaruŋku po, ni kan vuugi.>> 32Tugurik tɔŋdɔma yaa gebi mi sii ale yik ŋaaruŋ fiika a ta la a basi nyiamu po.
33Vari yaa jam moata ka veentika ate Pɔɔl yaa weeni ba ayen ba dɛ ŋandiinta yɔgla. Pɔɔl yaa ŋman pilim weeni ba ayen, <<Daa pi ale ŋanaansi ale jinla ate ni kasim a limisi a jam paari yɔgyɔgla de alege ni an diem dɛ jaaboa. 34Dila nyiŋ ate mi a weeni ni ayen ni dɛ ŋandiinta. Ku a fɛ kama ayen ni dɛ ate ni vuuk.
