Wen weeni mi kama ayen ni zuimaŋa zuisaŋa kanyi la a kan bɛ.>> 35Pɔɔl ale ga weeni nna a nueri la, wa yaa pai boroborok puusi a te Wen a nye wa jiam ba meena niŋ, a yaa wɛ boroboroku a piilim ŋɔbika. 36Ba yaa yik badek meena a dɛ ŋandiinta. 37Baai meena ale jam bo ŋaaruŋku po la a jam ka nuruba kobsiye ale pisiyopɔi ale bayuebi. 38Waai meena ale dɛ chak la, ba yaa kɔlim ŋanbieŋa meena a yuk basi nyiamu po ale ge ayen ŋaaruŋku a valima maga.
39Vari ale veenti la, ŋaaruŋku tuimtomdɔma yaa nya kunkɔŋni dinyi alege ba an jam miŋ ale ka juijui kunkɔŋi la. Ba jam nya ka nyakpiemu gugoruk kunyi ale tintain busuŋ a dua jueli maga ate ba yaa poli ayen ba dan baga abe ba dam ŋaaruŋku a ga zaani dula. 40Ba yaa gebi kuta tii ale jam yik ŋaaruŋku a zaani la miisaŋa yaa basi ate ti a cheŋ nyiamu po. Diipo ate ba boro a gebi kutaŋa miisaŋa la, ba jam maa foli dakpien tii ale bobi maŋ ŋaaruŋku ŋaaŋka ate nuruba pai a dam ku la ayen ba yaa pai tila a dam ku. Ba yaa zak garuk kuui ale bobi yiga ŋaaruŋku niŋka la ale ge ayen vioku fuk ku a basi niŋ. Ba yaa nye dila a deri a cheŋ kunkɔŋni. 41Alege ŋaaruŋku yaa nak kuŋkutinni ate ku niŋka yaa feri kuŋkutinni an ŋman baga cheŋ. Ku ale nye dila la, nyamiisaŋa mɛ a kasim jam a fɔbi ku ŋaaŋka ate ku a wɛ nna bunabuna a lo nyiamu po.
42Tugurik tɔŋdɔma yaa nye ba popola ayen ba ko ligrɔma meena ate ba waai a kan nya suik a puŋ nyiamu a chali bɛ. 43Alege tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagni a kan jam a yaali ayen wa ko Pɔɔl. Wa yaa weeni ba ayen ba kan nye dila. Wa jam weeni ba kama ayen waai meena ale baga a dɛ nyiam la, ba yɔk a zi nyiamu po a dɛ jueli kunkɔŋni 44ale ge ate mbala meena a yik ŋaaruŋku daataŋa yaase ku ŋan baai ale kasi a lo la a jueli. Ti meena ale jam nye dii a vuuk a paari kunkɔŋni la ale la.

english_text:
On the Island of Malta
1When we came ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta. 2The local people were very friendly, and they welcomed us by building a fire, because it was rainy and cold.
3After Paul had gathered some wood and had put it on the fire, the heat caused a snake to crawl out, and it bit him on the hand. 4When the local people saw the snake hanging from Paul's hand, they said to each other, “This man must be a murderer! He didn't drown in the sea, but the goddess of justice will kill him anyway.”
5Paul shook the snake off into the fire and wasn't harmed. 6The people kept thinking that Paul would either swell up or suddenly drop dead. They watched him for a long time, and when nothing happened to him, they changed their minds and said, “This man is a god.”
7The governor of the island was named Publius, and he owned some of the land around there. Publius was very friendly and welcomed us into his home for three days. 8His father was in bed, sick with fever and stomach trouble, and Paul went to visit him. Paul healed the man by praying and placing his hands on him.
9After this happened, everyone on the island brought their sick people to Paul, and they were all healed. 10The people were very respectful to us, and when we sailed, they gave us everything we needed.
From Malta to Rome
11Three months later we sailed in a ship that had been docked at Malta for the winter. The ship was from Alexandria in Egypt and was known as “The Twin Gods.” 12We arrived in Syracuse and stayed for three days. 13From there we sailed to Rhegium. The next day a south wind began to blow, and two days later we arrived in Puteoli. 14There we found some of the Lord's followers, who begged us to stay with them. A week later we left for the city of Rome.
15Some of the followers in Rome heard about us and came to meet us at the Market of Appius and at the Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and was encouraged.
Paul in Rome
16We arrived in Rome, and Paul was allowed to live in a house by himself with a soldier to guard him.
17Three days after we got there, Paul called together some of the Jewish leaders and said:
My friends, I have never done anything to hurt our people, and I have never gone against the customs of our ancestors. But in Jerusalem I was handed over as a prisoner to the Romans. 18They looked into the charges against me and wanted to release me. They found that I had not done anything deserving death. 19 The Jewish leaders disagreed, so I asked to be tried by the Emperor.
But I don't have anything to say against my own nation. 20I am bound by these chains because of what we people of Israel hope for. This is why I have called you here to talk about this hope of ours.
21The leaders replied, “No one from Judea has written us a letter about you. And not one of them has come here to report on you or to say anything against you. 22But we would like to hear what you have to say. We understand that people everywhere are against this new group.”
23They agreed on a time to meet with Paul, and many of them came to his house. From early morning until late in the afternoon, Paul talked to them about God's kingdom. He used the Law of Moses and the Books of the Prophets to try to win them over to Jesus.
24Some of the leaders agreed with what Paul said, but others did not. 25Since they could not agree among themselves, they started leaving. But Paul said, “The Holy Spirit said the right thing when he sent Isaiah the prophet 26 to tell our ancestors,
‘Go to these people
and tell them:
You will listen and listen,
but never understand.
You will look and look,
but never see.
27All of you
have stubborn hearts.
Your ears are stopped up,
and your eyes are covered.
You cannot see or hear
or understand.
If you could,
you would turn to me,
and I would heal you.’ ”
28-29Paul said, “You may be sure that God wants to save the Gentiles! And they will listen.”
30For two years Paul stayed in a rented house and welcomed everyone who came to see him. 31He bravely preached about God's kingdom and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ, and no one tried to stop him.
translation_text:
1Ti ale jam paari kunkɔŋni nalimnyiini la, tɛŋ kala demma jam weeni ti kama ayen tɛŋ kala yuei ale Malita. 2Tɛŋ kala demma a jam tuesi ti kama a te ti zula. Ŋmoruk yaa deri a ni ate ŋoota boro ate ba yaa jam cheem bolim a te ti. 3Pɔɔl yaa tigsi daata ayen wa nyo bolimu po. Wa ale pai boro a nyoro la, bolim wuluku yaa nye ate waab a nyini ti po a chali nyini a meli wa nisa a dom wa. 4Tɛŋ kala demma ale nya ale waamu meli Pɔɔl nisimaŋa la, ba yaa weeni chaab ayen, <<Nuruwa de ku a fɛ kama ayen wa ka nuru koorik. Wa baga nyini nyakpiemu po a nyini kama alege tama bɔglukku a kan nya ase ku magsi ayen wa vuuk la.>> 5Alege waamu ale meli Pɔɔl nisimaŋa la, wa yaa misi si ate waamu lo bolimu po alege wari an nye wa. 6Nuruma yaa jam a limisi ale a poli ayen ba nya ale wa nyiŋka fuusi yaase wa deri kpi dua. Alege ba ale jam a limisi ale a poli ate ku beni alege wari an nye wa la, ba yaa tagri ba popolaŋa ale ge weeni ayen, <<Wa ka wen.>>
7Tɛŋka naawa yuei a jam le Pubiliyosi. Naawa de kaduksa ale jam dua moata juijui ate ti jam kala la. Wa yaa jam nye ti tia. Daa ŋata meena ti kasim jam bo ka wala yenni ate wa a nya ti zuk nalimnyiini. 8Ŋoota ale poiyɔgsik ale jam ta wa kowa ate wa jam dua dɔk po. Pɔɔl yaa jo ayen wa nya wa a pai wa nisima a vi wa zuk a puusi te wa ate wa nya nyiŋyɔgsa. 9Wanni de ale ga nye la, yɔgnyieŋsa meena ale jam bo tɛŋ kala la, a jan jam kama a nya nyiŋyɔgsa. 10Ba jam te ti ka tiirita nna yegayega. Ti ale jam pai ŋaaruŋ ku choa ayen ti basi ba abe ti ŋman cheŋ la, ba jam pai ŋan baai ate ti jam a yaali la, a nyo ku po a te ti a magsi ti chelimu.
11Ti jam goa Malita ka chiisa sita ale ge yaa cheŋ Aroom. Ŋaaruŋku de ate ti jam jueli la yuei ale <<Wen Yibsa.>> Ku jam ka Alezandiria ŋaaruŋ. Ku be jam ka ŋoota wein ate ku jam wari Malita ayen ŋootaŋa taamu. 12Ti yaa jam paari Sirakusi tɛŋka goa dula daa ŋata. 13A zaani dula a ŋman paari tɛŋ ka choa ate ba a wi ayen Arigiyum. Vari ale ga veenti la, viok yaa nyini yeniŋ a gala geŋ a fuk. Daa ŋaye dai ate ti yaa ŋman paari Putiyooli tɛŋka. 14Dula jigini ate ti jam nya Kirisita bisa ate ba weeni ti ayen ti daa yaali ti goa daa ŋayopɔi ale ba. Ti yaa siak a goa daa ŋayopɔiwa ale ba ale ge yaa yiti cheŋ Aroom. 15Ti Kirisita bisa suataŋa ale bo Aroom, ale wom ayen ti cheena la, ba yaa nyini cheŋ paari Apiyas Yabaŋa ale Vuusum Yie Ŋatawa, a jam tu ti. Pɔɔl ale ga nya ba ale ba cheena la, ku yaa te wa nyiŋ pagra ate wa te Wen jiam.
16Ti ale jam paari Aroom la, ba jam basi ate Pɔɔl a boro ka wadek wa nyiini, ale tugurik tɔŋdɔ waai ale a limisi wa la.
17Daa ŋata ale jam taam la, Pɔɔl yaa wi Juuma kpaŋŋa Aroom tɛŋka po ate ba jam ayen wa nye tuka ale ba. Ba ale jam tigsi chaab jigi yeŋ la, Pɔɔl yaa weeni ba ayen, <<M mabisa mi an kaasi tama nuruma wari ya yaase kisi tii ate ti tuesi ti kokpieŋsaŋa jigi la, alege ba yik mu a lik ka Jerusalem tɛŋka a pai mu nyo Aroom demma nisima po. 18Ba ale bek mu bega a piisi la ŋaaŋnyiŋ, ba an nya wari a magsi ba ko mu. Ba yaa a yaali ba basi mu ate m cheŋ fasiyaa, 19alege Juuma ale ga wom Aroom demma ale biisi nna la, ba yaa zɛri ate ku yaa fɛ mi ate mi weeni ayen mi a yaali ayen m paari ka Siiza jigi ate wa wom m le ta diila. Alege mi jam ka chaab ale m dek nuruma ayen ba kaasi wari ya ate m toariŋ ba Siiza niŋŋa. 20Dila nyiŋ ate mi wi ni ayen m nya ni abe m weeni a sak ni. Mi be ta chɔrinni de kama dii nyiŋla mi ta yiila ŋaai mɛ ate Izirali demma meena mɛ a ta la.>>
21Ba yaa tulisi wa ayen, <<Tama an tuesi gbaŋ ate ka nyini Judia a biisi fi wari ya. Ti mabisaŋa wanyi mɛ la abe an nyini dula a jam weeni fi wari a sak ti yaase wa biisi wabiok a magsi chaab ale fi. 22Alege tama a yaali kama ayen ti wom fi mɛ popola ale ka diila, dii nyiŋla, jigi meena nuruba kasim a weeni kama ayen ba kan yaali nuru baai ate fi maa bo ba po la.>>
23Ba yaa dak dai yoŋ ayen ba ŋman nye tuka ale Pɔɔl. Dila danni ale jam paari la, ba yaa piisi a tigsi chaab juijui ate Pɔɔl a goa la. A ta nyini saluik a jam paari junɔi Pɔɔl kasim jam a biisi a magsi chaab ale ka Wen naamu wie. Wa kasim jam pii ka nyiŋ a biisi a ta a nyini Moosis Sinsaŋŋa gbaŋka po ale Wen Biisiteerɔma ale ŋmarisi dii la po ayen ku sak ayen wa ale a biisi diila ka wensie a magsi chaab ale Yeezu. 24Ba gela a jam siak kama ayen wa ale a biisi diila ka wensie. Ba gela mɛ an jam siak ya. Ba ale jam a nak nanpaŋŋa nna la, ba yaa waaŋ chaab. Ba ale diem kan jam waaŋ chaab diila, 25Pɔɔl yaa weeni wa dinyi ayen, <<Wen Chiika ale jam basi ate Wen biisiteerɔwa Azaya a biisi dii a te ni kokpieŋsaŋa la sum ka wensie. 26Wen Chiika ale jam biisi dii a te wa ayen wa weeni a sak ni la ale nna ayen, <Cheŋ ga weeni sak nuruma ayen, Nama le wom, a wom alege ni kan miŋ chagi. Nama le nya, a nya alege ni kan zamsi ŋa. 27Dii nyiŋla, nuruma de ka tukpari nyam. Ba kan wom, ba abe mum ba ninaŋa kama, kan daa di, ba ti sum miŋ a chak kama. Dii ate ba nya ale ba ninaŋa la ale a wom ale ba tueŋa la. Ba ti sum miŋ chak kama ale ba popolaŋa a ŋmani jam mi jigi a nya nyiŋyɔgsa.> 28Mi a yaali kama ayen ni seba ayen Wen a tom wa varibasika mɛ kama a te tɛŋsa meena ate ba le wom wa.>> 29Pɔɔl ale weeni nna nueri la, Juuma yaa nak nanpaga ale chaab a yaa waaŋ chaab. 30Pɔɔl jam bo dula ka bena ŋaye. Wa jam bo ka yeri dinyi po a tuni ale ge a goa di po. Waai meena nyiem dan jam wa yenni, wa a nye kula nyɔnɔwa tia ka nalimnyiini. 31Wa nyiem jam nyini ka peelim a kan chali yɔgsum a sak nuruba Wen naamu wie ale a sak ba mɛ Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita wie. Nuru an jam nye ate wa an baga sak wieŋa de.

english_text:
1From Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus.
God chose me to be an apostle, and he appointed me to preach the good news 2that he promised long ago by what his prophets said in the holy Scriptures. 3-4This good news is about his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ! As a human, he was from the family of David. But the Holy Spirit proved that Jesus is the powerful Son of God, because he was raised from death.
5Jesus was kind to me and chose me to be an apostle, so that people of all nations would obey and have faith. 6You are some of those people chosen by Jesus Christ.
7This letter is to all of you in Rome. God loves you and has chosen you to be his very own people.
I pray that God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace!
A Prayer of Thanks
8First, I thank God in the name of Jesus Christ for all of you. I do this because people everywhere in the world are talking about your faith. 9God has seen how I never stop praying for you, while I serve him with all my heart and tell the good news about his Son.
10In all my prayers, I ask God to make it possible for me to visit you. 11I want to see you and share with you the same blessings that God's Spirit has given me. Then you will grow stronger in your faith. 12What I am saying is that we can encourage each other by the faith that is ours.
13 My friends, I want you to know that I have often planned to come for a visit. But something has always kept me from doing it. I want to win followers to Christ in Rome, as I have done in many other places. 14-15It doesn't matter if people are civilized and educated, or if they are uncivilized and uneducated. I must tell the good news to everyone. That's why I am eager to visit all of you in Rome.
The Power of the Good News
16 I am proud of the good news! It is God's powerful way of saving all people who have faith, whether they are Jews or Gentiles. 17 The good news tells how God accepts everyone who has faith, but only those who have faith. It is just as the Scriptures say, “The people God accepts because of their faith will live.”
Everyone Is Guilty
18From heaven God shows how angry he is with all the wicked and evil things that sinful people do to crush the truth. 19They know everything that can be known about God, because God has shown it all to them. 20 God's eternal power and character cannot be seen. But from the beginning of creation, God has shown what these are like by all he has made. That's why those people don't have any excuse. 21 They know about God, but they don't honor him or even thank him. Their thoughts are useless, and their stupid minds are in the dark. 22They claim to be wise, but they are fools. 23 They don't worship the glorious and eternal God. Instead, they worship idols that are made to look like humans who cannot live forever, and like birds, animals, and reptiles.
24So God let these people go their own way. They did what they wanted to do, and their filthy thoughts made them do shameful things with their bodies. 25They gave up the truth about God for a lie, and they worshiped God's creation instead of God, who will be praised forever. Amen.
26God let them follow their own evil desires. Women no longer wanted to have sex in a natural way, and they did things with each other that were not natural. 27Men behaved in the same way. They stopped wanting to have sex with women and had strong desires for sex with other men. They did shameful things with each other, and what has happened to them is punishment for their foolish deeds.
28 Since these people refused even to think about God, he let their useless minds rule over them. That's why they do all sorts of indecent things. 29They are evil, wicked, and greedy, as well as mean in every possible way. They want what others have, and they murder, argue, cheat, and are hard to get along with. They gossip, 30say cruel things about others, and hate God. They are proud, conceited, and boastful, always thinking up new ways to do evil.
These people don't respect their parents. 31They are stupid, unreliable, and don't have any love or pity for others. 32They know God has said that anyone who acts this way deserves to die. But they keep on doing evil things, and they even encourage others to do them.
translation_text:
1Mi Pɔɔl waai ale ka Yeezu Kirisita tomteerɔ la ale a ŋmarisi gbaŋka de. Wen dek ale lueri mu a potim gaari mu ayen m chim wa tuimtomdɔ abe m weeni wa wamaŋsaŋa a sak nuruba. 2Wamaŋsaŋa de ka ŋaai ate wa puulim a biisi ŋa dipo ate wa biisiteerɔma a ŋmarisi nyo Wen gbaŋka po la. 3Wamaŋsaŋa a biisi ka Wa Nidoabinni waai ale ka Deevid ŋaaŋbiik la wie ase nurubiik la. 4A ta va Weleŋsa Chiika a mooli ale pagrim ayen wa ka Wen Nidoabili wa le yiti kum po la nyiŋ, wala ale Yeezu Kirisita ti Nyɔnɔwa. 5Yeezu Kirisita nyiŋ ale Wa Yuenni nyiŋ ate Wen a te mu suiku de ate m chim wa tuimtomdɔ ayen m baga a weeni wa wie a sak tɛŋsa meena nuruba ate ba ta siaka ale wa abe ba a va wa nɔi. 6Wen wi nama mɛ kama ayen Yeezu Kirisita soa ni.
7Mi a puusi nama meena baai ate Wen ta yaalika ale ni a lueri ni a te wadek Aroom tɛŋka po la. Ti Kowa Wen ale ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita le niak ni abe wa te ni suiyɔgni.
8Mi a yaali ayen m va ka Yeezu Kirisita nyiŋ a nye Wen jiam a te ni meena, dii nyiŋla, jigi meena nuruba a biisi ni wie kama ni ale ta siaka ale Yeezu Kirisita la. 9Wen dii ate m tom a te ale m suinum meena a sak nuruba Wa Nidoabinni wamaŋsaŋa wie la, ka wala ale mi seerɔ ate mi kasim a puusi a te nama daa meena. M maara puusi mɛ ayen, 10ku dan ka wa yaalika wa le te mu suik ate m jam ni jigi yɔgyɔgla. 11Mi a yaali ka nna yegayega ayen m nya ni ate m te ni Chiika tiirim ate ni ta pagrim. 12M jamka le maari ka ti meena. Dii nyiŋla, mi ale ta siaka dii ale Wen la, ku le maari ka nama. Nama mɛ abe le ta siaka dii ale wa la ale maari ka mi mɛ. 13M suata, mi a yaali ayen m weeni a sak ni kama ayen m kasim a yaali ayen m jam ni jigi kama, alege mi an baga a jam ya. Mi a yaali ayen ka m dan jam m nye ate nuruba ni po a pai badek a te Wen ase m le nye dii ale ni vaanchaab baai meena ale kan daa Juuba la. 14Mi ta ka tuima ayen m tom a te nuru meena. Baai ale ka Girik dem la ale nuru baai ale kan daa Girik dem la. Baai mɛ ale seba gbaŋ ale baai ale kan seba gbaŋ la. 15Dila ale soa ate m pii nyiŋ a yaali ayen m sak nama baai mɛ ale bo Aroom tɛŋka po la Wen wamaŋsaŋa.
16Mi a kan chali chivie ale Wen wamaŋsaŋa. Wen pai wa pagrimu a nyo ŋa po kama. Dila ale soa ate Wen baga a vari baai meena ale ta siaka ale ŋa la a basi mɛ ba tuimbaata po. Varibasika de a liŋ a cheŋ ka Juuma jigi ale ge a cheŋ baai ale kan daa Juuba la jigi. 17Dii nyiŋla, Wen wamaŋsaŋa a dak sak ti kama suik kuui ate Wen a nye ate ti a chim wayɔrisima nyam wa niŋ la. Wanni de abe ka siaka nyiini a ta nyini di piilimka po a ta ga paari di kpeglimka. Ase ba ale ŋmarisi Wen gbaŋka po dipo ayen, <<Nuru waai abe le ta siaka a chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ Wen niŋ la, wala a nya nyuvuri kama.>>
18Nuruba ale boro a ta gaasa nna yegayega a kan siak ayen wensieŋa a nyini peelim. Wen abe a sak ti kama ayen wa sui ale a puuri ale baai ale kaa va wa suiku la ale ba gaasa tuimaŋa. 19Ŋanta gela boro kama a sak nuruba ate ba baga a seba Wen wie. Nuruma de abe seba ŋantaŋa de kama. Dii nyiŋla, ka Wen dek abe le nye ate ŋantaŋa de a nyini peelim ate ti ba a nya ba. Dila nyiŋ ale soa ate Wen ale namsi ba. 20A ta nyini diipo ate Wen nye wenzuk ale tɛŋ la, a ta jam paari jinla, ŋan baai meena ate wa nye basi wenzuk ale tɛŋzuk de la a maa chaab a sak nurubiik kama Wen ale ka diila. Ba seba ayen wa pagrimu a kasim boro ka dila taam wuu. Wa be sum ka Wen. Nuru abe an baga a nya wa pagrimu de ale wa ale sum ka Wen diila, alege nuruba baga a seba wieŋa de meena kama. Dila nyiŋla, bala chaab a ka suik ale biisi a vari badek a basi ale ba ale nye diila. 21Ba jam seba Wen kama, alege ba an jam a siak ayen ba a nye wa jiam yaase ba a te wa zula. Ba popolaŋa ka betta popola, ŋa daa popola yɔrisima. 22Ba a poli ayen ba ka yam nyam, alege ba chim ka betta, 23a yaa zuli ŋan baai ale a neensi nuruba ale nuinsa ale duŋsa ale ŋan baai meena ale a cheŋ ba lɔga nyiŋsa la, alege kan zuli Wen dii ale kasim boro taam wuu la.
24Ba ale a nye dila la ale soa ate Wen yaa pai ba basi ayen ba va badek sui po ale mariŋ diila ate ba yaa pai badek nyiŋsaŋa a tom daŋta tuim ŋaai ale kan magsi ba pai ba nyiŋsaŋa a tom la ale chaab. 25Ba yaa pai Wen wensieŋa a tagri chim venta ale a puusi ale tom a te ŋan nyeentaŋa ale basi nyeerɔwa, waai ale ta niauŋ taam wuu la. Ku be nye dila.
26Kude nyiŋ, Wen pai ba basi kama ayen ba va badek sui po ale mariŋ dii le di basi ate ba nya chivie la. Ba nipooma mɛ dek a kan yaali ayen ba a goa ale nidoaba. Ba a yaali ayen ka ba a bobi nipooba ba chaab a goa. 27Nidoama mɛ kan yaali ayen ba a goa ale nipooba. Ba kasim a yaali kama ale ba koarisa meena ayen ba a bobi nidoaba ba chaab a goa. Nidoama de ale a nye nna la a magsi ka chivie yik ba alege ba kan chali chivie. Nya kude abe basi kama ate waali kaai ale magsi ba nya la a jam ba jigi.
28Ba jam a poli kama ayen ku an magsi ate ba ta wensie popola maŋsa a magsi chaab ale Wen ya. Wen yaa pai ba basi ate ba ta popola kaasima ate ba a tom tuim ŋaai ale kan magsi ba a tom la. 29Ba suiniimaŋa kasim sueri ale ka gaasa meena wuu, ate ba a yaali chaab ŋanta ale a kisi chaab ale a de nyuri ale chaab ale a ko nuruba ale a nye kpaliŋsa ale chaab ale a paasi chaab ale a poli kaasuŋ nyiini a te nuruba ale a zu chaab ŋaaŋ 30ale a kaasi chaab yue ale kisi Wen mɛ. Ba ka nuru leerisa mɛ ale kanjanta nyam ale a yaali yue a te badek ale a gisi ayen ba nya su paalita ate ba a tom tuimbaata. Ba kan wom ba koba ale ba maba noa. 31Ba be ka betta mɛ. Ba dan puulim ayen ba nye wari, ba kan nye. Ba poom ka yaalika ba suiniima po. Ba ka jiirim ale waai ya. 32Ba be seba ayen Wen weeni kama ayen ku magsi ka nuru baai meena ale a tom nna la, kpi, alege ba diem a tom ka dila ale poom a weeni mɛ ayen baai ale a tom tuim ŋala chaab la, a tom ka tuimaŋsa.

english_text:
God's Judgment Is Fair
1 Some of you accuse others of doing wrong. But there is no excuse for what you do. When you judge others, you condemn yourselves, because you are guilty of doing the very same things. 2We know that God is right to judge everyone who behaves in this way. 3Do you really think God won't punish you, when you behave exactly like the people you accuse? 4 You surely don't think much of God's wonderful goodness or of his patience and willingness to put up with you. Don't you know that the reason God is good to you is because he wants you to turn to him?
5But you are stubborn and refuse to turn to God. So you are making things even worse for yourselves on that day when he will show how angry he is and will judge the world with fairness. 6 God will reward each of us for what we have done. 7He will give eternal life to everyone who has patiently done what is good in the hope of receiving glory, honor, and life that lasts forever. 8But he will show how angry and furious he can be with every selfish person who rejects the truth and wants to do evil. 9All who are wicked will be punished with trouble and suffering. It doesn't matter if they are Jews or Gentiles. 10But all who do right will be rewarded with glory, honor, and peace, whether they are Jews or Gentiles. 11 God doesn't have any favorites!
12Those people who don't know about God's Law will still be punished for what they do wrong. And the Law will be used to judge everyone who knows what it says. 13God accepts those who obey his Law, but not those who simply hear it.
14Some people naturally obey the Law's commands, even though they don't have the Law. 15This proves that the conscience is like a law written in the human heart. And it will show whether we are forgiven or condemned, 16when God appoints Jesus Christ to judge everyone's secret thoughts, just as my message says.
The Jews and the Law
17Some of you call yourselves Jews. You trust in the Law and take pride in God. 18By reading the Scriptures you learn how God wants you to behave, and you discover what is right. 19You are sure that you are a guide for the blind and a light for all who are in the dark. 20And since there is knowledge and truth in God's Law, you think you can instruct fools and teach young people.
21But how can you teach others when you refuse to learn? You preach it is wrong to steal. But do you steal? 22You say people should be faithful in marriage. But are you faithful? You hate idols, yet you rob their temples. 23You take pride in the Law, but you disobey the Law and bring shame to God. 24 It is just as the Scriptures tell us, “You have made foreigners say insulting things about God.”
25Being circumcised is worthwhile, if you obey the Law. But if you don't obey the Law, you are no better off than people who are not circumcised. 26In fact, if they obey the Law, they are as good as anyone who is circumcised. 27So everyone who obeys the Law, but has never been circumcised, will condemn you. Even though you are circumcised and have the Law, you still don't obey its teachings.
28Just because you live like a Jew and are circumcised doesn't make you a real Jew. 29 To be a real Jew you must obey the Law. True circumcision is something that happens deep in your heart, not something done to your body. And besides, you should want praise from God and not from humans.
translation_text:
1Dila nyiŋla, ni wanyi ka suik ate fi suok a dan nye wari a kaasi, fi bo wa buusa. Fi dan nye dila, fi ta ka kaasuŋ a jam fidek jigi dii nyiŋla, wie ŋaai ate fi ayen wa nye a kaasi la, fidek a tom ka ŋala dekdega. 2Tama abe seba kama ayen ku sum magsi ka Wen ta kaasuŋ a jam baai meena ale a tom dila la jigi. 3Alege fi dan bo baai ale a nye nyaŋa de la buusa alege fidek a tom ŋa, fi a poli ayen fi le baga chali be ate Wen kan nya fu a bo buusa? 4Yaa fi zɛri Wen nye maŋ kaai ale suiduŋ dii ale wa ale ŋman ta chichiiba ale fi diila kama, fi a poli ayen wa le kasim a nye ka dila a ta a cheŋ. Fi zɛ ayen Wen nye maŋka fi jigi a sak fu kama ayen fi basi fi tuimbaataŋa tomka? 5Ni tue kan wom. Ni sue be kan kaasi ale ni tuimbaataŋa. Ni a tom tuimbaata kama alege jaab kan daani ni, alege Wen suipuurumu ale wa wensie buusaŋa danni a dan paari ate wa ayen wa bo wensie buusa ale ni, wa sui le puuri ka nna yegayega ale ni ate wa te ni waalika. 6Da dila danni, Wen le tuni waai meena a magsi chaab ale ka ti wanyi wanyi ale tom diila. 7Baai meena ale ta chichiiba a tom tuimaŋsa a gisi zula ale nalim ale nyuvuri Wen jigi la, wa le te ba ka nyuvuri dii ale kan ta kpeglimka la. 8Alege baai ale a yaali badek nyaka mwuli ale a zɛri wensie suiku vaka ale kasim a tom tuimbaata daa meena la, Wen le basi ate wa suipuurumu a jam ba zuk. 9Ninam ale kumsa nna yegayega le jam baai meena ale a tom tuimbaata la jigi. Juuma le ba liŋ nya ninammu de ale kumsaŋa de ale ge ate baai mɛ ale kan daa Juuba la a nya ninammu de ale kumsaŋa de dila dekdega. 10Baai meena ale a tom tuimaŋsa la le nya zula ale nalim a boro ale suiyɔgni. Baai ale ka Juuba la le ba liŋ nya zulaŋa de ale nalimu de ale suiyɔgni de ale ge ate baai mɛ ale kan daa Juuba la, mɛ a nya. 11Boan nyiŋŋa, Wen ta ka nyeyeŋ Juuma ale baai mɛ ale kan daa Juuba la jigi.
12Baai ale kan daa Juuba la, a jam ka Moosis Sinsaŋŋa ate ba jam a tom tuimbaata. Ba an jam ta Moosis Sinsaŋŋa. Ba be le kpi kama alege Wen a kan pai wa Sinsaŋŋa a bo ba buusa. Alege Juuma a jam ta Moosis Sinsaŋŋa alege ba jam a tom ka tuimbaata. Ba mɛ be le kpi kama ate Wen pai wa Sinsaŋŋa a bo ba buusa. 13Nuruba dan wom ka wa Sinsaŋŋa nyiini ale kan va ŋa, ba kaasuŋku a diem bo ale ba kama, alege baai ale wom ŋa a yaa va ŋa la, wa kan ŋman nya ba kaasuŋku. 14Baai ale kan daa Juuba la, bala an nya Moosis Sinsaŋŋa alege ba suiniimaŋa a dan basi ate ba a tom Sinsaŋŋa ale a weeni dii ayen ba va la, badek suiniima ale a te ba Sinsaŋŋa. 15Ba nyeka a sak kama ayen Wen ŋmarisi wa Sinsaŋŋa a nyo ka ba suiniima po. Ba popolaŋa mɛ ale a bo ba buusa a weeni a sak ba ase ba kaasi yaa ba an kaasiya. 16Da dii danni ate Wen le bo ba buusa la, le nye ka dila. Wa le pai nuru meena wasusuŋŋa a ta ŋa nyini peelim niŋ ate Yeezu Kirisita bo ba buusa. Wen wamaŋsaŋa ate mi a sak nuruba ale a sak ti diila ale la.
17Nama baai ate mi a biisi ale ni la, a wi nidek ayen ka Juuba. Ni kasim a poli kama a weeni nidek ayen, <<Tama ta Moosis Sinsaŋŋa kama. Dila nyiŋla, Wen a vari ti a basi kama.>> Ni a nak ka kuusa ale ni ale ka dii ale Wen la. 18Nama dek abe seba Wen ale a yaali ayen ni a tom tuimaŋsa diila kama, dii nyiŋla ni zamsi Sinsaŋŋa po ayen fi lueri dii ale nala la a tom. 19Fi seba chak ayen, fi baga a chim nuru waai ale cheŋ be Wen suiku po la kpagi kama. Fi a nye ase ka bolim la a te baai ale bo legini po la. 20Fi a weeni ayen fi baga nuru baai ale ka betta ale bi paaluk la a sak kama. Fi be seba fi popo a chak ayen, fi ale ta Wen Sinsaŋŋa la, fi ta yam meena ale wensie meena kama. 21Nyaŋa de meena abe dan ka wensie ale fi waai ale a sak nuruba la, ka boa ate fi kan sak fi dega? Ti a sak nuruba a weeni ayen, <<Kan zu>>, alege fidek a zu? 22Fi a sak nuruba a weeni ayen, <<Kan nye kaboŋsa.>> Alege mi le bek fu ayen fidek a nye yaa fi kan nye? Fi kisi bɔgta kama alege mi ale bek fu ayen, <<Fidek a zu ŋanta a ta nyini weleŋsa jigi a nyini yaa fi kan zu a ta a nyini? 23Fi ta zupagruk kama ale Wen Sinsaŋŋa, alege a kaasi ŋa. Kaasika de a basi ate Wen a nya chivie yaa wa kan nya?>> 24Ba be ŋmarisi Wen gbaŋka po kama ayen, << Baai ale kan daa Juuba la, a kaasi Wen yuei kama nama Juuma nyiŋ.>>
25Nama Juuma dan gebi ni yoaŋa ale a va Moosis Sinsaŋŋa, ni yoaŋa gebika ta kiri kama. Alege ni dan a kaasi wa Sinsaŋŋa ni a nye ase ni an gebi ni yoaŋa kama la. 26Nuruba abe dan kan gebi ba yoa ale ge a va dii ate Moosis Sinsaŋŋa a weeni ayen nuruba a nye la, Wen le nya ba ase ba gebi ba yoaŋa kama la. 27Nama ta Moosis Sinsaŋŋa kama ate ŋa ŋmarisi dua. Ni be a gebi ni yoaŋa mɛ kama. Alege Sinsaŋŋa ate ni ta la ale ni ale a gebi ni yoaŋa la, ni kan diem a va Moosis Sinsaŋŋa ale a weeni diila. Alege baai ale kan gebi ba yoaŋa la, bala gela a va Moosis Sinsaŋŋa ale a weeni diila kama alege ba ka ŋa. Ba be ale a nye nna la a basi kama ate ba biisi a gaam nama Juuma. 28Basi ate m bek ni beŋŋa de ayen, ka wana dek ale potim ka Juu? Ka waai ale gebi wa yoari la ale Juu? Nuru peelim nyeka nyiini a kan sak kama ayen nuru wala a sum ale Juu. Ku be daa fi nin gebi fi yoari ale a sak ayen fi sum ka Juu. 29Alege waai ale sum ka Juu la ale waai ale va Sinsaŋŋa a ta nyini wa suinum po la. Ku kiri mɛ ale fi an gebi ka fi yoanni nyiini ayen ku sak ayen fi sum ka Juu alege ku kiri ale, fi pai ka fi suinummu a te Wen. Gebika abe ka gebi kaai ate Wen Chiika a gebi fi suinummu la, daa fi nyiŋka wari ya. Nuruwa de choa abe kan nya pimpauk nuruba jigi, alege ka Wen pimpauk nyiini ate wa a nya.

english_text:
1What good is it to be a Jew? What good is it to be circumcised? 2It is good in a lot of ways! First of all, God's messages were spoken to the Jews. 3It is true that some of them did not believe the message. But does this mean that God cannot be trusted, just because they did not have faith? 4 No, indeed! God tells the truth, even if everyone else is a liar. The Scriptures say about God,
“Your words
will be proven true,
and in court
you will win your case.”
5If our evil deeds show how right God is, then what can we say? Is it wrong for God to become angry and punish us? What a foolish thing to ask. 6But the answer is, “No.” Otherwise, how could God judge the world? 7Since your lies bring great honor to God by showing how truthful he is, you may ask why God still says you are a sinner. 8You might as well say, “Let's do something evil, so that something good will come of it!” Some people even claim that we are saying this. But God is fair and will judge them as well.
No One Is Good
9What does all this mean? Does it mean that we Jews are better off than the Gentiles? No, it doesn't! Jews, as well as Gentiles, are ruled by sin, just as I have said. 10 The Scriptures tell us,
“No one is acceptable to God!
11Not one of them understands
or even searches for God.
12They have all turned away
and are worthless.
There isn't one person
who does right.
13 Their words are like
an open pit,
and their tongues are good
only for telling lies.
Each word is as deadly
as the fangs of a snake,
14 and they say nothing
but bitter curses.
15 These people quickly
become violent.
16Wherever they go,
they leave ruin
and destruction.
17They don't know how
to live in peace.
18 They don't even fear God.”
19We know that everything in the Law was written for those who are under its power. The Law says these things to stop anyone from making excuses and to let God show that the whole world is guilty. 20 God doesn't accept people simply because they obey the Law. No, indeed! All the Law does is to point out our sin.
God's Way of Accepting People
21Now we see how God does make us acceptable to him. The Law and the Prophets tell how we become acceptable, and it isn't by obeying the Law of Moses. 22 God treats everyone alike. He accepts people only because they have faith in Jesus Christ. 23All of us have sinned and fallen short of God's glory. 24But God treats us much better than we deserve, and because of Christ Jesus, he freely accepts us and sets us free from our sins. 25-26 God sent Christ to be our sacrifice. Christ offered his life's blood, so by faith in him we could come to God. And God did this to show that in the past he was right to be patient and forgive sinners. This also shows that God is right when he accepts people who have faith in Jesus.
27What is left for us to brag about? Not a thing! Is it because we obeyed some law? No! It is because of faith. 28We see that people are acceptable to God because they have faith, and not because they obey the Law. 29Does God belong only to the Jews? Isn't he also the God of the Gentiles? Yes, he is! 30 There is only one God, and he accepts Gentiles as well as Jews, simply because of their faith. 31Do we destroy the Law by our faith? Not at all! We make it even more powerful.
translation_text:
1Ku nyuenta abe le boa ase fi nin ka Juu? Fi gaam waai ale kan daa Juu la kama? Ka boan nyuenta ate ba a nya ku po ale ba ale gebi ba yoaŋa la? 2Juuma ta nyuenta kama wie yegayega po a gaam baai ale kan daa Juuba la. Ni basi ate m liŋ weeni a sak ni ayen Wen jam pai wa wieŋa a nyo ka Juuma nisima po. 3Alege ni basi ate m bek ni ayen ase Juuma gela a daam dan kan ta wensie ale Wen, nya kude a sak kama ayen Wen mɛ a kan ta wensie? 4Aaya, waai meena abe dan poom ka velimvendik, Wen kasim ka wensie nyɔnɔ. Ase ba ale ŋmarisi wa gbaŋka po ayen, <<Fi dan biisi, wensie boro kama. Fi be dan bo buusa, fi biisi a de kama.>> (Yiila 51:4) 5Ase ti tuimbaata a dan basi ate nuruba a nya Wen weleŋsaŋa, ku be ka wabiowa ase Wen a nin te ti waalika ti tuimbaataŋa nyiŋŋa? Mi a biisi kama ase nuru ale a biisi diila. 6Aaya, Wen a dan kan daa wensie Wen ya, wa le nye ka sɛ a bo tɛŋka demma buusa? 7Nuru abe ŋman baga a weeni kama ayen, <<Mi ale kan ta wensie la a basi kama ate nuruba a nya Wen wensieŋa a yaa a te wa zula dila nyiŋŋa? Ku be dan ka dila, Wen nye ka sɛ a baga a bo buusa a mini mi tuimbaata nyɔnɔwa?>> 8Ku be dan ka dila mɛ, ka boa ale soa ate ni kan kasim a tom tuimbaata ate wamaŋsa nyini ŋa po a nyini? Nuruba gela a toariŋ mi kama a weeni ayen ka mi ale a weeni wanni de choawa. Toariŋka de abe ka leeta a te mu. Wen abe dan bo mini ba ku ka wensie.
9Dila nyiŋla, tama baai ale ka Juuba la, tama chim ka nuru weleŋsa a gaam baai ale kan daa Juuba la? Aaya. M poom weeni a sak ni kama ayen biem ale soa baai ale ka Juuba la, ale baai ale kan daa Juuba la meena. 10Ba ŋmarisi Wen gbaŋka po ayen, <<Nuru yeŋ bola karo a chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ, 11Nuru karo mɛ a ta yammoa. Nuru karo a yaali ayen wa zuli Wen ya. 12Waai meena cheŋ wensie suiku po a be kama ale chim nuru kayaata mɛ. Nuru yeŋ bola karo a tom tuimaŋsa. 13Ba biika a basi ate ka nuruba a kpi. Ba noaŋa sueri ale ka venta nyiini. (Yiila 5:9) Ba biika ka leeta nna ase waapiisa domka la. (Yiila 140:3) 14Ba biik po ka kikaasa nyiini nna yegayega. (Yiila 10:7) 15Ba kan bola a beni ale ge a ko nuru. 16Juijui meena ate ba a cheŋ la, ba a basi ka kaasuŋ ale ninam ku jigini. 17Ba zɛ suik kuui ate suiyɔgni a boro la. (Azaya 59:8) 18Wen yɔgsum chalika a ka ba nina po.>> (Yiila 36:1)
19Ti seba ayen Juuma pɛ kama ayen ba le va Moosis Sinsaŋŋa ale a weeni dii meena la. Dila nyiŋla, Sinsaŋŋa ale a weeni dii meena la a cheŋ ka bala jigi. Wen nye ku ka dila ayen waai meena a nya wadek kaasuŋku. Nuru be kan ta wari a weeni wanni de po. 20Dila nyiŋla, nuru dan va Wen Sinsaŋŋa ale a weeni diila, dila kan basi ate wa a chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ Wen jigiya. Alege Wen Sinsaŋŋa weeni a sak ti kama biem ale ka diila.
21Alege yɔgyɔgla de Wen a pai sak wa le wa nye dii ate nuruba a chim wayɔrisima nyam la kama. Moosis Sinsaŋŋa ale Wen biisiteerɔma a biisi dila wari kama, alege ku ka wari a nye ale Moosis Sinsaŋŋa. 22Alege ka waai meena ale ta siaka ale Yeezu Kirisita la ate wa a nye ate nuru wala choa a chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ wa Wen jigi. Boan nyiŋŋa, lukka karo ale Juu ale waai ale kan daa Juu la. 23Nurubiik meena abe tom kaasi kama, a yaa yalima ale Wen zulaŋa. 24Alege Wen tiirim niaka nyiŋ ate ti nya da tuesika a yaa chim wayɔrisima nyam Yeezu Kirisita nyiŋ. 25Wen basi kama ate Yeezu kpi tama wabaataŋa nyiŋ ayen ti dan ta siaka ale wa, ti le nya vɔŋteka. Wen nye nna kama ayen ku sak nuruba ayen wa, Wen, ka wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ. Diipo ate Yeezu an diem jam kpi la, Wen jam ta chichiiba kama a yik wadek an namsi nuruba ba wabaata nyiŋŋa. 26Alege yɔgyɔgla de, Yeezu kummu nyiŋ ate Wen yaa nya nurubiik wabaataŋa zuk ayen ku sak ayen Wen ka nyemagsika nyɔnɔ. Ku be a sak kama ayen wa ka nyemagsika nyɔnɔ ate baai meena ale ta siaka ale Yeezu la, wa basi kama ate ba chim nyemagsika nyam.
27Be ka boan nyiŋ ate ni a nak kuusa? Kuusa nakka karo. Be ka boan ale soa ate kuusa nakka karo? Ku ka Moosis Sinsaŋŋa ale a weeni ti ayen ti nye diila nyiŋŋa? Aaya. Ku ka siaka ale Yeezu nyiŋ. 28Boan nyiŋŋa, ti yaa baga a weeni kama ale sebi chak mɛ ayen ku daa Moosis Sinsaŋŋa vaka nyiŋ ale soa ate nuru a chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ, alege ka wa siaka nyiini ale Wen ale baga a nye ate kula nyɔnɔwa a chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ. 29Ti baga a weeni ayen Wen ka Juuma nyiini Wen ya? Aaya. Wa ka baai ale kan daa Juuba la mɛ Wen. 30Dii nyiŋla, Wen ka Wen yeŋ dekki. Wen va ka boan nyiŋ a nye ate Juu a chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ? Ka wa siaka nyiŋ. Wa be va ka boan nyiŋ mɛ a nye ate waai ale kan daa Juu la a chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ? Ka wa mɛ siaka nyiŋ.
31Nya kude be a sak kama ayen tama siaka a nye kama ate Moosis Sinsaŋŋa ka kiriya? Aaya. Ku a sak kama ayen wensie bo ŋa po kama.

english_text:
The Example of Abraham
1Well then, what can we say about our ancestor Abraham? 2If he became acceptable to God because of what he did, then he would have something to brag about. But he would never be able to brag about it to God. 3 The Scriptures say, “God accepted Abraham because Abraham had faith in him.”
4Money paid to workers isn't a gift. It is something they earn by working. 5But you cannot make God accept you because of something you do. God accepts sinners only because they have faith in him. 6In the Scriptures David talks about the blessings that come to people who are acceptable to God, even though they don't do anything to deserve these blessings. David says,
7-8 “What a blessing
when God forgives our sins
and our evil deeds.
What a blessing
when the Lord erases our sins
from his book.”
9Are these blessings meant for circumcised people or for those who are not circumcised? Well, the Scriptures say that God accepted Abraham because Abraham had faith in him. 10But when did this happen? Was it before or after Abraham was circumcised? Of course, it was before.
11 Abraham let himself be circumcised to show he had been accepted because of his faith even before he was circumcised. This makes Abraham the father of all who are acceptable to God because of their faith, even though they are not circumcised. 12This also makes Abraham the father of everyone who is circumcised and has faith in God, as Abraham did before he was circumcised.
The Promise Is for All Who Have Faith
13 God promised Abraham and his descendants that he would give them the world. This promise wasn't made because Abraham had obeyed a law, but because his faith in God made him acceptable. 14 If Abraham and his descendants were given this promise because they had obeyed a law, then faith would mean nothing, and the promise would be worthless.
15God becomes angry when his Law is broken. But where there isn't a law, it cannot be broken. 16 Everything depends on having faith in God, so that God's promise is assured by his gift of undeserved grace. This promise isn't only for Abraham's descendants who have the Law. It is for all who are Abraham's descendants because they have faith, just as he did. Abraham is the ancestor of us all. 17 The Scriptures say that Abraham would become the ancestor of many nations. This promise was made to Abraham because he had faith in God, who raises the dead to life and creates new things.
18 God promised Abraham a lot of descendants. And when it all seemed hopeless, Abraham still had faith in God and became the ancestor of many nations. 19 Abraham's faith never became weak, not even when he was nearly 100 years old. He knew he was almost dead and that his wife Sarah could not have children. 20But Abraham never doubted or questioned God's promise. His faith made him strong, and he gave all the credit to God.
21Abraham was certain that God could do what he had promised. 22So God accepted him, 23just as we read in the Scriptures. But these words were not written only for Abraham. 24They were written for us, since we will also be accepted because of our faith in God, who raised our Lord Jesus to life. 25 God gave Jesus to die for our sins, and he raised him to life, so that we would be made acceptable to God.
translation_text:
1Ku be dan ka dila, ti ta ka boan wari ayen ti weeni a magsi chaab ale ti kokpieŋka Abrayam? 2Wen daam a dan nya ka Abrayam tuim maŋsaŋa nyiini a yaa weeni ayen wa ka wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ, ŋala nyiŋ, Abrayam daam ate te wadek ka pimpauk. Alege wa an jam baga a zaani Wen niŋ a pak wa dega. 3Boan nyiŋŋa, ba ŋmarisi wa wie kama Wen gbaŋka po ayen, <<Abrayam jam ta siaka kama ale Wen. Dila ale soa ate Wen jam nye ate wa chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ.>> (Piilimka 15:6) Nya kude ka tiirim, ku daa wari ate wa nye. 4Nuru dan pai nuru ayen wa tom a te wa ale ge ate wa tuni wa, nuruwa a tuni wa kama tutuna ŋaai ate wa a tuni wa la. Tutunaŋa de daa tiirimoa. 5Suik kula po, waai a dan pai wa tuim maŋsaŋa a ta jam Wen jigi ayen ŋala nyiŋ Wen nye ate wa chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ, Wen kan nye dila ase tutuna la a te wa. Ku ka tiirim. Suik kuui nyiini ate Wen a nye ate nuru a chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ la ale siaka nyiini ale wa. Dii nyiŋla, wa ka waai ale a nye ate wabaata nyam a chim wayɔrisima nyam ba siaka ale wa nyiŋ. 6Deevid ale jam weeni diila kiri ale la mɛ ayen nuru waai ate Wen a kan nya wa tuima alege a nye ate wa a chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ la, kula nyɔnɔwa sui abe le peenti ka nna yegayega. 7Wa ale weeni dii Wen gbaŋka po la ale nna ayen, <<Nuru baai ate Wen a vɔŋ ba wabaataŋa a te ba la, ba sue le peenti kama. Wa a duisi ba wabaataŋa a basi kama. 8Nuru waai ate Wen a kan ta wa wabaataŋa la, a ta suipeentik kama.>> (Yiila 32:1, 2)
9Be ka baai ale a gebi ba yoaŋa la nyiini ale ta suipeentiga? Yaa baai mɛ ale kan a gebi la ta suipeentik kama? Aaya. Ba meena ta suipeentik kama. M poom liŋ weeni sak ni kama a ta nyini Wen gbaŋka po a magsi chaab ale Abrayam ale ta siaka dii ale Wen la. Ka siaka de nyiŋ ale soa ate Wen nye ate wa chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ. 10Ka dimpo ate Wen wi Abrayam ayen wa yaa ka wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ? Ka diipo ate wa gebi wa yoanni la yaa ka diipo ate wa an diem gebi la? Wen jam nye ate wa chim ka wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ ale ge ate wa gebi wa yoanni. 11Gebika de abe jam a sak kama ayen ka wa siaka ale Wen nyiŋ ale soa ate wa wi wa ayen wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ ale ge ate wa yaa gebi wa yoanni. Dila abe ale soa ate baai meena ale ta siaka ale Wen alege an gebi ba yoaŋa, ate Wen nye ate ba chim wayɔrisima nyam la, a baga a wi Abrayam ayen ba ko. 12Baai mɛ ale gebi ba yoaŋa la a wi Abrayam ayen ba ko ase ba a nin ta siaka ale Wen ase Abrayam la, alege ate wa yaa gebi wa yoanni la.
13Wen jam puulim kama ayen Abrayam ale wa ŋaaŋbisaŋa le jam soa ka tɛŋka meena. Ku be jam daa Abrayam ale jam va Moosis Sinsaŋŋa la nyiŋŋa. Ku jam ka Abrayam ale ta siaka ale Wen ate wa nye ate wa chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ la nyiŋ ale soa ate wa jam puulim dila. 14Ku be dan ka nuru baai ale a va Moosis Sinsaŋŋa la le ba soa tɛŋka, nurubiik siaka ale Wen ka kiri ya ate Wen puulim ka a chim kinla nyiŋ. 15Wen ta suipuurum kama ale baai ale kaa va wa sinsaŋŋa la. Wa be le te ba ka waalika. Sinsaŋŋa abe dan kan karo, nuruba ate an baga le zɛri ŋa.
16Ka boan ale soa ate Wen le nye ate ti chim wayɔrisima nyam ti siaka nyiŋŋa? Dii nyiŋ ale soa ate wa le nye dila la ale wa ale puulim ayen wa le niak ti wa niaka nyiŋla. Dii abe le pai a saŋ la ale, pumpuulimaŋa de le sum chim ka wensie a te Abrayam ŋaaŋbisaŋa meena baai ale ta siaka ase Abrayam dek la. Baai ale va Sinsaŋŋa ale baai ale kan va ŋa la. Dii nyiŋla, Abrayam ka tama meena ko 17ase ba ale ŋmarisi Wen gbaŋka po dii ayen Wen weeni Abrayam ayen, <<Ka mi ale nye ate fi chim tɛŋsa yega ko.>> (Piilimka 17:5) Dila nyiŋla, Wen jigi, wa ka tama ko. Abrayam dek abe jam ta siaka kama ale Wenni de waai ale a nak kpilima a yiti kum po a te ba vum la. Wa be ka waai ale a basi ate jabuui ale kan boro la a boro.
18Ase Wen ale weeni Abrayam ayen wa le basi ate wa biak nidoabinni a yaa ta ŋaaŋbisa yegayega la, Abrayam jam ta siaka ale yiila Wen jigi kama alege ku an poom jam magsi ayen wa ta siaka ale yiila dila po. Alege ku sum jam chim ka wensie ate Abrayam chim tɛŋsa yega ko ase ba ale ŋmarisi Wen gbaŋka po dii ayen Wen weeni Abrayam ayen <<Fi ŋaaŋbisaŋa le piisi ka dila.>> (Piilimka 15:5) 19Dila powa, Abrayam jam boro a moata ka bena kook, alege wa powa Saara an diem jam biaya. Abrayam jam poli wadek jigi kama a yaa weeni wadek ayen, <<Mi poom moata ka kum. M powa mɛ a kan biagi,>> alege Abrayam siaka ale Wen an diem jam baliŋya. 20Wa jam ka chichama ale Wen pumpuulimaŋa. Wa siaka jam te wa ka pagrim ate wa a te Wen zula. 21Wa jam seba chak kama ayen Wen baga a nye wa ale puulim ayen wa nye diila kama. 22Wa siaka nyiŋ ale soa ate Wen nye ate wa chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ. (Piilimka 15:6) 23Ba ale ŋmarisi dii Wen gbaŋka po ayen m nye ate Abrayam chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ la, ba an ŋmarisi kama a te wadek wa nyiini, 24alege tama mɛ nyiŋ, ate ku le gum du te ti la, ase baai ale ta siaka ale wa la, waai ale nak Yeezu ti Naawenni a yiti kum po la, 25Waai ate wa pai wa a te ti tom kaasika nyiŋ la, ale nak wa yiti kum po ti nyemagsika nyiŋ la.

english_text:
What It Means To Be Acceptable to God
1By faith we have been made acceptable to God. And now, thanks to our Lord Jesus Christ, we have peace with God. 2Christ has also introduced us to God's gift of undeserved grace on which we now take our stand. So we are happy, as we look forward to sharing in the glory of God. 3But that's not all! We gladly suffer, because we know that suffering helps us to endure. 4And endurance builds character, which gives us a hope 5that will never disappoint us. All of this happens because God has given us the Holy Spirit, who fills our hearts with his love.
6Christ died for us at a time when we were helpless and sinful. 7No one is really willing to die for an honest person, though someone might be willing to die for a truly good person. 8But God showed how much he loved us by having Christ die for us, even though we were sinful.
9But there is more! Now that God has accepted us because Christ sacrificed his life's blood, we will also be kept safe from God's anger. 10Even when we were God's enemies, he made peace with us, because his Son died for us. Yet something even greater than friendship is ours. Now that we are at peace with God, we will be saved by the life of his Son. 11And in addition to everything else, we are happy because God sent our Lord Jesus Christ to make peace with us.
Adam and Christ
12 Adam sinned, and that sin brought death into the world. Now everyone has sinned, and so everyone must die. 13Sin was in the world before the Law came. But no record of sin was kept, because there was no Law. 14Yet death still had power over all who lived from the time of Adam to the time of Moses. This happened, though not everyone disobeyed a direct command from God, as Adam did.
In some ways Adam is like Christ who came later. 15But the gift of God's undeserved grace was very different from Adam's sin. That one sin brought death to many others. Yet in an even greater way, Jesus Christ alone brought God's gift of undeserved grace to many people.
16There is a lot of difference between Adam's sin and God's gift. That one sin led to punishment. But God's gift made it possible for us to be acceptable to him, even though we have sinned many times. 17Death ruled like a king because Adam had sinned. But that cannot compare with what Jesus Christ has done. God has treated us with undeserved grace, and he has accepted us because of Jesus. And so we will live and rule like kings.
18 Everyone was going to be punished because Adam sinned. But because of the good thing that Christ has done, God accepts us and gives us the gift of life. 19Adam disobeyed God and caused many others to be sinners. But Jesus obeyed him and will make many people acceptable to God.
20The Law came, so that the full power of sin could be seen. Yet where sin was powerful, God's gift of undeserved grace was even more powerful. 21Sin ruled by means of death. But God's gift of grace now rules, and God has accepted us because of Jesus Christ our Lord. This means that we will have eternal life.
translation_text:
1Dila nyiŋla, ku ka ti siaka nyiŋ ale soa ate Wen baga nye ate ti chim wayɔrisima nyam. Dila abe le soa ate tama va Yeezu Kirisita ti Nyɔnɔwa nyiŋ ate tama ale Wen a yaa ta suiyɔgni ale chaab. 2Ti siaka ale Yeezu Kirisita nyiŋ mɛ abe le soa ate ti baga a nya Wen niaka nyeka ate wa ta ale ti la. Wa te ti ka yiila ale ŋmanteka ayen dai yeŋ po Wen ale tama le jam maa chaab a ta Wen zulaŋa. 3Daa ti ale maa chaab ale wa a ta wa zulaŋa la ale basi ate ti sue peenti, alege nuruba dan poom basi ate ti a nam, ti sue le peenti kama. Dii nyiŋla, tama seba ayen ninammu de a basi kama ate ti a ta chichiiba ninammu po. 4Ti suiduŋmaŋa a basi kama ate ti a chim wensie nyam. Nya kude abe a te ti ka yiila ŋaai ate m poom weeni la. Yiilaŋa de abe daa kinla nyiŋŋa. 5Wen pai wa Chiika nyo ka ti suiniima po nalimnyiini. Chiika abe ale Wen tiirim ate wa pai te tama. Wa be va ka Chiika de nyiŋ a pai wa yaalika a sueri ti suiniimaŋa. Dila ale soa ate yiila ŋaai ate ti ta la daa kinla nyiŋŋa.
6Di po ti an jam ta pagrim a maari ti dega. Alege ka da dii dai ate Wen lueri la ate Kirisita yaa zaani tama tuimbaata nyama naŋkula po a kpi te ti. 7Nuru dan chim nuru maŋ, da dii dai nuru wa choa a baga a siak kama ayen wa zaani wa naŋkula po a kpi te kula nyɔnɔwa. Alege ku pagra kama ate nuru nye dila. 8Alege tama baai mɛ ale ka wabaata nyam la, Kirisita zaani ka tama naŋkula po a kpi te ti. Nya kude abe a sak ka Wen ale ta yaalika nalimnyiini ale ti diila. 9Wa kummu nyiŋ abe ale soa ate Wen baga a nye ate ti a chim wayɔrisima nyam. Ase Wen dan baga a nye ate tama a chim wayɔrisima nyam Yeezu kummu nyiŋ, be ka boa le ku kasi ate wa kan vari ti waali kaai ate wa le te ti la po a basi Yeezu nyiŋŋa? 10Ti jam ka Wen dachaasa, alege yɔgyɔgla de, wa va ka wa nidoabinni kummu nyiŋ a nye ate ti ŋman chim wa doaba. Wa nidoabinni abe dan baga a nye nya kude, ka boa le ku kasi ate yɔgyɔgla de wa ale vua la wa an baga a te varibasika? 11Daa ku meena abe ale dila. Wa dii ale ŋman gum du la ale, Wen basi kama ate ti sue peenti nna yegayega ale wa ale va Yeezu Kirisita ti Nyɔnɔwa nyiŋ a nye dii a te ti la. Yɔgyɔgla de be ka Yeezu Kirisita ale nye ate tama chim Wen doaba.
12Nuru ale jam bo tɛŋzuk de dipo. Wa yuei jam ale Adam. Biem va ka nuruwa de jigi a jam tɛŋzuk de meena. Biemu de abe ale soa ate kum jam nurubiik meena jigi. Dila be ale soa ate baai meena ale va wa ŋaaŋ la a kpi. Boan nyiŋŋa, ti meena tom ka biem. 13Biem liŋ jam boro kama ale ge ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ ate Wen yaa pai wa Sinsaŋŋa a te ba. Wa sinsaŋŋa ale kan diem jam boro diipo la, wa an jam a chiini wabaata. 14Alege a ta nyini diipo ate Adam boro la, a ta jam paari diipo ate Wen jam pai wa sinsaŋŋa a te Moosis la, nuruba jam a kpi kama. Baai mɛ ale jam poom kan zɛri Wen nɔi ase Adam ale nye diila, ba mɛ jam a kpi kama. Alege Wen jam poli kama ayen Adam nyeka a sak ti wari a magsi chaab ale waai ale wa jam la.
15Wen tiirimu ale Adam ale zɛri wa nɔi diila a daa bunyi. Ase sɛ la? Nuru yeŋ ale zɛri Wen nɔi la nyiŋ ale soa ate nuru boari kpi. Alege Wen ŋmanteka a gaam ka nna yegayega. Wa tiirim buui ate wa pai te nuru boari la, wa va ka nuru yeŋka Yeezu Kirisita ŋmanteka nyiŋ a te wa tiirimu nuru boanni. 16Adam ale jam tom biemu la, ka boan ale nye ya? Be ka boan jaab ale nye ase Wen ale va wa niaka nyiŋ a te ti wa tiirimu la? Be nya, Adam zɛri Wen nɔi kama ate Wen a bo ba buusa. Wen be ale va wa nyemagsika nyiŋ a te ti wa tiirimu la, wa yaa weeni ayen nurubiik yaa a chim wayɔrisima nyɔnɔ Yeezu nyiŋ. 17Nuru yeŋka ale zɛri Wen la nyiŋ ale soa ate kum a jam. Alege nuru yeŋka Yeezu Kirisita ale nye dii a te nurubiik la a zuak gaam taam kama. Baai meena abe ale a tuesi wa ŋmanteka yegayega ale wa ale nye ate nuruba a chim wayɔrisima nyam la, ka wa tiirim ale la ate wa pai te ba. Bala abe le va ka Yeezu Kirisita nyiŋ a ta nyuvuri. Ba le chim ka nalima mɛ.
18Suik kula po, nuru yeŋka ale zɛri Wen nɔi ate dila basi ate Wen a bo ba buusa, suik kula po dekdega ate nuru yeŋ waai ale siak a te Wen nɔnni la a basi ate waai meena a baga a chim wayɔrisima nyam a nya nyemagsika ale nyuvuri dii ale kan ta kpeglimka la. 19Nuru yeŋ ale jam zɛri Wen nɔi vaka la, dila basi kama ate nuru boari chim tuimbaata nyam wala nyiŋ. Nuru yeŋ mɛ ale jam va Wen nɔi la dila basi kama ate Wen nye ate nuru boari chim wayɔrisima nyam. 20Wen te wa sinsaŋŋa Juuma kama ayen ba seba ayen ba ale kasim jam a nye wie ŋaai la ba a zɛri ka wa nɔi. Alege nurubiik biemu ale ŋmasi chim a gum du la, Wen ŋmanteka mɛ a ŋmasi chim a gum du kama. 21Dila nyiŋla, biem ale va ka kum nyiŋ a soa nurubiik la, Wen ŋmanteka mɛ a va ka wayɔrisima nyiŋ a soa nurubiik dii nyiŋla, ka wa niaka nyiŋ ale soa ate ti chim wayɔrisima nyam. Dila abe basi kama ate ti yaa va Yeezu Kirisita ti Naawenni nyiŋ a nya nyuvuri dii ale kan ta kpeglimka la.

english_text:
Dead to Sin but Alive because of Christ
1What should we say? Should we keep on sinning, so that God's gift of undeserved grace will show up even better? 2No, we should not! If we are dead to sin, how can we go on sinning? 3Don't you know that all who share in Christ Jesus by being baptized also share in his death? 4 When we were baptized, we died and were buried with Christ. We were baptized, so we would live a new life, as Christ was raised to life by the glory of God the Father.
5If we shared in Jesus' death by being baptized, we will be raised to life with him. 6We know that the persons we used to be were nailed to the cross with Jesus. This was done, so our sinful bodies would no longer be the slaves of sin. 7We know sin doesn't have power over dead people.
8As surely as we died with Christ, we believe we will also live with him. 9We know that death no longer has any power over Christ. He died and was raised to life, never again to die. 10When Christ died, he died for sin once and for all. But now he is alive, and he lives only for God. 11In the same way, you must think of yourselves as dead to the power of sin. But Christ Jesus has given life to you, and you live for God.
12Don't let sin rule your body. After all, your body is bound to die, so don't obey its desires 13or let any part of it become a slave of evil. Give yourselves to God, as people who have been raised from death to life. Make every part of your body a slave that pleases God. 14Don't let sin keep ruling your lives. You are ruled by God's undeserved grace and not by the Law.
Slaves Who Do What Pleases God
15What does all this mean? Does it mean we are free to sin, because we are ruled by God's gift of undeserved grace and not by the Law? Certainly not! 16Don't you know that you are slaves of anyone you obey? You can be slaves of sin and die, or you can be obedient slaves of God and be acceptable to him. 17You used to be slaves of sin. But I thank God that with all your heart you followed the example set forth in the teaching you received. 18Now you are set free from sin and are slaves who please God.
19I am using these everyday examples, because in some ways you are still weak. You used to let the different parts of your body be slaves of your evil thoughts. But now you must make every part of your body serve God, so that you will belong completely to him.
20When you were slaves of sin, you didn't have to please God. 21But what good did you receive from the things you did? All you have to show for them is your shame, and they lead to death. 22Now you have been set free from sin, and you are God's slaves. This will make you holy and will lead you to eternal life. 23Sin pays off with death. But God's gift is eternal life given by Jesus Christ our Lord.
translation_text:
1Ku be dan ka dila, ti le weeni ka boa? Ku magsi ayen ti kasim a tom tuimbaata taam wuu ate Wen kasim ta wa ŋmanteka ale ti a gum du? 2Aaya. Dii nyiŋla, biem jigi, ti kpi kama. Dila nyiŋla, ku an magsi ayen ti ŋman a nye ase biem jigi ti vua kama la. 3Mi a yaali kama ayen ni seba ayen ba ale te ti soka ayen tama ale Yeezu Kirisita chim bunyi la, ku a nye ase tama ale wa maa chaab a kpi kama la. 4Ba ale te ti soka la, ku a nye ase ba gu tama ale wa a gum ka chaab la. Alege Wen ti kowa a nak Kirisita a yiti kum po kama ale Kowa zulaŋa. Tama mɛ abe yiti kum po kama ayen tama mɛ ta nyuvuri paali. Ti ŋman ka ti nye kpakka. 5Ti be dan siak ayen tama ale wa maa chaab kpi kama, ti baga a siak kama mɛ ayen Wen le nak ti kama a yiti kum po ase wa ale nak wa a yiti kum po diila. 6Tama be seba kama ayen ti nye kpakka a maa chaab a kpi kama ale Yeezu wa jabarimu nyiŋ ayen pagrim buui ale soa ate ti nye kpakka de a tom biem tuima la a yaa kaasi ate ti kan ŋman chim biem yɔmma. 7Diila waai ale kpi la, biem a ka pagrim wa zuwa.
8Tama ale Kirisita abe ale maa chaab kpi la, ti ta siaka kama ayen wa ale vua la, tama mɛ vua kama. 9Wen ale nak Kirisita yiti kum po. Tama mɛ abe seba kama ayen Yeezu abe kan ŋman kpi. Kum be ŋman ka pagrim wa zuwa. 10Wa kpi ka bunyi dekki. Wa be kpi kama ayen biem kan ŋman ta pagrim. Yɔgyɔgla de, wa vua kama ate Wen soa wa. 11Suik kula po, ni ta ku ni zuima po ayen biem jigi, ni kpi kama. Wen jigi mɛ, ni vua kama Yeezu Kirisita nyiŋ.
12Ni kan basi ate biem soa ni, bu le nye kama ate ni a nye ni nyiŋsaŋa ale a yaali waba tii la. 13Ni be kan pai ni nyiŋsaŋa juijui ya a te biem ate bu nye ate nyiŋka kabta a tom tuimbaata. Alege, ku a fɛ kama ayen ni pai nidek a te Wen ase nuru baai ale nyini kum po a nyini vum po diila, a pai ni nyiŋka kabta a te Wen ate wa pai ni a tom wayɔrisima tuima. 14Boan nyiŋŋa, biem a kan ŋman chim ni nyɔnɔ a soa ni dii nyiŋla, ni an boro ka Moosis Sinsaŋŋa ale a weeni ni ayen ni a nye diila nyiŋŋa, alege, ni boro ka Wen ale va wa ŋmanteka nyiŋ a nye jabuui a te ni la nyiŋ.
15Ku be dan ka wensie ayen ti an boro ka Moosis Sinsaŋŋa ale a weeni ti ayen ti nye diila, ku be nala kama ate ti kasim a tom tuimbaata ale ge a poli ayen ti boro ka Wen ŋmanteka nyiŋŋa? Aaya. 16Nama zɛ ayen fi dan pai fidek a te nuru ayen fi a siak wa nɔi, fi a chim ka kula nyɔnɔwa yɔma? Nama be dan pai nidek a te biem tuima ni a chim ka biem yɔm. Dila be a basi ate ni a kpi kama. Alege ni dan pai nidek a te Wen a va wa nɔi, ni a chim ka wa yɔm ate dila basi ate ni chim wayɔrisima nyam. 17Ni jam ka biem yɔm, alege yɔgyɔgla de, mi a nye Wen jiam nalimnyiini boan nyiŋŋa, ni siak kama ale ni suiniima meena a te wensie sinsak ŋaai ate ni nya la. 18Wen vari ni kama biem nisa po a basi ale ge ate ni yaa chim wayɔrisima yɔm. 19Mi a biisi ase ka nurubiik la, dii nyiŋla ni wobsa kama nyiŋka po. Dila ale soa ate m pai yɔmawa ale wa nyɔnɔwa a magsi a sak ni la. Ni nya de, dipo, ni jam pai ka nidek meena ase yɔm la a te tuimbaata ale gaasa tuima. Suik kula po dekdega, ku a fɛ kama yɔgyɔgla de ayen ni pai nidek meena ase yɔm la a te wayɔrisima tuima ate ni sum chim nuru weleŋsa.
20Ni ale jam ka biem yɔm la, wayɔrisima an jam soa ni. 21Ku be ale jam ka dii ni jigi la, be ka boan jaab nyuenta ate ni jam nya? Ni jam nya ka chivie nyiini. Wieŋa de ŋaai abe ale basi ate ni yaa ta chivie la, wa ŋala abe le ŋa basi ate ni kpi ase ni nin diem a tom ŋa. 22Alege yɔgyɔgla de, Wen vari ni a ta nyini biem po a nyini kama. Ni ka wala yɔm yɔgla. Ni nyuentaŋa abe le boa? Nyuentaŋa ale, ni yaa sum chim ka wa yɔm baai ale welema la. Ni be le nya ka nyuvuri dii ale kan ta kpeglimka la. 23Boan nyiŋŋa, biem tutuna ale kum. Alege Wen tiirimu ale nyuvuri dii ale kan ta kpeglimka la Yeezu Kirisita ti Naawenni nyiŋ.

english_text:
An Example from Marriage
1My friends, you surely understand enough about law to know that laws only have power over people who are alive. 2For example, the Law says that a man's wife must remain his wife as long as he lives. But once her husband is dead, she is free 3to marry someone else. However, if she goes off with another man while her husband is still alive, she is said to be unfaithful.
4That is how it is with you, my friends. You are now part of the body of Christ and are dead to the power of the Law. You are free to belong to Christ, who was raised to life so we could serve God. 5When we thought only of ourselves, the Law made us have sinful desires. It made every part of our bodies into slaves who are doomed to die. 6But the Law no longer rules over us. We are like dead people, and it cannot have any power over us. Now we can serve God in a new way by obeying his Spirit, and not in the old way by obeying the written Law.
The Battle with Sin
7 Does this mean that the Law is sinful? Certainly not! But if it had not been for the Law, I would not have known what sin is really like. For example, I would not have known what it means to want something that belongs to someone else, unless the Law had told me not to do this. 8It was sin that used this command as a way of making me have all kinds of desires. But without the Law, sin is dead.
9Before I knew about the Law, I was alive. But as soon as I heard that command, sin came to life, 10and I died. The very command that was supposed to bring life to me, instead brought death. 11 Sin used this command to trick me, and because of it I died. 12Still, the Law and its commands are holy and correct and good.
13Am I saying something good caused my death? Certainly not! It was sin that killed me by using something good. Now we can see how terrible and evil sin really is. 14We know that the Law is spiritual. But I am merely a human, and I have been sold as a slave to sin. 15 In fact, I don't understand why I act the way I do. I don't do what I know is right. I do the things I hate. 16Although I don't do what I know is right, I agree that the Law is good. 17So I am not the one doing these evil things. The sin that lives in me is what does them.
18I know that my selfish desires won't let me do anything that is good. Even when I want to do right, I cannot. 19Instead of doing what I know is right, I do wrong. 20And so, if I don't do what I know is right, I am no longer the one doing these evil things. The sin that lives in me is what does them.
21The Law has shown me that something in me keeps me from doing what I know is right. 22With my whole heart I agree with the Law of God. 23But in every part of me I discover something fighting against my mind, and it makes me a prisoner of sin that controls everything I do. 24What a miserable person I am. Who will rescue me from this body that is doomed to die? 25Thank God! Jesus Christ will rescue me.
So with my mind I serve the Law of God, although my selfish desires make me serve the law of sin.
translation_text:
1M suata, nama baai ale seba sinsaŋŋa la, ni basi ate m bek ni wanni de ayen, nuru waai ale kpi la sinsaŋŋa a diem soa wa kama? Aaya. Ŋa an ŋman soa wa. 2Sinsaŋŋa a weeni kama ayen nipok dan yali chora, ku a fɛ kama ayen wa ale wa chorɔwa a boro ale chaab. Alege wa chorɔwa dan kpi wa yaa ta suik kama a yali chora wa choa. 3Wa chorɔwa dan boro ale ge ate wa ŋman goa ale nidoa wa choa, nuruba le wi wa ayen wa ka kaboŋ nyeerik. Wa chorɔwa be dan kpi, sinsaŋŋa ŋman ka pagrim wa jigiya. Wa dan yali chora wa choa, wa daa kaboŋ nyeeriga.
4M suata, ase nipowa chorɔwa ale kpi ate wa ta suik a yali nidoa wa choa la, dila dekdega mɛ Sinsaŋŋa jigi, ni yaa kpi kama ate ni yaa gum chaab ale Yeezu. Sinsaŋŋa an ŋman soa ni. Yɔgyɔgla de, Yeezu Kirisita waai ate Wen nak wa yiti kum po la, ale soa ti. Wen nye dila kama ayen ti a tom tuimaŋsa a te wa. 5Diipo ate ti jam boro a va tidek suiku la, Sinsaŋŋa kasim jam basi kama ate ti nyiŋsaŋa kabta tɔgatɔgaka ale a yaali diila a jam bo ti nyiŋsaŋa po ayen ti a tom tuim ŋaai le ŋa basi ate ti kpi la. 6Alege yɔgyɔgla de, Moosis Sinsaŋŋa ŋaai ale jam yik ti a ta nna giŋgiŋ la, an ŋman soa ti. Dii nyiŋla, Sinsaŋŋa jigi tama kpi kama. Ŋa an ŋman soa ti. Dila nyiŋla, yɔgyɔgla de, ti kan ŋman a va Sinsaŋŋa su kpakka ale a weeni ti diila a tom a te Wen ya, alege ti a va ka Wen Chiika su paalukku ale a weeni diila a tom a te Wen.
7Ku be dan ka dila ti be le weeni ka boa? Ti baga a weeni ayen Moosis Sinsaŋŋa an nala? Aaya. Alege Moosis Sinsaŋŋa a daam dan kan jam ya, m daam ate an baga a miŋ ayen m jam a tom ka wabaata. Basi ate m pai m dek a magsi ayen, Sinsaŋŋa a daam dan kan sak mu ayen m kan a yaali m vaanchoa jaaboa, m te an baga a miŋ dila. 8Biem a yaa be va ka sinsak ŋaai nyiŋ ate m weeni la a nya suik a basi ate ŋan yaalik popola meena tɔgatɔga a yaa jam mi jigi. Boan nyiŋŋa, sinsaŋŋa a daam dan kan karo biem a nye ase ka jakpiuk la. 9Diipo ate mi jam zɛ sinsaŋŋa wensieŋa chak la, dipo m vua kama. Alege sinsaŋŋa ale jan jam la ate biem yaa yiri vua, 10ate mi yaa kpi. Sinsaŋŋa dekdega ŋaai ale ayen ŋa le te mu vum la ŋala dekdega abe ale ta kum a jam mi jigi. 11Boan nyiŋŋa, biem va ka sinsak ŋala nyiŋ a nya suik a paasi mi a yaa ko. 12Dila nyiŋla, Sinsaŋŋa meena welema kama. Ŋa welema kama ale chim wayɔrisima ale ŋman chim wamaŋ mɛ a te nuruba.
13Nya kude abe a sak kama ayen wa dii ale chim wamaŋ la ta ka kum a jam mi jigi ya? Aaya. Ku ka biem nyiini ale nye dila. Bu pai ka jaab maŋka a nye ate kum jam mi jigi. Suik kula po, biem abe va ka sinsaŋŋa po ayen ŋa sak ayen biem a sum ka biem.
14Ti seba ayen Sinsaŋŋa va ka Wen Chiika ale a yaali diila, alege mi kasim va ka m dek nyiŋka ale a yaali diila. Mi ka biem yɔma. 15Mi zɛ mi dek ale a tom diila. Mi an baga a nye wa dii ate mi a yaali ayen m nye la, alege m goanti a nye ka wa dii ate mi kisa a kan yaali di nyeka la. 16Dila nyiŋla, yɔgyɔgla de, m be dan a nye dii ate m kan yaali ayen m nye la, m siak kama ayen Sinsaŋŋa ka wamaŋsa. 17Dila nyiŋla, ku a sak ase daa mi ale nye wa dila la, alege ka biem buui ale bo m po la ale a nye dila. 18Mi seba kama ayen wamaŋ ka mi nyiŋka po. Boan nyiŋŋa, m kasim a yaali kama ayen mi a tom wamaŋsa alege mi an baga a nye. 19Mi kan nye wamaŋ kaai ate mi a yaali ayen m nye la, m goanti a nye ka wabiok kuui ate mi kan yaali ayen m nye la. 20M be dan a tom dii ate m kan yaali ayen m tom la, ku a sak ase daa mi ale a tom dila la, alege ka biem buui ale bo m nyiŋka po la ale a tom dila.
21Dila nyiŋla, ku a nye ase nyeka de a yaa ale a tom tuima mi nyiŋka po la. Mi dan a yaali ayen m nye wamaŋ, wabiok nyiini ate mi a nye. 22Mi popola po, ku a te mu ka popeentik ayen mi a tom sinsaŋŋa ale a weeni diila. 23Alege m nya ale ka nye ka choa ale boro a tom m nyiŋka po. Nyeka de ka biem nye kaai ale a nye kpaliŋ ale nye kaai ate mi popolaŋa a yaali la, a yaa basi ate m chim ŋa yɔma. 24Oo, ka boan jaab chivie ale a de mu nna! Ka wana ale wa vari mu a ta nyini nyiŋka de ale basi ate mi a kpi la po? 25M va Yeezu Kirisita ti Nyɔnɔwa nyiŋ a nye Wen jiam. Ku abe ale ka diila ale la. Mi dek jigi, m popola po, mi a tom sinsaŋŋa ale a weeni diila kama, alege mi nyiŋka a tom ka biem sinsaŋŋa ale a weeni diila.

english_text:
Living by the Power of God's Spirit
1If you belong to Christ Jesus, you won't be punished. 2The Holy Spirit will give you life that comes from Christ Jesus and will set you free from sin and death. 3The Law of Moses cannot do this, because our selfish desires make the Law weak. But God set you free when he sent his own Son to be like us sinners and to be a sacrifice for our sin. God used Christ's body to condemn sin. 4He did this, so that we would do what the Law commands by obeying the Spirit instead of our own desires.
5People who are ruled by their desires think only of themselves. Everyone who is ruled by the Holy Spirit thinks about spiritual things. 6If our minds are ruled by our desires, we will die. But if our minds are ruled by the Spirit, we will have life and peace. 7Our desires fight against God, because they do not and cannot obey God's laws. 8If we follow our desires, we cannot please God.
9You are no longer ruled by your desires, but by God's Spirit, who lives in you. People who don't have the Spirit of Christ in them don't belong to him. 10But Christ lives in you. So you are alive because God has accepted you, even though your bodies must die because of your sins. 11 Yet God raised Jesus to life! God's Spirit now lives in you, and he will raise you to life by his Spirit.
12My dear friends, we must not live to satisfy our desires. 13If you do, you will die. But you will live, if by the help of God's Spirit you say “No” to your desires. 14Only those people who are led by God's Spirit are his children. 15 God's Spirit doesn't make us slaves who are afraid of him. Instead, we become his children and call him our Father. 16God's Spirit makes us sure that we are his children. 17His Spirit lets us know that together with Christ we will be given what God has promised. We will also share in the glory of Christ, because we have suffered with him.
A Wonderful Future for God's People
18 I am sure what we are suffering now cannot compare with the glory that will be shown to us. 19In fact, all creation is eagerly waiting for God to show who his children are. 20 Meanwhile, creation is confused, but not because it wants to be confused. God made it this way in the hope 21that creation would be set free from decay and would share in the glorious freedom of his children. 22We know that all creation is still groaning and is in pain, like a woman about to give birth.
23 The Spirit makes us sure about what we will be in the future. But now we groan silently, while we wait for God to show that we are his children. This means that our bodies will also be set free. 24And this hope is what saves us. But if we already have what we hope for, there is no need to keep on hoping. 25However, we hope for something we have not yet seen, and we patiently wait for it.
26In certain ways we are weak, but the Spirit is here to help us. For example, when we don't know what to pray for, the Spirit prays for us in ways that cannot be put into words. 27 All of our thoughts are known to God. He can understand what is in the mind of the Spirit, as the Spirit prays for God's people. 28We know that God is always at work for the good of everyone who loves him. They are the ones God has chosen for his purpose, 29and he has always known who his chosen ones would be. He had decided to let them become like his own Son, so his Son would be the first of many children. 30God then accepted the people he had already decided to choose, and he has shared his glory with them.
God's Love
31What can we say about all this? If God is on our side, can anyone be against us? 32God did not keep back his own Son, but he gave him for us. If God did this, won't he freely give us everything else? 33If God says his chosen ones are acceptable to him, can anyone bring charges against them? 34Or can anyone condemn them? No indeed! Christ died and was raised to life, and now he is at God's right side, speaking to him for us. 35Can anything separate us from the love of Christ? Can trouble, suffering, and hard times, or hunger and nakedness, or danger and death? 36 It is exactly as the Scriptures say,
“For you we face death
all day long.
We are like sheep
on their way
to be butchered.”
37In everything we have won more than a victory because of Christ who loves us. 38I am sure that nothing can separate us from God's love—not life or death, not angels or spirits, not the present or the future, 39and not powers above or powers below. Nothing in all creation can separate us from God's love for us in Christ Jesus our Lord!
translation_text:
1Yɔgyɔgla de, baai ale Yeezu Kirisita ale ka bunyi la, Wen a kan te ba waalika, 2boan nyiŋŋa, biem ale kum nyeka a daam yik ti a lik kama. Alege yɔgyɔgla de, Wen Chiika nyeka vari ti basi kama. Wen Chiika de va ka Yeezu Kirisita nyiŋ a te mu vum. 3Wen nye dii ate Sinsaŋŋa an jam baga a nye la kama. Ŋa an jam baga a nye dila dii nyiŋla, tama dek nyiŋka ale a yaali diila a basi kama ate ka wobsa. Wen tom ka wadek biika ate wa siŋ jam tɛŋzuk de a neensi nurubiik a yaa nye ate biem ŋman ka pagrimoa. 4Wen nye dila kama ayen tama baai ale a va Wen Chiika ale a yaali diila, a kan a va tama nurubiik nyeka ale a yaali diila, alege ka ti a va wayɔrisima wieŋa ate Sinsaŋŋa a weeni ayen ti nye la. 5Baai ale a va badek nurubiik nyeka ale a yaali diila, a pai ba popola meena a te ka popola ŋala chaab. Baai mɛ ale a va Wen Chiika nyeka la, pai ba popola meena a te ka Wen Chiika wie. 6Waai abe dan basi ate nurubiik nyeka yaalika a soa wa popola meena, dila ku ta wa a cheŋ ka kum po. Waai mɛ abe dan basi ate Wen Chiika a soa wa popolaŋa meena, dila a ta ka vum ale suiyɔgni a jam wa jigi. 7Boan nyiŋŋa, waai abe dan basi ate wadek nurubiik nyeka yaalika a soa wa, wala choa ka Wen dachiak. Wa kan va sinsaŋŋa ale a weeni diila. Wa be an poom baga mɛ le va ŋa ale a weeni wa diila. 8Baai ale a va badek nurubiik nyeka yaalika ale a weeni ba diila, an baga a nye ate Wen sui a peenti.
9Alege nama kan va daa nurubiik nyeka yaalika ale a weeni diila. Nama va ka Wen Chiika ale a weeni ni diila, ase ku dan sum ka wensie ayen wa bo ni suiniima po. Waai ale kan ta Kirisitawa Chiika la, Kirisitawa an soa wa. 10Alege Kirisitawa a dan bo fi suinum po, nyiŋka kpi kama biem nyiŋ, alege fi chiika vua kama wayɔrisima nyiŋ. 11Ase Wen dii ale nak Yeezu a yiti kum po la, Wen Chiika a dan bo ni suiniima po, Wen mɛ le va ka wa Chiika waai ale bo ti suiniima po la nyiŋ a te ni tɛŋzuk de nyiŋsaŋa vum.
12Dila nyiŋla, m suata, nya kude a sak kama ayen ku ka fifiok, alege ku daa ayen ti va tidek nurubiik nyeka ale a yaali diila. 13Dii nyiŋla, ni dan a va dila, ni le kpi kama. Alege ni dan pai Wen Chiika pagrimu a ko nidek nurubiik nyeka yaalika, ni le vuuk kama. 14Baai ate Wen Chiika de ba niŋ a sak ba la, ka Wen bisa. 15Boan nyiŋŋa, Wen Chiika waai ate ni jam tuesi la, jam daa waai ale a basi ate ni ŋman a chim yɔm ate yɔgsum a yik ni la, alege wa jam ka waai ale a nye ate ni a chim Wen bisa ate Wen Chiika pagrim nyiŋ ate ti baga a kaari a wi Wen, ayen ti ko. 16Diipo meena, ate ti a wi Wen ayen ti ko la, ku ka Wen Chiika ale a weeni ti ti suiniima po ayen ti ka wa bisa. 17Ti be dan ka wa bisa, dai yeŋ po, ti be le jam soa ŋan baai meena ate wa puulim ayen wa le pai te ti la kama. Tama ale Kirisita abe le jam maa ka chaab a soa ŋan baai ate wa puulim ayen wa le pai te wa la. Yɔgyɔgla de, tama abe dan maara a nam Kirisita ninammu, dai yeŋ po, tama ale wa le maa chaab a nya wa zulaŋa.
18Mi a poli ayen nam kaai ate tama a nam yɔgyɔgla de la, ti an baga pai ka a magsi chaab ale Wen zula ŋaai le ŋa nyini peelim dai yeŋ ate ti nya ŋa la. 19Ŋanta meena ate Wen nye la, a kasim pii ka nyiŋ a limisi ayen Wen pai wa bisaŋa a ta nyini peelim a sak ba. 20Dii nyiŋla, Wen jam basi kama ayen ŋanta meena ate wa nye la boka kan ta kiriya. Be daa ŋantaŋa dek potim nyeka yaase badek yaalika ate ku nye dila, alege ka Wen yaalika ate wa basi ayen ba chim dila. Alege yiilaŋa de a jam diem boro kama 21ayen, ŋantaŋa dek dai yeŋ po le soa ka badek nna fasiyaa ate ŋan baai ale a basi ate ŋanta a poak la a kan ŋman soa ba. Ba le soa ka badek a yaa nya zula ŋaai ate Wen le pai te wa bisaŋa la. Soa m dekka de ate Wen bisaŋa le nya. 22Boan nyiŋŋa, ti seba kama ayen a zaani dipo a ta jam paari jinla, ŋanta meena ate Wen nye la a ŋusi kama ase nipok a nyiem ale boro a biak a ŋusi diila. 23Daa bala nyiini ale a ŋusi dila, tama dek baai ale ta Wen Chiik kaai ale ka Wen tiiritaŋa bunyi a liŋ jam tama jigi ayen ku sak ayen tiirita ti chaab a bo ŋaaŋ a cheena la, tama mɛ a ŋusi kama ti puusa po ase ti ale a limisi ayen Wen pai ti a chim wa nidoabilisa a yaa da tuesi ti ti wanyi wanyi nyiŋka a basi ate ti soa tidek nna fasiyaa la. 24Boan nyiŋŋa, ti ale jam nya varibasika la ate ti yaa ta yiilaŋa de. Alege ni basi ate m weeni ayen ti be dan a yiili ale jabuui ate ti ta ti nisima po la, yiila ŋala chaab abe sum daa yiila. Dii nyiŋla, ka wana ale a yiili ayen wa le nya jaab ate wa dan ga nya jaamu wa nisima po abe wa ŋman a yiili? 25Alege tama a dan ta yiila ayen ti le nya jabuui ate ti ka la, ti a limisi kama ale chichiiba ayen ti le nya.
26Wen Chiika mɛ a maari ti kama ale ti wobsimu meena. Boan nyiŋŋa, ti zɛ ti le ti puusi Wen ka dii ate ku magsi la. Wen Chiika dek ale tagri tama zuk a ŋusi a biisi a saalim dii ale Wen la, nuru an baga a weeni. 27Wen dii abe ale seba nurubiik suinum po ale ka diila, ale seba Wen Chiika popola ale ka diila. Dii nyiŋla, Wen Chiika ale tagri Wen nuruma zuk a saalim wa a magsi chaab ale wadek, Wen ale a yaali dii a te wa nuruma la.
28Tama be seba kama ayen baai ale ta yaalika ale Wen ate wa wi ba a magsi chaab ale wadek popolaŋa ale ka diila, wie meena ale a nye ba jigi la wa a basi kama ate ŋa a ta wamaŋsa a jam. 29Dii nyiŋla, Wen poom liŋ jam seba ba kama a ta nyini ku piilimka po baai ale baai ate wa lueri ayen ba ta nye kaai choa ate wa nidoabinni ta la. Wa nye dila kama ayen nidoabinni ta suata nna yegayega a yaa chim ba sua kpagi. 30Baai meena ate wa lueri la, wa wi ba kama mɛ. Baai meena mɛ ate wa wi la wa nye kama ate ba chim nyemagsika nyam. Baai mɛ ate wa nye ate ba chim nyemagsika nyam la, ka zula ate wa te ba.
31Ti be le weeni ka boan wari a magsi chaab ale nya kude? Wen abe dan za tama ŋaaŋ, ka wana le baga a nye ti wari ya? 32Wen abe ale kan zɛri wadek nidoabinni nyiŋ alege wa lak ka poi a pai wa a te tama meena la, ku a fɛ kama mɛ ayen ti be seba chak ayen wa be dan baga a nye wanni de, wa kan mini ti jabuui meena ate wa ta la. 33Nuru boro le toariŋ nuru baai ate Wen lueri la ayen ba kaasi wari ya? Aaya. Ka Wen ale weeni ayen ba ka wayɔrisima nyam. 34Nuru be boro a baga a ta biisigaamka ale ba? Aaya. Yeezu Kirisita waai ale kpi a yiti kum po a yaa kala zula jigini Wen tɛŋ la, tagri ka tama zuk a saalim wa a te ti. 35Ka boa ale baga a nye ate Kirisita yaalika a basi tama? Ka daanika yaa ninammoa yaa nuruba a nin basi ate ti nya ninam ti siaka nyiŋŋa yaa kɔm yaa chaboala yaa nyigsika yaase kummoa? 36Ase ba ale ŋmarisi Wen gbaŋka po ayen, <<Alege fi nyiŋ, ti a tu kum danni meena. Tama a nye ase ka pa ŋaai ate ba ayen ba tɔgri la.>> (Yiila 44:22) 37Alege nyaŋa de meena ale a nye ti jigi la, Yeezu Kirisita waai ale ta yaalika ale ti la, maari ti kama ate ti nak kpaliŋka a de nna chaalima. 38Dii nyiŋla, mi seba chak kama ayen kum yaase vum yaase Wen maarɔba yaase vioku po pagrita yaase jinla wie yaase chum wie yaase wenzuk pagrita 39yaase jaab wenŋmazuk yaase kpiluŋ tɛŋ yaase jabuui meena ate Wen nye la ale baga a poori tama Wen yaali ka ale bo Yeezu Kirisita ti Nyɔnɔwa po la a basi.

english_text:
God's Choice of Israel
1I am a follower of Christ, and the Holy Spirit is a witness to my conscience. So I tell the truth and I am not lying when I say 2my heart is broken and I am in great sorrow. 3I would gladly be placed under God's curse and be separated from Christ for the good of my own people. 4 They are the descendants of Israel, and they are also God's chosen people. God showed them his glory. He made agreements with them and gave them his Law.
