1Something important appeared in the sky. It was a woman whose clothes were the sun. The moon was under her feet, and a crown made of twelve stars was on her head. 2She was about to give birth, and she was crying because of the great pain.
3 Something else appeared in the sky. It was a huge red dragon with seven heads and ten horns, and a crown on each of its seven heads. 4 With its tail, it dragged a third of the stars from the sky and threw them down to the earth. Then the dragon turned toward the woman, because it wanted to eat her child as soon as it was born.
5 The woman gave birth to a son, who would rule all nations with an iron rod. The boy was snatched away. He was taken to God and placed on his throne. 6The woman ran into the desert to a place that God had prepared for her. There she would be taken care of for 1,260 days.
Michael Fights the Dragon
7 A war broke out in heaven. Michael and his angels were fighting against the dragon and its angels. 8But the dragon lost the battle. It and its angels were forced out of their places in heaven 9 and were thrown down to the earth. Yes, that old snake and his angels were thrown out of heaven! That snake, who fools everyone on earth, is known as the devil and Satan. 10 Then I heard a voice from heaven shout,
“Our God has shown
his saving power,
and his kingdom has come!
God's own Chosen One
has shown his authority.
Satan accused our people
in the presence of God
day and night.
Now he has been thrown out!
11“Our people defeated Satan
because of the blood
of the Lamb
and the message of God.
They were willing
to give up their lives.
12“The heavens should rejoice,
together with everyone
who lives there.
But pity the earth
and the sea,
because the devil
was thrown down
to the earth.
He knows his time is short,
and he is very angry.”
13When the dragon realized it had been thrown down to the earth, it tried to make trouble for the woman who had given birth to a son. 14 But the woman was given two wings like those of a huge eagle, so she could fly into the desert. There she would escape from the snake and be taken care of for a time, two times, and half a time.
15The snake then spewed out water like a river to sweep the woman away. 16But the earth helped her and swallowed the water that had come from the dragon's mouth. 17This made the dragon terribly angry with the woman. So it started a war against the rest of her children. They are the people who obey God and are faithful to what Jesus did and taught. 18The dragon stood on the beach beside the sea.
translation_text:
1Ate wakperikaliik kpien yaa jam nye wenŋmazuk. Nipok ate wenbinni a lik wa, ate chiika a bo wa naŋtaata po ate chiŋmarisa pi ale siye zutok a vuk wa zuk. 2Wa jam ta ka puuk a boro a yaali ayen wa biak, wa yaa jam a kaari ale nyiŋ wula.
3Wakperikaliik ka choa a yaa ŋman nye wenŋmazuk. Jakpioŋ ale jam a neensi waab mɔnuŋ la jam bo du. Wa jam ta ka zuima ŋayopɔi ale nyiila pi ale zutɔgsa siyopɔi wa zuimaŋa meena. 4Jaamu de jam labi chiŋmarisaŋa a soa se ka chaab la buta, a yaa lueri kaukku kunyi a yaa pai wa juiku a dari chiŋmarisaŋa meena a lɔnsi tɛŋ. Wa yaa nye dila alege za nipok waai ale a yaa wa biak la niŋ, ayen wa dan biak nueri abe wa nɛ biika. 5Nipowa yaa jam biak nidoabili waai le wa chim a soa tɛŋka meena nuruma ale pagrim la. Jaab yaa jam chiak biika wa jigi a pai te Wen dii ale jam kali wenŋmazuk wa naamu zukpaglika zuk la. 6Nipowa yaa chali ga jo sagi po. Wen ale jam gomsi jigi magsi te wa. Wa ale bo ka dula ate Wen a nya wa nalimnyiini ate ku ga paari daa tusidi ale kobsiye ale pisiyuebi (1,260).
7Ate Wen maarɔma ale ba kpagni Maakil, a yaa tigsi chaab ayen ba nye kpaliŋ ale jakpioŋku ale a neensi waamu la ale wa maarɔma wenŋmazukku po. 8Wen maarɔma yaa jam nak jaamu ale wa nuruma yiak, ale zɛri ayen ba kan ŋman bo dula. 9Wen maarɔma yaa yiak ba ayen ba siŋ tɛŋzuk a bo dula. Jaab kpioŋku de ale a neensi waamu la yuei jam le jabiok yaase Sitaana. Wala ale jam paasi tɛŋzuk de nuru meena la.
10Ate mi yaa wom lueluk kpioŋ ale ku nyini wenŋmazuk a weeni ayen, <<Yɔgyɔgla de Wen varibasika a jam kama. Yɔgyɔgla de Wen a sak pagrim kama ase naab la. Yɔgyɔgla de Kirisitawa a sak wa pagrimu kama. Diila waai ale jam zaani Wen niŋ a toariŋ ti suataŋa yok ale kantueŋ la, ba yiak wa a basi kama. 11Kirisita ka Wen nidoabinni waai ale kpi la. Ka wala ate ti suataŋa a jam sak nuruba wa wie alege a jam gomsi badek mɛ ayen ba kpi wa nyiŋla. Wieŋa de meena ale jam soa ate ba nak yiak Sitaana. 12Nama baai meena ale bo wenŋmazuk la basi ate ni sue a peenti. Alege ku le toa kama tɛŋzuk demma meena jigi, diila jabioku a siŋ jam ka nama jigi. Wa abe ta ka suipuurum dii nyiŋla wa daaŋa an soa dii ya.>>
13Jakpioŋku ale nya ale ba yiak wa a basi tɛŋzuk la, wa yaa daani nipok waai ale jam biak nidoabinni la nna yegayega. 14Ba yaa pai jiiruk kiŋkaŋŋi kpiema ŋaye a te nipowa ayen wa yiti cheŋ sagni po, ale ba le nya wa zuk a ga paari bena ŋata ale chiisa siyuebi ate jakpioŋku a kan nye wa wariya. 15Jakpioŋku yaa basi ate nyiam nna yegayega a nyini ka nɔnni po a nyini ase beli la, ayen nyiamu ji nipowa a ta cheŋ bɛ. 16Alege tɛŋka a jam nyu nyiamu meena ate bu an paari nipowa. 17Alege jakpioŋku ale jam nya dii ale nye la, ate ka sui yaa ŋman kaasi nna yegayega ale nipowa. Ka yaa ŋman pilim cheŋ ayen ka tu chaab a nye kpaliŋ ale baai meena ale a siak a te Wen sinsaŋŋa ale a weeni nuruba ayen Yeezu ale soa ba la. Bala chaama ka nipowa bisa.

english_text:
The Two Beasts
1 I looked and saw a beast coming up from the sea. This one had ten horns and seven heads, and a crown was on each of its ten horns. On each of its heads were names that were an insult to God. 2 The beast I saw had the body of a leopard, the feet of a bear, and the mouth of a lion. The dragon handed over its own power and throne and great authority to this beast. 3One of its heads seemed to have been fatally wounded, but now it was well. Everyone on earth marveled at this beast, 4and they worshiped the dragon who had given its authority to the beast. They also worshiped the beast and said, “No one is like this beast! No one can fight against it.”
5 The beast was allowed to brag and claim to be God, and for 42 months it was allowed to rule. 6The beast cursed God, and it cursed the name of God. It even cursed the place where God lives, as well as everyone who lives in heaven with God. 7 It was allowed to fight against God's people and defeat them. It was also given authority over the people of every tribe, nation, language, and race. 8 The beast was worshiped by everyone whose name wasn't written before the time of creation in the book of the Lamb who was killed.
9If you have ears,
then listen!
10 If you are doomed
to be captured,
you will be captured.
If you are doomed
to be killed by a sword,
you will be killed
by a sword.
This means God's people must learn to endure and be faithful!
11I now saw another beast. This one came out of the ground. It had two horns like a lamb, but spoke like a dragon. 12It worked for the beast whose fatal wound had been healed. And it used all its authority to force the earth and its people to worship that beast. 13It worked mighty miracles, and while people watched, it even made fire come down from the sky.
14This second beast fooled people on earth by working miracles for the first one. Then it talked them into making an idol in the form of the beast that did not die after being wounded by a sword. 15It was allowed to put breath into the idol, so it could speak. Everyone who refused to worship the idol of the beast was put to death. 16 All people were forced to put a mark on their right hand or forehead. Whether they were powerful or weak, rich or poor, free people or slaves, 17they all had to have this mark, or else they could not buy or sell anything. This mark stood for the name of the beast and for the number of its name.
18You need wisdom to understand the number of the beast! But if you are smart enough, you can figure this out. Its number is 666, and it stands for a person.
translation_text:
1Dila powa, jakpioŋku a jam za ka nyakpiemu nɔi. Ate mi yaa ŋman nya duŋ kperikaliik ka choa ale ka nyini nyakpiemu po a nyini. Kala a jam ta ka zuima ŋayopɔi ale nyiila pi. Ka jam vuk ka naam zutɔgsa ka nyiilaŋa meena zuk. Ka zuimaŋa meena nyiŋ yue ale jam doa ŋa nyiŋ a lɛ Wen. 2Duŋ ka de jam a neensi ka yɔŋni. Ka naŋsaŋa mɛ jam a neensi ka piuk naŋsa. Ka nɔnni mɛ a neensi gbeŋli nɔi. Jakpioŋ kuui ale a neensi waab la jam pai ka pagrimu ale ka naamu a te ka duŋ kperikaliika. 3Mi yaa ŋman ga a nya la ale, duŋ kperikaliika ale nyini nyiamu po a nyini la, ale ka zukku kunyi zuk lauŋ ale jam boro. Tɛŋzuk meena nuruma ale ga nya lauŋku de la, ku jam chim ka wakperikaliik ba jigi ate ba yaa deri va ka. 4Waai meena yaa jam a te jakpioŋ kuui ale a neensi waamu la zula nna yegayega dii nyiŋla, wa jam pai ka pagrimu a te duŋ kperikaliik kaai ale nyini nyiamu po a nyini la. Ba yaa a weeni chaab ayen, <<Ka wana ale a nye ase duŋ kperikaliika de a ta pagrim ayen wa nye kpaliŋ ale ka?>>
5Ba yaa te duŋ kperikaliik kaai ale nyini nyakpiemu po a nyini la suik ate ka biisi wie ŋaai ale ka leeta nna yegayega a te Wen la. Ba jam te ka ka pagrim ayen ka soa tɛŋzuk meena nuruma ate ku ga paari chiisa pisinaansi ale siye. 6Ka yaa jam biisi a kaasi Wen ale wa yuenni ale wa viuku, ku kiri ale baai meena ale jam bo wenŋmazukku po la. 7Ba yaa ŋman te ka suik ayen ka tu chaab ale Wen nuruma a nye kpaliŋ a nak yiak ba. Ba te ka mɛ pagrim ayen ka soa buura meena ale nuruba meena ale biisa meena ale tɛŋsa meena. 8Wen liŋ ŋmarisi baai meena ale ba tuesi wa nyuvuri dii ale kan ka kpeglimka la kama a nyo wa gbaŋka po alege yaa nye tɛŋka. Wa Pabiik kaai, ate ba ko la ale soa gbaŋka. Baai meena yue ale jam kan bo gbaŋka de po la, le puusi a te duŋ kperikaliik kaai ale jam nyini nyakpiemu po a nyini la.
9Ni lak ni tueŋa a wom dii ate mi a weeni la nalimnyiini. 10Ku ka Wen dek yaalika ayen ba le jam yik ni ba gela a lik dɔk po a pai gebik woŋta a ko ni gela. Nama baai ale ka Wen nuruba la, ku a fɛ ayen ni nam ale chichiiba a ŋmasi yik di ate ku ga paari ku kpeglimka. Wieŋa de ale sum nye kama.
11Ate mi yaa ŋman nya duŋ kperikaliik ka choa ale nyini tɛŋka a jueli. Ka jam ta ka nyiila ŋaye ase padiak nyiila la, alege a biisi ase jakpioŋku ale a neensi waamu la. 12Ka jam pai ka duŋ kperikaliika pagrim a tom ka dek nimbie po. Ka jam fɛ tɛŋka nuruma kama ayen ba a puusi duŋ kperikaliika ale kɔni la. 13Duŋ kaai ale ta nyiila ŋayewa la dɛ a tom ka wakperikaliisa nna yegayega. Ka jam nye kama ate bolim a nyiini wenŋmazuk a siŋ tɛŋzuk nuru meena niŋ. 14Ate ka paasi tɛŋzuk nuruma meena ale wakperikaliik sii ate ka tom duŋ kperikaliika niŋ la. Ka weeni ayen ba mɛ duŋ kperikaliik kaai ate ba kɔni ka ale gebi woŋku alege ate ka diem vua la ate ba a zuli ka. 15Ba yaa te ka suik ayen ka vuusi a basi duŋ kperikaliika ate ba mɛ la nyiŋ ate ka ta nyuvuri ate wa baga a biisi abe wa a ko baai meena ale kan puusi a te wa la. 16Duŋ ka de a yaa fɛ nuruma meena, baai ale chim nuru kpienta ale baai ale kan daa nuru kpienta, baai ale ka jigsirɔba ale baai ale kan daa jigsirɔba, baai ale ka yɔm ale baai ale kan daa yɔmma ate ba ŋmarisi ba juga nisima nyiŋ yaase ba dee nyiŋ. 17Nuru waai an baga jaab a da ka wa nin ta ŋmarisika de. Ŋmarisika de ale wa yuenni yaase dii ale a sak wa yuenni la.
18Kude abe a sak ka yam. Nuru waai a dan ta yam wa ale seba dii ale a sak wa yuenni la kiri. Dii abe ale a sak wa yuenni la ka kobsiyuebi ale pisiyuebi ale buyuebi.

english_text:
The Lamb and His 144,000 Followers
1 I looked and saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion! With him were 144,000, who had his name and his Father's name written on their foreheads. 2 Then I heard a sound from heaven that was like a roaring flood or loud thunder or even like the music of harps. 3And a new song was being sung in front of God's throne and in front of the four living creatures and the elders. No one could learn that song, except the 144,000 who had been rescued from the earth. 4All of these are pure virgins, and they follow the Lamb wherever he leads. They have been rescued to be presented to God and the Lamb as the most precious people on earth. 5 They never tell lies, and they are innocent.
The Messages of the Three Angels
6I saw another angel. This one was flying across the sky and had the eternal good news to announce to the people of every race, tribe, language, and nation on earth. 7The angel shouted, “Worship and honor God! The time has come for him to judge everyone. Kneel down before the one who created heaven and earth, the oceans, and every stream.”
8 A second angel followed and said, “The great city of Babylon has fallen! This is the city that made all nations drunk and immoral. Now God is angry, and Babylon has fallen.”
9Finally, a third angel came and shouted:
Here is what will happen if you worship the beast and the idol and have the mark of the beast on your hand or forehead. 10 You will have to drink the wine that God gives to everyone who makes him angry. You will feel his mighty anger, and you will be tortured with fire and burning sulfur, while the holy angels and the Lamb look on.
11 If you worship the beast and the idol and accept the mark of its name, you will be tortured day and night. The smoke from your torture will go up forever and ever, and you will never be able to rest.
12God's people must learn to endure. They must also obey his commands and have faith in Jesus.
13Then I heard a voice from heaven say, “Put this in writing. From now on, the Lord will bless everyone who has faith in him when they die.”
The Spirit answered, “Yes, they will rest from their hard work, and they will be rewarded for what they have done.”
The Earth Is Harvested
14 I looked and saw a bright cloud, and someone who seemed to be the Son of Man was sitting on the cloud. He wore a gold crown on his head and held a sharp sickle in his hand. 15 An angel came out of the temple and shouted, “Start cutting with your sickle! Harvest season is here, and all crops on earth are ripe.” 16The one on the cloud swung his sickle and harvested the crops.
17Another angel with a sharp sickle then came out of the temple in heaven. 18After this, an angel with power over fire came from the altar and shouted to the angel who had the sickle. He said, “All grapes on earth are ripe! Harvest them with your sharp sickle.” 19The angel swung his sickle on earth and cut off its grapes. He threw them into a pit where they were trampled on as a sign of God's anger. 20 The pit was outside the city, and when the grapes were mashed, blood flowed out. The blood turned into a river that was about 300 kilometers long and almost deep enough to cover a horse.
translation_text:
1Ate mi yaa nya ale Pabiik ale nuruba tusa kook ale pisinaansi ale banaansi (144,000) a za guuk kpioŋku Zayon zuk. Ba jam ŋmarisi ka Pabiika ale ka Kowa yue a dueni nuruma de nyiŋ. 2M jam wom ka lueluk kpioŋ mɛ a se nyiam ale nyini pina zuk a wuuri a siŋ la, yaa a se ŋmoruk ale a na la. Lueluk kpioŋku de jam nyini ka wenŋmazuk. Lueluk mɛ jam a nye ase nuru boari ale jam a nak kpanta la. 3Ate ba yaa jam yi yi paali wenŋmazuk naamu zukpaglika niŋ ale ŋanvuta tinaansiwa ale nisɔm pisiye ale banaansiwa niŋ, ate waai an jam baga a zamsi yiini ka nuruba tusa kook ale pisinaansi ale banaansiwa (144,000) nyiini ale nya da tuesika a nyini tɛŋzuk la. 4Ba de ale baai ale kan jam taŋ badek ale nipooba, diila ba jam yik badek ka cheri. Ba jam va Pabiika kama juijui meena ate ka a cheŋ la. Ba jam da ba kama nuruba po a pai ba a te Wen ale Pabiika ase yɔna ŋaai ale dɛ niŋ la. 5Nuru an jam baga a weeni ayen ba velim venta. Ba jam ka kaasuŋ ale kunyi mɛ la.
6Ate mi yaa ŋman nya maarɔ ale wa bo wenŋmazuk niŋniŋa a yaa yiri a cheŋ. Wa ta ka Wen wamaŋsaŋa ayen wa ta cheŋ ga a te tɛŋsa meena ale buura meena ale biisa meena ale nuruba meena. 7Wa yaa weeni ba ale lueluk kpioŋ, ayen, <<Ni a te Wen zula abe ni a pak wa, dii nyiŋla, wa ka pagrim nyɔnɔ. Diipo ate wa ayen wa bo nuru meena buusa la a paari kama. Wa nye wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋka ale nyakpiemu ale bulisa meena. Dila ale soa ate ku a fɛ ayen ni a puusi a te wa.>>
8Wen maarɔ wa choa mɛ yaa yiri a vi maarɔwa ŋaaŋ ale a weeni ayen, <<Tɛŋ kpieŋka Babilon, a lo kama. Kaboŋsa tuim ŋaai ate ka nuruma a jam a tom la, a nye se ka da pagrik ate ka fɛ ba ate ba nyu la.>>
9Wen maarɔ wa choa a yaa ŋman yiri a vi nwala ŋaaŋ ale a weeni ale lueluk kpioŋ ayen, <<Baai meena ale a puusi a te duŋ kperikaliik kaai ale jam nyini nyakpiemu po a nyini la, yaase baai meena ale basi ate ka bɔglukku a ŋmarisi ba nisa ale ba dee nyiŋ la. 10Wen ta ka suipuurum ale ba ate wa ayen wa le te ba waalika. Wa suipuurumu a nye ase ka da pagrik la. Wa suipuurumu a nye ase ka da bula ate wa yaa fɛ ba ayen ba nyu la. Wa le basi ate ba pai ba a nyo ka bolim po ate ba nam nna yegayega Pabiika ale ka maarɔma baai ate ka lueri a te ka dek la niŋ. 11Bolim buui ate ba le nam bu po la nyuisaŋa a kasim a jueli ka wenŋmazuk taam wuu. Baai ale jam puusi a te duŋ kperikaliika ale ka bɔglukku ale ŋman basi ate ku pai ku yuenni a ŋmarisi ba nyiŋ la, bala dek ale ba kasim a nam alege kan nya vuusum.>>
12Dila ale soa ate Wen nuruma baai ale a siak a te Wen sinsaŋŋa alege kan zɛri Yeezu vaka la, ku a fɛ ayen ba va yɔgyɔgla ale chichiiba.
13Ate mi yaa ŋman wom lueluk ale ku nyini wenŋmazuk siŋ jam a yaa weeni ayen, <<Ŋmarisi dii ate m le weeni la a dueni. Baai ale a tom tuima a te Naawen alege a kpi yɔgyɔgla la, ba sue le peenti kama.>> Wen Chiika mɛ a maa weeni gum du ayen, <<Fi biisi ka wensie. Wen le tuni ba abe wa basi ate ba vuusi ale ba tuim pagrisa yegayega abe wa basi ate ba sue peenti.>>
14Mi ŋman gaa nya la ale waai ale a nye ase saalɔbiik la, ale wa kali chiŋma peeluk zuk. Wa jam vuk ka zutɔk kaai ale a nye ase ligmɔniŋ ate ba pai nye la. Wa jam ta ka gɔtuk kuui ale ta nɔi la wa nisa po. 15Wen maarɔ a yaa nyini Wen yenni po a nyini a biisi ale lueluk kpioŋ a yaa weeni ayen, <<Ku paari tɛŋka ŋantaŋa ŋarika kama. Pai fi gɔtuku a nyini.>> 16Ate waai ale jam kali chiŋmanni zuk la a yaa misi wa gɔtuku a ŋari tɛŋka ŋantaŋa.
17Wen maarɔ wa choa mɛ yaa jam nyini Wen yenni dii ale bo wenŋmazukku la. Wa mɛ jam ta ka gɔtuk kuui ale ta nɔi la.
18Wen maarɔ waai ale a nya bolimu zuk la, yaa nyini kuŋkuŋku jigini a weeni maarɔ waai ale ta gɔtuku la ayen pai fi gɔtuku a ŋari tiisaŋa diila yɔnaŋa a muni kama. 19Maarɔwa yaa misi wa gɔtuku a ŋari tiisaŋa yɔnaŋa a lɔnsi tɛŋ a yaa tigsi ŋa a dueni juijui ate ba a ŋmiak ŋa nyiamu la. Dula jigini ale Wen suipuurumu ka bunyi. 20Ŋa nyiamu ŋmiaka jigini a jam bo ka tɛŋka ŋaaŋnyiŋ. Ba yaa le ga ŋmiak yɔna ŋaai ate maarɔwa a tigsi dueni la, ziim nna yegayega ale jam nyini ŋa po a nyini. Ziimu meena ale jam nyini la, bu jam chali tɛŋka kama a wɔŋa ase mɛɛla kobsiye la a yaa doa jueli a lim nuru zuk.

english_text:
The Last of the Terrible Troubles
1After this, I looked at the sky and saw something else that was strange and important. Seven angels were bringing the seven last terrible troubles. When these are ended, God will no longer be angry.
2Then I saw something that looked like a glass sea mixed with fire, and people were standing on it. They were the ones who had defeated the beast and the idol and the number that tells the name of the beast. God had given them harps, 3 and they were singing the song his servant Moses and the Lamb had sung. They were singing,
“Lord God All-Powerful,
you have done great
and marvelous things.
You are the ruler
of all nations,
and you do what is
right and fair.
4 Lord, who doesn't honor
and praise your name?
You alone are holy,
and all nations will come
and worship you,
because you have shown
that you judge
with fairness.”
5 After this, I noticed something else in heaven. The sacred tent used for a temple was open. 6And the seven angels who were bringing the terrible troubles were coming out of it. They were dressed in robes of pure white linen and wore belts made of pure gold. 7One of the four living creatures gave each of the seven angels a bowl made of gold. These bowls were filled with the anger of God who lives forever and ever. 8 The temple quickly filled with smoke from the glory and power of God. No one could enter it until the seven angels had finished pouring out the seven last troubles.
translation_text:
1Ate mi ŋman nya jakperikaliik tanjaŋini wenŋmazuk ate ku cha mi nna yegayega. Maarɔba bayopɔi ale jam ta ninam tɔgatɔga buyopɔi a jam bo dula. Ba le jam basi ate ninammu a yik ka tɛŋzuk nuruma a kpeglim. Dii nyiŋla, Wen sui ale jam a puuri ale nuruba diila ate wa ayen wa te ba waalika la a nueri kama yɔgla.
2Mi yaa nya Naawen nuru baai ale jam kan puusi a te duŋ kperikaliika yaase ka bɔglukku, yaase ka pai ka yuenni ale kobsiyuebi ale pisiyuebi ale bayuebi a ŋmarisi ba nyiŋ. Mi jam, nya ba ale za moata ka nyakpiemu ate bu a nyaksi nna ase nyaasuŋ la. Bolim ale jam bo nyiamu po. Nuruma a jam ta ka ŋanta nna a se kpanta la ate Naawen a jam pai a te ba. 3Ba yaa jam yi Moosis waai ale jam ka Naawen tomteerɔ la ale Pabiika yiili. Ba jam yi yiini ayen, <<Naawen dii ale ka Wen la, fi ka waai ale soa ŋanta meena pagrim la, ku chim ka wakperikaliik ti jigi, fi tuimaŋa nyiŋ. Fi ka waai ale ka tɛŋzuk meena nuruma Naab la. Tuim ŋaai meena ate fi a tom la, ŋa ka wensie. Ŋa daa wasusuga. 4Naawen yaa, fi nyiini ale nuru weleŋ. Dila ale soa ate ku a magsi ayen nuru meena a te fu zula abe ba a weeni a sak ba suata fi le ka Wen kpienni diila. Tɛŋzuk nuruma meena le jam za fi niŋ a puusi a te fu, dii nyiŋla ba seba ayen fi tuimaŋa meena a daa tuim susuga.>>
5Ba le jam yi yiini a nueri la, mi yaa nya ale Wen yenni nɔnni a lak ate pumpuulima viuku a boro. 6Maarɔba bayopɔiwa ale jam ta ninam tɔgatɔga buyopɔiwa la a yaa nyini dula a nyini. Ba jam jo ka garuk peelita ate ti nala nna yegayega. Ba jam maa ta ka garuk pali fiik sii ale a nyaksi a neensi ligmɔniŋ la yaa bobi gilim ba kuusa. 7Ba yaa cheŋ ga za ŋanvuta tinaansiwa wanyi niŋ. Ŋanvutaŋa a jam za gilim ka Wen naamu zukpaglika. Javuk kuui niŋ ate ba jam za la, a jam pai Wen dii ale kasim boro taam wuu la suipuurumu ale wa le wa te tɛŋzuk nuruma waalika la, a yaa jam pai Wen suipuurumu a nyo china ŋayopɔi po a te maarɔma wanyi wanyi. 8Wen zulaŋa ale wa nalimu ale wa pagrimu yegayega a jam a nye ase ka nyuisa la a yaa sueri wa Yenni. Ase ka maarɔma a nin basi ate ninam tɔgatɔga buyopɔiwa a yik tɛŋzuk nuruma a nueri, nuru an jam baga a jo Wen yenni po.

english_text:
The Bowls of God's Anger
1From the temple I heard a voice shout to the seven angels, “Go and empty the seven bowls of God's anger on the earth.”
2 The first angel emptied his bowl on the earth. At once ugly and painful sores broke out on everyone who had the mark of the beast and worshiped the idol.
3The second angel emptied his bowl on the sea. At once the sea turned into blood like that of a dead person, and every living thing in the sea died.
4 The third angel emptied his bowl into the rivers and streams. At once they turned to blood. 5Then I heard the angel, who has power over water, say,
“You have always been,
and you always will be
the holy God.
You had the right
to judge in this way.
6They poured out the blood
of your people
and your prophets.
So you gave them blood
to drink as they deserve!”
7After this, I heard
the altar shout,
“Yes, Lord God All-Powerful,
your judgments are honest
and fair.”
8The fourth angel emptied his bowl on the sun, and it began to scorch people like fire. 9Everyone was scorched by its great heat, and all of them cursed the name of God who had power over these terrible troubles. But no one turned to God and praised him.
10 The fifth angel emptied his bowl on the throne of the beast. At once darkness covered its kingdom, and its people began biting their tongues in pain. 11And because of their painful sores, they cursed the God who rules in heaven. But still they did not stop doing evil things.
12 The sixth angel emptied his bowl on the great Euphrates River, and it completely dried up to make a road for the kings from the east. 13An evil spirit that looked like a frog came out of the mouth of the dragon. One also came out of the mouth of the beast, and another out of the mouth of the false prophet. 14These evil spirits had the power to work miracles. They went to every king on earth, to bring them together for a war against God All-Powerful. But that will be the day of God's great victory.
15 Remember Christ says, “When I come, it will surprise you like a thief! But God will bless you, if you are awake and ready. Then you won't have to walk around naked and be ashamed.”
16 Those armies came together in a place that in Hebrew is called Armagedon.
17As soon as the seventh angel emptied his bowl in the air, a loud voice from the throne in the temple shouted, “It's done!” 18 There were flashes of lightning, roars of thunder, and the worst earthquake in all history. 19 The great city of Babylon split into three parts, and the cities of other nations fell. So God made Babylon drink from the wine cup filled with his anger. 20 Every island ran away, and the mountains disappeared. 21 Hailstones, weighing about 50 kilograms each, fell from the sky on people. Finally, the people cursed God, because the hail was so terrible.
translation_text:
1Ate mi yaa wom ale lueluk kpioŋ a nyini Wen yenni a yaa weeni Maarɔba bayopɔiwa ayen, <<Ni pai Wen suipuurum yegayega ale bo chinaŋa po la a cheŋ ga kpiiri basi tɛŋka zuk.>>
2Maarɔma wanyi a yaa dɛ niŋ nyini ga kpiiri suipuurumu wa chinni po a basi tɛŋka zuk, ate niri kperikaliisa a yaa nye nuru baai ate duŋ kperikaliika a ŋmarisi ba nyiŋsa ate ba jam a kaab ka bɔglukku la ate ba jam a nam nna yegayega.
3Wen maarɔ waai ale jam saari bayewa la jam kpiiri suipuurumu wa chinni po a basi nyakpiemu po. Nyiamu a yaa jam muni nna ase kpio ziim la ate jaabuuri ale jam bo bu po la a yaa kpi.
4Wen maarɔ waai ale jam saari batawa la mɛ yaa kpiiri suipuurumu wa chinni po a basi belaŋa ale bulisaŋa po ate nyaataŋa a chim ziim. 5Mi yaa wom ale maarɔwa a weeni ayen, <<Fi ka waai ale ka Weleŋsa Nyɔnɔ la. Fi ale piilimka, fi be boro kama taam wuu, fi ka Weleŋsa Nyɔnɔ, dii nyiŋ la fi buusaŋa ate fi bo la ka wensie. 6Ba jam ko fi nuruma ale biisiteerɔma ate ba ziimu a yaa nyini tɛŋ. Ku magsi kama ale fi ale pai ziimu ayen ba nyu yɔgyɔgla la.>> 7Ate mi yaa wom ale lueluk a nyini kuŋkuŋku jigini a yaa weeni ayen, <<Naawen dii ale ka Wen la, fi ka Waai Ale Soa Ŋanta Meena Pagrim, ku magsi kama ale ŋman chim wensie mɛ fi ale a bo nuruba buusa diila.>>
8Wen maarɔ waai ale jam saari banaansiwa la yaa kpiiri suipuurumu wa chinni po a basi wenbinni zuk ate di kantueŋka a yaa nya suik a dɛ nuruma. 9Kantueŋka ale jam dɛ ba la, ba yaa ka a te Wen, dii nyiŋ la, wa le basi ate ninammu a yik ba la. Alege ba an jam basi ba tuimbaataŋa tomka alege tagri ba popola a te Wen zula.
10Wen maarɔ waai ale jam saari banuwa la a yaa kpiiri suipuurumu wa chinni po a basi duŋ kperikaliika naamu jigini. Wa jigini ate wa jam boro la a yaa jam sobri ate wa ŋaaŋviirɔma sue a jam a puuri ate ba jam a dom ba giŋgeluŋta. 11Ba yaa jam ka a te Wen dii ale bo wenŋmazuk la ba niraŋa ale ninammu nyiŋ, alege ba an jam basi ba tuimbaataŋa tomka.
12Wen maarɔ waai ale jam saari bayuebiwa la yaa jam kpiiri suipuurumu wa chinni po a basi beli kpienni Yufiretis po. Nyiamu a yaa jam kpeeri alege ate nalima ŋaai ale nyini kori nummu po a cheena la a nya suik a taam jam. 13Ate mi yaa nya chichirik baata tita ale ti a neensi buntua. Chichirik baataŋa de a jam nyini ka jaab waai ale a neensi waamu a jam yiak nipowa ale duŋ kperikaliik kaai ale jam nyini nyakpiemu po a nyini la ale venta biisiteerɔwa nɔi po a nyini. 14Chichirik baataŋa a jam ta ka pagrim a tom wakperikaliisa yegayega. Ba jam nyiem kama a yaa tigsi tɛŋzuk nuruma meena nalimaŋa ale ba nuruma a nyo jigi yeŋ ayen Wen Kpienni dai kpienni danni ate wa le jam a bo buusa la a dan paari, ba le tu chaab ale wa a nye kpaliŋ.
15Ni wom ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita ale a weeni ayen, <<Nya, m kan beni m le jam ase ka zue la. Niauŋ a bo le ka waai ale a limisi ale basi ate wa gattaŋa a bo le wa la, ate wa kan cheŋ chaboala ate ba nya wa chivie.>>
16Ate chichirik baataŋa a dɛ nalimaŋa niŋ, a ta ba jam jigi ate ba a wi dula ale Juuma biika ayen Amagedon.
17Ate maarɔ waai ale saari bayopɔiwa la a jam kpiiri suipuurumu wa chinni po a basi wenŋmazuk. Mi yaa wom ale lueluk kpioŋ nyini wenŋmazuk naamu zukpaglika jigini Wen yenni po a siŋ a weeni ayen, <<Ku jam ya.>> 18Chiŋmaaŋa yaa nyaksi ale na ate tɛŋka a choa nna yegayega. Diipo ate Wen a nye nuruba ate ku ta dila a jam paari jinla, tɛŋka an diem choa nna la. 19Tɛŋ kpieŋka a jam poori ka buta ate tɛŋzuk tɛŋ kpieŋsaŋa a kaasi meena. Wen yaa teeri Babilon wari a yaa basi ate ka nuruma a nyu wa suipuurumu wa beerika po ase daam la. 20Guuk kpientaŋa meena a yaa muriŋ bɛ ate tɛŋsaŋa meena ale nya tii ale jam doa gilim tɛŋ sii meena la mɛ a muriŋ bɛ. 21Ŋmoruk tana a yaa jam nyini wenŋmazuk a lo nuruma zuima. Ŋmoruk tanaŋa dinyi a jam dobra a se ka za boorik geli la. Nuruma yaa jam ka a te Wen dii nyiŋla, wa le jam basi ate ŋmoruk tanaŋa a dobra la.

english_text:
The Prostitute and the Beast
1 One of the seven angels who had emptied the bowls came over and said to me, “Come on! I will show you how God will punish that shameless prostitute who sits on many oceans. 2 Every king on earth has slept with her, and her shameless ways are like wine that has made everyone on earth drunk.”
3 With the help of the Spirit, the angel took me into a desert, where I saw a woman sitting on a red beast. The beast was covered with names that were an insult to God, and it had seven heads and ten horns. 4 The woman was dressed in purple and scarlet robes, and she wore jewelry made of gold, precious stones, and pearls. In her hand she held a gold cup filled with the filthy and nasty things she had done. 5On her forehead a mysterious name was written:
I AM THE GREAT CITY OF BABYLON, THE MOTHER OF EVERY IMMORAL AND FILTHY THING ON EARTH.
6I could tell that the woman was drunk on the blood of God's people who had given their lives for Jesus. This surprising sight amazed me, 7and the angel said:
Why are you so amazed? I will explain the mystery about this woman and about the beast she is sitting on, with its seven heads and ten horns. 8 The beast you saw is one that used to be and no longer is. It will come back from the deep pit, but only to be destroyed. Everyone on earth whose names were not written in the book of life before the time of creation will be amazed. They will see this beast that used to be and no longer is, but will be once more.
9Anyone with wisdom can figure this out. The seven heads that the woman is sitting on stand for seven hills. These heads are also seven kings. 10Five of the kings are dead. One is ruling now, and the other one has not yet come. But when he does, he will rule for only a little while.
11You also saw a beast that used to be and no longer is. That beast is one of the seven kings who will return as the eighth king, but only to be destroyed.
12 The ten horns you saw are ten more kings, who have not yet come into power, and they will rule with the beast for only a short time. 13They all think alike and will give their power and authority to the beast. 14 These kings will go to war against the Lamb. But he will defeat them, because he is Lord over all lords and King over all kings. His followers are chosen and special and faithful.
15The oceans you saw the prostitute sitting on are crowds of people from all races and languages. 16The ten horns and the beast will start hating the shameless woman. They will strip off her clothes and leave her naked. Then they will eat her flesh and throw the rest of her body into a fire. 17God is the one who made these kings all think alike and decide to give their power to the beast. And they will do this until what God has said comes true.
18The woman you saw is the great city that rules over all kings on earth.
translation_text:
1Ate maarɔba bayopɔiwa wanyi waai ale jam ta china ŋayopɔi la a yaa jam weeni mi ayen, <<Jam ate m sak fu nidoa yaalika ale wa nya ninam diila. Waai ale kali nya boari zuk la. 2Tɛŋka nuruma ale ba nalimaŋa ale wala a maa chaab a tom ka kabonsa tuima. Nuruma ale wala ale jam nye diila a nye se ka daam ate ba nyu buk la.>>
3Wen Chiika ale basi ate maarɔwa a pai mi a ta cheŋ sagni po la. Duŋ kpieŋ mɔnuŋ ale jam ta zuima ŋayopɔi ale nyiila pi a jam za du. Ba jam ŋmarisi ka leeta yue nna yegayega ŋaai ale jam a lɛ Wen la a dueni ka nyiŋ ate nidoa yaalika a yaa jam kali ka zuk. 4Wa jam jo ka garuk sobluk ale garuk mɔnuŋ ale maa su ligmɔniŋ ale tintana ŋaai ale a nyaksi la ŋanta. Wa jam ta ka ligmɔniŋ beerik ate ŋan daŋtisa a sueri ka, kude a sak ka wa nidoa yaalik tuimaŋa. 5Ba jam ŋmarisi ka yuei a dueni wa diri nyiŋ. Yuenni kiri a jam suk kama. Basi ate m pai di kiri a ta nyini peelim a weeni sak fu. Yuenni kiri ale, <Mi ka Babilon, tɛŋ kaai ale ka tɛŋ kpieŋ ale nidoa yaalisa ma, waai ale maa chaab ale ba a jam a tom daŋta tuima.> 6Mi yaa jam nya ale nipowa a jam nyu ka Wen nuruma ale nuru baai ale jam kan basi Yeezu vaka la ziimu. Mi le jam nya wa la, ku jam ka wakperikaliik yegayega mi jigi. 7Maarɔwa yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Ka boan nyiŋ ate ku chim wakperikaliik fi jigiya? Nipowa ale duŋ kpieŋ kaai ale ta zuima ŋayopɔiwa ale nyiila piwa ate wa jam do ka la, wala ale duŋka a jam ta kiri kama ate di suk. M le weeni di kiri ale ka diila a sak fu. 8Duŋ kala a jam boro kama alege a ŋman karo. Ka abe za ka nyini ka vɔrup buui ale kan ka kpeglimka la po a nyini ate ba a kaasi ka. Nuru baai wie ale kan ŋmarisi dua ŋanvuta gbaŋka po a nyini diipo ate ba an diem nye tɛŋka la, ku le cha ba ase ba nin nya ka. Ka jam boro kama alege yɔgyɔgla de ka ŋman karo, alege ka le pilim vuri nyini.
9<<Be ka yam ale miŋka ate waai a miŋ wieŋa de. Zuima ŋayopɔiwa ka guuta tiyopɔi ate nipowa a kali ti zuk. 10Ŋa bɛ ka nalima ŋayopɔi. Nalima ŋanu ale jɔk ba naamu alege wanyi a dɛ wa naamu diema alege wanyi an diem jam ya, wa dan jam wa ale dɛ wa naamu ka maga. 11Duŋ kaai ale jam boro alege a ŋman karo la a yaa saari ka nalima naaniŋ. Wa abe ka ŋayopɔiwa po wanyi a za wa nyini ate ba kaasi wa.
12<<Nyiila piwa ate fi nya la, ka nalima pi baai ale kan diem piilim ba naamu dɛ ka, alege ba ale nya ka pagrim a dɛ ba naamu ase miita pisiyuebi la ale duŋka. 13Nalima piwa de meena a ta ka popola yena. Ba abe pai ba pagrimu a te ka duŋka. 14Ba ale nye kpaliŋ ale Pabiika alege Pabiika ale baai ate ka lueri ate ba va ka ale siaka la ale nak dɛ ba meena dii nyiŋla ka ka nyama meena Nyɔnɔ ale nalima meena Naab.>>
15Maarɔwa yaa weeni mi ayen, <<Nyaataŋa ate fi nya ate nidoa yaalika a kali du la, ka nuruba ale nuru boari ale tɛŋsa ale biisa. 16Nyiila piwa ate fi nya la ale duŋka ale kisi nidoa yaalika kama ate ba yaa yik jaabuuri meena ate wa ta la a tuesi alege basi wa chaboala. Ba ale ŋɔbi wa nyiŋ lammu abe ba kaasi wa ale bolim. 17Wen dek ale te ba suik ayen ba a tom ale chaab ate wa ale poli ayen dii a nye la, abe di nye. Abe ba pai ba pagrimu a te duŋka ate ka soa naamu a nya ate Wen wieŋa a chim wensie.
18<<Nipowa ate fi nya la ale tɛŋ kpieŋ kaai ale a nya tɛŋzuk nalimaŋa la.>>

english_text:
The Fall of Babylon
1I saw another angel come from heaven. This one had great power, and the earth was bright because of his glory. 2 The angel shouted,
“Fallen! Powerful Babylon
has fallen
and is now the home
of demons.
It is the den
of every filthy spirit
and of all unclean birds,
and every dirty
and hated animal.
3 Babylon's evil and immoral wine
has made all nations drunk.
Every king on earth
has slept with her,
and every merchant on earth
is rich because of
her evil desires.”
4 Then I heard another voice
from heaven shout,
“My people, you must escape
from Babylon.
Don't take part in her sins
and share her punishment.
5 Her sins are piled
as high as heaven.
God has remembered the evil
she has done.
6 Treat her as she
has treated others.
Make her pay double
for what she has done.
Make her drink twice as much
of what she mixed
for others.
7 That woman honored herself
with a life of luxury.
Reward her now
with suffering and pain.
“Deep in her heart
Babylon said,
‘I am the queen!
Never will I be a widow
or know what it means
to be sad.’
8And so, in a single day
she will suffer the pain
of sorrow, hunger, and death.
Fire will destroy
her dead body,
because her judge
is the powerful Lord God.”
9 Every king on earth who slept with her and shared in her luxury will mourn. They will weep, when they see the smoke from that fire. 10Her sufferings will frighten them, and they will stand at a distance and say,
“Pity that great
and powerful city!
Pity Babylon!
In a single hour
her judgment has come.”
11 Every merchant on earth will mourn, because there is no one to buy their goods. 12 There won't be anyone to buy their gold, silver, jewels, pearls, fine linen, purple cloth, silk, scarlet cloth, sweet-smelling wood, fancy carvings of ivory and wood, as well as things made of bronze, iron, or marble. 13No one will buy their cinnamon, spices, incense, myrrh, frankincense, wine, olive oil, fine flour, wheat, cattle, sheep, horses, chariots, slaves, and other humans.
14Babylon, the things
your heart desired
have all escaped
from you.
Every luxury
and all your glory
will be lost forever.
You will never
get them back.
15 The merchants had become rich because of her. But when they saw her sufferings, they were terrified. They stood at a distance, crying and mourning. 16Then they shouted,
“Pity the great city
of Babylon!
She dressed in fine linen
and wore purple
and scarlet cloth.
She had jewelry
made of gold
and precious stones
and pearls.
17 Yet in a single hour
her riches disappeared.”
Every ship captain and passenger and sailor stood at a distance, together with everyone who does business by traveling on the sea. 18 When they saw the smoke from her fire, they shouted, “This was the greatest city ever!”
19 They cried loudly, and in their sorrow they threw dust on their heads, as they said,
“Pity the great city
of Babylon!
Everyone who sailed the seas
became rich
from her treasures.
But in a single hour
the city was destroyed.
20 The heavens should be happy
with God's people
and apostles and prophets.
God has punished her
for them.”
21 A powerful angel then picked up a huge stone and threw it into the sea. The angel said,
“This is how the great city
of Babylon
will be thrown down,
never to rise again.
22 The music of harps and singers
and of flutes and trumpets
will no longer be heard.
No workers will ever
set up shop in that city,
and the sound
of grinding grain
will be silenced forever.
23Lamps will no longer shine
anywhere in Babylon,
and couples will never again
say wedding vows there.
Her merchants ruled
the earth,
and by her witchcraft
she fooled all nations.
24 On the streets of Babylon
is found the blood
of God's people
and of his prophets,
and everyone else.”
translation_text:
1Ku ŋaaŋnyiŋ mi yaa nya Maarɔwa choa ale wa nyini wenŋmazuk a siŋ tɛŋ. Wa ta ka pagrim nna yegayega ale a nyaksi a nya tɛŋka meena. 2Wa yaa kaari weeni ale lueluk kpioŋ ayen, <<Wa lo kama, tɛŋ kpieŋka Babilon a lo kama. Chichirik baata ale bo ka po ale nuim baata ale sii ale kisi nuruba ale sueri ka po. 3Ka kaboŋsa tuimaŋa a nye ase ka daam la, ate tɛŋsa meena a nyu. Tɛŋka zuk nalimaŋa a zamsi kaboŋsa tuima ka kala jigi. Tɛŋka zuk geruŋdɔma a va ka ka kɔrisa tuimaŋa nyiŋ a jigsi.>>
4Mi yaa ŋman wom lueluk ku choa wenŋmazuk a weeni ayen, <<Mi nuruma ni nyini ka po a nyini. Ni kan maara a tom ka tuimbaataŋa, ni kan maa nam ninam buui ate ba a nam la. 5Ka tuimbaataŋa a piisi ka nna yegayega, Wen abe teeri wa nyeka tuemu wie kama. 6Ni nye ka ase ka mɛ ale a nye nama diila, ka ale nye ni dii meena la, ni nye dila ku nɔi buye a tuni ka. Ka ale sueri beerika ale daamu a te nama la. Nama mɛ a sueri ku nɔi buye a te ka. 7Ni te ka ninam yegayega ase ka ale pai nalim ale masim a te ka dek diila. Diila wa kasim a weeni wadek kama ayen, <Mi nipok naawa kali ka dela. Mi daa pukɔgi ya. Mi kan maa seba jabuui ate ba a weeni ayen ninam la.> 8Wieŋa de nyiŋ, dai yeŋ ninam tɔgatɔga ase nyiŋtuila ale kum ale suipuurum ale kom ale yik wa. Ate bolim a dɛ wa dii nyiŋla Naawen dii ale ka Wen dii ale a bo wa buusa la a zuak kama yegayega.>>
9Tɛŋzuk de nalimaŋa baai ale maa tom ka kaboŋsaŋa ale ka kɔrisa tuimaŋa la ale kum te ka ase ba nin nya bolimu ale a dɛ ka ate nyuisaŋa a yiti la. 10Ba za ka nna niŋniŋa a nya dii nyiŋla ba a chali ka yɔgsum ale ba nin maa nam. Ba za kama a weeni ayen nya ku ale bie dii nna yegayega. Tɛŋ kpieŋka de ate miita pisiyuebi po ka deri nya ninam.
11Tɛŋka geruŋdɔma meena a kum a te ka diila waai a kan da ba ŋantaŋa. 12Waai a kan ŋman da ti ligmɔniŋka ale kpanaŋa ale tintana ŋaai ale a nyaksi la, ale ŋan baai ale a nyaksi la, ale ti garuk peelitaŋa ale ti garuk sobtaŋa ale garuk saalisaŋa ale ti garuk mɔntaŋa, ale ti daataŋa tɔgatɔga ka ale ŋan baai meena ate ba pai yauk nyina a nye ba la, ale da tii ligra ale pagra la, ale ti kutaŋa, ale ŋan baai ate ba pai nye diina puusa po la, 13ale ŋan baai nyum ale masa la ale ti daamu ale ti kpaamu ale zeuŋtaŋa ale ŋanbieŋa ale ti niiŋa ale ti piisaŋa ale ti wusumaŋa ale ŋa torokoma ale ti yɔmma ale nurubisa chiisaŋa. 14Ate geruŋdɔma yaa weeni wa ayen fi jɔk ŋan maŋsaŋa meena kama a jɔk fi nalimu mɛ. Fi be kan ŋman nya ba. 15Geruŋdɔ baai meena ale gerim tɛŋ kala po a jigsi la ale za ka nna niŋniŋa, dii nyiŋla ba a chali ka yɔgsum ale ba ale maa nam ale wa. Ba le kasim kaari kama, 16a weeni ayen, <<Ku bie ka nna yegayega tɛŋ kpieŋka de jigi. Ni nyiem kasim a jo ka garuk peeta ale garuk sobta ale garuk mɔnta ale a su ŋan baai ate ba pai ligmɔniŋ ale tintain naliŋsa ale ŋan baai ale a nyaksi a nye ba la. 17Ate ba deri jɔk ba ŋantaŋa meena miita pisiyuebi po.>> Ŋaaruŋtaŋa kpaŋŋa ale baai ale baai ale va ŋaaruŋtaŋa a nyiem ale baai ale a dam ŋaaruŋtaŋa ale baai meena ale a tom nyakpiemu po a dɛ la a yaa za niŋniŋa.
18A kaari dii nyiŋla ba ale nya bolimu ale a dɛ ba ate nyuisaŋa a yiti diila. Tɛŋ a jam karo a magsi chaab ale tɛŋka de. 19Ba jam kasim ŋari ka tanta a basi ba zuimaŋa po, ale a kaari a weeni ayen dii ale a nye tɛŋka de po la a bie ka yega. Ka ka tɛŋ kaai ate nuruba a jam ka ale ŋaaruŋta a gerim, a va ka ŋantaŋa nyiŋ a jigsi. Ate ka deri yiti dai yeŋ a jɔk jaab meena.
20Baai meena ale bo wenŋmazuk la, ni basi ate ni sue peenti Wen ale kaasi ka la nyiŋ. Wen nuruma ale Yeezu tuimtomdɔma ale Wen biisiteerɔma, ni basi ate ni sue peenti. Wen kaasi ka kama ba ale nye ni diila nyiŋ.
21Ate maarɔ kpioŋ a yaa pai tintain ate di soa ase niri la a yuk basi nyakpiemu po, ale weeni ayen, Wen a za wa yuk tɛŋ kpieŋka Babilon ale pagrim a basi ka dila dekdega ate waai a kan ŋman nya ka. 22Nuruba a kan ŋman wom nuruba luelita yaase kpanta nakka yaase paampuuŋta peerika yaase damunsa peerika. Nuru kan ŋman tom tuini tɛŋ kala po, waai abe kan wom niri num ka. 23Waai a kan nya zeuŋ toati ka tɛŋ kala po yaase nipok faarik wari du. Tɛŋ kala geruŋdɔma ale jam pagra tɛŋka meena zuk ate ka nuruma a tom kperisa tuima a paasi tɛŋka zuk nuruma meena.
24Babilon a nya ninam yegayega dii nyiŋla ba ale ko Wen biisiteerɔma ale Wen nuruma ale nuruba yegayega ate ba ziimu a nyini tɛŋka po la.

english_text:
1After this, I heard what sounded like a lot of voices in heaven, and they were shouting,
“Praise the Lord!
To our God belongs
the glorious power to save,
2 because his judgments
are honest and fair.
That filthy prostitute
ruined the earth
with shameful deeds.
But God has judged her
and made her pay
the price for murdering
his servants.”
3 Then the crowd shouted,
“Praise the Lord!
Smoke will never stop rising
from her burning body.”
4After this, the 24 elders and the four living creatures all knelt before the throne of God and worshiped him. They said, “Amen! Praise the Lord!”
The Marriage Supper of the Lamb
5 From the throne a voice said,
“If you worship
and fear our God,
give praise to him,
no matter who you are.”
6 Then I heard what seemed to be a large crowd that sounded like a roaring flood and loud thunder all mixed together. They were saying,
“Praise the Lord!
Our Lord God All-Powerful
now rules as king.
7So we will be glad and happy
and give him praise.
The wedding day of the Lamb
is here,
and his bride is ready.
8She will be given
a wedding dress
made of pure
and shining linen.
This linen stands for
the good things
God's people have done.”
9 Then the angel told me, “Put this in writing. God will bless everyone who is invited to the wedding feast of the Lamb.” The angel also said, “These things God has said are true.”
10I knelt at the feet of the angel and began to worship him. But the angel said, “Don't do that! I am a servant, just like you and everyone else who tells about Jesus. Don't worship anyone but God. Everyone who tells about Jesus does it by the power of the Spirit.”
The Rider on the White Horse
11 I looked and saw heaven was open, and a white horse was there. Its rider was called Faithful and True, and he is always fair when he judges or goes to war. 12 He had eyes like flames of fire, and he was wearing a lot of crowns. His name was written on him, but he was the only one who knew what the name meant.
13 The rider wore a robe that was covered with blood, and he was known as “The Word of God.” 14He was followed by armies from heaven that rode on white horses and were dressed in pure white linen. 15 From his mouth a sharp sword went out to attack the nations. He will rule them with an iron rod and will show the fierce anger of God All-Powerful by trampling the grapes in the pit where wine is made. 16On the part of the robe that covered his thigh was written, “KING OF KINGS AND Lord OF LordS.”
17 I then saw an angel standing on the sun, and he shouted to all the birds flying in the sky, “Come and join in God's great feast! 18You can eat the flesh of kings, rulers, leaders, horses, riders, free people, slaves, important people, and everyone else.”
19I also saw the beast and all kings of the earth come together. They fought against the rider on the white horse and against his army. 20 But the beast was captured and so was the false prophet. This is the same prophet who had worked miracles for the beast, so he could fool everyone who had the mark of the beast and worshiped the idol. The beast and the false prophet were thrown alive into a lake of burning sulfur. 21But the rest of their army was killed by the sword that came from the mouth of the rider on the horse. Then birds stuffed themselves on the dead bodies.
translation_text:
1Kude ŋaaŋnyiŋ mi yaa wom nuemka nna ase nuru boari la wenŋmazuk a weeni ayen, <<Pak Wen, varibasika ale zula ale pagrim, ka tama Wenni ale soa. 2Wa ka wensie nyɔnɔ ale a bo wensie buusa. Wen a bo mini nidoa yaalika wa ale kaasi tɛŋka ale wa kaboŋsa tuimaŋa la kama. Wen a namsi wa kama dii nyiŋla wa ale ko wa tomteerɔma la.>>
3Ba yaa ŋman pilim kaari a weeni ayen, <<Pak Wen, bolimu ale a dɛ tɛŋ kpieŋka la nyuisaŋa a kasim a jueli ka wein taam wuu.>>
4Nisɔm pisiye ale banaansiwa ale ŋanvuta tinaansiwa ale jam za gilim wenŋmazuk zukpaglika la, a jam a duak ka tɛŋ ale a yiti wenzuk a puusi Wen ale a weeni ayen, <<Ku be nye dila. Ni basi ate ti a pak wa.>>
5Ate mi yaa wom ale lueluk a ŋman nyini wenŋmazuk zukpaglika jigini a yaa a weeni ayen, <<Ku magsi ka nuru baai ale ka nuru kpienta ale baai ale kan daa nuru kpienta ale ge ba chim wa tomteerɔba ale a chali wa la, a te Wen pimpauk.>> 6Mi yaa ŋman wom nuru boari luelita ate ti jam a nye wai nna yegayega ase nyaata ale a chali la. Luelutaŋa mɛ a jam a na ase ka nanpansa ale a na la. Luelutaŋa a jam a weeni ayen, <<Ni basi ate ti a pak Wen. Wala ale soa ŋanta meena pagrim. Wa ka Naawen. 7Wa zuak a gaam ŋanta meena kama. Dila ale soa ate ku a fɛ ayen ti a pak wa ale suipeentik. Di danni a paari kama ayen Pabiika a faari nipok waai ale gomsi wadek a limisi wa la. 8Ba te wa powa ka suik ayen wa jo garuk tii ale nala ale a nyaksi la.>> Garuk naliŋtaŋa de ka tuim naliŋ sii ate Wen nuruma a jam nye la.
9Wen maarɔ wanyi a yaa jam weeni mi ayen, <<Ŋmarisi dii ate mi a weeni la a dueni. Baai ate ba le wi ba ayen ba jam maa dɛ ŋandiinta Pabiika nipowa faarika la, ba sue ale peenti.>> Wa le ga weeni nna a nueri la, wa ŋman pilim weeni maga a gum du ayen, <<Wieŋa de ka Wen wensie wie.>>
10Mi yaa kpi duna wa niŋ ayen m puusi wa, alege wa jam weeni mi ayen, <<Kan nye dila, dii nyiŋla mi ale fi ale fi suataŋa baai ale a weeni nuruba ayen Yeezu ale soa ba la, tama meena ka wa tomteerɔba. A puusi Wen nyiini.>> Wensieŋa ate Yeezu a pai sak la ale a basi ate biisiteerɔma a biisi.
11Ate mi yaa nya ale wenŋmazuk lak ate wusum peeluk a yaa jam za du. Ba jam a wi waai ale jam do bu la ayen ka, <<Wensie Nyɔnɔ.>> Wa yuei mɛ jam ale, <<Waai ale ta Siaka la.>> Daa meena wa kasim jam a cheŋ ka kpaliŋ po, ale a bo wa dachaasaŋa buusa ŋaai ale jam magsi wa boka la. 12Wa ninaŋa a jam muni ase ka bolim la. Wa mɛ jam vuk ka zutɔk boari. Ba jam ŋmarisi ka yuei dii ate nuru a jam zɛ di kiri la a dueni wa nyiŋ. Wadek wa nyiini ale jam seba yuenni kiri. 13Wa jam jo ka kasaauk ate ziim a jam muni ku meena. Wa yuei jam ale <<Wen Wanni.>> 14Tugurik tɔŋdɔba yegayega baai ale jam bo wenŋmazuk la a jam jo ka garuk naliŋta ale do wusum peeta a yaa jam a vi wa ŋaaŋ. 15Waai ale do wusum peelukku la a jam ta ka gebik ate ka ta noa ŋaye a yaa jam nyini wa nɔi po a nyini. Wa jam weeni ayen wa le pai kama a nye kpaliŋ ale tɛŋzuk nuruma a nak ba dɛ. Wa le soa ba ale pagrim nalimnyiini abe wa ŋmiak yɔnaŋa daamu. Dula jigini ale a sak Wen suipuurumu. 16Ba jam ŋmarisi ka yuei a dueni tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagni kasaauku ale wa naŋsaŋa kanyi nyiŋ. Yuenni jam ale, <<Nalima Meena Naab Ale Nyama Meena Nyɔnɔ.>>
17Mi yaa nya maarɔ ale wa za wenbinni zuk. Wa yaa jam kaari ale lueluk pagrik yegayega a weeni nuin sii meena ale jam bo wenŋmazuk a yiri la ayen, <<Ni tigsi chaab a jam dɛ ŋandiin tii ate Wen le te ni yegayega la. 18Wa le pai nalima ale tugurik tɔŋdɔba ale ba kpaga, ale wusuma ale baai ale do ŋa la, ale baai ale ka nuru kpienta ale baai ale kan daa nuru kpienta, baai ale ka yɔm, ale baai ale kan daa yɔm, bala meena ate Wen ale pai a te ate ni dɛ.>>
19Ate mi yaa nya duŋ kperikaliik kaai ale jam nyini nyakpiemu po a nyini la ale tɛŋzuk nalimaŋa ale ba tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale ba maa chaab a cheŋ ayen ba ga nye kpaliŋ ale nuru waai ale jam do wusum peelukku la ale wa tugurik tɔŋdɔma. 20Wenŋmazuk tugurik tɔŋdɔma a yaa jam nak yiak tɛŋzuk nuruma tugurik tɔŋdɔma ale ge yaa yik duŋ kperikaliika ale venta biisiteerɔwa. Biisiteerɔwa de a kasim jam a nye ka wakperikaliisa duŋ kperikaliika niŋ ayen ka paasi nuru baai ate duŋ kperikaliika a jam ŋmarisi ba nyiŋ ayen ba jam a kaab ka bɔglukku la. Wenŋmazuk tugurik tɔŋdɔma a yaa yik duŋ kperikaliika ale biisiteerɔwa a ta cheŋ ga yuk basi nyakpiemu po, juijui ate bolimu a kasim a dɛ la. 21Wenŋmazuk tugurik tɔŋdɔma kpagni waai ale jam do wusum peelukku la, a yaa yeeri gebik woŋ kaai ale jam ta noa ŋayewa la wa nɔnni po a yaa ko tɛŋzuk tugurik tɔŋdɔma baai ale jam tali la. Nuinsaŋa a yaa basi wenŋmazuk ale siŋ a dɛ ba chak ale tali.

english_text:
The Thousand Years
1I saw an angel come down from heaven, carrying the key to the deep pit and a big chain. 2 He chained the dragon for 1,000 years. It is that old snake, who is also known as the devil and Satan. 3Then the angel threw the dragon into the pit. He locked and sealed it, so 1,000 years would go by before the dragon could fool the nations again. But after that, it would have to be set free for a little while.
4 I saw thrones, and sitting on those thrones were the ones who had been given the right to judge. I also saw the souls of the people who had their heads cut off because they had told about Jesus and preached God's message. They were the same ones who had not worshiped the beast or the idol, and they had refused to let its mark be put on their foreheads or hands. They will come to life and rule with Christ for 1,000 years.
5-6These people are the first to be raised to life, and they are especially blessed and holy. The second death has no power over them. They will be priests for God and Christ and will rule with them for 1,000 years.
No other dead people were raised to life until 1,000 years later.
Satan Is Defeated
7At the end of the 1,000 years, Satan will be set free. 8 He will fool the countries of Gog and Magog, which are at the far ends of the earth, and their people will follow him into battle. They will have as many followers as there are grains of sand along the beach, 9and they will march all the way across the earth. They will surround the camp of God's people and the city God loves. But fire will come down from heaven and destroy the whole army. 10Then the devil who fooled them will be thrown into the lake of fire and burning sulfur. He will be there with the beast and the false prophet, and they will be in pain day and night forever and ever.
The Judgment at the Great White Throne
11 I saw a great white throne with someone sitting on it. Earth and heaven tried to run away, but there was no place for them to go. 12 I also saw all the dead people standing in front of that throne. Every one of them was there, no matter who they had once been. Several books were opened, and then the book of life was opened. The dead were judged by what those books said they had done.
13The sea gave up the dead people who were in it, and death and its kingdom also gave up their dead. Then everyone was judged by what they had done. 14Afterwards, death and its kingdom were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death. 15Anyone whose name wasn't written in the book of life was thrown into the lake of fire.
translation_text:
1Ate mi yaa nya maarɔ wanyi ale wa basi wenŋmazuk ale ge siŋ tɛŋzuk. Wa jam ta ka chɔrin dobdi wa nisa po. Wa jam maa ta ka Vɔrup buui ale kan ka kpeglimka la nɔnni safiika wa nisa po. 2Maarɔwa a yaa jam yik jaab waai ale a neensi waamu a jam yiak nipowa la, a yaa bobi wa ale chɔrin dobni ayen ku paari bena tusidi. Jaamu de ka jabiok yaase Sitaana ate wa boro a ta nyini dila po la. 3Maarɔwa yaa yik wa a yuk basi Vɔrup buui ale kan ka kpeglimka la po, a yaa pai wa saafiika a kpari vɔrumu nɔnni. Wa nye dila ayen ka wa kan ŋman baga a paasi tɛŋzuk nuruma. Wa le bo ka vɔrumu po ate bena tusini a ga nueri. Di danni a dan ga paari, ba le lak vɔrumu ate wa nyini boro maga.
4Ate mi yaa ŋman nya ale zukpaglik si chaab a za dula. Ba yaa jam pai pagrim a te baai ale jam kali si zuk la ayen ba bo buusa. Mi yaa jam nya baai ate tɛŋzuk nuruma a jam ko ba ayen dii nyiŋla ba jam a sak wensieŋa ate Yeezu a pai sak la ale Wen wanni. Ba an jam puusi a te duŋ kperikaliika yaase ba kaabi ka bɔglukku. Ba an jam basi mɛ ate ka ŋmarisi ka yuenni a dueni ba dee ale ba nisa nyiŋsa. Yeezu Kirisita a jam yeeri ba kama a ta nyini kum po a nyini ayen ba ale wa a maa chaab a chim nalima a soa tɛŋka ate ku ga paari bena tusini. 5Bala ate wa liŋ jam nak yiti kum po. Bena tusini a jam nueri kama ale ge ate wa yeeri baai ale jam liŋ kpi la kum po a ta nyini. 6Baai ate Kirisita a liŋ lueri a nye ate ba yiti kum po la, ba sue ale peenti kama. Ba le chim ka Wen ale Kirisita kaabteerɔba. Ba ale wa ale ba soa tɛŋka ate ku ga paari bena tusini la. Kum buui ale a saari buyewa la a kan nya pagrim ba zuwa.
7Bena tusini a dan ga nueri, ba le basi ate Sitaana nyini Vɔrumu po a nyini. 8Wa le nyiem a cheŋ kama a paasi tɛŋzuk nuruma, abe wa a tigsi ba a gum chaab ale Gɔg ale Megɔg ate ba maa chaab a tu Wen nuruma a nye kpaliŋ. Sitaana ale wa nuruma de ale piisi kama nna yegayega ase beli tintain busuŋ la ate nuru an baga a le chiini ba. 9Ba le nyini ka jigi meena a jam gilim Wen nuruma baai ale jam bo dula la. Wa mariŋ ba boka jigi ka yegayega. Wen ale basi ate bolim nyini wenŋmazuk a siŋ jam dɛ baai meena ale za gilim la. 10Ba yaa le yik jabioku waai ale jam a nyiem a paasi nuruma la a yuk wa a gum duŋ kperikaliika ale venta biisiteerɔwa po ate bolim buui ale kasim jam a dɛ nyakpiemu po la a dɛ ba meena. Dula, wala ale duŋ kperikaliika ale venta biisiteerɔwa ale kasim a nam ka nna yegayega taam wuu.
11Ate mi yaa ŋman nya zukpaglika wenŋmazuk. Ka jam ka zukpaglik kpieŋ peeluk ate nuru a jam kali ka zuk. Tɛŋka ale wenŋmazuk a jam muriŋ bɛ wa niŋ, jigi mɛ abe jam karo ayen ba sugi. 12Mi yaa nya tɛŋzuk nuruma baai ale jam ka nuru kpienta ale baai ale jam kan daa nuru kpienta ate Wen yaa nak ba yiti kum po la. Ba jam za ka wa zulaŋa zukpaglika niŋ. Ba yaa jam lak nyuvuri gbaŋka ale gbaŋsa si chaab. Wa jam bo ba buusa a magsi chaab ale ka dii ate ba nye la ale dii ale jam ŋmarisi a nyo gbaŋsaŋa po la. 13Baai ale jam kpi ate ba gu ba tɛŋka ale nyakpientaŋa po la, ale baai ale jam bo kpiluŋ tɛŋ la, nuruma de meena a jam za ka dula. Wen a jam bo ba buusa a magsi chaab ale ka tuim ŋaai ate ba jam tom la. 14Ba jam pai ka kum ale Kpiluŋ Tɛŋ a yuk basi nyakpiemu po ate bolimu a kasim jam a dɛ la ayen bu dɛ ba a kaasi. Kude ka kum buui ale a saari buye la. 15Baai ate ba an ŋmarisi ba yueŋa a nyo nyuvuri gbaŋka po la, ba jam maa pai ba a yuk basi ka dula.

english_text:
The New Heaven and the New Earth
1 I saw a new heaven and a new earth. The first heaven and the first earth had disappeared, and so had the sea. 2 Then I saw New Jerusalem, the holy city, coming down from God in heaven. It was like a bride dressed in her wedding gown and ready to meet her husband.
3 I heard a loud voice shout from the throne:
God's home is now with his people. He will live with them, and they will be his own. Yes, God will make his home among his people. 4 He will wipe all tears from their eyes, and there will be no more death, suffering, crying, or pain. These things of the past are gone forever.
5Then the one sitting on the throne said:
I am making everything new. Write down what I have said. My words are true and can be trusted. 6 Everything is finished! I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I will freely give water from the life-giving fountain to everyone who is thirsty. 7 All who win the victory will be given these blessings. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
8But I will tell you what will happen to cowards and to everyone who is unfaithful or dirty-minded or who murders or is sexually immoral or uses witchcraft or worships idols or tells lies. They will be thrown into that lake of fire and burning sulfur. This is the second death.
The New Jerusalem
9I saw one of the seven angels who had the bowls filled with the seven last terrible troubles. The angel came to me and said, “Come on! I will show you the one who will be the bride and wife of the Lamb.” 10 Then with the help of the Spirit, he took me to the top of a very high mountain. There he showed me the holy city of Jerusalem coming down from God in heaven.
11The glory of God made the city bright. It was dazzling and crystal clear like a precious jasper stone. 12 The city had a high and thick wall with twelve gates, and each one of them was guarded by an angel. On each of the gates was written the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel. 13Three of these gates were on the east, three were on the north, three more were on the south, and the other three were on the west. 14The city was built on twelve foundation stones. On each of the stones was written the name of one of the Lamb's twelve apostles.
15 The angel who spoke to me had a gold measuring stick to measure the city and its gates and its walls. 16The city was shaped like a cube, because it was just as high as it was wide. When the angel measured the city, it was about 2,400 kilometers high and 2,400 kilometers wide. 17Then the angel measured the wall, and by our measurements it was about 60 meters high.
18 The wall was built of jasper, and the city was made of pure gold, clear as crystal. 19Each of the twelve foundations was a precious stone. The first was jasper, the second was sapphire, the third was agate, the fourth was emerald, 20the fifth was onyx, the sixth was carnelian, the seventh was chrysolite, the eighth was beryl, the ninth was topaz, the tenth was chrysoprase, the eleventh was jacinth, and the twelfth was amethyst. 21Each of the twelve gates was a solid pearl. The streets of the city were made of pure gold, clear as crystal.
22I did not see a temple there. The Lord God All-Powerful and the Lamb were its temple. 23 And the city did not need the sun or the moon. The glory of God was shining on it, and the Lamb was its light.
24 Nations will walk by the light of that city, and kings will bring their riches there. 25 Its gates are always open during the day, and night never comes. 26The glorious treasures of nations will be brought into the city. 27 But nothing unworthy will be allowed to enter. No one who is dirty-minded or who tells lies will be there. Only those whose names are written in the Lamb's book of life will be in the city.
translation_text:
1Ate mi yaa ŋman nya ale wenŋmazuk ale tɛŋzuk ale nyakpiemu a deri bɛ mi nina po. Wen yaa ŋman nye wenŋmazuk paalik ale tɛŋzuk paalik. 2Mi yaa nya Wen tɛŋ kpieŋ kaai ate wa jam lueri a te wadek la a yaa basi wenŋmazuk a siŋ tɛŋzuk. Tɛŋ kpieŋ kala ale Jerusalem paalika. Ku jam a nye se ka nipok ale kasim jam a gomsi wadek ayen wa yali wa chora la. 3Mi yaa wom ale lueluk kpioŋ a nyini wenŋmazuk zukpaglika jigini a yaa a weeni ayen, <<Wom mi. Wen viuku a bo ka nuruba suŋsuŋ, wa ale bo ale ba, ate ba ale chim wa nuruba, ate Wen dek ale bo ale ba. 4Wa le duisi ba ninyaata a basi. Kum ale ninam ale nyiŋdomma a kan ŋman boro. Ku le liŋ jam ka diila, ku kan ŋman nye dila diipo diipo.>>
5Waai ale jam kali Wen zulaŋa zukpaglika zuk la a yaa weeni ayen, <<M nye ŋanta meena ka ŋanpaala.>> Wa ŋman pilim weeni mi ayen, <<Ŋmarisi dii ate m le weeni fu a dueni, dii nyiŋla m wieŋa ka wensie wie ale magsi mɛ. 6M tuimaŋa a nueri kama. M ka Piilimka, m be kasim boro kama taam wuu. M nyuvuri paalik kaai ate m pai a te nuruba la, a nye se ka nyiam la. Nyanyuila ale ta waai meena la, m le basi ate ba nyu bu ka tiirim. 7Waai ale ta pagrim wie meena zuk la ale wa tuesi ŋantaŋa de meena, mi ale chim wa Wen ate wa mɛ ale chim m nidoabili. 8Alege baai ale yɔgsa la, bumbobrɔma ale baai ale daŋ badek ale wabaata la ale nuru koorisa ale kaboŋ nyeerisa ale sampoporinni tuima ale baai ale a kaab bɔgta ale velimvendisaŋa, a za ba jo ka mɔgi diipo ate bolim a dɛ taam wuu. Ku la a nye ase ba a kpi a saari ka buye la.>>
9Wen maarɔ baai bayopɔiwa ale jam ta china ŋayopɔiwa ate ninammu a bo ŋa po la, wanyi a yaa weeni mi ayen, jam de ate m dak Pabiika powa a sak fu.
10Wen Chiika yaa sak mi ate mi nya ale maarɔ a ji mi a ta jueli guuk zuk. Wa yaa sak mi Tɛŋ Weleŋka Jerusalem ale ka nyini wenŋmazuk Wen jigi a cheena ale 11a nyaksi ale Wen zulaŋa. Tɛŋka a kasim a nyaksi kama ase tintain mɔnta la, a nya nna cheri ase nyaasuŋ la. 12Ka jam ta ka parik kpieŋ nna woŋwoŋŋoa ale nansuiŋta pi ale tiye, ate maarɔba pi ale baye a limisi nansuiŋtaŋa. Nansuiŋtaŋa nɔi ba ŋmarisi ka Izirali bisaŋa pi ale bayewa yue a dueni du. 13Nansuiŋta tita ale jam bo kauk kunyi meena. Tita ale jam bo kori geŋ. Tita ale jam bo yeseoku geŋ. Tita ale jam bo wiilukku geŋ. Tita mɛ ale jam bo yeniŋ geŋ. 14Ba pai ka tintana pi ale ŋaye a dueni nyubini ase parika ale ŋmarisi Pabiika tuimtomdɔma pi ale bayewa wie a dueni ŋa nyiŋ la. 15Wen maarɔ waai ale biisi ale mi la, a jam ta ka tachek ate ba pai ligmɔniŋ a nye ka ayen wa magsi tɛŋka, ale nansuiŋtaŋa ale parisaŋa. 16Tɛŋka labsimu ale ka woglimmu a jam soa ase ka chaab la. Maarɔwa a jam pai ka wa tachekka a magsi. Ka woglimmu jam ka mɛɛla tusidi ale kobsinu (1,500). Ka labsimu ale ka juelika a jam soa ase ka dila la. 17Maarɔwa jam magsi ka parika ate ka biglimu a chim ka anamagib kobsiye ale pinaanuŋ ale naaniŋ, a va chaab ale nurubiik magsika. 18Tɛŋka parika ba jam pai ka tintain mɔnta a nye ka alege tɛŋka po dek ligmɔniŋ a nye nna ase nyaasuŋ la. 19Ba pai ka tintain naliŋsa tɔgatɔga a ŋmirisi nyubini. Ba ale liŋ pai ka tintain mɔnta a dueni nyubini, buyewa po ka tintain sobta, butawa po ka tintain paasa, bunaansiwa po ka tintain ŋaai ale a nye ase gunungoona la, 20bunuwa po ka tintain ŋaai ale a nye ase mɔnuŋ ale peeluk a gum chaab la, buyuebiwa po, ka tintain ŋaai ale a nye ase kpabunyiam la, buyopɔiwa po ka tintain salima, naaniŋka po ka tintain paata, neokku po ka tintain ŋaai ale a nye ase dubuulim la, piwa po ka tintain ŋaai ale a nye ase gunungoona ale peela la, pi ale bunyiwa po ka tintain bibituk, pi ale buyewa po ka tintain ŋaai ale a nye ase busumbooŋ la. 21Ba yaa jam pai ka ŋanta pi ale baye wa ate ba a nyaksi ase tintana la, a nye parika nansuiŋta pi ale tiyewa meena. Ba jam maa pai ka ligmɔniŋ mɛ a se nyaasuŋ la a piisi suik kpioŋku.
22Mi an jam nya Wen yenni tɛŋka po dii nyiŋla Yenni ale Naawen dii ale ka Wen Kpienni la dek ale wa Pabiika ka Yenni. 23Baai ale jam bo dula la, an jam a yaali wenbiri yaase chiika. Wen ale wa nalimu ale a nyaksi ate ba a nya. Pabiika mɛ ale ba bolim ate ba a nya. 24Tɛŋzuk nuruma le ba nya bolimu dɛ a cheŋ. Ba nalimaŋa mɛ le pai ba zulaŋa a jam gum du. 25Ba kan lik siaka noaŋa. Ŋa le kasim a lak kama daa meena. Dii nyiŋla yok a kan bo du. 26Tɛŋzuk nuruma mɛ le ba zula yegayega a jam gum tɛŋka po. 27Tuim baata nyama ale baai ale a nye kaboŋsa ale maara velim la, ba kan baga a maa jo dula. Baai ate ba ŋmarisi ba yueŋa a nyo Pabiika nyuvuri paalika gbaŋka po la, bala nyiini ale ba jo du.

english_text:
1 The angel showed me a river that was crystal clear, and its waters gave life. The river came from the throne where God and the Lamb were seated. 2 Then it flowed down the middle of the city's main street. On each side of the river are trees that grow a different kind of fruit each month of the year. The fruit gives life, and the leaves are used as medicine to heal the nations.
3 God's curse will no longer be on the people of that city. He and the Lamb will be seated there on their thrones, and its people will worship God 4 and will see him face to face. God's name will be written on the foreheads of the people. 5 Never again will night appear, and no one who lives there will ever need a lamp or the sun. The Lord God will be their light, and they will rule forever.
The Coming of Christ
6Then I was told:
These words are true and can be trusted. The Lord God controls the spirits of his prophets, and he is the one who sent his angel to show his servants what must happen very soon. 7Remember, I am coming soon! God will bless everyone who pays attention to the message of this book.
8My name is John, and I am the one who heard and saw these things. Then after I had heard and seen all this, I knelt down and began to worship at the feet of the angel who had shown it to me.
9But the angel said,
Don't do that! I am a servant, just like you. I am the same as a follower or a prophet or anyone else who obeys what is written in this book. God is the one you should worship.
10Don't keep the prophecies in this book a secret. These things will happen soon.
11 Evil people will keep on being evil, and everyone who is dirty-minded will still be dirty-minded. But good people will keep on doing right, and God's people will always be holy.
12 Then I was told:
I am coming soon! And when I come, I will reward everyone for what they have done. 13 I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.
14 God will bless all who have washed their robes. They will each have the right to eat fruit from the tree that gives life, and they can enter the gates of the city. 15But outside the city will be dogs, witches, immoral people, murderers, idol worshipers, and everyone who loves to tell lies and do wrong.
16 I am Jesus! And I am the one who sent my angel to tell all of you these things for the churches. I am David's Great Descendant, and I am also the bright morning star.
17 The Spirit and the bride say, “Come!”
Everyone who hears this should say, “Come!”
If you are thirsty, come! If you want life-giving water, come and take it. It's free!
18 Here is my warning for everyone who hears the prophecies in this book:
If you add anything to them, God will make you suffer all the terrible troubles written in this book. 19If you take anything away from these prophecies, God will not let you have part in the life-giving tree and in the holy city described in this book.
20The one who has spoken these things says, “I am coming soon!”
So, Lord Jesus, please come soon!
21I pray that the Lord Jesus will be kind to all of you.
translation_text:
1Maarɔwa yaa dak Wen nyuvuri benni nyiamu ale jam a nyaksi nna ase nyaasuŋ la. Di jam nyini ka Wen ale Pabiika jigi wenŋmazuk. 2Benni a jam chali va ka tɛŋka suik kpioŋku suŋsuŋ. Wen nyuvuri tiimu a jam za ka benni kabtaŋa meena a yɔn yɔna. Bu jam a yɔni ka pi ale buye ben yeŋ po. Si vaataŋa ale jam a basi ate tɛŋzuk nuruma a nya nyiŋyɔgsa. 3Ŋan baai ate Wen a ka te ba la, a kan maa bo tɛŋka po. Wen ale Pabiika zulaŋa zukpaglika a bo ka dula ate wa tomteerɔma puusi a te ba. 4Ba le nya Wen nimbidiaka ate wa ŋmarisi wa yuenni a dueni ba dee nyiŋ. 5Abe wa basi ate ba chim nalima taam wuu. Yɔk a kan bo dula, dii nyiŋla ba Naawen dii ale ka Wen la ale wa te ba kantueŋ. Ba kan ba a yaali kantueŋŋa yaase zeuŋta ayen ba a nya.
6Ate maarɔwa a yaa weeni mi ayen, <<M le a yaali ayen m weeni fu diila a magsi kama ale ŋman chim wensie mɛ. Naawen dii ale ka Wen la waai ale pai wa Chiika a nyo wa biisiteerɔma suiniima po la, a tom ka mi wa maarɔwa ayen wa jam sak wa tomteerɔma dii ale di nye yɔgyɔgla la.>>
7Yeezu a weeni ayen, <<Wom m wieŋa de. Ku kan beni ale ge ate m pilim ŋman jam. Baai meena ale a zuli dii ate m ŋmarisi nyo gbaŋka de po la, ba sue ale peenti kama.>>
8Mi, Jɔɔn, a nya kama ale wom wieŋa de meena. Mi le ga nya ale wom wieŋa de meena a nueri la, m jam kpi ka duna tɛŋ ayen m puusi maarɔwa waai ale dak wieŋa de meena a sak mu la. 9Alege wa weeni mi ayen, <<Kan nye dila, dii nyiŋla mi ale fi ale fi suataŋa baai ale ka Wen biisiteerɔba ale a va gbaŋka de wieŋa la, tama meena ka Wen tomteerɔba. Puusi a te wala nyiini.>> 10Wa ŋman pilim weeni mi ayen, <<Kan fi pai wie ŋaai ale bo gbaŋka de po la a sugi, dii nyiŋla, ku kan beni ale ge ate ŋa chim wensie. 11Basi ate waai ale a tom tuimkaasima la a kasim tom tuimkaasima a cheŋ, basi ate waai ale a tom tuimdaŋtisa la a kasim tom tuimdaŋtisa a cheŋ, basi ate waai ale a tom tuimaŋsa la a kasim tom tuimaŋsa a cheŋ, a basi mɛ ate waai ale welema la a kasim welema a cheŋ.>>
12Yeezu a weeni ayen, <<Nya, m cheena ku kan beni. M ta m tutunaŋa kama, ate m le te waai meena a magsi chaab ale wa le tom diila. 13Mi ale Piilimka ale Kpeglimka, mi ale dɛ niŋ ale wari ŋaaŋ, mi ale piilim ale kpeglim.
14Baai ale a sugri ba gattaŋa ayen daŋta a kan tiri ba ate ba nya suik a jo tɛŋka po a dɛ Wen nyuvuri tiimu yɔnni la, ba sue le peenti. 15Alege baai ale a tom tuimbaata ale a porisi ale a nye kaboŋsa ale a ko nuruba ale a kaab bɔgta ale a velim venta ba biik po ale ba tuima po, bala meena le wari ka tɛŋka peelimmu po. Ba kan nya suik a jo ka po.
16<<Mi, Yeezu, ale tom m maarɔwa ayen wa jam mooli wieŋa de ate baai meena ale a va mi la wom ŋa. Mi ka Naawa Deevid ŋaaŋbiik. Mi a nyaksi ka nna yegayega ase vari chiŋmarika la.>>
17Wen Chiika ale Pabiika powa a maa chaab a weeni ni ayen, <<Ni jam.>> Baai meena ale a wom ba wieŋa la, ale maa weeni kama mɛ ayen, <<Ni jam.>> Nama meena baai ate nyanyuila a ta ni la, ni jam nyu Wen nyuvuri nyiamu tiirim.
18Mi, Jɔɔn, a kaam baai meena ale wom gbaŋka de wieŋa la kama. Waai a dan pai wari di choa a gum mi wieŋa de po, Wen le pai ninam ate maarɔba bayopɔiwa a jam ta la a gum ku nyɔnɔ waali kaai ate wa le waali wa la po. 19Waai mɛ a be dan yeeri wari gbaŋka de po a basi, Wen a kan basi ate ku nyɔnɔ a jo wa tɛŋka po a maa dɛ wa nyuvuri tiimu yɔnaŋa, ŋaai ate m poom weeni ŋa wari gbaŋka de po la.
20Nuru waai ale za m wieŋa ŋaaŋ la a weeni ayen, <<Wensie, ku kan beni ale ge ate m pilim ŋman jam.>> Basi ate fi le weeni diila a sum nye. Ti Nyɔnɔ Yeezu Kirisita, pilim ŋman jam.
21M be ŋman a saalim ayen ti Nyɔnɔwa Yeezu Kirisita ŋmanteka a bo ale ni meena. Ku be nye dila.
